title: Keep prepared spawn-all children handler-resolvable after registry mutation
description:
PR #6262 skips the child-local registry recheck when a spawn-all child has an authoritative prepared entry, but the installed snapshot still stores only the original registered TYPE keyword under :rf/machine-type. Spawned actors have no per-instance handler; the lazy resolver must resolve that keyword back through the current registrar. Therefore the exact unregister seam the patch accepts installs a snapshot that is not a live/resolvable actor.

Current-origin/main JVM reproduction: register a child whose :idle handles the synthetic :rf.machine.spawn/spawned bootstrap by transitioning to :ready; unregister its TYPE from a :rf.machine.spawn-all/started listener; dispatch the parent. The child snapshot exists, but it remains :idle with :rf/bootstrap-pending? true, and the bootstrap tail emits exactly one :rf.error/no-such-handler. The shipped test uses an already-terminal-looking :running child and asserts only snapshot presence/state, so it false-greens this inert actor. Re-registering to a different spec has the related split-authority problem: initial snapshot is prepared from v1 while lazy dispatch resolves the handler from current v2.

Preserve the authoritative handoff as one coherent runtime authority, not merely an initial snapshot copy. A prepared child must remain handler-resolvable for bootstrap and later events under the supported unregister/re-register mutations. Prefer a small prepared-spec/resolver or ordering fix; do not add a spawn coordinator or registry transaction system.
acceptance_criteria:
- The unregister-between-preflight-and-install fixture uses a child whose synthetic bootstrap event causes an observable transition; after the invoke, the child has completed bootstrap and no :rf.error/no-such-handler fired.
- A later ordinary event also executes against a coherent machine definition; snapshot and handler never mix prepared v1 state with an unrelated current v2 definition.
- Re-register, unregister-one, unregister-all, standalone/no-preparation fail-closed, prepared-scratch consumption, mixed rejection, and exact-incarnation behavior remain covered on CLJ and CLJS.
- State the chosen definition-lifetime rule explicitly and preserve hot-reload semantics intentionally; no coordinator, global registry lock, or transaction layer.

title: Keep epoch restore exact-owned inside callback-bearing cleanup fan-outs
description: PR #6221 threads the captured incarnation token to outer restore seams, but callback-bearing cleanup batches still re-enter bare frame-id state after a single check. Resources checks A once, then timer/work-ledger cleanup runs by id; work-ledger abort-slot! calls an abort callback before a bare-key dissoc, so callback churn can seat B and reuse the same slot before A's returning cleanup deletes B's handle. Post-install quiesce checks once around a Machines→HTTP hook loop; a machine cancellation trace can seat B, after which the HTTP hook snapshots and aborts B's requests. Deferred resource-intent emission similarly fans out multiple callbacks under one outer check. This violates the promised exact-incarnation transaction and can mutate a live successor.
acceptance_criteria:
- Preinstall cleanup atomically detaches only A-owned timer/work handles while A's token is live; callbacks act on detached attempt identities and never re-read or dissociate a successor slot.
- Exact ownership is revalidated at every callback boundary inside deferred trace commit and the Machines/HTTP quiesce chain, or the captured token/A-owned snapshot is carried into each helper.
- A deterministic resource-abort callback seats B and reuses the same [frame-id work-id]; B's handle survives byte-for-byte and the stale restore fails.
- A deterministic first quiesce hook/trace intent seats B; no later A tail aborts, stamps, emits against, or quiesces B, while an already committed A install still returns true.
- Keep tokens internal and preserve the ordinary restore path; no public token, retry, lock, or general transaction framework.

title: Serialize trace listeners across concurrent frame drains at a post-drain seam
description:
PR #6248 (`127722fff4bf33d7dfad428319547c8f6d8f897c`, applied as `95ac9396cd8a0fe06ea50ebc8fad9841899197c4`) fixed the shape-based trace-listener bypass but did not restore the serial-listener contract required by source bead rf2-rakqk and Spec 009. `re-frame.trace.tooling/deliver-to-tooling!` still drives any drain-lock-owning emit inline, outside the process fanout monitor. Two DIFFERENT frames may drain concurrently on the JVM; each drainer owns its own frame lock, so both can enter the same arbitrary listener callback at once. The current implementation comment says "two ... drains of the SAME frame"; a single frame cannot have two simultaneous drain-lock owners, while independent frames are the actual public failure.

Deterministic current-main reproduction: register one listener; start `dispatch-sync` into `:rf/default`; latch its `:rf.event/run-start` callback while frame A's drain lock is held; start `dispatch-sync` into `:audit/other` on another thread. Frame B entered the same listener before A returned. Evidence: `{:b-entered-before-a-return true, :max-concurrent 2, :log-before-release [[:enter :rf/default] [:enter :audit/other] [:exit :audit/other]]}`. Both threads then completed, proving overlap rather than deadlock. The merged three focused suites remain green (3 tests / 275 assertions) because they cover clean-vs-clean, frame-shaped public emits outside a drain, and the one-frame AB-BA cycle, but not drain-vs-drain.

This also leaves arbitrary programmer/tool listener code running while the framework owns the target frame drain lock, directly contrary to rf2-rakqk's acceptance criterion. The practical risks are overlapping mutation in devtools/recorders, nondeterministic observation order across independent frames, and new lock cycles through listener-authored work.

Repair the timing seam, not the classifier. Preserve synchronous public/manual emits and same-thread nested ordering, but defer internal drain-owned listener fanout to one explicit post-drain boundary before the enclosing dispatch/drain call returns. That boundary must serialize listener callbacks process-wide without holding or waiting on a frame drain lock. Keep the mechanism bounded: no public lock/token API, compatibility mode, listener restriction, per-listener locking maze, or general scheduler.
acceptance_criteria:
- On the JVM, one registered trace listener is never entered concurrently with itself across concurrent drains of different frames, clean-vs-drain, and clean-vs-clean emits; each listener sees one defined total order.
- Arbitrary listener code is neither invoked nor awaited while the framework owns any target frame drain lock.
- The existing monitor→listener→`dispatch-sync(F)` versus `F.:drain-lock`→trace interleaving remains bounded and every event/trace settles exactly once; no fanout-monitor/drain-lock AB-BA edge returns.
- Externally authored/public emits remain synchronous through callback completion. Internal drain traces delivered at a post-drain boundary preserve emission order, expose no partially settled state, and complete before the enclosing public dispatch/drain operation returns.
- Same-thread reentrant outer-before-inner ordering, nested synchronous completion, listener exception isolation, continuation suppression, registration replacement, CLJS behavior, and production elision remain correct.
- Deterministic controls include two different simultaneous frame drains and prove both non-overlap and callbacks-outside-drain-lock ownership; existing deadlock and public frame-tagged controls stay green.
- The solution is one private ownership/post-drain seam, not event-shape inference, a public synchronization surface, listener prohibitions, or a general scheduler.
notes:
BLOCKED — #6365 MUST NOT MERGE AS-IS. Two genuine regressions found by an independent fix-worker (2026-07-18), verdict (b) on both, proven by controlled experiment rather than inferred.

REGRESSION 1 — deferred-continue latch is SINGLE-USE (the serious one).
The first check passes; every later check consults the LIVE predicate. Its docstring assumes a later false reading means a listener suppressed the event — but under deferral the fence is already false post-drain for ordinary reasons. So drive-fanout! abandons after listener #1 and SKIPS LISTENERS 2..N for every emit carrying a continuation fence.
Measured: reverting ONLY the five core source files, test tree untouched -> 25 traces with :rf.event/dispatched for four events. On the branch -> 22 traces with one. Three dispatch envelopes are DROPPED, not delayed (absent after an 800ms settle). run-start/run-end/frame-state-changed still arrive; only the dispatch envelope vanishes, taking the :source :router axis with it. A 3-listener probe confirms listeners 2 and 3 receive nothing.
BLAST RADIUS: any app with two or more trace listeners (Xray + Story + app) silently loses every cascaded event dispatch envelope.

REGRESSION 2 — machines spawn-all: DURABLE CORRUPTION, not an observation artifact.
install-spawn! selects the child TYPE reference on an explicitly documented premise that :rf.machine.spawn/spawned and :rf.error/system-id-collision fan SYNCHRONOUSLY to application listeners before the write. This PR falsifies that on JVM: type-ref-fn reads an un-diverged registrar, stamps the cheap keyword, and the unregister lands after. Children hold a dangling :rf/machine-type, raise :no-such-handler and stay inert — or SPLIT (v1 snapshot on a v2 handler). Exactly the modes rf2-rxjy3 and rf2-zo5n9 removed. Rewriting those assertions would BLESS REAL CORRUPTION.

FAMILY 3 — destroyed_exit_order (needs a ruling, does not block on its own): inline :exit action and deferred :destroyed listener no longer interleave. The file cites Spec 005:2138 for "a consumer observing the db between :exit and :rf.machine/destroyed sees the live snapshot" — deferral removes that. Flagged rather than silently rewritten.

THE DESIGN QUESTION THE REWORK MUST ANSWER: how to distinguish "the predicate went false because a listener body acted" (a real suppression, honour it) from "already false when the deferred fan-out began" (ordinary post-drain state, must NOT abandon the remaining listeners). The previous brief fenced off redesigning the deferral mechanism, so the worker correctly stopped. THAT FENCE IS NOW LIFTED for the rework.

ALSO STILL TRUE from the original work (preserve): the ThreadLocal (NOT a ^:dynamic Var — a Var binding leaks through bound-fn into next-tick/set-timeout! executor threads); the retired frame/thread-owns-drain-serialization? plus its late-bind hook and directory row; the unreachability argument (monitor at 2 sites, drain-lock at 3, each fully enclosed).

Evidence and control table posted on PR #6365.
REGRESSION 1 FIXED (44386ba13b). Root cause was NOT a stale latch as first theorised: deferred-continue LEVEL-TESTED a predicate that is not a pure function of registry state. router/dispatch!s target-live? reaches frame/event-owner-live?, which reads the DYNAMIC frame/*event-owner*. A deferred fan-out runs after the drain unwinds, so that var is unbound and the fence reads FALSE for every cascaded dispatch — no destroy, no suppression, just an unwound stack. drive-fanout! read that as suppression and abandoned listeners 2..N.
FIX: detect a TRANSITION, not a level. The first continue? call — taken in the flush, immediately before listener 1 — records a BASELINE and passes. Later calls run in that same flush context, so a change from baseline is attributable to the listener body that ran between the two reads. Baseline TRUE -> consult live; a later false is genuine suppression and still stops the remainder (preserves rf2-eaxnai exactly where it was about). Baseline FALSE -> already false before any listener could act; ordinary post-drain state, never suppression, cannot abandon anyone.
PROOF (3 listeners, 4-event cascade, 800ms settle): origin/main 35 traces/4 envelopes on each of L1,L2,L3. Branch pre-fix: L1 35/4 but L2 and L3 32/1. Branch post-fix: 35/4 on all three — IDENTICAL TO MAIN. The 25-vs-22 signature is gone. Both routing failures were the same defect; routing now green with NO routing change.

⚠️ REGRESSION 2 IS AN IRREDUCIBLE CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO PRIOR RULINGS — OPERATOR RULING REQUIRED. THE MAYOR IS NOT DECIDING THIS.
The worker established that install-spawn! needs NO change and the emit must NOT be carved out. type-ref-fn is still forced at the last point before the write; the definition-lifetime rule still evaluates at commit. Deferral falsifies only a PREMISE IN A COMMENT ("fan synchronously to application listeners") — under deferral there are NO pre-install callbacks, so the rxjy3/zo5n9 window is closed BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by late selection. Nothing in the mechanism weakens.
A 3-arm controlled probe shows what actually changes: arm 1 (listener unregisters mid-drain) on main gives a PINNED-MAP live child reaching :working; on the branch it gives a keyword, stranded, 1 no-such-handler. Arm 2 (same unregister one line AFTER dispatch-sync) is identical on both. Arm 3 (undisturbed) identical on both. So deferral RECLASSIFIES arm 1 into arm 2 — and that end state is not novel corruption, it is what re-frame2 already produces and accepts for a post-drain unregister (the deliberate cost of the revertible keyword; this suites own booting-child-v2 pins it).
THE CONFLICT, EXACTLY: rxjy3/zo5n9 protection is DEFINED as "the install observes what the listener did" -> the listener must run under the drain lock -> the exact negation of wxy1c charter ("neither invoked nor awaited while the framework owns any drain lock"). An inline carve-out would restore drain-vs-drain overlap and the jl75r AB-BA edge at precisely the emits most likely to carry tool listeners, via operation-keyed shape inference this bead forbids by name. NO THIRD OPTION EXISTS.
OF THE 17 MACHINES FAILURES: 13 are listener-as-intra-drain-MUTATOR (the semantic question above). 4 are listener-as-intra-drain-CLOCK — pure instrument artefacts (the validator still runs once by install time; the test samples at a trace listener and its own docstring names the assumption).
NO ASSERTION WAS REWRITTEN.

FAMILY 3 — CONTRACT CHANGE, CANNOT BE PRESERVED. Both children are torn down inside a single events fx walk, so no flush granularity short of inline delivery interleaves them. Spec 005:2138 ("a consumer observing the db between :exit and :rf.machine/destroyed sees the live snapshot") is in direct tension with this beads own criterion that post-drain traces expose no partially settled state. Flagged, not rewritten.

STATE: #6365 has 52 pass, 11 skip, ONE real failure — JVM machines (plus the aggregate rollup mirroring it). Routing, core and node-test are green. ThreadLocal intact; retired classifier still retired; unreachability argument and envelope ordering untouched. Ruling request posted as a PR comment.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 09:54 AUSEST)

RULING: Trace listeners are OBSERVERS, not participants. The wxy1c/rakqk charter stands in full: arbitrary listener code is never invoked nor awaited while the framework owns any frame drain lock; internal drain-owned emits deliver at the post-drain boundary, serialized process-wide, in emission order, completing before the enclosing dispatch/drain returns. Externally-authored/public emits stay synchronous through callback completion.

WHICH PRIOR RULING YIELDS: the rxjy3/zo5n9 "install observes what the listener did" framing yields — it was never a ruled principle, only the incidental mechanics of the inline delivery that existed when those beads shipped (a comment premise in install-spawn! plus fixture choices). Their REAL deliverable stands untouched and composes cleanly with this ruling: pinned prepared definitions, type-ref-fn forced at the last point before the write, definition-lifetime evaluated against the registrar at commit. Under deferral there are no pre-install listener callbacks, so the mid-drain-divergence window rxjy3/zo5n9 closed is closed BY CONSTRUCTION. install-spawn! needs no code change — only its "fan synchronously to application listeners" comment premise is now false; update that comment (2 sites in implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc).

CROSS-PLATFORM CONTRACT: intra-drain influence by listener side effects is OUT OF CONTRACT on every platform. A mid-drain listener mutation takes effect when its callback runs — post-drain — equivalent to mutating after dispatch-sync returns (the worker's 3-arm probe: arm 1 becomes arm 2, an already-pinned, already-accepted end state). CLJS's inline delivery (the :cljs branch of the trace.cljc seam, load-bearing for bundle isolation) is an implementation detail, not a promise. Re-based tests must be platform-uniform on this point.

FAMILY 3: ACCEPTED. destroyed_exit_order_test moves to the batched order [:exit :exit :destroyed :destroyed]. Correction to the record: the test's Spec 005:2138 citation is stale and over-read — line 2138 is the state-tags worked example; the governing section is Spec 005 §"Composition with explicit :entry/:exit" (~line 3026), which guarantees only that the user's :exit ACTION reads the actor's final snapshot before auto-destroy — an in-drain action-vs-fx ordering deferral does not touch. The "consumer observing the db between :exit and :rf.machine/destroyed sees the live snapshot" sentence exists only in the test docstring, which extended an action-ordering guarantee into a trace-interleaving guarantee the spec never wrote. The batched order is also what wxy1c's own "no partially settled state" criterion prefers (the old interleaving let a listener at child A's :destroyed read the db with child B half-alive). Fix the docstring citation and narrow its claim when updating the test.

TEST REWORK DIRECTIVE (PR #6365, fence lifted):
1. Re-base the 13 listener-as-mutator machines tests (spawn_all_prepared_unregister_cljs_test.cljc, spawn_all_authoritative_preflight_cljs_test.cljc) onto a NON-LISTENER mid-drain mutator — an fx interleaved in the entry vector between preflight and install — asserting the same pinning outcomes, so the spawn-pinning mechanism (pinned prepared definition + last-point type-ref forcing) stays red/green meaningful under mid-drain registrar divergence. Add one JVM test pinning the new contract directly: a mid-drain listener mutation lands post-drain, arm 1 ≡ arm 2.
2. Fix the 4 listener-as-clock tests' sampling instrument (validator still runs exactly once by install time; the trace-listener sampling point moved past a later macrostep — their own docstrings name the assumption).
3. Family 3 per above.
4. Amend Spec 009 delivery prose (~lines 17 and 624) to the two-tier contract per rakqk's accepted criteria: public emits synchronous; internal drain-owned emits post-drain, serialized process-wide, emission order preserved, no partially settled state, complete before the enclosing operation returns; intra-drain listener influence out of contract on all platforms. Spec 009 is HOT-ZONE — sequence that edit, do not parallel it.
5. The inverted frame_destroy_incarnation_jvm_test assertion already on the branch (listener can no longer veto the handler its run-start names by destroying the frame mid-fan-out) is part of this ruling's package.

PATH TO GREEN: PR #6365 (head 44386ba13b, verified OPEN 2026-07-19) proceeds — regression 1 is already fixed on the branch with proof (35 traces/4 envelopes on all 3 listeners, identical to main); the only real CI failure is the 17 JVM machines tests this ruling re-bases. Merge on green. Option B was rejected because every variant provably breaks an accepted ruling (uw7hg overlap, jl75r AB-BA deadlock, or jl75r's "no listener prohibition"); option C (carve out spawn emits) is rejected as the event-shape classifier disease both rakqk and wxy1c forbid by name.

Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-wxy1c.trace-listener-ruling-conflict.md retired (deleted) — this note is the durable record.
close_reason: shipped #6365 — the session's longest-held PR, unblocked by the wxy1c ruling (trace listeners are OBSERVERS, not participants; the rxjy3/zo5n9 'install observes what the listener did' framing YIELDS, never having been a ruled principle). All five directives delivered: 17 JVM machines failures -> 0 (1195/4164 green). ⚠️ FINDING WORTH KEEPING: the ruling named 'an fx interleaved in the entry vector between preflight and install' — NO SUCH SLOT EXISTS. apply-transition-once composes all-fx as cascade-fx ++ after-cancel ++ destroy ++ spawn-fx ++ after ++ done, and handle-spawn-all-decl contributes [init-fx, spawn-a, spawn-b] as one contiguous framework-owned block, so application fx land strictly BEFORE the preflight. The worker REFUSED to add an fx-ordering hook to serve a test and instead used the mutator already in that window — the child's own [:schemas :data] validator, which prepare-spawn-all-child runs LAST, after the snapshot and before install-spawn! forces prepared-type-ref. Probed before rewriting. Delta -4 deftests: three rf2-zo5n9 later-seam suites FOLDED because their window is closed BY CONSTRUCTION under deferral, making them verbatim duplicates — the ruling's own logic applied. New JVM contract test (2 tests/12 assertions) pins arm 1 = arm 2 with its own lever: making call-with-deferred-listener-delivery the identity on JVM reds 7 of 12, arm-1 {:pinned? true :state :working} vs arm-2 {:pinned? false :state :hot-reloaded}. Family 3 batched to [:exit :exit :destroyed :destroyed] with the stale Spec 005:2138 citation corrected to :3026 and the docstring narrowed. title: Restore serial trace-listener delivery without the drain-lock deadlock
description:
PR #6200 removes the fanout-monitor/frame drain-lock AB-BA deadlock by sending any event that looks frame/drain-related through an independent inline fan-out. That fixes the hang but regresses the public trace-listener law established by closed rf2-uw7hg and explicitly required by closed rf2-jl75r: one listener callback is serial across JVM threads and concurrent outer emits have one defined order.

`frame-drain-emit?` is event-shape inference, not lock-ownership evidence. Any `:frame`, caller-supplied dispatch id, ambient frame, or `retain? false` bypasses the monitor; dispatch-id alone bypasses even though ring routing requires both dispatch id and a resolved frame. Two drains, clean-versus-drain, frame-tagged public emits, and structural terminals can therefore enter the same callback concurrently. The implementation comments admit this relaxation. The new deadlock fixture also depends on it: while T1 remains inside the sole listener and blocks in `dispatch-sync`, the drainer's traces enter that same listener inline; the callback predicate merely ignores them.

A deterministic current-main public probe started two frame-tagged `trace/emit!` calls while the first callback was latched. The second entered before the first returned and maximum concurrent invocations was 2. Existing focused suites remain green because their serialization fixture exercises only frameless clean emits.

The four original laws expose an inherent cycle if arbitrary callbacks are invoked while the target drain lock is held: process-wide non-overlap, callback completion before each internal emit returns, listener-owned blocking `dispatch-sync`, and drain-lock-held fan-out cannot all coexist. Replace the data classifier with one explicit ownership/timing seam. Prefer moving arbitrary fan-out beyond drain-lock ownership and making the internal timing ruling exact; do not hide a contract relaxation behind tags or build a general scheduler.
acceptance_criteria:
- On the JVM, one registered trace listener is never entered concurrently with itself across any combination of clean, frame-routed, ambient-frame, dispatch-id-tagged, retentionless, epoch-trailer, or two-drain outer emits. Each listener observes one defined total order.
- The original deterministic monitor→listener→`dispatch-sync(F)` versus `F.:drain-lock`→trace interleaving completes within the bound and every dispatched event/trace settles exactly once; no global-monitor/drain-lock AB-BA edge remains.
- Event payload shape is not treated as proof of lock ownership. Public/manual/stale/malformed `:frame` or `:rf.trace/dispatch-id` tags cannot opt out of serialization.
- Arbitrary listener code is neither invoked nor awaited while the framework owns the target frame drain lock. The implementation has one explicit private ownership/post-drain seam rather than per-event classifier guesses.
- Externally authored/public emits remain synchronous through callback completion. If internal drain traces fan out at a post-drain boundary, Spec 009, generated/core API docs, and source docstrings define that boundary precisely, preserve emission order, expose no partially settled state, and complete before the enclosing public dispatch/drain operation returns.
- Same-thread reentrant delivery retains outer-before-inner observation and nested synchronous completion; listener throws, continuation suppression, registration replacement, and CLJS/production-elision behavior remain correct.
- Deterministic controls cover clean-vs-drain, drain-vs-drain, frame-tagged public emits, retentionless terminals, ambient/current-frame and epoch trailers. Mutations restoring shape-based bypass or callbacks-under-drain-lock go red.
- No listener prohibition on `dispatch-sync`, public lock/token API, per-listener locking maze, general scheduler, compatibility mode, or documentation-only escape is introduced.

title: Make Shadow compile provenance total and unforgeable by output-map replacement
description:
PR #6198 replaces `:js` object identity with a private per-pass marker, but two finish-time states still violate closed rf2-v7wqk's fail-loud provenance contract.

First, `actually-recompiled-member-nss` calls the classifier only when a CLJS build member has a non-nil final output. A missing `[:output resource-id]` is silently skipped, so the accepted row/digest can survive and be published even though the per-resource evidence is absent. The current ambiguous-provenance tests cover an unmarked map with no usable `:cached` value and a stale token, not an absent final output.

Second, marker absence is not itself causal when a later non-scheduling Shadow hook reconstructs a retained output map. Copying Shadow's sticky `:cached false` and output data into a fresh map drops re-frame.ui's unknown private key without scheduling compilation; finish then classifies it as a genuine compile and can evict a valid accepted row/digest. Current tests deliberately use `assoc`/`update-in`, which preserve the marker, while the real-Shadow forced-recompile arm removes the output to schedule real compilation. A current-main probe returns `true` for the reconstructed unmarked `{:cached false ...}` map and `#{}` for a missing member output.

Close the classifier authority without another inference ladder: every graph member must produce valid evidence, and a whole-map transform cannot silently counterfeit compilation. Either establish and causally prove one enforceable marker-preservation/hook-order contract or use a private compile fact that distinguishes Shadow compilation from non-scheduling replacement. This is separate from rf2-qbjdu's compiler-carrier build-id checks, rf2-vxgfnd.196's installation docs, and rf2-vxgfnd.271's served-file atomicity.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every CLJS resource in the authoritative final build graph is reconciled. A missing, nil, non-map, or otherwise unusable final output throws a stable typed compiler error before candidate derivation/publication; it is never treated as untouched.
- A later non-scheduling hook that replaces an entire retained output map while preserving Shadow fields (including sticky `:cached false`) cannot be silently classified as a compile. A supported transform preserves the accepted registry/digest; evidence outside the supported contract fails loud before publication.
- Genuine fresh recompiles, equal/backwards timestamp recompiles, warm retained hits, metadata/JS-only transforms, and disk-cache loads retain their correct existing classifications in sequential and parallel Shadow modes.
- The one private provenance authority has an enforceable integration story: hook ordering or marker preservation is validated causally, or a causal compile fact distinguishes compiler replacement from hook replacement. Comments alone are not the contract.
- Typed failures name at least build id, resource id, declaring namespace/provides, reason, and an accurate recovery. A later-hook evidence loss does not misleadingly report only `:configure-ui-build-hook-once`.
- Synthetic mutation controls cover absent final output and whole-map same-/changed-JS replacements; the real-Shadow fixture proves the chosen authority and fails before any accepted/served candidate changes.
- No public provenance token, wall-clock fallback, compatibility branch, second registry model, or generalized hook framework is added.

title: Make captured subscribe cache misses one exact-incarnation operation
description:
PR #6186 / closed rf2-dlld6 added an `expected-incarnation` comparison to `subscribe-in-frame`, but that comparison is not joined to subscription consumption. The outer read resolves record A and validates the captured token against A; on a cache miss or concurrent hit eviction it then calls `compute-and-cache!` with only `frame-id`. That path re-resolves the layer-1 container by ID, recursively subscribes inputs by ID, and re-resolves the cache by ID. On the concurrent JVM host, A can therefore be destroyed and same-ID B installed after the comparison but before build/install, allowing a stale capture to read B and cache a reaction in B. The cache-hit/eviction boundary likewise needs an explicit exact-incarnation linearization story rather than falling through to a bare-ID rebuild.

A deterministic current-main interposition made the capture precheck pass, let the outer subscribe read A, then destroyed A and constructed B before returning that A record. Exact result: `{:interposition-fired true, :stale-capture-returned-reaction? true, :stale-capture-result :B, :successor-db {:owner :B}, :successor-cache-keys ([:audit/value])}`. The focused existing lane remains green because its race fixture replaces A before the new outer comparison, not after it.

There is a second host-specific bypass at the same semantic boundary: in CLJS dev, `resolve-sub-override` runs before the frame-record/token check and an override hit short-circuits the fenced branch entirely. A stale captured subscribe must not surface an override for a superseded incarnation.

Make the captured subscribe operation consume exactly the validated incarnation across override, hit, miss, recursive input, and install paths. Keep the repair private and proportional: no public token API, global lock, new cache substrate, or change to ordinary address-directed subscription semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
- A captured subscribe pinned to A cannot read B, recursively resolve inputs in B, install/adopt a reaction in B, or return a dev sub override after A is superseded.
- A deterministic JVM fixture exercises the post-comparison boundary (not only the earlier capture precheck) and proves nil recovery, exactly one `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` emit, and an untouched successor DB/cache.
- A focused CLJS dev fixture proves a stale captured subscribe is fenced before override resolution can return a value; a live captured subscribe retains existing override behavior.
- Cache-hit, concurrent-eviction/rebuild, layer-1 container, and layer-2+ recursive-input paths have an explicit exact-incarnation linearization story; a path that truly consumes A before teardown may succeed, while one that has not must not retarget B.
- Ordinary ambient/explicit address-directed subscribe behavior, cache identity/ref-count balance, cycle unwind, image-generation resolution, and production CLJS behavior remain unchanged.
- The fix reuses the private captured authority already present; it adds no public incarnation surface, global lock, new error category, or general transaction mechanism.
- Focused tests include mutation teeth that fail if override precedes the captured fence or post-validation build/install falls back to a bare frame ID again.

title: Make epoch restore one exact-incarnation transaction end to end
description:
PR #6179 fences only the physical `replace-frame-state!` call, not the full restore transaction promised by closed `rf2-bjh6y`.

Three current seams can cross from frame incarnation A into a same-ID successor B:

1. `check-restore-preconditions!` captures a frame record, then independently re-resolves the incarnation token and history by bare frame ID. In the documented late-cleanup overlap, a deterministic staged-read probe combined A's retained epoch/history with B's live token; `perform-restore!` accepted the ticket and installed A's db into B.
2. `perform-restore!` runs late-bound reconciliation after one early token check but before the exact physical write. The Resources reconciler performs non-deferred bare-ID timer/work-ledger clearing in this phase. A deterministic hook probe churned A to B, performed a B-addressed side effect, then the exact write correctly failed and restore returned false: B had already been touched.
3. After an exact install, synchronous `:rf.epoch/restored` telemetry runs before bare-ID last-settled anchoring, resource trace commit, and host-work quiescence. A listener can replace A with B; a deterministic probe then stamped/quiesced B while restore still returned true.

The current physical write fence is correct and should remain. Make the transaction coherent without exposing tokens publicly, retrying against B, or introducing a general locking framework: derive the token from one captured record, exact-owner-gate the history/validation snapshot, keep preinstall reconciliation pure, and anchor/detach only A-owned post-install work before callback boundaries. Internal hooks may receive the captured opaque owner/token or detached A snapshots instead of re-sampling the current frame by ID.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic record-A -> same-ID-B interleaving inside precondition sampling cannot produce an A epoch paired with B's token; restore returns false and B is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Every preinstall reconcile hook is pure with respect to host tables. If a callback churns A to B, the exact write returns false and no B timer, request, work-ledger, db, trace, or bookkeeping state is touched.
- After A is installed, framework-owned anchoring and host-work selection remain scoped to A even if a synchronous trace listener destroys A and seats B. No A tail operation stamps, releases, aborts, or quiesces B.
- Once the exact A install commits, the public success result remains truthful; later listener churn may stop remaining A-only work but cannot retarget it.
- The public restore API and typed failure vocabulary remain coherent; no opaque incarnation token becomes public and no retry/global transaction framework is added.
- Focused adversarial regressions cover all three callback/read seams, and the full epoch JVM gate passes.

title: Remove the trace fanout-monitor ↔ frame drain-lock deadlock
description:
Current JVM trace fan-out serializes every outermost emit by holding the process-global `fanout-monitor` across `run-outermost-fanout!`, including each arbitrary registered listener body (`trace/tooling.cljc`: listener invocation around 821; monitor critical section around 890). Public trace listeners are allowed to call `dispatch-sync`.

That forms a hard AB-BA cycle with a frame's `:drain-lock`. T1 acquires `fanout-monitor`, enters a listener, calls `dispatch-sync` to frame F, and spin-waits for F's drain lock. T2 already holds F's drain lock for `drain-loop!`/`run-one-pass!`, reaches an ordinary `:rf.event/run-start` trace emit, and blocks acquiring `fanout-monitor`. Neither can progress. This is JVM dev/test behavior and uses only public listener/dispatch operations; `drain-block!`'s bounded-wait assumption is false because the active drainer is waiting on the caller.

Closed `rf2-uw7hg` introduced whole-fanout monitor serialization, `rf2-s522m` repaired nested synchronous completion, and `rf2-8b9twg` removed a different epoch-ledger/drain inversion. None owns this remaining monitor/drain edge. Preserve their delivery laws while removing this cycle. Do not forbid `dispatch-sync` from listeners or push complexity onto the programmer; use the smallest explicit fan-out ownership/scheduling seam that keeps synchronous semantics without holding a blocking monitor across arbitrary listener work.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic JVM barrier/latch fixture forces T1 `fanout-monitor -> listener -> dispatch-sync(F)` against T2 `F.:drain-lock -> run-start trace emit`; both threads complete within a bounded timeout and the dispatched event settles exactly once.
- No trace fan-out lock needed by a frame-drain emit is held across arbitrary listener code that may synchronously dispatch to that frame.
- The public trace contract remains intact: callbacks for one listener never overlap, concurrent outer emits have a defined order, each emit returns only after its eligible callbacks complete, listener throws remain isolated, and continuation suppression is unchanged.
- Reentrant delivery still preserves outer-before-inner observation for every listener and a nested emit still completes synchronously before returning.
- Public listeners remain free to call `dispatch-sync`; no documentation-only prohibition, async deferral burden, general scheduler, or public lock/token API is introduced.
- Focused JVM concurrency/reentrancy gates, CLJS listener gates, and production-elision checks pass.

title: Keep throwing-root containers quarantined until real host settlement
description:
PR #6079's queue-then-throw acceptance arm is only closed for a stale captured frame dispatch. When host `.unmount` queues arbitrary cleanup and then throws, `reclaim-and-retire-quarantine!` clears the container's current DOM and React ownership marker, retires reporter authority, and releases the predecessor claim. That is a snapshot cleanup, not proof that already-queued host authority has settled. The successor-generation admission fence therefore reopens and permits exact-container reuse while the queued predecessor task can still mutate that container.

The existing browser test queues a captured dispatch, whose separate incarnation fence protects same-ID frame B. Replacing that task with a later `container.replaceChildren(...)` provides the missing counterexample: destroy reclaims/releases, immediate init mounts the successor on the exact container, then the predecessor task clears or replaces the successor DOM. Spec 006 nevertheless says throwing-path reclaim proves the surface free and makes the exact container reusable. A failed reclaim has the opposite problem: the claim can remain permanently `:tearing-down` while its public recovery says retry after settlement even though no settlement signal exists.

Keep this bounded. Do not invent a general scheduler or attempt to track arbitrary host tasks. After a throwing/consumed unmount, exact-container reuse needs an affirmative settlement boundary; if none exists, fail closed for that container and make the ergonomic recovery a fresh container while allowing unrelated successor work where safely possible.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic browser fixture makes `.unmount` queue late DOM mutation against its container and then throw; after destroy and re-init, predecessor work can neither clobber nor replace a successor tree.
- Clearing current DOM and deleting React's private marker are not treated as proof that queued host authority settled.
- Exact-container reuse after a throwing/consumed handle is admitted only with an affirmative settlement signal; otherwise it remains fail-closed with an honest typed recovery that directs the programmer to a fresh container.
- A quarantined failed container does not unnecessarily block safe successor roots on unrelated fresh containers; normal deferred-return teardown still globally fences until its real reporter settlement.
- Captured dispatch/subscribe incarnation fencing remains a separate last-line state boundary and is not used as proof of DOM settlement.
- Spec 006, Spec 009 recovery wording, client lifecycle state, and browser coverage agree. No general task tracker or scheduler is introduced.

title: Carry capture-frame incarnation authority through router target consumption
description:
`capture-frame` checks its pinned incarnation in `capture-target-superseded?`, then calls the ordinary address-directed dispatch/subscribe implementation. On the supported concurrent JVM host those are separate operations: frame A can be destroyed and same-ID successor B installed after the check returns true but before the ordinary implementation resolves the bare ID. The stale capture then targets B, violating the exact-incarnation promise.

A deterministic current-main interposition around `frame-incarnation-live?` reproduced the dispatch-sync arm: the stale capture validated A, the other thread destroyed A and created B, then the dispatch resumed and produced `{:successor-db {:owner :B, :marked-by :stale-capture}}`. Router target-local locking begins only after ordinary dispatch resolves B, so it cannot recover the lost capture authority. The later subscribe/value repair (`rf2-tdjv7p`/`rf2-vclh63`, #6084) shares the same check-then-use shape for subscribe; async dispatch shares it too.

Keep the boundary small and exact: carry the captured incarnation into target selection/enqueue/read, or otherwise make validation plus target consumption one exact-incarnation operation. Do not expose the token publicly, add global locking, or remove the intentionally address-directed behavior of a capture made while its target is absent.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic JVM A-validates -> destroy A -> same-ID B -> resume interleaving leaves B byte-for-byte unchanged for captured dispatch and dispatch-sync; the async arm enqueues nothing into B.
- Captured subscribe under the same interleaving neither reads B nor installs a reaction/cache entry in B.
- The exact captured token remains authoritative through router target selection and queue/read consumption; there is no liveness-check-to-bare-ID-use window.
- A superseded pinned capture keeps the existing recover-but-emit `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` behavior exactly once, with call-site/frame attribution; current CLJS behavior stays intact.
- A one-arity capture created while the named target is absent remains deliberately unpinned/address-directed, and live exact-ID plus frame-value captures keep working.
- Focused JVM adversarial tests and core JVM/CLJS gates pass; no general scheduler or public incarnation-token API is introduced.
notes: COMPLETENESS DOC ADDITION (rf2-y3zd6): when closing the exact-consumption race, reconcile the active contract/docs too. Spec 006 §Successor-generation settlement fence currently describes only stale captured dispatch even though #6084 also fences :subscribe; router.cljc emit-captured-frame-superseded! still says it is called only from dispatch/dispatch-sync. State the uniform dispatch/dispatch-sync/subscribe behavior, nil return for stale subscribe, exactly-once :rf.error/frame-destroyed emission, and exact-incarnation consumption rather than leaving the check-then-use wording implied.

title: Fence epoch restore to the exact frame incarnation it resolved
description:
`restore-epoch!` resolves the target record from frame incarnation A in `check-restore-preconditions!`, then passes only the bare frame ID and resolved epoch into `perform-restore!`. The latter serializes on the ID, checks only that some current container exists, reconciles A's saved state, and calls `frame/replace-frame-state!` by ID. If A is destroyed and same-ID successor B is created between those phases, the restore installs A's state into B and reports success.

A deterministic current-main interposition after precondition resolution reproduced `{:restore-result true :b-db-before {:owner :B :n 99} :b-db-after {:owner :A :n 1}}`. The #6074 replay fixture is load-bearing within one incarnation, but it does not churn the frame across this split. Closed `rf2-3fc89f.4` serialized restore against drains; it did not retain exact incarnation identity across precheck and write.

Keep the repair bounded: resolve history, validate, reconcile and install inside one exact-incarnation serialized operation, or carry A's opaque incarnation token and reject if it is no longer current. Do not make tokens public or retry against B.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic A-precheck → destroy A → create same-ID B → restore-write interleaving returns false, leaves B byte-for-byte unchanged, and emits no success telemetry.
- Ordinary restore still resolves and installs one epoch atomically relative to the event drain.
- History lookup, schema/registration checks, subsystem reconciliation, physical install, last-settled anchoring, deferred traces and host-work quiescence all remain fenced to the same exact incarnation.
- The no-frame/incarnation-loss result uses one coherent typed failure path; no internal token becomes public API.
- The full epoch JVM gate and a focused adversarial regression pass.

title: Finish deferred-callback frame truth across examples and Reagent adapters
description:
PR #6062 correctly fixed Core Views and added a stock-Reagent real-DOM proof, but the same deferred-callback frame law remains inconsistent across first-party teaching surfaces and its adapter proof is incomplete.

In real applications these callbacks run after render scope unwinds and raise `:rf.error/no-frame-context` unless they use a render-captured/injected dispatch or an explicit frame.

The two Core live cells appear to work only because the SCI playground deliberately substitutes `dispatch`/`subscribe` wrappers that inject `:rf/default` and dynamically binds plain component renders. That harness convenience masks non-portable source and conflicts with Core AUTHORING's "true snippets" and pure-pipeline `frame-root` + `reg-view` rule. The migration reference also still says a `frame-provider` makes every bare dispatch/subscribe in the tree resolve, which is false for callbacks that fire later.

The #6062 browser proof covers stock Reagent only. Existing reagent-slim smoke proves the captured/injected happy path but not the bare-dispatch failure required by closed `rf2-xzgs3j` for the applicable Reagent adapters. The stock fixture also relies on two fixed 10 ms timers and has fallible setup outside its guaranteed cleanup path.

Treat this as one contract-completion sweep: align active/copyable first-party examples and strengthen one compact cross-adapter proof. Preserve explicitly labelled WRONG/BEFORE/history examples and explicit-frame callbacks. No live Bead owns the residual work.

- The browser proof uses a causal settle signal and one guaranteed finalizer that unmounts roots, destroys frames, removes DOM, and completes the async test on every path; no fixed-sleep evidence.

title: Make canonical auth guard fail closed for :rf.route/self
description:
PR #6058 repaired the canonical cross-cutting auth guard for raw `{:url ...}` navigate targets, but every one of its five synchronized copies still treats every non-map `:rf.route/navigate` target as a registered route id. `:rf.route/self` is a reserved third target form: the runtime resolves it from the current route slice (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/navigate.cljc`), while the recipe resolves it to `{:id :rf.route/self}`. `handler-meta` then finds no `:requires-auth` tags and the guard stands aside.

This remains on current main in docs/routing/how-to/require-sign-in-on-a-route.md, docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md, docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md, examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/routing.cljs, and spec/012-Routing.md. The spec also incorrectly says the navigate door has only two target forms despite its own earlier reserved-self section.

Reproduced on current main: the recipe returns `{:id :rf.route/self :params {}}` and reports the guard false while the runtime keeps the active route at protected `:app/settings`. A signed-out/expired session already on a protected route can therefore self-navigate (for example, query changes) without the cross-cutting policy recognizing the protected destination; route loading may proceed.

The new matrix is a false tooth: it duplicates `nav-target` privately and never executes the canonical example interceptor or proves redirect/noncommit. Reverting an example copy leaves it green. Close both gaps with one shared executable guard seam or an integration fixture that exercises the actual canonical implementation; do not add a new public routing API.
acceptance_criteria:
- `:rf.route/self` resolves against the carried current route slice before route metadata is read; protected self-navigation fails closed and public self-navigation remains allowed.
- Route-id and raw-URL targets retain their current behavior, including pre-navigation/no-current-route handling.
- All five canonical recipe/spec/example copies and the target-form prose agree that navigate has route-id, raw-URL, and reserved-self forms.
- An executable integration matrix drives the actual canonical guard/interceptor (or one shared production/example seam), not a free-standing duplicate, across protected/public route-id, raw URL, self, route-link, and URL-change doors.
- Protected rows prove redirect/skip and that the protected route/loaders do not commit; public rows prove normal delivery.
- Focused Routing JVM/CLJS/example gates pass.

title: Define recursive defviews on the same current-namespace Var they reference
description:
PR #6053 fixed the recursive JSX head but left the defining Var on the raw bare name. In a real cljs.user analyzer namespace that refers re-frame.ui/sub, lease, and frame, emit-defview now produces a self reference such as cljs.user.sub while the complete generated (declare/defn/def) form still defines re_frame.ui.sub. The result is a split identity: cljs.user.sub$render recurses through cljs.user.sub, which is never defined, while compilation overwrites the public authoring Var.

Reproduced on current origin/main 0f2fc095321831ba1d30d8e7cbe0706784a8c2ae by analyzing and emitting the entire production form: {:defines-current false, :defines-authoring true, :recursive-ref-current true}; representative JS is re_frame.ui.sub = (...). The same result holds for sub, lease, and frame. The focused committed suite remains green (9 tests / 86 assertions) because it checks the raw def is bare and compiles extracted reference symbols independently instead of compiling the complete form. Closed rf2-rr26cq explicitly required one canonical current-view symbol for both reference and definition; it cannot be amended and no live follow-up owns the residual bug.

Keep the fix small: make the defining declaration/Var/final result share the canonical current-namespace target already used for the recursive head, without broad component-emission machinery.

title: Serialize each trace listener across concurrent JVM emits
description:
PR #6051's listener fan-out queue is dynamically bound and therefore thread-local (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc`). It restores same-thread re-entrant A→B order, but two concurrent JVM emits each create an independent outermost queue and can invoke the same registered callback concurrently.

A latch probe on current main blocked listener L while handling event A, emitted B on another thread, and observed B enter L before A returned (`same-listener-overlapped? true`). This violates the public listener contract: `docs/api/re-frame.core.md` says delivery is synchronous and “the callback returns before the next record”; Spec 009 requires synchronous, in-order, event-at-a-time delivery per listener. It also permits B to overtake A for a listener even when A emission began first, and exposes ordinary tool callbacks/appenders to concurrent invocation they were told cannot happen.

Existing #6051 tests cover same-thread reentrancy only. Open `rf2-s522m` owns the separate nested-emit completion regression (a nested emit returns before its listeners run); it does not cover cross-thread per-listener serialization.
acceptance_criteria: For each registered trace listener on the JVM, callback invocations never overlap and records are delivered in a defined emission/linearization order consistent with the synchronous event-at-a-time contract. An emit does not return before its record's callback completes. Preserve same-thread re-entrant ordering, listener exception isolation, exact-continuation suppression, registration replacement semantics, CLJS behavior, and production elision. Add a deterministic two-thread latch test proving one listener cannot enter B until its A callback has returned, plus stress/registration-change coverage sufficient to prevent deadlock or retroactive delivery.

title: Bind machine timer cancellation batches and reschedules to one frame incarnation
description:
PR #6049 made single timer-entry resource release successor-aware, but the cancellation attempt is still not bound end-to-end to the frame incarnation observed by its caller. In current `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc`, the 3-arity `cancel-after-timer-entry!` captures a frame token and then separately reads/claims the current entry. On the JVM, A can be replaced by same-id B between capture and read; the stale cancellation then claims/removes B's same-key entry. Deterministic audit probe ended with `{:successor-entry nil, :successor-frame-live? true}`.

Synchronous callback seams make the same defect deterministic without a thread race. `after-cancel-fx`, frame-destroy cancellation, and restore cancellation snapshot keys but invoke the 3-arity helper separately for each key. If cancelling A/k1 emits `:rf.machine.timer/cancelled` and a listener replaces A with B and arms B/k2, the stale outer batch advances to k2, recaptures B, and cancels B's host work. `cancel-actor-timers!` already demonstrates the intended loop-wide monotonic owner predicate, but the other batches do not.

The reschedule paths need the same entry-wide fence. `on-sub-changed!` cancels and then bare-ID reads/reschedules; `schedule-after-timer!` can perform a second `:on-supersede` cancel before installing. A cancellation listener can therefore replace A with B, after which stale A watcher work can cancel B's re-arm and/or install A-derived work into B.

This remains on current main. Closed `rf2-rbxdxa`/PR #6049 attempted the callback fence but tested only one timer and did not cover capture→read, cross-key iteration, or cancel→reschedule continuation. Closed `rf2-j538f7.7` covers attempt-token publication/replacement races, not binding cancellation to one frame incarnation.
acceptance_criteria: Bind each cancellation/reschedule attempt to one captured frame incarnation before any entry read or callback. A cancellation may claim/release only an entry belonging to that incarnation; once ownership is lost, multi-key loops stop and post-cancel bare-ID reads, supersede cancels, scheduling, and publication do not run against the successor. Preserve ordinary live-owner cancellation, exact attempt-token replacement safety, cancellation reasons/reply facts, and balanced handle/watch/subscription cleanup. Add deterministic JVM capture→read and two-key callback replacement tests, plus an on-resolution/supersede test proving B's entry/handle survives and no A-derived timer is installed in B; cover the supported CLJS callback path too.

title: Preserve synchronous completion for nested trace emits while ordering fan-out
description:
PR #6051 preserves per-listener A→B order by deferring a re-entrant trace event B onto `*listener-fanout-queue*`, but this changes the documented synchronous completion law. spec/009-Instrumentation.md says listeners receive each event synchronously while the runtime is still on that emit call stack (lines 17, 609) and that emit returns only once every listener has been invoked (around line 963). tooling.cljc comments claim the nested emit's synchronous-return contract is unchanged, yet the nested call only appends `[event continue?]` and returns; the outer fan-out drains it later.

Confirmed on current main with two listeners. Listener 1 handling :audit/outer called `(trace/emit! :audit :audit/inner {})`, then checked whether listener 2 had seen :audit/inner. Observed order:
`[[:first :audit/outer] [:after-inner-return false] [:second :audit/outer] [:first :audit/inner] [:second :audit/inner]]`.
Thus the nested emit returned before either listener saw its event. Any listener/tool using the ratified synchronous boundary to observe another listener's completed state or to sequence nested instrumentation now sees stale state, despite the public contract and implementation prose saying otherwise.

Preserve both laws: each listener must see events in emission order, and every emit—including a nested one—must return only after its event has reached all eligible listeners. This likely needs a re-entrant fan-out scheduler/completion marker that can advance pending outer deliveries before completing the nested call, rather than a fire-and-drain-later append. If the project intentionally relaxes nested synchronicity, make that a deliberate spec/API decision and update every promise/test; do not leave code and contract contradictory. Add a regression that asserts listener-2 has observed inner before the nested emit returns while both listeners still observe outer before inner.
acceptance_criteria: A nested trace emit returns only after all eligible listeners received that event, every listener still observes outer-before-inner emission order, and spec/code/tests agree on the nested synchronous contract.

description:

title: Resolve join completion overrides once under the exact-owner fence
description: For a real but non-applying canonical join-completion override, `join-dispatch-fx` calls `resolve-fx-with-overrides` only to emit the synchronous fallthrough diagnostic, then unconditionally calls `child-dispatch!`. An error listener can destroy the current frame during that emit. The outer `handle-one-fx` fence notices only after the registered handler returns, too late to undo the inner side effect. Current-main repros: the immediate path called the router hook with the completion after the listener destroyed `:rf/default`; a 60s delayed completion installed `[:rf/default 1]` in `dispatch-later-timers` after destroy had already released that table. The delayed timer is therefore post-cleanup and can later fire dead-on-arrival. Separately, `override-applies?` duplicates resolver policy/registrar lookup and execution resolves again, so concurrent JVM registration churn can change the disposition between preflight and use. One structured resolution consumed under exact-owner continuation removes both bugs and the duplicated policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- Override resolution returns one structured disposition (noop/fallthrough/applied fn/applied redirect/protected rejection) from the shared resolver; join does not independently duplicate registrar/protected-target policy.
- Diagnostic emission and the selected execution/transport branch are fenced by the originating event's exact frame owner.
- If a fallthrough listener destroys A, neither immediate router dispatch nor numeric-ms timer reservation/host timer occurs afterward; a same-id successor B remains untouched.
- Concurrent registration/unregistration cannot flip an applies preflight into a different execution disposition or produce coordinate-less completion.
- Tests cover immediate, positive delay, zero delay, malformed/unregistered/protected redirects, applied fn/redirect controls, listener-induced destroy/reincarnation, and JVM registration churn.

title: Canonicalize and validate spread-safe caller keys before the every-build deny
description: `ui/spread-safe` promises that caller keys `:key`, `:ref`, `:value`, `:checked`, and owned handlers are denied in every build. The guard compares raw map keys, while both host converters canonicalize with `(name k)`. Namespaced keywords, strings, and symbols therefore bypass the guard and become the same React/DOM names (`:caller/ref` -> `"ref"`, `"checked"` -> `"checked"`). A non-map sequence of pairs also bypasses the map-only guard and is accepted by the CLJS walk. Non-nameable keys fail later with host-specific untyped exceptions. Reproduced on current main: `assert-safe-caller!` accepted string/namespaced ref/value/checked keys, and the JVM tree retained them; CLJS conversion installs their canonical names. This breaks the production deny contract and permits structural/controlled slots through alternate spellings.
acceptance_criteria:
- Define one validated author-space caller-key grammar shared by compile-time denial, CLJS conversion, and JVM tree conversion.
- Compare the canonical emitted name against the denied structural/controlled names and canonical owned-handler names; alternate representations cannot bypass the law.
- Reject non-map callers and non-nameable/nonconforming keys with the typed `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` boundary error, consistently on both hosts.
- Add literal and runtime tests for namespaced/string/symbol aliases, pair sequences, nil/false/non-nameable keys, exact allowed keys, and owned handler aliases.
- The advanced-production G-17 proof covers at least one alternate spelling, not only exact keyword keys.

title: Use per-pass provenance for Shadow compile membership, not :js identity
description:
`compiled-this-pass?` treats `:cached false` plus a non-identical `:js` object as causal proof that Shadow compiled a source after the UI hook's prepare snapshot. The `:cached` bit is sticky on retained outputs, however, and build hooks may transform a retained output's JS without scheduling compilation. A later prepare hook that replaces only `[:output rid :js]` with an equal-byte fresh String leaves `:cached false`; current finish classifies it as recompiled, touches the namespace although no macros ran, evicts its valid accepted view, and changes the whole-build digest.

A current-main full hook reproduction produced `same-bytes=true`, `same-object=false`, then changed accepted views from `{a,b}` to `{a}` with `digest-changed=true`. The existing metadata test changes only the outer map while deliberately preserving the nested JS object, so it cannot detect this ordinary output-transforming shape.

The inverse ambiguity is also silent: missing/corrupt `:cached` or `:js` is classified as untouched rather than failing before publication, contrary to closed `rf2-ialoij`'s explicit missing/ambiguous-evidence criterion. There is no open owner.

Use an actual per-pass fact. The smallest shape appears to be an opaque marker stamped onto retained output maps at UI prepare: non-scheduling annotations/JS transformations preserve it, while real compile output replaces the map and loses it; `:cached true` continues to distinguish disk-cache loads. Validate provenance shapes explicitly. No wall-clock fallback or public token.
acceptance_criteria:
- A later non-scheduling hook that replaces retained `:js` with either equal-byte or changed-byte fresh strings preserves the accepted registry and digest.
- Genuine equal-stamp and backwards-stamp zero-declaration recompiles still evict the prior accepted row in sequential and parallel Shadow modes.
- Warm retained hits, outer-map metadata changes, and disk-cache loads are not classified as current-pass compilation.
- Missing, malformed, or contradictory per-source provenance fails with a typed compiler error before accepted publication; it is never silently treated as untouched.
- The real Shadow fixture proves the per-pass fact, including hook ordering, without relying on object identity or a wall-clock relationship.
- One private compiler authority; no public provenance API, compatibility branch, or timestamp fallback.
close_reason: shipped #6198 (merged)

title: Close ui/render-fn purity across effects and committed callbacks
description:
## Current defect

The #6032 `ui/render-fn` contract promises a PURE deferred render body, but the purity fence is not transitive across later S3 forms on current main. `analyze-render-fn` sets `:in-render-fn?` while inheriting the enclosing `:hooks-region?`; `analyze-effect-statement` checks only ordinary hook placement, so a leading `(ui/effect ...)` inside a render-fn top-region `let` is accepted and emitted as a React hook inside the callback. Component-prop `ui/event` / `ui/handler` and error-boundary `:on-error` likewise do not reject `:in-render-fn?`.

The callback escape is correctness-critical for repeated slots: one render-fn invoked for several rows emits the same lexical event-site key into the seam view candidate. Later rows reuse the stable callback and overwrite that key's descriptor, so every row callback can read the last row's closure. The intended pattern remains legal: a slot body may mount a static defview, and that mounted view owns its own hooks/handlers.

## Required correction

Close the one purity boundary, rather than patching individual fixtures: every effect/committed-callback/error-boundary dispatch surface encountered inside `:in-render-fn?` must fail at compile time with `:rf.ui.compile/impure-slot-body`. Preserve static child defviews with their own state and callbacks.
acceptance_criteria:
- A top-region and nested-let `(ui/effect ...)` inside `ui/render-fn` fail with `:rf.ui.compile/impure-slot-body`; conditional/nested variants cannot escape.
- Component-prop `ui/event` and `ui/handler` inside a render-fn fail at compile time, including a repeated-row counterexample that otherwise aliases all callbacks to the last row.
- `ui/error-boundary :on-error` inside a render-fn fails through the same purity diagnostic.
- A render-fn that mounts a static defview whose own body owns handlers/hooks remains legal and works on CLJS and JVM.
- The G-16 purity roster and causal tests cover every current S3 effect/callback form; removing any fence makes its focused fixture fail.
close_reason: shipped #6169 (merged)

title: Use Object.is semantics for effect dependencies; keep rf= for memo values
description:
## Current defect

PR #6020 makes `rf=` the dependency comparator for the future `react/use-effect` and `react/use-layout-effect` wrappers and claims its extra equalities make skipped reruns unobservable. Current main has since shipped the same law in `re-frame.ui.hooks/effect-value`, so this is already a runtime contract, not just future prose.

`rf=` is the right memo/value doctrine but is too coarse for synchronization effects. The checked-in truth table deliberately equates `-0.0` with `+0.0`, distinct equal-valued Date objects, and value-equal CLJS collections. React's `useEffect` compares dependencies with `Object.is`; changing any of those values can be observable to an external/foreign system and can require cleanup plus setup. The current stable-token lowering therefore leaves the old effect installed and the new closure unapplied even though native React would resynchronize.

The distinction is semantic, not an optimization preference: component repaint equality answers whether two render inputs have the same value, while effect dependency equality answers whether an external synchronization input is the exact same dependency.

## Bounded correction

Keep `rf=` for memoized rendering, but use React-compatible `Object.is` comparison per authored effect dependency on CLJS. Preserve the one-element internal token passed to React so authored deps arity can remain compiler-managed without changing hook order. Update the foreign interop contract before `rf2-vxgfnd.95.4` reuses the faulty law.
acceptance_criteria:
- Current `ui/effect [deps…]` reruns cleanup/setup when any authored dependency changes by `Object.is`, including `-0.0` to `+0.0` and distinct value-equal host values; unchanged dependencies do not rerun.
- Focused mounted fixtures prove the old effect is cleaned up and the new closure/value reaches an identity-sensitive external sink for at least one `rf=`-equal/`Object.is`-different case.
- `react/use-effect` and `react/use-layout-effect` inherit the corrected effect-specific comparator; Spec 004, the tracked interop draft/brief, Guide/API prose, and implementation agree.
- `rf=` remains the memo/prop value comparator; the repair does not globally change component repaint equality or add a new public comparer API.
- Fast Refresh generation forcing, StrictMode replay, disconnect/unmount cleanup, deps arity handling, and JVM metadata-only behavior remain covered.
- Focused JVM/compiler/browser tests and docs/API-manifest checks pass.
close_reason: DELIVERED in #6133 (rf2-vxgfnd.95.4): the .95.4 react-interop implementation absorbed both audit corrections — use-effect-event as native React 19.2 (unstable identity, latest body, no shim) and Object.is per-slot effect-dep comparison (rf= retained only for memo values). Code is on main + gated green (ui-digest-probe-lazy 0 warnings, react_interop_jvm_test 24/0). Spec-prose reconciliation rides .95.13. Reopen if separate verification wanted.

title: Correct react/use-effect-event to React 19.2 identity and call-site semantics
description:
## Current defect

PR #6020 promoted an incorrect React 19.2 contract into `spec/004-Views.md` and the tracked interop draft. The `react/use-effect-event` row says the returned function has stable identity across renders, and the HMR section says that identity stays stable across same-signature refreshes. The draft appears to conflate the API becoming stable in React 19.2 with the identity of the function it returns.

This repository pins React 19.2.0. Its installed `react-dom` `updateEvent` implementation allocates and returns a new function on every update. React's authoritative `useEffectEvent` reference is explicit: identity intentionally changes every render; an Effect Event may only be called from Effects or other Effect Events in the same component, and must not be passed to other components or hooks or included in deps.

If S3 implements the written stable-shell promise, it will diverge from the named host primitive, mask React's deliberate misuse signal, and require extra machinery/enforcement the contract never rules. If it directly wraps React as stated, the public spec and HMR claims will simply be false.

## Bounded correction

Correct the normative and tracked contract before `rf2-vxgfnd.95.4` implements the tier. Prefer native React semantics rather than adding an identity shim: unstable returned identity, latest committed body, no deps entry, and effect-local invocation only. If a stable shell is deliberately retained, rule it explicitly as a product divergence and prove why masking the host signal is worth the extra surface.
acceptance_criteria:
- `spec/004-Views.md`, the tracked `ui-react-interop-contract.md`, the S3 brief, and API-facing prose agree on the returned identity and do not justify stable identity by saying React 19.2 provides it.
- The legal call-site contract says Effect Events may be invoked only from Effects or other Effect Events in the same component; they are not passed to components/hooks, called during render, or included in dependency vectors.
- HMR prose no longer promises identity preservation that the host primitive does not provide.
- S3 browser fixtures render the same component more than once and pin the ruled identity behavior plus latest-body behavior; misuse diagnostics/guards match the ruled call-site boundary.
- `rf2-vxgfnd.95.4` absorbs the corrected contract before the public wrapper lands; docs/link/API checks and focused compiler/browser tests pass.
close_reason: DELIVERED in #6133 (rf2-vxgfnd.95.4): the .95.4 react-interop implementation absorbed both audit corrections — use-effect-event as native React 19.2 (unstable identity, latest body, no shim) and Object.is per-slot effect-dep comparison (rf= retained only for memo values). Code is on main + gated green (ui-digest-probe-lazy 0 warnings, react_interop_jvm_test 24/0). Spec-prose reconciliation rides .95.13. Reopen if separate verification wanted.

title: Bump the evidence-store contract and close ownership/exactness gaps
description:
## Confirmed current failures

PR #6016 creates a same-version migration hole across its own commit sequence:

1. Commit `7464025405` introduced `::weak-cell-entries-v2` and migrated legacy rows through the copier that still returned metadata-bearing symbols verbatim.
2. A live page HMR-migrated at that head therefore obtained a **v2** store whose value can still hold `symbol metadata -> ViewCell`.
3. Commit `582d3f0337` fixed the copier but left the current tag at v2.
4. Current `migrate-weak-store!` trusts any v2 store and skips sanitization forever.

The independent audit seeded exactly that intermediate v2 shape, re-armed the same owner on current code, and observed the metadata/back-reference survive. This defeats the weak key and is the compatible-HMR retention defect `rf2-vxgfnd.94.18` was meant to close.

A second current honesty failure is in the same retained-value contract. Every vector/list/map/set branch reconstructs a metadata-free collection but derives `exact?` only from its children. On current main:

```clojure
(#'re-frame.ui.tool.evidence/project-target-value
  (with-meta [:q 1] {:hidden :lost}))
;; => [[:q 1] true]
```

The copier explicitly treats dropping symbol metadata as information loss, so claiming a metadata-bearing collection is exact is inconsistent and makes `:targets-exact?` / `:dropped-exact?` lie. The existing adversarial collection test checks that metadata disappeared but omits the exactness assertion.

## Deliverable

Advance the retained-value contract once (v3 or an equally monotonic identity) so every store produced before the final copier is sanitized. In the same copier correction, lower exactness whenever any reconstructed collection carried metadata. Preserve the existing weak host machinery, row order/ordinals, counters, evidence caps, and monotonic loss floors.

Use the repository's deterministic CLJS WeakRef/FinalizationRegistry modeling to prove the real evidence-store lifecycle and compatible-HMR path; the current fake holder whose `.deref` simply returns nil is useful unit coverage but is not a cross-host retention proof.

Do not clear all evidence, replace weak storage with a strong compatibility map, or add a general serializer.

## Provenance and dedupe

Found during the chronological audit of PR #6016 on current main. All-status Beads search found only the closed source owners `rf2-vxgfnd.94.17` and `.94.18`; this is their current follow-up, not a reopen.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every untagged/v1/v2 evidence store is reprojected through the final ownership-safe copier before being marked current; only the new current tag skips migration.
- A v2 store containing direct or nested value -> ViewCell back-edges loses those back-edges, preserves ordinals/order/counters, lowers exactness, and releases the weak key on JVM and CLJS.
- JVM exact numeric admission is restricted to known immutable platform numeric values; an arbitrary `Number`/`IObj` subclass is projected opaque/inexact and cannot retain a ViewCell through fields or metadata.
- Repeated migration of the new current format is idempotent and does not reset accumulated evidence.
- Metadata on vector/list/map/set containers is stripped and makes `:targets-exact?` / `:dropped-exact?` false, including nested and migrated values.
- Metadata-free bounded EDN remains exact and existing cap/collision honesty remains unchanged.
- Real weak-GC fixtures cover the adversarial Number and legacy-v2 shapes; CLJS proof exercises the actual evidence-store WeakRef/finalizer/compaction path with deterministic host modeling.
- No strong compatibility copy, unbounded retained value, public API, or production cost is introduced.
notes: SURFACE CORRECTED + BLOCKED behind rf2-vxgfnd.95.6 (1hob1 worker STOP 2026-07-17, no edits): the P1 lives ENTIRELY in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/tool/evidence.cljc (re-frame.ui.tool.evidence), NOT reactive.cljc (my prior brief was wrong). That IS .95.6's surface (.95.6 re-versions the evidence store + weak-retention) — same file, contradictory-contract risk → SEQUENTIAL after .95.6 merges. Three real gaps confirmed on current main (post-s2cfv 3a1010ec87): (1) migration hole [P1] — copier at evidence.cljc:140-149 is now clean but the TAG is still ::weak-cell-entries-v2 (:329); weak-store-current? trusts any v2 (:382) + migrate-weak-store! returns v2 untouched (:500) → a store HMR-migrated at intermediate head 7464025405 (metadata-bearing symbols tagged v2) is trusted forever, symbol-meta→ViewCell survives. FIX: bump tag to v3 so every pre-final store re-projects. (2) container-metadata exactness lie — vector/list/set branches (:157-191) derive exact? from children only; (with-meta [:q 1] {:hidden}) drops container meta but reports exact. FIX: lower exactness when a reconstructed container carried (meta x). (3) JVM Number admission hole — evidence.cljc:126 (number? x) admits arbitrary Number subclasses; a proxy[Number IObj] holding a ViewCell in meta roots its key. FIX: restrict exact-number to a closed set of immutable platform numeric classes. Re-dispatch surface=evidence.cljc AFTER .95.6.
