title: Recognize reagent-slim Form-3 classes in the shared source-coordinate wrapper
description:
## Current defect

Current policy (rf2-ukq8qt / PR #6087) keeps reagent-slim as a first-class supported adapter, but `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/source_coord_annotation.cljs` deliberately recognizes only stock Reagent Form-3 classes and still says slim is scheduled for deletion. In debug builds, a real slim `create-class` carries constructor tags `cljsReagentClass` / `cljsReagentRender` plus `prototype.render`, not stock `prototype.reagentRender`. The shared source-coordinate walk therefore sends it through the plain `fn?` Form-2 branch, returns a wrapper instead of the original class, and later invokes the class as an ordinary function rather than preserving its React lifecycle.

A compiled current-runtime repro confirmed the slim tag is present while class identity is lost and the returned value is `inject_source_coord_attr_$_form_2_wrapper`. Existing slim source-coordinate/view-id suites cover Form-1, Form-2, fragments, and elision, but not Form-3. The closest live issue, rf2-vxgfnd.290, owns policy-authority prose and does not own this runtime branch.

## Bounded repair

Broaden the dependency-free structural predicate to recognize both supported Reagent-family class shapes, correct its obsolete policy comment, and add real reagent-slim Form-3 coverage. Keep core substrate-neutral: do not add a static dependency on either Reagent implementation or invent a general adapter hook unless concrete additional class shapes require one.
acceptance_criteria:
- A stock Reagent `create-class` and a reagent-slim `create-class` are both classified as Form-3 without importing either adapter into neutral core.
- Passing a real slim Form-3 result through a registered view under debug/source annotation preserves the exact class identity; it is never invoked or wrapped as Form-2.
- A mounted slim fixture proves render plus representative lifecycle behavior, and the existing non-DOM-root warning contract remains one-shot and truthful.
- Slim source-coordinate/view-id tests include the Form-3 case and fail against the pre-fix predicate.
- The stale “slim is scheduled for deletion” comment is removed/reconciled with rf2-ukq8qt.
- Focused slim tests and bundle-isolation/core-only compile gates remain green; no new core-to-adapter dependency is introduced.

title: Make spawn-all preflight verdict and prepared children authoritative
description: PR #6010 made `spawn-all-init-fx` the authoritative batch-admission preflight, but it only retains a boolean verdict. `schema-rejected-child?` resolves the spec, builds the initial snapshot, and runs the application schema validator; every accepted per-child `spawn-fx*` then resolves/builds/validates the same child again. A direct all-valid repro observes two validator calls. A `:rf.machine.spawn-all/started` listener can also re-register the type between those passes: preflight accepts v1 and publishes a live child-bearing join, then child spawn resolves rejecting v2 and installs no snapshot, leaving an impossible half-live join. This violates closed source Bead `rf2-7u8gen`'s authoritative-preflight and user-functions-at-most-once acceptance criteria and remains on current main.
acceptance_criteria: Each declarative `:spawn-all` child is resolved, prepared, and schema-validated exactly once for an attempt, before any live join or child side effect is published. Accepted per-child effects consume that exact framework-owned prepared result rather than re-resolving, rebuilding, or revalidating application state; it must not be forgeable as an unchecked public boolean. Prove validator/data callback cardinality, type re-registration and other callback mutation seams, all-valid behavior, and mixed rejection atomicity on CLJ and CLJS. No accepted preflight can end with a child-bearing join whose snapshot was omitted by a second verdict.
close_reason: shipped #6213 (merged)

title: Fence spawn-all-init admission and join writes to the exact frame incarnation
description: `spawn-all-init-fx` captures an exact-incarnation `continue?` before application callbacks, but after `schema-rejected-child?` and `reject-unregistered-spawn!` it writes the reject sentinel or live join through bare-id `frame/swap-runtime-db!` without rechecking ownership. A schema validator (or rejection trace listener) can synchronously destroy owner frame A and publish same-id successor B. Validation then reports `:rf/stale-incarnation`, which is deliberately not a schema rejection, and the outer handler installs A-derived live join state into B; later child fxs fence/no-op, leaving B with an impossible join. Confirmed by direct current-main repro after PR #6010. Closed `rf2-vxgfnd.153` covers the single-spawn pipeline, not `spawn-all-init`.
acceptance_criteria: Every callback/emission in `spawn-all-init-fx` is followed by an exact-owner continuation check before durable state or framework-owned tail work. Join/sentinel writes are bound to the raw owner token (including loss during the physical write), so same-id successor B remains byte-identical. Cover conforming, failing, and throwing schema validators plus unregistered-child rejection/listener replacement on CLJ and CLJS; prove no stale join/sentinel/started trace or child side effect lands on B while ordinary all-valid and rejection behavior remains unchanged.

title: Fail closed when stale frame bundles report payloads across reincarnation
description:
PR #5954 made stale compiled frame-bundle failures production-observable by passing the attempted event/query plus frame-id into error-emit/emit-error-both!. The always-on path elides the payload by looking up policy through that frame-id at emission time.

A stale bundle is locked to exact incarnation A, but frame-id may already name a same-ID successor B. Current-main reproduction:
1. create A with sensitive/elision ownership and capture its (frame) bundle.
2. destroy A.
3. create an unclassified successor B under the same id.
4. invoke A's stale :dispatch-sync with [:audit/secret {:password :TOP-SECRET}].
5. the operation is correctly rejected as stale, but the production-survivable error record contains the raw attempted event because elision borrowed B's policy.

This is an off-box/log privacy leak: incarnation A's payload is projected under unrelated successor B authority. Existing tests separate same-ID fencing from observability, so neither sees the composition. No open bead owns it.

Fail closed for stale-bundle payload egress. The smallest safe option may retain only structural event-id/op and replace the body with a redacted marker; alternatively carry exact captured elision authority and validate it without consulting a successor. Do not create a general policy snapshot system unless the simple fail-closed projection is insufficient.
acceptance_criteria: A stale frame bundle invoked after same-ID recreation never exposes attempted payload fields under the successor's elision policy. A regression uses divergent A/B policies and proves the always-on record is safely redacted/elided while retaining category, captured frame id, operation, and structural event/query head. Absent-frame and ordinary destroyed-without-successor paths fail closed too. Dispatch, dispatch-sync, and subscribe remain exact-incarnation fenced and throw after exactly-one observability fan-out. Advanced-production listener coverage proves no raw secret reaches the record or logs. No successor policy is borrowed and no general policy framework is added.

title: Remove public event metadata as a join-completion authority path
description: The spawn-all join interceptor still treats public event-vector `:rf/join-auth` metadata as a fallback authority carrier. `carrier-auth` prefers protected recordable cofx but otherwise reads user-authored metadata; `join-auth-current?` verifies only equality with observable runtime state. Application code that supplies an exact-current parent/invoke/child/spawned-id/attempt tuple can therefore forge completion. A real `rf/dispatch-sync` reproduction changes an unresolved join from `:done #{}` to `:done #{:a}` without child `:a` completing. This bypass survives the protected/non-redirectable join-dispatch work because it enters through the ordinary public event path. Remove metadata as an authority-mint channel; freshness is not provenance. Keep the recordable `:rf.machine/join-auth` coeffect as the single protected carrier, with no secret-token or public-authentication API.
acceptance_criteria:
- A public dispatch carrying an exact-current `:rf/join-auth` metadata tuple fails closed before any `:done`/`:failed` fold, resolution, child reap, parent event, or late-completion attribution.
- `carrier-auth` accepts join authority only from the protected recordable `[:rf/cofx :rf.machine/join-auth]` transport (or an equivalently non-authorable internal seam); event metadata is never an authority fallback.
- Existing stale, duplicate, and post-resolution tests inject protected cofx or use real child completions rather than proving behavior with forged public metadata.
- Real immediate and delayed child completions still fold once; record/replay preserves the protected coeffect fact; fallthrough overrides still reach the authenticated internal transport.
- Hand-authored/redirected private effects and ordinary public events cannot mint, capture, replay, or forge authority, including when every tuple field matches current runtime state.
- Active specs, Conventions, source docstrings, and tests describe one primary protected carrier and no metadata fallback; no public auth API or secrecy assumption is introduced.

title: Linearize final ViewCell body authority with publication
description: PR #5938 completed synchronous proof around the final ViewCell HMR body-authority fence, but the runtime fence is not a publication linearization point on JVM. `commit*` samples the cell generation and registered view revision, then performs an independent `swap!` that publishes the candidate. A concurrent `advance-generation!` or same-view re-registration can land after the final sample but before that swap, so a generation-0 capture publishes, connects, and owns leases while current authority is generation/revision 1. A deterministic latch reproduction pauses the second/final `registered-view-revision` read after it captures revision 0, advances authority on another thread, then lets the stale read return; current main reports `:published`, `:connected`, and the committed site. title: Fence successor adapter generations until deferred root cleanup settles
description: PR #5931 proves adapter destruction may return synchronously while old React root cleanups remain deferred, but it installs the successor only after settlement. The real destroy -> immediate `rf/init!` composition is unfenced: core clears the installed generation when the adapter drain returns, UI clears its admission guard, and install clears the disposed breadcrumb. A predecessor layout/effect cleanup then runs after the successor is live. Frame captures are keyed by target/id rather than incarnation, and dispatch resolves the drain lock at call time, so an old cleanup can dispatch into a recreated same-id frame B (or otherwise mutate state observed by fresh-adapter roots). Root id/container quarantine prevents DOM reuse but does not fence arbitrary cleanup side effects. Establish an honest generation boundary: successor installation/admission must not become usable until all predecessor host cleanup authority has settled, or provide an equivalently strong incarnation fence. Preserve the small closed contract; do not build a general scheduler.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic browser regression performs destroy and immediate init before deferred settlement, with an old root cleanup dispatching through a capture from frame A after a same-id frame B exists; B is never mutated by predecessor cleanup.
- Before the predecessor settlement boundary, successor init/root admission is rejected or remains unusable with a typed lifecycle error; after settlement, a fresh adapter can install and the exact id/container can be reused.
- The proof covers a committed zero-ViewCell root and multiple deferred roots, so completion waits for root-level reporter authority rather than cell population.
- A queue-then-throw host regression schedules late DOM cleanup or an old captured dispatch, throws from `.unmount`, then exercises destroy/reclaim -> immediate init/successor on the same id/container; clearing DOM/React markers is not treated as settlement proof and predecessor work cannot clobber or enter the successor.
- Cleanup failure remains fail-closed and cannot silently unblock successor generations; any recovery path is explicit and exact-incarnation guarded.
- Spec 006 reconciles synchronous return, surviving ownership quarantine, throwing-host reclaim, and its `Disposal is total`/`no state survives` language with the implemented boundary.
- Existing synchronous-settlement and immediate-remount behavior remains intact.

title: Collapse defview header collisions through the canonical host binding plan
description: PR #5932 claims one host-faithful binding plan, but the plan contains only local names. `parse-header` retains every original entry and `emit_cljs/header-bindings` stable-sorts those entries, so host destructuring's overwrite/collapse semantics are lost when entries bind the same local. For `{:keys [x] x :foo}`, the host plan has one binding `x <- :x`, while CLJS emits both `x <- :x` and `x <- :foo`; JVM and CLJS therefore disagree. The existing collision-named fixture uses distinct locals and cannot catch this. Make the canonical host transformation authoritative for complete emitted binding units (local, winning lookup slot, default semantics), or reject duplicates with a typed compile error if host-faithful support is intentionally narrowed. Do not add a general macroexpander or compatibility layer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Real JVM and CLJS defview behavior agrees for explicit/`:keys` collisions in both source orders, with present, absent, and defaulted props.
- Qualified symbols in `:keys` preserve the host lookup key (`{:keys [acct/id]}` reads `:acct/id`, never bare `:id`) on both JVM and CLJS.
- Namespaced group versus explicit/group collisions are covered, including the host's winning lookup slot.
- Header parsing, emitted lets, schema slots/comparator inputs, and manifest-facing metadata consume the same collapsed canonical entries; no downstream path re-sorts unnormalised duplicates or strips qualified lookup keys.
- Mutations that restore duplicate entry emission or bare-slot qualified-key lowering fail the regressions.
- Non-colliding headers retain current diagnostics and behavior.
notes: Correctness audit added a second deterministic counterexample on current main: header `{:keys [acct/id]}` with props `{:acct/id :namespaced :id :bare}` returns `:namespaced` on JVM, but `header/parse-header` derives slot `id`, so CLJS reads `:bare`. This belongs to the same split-authority fix: the canonical unit must retain the winning qualified lookup key, not only the local name/rank.
close_reason: shipped via PR #6075 (merged): defview header binding was split across two authorities (parse-header per-raw-entry + emit sort) while the true collapse sat unused in analyze; CLJS path emitted duplicate reads (silent last-wins) + stripped namespace off qualified :keys. Fixed by extracting canonical binding_plan.cljc (complete de-collided units) consumed by all paths; proven against real clojure.core/destructure

title: Keep delayed-silence generation authoritative through trace emission
description:
PR #5914 (`rf2-vxgfnd.285`) says delayed `:rf.epoch.cb/silenced-on-frame-destroy` is exact and linearizable, and specifically that a callback swapped between eligibility and delivery cannot inherit the old generation's unqualified signal. Current main reserves under `silence-lock`, releases that lock, and only then calls external `trace/emit!`. `put-listener!`, `drop-listener!`, observation recording, and reset do not participate in the lock at all.

A deterministic current-main seam probe reserves for generation G, installs generation H immediately after the original claim returns but before `trace/emit!`, and observes `{:reservation-granted? true, :replacement-landed-before-emit? true}` followed by the unqualified `{frame, cb-id}` silence. A real JVM registrar thread has the same legal window. Replacement can also land between the claim's first listener-generation read and its later observation read because the lock excludes registry mutation. The fresh generation can therefore be current before an old-generation signal is emitted, contrary to the exact-generation contract.

This was deduplicated against all bead states. Closed `rf2-vxgfnd.285` owns the attempted implementation and cannot be amended; no open/in-progress bead owns this residual defect. Preserve the current per-generation model, exactly-once reservations, rollback, and bounded ledger. Prefer one small authority protocol over another parallel registry or a general transaction layer.
acceptance_criteria:
- An `(cb-id, generation)` that wins delayed-silence eligibility remains the authoritative generation through the signal's emission linearization point; a replacement or unregister that becomes current before that point cannot receive/inherit the old generation's unqualified silence.
- Listener replacement/drop/reset and the relevant observation/re-arm mutations participate in the same coherent authority decision as eligibility and mark reservation, or an equivalently small protocol proves the same ordering without split-state windows.
- A deterministic JVM barrier test parks after reservation and replaces G with H before allowing publication; the result is either a silence linearized before H becomes current or no stale silence, never H current first followed by G's unqualified signal.
- A second deterministic test replaces/drops between the individual eligibility reads and proves no old-generation claim is granted from a mixed state.
- Existing overlapping-publisher exactly-once, successor re-arm, A→B→nil ABA, failed-delivery rollback, reset, and bounded-retention tests remain green.
- Mutation teeth that remove registry/observation participation in the authority protocol or reopen claim-to-emit replacement make the focused tests fail.
- Avoid a second listener registry, broad transaction framework, or unrelated fan-out serialization; document the chosen linearization point and any deliberately held critical section/reentrancy behavior.
notes: COMPLETENESS FOLLOW-UP (PR #5914 audit): the PR explicitly deferred the canonical Spec 009 / Tool-Pair lineage wording. When fixing the runtime ordering, update both canonical homes to state the final generation/re-arm/late-predecessor emission linearization law; do not leave the current broad "repeated destroy does not re-emit" sentence as the whole concurrency contract.

title: Complete stepwise exact-incarnation handoffs across machine lifecycle tails
description: PR #5913 adds broad lifecycle fences but several adjacent stages still share one precheck even though the first stage can run user callbacks or exact container callbacks. Current-main reproductions show: (1) ordinary destroy emits `system-id-released`, a listener creates same-id B and registers B's actor handler, then A unconditionally unregisters B; (2) spawn loses A inside exact classification lowering, then records A's ghost child in B's bare-ID spawn-order; (3) finalize loses A inside exact classification drop, then forgets B's spawn-order and can continue into release/unregister/error stages; (4) `destroy-single-actor!` returns true after teardown aborts on owner loss, so spawn-all can emit a phantom `destroyed`; and (5) non-destroy timer cancellation reasons use the explicitly unfenced helper arity, allowing a cancellation listener to re-arm B's same subscription-vector before A decrements B's shared subscription ref. Existing #5913 tests prove the first exact write or broad tail guard, but do not seed/assert the downstream successor-owned state, creating false greens against the PR's 'after every callback boundary' claim.
acceptance_criteria:
- Recheck exact ownership after every callback-bearing trace or exact container write before starting the next bare-ID lifecycle action; reuse one small stepwise fence discipline rather than adding transactions or another ownership registry.
- Ordinary destroy: after system-ID release loss, B retains its event handler, registrar metadata/source provenance/resolved generation, and dispatch succeeds; live-owner destroy unregisters exactly once.
- Spawn: loss during classification lowering prevents spawn-order record, lifecycle trace, snapshot/bootstrap, and start work from reaching B; include a live control.
- Finalize: loss during classification drop prevents spawn-order forget, system-ID release, unregister, resource/evidence cleanup, and on-error work against B; include a live control.
- `destroy-single-actor!` reports success only when teardown actually commits while authority remains exact; spawn-all emits `destroyed`, clears slots, and continues iteration only for genuinely torn-down children.
- Fence every callback-bearing timer-cancellation reason (`:on-exit`, `:on-resolution`, `:on-supersede`, `:on-frame-destroy`, `:on-restore`, plus existing `:on-destroy`) so A releases its private host resources without decrementing successor B's shared subscription ownership.
- Add mutation-tooth regressions that seed the actual successor registrar, spawn-order, timer/subscription, and runtime state named above; cover CLJ and CLJS, plus dev/prod-shaped paths where evidence differs.
- Record the ordinary-destroy terminal-fence law in Spec 005 and retain explicit eventless frame-destroy authority.

title: Preserve per-listener event order across nested trace emissions
description: While auditing #5912's synchronous listener pipeline, a current-main reproduction showed that reentrant trace emission reverses runtime event order for later listeners. Listener 0 handles an outer `:rf.flow/cleared` by re-registering the same flow, synchronously emitting nested `:rf.flow/registered`. Listener 1 then observes `[:rf.flow/registered :rf.flow/cleared]`, although the outer clear event was authored first; after return the flow is live but a stateful tool can finish in the cleared state. Spec 009 requires every listener to receive trace events in runtime emission order. This is a central trace-delivery law, not a flow-local fence. The in-progress `rf2-eaxnai` owns neutral callback authority, but neutralizing the listener does not preserve cross-listener nested event order.
acceptance_criteria:
- Define and implement one truthful central law for nested trace delivery such that every listener observes outer event A before a reentrantly emitted event B.
- Preserve listener registration order, per-listener exception isolation, ring/capture/policy ordering, and the exact-continuation checks around framework-owned fan-out.
- Explicitly reconcile the documented synchronous-return contract for a nested `emit!`; do not silently introduce a queue whose return semantics contradict the spec.
- Add a deterministic two-listener regression where listener 0 nested-emits and listener 1 observes A then B; include stateful tooling evidence and nested exception/control cases.
- Cover CLJ and CLJS and coordinate with `rf2-eaxnai` so public-listener neutral authority and event ordering compose.
- Fix the trace bus once; do not patch flow lifecycle emitters or add subsystem-specific queues.

title: Emit recursive defviews against their current-namespace Var
description:
PR #5909 correctly makes exact self-heads win during analysis, but the CLJS emitter still uses the raw authored :sym instead of the canonical :fqn. With a namespace that refers re-frame.ui/sub, compiling (defview sub [] [sub {}]) emits the render call against re-frame.ui.sub and defines the view at re-frame.ui.sub, rather than audit.self.sub. The analyzer warning confirms that the defining name replaced the referred name, while the emitted JavaScript still targets the authoring Var.

Existing coverage stops at AST or regex macroexpansion and uses a qualified authoring head, so it cannot detect bare referred-name capture in real JavaScript output.
acceptance_criteria:
- Carry and use one canonical current-view emitted symbol/FQN for both self component nodes and the defining Var; raw authored spelling is diagnostic only.
- The CLJS emitter targets the current namespace for the component call and definition.
- Handle declaration/order so the render function's self reference is valid without undeclared-name or public-authoring-Var capture.
- Add real cljs.analyzer plus cljs.compiler JavaScript-output tests for referred sub, lease, and frame: current-namespace definition/reference and zero authoring-Var definition/reference.
- Preserve local-shadow precedence, root reservation, and unrelated component-head behavior.
- Avoid a broad component-emission rewrite unless the canonical-symbol fix genuinely requires it.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6879 (2026-07-25) — REOPENED as the exact existing owner of the canonical-self-Var invariant. The PR retired the old dead `emit-defview` chain and its `*self-fqn*` carry, but the live Freehand emitters still emit `(:sym node)` for self boundaries.

Real CLJS analyzer reproduction in a `cljs.user` namespace that refers `re-frame.freehand/sub`: the self AST is `{:sym sub, :fqn cljs.user/sub, :view-id :cljs.user/sub}`, while both `emit-jvm/emit-structural-body` and `emit-react/emit-react-body` produce mount heads `[sub]`. Real `cljs.compiler` resolves that raw head to `re_frame.freehand.sub`; the canonical `cljs.user/sub` compiles to `cljs.user.sub`. A compiled view named `sub` therefore mounts the authoring verb instead of recursing on itself in both realisations.

Bounded repair: for self `:view` nodes, carry/use the AST's canonical current-namespace `:fqn` in both live emitters; retain raw authored symbols for ordinary non-self heads. Add the real referred-namespace emitter regression. No emitter redesign or compatibility layer.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6886 — REOPENED exact canonical-self/defining-Var owner; no duplicate.

CORRECTNESS / COMPLETENESS: The new canonical `:fqn` head emission is correct for an exact recursive self node, but `emit-react-body` removes the declaration name from the live CLJS namespace `:uses` only when `:self-ref?` became true. A non-recursive compiled `(defview sub {:compiled true} [] [:div "x"])` in a namespace referring `re-frame.freehand/sub` therefore still compiles its `(def sub …)` against the AUTHORING Var. Independent real `cljs.analyzer` + `cljs.compiler` probe on merged main returned `{:defines-current? false, :defines-authoring? true, :refer-after re-frame.freehand}`. That clobbers `re_frame.freehand.sub` and leaves no `cljs.user.sub`, even though every declaration — recursive or not — must define its current-namespace Var. The added `a-non-recursive-view-leaves-the-refer-and-heads-untouched` test currently pins this wrong definition behavior by requiring the refer to remain.

Move/extend same-named-refer shadow completion to the declaration boundary so every `defview` definition shadows its same-named refer, independent of whether its body happens to recurse; do not rewrite unrelated component heads. Invert/extend the real JavaScript regression to prove a non-recursive colliding declaration defines `cljs.user/<name>`, emits zero authoring-Var definition/reference, and still preserves unrelated head spelling. (:fqn node) (:sym node)) - canonical current-namespace Var for an exact self head. But the refer-shadow completion at emit_react.cljc:769-772 is STILL gated on recursion: (when (and (:self-ref? @st) (:self e) (some? cljs.env/*compiler*)) (swap! cljs.env/*compiler* update-in [:cljs.analyzer/namespaces (:ns e) :uses] dissoc (:self e))). So a NON-recursive compiled defview named sub in a namespace referring re-frame.freehand/sub never drops the refer and still compiles its def against the AUTHORING Var. The test that pins the wrong behaviour is also still present at implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/compiler_macro_resolution_jvm_test.clj:365, deftest a-non-recursive-view-leaves-the-refer-and-heads-untouched. title: Keep join authority inside an authenticated, non-redirectable effect path
description:
PR #5908 routes canonical join completion overrides through the public effect engine but does not preserve authenticated fallback. Unregistered-keyword and malformed overrides emit canonical override-fallthrough, then ordinary :dispatch reaches the parent without private join authority and is suppressed as attempt-unverified, hanging the join.

The private :rf.machine/join-dispatch transport is also globally registered inside the public override domain. A direct override captures and suppresses its authenticated payload. Redirecting canonical :dispatch to :rf.machine/join-dispatch bypasses the current reserved-key check, recursively re-enters override resolution until StackOverflowError, and leaves the join unresolved. These are one authority-boundary defect: public override choice and private completion transport need a single explicit, non-redirectable policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- Canonical resolution distinguishes an applied override from noop/fallthrough.
- Valid function and registered-keyword public overrides preempt completion without minting private authority.
- Nil, false, unregistered-keyword, and malformed overrides fall through as specified; canonical errors are emitted where applicable, then authenticated private transport runs exactly once and the join folds.
- A direct override for the private join key cannot capture, suppress, forge, or replay join authority.
- Redirecting canonical effects to private/protected IDs fails safely exactly once, with no recursion or StackOverflowError.
- A hand-authored private effect cannot execute outside the framework machine boundary, or the implementation replaces the globally authorable surface with a truly internal seam.
- Cover immediate and delayed completion, including 0 ms, in CLJ and CLJS and production-shaped paths.
- Document one authoritative internal/non-authorable/non-redirectable policy in Conventions and StateMachines.
- Keep one override engine and expose no public authentication API.

title: Use causal Shadow compile membership instead of wall-clock stamp ordering

A current-main reproduction shows that a same-stamp zero-declaration recompile is treated as untouched and leaves ghost accepted views/digests. The changed test only proves increasing timestamps and no longer exercises the same-millisecond requirement from rf2-vxgfnd.255.

This is a deterministic compiler correctness problem, not merely a missing integration test. Coordinate real-host coverage with rf2-vxgfnd.195, but keep one compiler authority and do not make test infrastructure the source of truth.
acceptance_criteria:
- Determine current-pass source membership from an actual causal Shadow build fact; do not use >, >=, !=, not=, or another wall-clock relationship.
- Prove genuine equal-stamp and backwards-stamp compiles in sequential and parallel pass shapes.
- Prove a fresh metadata/output object with an unchanged stamp remains a non-compile.
- Prove a real zero-declaration recompile evicts prior accepted rows and changes the digest.
- Missing or ambiguous compile evidence fails before publication.
- Add the real Shadow host proof under rf2-vxgfnd.195 and correct false timestamp-ordering prose/tests.
- Preserve a single compiler authority and avoid a second shadow state model.

title: Neutralize outer continuation authority inside public trace listeners
description:
PR #5904 correctly fenced an outer flow-registration trace to frame incarnation A, but public trace listeners run while A's dynamic continuation predicate remains bound. If a listener destroys A and creates same-id incarnation B with :initial-events, B's seed dispatch consults trace/continuation-live?, inherits A's now-false predicate, and is silently suppressed. B remains live with {}, and make-frame's reuse/no-reseed law means a later re-ensure cannot recover the seed. Current-main reproduction: after callback {:b-live? true :seed-runs 0 :b-db {} :later-a-listener-hits 0}; after re-ensure still 0/{}; an independent dispatch later runs normally. The later A listener staying at zero proves the outer fence itself works.

Fix this centrally at the trace/tooling callback boundary, not separately in flow registration/replacement/clear. Public callback-authored nested work needs a neutral continuation scope, while deliver-to-tooling!'s explicit outer continue? checks before and after each callback must retain A's predicate so A destruction suppresses the remaining A listener fanout. Keep terminal structural/retention scope behavior intact.
acceptance_criteria:
- A public trace listener body runs under a neutral/ordinary continuation scope for nested authored work; the surrounding delivery loop restores and checks the caller's exact continuation predicate before and after the callback.
- Causal CLJ and CLJS coverage registers a listener which, during A's flow-registration trace, destroys A and creates same-id B with an initial seed event. B's seed handler runs exactly once and its DB is initialized; re-ensuring B does not replay it.
- The same proof shows remaining listeners for A are suppressed after destruction, while unrelated-frame nested dispatch/trace work from a public listener is unaffected.
- The central boundary covers registration, replacement, and clear/other callers without flow-local patches.
- Existing terminal structural facts, exact-incarnation fencing, ring retention, and listener error isolation remain green.

description:

The S-5 sync-door predicate admits only LITERAL vector handlers, so a reusable library input — which receives an application event prefix through props and appends the live payload with (ui/event [e] (conj on-value (.. e -target -value))) — forfeits the IME/caret guarantee at exactly the sites it matters most. rf2-vxgfnd.95.1 (in progress) implements the literal-only law; that law must not be declared S3-conforming.

At a compiler-proven controlled DOM site (unchanged S-5 predicate: literal :value/:checked co-present with the handler site), a SYNCHRONOUS ui/event body whose result is an EVENT VECTOR dispatches through the same synchronous drain as a literal vector handler. nil still means no dispatch. title: Make Reagent Form-3 lifecycle guidance StrictMode-safe
description:
## Problem
PR #6000 teaches and tests acquiring a render-owned subscription in a Form-3 outer callable, dereferencing it in `:reagent-render`, then explicitly unsubscribing it in `:component-will-unmount`. React 19 StrictMode performs didMount -> willUnmount -> didMount without an intervening render. Reagent intentionally preserves/cancels cleanup of its render reaction across that replay; the user cleanup disposes the underlying subscription, so the preserved render reaction can become reactively dead after remount. Current fixtures neither wrap this path in StrictMode nor update app-db after replay.

## Required correction
Make the documented model distinguish Reagent-owned render derefs from genuinely imperative subscriptions. Prefer Form-1/outer reactive reads passed as values. If an imperative live subscription is needed, acquire it in did-mount and release it in will-unmount so replay is balanced; do not manually unsubscribe a reaction owned by `reagent-render`.

## Proof
Add a real React StrictMode browser counterexample that completes replay, changes app-db, proves the mounted view updates, performs real unmount, awaits cleanup, and returns subscription/cache state to baseline.
acceptance_criteria:
- Recommended docs and fixtures do not manually dispose subscriptions owned by a Reagent render reaction.
- A StrictMode browser test proves reactivity survives mount replay and updates after a subsequent dispatch/app-db change.
- The real unmount releases imperative ownership exactly once and restores cache/live-subscription baselines.
- Normal Form-3 lifecycle behavior remains green outside StrictMode.
close_reason: Closed

title: Make guide mounted-frame cleanup safe for synchronous and Promise failures
description:
## Confirmed exact-head counterexample
The #5995 guide helper `destroy-frame-after!` receives an already-evaluated Promise. Call sites evaluate `ui.test/with-root` before the helper is entered. `with-root` can throw synchronously (for example no DOM host or overlapping-act after a forgotten await), leaving the caller-created frame live. The new JVM tests only string-match this recipe or exercise synchronous `with-new-frame`; they do not execute mounted Promise settlement, synchronous construction failure, cleanup precedence, or live-frame restoration.

## Required correction
Make the owner helper accept a thunk and catch synchronous construction failure before normalizing the result to a Promise. Destroy the caller-owned frame exactly once on synchronous throw, fulfillment (including nil/false), and rejection. Preserve the primary thrown/rejected value/identity; a cleanup failure must surface when it is the only failure and must not replace a primary failure (attach/report it according to the existing error-precedence law). Update guide call sites to pass thunks.

## Proof obligations
Add real CLJS mounted fixtures, not lexical checks, for fulfilled truthy/nil/false, primary rejection identity, cleanup-only failure, primary+cleanup failure, synchronous `with-root` throw, forgotten-await overlap, and post-run live-frame/sub-cache baseline.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every synchronous or Promise exit path destroys the caller-owned frame exactly once and restores the live-frame/sub-cache baseline.
- Fulfilled values including nil/false pass through unchanged; primary rejection/throw identity is preserved.
- Cleanup-only failure surfaces; primary+cleanup retains the primary under the repository's exact error-composition convention.
- A synchronous overlap/no-host failure before Promise creation is covered by a red-before-fix CLJS mounted fixture.
- JVM guide fixtures, browser mounted tests, and truth/link gates are green; no general Promise utility is introduced.

title: Make advanced evidence-elision gate discriminate renamed rooted state mutations
description:

title: Unregister cleared evidence holders during opportunistic compaction
description:
## Confirmed exact-head counterexample
In #5998 CLJS opportunistic compaction removes a holder whose WeakRef cleared from the members Set, but does not unregister its FinalizationRegistry registration. The registration's held value is the holder itself, so bounded evidence/query data remains strongly retained until a finalizer callback that JavaScript never promises to run. The explicit-dead path unregisters correctly; the cleared-ref path does not.

## Required correction
Before deleting a cleared holder during compaction, unregister that exact holder/token when a reaper exists. Preserve unique-token stale-finalizer safety and tolerate already-run callbacks/idempotence. Do not depend on prompt finalization.
acceptance_criteria:
- A delayed/never-run finalizer fixture proves read-time compaction unregisters cleared holders and releases held evidence promptly.
- An already-fired or stale token cannot remove a replacement; unregister is idempotent/tolerant.
- No-reaper and normal reaper paths both compact correctly, and public snapshots remain stable during their read.

title: Prevent evidence values from retaining their weak ViewCell keys
description:
## Confirmed exact-head counterexample
Weak keys do not prevent retention when the stored value points back to the key. #5998 evidence entries retain exact observation target/query values; re-frame2 query vectors permit arbitrary arguments. A query such as `[::q cell]`, or a nested value indirectly referencing the cell, yields entry → query → cell. JVM `WeakHashMap` and the CLJS rooted holder Set then keep the supposedly weak cell alive forever, contradicting the claim that bounded values never point back.

## Required correction
Ensure retained evidence values cannot strongly own their ViewCell key or host identity. Prefer a bounded serializable/tool projection of target arguments with explicit opaque/dynamic markers for non-data identity rather than narrowing public query grammar or retaining handles. Preserve truthful event/sub identification and mark information loss explicitly. No general graph serializer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Direct and nested key/value-cycle fixtures prove an observation query containing its own ViewCell does not keep the cell alive on JVM or CLJS.
- Ordinary EDN queries remain exact; identity/host values become a documented opaque/dynamic projection with explicit loss, never a fabricated value.
- Activity-retained evidence remains intentionally live and distinguishable.
- No lease, ViewCell, React object, host object, or arbitrary back-reference escapes through public tool projections.

title: Make weak evidence state representation stable across CLJS HMR constructor churn
description:
## Confirmed exact-head counterexample
PR #5998 (`e945f5f57a29cde2c18a0ce73641a7ac78c81f38`) stores a `defrecord WeakCellEntries` in `defonce state*` and recognizes it with constructor-identity `instance?`. CLJS hot reload replaces the record constructor while preserving the old store. Same-owner `install!` can then misclassify the old record as a legacy strong map, iterate record fields as cell/entry pairs, and call reactive lifecycle operations on `:members` or `:by-cell`.

## Required correction
Use a reload-stable tagged/structural representation for weak evidence state, or explicitly recognize/migrate pre-reload record-shaped values without constructor identity. Preserve same-owner evidence/ordinals and re-arm the reaper exactly once. Do not discard evidence on compatible HMR or add a second state registry.

title: Bound weak root membership when FinalizationRegistry is absent
description:
## Confirmed counterexample
PR #5997 explicitly supports hosts with `WeakRef` but no `FinalizationRegistry`. Ordinary reconciliation departure disconnects a cell without deterministic membership removal. Cleared weak refs are compacted only by scans; the hot attach path appends without scanning. A long-lived root that repeatedly mounts, reconciliation-unmounts, collects, and mounts new cells can therefore grow `members.refs` without bound even though cells themselves collect. This contradicts the bounded weak-registry and optional-finalizer contract.

## Required correction
On the no-reaper arm, compact cleared refs for the affected incarnation before enrolment (or an equally small amortized bounded operation). Keep the normal FinalizationRegistry-capable path unchanged. Weak refs remain observability/lifecycle bookkeeping only, never authority. Do not add polling, timers, a strong reverse index, or a general GC subsystem.

## Proof obligations
Create a no-FinalizationRegistry churn fixture that models ordinary reconciliation departure—not deterministic root teardown—then repeated collection/attach. It must prove dead ref husks remain bounded/compacted, live members and occurrence identity survive, and stale/dead refs cannot remove a replacement. Include root/frame/tool scans and no-scan attach counterexamples.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repeated ordinary reconciliation churn under WeakRef-present/FinalizationRegistry-absent does not grow dead membership refs without bound.
- Live refs, Activity-retained evidence, occurrence identity, and loss accounting remain exact.
- Stale cleared refs/finalizer-like tokens cannot remove a replacement incarnation.
- The FinalizationRegistry-capable production path adds no new scan on attach; no polling/timer/fallback authority is introduced.
- Red fixture fails on #5997 exact head; focused CLJS/browser/advanced-production gates pass after correction.
close_reason: Closed

title: Adapter destroy must reclaim pre-existing cleanup-failure root quarantine
description:
## Confirmed counterexample
Independent exact-head review of PR #5997 (`9592f10d95cdddc293c3ab973a76e10d24039485`) found that `unmount!*` no-ops for every already-`:tearing-down` root, while `drain-live-roots!` calls `reclaim-consumed-container!` only when the drain's own `unmount!*` invocation throws. A root quarantined earlier by failed-first-mount cleanup or a public unmount cleanup throw is therefore silently skipped during later adapter destroy. Its registry/container claim survives adapter re-init and the same root/container cannot be reused.

## Required correction
Represent enough teardown cause/state to distinguish a cleanup-failure quarantine that adapter destruction must reclaim from an ordinary deferred host settlement that must not be reclaimed prematurely. Adapter destruction must finish/reclaim a pre-existing cleanup-failure quarantine and release exact root/container ownership, without allowing stale settlement or destroying a genuinely pending incarnation. Preserve exception aggregation and original failure precedence.

## Proof obligations
Add composed red-before-fix fixtures for (1) failed first mount whose cleanup throws, then adapter destroy, re-init, and same root/container reuse; (2) public unmount cleanup throw followed by adapter destroy and reuse; and (3) an ordinary deferred teardown proving adapter destroy does not reclaim before its host settlement unless the established adapter-destroy contract explicitly owns that completion. Exercise stale/incarnation callbacks after reclaim.
acceptance_criteria:
- The two pre-quarantined cleanup-failure paths are fully reclaimed by adapter destroy and exact root/container claims are reusable after re-init.
- Deferred host settlement is not consumed early or confused with cleanup-failure quarantine.
- Late/stale settlement from the reclaimed incarnation cannot mutate or release a successor.
- Red fixtures fail at #5997 exact head and pass after the smallest state distinction/fix.
- Existing mount rollback, public unmount, adapter destroy, HMR, root registry, and diagnostic tests remain green; docs/spec state the same lifecycle.

title: S3 committed event spine: data handlers, placeholders, stable committed callbacks, and sync door
description:
## Problem

S3 cannot become real until compiled native event sites stop being inert/staging-only and deliver event intent through the frame that actually committed the DOM. The compiler/runtime must lower event vectors into stable site callbacks without per-render closure churn, while preserving the program's central scheduling law: many queued events may each commit an epoch, but the write-side drain reaches quiescence before dirty ViewCells advance once and React receives one read/render batch. "Eight epochs = eight renders" is explicitly wrong.

## Current contracts

Implement against the checked-in `spec/004-Views.md` Event handlers / Controlled inputs sections and I-6, plus `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/02-programming-model.md` §3 and `03-reactivity-and-ownership.md` §3. The exact v1 placeholder set is closed: `:rf.ui/value`, `:rf.ui/checked`, `:rf.ui/key`; substitution occurs only at top-level positions of a compiler-known literal vector. The callback reads the committed frame and committed site slots when invoked, not the abandoned/current render attempt. Dynamic values classify at runtime (vector dispatch, compiled handler object, map options form, fn only where the boundary law permits, nil absent); a placeholder-looking keyword inside a dynamic vector is ordinary data plus a dev warning.

## Scope

Build the compiler and client-runtime event spine for known native DOM/custom-element `:on-*` sites:

- Lower literal event vectors to per-site stable callbacks and exact scalar placeholder projection from the native event.
- Publish/retarget callback reads with the winning commit so an abandoned render or later uncommitted render cannot affect delivery.
- Dispatch through the committed frame and preserve event-site/source coordinates for later manifest/Xray consumption.
- Make `re-frame.ui.test/dispatch!` exercise the real native `dispatchEvent` path for compiled vector handlers; do not introduce a gesture DSL.
- Implement runtime classification for dynamic handler-position values without treating placeholder keywords as syntax there.
- Emit the dev-only `:rf.warning/unregistered-event-id` and `:rf.warning/placeholder-in-dynamic-vector` diagnostics with stable site coordinates and useful recovery text. Registration is process-global; the unregistered warning must admit lazy registration can make it transient.
- Implement the one synchronous door only where the compiler proves all three facts: native `:on-input`/`:on-change`/`:on-before-input`, literal controlled `:value` or `:checked` on the same element, and a literal vector handler. `ui/spread`, dynamic prop maps, `ui/event`, and bare functions use ordinary batching and get the specified dev diagnostic when relevant.
- Preserve ordinary batching: run all queued write-side events to quiescence, commit each event's epoch, then advance dirty cells once and give React one host-checkpoint read/render batch. The controlled-input exception drains within the DOM event; it does not generalize `flushSync` or render once per epoch.

## Sequencing and ownership

Mike explicitly authorized S3 to advance conditionally while bounded S2 corrections continue. Start compiler/runtime/source and red-before-fix fixtures immediately. The current S2 root worker owns `spec/*`; do not edit `spec/*`, `deps.edn`, `shadow-cljs.edn`, or `.github/workflows/*` until the lead explicitly transfers the hot zone. Once cleared, add only the catalogue/schema/conformance deltas this slice requires. Do not commit `.beads/issues.jsonl`.

## Non-goals

This leaf does not implement `local`, `effect`, `dispatch-fn`, foreign callback forms, `.react/*`, presence, portals, resumability, or a generic DOM/gesture abstraction. It must not add a second scheduler, process monitor, fallback pull path, per-event render, or production-only diagnostic baggage.
acceptance_criteria:
- A browser fixture mounts a compiled native element, uses real `dispatchEvent`, and proves the exact committed frame/slot values and exact top-level `:rf.ui/value` / `:rf.ui/checked` / `:rf.ui/key` substitution reach the registered event.
- A commit-retarget fixture proves one stable callback object dispatches through the newest committed frame/slots, while an abandoned render cannot retarget it.
- Literal, normalized-branch, dynamic-vector, nil, and invalid dynamic-handler classifications have red-before-fix coverage; placeholder-looking keywords in runtime vectors remain ordinary arguments and warn only in dev.
- Unregistered literal event ids warn at render with stable site coordinates and lazy-registration caveat; registered ids do not warn; the warning and its evidence are absent from advanced production.
- A scheduling fixture queues multiple write-side events, observes one epoch per event, and proves exactly one dirty-cell advance/host read-render batch after drain quiescence.
- The controlled-input browser matrix proves the narrow sync predicate, and fallback cases remain normally batched with a useful diagnostic. Chromium coverage lands in this slice; WebKit/IME/caret/order/pre-paint G-8 completion may be the final gate leaf but cannot be replaced by jsdom-only proof.
- Existing S1 parity/JVM tree behavior and S2 ownership/HMR/root tests remain green; focused tests run before PR, full coverage runs in CI.
- Required Spec 009 catalogue/schema/conformance rows land after hot-zone transfer, without broad unrelated spec edits.

title: Fence failed-first-mount rollback until host teardown settlement
description:
## Correctness finding

The S2 root lifecycle shipped by PRs #5885/#5936 is still non-transactional on failed first mount. In `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/client.cljs` the failed-first-render rollback releases the exact root/container/prefix claim before invoking raw host cleanup. If that cleanup settles later or throws, an immediate same-id or different-id/same-container retry is admitted while the predecessor host root still owns the surface. This contradicts the ratified `:live -> :tearing-down -> :released` settlement law and rf2-vxgfnd.275/.277 acceptance criteria.

The remaining contract pass also exposed two coupled truth gaps: Spec 006 says all tearing-down reuse diagnostics carry `:existing {:tearing-down? true}`, but current `root-container-in-use` and `root-not-live` branches omit it; and Spec 006 says a tearing-down claim's ViewCells/leases are not yet released, which is false for the throwing-host path where framework ownership is deliberately force-dead while the host claim remains quarantined.

This is a follow-up to the already-merged partial work; do not amend the closed `.275` or treat merged #5936 as completion of open `.277`.

## Smallest correct design

Failed-first-mount rollback must enter the same exact-incarnation teardown transaction as every committed root: keep the claim, mark it `:tearing-down` before raw host cleanup, preserve the original mount error as primary, and release id/container/prefix only after host settlement. Because no committed reporter exists for this path, a normally returning cleanup may settle conservatively at the next FIFO microtask; a throwing cleanup remains fail-closed quarantined and is attached as secondary evidence. Preflight receipts and successor identity fencing remain authoritative.

Then finish `.277` atomically: exact diagnostic evidence, Spec 004C/006/009 lifecycle truth, public/internal docstrings, guide paragraph, and one narrow drift guard. No new lifecycle state, error id, public API, retry loop, compatibility shim, or general prose parser.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic red-before-fix fixture proves current main admits a retry before failed-first-mount host cleanup settles; the corrected implementation rejects same-id and different-id/same-container retries before any successor React allocation.
- Failed-first-mount rollback retains the exact id/container/prefix claim in `:tearing-down` until normally returning cleanup reaches the defined settlement checkpoint; after settlement, the same claim can be acquired and a predecessor cannot release or corrupt its successor.
- Cleanup throw preserves the original mount failure as primary, attaches `rfUiRollbackCleanupError` (or the existing canonical secondary channel), force-deads framework ownership, and leaves exact host ownership quarantined fail-closed; double cleanup/retry cannot reopen it.
- `duplicate-root-id`, `root-container-in-use`, and `root-not-live` emit their current IDs plus truthful conditional `:existing` tearing-down evidence; tests assert full ex-data for all three without adding an error ID.
- Spec 004C owns the complete `:live -> :tearing-down -> :released` lifecycle and edge-case/reuse table; Spec 006 distinguishes framework-unusable from host-settled and stops claiming all tearing-down cells remain live; Spec 009, API docs, guide, and docstrings agree.
- A focused drift guard pins the three states, three diagnostic IDs, and tearing-down evidence across the known implementation/004C/006/009 homes; mutation self-tests prove each axis can fail. It is not a general prose parser.
- Focused UI JVM/browser tests, full `npm run test:ui`/`npm run test:browser`, docs/link/spec-projection gates, and independent ownership-surface reread are green. Every correctness fixture is demonstrated red pre-fix and green post-fix; touched claims are diff-checked against shipped behavior.

title: Complete fixed spawn-all attempt identity and one-terminal projection
description:
PR #5990 (merged at exact head e7ca6d3c8014bc86bd4cb09d7024ff6b6bc6e95a, merge 5fc7658b654266ebb0dc77450d07fc1e4cefdc0a) made fixed :spawn-all attempts use the private join attempt in the canonical machine work-id. A post-merge independent audit found three untested counterexamples that leave the end-to-end invariant incomplete.

1. Numeric-suffixed fixed IDs still collapse. implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/reply.cljc parses every keyword ending in #<digits> as generated and canonical-spawn-generation prefers that suffix over the private attempt. The public InvokeAllChildSpec accepts any keyword as :fixed-actor-id, so sequential fixed attempts using :worker#7 both produce generation 7. The runtime must derive generated-vs-fixed provenance from runtime-owned spawn data, not actor-id spelling. Preserve generated <type>#n work generations and ordinary single-spawn behavior while giving every fixed join attempt its exact private discriminator.

2. A completed join child can receive a contradictory cancellation terminal. A non-decisive child first emits :completed/:failed from join.cljc. If the parent exits before the remaining children resolve, destroy-spawn-all-children!* tears down every child and the completed child's :rf.machine/destroyed row defaults to :explicit cancellation using the same work-id. Teardown must still happen, but an already-terminal child must be classified as post-terminal cleanup and must not publish a second cancelled terminal.

3. Xray does not close cancellation-only attempts. tools/xray reply-envelope projection does not map :rf.machine/destroyed, and races-by-work-id terminalizes completed/stale but not cancelled. The #5990 fixture forges a later stale carrier, which creates the attempt arc and masks the ordinary no-straggler cancellation case. A fixed attempt cancelled on parent exit, followed by a successful reuse, must appear as two distinct closed arcs without needing a stale arrival.

These are one end-to-end work-identity invariant: one attempt has one canonical work-id and exactly one terminal status, visible in Xray. Fix them together with causal pre-fix fixtures. Do not add a public compatibility layer, parse more identity from strings, or change the public event/destroy trace grammar.
design: Prefer explicit runtime provenance over actor-id parsing. The spawn/join seed already knows whether a child address was generated or fixed and owns the exact join attempt token; carry the canonical private discriminator from that authority into completion, stale, destroy, and cancellation reply construction. For a terminal child torn down during pre-resolution parent exit, reuse the existing non-cancellation post-terminal-cleanup semantics rather than inventing a second public terminal. Extend Xray only at the canonical reply projection: :rf.machine/destroyed with cancelled reply facts closes the row; :cancel-requested remains nonterminal.
acceptance_criteria:
- A CLJ+CLJS red fixture runs sequential :spawn-all attempts with an explicit numeric-suffixed :fixed-actor-id such as :worker#7 under the same parent/invoke path and proves distinct canonical work-ids; both platforms agree.
- The implementation carries runtime-owned generated/fixed provenance (or an equivalently explicit private work discriminator) so generated <type>#n children retain their established suffix generation, fixed children use exact attempt identity, ordinary single :spawn remains unchanged, and no decision depends on keyword spelling.
- A parent exits after one non-decisive child has completed/failed but before join resolution. That child is torn down without a second cancelled reply; each child attempt has exactly one terminal status. A mutation that restores default :explicit cancellation for the already-terminal child fails.
- A cancellation-only fixed attempt A (no late/stale carrier) followed by successful fixed attempt B yields two distinct, closed Xray arcs: A cancelled and B completed. Xray consumes the canonical destroyed cancellation reply and terminalizes cancelled status without treating cancel-requested alone as completion.
- Existing generated-id, suffix-free fixed-id, stale/superseded, survivor-cancellation, destroy, reply-envelope, work-ledger, and Xray fixtures remain green in CLJ and CLJS; the focused browser/Xray gate is green.
- Public event vectors, public destroy grammar, and canonical work-id arity remain unchanged; no compatibility shim or string-grammar restriction is introduced.

Exact-head CI: 49 success, 13 intentional skips, zero pending/fail; full machines/Xray/CLJS/browser green; one-attempt/one-terminal and Xray suppression semantics complete.

title: Make the Form-3 lifecycle migration recipe executable and frame-exact
description:
Merged PR #5898 at exact authored head cf858710839b1a7f7a1bc7f27d7d038774b03d94 closes the Form-3 migration bead, but its lifecycle subscription escape hatch is non-executable and the behavioral proof explicitly remains deferred.

The new text correctly says Reagent lifecycle hooks run after frame resolver scope unwinds, then recommends bare (rf/subscribe-once query-v) in did-mount and pairs rare @(subscribe ...) with bare (rf/unsubscribe query-v) in will-unmount. Both bare calls require ambient frame context and raise :rf.error/no-frame-context there; failed unsubscription retains the cache reference. capture-frame supplies :frame and :subscribe, not bound subscribe-once/unsubscribe. The honest recipe must retain the captured frame and use (rf/subscribe-once query-v {:frame frame}) plus (rf/unsubscribe frame query-v).

The PR is docs-only and every CLJS/browser check was skipped, despite closed rf2-vxgfnd.272 requiring a real frozen-stock-Reagent matrix: outer-factory capture across render/hooks, isolated instances, lifecycle negative controls, subscription refcount cleanup, provider retargeting, singleton migration and a drift guard. The adapter README still says capture merely during render and claims frameless callbacks silently route to :rf/default, contradicting loud no-frame-context behavior.

Complete the existing migration recipe and one compact browser/drift proof. Do not introduce mutable capture, compatibility machinery, another Form-3 abstraction, or broaden the frozen tier.

- The recipe destructures/captures :frame with non-reactive operations. did-mount one-shot reads use subscribe-once with {:frame frame}; imperative subscribe cleanup uses unsubscribe with explicit frame-id first.

title: Fence flow replacement and clear trace pipelines to exact incarnation
description:
Merged PR #5897 at exact authored head 945f6e2fab62f5d23a7718ceca880335bc3c13ce makes clear/registration app-db vacation and epoch writes exact, but replacement and clear lifecycle traces leave exact ownership before their callback-bearing pipelines complete.

Replacement dedup and :rf.registry/handler-replaced emission run after a point-in-time liveness check without trace/call-with-continuation-predicate. :rf.flow/cleared is emitted after the serialized drain section has released and no longer carries the pinned token. Trace emission itself performs frame-policy lookup, classification projection, epoch capture, ring retention and ordered listener delivery; those internal fences work only when an exact continuation predicate is bound. A successor B can therefore be published before clear emission begins, or during a replacement trace callback, and receive A's policy/ring/capture/listener effects.

The new loss fixtures assert frame/flow/cache/epoch/declaration state but record no trace evidence or dedup-policy consultation. They also remain green if only the first post-vacation check is removed because the later exact mark and second check stop visible writes. Thus the test does not prove the source bead's trace-byte-identity or the claimed immediate stop.

Emit clear evidence inside exact-owner serialization and wrap direct replacement/clear lifecycle traces in the existing continuation-predicate mechanism. Preserve the approved rule: an already-entered callback may unwind, but every later framework-owned trace stage is fenced. Open rf2-pwum1g owns first registration and is in progress; do not amend or duplicate it. Decide causally whether the first post-vacation check is load-bearing—prove its call-boundary effect or remove the redundant check/comment. No rollback or new trace path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Direct replacement and clear fixtures install multiple ordered trace stages/listeners, then replace A with same-ID B between clear unlock/emission and during policy/classification/capture/ring/listener delivery.
- An already-entered callback may complete once. No later A policy lookup, dedup action, projection, epoch capture, ring retention or listener delivery reaches B; B's policy, trace ring/capture, frame/flow state and evidence remain byte-identical.
- B's subsequent independent registration/replacement/clear evidence emits exactly once.
- Clear evidence is initiated while exact-owner serialization/token is still authoritative; replacement and clear use trace/call-with-continuation-predicate. Coordinate, but do not overlap, the first-registration fix in rf2-pwum1g.
- The fixtures record trace/dedup consultation, not only app-db/cache state. Moving emission outside serialization or removing the wrapper makes them fail.
- Removing only the immediate post-vacation check either fails a focused no-stale-call assertion (if retained) or the redundant check and its claim are removed. Downstream exact fences remain explicit.
- CLJ and CLJS exercise replacement and clear. No rollback, public incarnation data, second trace implementation, or compatibility path is added.

title: Complete the spawn-all schema and make its catalogue proof authoritative
description:

title: Make Xray ViewCell evidence ownership exact, reactive, and lifecycle-complete
description:
Merged PR #5893 at exact authored head 27076f2efa5567708810e12e628a6187053fd66c fences Xray evidence reads by comparing a logical owner ID, but owner equality is not exact-incarnation ownership and the surrounding reactive/reset integration can retain stale evidence.

The evidence tier's uninstall! accepts only owner-id, and Xray installed?/rows compare only that reusable key. After ownership span A closes and span B reclaims the same :rf.xray/viewcell-evidence ID, an A-era reader is accepted as B and an A-era teardown can uninstall B. The authored ABA test uses different IDs for stale uninstall, so it misses same-key reuse.

Even for different owners, rows checks ownership only when it executes. :rf.xray/viewcell-evidence caches that result behind epoch-history alone; uninstall changes ownership without changing that reactive input. A live subscription and rendered panel can therefore keep A's row after Xray uninstalls and a foreign owner takes the slot, until an unrelated epoch pump. Finally, core/init! now installs this foundation owner, but canonical reset-all!/reset-runtime! omit owner-checked uninstall. The bespoke new fixture force-releases it, hiding cross-test/global sentinel leakage. Core/manual launch docs also still enumerate the old foundation sequence.

Give the evidence tier one opaque ownership-span receipt: same-span HMR re-arm preserves it; close/reclaim mints a new one; authorized read and release compare receipt/generation atomically. Make ownership revision a reactive input to the single derived subscription while retaining the final computation-time receipt fence. Integrate owner-checked teardown into the full clean-slate reset tier and reconcile the existing launch descriptions. Do not add a second registry, polling, or a public general lifecycle system.
acceptance_criteria:
- Acquire span A and retain its reader/release receipt; close A; reclaim the same logical ID as B and publish a real B row. A reads no B data and A release cannot clear B's owner, sink, entries, sentinel or later delivery.
- Same-span HMR re-arm preserves the receipt and valid in-flight evidence; close/reclaim changes it. installed-owner remains diagnostic-only.
- Hold a live :rf.xray/viewcell-evidence subscription and rendered panel after a non-empty A read. Uninstall A and optionally install a foreign owner; the same subscription/panel becomes empty immediately without an epoch-history pump.
- Ownership revision participates only in this reactive query; final computation still checks exact receipt so cache invalidation cannot authorize a stale reader.
- core/init! followed by canonical reset-all!/reset-runtime! leaves owner, sink, rows, retained entries and sentinel at baseline. A foreign registration survives owner-checked reset.
- Spec/API/launch and source descriptions remove fragile foundation counts and place evidence acquisition/release accurately for preload and manual init, including foreign-owner rejection/load inertness.
- Same-key ABA, cached-uninstall, canonical-reset and HMR controls run in the real Xray/CLJS surface. Reverting receipt checks to owner equality or removing ownership reactivity/reset cleanup makes them fail.
- No polling, parallel registry, compatibility shim, or production ViewCell retention is added; existing production elision remains green.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5915 (commit 1468d7a1601c7bd5eba690e867f5b5315b24c850, branch worker/xray-evidence-286). Exact (per-span receipt) + reactive (ownership-revision app-db input) + lifecycle-complete (owner-checked reset tier). Full xray CLJS suite green (3253 tests / 13760 assertions, 0 failures); exactness red-before-fix reproduced+reverted. implementation/ untouched. Left OPEN for review/merge.

title: Make delayed-silence lineage exact, linearizable, and bounded
description:
Merged PR #5892 at exact authored head e95d4b46dff5c3029c9feada982318bd50966f2b improves delayed silencing by recording callback generation, but snapshot, eligibility, publication and retention are still split across non-linearizable reads/writes.

First, snapshot-terminal-destroy-evidence! validates generation G through cbs-observing-frame, then re-reads listeners to build cb-id->generation. Replacement between those operations records fresh H as having observed A. Second, on-frame-destroyed! snapshots live observers once, then for each identity separately checks delayed-silence-owed?, emits externally, and only afterward records the terminal mark. Two destroy publishers can both pass before either mark; a trace listener for U can re-arm V on successor B while A still uses the stale pre-loop observer set; and callback replacement between predicate and emit can inherit an unqualified silence it never observed.

Finally, terminal-silence-marks grows one [frame-id cb-id] tombstone for every unique destroyed frame until that same ID/callback is reused or individually removed. A persistent Xray callback therefore retains unbounded lineage. reset-listeners! claims to clear observation bookkeeping but leaves marks, while reset-frame-silences! recycles the supposedly monotonic sequence and can make a post-reset successor mark compare below an outstanding predecessor baseline.

Implement one small delayed-silence state machine: capture validated generation/evidence in one state operation; atomically claim per-identity publication by rechecking current generation, current live observations and existing lineage before external delivery; and retain lineage only while outstanding predecessor evidence can consume it. Roll back a reservation only if envelope delivery itself fails. Do not introduce a scheduler, public generation field, or general transaction framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Snapshot evidence returns the exact cb-id->generation map validated against the same listener/observation snapshot. Replacing G with H between the former two reads leaves evidence at G and never emits A silence for H.
- Two overlapping same-ID predecessor/successor terminal hooks synchronize immediately before publication; exactly one publisher atomically claims the signal.
- A synchronous trace listener re-arms remaining identities on B during the first A silence. Every later identity is rechecked and receives no stale A projection, ring entry, or delivery.
- Callback replacement between eligibility and delivery cannot inherit an unqualified prior-generation silence. Already-entered external delivery/error behavior remains contained and deterministic.
- One persistent callback observes and destroys thousands of unique frame IDs; after terminal evidence settles, lineage storage returns to a constant baseline. Held predecessor evidence keeps only the marks it still needs and they are reclaimed afterward.
- clear/reset removes callback lineage coherently and never recycles the monotonic comparison domain while outstanding evidence survives.
- CLJ concurrent and CLJS synchronous/reentrant fixtures cover the claim seam. Mutations restoring snapshot reread, predicate->emit->mark, stale observer reuse, or permanent tombstones fail.
- No public API, scheduler, polling loop, or generalized transactional subsystem is added.
notes:
PR opened (leave open, do not merge): https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5914 (SHA 4e11b99810). Gap RE-VERIFIED still open against origin/main after #5892/.265: snapshot re-read tear, non-linearizable predicate->emit->mark publish loop, and unbounded terminal-silence-marks all present. Fix: (EXACT) single-read stamp-based snapshot-terminal-observers; (LINEARIZABLE) atomic claim-delayed-silence!/rollback under silence-lock + deterministic fan order; (BOUNDED) per-frame open/close-silence-lineage! bracket + reset-listeners! clears + seq never recycled. Gates green: epoch JVM 402, core JVM 1984, CLJS node 9410; all fixtures red-before-fix (6 mutations verified). Spec 009/Tool-Pair silencing-lineage prose noted as PR-body follow-up (spec/** fenced).
CI elision fix (force-pushed, new SHA 5c6e4b6aba): PR #5914's 'CLJS production elision' gate went red — my on-frame-destroyed! rewrite used a compound gate (when (and interop/debug-enabled? terminal-evidence) ...) which defeats the sole-condition debug-enabled? DCE idiom, so emit-snapshotted+outcome!'s 'rf.epoch/outcome' dev sentinel survived :advanced+goog.DEBUG=false. Fix: nest the nil-check inside the sole-condition gate — (when interop/debug-enabled? (when terminal-evidence ...)); semantically identical, restores DCE. Verified locally: test:elision PASS (production 52/52 absent, control 52/52 present); epoch JVM 402 still green. No logic change to the exact/linearizable/bounded fix.
close_reason: Merged PR #5914 (delayed-silence lineage exact/linearizable/bounded: EXACT via snapshot-terminal-observers deriving {cb->generation} from ONE consistent (listeners,observed) read using the observation stamp; LINEARIZABLE via claim-delayed-silence! atomic eligibility-recheck+monotonic mark reservation under silence-lock before external delivery, deterministic cb-id fan order, rollback on delivery throw; BOUNDED via per-frame outstanding-predecessor counter reclaiming marks + reset clears lineage, seq never recycled; preserved halted-record/compare-owned cleanup; 6-mutation red-before-fix; ALSO fixed real elision leak — (and debug-enabled? x) compound gate defeated sole-condition DCE, dev sentinel survived :advanced, fixed by nesting; CI green)

title: Complete the JVM slice-memo lifetime contract and causal isolation proof
description:
Merged PR #5891 at exact authored head f03c292af3d21ad955ce282069bcfb72d6c5a6ff implements the JVM slice-memo lifetime correctly, but closes its source bead while the authoritative contract still describes a different host mechanism and one concurrency claim remains non-causal.

Spec 006 and synthesis 03 unconditionally say the slice table is held in a module holder and cleared by queueMicrotask. The implementation now deliberately uses a re-entrant dynamic/thread-local JVM render scope discarded synchronously when the render returns; only CLJS uses the module holder/microtask checkpoint. The common semantic law is that no table survives into a later slice. This documentation reconciliation was an explicit acceptance criterion of closed rf2-vxgfnd.267 and has no live owner.

The new concurrent-render fixture synchronizes only before ui.test/render and asserts parent-runs=2. It does not force overlap at memo acquisition or observe handle identity. A faulty process-global handle reset at each render entry can pass depending on scheduling. Production code is correct, but the claimed isolation proof is false-green.

Perform one compact completion pass: reconcile the two authoritative texts and strengthen the existing JVM fixture with an internal-only identity witness. Do not change the runtime design or add a public memo token.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 006 and synthesis 03 explicitly distinguish JVM's re-entrant dynamic/thread-local render scope discarded on return from CLJS's module holder cleared at the microtask checkpoint.
- Both documents state the shared semantic law: within-slice sharing is allowed, but no table or handle remains reusable by a later render slice.
- A narrow wording census fails while either document applies queueMicrotask lifetime to the JVM or omits the common law.
- The concurrent JVM fixture deterministically observes distinct memo-handle identity per independent top-level render (for example by wrapping make-slice-memo in the test) and forces overlap at acquisition/probe, rather than inferring identity from aggregate recomputation count.
- Replacing the two dynamic scopes with one shared/reset global handle fails deterministically; sequential-thread reuse, within-render sharing, nested re-entry, and bare-probe controls remain green.
- Production reactive code and the frozen public API remain unchanged unless the stronger fixture reveals a real defect.
