title: Correct Form-3 capture placement and no-frame migration recipes
description:
## Problem

PR #5869 (head b6bc0259a9fff87aad92e9229f6fd3b5fc8abeca) closed the no-frame documentation sweep while leaving recipes that still fail at runtime.

`skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md` and `guided-handlers-state.md` present a captured zero-arity `(rf/capture-frame)` as a repair for a scope-less plain function, directly contradicting the adjacent statement that it re-raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`. The Form-3 guidance is worse: it permits capture inside render/lifecycle hooks. Reagent lifecycle callbacks run after the resolver scope has unwound, so capture in component-did-mount/unmount throws. The correct stateful shape captures once in the live `reg-view*` outer callable before constructing `create-class`, then closes that locked handle over render and lifecycle callbacks.

Several changed passages also say zero-arity capture works only in registered render or synchronous `with-frame`. That is falsely exhaustive: router handlers and other standard handler/effect/test/SSR lexical bindings legitimately resolve a frame. The rule should be resolver-based, with view examples, not a brittle whitelist.

## Smallest correction

Correct the skill, migration guide and mirrored active guidance in one bounded sweep. Use explicit-id/explicit-frame/passed-in bundles for scope-less code; mention zero-arity capture only where the standard resolver is live. Do not add runtime or adapter compatibility machinery.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every scope-less M-11 repair spells explicit-id capture, explicit {:frame ...}, or a frame-locked value passed from a frame-aware ancestor.
- Form-3 captures once in the live reg-view* outer callable before create-class and shares that handle with render/lifecycle callbacks; no recipe captures zero-arity inside lifecycle hooks.
- Wording says zero-arity capture succeeds wherever the standard resolver currently yields a frame; registered render and with-frame are examples, while handler/effect/test/SSR scopes remain legitimate.
- The migration drift guard and self-test reject a no-arg capture presented as a scope-less/plain-function repair.
- A frozen-stock-Reagent browser fixture under provider A proves did-mount/unmount work through the outer-captured handle; moving capture into either lifecycle callback fails with :rf.error/no-frame-context.
- Existing rf2-vxgfnd.236 retains ownership of the separate plain-function boundary matrix; no UIx/Helix/slim additions.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5882 (SHA 4770268dd1) — Form-3 capture moved to reg-view* outer callable + resolver-based no-frame recipes. Hot-zone follow-up: migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:478 same falsely-exhaustive whitelist. Out-of-scope (docs-only): drift-guard rule for no-arg-capture-as-scope-less-repair; browser fixture owned by rf2-vxgfnd.236.
close_reason: Merged PR #5882 (Form-3 capture placement: capture once in the live reg-view* outer callable before create-class, close the locked handle over render+lifecycle hooks — lifecycle callbacks fire after resolver scope unwinds; no-frame migration recipe tightened to ratified carried-targeting spelling; hot-zone README:478 whitelist flagged as follow-up; CI green)

title: Stop structural trace-delivery scope from tainting listener-triggered work
description:
## Problem

PR #5865 (head 649a8e9d380dfcbfb5e2dbbd4bc8a925d33fb2b0) binds structural delivery flags, including ring-retention=false, around the entire synchronous outer trace emit. Public tooling listeners are invoked before that dynamic scope unwinds. Spec 009 explicitly makes listener invocation synchronous and does not forbid dispatch or nested emission.

A listener reacting to A's structural terminal fact can dispatch legitimate work into same-id successor B or unrelated frame C. That work commits and streams live, but all nested events inherit retentionless scope; they also bypass their own epoch capture and frame no-emit policy. Exact-head reproduction produced seven live nested events and an empty C trace ring. Merged fixtures use passive atom listeners and miss the callback scope.

## Smallest correction

Make structural flags properties of the current outer envelope, not ambient authority for external callbacks. Capture the outer retain? decision, restore ordinary delivery defaults while invoking public tooling listeners, and pass captured retain? explicitly for the outer ring push. An explicitly nested structural delivery must still be able to request structural semantics. Avoid a scheduler or second event bus.
acceptance_criteria:
- CLJ and synchronous CLJS use a real structural terminal fact and a public listener that dispatches into unrelated C plus same-id B control.
- A's structural fact reaches listeners once and is never retained in A/B rings.
- Nested legitimate B/C work obeys its own no-emit policy, epoch capture and normal ring retention.
- Direct nested public emit! has the same isolation.
- Explicitly nested call-with-structural-delivery remains retentionless.
- Restoring ambient structural bindings during listener fan-out makes the fixtures fail; no scheduler/API is added.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5872 (fix in trace.cljc deliver! — restore ordinary delivery defaults around the tooling listener fan-out; outer ring push keeps captured retain?). Red-before-fix fixtures: structural_retention_cljs_test (sync direct nested emit!) + frame_destroy_incarnation_jvm_test (dispatching listener into unrelated C + no-emit D). Repro re-verified RED on fresh origin/main. Left open for mayor.
close_reason: Merged PR #5872 (structural-delivery scope no longer taints listener-triggered work: deliver! restores ordinary delivery defaults around the tooling fan-out; dispatching-listener fixtures — the case passive-atom fixtures missed; CI 53/0/0)

title: Run G-13 mutation teeth against real code with same-optimizer controls
description:
## Problem

PR #5860 (head f375f4bf45bcc7732fd637cdc49e1b8b28e7c2bf) advertises source-level mutation teeth, but per-write flushing, V-wide enrollment, stable-parent fan-out and multiple commits are simulated by editing an already-successful JSON result. Those tests prove only that the validator rejects bad reports; real mutated runtime code never executes.

The new counter/Profiler/debug sentinels also use a :none development bundle as their only positive control, while the negative production bundle is :advanced/goog.DEBUG=false. A sentinel definition can survive :none even when its owning call was DCE-disconnected, so later instrumentation leakage may become unmarked and pass the negative scan. The only advanced positive control covers a different owner-mint sentinel.

## Smallest correction

Add a bounded gate-local source-mutation runner with guarded exact anchors and one production-equivalent advanced positive-control build that independently proves each owning branch reachable. Keep JSON edits as validator unit tests. Do not build a general mutation framework or ship runtime instrumentation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Real mutants execute through dispatch, observation, ViewCells/uSES, React and the normal validator for per-write read flushing, V-wide enrollment, stable-parent notification and multiple commit batches; each independently exits red.
- Production-equivalent :advanced/goog.DEBUG=false controls force counter, Profiler and debug-evidence owners reachable and prove each sentinel survives when its owner is present.
- Disconnecting each witness while retaining its owner, and leaking each owner into production, both make the gate fail.
- Existing JSON tampering is labelled validator-only.
- Normal C=8/Q=8 one-read/render-batch semantics and G-13 bundle elision stay green; no public API or broad mutation system.

NOT addressed by PR #5888 (that PR is .255 only). BLOCKED in shadow-prov-255's scope: (1) #5870-audit obligations (mutate membership/owner-selection seam; close reactive/current-live-cells bypass of the candidate witness; same-optimizer reachability/elision proof for the candidate-iteration witness RF2_G13_PORT_CANDIDATE_SENTINEL) require editing ui/reactive.cljc + core/substrate/observation.cljc — fenced off this worker; (2) the in-scope portion (real gate-local source-mutation runner over the g13 fixture + advanced same-optimizer positive controls for counter/Profiler/debug-evidence owners in fixture.cljs + assert :candidate-work-projection/:proof-scope + relabel JSON teeth validator-only) is only validatable via the full heavy G-13 browser+compile gate, reserved for CI, and a multi-build real-mutant runner exceeds the one-targeted-build allowance. NOTE dev.cljs ALREADY emits :candidate-work-projection + :proof-scope; run-ui-g13.cjs ignores them (in-scope gap). RECOMMEND: re-dispatch solo now that .182/observation PRs merged (surfaces free), browser-gate-authorized.

title: Replace timestamp inference with exact per-pass Shadow compile provenance
description:
## Problem

PR #5864 (head c250bdf10b427714913ba5e023f64a6b34e62fb3) infers final-schedule membership with `compiled-at >= pass-start`, where both values are millisecond System/currentTimeMillis stamps. A retained warm-cache output B from the immediately preceding pass can have old compiled-at T while the next prepare records pass-start T. B is then falsely classified as compiled in the current pass. Because no macro ran for B, final reconciliation treats B as touched with no staged declaration and evicts its accepted defview rows, silently changing view authority and the whole-build digest.

Changing >= to > is not a fix: a genuine compile can also stamp in the same millisecond, reopening the ghost-row false negative. The test forces true compile to pass-start+1 and gives retained B no stamp, excluding the collision.

## Smallest correction

Use unambiguous per-pass compile provenance from final Shadow build state, or fail loud when unavailable. Do not use sleeps or wall-clock ordering as membership authority. Preserve prepare pre-touch needed for cross-file conflict detection.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deterministic fixture: accepted A+B, retained warm B has stamp exactly equal to next pass start, only A truly recompiles; B remains accepted and digest-stable for B.
- Companion same-millisecond true-compile removes a final defview and is reconciled/evicted correctly.
- Both cases run in sequential and parallel modes alongside ordinary warm-cache and later-hook forced-recompile controls.
- Missing/unobservable final provenance fails loudly rather than assuming an empty schedule.
- Restoring timestamp-only membership makes the fixture fail; existing digest/HMR gates remain green.
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5888 — replaced timestamp inference (compiled-at >= pass-start) with exact per-pass output-object identity provenance in build_hook.clj; snapshot :pass-output at prepare, identical? at finish; fail-loud on missing provenance. Fixtures red-before-fix (collision + fail-loud), 54/217 green. Left OPEN for mayor to close on merge.
close_reason: Merged PR #5888 (replace timestamp inference with exact per-pass Shadow compile provenance in build_hook; re-verified vs #5880/.237; red-before-fix; CI green)

title: Bind observation emission provenance to the exact throwable
description:
## Problem

PR #5861 (head f9a5af906627a649a0d8a9778cba38360223ad08) calls EmissionProvenance opaque and unforgeable, but it is a public deftype. CLJ and CLJS generate the callable cross-namespace ->EmissionProvenance constructor, and source-covered-always-on? trusts any instance containing :always-on. An application callback can therefore construct a passing token under the known ex-data key and suppress :rf.error/observation-on-change-failed.

Even hiding the constructor is insufficient. Authentic provenance is carried in public exception data and is not bound to the exact Throwable, so an app can copy a token from a caught read-after-release error into an unrelated exception. Both cases make the drain emit nothing; registrar/next-tick boundaries then swallow the rethrow, restoring production silence. The merged spoof fixture tries only a Boolean and map reconstruction.

## Smallest correction

Authenticate channel coverage for the exact throwable identity through a private construction/verification seam. A throwable-bound private verifier or weak identity association is acceptable; no global dedupe registry, new error category, or public API.
acceptance_criteria:
- CLJ and CLJS fixtures forge via the generated constructor; the fresh callback failure still produces exactly one stable wrapper.
- A token transplanted from an authentic caught framework throwable cannot suppress an unrelated exception.
- Re-throwing the exact legitimately emitted throwable remains exact-once with original source attribution.
- HMR and disposed drains both preserve sibling drain and first-original-escape identity.
- Replacing exact-throwable authentication with instance?/channel membership makes the tests fail.
- Coordinate the separate Spec/schema slice with rf2-xakb4p; this bead changes runtime/tests only.
notes: PR opened (do not merge; left for mayor): https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5875 — commit 60f7bd4d7b. Re-verified: the gap STILL reproduced against current origin/main observation.cljc (post-#5861/#5870). rf2-w55bh0 carried the EmissionProvenance token in public ex-data + trusted instance?; two live spoof vectors remained (generated-constructor forge + authentic-token transplant), both suppressing the always-on :rf.error/observation-on-change-failed record. Fix: bound provenance to the EXACT throwable via a private weak identity map (WeakHashMap/js/WeakMap keyed by throwable object), written only by attest-provenance!, read by source-covered-always-on!; provenance left public ex-data entirely. No schema/009 touch needed (rf2-xakb4p owns the spec slice). Red-before-fix fixture: disposed-drain-binds-emission-provenance-to-the-exact-throwable (proven 4-failure red vs pre-fix source, green after). Gates green: core JVM 1962t, ui 492t, CLJS 9355t, fast-pr spine PASS.

title: Fence first-time flow registration evidence after exact ownership loss
description:
## Problem

PR #5859 (head 3781640f3d2d14d385c1e589bac03771de30056a) fences replacement registration tails, but first-time :rf.flow/registered is emitted outside the exact-owner continuation. A first-time flow with output marks can reach a callback-bearing runtime-db write; a synchronous container callback destroys A and publishes same-id B. The exact write correctly reports ownership loss, but prior-on-frame is nil, so the outer first-registration trace still fires after the terminal fence.

The stale event has no incarnation discriminator and can consult B's current trace policy/capture and synchronously notify tooling after A is gone. The merged fixture exercises only replacement (prior non-nil), so it cannot reach this branch. Closed rf2-vxgfnd.155 explicitly required later traces fenced and B evidence unchanged.

## Smallest correction

Keep first-registration evidence inside the same exact-owner continuation, or return one internal completed-for-owner? fact from the serialized body. Do not add rollback, a second trace model, or compatibility handling.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic first-time marked-flow fixture replaces A with B synchronously during the mark write.
- After loss, zero A :rf.flow/registered deliveries occur, B state/token/trace evidence remain byte-identical, and B trace policy is not consulted for A.
- An ordinary first registration retaining A emits exactly once.
- Cover direct reg-flow and the reserved effect only if they use distinct continuation plumbing.
- Removing the final exact-owner condition makes the fixture fail; flow suites pass.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5879 (SHA 4b6599f348). Fix: moved first-time :rf.flow/registered emit INSIDE reg-flow's terminal exact-owner postcheck (registry.cljc) so a container watch that destroys A during the first-time output-mark write withholds A's registration evidence from same-id successor B — mirrors clear-flow's cleared-path fence. No core hook needed (frame.cljc untouched). Red-before-fix fixture flows_first_registration_watch_incarnation_test.clj. Gates green: flows 225t, core 1967t, cljs 9358t. Left OPEN for mayor to merge.
close_reason: Merged PR #5879 (fence first-time flow registration evidence to exact incarnation — first-time registration after owner-incarnation loss no longer publishes evidence against a successor; red-before-fix; CI 37/0)

title: Finish the frame-root/provider split in tracked synthesis and implementor guidance
description:
## Problem

PR #5858 (head 062726ae6dde13e54083746577bf7d5b882c1bb9) closed the frame-root/frame-provider reconciliation while excluding material it described as local-only. That premise is false: ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis is force-tracked and authoritative until S7. Active tracked guidance still teaches the retired merged provider or omits frozen Reagent frame-root.

Affected active surfaces include the implementor skill phase-2 ordering; synthesis README and 03 reactivity/ownership; reagent compatibility and Spec-004A drafts/tables; the Spec-004 rewrite draft; and W9 CI disposition. These passages can cause an implementer to ship frame-provider {:id} (which now throws), wait on an already-landed gate, or delete/fail to test the frozen frame-root export. Closed rf2-kopcit only fixed UIx/Helix adapter docstrings/tests and is not this owner.

## Smallest correction

title: Make every ambient sub/lease ViewCell a real frame-context consumer
description:
## Problem

PR #5857 (head 0b29b86334d577b090da08257e2be8995647ab20) makes frame-only views consume React frame context, but production sub-only, lease-only, and sub+lease wrappers still do not call use-frame-context!. This is incorrect because subscription target resolution and every lease site implicitly capture the ambient frame/incarnation.

Counterexample: mount an empty-props sub-only view under provider A, then retarget the provider to B with rf=-equal props. React.memo can bail the non-context-consumer, leaving the ViewCell subscribed to A; B never paints or invalidates it. A lease-only view likewise retains A's resource owner and never ensures B. DEV masks the defect because render-dev always consumes context. Existing production coverage includes frame-only and frame+sub, not the implicit sub/lease cases.

## Smallest correction

Treat every sub or lease site as an ambient-frame dependency until an explicit immutable pin exists. Make the base sub/lease/combined production wrappers consume the shared context once. Retain the direct path for truly inert views; simplify redundant *-frame variants if that yields the clearest wrapper taxonomy.
acceptance_criteria:
- Advanced/goog.DEBUG=false mounted tests retarget A -> B with unchanged props for sub-only, lease-only, and sub+lease views.
- Sub-only immediately paints B and detaches A.
- Lease-only ensures B and releases A exactly once in the correct ownership order.
- Same-provider renders add no redundant work; genuinely inert views stay on the direct path.
- Removing context consumption from any ambient reactive wrapper makes its fixture fail.
- Production economics and bundle-elision gates remain green; no API addition.

title: Preserve reserved dispatch semantics while transporting recordable join authority
description:
## Problem

PR #5856 transports join authority by rewriting ordinary :dispatch and :dispatch-later effects to :rf.machine/join-dispatch. The new effect constructs a partial child options map and uses a raw timeout. It therefore bypasses established reserved-dispatch semantics: :fx-overrides cannot capture the completion, interceptor overrides/trace-id/origin are lost, per-call strict coeffect mint policy can fall back to live minting, and delayed work bypasses frame-owned timer cancellation and source-detail behavior.

The replay fixture manually reconstructs and redispatches a final event. It never records an actual child completion, restores pre-event state, or drives strict replay through the new transport. The ambiguous selection proof is JVM-only and omits wrong-invoke, wrong-spawned-id, unstamped, and unknown-child controls in the parallel shape.

## Smallest correction

Preserve ordinary reserved :dispatch/:dispatch-later behavior and lift the private recordable join authority into the child at the existing queueing seam. Prefer one core child-dispatch implementation over duplicating override, lineage, ordering, timer, and replay semantics in a second effect. Keep the authority private and serializable; do not add public API.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real join-child completion is intercepted by a documented :dispatch capture override; interceptor overrides, trace-id, origin and source lineage propagate unchanged.
- Per-call :rf.cofx/mint-policy :strict propagates and rejects a missing recorded fact rather than live-minting.
- Positive delay uses the normal frame-owned timer table and is cancelled on frame destruction; same-id B receives no stale completion.
- Actual completion record -> EDN roundtrip -> restore -> strict replay produces the same resolution/evidence.
- CLJ and CLJS cover legitimate success/failure plus wrong-invoke, wrong-spawned-id, unstamped and unknown-child selection in an ambiguous parallel join.
- Mutations restoring the partial join-dispatch options or raw timeout fail.
notes:
REMAINDER from PR #5873 (machines-tails worker): fix genuinely needs core/fx.cljc — parent-envelope inheritance (child-dispatch-opts) + frame-owned dispatch-later timer table (arm-dispatch-later!/dispatch-later-timers/release-frame!) are PRIVATE to core/fx.cljc; :rf.machine/join-dispatch is a plain reg-fx that never gets the parent envelope. Core shape needed: one shared child-dispatch! in core/fx + a thin reserved :rf.machine/join-dispatch handler. router.cljc likely needs no change (build-envelope already merges supplied :rf.cofx). Fixture work to land WITH the core fix: real-completion strict-replay + wrong-invoke/wrong-spawned-id/unstamped/unknown-child parallel controls. REDISPATCH to a core/fx.cljc-scoped worker (fx.cljc is free now).
PR #5881 opened: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5881 (SHA 40b7396477). Core fix: expose shared re-frame.fx/child-dispatch! (the reserved :dispatch/:dispatch-later seam); :rf.machine/join-dispatch is now a thin handler routing through it (reads emitting child's :envelope from fx ctx), preserving :fx-overrides/:interceptor-overrides/:trace-id/:origin/:rf.cofx-mint-policy inheritance + frame-owned dispatch-later timer cancellation + :source-detail, while still recording :rf.machine/join-auth. router.cljc unchanged (build-envelope already merges supplied :rf.cofx; do-fx already threads parent envelope as :envelope). Fixtures: join_reserved_dispatch_semantics_test.clj (crit 1-4, 6 inheritance/timer assertions RED before fix) + join_parallel_recordable_controls_cljs_test.cljc (crit 5, parallel controls via recordable cofx). Gates green: core JVM 1967t, machines JVM 1053t, CLJS node 9364t, full fast-pr spine PASS. Left OPEN for mayor to merge.

title: Fence machine spawn and finalization tails after every callback boundary
description:
## Problem

PR #5856 (head bb65b8f1439f5389918d1ee472a7c76ca2bbfae1) adds exact-incarnation fences, but framework-owned tails still cross later callback boundaries.

In spawn.cljc, a system-id-collision listener can destroy A and publish same-id B. install-spawn! skips its swap, yet its caller ignores that outcome and still writes classification/spawn order and emits lifecycle-spawned against B. Replacement from system-id-bound has the same shape. In finalize.cljc, ownership is checked before machine-destroyed, but no fresh fence protects later HTTP/timer cancellation, classification/order removal, system-id release, registrar unregister, and on-error dispatch. machine-destroyed, system-id-released, or late abort hooks can therefore publish B and let A's tail mutate B.

This violates closed rf2-3evq0x's terminal-fence rule. Existing fixtures cover earlier callbacks only.

## Smallest correction

Return an explicit committed/live result from install-spawn! and run no caller tail unless it remains exact-owner current. In completion teardown, recheck after every callback-bearing trace or hook before the next framework action. Preserve already-delivered callbacks and the approved unwind posture; do not add rollback or a transaction framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deterministic fixtures replace A with same-id B from system-id-collision, system-id-bound, lifecycle-spawned, machine-destroyed, system-id-released, and one late-bound teardown hook.
- After each loss, B's runtime, registrar, classification, spawn order, timers, requests, queued effects, and evidence are byte-identical.
- Ordinary A spawn/finalization still completes exactly once.
- Removing any post-callback exact-owner fence makes its fixture fail.
- CLJ/CLJS machine suites and replay/conformance gates pass; no rollback framework or public API is added.
notes: Fix shipped in PR #5873 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5873), commit 1c7fc5713a. spawn.cljc install-spawn! now returns :committed/:skipped and caller gates the classification/spawn-order/lifecycle-spawned tail on committed+continue?; finalize.cljc rechecks owner-gone? after each callback-bearing teardown hook (destroyed trace, http-abort, system-id-released). Red-before-fix fixture machine_post_callback_tail_fence_test.clj (8 tests/42 assertions green; 5 loss fixtures were red pre-fix). Machines JVM 1043t, core JVM 1958t, CLJS node 9352t, fast-pr spine all green. Left OPEN for mayor merge.
close_reason: Merged PR #5873 (fence post-callback spawn/finalize tails to exact incarnation: install-spawn! returns :committed/:skipped + caller runs tail only if committed AND owner current; finalize rechecks owner-gone? after each callback-bearing hook before cancellation/unregister/dispatch/publication; 5 loss fixtures red-before-fix; CI green)

title: Reject reactive authoring vars that escape into computed callee value flow
description:
## Problem

PR #5855 (head bef474dc83418911d290a3feda4b6891fd043e5c) recursively lowers genuine reactive calls inside computed callee expressions, but still permits the public authoring vars themselves to flow as values. The analyzer consults bare-reactive-reference-kind only under transparent macro arguments; ordinary symbols can survive unchanged.

Concrete counterexample: `((if p sub inc) [:q])` yields an empty subscription manifest and retains bare `sub`. If that branch is selected, production either chooses a sub-free component shape or calls the public re-frame.ui/sub placeholder, which throws because the compiler did not lower it. Equivalent escapes exist for lease, frame, `((identity sub) q)`, and let-bound aliases. Existing tests cover direct `(sub ...)` calls nested in computed callees, not a computed callee whose result is the reactive authoring var.

## Smallest correction

Make the compiler's binder-aware legality rule explicit: an unquoted resolved sub/lease/frame authoring var is legal only as a compiler-owned direct call head. Reject value flow that could become an invocation target; preserve quoted data, lexical shadowing, and genuine direct calls. Coordinate grammar wording with open rf2-vxgfnd.224 without treating that bead as the owner of this defect.
acceptance_criteria:
- `((if p sub f) q)`, `((identity sub) q)`, and equivalent lease/frame/value-alias forms fail with a stable typed compiler diagnostic on CLJ and CLJS.
- Quoted forms and lexical locals shadowing sub/lease/frame remain legal.
- Direct reactive calls nested in a computed callee still lower to one deterministic site.
- Mounted and advanced-output proof shows no public authoring var survives and the ownership-bearing wrapper is selected.
- Removing the computed-callee bare-reference guard makes a focused mutation fixture fail.
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5874 (SHA af0709c631a05cb720dd055ded55b7db70b08215) — reject bare reactive authoring var escaping into computed-callee/value flow. Re-verified defect LIVE on origin/main @18d909eefb (not closed by #5821/#5855); repro empty-manifest confirmed then fixed. Leaf rule in rewrite-expr rejects bare sub/lease/frame value flow (unsupported-form). Foreground gates green: ui clojure -M:test 494t/6365a 0f/0e (incl g14 budget); npm run test:cljs 9357t/44331a 0f/0e. New fixtures: computed-callee-value-escape (reject) + legitimate-value-flow-still-compiles (accept) + roster row. Left OPEN for mayor to merge.

title: Require positive root-incarnation evidence during explicit ViewCell teardown
description:
## Problem

PR #5854 (head c85ffb71574c664c569fde99ce45701e71609b06) weakened explicit root teardown's ownership test. In implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc around 2657-2675, a captured cell is retained as a teardown victim when cell-root is nil; only a known-different non-nil root is rejected. The nil exception exists to support a bare wiring fixture, but absence of ownership evidence is not evidence that the named incarnation owns the cell.

A re-entrant callback can disconnect both a cell attached to root A and an unrelated unattached/reconnectable cell. Explicit teardown of A then force-deads both. The new sibling fixture proves isolation only for a cell carrying non-nil root B and misses this case. In a pre-alpha ownership substrate, the exact-token overload must be authoritative rather than guessing.

## Smallest correction

For explicit teardown, reap only cells whose cell-root is identical to the supplied root incarnation. Repair the bare fixture by attaching its cell to the real token, or exercise the separate legacy structural-inference form. Do not add rollback, compatibility inference, or a second ownership registry.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic A teardown re-entrantly disconnects attached A and an unattached nil-root sibling; A is reaped and the sibling remains alive/reconnectable with unchanged lease state.
- A correctly attached A cell is still reaped.
- A non-nil B sibling remains isolated.
- A mutation restoring the nil-root-as-owned exception makes the fixture fail.
- CLJ/CLJS ownership suites and relevant UI gates pass; no public API changes.

title: Finalize root preflight evidence only after an actual React commit
description:
## Problem

PR #5853 (authored head `51aafc67b5464ab96b5385ec499a1b063b443a50`, merged as `3059e99042eaea5b5f156ecb094c1d5bb774da5f`) says preflight evidence is finalized at the host commit boundary. The client actually calls `frames/finalize-preflight-attempt!` immediately after `ReactDOMRoot.render` returns:

- `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/client.cljs:493-499`
- `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/client.cljs:537-542`
- `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/client.cljs:620-624`

That is not a React commit acknowledgement. React 19.2's `root.render` enqueues/schedules the update and can return before layout effects fire. React's official `createRoot` reference states that code after `root.render()` can run before that render's effects; `flushSync` is the exceptional API that forces the DOM update before return: https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/client/createRoot and https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/flushSync.

The pinned source says the same thing: `implementation/node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:27873-27894` routes `root.render` to `updateContainerImpl`, whose `:23496-23510` path enqueues and schedules the update without a commit callback.

The repository already demonstrates the important failure shape. A component render failure is caught/reported by React through `onUncaughtError` and can abort the commit after `.render` returned normally (`implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/frame_scope_resolve_dom_cljs_test.cljs:78-89,202-230` and `preflight_frame_wiring_dom_cljs_test.cljs:306-316`). PR #5853's new host-failure test instead throws from the eager `element-thunk` before React receives an element. Its success tests wrap the operation in `act`/`flushSync`, but the runtime sets `:committed` inside `mount*` before the surrounding helper performs its flush.

## Deterministic counterexample

1. A fresh root's preflight installs frame F and returns an attempt receipt.
2. The element thunk succeeds and returns a React element whose component throws during React rendering.
3. `root.render` schedules the update and returns normally.
4. re-frame.ui immediately clears attempt-failure evidence and stores `:committed true`.
5. React later renders, invokes `onUncaughtError`, and aborts the commit. The `mount*` catch and `abort-preflight-attempt!` never run.
6. F is now presented as a committed root scope with a committed render even though that render never committed.

The same premature finalization affects later `render!`/same-root remount attempts: rejected, suspended, superseded, or asynchronously failed work can be recorded as committed before React settles it.

## Required correction

Bind attempt settlement to authoritative host evidence, not `.render` return. The recommended shape is a small internal root commit reporter (for example, an identity-bearing layout-effect signal under the root provider) that finalizes exactly the matching attempt after React commits it. React's error/abandonment path must leave or record truthful failed/incomplete evidence. The signal must be fenced by exact root incarnation, attempt identity, and install-record revision so an old, replayed, or overtaken commit cannot settle newer work.

Do not put every production render behind global `flushSync`: React documents its performance and Suspense costs, and exceptional synchronous flushing would conflict with this package's production-efficiency goal. Do not preserve the name `:committed` or diagnostics claiming committed Root/DOM if the implementation deliberately chooses the weaker meaning "update accepted/scheduled"; such a choice requires a complete contract/diagnostic rename and must not be presented as commit evidence.

Coordinate the root lifecycle surface with open `rf2-vxgfnd.182` (deferred/failed teardown settlement). This bead owns preflight evidence settlement after render; `.182` owns root/container release through teardown. Keep the frozen public API unchanged unless a contract-level choice is surfaced to Mike.

## Dedupe and provenance

Two independent adversarial audits of exact PR #5853 reproduced this issue. The complete live inventory was read before filing. Open `rf2-vxgfnd.164` covers Activity/StrictMode observability and microtask timing, not preflight receipts. Open `.182` covers teardown admission/release, not false preflight commit evidence. Open `.191` covers plan authority and overlapping runs, not React commit acknowledgement. No current open/in-progress bead owns this failure.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real React browser fixture has the element thunk return successfully, then makes a component throw during the initial React render. It proves `.render` returned and `onUncaughtError` fired, yet no completed-scope/committed-render evidence is published.
- A successful initial mount finalizes only after an authoritative host commit signal for that exact root incarnation and attempt.
- A failed later render preserves the prior committed Root/DOM while recording the new attempt truthfully; it cannot clear failure evidence merely because `.render` returned.
- Error-boundary-contained failure, Suspense/deferred work, StrictMode effect replay, ordinary update, root supersession, unmount-before-commit, and stale/overtaken attempt controls have defined, identity-safe outcomes.
- A stale, duplicated, or replayed commit signal cannot finalize a newer receipt or another root's evidence.
- A mutation moving finalization back immediately after `.render` deterministically fails.
- Production does not globally force `flushSync`; advanced output pays only the minimal bookkeeping needed for correctness, and the frozen public API is unchanged.
- Spec/runtime/docstrings never call scheduled work committed unless backed by the authoritative commit signal.
- Relevant browser, UI node/JVM, root lifecycle, and fast PR gates pass.
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5871 (root-commit-reporter binds finalize to a real React commit; red-before-fix DOM fixture render-abort-after-render-returns-does-not-finalize-committed). Gates green: node UI 494, browser 352, JVM UI 492, fast-pr spine PASS.
close_reason: Merged PR #5871 (finalize root preflight evidence only on a real React commit — root-commit-reporter useLayoutEffect finalizes only for committed renders; aborted/abandoned/StrictMode renders never finalize; rev-guarded; red-before-fix render-abort fixture; CI 39/0/0)

title: Finish the closed no-frame guidance sweep without erasing lexical scope
description:
## Problem

Merged PR #5852 (authored head `b45c25ee4ab951182d42380584b5da1090ab9517`) closed P1 `rf2-vxgfnd.240`, but the merged sweep fails the central distinction in that bead and leaves its migration/skill scope untouched.

The frame-resolution contract has two different cases:

1. A plain, unregistered Reagent component cannot read a surrounding `frame-provider` through React context because it lacks the `:contextType` wiring installed by `reg-view`. If no dynamic binding or explicit target is present, ambient `dispatch`/`subscribe` and no-arg `(rf/capture-frame)` correctly raise `:rf.error/no-frame-context`.
2. `with-frame` binds `re-frame.frame/*current-frame*` for its synchronous lexical body, and that dynamic tier is consulted before React context. Therefore an unregistered function that executes the actual operation—or calls no-arg `(rf/capture-frame)`—inside its own live `with-frame` body succeeds. What does not work is wrapping returned Hiccup or a render-scheduling call: that binding unwinds before React later invokes the descendant.

PR #5852 instead makes the absent-scope case categorical. `spec/AI-Audit.md:380` says deliberately unregistered code must carry an explicit target and that no-arg capture plus `with-frame` both re-raise. `docs/core/views.md:216-218` likewise presents the provider-only failure and no-arg capture as an unqualified property of a plain function. The passages declared “verified correct” repeat the same overstatement in `spec/000-Vision.md:535`, `spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md:120`, `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1614`, and `docs/core/25-from-re-frame-v1.md:189`.

This is contradicted by the implementation and executable proof: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc:247-248` installs the dynamic binding; `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:291-332` prioritizes it; `implementation/core/test/re_frame/capture_frame_test.clj:58-90` proves no-arg capture succeeds inside `with-frame` and the resulting operations remain locked after unwind. The real-React fixture around `cross_spec_dom_cljs_test.cljs:496-504` explicitly clears an ambient binding because synchronous `flushSync` would otherwise make the plain operation succeed.

The sweep was also incomplete. The PR body says it searched only `spec/*.md` and `docs/**/*.md`, although `.240` required migration and skill references. Incorrect or ambiguous recovery recipes remain in `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` (notably M-11 around lines 458-478 and its summary near 1816), `skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md`, `skills/re-frame-migration/references/*`, and `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/{frames,views,subs}.md`. Several tell an unregistered component to use bare `(rf/capture-frame)` “at render time” without a live scope or explicit target.

Two older contract residues belong in the same bounded sweep: `spec/000-Vision.md:436` still says plain Reagent functions target `:rf/default`, and `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:884` still uses a plain-function-under-non-default-frame warning as the example for `:rf.warning/*`, although the live contract is an always-loud `:rf.error/no-frame-context` when resolution is genuinely absent.

Closed `.240` cannot be amended. Open `rf2-vxgfnd.236` owns the real-React boundary fixture and open `rf2-vxgfnd.179` owns the broader canonical re-frame.ui versus frozen-Reagent classification; do not duplicate either. This bead owns the missed semantic wording and complete tracked guidance sweep.

## Bounded correction

Reconcile all live stock-Reagent guidance across `spec/**`, `docs/**`, `migration/**`, and `skills/**` to one exact rule:

- provider-only unregistered invocation has no readable React context and fails ambiently;
- a synchronous lexical `with-frame` enclosing the actual operation works, including no-arg `capture-frame` created inside that body;
- wrapping returned Hiccup or scheduling later React work does not transmit the binding;
- `reg-view` is the preferred seam within the frozen stock-Reagent tier;
- deliberately unregistered code without a genuine live scope must carry an explicit frame id, per-call `{:frame ...}`, or a locked operation bundle.

Classify every residue rather than mechanically replacing legitimate no-arg capture in registered views, handler/effect scopes, tests, SSR, or other synchronous lexical regions. Coordinate fixture wording and the positive lexical counterexample with `.236`; leave the general canonical/frozen/transitional rewrite to `.179`. Add no UIx/Helix/slim compatibility work—they are retiring. No runtime API or implementation change is required.
acceptance_criteria:
- `spec/AI-Audit.md`, `docs/core/views.md`, `spec/000-Vision.md`, `spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md`, `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`, and `docs/core/25-from-re-frame-v1.md` all distinguish a live inner lexical binding from an already-unwound subtree wrapper.
- No live passage says no-arg `capture-frame` always fails in an unregistered function; it fails only when neither a genuine dynamic scope nor readable adapter context exists.
- Migration M-11, its summaries, `skills/re-frame-migration/**`, and relevant `skills/re-frame2/**` leaves no longer recommend bare ambient capture as recovery when the component has no scope to capture.
- `spec/000-Vision.md` no longer says plain Reagent functions target an implicit `:rf/default`, and `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` no longer presents this always-loud absence error as a `:rf.warning/*` example.
- Examples include both discriminating shapes: `with-frame` around the actual synchronous operation/capture succeeds; `with-frame` around returned Hiccup or render scheduling fails after unwind.
- A complete classified residue inventory covers tracked `spec/**`, `docs/**`, `migration/**`, and `skills/**`, preserving legitimate registered, handler/effect, test, SSR, and lexical-scope uses.
- The focused browser proof remains owned by `rf2-vxgfnd.236`, and canonical re-frame.ui versus frozen compatibility classification remains owned by `rf2-vxgfnd.179`; this work does not duplicate them.
- No UIx/Helix/slim compatibility machinery or runtime API change is added.

RE-VERIFICATION (worker/noframe-macro-247, 2026-07-14): The dispatch brief framed this as an IMPLEMENTATION bug (lexical-scope erasure in core_reg_view_macro.cljc + frame.cljc). That framing DOES NOT REPRODUCE. The implementation already preserves legitimate lexical scope AND fails the ambient footgun loud: capture_frame_test.clj is GREEN (12 tests / 40 assertions, 0 failures), including capture-frame-captures-frame-at-creation (the exact claimed path: (with-frame :A (capture-frame)) captured + fired after unwind routes to :A) and capture-frame-outside-with-frame-raises-no-frame-context (ambient no-arg raises :rf.error/no-frame-context). require-current-frame!/resolve-current-frame are correct. The REAL defect (docs overstatement) is STILL LIVE on origin/main and is a docs/spec/migration/skills reconciliation sweep, which the brief explicitly FENCED OUT (no spec/**, don't re-touch no-frame docs, hot-zone files spec/006 + Spec-Schemas + migration/README involved). title: Make delayed predecessor epoch fan-out honest after same-id listener rearm
description:
PR #5850 snapshots predecessor A's `silenced-cbs` before dissociation and later publishes that saved set unconditionally, even if same-id B has claimed the epoch stores and the same current listener generation has already received B's newer record.

Counterexample:
1. A snapshots callback `cb`, dissociates, and pauses at the post-dissoc hook.
2. B is created and settles an ordinary event. `cb` receives B's `:ok` record and is re-armed for the same bare frame id.
3. A resumes, delivers its older `:halted-destroy` record, then emits `:rf.epoch.cb/silenced-on-frame-destroy {:frame id :cb-id cb}`.
4. The newest signal now claims `cb` went silent even though it is live on B. B's later destroy emits the identical unqualified signal again.

Spec 009 and Tool-Pair define this event as a current one-shot explanation for why a previously firing callback stopped, and explicitly say a fresh same-id delivery re-arms it. Historical A evidence and current listener state therefore cannot share the same unconditional publication rule.

The bounded recommendation is to preserve A's halted record/trailers but emit A's silencing fan only when A still wins its compare-owned cleanup (equivalently, only when no successor has re-armed the id-keyed observation state). Also make the late-record consumer rule explicit: a predecessor terminal record may arrive after a newer same-id epoch, is historical, and must not be treated as the successor's current ring/focus. If the existing globally monotonic epoch id is insufficient to make that safe for every consumer, surface the smallest serializable discriminator rather than leaking the opaque owner token or introducing a general event-ordering system.

Sequence after rf2-vxgfnd.244 because both update the same successor fixtures and terminal fan-out.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fail-before fixture pauses A after its snapshot, lets the unchanged callback generation receive B's settled record, resumes A, and proves no later bare A silencing notification is emitted.
- The listener continues to receive B records; when B later destroys, exactly one truthful silencing notification is emitted for B.
- Control: if no same-id successor has re-armed the callback/frame observation, A still emits exactly one silencing notification.
- Re-registering the same cb-id with a new generation in the gap cannot let A silence or invoke the new generation incorrectly; old/new callback behavior is explicitly pinned.
- A's required halted record/trailers remain observable exactly once without entering B's history/rings or moving B's current focus. Consumer ordering/identity semantics are documented in Spec 009 and Tool-Pair.
- CLJ and synchronous/reentrant CLJS fixtures cover unchanged and replacement generations; repeated destroys remain one-shot.
- No general scheduler, opaque host owner token, or speculative multi-incarnation API is introduced.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5872 (fix in epoch/listeners.cljc on-frame-destroyed! — gate A's silencing fan on cleanup-frame-owner! winning; halted record/trailers stay unconditional). Red-before-fix: predecessor-silencing-fan-suppressed-after-successor-rearm + regen-in-gap (CLJ) + reentrant CLJS. Flips the incidental silencing assertion in the #5865/.244 ring fixture (observer re-armed by B). Spec 009/Tool-Pair late-record + silencing-suppression doc noted as follow-up. Left open for mayor.

title: Keep predecessor terminal evidence out of a same-id successor trace ring
description:
PR #5850 preserves predecessor A's terminal epoch evidence after same-id successor B can become live, but "structural delivery" prevents only epoch capture and no-emit policy lookup; it does not prevent per-frame trace-ring retention.

Exact path at authored head d7d88b39323653ee082cf7e44e4ffe35be6f1d8e:
- `frame.cljc` releases A's trace ring before the new pre-dissoc snapshot/post-dissoc publication sequence.
- `listeners.cljc` later emits A's `:rf.epoch/snapshotted`, `:rf.epoch/outcome`, silencing, listener-exception, and teardown-hook-exception events under `call-with-structural-delivery`.
- `trace.cljc`'s structural scope disables epoch capture and frame no-emit, but retains the inherited A handler `dispatch-id`.
- `trace/tooling.cljc` routes an event carrying a dispatch id plus bare frame id into the current ring for that id. If B is now installed, A's terminal facts are appended to B's ring. A snapshot-hook failure can similarly recreate A's already-released ring.

This violates exact-incarnation isolation and makes a public `(rf/trace-buffer B {:flat true})` contain predecessor facts. The merged fixtures assert B's epoch buffer/history, not the trace ring, so CI remains green.

Use the smallest local notion of retentionless structural delivery: global live trace listeners must still receive required terminal facts exactly once, but no current/future frame ring may retain them. Do not clear a ring by bare id after dissociation, because that could erase B's legitimate evidence. Move the snapshot call before A's ring release if needed so a snapshot-failure warning is cleared by A's normal release.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic fail-before fixture pauses A after dissociation, installs same-id B with an ordinary retained ring sentinel, resumes A, and asserts B's public flat trace buffer remains byte-identical.
- None of A's terminal operations or inherited dispatch id appears in B's ring; no ring is recreated for destroyed A.
- Global trace listeners still receive each required A terminal trailer/diagnostic exactly once, including listener and post-dissoc hook exceptions.
- A throwing `:epoch/snapshot-frame-destroyed` during a mid-run destroy leaves no residual per-frame ring while still producing the required global diagnostic/report.
- Ordinary nonterminal events retain their existing ring/capture/no-emit behavior.
- The fix does not perform any post-dissoc bare-id ring clear and has CLJ plus synchronous CLJS coverage for the structural retention boundary.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5865 (worker/trace-ring-244 @ 649a8e9d380dfcbfb5e2dbbd4bc8a925d33fb2b0). Retentionless structural delivery: *ring-retention-enabled?* bound false in call-with-structural-delivery (trace.cljc) + threaded to deliver-to-tooling!'s new retain? arg (trace/tooling.cljc); snapshot moved before ring release (frame.cljc). No listeners.cljc edit needed. Red-before-fix RING fixtures: predecessor-terminal-facts-never-retained-in-successor-ring + snapshot-hook-failure-leaves-no-residual-ring (JVM) + structural-retention-cljs-test (CLJ+CLJS). Foreground green: core 1955/8916, epoch 388/2413, machines 1035/3509, CLJS 9339/44214. Left OPEN for mayor merge.

Spec/009 ripple filed.

title: Terminally fence machine completion and spawn tails after incarnation loss
description:
PR #5849 added lifecycle schema validation to protect exact machine incarnations, but two callback-bearing tails still cross the terminal fence after ownership changes.

Completion path: `validate-completion-output!` can return `:rf/stale-incarnation`, but `finalize.cljc` binds the result to `_` and continues parent resolution/on-done, done tracing, teardown projection, HTTP/timer cancellation, classification/spawn-order removal, unregister, on-error dispatch, and result/fx publication. A validator or nested trace callback that destroys incarnation A and creates same-id B can therefore erase or mutate B.

Spawn path: the accepted spawn cascade checks ownership once, then emits callback-bearing spawned/collision traces before install/classification/order/dispatch. A trace listener can replace A with B and the old cascade still commits framework-owned actions into B's name.

Apply the ruled policy consistently: already-entered authored callbacks may unwind, but loss of exact incarnation ownership is a terminal fence for every subsequent framework-owned action. Do not roll back already-delivered user callbacks or invent transactional machines.
acceptance_criteria:
- `finalize` consumes the stale-incarnation result immediately and returns the specified inert outcome before every subsequent framework-owned side effect.
- Exact ownership is rechecked after every callback-bearing completion trace/fanout and after each callback-bearing spawn/collision trace before installation, bookkeeping, dispatch, cancellation, unregister, or fx/result publication.
- Fail-before fixtures cover completion success, validator false, validator throw, and nested diagnostic/trace replacement of A by same-id B; B's runtime, resources, classification, spawn order, registry entry, and queued effects remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Spawn fixtures replace A from both normal spawned and collision trace callbacks and prove no stale install/bookkeeping/dispatch crosses into B.
- Already-delivered trace/callback observations occur at most once; no compensation or rollback is added.
- The implementation follows the accepted "unwind authored chain, terminally fence subsequent framework actions" ruling.

title: Make frozen Reagent no-frame recovery guidance exact across all live docs
description:
PR #5846 corrected part of the stock-Reagent no-frame recovery story, but live migration/reference material still gives unregistered components a no-argument `(rf/capture-frame)` recovery and some newly changed text overcorrects by implying lexical capture can never work.

The exact contract has two distinct cases:
- An unregistered Reagent component cannot read React provider context. With neither an ambient dynamic binding nor an explicit target, no-arg capture must fail, including inside a non-default provider subtree.
- `with-frame` can supply a synchronous lexical dynamic binding when it is active inside the plain function around the actual operation. Wrapping returned Hiccup or a scheduling call is not a durable subtree/provider bridge because the binding has unwound before React later invokes the component.

Correct all frozen stock-Reagent guidance consistently. Prefer `reg-view` as the canonical registered seam and an explicit frame/handle for genuinely unregistered code. Do not spend work on UIx/Helix/slim; they are scheduled for deletion. Coordinate rather than duplicate the browser-boundary proof in rf2-vxgfnd.236 and the canonical-surface wording in rf2-vxgfnd.179.
acceptance_criteria:
- All live stock-Reagent docs, migration references, and skill references distinguish absent context, synchronous lexical `with-frame`, explicit target capture, and registered `reg-view` behavior precisely.
- No passage suggests that wrapping a returned Hiccup subtree makes an unregistered component provider-aware.
- No passage says no-arg capture always fails when a synchronous dynamic binding is genuinely active.
- Canonical examples use `reg-view` or an explicit target; any lexical example is narrowly scoped and warns that the binding must enclose the operation itself.
- A residue search/test covers the affected docs and does not add compatibility work for retiring UIx/Helix/slim adapters.

Two NEW wrong-recovery instances found + fixed: spec/AI-Audit.md G-D (listed with-frame + no-arg capture-frame as valid fixes) and docs/core/views.md §Plain defn views (taught no-arg capture-frame recovery; also tightened 'non-default provider' -> 'frame-provider'). The four prior PRs (#5843/#5846/#5851) verified correct, not re-edited. All other hits classified legitimate (EP history, contract/API descriptions, synchronous with-frame harness/registration scopes, async-callback captures in registered renders/effects, reg-view*-registered inners). Gates green: check_doc_slugs, check_readme_links, mkdocs --strict, ep-status-sync, runtime-subsystem-grading, readme-inventories. Docs-only. Do NOT merge — mayor owns.

title: Make the README truthful about pre-alpha status, XState, and the human guide
description:
PR #5845 rewrote the repository front page, but the resulting first-contact narrative is ahead of the ratified delivery state and leaves fresh readers without an accurate human path.

- README now calls re-frame2 "Alpha" and says changes are minimal while the substrate program is still pre-alpha and S3-S7, proof gates, adapter deletion, and the alpha tag remain open. The front page must not declare the state that Stage 7 is meant to establish.
- It claims near-parity with "XState v6" without explaining that v6 is an alpha/design direction; Spec 005 explicitly treats it as direction rather than a released compatibility target.
- The previous human reading paths disappeared. The remaining project-layout reference says `docs/guide/`, but the live user material is rooted at `docs/index.md` and `docs/core/`. AI-agent instructions are not a substitute for a clear human start link.

Keep this compact: correct truth and navigation, not a second documentation architecture.
acceptance_criteria:
- README describes the current state as pre-alpha until the ratified S7/tag gate is actually complete; stability language matches the live delivery contract.
- The machines claim accurately describes XState v6 as an alpha/design-direction comparison and links the local comparison/contract without claiming released-version parity.
- A concise human "Start here"/user-guide link reaches the real docs index, and project-layout paths match the repository.
- A repository check or focused review prevents the root README and docs landing page from making contradictory lifecycle claims.

I'm still preserving optionality."), L86 (unqualified XState v6 claim), L155 (docs/guide/ listed; directory absent — docs/index.md + docs/core/ are the live human material), docs/index.md L17 ("Alpha, although changes are now minimal.").

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:

title: Artifact generation/activation separation: stable URLs must resolve to accepted generation until pipeline succeeds (rf2-vxgfnd.193 followup)
description:
Counterexample 1 from rf2-vxgfnd.193 (PR #5848) is reproduced+gated but NOT fixed: it needs a Shadow output/flush surface beyond the digest-carrier 3-file fence.

## Gap (proven by the RF2_PROBE_ACTIVATION_TXN probe in check-ui-digest-carrier.cjs)
Shadow's browser target flushes candidate d3 to the stable module URLs (/base.js carrier, /lazy.js) BEFORE a later :flush hook fails; Shadow then rolls its functional build-state back to accepted d2. re-frame.ui's hooks run at :compile-prepare/:compile-finish only — there is NO re-frame.ui hook point after Shadow flushes the candidate bytes, so nothing in-fence can restore or fail-close the served files after a downstream failure. A hard reload or first lazy import executes/advertises rejected d3.

## Required correction
Artifact generation/activation separation: candidate module bytes may be generated speculatively, but stable URLs/manifests must keep resolving to the accepted generation until the whole configured pipeline succeeds; a downstream failure must retain/restore the accepted generation or make new-page/lazy activation fail-closed. Prefer a single small generation/activation protocol reusing the existing carrier machinery; keep it dev-only and fully elided from advanced production.

## Hot-zone / scope
Needs top-level implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (candidate vs stable output-dir/asset-path or an activation-indirection module) — HOT-ZONE, sequence it — plus likely module-load gating in ui/runtime + ui/client (out of the .193 fence). Flip check-ui-digest-carrier.cjs's downstream-output probe to assert by default (or set RF2_PROBE_ACTIVATION_TXN=1) once the separation lands.

## Acceptance
- After the intentional post-output :flush failure, a hard reload AND a first lazy import both receive the prior accepted generation or a stable fail-closed response; neither executes/advertises candidate d3.
- A successful recovery publishes the next generation atomically to compiler state, stable browser URLs/module manifest, and runtime digest readers.
- Advanced production contains no generation ledger / reload hooks / carrier sentinel / digest literal / fallback runtime branch.

Deferred by the digest cluster worker (PR forthcoming for .194/.205/.199): .237 (accepted-generation stable-URL resolution) requires a HOT-ZONE top-level implementation/shadow-cljs.edn change (verified still fully reproducing). Needs a dedicated sole-owner dispatch sequenced against shadow-cljs.edn (no other worker touching it). Dispatch solo when the hot-zone is free.
PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5864 — .237 NOT fixed in this PR. Re-verified: gap fully remains on main (probe: lazy=true, carrier-not-d2=true; #5848 fixed active-runtime LKG only, not on-disk stable-output). Fix requires HOT-ZONE implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (candidate vs stable output-dir/asset-path or activation-indirection module) — outside worker fence, no in-fence lever (a hard reload reads d3 from disk with no d2 reference; only the JVM compiler knows d2 is accepted). title: Give fixed-id spawn-all attempts distinct canonical work identity
description:
## Problem

PR #5842 makes the join-attempt token a load-bearing exact-authority fact and claims one observable terminal authority per child attempt, but machine reply identity still collapses sequential `:fixed-actor-id` join children.

`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/reply.cljc` around lines 93-149 defines a machine work-id as `[:rf.work/machine actor-id invoke-id generation]`; `actor-generation` returns 1 for every actor id without a generated `#n` suffix. A fixed actor can legitimately be destroyed and respawned at the same parent/invoke path. The runtime gives those attempts different `:rf/attempt` authority tokens (`spawn.cljc` around lines 595-609 and 690-700), yet both publish the identical work-id.

Xray groups terminal and stale evidence solely by work-id (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reply_envelope.cljc` around lines 673-708). Therefore a completed/suppressed old fixed-id attempt and its live successor collapse into one arc. A stale prior carrier can make the successor's grouped arc appear suppressed, contradicting the promised attempt identity and one-terminal model even though the join fold itself is fenced.

This is distinct from rf2-ixjd48, which fixes validation order and prevents a stale carrier borrowing the current actor's identity, and rf2-t154jx, which makes authority survive delayed dispatch/replay. They are prerequisite coordination points, not substitutes for giving two valid fixed-id attempts distinct work identity.

## Bounded correction

Give every spawn-all child attempt a stable attempt discriminator in its canonical work-id. The simplest shape is for join-child reply construction to use the runtime-minted `:rf/attempt` token as its generation/discriminator (including terminal, stale, cancellation/reap-correlated rows), while preserving the existing generated actor-id contract where it is already exact. A superseded carrier must be attributed using its carried attempt authority, never the successor join's live token. Keep the public event grammar unchanged and do not add a parallel identity system.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two sequential `:spawn-all` attempts using the same `:fixed-actor-id`, parent and invoke path produce distinct canonical work-ids and distinct Xray/work-ledger arcs.
- Each valid attempt has exactly one terminal authority; the first attempt's completion or suppression cannot set the second attempt's terminal/suppressed state.
- A stale carrier from attempt A arriving during attempt B is attributed to A using carried exact authority and never receives B's work-id.
- Generated `<type>#<n>` actors retain stable existing identity semantics; normal single-spawn behavior is not broadened accidentally.
- All reply-bearing join paths (non-decisive, decisive, stale, late, cancellation/reap as applicable) agree on the same attempt discriminator.
- CLJ and CLJS counterfixtures fail when fixed-id generation is forced back to constant 1, and Xray grouping tests consume actual emitted tag maps.

title: Select parallel spawn-all joins by exact authority before folding
description:
## Problem

PR #5839's exact-authority check occurs after the runtime has selected which active spawn-all join owns an inbound completion. That selection remains ambiguous when parallel regions legitimately reuse both the completion event keyword and the logical child ID.

At authored head c6db0e0cbf99b33c21a26a8f7a5969aab6cdd666:

- implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/join.cljc around lines 236-255 permits multiple simultaneous region matches for the same completion event.
- The selection around lines 630-642 chooses the first matching join whose :children contains child-id.
- The exact :rf/join-auth tuple, including the region-prefixed invoke-id and spawned-id, is checked only after that choice around lines 767-791.

If region R1 and R2 both declare child :worker and share :on-child-done/:on-child-error, a legitimate R2 completion also satisfies R1's child-ID predicate. It is selected against R1, then rejected as attempt-superseded because its exact authority names R2. R2 never folds and its join can hang.

Existing parallel coverage deliberately uses different child IDs, so it cannot expose the collision. This follows closed rf2-w84jv's earlier child-ID routing repair; no live follow-up covers the remaining ambiguity.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two simultaneously active parallel regions use identical success/failure event keywords and identical logical child ID :worker.
- Completing the later region first resolves/folds only that exact region; the first region and sibling actor remain untouched.
- Neither attempt-superseded nor bad-child evidence fires for the legitimate carrier.
- Cover both success and failure on CLJ and CLJS.
- Unstamped, wrong-invoke, wrong-spawned-id, and unknown-child carriers remain fail-closed with stable evidence.
- Mutating selection back to child-ID-only deterministically suppresses/hangs the later region and fails the fixture.
- No public grammar restriction, compatibility alias, global child-ID uniqueness rule, or new coordinator is introduced.

title: Carry spawn-all join authority through replay and delayed dispatch
description:
## Problem

PR #5839 at authored head c6db0e0cbf99b33c21a26a8f7a5969aab6cdd666 authenticates spawn-all child completions by placing the only exact-attempt credential in metadata on the inner event vector. That authority does not survive two supported delivery paths.

### Recorded strict replay

implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/join.cljc around lines 69-120 stamps :rf/join-auth in vector metadata. The parent gate around lines 767-773 treats missing metadata as :rf.machine.spawn-all/attempt-unverified and performs no fold.

Event metadata is not part of the event/options recording contract. An EDN round trip preserves the event value but drops the inner metadata:

original: [:parent (with-meta [:done :a] {:rf/join-auth {...}})]
round-trip: [:parent [:done :a]]

Tool-Pair strict replay records and redispatches event plus causal coeffects. Replaying a real completion therefore silently no-ops instead of reproducing the original fold/terminal/resolution. This violates the project's replay-faithfulness contract and the exact-authority promise closed by rf2-nvxehu.

### Live delayed dispatch

stamp-fx-entry around lines 122-140 handles :dispatch and the retired top-level :dispatch-n spelling, but not the live reserved :dispatch-later shape {:ms n :event event}. A valid child completion emitted through :dispatch-later reaches the parent without authority, is suppressed as attempt-unverified, and can leave an :all join hung forever.

Two independent audits reproduced the delayed-path gap. Exact-head tests cover only direct dispatch. No all-status follow-up covers replay or delayed authentication.
acceptance_criteria:
- Record a real authenticated child completion, EDN-roundtrip its recorded event plus causal coeffects, restore the pre-event runtime state, and strict-replay it; runtime-db, parent resolution, and terminal evidence match the original.
- Removing the recordable authority fact makes the replay proof fail.
- A real zero-delay :dispatch-later child completion resolves on CLJ and CLJS/browser and publishes its terminal exactly once.
- A nonmatching delayed event is unchanged; arbitrary custom effect payloads are not traversed.
- An old-attempt delayed completion across re-entry is classified attempt-superseded and cannot fold.
- Missing or tampered recorded authority has an explicit, stable rejection outcome and cannot be reported as successful replay.
- The retired :dispatch-n authentication arm is absent.
- Public event grammar, application data, and production hot-path shape remain unchanged except for the smallest internal envelope fact.

title: Linearize frame-ops cache publication across same-ID reincarnation
description:
## Problem

PR #5838's per-incarnation frame-ops cache is vulnerable to a same-ID destroy/recreate race on the JVM.

At implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/frames.cljc around lines 690-711, frame-ops captures incarnation token A, checks that A is current, and later performs an independent cache update. If A is destroyed and replacement incarnation B is created/read between that check and publication, the paused A reader can overwrite B's cache entry and return A's already-dead bundle.

An exact-head deterministic audit produced:

{:stale-frame :audit/reused
 :stale-is-fresh-1 false
 :fresh-identity-survived false
 :stale-dispatch-error :rf.error/frame-destroyed}

Thus the read returns a bundle that was no longer live at return time, and B's repeated reads lose the promised stable identity because the stale A publication displaced B. Green authored tests cover sequential replacement, not this interleaving.

No all-status bead matched frame-ops cache publication or same-ID reincarnation.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic JVM fixture pauses an A reader after its initial liveness check, destroys A, creates and reads B under the same frame ID, then resumes A.
- The A reader cannot overwrite B's cache entry or return a dead A bundle as a valid frame-ops read.
- B1 and B2 remain identical after the stale reader resumes.
- A stale operation remains incarnation-fenced and cannot target B.
- Disjoint frame IDs retain independent progress; ordinary same-incarnation reads keep stable identity.
- A mutation restoring check-then-independent-publish fails deterministically.
- CLJ/CLJS frame lifecycle, drain, and compiled-frame gates remain green without a new public API or unbounded cache.

title: Make frame-only compiled views real React context consumers
description:
## Problem

PR #5838 at authored head 87b42778bed9d79bd7537668f92bd54a9b230f7e ships the compiled (frame) operation bundle, but a view whose only reactive dependency is ambient frame context is not made a React context consumer.

The compiler records :frame-ops sites, yet the CLJS emitter's wrapper selection considers subscription and lease sites when choosing the context/hook-aware path. A frame-only view can therefore remain on the direct React.memo path. re-frame.ui.frames/frame-ops resolves ambient context through function-component-current-frame, which reads React context's current value directly rather than registering the component through useContext.

Counterexample:

1. Mount a compiled child that calls (frame) and renders the returned :frame under frame-provider A.
2. Retarget the ancestor provider from A to B without changing the child's rf=-equal props.
3. React may correctly memo-bail the non-consumer child.
4. Its body does not rerun and its held operations remain locked to A, so UI and later imperative work use the wrong frame.

The mounted PR fixture proves only initial provider resolution; it never retargets A to B. This contradicts the context-change repaint promise in spec/004-Views.md around line 130 and violates frame isolation. No all-status bead matched this frame-only provider-retarget gap.
design:
Treat ambient frame dependency as a real compiler-visible React context dependency:

- Select a context-consuming wrapper for compiled views whose (frame) operation bundle depends on ambient frame context.
- Register through the supported React context-consumption mechanism so provider changes bypass memo equality as React intends.
- Preserve the direct zero-hook path for genuinely frame-independent views.
- If an explicit immutable frame target does not depend on ambient context, avoid charging it unnecessarily.

Reuse the existing compiler wrapper taxonomy; do not introduce a parallel view/component abstraction.
acceptance_criteria:
- A mounted frame-only child under provider A rerenders on provider retarget A to B even when its ordinary props remain rf=-equal.
- The new render returns B's bundle and subsequent dispatch/subscribe operations target B, never A.
- Intended component/local-state identity survives the provider retarget.
- A same-provider rerender does not add needless work.
- A genuinely frame-independent compiled view stays on the inert/direct production path, with the existing production economics gate green.
- A mutation that removes :frame-ops from context-wrapper selection fails the A-to-B fixture.
- No public API or compatibility branch is added.
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5857 (worker/frame-ops-228, HEAD 0b29b86334). Fix + red-before-fix retarget fixtures (dom-cljs + elision-prod) committed. Left open for mayor review/merge.
