title: Make observation error provenance opaque and channel-aware
description:
## Problem

PR #5836 at authored head 554cfc52c89276181821352db766c1fb7c220189 replaces truthy error-id inference with first-emission provenance, but the provenance is both channel-blind and reconstructible from public ex-data. Two independent exact-head audits reproduced production silence and category/suppression spoofing outside the authored fixtures.

### Channel-blind suppression/promotion

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc around lines 460-479 marks :rf.error/sub-cycle as "fanned at source", although that source emission is diagnostic-only.
- report-disposal-notify-escape! around line 674 treats the Boolean marker as proof that all required channels were covered and emits nothing further.
- :rf.error/sub-cycle is production-elided. When an on-change callback reaches cyclic acquire during HMR or disposed-drain, production receives no always-on record; those boundaries swallow the later rethrow.
- Conversely, an unfanned diagnostic-only category such as :rf.error/observation-malformed-target can be dynamically sent through emit-error-both!, promoting a category that Spec 009 excludes from the always-on axis.

The isolated cyclic-acquire test does not compose the error with either swallowing drain boundary.

### Reconstructible provenance and canonicality

- error_emit.cljc around lines 426-441 accepts any :rf.error/* keyword plus a string :reason as a canonical framework throwable. A reserved but uncatalogued :rf.error/not-in-catalogue with :reason returns true.
- The authored spoof fixture omits :reason, so it does not exercise the shape accepted by the new predicate.
- fanned-at-source? trusts a publicly reachable namespaced ex-data key whose literal value is true. Application callback data can therefore imitate an existing/unknown category or mark an un-emitted throwable as already fanned, injecting arbitrary vocabulary or suppressing reporting entirely.

This violates the exact-once, stable-category, always-on production contract. Closed rf2-wbkjk9 cannot be amended; no matching all-status follow-up was found.
design:
Replace the Boolean/public-shape inference with the smallest opaque, channel-aware internal attestation:

- Track which channel(s) a source actually emitted, not merely "fanned".
- Let the drain preserve an already-emitted diagnostic fact while adding the stable always-on callback-failure fact when production coverage is still required.
- Never promote a diagnostic-only category to the always-on vocabulary merely because it escaped a callback.
- Attest canonical builder output and source emission with opaque internal identity tokens (or an equivalently non-forgeable internal representation), not namespace + :reason or literal public values.
- Avoid a global seen-error registry and preserve the original throwable/cause and complete sibling drain.

Keep the mechanism compact: one internal provenance representation shared by existing emit seams and the drain.
acceptance_criteria:
- Actual HMR and disposed callbacks that reach cyclic acquire produce one :rf.error/sub-cycle diagnostic in debug and exactly one production-survivable callback-failure record; advanced production has no trace event.
- An escaping diagnostic-only malformed-target category is never promoted onto the always-on category axis.
- Reserved unknown IDs with plausible :reason, imitated existing IDs with :reason, and application ex-data containing the public-looking marker all receive exactly one stable wrapper and can neither inject nor suppress a category.
- Legitimate already-emitted typed failures remain exact-once with original attribution.
- All siblings drain and the first original throwable is rethrown to a direct caller with identity/cause intact.
- CLJ, CLJS, debug, and advanced fixtures fail if channel coverage is collapsed to a Boolean or if opaque attestation is replaced with reconstructible map shape.
- No global dedupe registry, public API, compatibility branch, or additional error category is introduced.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5861 (SHA f9a5af9066). Fix entirely in observation.cljc: opaque channel-aware EmissionProvenance token replaces the forgeable fanned-at-source-key + canonical-typed-error shape test; drain now channel-aware (source-covered-always-on?), wraps trace-only/diagnostic-only/untyped/spoof escapes in the stable :rf.error/observation-on-change-failed without promoting any diagnostic category. No error_emit.cljc change; no new error category. Behaviour change: :rf.error/reentrant-graph-op (Spec 009 diagnostic) now wrapped, not promoted — 3 existing fixtures updated. 3 new red-before-fix fixtures added. Gates green: core JVM 1951/8898, ui JVM 483/6278, CLJS node 9338/44229, fast-PR spine PASS. Follow-up: Spec 009 observation-on-change-failed row prose refinement (no new id/row needed). Leaving OPEN for mayor to merge.
close_reason: Merged PR #5861 (opaque, channel-aware observation error provenance: EmissionProvenance token records covered channels; escapes not covered on always-on get one stable wrapper, never promoting a diagnostic category; :reentrant-graph-op now wrapped not promoted; re-verified still-live + red-before-fix; CI 49/0/0)

title: Land the observation callback-failure contract and schema slice closed prematurely by PR 5836
description:
## Problem

PR #5836 at authored head 554cfc52c89276181821352db766c1fb7c220189 explicitly stopped the rf2-gg3om8 frozen-contract/schema slice because its hot-zone gate had not yet cleared. The PR changed only:

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_port_cljs_test.cljc

Nevertheless rf2-gg3om8 is now closed with reason "Merged PR #5836", while its own final comment says STOPPED and unshipped.

The promised contract remains absent/drifted on current main:

- spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md around lines 1143-1205 does not define callback-failure containment, classification, sibling-drain, first-escape, source-attribution, or channel semantics.
- spec/Spec-Schemas.md around lines 893-901 promises a per-category schema for every Spec 009 error/warning category, but contains no schema for :rf.error/observation-on-change-failed.
- spec/009-Instrumentation.md around line 1887 still describes only an untyped failure and direct dispatch-on-error!, while runtime now has already-fanned typed, unfanned canonical typed, and wrapper arms and uses emit-error-both!.
- No advanced-production fixture proves one always-on record with the diagnostic trace leg elided.

The original bead is closed and must not be amended. Its former hot-zone prerequisite was PR #5835, which has now merged, so the stopped slice is ready to land. Targeted all-status searches found no open follow-up.
design:
Deliver the bounded scope already specified by rf2-gg3om8, against the actual post-#5836 runtime:

- Add one canonical :rf.error/observation-on-change-failed schema matching the real record and trace-tag shapes.
- Amend Spec 006 with the exact callback boundaries, classification arms, containment/drain ordering, first-escape propagation, source attribution, HMR/disposed parity, and advanced-production channel behavior.
- Reconcile the Spec 009 row and links with emit-error-both! and the resolved runtime vocabulary.
- Wire actual HMR/disposed records into the schema check.
- Add a focused advanced/goog.DEBUG=false proof: exactly one always-on record and zero trace events.

Do not invent a second schema system or alter runtime semantics in this documentation/schema slice. Sequence its Spec 009 edit with rf2-vxgfnd.227 to avoid a hot-zone conflict.
acceptance_criteria:
- The new follow-up, not closed rf2-gg3om8, owns and lands the omitted slice.
- :rf.error/observation-on-change-failed has one canonical per-category schema matching actual HMR and disposed records.
- Spec 006 defines all classification, containment, drain, attribution, and channel semantics implemented by #5836.
- Spec 009 names emit-error-both! and agrees with the schema/runtime arms.
- Structural removal or required-key/channel mutations fail a catalogue-to-schema/record validation gate.
- Advanced production proves one always-on record, zero diagnostic trace events, full sibling drain, and unchanged original first escape behavior.
- No runtime behavior, new category, public API, or parallel schema vocabulary is introduced.

title: Finish frame-root/frame-provider reconciliation in final-state and frozen-compat surfaces
description:
## Problem

PR #5833 at exact authored head cf3ad3cf8ff47e3202cb309de743e6b6b0bd597c closed rf2-vxgfnd.110 as a residue-zero reconciliation of the ratified frame-root/frame-provider split, but active final-state material still teaches or freezes the retired merged-provider model.

Confirmed contradictions on current origin/main:

- skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-2-impl-order.md:177 tells a fresh port implementor to build one config-shaped frame-provider whose {:id ...} arm ENSUREs and whose {:frame ...} arm SCOPEs.
- ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/03-reactivity-and-ownership.md:302-305 says the checked-in spec/implementation still carries the merged provider and that landing the split remains an outstanding gate.
- ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/README.md:51-56 likewise presents R-7 reconciliation as outstanding.
- ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/drafts/reagent-compat-boundary.md:161-165 says a frozen-tier frame-provider {:id ...} can ENSURE; line 311 asks the frozen compatibility suite to retain frame-provider SCOPE + ENSURE fixtures.
- ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/prep/w9-ci-matrix-disposition.md:26 repeats that incorrect SCOPE+ENSURE fixture roster.
- ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/drafts/spec-004A-reagent-compat-appendix.md:86-100 and reagent-compat-boundary.md:344-360 retain frame-provider in the frozen facade table but omit the already-live Reagent frame-root component. If S7 follows those tables literally, the frozen stock-Reagent tier loses its canonical ENSURE/boot boundary even though the ruling freezes stock Reagent rather than shrinking it.
- spec/API.md:280 and :303 (plus the UIx/Helix adapter READMEs) say use-current-frame returns the no-provider sentinel whenever no frame-provider is above. frame-root installs the same React context provider, so beneath a frame-root with no frame-provider the correct result is the frame id, not the sentinel.

These are not historical preference notes. The synthesis suite is the authoritative implementation program, the implementor skill directs ports, the 004A/compat drafts define the S7 frozen tier, and the API rows describe current behavior. A reader can implement an API the runtime rejects with :rf.error/frame-provider-given-id or accidentally delete/under-test the retained root at S7.

## Deliverable

Finish the split across these active surfaces without changing the frozen public API:

- State the invariant everywhere as frame-provider {:frame ...} = SCOPE only and frame-root {:id ...} = ENSURE.
- Preserve the important timing distinction: current Reagent/UIx/Helix frame-root is commit-owned/two-pass; re-frame.ui frame-root ENSURE is extracted into host preflight.
- Remove stale outstanding-gate/history wording from final-state synthesis prose, while retaining explicitly labelled decision history where appropriate.
- Freeze both Reagent boundary components in 004A and the compatibility roster: frame-provider SCOPE plus frame-root ENSURE. Ensure both boundary directions can acquire the shared React context under either component.
- Correct use-current-frame documentation to say the sentinel occurs only when neither frame-provider nor frame-root supplies context, and pin that behavior through each applicable adapter before UIx/Helix deletion.
- Reconcile any active cross-spec ripple/diff-ready draft entry that still describes the split as future work.

Do not retain a compatibility {:id} arm on frame-provider, change root timing, or delete UIx/Helix/slim early. Explicit negative/did-you-mean fixtures and genuinely historical EP text remain valid.

## Proof

Run a classified repository grep for merged-provider and frame-provider-ENSURE claims. Review every remaining hit as final contract, explicit history, or negative diagnostic. Run docs/links/skills gates and the narrow adapter frame-context fixtures. The final S7 compatibility tables and W9 fixture roster must name both retained stock-Reagent boundary components exactly.
acceptance_criteria:
- No active positive guidance spells ENSURE as frame-provider {:id ...}; every final-state surface teaches roots ensure, providers scope.
- The synthesis README and 03 section no longer claim the already-landed split is an outstanding gate.
- The 004A/reagent-compat retained-surface table includes re-frame.core/frame-root, and the frozen suite separately covers frame-provider SCOPE and frame-root ENSURE.
- The compat boundary text proves exported re-frame.ui views acquire frame context under either retained Reagent boundary without adding a root or re-seeding.
- use-current-frame docs name absence of both provider and root; a focused adapter test returns the frame id beneath frame-root and the sentinel beneath neither boundary.
- Classified residue grep, docs/link/skill gates, and applicable adapter tests are green.
- No frozen API delta, provider compatibility arm, runtime timing change, or early adapter deletion is introduced.

Docs-only reconciliation of final-state + frozen-compat surfaces: spec/API.md (uix/helix use-current-frame rows), docs/api/re-frame.adapter.{uix,helix}.md, docs/core/25-from-re-frame-v1.md, spec/007-Stories.md. Deferred to an implementation-lane follow-up (respected 'do NOT touch implementation/**'): adapter READMEs + adapter source docstrings still carry the stale use-current-frame sentinel wording, plus the acceptance-criterion focused adapter test. No spec/002 edit needed. skills/re-frame2-implementor left out of this lane's scope. All runnable doc gates + api-md-check green; mkdocs runs in CI. Leaving OPEN for the mayor.

title: Project inline sub traces from captured image-local classification
description:
## Problem

PR #5820 at exact authored head `97f64ae8f125edef9a648a3dc4e29581cded9247` made inline image metadata available to subscription validation, but `:rf.sub/run` trace projection still re-resolves classification through the ambient registrar instead of using the exact metadata captured by the reaction.

A current-main reproduction registers a real image-local sub with `{:sensitive [[:token]]}` and returns `{:token "SECRET" :public 1}`. Subscribers correctly receive the raw value, but the emitted `:rf.sub/run` tag contains the raw secret at `:rf.sub/value`. A namespace/global `reg-sub` control correctly emits `{:token :rf/redacted :public 1}`.

The reaction already captures the authoritative image-local `sub-meta` for schema validation (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc`), but trace building later resolves classification through the registrar (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc`). One-shot dereference can occur after the frame-generation binding has ended, and ongoing reactions can outlive HMR/incarnation changes. The trace may therefore see no image metadata or a conflicting global registration. This leaks values the author explicitly classified as sensitive and can misapply `:large` projection as well.

No all-status bead matches image-local sub classification, sensitive inline sub traces, or `:rf.sub/run` re-resolution. The closed source bead `rf2-vxgfnd.111` did not cover classification projection and cannot be amended.

## Expected behavior

Every subscription computation projects observability from the exact registration metadata captured for that reaction. Image-local classification is isolated by frame/incarnation and remains stable for the lifetime of the reaction; it never falls back to a same-id global registration.
design:
Carry the exact captured `sub-meta` or a pre-normalized immutable classification projection through the `:rf.sub/run` trace-building chokepoint. Do not re-resolve the current global or frame registrar during emission: that remains wrong after the frame binding unwinds and across HMR/incarnation replacement.

Keep raw values available to the subscriber; redact only observability/egress. Reuse the canonical classification projector for `:sensitive` and `:large`. Cover one-shot and ongoing reactive paths, including tools that consume the mediated trace. Do not add UI-specific trace logic or a compatibility branch.
acceptance_criteria:
- An image-local sub declaring sensitive output paths emits `:rf/redacted` at those paths in `:rf.sub/value` while subscribers still receive the raw value.
- Declared large paths emit the canonical large marker and do not expose the original large value.
- A conflicting global registration with the same sub id cannot supply or override image-local classification.
- Two live frames using the same sub id with different classifications remain isolated.
- An existing reaction retains its captured classification across HMR/incarnation replacement; a successor uses the new registration's classification.
- Both one-shot subscription and ongoing reactive recomputation are covered, along with the mediated observation/Xray-facing output.
- A mutation that restores ambient registrar re-resolution fails the focused fixtures; core subscription, trace, image, schema, and UI gates remain green.
notes: PR #5855 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5855) opened 2026-07-14; head bef474dc83. Repro re-verified live on origin/main before fix. Gates green (core JVM 1947t, ui JVM 475t, CLJS node 9313t, fast-pr spine PASS). Left OPEN for mayor to merge.

title: Normalize inline sub metadata through the canonical registrar contract
description:
## Problem

PR #5820 at exact authored head `97f64ae8f125edef9a648a3dc4e29581cded9247` fixed inline `:reg-sub` schema visibility by projecting the inline metadata map directly onto the runnable descriptor in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc` `lower-inline-sub`. That projection does not pass through the metadata normalization/validation contract used by public `reg-sub`.

Executed exact-head and current-main counterexamples show the paths now disagree:

- `reg-sub` with retired `{:spec :int}` throws `:rf.error/retired-registration-key`, while an equivalent inline image registration assembles and retains `:spec`.
- `reg-sub` with malformed classification such as `{:sensitive :wrong}` throws `:rf.error/bad-classification`, while inline assembly and subscription succeed.
- With production/debug disabled, the public registrar strips documentation metadata such as `:doc`; the inline runnable descriptor retains it at top level.

The divergence violates EP-0026's requirement that inline registration follow the same registrar contract, neither looser nor stricter, and Conventions' fail-loud retired-key rule. It also creates a production-efficiency regression by retaining dev-only documentation in inline runtime descriptors.

No all-status bead matches inline registrar normalization, retired registration keys in images, or inline classification validation. The closed source bead `rf2-vxgfnd.111` established schema visibility but cannot be amended.

## Expected behavior

Inline and public subscription registrations accept, reject, normalize, and elide the same metadata. Image assembly must remain side-effect-free with respect to the global registrar, and runtime-owned descriptor slots must continue to win over user metadata.
acceptance_criteria:
- Public and inline `{:spec :int}` both fail with `:rf.error/retired-registration-key` naming `:schema` as the replacement.
- Public and inline malformed `:sensitive`/`:large` declarations both fail with `:rf.error/bad-classification`; valid declarations survive identically.
- Unknown bare-key warnings and namespaced extension behavior match public `reg-sub`.
- Production inline runnable descriptors do not retain `:doc`; development descriptors do.
- Runtime-owned runnable slots cannot be overridden by metadata, while nested original metadata/provenance remains available for inspection.
- A failed image assembly is not cached; correcting the metadata permits a subsequent assembly.
- Mutation tests that restore direct raw-metadata `assoc` fail, and affected JVM/CLJS image, registrar, schema, and UI override gates remain green.

title: Rewrite reactive sites in computed function positions
description:
## Problem

PR #5821 at exact authored head `355f9beb112611d9f13d5569684a7562732eb1aa` replaced the side-effect expression walk with a returned-form rewriter so every finite lexical `ui/sub` becomes a site-bearing internal call. One evaluated Clojure position is still skipped: the function/callee position of a generic invocation.

In `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/analyze.cljc`, the generic call branch preserves `head` verbatim and rewrites only `(rest f)`, with the comment that a call head "is not an evaluated argument and cannot itself contain a reactive site." Clojure evaluates a computed callee before its arguments, so that premise is false.

Executed current-main reproduction using the real rewriter:

```
input  = ((if (re-frame.ui/sub [:which]) inc dec) 1)
output = ((if (re-frame.ui/sub [:which]) inc dec) 1)
sites  = {:subs [] ...}
```

A defview expression such as:

```
(str ((if (ui/sub [:operation]) inc dec) 1))
```

contains one explicit, finite, render-time reactive site, but the compiler emits no sid and declares the view sub-free. At runtime the surviving public `ui/sub` fails as an unlowered call; optimized output can also choose the sub-free component shape. Computed map/vector/set/function operators have the same skipped evaluated position.

This violates the source bead's requirement to thread rewritten forms through every opaque evaluated position and the compiler's finite-ownership manifest authority. It is not the intentional fail-loud case of a helper or opaque macro hiding a read: the `ui/sub` call is syntactically present to the compiler.

No all-status bead matches "call head", "function position", "computed callee", or this unindexed-reactive shape. Open `rf2-vxgfnd.112` documents the closed macro grammar; it does not repair analyzer traversal.

## Expected behavior

Every evaluated expression position is either rewritten under the correct lexical/phase rules or rejected didactically. A visible render-time `ui/sub` in a computed callee must never silently disappear from the site manifest.
design:
Fix the generic invocation traversal narrowly:

- Preserve simple symbol/keyword call heads that cannot contain a nested site.
- Recursively rewrite computed seq/vector/map/set callee forms under a stable `:callee` expression-path token, before rewriting arguments, matching Clojure evaluation order.
- Reuse existing binder/deferred/macro rules. If an immediately-invoked fn or other callee shape cannot be proven finite, reject it with the existing didactic recovery rather than allowing an invisible site.
- Keep sid construction compiler-owned and deterministic; do not add runtime dynamic sites or macro interpretation.
- Ensure the returned rewritten callee is actually threaded into the emitted invocation on both JVM and CLJS hosts.
acceptance_criteria:
- CLJ and CLJS compiler fixtures cover a computed `if` callee containing one `ui/sub`; exactly one deterministic sid appears in the manifest and emitted internal call.
- Mounted/headless fixtures show the selected function receives the reactive value, ownership is acquired once, movement rerenders once, and unmount releases once.
- Computed vector/map/set callee expressions containing visible subs are either correctly indexed or explicitly rejected; none survives as public `ui/sub` with an empty sub manifest.
- An immediately-invoked fn with a reactive body follows a documented finite rule or fails didactically; it never becomes an invisible dynamic site.
- A mutation restoring verbatim generic call heads fails the compiler/runtime fixtures.
- Advanced output selects the ownership-bearing ViewCell shape when the only sub is in the callee; scalar sid/direct-call cost and G-1/G-13/elision gates remain green.
- No public API, runtime site registry, generic macroexpansion, or compatibility fallback is added.
notes:
PR #5833 exact head cf3ad3cf8ff47e3202cb309de743e6b6b0bd597c makes this implementation defect a direct normative contradiction: spec/004-Views.md:194-196 now says an ordinary call head is not evaluated and cannot contain a reactive site. Clojure does evaluate a computed callee. The fix for this bead must also revise that paragraph to distinguish simple symbol/keyword heads from recursively analyzed computed callee expressions; otherwise the code can be repaired while Spec 004 continues to teach a false evaluation law. No separate docs bead was filed because this is the same causal defect and this bead is OPEN/not in progress.

title: Fence ViewCell publication against HMR authority changes during commit
description:
## Problem

Merged PR #5817 (`dfe01fcd6a284b7c484413fdf3f5ba77ed1a1263`) made Fast Refresh use a stable component shell and reject captures whose body revision was already stale when ViewCell `commit!` began. The authority check is performed only once, before several callback-capable operations.

On current main, `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc` checks the cell generation and `registered-view-revision` at commit step 1, then invokes the `:pre-acquire` barrier, calls `obs/acquire!` for staged targets, performs evidence reads, invokes the `:post-acquire` barrier, and publishes the captured dependency/value set. Subscription/cache construction and the explicit barriers can synchronously register a newer body revision after the one stale check. No final HMR-authority fence runs before publication.

Deterministic counterexample:

1. Register view revision 0 and form a revision-0 capture with a subscription site.
2. Begin `commit!`; step 1 accepts revision 0.
3. At `:pre-acquire`, from an acquisition/cache callback, or at `:post-acquire`, synchronously register the same view at revision 1.
4. `commit!` stages ownership and publishes the revision-0 capture instead of returning `:stale`.
5. The old render temporarily owns dependencies despite the HMR contract that a stale capture obtains no ownership.

The independent #5817 correctness audit reproduced the shape at the exact head and verified it remains on current main. `rf2-vxgfnd.105` owns binding a commit to its exact selected render capture before entry; it does not cover authority changing during commit. `rf2-vxgfnd.147` is an Xray evidence publication race, not HMR body authority.

## Expected behavior

A capture must remain authoritative through the linearization point that publishes ownership. If body authority changes at any callback-capable point during staging, newly staged leases are rolled back and the prior committed state remains untouched.
design:
Add one final authority fence at the narrowest correct publication boundary:

- After all staging, evidence reads, and callback-capable hooks, immediately before the state publication, re-read both the cell generation and authoritative registered revision.
- If either differs from the capture, release only newly staged leases in reverse acquisition order, preserve all prior committed leases/values/lifecycle, and return `:stale`.
- Ensure no callback-capable operation exists between this final check and publication. If that cannot be guaranteed, use the existing HMR publication token/revision as a CAS predicate rather than adding locks.
- Do not release retained prior ownership or advance the cell merely because a stale candidate was rejected.
- Keep the production direct-view path lean; the authoritative registry check remains DEV/HMR-only and must elide under `goog.DEBUG=false`.

Prefer one final check over peppering revalidation after each callback.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deterministic CLJ and CLJS fixtures re-register the same view at `:pre-acquire`, from an acquisition/cache callback, and at `:post-acquire`; every candidate returns `:stale` and publishes no stale dependency/value state.
- Cover both same-hook-signature body replacement and changed-hook-signature remount generations.
- Every newly staged lease is released exactly once in reverse order; staged refcounts return to baseline.
- Prior committed leases, values, revision, and lifecycle remain unchanged on rejection.
- A normal unchanged-authority commit still publishes once and retains acquire-before-release ordering.
- A mutation deleting/moving the final fence before a callback-capable operation makes the fixture red.
- Advanced production output contains no HMR registry lookup/fence or additional hot-path bookkeeping; existing G-1/G-13/elision gates remain green.
close_reason: Merged PR #5862 (fence ViewCell publication against HMR body-authority change at the final publication boundary — two-point authority check; debug-gated, DCEs from production; red-before-fix at pre/post-acquire; CI green). Spec follow-up filed.

title: Require G-13 to execute each V workload exactly once
description:
## Problem

The G-13 runner merged in PR #5815 at exact head `21c80416184a9fdd7080a024747922696e8632ca` does not prove that both required graph sizes actually ran. `implementation/scripts/run-ui-g13.cjs` checks metadata `sizes: [100,500]`, but validates each result row only as a member of that allowed set and then requires two equal count projections. It does not require one unique result for each size.

A concrete false green is to replace the V=500 result with a deep copy of the V=100 result while leaving `sizes: [100,500]`. Both rows are individually allowed, there are still two equal projections, and validation passes. A fixture or harness regression that executes V=100 twice can therefore omit the scaling arm while G-13 still claims V-independence.

This is distinct from whether the observed projection is strong enough: even a perfect projection proves no V-scaling statement if one workload never ran. No existing open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead owns this exact roster-cardinality defect.

## Expected behavior

The report and validator must prove an exact one-to-one workload roster: one independently executed V=100 result and one independently executed V=500 result, with no duplicate, missing, or extra sizes, before comparing their projections.
design:
Tighten the existing runner schema directly:

- Validate the result-size roster as exact set/order equality with the declared required sizes.
- Require each size exactly once and reject duplicate, missing, unexpected, non-numeric, or metadata-only rows.
- Keep execution identity simple: the browser fixture should stamp its actual mounted V into each result; the runner should not synthesize it from expected metadata.
- Add runner self-tests/mutations for duplicate-100, duplicate-500, missing-size, extra-size, swapped order if order is normative, and a forged metadata-only row.
- Do not add a general schema library or benchmark framework for this two-workload contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- A normal run contains exactly one independently executed V=100 row and one V=500 row.
- Duplicate-100, duplicate-500, missing-100, missing-500, extra-size, and forged-metadata mutations each fail validation deterministically.
- Projection equality is evaluated only after the exact workload roster is proven.
- Each row's V is produced by the mounted fixture's actual graph size, not copied from runner expectations.
- Existing C=8/Q=8 count, DOM, one-commit-batch, production-elision, evidence upload, and cleanup checks remain green.
- No production source/API or timing threshold changes.

title: Make G-13 production-elision checks causal to real instrumentation
description:
## Problem

PR #5815's G-13 advanced companion claims to prove that benchmark counters, React Profiler work, result globals, and debug evidence are absent from production. The current proof is not causally attached to the machinery it names.

In `implementation/ui/g13/re_frame/ui/g13/fixture.cljs`, the scanned counter/Profiler/debug sentinel strings are colocated in one standalone bench-registration branch. The actual counter mutations live in `count!`; the actual `React.Profiler` wrapper and callback live in the separate `profiled` render path. `implementation/scripts/run-ui-g13.cjs` scans only the detached strings and its mutation tooth appends a sentinel to an already-built blob.

Two production leaks can therefore remain green:

1. Make `count!` unconditional while leaving the standalone sentinel branch behind its folded guard. Counter atoms and updates ship and execute, but no scanned marker survives.
2. Always render the Profiler wrapper while leaving its named marker in the folded registration branch. Profiler/callback work ships, ordinary DOM is unchanged, and the bundle scan still passes.

The paired adversarial audits of merged PR #5815 at exact head `21c80416184a9fdd7080a024747922696e8632ca` independently identified this false proof. Open `rf2-qmb01i` concerns the canonical general bundle-isolation checker and artefacts; it does not own this custom G-13 fixture/runner or its detached sentinels.

## Expected behavior

Every elision assertion must be causally owned by the exact executable branch it claims is absent. A real source mutation that makes counter or Profiler work unconditional must make the advanced gate red. The ordinary production build remains instrumentation-free and exceptionally lean.
design:
Repair the existing G-13 companion without building a general bundle-analysis framework:

- Put independent, unique proof tokens in the actual counter mutation path, Profiler wrapper/callback path, result-global publication, and debug-evidence path.
- Use same-optimizer reachable controls to prove the scanner could see each token when the owning branch is enabled.
- Compile real source mutants that make the counter path and Profiler path unconditional; run the normal advanced build/scanner and require red.
- Treat appending a token to an already-built blob only as a parser/unit check, not as proof of source elision.
- Prefer structural output checks that remain stable under Closure optimization; do not retain names merely to make scanning easy.
- Keep all fixture-only proof machinery behind the existing bench-local define and outside ordinary production paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- An unconditional-`count!` source mutant makes the real G-13 advanced elision check fail.
- An always-Profiler source mutant makes the real G-13 advanced elision check fail while ordinary DOM remains otherwise valid.
- Result-global and debug-evidence owners have independent causal tokens/controls; deleting or leaking one cannot be masked by another branch's marker.
- The development/control build proves each checked owner and marker is reachable under the same optimizer configuration used for the control.
- The unmutated `goog.DEBUG=false` advanced output contains no counter mutation, Profiler wrapper/callback, result-global publication, debug evidence, or their causal proof tokens.
- G-13 behavioral counts still express all queued writes followed by one read/render batch; no UIx/Helix dependency, production counter, public API, or broad analyzer is added.

title: Make G-13 causally prove V-independent candidate work
description:
## Problem

G-13, merged in PR #5815 at authored head `21c80416184a9fdd7080a024747922696e8632ca`, claims to falsify the cost law that push work is proportional to the affected set C and independent of total mounted views V. Its current projection counts enrollments, revisions, recomputations, component bodies, commits, and DOM outcomes. Equal downstream counts at V=100 and V=500 do not observe the candidate work used to discover those eight affected cells.

A deterministic counterexample remains green: add a redundant traversal of every member of the private live-cell/root membership at the start of invalidation, then enroll the same C=8 cells normally. The implementation has become O(V) per movement, but all gated 8/8/0/1 projections and DOM assertions remain identical. Timing is intentionally evidence-only, so it cannot close this proof gap.

The advertised mutation teeth also edit completed JSON projections rather than executing mutated scheduler/owner/equality/commit code. Those edits prove the validator rejects bad reports; they do not prove a real source regression produces a bad report. The paired #5815 audits independently found this mismatch between the source bead's structural claim and the gate's actual observation.

This finding does not question the correct batching law: Q=8 queued events perform all writes first and then one coalesced read/render batch. It questions whether G-13 can detect additional hidden work around that law.

## Expected behavior

G-13 must deterministically fail when the real invalidation/owner-selection path scans all V mounted cells while still notifying only C affected cells. If that is not the desired proof scope, the contract must be narrowed honestly to V-independent observable downstream notifications/renders rather than total push work.
design:
Add the smallest gate-local, production-erased witness at the actual candidate-iteration/fan-out choke point:

- Count real candidate inspections or equivalent bounded owner-selection work in the G-13 build only.
- Keep the witness behind the existing bench-local define and prove it absent from advanced `goog.DEBUG=false` output.
- Compare the witness across V=100 and V=500 for the same C=8 movement.
- Replace or supplement JSON tampering with a real source mutant that scans every live cell/owner but enrolls only C; compile and run the browser gate and verify it fails.
- Keep wall-clock measurements evidence-only. Do not introduce timing thresholds, runtime-global counters, a benchmark framework, or hot-path bookkeeping in ordinary builds.
- Preserve one read/render batch after write-side drain-to-quiescence.

If there is no narrow causal seam that can be observed without contaminating production, amend the G-13 claim to exactly what the existing projection proves and record the stronger total-work property as unproven rather than pretending timing establishes it.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real source mutant that enumerates all V mounted cells/owners while enrolling only C=8 makes G-13 deterministically red.
- The normal V=100 and V=500 runs expose one explicitly named candidate-work projection whose expected value depends on C, not V.
- Immediate/per-write read-side flushing, V-wide enrollment, stable-parent fan-out, and multiple commit-batch mutants run real mutated code and each fail the gate; report-only JSON tampering is not credited as source-level mutation proof.
- The normal path still proves Q=8 write-side events settle before C=8 affected bodies render in exactly one root commit batch.
- The witness and all gate instrumentation are absent from the advanced production bundle, with a same-optimizer reachable control.
- No production API, runtime-global diagnostic collection, wall-clock threshold, UIx/Helix dependency, or broad benchmark framework is added.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5860 (worker/g13-hardening @ f375f4bf45). SCOPE DECISION (mayor): criterion 1 (pure V-wide membership SCAN that inspects V but delivers only C) is NOT closed by this PR — a pure scan has no observable downstream effect, so no count and no threshold-free timing can catch it; the only causal seam is a production-erased counter at the observation-port fan-out choke point (core/substrate/observation.cljc), out of this worktree's scope (concurrent owner). Per the bead's explicit fallback, the claim is narrowed honestly (gate :proof-scope = 'v-independent delivered push work; pure candidate scan is timing-evidence-only') and the named V-independent candidate-work axis port-fan-out=C*Q is added. Production-side witness filed as rf2-vxgfnd.250. Left open for mayor review/merge.

title: Run G-13 for core changes that can alter re-frame.ui push economics
description:
## Problem

Merged PR #5815 (`21c80416184a9fdd7080a024747922696e8632ca`) introduced G-13 as the end-to-end mounted falsifier for re-frame.ui push economics, but the changed-surface classifier does not schedule it for core-only runtime changes. `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` arms Node/browser work for `implementation/core/*` without setting `ui_gates=true`; `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs `cljs-ui-g13` only when `ui_gates` is true.

This is a causal coverage hole, not merely missing convenience. G-13 traverses core dispatch/drain, frame scheduling, the observation port, ViewCell enrollment, uSES, compiled bodies, and React commit. A PR changing only `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc`, router drain behavior, or frame scheduling can introduce V-wide fan-out or split write/read batching while the one gate intended to falsify those regressions is skipped. The required-check aggregator accepts that skip.

Executed at the reviewed head and current main:

```
report-changed-surfaces.sh implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc
ui_gates=false
```

The paired adversarial completeness and correctness audits independently found the same gap. `rf2-vxgfnd.90` is the closed analogous UI/browser routing repair; open `rf2-vxgfnd.137` concerns rename endpoints, not core-to-G-13 routing.

## Expected behavior

Any change to a source that can affect the real G-13 path schedules G-13. All queued events still complete their write side before the single coalesced read/render batch; the gate must be present to catch violations of that contract.
design:
Use the existing changed-surface classifier, without inventing a dependency graph service:

- Set `ui_gates=true` for the bounded core dependency surface. Conservatively classifying all `implementation/core/*` is acceptable if a smaller explicit list would be brittle.
- Add classifier self-tests for representative observation-port, router/drain, frame/scheduler, and unrelated non-runtime paths.
- Keep G-13 surface-gated; do not make every documentation-only PR pay the browser gate.
- Preserve the required-check aggregator's skip semantics for genuinely irrelevant changes.

The verification PR must show a classifier mutation or pre-fix run going red/missing and the corrected classifier scheduling the real job.
acceptance_criteria:
- Representative core observation, router/drain, and frame/scheduler paths report `ui_gates=true`.
- A core-only PR changing each representative path visibly executes `cljs-ui-g13`; it is not accepted as a skipped required check.
- A deterministic G-13 source mutant reachable only through `implementation/core/*` makes that scheduled job red.
- Unrelated docs/tool-only paths retain their existing skip behavior.
- Changed-surface self-tests, G-13, and the required-check aggregation are green after the repair.
- No production API, runtime counter, timing threshold, or UIx/Helix dependency is added.

title: Make re-frame.ui adapter flush-render! settle pending ViewCells before returning
description:
## Problem

The first-party `re-frame.ui/adapter` inherits the generic React `:flush-render!` implementation, which only runs `(react-dom/flushSync f)`. Compiled ViewCell invalidation does not notify React inside `f`: it marks cells dirty and schedules a later microtask. Therefore `flush-render!` can return while the compiled view's DOM is still stale, contrary to the substrate/draft contract that synchronous render flush settles queued writes and React work before returning.

The current conformance fixture exercises `flush-render!` with a static React element. The mounted G-13/Tier-3 proofs use `ui.test/flush!`, which explicitly flushes the ViewCell registry. Neither proves the adapter verb against a reactive compiled view.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Initialize `re-frame.ui/adapter` and mount a compiled sub-bearing view.
2. Call `(:flush-render! ui/adapter)` with a thunk that performs `dispatch-sync!` and changes the subscribed value.
3. The router write completes inside the thunk, but `reactive/mark-dirty!` only arms the global ViewCell microtask.
4. The inherited `react-dom/flushSync` sees no React update scheduled inside its callback and returns.
5. Read the DOM immediately: it still shows the old value and the ViewCell remains pending.
6. Let the queued microtask run; only then does `flush-pending!` advance the snapshot and React update the DOM.

## Expected Behavior

For the first-party adapter, `flush-render!` returns only after synchronous writes, pending ViewCell snapshot notifications, and the resulting React commit are settled according to its closed adapter contract. An open router drain still fails loudly rather than publishing a partial read side.

## Actual Behavior

The generic static-React flush returns before the first-party ViewCell scheduler publishes its pending read side.

## Provenance

Independently reproduced by the completeness and correctness audits of merged PR #5814 at exact head `797431e8e283b63be52309e52c394697629781c8`. Current main still inherits the generic `spine.cljs` flush and overrides only adapter disposal. Full all-status search found no active semantic owner; closed `rf2-40a84`/`rf2-vk79g` predate the ViewCell scheduler.
design:
Override only the first-party adapter's `:flush-render!` at its composition boundary. Run the supplied thunk and the pending ViewCell registry publication inside the React synchronous commit boundary, then continue to a bounded fixed point if a commit legitimately dirties more cells.

Reuse the existing internal registry/open-drain guards used by `ui.test/flush!`; do not create a second scheduler, expose a new public API, or change the generic React adapter contract for stacks that do not use ViewCells. Preserve the write-all-queued-events then one read/render law: this is not a per-epoch renderer.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real mounted compiled sub-bearing view changed by `dispatch-sync!` inside `(:flush-render! ui/adapter)` exposes the new DOM before the call returns.
- The relevant ViewCell dirty registry/pending flag is empty on return and no redundant later microtask causes a second render.
- Multiple writes performed by one queued drain still settle as one read/render batch, not one render per epoch/event.
- Legitimate commit-triggered re-dirty work reaches a bounded fixed point or fails through the existing non-quiescence diagnostic; it cannot loop silently.
- Invoking the operation inside an open drain fails before publishing partial UI state.
- Static/no-op flush behavior, exception propagation, sibling roots, and adapter dispose/re-init remain correct.
- The mounted regression fails against the inherited pre-fix implementation and runs in normal browser CI.
close_reason: Merged PR #5903 (flush-render! settles pending ViewCells: adapter overrides :flush-render! at composition boundary — runs thunk + reactive/flush-pending! in the synchronous commit + drains re-dirty to a bounded fixed point via hoisted guard-open-drain!; adapter inherited bare flushSync so dispatch-sync returned with stale DOM; red-before-fix DOM fixture; CI green)

title: Make every digest-carrier read reject the hookless sentinel
description:
## Problem

The hookless real-Shadow proof added by PR #5813 accepts runtime exposure of the raw digest sentinel as evidence that publication failed closed. In Shadow `:script` loader mode, however, the top-level namespace-load throw is reported as `pageerror` and later independent scripts continue. The later base script installs `__rf2ReadDigest`, and `digest-carrier/current` returns `__RF2_UI_DIGEST_XX__` without revalidation.

That means the green fixture proves the runtime continues after the one-shot error and exposes an invalid build identity. Any later descriptor read can stamp the sentinel into `:build-digest`. The browser has not failed closed; it has emitted one diagnostic and retained a callable invalid identity source.

The fixture's last-known-good claim is also non-causal: the hooked and hookless pages use separate configs, output/cache roots, processes, and globals. Their non-interference does not prove what happens when one accepted build lineage later loses its hook.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `cd implementation && npm run test:ui-digest-carrier` on current main.
2. Observe the hookless Shadow build raises the expected `pageerror`.
3. Observe the test then requires `__rf2ReadDigest()` to equal `__RF2_UI_DIGEST_XX__` and logs `rejected before publication`.
4. The accessor exists only because later base initialization continued after the error.
5. Replace the diagnostic read with an ordinary `current-build-digest`/descriptor read; `digest-carrier/current` returns the raw sentinel and `client.cljs` can stamp it into a complete descriptor.

## Expected Behavior

An unfinalized development digest is unavailable at every read boundary. Later scripts may continue under Shadow's loader, but no public/internal descriptor-producing operation can observe or publish the sentinel. A same-lineage hook-loss scenario either retains the last accepted digest under explicit authority or makes identity unavailable; it never creates a sentinel-stamped descriptor.

## Actual Behavior

Only namespace load validates the digest. Subsequent `current` calls return the sentinel, and the hookless test explicitly treats that raw value as success. The LKG assertion compares independent runtimes rather than a prior accepted build followed by hook loss.

## Provenance

Found independently in the completeness audit of merged PR #5813 at authored head `f32ef7c720848440d8614c1528c23c339d2fd394`. The carrier and harness remain unchanged on current main. Full all-status search found no duplicate: `rf2-vxgfnd.193` owns candidate activation/HMR authority, `.195` owns other real-host gates, and closed `.108` is the audited implementation claim.
design:
Make `digest-carrier/current` itself fail closed in development whenever its slot is not a finalized `bd1-*` digest. The namespace-load check may remain for an early diagnostic, but it cannot be the sole enforcement boundary.

Change the hookless browser fixture so any later digest or descriptor read must throw or remain unavailable; never assert the sentinel as a readable value. For LKG, either narrow/remove the independent-runtime preservation claim or add a same-build-lineage sequence that shares the actual cache/output/HMR authority and then removes the hook.

Keep advanced-production output unchanged: goog.DEBUG gating must allow Closure to remove carrier validation and diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria:
- Under real Shadow `:loader-mode :script`, later scripts may run after the page error, but every digest and descriptor read rejects or remains unavailable while the carrier is unfinalized.
- No complete descriptor can contain `__RF2_UI_DIGEST_XX__`; add an explicit negative assertion over descriptor publication.
- A configured hooked build still exposes the byte-identical finalized `bd1-*` digest in JVM snapshot, emitted bytes, and browser runtime.
- If LKG preservation remains claimed, a same-build-lineage accepted→hookless transition proves the accepted digest is retained under named authority or becomes explicitly unavailable; separate pages/configs are not used as causal proof.
- The pre-fix carrier causes the new read/descriptor fixture to fail.
- Advanced production elision remains byte/identifier clean and adds no runtime validation cost.

title: Revalidate exact ui/adapter generation after mount preflight before allocating a React root
description:
## Problem

PR #5808 closed public compiled-root admission while ui/adapter disposal runs, but fresh ui/mount checks that admission only before side-effecting frame preflight. run-preflight! can drain arbitrary synchronous initial-events and override code. If that code destroys the adapter, disposal sees no outer React root because it has not yet been allocated or registered. The outer mount then resumes, rechecks only root-id/container ownership, and calls React createRoot/register/render after terminal adapter disposal.

Current order in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/client.cljs is:

1. require-root-creation-open!
2. run-preflight!
3. check-root-claim!
4. createRoot, register-live-root!, render

check-root-claim! says nothing about adapter lifecycle. This reopens the exact disposed-adapter/live-public-root state rf2-vxgfnd.104 was intended to exclude, but through re-entrant preflight rather than a separate racing thread.

A boolean recheck is necessary but not fully sufficient. Preflight can destroy adapter generation A and synchronously initialize generation B. An outer mount admitted under A must not resume and publish a root into B merely because admission is open again. The fresh root attempt needs a private exact-generation receipt spanning preflight.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Initialize re-frame.ui/adapter generation A.
2. Start a fresh ui/mount whose frame plan initial-event calls rf/destroy-adapter! and returns normally.
3. Adapter disposal completes; no outer root is in live-roots yet.
4. run-preflight! returns and the outer call passes check-root-claim!.
5. Observe createRoot/register/render execute after adapter-disposed? became true, leaving DOM and a public live-root under a disposed adapter.

Variant:

1. The preflight callback destroys A and initializes generation B.
2. The outer A attempt resumes.
3. Without exact-generation validation it creates a root under B despite never being admitted by B.

## Deliverable

Introduce a small private adapter-admission receipt for fresh public root creation.

- Capture the exact live adapter generation before preflight.
- Immediately after every side-effecting fresh-path preflight and before the final root claim/createRoot boundary, require that admission is still open and the exact generation is unchanged.
- On terminal disposal or replacement, fail with the canonical typed adapter-disposed/stale-generation error before any React allocation, live-root registration, DOM mutation, ViewCell creation, or observation acquisition.
- Cleanup must remove only the attempt's frame-plan/evidence ownership; it must not affect generation B or a root created by re-entrant code.
- Apply the same receipt discipline to any hydrate/create-root path that can execute user/preflight code between admission and host allocation.
- Keep this private; no frozen public API change or compatibility layer.

This is a new follow-up to closed rf2-vxgfnd.104. Do not reopen or amend that completed bead.

## Evidence and Scope

title: Make frame construction a per-ID transaction through setup and final publication
description:
## Problem

Independent completeness and correctness audits of merged PR #5807 at authored head fce2d2aea14ab965437dab6f69c481daabaf54cd exposed one underlying construction-admission defect across five deterministic counterexamples. The current upsert path protects only fragments of construction: it uses a process-wide JVM monitor for decide/install, publishes a live-looking frame before trace policy and initial-events finish, and treats any raw registry key as re-registerable even when that record is lifecycle-dead. Arbitrary adapter callbacks and synchronous setup code can therefore enter the same API while ownership is only partial.

Consequences on current main:

1. A custom adapter can synchronously construct the same ID from make-state-container or make-derived-value. The nested call installs and returns success; the outer call resumes and overwrites it. Two constructors report success, one opaque container becomes abandoned, and final config is last-resume rather than one linear winner.
2. The single JVM create lock is held across arbitrary adapter callbacks. Constructing frame A while the adapter synchronously waits for unrelated frame B deadlocks because B cannot enter the global lock. This violates the established requirement that disjoint frame IDs proceed independently.
3. A second same-ID make during the first constructor's initial-events can surgically re-register and return success. If the original setup then fails, its rollback destroys the shared incarnation and erases the later successful config. Exact incarnation tokens alone do not distinguish these two config revisions because surgical re-registration preserves the drain-lock token.
4. In destroy's lifecycle-dead/pre-dissoc window, upsert reads the raw registry row, updates it because the key is present, and returns success even though public frame lookup is nil. Destroy then removes the row. The caller observed a successful frame construction/re-registration that was never live.
5. Current comments claim every constructed candidate is installed and no creator can seat the ID between absence check and assoc; the reproductions falsify those invariants on both the re-entrant JVM monitor and CLJS's direct call path.

This is not rf2-wduv35. That open bead carries exact incarnation tokens for later cleanup and rollback. Here a newer surgical config commit can share the same incarnation token, and the defect begins before ownership/final construction has been published. It is also not UI-only preflight bead rf2-vxgfnd.191.

## Steps to Reproduce

Same-ID adapter re-entry:

1. Install a conforming custom adapter whose first make-state-container call synchronously calls make-frame for the same ID.
2. Let the inner call complete and retain both returned values/containers.
3. Resume the outer callback.
4. Observe two successful results, two allocations, the outer record overwriting the inner record, and the inner opaque container no longer owned by any live frame.

Setup rollback race:

1. Start first construction of frame F with an initial-event that pauses before ultimately failing.
2. While F is published but setup is incomplete, call make-frame F with newer config and observe success.
3. Resume the first setup failure.
4. Observe the successful newer config is destroyed by the older constructor's rollback.

Lifecycle-dead false success:

1. Pause destroy-frame! after lifecycle-dead publication and before registry dissociation.
2. Call ordinary and must-create construction for the same ID.
3. Observe the current implementation can update the raw dead row and return success.
4. Resume destroy and observe the supposedly successful result disappears.

Disjoint-ID lock:

1. Begin construction of A and block inside an adapter callback waiting for construction of B.
2. Start B on another thread.
3. B cannot complete until A abandons the wait because both IDs share the same global create monitor.

## Deliverable

Replace the fragmented/global construction lock with one exact per-frame-ID construction transaction or reservation.

- Acquire the per-ID reservation before invoking any adapter constructor callback.
- Keep it through candidate allocation, authoritative registry install, auxiliary trace-policy publication, synchronous initial-events, created trace/hook publication, and either final success or complete rollback.
- Same-ID synchronous/re-entrant entry must fail promptly with a stable typed construction-in-progress outcome; it must never wait on itself. A different thread may wait/retry and then evaluate against the final committed state.
- Unrelated IDs must never share a blocking monitor and must be constructible concurrently, including from adapter callbacks.
- Do not allow a closing or lifecycle-dead raw record to take the surgical re-registration branch. Such a call must fail promptly or coordinate to a clean post-dissoc retry without spinning in a synchronous teardown callback.
- A failed provisional constructor must undo only its own provisional revision. No older setup failure may erase a later reported success.
- Final destroy registry removal should remain exact-incarnation/identity conditional as defense in depth.
- Preserve current successful refresh, must-create collision, setup exactly-once, frame-token, and trace-policy semantics. Do not add a public handle or compatibility layer.

Prefer the smallest internal state machine with explicit provisional/final states over more locks or timing conventions.

## Evidence and Scope

The narrow trace-policy correction in #5807 is sound and should remain. These gaps persist on current origin/main after later destroy-tail work. Relevant surfaces are implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc (new-frame-record, try-install-new-frame!, upsert-frame!, setup failure rollback, destroy tail), its custom-adapter and lifecycle tests, and the construction portions of Spec 002/Spec 006 only if the stable outcome requires contract text.
acceptance_criteria:
- A same-ID re-entry from make-state-container and from each make-derived-value callback has exactly one committed winner, no overwritten successful frame, no deadlock, and no leaked provisional reservation on CLJ and CLJS.
- A synchronous initial-event same-ID make cannot report success against a provisional construction; if outer setup fails, no later successful revision is erased.
- A barrier in the lifecycle-dead/pre-dissoc window proves ordinary and must-create calls neither mutate the dead raw row nor report a frame that destroy later removes; a clean retry after destroy succeeds.
- Disjoint frame IDs construct concurrently; an adapter callback constructing/waiting for B cannot be blocked by A's admission lock.
- Same-ID competing threads have a deterministic wait/retry or typed-loss result, while same-thread re-entry fails promptly and never self-deadlocks.
- Every success is fully initialized and policy-aligned when returned; every failure removes its exact reservation and all registry/policy residue.
- Existing guarded-CAS, must-create, trace-policy, setup-failure, destroy/recreate, and JVM/CLJS lifecycle suites remain green.
- New fixtures use barriers/latches or synchronous re-entry, never sleeps, and are demonstrated red before the fix and green after it.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option A — dispatch as specified. ONE core-owned per-frame-ID exact-owner reservation registry (frame-id -> opaque owner-token in a defonce atom; non-generational; identity-compared) IS the construction transaction, shared with rf2-vxgfnd.191 part C's preflight surface. Same-ID contention fails fast with typed :rf.error/frame-construction-in-progress on BOTH hosts and for BOTH same-thread re-entry and cross-thread contention — never wait, never queue. Lifecycle-dead raw rows fail fast (never take the surgical re-register branch; a clean post-destroy retry succeeds). Disjoint IDs proceed independently; frame-create-lock is removed once the reservation covers the cold-install path.

RATIONALE: Every recorded opinion (decision packet + CComposer here; CComposer + Codex on the .191 sibling) independently verified the five counterexamples on origin/main and converges on Option A with a shared per-ID reservation; re-verified frame.cljc directly (frame-create-lock ~L2175 guards only cold install; registry assoc publishes before trace-policy/setup/hooks; the re-register branch ~L2539 does a raw contains? that a lifecycle-dead row passes) — the premises hold. On the one split — cross-thread same-ID wait/retry (CComposer) vs uniform fail-fast (Codex) — fail-fast wins on all lenses: the reservation is held across arbitrary adapter callbacks and synchronous :initial-events, so a foreign thread blocking on it re-creates the unbounded-wait/deadlock class this bead exists to remove (callback-waits-for-contender cycle); uniform fail-fast gives identical CLJ/CLJS semantics (CLARITY/ELEGANCE) and satisfies the acceptance criterion's typed-loss branch (CORRECTNESS). Options B/C rejected: holding or deferring leaves double-success, phantom-success, and setup-rollback erasure reachable on CLJS's direct-call path with no adapter fiction required.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE: Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc (new-frame-record, try-install-new-frame!, upsert-frame!, setup rollback, destroy tail) + its custom-adapter/lifecycle tests.
(1) Reservation: acquire before ANY adapter constructor callback; hold through candidate allocation, authoritative install/re-register decision, trace-policy publication, synchronous :initial-events, and :rf.frame/created + hook publication; release in finally, removing the entry only while the owner-token is still identical. Owner-token: opaque identity plus diagnostic metadata (e.g. {:kind :construction, ...}); NO generation counter — generations already live on :drain-lock / policy-token / install-record :rev. The claim op should accept a SET of ids atomically in one CAS so .191's multi-plan preflight can consume the same primitive unchanged (core claims singletons). Provide a narrow internal seam for the future .191 UI->core hand-off (a preflight that owns F invokes the one intended make-frame for F without self-collision) but do NOT implement blanket dynamic same-owner reentrancy — an arbitrary nested public make-frame must still fail; exact hand-off semantics are ruled on .191, not here.
(2) Internal states (smallest state machine, per deliverable): reserved -> provisional (row installed / config staged, setup unfinished) -> final. A failed provisional constructor rolls back only its own revision (owner-token + policy-token/config-generation pin, not :drain-lock alone). With admission closed, counterexample #3 is prevented at entry; exact-token rollback stays as defence in depth, and destroy's registry removal stays exact-incarnation conditional.
(3) Lifecycle-dead: a raw row with :destroyed? true (or in destroy's claim window) must not take the re-register branch — prompt typed failure (either the in-progress row with a distinguishing detail or a distinct row; either way it needs a Spec 009 error-roster entry — note spec/009-Instrumentation.md is hot-zone if touched). must-create? meeting a dead raw key gets the lifecycle-dead failure, NOT :rf.error/frame-id-taken (a dead row is not a live collision). Ordinary retry after destroy completes succeeds. Destroy-frame! MAY hold the same reservation for its teardown window if that falls out cleanly, but a dead-row check is sufficient; do not spin/retry inside teardown callbacks.
(4) Remove frame-create-lock. JVM cross-thread safety = atomic CAS claim on the reservation map + existing guarded-CAS registry ops. Preserve unchanged: sequential surgical refresh (EP-0024 — the reservation rejects only overlap with an IN-FLIGHT transaction, never a make-frame against a completed live frame), must-create collision, setup exactly-once, frame-token, trace-policy semantics, and the :rf.error/frame-construction-in-handler guard.
(5) Acceptance/fixtures: red-then-green fixtures for all five counterexamples; barriers/latches or synchronous re-entry, never sleeps; include the disjoint-ID concurrent-construction proof regardless of .225's status. Existing race fixtures that asserted a mid-flight same-ID call succeeding as a refresh must be updated to assert the typed conflict — that behaviour IS the bug; all other listed suites stay green. New roster row :rf.error/frame-construction-in-progress in the Spec 009 companion. Sequencing: this bead is slice 1; .191 part C (slice 2) consumes the same reservation map — do not fork a second scheme there.
CROSS-REF (2026-07-15, orchestrator): rf2-vxgfnd.191 was ruled the same day — its ruling #2 consumes THIS bead's reservation registry as the one shared primitive (core-owned, non-generational, never-blocking, fail-fast) for both frame construction and UI preflight; .191 rules disjoint-proceed + typed overlap rejection + settlement fail-closed on foreign authority. Proof gate carried from .191: the .225 counterfixture must exist before the frame-create-lock removal merges. Expose the atomic multi-ID claim + narrow hand-off seam as already noted so .191 consumes it unchanged.
close_reason: Merged PR #5987 at exact independently reviewed head f139015f53b3e09978f9ce500a18236e96c3a2ee; full exact-head CI green, with deterministic pre/post-stage rollback race proofs and no lost updates.

title: Observe the final Shadow compile schedule before reconciling accepted view membership
description:
## Problem

PR #5806 derives and pre-touches the supposedly exact scheduled source set in the inherited re-frame.ui `:compile-prepare` hook before build-local prepare hooks run. Shadow deep-merges build-local hooks after `:build-defaults`, and later hooks are permitted to mutate build state and therefore the final compile schedule.

A later hook can remove retained output for a source, forcing that source to compile after re-frame.ui observed the schedule. If the source has removed its final `ui/defview`, macro expansion contributes no replacement row. Because the source was not pre-touched, commit-slice retains its old accepted row and whole-build digest membership. The build succeeds with a ghost view that no longer exists in source.

This contradicts the exact-source reconciliation and warm-cache completeness obligations of CLOSED rf2-n7ff9f. It persists on current main and has no exact tracker entry.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Accept a build in which `app.a` contributes one view and has retained Shadow output.
2. Edit `app.a` to remove its final `ui/defview`.
3. Configure a build-local `:compile-prepare` hook after the inherited re-frame.ui hook; have it remove `app.a` output so Shadow schedules that source for compilation.
4. The UI hook observes the earlier retained output and does not pre-touch `app.a`.
5. Compilation of the now-empty source emits no contribution; successful finish leaves the old `app.a` row and digest member accepted.

## Required Correction

Make re-frame.ui reconcile against Shadow's final authoritative compile schedule, not an intermediate hook-order snapshot. Either observe after all schedule-mutating prepare hooks, enforce and verify the UI observer as the final scheduler hook, or detect subsequent schedule changes and fail loudly. The solution must work for inherited and build-local hooks without relying on undocumented merge order.

Successful zero-declaration recompilation must replace the source's accepted contribution with absence. Preserve parallel/sequential source compilation and warm-cache reconstruction semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic real-Shadow fixture installs a later prepare hook that forces recompilation of a source whose final view was removed; the successful build evicts the source row and changes the accepted digest accordingly.
- The fixture covers both sequential and parallel compilation modes and fails against current main.
- Re-frame.ui observes or verifies the final authoritative scheduled source set; later schedule mutation cannot silently bypass pre-touching.
- A configuration whose final schedule cannot be observed fails loudly before accepted-state publication rather than retaining ghost declarations.
- Ordinary clean, incremental, watch, warm-cache, source-rename/removal, lazy-module, and duplicate-id gates remain green.
- No per-source runtime bookkeeping or production cost is introduced.
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5864 (fix committed; red-before-fix fixture confirmed; gates green). Left OPEN for the mayor to merge.
