title: Wire the native ViewCell evidence projection into the real Xray runtime
description:
## Problem

PR #5829 (head 557cf281c7f03d6a1ba127a4caf80c8eca6629cd; merge 6eee4e91c31ef120c63335465d8331ad64cc8136) introduces `re-frame.ui.tool.evidence`, but no actual Xray runtime or preload installs or consumes it. Runtime references outside the namespace are docstrings; `tools/xray` has no dependency on `implementation/ui`. The integration fixture calls `evidence/install!` and queries the projection itself, so it proves the seam in isolation rather than the bead's required Xray consumer.

Exact-head CI skipped both Story/Xray browser gates and JVM tools/xray. In a normal Xray session, driving a ViewCell invalidation leaves `installed-owner` nil and produces no Xray row, query, navigation, or rendered evidence. This leaves rf2-vxgfnd.75's original problem and AC1/AC6 materially open despite the seam being implemented.

## Required correction

Wire the smallest real native consumer into Xray's actual preload/runtime lifecycle. Xray must own install and uninstall with a stable identity, project the bounded schema through its existing data/API/UI model, and expose root/view/cell identity plus first/latest epoch, count, batches, causes, bounded targets, and honest loss metadata in a useful developer-facing query/render path.

Add the UI artefact dependency at the correct optional/tool boundary without pulling Xray into production applications or making re-frame.ui depend back on Xray. HMR/reinstall and tool shutdown must release the exact owner. Tool absence remains zero-cost; retiring UIx/Helix/slim receive no compatibility plumbing.

## Proof discipline

Launch the real Xray preload/browser runtime, not `evidence/install!` directly from the test. Drive an actual observation movement through ViewCell flush and assert the Xray query/rendered row, stable navigation identity, bounded fields, and teardown. A mutation removing the Xray install must fail. The Xray jobs must be selected by the PR classifier.
acceptance_criteria:
- The normal Xray preload/runtime installs the native evidence projection with an identity-owned lifecycle; no test-only direct install is required.
- A real observation-port movement -> ViewCell flush -> evidence projection appears in an actual Xray query/API/UI row with stable root/view/cell identity and bounded epoch/count/batch/cause/target/loss fields.
- HMR/reinstall, Xray shutdown, root teardown, and tool disable release the exact registration and references without clobbering another owner.
- A browser fixture launches the real Xray preload and fails if the install/consumer wiring is removed; relevant Xray browser/JVM gates run rather than skip.
- re-frame.ui does not depend on Xray, production apps do not acquire Xray transitively, and tool absence stays zero-cost.
- No UIx/Helix/reagent-slim compatibility path or duplicate evidence store is introduced.

title: Authenticate join folds and reaps to the exact child attempt and resolved join
description:
## Problem

PR #5779 verifies join reaps against live join state, but join completion and reap authority are still not bound to the exact spawned child attempt and resolution phase.

The join completion path identifies the logical child id and updates the current join's `:done`/`:failed` sets without proving that the reported actor id is the actor currently mapped to that child. After parent re-entry or child respawn, a stale completion from A1 can therefore fold into the new join attempt and make current child A2 appear completed. The subsequent “verified” reap derives A2 from the current mapping and destroys it with `:rf.machine/join-reaped` even though A2 never completed.

Observed counterexample: A1 and A2 have distinct actor ids; dispatching stale `[parent [:done :a A1]]` after re-entry updates the current join to `:done #{:a}` and later reaps A2.

Separately, the public reserved-fx reap carrier accepts any current child already present in `:done ∪ :failed` even when the join's `:resolved?` latch is false. An application can therefore invoke the internal cancellation-suppressing reap early during a still-waiting `:all` join. Checking only `:resolved?` would not fix stale-attempt poisoning; checking only actor identity would not close the pre-resolution authorization gap. They are one exact-authority contract.

## Required correction

Bind each accepted child terminal and later reap to the exact current join attempt and child actor identity. At minimum, the completion carrier must match the current join's parent/invoke identity, logical child id, and exact actor id/attempt before it may update `:done` or `:failed`. Stale prior-incarnation signals must be classified stale and perform no fold, terminal publication, resolution, or reap.

The internal reap must additionally require that this exact join attempt has resolved and that the named child terminal belongs to the same exact actor attempt. Derive the actor id and semantic reason from runtime-owned state; do not trust caller-supplied actor or reason. If existing public event/fx data cannot authenticate the attempt without guessable fields, use one small opaque internal attempt token carried through the existing private lifecycle path. Do not expose a new application-facing control surface.

Malformed, stale, current-but-unresolved, and cross-incarnation claims fail closed with stable evidence and no teardown. Preserve genuine completed/failed reaps and silent idempotence for already-auto-destroyed exact actors.

## Proof discipline

Add CLJ/CLJS counterfixtures for stale A1 completion after A2 respawn, current actor completed while `:resolved? false`, wrong actor for correct child, wrong child for correct actor, old parent/invoke attempt, duplicate exact completion, and genuine post-resolution reap. Mutating away actor/attempt comparison or the resolved latch must fail distinct tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- A child completion/failure is accepted only when parent, invoke/join attempt, logical child id, and exact current actor attempt all match runtime-owned state.
- A stale A1 signal after A2 respawn/re-entry is classified stale and cannot mark A2 done/failed, resolve the join, publish A2's terminal, or reap A2.
- The cancellation-suppressing reap is authorized only after the exact join attempt's `:resolved?` latch is true and the exact child attempt is recorded completed/failed.
- A current completed child in an unresolved `:all` join cannot be reaped through the reserved public fx boundary.
- Wrong actor/child/attempt, malformed, duplicate, and stale claims are fail-closed with stable typed evidence and no slot/actor/trace/reply mutation.
- Genuine exact completed/failed reaps remain cancellation-free; survivors remain explicit cancellation; already-auto-destroyed exact actors remain silent-idempotent.
- CLJ and CLJS mutations independently prove the actor/attempt correlation and resolution-phase fences.
- No application-facing actor/reason authority, public API expansion, or global coordinator is introduced.

title: Fail closed on false-valued and overlapping join-reap carriers
description:
## Problem

PR #5779 (head ccbe3a67c28cead8a016f214304c01ab32095b38; merge ee47983c1ccfcc958868923464f5097d269b4865) authenticates the internal join-reap carrier, but its map-shape dispatch tests the truthiness of `(:rf/reap args)` instead of treating presence of the discriminator as a closed shape.

A carrier such as `{:rf/reap false :rf/parent-id p :rf/invoke-id i :rf/child-id c}` misses the reap branch and falls through to the tracked single-spawn branch. With a spawn-all join at the addressed slot, that branch reads the entire join-state map as the slot's actor id, clears the join slot, leaves the real children live and orphaned, and emits a bogus `:rf.machine/destroyed`/cancellation trace whose actor id is the join-state map. It emits no `:rf.error/machine-destroy-bad-arg`.

This violates #5779's core fail-closed promise: malformed map forms must fail loud and perform no teardown. The defect persists on current main.

## Deterministic reproduction

Create a live two-child spawn-all join and dispatch the false-valued carrier above. Before: join slot present; both child actors live. Current result: join slot nil; both children still live; one destroyed trace names the entire former join-state map; bad-arg count zero.

## Required correction

Make map-form dispatch a closed discriminated grammar. Presence of `:rf/reap` selects the reap shape; require its value to be exactly true and require the exact coordinate fields/types. Any malformed/unknown/overlapping map shape must emit the stable typed bad-arg error and return without slot, actor, child, trace, terminal-reply, or ownership mutation.

Admit the tracked single-spawn form only when reap/spawn-all/child discriminator keys are absent and the resolved slot is a valid actor id for that shape, never a join-state map. Do not add permissive coercion, truthy aliases, or a compatibility fallback.

## Proof discipline

Add CLJ and CLJS fail-before fixtures for `false`, nil, wrong-type, missing-field, extra/overlapping discriminator, and a tracked-form request pointed at a spawn-all slot. Mutate the predicate back to truthiness to prove the fixture catches the corruption.
acceptance_criteria:
- Presence of `:rf/reap` is parsed as the reap carrier and only the exact value true plus required coordinates is accepted.
- `:rf/reap false`, nil/wrong values, missing coordinates, and overlapping/unknown map shapes emit exactly one `:rf.error/machine-destroy-bad-arg` with stable cause evidence.
- Every malformed carrier leaves the join slot, child actors, snapshots, timers/resources, terminal replies, and lifecycle traces unchanged.
- The tracked single-spawn branch cannot consume a spawn-all join-state map as an actor id and is admitted only for its exact closed shape.
- Genuine completed/failed resolution reaps and genuine tracked single-spawn destroys remain green on CLJ and CLJS.
- The pre-fix false-valued carrier deterministically demonstrates join-slot corruption; restoring the truthiness dispatch makes the regression fail.

title: Bind preflight evidence to the exact root attempt and host commit boundary
description:
## Problem

PR #5781 (head 729a62b8b8665e94c875dad4990d7f0dbaed58b0; merge 293e8fd4916fc27bde55cb5561861a6191432a79) separates `:mount-incomplete` from `:preflight-attempt-failed`, but the runtime still derives root-lifecycle truth solely from the frame plan action and finalizes evidence before the host operation has succeeded.

In `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/frames.cljc`, action selection is based on frame/install records; every `:refresh` and `:adopt` is classified as `:live`, and a later plan failure becomes a diagnostic claim that the frame is “still LIVE and scoped” by a prior root with its last committed render intact. That inference is unsound: an install record proves plan authority, not a committed React root. The new executor-only tests call `execute-frame-plans!` directly and create no client Root, live-root registry entry, or DOM commit, so they cannot prove their own “genuinely live root” comments.

The complementary boundary is also missing. `execute-frame-plans!` clears failed-attempt evidence as soon as all plans return, before `client.cljs` performs the post-preflight ownership fence, creates/adopts the host root, evaluates the element thunk, or invokes render. A later synchronous failure leaves a frame record that looks like a completed installer even though no root survived.

Marker ownership is too broad as well: mark/clear operations are keyed by bare frame id. An unrelated root with an equal plan, a stale attempt, or an old frame lifetime can clear or stamp evidence belonging to a different root attempt or replacement incarnation.

## Deterministic counterexamples

### Failed fresh-mount retry mislabeled live

1. Fresh root A preflight installs F/v1; a later malformed plan throws. A never mounts; F is `:mount-incomplete`.
2. Retry still-unmounted A with changed F/v2; a later plan throws again.
3. Because `:installed-by` equals A, F is selected as `:refresh` and classified `:live`; the old incomplete marker is replaced by `:preflight-attempt-failed`.
4. Root C's conflict now says F is “still LIVE and scoped by root A” with a prior render, while `client/live-root-ids` contains no A.

A newly attempted `:adopt` has the same category error: the boot frame may be live, but the new root-to-frame scope has not committed.

### Successful preflight followed by host failure

1. Fresh `client/mount*` for root A executes a valid frame plan F.
2. Plan completion clears incomplete evidence.
3. The post-preflight ownership fence, root creation, element thunk, or first host render fails synchronously.
4. Client cleanup removes A's root claim, but F remains `{:installed-by A}` with no incomplete marker. A later conflict presents A as a completed installer.

The same premature finalization affects create-root plus first `render!`, idempotent remount, and live rerender failure. A live rerender must preserve the previous root/DOM while recording only the failed new attempt.

## Required correction

Introduce one small internal, identity-guarded preflight attempt receipt/context shared by frames and the client boundary. It must distinguish:

- frame/boot authority from committed root scope;
- fresh/uncommitted install or adoption from a previously committed live root;
- plan-phase failure from post-preflight ownership, element, or host-render failure;
- exact root attempt, install record revision, and frame incarnation.

Plan execution may retain irreversible sibling effects and initial events, but it must not declare the root attempt successful. Finalize/clear evidence only after the client's existing ownership fence and synchronous host invocation succeed. On abort, mark a fresh attempt incomplete; for a genuinely committed root, preserve its prior Root/DOM and attach neutral attempt-failure evidence. Mark/clear only when the receipt still matches the exact record and frame incarnation. Do not infer liveness from `:refresh`, `:adopt`, app-db contents, or frame existence.

This is internal bookkeeping; no public API or frozen-table addition is authorized. Do not add rollback, destroy/reseed, or a second global coordinator.

## Contract reconciliation

After the runtime shape is settled, update Spec 004C's installed/adopted record variants, `installed-plan-entry` tool/test docstring, and the relevant Spec 009 diagnostic projection/cross-reference. They must define frame liveness, committed root scope, failed attempt phase, identity ownership, and clearing rules separately. Current Spec 004C names only `:mount-incomplete` and omits `:preflight-attempt-failed`.

## Proof discipline

Use executor tests only for plan bookkeeping. Claims about live roots and last committed DOM require real mounted browser/registry fixtures, and the changed surface must activate the browser lane. Demonstrate each counterexample red before the fix. Mutate away receipt identity checks to prove stale-attempt/reincarnation tests have teeth.
acceptance_criteria:
- A changed-config retry after a failed fresh mount cannot become committed/live-root evidence until its host operation succeeds; conflict diagnostics never claim a never-mounted root is live or has a prior render.
- A new adoption distinguishes live boot-frame authority from committed scope by the adopting root; failed adoption does not present `:adopted-by` as a completed root scope.
- A genuinely mounted root's failed refresh/rerender preserves and truthfully reports the prior committed Root and DOM while recording the failed new attempt separately.
- Failures after plan success at the post-preflight ownership fence, root creation/adoption, element thunk, first host render, idempotent remount, and later `render!` leave phase-correct evidence.
- Evidence is owned by an exact root attempt, install/adopt record revision, and frame incarnation. An unrelated equal-plan root, stale receipt, or destroyed/recreated frame cannot mark or clear newer evidence.
- Successful completion clears only matching attempt evidence after the synchronous host boundary succeeds.
- Irreversible sibling work and initial events remain committed per Q49; no rollback, destroy/reseed, public API, frozen-table change, or second coordinator is introduced.
- Real browser fixtures prove committed root/DOM claims and are selected by CI; executor-only tests stop claiming host proof.
- Spec 004C, Spec 009 projection/cross-reference, runtime record docstrings, tool/test accessors, diagnostics, and tests use one closed vocabulary for fresh, live-refresh, adoption, retry, and host-phase failure variants.
- Pre-fix counterexamples and mutations are recorded; focused frame/root/browser suites and the full relevant spine pass.

Both counterexamples re-verified RED on origin/main 3af2e07 and GREEN after. Gates: ui/JVM 474/0, npm test:ui 473/0, test:browser 346/0, fast-pr spine PASS (9308 CLJS). NOTE: Spec 004C record-variant + Spec 009 projection reconciliation (:committed / :mount-incomplete / :preflight-attempt-failed / rev-identity vocabulary) still needed — fenced out of spec/** for this worker; needs a follow-up spec bead. Left open for mayor.

title: Classify both endpoints of renames in changed-surface discovery
description:
## Problem

PR #5780 (head 0ce85e8c2c0e7a7b0bee92f9f98bc288fa4876ae; merge 43ce4cf9f69e786c0cedfcac2cc914b007f15d78) correctly routes ordinary `implementation/ui/**` paths to the JVM UI, node, UI-economics, and browser gates. Its automatic path discovery still uses `git diff --name-only` in both PR and local modes (`.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` around lines 24-31). Git rename detection reports only the destination path for a detected rename.

A pure rename out of `implementation/ui/**` can therefore delete or move production UI code while every UI gate remains false. For example, renaming `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc` unchanged to an otherwise unclassified path reports only the destination; the classifier never sees the deleted UI endpoint. Existing explicit-path tests cannot catch this because they bypass Git-derived discovery. The inverse rename and within-surface rename happen to be safer only when the reported destination is classified; the general contract must classify both endpoints.

This contradicts #5780/rf2-vxgfnd.90's guarantee that every first-party UI source or test change runs the browser and related UI gates. It is a repository-wide changed-surface hazard, but this bead's proof is bounded to the demonstrated UI false-green.

## Deterministic reproduction

In a temporary two-commit Git repository, commit a file under `implementation/ui/src/**`, then rename it unchanged to `docs/**` or an unclassified implementation path. Invoke `report-changed-surfaces.sh` without explicit path arguments. Current behavior derives `git diff --name-only ...`, sees only the destination, and leaves `implementation_jvm`, `cljs_node_test`, `ui_gates`, and `cljs_browser` false. `git diff --no-renames --name-only` reports the old deletion plus new addition and arms the correct gates.

## Required correction

Use `git diff --no-renames --name-only` in both automatic discovery branches. This is the smallest fully correct shape: every rename is classified as deletion plus addition, without adding name-status parsing or a rename-specific rules engine. Keep explicit-path mode unchanged.

## Proof discipline

Add integration self-tests that create real temporary Git histories and invoke discovery mode, rather than passing paths directly to the classifier. Prove UI-to-docs, docs-to-UI, and within-UI renames. The first must fail before the fix. Retain the existing classifier matrix.
acceptance_criteria:
- Both endpoints of every detected rename are classified in PR (`origin/$GITHUB_BASE_REF...HEAD`) and local (`HEAD^ HEAD` plus fallback) discovery modes.
- A pure `implementation/ui/** -> docs/**` or otherwise unclassified rename arms `implementation_jvm`, `cljs_node_test`, `ui_gates`, and `cljs_browser` exactly as a UI deletion does.
- A reverse rename into UI and a rename within UI also arm the complete UI gate set.
- Regression tests invoke the script's real Git-derived discovery mode in a temporary repository; they do not only pass explicit paths.
- Restoring rename detection or removing `--no-renames` makes the UI-to-non-UI regression fail.
- Existing explicit-path/add/modify/delete classifier cases remain green; no workflow/gate weakening is introduced.
close_reason: Merged PR #5840 (classify both rename endpoints in changed-surface discovery; red-before-fix proven; classifier tests 138 green)

title: Make Guide 09's executable-coverage claim exact and genuinely reactive
description:
## Problem

PR #5826 (head 337a7d602ea2b92aa71399ed9e1205d369c9803f; merge 02e6f8eb3269c5b6a3ac640d61f43fc2f8097698) says the tracked guide has executable coverage and that Guide 09's Tier-1 examples run. The only executable Guide 09 fixture still identifies itself as an S1 adaptation: `implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/test_guide09_fixture_jvm_test.clj` passes membership as a prop, reads app-db manually, and contains no `(sub ...)`. Yet `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/guide/09-testing.md` now claims the complete dispatch -> sub -> rerender loop on main, and `guide/README.md` says the chapter's Tier-1 examples run. The draft pipeline says S2 adaptations must disappear when S2 ships; README and Guide 09 both declare S2 shipped.

This is not only wording drift. The named fixture currently proves dispatch plus prop-driven rerender, not the first-party reactive path that the guide teaches. It also covers one selected fence and prose assertions, not every Tier-1 example in the chapter; there is no guide fixture manifest that would justify the broader coverage wording.

## Reproduction

At current main:

- `rg 'sub reads land S2|membership is a prop' implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/test_guide09_fixture_jvm_test.clj` finds the obsolete adaptation.
- `rg '\(sub ' implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/test_guide09_fixture_jvm_test.clj` finds no real subscription read.
- Compare the fixture with `guide/09-testing.md` Tier 1 and `drafts/guide-fixture-pipeline.md` coverage/bridge rules.

## Required correction

De-adapt the toggle-card fixture so membership is obtained through the shipped compiled `sub` path. Its dispatch proof must show a dispatched write followed by a render whose result depends on that subscription. Narrow the README and chapter coverage statement to the exact enrolled fences/assertions unless the remaining Tier-1 selectors and literal-root examples are actually enrolled. Reconcile the bridge-status prose with the executable inventory. Do not paper over the gap by weakening the shipped S2 guide example back to prop injection.

## Proof discipline

First demonstrate that replacing/removing the reactive read makes the fixture fail for the intended reason. Then run the exact Guide 09 JVM fixture and the relevant compiler/reactive suites. The PR body must list the exact enrolled guide fences and distinguish executable examples from prose-only claims.
acceptance_criteria:
- No S1 `sub reads land S2` or membership-as-prop adaptation remains in the Guide 09 fixture.
- The dispatch scenario uses the shipped `sub` path and proves dispatch -> write drain -> subscription read -> changed rendered tree.
- README and Guide 09 coverage wording names exactly the fences/assertions exercised; no whole-section/chapter implication exceeds the fixture inventory.
- Any referenced fixture manifest or activation state exists and is executable rather than aspirational.
- A demonstrated pre-fix mutation/removal of the reactive read fails; the focused Guide 09, compiler, and reactive gates pass after the fix.
close_reason: Merged PR #5841 (genuinely-reactive Guide 09 fixture through compiled sub path + exact coverage wording; CI 62/0/0; read mutation-proven load-bearing)

title: Finish, audit, green, and merge rf2-vxgfnd.106 ui/lease
description:
## Purpose

Bring the already-started rf2-vxgfnd.106 ui/lease implementation to one coherent, independently audited, fully green merged PR. This is a close-out bead for the existing branch, not new product scope.

Owning bead: rf2-vxgfnd.106
Worktree: C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2-worktrees\vxgfnd106-ui-lease
Branch: worker/vxgfnd106-ui-lease
Current local head at filing: 099c6757a0 (rf2-vxgfnd.106: complete resource lease lifecycle proof)
Remote relation at filing: 22 commits ahead / 3 behind the remote worker branch; local head is 4 ahead / 0 behind current origin/main.
PR state at filing: no pull request exists for this branch.

The worktree is clean at 099c6757a0, but that candidate is obsolete: the independent live audit found additional exact-scope and synchronous-dispatch reentrancy defects that must be fixed before push.

## Frozen contract to preserve

- Public ui/lease accepts only nil or the closed descriptor {:resource qualified-keyword, optional :scope, optional :params}; missing params remains distinct from explicit nil.
- Compiler-authoritative lexical site identity is shared with sub; no render-order counter or second identity system.
- Render and abandoned render own nothing. Exact layout acceptance publishes desired resource state; passive reconciliation owns ensures/releases.
- Resource ownership is not observation. Lease frame pins exist for exact teardown/liveness only and must not enlarge subscription/flush scope.
- Equal same-site descriptors retain owners; retarget mints fresh owners. Prevalidate the complete desired plan, enqueue all ensures before releases in deterministic per-frame order, and use ordinary FIFO drain-to-quiescence followed by one read/render batch. No global coordinator or cross-frame rollback.
- Lease-only views use the fixed ViewCell/lifecycle skeleton with zero useSyncExternalStore; sub+lease views share one cell and one subscription hook.
- StrictMode, Activity, unmount, root/frame destroy, throwing cleanup, and HMR must retain/release exact ownership without leaks or resurrection.
- Lease-free advanced output erases resource ownership hooks, mint/debug strings, and optional Resources artefact/dependency sources.
- The neutral process-global owner mint is shared with stock Reagent. No adapter dependency or frozen API-table delta.

## Follow-up findings already tracked

- rf2-vxgfnd.116: reject mixed same-id A/B resource pins before layout publication.
- rf2-vxgfnd.119: make the real mint and hook-matrix production proof non-vacuous and actually executed.
- rf2-vxgfnd.120: a terminally dead ViewCell must not be reattached by the second layout effect.
- rf2-vxgfnd.122: teardown discovery must deduplicate repeated exact-token references while preserving transient A+B tokens for one frame id.

The branch already contains focused fixes/proofs for these, including the transient A+B cardinality-two/exact-A-teardown fixture. They remain open until the final exact head is audited and merged.

## Confirmed blockers after 099c6757a0

1. Reactive flush scope contamination

cell-frames currently unions resource lease frame pins into reactive flush-frame! scope. A view can read frame A while merely leasing frame B; flushing B may then flush pending A work. This violates scoped read-after-drain/no-leak semantics. Resource teardown already has its own exact index. Remove lease pins from reactive cell-frames and prove mixed A-sub/B-lease isolation.

2. Passive ensure reentrancy can resurrect a dead cell

Resource dispatch emits trace listeners synchronously. If the first ensure listener tears down the cell, teardown releases/clears the prepublished candidates, but the old reconcile can continue later ensures and final-swap held/reservations back onto :dead. A two-site sequence can become ensure-A, release-A, release-B, ensure-B and leak B. Reconcile must detect terminal/replaced lifecycle after each reentrant dispatch and must never publish stale held/reservation state.

3. Teardown release reentrancy can recurse

teardown! currently dispatches resource releases while lifecycle is still connected and only later marks :dead. A synchronous release listener/frame destroy can re-enter teardown against the same connected state and recurse indefinitely. Publish terminal/idempotence state before dispatching cleanup and make nested teardown harmless.

4. Disconnect reentrancy can overwrite terminal state

disconnect releases while lifecycle is still connected, then writes :disconnected afterward. A release listener can perform nested teardown, after which the outer disconnect overwrites :dead with :disconnected. Publish the disconnected/live-registry transition before resource dispatch, and perform no unconditional lifecycle write after reentrant cleanup.

5. Source-doc honesty

The reactive.cljc namespace documentation still describes target-key dedupe/shared leases, capture stashed directly on the cell, and per-site identity as future work. Those claims were superseded by merged .100/.105 and must be corrected to current behavior while the source is already touched.

These are implementation defects under the frozen contract, not new API/design decisions.

## Existing pre-final evidence

Before the latest blocker fixes:

- JVM UI: 418 tests / 5,360 assertions
- Node UI: 424 tests / 2,120 assertions
- Browser UI: 339 tests / 1,650 assertions
- Advanced production-elision: 80 tests / 258 assertions; the 0/0, 1/0, 0/1, 1/1 hook matrix is visibly executed.
- G13 production-faithful run without pseudo names: lease-free advanced bundle 619,947 bytes; compiled real-mint control 92,434 bytes; owner sentinel present only in control; optional Resources runtime/dependency/source-manifest absent; all 13 mutation teeth fail as expected.

This evidence establishes the proof machinery but does not approve 099c6757a0. Every affected gate must run again on the final exact head.

## Finite close-out sequence

1. Patch only the five confirmed blocker/doc-honesty items above, with deterministic fail-pre-fix fixtures for flush isolation and each synchronous-dispatch reentrancy ordering.
2. Prove terminal/reentrant paths mint no unexpected owner, leave no ensure/release leak, never resurrect held/reservations/root membership, and remain idempotent.
3. Run focused JVM and Node regression suites while iterating.
4. Commit/amend one coherent candidate. Fetch origin and rebase if main has advanced; verify no compiler/lifecycle/proof behavior is lost.
5. Run the exact-head matrix with hard timeouts: JVM UI, Node UI, browser UI, advanced production-elision, G13 including every mutation tooth and optional-artifact manifest check, and script-policy/fast-PR gates required by the touched surfaces.
6. Push with force-with-lease to worker/vxgfnd106-ui-lease and open/update one PR with the frozen contract, exact SHA, fail-pre-fix evidence, test counts, G13 sizes/mutations, and associated bead IDs.
7. Have s2_capstone_live_audit adversarially review the exact pushed SHA. Fix only confirmed defects on the same branch; any new delta gets a narrow exact-head re-review.
8. Make the PR ready only after the audit is clean. Wait for every required GitHub check; inspect and fix real failures on the same branch, rerunning only proven infrastructure flakes.
9. Merge only the exact audited green head.
10. Pull origin/main into the mayor checkout and verify HEAD equals origin/main and contains the merge. Close this bead, rf2-vxgfnd.106, and rf2-vxgfnd.116/.119/.120/.122 with exact SHA, tests, audit, CI, and merge evidence. Commit/push the bead mirror. Do not close parent rf2-vxgfnd.12 unless its separate remaining obligations are independently complete.

## Non-goals

No new public API, resource transaction coordinator, adapter compatibility path, broader mounted stress fixture beyond the decisive central invariants, future-stage behavior, or unrelated cleanup. Finish the existing ui/lease slice elegantly and completely.

title: Keep claimed destroy recipe authority local across successor claims
description:
## Problem

rf2-q4uh2p originally derived an already-claimed destroy recipe's terminal trace authority from frame-incarnation-closing?(id, token), which rereads the mutable id-keyed destroying-frames marker. After A is dissociated, same-id B may legitimately claim its own destroy and replace that marker with token B. A's local exact-token recipe still owns completion, but its terminal continuation predicate becomes false: required halted epoch trailers and the corpus-only teardown report disappear.

Anchors: implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc claim-frame-destroy!, destroy-frame!, and frame-incarnation-closing?; implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc terminal continuation; implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/listeners.cljc structural trailer delivery; implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc corpus fanout. The existing fresh-same-id-destroy-replaces-stale-marker-token-safely test proves B's overlapping claim is supported.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. A owns an in-flight run and one forced teardown-hook failure.
2. Pause A post-dissoc at epoch teardown.
3. Install B with the same id and start B destroy; pause B after its successful claim, so the shared marker now contains token B.
4. Resume A while B remains claimed.
5. With marker-derived continuation, A's halted snapshotted/outcome facts and corpus teardown report are suppressed even though A's lexical recipe remains valid. A's compare-remove correctly leaves B's marker intact.

## Contract violation

Successful claim grants immutable local authority for that exact recipe. The id-keyed marker exists for acquisition, idempotence, and compare-remove; a successor claim cannot retroactively revoke predecessor terminal facts. Exact guards must still fence every id-keyed mutation and fresh B must remain untouched.

## Required direction

Bind terminal continuation to the locally acquired recipe authority for the lexical recipe duration, not the mutable marker. Retain exact-token checks on all shared/id-keyed mutations, epoch ownership, cascade allowances, report frame-routing suppression, and marker compare-remove. Do not revive A's returned ordinary event tail.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic A-post-dissoc/B-post-claim overlap fixture is verified red before the fix by missing A's three terminal publications.
- While B remains claimed, exactly one A halted-destroy snapshotted row, one blocked outcome, and one corpus frame-teardown-failed report are delivered.
- The report routes zero times into B; no A terminal trace enters B capture/history; B state and policies are unchanged.
- A's finalizer preserves B's token/claim marker and B later completes exactly once.
- Restoring marker-derived continuation makes the A publications disappear.
- Removing structural delivery exposes B policy/capture contamination; restoring ordinary report routing contaminates B; suppressing the report makes corpus count zero.
- Exact-token mutation fences and ordinary event-tail suppression remain green.

title: Do not reattach terminally dead ViewCells after layout rejection
description:
## Problem

The rf2-vxgfnd.106 resource ViewCell uses two layout effects. The first calls commit-resources!, whose superseded-frame or mixed-incarnation rejection can call teardown! and leave the cell terminally :dead. React then runs the second layout effect, which unconditionally calls attach-root!. attach-root! currently has no dead guard, so it re-adds the dead cell to root-cells and stores the root token.

Later cleanup is inert because disconnect* acts only on fresh/connected cells, while normal root teardown's hidden scan selects disconnected cells. The dead reattached cell and root incarnation can therefore remain registered permanently. The same latent ordering defect applies to existing superseded-frame commit teardown, not only the new mixed-token path.

Anchors: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/viewcell.cljs use-resource-commit-and-lifecycle!; implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc commit-resources!, common commit rejection, teardown!, attach-root!, disconnect*, and teardown-root!.

## Required direction

Make the terminal lifecycle invariant central: attach-root! must harmlessly refuse a :dead cell. Do not reorder hooks, add a lifecycle state, or rely only on a caller-side guard.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic headless fixture drives commit rejection to :dead and then calls attach-root! in second-layout-effect order; it is verified red before the fix with cell-root set and root-cell-count 1.
- After the fix, the dead cell has no root and root-cell-count is 0.
- A mounted rejection/unmount proof returns global and root-specific registries to their exact baseline.
- Repeated rejected mounts do not grow root incarnation or cell counts.
- Ordinary connected cells attach, Activity-disconnected cells retain valid membership, and final teardown removes membership.
- Rejected mixed capture still mints/displays no ensure or release actions.

title: Make the resource mint and hook-matrix production proof non-vacuous
description:
## Problem

The in-progress rf2-vxgfnd.106 production proof has two independent ways to report a false green on the resource-hook/mint elision contract.

First, implementation/scripts/run-ui-g13.cjs checks that pseudo-name resource_lease_owner is absent from the lease-free advanced bundle, but its positive control only reads the neutral mint source and its mutation tooth appends a synthetic string. No reachable lease-bearing build compiled with the same Closure settings proves that the selected pseudo-name is actually emitted when the real mint! is reachable. If Closure inlines/renames differently, both reachable and lease-free bundles can lack the token and the absence assertion remains vacuous.

Second, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn routes browser-test-prod-elision through the explicit re-frame.prod-elision-runner require roster. The new resource-lease-hook-matrix-elision-prod-test namespace matched the source regex but was omitted from that runner, so the build could compile while run-all-tests never executed the 0/0, 1/0, 0/1, 1/1 hook matrix.

## Required direction

1. Add a tiny advanced, pseudo-names, goog.DEBUG=false control entry that directly invokes the real neutral resource owner mint. Require token presence in that compiled control before requiring token absence in the lease-free subject. Retain source checks and contamination mutation as secondary guards.
2. Enrol the hook-matrix namespace in the existing explicit production-elision runner. Do not add another runner or weaken optimizer settings.

These are one proof-surface repair: the gate must prove a reachable positive and must execute the matrix it claims.
acceptance_criteria:
- G13 fails if the same-options compiled mint control lacks the expected pseudo-name.
- G13 fails if the lease-free subject contains the mint pseudo-name.
- Independent mutations remove the token from the control and inject it into the subject; both make the gate red.
- The control invokes the actual neutral mint!, not a duplicate sentinel helper.
- The production-elision browser test count increases by exactly the new matrix test/assertions and output identifies its execution.
- Mutating one expected hook cardinality makes the actual advanced browser gate red.
- Both builds remain :advanced with goog.DEBUG=false; compile-only or source-presence evidence is insufficient.

title: Keep predecessor teardown-failure reports out of successor frame sinks
description:
## Problem

During rf2-q4uh2p destruction, A's teardown-hook failures are accumulated safely, but the final :rf.error/frame-teardown-failed report is emitted only after A has been dissociated. The general union error path publishes to the corpus and then resolves the record's bare frame id for frame-owned observability routing. If same-id B exists by then, A's failure is incorrectly delivered into B's error sinks.

Anchors: implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc destroy-frame! finalizer; implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc dispatch-frame-teardown-report! and union fanout; implementation/core/src/re_frame/observability.cljc route-error-record!.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Create A at id F and register a corpus error listener.
2. Force one A teardown hook to throw so the safe accumulator contains one failure.
3. Pause A's epoch teardown hook after A has been dissociated but before the final report flush.
4. Install same-id B with a frame-owned error sink and snapshot B's exact token/state.
5. Resume A.
6. Corpus correctly receives A's report, but the general bare-id route sends it to B's sink.

## Contract violation

Option A + unwind permits A's bounded terminal teardown facts but fences all later framework-owned actions from B. Routing A's post-dissoc error into B violates exact attribution and falsely makes B own A's failure.

## Required direction

Publish the destroy-finalizer report to the global corpus exactly once while suppressing only the frame-owned route for this post-dissoc call. Preserve normal frame routing for live/general errors. The current narrow internal route-frame? seam is appropriate; do not suppress the report or globally change union routing.
acceptance_criteria:
- A latch-controlled overlap fixture is verified red before the fix with B frame-route count 1.
- After the fix, corpus sees exactly one :rf.error/frame-teardown-failed with A's id and one failure entry, while B's frame-owned sink count is zero.
- B's token, app/runtime state, and error policy are unchanged.
- Destroy completes with no duplicate report.
- Mutation back to the general route makes B count 1; suppressing the full record makes corpus count 0.
- Existing general/live error union tests prove ordinary frame-owned routing remains intact.

title: Prevent successor no-emit policy from suppressing predecessor epoch trailers
description:
## Problem

In the in-progress rf2-q4uh2p exact-incarnation destroy fix, incarnation A is dissociated before its late-bound epoch destruction hook emits the required terminal :rf.epoch/snapshotted and :rf.epoch/outcome :blocked trailers. Trace emission is tagged only with the bare frame id. If same-id incarnation B is installed with :rf.trace/frame-no-emit? true while A's hook is paused, the trace layer consults B's current id-level policy and suppresses A's terminal trailers.

Anchors: implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc destroy steps 10-11; implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/listeners.cljc on-frame-destroyed!; implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc emit-snapshotted+outcome!; and implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc frame no-emit resolution.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Make A under id F, collect epoch trailer traces, and destroy A from an event.
2. Pause late-bind :epoch/on-frame-destroyed after A has been dissociated but while A's exact destroy marker remains owned.
3. Install same-id B with frame-no-emit enabled and snapshot B's history/capture state.
4. Resume A's original epoch hook.
5. The epoch listener receives A's halted record, but the global trace listener misses A's two required terminal rows because B's policy suppresses them. Installing B without no-emit is the mutation control.

## Contract violation

Mike's Option A + unwind contract authorizes A's exact-token terminal teardown facts while fencing every later framework action from B. Consulting B's policy lets the successor erase the predecessor's required terminal observability and makes A's outcome timing-dependent. It is the same stale-A/bare-id attribution class already rejected for structural drain facts, not a new product choice.

## Required direction

Deliver only A's already-assembled terminal halted-destroy trailers through the existing structural/exact-terminal trace seam so successor frame policy and epoch capture cannot suppress or absorb them. Preserve B's ordinary no-emit policy and do not broaden the bypass to normal epoch settles.

This independent finding must be fixed and mutation-proved before rf2-q4uh2p is accepted.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic overlap fixture is verified red before the fix by missing A's terminal :rf.epoch/snapshotted and :rf.epoch/outcome :blocked.
- After the fix, exactly one of each A trailer is visible despite B's frame-no-emit policy.
- The terminal epoch listener still receives exactly one :halted-destroy record with A's before/after snapshots and trigger.
- B's epoch history, last-settled anchor, capture buffer, and trace policy are byte-identical before and after A resumes.
- No normal :ok A epoch settlement appears.
- Ordinary B frame-tagged traces remain suppressed, proving the bypass is terminal-only.
- Existing halted-destroy, privacy/no-emit, stale-A structural-drain, and same-id epoch ownership suites remain green.

title: Reject mixed same-id resource incarnation pins before layout publication
description:
## Problem

The in-progress rf2-vxgfnd.106 resource-lease implementation records an exact frame token per lexical lease site, but its current layout-validation fold collapses all resource records into {frame-id -> token} with unconditional last-write-wins. If executable descriptor computation destroys ambient incarnation A and recreates the same frame id as B between two leading lease sites, the second B token erases the first A token. Layout validates only B and can accept/connect/publish a mixed A/B resource plan; passive reconciliation notices stale A only after the layout acceptance boundary.

Current WIP anchors: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc functions lease-site, resource-capture-incarnations, commit-resources!, and commit*.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Enter a compiled lease-bearing view under frame id F, exact token A.
2. Leading site S1 records F/A.
3. Evaluation of the dynamic descriptor for later site S2 synchronously destroys F and recreates F with token B.
4. S2 records F/B.
5. The fold overwrites F/A with F/B.
6. Layout accepts and publishes both records because only B is revalidated.

The source evidence is complete at each site; the defect is the lossy reduction.

## Contract violation

The frozen S2 contract requires every resource declaration to retain exact-incarnation ownership and requires layout commit to reject a superseded render capture before publishing desired ownership. Same-id replacement must not silently retarget or defer invalidation until passive time.

## Required direction

Keep the compact common revalidation shape, but detect conflicting non-identical tokens for the same frame id during resource layout validation, or validate every resource record individually. Reject through the existing superseded-incarnation path before publish/connect. Do not add a transaction coordinator, change public API, or alter ordinary passive ensure/release ordering.

This finding was independently constructed during the live .106 audit and is being fixed before the .106 candidate is pushed.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic mixed-site F/A then F/B fixture is verified red before the fix by observing layout acceptance, connection, or published resource state.
- After the fix, layout rejects the mixed capture before accepting, connecting, or publishing it.
- Rejection mints no owner, dispatches no :rf.resource/ensure or :rf.resource/release-owner, and leaves reservations/held state empty.
- Same-id/same-token multi-site capture remains legal and produces independent owners in passive reconciliation.
- Distinct frame ids remain legal and deterministic ensure-before-release ordering remains green.
- The exact candidate passes focused JVM, Node, browser, production-elision, and G13 gates.

title: Make the tracked re-frame.ui guide stage-honest and executable-claim accurate
description:
## Problem

The tracked preliminary `re-frame.ui` guide now declares in `guide/README.md` that unmarked statements describe behavior shipped on `main` and that every example compiles and runs as a CI fixture. Post-merge audit of PR #5823 found five concrete contradictions. These are current stage-truth defects, not preferences and not duplicates of the existing frame-root/provider, macro-grammar, or lease-error reconciliation beads.

1. `guide/08-ssr.md` and `guide/09-testing.md` teach unmarked S3-S5 behavior (local/effect semantics, client-only fallback, presence, error-boundary behavior) even though the frozen per-verb matrix in `12-implementation-plan.md §2b` places those surfaces after S2.
2. The README's every-example-is-a-fixture claim is false. Only a narrow Guide 09 fixture exists; several fences are schematic or use future-stage forms. The guide-fixture and docs-move drafts still claim the synthesis tree is gitignored and unavailable to CI, but it has been force-tracked since #5800.
3. `guide/05-frames.md` says its multi-view root authors `:root-id`, but the displayed form supplies no mount options and fails the compiler's no-single-mounted-view fence when used as advertised.
4. `guide/09-testing.md` attributes `ui.test/dispatch!` to S1, while the frozen matrix and Spec 004 place its mounted semantics in S2.
5. The guide says the checkout carries React/ReactDOM 19.2.4+, while `implementation/package.json` currently pins 19.2.0.

Leaving these claims in a guide that explicitly distinguishes shipped from future behavior makes the guide unsafe as stage evidence and undermines the S2 boundary review.

## Deliverable

Reconcile the guide and its pipeline drafts to one honest, mechanically checkable stage-truth model:

- Preserve the useful README rule that unmarked behavior is shipped, and explicitly qualify every S3-S5 passage or define an equally unambiguous governing stage marker that a fresh reader cannot miss.
- Replace the false universal fixture claim with exact current coverage. Mark schematic/future fences, identify the fixtures that actually execute today, and update the pipeline/move drafts to the tracked-tree reality. Do not build a speculative universal extractor merely to preserve old prose.
- Make the multi-frame example executable and complete by showing the required `ui/mount` call with authored `:root-id`, or clearly label the inner form schematic and immediately show the complete mount.
- Move `ui.test/dispatch!` to the S2 attribution.
- Reconcile the React version statement with the authoritative package/peer contract; do not silently change dependency versions in this guide-only slice.
- Deduplicate edits with rf2-vxgfnd.110, .112, and .113 when the serialized S2 documentation cluster lands.

## Proof

Fresh-read every changed guide statement against the frozen API/stage matrix, live Spec 004, compiler root fence, tracked-file state, package metadata, and actual test discovery. Run docs/link/slug gates and classified searches proving no current guide or draft still says the tracked synthesis tree is gitignored, no unmarked future-stage guarantee remains, and no universal fixture promise exceeds executable coverage. If examples become executable, run their owning focused fixture; otherwise ensure their schematic/future status is explicit.

## Non-goals

No frozen API change, new runtime behavior, source-code implementation, dependency bump, or re-litigation of ratified decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
- All guide statements are either true on current main or carry an explicit future-stage marker consistent with the frozen matrix.
- Current executable guide coverage is stated exactly; schematic/future fences are not represented as CI fixtures.
- Both guide pipeline drafts recognize the tracked synthesis tree and name the real CI route.
- The multi-frame/root-id example is complete and cannot trip the no-single-mounted-view compiler fence when followed.
- ui.test/dispatch! is attributed to S2.
- React version prose matches the authoritative package/peer contract without an unrelated dependency mutation.
- Docs, link, slug, and relevant focused fixture gates pass.

title: Reconcile closed compiler macro grammar with Spec 004 and guide
description:
## Problem

rf2-vxgfnd.100 / PR #5821 established a load-bearing soundness rule: compiler-owned defview expressions cannot preserve arbitrary macros as opaque source. A user macro or helper macro can inject ui/sub or ui/lease without any reactive token in the authored invocation; the manifest then falsely declares a sub-free view, optimized production elides the ViewCell, and the hidden read becomes stale or escapes ownership. The ruled implementation therefore accepts only special forms and an explicit audited, position-aware macro set and rejects every unaudited macro at compile time.

Active Spec 004, guide, migrator drafts, and compiler error prose still call property values, condition tests, for collections, and wrapper expressions opaque. Read literally, that promises arbitrary macro acceptance and contradicts the sound compiler grammar. This is public programming-model drift and must close before the S2 boundary.

## Deliverable

After rf2-vxgfnd.100 lands, reconcile the authoritative grammar and teaching surfaces with the exact landed compiler behavior. Explain that expression values remain ordinary Clojure values and are opaque with respect to DOM/template interpretation, while their lexical syntax is still audited for finite reactive ownership. State the exact initial supported macro set from the landed compiler; distinguish special forms, audited transparent/position-aware macros, ordinary function calls, and rejected unaudited macros. Document the didactic diagnostic and recovery paths: use a supported core form, move pure computation into an ordinary function/value, pass reactive values into helpers, or make the reactive boundary a defview.

Required surfaces include spec/004-Views.md, the active synthesis Spec-004 draft/guide wording used for S2 conformance, TESTING or the compiler test inventory, and any current migrator rule that promises wrappers/macros are universally untouched. Classify historical/ignored copies rather than sweeping blindly. Keep ui/sub and ui/lease source call shapes unchanged; this is grammar documentation, not a blessed-table delta.

Do not add generic double macroexpansion, runtime dynamic sites, a macro interpreter, ViewCell overhead for sub-free views, or a compatibility fallback. Do not broaden the allowlist speculatively: any future addition needs lexical-scope plus hidden-reactive-injection counterfixtures.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 004 and the active guide no longer imply that arbitrary macros are accepted inside compiler-owned expressions.
- The exact landed audited macro set and the distinction between value opacity and lexical ownership analysis are clear and consistent across normative and teaching text.
- Public ui/sub and ui/lease remain compiler-owned source forms; direct/unlowered helpers are not taught as dynamic reactive sites.
- A didactic rejected-macro example names practical recovery paths without suggesting a runtime shim.
- Migrator/guide claims about or/threading/other wrappers match the landed allowlist exactly and do not promise unsupported custom macros.
- Existing hidden-sub/helper/macro compiler fixtures from rf2-vxgfnd.100 are cited as executable proof; docs and compiler error-roster gates pass.
- No frozen API table change, production runtime cost, generic macroexpansion system, adapter work, or generated docs/spec edit is introduced.
notes:
Sequence after rf2-vxgfnd.100 and active spec owner rf2-q4uh2p. Prefer clustering into the serialized rf2-vxgfnd.103 + rf2-vxgfnd.110 spec/docs PR if both predecessors have merged, while preserving separate closure evidence. Blocks the S2 boundary review.

Spec 004 gains the normative closed expression-macro grammar (exact audited set or/and/when/when-not/cond/->/->>/some->/some->>/cond->/cond->>; value-opacity vs lexical ownership; didactic rejection + recovery paths; S2 stage row citing the rf2-vxgfnd.100 fixtures in re-frame.ui.compiler-macro-resolution-jvm-test); synthesis 02 draft + migrator-rewrite-rules reconciled (no universal-wrapper promise). title: Normalize inline image reg-sub metadata for ordinary and override schema validation
description:
## Problem

An inline frame image registration such as `:reg-sub [[q {:schema :image/int} body]]` is lowered into a registrar descriptor whose schema remains under `:metadata`. Both the ordinary subscription return validator and re-frame.ui's static sub-override validator read runnable metadata from the descriptor's top level. Consequently the real image-authoritative path invokes no schema validator: an invalid ordinary subscription value or frame-scoped static override can surface raw even though the inline image declares a schema.

This was reproduced against PR #5819's merged runtime using `rf/image` -> `rf/make-frame {:images [...]}` -> frame-scoped `reactive/sub-read`; validator calls were empty. Flat selected/global registrations are not a valid substitute because the required S2 proof specifically exercises inline image authority and conflicting global metadata.

## Deliverable

Establish one canonical runnable descriptor shape for inline `:reg-sub` entries. Prefer normalizing inline metadata at the image lowering/registration boundary so `:schema` and the other runtime-consumed registration metadata are available where every subscription path already reads them, while preserving the nested metadata/provenance required by introspection. If an accessor is chosen instead, it must be shared by ordinary subscription validation and the re-frame.ui override path; do not add a UI-only merge that leaves ordinary subscriptions broken.

Preserve image-over-global authority, exact frame incarnation routing, schema identity/explain/reason evidence, omitted-versus-explicit values, and existing registrar/introspection output. Do not introduce adapter compatibility plumbing or make re-frame.ui depend on Reagent/UIx/Helix. This is a focused metadata-shape correction, not a second validation system.

## Proof

Add a core regression using a real inline image registration that proves both arms:

1. ordinary frame-scoped subscription return validation rejects an invalid value according to the inline schema;
2. static sub-override validation resolves the same inline image metadata rather than conflicting global metadata and rejects an invalid override with the correct `:where :sub-override`, frame, sub/query, schema, explain, and reason evidence.

Include a valid control and a deliberate conflicting global schema so flattening authority or selecting the wrong descriptor fails. Add mutation proof that restoring nested-only runtime metadata makes both validation assertions red. Run focused image/sub/schema tests plus UI JVM/CLJS/browser gates needed by the shared descriptor consumer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Inline `:reg-sub` runnable descriptors expose one authoritative metadata shape consumed consistently by ordinary subscription and re-frame.ui override validation.
- Invalid ordinary values from a real frame image are rejected by that image's declared schema.
- Invalid static overrides are rejected by that same image schema, with correct typed evidence; conflicting global metadata does not win.
- Valid values continue to pass, nested provenance/introspection remains correct, and image/frame incarnation routing is unchanged.
- The correction lives at a shared canonical boundary or accessor; there is no UI-only workaround that leaves ordinary subscriptions unvalidated.
- No adapter compatibility layer, frozen public API delta, or second validation implementation is introduced.
- Focused core image/sub/schema suites and affected UI JVM/CLJS/browser gates pass, with a mutation proving nested-only metadata reopens the hole.
notes: Confirmed empirically while preflighting rf2-vxgfnd.58 after PR #5819. Fix before the mounted image-schema/HMR matrix; do not weaken .58 to a flat selected/global registration.

title: Close mounted G-3 hook cardinality and clarify the G-6 stress split
description:
## Problem

The S2 boundary-review preflight found that the normative G-3 and G-6 rows are not yet matched by executable proof.

G-3 in ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/07-testing.md requires a compiled view with 1/4/8/16 subscription sites to use one React subscription hook, one body invocation, and at most one notification per dirty cell after drain quiescence. The merged reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc fixture is headless. It proves one capture/body invocation, N real leases, and one notification, but it never mounts React and cannot detect a compiler/runtime regression that calls useSyncExternalStore once per site. Such a duplicate-hook implementation could pass every current G-3 assertion while violating the production cost model.

G-6 currently reads `10k abandoned / mount-unmount / Activity cycles => baseline owners, zero retention`. The actual intended evidence is split: the merged headless gates run 10k abandoned renders/cold probes, while rf2-vxgfnd.12.2 deliberately adds bounded repeated real-browser StrictMode mount/unmount and Activity hide/reveal cycles. Reading the row as 10k browser lifecycle cycles conflicts with the filed proof and would add a slow browser stress test without a distinct correctness discriminator.

## Deliverable

After rf2-vxgfnd.12.2 lands, add one mounted first-party re-frame.ui G-3 fixture for 1/4/8/16 lexical sub sites. Prove exactly one useSyncExternalStore/ViewCell subscription boundary for the compiled view, one body execution for the changed batch, the expected independent leases, and one post-quiescence notification/commit batch. The proof must run through ui/adapter and real React; it must not infer hook cardinality merely from one ViewCell object. Add a deliberate per-site-uSES mutation or equivalent structural mutation that fails the fixture.

Reconcile G-6's normative and TESTING rows to explicitly require both: (a) 10k headless abandoned/cold-probe iterations returning to zero ownership/retention, and (b) bounded repeated real-browser StrictMode mount/unmount plus Activity hide/reveal cycles returning every root, ViewCell, observation owner, sub-cache, DOM container, and scheduled-work count to baseline. Reuse the .12.2 browser proof; do not duplicate it or inflate it to 10k browser cycles unless measurement finds a distinct failure threshold.

Keep the proof on native re-frame.ui. Do not import UIx/Helix/slim, add production counters, change the frozen API, or broaden this into a benchmark framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Mounted 1/4/8/16-site compiled views prove exactly one useSyncExternalStore/ViewCell hook boundary, one affected body execution, independent site leases, and one notification/root-commit batch after drain quiescence.
- A per-site-hook structural mutation fails deterministically while the correct single-hook implementation passes.
- G-6 wording unambiguously splits the existing 10k headless abandonment/cold-probe stress from bounded repeated real-browser StrictMode/Activity lifecycle proof.
- The existing 10k headless assertions remain unchanged and green; .12.2's mounted lifecycle evidence is reused rather than duplicated.

title: S2 gate contract: correct G-5 epoch fan-in to drain-quiescence render batching
description:
## Problem

At current HEAD, `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/07-testing.md:100`, in §5 "Gates that decide the architecture", still defines G-5 as:

`8 deps in one event ⇒ 1 render; 8 epochs ⇒ 8`

The second clause is a live normative contradiction. It equates causal/write-side epoch evidence with read/render-batch count. Mike has ruled the opposite scheduling law: all queued write-side events in one run-to-completion drain execute and settle to quiescence, then the affected ViewCells are read/rendered in one batch. Eight epochs occurring within that same drain are therefore not eight renders. Only distinct drains separated by a real host yield establish separate render batches.

The current S2 proof bead `rf2-vxgfnd.12` already records the correction and its G-13 accounting refinement: for C affected ViewCells, expect C enroll/advance operations and C component-body renders, but exactly one root commit batch per drain—not C commits. Merged Spec 006 invariant 6 and the mounted queued-cascade fixture use the same drain-quiescence semantics. Leaving §5 stale makes the gate suite contradict the gate implementation brief and invites a future worker to encode the obsolete behavior.

A prior documentation sweep, closed `rf2-vxgfnd.66`, did not eliminate this sentence. Do not reopen or amend that closed bead; this is the current-S2 follow-up.
design:
## Required correction

1. Rewrite the G-5 row at `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/07-testing.md:100` so it distinguishes epochs/write evidence from post-quiescence reads and render batches.
2. State positively that every queued write still executes; coalescing the read/render side must not be described as dropping, merging, or skipping write epochs.
3. Make the row and any nearby explanatory prose consistent with `rf2-vxgfnd.12` and its G-13 accounting: C affected ViewCells may each enroll, advance, and body-render once while React performs one root commit batch for the drain. Never infer the number of render batches or commits from epoch count alone.
4. Preserve the cross-drain falsifier: events separated by a real host yield belong to distinct drains and should produce distinct post-drain render batches.
5. Audit the current normative synthesis/guide/draft/gate prose for equivalent stale claims. Historical review/disposition text may remain only when it is unambiguously labelled as historical or superseded.

This bead changes contract prose only. It must not alter runtime scheduling, tests, thresholds, or the frozen API.
acceptance_criteria:
- `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/07-testing.md` §5 no longer says or implies `8 epochs ⇒ 8` renders/commits. Its G-5 example says that eight queued write epochs in one drain all execute and are followed by one post-quiescence read/render batch; separate batches require separate drains established by real host yields.
- The corrected prose agrees with `rf2-vxgfnd.12`, G-13, and Spec 006 invariant 6: count C affected ViewCell enroll/advance operations and C component-body renders separately from exactly one root commit batch per drain. It does not use epoch count as render-count evidence.
- A repository prose audit covers current normative material under `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/` (including guide and drafts), relevant `TESTING.md` gate text, and re-frame.ui runtime/test docstrings. The PR records the grep command and result; at minimum it searches stale equivalences such as `8 epochs.*8`, `epochs?.*(renders?|commits?)`, and `C React commits` (or demonstrably equivalent patterns), and explains any retained historical hits.
- The PR includes a manual prose check of the corrected row and its neighboring gate/cost-model cross-references, explicitly citing `07-testing.md` §5, `05-production.md` §3, `rf2-vxgfnd.12`/G-13, and Spec 006 invariant 6.

title: DECISION: adapter lifecycle state when teardown throws
description:
## Problem

The S2 Tier-3/public-root teardown work exposes a frozen lifecycle ambiguity in re-frame.substrate.adapter/dispose-adapter! and public rf/destroy-adapter!. Current implementation and docstrings define adapter-disposed? as true iff disposal completed successfully. If the installed adapter's cleanup throws, control never clears installed-adapter and never sets the breadcrumb. The process therefore retains an adapter that may be partially torn down, blocks fresh installation with :rf.error/adapter-already-installed, and lets later delegation reach an indeterminate host.

re-frame.ui adapter teardown is total at the framework ownership level: it snapshots the exact installed generation, attempts all public-root/ViewCell/observation cleanup, force-deads targeted ownership even when a host unmount throws, and reports failures. Core must decide whether a cleanup exception makes destroy transactional/rollback-like or is a one-way terminal lifecycle boundary.

## Decision for Mike

Option A — successful-only breadcrumb and seated slot. Preserve the current frozen wording. If adapter cleanup throws, leave the adapter installed and adapter-disposed? false. This implies the installed adapter remains valid/retryable after a partial teardown, so every adapter would need a specified rollback or retry-safe state machine. The current adapters do not provide that guarantee; a fresh install remains blocked.

Option B — terminal teardown boundary (recommended). Once destruction of the exact installed adapter begins, the lifecycle is one-way. Attempt every cleanup action, retain the primary failure and attach/report secondary failures, then in a finally-shaped core boundary clear the exact install slot and set adapter-disposed? true even if cleanup threw. Rethrow the primary error. Subsequent delegation reports :rf.error/adapter-disposed and a fresh adapter may install. A concurrent/replacement generation must never be cleared by stale teardown.

## Consequences

Option B changes frozen public wording from successful disposal to terminal teardown having begun. It does not make cleanup failures silent or claim cleanup succeeded; adapter-disposed? describes the lifecycle/slot state, not outcome quality. It simplifies every adapter, avoids an unusable half-live process, and matches frame/root teardown's one-way terminal posture. Diagnostics must preserve all failures and exact-generation fencing.

Option A avoids a wording change but requires substantially more machinery and an unjustified semantic promise: rollback of arbitrary host cleanup, DOM unmount, subscriptions, effects, and user callbacks. Retrying a partly completed cleanup can double-release ownership. It is neither implemented nor naturally implementable.

## Required ruling

Approve A or B. If B is approved, update Spec 006, API/core docstrings and lifecycle tests atomically with the Tier-3 adapter teardown PR. If A is chosen, the current Tier-3 branch's finally-clear commit must be dropped and a separately designed retry/poisoned-adapter contract is required before S2 can close.
acceptance_criteria:
- Mike selects successful-only seated semantics or one-way terminal semantics.
- The ruling states the meaning of adapter-disposed? when cleanup throws.
- Exact-generation slot clearing, primary/secondary error behavior, reinstall behavior, and subsequent delegation are explicit.
- The selected wording is applied atomically to Spec 006, public API/core docstrings, implementation, and fixtures before S2 conformance.
close_reason: Mike auto-approved the Codex recommendation on 2026-07-13: Option B. Adapter teardown is a one-way terminal lifecycle boundary. Once teardown of the exact installed generation begins, attempt all cleanup, preserve/rethrow the primary failure and attach/report secondaries, clear only that generation in finally, set adapter-disposed? true even on cleanup failure, permit a fresh install, and never clear a replacement generation. Implementation/spec/docstring/fixture delivery remains tracked by rf2-vxgfnd.12.1 and rf2-vxgfnd.104.

title: Reconcile Spec 002 and drain docs with claim-before-dead destroy fence
description:
## Problem

PR #5811 correctly adds the exact-incarnation destroy claim as the ordinary-queue cutoff before lifecycle-dead publication, but current normative and implementation prose still teaches destroyed?-only cutoff or an incomplete teardown order. That mismatch is load-bearing for concurrent frame teardown.

Spec 002 currently says mid-drain disposal is detected by :destroyed? before dequeue (around line 2093), while production now rejects an envelope when the exact incarnation has been claimed, is lifecycle-dead, or is absent. The claim is deliberately earlier than :destroyed? publication: it atomically cuts pre-claim waiting envelopes, post-claim ordinary arrivals may enqueue but are dropped before handler/effect/child execution, and the private token-scoped on-destroy cascade remains permitted while lifecycle is still live. The emitted dropped count combines claim-time and ordinary-drain removals.

Other stale clauses describe on-destroy as the first teardown step or promise that every newly queued envelope is picked up by the single drainer/fixed-point loop without naming the disposal exception. Frame/router/core docstrings likewise omit the claim boundary or describe only events still queued at the later check. A future implementer following those words can reintroduce the exact race #5811 fixes.

## Deliverable

After the current spec hot-zone owners finish, reconcile Spec 002 and the frame/router/core lifecycle docs with the shipped claim-before-dead linearization. Define the exact order:

1. An already-dequeued ordinary event may finish.
2. Claim the exact frame incarnation and atomically cut its pre-claim waiting ordinary queue.
3. Run on-destroy and synchronous descendants only through the private token-scoped cleanup cascade while the frame remains lifecycle-live.
4. Drop post-claim ordinary arrivals before invocation, effects, or child dispatch.
5. Publish lifecycle-dead and retain immediate :rf.error/frame-destroyed behavior for later dispatch.

State that disposal evidence/drop counts combine claim-time and later check-time removals. Preserve the distinction between the claim-window drain-interrupted outcome and dispatch after lifecycle-dead. Add narrow cross-links/exceptions to single-drainer and fixed-point absolutes. This is contract/doc reconciliation only; do not change the now-proven runtime algorithm.

Required anchors include spec/002-Frames.md around 591, 611-619, 613, 1637, 1677, and 2093; implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc destroy-order docstring around 2918-2950 and inline wording around 3059; router.cljc around 2904-2961 and 3450-3453; and the public core.cljc destroy-frame documentation around 867-870 where the concurrency boundary belongs. Re-check line numbers after #5811 lands.

## Proof

Mechanically compare every revised claim with #5811's exact production predicates and fixtures. The existing tests must demonstrate: post-claim/pre-dead ordinary dispatch cannot execute; pre-claim waiting work is cut; on-destroy private cascade still completes; destroy from an active handler is ordered; and old-incarnation A cannot affect replacement B. Grep must find no current destroyed?-only dequeue claim or unconditional newly-queued-is-picked-up promise. Run focused frame lifecycle/incarnation/late-bind tests plus docs/link gates.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 002 defines claim-before-dead as the exact-incarnation ordinary-queue cutoff and preserves private cleanup-cascade execution.
- Pre-claim queued work, post-claim arrivals, already-dequeued work, lifecycle-dead dispatch, and combined drop evidence are distinguished precisely.
- Single-drainer/fixed-point wording includes the teardown exception and correct cross-links.
- frame.cljc, router.cljc, and core.cljc docs match the shipped order and predicates.
- No runtime semantics change in this slice.
- Existing #5811 mutation-proven fixtures and focused lifecycle/incarnation suites remain green; docs/link gates pass.
