title: Eliminate retained production JSX lowering overhead exposed by matched G-1
description:
## Problem

The Mike-ruled matched G-1 direct-render gate now compares each compiled sample with a semantically memo-matched hand JSX sample and computes p50/p95 from paired compiled/hand ratios at the unchanged 1.10 limits. PR #5812 proves the estimator is no longer the cause of the todos-20 red: repeated normal runs measure about 1.0817-1.0921 p50 and 1.1335-1.1398 p95, while a controlled generic classes-string slow path measures about 1.44-1.55. The compiled production output therefore has a real p95 lowering-cost miss.

Inspection of the :advanced bundle identifies four concrete costs absent from competent hand JSX:

1. emit_cljs.cljc routes every element through runtime/jsx2, jsx3, jsxs2, or jsxs3. runtime.cljs claims Closure inlines these wrappers, but the optimized bundle retains wrapper functions and compiled call sites invoke them while hand code calls React's jsx/jsxs directly.
2. jsx-call constructs dynamic props through immediately invoked functions around js-obj; the compiled todo row pays these IIFEs for ordinary elements while hand JSX emits direct object literals.
3. Dynamic class concatenation lowers through generic str/truthiness helpers rather than a direct conditional string expression.
4. Known DOM attrs such as data-priority and checked retain generic conversion calls at each row.

This is production substrate overhead on the flagship compiler path, not benchmark noise and not the always-memo policy cost already isolated by #5812. The existing emitted-JS golden is too broad to prove call-site inlining because direct calls from the hand baseline and the wrapper bodies themselves can satisfy it.

## Deliverable

After the active digest-carrier compiler owner releases the hot zone, make the smallest structural emitter/runtime correction that removes the measured avoidable calls from optimized compiled output. Start with the shared JSX wrapper choke point: either emit direct React jsx-runtime calls or provide an actually inlinable shape proven at compiled call sites. Then address only remaining measured costs needed to restore robust headroom; do not build a second lowering system, special-case the todos view, or tune the benchmark/threshold.

Preserve all template semantics: React key/ref behavior, children cardinality, nil/boolean/keyword/string coercion, custom elements, controlled inputs, class ordering, goog.DEBUG diagnostics, source annotations, foreign components, JVM AST parity, HMR signatures, and production elision. Prefer a single elegant emitter-level shape over per-attribute patches. Any optimization beyond wrapper removal must name a measured hot operation and demonstrate benefit.

## Proof

Use PR #5812's paired matched baseline unchanged. Repeated optimized runs must satisfy both 1.10 limits with at least approximately 0.03 headroom, while the controlled slow-path mutation still fails decisively. Add narrow optimized-output assertions that inspect compiled view call sites, not merely the whole bundle, proving the removed wrapper/IIFE/generic-helper shapes are absent where claimed and React jsx/jsxs calls remain semantically correct.

Run compiler JVM tests, direct-render byte equality and emitted-JS goldens, the G-1 advanced gate repeatedly, production-elision/bundle isolation, and the focused browser/controlled-input/custom-element fixtures for any changed lowering path. For each removed generic conversion, include counterexamples proving values that require conversion still behave correctly. Record bundle-size and paired-ratio before/after evidence in the PR.
acceptance_criteria:
- The unchanged paired G-1 todos-20 gate passes p50 and p95 <= 1.10 with approximately 0.03 repeated-run headroom.
- The controlled slow-path mutation remains a deterministic gate failure.
- Optimized compiled view call sites no longer pay retained runtime JSX wrapper calls; any additional removed IIFE/generic conversion is proven at the exact call site.
- Direct-render HTML remains byte-identical to the memo-matched hand baseline.
- Key/ref/children, dynamic class/attrs, controlled inputs, custom elements, debug diagnostics, JVM parity, HMR, and production elision remain correct.
- No benchmark threshold, estimator, fixture workload, or product semantics are weakened.
- Compiler, G-1, browser slice, and bundle/elision gates pass.
notes:
Sequence only after rf2-n7ff9f releases compiler/emit_cljs.cljc. PR #5812 is the honest benchmark carrier and remains draft while this defect is red. Do not amend the locked rf2-xwmpm4 bead; this is its separately tracked follow-up. The simplest delivery may continue #5812 after its current owner hands off, but never allow two workers to edit that branch concurrently.

INDEPENDENT ADVANCED-OUTPUT REVIEW 2026-07-13: the dominant differential is 84 surviving runtime JSX forwarding calls per todos-20 render (24 parent + 60 row); runtime.cljs's inlining claim is empirically false. First fix must emit a direct react/jsx-runtime module-property call with exact 2/3 arity and falsey-but-present key preservation. Do not bind the imported function as a CLJS var, which reintroduces IFn dispatch. If more headroom is needed, the next measured cost is 40 compiler-generated cljs.core/js-obj IIFEs; a direct ordered literal-object emission is eligible only for compile-known string keys and must preserve evaluation order/advanced property spelling. The exactly-one-flag static-base conditional is a small safe optional win with empty-base/evaluate-once proofs. Do NOT generically elide runtime/attr-val: keyword/string/number and checked-value counterexamples show its total conversion is semantically earned without type proof. Header destructuring, seq traversal, memo comparator, and loop shape are already materially matched; do not target them.

title: Implement the frozen S2 ui/lease ownership contract
description:
## Problem

The frozen S2 API table exposes `(ui/lease descriptor)`, but the current JVM and CLJS implementations are placeholders that throw. A compiled view therefore cannot own a Resources lease even though S2 claims the view-side surface and ownership contract. Leaving the stub would make S2 conformance false and push resource lifetime back into adapter-specific imperative code.

## Ruled contract

Mike approved the simplest fully correct semantics. The closed descriptor is `nil` (inactive site) or `{:resource qualified-keyword, :scope optional, :params optional}`; unknown keys and malformed literals/dynamic values fail before capture/dispatch. Frame comes from render context, owner is framework-minted, cause is framework-owned dev evidence. Preserve missing `:params` versus explicit nil.

Resource reconciliation does NOT promise all-or-nothing success across multiple resource handlers or frames. Prevalidate the complete desired set, retain rf=-equal same-site owners, mint a fresh owner for retarget, queue every ensure before any release in deterministic order per frame, and let each frame's ordinary FIFO router drain all writes to quiescence before one read/render flush. No global coordinator or synchronous dispatch.

## Deliverable

Use the compiler-authoritative generic lexical site identity from rf2-vxgfnd.100 for both sub and lease sites; do not invent a render-order counter or second indexing scheme. Lower to a compact internal lease-site capture. Permit recognized leading lease declarations before one final template without opening arbitrary multi-form view bodies. JVM evaluates descriptor structure/manifest metadata but performs no host acquisition and returns no tree node.

At commit, reconcile site-keyed held state transactionally with acquire-before-release ordering. Two lexical sites targeting the same resource retain independent owners. Lease-only views must use the fixed lifecycle/capture skeleton but must not pay `useSyncExternalStore`; sub+lease views share one ViewCell. Activity hide, unmount, root teardown, frame destroy, throwing host cleanup, StrictMode replay, and HMR must release or retain ownership according to the committed site identity. Use the optional Resources feature gate without pulling `re-frame.resources` into lease-free bundles. Share the process-global resource-owner mint with frozen stock Reagent rather than minting collisions in UI.

Expose dev-only committed lease evidence for Xray join by view/render/site/frame/owner; production retains only correctness-required compact site/descriptor/frame/owner state. No public API/table delta beyond implementing the already-frozen `(lease descriptor)` row.

## Proof

Compiler/runtime/browser/JVM fixtures must cover: two identical descriptors at distinct sites; conditional site disappearance without alias; literal/dynamic validation; missing-vs-nil params; render/abandoned render owns nothing; lease-only view; equal rerender zero churn; retarget ensure-before-release with fresh owner; multi-site ordering; one same-frame drain/read batch; independent owners; StrictMode; Activity hide/reveal; unmount/throw/frame-destroy; cross-frame retarget; missing Resources typed error; JVM structural neutrality; HMR retention/release; advanced lease-free isolation and no uSES for lease-only. Mutation must show site-id loss or shared capture fails before fix.

## Sequencing

Current S2 close-first work. Depends on compiler digest -> rf2-vxgfnd.100 generic site identity and on the exact-render-capture correction. Do not dispatch until those merge; avoid concurrent compiler/reactive hot-zone owners.
notes:
S2 BOUNDARY-PREFLIGHT PIN (2026-07-13): keep the two lease families explicit in implementation prose and conformance rows. Observation-port subscription acquire has transactional rollback of partially acquired observation targets. ui/lease resource reconciliation does NOT make cross-handler/cross-frame event dispatch globally all-or-nothing: prevalidate the desired set, retain equal owners, mint fresh owners for retarget, queue all ensures before releases in deterministic per-frame order, and let ordinary FIFO drains report failures. title: Bind ViewCell commit to the exact render capture
description:
## Problem

`re-frame.ui.reactive/with-capture` currently writes a render's `:latest-capture` into the shared ViewCell ref, and the later React effect reads that shared slot to decide what to commit. In concurrent/speculative React, an abandoned render can run after the render that actually commits and overwrite the slot. The committed effect can then acquire/release subscription or resource ownership for the abandoned render rather than its own render. Current headless abandoned-render tests do not exercise this exact real-React closure/commit race.

This is already a subscription correctness defect and becomes externally causal when `ui/lease` owns Resources. It must be fixed before resource-site ownership lands.

## Deliverable

Make each rendered React element/effect close over its exact immutable capture. Change the internal render contract to return or otherwise bind `[host-element capture]` without publishing speculative capture into shared ViewCell state. The commit/layout/passive effects must call `reactive/commit!` and later resource reconciliation with the capture produced by that same committed render. An abandoned render must leave no shared capture that a later effect can observe. Preserve StrictMode replay, HMR generation checks, before-paint subscription publication, and the one stable hook skeleton.

No public API or frozen-table change. Do not serialize renders, add global registries, or disable concurrency.

## Proof

Add a deterministic mounted React fixture that interleaves two captures so render A commits while a later speculative/abandoned render B writes a different dependency set. Prove A's effect commits A only, B owns nothing, late B notifications cannot render, and final unmount returns ViewCells/observation owners to baseline. Include a mutation restoring shared `:latest-capture` and demonstrate red-before-fix. Cover StrictMode replay and same-signature HMR; verify optimized output adds no debug bookkeeping.

## Sequencing

Current S2 P1. Sequence after active PR #5808 releases `reactive.cljc`/mounted harness, then before the `ui/lease` implementation bead. Coordinate with rf2-vxgfnd.100 lexical-site work but avoid compiler edits here.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION PREP 2026-07-13: smallest correct internal contract is with-capture returning [host-element immutable-capture] and commit! accepting (cell capture). Remove :latest-capture, its inspection fn, render-time shared atom mutation, :no-capture, and all compatibility arities. In viewcell/render, destructure the pair and let the no-deps layout-effect closure capture that exact immutable value; preserve hook order, lifecycle effect, generation checks, transactional acquisition/rollback, and evidence comparison. React commits the effect closure stored on the selected finished Fiber, so an abandoned render cannot overwrite the committed Fiber's capture. This also removes one atom mutation/state-map allocation per reactive render.

DETERMINISTIC BROWSER PROOF: add a dedicated -dom-cljs-test using real React Suspense + StrictMode. Render A and register A's layout-effect closure, then have a later sibling invoke original with-capture on the same recorded cell for B and throw one stable never-resolving Promise. Suspense abandons B and commits fallback, then A's effect runs. Assert DOM/committed targets/owners are A-only, B movement cannot render, A movement does, and unmount restores all baselines. Mutation restoring shared :latest-capture must commit B and fail. Do not use scheduler mocks; ReactDOM is not linked to the installed scheduler mock.

Migrate every internal caller atomically. Headless proof retains cap-a, captures/discards cap-b, then commits cap-a. HMR proof covers same-signature A capture followed by abandoned B while changed-signature remains stale-rejected. Correct the nearby advance-generation! doc typo saying same-signature bumps; it is changed-signature. No spec/public API/build/workflow change. Sequence strictly after #5808 because it overlaps reactive.cljc and several teardown tests.

title: Destroying ui/adapter must tear down public compiled roots
description:
## Problem

The first-party `ui/adapter` and public compiled-root API currently maintain disjoint root registries. `re-frame.ui.client` records roots created by `ui/mount` / `ui/create-root` in its `live-roots` registry. `ui/adapter` delegates disposal to the generic React spine, whose `:dispose-adapter!` only unmounts roots enrolled through the adapter map's generic `:render` path in its private active-roots cell. Public compiled roots never enter that cell.

Consequently `(rf/destroy-adapter!)` can clear the adapter/substrate while leaving compiled DOM mounted, `client/live-root-ids` occupied, ViewCells connected, and observation owners alive. This contradicts Spec 006's total adapter-disposal/active-root lifecycle and the compiled substrate's adapter-destroy => dead ownership claim. It also prevents deterministic same-id/container reuse after re-init.

## Deliverable

Make first-party adapter disposal own every live public compiled root. Compose `ui/adapter` disposal with an identity/incarnation-safe `re-frame.ui.client` all-root teardown before final substrate disposal, without teaching the generic spine about compiled client internals or creating a second public teardown API. Teardown must clear DOM, unregister root ids, mark/enforce ViewCell dead state, release observation ownership, and remain total when host unmount/effect cleanup throws. A stale disposal from an old adapter/root incarnation must not tear down a newly installed same-id root.

Keep UIx/Helix/slim transition adapters unchanged; they are removed at S7. Preserve stock Reagent compatibility. No frozen public API/table change.

## Proof

Add a real-browser fixture that initializes `ui/adapter`, mounts a subscription-bearing compiled view through public `ui/mount` or `ui/create-root`, then calls `rf/destroy-adapter!`. Assert the connected DOM is cleared, `client/live-root-ids` is empty, root-cell/live-cell and observation-owner counts return to baseline/dead, and no post-destroy notification can render. Reinitialize `ui/adapter` and reuse the same root id/container successfully. Exercise multiple roots, a throwing host unmount/effect cleanup path, and an old-dispose/new-incarnation race. Include a mutation showing generic-spine-only disposal fails.

## Sequencing

S2 close-first correctness follow-up found during independent review of PR #5808 after #5809 introduced public `ui/adapter`. Coordinate with the active Tier-3/browser harness owner; bundle only if one owner can retain a clean diff. Do not merge #5808 as S2-complete without this behavior being covered, whether in that PR or a sequenced follow-up.

title: Frame destroy claim can release queued drain before lifecycle-dead publication
description:
## Problem
Independent review of PR #5807 exposed a pre-existing current-main race in re-frame.frame-lifecycle-test/destroy-frame-pending-drain-pins-no-op-contract. claim-frame-destroy! runs through call-serialized-with-drain!. When the cold serialization lock releases, it observes queued events and re-kicks a real drain while the frame record is still live: the destroy claim is set, but :lifecycle :destroyed? has not yet been published by mark-frame-destroyed!. Queued handlers can therefore execute and produce side effects in the destroy window. Repeated/single-var runs observe actual side-effects 2 where the contract expects 0; ordinary CI can pass because timing hides it.

## Contract
Once frame destruction is claimed, already-queued handlers for that incarnation are no-op: they must not mutate app-db, emit user effects, or re-enter lifecycle work. Destroy cleanup and queue release must have one linearization order; a cold-lock release must not start a drain in the gap between claim and dead publication.

## Deliverable
Make destroy claim/dead publication/drain-release structurally atomic with respect to queue execution. Prefer one lifecycle/serialization choke point over timing sleeps or test-only flags. Preserve idempotent destroy, current incarnation fencing, queued-work disposal evidence, and concurrent create/destroy semantics. Audit call-serialized-with-drain! callers so a narrow fix does not strand unrelated queues or reintroduce same-thread dispatch deadlock.

## Proof
Turn the existing timing-sensitive fixture into a deterministic barrier test that pauses after claim and before dead publication, forces lock release/queued work, and fails on current main. Cover cold and already-draining paths, concurrent duplicate destroy, queued child dispatch/effects, and a normal non-destroy release that still re-kicks exactly one drain. Run core JVM lifecycle/concurrency suites.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deterministic pre-fix fixture proves queued handlers can run in the claim→dead window.
- After fix, no queued handler/app-db/effect work executes once destroy is claimed.
- Destroy claim, lifecycle-dead publication, and drain release have a documented linearization point.
- Normal serialized queue release still drains to quiescence without stranding or double-draining.
- Duplicate/concurrent destroy remains idempotent and incarnation-safe.
- Core lifecycle and concurrency gates pass without sleeps.

title: S2 compiler: carry lexical sub-site identity and preserve rf=-equal parametric query objects
description:
## Problem
Spec 004 §Reactive reads promises compiler-indexed lexical subscription sites and preservation of the prior query object when newly evaluated query arguments are rf= equal. The current emitter records sites only in the manifest: emitted calls are ordinary (sub query), sub-read accepts only query, and stabilization is keyed by frame+query. A parametric view such as (ui/defview item [{:keys [id]}] [:span (ui/sub [:item/by-id id])]) reconstructs a fresh vector on an rf=-equal rerender; no site token reaches runtime, so the promised identity/reuse contract is unimplemented even though target-key tests pass.

## Deliverable
Emit a stable lexical sub-site identity into the client/JVM runtime call shape and make the reconciler preserve the previously committed query object when the same site's new query is rf= equal. A genuinely changed query must retarget transactionally (acquire new before releasing old), and conditional absence must not alias another site. Keep site metadata/dev diagnostics elided from optimized production unless needed for the O(1) runtime key; do not introduce a registry interpreter or per-render global scan.

## Proof
Add compiler golden/AST tests plus mounted/headless runtime fixtures covering fresh-but-rf=-equal parametric queries, real changes, two equal queries at distinct lexical sites, HMR same-signature reuse, and abandoned renders. Include a mutation that drops the site identity or keys only by query and fails before the fix. Measure/guard no V-wide work.

## Sequencing
Current S2 obligation. Sequence after rf2-n7ff9f digest carrier lands; coordinate with rf2-8hf77d because both touch compiler/runtime HMR authority. No frozen-table change is authorized.
acceptance_criteria:
- Emitted CLJS and JVM forms carry a deterministic compiler-indexed site id.
- rf=-equal reevaluation at one site reuses the prior committed query object and does not churn observation leases.
- Changed queries acquire-before-release and abandoned renders retain nothing.
- Two lexical sites with equal queries remain distinct owners.
- Same-signature HMR preserves site identity; incompatible signature follows the ruled remount path.
- Compiler/runtime tests include a deterministic pre-fix mutation and production-cost/elision proof.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION PREP 2026-07-13: this is a ViewCell identity correction, not only an emitted arity. Current capture/committed/value maps key by (frame, query), so two lexical sites with rf=-equal queries collapse to one lease/callback. Reconcile ownership by compiler site id; observation target remains destination/evidence identity only. Recommended internal token is a deterministic view-scoped compact source-anchor + structural/expr-path scalar. Ambiguity or anchor loss yields a new token and safe drop/acquire; never history-match old/new ASTs and never use a bare preorder ordinal that can transfer identity to a different site. The manifest retains index/source/path/expr-path for tools; production hot calls carry only the compact scalar.

EMISSION: rewrite every resolved lexical sub occurrence on both hosts to (reactive/sub-read sid query) and add sid to its manifest row. Refactor expression walking to return rewritten forms with metadata and thread them through every opaque expression position; current side-effect walk + raw-form retention would miss attrs/style/class/spread/component props/key/control tests/let/for/frame/handler data. Literal queries remain hoistable; parametric candidates may allocate but runtime preserves the last committed exact object. Do not put sid into the observation-port target ABI or add a query interpreter.

RUNTIME: capture is ordered by sid with per-site query/target/evidence/value; committed state is one sid-keyed map carrying exact query, target, lease, and value. sub-read compares only the same sid's prior committed query; rf=-equal uses the prior exact query object before target resolution and preserves that site's exact value. Commit keeps/acquires/releases by sid, stages all new/retargeted owners before releases, and gives equal-query sites distinct opaque leases/callbacks/refcount shares. Conditional absence releases only that sid. Tool/test accessors should expose committed sites/query/lease and derive legacy target projections only where useful.

HMR COORDINATION: serialize after rf2-8hf77d. Capture stamps body revision, which increments on every successful registration and is distinct from hook-signature remount generation. Commit rejects a capture whose body revision is no longer current. Same-signature stable shell then preserves the cell and stable sids; incompatible signature remounts. Without this split an old-body capture can acquire a deleted ghost site after same-signature reload.

PROOF: same-sid fresh rf=-equal query preserves identical query+lease; changed query logs acquire before release; two equal-query sids own two leases/refcount 2; conditional disappearance does not alias; 10k abandoned candidates own nothing and cannot become the preserved query; same-signature HMR keeps stable anchor ownership while old-body capture is stale; anchor ambiguity safely reacquires. Primary mutation keys capture/commit by target again and must collapse the two-site fixture. Advanced output retains only scalar sid + direct call and no source/path metadata/global scan. FINAL PREFLIGHT AFTER #5817 (2026-07-13): one .100 PR owns compiler analyzer/env/fingerprint/emission + reactive site-state migration. Generic allocator records both sub and future lease manifest rows; only scalar sid emits. Replace side-effect expression walker with metadata/evaluation-order/shadowing-aware rewriter and THREAD its returned form through every opaque expression position; lower resolved unshadowed ui/sub to reactive/sub-read sid query. Critical: strip sid from template-fingerprint/build-digest projection while retaining semantic query, so line/path-only changes do not perturb digest. Runtime capture/committed state keys by sid, stores exact query/target/value/lease; stabilize rf=-equal candidate to prior exact query BEFORE override/target resolution, then stabilize value per site. Keep one-arity sub-read only outside ViewCell; under ambient capture it fails loud. title: Implement compiler-authoritative whole-build digest carrier (Mike-approved Option A)
description:
## Problem

Spec 004C §2.1 requires one whole-build `:build-digest`: it covers every compiled `defview` across all modules, is identical for every root, and is byte-identical between the JVM/compiler projection and the browser client. The compiler already hashes the finalized committed whole-build view ledger, but `re-frame.ui.client/current-build-digest` independently hashes only runtime-registered/loaded views. Multi-entry or lazy-module builds therefore diverge whenever compiled views have not executed their registration code.

Mike approved Option A on 2026-07-13: preserve the ratified whole-build law and make the compiler the sole digest authority. This is a ruled implementation follow-up split from rf2-1rxznn after findings 1/2 merged in PR #5805. It does not change the frozen public API.

## Ruled design

Deliver the finalized compiler digest through a tiny checked-in CLJS carrier namespace transitively required by the UI runtime/client. The carrier is `^:dev/always`, contains a unique equal-length sentinel inside a `goog.DEBUG`-guarded O(1) reader, and is already compiled before Shadow's successful `:compile-finish` hook. At `:compile-finish`, using the hook's explicit `build-id`, compute the candidate whole-build digest and replace exactly one sentinel in that build-state's carrier `:output/:js`. Do not append modules, mutate output files directly, or rely only on late Closure defines: those shapes do not update ordinary HMR safely.

Compiler-state publication and carrier projection are one transaction: construct the candidate finalized slice, invoke a pure build-state projection that locates the carrier and patches exactly one sentinel, and commit the compiler authority only if projection succeeds. Missing/duplicate sentinel or carrier is a loud failure that leaves both JVM and client on the previous last-known-good digest. Failed compilation never reaches finish and likewise retains the prior digest.

`client/current-build-digest` reads the carrier scalar; delete its runtime registrar traversal/client-side fingerprint calculation. `^:dev/always` makes the carrier recompile/evaluate on every watch pass, including dependency-JAR use. Release optimization sees the patched source after compile-finish and must remove carrier, sentinel, digest literal, and traversal under `goog.DEBUG=false`.

REPL rule approved with Option A: a successful no-pass `defview` REPL evaluation is a digest commit boundary and its emitted development registration also installs the compiler's resulting digest into the carrier. An open real build must never emit a partial assignment. A configured/hookless CLJS build is unsupported and must fail loudly; both the build hook and existing `:cache-blockers #{re-frame.ui}` are load-bearing for warm-daemon completeness.

## Proof obligations

- Whole-build multi-entry/lazy-module fixture: a view in an unexecuted lazy module is included and client/JVM digests match.
- Two successful watch passes update the carrier; an intervening failed pass changes neither host's last-known-good digest.
- Two interleaved build IDs patch isolated carrier outputs and yield isolated scalars.
- Missing carrier, missing sentinel, and duplicate sentinel fail before compiler-state publication.
- Warm-cache build includes every view; document and test the required hook/cache-blocker configuration.
- Successful no-pass REPL `defview` updates compiler and client carrier; open-pass builds do not emit partial assignments; misconfigured hookless build fails loud.
- Advanced `goog.DEBUG=false` output contains none of `bd1-`, the sentinel, carrier code, client fingerprint traversal, or registry traversal. Preserve current production performance/elision gates.
- HMR uses the compiled carrier source, not module append/prepend; test the actual watch update shape.
- Existing root manifests continue to carry one identical whole-build scalar. No public API or Spec-004C semantic change.

## Implementation posture

Pre-alpha masterpiece: one authority, one scalar, explicit failure, minimal runtime work. Keep the carrier/injection internal and dev-only. Do not introduce module/root bookkeeping, per-entry identities, compatibility shims, or a second digest algorithm.
acceptance_criteria: Option A is complete when compiler/JVM and client read the same compiler-finalized whole-build digest for initial, watch/HMR, lazy-module, parallel-build, warm-cache, and REPL paths; failed/projection-failed passes retain last-known-good transactionally; advanced output fully elides the mechanism; all focused UI/compiler/CLJS/elision gates and CI are green; no frozen public API changes.
notes: MIKE RULING 2026-07-13 — REPL/build-digest semantics: approve Option C. `:build-digest` identifies the last successfully finalized configured build/watch pass. Direct unsaved no-pass REPL evaluation may replace a runtime view body/dev manifest but MUST NOT mutate the published build digest or client carrier. Compiler no-pass bookkeeping must be isolated from finalized file/build state so macroexpand-only, compile/runtime failure, never-evaluated actions, and later unrelated builds cannot publish ghost declarations. Saving/rebuilding reconciles source state and publishes the next digest. Preserve whole-build lazy-module membership, byte-identical JVM/client projection, O(1) client reads, LKG on failure, and production elision. This supersedes the description's earlier successful-no-pass-REPL commit rule. Independent review additionally requires the JVM authority not advance at `:compile-finish` if later optimization/check/flush/hook failure can still abort the build; publication must occur only at the latest supported successful build boundary, or the worker must surface an implementation blocker. title: Complete the retained Tier-3 ui.test API and remove simulate!
description:
## Problem

The S2 boundary audit found that the frozen re-frame.ui.test surface promises `with-root`, mounted `query`, the React-act half of `flush!`, and `simulate!`, but the current implementation still marks Tier-3 mounting pending: `query` always throws, `flush!` only drains the framework registry, and there are no `with-root` or `simulate!` definitions. Mike has now ruled the contract shape: `simulate!` is removed from v1 rather than inventing an underspecified gesture DSL. Tier-3 tests use `with-root`, native CSS `query`, ordinary DOM event APIs, and the single public test flush `re-frame.ui.test/flush!`. There is no public production `re-frame.ui/flush!`.

## Scope

Complete the retained S2 Tier-3 test API and reconcile every contract/export reference. Implement exception-safe `with-root` mounting with total teardown; make `query` apply native `querySelector` within the mounted root/container; make `ui.test/flush!` settle framework work and React commits under the supported React test primitive. Remove `simulate!` from the frozen API table, stage matrix, Spec 004/008 references, guide/skill/examples, exports, and API-surface gates. Keep any scoped host flush helper internal.

This is an S2 stage blocker. Spec files are a hot zone: sequence all `spec/*` edits after the active rf2-slfhkx Spec-005 owner has landed. Do not weaken the frozen table beyond the explicitly ruled removal.

## Verification protocol

The fix PR must include a fixture verified to fail before the fix (or against a deliberate reverted/mutated implementation) and must state the red-to-green method in the PR body. Diff-check every touched docstring/spec claim against shipped behavior. Exercise real mounted React/DOM behavior, exception-path teardown, query scoping, and flush determinism; JVM calls must remain honest typed tier errors where host behavior cannot exist.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `re-frame.ui.test/simulate!` is absent from implementation, exports, the frozen v1 table/matrix, Spec 004/008, guide/skill text, and API-surface assertions; no replacement gesture DSL is added.
2. `with-root` mounts a real Tier-3 root and always tears it down, including body/mount/flush failure paths, without leaking root ids, ViewCells, observation owners, or DOM ownership.
3. `query` accepts only a mounted Tier-3 root plus native CSS string and scopes `querySelector` to that root; tier/argument mismatches fail with the catalogue-backed typed error.
4. `ui.test/flush!` remains the sole public test flush and deterministically settles framework drain-to-quiescence followed by React commit work; flushing inside an open drain throws `:rf.error/flush-in-open-epoch`. No public `re-frame.ui/flush!` is exported.
5. Mounted CLJS fixtures cover success and adversarial teardown/query/flush paths; the required fixture is demonstrated red pre-fix and green post-fix, and touched documentation claims match code.
6. Relevant UI JVM/CLJS/browser gates and API/export/bundle-isolation checks are green.
notes: MIKE RULING 2026-07-13 — ASYNC TIER-3 TEST CONTRACT: approved Promise-backed CLJS semantics under the EXISTING public names. `ui.test/with-root` returns a Promise on CLJS, establishes an async body context, settles initial mount before the body, awaits body completion/rejection, and awaits total teardown before settling. `ui.test/flush!` has zero-arg and thunk arities on CLJS; both return Promises, and the thunk runs inside awaited React 19 `act` before framework/React fixed-point settlement. JVM behavior stays synchronous/React-free (`flush!` returns nil; with-root remains typed Tier-3-unavailable). No new public symbol or gesture DSL. The open-drain guard must run BEFORE Promise construction so `flush!` inside a handler still throws `:rf.error/flush-in-open-epoch` synchronously. Preserve primary error over cleanup failure with cleanup diagnostic attached; nested roots tear down LIFO; overlapping un-awaited act operations fail loud. Update the blessed §2 row/signatures, Specs 004/008, 07-testing, guide/skill/docstrings, and bundle isolation. This is test-only with zero production residue.
close_reason: Completed and merged in PR #5808 (2d51830e37): Promise-backed Tier-3 with-root/query/dispatch!/flush!, fixed-point queued-write then single read/render batch, total teardown, and production isolation all independently reviewed and 61-check green

title: (P1 BUG) NaN-valued subscription drives an unbounded re-render loop (advance-node-record! versions by = not rf=)
description: rf2-vxgfnd.22 adversarial review (observation+reactive, 2026-07-13) — the deep host-agnostic P1. observation.cljc:306 (and :318 CLJS) advance-node-record! bumps version when value differs by clojure.core equals, but NaN is never equals-to-NaN on either host, so a NaN-valued node bumps version on EVERY observation though nothing changed. The step8 guard (retained-moved? and not dirty?) does not save it (advance-revision never sets dirty?). Value stabilization does not help (loop driven by the version integer). title: (BUG) Authenticate the internal join-reap destroy form before suppressing cancellation
description:
PR #5772 introduces a third `:rf.machine/destroy` argument shape, `{:rf/actor-id id :rf/reason reason}`, intended only for the join runtime to reap an already-terminal `:spawn-all` child without emitting a contradictory cancellation reply. `destroy-single!` recognizes the form solely by `(contains? args :rf/actor-id)` and then forwards the caller-provided reason. `emit-destroyed!` classifies every reason other than `:explicit` as post-completion cleanup and emits no terminal cancellation facts.

That makes the new internal distinction forgeable at the public reserved-fx boundary. Any application action can already emit the documented `:rf.machine/destroy` fx. It can now emit `[:rf.machine/destroy {:rf/actor-id victim :rf/reason :typo-or-finished}]`; the actor is fully destroyed, but its in-progress work attempt receives no `:cancelled` terminal because the arbitrary non-`:explicit` reason bypasses the cancellation gate. The same malformed form can mint an undeclared reason into `:rf.machine/destroyed`, contradicting the closed reason vocabulary and leaving Xray/work-ledger state open or dishonest.

This is not a request to validate every programmer keyword. It is a recognized internal-only form that claims evidence (the actor already completed this exact join attempt) and changes terminal semantics. The runtime must verify that claim or keep the form inaccessible. The smallest data-native repair is to carry parent-id, invoke-id, and child-id in the reap request and verify against the live join state that the child maps to actor-id and belongs to `:done ∪ :failed`; only then may `:rf.machine/join-reaped` suppress cancellation. Alternatively use a truly internal teardown path that cannot be reached through the public destroy arg grammar. Unknown/malformed map shapes should fail loud with a typed machine error, not silently choose a semantic reason.
acceptance_criteria:
- The public/documented `[:rf.machine/destroy actor-id]` path always classifies a live in-progress actor teardown as `:explicit` cancellation.
- A join reap can suppress cancellation only when runtime evidence proves the named actor is the completed/failed child of the named active join; arbitrary caller-supplied `:rf/reason` cannot select post-completion semantics.
- Malformed/forged direct-actor map forms fail loud with a stable typed error and do not destroy the actor or emit a dishonest terminal trace.
- A regression emits `{:rf/actor-id live-id :rf/reason :rf.machine/join-reaped}` from an ordinary app action without valid join evidence and proves it cannot silently destroy-without-cancellation.
- Genuine completed and failed join children still reap fully with `:reason :rf.machine/join-reaped` and no second cancellation; survivors remain `:explicit` cancellations.
- Spec/API continues to expose only the intended public actor-id destroy form; any internal carrier and its validation are documented as implementation-only.
close_reason: Closed

title: (BUG) Remove the global custom-element mirror from per-build compiler reads
description:
PR #5770 correctly makes the compiler registry authority one atom keyed by build id, and most consumers read `build/aggregate` using the ambient compiler build identity. The custom-element compiler path is the exception. `build/register! build/elements rules/custom-elements` registers one process-global mirror atom; every contribution/begin/commit/abort calls `sync-mirror!`, resetting that single atom to the aggregate of whichever build mutated most recently. Compiler analysis (`compiler/analyze.cljc:408`) and JVM tree lowering (`tree.cljc`) then call `rules/custom-element-properties`, which dereferences that global mirror without a build id.

This reintroduces cross-build timing dependence precisely on the fifth registry #5770 claims to isolate. Concrete interleaving: build :app declares `:x-card` property `:model`; build :node-test declares a different custom-element table and its contribution resets the mirror; the :app compile thread then analyzes an `:x-card {:model ...}` node. Although `build/aggregate build/elements :app` remains correct, analysis reads the node-test mirror and lowers `:model` as an attribute instead of a property (or vice versa). A later write from :app flips the mirror back, so output depends on parallel scheduling.

Current tests cover per-build isolation for views/root indexes and sequential custom-element removal, but do not interleave a custom-element contribution in one build between another build's declaration and property-classification read. The open hook-wiring bead rf2-phlhfd is not a duplicate: hooks cannot fix a global consumer mirror, and this race exists before lifecycle wiring.

Eliminate the global mirror as compiler authority. CLJ compiler/tree consumers should resolve `build/aggregate build/elements` through the same ambient build-id accessor as the other four registries (or receive an explicit per-build registry through analysis context). Keep the separate CLJS runtime custom-element reconciliation protocol intact; that client registry has different runtime ownership.
acceptance_criteria:
- Compiler analysis and JVM tree lowering obtain custom-element declarations from the ambient/explicit build slice, never from one last-writer-wins process-global mirror.
- A barrier-controlled concurrency fixture drives two build ids with conflicting property declarations for the same tag, interleaves contribution and analysis reads, and proves each build emits its own correct property/attribute classification deterministically.
- Begin/commit/abort/reconcile in one build cannot change another build thread's effective custom-element read.
- Clean, incremental, failed-pass retry, REPL upsert, and declaration-removal tests remain green for all five registries.
- The CLJS runtime `rules/custom-elements` hot-reload protocol remains correctly separated and is not accidentally replaced by JVM build state.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5778: removed the global custom-element mirror; analyze.cljc reads the per-build build/elements slice via build/element-properties; tree.cljc render read stays on the runtime-arm ledger (no compiler env at render), now unclobbered by the mirror removal. Interleave race proven + closed; all gates green.

title: (BUG) Route re-frame.ui DOM and runtime changes to the browser CI gate
description:
PR #5767 changed exactly one browser-only test file under `implementation/ui/test`: `frame_scope_resolve_dom_cljs_test.cljs`. Its CI result shows `CLJS (shadow-cljs :browser-test, headless Chromium)` SKIPPED, even though this namespace is selected specifically by the browser build and the PR's purpose was to fix React DOM/act behavior that Node/JVM cannot validate.

The cause is explicit in `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh`: the `implementation/ui/*` case sets `implementation_jvm=true`, `cljs_node_test=true`, and `ui_gates=true`, but deliberately leaves `cljs_browser=false` based on the now-stale comment "No production build :requires re-frame.ui.* yet". re-frame.ui now has real DOM tests (`*-dom-cljs-test`) in `:browser-test`; a test-only UI PR can therefore merge green while its only relevant test never runs. #5767 demonstrates the false-green path: JVM/node/G-1 passed while the browser job that would check React act warnings was skipped.

Update the classifier conservatively. At minimum, any changed `implementation/ui/test/**/*-dom-cljs-test.{cljs,cljc}` must trigger `cljs_browser=true`; because UI runtime changes can affect those tests transitively, the simpler and safer pre-alpha posture is to trigger the browser gate for every `implementation/ui/**` source or test change. Production-elision/bundle gates can remain separately reasoned if they truly have no UI build surface. Add classifier self-tests using explicit paths so this cannot regress.
acceptance_criteria:
- The changed-surface classifier reports `cljs_browser=true` for `implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/frame_scope_resolve_dom_cljs_test.cljs` and representative other `*-dom-cljs-test` paths.
- A representative `implementation/ui/src/**` change also triggers the browser gate, unless a narrower rule is documented and proven to cover every transitive DOM test dependency.
- Classifier self-tests pin UI source, ordinary UI CLJS test, and UI DOM-test routing, plus a docs-only negative.
- A test-only PR equivalent to #5767 runs `CLJS (shadow-cljs :browser-test, headless Chromium)` instead of reporting SKIPPED.
- The change does not add UIx/Helix/Reagent smoke dependencies; this is the first-party re-frame.ui browser gate.
close_reason: PR #5780: classifier fires cljs_browser for every implementation/ui/** change; stale comment updated; classifier self-tests added. Browser gate now runs for UI PRs instead of SKIPPED — false-green path closed.

title: (BUG) Finish React act discipline in the re-frame.ui frame-scope DOM fixture
description:
PR #5767 is titled "harden keystone DOM fixture act discipline" and closes rf2-vxgfnd.87, whose acceptance criteria explicitly require the repository's canonical React `act` helper/pattern and state that `flushSync` is not an `act` substitute. The PR correctly retains every Root, unmounts it in `finally`, resets scheduler/bookkeeping, and asserts no live roots/ViewCells survive. But it never imports or calls React `act`.

Verified 0 act warnings for this fixture + browser gate green (0 fail/err/pageerror).

title: (BUG) Make parallel :always stabilization select-then-apply across all regions
description:
PR #5765 fixed parallel `:on` event-guard selection by selecting every region against frozen pre-event `:data`, then applying the selected transitions in declaration order. It did not apply the same two-phase rule to eventless (`:always`) transitions. Instead, `reduce-regions` fully applies and settles one region (including that region's `:always` fixed point) before visiting the next region, while threading the shared evolving `:data`. The PR then added Spec 005 prose declaring this a "blessed residual" and explicitly retained it at machine birth.

This is not a harmless apply-order detail. Given orthogonal regions A then B, A can write `:flag` in an event action or birth `:always` action, and B's `:always` guard can observe that write and transition; reverse the region declarations and A's `:always` guard runs before B's write. The selected eventless-transition set therefore depends on declaration order. It can also see only a prefix of the selected event actions: A's `:always` settles before B's selected `:on` action has run. That is not select-then-apply statechart stabilization.

The originating bead rf2-lq5yo3 explicitly called out "Same leak at settle-birth" and Mike ruled option (a), SELECT all regions against a frozen view then APPLY. #5765 closed the bead while narrowing the fix to `:on` and unilaterally documenting the remaining `:always` behavior. This follow-up does not re-open or amend that closed bead; it tracks the undelivered eventless half.

Reproduction fixture: two parallel regions in both declaration orders. Region A writes `:flag` during its selected event action (and in a separate birth fixture during an initial eventless step). Region B has guarded `:always` reading `:flag`. The reached configuration must not change merely because A/B declarations are reversed. Include a fixture where both selected event actions write data, proving eventless selection begins only after the whole selected set has applied, not after a region prefix.

Likely direction: make eventless stabilization a parent-level sequence of microsteps. For each microstep, select every enabled region `:always` transition against one snapshot, apply the selected set deterministically, then repeat to fixed point; do the same after initial entry and after a broadcast apply. Preserve deterministic action/fx ordering and existing raise-depth/always-depth rollback semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
- Parallel `:always` selection is declaration-order-independent: paired A/B and B/A fixtures reach the same state/data for normal event stabilization and birth stabilization.
- All selected `:on` transitions apply before the first cross-region `:always` selection; a region cannot stabilize against only a prefix of sibling event actions.
- Each eventless microstep selects all regions against one frozen configuration/data view, then applies deterministically, repeating to the existing bounded fixed point.
- `:raise`, `:fx`, trace ordering, depth limits, atomic rollback, and one-commit macrostep semantics remain pinned on JVM and CLJS.
- Spec 005 removes/replaces the "blessed residual" prose and accurately states the implemented eventless select/apply contract.
notes:
HELD FOR MIKE — CONTESTS the lq5yo3 ruling, does not merely follow up. Mike's option (a) ruling EXPLICITLY blessed the settle-birth / :always residual: impl-guidance point (2) said 'Settle-birth: keep threading; extend 005:1731's guarded-:always note to name :data as part of the blessed per-region-drain shape', and named ':always guards reading sibling :data remain declaration-order-sensitive' as a deliberate RESIDUAL (not a regression). #5765 implemented EXACTLY that. slfhkx argues the option-(a) headline ('SELECT all regions against a frozen view then APPLY') should extend to :always/settle-birth too, un-blessing the residual. That REVERSES a ruled decision → Mike's call, NOT an overnight dispatch. Mayor (overnight, 2026-07-12): held, not dispatched. If Mike agrees :always should also freeze-select, this becomes a parallel.cljc worker; if he confirms the residual stays blessed, close as wont-fix.
DECISION (Fable delegated, 2026-07-13): DECISION-FLAGGED for Mike — a ruled-reversal is yours, I do NOT rule it. WEIGHED CONCLUSION ON THE MERITS: option (ii) EXTEND — un-bless the :always/settle-birth residual and make eventless stabilization a parent-level select-then-apply microstep loop. Three load-bearing reasons: (1) The residual is a GENUINE parity divergence, not a substrate exception. Code verified: broadcast-once freezes :data/:all-state/:tags for SELECT (parallel.cljc:912-914) but the APPLY fold drains each region's OWN :always against the EVOLVING threaded :data mid-fold (parallel.cljc:890-893 -> apply-region-transition:850-872 -> machine-transition-single), and a declining region still drains (transition.cljc:4333 (ok snapshot []) -> 4342-4344 drain-to-fixed-point). Confirmed order-dependence: A writes :flag in its :e action, B has {:always {:guard (:flag data)}}; declared [A B] -> {a2 b2}, declared [B A] -> {a2 b1} (B strands to the NEXT event). XState v5/v6/SCXML converge in-macrostep either order (machine-level selectEventlessTransitions loop re-selects the whole config against a fresh snapshot each round; .start() runs the identical loop — no per-region eventless fixed point anywhere). CLJS can run that loop fine, so this is a blessed SHORTCUT, which your XState-v6-parity protocol forbids (substrate-only exceptions). (2) The blessing's factual premise was INCOMPLETE. reduce-regions' docstring (parallel.cljc:552-554) and 005:1732 justify keeping birth threading because "freezing would retime data-coupled birth convergence to the next event" — but that is true ONLY of a WHOLE-settle freeze against pre-birth data. The parent-microstep design RE-FREEZES per round, so birth convergence lands WITHIN the birth macrostep — STRICTLY CLOSER to XState's .start() than the current threading (which strands B at birth under [B A]), not further. lq5yo3(a)'s headline ("SELECT all regions against a frozen view then APPLY") and its impl-guidance point (2) ("settle-birth: keep threading") are in direct tension; the premise that resolved it toward threading dissolves under the microstep design. (3) It SIMPLIFIES, not gold-plates: end-state = one convergence story, LESS spec prose (delete 1731's next-event bullet + 1732's residual), full parity, and declaration order stops being a silent semantic input — exactly the AI-refactor trap this project exists to kill. Pre-alpha, no compat burden = cheapest it will ever be. Cost is real but bounded (hot-loop redesign, ~962 JVM + ~9030 CLJS pinned-test churn on ordering/counts, hot-zone 005 edit) — single sequential worker, no bundling.

WEIGHED (Fable vs Codex): Both recommendations reach the SAME conclusion (option ii, extend) and agree on every parity fact — I adopt the shared verdict, and fused the two because they are COMPLEMENTARY not competing. Fable owns the DECISION-REVERSAL argument: it alone surfaces the lq5yo3 headline-vs-point(2) tension, proves the birth-blessing premise dissolves under per-round re-freezing (the strongest reason this is a ruling worth reopening rather than a mere follow-up), and flags the 005:1661 overclaim + the required 1731 blessed-divergence entry for the confirm branch. Codex owns the IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT: a crisp 5-step parent-owned loop, the "narrow apply-one-preselected-transition-WITHOUT-local-draining seam reused for both event and eventless sets (no compat mode = no gold-plating)" factoring, round-based trace semantics (co-selected regions share one :microstep-index; :microsteps counts ROUNDS not regions), and a thorough gate list. Neither alone is sufficient; the fusion is the ruling.

IMPLEMENTATION (for whichever way Mike rules):

  IF EXTEND (ii) — the microstep redesign shape (Codex's contract, adopted): Factor a narrow seam that applies ONE pre-selected transition WITHOUT running the region-local :always drain (suppress drain-to-fixed-point's :always loop for :rf/region specs in the parallel path), and reuse it for BOTH the event set and each eventless set. Parent-owned loop: (1) apply the complete event/raise transition set (guards already frozen; actions run canonical region order, :data accumulates); (2) from the whole-machine snapshot, SELECT every enabled region :always against ONE frozen config/tags/data; (3) apply the selected eventless set in canonical region order (actions see earlier actions' writes within the apply, guards never recomputed); (4) repeat 2-3 to quiescence, THEN dequeue the next raised event (raises append to the parent FIFO); (5) at birth, run run-initial-cascade for every region, then this identical loop before publishing — settle-birth's single reduce-regions/settle-region-birth pass (parallel.cljc:1672) becomes the parent loop, birth converges in-macrostep. Re-home :always-depth-limit to the PARENT (count parent eventless rounds, not per-region drains). Preserve one-commit macrostep atomicity + failure rollback (a guard/action throw or depth breach publishes no partial snapshot/effects). Trace: co-selected regional transitions in one round share :microstep-index; keep per-region trace events; Xray groups a round without inferring from differing indices. title: (BUG) Make ViewCell frame-close revalidation incarnation-safe
description:
## Problem

PR #5764 at head `c1a635275a4e1b6d2c1883bd06305605b526e3c5` fixes the original late-enrolment window by checking `frame/frame-closing?` after `connect!`. The check is keyed only by the bare frame id: `destroying-frames` is a set of ids, `cell-frames` projects committed targets to ids, and `frame-closing?` treats any currently live record under that id as continuity. That does not satisfy the originating bead's explicit incarnation-safety requirement.

There are two reciprocal failures:

1. **An old-incarnation commit can survive on a replacement frame id.** A commit can acquire/read a lease from incarnation A, pause before step 6 publishes it, then let A finish destruction and let incarnation B be created under the same id. When the commit resumes, it publishes A's now-disposed lease, calls `connect!`, and asks `frame-closing?` about the bare id. The old `destroying-frames` marker has been cleared and `(frame id)` now returns live B, so the predicate is false. The cell remains `:connected` with A's stale committed target instead of joining A's teardown or failing before publish. The new test pauses only between sweep and liveness flip and never recreates the id, so it cannot expose this.

2. **An old close marker can kill a new-incarnation cell.** `destroy-frame!` dissociates A's frame record before its terminal epoch notification/failure flush and before the `finally` clears `destroying-frames`. `upsert-frame!` does not consult that set. Another thread can therefore create B after A's dissoc but while A's bare-id marker remains. A cell that legitimately acquires B and then calls the new post-connect check sees the old marker and tears itself down as though B were closing.

The first failure leaves old ownership connected to a replacement id; the second lets an old close gate tear down new ownership. Both contradict `rf2-vxgfnd.61`'s acceptance criterion: “Destroy/recreate of the same frame id cannot let an old close gate or sweep kill cells belonging to the new incarnation.”

This is not a duplicate of open bead `rf2-vxgfnd.14`. That bead covers destroy/recreate **before commit acquisition**, where a newly acquired node can have evidence numerically equal to the render probe. This finding covers an old lease already acquired before destroy and the new id-only lifecycle check itself; node-evidence comparison alone does not make the closing authority incarnation-specific.

## Steps to Reproduce

### Old lease published after replacement

1. Create frame incarnation A and render a fresh ViewCell against one of its live subscriptions.
2. Start `reactive/commit!` and use a barrier after the staged lease has been acquired/read but before step 6 publishes `:committed`.
3. On the other thread, fully destroy A, recreate the same frame id as incarnation B, and install different app-db/cache state.
4. Resume commit.
5. `connect!` enrols the cell; `cell-frames` returns only the reused id; `frame-closing?` returns false because B is live and A's marker is gone. The cell can finish `:connected` with the lease acquired from A.

### Old close marker applied to replacement

1. Start destroying A and pause after `dissoc-frame!` but before the terminal `finally` removes the id from `destroying-frames` (the epoch listener seam after dissoc can provide a deterministic barrier).
2. Create B using the same id and commit a cell that acquires B's subscription node.
3. The post-connect `frame-closing?` sees A's still-present bare-id marker and tears down B's cell.

## Deliverable

Make the close/acquire boundary incarnation-aware. A commit must revalidate the exact frame incarnation from which each subscription lease was acquired before publishing it, and a close marker/sweep for incarnation A must never classify incarnation B as closing. Use the existing stable `frame-incarnation-token` or an equally exact identity; do not attempt to infer incarnation continuity from a live record under the same keyword. If construction must be serialized until same-id teardown fully completes, make that an explicit, tested lifecycle rule rather than an accidental timing dependency.

Preserve #5764's successful ordinary race fix and its constant-work production posture. Coordinate with `rf2-vxgfnd.14`, but do not collapse the two distinct interleavings into one under-specified test.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic JVM barrier pauses commit after acquiring/reading an A-incarnation lease but before publication, then fully destroys A and creates B under the same id; resuming cannot leave the cell `:connected` or committed to A's lease. It either retries/reconciles against B or fails before publish through a truthful typed outcome.
- A second deterministic fixture pauses A after its registry dissoc but before its close marker is cleared, then exercises same-id B creation/commit; A's close authority cannot tear down a cell that owns B.
- Closing state is associated with an exact incarnation token (or equivalent identity), not inferred solely from a bare frame id.
- After A's destroy returns, no ViewCell retains a live committed lease from A, even when B already occupies the id; release remains identity-guarded and cannot decrement B's cache entry.
- The original #5764 snapshot/late-enrolment fixture remains green, as do multi-target and disjoint-frame cases.
- The fixtures explicitly distinguish this acquire-before-destroy interleaving from `rf2-vxgfnd.14`'s destroy-before-acquire evidence collision; both contracts remain covered.
- CLJS stays simple, and the normal production commit path retains constant-time/constant-allocation lifecycle revalidation per observed frame.
- The S2 ownership/frame-destroy conformance gate includes same-id reincarnation on both sides of the close boundary.
notes: HELD — reactive.cljc (ViewCell frame-close revalidation incarnation-safe, follow-up to .61). Same file as the .92/.93 reactive-activation cluster. Fold into that cluster OR sequence after it; dispatch after #5774 merges + the .92/.93 cluster lands. Do not parallel on reactive.cljc.
