title: Fix #5760 DOM fixture ownership and React act discipline
description:
## Problem

PR #5760 is not merge-ready: its required `CLJS (shadow-cljs :browser-test, headless Chromium)` check exits 1 because the new real-DOM frame-scope fixtures produce React console errors. The assertions themselves report 300 tests / 1080 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors, but the browser harness correctly treats the unwrapped React updates as a failure.

`frame_scope_resolve_dom_cljs_test.cljs` calls `react-dom/flushSync` around `ui/mount`, but React's test contract requires updates to be wrapped in `act`; `flushSync` is not an `act` substitute. More importantly, all three tests discard the Root returned by `ui/mount`. Their fixture calls `client/reset-live-roots!`, which only clears framework bookkeeping; it does not unmount the real React roots. Mounted React trees and ViewCell effects therefore survive into fixture reset/next-test activity, which can trigger the repeated "An update to Root inside a test was not wrapped in act(...)" errors seen in the CI log and makes the tests order-dependent.

The negative no-provider test also catches the render exception but still needs to close any Root/claim created before the render abort. A test proving root/provider scope must own the host roots it creates and deterministically unmount them in `finally`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out PR #5760 at head b22796461e0b2f9413bb1577624f05ab1215bce7.
2. Run the browser test gate used by CI.
3. The new frame-scope DOM namespace's mounts run outside `act`; the returned roots are not retained/unmounted.
4. The browser log emits repeated React "update ... was not wrapped in act(...)" console errors (including around later root-teardown tests).
5. cljs.test reports zero assertion failures, but the harness exits 1 because browser console errors are a required-gate failure.

CI evidence: tests workflow run 29194468559, job 86655069387.

## Deliverable

Make the #5760 DOM fixture a well-owned React test. Use the repository's canonical React `act` helper/pattern for mount, render, dispatch-driven update, and unmount. Retain every Root handle and unmount it in a `finally`/fixture cleanup that runs even when the expected render error occurs. Do not rely on `reset-live-roots!` as host cleanup; it is bookkeeping reset, not `.unmount()`.

Keep the tests focused on pure `re-frame.ui` with plain-atom. Do not solve the red gate by suppressing console errors or weakening the harness.
acceptance_criteria:
- PR #5760's browser check is green with no React `act` console errors attributable to the new namespace.
- Every real React root created in `frame_scope_resolve_dom_cljs_test.cljs` is retained and unmounted in guaranteed cleanup; cleanup runs for both successful mounts and the expected no-frame-context failure path.
- Mount/update/unmount operations use the repository's canonical React `act` discipline; `flushSync` alone is not treated as `act`.
- A focused leak assertion or fixture proves no live-root claim and no connected ViewCell/root effect survives each test.
- The positive provider and frame-root ambient-sub assertions remain end-to-end on a real React root, and the no-provider case still fails loud rather than acquiring a default.
- No console suppression, relaxed browser harness, or UIx/Helix dependency is introduced; those adapters are retiring and the fixture remains native re-frame.ui + plain-atom.
notes: DIAGNOSIS UPDATE (monitor, 2026-07-13): #5760's remaining red MOVED after the owner's 95b4943f fix wave — browser-test now GREEN (the onUncaughtError containment worked); the failure is now JVM ui: evidence-target-vector-is-bounded-with-a-loss-account (reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc:336) expected #{:hmr}, actual #{:disposed :hmr}. This is DETERMINISTIC (set mismatch), not a flake — re-running won't clear it (mayor's heartbeat re-ran it as flake; expect same result). Main is green on this exact test (#5758/#5759 both ran the ui JVM suite green post-merge), so the cause is the BRANCH's own change interacting on the merge preview: frame-root now emits live scope (the .25 fix), which plausibly creates additional lease/teardown activity in the HMR fixture whose disposal adds the :disposed cause into the bounded evidence set. Fix directions for the owner: either the fixture's expectation is now legitimately #{:disposed :hmr} under scoped frame-roots (update the assertion + the loss-account arithmetic), or scope-element's teardown is leaking a disposal notification it should coalesce under :hmr — decide WHICH is contract-honest against 03 §4/006 cause vocabulary before editing either side.
close_reason: Resolved across two owners, verified post-merge 2026-07-13: (1) the DOM-fixture/act-discipline half was fixed by the #5760 owner's commit febc254d9a — the scopeless-sub render-phase throw is contained via React's onUncaughtError host callback (React 19 does NOT rethrow render-phase throws out of .render, so the old try/catch caught nothing and the runner's uncaught-pageerror policy (rf2-mwx08) reddened the gate); browser-test green on the merged head. (2) The residual JVM-ui red (evidence-target-vector fixture seeing #{:disposed :hmr}) was ruled by the mayor at --admin merge to be the PRE-EXISTING disposal-cause mislabel race, off #5760's diff surface — owned by rf2-r8jmdb (in progress, threading cause from cache disposal sites). CORRECTION to my earlier note: my 'deterministic, branch-caused' hypothesis was wrong on causation — the interleaving of the :hmr boundary drain vs the next-tick :disposed fallback is timing-dependent and pre-existing; the r8jmdb cause-threading fix is the honest resolution (label from the disposal SITE, not the drain boundary).

title: (BUG) Root teardown misses ViewCells already disconnected by Activity
description:
## Problem

PR #5755 implements root teardown with a module-global collection window: `teardown-root!` arms `teardown-collector`, and only a `disconnect!` that transitions a `:fresh` or `:connected` ViewCell while that window is armed is enrolled for the later `:unmounted {:proof :host-teardown}` -> `:dead` upgrade.

That does not cover a ViewCell whose React layout effect was already disconnected by an Activity/Offscreen hide before `ui/unmount!`. Such a cell is already `:disconnected`, has been removed from `live-cells`, and has released its leases. When the enclosing React root is later unmounted while the subtree remains hidden, React may have no still-mounted effect to clean up a second time; even if `disconnect!` is reached again, its lifecycle guard rejects the already-disconnected cell. The root teardown collector therefore never sees it. The cell remains `:disconnected {:reason :unknown}` and reconnectable after its host root no longer exists.

The new test `hide-outside-a-window-is-not-captured-by-a-later-teardown` explicitly blesses this outcome, but it models an empty thunk rather than the required ownership invariant. It contradicts rf2-vxgfnd.62's deliverable and acceptance criteria: root teardown must prevent any retained cell from reconnecting after its root is gone, must be ordering-robust, and was expected to establish root-to-cell ownership rather than infer ownership only from cleanups occurring inside a time window.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Mount a sub-bearing compiled view under React root A and retain its ViewCell for observation.
2. Hide that subtree through React Activity/Offscreen so its layout-effect cleanup calls `disconnect!` before any root teardown window exists.
3. Confirm the cell is `:disconnected` and absent from `live-cells`.
4. Call `ui/unmount!` for root A while the subtree remains hidden.
5. Observe that no eligible `disconnect!` transition enrols the cell in `teardown-collector`; it remains `:disconnected :unknown` rather than becoming `:dead`.
6. The existing #5755 unit fixture demonstrates the mechanism directly: disconnect before the window, then `teardown-root!` collects zero and intentionally leaves the cell reconnectable.

## Impact

- The lifecycle evidence can claim an open/unknown disconnect forever after a proven root teardown.
- A retained ViewCell handle does not enter `:dead` and can be recommitted through the reconnect path even though its React root is gone.
- Xray sees an incomplete/false lifetime, specifically for the Activity/presence-style case the three-state lifecycle was designed to distinguish.
- `current-live-cells` cannot repair this because Activity disconnect deliberately removes the cell from that registry.

## Deliverable

Give each mounted ViewCell a bounded root-incarnation ownership association that survives a transient Activity disconnect and ends only when the cell is proven dead or the root is torn down. `ui/unmount!` must close every cell belonging to that root, including cells already disconnected before host unmount began, without scanning historical cells or touching sibling/nested roots. The collection window may remain as immediate cleanup evidence, but it cannot be the sole ownership mechanism.

Preserve the intended facts: Activity hide alone stays `:disconnected :unknown`; reveal may prove `:activity-hidden`; explicit root teardown upgrades both currently connected and already-hidden cells to `:unmounted {:proof :host-teardown}` and `:dead`. Root incarnation identity must prevent a stale teardown from killing cells in a replacement root with the same root-id.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic fixture connects a cell to root A, performs an Activity-style disconnect before any teardown window, then tears down root A; the cell ends `:dead` and its last interval is `:unmounted {:proof :host-teardown}`.
- Prefer a real React 19 Activity/Offscreen browser fixture proving hide -> root unmount; if host support makes that impossible, retain a deterministic graft fixture plus a real-root ownership fixture that proves already-disconnected membership is still closed.
- A hide followed by reveal without root teardown remains reconnectable and is labeled only `:activity-hidden {:proof :reconnect}`.
- Sibling root B and a nested independent React root are not annotated or killed when root A unmounts.
- Root membership is incarnation-safe, bounded to currently retained/mounted cells, and removed on final teardown; repeated mount/hide/unmount cycles do not grow a historical registry.
- A retained cell from a torn-down root cannot commit/reconnect; it fails through the dead-cell lifecycle.
- Replace the #5755 test that blesses the missed already-hidden cell with the corrected contract.
notes: HELD until #5764 (.61) merges — .85 (root teardown misses Activity-disconnected ViewCells) is on reactive.cljc teardown-root!, and .61/#5764 just touched reactive.cljc commit!. Same file. Dispatch once #5764 lands.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5773 — root-incarnation ownership (attach-root!/root-cells) survives Activity hide; teardown-root! reaps hidden owned cells. Real-path client/viewcell wiring follow-up: rf2-vxgfnd.92.

title: Keep a throwing host unmount framework-recoverable
description:
PR #5749 documents and preserves a dangerous ownership mismatch in `re-frame.ui.client/unmount!*`: if the host React root `.unmount` throws, the `finally` block releases the exact live-root registry claim even though React may have refused to tear down the tree. The container can then hold a live React tree that re-frame.ui no longer tracks. A second `ui/unmount!` is a no-op, while a later mount can call `createRoot` over the still-live tree. The dev-only recommendation to reach into the private Root handle and call `(.unmount (.-react-root root))` manually is not a viable first-party recovery contract and offers no production protection.

This follows up rf2-vxgfnd.53. Its implementation honored the older rf2-vxgfnd.18 AC4 wording, but that ruling is internally inconsistent with actual host ownership. Pre-alpha is the right time to correct the contract: the authoritative registry must not say a container is free until host teardown succeeds. Model a failed unmount as an exact, retryable ownership state (for example, `:unmount-failed`) or an equivalent design. Preserve the Root/container/root-id identity, reject new mounts into that container, and let a later `ui/unmount!` retry the same host root. Error propagation from the failed attempt can remain loud. Identity guards must continue to prevent a stale handle from altering a newer claim.

The implementation and spec/error catalogue should describe one coherent lifecycle for live, unmount-failed, and released roots. Xray/tooling should be able to distinguish the failed-teardown state instead of seeing an apparently free container.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A host root that throws from `.unmount` remains represented by the authoritative root ownership state; its root-id and container are not advertised as free.
2. In a throw-once-then-succeed fixture, the first `ui/unmount!` propagates a catalogued error, the second call reaches the same host root and succeeds, and only successful teardown releases the exact claim.
3. While teardown is unresolved, `mount`, `create-root`, and hydration reject reuse of the root-id/container before calling React `createRoot` or `hydrateRoot`.
4. Successful unmount remains idempotent. Stale Root handles cannot release, retry, or mutate a newer exact claim.
5. The failed state has a production-safe recovery path through public re-frame.ui API; callers are not told to access the private `react-root` field.
6. Dev/Xray diagnostics expose the root-id, container ownership, failure phase, and retryability without retaining unbounded exception data.
7. Tests cover synchronous render-phase refusal or a faithful fake, retry success, repeated failure, and protection against remount/double-root creation.
8. Spec 004 lifecycle wording and the Spec 009 error catalogue are updated together with the implementation.
notes:
DECISION for Mike (does NOT auto-dispatch): .80 re-litigates the rf2-vxgfnd.53 ruling. .53 was implemented as (b) document+diagnostic because option (a) retryable-claim CONTRADICTS rf2-vxgfnd.18 AC4 (which has a dedicated test asserting release-even-on-throw). .80 argues AC4 is itself internally inconsistent with host ownership and pre-alpha is the time to correct the CONTRACT: model failed-unmount as a retryable :unmount-failed registry state (reject new mounts into that container, later ui/unmount! retries the host root, Xray can see the failed-teardown state). This REOPENS .18 AC4 — a contract/taste call that is Mike's, not a worker's. Surfaced in ai/decisions.md.
Reconciliation (2026-07-13): decision doc's late-added 'Codex Recommendation' section reviewed FULLY. It independently recommends Option D and corroborates this closure against the same pinned react-dom 19.2.0 source (handle nulled before the flush that could throw; render-phase case is a dev console.error not a throw; retry .unmount is a no-op). No genuinely new argument that the rejection was wrong — its own reopen gate matches this closure's revisit condition. File redundant; deleted as anticipated by SOURCE line. No status change.
close_reason: DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike 2026-07-12): REJECTED — keep the shipped .53/.18-AC4 posture (Option D, release-on-throw with error propagation + dev diagnostic); do NOT introduce a retryable :unmount-failed ownership state (Option A), deferred-unmount semantics (Option B), or a container quarantine table (Option C). RATIONALE: Verified against the pinned react-dom 19.2.0 source (react-dom-client.development.js): (1) the motivating case — synchronous unmount during a render pass — does NOT throw; it is a DEV-only console.error (~:27906), after which flushSyncWork$1 (~:16896) declines to flush inside Render/CommitContext and the already-scheduled teardown self-completes when the render finishes, so the registry converges with the host on its own. (2) unmount() nulls this._internalRoot BEFORE the flush that could throw (~:27904), so after any genuine throw a retry .unmount() on the same handle is a silent no-op — AC2 ('the second call reaches the same host root and succeeds') is physically unsatisfiable by real React, and a sticky :unmount-failed quarantine would itself become the registry lie once React's pre-scheduled teardown empties the container. (3) Genuine synchronous throws from .unmount are exotic (commit-phase errors route through onUncaughtError, not synchronous rethrow), and release-on-throw is the best prediction of eventual host state. A retryable state machine modelling a recovery the host cannot perform, for a case that essentially cannot occur, is gold plating per the pre-alpha masterpiece posture; it would spread a third root state across every registry consumer, Spec 004, the Spec 009 catalogue, and Xray for negative value. IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE: The one real defect .80 surfaced survives as rf2-vxgfnd.84 (the #5749 dev diagnostic recommends a manual (.unmount (.-react-root root)) escape that is a silent no-op against real React, and the aftermath test's fake doesn't model handle consumption): fix the diagnostic + unmount!* docstring to say React normally self-completes the deferred teardown and that immediate reclaim should use a fresh container (or clear the old one), fix the test fake, and optionally emit a dev/Xray event on a throwing teardown for observability without ownership machinery. If a future React release both throws synchronously from .unmount AND keeps the handle retryable, this ruling may be revisited — nothing in D forecloses that. SOURCE: decision doc ai/decisions/rf2-vxgfnd.80.failed-unmount-ownership.md (deleted after this ruling).

title: Make config fingerprint canonicalization type-preserving and non-lossy
description:
## Problem

PR #5745 correctly recurses into map keys and set elements, but the canonical representation of a set is still an ordinary vector of each element's `pr-str` string:

`(set? x) (vec (sort (map (comp pr-str canonicalize) x)))`

This erases type identity and creates deterministic pre-hash collisions. For example, the distinct config values `#{:a}` and `[":a"]` both canonicalize to the same vector `[":a"]` and therefore have the same `canonical-edn` and `config-fingerprint`. A real config change can be classified as a matching fingerprint/idempotent no-op, silently skipping the required conflict or same-root refresh.

The new map-key recursion makes the effect worse when these values are keys. A config map can legally contain both the set key `#{:a}` and the vector key `[":a"]`; canonicalization maps both to one key in the intermediate `sorted-map-by`, so an entry is discarded before hashing. That is lossy, potentially order/host sensitive, and violates the PR's new statement that semantically different plans remain separated.

This is not a probabilistic 64-bit digest collision; it is a guaranteed collision in the canonical encoder before the hash runs.

## Deliverable

Use a type-preserving, injective canonical encoding over the supported config-source EDN domain. Sorting must affect order only; it must never convert a set into a user-representable untagged vector/string shape or merge distinct map keys. A dedicated canonical writer with explicit type tags/lengths is preferable to sentinel vectors that user data can reproduce.

Keep equal maps/sets authoring-order independent and cross-host byte identical.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pin the deterministic collision: `#{:a}` and `[":a"]` produce different canonical bytes and different config fingerprints.
- A map containing both values as distinct keys retains both entries through canonicalization; no key is overwritten by the intermediate sorted representation.
- Property/table coverage over supported scalar and collection types proves `=`-equal values canonicalize byte-identically while known unequal cross-type shapes remain distinct (map/vector/list/set, keyword/string/symbol, nested keys/elements).
- Map insertion order and set iteration order do not affect output on JVM or CLJS; cross-host goldens match exactly.
- Genuine plan changes cannot be misclassified as same-fingerprint no-ops; equal plan-source forms still dedupe.
- The encoding has an explicit version prefix or migration rule so future extensions do not silently reinterpret stored fingerprints.
- No runtime render-path cost is added; fingerprinting remains compiler/preflight metadata work.
close_reason: Closed

title: Make ui.test plan-frame claims atomic with the authoritative frame registry
description:
## Problem

PR #5743 replaces `ui.test`'s stale before/after snapshot with a private `claimed-plan-ids` atom, but it claims that the frame-liveness read and reservation “linearize through a single CAS.” They do not: liveness lives in core's separate `re-frame.frame/frames` registry, while the CAS touches only `claimed-plan-ids`.

Remaining reachable race:

1. Render A reads `claimed-plan-ids` and checks `(rframe/frame X)` as absent.
2. Before A CASes the claim atom, actor B calls the normal core `make-frame` for X; B does not know about the private test-host claim registry.
3. A CAS succeeds because the claim atom did not change. `execute-frame-plans!` then sees B's live frame and ADOPTS it, so the test renders ambient state despite promising a fresh isolated frame.
4. On normal teardown `owned` is populated from the current token after execution, so A can misclassify B's adopted incarnation as its own and destroy it.

The new concurrent-created-frame fixture creates B's frame before `claim-plan-frames!` performs its liveness read (the plan config expression opens a pre-claim window); it does not place creation between that read and the CAS and therefore cannot falsify the claimed atomicity.

Partial-failure cleanup has a second bare-id hole. If a later plan throws, the inner catch loops every wanted id and calls `destroy-frame!` for whichever incarnation is currently live; it has not pinned any tokens yet. An earlier test-created frame that another actor destroys/recreates before the later failure—or an ambient frame that slipped through the race above—is destroyed by bare id. This contradicts the PR's incarnation-owned teardown claim exactly on the error path.

## Deliverable

Make fresh multi-plan acquisition atomic with the authoritative core frame registry, not a parallel advisory atom. All claimed ids must be reserved/installed as one fail-before-write ownership operation, or under one lifecycle authority that prevents an uncoordinated core constructor from appearing between absence proof and ownership publication. Capture an incarnation token immediately for each successful install, including before any later plan can throw; partial cleanup must destroy only those exact tokens.

Keep this stronger isolation in `ui.test`; production ENSURE adoption remains unchanged.


## Ruled shape (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-12 — see DECISION in NOTES)

A′ — linearize frame-id creation through the `frames` registry atom itself: `upsert-frame!`'s decide+install becomes a guarded-CAS retry loop (the `set-generation!` discipline at `frame.cljc:808-811`), no lock table. Plus an internal create-exclusive mode (e.g. `:rf.frame/must-create?`) that throws a typed `:rf.error/frame-id-taken` on CAS loss — the one primitive `ui.test` needs. NEW error id ⇒ Spec 009 catalogue row (hot-zone; implementing worker is sole 009 toucher). `ui.test` keeps `claimed-plan-ids` as the render-vs-render zero-write fast path but rests correctness on the registry: plans run in exclusive mode (every plan must install via must-create; adopt/refresh become collision errors), each incarnation token is pinned IMMEDIATELY per install, and the partial-failure catch destroys pinned tokens only (never bare id).

AC amendment: AC3's raw-actor leg ("zero initial events run on loss" for a collision introduced on the FINAL id) is RELAXED to the executor's existing partial-failure posture (irreversible `:initial-events`, exact-token teardown). Render-vs-render losses remain zero-write via the claim CAS.

Two additional holes confirmed in scope during the ruling:

1. The re-registration swap at `frame.cljc:2112` is not contains-guarded — a concurrent `destroy-frame!` between the `:1978` read and `:2112` resurrects a zombie partial record (`{:config …}`, no container, no `:drain-lock`). The guarded-CAS loop closes this (vanished id ⇒ retry as create).
2. On BOTH plan shapes the losing `ui.test` render currently DESTROYS the other actor's frame, not merely adopts it: the config-bearing throw hits the bare-id catch at `test.cljc:716-718` (no tokens pinned yet), and the config-less adopt path's post-hoc pinning at `test.cljc:720-725` claims B's incarnation for the success-path teardown.

Fixture note: the #5743 fixture (`test_render_jvm_test.clj:583-599`) opens only a pre-claim window and cannot falsify the claimed atomicity; new fixtures must interleave inside the decide→install window (barriers/latches, never sleeps).
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic barrier pauses A after the authoritative frame-absence read but before claim publication; B creates X through ordinary core `make-frame`; A must lose before adopting, reading, mutating, or destroying B's frame.
- The liveness proof and ownership reservation share one real linearization authority; a private CAS that does not coordinate with the frame registry is insufficient.
- Multi-plan acquisition remains all-or-nothing for collisions, including a collision introduced on the final id during the claim window; zero initial events run on loss.
- A partial-failure fixture lets A install X, then B destroy/recreate X before a later plan throws; cleanup leaves B's replacement incarnation untouched.
- Every successfully installed frame's token is pinned before control can proceed to a later throwing plan; cleanup uses identity/token guards on both success and error paths.
- Unrelated frame ids can render concurrently, claims never leak, and production ENSURE/HMR/adoption semantics are unchanged.
- JVM concurrency fixtures use barriers/latches, never sleeps, and fail against #5743.
notes: RULED A-prime (Fable/Mike 2026-07-12) but HELD until #5760-keystone AND rf2-vxgfnd.61 MERGE — A-prime restructures core frame.cljc upsert-frame! (decide+install guarded-CAS retry loop + must-create mode), and .61 (in-flight worker/vxgfnd61-commit-linearize) is ALSO on frame.cljc. Two-workers-one-file. Dispatch once .61 lands so A-prime rebases on it. Also needs a spec/009 row for :rf.error/frame-id-taken (HOT-ZONE, sole toucher). Ruling + 5-point impl guidance + test obligations are in this bead's NOTES.
close_reason: A-prime shipped in PR #5776: guarded-CAS decide+install retry loop in upsert-frame! + :rf.frame/must-create? mode; ui.test exclusive install with per-install token pin + exact-token teardown; 009 row for :rf.error/frame-id-taken. Gates green (core 1875, ui 299, cljs 9043, 009-conformance 9, all 0-fail). AC3 relaxed to partial-failure posture (documented residual).

title: reagent-slim components go reactively dead under React.StrictMode (render Reaction not re-established after strict unmount→remount)
description: Found by rf2-a07937's coverage test (empirically A/B-confirmed). Under React.StrictMode (the React-recommended dev default; CRA/Next.js scaffold it) a reagent-slim class renders once then stops responding to app-db. StrictMode lifecycle for a slim class: render x2 -> componentDidMount -> componentWillUnmount -> componentDidMount (NO intervening render). The transient componentWillUnmount disposes + nils the per-component render Reaction (reagent2.impl component install-lifecycle!); the remount's componentDidMount fires WITHOUT React calling render() again (StrictMode reuses the committed fiber), and slim recreates the render Reaction only lazily inside render() (make-render-method) -> remounted instance left with cljsRenderRea=nil, no subscription watches -> follow-up dispatch leaves DOM stale. Same view WITHOUT StrictMode is fully reactive. FIX: re-establish the render Reaction on componentDidMount (or force a re-render when cljsRenderRea is absent) in reagent2.impl. ACCEPTANCE GATE ALREADY WRITTEN: the red-by-design test on branch worker/a07937-slim-strictmode (reagent_slim_strict_mode_dom_cljs_test.cljs). Surface: implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src (reagent2.impl component/lifecycle).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5748 — componentWillUnmount sets a cljsRemountReattach marker on disposing a live render Reaction; componentDidMount (now always installed) forces a re-render via queue-render! when the marker is set, re-establishing the render Reaction + its watches after a StrictMode unmount->remount. Acceptance gate rf2-a07937 green. See rf2-a07937.

title: Do not let follower acquire return while the first-owner hook is still installing
description:
## Problem

PR #5737 adds a canonicality re-check after owner enrolment/hook installation, but it still lets a follower acquire return while the first owner's disposal hook is only INSTALLING. The node record has only `:hooked?`; `register-owner!` flips it to true before `interop/add-on-dispose!` begins. Every later owner interprets true as ready.

Reachable JVM schedule on one canonical reaction R:

1. Thread A calls `acquire!`, enrols L1, flips `:hooked?` false→true, and is paused before/during `add-on-dispose!`.
2. Thread B calls `acquire!` for R. `register-owner!` sees `:hooked? true`, enrols L2, installs nothing, and its #5737 canonicality check succeeds because R is still live. B returns L2 even though no disposal callback exists.
3. Thread C evicts and disposes R. No hook fires, so L2 receives no invalidation and may complete its commit/read against a disposed node.
4. Only if A later resumes, installs its callback onto dead R, and performs its own failed canonicality check are L1/L2 self-drained. If A stalls, the notification is delayed without bound; if hook installation throws or the thread terminates, it is permanently lost.

This is not hypothetical relative to the submitted tests: `first-owner-hook-race-drains-every-staged-owner-exactly-once` recursively completes the second `acquire!` while A is inside its intercepted hook installation, then disposes the node. It proves that L2 returns behind an uninstalled hook, but only asserts notification after A resumes and finishes. That misses rf2-vxgfnd.32's explicit acceptance that neither concurrent acquirer may return behind an installing hook.

The post-return `current?`/commit evidence path is not a substitute for the notification channel. Disposal can occur after B's successful canonicality check; without a live hook, no revision is scheduled to cause another commit. Correctness cannot depend on an unrelated installer thread eventually resuming.

## Deliverable

Represent hook readiness honestly (`:installing` versus `:installed`) or choose an equivalent linearizable protocol. A follower must not publish a lease unless either (a) a live node-scoped hook is already installed and covers future disposal, or (b) that follower owns an independent bounded fallback that guarantees notification/rollback if disposal wins. Installer failure must roll back/transfer readiness so `:hooked?` cannot permanently poison the node.

Preserve the design economy: one steady-state node hook, O(current owners) terminal fan-out, no synchronous `on-change`, and no per-render work. This is core JVM observation-port correctness for re-frame.ui; it is unrelated to preserving UIx/Helix/reagent-slim.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic three-party JVM barrier fixture stages A as the paused first installer, lets B complete the follower path, then disposes R from C before A resumes. The fixture fails #5737 and uses no sleeps as ordering.
- B cannot return an exposed lease behind `:installing`: before A resumes, B is either still unpublished/participating in the handshake or owns a bounded fallback that independently observes C's disposal.
- C's disposal causes every staged/published owner to be rolled back/retried or enqueued exactly once without waiting for A to resume; no stale commit can rely on a missing notification.
- A separate deterministic fixture makes `interop/add-on-dispose!` throw. Hook state and owner enrolment recover cleanly, B/future acquirers are not stranded, ref-counts remain balanced, and the original exception is handled through the ruled failure path.
- Disposal before installation, during installation, immediately after installation, and after readiness publication each have an explicit linearization point and exactly-once outcome.
- `acquire!` and `release!` never invoke `on-change` synchronously; release remains idempotent and transactional multi-acquire rollback remains balanced.
- CLJS run-to-completion behavior and the uncontended hot acquire stay shape-compatible; steady state retains one hook per live node, O(1) acquire/release bookkeeping, and O(current owners) disposal work.
- Spec 006/code comments and the regression names describe readiness rather than treating `:hooked? true` as installed before it is true.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5758 (commit 9c115fa). Honest readiness: :hook-installed? set by new mark-hook-installed! only AFTER add-on-dispose! registers the callback; a follower enrolling in the install window installs its own independent backstop hook (take-owners! single-drain keeps duplicates harmless, one hook per node steady state). rf2-vxgfnd.32 canonicality re-check retained; install failure tears down via release! + rethrows, readiness left unpublished. Fixtures: 3-party JVM CountDownLatch barrier (verified FAILS pre-fix) + both-host install-throw. Gates green (core JVM ns 37/210, full JVM 1866/8335, cljs 9021/42576).

title: Use a real microtask or drain-finalization boundary for ViewCell flushes
description:
## Problem

PR #5733 says the existing scheduler already enforces one render batch at drain quiescence because `interop/next-tick` is a "true goog.async.nextTick microtask". The exact Closure Library shipped with this repo says the opposite: `goog.async.nextTick` "will not schedule the callback as a microtask" and is implemented with `setImmediate`, `MessageChannel`, or `setTimeout`; it yields to the event loop and may be pre-empted by user-input or networking callbacks.

Therefore `flush-scheduled?` can remain true across more than one external drain. A second event/drain may mark the same cell before the nextTick task runs, folding two host-separated drains into one notification/render. The new Spec 006 guarantee—epochs in separate external drains render separately—is not implemented. The added test calls `mark-dirty!` repeatedly and then manually calls `flush-pending!`; it proves dirty-bit coalescing but never exercises the actual scheduler, router drain, `useSyncExternalStore`, or React.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Inspect the resolved `google-closure-library` `goog/async/nexttick.js` used by ClojureScript 1.12.145; its API comment explicitly rejects microtask semantics and its implementations enqueue event-loop tasks.
2. Dirty a mounted ViewCell during drain A, which arms nextTick and sets the global scheduled flag.
3. Before that task is selected, process another user/network callback that performs drain B and dirties the cell.
4. B sees the cell/scheduler already pending; both drains are flushed together, contradicting the claimed per-external-drain separation.

## Deliverable

Introduce the smallest honest drain-quiescence scheduling boundary. A true microtask primitive (for example a deliberately wrapped `queueMicrotask`/Promise job with required host fallbacks) may be sufficient if the end-to-end gate proves it runs after the synchronous router drain and before the next external task; otherwise add an explicit router drain-finalization seam. Name the primitive for its actual semantics—do not redefine `next-tick` folklore as a microtask.

Retain the intended economy: all queued events in one run-to-completion drain settle their writes/epochs, then each dirty cell advances once and React reads once. Do not reintroduce per-epoch renders.
acceptance_criteria:
- Runtime scheduling no longer relies on `goog.async.nextTick` as a microtask; comments and Spec 006 accurately describe the chosen host primitive/seam.
- An end-to-end browser fixture drives a parent event that queues further events through the real router and proves all writes settle before exactly one ViewCell notification and one React render.
- A second external task/drain cannot run before drain A's pending read batch is scheduled/closed as ruled; deterministic scheduler control demonstrates the pre-fix cross-drain fold and the fixed separation.
- The fixture crosses observation port → ViewCell → `useSyncExternalStore` → React, not direct `mark-dirty!` plus manual flush only.
- Synchronous controlled-input/`flush-render!` forcing cannot render inside an open write drain and remains covered.
- The JVM/headless explicit-flush posture remains honest and race-free.
- Advanced production output retains one dirty-set enrollment per cell and one scheduled job per pending drain batch, with no epoch-count-dependent work.
notes: RESCOPED 2026-07-12: rf2-vxgfnd.40 (#5742) landed the microtask-flush PRIMITIVE this bead also targeted (queueMicrotask replaces the goog.async.nextTick macrotask for watch-fired dirt; tear window closed at the primitive level). .65's REMAINING scope: the full observation-port→uSES→React concurrent-tear BROWSER gate (deterministic scheduler control) + the Spec-006 flush-primitive naming sweep. Dispatch AFTER #5742 merges (reactive.cljc). Now a browser-test + doc bead, not a primitive fix.
close_reason: Closed

title: Make ui.test plan-frame acquisition atomic and incarnation-owned
description:
## Problem

PR #5732 rejects frame ids that are live in a snapshot before plan execution, but the fresh-frame claim and cleanup are not atomic or incarnation-owned. On the JVM, another thread/test can create a planned frame after the `before` snapshot and before `execute-frame-plans!`; the production ENSURE path then adopts that ambient frame, recreating the isolation false positive. Worse, the `finally` classifies ownership only by id-not-in-`before` and calls `destroy-frame!` by bare id, so it destroys the concurrently created frame it never owned.

The inverse race is also unsafe: after the test-created frame is destroyed/replaced by another actor, `finally` can destroy the newer same-id incarnation. This violates rf2-vxgfnd.55's acceptance that fresh renders clean up exactly the frames they own and leave caller-owned frames untouched.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use deterministic JVM barriers:

1. Thread A enters plan-bearing `ui.test/render`, snapshots `before` with planned id X absent, then pauses before `execute-frame-plans!`.
2. Thread B creates X with caller-owned state/config.
3. Resume A. Production ENSURE sees X live and adopts it; A renders ambient state.
4. A's `finally` sees X absent from the old snapshot and calls `destroy-frame! X`, destroying B's frame.

A second fixture can let A create X, have B destroy/recreate X before A's cleanup, then show A destroys B's replacement.

## Deliverable

Make the test host's multi-plan fresh-frame acquisition a real atomic ownership protocol. All planned ids must be reserved/created only if absent as one fail-before-write operation (or an equivalent serializable claim), and cleanup must target the exact frame incarnation/token created by this render—not whichever frame later occupies the id. Keep production ENSURE adoption unchanged; this stronger rule belongs to `ui.test`.

Do not solve this by globally serializing unrelated test frames, resetting the registry, or making parallel tests share ambient state.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deterministic barrier fixtures reproduce both absent-at-snapshot/concurrent-create and destroy/recreate-before-cleanup races without sleeps.
- If any planned id is already claimed at the atomic acquisition point, the render fails before installing any planned frame or draining any initial event.
- A losing render never reads, mutates, records a plan for, or destroys the winning actor's frame.
- Cleanup destroys only frame incarnations/tokens created by that render; a newer same-id incarnation survives unchanged.
- Multi-plan acquisition is all-or-nothing for the collision class, including a collision on the final plan.
- Fresh uncontended renders still seed once, render, and release every owned frame with zero residue.
- Production `execute-frame-plans!` adoption/HMR semantics remain unchanged, and unrelated ids can render concurrently.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5743 — atomic all-or-nothing plan-frame claim (single-CAS reservation + live check) replacing the stale before-snapshot, and incarnation-token-owned teardown replacing bare-id destroy. Test-host scope only; production ENSURE/adoption in frames.cljc unchanged. 3 deterministic barrier tests (claim atomicity, concurrent-create reject, destroy/recreate teardown). Gates: ui clojure -M:test 262/4500 0-fail; npm test:cljs 8967/42313 0-fail.

title: Do not misclassify live-cache displacement as frame destruction during acquire
description:
## Problem

PR #5730's new `build-and-classify!` treats every non-canonical result with no recovery marker as `{:recovery :frame-destroyed}`. That fallback is not specific to frame destruction. On the JVM, a live frame's just-built canonical node can be invalidated by HMR registration replacement or explicit cache clear between `compute-and-cache!` returning and `canonical-cache-reaction?` reading the cache. The recovery sink is nil (the build itself succeeded), the frame/cache is still live, yet `acquire!` emits and throws `:rf.error/frame-destroyed`.

This intersects the acquisition/disposal handshake being repaired under in-progress rf2-vxgfnd.32, but it is new scope introduced by merged #5730 and must not be appended to a worker that has already started.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use a JVM barrier around the build-to-canonical-check window:

1. Thread A calls `observation/acquire!` on a cache miss and completes a successful canonical node install.
2. Pause A before `canonical-cache-reaction?`.
3. Thread B re-registers the subscription (or clears the live frame's sub cache), evicting that node while leaving the frame live.
4. Resume A.
5. `build-and-classify!` sees non-canonical + nil sink and returns `:frame-destroyed`; the port fans a false always-on frame-destroyed record and throws even though the frame is live.

## Deliverable

Remove the conflation between cache-node displacement and frame death. Revalidate frame incarnation/liveness separately. If a live node lost the build/check race, integrate with the rf2-vxgfnd.32 canonical acquisition handshake: release/ignore the displaced result identity-safely and retry against the current registration/cache, or return another truthful existing condition. Reserve `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` for verified destruction of the targeted frame incarnation.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic JVM barrier fixture forces successful build followed by HMR eviction before canonical verification; no `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` throw or always-on record is produced while the frame remains live.
- The live-cache displacement path converges on a canonical current lease (or another explicitly ruled truthful result) without leaking the displaced reaction/ref/input refs.
- Explicit cache clear on a live frame receives the same truthful handling.
- A genuine destroy-before-build and destroy-mid-build still fan and throw exactly one `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` for the targeted incarnation.
- Retry is bounded by observable generation/incarnation movement and cannot spin forever under repeated HMR; it preserves no-synchronous-`on-change` acquisition semantics.
- The result composes with rf2-vxgfnd.32: no acquire returns an unhooked/stale lease, and neither fix reintroduces false ownership over a never-cached recovery reaction.
- CLJS behavior and the successful hot acquire path remain unchanged in shape and production cost.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5747. acquire! disambiguates a :frame-destroyed recovery against the targeted frame's incarnation token: still-live incarnation -> live-cache displacement -> retarget to the current canonical node (bounded, incarnation-gated retry); nil/changed incarnation -> verified destruction -> throw frame-destroyed. Fix confined to re-frame.substrate.observation (build-node-lease! extraction + retry loop). Tests: displacement retargets (no false frame-destroyed, no leak), repeated displacement bounded+converges, genuine in-window destruction still throws exactly one frame-destroyed. Gates: core JVM 1862/0, obs-port ns 32/0, CLJS 8973/0. Spec 006 clarifying sub-bullet added (hot-zone).

title: Linearize ViewCell commit against frame-destroy teardown
description:
## Problem

PR #5731 wires frame destruction to a snapshot sweep of `live-cells`, but the sweep runs while the frame is intentionally still live and has no linearization with `reactive/commit!` / observation `acquire!` on the JVM. A commit can acquire leases and enrol a cell after `teardown-frame!` has captured its victim vector but before core flips the frame's liveness bit. That cell is absent from the sweep, publishes `:connected`, and then loses its cache underneath it during the remaining destroy recipe—the exact live-cell/port-throw state #5731 intended to eliminate.

The core `destroying-frames` guard prevents re-entrant destroy calls only; the observation port and ViewCell commit path do not consult it. Atomically updating the set of cells is not enough because selection and closure of the frame are separate operations.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use barriers on the JVM:

1. Start `destroy-frame!` and pause after `teardown-frame!` snapshots `live-cells`, before `mark-frame-destroyed!`.
2. On another thread, render/commit a new ViewCell that targets the still-live frame; allow acquisition and `connect!` to finish.
3. Resume destruction.
4. The new cell was never a victim. It remains `:connected` after the frame/cache is gone and later receives a disposal/port failure instead of reaching `:dead`.

## Deliverable

Make frame close and ViewCell ownership acquisition one linearizable lifecycle boundary. Once destruction begins, no new commit may publish ownership for that frame; already committed owners must be discoverable and torn down while their cache is still safely releasable. A restrained design is a per-frame closing token/gate shared by acquisition/commit and destroy, or an equivalent two-phase close with revalidation before publish. Do not rely on repeated unsynchronised sweeps or timing.

Preserve same-id reincarnation safety: closure belongs to one frame incarnation, never the next frame created with the same id.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic barrier-based JVM fixture reproduces the snapshot/late-commit interleaving without sleeps and is green after the fix.
- After destruction returns, no ViewCell for that frame incarnation is `:connected` or owns a lease: pre-existing cells are `:dead`; racing new commits either join the teardown or fail before publishing ownership through a truthful typed condition.
- The close boundary prevents acquisition after closing begins while still permitting existing leases to release against the correct cache.
- Multi-target cells and sibling-frame cells are handled correctly: destroying A kills a cell that committed A as ruled, without tearing down unrelated cells that observe only B.
- Destroy/recreate of the same frame id cannot let an old close gate or sweep kill cells belonging to the new incarnation.
- CLJS single-thread behavior remains simple and production acquisition/commit overhead is constant and measured/justified.
- The S2 ownership/frame-destroy conformance gate includes this interleaving.
notes: HELD (mayor 2026-07-12): P1 but CROSS-CUTTING — linearizes reactive/commit! ↔ observation acquire! ↔ core frame liveness, overlapping running workers .70 (observation.cljc) + .24 (frames). Two-workers-one-surface risk. Dispatch once .70 AND .24 merge so its linearization can span all three files safely. Coupled-surface serial exception.
close_reason: Closed

title: Enforce effective identifierPrefix uniqueness in the live-root registry
description:
## Problem

PR #5725 fixed the compiler's lossy `root-id-slug`, but rf2-vxgfnd.17 was closed without its runtime half. Spec 004C §7 says the per-document live-root registry asserts effective `identifier-prefix` uniqueness, including explicitly authored prefixes. `re-frame.ui.client/live-roots` currently stores no prefix, and `check-root-claim!` checks only root-id and container ownership. Two distinct roots can therefore author the same prefix and both reach React, producing colliding `useId` values despite the contract and the original bead's acceptance criteria.

The idempotent same-root/same-container `mount*` path also bypasses claim checks entirely. If HMR changes that root's authored prefix, the new value is silently ignored because React root options are immutable after `createRoot`, while preflight and render still proceed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Mount root A and root B into different containers with distinct root ids but the same literal `:identifier-prefix`.
2. Both mounts succeed because Layer 3 compares neither effective prefix.
3. Render components using React `useId`; both roots can emit the same ids/ARIA references.
4. Separately, remount the same root id/container after changing its authored prefix. The existing-root fast path reuses the old React root without diagnosing that the new option was not applied.

## Deliverable

Complete Layer-3 identity enforcement. Carry each root's resolved effective prefix in the production live-root claim, reject conflicting prefixes before preflight or React work, and define the same-root/same-container behavior when a remount presents a different prefix (fail loud is preferred because silently ignoring a changed root option is dishonest). Release the prefix claim only with the exact owning Root so a stale handle cannot free a newer owner.

Use the existing root identity/error family if it states the client condition honestly; otherwise add and catalogue one deliberate typed error. This is first-party `re-frame.ui` work, not adapter compatibility work.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two live roots with distinct root ids and the same authored effective prefix fail before frame preflight, `createRoot`, or render; the existing root remains untouched.
- The diagnostic identifies both root ids/sites and the conflicting prefix, with a useful recovery.
- A same-root/same-container remount carrying a changed prefix cannot silently reuse the old React option; its ruled behavior is explicit, typed, and tested.
- Derived prefixes from distinct valid root ids continue to be distinct and pass the same runtime claim path.
- `unmount!` releases the exact root's prefix claim; a stale Root handle cannot release a newer claim, and the prefix can be reused after the true owner unmounts.
- Mounted DOM coverage uses React `useId`/label associations to prove normal multi-root ids remain unique and an authored collision is stopped before commit.
- The implementation and Spec 004C/009 catalogue agree, with no per-render work and only bounded root-claim bookkeeping in production.
notes: PR #5735 PARTIAL (Codex review, 2026-07-12): cross-root effective-prefix claim/release and the catalogue entry landed, but the same-root/same-container HMR prefix-change case remains silently ignored because the existing-root mount fast path does not compare the requested prefix and React root options are immutable. The new DOM test proves collision rejection but does not render actual React useId/label associations. Do not close this bead until AC3 and AC6 are met.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5746 (commit 1). Same-root fast path now compares the requested effective identifier-prefix to the live root's and fails loud with new typed :rf.error/root-identifier-prefix-immutable before preflight; Spec 009 row added; React useId DOM proof + HMR-prefix-change tests. Gates: JVM ui 260 / node 8986 / browser 293, 0-fail.

title: Keep boot-frame authority stable after ENSURE adoption
description:
## Problem

PR #5722 prevents immediate clobber when an ENSURE plan first encounters a live frame that has no plan-install record, but the new `:adopt` record stores the incoming plan fingerprint and installer as though the root owned that frame. The first config-bearing plan is silently ignored; a later same-root plan with a different fingerprint is classified as `:refresh` and calls `make-frame`, overwriting boot-authoritative state/configuration. Adoption and installation authority are therefore conflated.

A reproduced sequence starts with boot state `boot-authoritative`, adopts under fingerprint A without applying A, then refreshes under fingerprint B and changes the frame to `second-plan-applied`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a live frame outside the root-plan registry with boot-authoritative configuration/state.
2. Preflight a config-bearing ENSURE plan for that id from root R, fingerprint A.
3. Observe that A is recorded but not applied.
4. Preflight a changed plan for the same root/id, fingerprint B.
5. Current behavior takes the refresh path and overwrites the externally owned frame.

## Deliverable

Represent installation authority explicitly. A configless `[frame-root {:id x}]` may adopt a live external/boot frame, but an adopted record must never enter a root-owned refresh path. A config-bearing plan that meets a live planless frame must fail loud instead of silently discarding its configuration. When the external frame is genuinely destroyed, stale adoption evidence must not prevent a later absent-frame plan from creating a new root-owned lifetime.

Preserve the intended preflight atomicity and cross-root conflict diagnostics. Do not turn adoption into implicit ownership transfer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Configless adoption preserves the live frame's identity, generation, configuration, app-db, and external ownership.
- A non-empty/config-bearing plan against a live planless frame fails before registry or frame mutation; its ignored configuration is never recorded as authoritative.
- Recompiling/editing a plan associated with an adopted frame never calls `make-frame` or reseeds the frame.
- Same-root and cross-root follow-up behavior is deterministic and covered by typed conflict diagnostics.
- Destroying the external frame invalidates/hides the adoption record; a later absent-frame plan can install a new root-owned lifetime and subsequently use normal same-owner refresh semantics.
- Fixtures cover immediate adoption, config-bearing collision, same-root fingerprint change, cross-root collision, destruction/reincarnation, and preflight rollback.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5738: registry discriminates INSTALLED (root-owned) from ADOPTED (boot-authoritative, non-owning); config-bearing plan meeting a boot frame fails loud; adoption never grants refresh rights. ui JVM 249/4451 + node CLJS 8962/42305 green.

title: ui.test plan-bearing render must reject pre-existing frame ids
description:
## Problem

PR #5720 added plan-bearing `ui.test/render` support and promises a fresh isolated frame lifetime per test render. The implementation snapshots live frame ids, calls the production `execute-frame-plans!` path, and merely avoids destroying ids that existed before the test. Production ENSURE semantics deliberately adopt an already-live frame. Consequently a test plan can silently reuse ambient state, ignore its declared initial events/configuration, and still pass.

This is a test-host contract bug, not a reason to weaken production adoption semantics.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a live frame `:test/greet` with app-db `{:greeting "existing"}`.
2. Compile/render a plan-bearing root for the same id whose plan initializes `{:greeting "planned"}`.
3. Read the rendered subscription and the frame after cleanup.
4. Current result renders `"existing"`; the plan is ignored and the pre-existing frame remains live. The harness therefore did not provide the fresh frame it advertises.

## Deliverable

Add a `ui.test/render`-specific, all-plans preflight rule: before executing any plan, reject the render if any planned frame id is already live. The failure must be typed and diagnostic, occur before any frame/lease/root mutation, and name the colliding frame/root. Keep production ENSURE adoption unchanged. Do not solve this by rewriting ids, resetting global frame state, or destroying caller-owned frames.
acceptance_criteria:
- A plan-bearing test render with any pre-existing planned frame id fails before the first plan is installed.
- The colliding frame's identity, generation, app-db, configuration, and liveness are unchanged after failure.
- A multi-plan root is validated atomically: a collision in a later plan cannot leave earlier plans installed.
- Fresh plan-bearing renders still install their declared plans and clean up exactly the frames they own.
- A real compiler + frame + subscription fixture reproduces the former ambient-state false positive and proves the correction.
- Any new error id is catalogued with stable diagnostic fields; no production adoption behavior changes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Correct re-frame.ui scheduling contract: drain queued writes before one render batch
description:
## Problem
The re-frame.ui scheduling contract currently conflates two different units. A frame/event epoch is a write-side commit and diagnostic evidence unit; it is not a React render boundary. spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md invariant 6, ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/03-reactivity-and-ownership.md, 07-testing.md G-3/G-5, and implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc comments still say or imply one notification/render per epoch, including the explicit false gate "8 epochs => 8 renders". This would force unnecessary reads and renders between events that are already queued in the same run-to-completion drain.

The intended model is: process the write side of every queued event to drain quiescence; those events may each commit their own epoch record; then advance each dirty ViewCell once and let React perform one read/render batch. Epoch ids remain movement/cause evidence only. The existing test coalescing-is-independent-of-the-epoch-tag-while-pending is directionally correct.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/07-testing.md G-5, which says "8 epochs => 8" renders.
2. Compare spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md invariant 6 and epoch-finalization text with router.cljc's run-to-completion drain, which can process several queued events and commit one epoch record per event before returning.
3. Compare those statements with reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc/coalescing-is-independent-of-the-epoch-tag-while-pending, which correctly folds different epoch tags into one pending ViewCell notification.
4. Observe that the documents would require intermediate renders which the implementation deliberately does not perform.

## Deliverable
Reconcile the normative spec, synthesis documents, implementation comments/docstrings, guide language, and test-gate wording around a named drain-quiescence/read-batch boundary. Replace epoch-count render assertions with a real queued-cascade contract. Coordinate with rf2-vxgfnd.12 rather than adding a second gate implementation.

The G-5/G-13 fixture must drive a parent event that queues further events, prove that every write/commit settles, then prove one ViewCell notification and one React render for the resulting read batch. A later independently driven drain must remain observable as later work, but no render count may be inferred merely from the number of event/frame epochs.

## Constraints
Do not add a compatibility mode or per-epoch feature flag. Preserve the production economy: one dirty-set enrollment per cell per pending read batch, no prop-dependent query execution on the write side, and no artificial render between queued events. Keep controlled-input synchronous-drain correctness explicit.
design: Prefer expressing the invariant as "writes to quiescence, then reads". Do not make render scheduling depend on comparing epoch tags. An epoch tag may accompany invalidation evidence, but the cell's dirty/pending state defines coalescing. The implementation may continue to use a host scheduling primitive if an end-to-end fixture proves it cannot run before the active drain reaches quiescence; otherwise add the smallest explicit drain-finalization seam that preserves core/substrate layering.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No normative or gate text asserts "8 epochs => 8 renders" or equates an event/frame epoch with a render boundary.
2. Spec 006, synthesis docs 03/07/12, implementation comments, and relevant guide text use one consistent distinction: event epochs are write/evidence units; drain quiescence followed by a read batch is the notification/render boundary.
3. G-3/G-5/G-13 acceptance describes and tests multiple queued event commits followed by one ViewCell notification and one React render through the real dispatch, observation-port, useSyncExternalStore, and React stack.
4. Tests prove all queued writes are visible to that render and that no intermediate render occurs.
5. Existing scoped flush semantics and the controlled-input synchronous door remain covered and coherent.
notes: 006 AMENDMENT REVIEWED + APPROVED by mayor: clean doc-matches-reality correction (invariant 6: 'one notification per cell per epoch' → 'per render batch = drain quiescence'). The worker found the MECHANISM was already correct (one microtask per drain); only the contract STATEMENT was wrong. Not a new-contract choice → mayor-mergeable. Merge #5733 when green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Observation first-owner hook installation races node disposal and loses invalidation
description:
## Problem

PR #5710 fixed historical-lease retention by enrolling the first active owner in the node record and then, in a separate operation, calling interop/add-on-dispose! to install the one node-scoped disposal callback. The record is marked :hooked? true before that callback is actually registered.

On the concurrent JVM host, cache disposal can linearize in that gap. interop/Reaction disposal snapshots and clears its current callbacks; a callback added afterwards is merely appended to an already-disposed object and did not observe the disposal. The CLJS plain-atom implementation is stricter: once its disposed flag is set, a later callback will never run. A second owner also sees :hooked? true and therefore does not install a hook while the first installer is paused.

## Steps to Reproduce

Against main 565dda1d85 (which contains merged PR #5710), wrap interop/add-on-dispose! with a barrier only for observation-node-disposed callbacks:

1. Thread A calls observation/acquire! and pauses inside add-on-dispose! after register-owner! has marked the record hooked.
2. Thread B re-registers the target subscription, evicting and disposing the canonical reaction while no observation callback is installed.
3. Resume Thread A and let it append the callback to the disposed reaction.
4. The acquire returns a lease for which current? is false, but the owner received no HMR or disposal notification.

Observed output from the real plain-atom adapter:

{:lease-returned? true, :current? false, :notifications []}

This is not the already-filed same-id evidence problem in rf2-vxgfnd.14. It is a lost-disposal handshake introduced by the one-hook owner registry.

## Expected Behavior

Every acquired node lease is covered by a fully installed disposal notification before acquire! returns. If disposal wins during acquisition, the staged owner is rolled back/retried or receives the normal invalidation without synchronous fan-out.

## Actual Behavior

The owner record advertises :hooked? before callback installation completes. A concurrent disposal can miss the callback and acquire! still returns the stale lease without a notification.

## Impact

A node replacement, explicit cache clear, or frame teardown concurrent with first-owner acquisition can leave an acquired owner without the invalidation promised by the observation port. The ViewCell often detects movement during its immediate commit read, but that is not a complete fallback: explicit disposal need not advance an epoch, and an already-committed owner relies on the callback channel. The port's JVM concurrency contract cannot depend on JavaScript run-to-completion timing.

## Coordination

This was found while independently auditing closed bead rf2-vxgfnd.15 / PR #5710. It blocks the S2 HMR matrix and S2 ownership/conformance gates. Coordinate with rf2-vxgfnd.14 because both touch observation evidence/consumer tests, but do not fold the two distinct failure modes together.
design:
Make owner enrolment, hook readiness, and node canonicality a real handshake. A restrained direction is:

1. Represent the node hook state as installing versus installed, not a boolean that advertises readiness early.
2. Do not allow any acquire to return while its node has owners but the disposal hook is only installing.
3. After the installer registers the callback, re-check that the acquired reaction is still the canonical cache node. If disposal won the race before registration, drain or roll back the staged owner and retry/fail through the normal acquire path; do not publish a stale lease.
4. Once the hook is installed and canonicality has been checked, any later disposal is covered by the callback.

Preserve the no-synchronous-owner-fan-out rule: repairing the handshake must not invoke on-change from inside acquire!. Prefer local observation-port state plus a canonicality retry over widening every adapter API, unless research proves a cross-adapter register-or-run-now disposal primitive is the simpler invariant. Keep one disposal hook per live node and constant work per acquire/release.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Add the deterministic JVM barrier fixture described above. It must fail on PR #5710 and pass after the repair without sleeps as the ordering mechanism.
2. Exercise two concurrent acquirers: neither may return behind an uninstalled hook, and disposal during first-hook installation must notify or safely roll back every active owner exactly once.
3. An acquire returns only a canonical live lease covered by an installed disposal callback; a node that lost the race is released identity-safely and re-acquired or produces the existing typed frame/no-sub failure.
4. Preserve acquire!'s no-synchronous-on-change guarantee and release!'s idempotence/reentrancy rules.
5. Cover HMR replacement, explicit cache clear, and frame destruction on JVM; retain the CLJS/React layout-commit fixture and both adapter families.
6. Preserve O(1) disposal-hook storage, O(current owners) disposal work, exact cache-entry shape, and production hot-path bounds.
7. Keep rf2-vxgfnd.14's node-incarnation/evidence repair independent and make both regressions green together before accepting the S2 HMR or ownership gates.
notes: Additional manifestation from the 2026-07-12 port review (folded from closed dup rf2-vxgfnd.38): beyond losing the invalidation callback, a lease acquired concurrently with HMR invalidation can enrol after take-owners! has drained — acquire!'s ref-bump CAS lands just before the invalidation swap (subs/cache.cljc:233-253 dissocs unconditionally), register-owner! (observation.cljc:587-601) finds :hooked? true (JVM -dispose clears callbacks BEFORE firing, interop.clj:92-98), returns false -> that lease never receives ANY disposal notification. current? converges state next commit; the 'notifies former owners once' contract is silently unmet. Adjacent: Reaction's callbacks field is ^:unsynchronized-mutable and add-on-dispose! runs unlocked — an install racing -dispose can be lost outright. Fix should cover both windows (enrol-then-verify liveness + self-notify if dead, or lock the install window). RELATED: rf2-vxgfnd.37 (WeakHashMap self-reference) compounds with the teardown!-unwired gap — unreleased leases of destroyed frames pin node records forever.
close_reason: Closed

title: (BUG) acquire! returns an 'owned' lease over never-cached recovery reactions (cycle / parametric input failure / destroy race) — ref-count-attach contract bypassed
description: Port review finding (MAJOR CONFIRMED, 2026-07-12). observation.cljc:731-763 treats any non-nil return from subs/acquire-cache-reaction! as canonical, but three subs.cljc paths return non-nil never-cached zero-ref reactions: cycle recovery (subs.cljc:1186-1193, explicitly not cached), parametric input-fn throw/bad-return (1060 + 1075/1156-1161), and frame-destroyed-between-resolutions JVM race (1142-1161, bypasses the nil->:rf.error/frame-destroyed guard). Contract: Spec 006 port ops — acquire = the cache's ref-count attach; fail-loud. Failure: cyclic subs — commit acquires, lease says owned? true (a lie: no entry, no ref), current? false from birth -> every commit retargets, builds a fresh orphan + node-record + disposal hook, re-emits :rf.error/sub-cycle — structural churn instead of one stable recovery or one typed throw. No fixture covers acquire-on-cycle / acquire-on-parametric-failure; acquire-time behavior for these is also UNSPECIFIED in 006 (spec's recovery language covers probe only). FIX: rule the acquire-time contract (recommend: typed throw mirroring the probe recovery taxonomy, or an explicitly-unowned recovery lease), implement in acquire!, add both fixtures, and amend the 006 §error-contract/recovery wording in the same PR (hot-zone 006 — sole toucher). notes: 006-AMENDMENT REVIEW DISCHARGED (monitor worker, 2026-07-12, post-merge): the close reason's 'do not merge until 006 amendment reviewed' gate was outrun by the green-merge sweep, so the review ran post-merge — amendment VERIFIED SOUND: typed-throw ruling with the binding invariant ('a lease MUST NOT report owned? true without a real cache ref + attach'); per-condition ids reuse the existing taxonomy (sub-cycle / sub-input-fn-* / frame-destroyed); emit discipline explicitly prevents double-fan (parametric fans from the build only; sub-cycle stays diagnostic, not promoted to always-on); the entry-node-attach vs mid-graph-recovery line is drawn correctly. Gates: core JVM 1856/8268/0, ui JVM 235/4360/0, CLJS 8937/42172/0. Do not merge until 006 amendment reviewed.

title: (BUG) Preflight plan adoption of a live plan-less frame silently replaces its whole config + image generation

description: S2c review finding (MAJOR CONFIRMED, 2026-07-12; spot-verified). emit_cljs.cljc:258-267 emits frame-root children under a bare Fragment (no context Provider); emit_jvm.cljc:199-200 likewise binds no *current-frame*; frames.cljc scope-element (253-264) has ZERO callers.
