title: New UI override path bypasses sub schema validation and adds an unelided per-sub consult
description:
## Problem

The existing Reagent-family `subscribe` override path validates a Story `:sub-overrides` HIT against the target sub's output `:schema`, emits `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` with `:where :sub-override`, and substitutes nil. The new compiled UI path must preserve that honesty rule while keeping Story machinery out of production.

The in-progress S2b implementation currently resolves `*sub-overrides*` directly for every `sub` call, lowers a hit to `{:value v :override-id query :version v}`, and passes it to the observation port. It performs no schema lookup/validation. The consult is unconditional rather than guarded by `interop/debug-enabled?`, so a dynamic-var read/function call remains on the production subscription render path even when Story is absent. The chosen query-as-id/value-as-version lowering is also not recorded in the target ABI, which specifies an opaque id/version change token.

## Steps to Reproduce

After rf2-vxgfnd.8 lands:

1. Register a sub with an output schema that rejects a chosen override value.
2. Render the same Story override through stock Reagent and through `re-frame.ui`.
3. Reagent emits the structured schema failure and surfaces nil; the new UI surfaces the invalid value without validation.
4. Compile an `:advanced`, `goog.DEBUG=false` view containing `(sub ...)` and inspect emitted/bundle code: the new path still invokes the override consult and reads `*sub-overrides*` for every sub site.

## Expected Behavior

Both compatibility tiers apply the same registered output-schema validator and recovery to Story overrides. Override resolution happens once during render, commit never re-consults context, and production builds contain zero Story-override bytes or per-sub branches.

## Actual Behavior

The compiled UI can display a state the declared sub schema says is impossible, diverges from stock Reagent, and taxes every production sub read for a dev/tool feature.

## Coordination

rf2-vxgfnd.8 is already in progress and owns ViewCell/live sub wiring. Do not amend that active bead. Sequence this follow-up immediately after its PR and before rf2-vxgfnd.12's S2 production/performance gates. Coordinate with the later Story adoption work; do not introduce a tools dependency into core or UI.
design:
Extract/reuse one internal override-validation primitive from the current `re-frame.subs` path so both Reagent and `re-frame.ui` resolve metadata through the correct frame generation and invoke the same registered validator/error contract. The UI render path should pass the already validated HIT into `resolve-target`; commit acquires that exact captured static target and never reads React context again.

Pin a minimal, explicit lowering from the public raw `{query value}` context to `override-id`/`version` (or amend the internal ABI if value equality is intentionally the change token). Keep the entire CLJS Story context consult behind an outer compile-time debug gate so Closure removes it. JVM `ui.test/render {:sub-overrides ...}` may use its explicit dynamic door in test/debug code without pretending it is React context.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A schema-invalid override emits the same `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` shape (`:where :sub-override`) and surfaces nil through both stock Reagent and `re-frame.ui`; valid and nil-valued hits remain distinguishable from misses.
2. Validation resolves the sub metadata through the target frame/image when one exists and reuses the registered validator; no duplicate schema engine or tools dependency is added.
3. Override context is read exactly once at render; commit/acquire/current/read never re-consult React context.
4. Pin and document `override-id`/`version` semantics, including equal-value provider replacement, nested providers, value changes, and HMR/schema changes; static leases remain `:owned? false` and callback-free.
5. `ui.test/render {:sub-overrides ...}` retains the explicit JVM test door and the same validation/recovery semantics.
6. Under `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false`, override context imports, strings, dynamic-var consults, and branches are absent from the production UI bundle; add an elision sentinel and retain G-1/G-13 budgets.
7. Add cross-tier parity fixtures and a Tier-3 Story context fixture; keep bundle-isolation intact.
notes: Dispatched 2026-07-12 (solo P1) after #5713 freed reactive.cljc + #5710 freed observation.cljc. Worktree override-schema-vxgfnd21. Surface reactive.cljc (override resolution) + observation.cljc (change-token ABI). rf2-vxgfnd.14 (also reactive+observation) SEQUENCED behind this — dispatch .14 after .21 merges.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5721 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5721). Compiled-view Story :sub-overrides now (1) reuse the ONE shared re-frame.subs.override-schema/validate-sub-override! primitive for schema validation + :where :sub-override recover-to-nil parity with the Reagent path; (2) gate the whole consult behind interop/debug-enabled? so it DCEs in prod (new check-elision.cjs sentinel, probe 48/48 absent / 48/48 control-present); (3) record :override-id/:version as an OPAQUE port change token. Gates: test:elision PASS, test:cljs 8928/0-fail, ui JVM 214/0-fail. Tier-3 mounted Story-context fixture deferred to S2f (React-context seeding not landed).

title: Root-id slug is non-injective, allowing distinct roots to share identifierPrefix and hydration locator
description:
## Problem

`re-frame.ui.compiler.root/root-id-slug` replaces every character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` with `-`, joins a keyword namespace/name with `-`, and joins vector components with `--`. This mapping is not injective even over the closed valid root-id grammar.

Distinct root ids can therefore receive the same default React `identifierPrefix` and, at S5, the same synthesized element locator. The root contract currently claims synthesized locators are unique because root ids are unique, but uniqueness of the input does not imply uniqueness after a lossy transform. The live-root registry checks root-id/container ownership, not effective prefix uniqueness.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Evaluate `root-id-slug` for the two valid qualified keywords `:a/b-c` and `:a-b/c`.
2. Both yield `"a-b-c"`, and both default to `"rf2-a-b-c-"`.
3. A vector collision also exists: `[:x/y "a--b"]` and `[:x/y "a" "b"]` both flatten to `"x-y--a--b"`.
4. Mount the distinct roots concurrently. Layer-3 accepts them because their root ids and containers differ, while React receives the same identifier prefix.

## Expected Behavior

Every valid root id has a deterministic collision-free identity encoding. Distinct live roots cannot share an effective `identifierPrefix`, whether derived or explicitly authored. Synthesized hydration locators cannot alias.

## Actual Behavior

The slug loses namespace/name punctuation and vector boundaries. Two accepted roots can generate duplicate React `useId` values and later resolve the same hydration locator without triggering current duplicate-root checks.

## Impact

Duplicate `useId` output can cross-wire labels, controls, descriptions, and ARIA references across independent React roots. Locator aliasing can hydrate the wrong container. This is a correctness/accessibility problem, not cosmetic naming.

## Coordination

rf2-vxgfnd.13 is currently promoting the root-identity contract into tracked spec pages. Do not edit that in-progress bead. Sequence this follow-up after its PR, then amend the promoted contract and implementation together before S5 manifests/hydration build on the false uniqueness claim.
design:
Replace the lossy identity slug with a canonical injective encoding for the closed root-id grammar. Prefer a type-tagged, length-delimited encoding of keyword namespace/name and vector scalar components; it can retain a short human-readable prefix for diagnostics, but uniqueness must not depend on a truncated hash or punctuation normalization. Define the encoding once and use it for default `identifierPrefix` and synthesized locators.

Independently enforce effective `identifierPrefix` uniqueness in the live-root registry for all roots, including explicitly authored prefixes. Store the resolved prefix in the live-root entry, claim/release it with the root, and fail loudly on conflict using the contract's existing root-manifest/identity error family or a deliberately catalogued replacement. Do not rely solely on compile-time detection because roots can originate in independent bundles.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Pin the known keyword and vector collision pairs and a property test over the valid root-id grammar asserting distinct ids produce distinct canonical encodings.
2. Preserve deterministic output across JVM/CLJS, compile order, process restarts, SSR, and client builds.
3. Use one encoding implementation for default identifier prefixes and synthesized manifest locators; update every golden fixture and the promoted root-identity contract.
4. Two live roots with different ids but the same authored or derived effective prefix fail before React render/hydration; the error identifies both roots/sites and the conflicting prefix.
5. Releasing/unmounting a root releases its prefix claim, and a stale Root handle cannot release a newer owner's claim.
6. Multiple normal roots continue to produce stable, practical-length identifiers; no per-render hashing or production hot-path work is introduced.
7. Add multi-root DOM coverage proving `useId`/label associations remain unique and S5 hydration chooses the correct container.
notes: Dispatched 2026-07-12 (solo P1) after #5719/.16 freed compiler. Worktree rootid-slug-vxgfnd17. Surface compiler/root.cljc (root-id-slug injectivity). Corrected brief: no full spine.
close_reason: Closed

title: Observation release retains one disposal closure per historical lease on shared live nodes
description:
## Problem

Every observation-port `acquire!` registers a fresh `interop/add-on-dispose!` closure on the canonical reaction. `release!` removes the lease's change watch and decrements the cache ref-count, but the disposal API has no corresponding removal operation. A released lease therefore remains strongly reachable from the reaction until that node is eventually disposed.

If any long-lived owner keeps a shared node above zero references, repeated route mounts, conditional views, or StrictMode acquire/release cycles accumulate one dormant closure per historical owner. This is an unbounded production memory leak and makes eventual HMR/cache disposal O(all owners ever acquired), rather than O(current owners).

## Steps to Reproduce

Against main `f7a85999` with the real JVM plain-atom reaction:

1. Register a layer-1 sub and keep its cache node live with one public subscriber.
2. Run 1,000 observation `acquire!`/`release!` pairs against that same target.
3. Inspect the reaction's disposal callback storage and cache ref-count.

Observed:

```
{:dispose-callbacks-before 1
 :dispose-callbacks-after 1001
 :retained-released-lease-callbacks 1000
 :cache-ref-count 1}
```

The existing 10k cold-probe test cannot catch this because cold probes acquire no leases.

## Expected Behavior

A released lease is no longer retained by the live node. Node disposal work is proportional to currently active owners, regardless of how many owners mounted and unmounted historically.

## Actual Behavior

The reaction retains every historical lease closure until its eventual disposal. A permanently shared node can retain them for the process lifetime and later executes all dormant callbacks.

## Relevant Surfaces

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc`: per-lease disposal registration and release.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.clj` / `.cljs` and adapter disposal protocols: append-only callbacks.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_port_cljs_test.cljc`.
- S2 ownership/HMR/leak gates under rf2-vxgfnd.11/.12.

## Coordination

The defect is already merged in rf2-vxgfnd.7 and will be exercised heavily by rf2-vxgfnd.8. Fix before accepting the S2 HMR and ownership-gate wave. Do not assume nodes regularly reach zero; app-shell subscriptions commonly stay live for the process lifetime.
design:
Use one node-scoped disposal hook plus an identity-keyed collection of ACTIVE leases, rather than one non-removable hook per lease. The weak per-node observation record is the natural home: install the reaction disposal hook once; add a lease on acquire; remove it on release; on node disposal snapshot/clear active owners and enqueue each live owner once. Preserve the exact cache-entry key set and the existing per-lease removable change watches.

The JVM path must update the owner collection with the same concurrency discipline as node version records. The CLJS path may use identity semantics directly. Do not broaden the public adapter protocol with callback-removal machinery unless a concrete second consumer justifies that wider change.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Add a shared-node churn fixture: one permanent owner keeps the node live while 10,000 observation leases acquire/release; active-owner count returns to the permanent set and disposal-hook storage stays O(1), not O(10,000).
2. Prove released lease objects/callbacks are GC-reclaimable while the reaction remains live (weak-reference/FinalizationRegistry where supported plus a deterministic active-owner assertion).
3. Preserve two-live-sibling behavior: distinct callbacks, balanced ref-counts, exactly one HMR/disposal notification per active lease.
4. A lease released before a queued disposal drain receives no notification; a second release is a no-op.
5. HMR replacement, frame destroy, explicit cache clear, and zero-owner synchronous disposal drain active owners once and never scan historical owners.
6. Keep cache entry shape exactly `{:reaction :inputs :ref-count}` and public adapter/disposal APIs unchanged unless separately ruled.
7. Run dual-host observation-port tests and S2 ownership/HMR leak gates, including a production-mode retention/performance check.
notes: Dispatched 2026-07-12 (mayor 10m loop, solo P1). Worktree obs-release-vxgfnd15 at main e2badc62ba. Isolated to implementation/core observation port + reaction disposal API — no overlap with in-flight #5708 (ui reactive) / s2c / vxgfnd.13 (spec).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5710 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5710): per-lease non-removable add-on-dispose! closure replaced with one node-scoped disposal hook + identity-keyed active-owner set in the weak node record; release! de-enrols the lease so a released lease is no longer reachable from the live reaction (storage O(current owners)). interop/adapter disposal API unchanged. Adversarial retention fixture added (active-owner-count both hosts + JVM callback-storage O(1); verified it fails with retained-released-lease-callbacks=1000 on a simulated pre-fix closure). Gates green: fast-PR spine PASS; core JVM 1853/8242; CLJS 8893/42006 (incl. rf2-vxgfnd.8 ViewCell consumer). PR not merged.

title: Observation live-evidence misses same-id frame reincarnation between render and commit
description:
## Problem

The merged observation port cannot distinguish a live subscription node observed in one frame incarnation from a newly acquired node in a later incarnation that reused the same frame id when their node versions and epochs happen to match. This violates the frozen S2 invariant that render-to-commit movement is detected and corrected before paint.

`resolve-target` collapses a frame target to `:frame-id`; probe evidence carries `:node-key`, `:node-version`, `:frame-epoch`, and global `:registry-epoch`; but `read` omits `:node-key`. `frame/dissoc-frame!` removes the commit-epoch entry, so destroy + recreate of the same id restarts its epoch. The S2b reconciler consumes the contract literally: a live probe compares only node version plus frame/registry epochs.

## Steps to Reproduce

Against main `f7a85999` with the real plain-atom adapter:

1. Create frame `:codex/reincarnation`, install app-db `{:v 1}`, subscribe to make the node live, and probe it.
2. Destroy the frame, recreate the same id, install `{:v 2}`, and acquire/read the same observation target.
3. Observe:

```
render {:value 1, :node-version 0, :node-key 1,
        :frame-epoch 1, :registry-epoch 1}
commit {:value 2, :version 0,
        :frame-epoch 1, :registry-epoch 1}
```

Every field the specified live-evidence check compares is equal while the values differ.

## Expected Behavior

A node/frame replacement in the render-to-commit gap is classified as moved and causes the required synchronous pre-paint corrective render.

## Actual Behavior

The version/epoch-only live check classifies this capture as unchanged, so concurrent React can commit DOM derived from the destroyed incarnation without the required correction.

## Relevant Surfaces

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc`: target resolution, evidence, and `read`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc`: existing `frame-incarnation-token`; commit epochs cleared at destruction.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`: target/evidence/read ABI and correction invariant.
- S2b ViewCell evidence comparison once rf2-vxgfnd.8 lands.

## Coordination

rf2-vxgfnd.8 is already in progress and has committed the current version/epoch-only comparison. Do not amend that active bead. Land this as an immediate follow-up, coordinating/rebasing against its PR, before the S2 conformance-gate bead is accepted.
design:
Prefer the smallest structural repair: make `read` return the acquired node's existing `:node-key`, and make the live-probe evidence check compare node key in addition to node version and epochs. The node key is already minted and carried in probe evidence, so this is constant-time and avoids deep value equality on the production commit path. Cold probes continue to compare values by `rf=`.

The wider alternative is threading `frame/frame-incarnation-token` through target/evidence/lease state. Choose that only if exact-incarnation target semantics are needed beyond observable movement detection. Do not attempt to solve this by retaining/resetting epoch integers alone.

Because the port has an explicit ABI guard, update `port-abi-version` and the UI consumer's expected version if `read` changes. Keep the cache-entry key set unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Add a deterministic render-gap regression: probe a LIVE node, destroy/recreate the same frame id, install a different value while reproducing equal node-version/frame-epoch/registry-epoch values, then acquire/read and prove the reconciler classifies it as moved.
2. Run the primitive regression on JVM/plain-atom and CLJS; include a React layout-commit fixture proving correction occurs synchronously before paint.
3. Preserve the cold-probe rule (`:node-version nil` falls back to `rf=` value comparison).
4. Preserve the unchanged-node fast path: equal node key/version/epochs yields no correction, notification, or ownership churn.
5. Preserve HMR replacement and frame-destroy behavior; a disposed old node is never retained as canonical.
6. Update Spec 006, port docstrings/tests, ABI guard, and the S2b consumer coherently.
7. Keep comparison constant-time and add no cache-entry fields or public adapter API.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5774 — read now carries :node-key so a same-id frame reincarnation with coincident node-version+frame/registry epochs is detected as movement. port-abi-version bumped to 2. Cross-host regression proven to fail pre-fix then green. ui-side reconciler consumption tracked as follow-up rf2-vxgfnd.93.

title: [correctness-review][story] assertions-passing?/passing? on a run-result ignores :status floor + run-level :cannot-run -> false GREEN
description:
SURFACE: tools/story public test-adapter predicate.
FILES: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/assertions.cljc:260-274 (passing?); tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:1379-1392 (public assertions-passing?, delegates to passing?).

DEFECT (false GREEN): when handed a run-RESULT map, passing? reads only (:assertions result) and folds (every? :passed? items). It NEVER consults (:status result). So it is blind to (a) the agreement floor -- an unconsumed schema violation / failing epoch outcome / error effect that escalates :status to :fail in result/run-result (result.cljc:779) -- and (b) run-level :cannot-run refusals, which live in the top-level :cannot-run slot (result.cljc: (assoc :cannot-run unmet)), NOT in :assertions. The correct authority is result/passed? (result.cljc:890-895 -> (= :pass (:status result))), which reads :status.

This directly contradicts result.cljc's stated core invariant (lines 9-13): 'a verdict and the assertions slot can never disagree (the false GREEN class).' assertions-passing? is a floor-blind second verdict path.

REPRO 1 (floor-escalated :fail): build a run-result whose tape carries an unconsumed schema violation and whose only assertion passes -- the exact shape in result_test.cljc:202-216. No :rf.assert/schema-error expectation is declared, so match-schema-expectations mints no record; :assertions = [{:passed? true}]; base-status :pass; tape-red? true -> :status :fail. Then: (story/assertions-passing? r) => true  [FALSE GREEN] while (story/result-passed? r) => false.
REPRO 2 (run-level :cannot-run): a variant with an unmet requirement (or a :rf.assert/visual-snapshot under headless) -> :status :cannot-run with :assertions empty/all-passing -> assertions-passing? => true while the runner proved nothing.

WHY IT MATTERS: assertions-passing? is DOCUMENTED as 'the canonical predicate for the cljs.test / clojure.test adapter pattern' (story.cljc:1385-1390; spec/004-Assertions.md:309,370) with the example (is (story/assertions-passing? result)). It is actively used on result maps across testbeds (counter_with_stories/stories_cljs_test.cljs:247,320,335,346,360,372,392,410; login_form/stories_cljs_test.cljs:155; spec/006-MCP-Surface.md:87). A consumer's green test can hide a floor-failed / cannot-run run. NOTE the spec tension: spec/017-Testing-Story.md:1896 + API.md:107 already say 'there is NO :passing? boolean, use result-passed?/result-status' -- so newer guidance already points at the correct predicate while 004 + the live fn still promote the floor-blind one.

FIX SKETCH (mayor to rule direction): EITHER (a) make passing? on a result MAP delegate to result/passed? (read :status) -- keep the bare-assertions-vector path as-is for the render-only 'zero assertions is vacuously green' duality; OR (b) deprecate assertions-passing? for result maps and route consumers/spec/004 to result-passed? (aligning with 017/API). Keep the empty-assertions-vector vacuous-pass (render-only story-as-test duality) intact under (a).

ACCEPTANCE: a run-result with :status :fail (floor) or :cannot-run and all-passing/empty :assertions makes (story/assertions-passing? result) return FALSE (not true); the empty-assertions render-only vacuous-green case still returns true; a regression test pins both. Verified against HEAD 79fb2f2da.

title: Four guide pages still teach the pre-EP-0037 route-auth and loader model
description:
Found by the EP-0037 R6 integrated-proof pass (rf2-kqxe6.10) while spot-auditing the pages the EP-0037 waves rewrote against the shipped surface. Filed rather than patched, per R6's process rule.

The routing guide tree itself is coherent — `docs/routing/concepts.md`, `glossary.md`, the two how-tos, `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md`, the skill's routing reference and `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/` all verified correct end to end, and the retirement roster (`:query-retain`, `:rf.route/entry-blocked`, `:bypass-guards?`, route `:on-error`, `:enter-attempts`, `:rf.error/route-guard-loop`, `:inherit-resources?`) has ZERO residue in tracked docs/skills/examples.

But four pages the waves did not reach still teach the pre-EP-0037 model, and a reader who lands on one of them gets the retired mechanism as the primary recipe.

1. `docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md:212` — "Route-level auth is an ordinary interceptor over the navigation events — **not a special routing mechanism**". Section 4 (lines 210-317) then builds a hand-rolled `:app/auth-guard` interceptor with `:rf/skip-handler?` over `:tags #{:requires-auth}`. `:can-enter` and `:rf.route/entry-denied` appear nowhere on the page. Shipped: `:can-enter` is first-class route metadata evaluated in the one planning pipeline for every door, and `spec/012-Routing.md` says in as many words that an interceptor attached only to `:rf.route/navigate` fails OPEN. The EP's Guide-impact roster ("the auth and unsaved-change how-tos split the fresh-entry and resumable-leave recipes") was executed for the leave half (`docs/routing/how-to/guard-unsaved-changes.md` is correct) and never for the entry half.

   Compounding: line 230 attributes the recipe to `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/routing.cljs`, which now contains no interceptor at all (`git grep -E "auth-guard|reg-interceptor"` over that dir returns nothing) — it is `:can-enter` + a public `rf/reg-event :rf.route/entry-denied`. The attribution points at code that no longer exists.

2. `docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md:479` — "Route protection is an ordinary event interceptor, because every way of reaching a route is an event", followed by the same hand-rolled normaliser + `:tags #{:requires-auth}` recipe at 477-593. Same defect. Two smaller errors on the same page: `:can-leave :editor/can-leave?` at 604 uses the bare-keyword form (accepted by the runtime, but every other spec/doc/skill sample uses the vector form), and 609 tells the reader to "dispatch `:rf.route/continue`" with no pending-navigation id — a form `docs/routing/how-to/guard-unsaved-changes.md:65` explicitly calls wrong.

3. `docs/routing/coming-from-react-router.md:65` — "An auth guard doesn't need a wrapper around the protected subtree; it's an **interceptor** that reads a tag off the route table." Residual pre-EP prose. Line 38 of the SAME page already maps `throw redirect(...)` onto "`:can-enter` guard + a `:rf.route/entry-denied` handler ... Denial is terminal", and 136-142 explain the asymmetry correctly. The sweep fixed the table row and the divergence section and missed this paragraph.

4. `docs/routing/tutorial.md` still calls `:on-match` the loader, in four places: 136-139 ("give a page its data ... Declare it next to the route with `:on-match`"), 148 ("The loader is a normal event handler."), 186 ("**Loader as data.** `:on-match` is a vector of event vectors"), 345 (table row `| Data | :on-match or :resources | Loaders as data |`). Shipped and ratified: `:on-match` is fire-and-forget activation work and explicitly NOT the loader; page data is `:resources`. Three sibling pages the same wave rewrote already say so (`docs/routing/glossary.md:36`, `docs/routing/concepts.md:354` §"Activation work and page data", `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md:65`, `skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/routing.md:160`), so the tutorial now contradicts its own guide tree.

One smaller item worth folding in while the same worker is in the files: `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md:197` describes `route-meta` as carrying "`:path`, `:on-match`, `:params`, `:query`, `:scroll`, and `:can-leave`" — omitting `:can-enter` and `:parent`, which are exactly what the auth and branch-composition recipes read back. Same omission in the implementation docstring at `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:625`.

Deliberately NOT included, having been considered and rejected as minutiae: a stale inline comment at `skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/routing.md:130` that is corrected ten lines later, and the abbreviated (non-copy-pasteable) test snippet at `docs/routing/how-to/guard-unsaved-changes.md:115-130`.

Note on scope boundaries: the missing `:sensitive` re-declaration in every canonical `:rf.route/entry-denied` override is NOT part of this bead — it is rf2-kqxe6.20's acceptance criterion 3, and the roster I found is recorded on PR #6941.
acceptance_criteria: 1. docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md teaches :can-enter + :rf.route/entry-denied as THE route-auth mechanism, with the interceptor demoted to an appendix (as docs/routing/how-to/require-sign-in-on-a-route.md already does), and its example attribution matches code that exists. 2. docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md likewise; its :can-leave sample uses the vector form and its continue sample carries the pending id. 3. docs/routing/coming-from-react-router.md:65 no longer calls the auth guard an interceptor. 4. docs/routing/tutorial.md describes :on-match as fire-and-forget activation work and :resources as page data, in all four places. 5. docs/api/re-frame.routing.md route-meta lists :can-enter and :parent. 6. mkdocs build --strict and the doc-slug/README-link gates stay green.

title: O-8 sends popstate and SSR through the forward-only route event
description:
Found while auditing merged PR #6935 under completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality lenses.

PR #6935 accurately fixes O-8's retired `:on-match`-as-loader role, but the same edited migration recipe still sends two URL-driven doors through the wrong event and never tells the adopting app to declare a URL owner:

  step 5: replace popstate listener bodies with
          `(rf/dispatch [:rf.route/transitioned url])`
  step 6: dispatch `:rf.route/transitioned` for the SSR request URL

The canonical contract is explicit and consistent elsewhere:

- `:rf.route/transitioned` is the FORWARD door for route-link/programmatic pushes, with default scroll `:top`.
- `:rf.route/handle-url-change` owns popstate, initial page load, and SSR request URLs, with default scroll `:restore` and the SSR attribution path.
- Browser URL ownership is positive bootstrap policy: a frame must carry `:url-bound? true`; there is no default-frame floor. That frame lifecycle installs/removes the strategy-aware popstate/hashchange listener and performs initial URL sync automatically. With no URL owner, outbound history fxs no-op and inbound changes are skipped.

So O-8 step 5 is self-contradictory (keep a listener body, then remove the bespoke listener) and operationally incomplete: following the six steps without `:url-bound? true` yields a router whose slice can move while the address bar does not. Sending Back/Forward through `:rf.route/transitioned` also selects forward-navigation scroll semantics. Step 6 names the sibling event instead of the SSR door even though its new prose correctly links the SSR contract.

Evidence: spec/012-Routing.md public-surface rows 37-38, URL-changes section 517-522, SSR flow 1802, and URL ownership/lifecycle 1851-1869; docs/api/re-frame.routing.md rows 435-440 and 501-502. No exact Bead owns this door/ownership defect. rf2-3uiy8 was exact for the separate `:on-match` loader drift and was correctly closed by #6935.

Keep the repair documentary and small. Correct O-8's two door instructions and add the missing positive URL-owner bootstrap; do not change routing runtime or build a new checker for two stale sentences.
acceptance_criteria:
1. O-8 tells an adopting browser app to declare one URL-owning frame with `:url-bound? true` and to remove its bespoke popstate/hashchange listener because the frame lifecycle owns install, initial sync, and teardown.
2. Any URL-change event named for Back/Forward or initial browser load is `:rf.route/handle-url-change`; `:rf.route/transitioned` remains described only as the forward link/push door.
3. O-8's SSR step feeds the request URL through `:rf.route/handle-url-change`, matching Spec 012's canonical initial-event flow.
4. Step numbering and existing migration citations remain stable; prose/link gates pass. No runtime or checker machinery is added.

title: story-mcp still has no publish path: day8/de-dupe absent from Clojars, mcp-base un-buildable and un-inventoried
description:
rf2-4u3t1 ruled that BOTH `tools/story-mcp` and `tools/machines-viz` get a release path.
The machines-viz half shipped (new `.github/workflows/release-machines-viz.yml` on a
`machines-viz-v*` glob, plus the `:main` fix its `:clein/build` map needed). The story-mcp
half CANNOT be delivered inside that bead's fence, for three reasons found by actually
running clein rather than reading deps.edn. All three verified locally at main bb86e780a2.

## Blocker 1 — `day8/de-dupe` is not on Clojars, and clein cannot express a git coord in a pom

`tools/story-mcp/deps.edn` declares `day8/de-dupe {:git/url … :git/tag "v0.3.0" :git/sha …}`
as a main-`:deps` RUNTIME dependency (the wire-boundary structural dedup, applied before the
wire-cap check). `clojure -M:clein pom` in `tools/story-mcp` reports:

    Skipping coordinate: {:git/url https://github.com/day8/de-dupe.git, :git/tag v0.3.0, …}

and the generated pom carries exactly two dependencies — `org.clojure/clojure` and
`cheshire/cheshire`. This is the same silent-skip behaviour `clein pom` has for `:local/root`
(rf2-do3m2 / #6340), which the `:local/root → :mvn/version` rewrite exists to repair. There
is no equivalent repair for a git coordinate: a Clojars search for `de-dupe` returns no
results, so there is no `:mvn/version` to rewrite it to.

Consequence: publishing `day8/re-frame2-story-mcp` today would ship a jar whose pom omits a
runtime dependency, and a consumer would fail to resolve `de-dupe.*`. That is precisely the
failure class `preflight-story-package.sh` was written to prevent, and Clojars has no yank.
`tools/mcp-base` carries the same coord and the same problem.

Resolving this is a product decision, not a mechanical fix: publish `day8/de-dupe` to
Clojars, vendor it, or accept that these two artefacts are not Clojars-publishable.

## Blocker 2 — `day8/re-frame2-mcp-base` has no release path either, and is un-BUILDABLE

`tools/story-mcp/deps.edn` depends on `day8/re-frame2-mcp-base {:local/root "../mcp-base"}`.
`tools/mcp-base/deps.edn` declares its own publishable `:clein/build {:lib
day8/re-frame2-mcp-base …}` — so story-mcp cannot publish until mcp-base does. mcp-base is
NOT in `verify-version-lockstep.sh`'s four-entry `TOOLS` array, so it is a fifth publishable
tool jar the lockstep gate does not guard. rf2-4u3t1's fence explicitly barred changing that
array, which is why the story-mcp half stopped there rather than quietly publishing an
unguarded coordinate.

mcp-base is also un-buildable for the same reason machines-viz was:

    $ cd tools/mcp-base && clojure -M:clein pom
    Error in the :clein/build map: {:lib day8/re-frame2-mcp-base, …} - failed:
      (contains? % :main) spec: :noahtheduke.clein.specs/build-opts

The day8 clein fork's `build-opts` spec requires `:main`. Every clein invocation in that
directory aborts before doing any work.

## Blocker 3 — the lockstep gate cannot see either failure

Both blockers are invisible to `verify-version-lockstep.sh`: it reads `:version` and the
`:local/root` coordinates, never whether clein would accept the `:clein/build` map, and
never whether a non-`:local/root` runtime coordinate survives into the pom. It reported
"all 17 artefacts … pinned" while `day8/re-frame2-machines-viz` could not be built at all.
Two candidate hardenings, both cheap:

  - assert every `:clein/build` map satisfies clein's own spec (in practice: assert `:main`
    is present, which is the only required key the repo's maps have been missing); and
  - assert every main-`:deps` coordinate for a publishable artefact is a kind `clein pom`
    can express — i.e. flag `:git/url` coords in a publishable artefact's `:deps`, since
    those are dropped silently.

## Suggested order

1. Rule on `day8/de-dupe` (publish / vendor / accept unpublishable). Blocker 1 gates
   everything else; without it neither story-mcp nor mcp-base can ship a correct pom.
2. Add mcp-base to the `TOOLS` inventory (five tools) and give it `:main`.
3. Add the deploy jobs. Per rf2-4u3t1's ruling story-mcp joins the EXISTING
   `release-story.yml` on the EXISTING `story-v*` glob so the pair cannot skew; mcp-base
   needs to deploy ahead of it on that same glob.

title: Freehand manifest: publish the per-event-site classification the analyzer already records
description:
Found while landing increment 1 of rf2-lvvl2 (`re-frame.freehand.tool/
read-view-event-sites`). This is the SAME defect rf2-hytu5 fixed for
`:diagnostics`: a fact the compiler already records, collected in the analyzer
site index and published nowhere a reader can reach.

`re-frame.freehand.compiler.analyze` records five facts per event site beyond
its coordinates - `:prop` (the authored handler prop), `:classification`
(`:vector` / `:options` / the dynamic kinds), `:serializable?`, `:sync?` (the
controlled-input synchronous door, back-filled by `record-event-sync!`) and
`:handler` (the analyzed event vector). `re-frame.freehand.compiler/
structural-manifest` projects `(select-keys % [:sid :source-coord :path])` and
drops all five, so `read-view-event-sites` can say WHERE a view dispatches from
and cannot say WHAT it dispatches. That is the difference between an event-site
read an inspector can act on and one that only counts lines.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN INCREMENT 1: `spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/
fh-struct-010.edn` pins `:required-keys {:events #{:sid :source-coord :path}}`
and both `manifest_census_cljs_test` and `manifest_roster_coverage_cljs_test`
assert `(= ks (set (keys entry)))` - an EXACT key set, not a subset. So the
manifest change and the fixture row are one atomic edit, and that fixture was
fenced off increment 1 (another worker held the Freehand analyzer/emitter
serial lane that wave). Nothing about the change is hard; it is a lane
conflict, not a design question.

SCOPE:
  1. Widen `structural-manifest`'s `:events` projection to carry the per-site
     facts the analyzer already records.
  2. Update `fh-struct-010.edn`'s `:required-keys {:events ..}` row in the same
     commit (exact-key-set assertions, so the two move together).
  3. Apply the honesty rule the sibling `read-view-dependencies` already
     applies to `:query`: project the authored event vector VERBATIM only when
     it is fully literal, and otherwise carry the literal event-id with the
     dynamic arguments marked rather than shipping a lowered host expression
     to a reader as though it were the author's form.
     `re-frame.freehand.tool/literal-form?` is the predicate; do not write a
     second one.
  4. Retire or update the `:site-facts` key `read-view-event-sites` currently
     carries. It exists for one reason - to say "an absent `:handler` means
     unpublished, not absent" - so it must not outlive the gap it names.

HOT-ZONE / LANE: `spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-struct-010.edn` plus
`implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/compiler.cljc` - sequence this
behind any open worker on the Freehand analyzer/emitter lane.

title: Freehand tool tier live reads, source (3): the bounded explain-render over the Spec 009 ring
description:
Source (3) of rf2-lvvl2, split out because increment 1 (the manifest-backed
declaration reads) landed on its own. rf2-lvvl2 stays OPEN; this bead owns its
DONE WHEN criteria 4 and 5.

SCOPE: a BOUNDED `explain-render`. Enrich the selected-commit record only with
facts Freehand ALREADY HAS at commit - frame, committed reads/dependencies,
committed event sites, lowering, generation, and a trigger cause IF that cause
can be carried to commit without keeping history. Publish validated commit and
lifecycle facts into the EXISTING Spec 009 trace path. `explain-render` folds
the configured retained ring AT READ TIME and reports truncation or missing
basis through the schema's existing `:complete?` and `:loss` fields
(`re-frame.freehand.evidence/projection` refuses a projection that claims
completeness while reporting loss, so this is enforced at the door rather than
asked for). Background tools may fold those bounded records into UI summaries;
the substrate MUST NOT persist the summary.

IMPLEMENTATION HAZARD, worth the whole bead if missed: **Spec 009 DOES NOT
RETAIN FRAMELESS EVENTS.** So Freehand evidence must either join the applicable
frame/run correlation, or use an equally explicit RETAINED Freehand trace
operation under the SAME ring and the SAME retention knob
(`:rf.trace/events-retained`, applied via
`(rf/configure! {:trace-buffer {:events-retained N}})` - see
`re-frame.freehand.evidence/retention`). Merely calling a listener with an
uncorrelated record makes late explanations DISAPPEAR and does not satisfy the
contract. Pair attaches late; an explanation that only exists in the callback
that already fired is not an explanation.

NO SECOND RETENTION KNOB, and no Freehand history store. `evidence_boundary_
jvm_test.clj` proves both over interned vars and will govern this work: any
Freehand var whose name matches retain|retention|history|ring-buffer must be an
immutable value, and `re-frame.freehand.evidence` must hold nothing at all.

WHAT INCREMENT 1 ALREADY GIVES YOU: `re-frame.freehand.tool` is the read door
and is already OFF the render path, which is what lets it reach
`re-frame.freehand.evidence` without widening the one-seam roster that test
pins. `explain-render` belongs there beside `read-view-manifest` /
`read-view-dependencies` / `read-view-event-sites`.

DONE WHEN (rf2-lvvl2 criteria 4-5):
  4. A recent selected commit can be explained from the configured Spec 009
     window.
  5. Eviction and missing correlation are reported as LOSS, never silently
     presented as complete evidence.

SEQUENCING: spec/009-Instrumentation.md is HOT-ZONE (sequential, never
parallel) and a retained Freehand trace operation is a 009 change - hold this
until no other worker holds that file. Cross-host coverage (JVM + CLJS) in the
shape rf2-hytu5 and the increment-1 PR used. Pair's tool catalogue is a CLOSED
WORLD, so the consumer rewire (F6 ledger rows 392/393/394/395/397) stays a
separate slice and stays pending.

title: Freehand tool tier live reads, source (2): the minimal current-occurrence index and mounted-views
description:
Source (2) of rf2-lvvl2, split out because increment 1 (the manifest-backed
declaration reads: `re-frame.freehand.tool/read-view-manifest` /
`read-view-dependencies` / `read-view-event-sites`, plus the dev-only
declared-view index `re-frame.freehand.registry`) landed on its own and a
half-delivered live-state slice is the worst possible outcome. rf2-lvvl2 stays
OPEN and keeps its six DONE WHEN criteria; this bead owns criteria 1, 2 and 3.

THE ONE REQUIREMENT THAT JUSTIFIES ANY LIVE STATE AT ALL: Pair attaches LATE.
An MCP agent attaches to an ALREADY-RUNNING application, so Freehand's
fire-and-forget commit sink (`re-frame.freehand.cell/emit-commit-evidence!`,
cell.cljc:901) can never answer "what is mounted right now" - a sink installed
at attach time sees only commits that happen AFTER it. `read-mounted-views` is
a shipped tool in `skills/re-frame2-pair`. Nothing else in rf2-lvvl2 needs
retained state.

SCOPE: a MINIMAL LIVE INDEX of current dev-mode occurrences and their latest
committed projection. Insert-or-update on the selected commit, remove on
disconnect. Freehand's explicit shell cleanup is the natural release seam. It
must distinguish two simultaneous occurrences of one view, stay correct across
a COMPATIBLE hot reload, and report unknown facts as UNKNOWN rather than
manufacture root or lifecycle fidelity. `mounted-views` is a read over this
index.

HARD FENCE, carried forward VERBATIM from the rf2-drpa3.167 ruling: this is
CURRENT STATE, NOT HISTORY.
  - No lifetime render/batch counts.
  - No accumulated target union.
  - No lifecycle interval ledger and no hide-versus-unmount proof labels.
  - No weak-keyed store and no HMR store migration.
  - No cell-to-root attribution.
  - No second retention knob.
If this starts to look like the donor's 1,049-line per-occurrence evidence
accumulator, STOP - that is the gold-plating signal and .167 already ruled
against it.

SEAM ALREADY PREPARED: `re-frame.freehand.cell/set-evidence-sink!` is the
installation point, and its docstring (reconciled by the increment-1 PR) now
names THIS bead as what installs there - a minimal current-occurrence index,
never the donor per-cell accumulator.

WHAT INCREMENT 1 ALREADY GIVES YOU:
  - `re-frame.freehand.registry` - the dev-only view-id to declaration index,
    gated in the `v/defview` expansion so it DCEs in production. Keyed by
    DECLARATION, one row per view id; the occurrence index is a SEPARATE
    structure keyed by runtime occurrence (`re-frame.freehand.evidence/
    occurrence?` - `{:parent .. :key ..}`), and the two must not be merged.
  - `re-frame.freehand.tool` - the read door, already off the render path
    (nothing reachable from `re-frame.freehand` requires it), which is what
    lets it reach `re-frame.freehand.evidence`. `mounted-views` belongs here.
  - `re-frame.freehand.evidence/commit-projection` + `commit-record` - the
    validated per-commit record the sink already receives.

BOUNDARY TESTS THAT WILL GOVERN THIS WORK (read them before writing code):
  - `evidence_boundary_jvm_test.clj` - `re-frame.freehand.evidence` may be
    mentioned by exactly the roster the test names, and only `cell` may be
    REACHABLE from the public door. A live index in a new namespace that the
    render path requires would need that roster widened DELIBERATELY, with the
    reason stated; do not widen it silently.
  - the same file's `no-freehand-namespace-publishes-a-second-retention-store`
    - any Freehand var whose NAME matches retain|retention|history|ring-buffer
    must be an immutable value.
  - `npm run test:freehand-evidence-elision` - the control-build probe. A live
    index is exactly the kind of state that must not ship: add a dev-only
    sentinel for it to
    `implementation/scripts/check-freehand-evidence-elision.cjs` (increment 1
    added no new string literal to root one on, so this is the first slice
    that can).

DONE WHEN (rf2-lvvl2 criteria 1-3):
  1. Two live occurrences of one view are distinguishable.
  2. A late-attaching Pair session sees occurrences that were already
     connected before it attached.
  3. Disconnect removes an occurrence and releases its current projection.

Cross-host coverage (JVM + CLJS) in the shape rf2-hytu5 and the increment-1 PR
used. Pair's tool catalogue is a CLOSED WORLD - any change to the five view
tools is also `descriptors_data.cljs`, `registry.cljs`,
`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md` and the mcp-conformance
gate - so the consumer rewire (F6 ledger rows 392/393/394/395/397) stays a
separate slice and stays pending.

title: Freehand: two conformance fixture rows pin a structural-tier event diagnostic that diverges from the mounted tier
description:
Split out of rf2-5xjxj. That bead fixed the ACCEPTANCE divergence (the
structural render recorded a non-roster map at an event position
verbatim). What remains is a DIAGNOSTIC-ID divergence for values both
tiers already refuse, and it is pinned by two conformance fixture rows
that rf2-5xjxj's worker was fenced from touching (an F6a false-green
worker was live on spec/conformance/freehand/** at the time).

THE IDEAL SHAPE, and why it is not what landed. node/classify-event
should delegate wholesale to events/event-plan:

  (case (:role (events/event-plan v))
    nil            nil
    :event-vector  (reject-non-data! tag k v "event intent")
    :event-options (reject-non-data! tag k v "options map")
    {:rf.ui/opaque :fn})

That is strictly LESS code than the cond it replaces, and it makes one
authored mistake get one verdict on every tier. It was written, run, and
backed out because exactly two fixture rows go red under it:

1. spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-struct-003.edn:92
     {:form [:div {:on-click "go"}] :error-id :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed}
   A STRING at an event position. fh-event-002.edn:44 says the same
   authored mistake is :rf.error/view-bad-event, and FH-EVENT-002's modes
   are `common jvm browser`. So the two active rows describe one input
   two ways. Both tiers REFUSE it — only the id differs — which is why
   this is a diagnostic bug rather than the acceptance bug rf2-5xjxj was.
   Same for :number, :keyword and :set.

2. spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-struct-002.edn:73
     {:form [:form {:on-submit {:event [:cart/checkout] :after :fh/fn}}]
      :error-id :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed}
   The row's stated intent is the DATA law ("an options map is recorded
   verbatim, so it too is data all the way down"), but the map it uses to
   demonstrate that law ALSO carries an off-roster key (:after), so it
   fails two laws at once and the row silently pins which one wins. The
   row is under-determined rather than wrong. Remedy: make it
   roster-clean, e.g. {:event [:cart/checkout] :once :fh/fn} — then only
   the data law can fire and the ordering stops mattering.

WHAT LANDED INSTEAD (PR for rf2-5xjxj): the map arm alone consults
events/event-plan, and reject-non-data! runs BEFORE that consult so
fixture row 2 keeps its current verdict. That ordering is defensible on
its own terms (a value that could never be recorded under ANY spelling
is not fixed by renaming the key it rode in on) but it is NOT what the
compiled tier does — analyze.cljc reports the roster first
(:rf.ui.compile/bad-handler-options) and has no data check at all. Once
row 2 is roster-clean, roster-first becomes available and the three
tiers can agree on ORDER as well as on verdict.

DO: fix the two fixture rows, then collapse classify-event to the `case`
above and drop the now-dead fn-carried? helper and the :else malformed!
arm. Verify with `cd implementation/freehand && clojure -M:test` and
`cd implementation && npm run test:freehand` (the structural walk is
.cljc, so both lanes exercise it).

SEPARATELY OBSERVED, same seam, not yet filed anywhere: analyze.cljc
refuses `:passive true` with `:prevent-default true` as
:rf.ui.compile/contradictory-handler-options, but events/options-plan
accepts that combination at render. So the compiled tier refuses a
declaration the interpreted and structural tiers accept — the mirror
image of rf2-5xjxj, and arguably the same class. Worth deciding whether
options-plan should carry the contradiction check too.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #6931 (2026-07-25): scope this exact owner to the remaining same-seam ACCEPTANCE divergence already observed in its description. Reproduced on current main: events/event-plan accepts {:event [:probe/run] :passive true :prevent-default true} and returns both mechanics in its plan (exit 0); node/classify-event now delegates maps to that plan, so the structural tier accepts it too; compiler/analyze rejects the identical authored map as :rf.ui.compile/contradictory-handler-options, explicitly saying the combination is contradictory in any stage. This is material tier drift, not diagnostic polish: a structural/JVM test and mounted development accept code that a compiled build refuses. Keep the repair small and inside this bead: teach the canonical events/options-plan the same passive-plus-prevent-default contradiction, so the PR #6931 delegation gives mounted and structural tiers one runtime verdict without another classifier; add one cross-tier regression row while performing the already-scoped fixture cleanup/case collapse. No new validation framework or option matrix. Audit evidence: authored/applied aggregate patch-id 9a6fb5f168e8a5f800c0a118e2ce8affc318e10b; diff-check clean; events namespace 33 tests/214 assertions and analyzer-reject namespace 35/286 green.

title: Freehand: the JVM structural render passes a non-roster map at an event position through unclassified
description:
Split out of rf2-rczed (its notes raise it; that bead was docs-only and implementation/freehand/** was fenced to live workers).

The two hosts disagree about a MAP at an event position.

BROWSER / mount: re-frame.freehand.events/event-plan classifies it against the closed roster #{:event :prevent-default :stop-propagation :once :passive :capture} and raises :rf.error/view-bad-event for anything else.
COMPILED build: analyze.cljc raises :rf.ui.compile/bad-handler-options for the same map.
JVM structural render: passes it straight through, unclassified.

Reproduced on the real classpath (rf2-rczed evidence run):

  (v/defview menu-bad [_]
    [:ul {:on-key-down {"Enter" [:menu/activate] "Escape" [:menu/close]}} [:li "Open"]])

  (t/attrs (t/find (t/render [menu-bad {}]) #(= :ul (:tag %))))
  ;; => {:on-key-down {"Enter" [:menu/activate], "Escape" [:menu/close]}}

So t/render does not catch this class at all. This is exactly how the deleted D007 exact-key map could sit in the guide and in a consumer's codebase behind a green .cljc structural suite: the interpreted browser tier and the compiled tier both reject it, and the tier a consumer actually tests on accepts it silently.

testing.md promises 'the same declaration answers the same tree on the JVM and in ClojureScript, so a .cljc structural test is a cross-host claim'. For event positions that promise does not hold today.

DO: run the site plan (events/event-plan) on the JVM structural render path too, so a non-roster map is rejected identically in all three tiers. FH-EVENT-002 already says 'rejected in both tiers' and lists 'common jvm browser' as its modes, so the conformance row arguably already binds this - check whether the row's JVM arm actually exercises a bad map, and add the tooth if not.

Distinct from rf2-erqin, which is the presence-phase host divergence.
close_reason:
Fixed on PR #6931 (worker/jvm-eventmap-5xjxj).

node/classify-event's map arm now CONSULTS re-frame.freehand.events/event-plan
instead of recording whatever it was handed. event-plan already owned the closed
event grammar and was total over it; the structural path simply never asked. The
plan is discarded deliberately — this seam takes the VERDICT, never the
normalization, because the plan drops a listener option authored false while the
structural tree records the authored map exactly as written (FH-STRUCT-002).

Before/after on the real classpath, the bead's own transcript:
  BEFORE  t/render => ACCEPTED {:on-key-down {"Enter" [...], "Escape" [...]}}
  AFTER   t/render => REFUSED  :rf.error/view-bad-event
                               :recovery :use-the-closed-listener-options
                               :unknown-keys ["Enter" "Escape"]

Cross-host verdict now IDENTICAL to the mounted tier — same error id, same
recovery, same :unknown-keys — and that agreement is asserted as an EQUALITY
between the two tiers rather than as two independent expectations, so a later
change moving one diagnostic without the other reds.

The bead's DO asked whether FH-EVENT-002's JVM arm actually exercises a bad map:
it does NOT. The row drove events/event-plan and events/site directly, never
tree/render. Added the tooth — three new .cljc rows in the FH-EVENT-002 suite
(structural verdict, structural-vs-mounted equality, non-vacuity control). No
conformance-index change needed: the row's stated law and its 'common jvm
browser' modes already bind this.

Gates all green, foreground: freehand JVM 1005/6982 exit 0; freehand node
1072/6019 exit 0; test:cljs 11228/56339 exit 0; browser 762/4771 exit 0;
test-fast-pr.sh PASS exit 0. Non-vacuous on BOTH hosts: reverting the one-line
consult reds exactly the 6 new assertions in the JVM lane and the same 6 in the
node lane.

RESIDUAL, filed as rf2-uvcm3: the :else arm (string/number/keyword/set at an
event position) still raises :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed structurally vs
:rf.error/view-bad-event mounted. Both tiers REFUSE it, so that is a

Collapsing it needs two conformance fixture rows edited (fh-struct-002.edn:73,

title: spec/API.md reserved route-metadata line: drop retired :query-retain and :on-error
description:

  - `:on-error` — retired by R1, so API.md has been stale on this since R1 landed.

Nothing else moves: no facade row changes, and `spec/api-manifest.edn` carries no query-retain/on-error row (verified by grep during R5), so this is NOT an api-manifest regeneration — it is a one-line prose correction. The api_md_check gate only validates var-rows against the manifest, so this line reds no gate today; it is a correctness/coherence fix that R6 (integrated proof, guide coherence) will want green.

Canonical current vocabulary after R5: `:doc`, `:params`, `:query`, `:query-defaults`, `:tags`, `:parent`, `:on-match`, `:can-leave`, `:can-enter`, `:scroll`, `:sensitive`, `:large` (+ cross-feature `:head`, `:resources`). notes:

The two retired keys are gone, but spec/API.md still calls its 12-item enumeration “reg-route metadata reserved keys” while omitting the framework's cross-feature reserved keys. description:
Two loose ends after rf2-zt65l / rf2-txm8g, both cheap, both easy to lose.

1. RE-INSTALL AFTER #6921 MERGES. The mayor ran the installer BEFORE PR #6921 landed, so the install predates the new post-merge staleness block. Measured from a linked worktree at 2026-07-25 with the PR's registry:

     install-git-hooks: C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/.git/hooks/post-merge block missing
     exit 1
     grep -c 'BEGIN re-frame2 worker beads boundary (rf2-ia8o7)' .git/hooks/pre-commit  -> 1   (repaired, good)
     grep -c 'BEGIN re-frame2 hook-install staleness check (rf2-zt65l)' .git/hooks/post-merge -> 0

   So the boundary guard IS armed, but the arm that NOTICES future drift is not - and it cannot notice its own absence. One more run closes it:

     git pull --ff-only && sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh && sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh --check   # expect exit 0

   After that the loop is self-reporting: every subsequent pull that lands a change under scripts/git-hooks/ without an install prints the repair command.

2. VERIFY PER-WORKTREE ARMING WHEN WORKTREES ARE IDLE. Deferred by the mayor on rf2-txm8g: the installer arms one shared hooks directory, and 'git rev-parse --git-path hooks' from a linked worktree returns the mayor's .git/hooks, so inheritance is structural rather than per-worktree. PR #6921 layer 6 case (6d) asserts that property in a sandbox, and case (6e) proves the guard bites through an inherited install. An independent live check needs a probe commit inside a worker branch, so do it when no worker is in flight.

   Non-destructive probe (no commit, real hook, scratch index):
     IDX=$PWD/.git-scratch.index; git read-tree HEAD  # with GIT_INDEX_FILE=$IDX
     printf 'x\n' >> .beads/issues.jsonl
     GIT_INDEX_FILE=$IDX git add .beads/issues.jsonl
     GIT_INDEX_FILE=$IDX sh "$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks)/pre-commit"   # expect exit 1
     rm -f $IDX; git checkout HEAD -- .beads/issues.jsonl

ACCEPTANCE: --check exits 0 on the mayor checkout with the post-#6921 registry, and one worker worktree is observed refusing a staged .beads/issues.jsonl through the INSTALLED hook.
close_reason:
Post-merge reinstall DONE by the mayor 2026-07-25, immediately after PR #6921 merged (merge commit 4f047b8924). Ran 'sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh' from the mayor checkout: appended the new rf2-zt65l block to .git/hooks/post-merge; pre-commit and mayor-marker already up to date; exit 0. Then 'sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh --check' -> EXIT 0, so the checkout is now fully guarded on both blocks. The chicken-and-egg the worker named (the arm that notices drift could not notice its own absence) is closed.

MAYOR RULING on the open question that PR left: DO NOT wire 'install-git-hooks.sh --check' into scripts/test-fast-pr.sh. The worker correctly declined to make that call unilaterally and flagged the reason — CI legitimately runs without hooks installed, so the check would false-red on every CI run of the spine. A gate that is red for a correct reason trains people to ignore it, and this repo already relies on the spine being meaningfully green. The post-merge advisory is the right arm: it fires exactly where a stale hook matters (a developer checkout that just pulled new hook sources), is silent on a healthy checkout, and costs nothing at commit time. The CI arm remains scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh, which is where a boundary violation actually needs catching regardless of anyone's local setup.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER REPORT, recorded so it is not repeated: I told Mike '.git/hooks/pre-commit does not exist at all'. That was WRONG. The file existed (1914 bytes, dated 2026-06-01) carrying the rf2-ydl2p mayor-boundary block; what was missing was the rf2-ia8o7 beads-boundary block. My diagnostic was 'grep -c beads .git/hooks/pre-commit || echo NO HOOK' — grep exits 1 when the count is ZERO, not only when the file is absent, so the || fired on a present-but-unmatching file. Same shell-semantics class as the earlier && / || precedence bug that truncated issues.jsonl. Use 'test -f' for existence and grep only for content, never conflate the two.

STILL OPEN, deliberately: live per-worktree verification. The installer arms all worktrees through the shared hooks directory (measured: core.hooksPath unset; from a linked worktree 'git rev-parse --git-path hooks' resolves to the primary checkout's .git/hooks), so inheritance is established structurally. What is NOT verified is a refusal actually firing inside a worker worktree, because proving it means writing a probe commit into someone else's in-flight branch. Do that at the next hygiene pass when worktrees are idle, using the non-destructive scratch GIT_INDEX_FILE probe this PR demonstrates.

title: Operator: run scripts/install-git-hooks.sh on the mayor checkout (arms mayor + all live worktrees)
description:

PR #6921 fixed the MECHANISM (post-merge staleness advisory, installer registry parity, installer end-to-end test layer) but deliberately did NOT run the installer: writing to <common-dir>/hooks from a worker worktree reaches into the mayor checkout and re-arms five live worker worktrees mid-flight.

MEASURED STATE (2026-07-25, from a linked worktree, read-only --check):
  install-git-hooks: C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/.git/hooks/pre-commit block missing
  install-git-hooks: mayor-marker content drifted at C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/.git/mayor-marker
  exit 1

ACTION, after #6921 merges and 'git pull --ff-only', from the mayor checkout:
  sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh          # idempotent, ~1s
  sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh --check  # expect exit 0

One run guards the mayor checkout AND every linked worktree - they share one hooks directory (core.hooksPath unset; 'git rev-parse --git-path hooks' from a worktree returns the mayor's .git/hooks). Nothing per worktree, then or ever.

ACCEPTANCE: 'sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh --check' exits 0 on the mayor checkout, and .git/hooks/pre-commit contains the rf2-ia8o7 marker block.
close_reason: DONE by the mayor 2026-07-25. Ran 'sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh' from the mayor checkout C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2, exit 0. Output: post-merge up to date; pre-commit up to date; APPENDED BLOCK to .git/hooks/pre-commit; refreshed mayor-marker at .git/mayor-marker. Verified after: grep -c beads .git/hooks/pre-commit returns 7. WHY THIS MATTERED: before this, .git/hooks/pre-commit DID NOT EXIST on the mayor checkout at all — not merely outdated. CLAUDE.md states the .beads database boundary is enforced by a pre-commit hook in linked worktrees, and that enforcement had been absent for this entire session; the boundary held on worker discipline alone (every dispatch brief carries the rule and no worker violated it), but the belt-and-braces the method describes was simply not installed. A single 'git add -A' in a worktree would have time-travelled the tracker, which is the failure PR #6677 already caused once (135 insertions / 136 deletions of pure collateral). BEHAVIOUR CONFIRMED, and worth recording because it looks like a failure and is not: a probe commit staging .beads/issues.jsonl from the MAYOR checkout SUCCEEDED. That is correct — the mayor is explicitly permitted to commit the tracker database ('the tracker database is the mayor's to commit'), and the installer refreshes .git/mayor-marker precisely so the hook can tell the two cases apart. The refusal path is for WORKER worktrees, which is where the boundary actually needs enforcing. The probe commit was reset --soft and removed; nothing junk was pushed. NOT YET VERIFIED: whether the five live worker worktrees each picked up the guard — the installer reports arming the mayor plus live worktrees, but I did not independently confirm the refusal fires inside a worker worktree, because doing so means writing a probe commit into someone else's in-flight branch. rf2-zt65l's PR carries the mechanism and its own bite-proof; re-verify per-worktree arming at the next hygiene pass, when worktrees are idle.

title: Freehand guide: accessibility.md claims exact-key maps on :on-key-down are a supported closed data form
description:
docs/core/freehand/accessibility.md (Keyboard section) says:

  'Exact-key maps on :on-key-down / :on-key-up are a **closed data form** for common chords (see [Events](events-and-handlers.md)).'

That is false, and events-and-handlers.md says the opposite two pages earlier: 'There is no key-condition map. A handler slot holds ONE handler form.'

The implementation is decisive. re-frame.freehand.events/event-plan classifies a MAP at an event position as the OPTIONS map and nothing else, against the closed roster #{:event :prevent-default :stop-propagation :once :passive :capture}. So {"Enter" [...] "Escape" [...]} raises :rf.error/view-bad-event at browser mount time (re-frame.freehand.events/site calls event-plan). Note the JVM structural render passes the map through unclassified, so t/render does NOT catch it — a consumer would ship this and find out in the browser.

rf2-qwsmv already corrected the two SAMPLES that taught the unsupported spelling (semantic-controllers.md blocks 1 and 14, replaced with the v/event branch events-and-handlers.md teaches). The accessibility.md PROSE bullet was left alone because that worker's write surface was sample corrections only.

DO: reword the accessibility.md bullet to name the two supported spellings (a key projection [:ev ::v/key] into a branching handler, or v/event at the site) and drop the 'closed data form' claim.

Separately worth considering: should the JVM structural render refuse a non-roster map at an event position, so t/render catches this class at all? Today the two hosts disagree.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #6926 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6926), green 19/19.

The accessibility.md Keyboard bullet no longer claims exact-key maps are a closed data form. It now teaches the two spellings the substrate has, in the words spec/004-Views.md uses: 'Keyboard branching is an ordinary event' - send the key with the intent ([:menu/key-pressed ::v/key]) and decide in the handler, or write (v/event [e] ...) at the site when preventDefault depends on which key it was. Links to events-and-handlers.md#keyboard-branching. The a11y point the bullet was really making - a real listbox/combobox wants a host widget, not a handful of key branches - is kept.

A SECOND instance was found and fixed in the same PR: compilation.md:43 listed 'key maps' among the finite manifests compilation buys. The manifest rosters are :subscriptions/:events/:slots/:html-sites/:frame-ops (re-frame.freehand.descriptor/manifest); confirmed empirically by printing the compiled manifest.

The two semantic-controllers.md SAMPLES (blocks 1 and 14) were left alone as this bead's description directs - they are already corrected on origin/worker/guide-samples-qwsmv, in flight, and duplicating them would have conflicted with a live worker.

Evidence, run against the real implementation/freehand classpath (exit 0):
- OLD form rejected interpreted: :rf.error/view-bad-event, :recovery :use-the-closed-listener-options, :unknown-keys ["Enter" "Escape"].
- OLD form rejected compiled: :rf.ui.compile/bad-handler-options, 'unknown handler options "Enter", "Escape" at :on-key-down'.
- NEW [:menu/key-pressed ::v/key]: event-plan -> :event-vector; survives t/render as data; materialize-event with {::v/key "ArrowDown"} -> [:menu/key-pressed "ArrowDown"]; compiled tier accepts, one :events manifest site, :capabilities #{:event}.
- NEW (v/event [e] ...): event-plan -> :event; survives t/render.

Gates: mkdocs build --strict PASS exit 0 (run EXPLICITLY - test-fast-pr.sh soft-skips it on this machine); check_doc_slugs.py, check_readme_links.py, check_readme_inventories.py, check_retired_spellings.py all PASS exit 0; test-fast-pr.sh PASS exit 0 incl. the docs corpus anchor validator.

The host divergence raised in this bead's last paragraph is REPRODUCED and split out as rf2-5xjxj (P2 bug): t/render of {"Enter" [...] "Escape" [...]} at :on-key-down returns the map unclassified in :attrs, so the structural tier catches this class not at all. Not fixed here - implementation/freehand/** was fenced to live workers.

title: Freehand: t/render of a presence-phase-reading view throws in CLJS but renders on the JVM
description:
docs/core/freehand/presence.md and accessibility.md teach a presence-aware child that reads (v/presence-phase) to stamp its own exit class / inert / aria-hidden. testing.md promises 'the same declaration answers the same tree on the JVM and in ClojureScript, so a .cljc structural test is a cross-host claim'.

Those two claims do not both hold. presence-phase is react/useContext on CLJS and an unconditional :present on the JVM. t/render opens no React render, so on CLJS a structural render of such a child throws TypeError 'Cannot read properties of null (reading useContext)' / 'Invalid hook call'; on the JVM the same call renders and yields :present.

Reproduced by rf2-qwsmv's guide fixtures: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/guide/host_cljs_test.cljc had to fence presence-phase-reads-present-outside-a-boundary and a-presence-boundary-inserts-no-wrapper-node to #?(:clj ...) with a comment naming this bead. Un-fence them when it is fixed.

Consumers hit this the moment they write the .cljc structural test testing.md tells them to write for the toast card presence.md tells them to write.

Options: give the CLJS presence-phase a no-React fallback of :present (matching the JVM arm and the documented 'outside a boundary it returns :present' rule), or state the asymmetry in testing.md and presence.md.
close_reason:
Fixed on PR #6927 (branch worker/presence-render-erqin).

REPRODUCED on both hosts first. CLJS (npm run test:freehand, exit 1): 'Invalid hook call' + 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading useContext)' from t/render of a view whose body reads (v/presence-phase). JVM, identical declaration, same commit: renders {:tag :div :attrs {:class "toast"} :children ["present"]}.

RULED THE JVM CORRECT. A structural render carries no lifecycle — its presence node already says {:phase :present :timeout-ms n} — so :present is the only phase it can truthfully report, it is what Spec 008's cross-host-claim promise depends on, and it is what v/render-static needs (a server render of a presence-aware child must produce markup). Refusal-on-both was considered and rejected: the answer exists, and refusing would make every presence-aware child structurally untestable and un-render-static-able.

THE FIX is NOT the bead's suggested blanket no-React fallback. presence-phase discriminated on the COMPILER; on the JVM that is the same question (only one renderer there) but in CLJS both renderers run in the same compiled code, so the reader conditional answered the wrong one. It now discriminates on the RENDERER: node/*structural-render?* (a walk-scoped dynamic binding beside *ns-context*) is bound true for the extent of tree/render and tree/render-root-tree on both hosts, and the CLJS arm consults it before reaching for the context. Outside ANY render it is still a hook outside a component and React still says so — deliberate.

PINNED in both lanes: two new tests in presence_parity_cljs_test.cljc (a .cljc suite that runs on the JVM via clojure -M:test and in CLJS via the node-test-freehand build) — the phase-reading child alone, and the same child under a real (v/presence ...) boundary. RED pre-fix on CLJS (2 errors, the quoted TypeError), green post-fix on both.

GATES all foreground, all exit 0: freehand JVM (954/6848), test:freehand (1023/5892), test:cljs (11179/56210), test:browser (762/4771 — the mounted useContext path stays correct), scripts/test-fast-pr.sh ('PASS fast PR spine').

No API shape change; spec/api-manifest.edn and spec/conformance/** untouched. Follow-ons filed: rf2-7z78v (un-fence rf2-qwsmv's two guide rows once both PRs land), rf2-per51 (t/find + contains? predicate: JVM throws, CLJS returns false — same class of divergence), rf2-nxykb (whether the structural phase read wants a governed conformance row).
