title: FH-STRUCT-010: the :slots roster's :analyzer rationale is false — v/slot IS published
description:
Confirmed while implementing rf2-085ai (PR #6919), which deliberately left it alone: it is a design call, not a mechanical fix.

`spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-struct-010.edn` marks the `:slots` row
`:surface :analyzer` on the stated grounds that 'slot, html and frame have no
published var behind them, so no census declaration can carry one'.

That is TRUE for `html` and `frame` and FALSE for `slot`:
  - `(defn slot …)` sits on the door at implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1093
  - it carries an api-manifest row: spec/api-manifest.edn:221
    {:namespace "re-frame.freehand" :var "slot" :tier :advanced :kind :fn …}
  - neither `html` nor `frame` has a var or an api-manifest row (verified)

The ROW is currently right for a DIFFERENT and more ordinary reason: no
declaration in `re-frame.freehand.manifest-views` uses a slot, so the roster is
in fact empty across the public census and
`manifest-roster-coverage-cljs-test/the-public-door-gap-is-asserted-rather-than-assumed`
passes. The rationale is stale, not the verdict.

The same false claim is repeated in prose in
`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/manifest_roster_coverage_cljs_test.cljc`
— its ns docstring ('Two surfaces, and the gap named rather than hidden') and the
`resolver` stub docstring, which manufactures `re-frame.freehand/slot` alongside
the genuinely-unpublished `html` and `frame`.

TWO WAYS TO RESOLVE, and picking one is the decision:
  a. Move `:slots` to `:surface :public`: add a slot-bearing declaration to the
     manifest-views census and prove the roster through `v/manifest` like
     `:subscriptions` was moved when its runtime landed. This is the move the
     split exists to force, and `v/sub` is the precedent. Knock-on: the census
     cardinalities in fh-struct-010.edn's `:views` table move, and the resolver
     stub drops `slot`.
  b. Keep `:analyzer` and correct the rationale in both files: the roster is
     empty because no census declaration uses a slot, not because the form is
     unpublished — which makes the `:analyzer` tier mean two different things
     and is the weaker answer.

(a) looks right, since the fixture's own header says the analyzer tier is 'NOT
reachable through the public door today' and slot IS reachable.
close_reason: Landed in PR #6943. Ruled option (b) by the dispatch brief: the :analyzer VERDICT is unchanged, the RATIONALE is corrected. v/slot IS published (door + api-manifest row); the :slots roster is empty because no re-frame.freehand.manifest-views census declaration uses a slot. Corrected in fh-struct-010.edn's header, in manifest-roster-coverage-cljs-test's ns + resolver-stub docstrings, and in manifest-views' own docstring. The executable tripwire is unchanged. NOTE: the bead's own closing paragraph leaned option (a) (move :slots to :public with a slot-bearing census declaration); if still wanted that is a separate slice — it moves the :views census cardinalities.

title: Retire the in_review custom bd status: invisible to every view, consumed by nothing, breaks fresh-clone bootstrap
description:
FILED 2026-07-25 10:55 AUSEST from the in_review cluster dossier (delegated ruling). As of this filing ZERO beads use the status - the eight that sat in it (rf2-142b, rf2-cgcv, rf2-kfpf, rf2-94b0, rf2-byyi9, rf2-d0n1e, rf2-m6tu, rf2-ro7e) were all closed 2026-07-25 as delivered or superseded, so retirement is now a pure config change.

WHY IT MUST GO:
1. INVISIBLE: in_review is a custom status whose workflow class is [unspecified] - not active, not wip, not frozen, not done - so every class-driven view skips it. bd list --status=open omitted the eight; even bd list --status=in_review printed Total: 8 issues (0 open, 0 in progress) with all eight on screen. Beads entered it and nothing ever came for them: no workflow, skill, script, gate, or CLAUDE.md line references in_review anywhere in tracked files (grep verified). A status no process consumes and no view surfaces is a trap, and eight beads (five provably delivered, hidden ~7 weeks) are the proof.
2. BREAKS THE RECOVERY FLOOR: bd bootstrap --yes from the tracked issues.jsonl fails with: invalid status: in_review (reproduced in a disposable repo during the dossier investigation; the failing row was rf2-kfpf). This is the second instance of the fresh-clone bootstrap trap that rf2-cchlf / PR #6894 (MERGED 2026-07-24) fixed for the unpinned issue-prefix: local-only config the export depends on, or here a status the importer rejects outright.

FIX: (1) confirm no bead has status=in_review; (2) remove the custom status from bd config (bd config unset status.custom or the current equivalent) and align tracked .beads/config.yaml so a fresh clone matches; (3) checkpoint/export through the normal mayor path; (4) ACCEPTANCE: a fresh bd bootstrap --yes from the exported JSONL succeeds. Fresh-bootstrap proof also serves rf2-4l67v acceptance - coordinate, do not duplicate.

RULE going forward (one line in .beads/README.md or CLAUDE.md): custom statuses must be bootstrap-safe, and no status is introduced without a producer, a consumer/sweep, and an exit transition. Until a review state has all three, review-gated beads sit in open with a label or comment, where bd ready keeps them visible. Pre-alpha default: every bead is either visible or closed.

OWNERSHIP: this is tracker configuration - mayor-checkout work, not a worker-worktree dispatch. The database-derived exports stay mayor-owned; .beads/config.yaml itself is human-authored and allow-listed, but the retirement touches the database, so run the whole change from the mayor checkout.
close_reason: Retired. PR #6928 (worker/apimd-bdstatus-19), commit d56a402ab7. FIX steps: (1) zero beads stranded - bd list --status=in_review and bd count --status=in_review both returned none BEFORE the change, so nothing needed moving. (2) Status retired on the tracker DB; bd statuses now reports 'No custom statuses configured' and bd update <id> --status in_review is REJECTED exit 1, so it can no longer be re-entered. (4) ACCEPTANCE MET: fresh-clone bd bootstrap --yes from the tracked export exits 0 (2390 issues). Before/after proved end-to-end in disposable dirs touching no real bead: a DB mirroring the old live config accepted a bead into in_review, exported it, and a fresh bootstrap of that export failed exit 1 with the bead's exact error 'validation failed for trap-jbq: invalid status: in_review'; after retirement the same entry attempt is rejected. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the FIX text: 'bd config unset status.custom' DOES NOT WORK - it reports success and bd config get then reads '(not set)', but bd statuses still lists the status and beads can STILL be moved into it (verified: update exit 0 after unset). Only 'bd config set status.custom ""' actually retires it. That footgun, plus the RULE (bootstrap-safe; no status without a producer, a consumer/sweep and an exit transition), is recorded in .beads/config.yaml - chosen over .beads/README.md/CLAUDE.md because it already documents the identical issue-prefix (rf2-cchlf) failure mode and is what a fresh clone reads. Step (3) checkpoint/export remains the mayor's: no DB-derived path (.beads/issues.jsonl, .beads/metadata.json) is in either commit; bd auto-staged the mayor checkout's export, left for the mayor heartbeat. Fresh-bootstrap proof also serves rf2-4l67v acceptance.

title: Local git-hooks install drift: installed pre-commit lacks the rf2-ia8o7 beads-boundary guard on the mayor box and every linked worktree
description:
FILED 2026-07-25 10:55 AUSEST from the in_review cluster dossier (delegated ruling).

EVIDENCE (measured on the mayor checkout): installed .git/hooks/pre-commit is 1914 bytes dated 2026-06-01 and contains ZERO rf2-ia8o7 marker blocks; the source scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit is 4956 bytes dated 2026-07-22 and carries both guard blocks (rf2-ydl2p mayor boundary + rf2-ia8o7 worker beads boundary). .git/hooks/post-merge is stale from the same 2026-06-01 vintage. Linked worktrees share the primary checkout hooks directory (verified via git rev-parse --git-path hooks), so ALL linked worker worktrees (16 at filing time) run the stale hook too - NONE is guarded locally. Nothing invokes scripts/install-git-hooks.sh automatically; grep finds only documentation and the hooks own header comments. The hooks went seven weeks out of date silently and would have stayed that way indefinitely.

RISK CONTEXT: the CI arm (beads-pr-boundary job in test.yml, unconditional, in all-required-passed) is LIVE and closes the PR vector, so this is a defence-in-depth gap, not an open wound. But the local arm is the only one that catches the mistake BEFORE it is committed and pushed.

FIX (two parts, both small):
1. Operator or mayor runs: sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh from the mayor checkout. Seconds; because worktrees share the hooks dir, one run re-arms every worktree at once.
2. Add a staleness check so drift gets noticed: scripts/install-git-hooks.ps1 already has a -Check switch - wire an equivalent assertion into an existing gate or the post-merge hook (warn when installed blocks lag scripts/git-hooks/), rather than building a new hook framework. Keep it an installation repair, not a drift programme.

title: re-frame.ui ships the namespace docstring into :advanced bundles, same defect as rf2-9y9uv
description:
`re-frame.ui` carries the same defect Freehand just removed (rf2-9y9uv).

MEASURED MECHANISM (from rf2-9y9uv, PR for rf2-9y9uv/rf2-qimh0): shadow-cljs
hangs the whole namespace DOCSTRING off the ns-name symbol
(`shadow.build.ns-form/parse` does `:name (vary-meta name merge meta)` with
`{:doc <docstring>}`), that symbol becomes `cljs.analyzer/*cljs-ns*`, and
macroexpansion binds `*ns*` to it. So `(ns-name *ns*)` inside a macro answers
a symbol dragging the consuming namespace's entire prose behind it — and a
QUOTED symbol carries its metadata into the bundle, because
`cljs.analyzer/analyze-wrap-meta` elides only reader and analyzer keys and
emits everything else beside the symbol as a real `cljs.core/with-meta` call.

On Freehand this shipped the ns docstring once per declared view: 9,136 bytes
of a 739,838-byte `:advanced` artefact (-1.23%), including the substrate's own
door docstring twice into every consumer bundle.

`re-frame.ui` has the same raw `(ns-name *ns*)` / `(-> menv :ns :name)`
spelling at:

  - implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler.cljc:588 -> quoted into emitted
    code at :577 (`~tag {:properties ~props} '~ns-sym` in the
    register-custom-element! call) — CONFIRMED emitting site
  - implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler.cljc:248, :470
  - implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/root.cljc:928
  - implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/test.cljc:676 (test surface)

DO: audit which of those reach emitted code and apply the same one-token
removal — `(symbol (str ...))`, the metadata-free ns symbol, which
`re-frame.core-reg-macros` already states as the caller contract for every
`reg-*` macro (rf2-xnym). Prefer removing the redundancy over adding a
stripping pass; do NOT build a docstring-elision framework; do NOT touch
per-view docstrings (they live in var metadata, which ClojureScript drops, and
do not ship).

EVIDENCE REQUIRED: a before/after byte count from a real `:advanced` build of a
re-frame.ui entry (`:ui-g13-prod` or similar), not just a shape test. Freehand's
law — `re-frame.freehand.ns-docstring-absence-jvm-test` — is the model for the
accompanying test: it builds a namespace the way shadow-cljs leaves one
(`(create-ns (with-meta 'fresh.ns {:doc sentinel}))`), expands the declaration
forms against it, and proves its own subject contaminated first so the absence
claim cannot pass vacuously.

Filed by the rf2-9y9uv worker: implementation/ui/** was outside that bead's
write surface.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS MOOT by mayor triage 2026-07-25 — the defect is real but it can no longer reach anyone.

THE DEFECT AS FILED is genuine: re-frame.ui carries the identical ns-docstring leak fixed for Freehand in rf2-9y9uv, with a confirmed emitting site at implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler.cljc:577 ('~ns-sym in the register-custom-element! call) plus three more raw (ns-name *ns*) sites. Mechanism identical: shadow-cljs's ns-form/parse attaches {:doc <ns docstring>} to the ns symbol, the macro quotes that symbol into emitted code, and cljs.analyzer/analyze-wrap-meta emits it as a real with-meta call that :advanced does not strip. For Freehand the measured cost was 9,136 bytes (1.23%) per consumer bundle.

WHY IT IS MOOT: day8/re-frame2-ui IS NON-PUBLISHABLE as of rf2-a32r7 / PR #6899. It has no :clein/build descriptor, no deploy leaf, no release-notes row, and it is absent from the publishable authority (implementation/scripts/publishable-runtimes.cjs returns 13 coordinates, ui not among them). A v* release tag cannot publish it. So no consumer can take a dependency on re-frame.ui, and therefore no consumer bundle can pay this cost. The only bundles affected are in-repo builds, where a 1.2% :advanced size difference buys nothing.

AND IT IS SHORTLY DELETED ANYWAY: Mike ruled 2026-07-25 that re-frame.ui is being removed and Freehand is the substrate; rf2-drpa3.57 (F6e) deletes the artefact and the public surface outright, and its runway is now clear (release contract, template :ui variant, dead build hook, guide replacement and donor ledger have all landed).

POSTURE: pre-alpha, do not over-engineer, close minutiae rather than actioning them. Optimising the bundle size of an artefact that cannot be published and is scheduled for deletion is work on a corpse. Reopening is cheap if F6e is ever abandoned and re-frame.ui becomes publishable again — the mechanism and the four sites are recorded above, so nothing is lost by closing.

NOT A JUDGEMENT ON THE FREEHAND FIX: rf2-9y9uv shipped and stands; that one reaches every consumer.

title: Durable executable-sample harness for the Freehand guide
description:
rf2-fby7o acceptance criterion 1 wants the guide's samples EXECUTED by a checked-in mechanism, not a one-shot. PR #6914 verified 57 samples by compiling two scratch .cljc fixture namespaces against implementation/freehand's classpath, but could not commit them: implementation/** was fenced to other workers that wave.

DO: land the fixtures under implementation/freehand/test/ (grouped by chapter), link each runnable guide block to its fixture, and add ONE cheap coverage check that rejects an unowned runnable block. Do NOT build a general markdown interpreter - that shape is already rejected on rf2-fby7o.

The scratch fixtures are reproducible from the guide; start from docs/core/freehand/.
notes: AUDIT REOPEN (PR #6923, 2026-07-25): reproduced a CI false green at the harness boundary. `bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh docs/core/freehand/mental-model.md` returns every output false, including `implementation_jvm=false` and `cljs_node_test=false`. The only home of `samples_coverage_jvm_test.clj` is the `jvm-freehand` job, whose condition is `implementation_jvm == true`; `all-required-passed` explicitly accepts skipped jobs. Therefore a docs-only edit/add/delete of a fenced guide block — the primary change class this PR says will red — skips the digest/roster suite and can merge green. The PR's own run was armed only because it also added implementation/freehand tests. Focused suite itself is healthy (4 tests, 14 assertions; 112/134 blocks). Minimal acceptance: classify `docs/core/freehand/*.md` to run the JVM Freehand suite and pin that routing in `_changed-surfaces.test.cjs`; no broader docs fan-out is needed.
close_reason: RE-CLOSE. Delivered in PR #6923, MERGED to main. Zero AUDIT-REOPEN notes — mayor checkout-race, not a reviewer finding. THE WORK: seven chapter fixture namespaces under implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/guide/ (first_view, composition, events, controllers, compilation, host, testing), all .cljc so every transcription compiles and runs on BOTH hosts, plus samples_coverage_jvm_test.clj. 2582 lines, 8 new files, one 19-line doc correction. COVERAGE RULE: every fenced block in docs/core/freehand/ carries a roster row naming either the fixture var that proves it or a reason from a CLOSED unexecutable set, and the row pins a digest of the block exact text. Adding a sample reds (no row), editing one reds (digest), deleting a fixture reds (each row symbol is requiring-resolved). The digest deliberately covers COMMENTS, because in these samples a trailing arrow line frequently IS the claim, so a rule stripping comments would ignore the assertions most likely to go stale; only CRLF and trailing whitespace are normalised. The check never parses or evaluates guide source — it splits on fences, hashes bytes, compares two sets; executing samples is the fixtures job, and that boundary is what keeps it from becoming a markdown interpreter. COVERAGE: 112 of 134 fenced blocks. The 22 uncovered are enumerated as a closed set: 5 non-Clojure, 5 prose-shape, 4 foreign-npm, 3 app-scaffold, 3 host-boot, 2 build-config. RED-PROOFS, four, all run for real and reverted: renaming v/spread-safe gives a compile failure at the composition fixture; renaming the CLJS mount re-export reds the browser-only-door-verbs assertion naming v/mount across install.md, ssr.md and build-a-view.md (that assertion exists because a missing CLJS var is only a WARNING at compile and undefined at run time); editing a block reds the coverage check naming page and block and printing the replacement row; appending a fence reds with "block 2 has no roster row". Plus the-check-has-teeth driving roster-drift against synthetic input for every mode including page add/remove. IT FOUND A LIVE GUIDE BUG WHILE BEING BUILT: semantic-controllers.md blocks 1 and 14 taught an exact-key map at :on-key-down, which event-plan classifies as the options map and nothing else, so that site raises view-bad-event at mount — while events-and-handlers.md said "There is no key-condition map" two pages earlier. Both replaced with the v/event branch that page teaches. GATES all exit 0: freehand JVM 991 tests/6931 assertions; test:freehand 1061/5974; test:cljs 11217/56291; test-fast-pr.sh PASS. Follow-ons filed and separately owned: rf2-rczed (accessibility.md prose, since fixed and merged), rf2-erqin (presence-phase host divergence, since fixed and merged), rf2-ynq9h (compilation.md render-fn caller).

title: F6a residue: no CI job binds the freehand lane RUNS to the conformance rows
description:
Split out of rf2-drpa3.53 (PR #6912). NOT a defect in the census - a boundary the census cannot cross from where it runs.

WHAT IS TRUE NOW. The execution census (scripts/check_freehand_conformance_index.py) proves the STATIC half soundly: every active row is reached by a real assertion (forms, not text; reader conditionals resolved per platform) in a lane serving every mode/host cell it claims. The DYNAMIC half - that those assertions PASS - comes from the lane exit codes (JVM freehand, node test:freehand/test:cljs, browser). Both halves were green locally on #6912: 924 / 1005 / 11159 / 759 tests, all exit 0.

THE GAP. No single CI job holds both halves. .github/workflows/freehand-conformance.yml runs Python only; the lanes live in test.yml behind surface filters. So a PR touching ONLY spec/conformance/freehand/** gets the census green with the lanes skipped - which is exactly the shape the #6907 merged-PR audit flagged ('freehand-conformance passed, while JVM freehand, CLJS node, and browser lanes were all skipped').

WHY NOT FIXED IN #6912. .github/** was fenced to a concurrent worker for that wave.

OPTIONS (needs a ruling, cheapest first):
1. Add spec/conformance/freehand/** to the surface classifier inputs that arm jvm-freehand + the cljs node/browser lanes. Smallest change; makes an index-only PR run the suites that prove it.
2. Leave as is and rely on the unfiltered pull_request trigger plus the fact that a row change almost always lands with a test change.

CORROBORATION WORTH KEEPING. The census's model of what each lane runs was validated against the runners: the scanner independently derives 924 deftest vars for the JVM lane and 1005 for the node freehand lane, and the runners reported exactly 'Ran 924' and 'Ran 1005'. The browser lane derives 635 against a reported 759 - CONSERVATIVE, because shadow.test also runs test namespaces merely REQUIRED by a -dom-cljs-test ns. Conservative is the safe direction (it can only cause a false red), but if anyone later tightens browser attribution, that is the reason for the gap.

RELATED: rf2-drpa3.180 (push path filter does not watch implementation/freehand/test/**).
notes:
2026-07-25 — PR #6917 open (branch worker/conf-lane-binding-49upn): https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6917

DIRECTION: option 1 from the OPTIONS list, taken as (a) at COMMIT granularity rather than one physical job. report-changed-surfaces.sh now arms implementation_jvm + cljs_node_test + cljs_browser for the whole ledger — the fixtures root (already, rf2-drpa3.66) AND spec/conformance/freehand/conformance-index.md. An index-only PR now runs jvm-freehand, cljs and cljs-browser, all three already required by all-required-passed, so both halves land on one commit.

DECLINED: running the lanes inside freehand-conformance.yml. That workflow is deliberately unfiltered (it is the always-present required status context), so a lane step there would put a JVM suite, a Node suite and a Chromium run on EVERY pull request to duplicate three jobs that already block the merge. No new job and no new classifier output were needed — unlike the two sibling gates, all three lanes already exist, are already surface-gated and are already in the aggregator. What was missing was one arm.

HONEST FLOOR ALSO LANDED: _binding_note in check_freehand_conformance_index.py prints, under both --verbose and --report, that execution is DERIVED rather than observed, and names the lanes the rows require with the jobs that run them. Conservative browser attribution (635 vs 759) deliberately NOT widened.

SCOPE GUARD, pinned both ways in _changed-surfaces.test.cjs and demonstrated to bite: the index arms the three lanes; donor-inventory.md (a different checker) and README.md (defines the scheme, excluded from the census's own citation scan) do not.

CI COST: ~zero on the common path — a row lands with its proof, and the proof already armed all three. Three lanes are added only on an index-only PR, the exact false-green shape.

Deliberately left OPEN: this bead is about what runs ON MAIN, so close it when #6917 merges, not on PR-open. Related rf2-drpa3.180 untouched.
close_reason: PR #6917 merged (2e509bf233): the exact conformance-index path now arms implementation_jvm, cljs_node_test, and cljs_browser; their jvm-freehand/cljs/cljs-browser jobs remain dependencies of all-required-passed. The negative scope guards keep donor-inventory.md and README.md from paying for unrelated lanes, and the checker now states honestly that its execution evidence is derived. Audit reran the changed-surface suite (229 passed on current main) and the 48-case census self-test successfully. This closes only the CI scheduling/binding residue; rf2-drpa3.53 remains open for the independently reproduced static-census assertion/mode false greens.

title: B5's published per-promotion byte delta is not reproducible: shadow-cljs build-cache state moves it 4,075 bytes (23% of the delta)
description:
POST-MERGE REVIEW of main 9cdc3652e6..d5794fded8. Measured, reproduced twice per posture, in worktree agent/post-merge-review (Windows, npm ci from package-lock).

## What was measured

`npm run build:freehand-matched` (implementation/package.json:50) = `shadow-cljs release freehand-release freehand-release-interpreted freehand-release-compiled`. One invocation, one JVM, three builds whose compiler-options are identical apart from the entry (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:853-902).

Posture A — all three build caches and out/ dirs removed first (what CI and a fresh checkout do):
  out/freehand-release-interpreted/main.js  729,319 bytes
  out/freehand-release-compiled/main.js     747,224 bytes
  interpreted -> compiled raw delta         +17,905

Posture B — identical source; only `out/freehand-release-compiled` and `.shadow-cljs/builds/freehand-release-compiled` removed, so the two siblings are cache hits (0 compiled) and only the compiled twin recompiles:
  out/freehand-release-interpreted/main.js  729,319 bytes  (byte-identical to A)
  out/freehand-release-compiled/main.js     743,149 bytes
  interpreted -> compiled raw delta         +13,830

Both postures reproduce EXACTLY on a second run. The mixed bundle (739,874) and the interpreted bundle (729,319) are byte-identical across every run; the variance lands entirely on whichever build recompiles in a process where its siblings did not. The bundles are semantically identical — a function-keyword census over the two variants of the reachability control (the same effect, larger there) gives 4,279 functions in both at 748,141 vs 739,072 chars, so this is Closure identifier/property renaming shifting, not content.

## Why it is a defect

The delta is PUBLISHED EVIDENCE, not a local curiosity. `promotion-delta-workload` emits :B5/promotion-delta-raw-bytes plus gzip6/gzip9/brotli and a per-view mean through the provenance door (implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/bench/b5.cljs:319-348), and the record carries a `not-matched-on` fixture (b5.cljs:262-272) whose whole purpose is to name every confound so a reader can discount it. It names exactly one:

  "Measured at 7ce0788d7e this accounted for +297 raw bytes of an 18,475-byte raw delta (1.6%)"  (b5.cljs:271-272; repeated in the promotion-delta docstring at b5.cljs:241-243 and in the suite docstring at implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b5_matched_builds_cljs_test.cljs:18-20)

The unnamed confound measured here is +/-4,075 bytes — 22.8% of the same 17,905-byte delta, or 14x the confound the fixture does name. `matched-on` (b5.cljs:256-260) asserts the twins hold ":advanced optimisation" still; they do as a SETTING, but not as an OUTCOME. So the published figure — and the per-promoted-view mean derived from it, which is the number a reader would actually cite — depends on a state nothing in the record captures, and two honest runs on the same revision publish different evidence under the same `:revision` provenance.

## Fix sketch

Cheapest honest fix: make the measured artefacts cache-independent, then say so. Either
  (a) have the matched-build entry point clear `.shadow-cljs/builds/freehand-release{,-interpreted,-compiled}` and the three out/ dirs before compiling, so the published figure is always the from-clean one; or
  (b) if that is too slow for a local run, add the build posture to the provenance record (`b5/release-build` / the fixture) and widen `not-matched-on` to state the measured magnitude, so a delta is never cited without it.

(a) is preferable: the figure is only citable if it is the same figure twice.

Related, not duplicates: rf2-x4jda (builds the lane; owns the one-shared-entry-shape work that removes the +297 confound) and rf2-rhg4q (:mixed not byte-matched to the pair). Neither addresses reproducibility.

Secondary datum, same mechanism, NOT a gate defect: the comment at .github/workflows/test.yml:2582 records the reachability control pair as "744,100 vs 752,791 chars — 8,691 chars of controller runtime". From clean that reproduces (748,141 control vs 739,455 production, +8,686). With the evidence-elision gate run first in the same tree it inverts: control 739,072 vs production 739,455, i.e. -383. The reachability GATE is unaffected — its claim is present/absent and it passed 2/2 in both postures — but the byte figure in that comment only holds from clean.
notes:
CI POSTURE (checked after filing, softens the urgency but not the defect): .github/workflows/freehand-bench.yml's react-evidence job caches only ~/.m2 and ~/.gitlibs (lines 192-199) — never .shadow-cljs/builds — and builds all three shapes in ONE invocation on a fresh checkout (line 231). That is posture A, so the figure PUBLISHED BY CI is stable run to run and matches the 18,475 in the record. What is not stable is the same measurement taken anywhere else: scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh:46-47 runs the evidence-elision pair before the reachability pair in one tree, and any incremental local rebuild of one twin lands in posture B. So the defect is that the record's reproducibility is a property of the CI job's cache configuration that nothing in the record, the fixture, or the docstring states — a developer who re-measures and gets +13,830 has no way to tell drift from posture.
PUBLISHED RECORD CAPTURED (RF2_REVISION=d5794fded8, posture A / all-clean, npm run test:freehand with the three bundles on disk). The delta row certifies itself :status :evidence and prints as 'citable':

  :B5/promotion-delta-raw-bytes                 17905
  :B5/promotion-delta-gzip6-bytes                4795
  :B5/promotion-delta-brotli-bytes               3776
  :B5/promotion-delta-raw-bytes-mean-per-view    5968.3333   (17905 / :promoted-views 3)
  :interpreted-sha256 0505251a6fd0effd68df423ffa3527ecc632c7bf9ab1571a8d74cd9b2fafebc7
  :compiled-sha256    89e14a29bed9ee819f53c14cd9b5d56aab1f5233f5f0589934b2090478034e42

Under posture B the compiled twin is 743,149 bytes instead of 747,224, so the SAME revision publishes raw-bytes 13,830 and mean-per-view 4,610 — with a different :compiled-sha256, and still 'citable'. The sha ties a number to bytes, which is right; what nothing ties is the bytes to the source, so two honest runs at one revision certify two different answers.

Second, smaller, inside the SAME record: the static :not-matched-on fixture (b5.cljs:262-272) quotes '+297 raw bytes of an 18,475-byte raw delta (1.6%)' while the record it rides on reports 17,905. A reader comparing the caveat's denominator with the measurement beside it finds them 570 apart. Either recompute the confound alongside the delta, or state the revision the 18,475 belongs to as a past reading rather than as this record's denominator.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #6915 (branch worker/b5-reproducible-hce4p), direction (a): posture pinned at the producer, and named in the record.

REPRODUCED FIRST, at c8f0ae6ddb in a dedicated worktree, one npm run build:freehand-matched per posture:
  posture A (all three caches + out/ cleared)  interpreted 724,754  compiled 742,512  delta +17,758
  posture B (only the compiled twin's cache/out cleared; siblings are cache hits)  interpreted 724,754 (byte-identical)  compiled 738,437  delta +13,683
Swing 4,075 raw bytes, 23% of the delta, exactly as filed. Function census 4,312 in BOTH compiled variants - Closure renaming, not content.

MECHANISM PINNED, and it is not 'all three recompile': shadow-cljs release of the pair alone from clean gives compiled 742,512, and of the compiled twin ALONE from clean also gives 742,512. A build compiling fresh is deterministic regardless of how many siblings preceded it; what moves it is a sibling served from the CACHE in the same process. :advanced was held still as a setting and not as an outcome.

FIX (a), no Closure internals pinned, no build-reproducibility framework:
  - implementation/package.json: new clean:freehand-matched (node -e fs.rmSync over the three shapes' out/ and .shadow-cljs/builds/; no new dependency, verified under cmd.exe and POSIX sh), and build:freehand-matched runs it first.
  - .github/workflows/freehand-bench.yml: the matched-build step goes through npm run build:freehand-matched instead of a bare npx shadow-cljs release. CI's stability stops being an unstated property of that job's cache config and becomes a property of the entry point.
  - implementation/shadow-cljs.edn: the matched pair's comment names the script and the reason.
  - b5/matched-build-posture: new def stating the posture and what deviating costs (742,512 vs 738,437, 4,312 functions both, 4,075 bytes apart), riding the delta fixture as :build-posture; matched-on gains the posture clause; b5-matched-builds-cljs-test asserts the fixture carries it and that it names the entry point, the cache cleared, and the measured cost.

AFTER, three starting states through the one script: cleared / posture-B setup / every cache warm -> interpreted 724,754, compiled 742,512, delta +17,758, compiled sha256 03f291d6... in all three. One answer. Published record: raw-bytes 17,758, mean-per-view 5,919.3333, citable, :status :evidence, fixture carries :build-posture.

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY RESOLVED: the 17,905 denominator quoted in b5.cljs (the +252 confound) and in b5_matched_builds_cljs_test.cljs (the +339 confound) is now attributed as a past reading 'read at d5794fded8', so no stale figure stands as this record's denominator beside a live measurement.

GATES all green, foreground: build:freehand-matched x3 (0/0/0); test:freehand WITH RF2_REVISION 1017 tests/5889 assertions 0 failures 0 errors; test:freehand WITHOUT it 1017/5879 0/0; implementation/freehand clojure -M:test 943/6805 0/0; test:freehand-reachability PASS 2/2; test:freehand-evidence-elision PASS 2/2; YAML parse of freehand-bench.yml OK; JSON parse of package.json OK; clean:freehand-matched under cmd.exe removed exactly the three matched shapes.

Follow-on filed: rf2-bl1gp (P3) - the same mechanism moves the byte figure in .github/workflows/test.yml:2582's reachability comment; that file was fenced to another worker this wave. Not a gate defect (the reachability gate asserts present/absent and passed 2/2 here).

title: FH-STRUCT-010: give the manifest :diagnostics roster its own conformance row
description:
Follow-on from rf2-hytu5, which published `:diagnostics` on
`compiler/structural-manifest` (the compile-tier a11y findings, INCLUDING
suppressed ones with their reason — previously collected in the compiler env
and reachable by no reader).

`spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-struct-010.edn` governs the manifest's
rosters through `:roster-coverage` + `:required-keys`, and
`re-frame.freehand.manifest-census-cljs-test/every-roster-entry-is-source-locatable`
asserts the fixture names every roster the manifest carries. `:diagnostics` is
currently EXCLUDED from that assertion, because its entries are compile-tier
FINDINGS rather than lexical SITES: a finding names the `:tag` and `:path` of
the node it was minted from and carries no `:source-coord`, so the fixture's
per-entry total-coordinate law cannot govern it as written. The exclusion is
stated explicitly at the site rather than lumped in with the non-roster keys,
and `re-frame.freehand.tool-reader-jvm-test` pins the roster's shape,
non-emptiness and suppressed-finding round trip meanwhile.

rf2-hytu5 did not edit the fixture because the F6a conformance lane
(rf2-drpa3.53) held it.

SCOPE — two decisions, then one PR:
  1. Should a `:diagnostics` entry carry a `:source-coord`? The analyzer has
     `env/site-source-coord` and a11y's `report!` has the env, so it is
     available; the question is whether a finding is coordinate-bearing in the
     same sense a site is. If yes, add it and the row is an ordinary
     `:required-keys` entry.
  2. If no, FH-STRUCT-010 needs a second class of roster row — one governed by
     cardinality and key-shape but not by the coordinate law — and the census
     suite's exclusion becomes a fixture fact instead of a test-local one.

Then move the exclusion out of manifest_census_cljs_test.cljc.

WHILE HERE, an unrelated staleness in the same fixture worth confirming: the
`:slots` row is marked `:surface :analyzer` on the stated grounds that its
authoring form has no published var, and the `manifest-roster-coverage`
suite's resolver stub manufactures `re-frame.freehand/slot` for it. But
`v/slot` IS published (`(defn slot …)` on the door, and it carries an
api-manifest row). The row may be empty across the public census for a
different and more ordinary reason — no census declaration uses a slot — in
which case the stated rationale is wrong even though the row is right.
notes: Test name correction: the suite that pins the :diagnostics roster shape, non-emptiness and suppressed-finding round trip is re-frame.freehand.tool-reader-cljs-test (it was renamed from *-jvm-test so the reader door is proved on the browser host too, which is where Pair reads).
close_reason:
Done in PR #6919 (branch worker/fh-struct-010-085ai).

DECISION 1 — should a :diagnostics entry carry a :source-coord? NO. A finding is
minted from a NODE, not read as a form: :tag + :path + the compiler-minted :sid
its warning quotes are what locate it. A synthetic coordinate would satisfy
FH-STRUCT-010's assertion and state nothing true. The manifest projection is
UNCHANGED — implementation/freehand/src/** carries no diff in this branch.

DECISION 2 — the second class of row. New index row FH-DIAG-003 + fixture
spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-diag-003.edn, applicability
'compiled jvm browser', citing 004D §Compile-tier warnings (filed under DIAG
rather than STRUCT because the allocation rule takes the area from the canonical
paragraph, and §The finite manifest's roster table does not list :diagnostics).
It governs: roster total over what the compiler collected, in source order;
empty rather than absent; every entry exactly #{:sid :id :tag :path :suppressed?};
:reason rides a suppressed entry and no other; NO entry carries a :source-coord,
asserted rather than assumed. :sid pinned by shape only — it genuinely differs
per compiling host (sid1-3a59ca33e60adc6c JVM vs sid1-b817c7594a47e73d shadow).

Proof: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/manifest_diagnostics_cljs_test.cljc
— three real v/defview {:compiled true} declarations through the production door,
one per case the law distinguishes (clean / waived / reported), so neither arm of
the conditional shape is vacuous. The reported arm prints one WARNING line at
expansion, deliberately.

EXCLUSION MOVED OUT OF THE TEST: fh-struct-010.edn gains :finding-rosters
#{:diagnostics}; manifest_census_cljs_test.cljc now asserts site rosters ∪ finding
rosters == every roster key the manifest carries, replacing the dissoc. A new
roster key must be classified rather than dropping through.

Row accounting 94 -> 95 total, 93 -> 94 active/applicable, 1 retired unchanged.
Census counts the row reached: FH-DIAG-003 compiled 'jvm browser' jvm,node.

RED-PROOF (both reverted, neither committed): dropping :reason from the
projection's select-keys -> 2 failures naming FH-DIAG-003, exit 1; emptying
:finding-rosters -> 2 failures in manifest-census, exit 1.

GATES all green, foreground: index validator --self-test/--verbose/--report all
exit 0; clojure -M:test 947/6826 0F0E; npm run test:freehand 1021/5881 0F0E;
npm run test:cljs 11177/56198 0F0E.

WHILE-HERE ITEM CONFIRMED and filed as rf2-rl8s2 rather than fixed here: v/slot
IS published (freehand.cljc:1093 + api-manifest.edn:221) while html and frame are
not, so the :slots row's :analyzer rationale is false even though the row is
right (no census declaration uses a slot). Resolving it is a design call —
promote :slots to :public with a slot-bearing census declaration, or correct the
rationale in both the fixture and manifest_roster_coverage_cljs_test's prose.

title: Freehand: ship v/html — publish the verb, admit :html, lower on all four rendering paths (RULED: option A)
description:
RULED 2026-07-25 (delegated authority, Mike Thompson): SHIP IT — option (A). Publish v/html, admit :html, and lower it on ALL FOUR rendering paths. This bead is now the IMPLEMENTATION bead for that slice; the ruling record and corrections are in NOTES. The retired dossier ai/decisions/rf2-rrosy.rule-on-v-html.md was folded in here.

WHY (short). Spec 004B calls v/html "the one visible trusted-markup spelling" in six passages (:461,:500,:524,:556,:558,:597) and 004D carries a full trusted-markup section — the spec is the artefact and it promises this door. The donor already implements the entire missing half, working and runtime-verified: re-frame.ui/html at implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui.cljc:519-530, tree constructor ui/tree.cljc:349-357, React arm ui/compiler/emit_cljs.cljc:273-276,432, JVM arm ui/compiler/emit_jvm.cljc:178-179, manifest row spec/api-manifest.edn:533 with :runtime-verified? true. The SSR serialiser is NOT donor code and survives F6e — implementation/ssr/.../ui_tree.cljc:521-553,696-698,733-736,980 already serialises {:html s} end to end. Freehand's transplant kept all the supervision (sole-child rule, <textarea> refusal, three-tier alias deny, :html-sites roster, a11y reasoning) and dropped only two ~10-line emitter arms. Removal (option b) costs MORE code and spec churn than finishing the port, and deletes a shipped capability by attrition at a migration boundary. Sanitised-HTML insertion (markdown renderers, CMS body copy — see MIG-34) is an ordinary SPA need: a substrate that refuses dangerouslySetInnerHTML on three tiers AND offers no alternative does not prevent raw HTML, it pushes authors outside with no site record, no sole-child rule, no manifest entry. A supervised visible door beats an unsupervised workaround. Today the compiler recommends (v/html ...) on all three tiers, in production builds, and the form then throws "re_frame.freehand.html is not a function" at render.

THE FLIP CONDITION was weighed and declined: option (b) would be a deliberate spec amendment retiring six 004B passages plus 004D's trusted-markup section. No such amendment has been proposed; trust-the-programmer and spec-is-the-artefact both argue for shipping the promised door.

CRITICAL SCOPE CORRECTION (Codex review, adopted into the ruling): the donor port covers only the COMPILED emitters. Freehand's paved path is interpreted (:compiled defaults false, freehand.cljc:219); the interpreted browser walker rejects an arbitrary map child and the interpreted structural walk has no trusted-markup constructor. The slice MUST make (v/html s) work in interpreted AND compiled views on both hosts — four paths total — or it is not an acceptable public contract.

ATOMICITY (hard constraint, carried forward from the mayor amendment): NEVER publish the var without all the lowerings. Var-without-lowering = (v/html s) analyzes cleanly, records a site, and renders NOTHING — silent markup loss, strictly worse than today's loud crash. If the slice cannot land atomically, the ONLY safe first increment is the honest-diagnostic half (rewrite rules.cljc:362-364 recovery strings to name what exists today), leaving the loud failure intact; then land var + admitted-ops + all arms as ONE change. If the whole slice lands atomically, rules.cljc:362-364 needs NO edit — the recovery string simply becomes true.

IMPLEMENTATION MAP
1. Publish re-frame.freehand/html (port ui.cljc:519-530). Back it with a small internal nominal trusted-markup value for interpreted rendering — a private type, NOT {:html ...} maps as an authoring form (arbitrary maps must not become a second, less-visible bypass).

Compiled emitters: emit_react.cljc emit-element* (:343-345) builds dangerouslySetInnerHTML from (:html node) (port emit_cljs.cljc:273-276,432); emit_jvm.cljc emit-element (:140-141,165) sources child-forms from (:html node) (port emit_jvm.cljc:178-179); delete the dead ":html nil" arm at emit_jvm.cljc:387. A shared runtime string check keeps compiled and interpreted behaviour aligned on dynamic expressions.
6. Carrier regression fence: :html hangs off the element node, OUTSIDE grammar/element-props-carriers (grammar.cljc:54-69) — which is exactly how both emitters dropped it with nothing raised (the v/spread bug class the roster docstring names). Put :html under a roster the emitter-coverage suites read (widen the roster to non-props element carriers, or add one sibling). Compact fence only — no generic carrier framework.
7. Manifest — SERIAL LANE, five co-edited files per public verb; sequence behind any in-flight manifest PR: regenerate spec/api-manifest.edn (generated, header :1-5); hand-add the curated row to spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn (tier :advanced, owner 004, mirroring donor row api-manifest.edn:533); spec/API.md row; docs/api member.

Conformance: fh-struct-010.edn:33,52 — :html-sites moves {:surface :analyzer} to the public census surface; that tripwire firing is the design working (manifest_roster_coverage_cljs_test.cljc:26-32). fh-struct-009.edn:142,144,173,175 stay unchanged — v/html is a node form, not a privileged prop key; every dangerouslySetInnerHTML prop/spread spelling stays refused; their recovery text just stops being a lie.
9. Spec: 004B needs NO edits — its six passages become true. 004D: ui/ -> v/ respelling at :336,338,858,1252,2235,2249,2258 and in the section "Trusted markup — what ui/html does not do" (:1305-1395). State plainly that neither Freehand nor SSR sanitises; compiled manifests enumerate sites statically, interpreted views make the call visible at runtime only — do not promise a compile-time census for interpreted views, and do not weaken the compiled grammar to accept an opaque helper result that happens to contain a markup marker. Update migration catalogue/eval MIG-34 (the CMS/article-body path gains its route). Document the Trusted-Types/CSP require-trusted-types-for limitation instead of integrating it.
10. Ledger: flip the rf2-drpa3.56 absorption-ledger row for the donor html slice to MOVE/DONE and record the resolution at ai/decisions/rf2-drpa3.57.donor-deletion-terminal-gate.md:125.

ALSO IN THE SAME PR (corrections to files the slice touches):
- manifest_roster_coverage_cljs_test.cljc:20-25,70-79 is stale: slot IS published (freehand.cljc:1048; api-manifest.edn:221); only html and frame are genuinely unpublished. Fix the comment and the injected resolver stub.

The rulings legitimately diverge: v/html has no alternative spelling, a live :html-sites roster, and a working donor implementation; v/raw names a capability authors already have and entangles the :foreign crossing-prop markers (grammar.cljc:71-84). This ruling is NOT a ruling on raw. (Minor correction for 4gnrs's text: :html gates no elision verdict — view-cell-elided?, compiler.cljc:108-128, reads :subs/:events/:frame-ops only.)

SEQUENCING: the Freehand emitter is a serial lane — dispatch after any in-flight emitter PR merges. This gates F6e (donor deletion); sibling donor call rf2-5gliq gates F6c.

notes:

THE EMITTER-LANE WORKER (PR #6910) ESTABLISHED: NEITHER EMITTER LOWERS v/html. It also found this bead's earlier note ('both prior reviewers recommended shipping v/html') did not survive verification — those reviewers reasoned from the machinery that recognises, validates, records and recommends the form, and never reached the emitters.

WHY THE RULING SURVIVES: option (a) was never 'publish the var'. It was 'publish the var, admit :html to admitted-ops, AND LOWER IT IN BOTH EMITTERS (React dangerouslySetInnerHTML; JVM tree + SSR serialiser), keep the textarea/raw-text laws, keep the :html-sites roster.' Emitter lowering is the load-bearing half and always was.

  - Do NOT land var publication as a first increment.
  - If the slice must be split, split it the OTHER way: land the honest-diagnostic half FIRST (rewrite rules.cljc:362-364's dangerouslySetInnerHTML recovery strings to name something that exists today), removing the lying diagnostic while leaving the loud failure intact. Then land var + admitted-ops + both emitter arms as ONE atomic change.
  - Acceptance MUST include a rendered-output proof on BOTH hosts (React DOM and JVM/SSR serialiser), not a manifest or analyzer assertion. An :html site in the roster that emits nothing is exactly the failure this note prevents.

FLAGGED FOR MIKE, unchanged: I treat spec/004B as authoritative on whether Freehand offers a raw-HTML door. If v/html was never intended to ship, this flips to (b) RETIRE. Either way the invariant is not in dispute: A DIAGNOSTIC MUST NOT RECOMMEND A PUBLIC FORM THAT DOES NOT EXIST.
RULING 2026-07-25 10:54:00 AUSEST (delegated authority per Mike): OPTION (A) SHIP IT — confirmed and finalised. The mayor's 2026-07-25 SHIP amendment stands; the dossier ai/decisions/rf2-rrosy.rule-on-v-html.md was weighed in full, folded into the rewritten description, and deleted per instruction. The flip condition (a no-escaping-bypass substrate, i.e. a deliberate spec amendment retiring six 004B passages plus 004D's trusted-markup section) was considered and DECLINED: the spec is the artefact and promises this door; a supervised visible trusted-markup verb beats pushing authors outside the substrate with no site record; sanitised-HTML insertion is an ordinary SPA need.

DECISIVE EVIDENCE: the donor ships the entire missing half, working and runtime-verified — re-frame.ui/html ui.cljc:519-530, tree ctor ui/tree.cljc:349-357, React arm emit_cljs.cljc:273-276,432, JVM arm emit_jvm.cljc:178-179, manifest row api-manifest.edn:533 with :runtime-verified? true — and the SSR serialiser already implements the leaf end-to-end OUTSIDE donor code (ssr/ui_tree.cljc:521-553,696-698,733-736,980), surviving F6e. Options (c) publish-var-only and (d) defer were rejected — (c) is silent markup loss, the worst outcome available; (d) leaves the lying diagnostic on main and the trigger fires after the donor is deleted.

SCOPE AMENDMENT ADOPTED (Codex review): the slice must also cover interpreted Freehand (:compiled defaults false, freehand.cljc:219) — four rendering paths, landed atomically. title: Freehand ships the namespace docstring once per declared view into :advanced bundles
description:
Measured while discharging rf2-x4jda R1.

A Freehand view's manifest/descriptor carries its NAMESPACE's docstring, and
`:advanced` does not strip it. A namespace declaring N views therefore ships
its docstring N times into the production bundle. Per-VIEW docstrings do not
ship (checked, 0 occurrences) - only the ns one, repeated.

Measured on the B5 release entries (three declared views each): a 1,496-byte
namespace docstring landed 4,488 bytes in the :advanced artefact; its sibling's
1,609-byte docstring landed 4,827. This is a cost every consumer app pays, not
a fixture artefact - a well-documented 10-view namespace ships its ns docstring
ten times.

It is also why B5's own headline shipped-cost figure is inflated: the mixed
entry re-frame.freehand.release-app carries a ~1,486-byte docstring x3, about
4.5 KB of the 739,838-byte figure (0.6%).

The B5 matched pair worked around it by carrying its prose in ;; comments, which
is right for a fixture that exists to be measured and wrong as general advice.

QUESTION FOR TRIAGE: is the ns docstring load-bearing in the descriptor at all -
does any tool read it? If not, dropping it from the emitted descriptor is a
free win for every consumer bundle. If a tool does read it, the fix is to carry
it once per namespace rather than once per view.

The producing surface is the Freehand analyzer/emitter (fenced to the emitter
lane at the time of filing), not the bench surface.
notes: MAYOR TRIAGE 2026-07-25: RAISED P3 -> P2. This is a production shipped-cost defect that every consumer app pays, not a benchmark artefact, and it is measured rather than suspected: a 1,496-byte namespace docstring landed 4,488 bytes in the :advanced artefact across three declared views; its sibling's 1,609-byte docstring landed 4,827. A well-documented 10-view namespace ships its ns docstring TEN times into production. Per-VIEW docstrings do not ship (verified, 0 occurrences) — only the namespace one, repeated per declared view. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE BYTES: re-frame2 markets bundle economy and the whole B5 evidence lane exists to measure shipped cost honestly — a substrate that silently multiplies documentation into the production bundle penalises exactly the authoring behaviour the project wants to encourage. It also contaminated B5's own headline figure until rf2-x4jda R1 removed the docstrings from the fixture, so the defect was masking itself. SEQUENCING: the repair site is the analyzer/emitter (implementation/freehand/src/compiler/**), which is a SERIAL lane currently held by the in-flight emitter cluster (rf2-rr26cq + rf2-tb5yq + rf2-hytu5). Dispatch after that PR merges. SCOPE FENCE for whoever takes it: the manifest/descriptor should carry what a reader needs, and the namespace docstring repeated per view is not that. Prefer removing the redundancy over adding a stripping pass — pre-alpha, no compatibility concern. Do NOT build a general docstring-elision framework, and do NOT remove per-view docstrings from the authoring surface (they do not ship today, so they cost nothing). If the fix needs more than changing what the descriptor carries, stop and report.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6918 (worker/fh-docstring-9y9uv). ROOT CAUSE: shadow-cljs hangs the ns docstring off the ns-name symbol (shadow.build.ns-form/parse merges {:doc ...} into it); that symbol becomes *cljs-ns*, macroexpansion binds *ns* to it, and defview's :source map QUOTES it — a quoted symbol carries its metadata into the bundle because cljs.analyzer/analyze-wrap-meta elides only reader/analyzer keys. FIX: the one-token removal the scope fence asked for — pass the metadata-free (symbol (str ns-sym)), the same caller contract re-frame.core-reg-macros already states for every reg-* macro (rf2-xnym). Normalised inside expand-defview (covers every expansion path) and at custom-element* (the other site quoting an ns symbol into emitted code). No stripping pass, no elision framework, per-view docstrings untouched. MEASURED on :freehand-release (:advanced, goog.DEBUG false): 739,938 -> 730,802 bytes, -9,136 (-1.23%); release-app's 1,643-byte ns docstring 3 occurrences -> 0, and re-frame.freehand's OWN 1,960-byte docstring 2 -> 0 (the substrate was shipping its door docstring into every consumer bundle). LAW: re-frame.freehand.ns-docstring-absence-jvm-test builds a namespace the way shadow-cljs leaves one and proves its own subject contaminated first; all three laws go red with the fix reverted. GATES green: freehand JVM 948/6819, test:freehand 1017/5862, test:cljs 11172/56169, browser 762/4771, reachability, evidence-elision, changed-surfaces 227, test-fast-pr.sh PASS. FOLLOW-ON FILED: rf2-8cted — re-frame.ui carries the same defect (implementation/ui/** was outside this bead's write surface).

title: FH-EVENT-005 was deleted, not retired — the id ledger now dangles and will recycle
description:
Found while completing rf2-drpa3.53 (F6a conformance completion), 2026-07-25 08:22 AUSEST. Reported, not fixed: reversing a just-ruled deletion is not a worker's call.

FACT. rf2-drpa3.178 (PR #6900) discharged the D007 gate with outcome DELETE and removed the FH-EVENT-005 row from spec/conformance/freehand/conformance-index.md outright, taking the index 93 rows -> 92. The FH-EVENT section now runs 001..004.

THE INCONSISTENCY. spec/conformance/freehand/README.md rules the opposite disposition for a withdrawn law, in two places:

  'Ids are therefore permanent - they are never renumbered, never reassigned, and never recycled. A law that is withdrawn keeps its id at status retired so an old citation resolves to an honest answer instead of dangling.'

  Status vocabulary: 'retired | The id is burned so citations stay honest. The law no longer binds. | fixture cell: em dash'

Two consequences, both live today:

1. DANGLING CITATION. FH-EVENT-005 is still cited in spec/conformance/freehand/donor-inventory.md:154, in the D007 design record, and across the rf2-drpa3.178 / .23 / .57 bead notes. A reader resolving that id against the index gets nothing - exactly the outcome the retired status exists to prevent.

2. THE ID WILL RECYCLE. The allocation rule is 'take the next number after the highest already allocated in that area - INCLUDING RETIRED ONES'. The highest EVENT ordinal is now 004, so the next EVENT law lands as FH-EVENT-005 and silently inherits a citation trail belonging to the deleted key-condition form. Nothing detects this: a deleted TOP-of-area id leaves no gap, so the validator's ascending-ordinal rule cannot see it, and the F6a census added by rf2-drpa3.53 cannot either (the fixture and tests went with the row).

CANDIDATE RESOLUTIONS, for Mike or the mayor to choose:

  (a) Restore the row at status retired with an em-dash fixture cell. Costs one line, makes the ledger self-consistent, and burns the id so it cannot recycle. Passes both guards as-is: the structural check requires a retired row to name no fixture, and the census counts only active rows.
  (b) Rule that pre-alpha id-burning is not worth it, and AMEND README.md's retirement paragraph and status table to say deletion is the disposition - accepting that old citations dangle and ids recycle. Currently the README says one thing and the shipped index does another; either is defensible, but not both.

Whichever is chosen, the two must agree. Right now the addressing scheme's own documented rule is contradicted by the index it governs.
notes: CORRECTION to the line above: closed on PR-open per repo convention (beads close when the PR opens, not when it merges) — PR #6907. Closed != on main; the mayor's merge sweep owns the landing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Freehand tool tier live reads: minimal live-occurrence index, mounted-views, and bounded explain-render over the Spec 009 ring
description:
Filed 2026-07-25 out of the rf2-drpa3.167 ruling, which rejected porting the donor per-occurrence evidence accumulator into Freehand and re-dispositioned donor rows 195-196 as REPLACE. This bead is the part of the job that IS real. It belongs to F6c (rf2-drpa3.55), not to F4g.

THE ONE REQUIREMENT THAT JUSTIFIES ANY LIVE STATE AT ALL: Pair attaches LATE. An MCP agent attaches to an already-running application, so Freehand's fire-and-forget commit sink (cell.cljc:901 emit-commit-evidence!) can never answer "what is mounted right now". read-mounted-views is a shipped tool in skills/re-frame2-pair. Nothing else in this bead needs retained state.

SCOPE - three sources, one thin read tier:

1. STATIC DECLARATION FACTS. Already filed as rf2-hytu5 (create re-frame.freehand.tool, publish the compiler's a11y :diagnostics on structural-manifest, fix the dangling docstring at compiler/a11y.cljc:46). Sequence this bead AFTER hytu5. The manifest-backed reads that Pair needs - read-view-manifest, read-view-dependencies, read-view-event-sites - are reads over the manifest Freehand's compiler ALREADY builds; they need no accumulator, no root registry and no interval log. Note: Freehand has no browser-global descriptor registry today, so this slice must either add a small dev-only registry keyed by view id or make the descriptor an explicit input. Pair's view-id-oriented API makes the dev-only registry the more ergonomic default.

2. CURRENT OCCURRENCES - a MINIMAL LIVE INDEX. Only current dev-mode occurrences and their latest committed projection. Insert-or-update on selected commit, remove on disconnect. Freehand's explicit shell cleanup is the natural release seam. It must distinguish two simultaneous occurrences of one view, stay correct across a compatible hot reload, and report unknown facts as UNKNOWN rather than manufacture root or lifecycle fidelity. mounted-views is a read over this index.

   HARD FENCE, from the .167 ruling: this is CURRENT STATE, NOT HISTORY. No lifetime render/batch counts. No accumulated target union. No lifecycle interval ledger and no hide-versus-unmount proof labels. No weak-keyed store and no HMR store migration. No cell-to-root attribution. No second retention knob. If this starts to look like the donor's 1,049-line re-frame.ui.tool.evidence, STOP - that is the gold-plating signal and .167 already ruled against it.

3. RECENT EXPLANATIONS - a BOUNDED explain-render. Enrich the selected-commit record only with facts Freehand ALREADY HAS at commit: frame, committed reads/dependencies, committed event sites, lowering, generation, and a trigger cause IF that cause can be carried to commit without keeping history. Publish validated commit and lifecycle facts into the existing Spec 009 trace path. explain-render folds the configured retained ring AT READ TIME and reports truncation or missing basis through the schema's existing :complete? and :loss fields. Background tools may fold those bounded records into UI summaries; the substrate must not persist the summary.

   IMPLEMENTATION HAZARD, worth the whole bead if missed: Spec 009 DOES NOT RETAIN FRAMELESS EVENTS. So Freehand evidence must either join the applicable frame/run correlation, or use an equally explicit retained Freehand trace operation under the SAME ring and the SAME retention knob. Merely calling a listener with an uncorrelated record makes late explanations disappear and does not satisfy the contract.

CONSUMERS. Xray and Pair consume the Freehand tool namespace and the Freehand schema; they do not emulate donor schema v3 (:rf.ui.tool/version 3). "Mounted" means current connected occurrences. "Explain render" means recent, bounded, possibly incomplete evidence. Scope, basis, completeness and loss are visible. Production builds retain no detailed evidence and no tool registry. The consumer rewires are the F6 ledger rows 392 (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/viewcell_evidence.cljs, 466 lines), 393 (xray reactive_panel_*), 394/395 (xray evidence tests) and 397 (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/view_tool.cljs) - they stay pending until this lands. Pair's tool catalogue is a closed world, so any change to the five view tools is also descriptors_data.cljs, registry.cljs, tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md and the mcp-conformance gate.

DONE WHEN:
1. Two live occurrences of one view are distinguishable.
2. A late-attaching Pair session sees occurrences that were already connected before it attached.
3. Disconnect removes an occurrence and releases its current projection.
4. A recent selected commit can be explained from the configured Spec 009 window.
5. Eviction and missing correlation are reported as LOSS, never silently presented as complete evidence.
6. Compiler diagnostics, dependency sites and event sites are reachable through the Freehand tool read path.
7. Xray and Pair carry no donor-tool dependency for Freehand views.
8. There is NO cumulative Freehand evidence accumulator and NO second retention knob - proved the way evidence-boundary-jvm-test proves it now.
9. Detailed evidence and registries stay dev-gated and elide from production - the npm run test:freehand-evidence-elision control-build technique, already shipped.

SPLIT IF IT GETS BIG: the natural cut is (1)+(2) as one PR - reads plus live index - and (3)+consumers as a second. Do NOT split root attribution, interval proof, weak retention or target sampling into speculative follow-ups; .167 ruled they are not required by this design and will not be built.

HOT-ZONE: spec/API.md and spec/009-Instrumentation.md are sequential, never parallel. spec/API.md:370 currently rows re-frame.ui.tool/* as "v1, tool tier, dev-only" and spec/Conventions.md:107 reserves :rf.ui.tool/* - both need a Freehand counterpart row when this lands.

  - `re-frame.freehand.registry` (NEW) — the DEV-ONLY declared-view index,
    view-id -> declaration, one row per declaration, replaced on redeclare. No

rf2-cpfbg), 7 (the Xray/Pair consumer rewires — F6 ledger rows

notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6888 (merged 2026-07-24T19:13:34Z) — REOPEN this exact CI-wiring owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: PR #6888 makes the focused probe a required job and covers the schema, cell seam, release entry, checker, and build config, but its narrow classifier omits `implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/shell.cljs`. That file owns the sole mounted production call `cell/commit!` (shell.cljs:165), which is what roots `emit-commit-evidence!` and the two control sentinels from `release_app.cljs`. The classifier reports `implementation_jvm=true`, `cljs_node_test=true`, `cljs_browser=true`, but `freehand_evidence_elision=false` for shell.cljs. A shell change that removes or redirects that commit edge can therefore make the control bundle lose both evidence doors while the new required gate is skipped. The cited JVM law does not close this hole: it walks namespace requires and asserts `cell` is the sole schema requirer; it remains green when the call edge is removed because both namespaces are still require-reachable. Add shell.cljs to the bounded producer arm (and pin it in the classifier tests); do not widen to all Freehand.

CORRECTNESS: the job/output/aggregator wiring itself is sound, all merged checks passed, and the unconditional nightly/local arms are useful backstops. The current two-build probe remains non-vacuous and correctly treats missing control sentinels as failure; the defect is only that a direct input to that positive-control reachability does not schedule it at PR time.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the dedicated output and helper reuse are focused and ergonomic. Keep the correction as one extra exact producer surface plus its regression row; no workflow refactor or general dependency framework.
RULING 2026-07-25 05:58 AUSEST (dossier ai/decisions/rf2-xwa4n.evidence-elision-ci-gate.md folded in and deleted) — KEEP the merged gate. Do NOT revert it, do NOT fold it into cljs-elision, do NOT demote it to nightly-only, do NOT widen it to implementation/freehand/**. Repair the ONE verified arming gap and close. Verdict reached under the pre-alpha posture with the explicit bar that a new CI gate must catch a real, recurring, expensive defect class that cheaper means cannot; this one clears that bar, and the remaining work is a one-line classifier fix, not a new gate.

LIVE STATE (the dossier header was stale). PR #6888 is MERGED — 2026-07-24T19:13:34Z, merge commit eeafe3f2d19c0ecdd0ee86d4c05af6c59f889413. The gate runs on main today. This bead was reopened by the merged-PR audit and now owns exactly one completeness defect, not the wire-it-or-not question.

WHY THE GATE EARNS ITS KEEP (measured, do not re-litigate).
Cost, from PR #6888 run 30119055201: whole job 85s wall clock; the gate step (both :advanced builds + grep) 63s; fixed setup before it (checkout, JDK, Node, cache, npm ci) 19s. Longest job in that same run 509s (JVM tools/template) — so the gate adds ~0s to PR wall clock, running in parallel far inside the critical path. Siblings for scale, nightly run 30106705162: test:elision (the 2-build pair) 54s warm, test:bundle-isolation (6 :advanced builds) 98s warm.
No invoice. day8/re-frame2 is PUBLIC and the job is ubuntu-latest, so GitHub-hosted minutes are not billed. The bead description premise — "a maintainer CI-cost call (added job minutes)" — does not survive contact with that fact. The real cost is one runner slot and some cache traffic.
Arming rate: exactly 5 of the last 110 non-beads commits on main touched an armed path (~4.5%, about one PR in twenty-two). Adding shell.cljs raises it to ~5.5%. Amortised expected added compute ~4s per PR.

WHY THE CHEAPER ORACLES ARE NOT ON THE MENU (each already measured failing in this repo).
- Counting a debug flag in the release bundle: 225 occurrences survived — inside DOCSTRINGS — in a build where the entire surface had in fact been eliminated. Reports a leak that does not exist.
- Grepping for a small function name: Closure inlines small functions, so the name is gone whether or not the behaviour shipped. The check can never go red; a green light wired to nothing.
- A require-graph reachability walk: this WAS the honest claim before rf2-3naow, when there was no emission site — the schema was pure values reached by nothing, so there was no gate for a control build to toggle. Measured then: 705,206 bytes release, 741,967 control, every schema string absent in BOTH. Its own docstring instructed that it be REPLACED, not relaxed, the moment an emission site appeared. That happened and it was replaced. The walk survives in evidence_boundary_jvm_test.clj answering a different question (how a render reaches this code) and explicitly disclaims the bundle question: a require-graph walk cannot see what dead-code elimination removed.
A two-build control probe is therefore the only non-vacuous oracle available for this claim.

WHY NOT FOLD INTO cljs-elision (the intuitive move; rejected on numbers). The Closure compile is paid PER BUILD ID, not per job — hosting the Freehand pair inside cljs-elision saves only that job's fixed setup, measured at 19s. And cljs-elision is gated on cljs_prod, which is armed very broadly: across the last 40 test.yml runs it RAN 19 and SKIPPED 21 (~48% of PRs). So piggybacking buys 19 seconds and pays for it by running two :advanced compiles roughly ten times more often than the proof can possibly have been invalidated, while lengthening the critical path of a frequently-armed required job. General lesson worth keeping: piggybacking is nearly free when a job's cost is SETUP; it is not when the job's cost is CLOSURE.

WHY NOT NIGHTLY-ONLY. Nightly alone is the reasonable minimum — it catches everything, a day late — but the regression then arrives as a red nightly against a batch of merged PRs rather than a red check on the causative PR, and bisecting a Closure-DCE regression across a day of merges is genuinely unpleasant. Scheduled workflows can also be delayed and, under load, dropped. The shipped split is right: the path-armed required job puts the red check on the PR that can break it, and the unconditional nightly (expensive-tests.yml + test-rigorous-local.sh) is the honest superset for breaks originating OUTSIDE Freehand — a core interop/debug-enabled? change, an adapter change, a shadow-cljs/Closure bump.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY AT STAKE IF THE PROOF SILENTLY ROTS.
- Bundle: the control/release delta is 51,304 chars — about 50 KiB raw, 6.9% of the release bundle. Gzipped that is materially smaller; extrapolating rf2-drpa3.52's measured 3.38:1 gzip ratio on this same artefact gives ~15 KiB, and that number is an ESTIMATE — nobody has actually gzipped the control.
- Runtime, and this is worse than the bytes: the seam builds AND VALIDATES a record through evidence/record then projection then defects on EVERY selected commit, which is the render hot path. That is per-frame work in production, not a one-off load cost.
- NOT a privacy leak, and do not inflate it into one. D019 is explicit that the envelope must not contain raw props, app-db, event payloads, host nodes/instances, the exception object, or arbitrary ex-data, and the schema is built to that shape — the record carries occurrence, generation, lowering and the four axes (:scope, :basis, :complete?, :loss). Shipped evidence code would be WASTEFUL, not exfiltration. The one residual concern is that set-evidence-sink! would become a live installation point on a production page, letting anything already running there receive per-commit metadata (view ids, generations, lowering). A surface you would not choose to ship; not user-data exfiltration.
- The load-bearing risk is the normative CLAIM. rf2-drpa3.37 acceptance criterion 6 states flatly that evidence/debug code does not ship, and rf2-drpa3.166 exists solely to prove it. In a repo where the spec is the artefact, silently publishing a false normative claim is the real cost. Note that the positive-control half degrades the same way: rename a door string and the sentinel goes absent in the CONTROL too, which is exactly what the control is designed to catch — but only if the gate RUNS. An un-run gate does not merely fail to catch regressions; it accumulates silent rot in its own oracle. That is the specific failure mode this project has already been bitten by twice (see the 225-docstring false positive and the inlined-name never-red above).

THE REMAINING DEFECT, RE-VERIFIED THIS SESSION RATHER THAN ASSERTED.
Running sh .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/shell.cljs prints implementation_jvm=true, cljs_browser=true, freehand_evidence_elision=FALSE.
implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/shell.cljs:165 is the SOLE call site of cell/commit! in the artefact — grepping implementation/freehand/src for commit! returns only docstring mentions, the cell.cljc definition, and the unrelated events/commit!. That call sits inside a react/useLayoutEffect reconcile on the mounted render path, and it is what roots emit-commit-evidence! and therefore BOTH positive-control door strings in the control bundle. release_app.cljs reaches it by mounting through v/mount into the shell.
So a shell-only change that removes or redirects that commit edge makes the control bundle lose both sentinels — the checker would correctly fail — while the required PR job is SKIPPED and the PR merges green. The always-armed jvm-freehand walk does NOT close this hole: evidence_boundary_jvm_test.clj asserts that cell is the SOLE namespace REQUIRING the schema, and it stays green when the CALL edge is removed, because both namespaces remain require-reachable. Require-reachability is not call-reachability.
Arming shell.cljs is the right bounded fix precisely because it is a DIRECT primary input to the positive control, not a transitive one. It does not justify arming all of implementation/freehand/** — many transitive changes could theoretically stop the release app reaching a mounted commit, just as a core or compiler change could, and the unconditional nightly is the honest superset for those.

STANDING PREMISE, KEEP IT NON-SILENT. The narrow arm's honesty is BORROWED from the always-armed jvm-freehand walk that pins cell as the schema's sole requirer: a fourth producer file cannot appear without reddening that walk first. If that law is ever relaxed, the arming list must widen in the SAME PR. The classifier comment says so and _changed-surfaces.test.cjs pins the premise — that is the right way to make a borrowed guarantee non-silent. Keep it that way.

SHARED LANE FOR rf2-drpa3.52 (B5, IN_PROGRESS). B5 depends on the same :freehand-release target and the same control-build technique — its acceptance #1 is a control-build reachability gate. PR #6887 (rf2-x4jda) merged 2026-07-24 and added :freehand-release-interpreted and :freehand-release-compiled to implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, so that file now declares FOUR Freehand release builds. Those serve the per-promotion byte delta, are built by the bench lane, and are NOT part of this probe pair, so they do not change any arithmetic above. When B5's own gate lands, REUSE the freehand_evidence_elision classifier output rather than minting a second Freehand bundle output, and host it in the SAME job so both proofs share one runner and one npm ci — the :freehand-release build is already paid for by this gate's release half. That is where piggybacking genuinely is nearly free: same artefacts, same setup.

BEAD HOUSEKEEPING CHECKED. rf2-drpa3.166 is already CLOSED and its close reason correctly credits the merged #6888 for its COMPLETENESS finding — no action. rf2-drpa3.37 stays OPEN for rf2-drpa3.167 (the donor MOVE / accumulator slice); do not let the criterion-6 satisfaction pull .37 shut. description: Discovered-from rf2-kqxe6.7 (R3 intent prefetch, PR #6878). R3 published the consumable seam (:routing/prefetch-payload + :routing/prefetch-on-intent!) but deliberately did NOT wire the two route-link DESCRIPTORS (Freehand was off-limits with a live render-path worker; ui/route-link out of R3's routing/resources surface). MECHANICAL follow-up, one small change per artefact: (a) Freehand v/route-link (implementation/freehand — the descriptor) — add :prefetch to its control-key strip set + bind the 3 intent handlers (hover/focus/etc.) to prefetch-on-intent!, exactly as :activate! is bound for the click; (b) re-frame.ui ui/route-link (implementation/ui) — same wiring. Reuse the published seam; add NO new API. FENCE: two disjoint descriptors; can be one worker touching both (freehand descriptor + ui view) or split. notes:
MAYOR HOLD 2026-07-25 — PR #6890 IS NOT AUTO-MERGE. Do not merge on green without Mike's sign-off; this note exists so a later merge tick does not sweep it up.

WHY: the bead specified a MECHANICAL follow-up — 'one small change per artefact', 'reuse the published seam', 'add NO new API'. What landed is 10 files, +742/-99, and includes a SPEC-VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE beyond the wiring, which the worker flagged honestly and asked to have reviewed before merge.

THE JUDGEMENT CALL: in Freehand an :on-* position otherwise accepts an EVENT VECTOR (e.g. [:app/hovered]), but routing's prefetch-on-intent! must CALL the caller's handler in order to compose with it. Silently dropping a caller's handler was correctly rejected. The worker instead generalised the existing veto normalizer into one shared normalize-callback (one rejection shape, one roster) and applied it to the three intent positions — NARROWING the accepted grammar at those positions — conditional on the :prefetch opt-in, so every non-opted-in link keeps the open grammar. Existing error id and recovery reused; no new public surface added. re-frame.ui/route-link needed none of this (React props are already fns).

THE QUESTION FOR MIKE: is a conditional grammar narrowing on the three intent positions acceptable under trust-the-programmer / minimal-API, or should the composition problem be solved without removing the event-vector spelling at those positions? It is defensible — the narrowing only applies where the framework must own the handler — but it is a taste/ergonomics call on a public authoring surface, and the bead that authorised the work said mechanical + no new API.

title: EP-0037 R1 completion: unify resources/core readiness reconciliation onto the shared projector
acceptance_criteria:
- One shared pure projector consumes Spec 016 resource facts at commit, retained-owner adoption/handoff, resource settle, hydration, and epoch restore.
- A fresh blocking resource that already has usable data commits :idle; a true first load commits/remains :loading only while work capable of settling that requirement exists.
- The adopt/handoff path has no private has-data/error/else readiness branch: missing, idle/no-work, in-flight, usable-data, refresh-error, and restored states project through the shared rules. rf2-kqxe6.6 owns the bounded missing/unusable-entry ensure fallback.
- Refresh failure with usable data stays on :refresh-error and does not become route :error; previous-data for a newly keyed requirement does not complete that first load.
- Hydration and restore recompute cached route :transition/:error from restored resource facts instead of preserving contradictory readiness.
- Remove the now-unconsumed :routing/route-blocking? hook and its settle-transition descriptors/comments, with focused cross-artifact regressions and no second readiness state machine.
notes:

The routing projector currently reduces only plan-error/blocking presence, while resources settle, hydration, and restore still do not share its resource-fact projection. Deduped here rather than creating another issue; acceptance now makes fresh-cache, refresh-error, previous-data, hydration/restore, and obsolete-hook outcomes explicit.

That branch can strand blocking readiness for an idle/no-work or restored contradiction and would become a second readiness state machine. Feed adoption/handoff facts through the shared projector here; rf2-kqxe6.6 separately owns falling back to ensure when a retained entry is missing/unusable.
