The command effect was registered {:platforms #{:client}}, so the generic fx gate SKIPPED it on the structural host and emitted no error record at all — while Spec 004 and Spec 009 independently describe a typed refusal, and command!'s #?(:clj) refusal had been dead since the commit that introduced it. Gate removed; the effect is universal and refuses itself. SEE THE MAYOR NOTE ON THIS BEAD: this widens blast radius to real SSR (a command during an SSR drain now refuses rather than skipping, and a thrown fx fails SSR closed to 500) — flagged to Mike, reversal is small and local if he disagrees.

title: The compiled tier refuses v/behavior as a FOREIGN component boundary, misnaming the framework's own attachment
description:
F5i pilot (rf2-drpa3.46) finding. Sharpens rf2-drpa3.127 rather than duplicating
it: .127 records that a compiled view cannot attach a behavior. This is about
WHAT THE DIAGNOSTIC SAYS, which is a separate defect and cheaper to fix.

REPRODUCTION. A {:compiled true} body containing [v/behavior {...} [:div]] is
refused at build with:

  :rf.ui.compile/error  :rf.ui.compile/unsupported-form
  :op                   :foreign
  message               "a foreign component boundary is outside
                         :re-frame.freehand/v1 - the finite grammar
                         {:compiled true} selects"
  :recovery             [:extract-declared-child :keep-interpreted ...]

v/behavior is NOT a foreign component. It is a framework-supplied boundary
declared on the public door, alongside v/route-link, v/markup and
v/error-boundary. An author who reads "a foreign component boundary" goes looking
for the third-party component they did not write.

THE ASYMMETRY MAKES IT LEGIBLE AS A BUG. Two sibling framework boundaries compile
without comment, because they are ordinary v/defview declarations carrying the
:re-frame.freehand/view var metadata the compile-time head classifier reads:

  [v/route-link {:to :x} "t"]   => accepted
  [v/markup {:value nil}]       => accepted
  [v/behavior {:use b} [:div]]  => :op :foreign

v/behavior and v/error-boundary are built with descriptor/declare-view directly,
so their vars carry no view metadata and the classifier falls through to
:foreign. The classification is an accident of how the boundary is CONSTRUCTED,
not a statement about what it IS.

SUGGESTED FIX (cheap, and independent of .127 shipping a real compiled form):
recognise the framework boundary vars at compile time and refuse with a message
that names what it actually is - e.g. "v/behavior is a framework host attachment
and has no compiled form yet; extract the decorated node into its own interpreted
child". The existing :extract-declared-child recovery is already correct and the
pilot proves it works end to end.

EVIDENCE: a-compiled-body-cannot-attach-the-one-reachable-host-shape in
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_react_interop_cljs_test.cljc
pins the id, the :op, the sentence, the recovery, AND the two accepted siblings -
so a fix that renames the diagnostic fails the test and has to update it
deliberately.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6856 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6856. Compiled-tier v/behavior: analyzer lowers [v/behavior …] to :op :behavior (no longer misnamed :foreign, .153), grammar admits it, all three emitters emit it reaching the one re-frame.freehand.behaviors runtime; FH-BEHAVIOR-001/002/003 re-cut to common (.116); a compiled view attaches AND runs a behavior with cross-mode transcript equality proven (.127). F6b behavior-matrix compiled cell + pilot refusal cells flipped to the compiled PASS.

title: A nested React root cannot be unmounted synchronously from a behavior disconnect
description:
F5i pilot (rf2-drpa3.46) finding. Sibling of the nested-root headline bead.

A behavior :disconnect runs from the OUTER React tree own unmount. Calling
root.unmount() on a nested React root there is calling into React while React is
already rendering, and React 19 refuses it loudly:

  Attempted to synchronously unmount a root while React was already rendering.
  React cannot finish unmounting the root until the current render has
  completed, which may lead to a race condition.

Reproduced in the pilot: the first browser run emitted this error three times.
React documented remedy is to defer the unmount out of the current render, and a
microtask is sufficient - close-root! in pilot_react_interop_react.cljs does
exactly that and the error is gone.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every other release the substrate performs is SYNCHRONOUS and
assertable at the instant of unmount - that is the whole basis of the
FH-BEHAVIOR-005 "cleanup is asserted as an absence" law. The nested React root is
the one participant that cannot honour it, so an application counting live
instances, or a leak check in CI, has to know to wait a tick for exactly this one
kind of resource, and nothing tells it so.

This is NOT a substrate defect. It is a cost of the nested-root workaround, and
it disappears entirely if a qualified host leaf lands - a leaf renders inside the
Freehand tree own React root and has no second root to close. Filing it because
it is a concrete, measured argument for the leaf, in the currency of a console
error, and because any guide that teaches the nested-root workaround before the
leaf lands MUST teach the deferral with it.

NOT A REQUEST FOR A PRIMITIVE. No framework verb would help; deferring is two
lines the author writes once per registration.

EVIDENCE: a-nested-react-root-carries-the-whole-react-abi and
a-real-third-party-react-component-renders-and-releases in
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_react_interop_dom_cljs_test.cljs.
The browser runner fails the whole lane on an uncaught pageerror, so the ABSENCE
of the warning is now gated rather than merely observed.
notes: CONTEXT ADDED 2026-07-24 from the rf2-drpa3.151 re-examination: the cost this bead measures is a property of THE NESTED ROOT SPECIFICALLY, and it EVAPORATES on the ordinary-child path. Verified by real mount: a third-party React component held as a plain child tears down SYNCHRONOUSLY — (= "" innerHTML) immediately after v/unmount!, no microtask tick. This bead remains correct about the nested root; it should say so explicitly rather than implying the asynchrony is unavoidable for React interop generally.

Spec 004 now draws that line. The test MEASURES the gap rather than describing it (unmounts outside act in one synchronous turn: substrate table already empty, nested root still open with its foreign listener, closed one microtask later) and states in its own docstring what it cannot assert.

title: Prevent key-map branches from silently ignoring :once/:capture/:passive
description:
## Defect

PR #6761 allows an existing listener-options map as each key-map branch, so normalization accepts all five options. Only `:prevent-default` and `:stop-propagation` are honored after a key is selected. `events/invoke!` checks `:once` only on the top-level site plan, while `events/site` derives `:capture` and `:passive` only before native listener attachment from that same top-level plan. Branch-local `:once`, `:capture`, and `:passive` are consequently accepted and then silently ignored.

## Steps to Reproduce

Commit a site with `{"Enter" {:event [:picker/accept] :once true}}`, then invoke its proxy twice with Enter. The merged implementation dispatches `[:picker/accept]` twice. Likewise, branch-local `:capture`/`:passive` normalize, but the native attachment reads those flags only from the outer `:key-map` plan.

## Evidence

The source applies selected-branch mechanics in `fire!`, but reads site retirement and native attachment facts only from the outer plan. Existing FH-EVENT-005 coverage proves branch-local preventDefault, but has no row for the other accepted options.

## Bounded correction

Make the closed branch grammar honest. The smallest correction is to admit only `:event`, `:prevent-default`, and `:stop-propagation` inside a selected branch and reject `:once`, `:capture`, and `:passive` there with the existing typed event diagnostic. Do not invent a wrapper grammar or per-key native-listener machinery merely to preserve options that cannot be selected at attachment time.

## Origin

Correctness/implementation-quality audit of merged PR #6761.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A key-map branch can no longer normalize successfully while silently discarding `:once`, `:capture`, or `:passive`; unsupported forms fail with a typed, didactic event error (or receive exact documented semantics without changing native attachment facts after dispatch).
2. Branch-local `:prevent-default` and `:stop-propagation` continue to run before the selected dispatch, and ordinary event vectors/`v/event`/nil branches remain unchanged.
3. Runtime and compiled validation accept and reject the same branch grammar.
4. FH-EVENT-005 gains focused rows covering every branch option, including the repeated-Enter `:once` counterexample, without adding wildcard/modifier/nested-key syntax.

JVM 740/5356 EXIT=0, test:freehand 694/4369 EXIT=0, non-vacuity probe redded naming the test then restored byte-identical. Awaiting PR.

title: Run B2 as a real matched mount after compiled browser lowering lands
description:
## Defect

PR #6759 closes rf2-drpa3.49 with a useful deterministic manifest gate, but the B2 workload never mounts a boundary. `observe` only sums manifest verdicts over `[view scale]` plans; `:retained-view-cells` is `total - omitted`, and the published `:bench/iteration-ms` distribution therefore times static manifest lookup and arithmetic. No ViewCell or retained runtime object exists in the workload being reported.

That is honest in the new namespace docstring, but it leaves an unowned remainder of D021's B2 contract: a cells-shaped mount storm compared as interpreted, compiled, and compiled-with-cell-elision, publishing mount time, per-boundary decomposition, retained objects, and exact omitted-cell count. rf2-drpa3.113 supplies the missing browser lowering but does not own the B2 benchmark; rf2-drpa3.131 and .52 own B1 and B5 only.

## Evidence

At merge `2d7590424aca42507578b5be5467254e090d71e4`:

- `plan` creates data pairs; no root or view occurrence is rendered.
- `observe` calls only `omitted`, which reads `v/manifest`.
- `arm-decomposition` calls its derived subtraction a retained-object count.
- The tests verify static counts and the harness clock, but contain no non-vacuity witness for mounted boundaries, selected wrappers, or live retained cells.

The static exact-count gate is valuable and should remain. It is not, by itself, the mass-mount/runtime evidence named by D021 or the closed Bead's outcome.

## Bounded Correction

After rf2-drpa3.113 lands, reuse this roster and standing harness in a real browser mount fixture. Keep the exact manifest count as a deterministic gate, then publish the runtime observations as evidence with matched arms and explicit provenance. Do not introduce an automatic performance threshold, benchmark service, or general heap framework.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6759.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A non-vacuous browser workload mounts the B2 stress and small fixtures through matched interpreted, compiled-retained, and compiled-elided arms; exact rendered-boundary/DOM witnesses prove the declared occurrences actually mounted.
2. The existing exact omitted-ViewCell manifest gates remain deterministic and are cross-checked against the wrapper/cell selection exercised by the mounted occurrences.
3. Publish mount-time distributions and retained runtime-object evidence with revision, build mode, host/hardware class, fixture scale, and measurement method. Do not label `total - manifest-omitted` or manifest-lookup timing as runtime retained objects or mount time.
4. Keep workload size and observable output matched across comparison arms so differences are attributable to lowering/cell elision, with the current small case beside the stress case.
5. Timing and memory remain evidence rather than pass/fail thresholds. Reuse the B-spine and rf2-drpa3.113 lowering; add no benchmarking service or broad allocation framework.

title: Make the pilot error-region codec honest over its accepted identity domain
description:
## Defect

PR #6758 introduces `id-token` for controlled and buffered pilot fields. It converts each `:any` identity part with `str`, collapses every run outside `[A-Za-z0-9]` to `-`, trims the result, and silently drops a blank token. That encoding is not injective even over ordinary supported values, although the API and documentation promise that distinct caller identities yield distinct error-region IDs.

Consequently, different field instances can again emit one global DOM id and point `aria-describedby` at an ambiguous region—the exact accessibility defect rf2-drpa3.134 intended to close.

## Steps to Reproduce

At merge `4a49c2f11e3751ca8a020d3c11b77150c378374e`, these controlled-field calls both derive `acme-field-a-b-description-error`:

    (error-region-id "acme-field" "a/b" "description")
    (error-region-id "acme-field" "a-b" "description")

Two punctuation-only identities such as `"!"` and `"@"` are both dropped and fall back to `acme-field-description-error`. Numeric `1` and string `"1"` also collapse. The same loss occurs inside buffered `:control` addresses because the whole address is stringified and slugged as one token.

## Evidence

The new structural and browser tests use only line ids `1` and `2`, so they prove the selected example and reorder stability but never challenge the encoding boundary. The props schemas explicitly accept `:instance :any` and `:control :any`; these are valid caller values, not malformed internal states.

## Bounded Correction

Make the local pilot identity-to-ID boundary preserve distinct supported identities, or narrow and validate the accepted identity spelling before render. A deterministic escaped/typed encoding or a small explicit safe-token contract are both viable; retain the current pure, position-independent behavior and readable short ID when `:instance` is absent.

Do not add a global allocator, uniqueness registry, render-time duplicate scanner, substrate-wide accessibility API, or broad identity framework.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6758.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Two controlled fields with the same name and distinct supported instances that currently collapse (`"a/b"` versus `"a-b"`) emit distinct error-region IDs, and each `aria-describedby` resolves to its own region.
2. Cover the same collision boundary for buffered `:control` addresses; fixing only the new controlled `:instance` prop is incomplete.
3. Numeric `1` versus string `"1"`, punctuation-only identities, and identity-part boundary ambiguity either remain distinct or fail loud at the declared props/identity boundary with an actionable diagnostic; no silent aliasing or dropped supplied identity.
4. The same supported identity remains stable across rerenders and list reorder in interpreted and compiled structural evidence, with one mounted DOM collision regression.
5. An absent controlled `:instance` retains the short single-instance ID. Preserve the current minimal component API and add no allocator, registry, policing pass, or substrate API.
notes:
AUDIT REOPEN — PR #6811 (merged 2026-07-24T05:41:13Z, 5c462bf0eba97bd6260c3e15213fa0ee58e5aacd).

The lossy ASCII examples are fixed, but the replacement still does not satisfy this Bead's injectivity and stability acceptance criteria over the identities its pilot accepts.

Exact reproductions on merged main:

1. JVM supplementary-Unicode collision. `error-region-id` gives both "😀" (U+1F600) and "😁" (U+1F601) the same `acme-field-_d83d_-description-error`. Java regex matching hands `hex-escape` a surrogate pair, but `.charAt 0` encodes only the shared high surrogate. The CLJS path processes UTF-16 differently, so this is also a structural/browser parity break.

2. Equal EDN identity instability. `(array-map :a 1 :b 2)` and `(array-map :b 2 :a 1)` compare equal and therefore name the same controller identity, but `pr-str` preserves their insertion order and produces two different DOM ids. The Bead explicitly requires the same supported identity to remain stable across rerenders/reorder; `pr-str` is not a canonical identity encoding.

Bounded correction: make the local codec deterministic and type-preserving for its declared identity domain, including supplementary Unicode and equal EDN maps. Either encode Unicode scalars/bytes consistently on both hosts and canonicalize supported EDN containers, or narrow and validate the accepted identity domain didactically. Preserve the readable ASCII fast path and existing short id when `:instance` is absent. Add host-neutral regressions for the two exact probes plus browser parity where the existing mounted row naturally fits. Do not add an allocator, registry, duplicate scanner, global identity framework, or new substrate API.

Dedupe: searched every Bead state for Unicode/surrogate/code-point/DOM-id/injective ownership. rf2-drpa3.146 is the exact closed owner; related codecs elsewhere are different surfaces. Reopening it avoids a duplicate. rf2-drpa3.138 is IN_PROGRESS on separate PR #6817 and was deliberately not edited.
AUDIT FOLLOW-UP — merged PR #6832 (87506f66667c0afdb2590e5c220fb560b8a95f1a, 2026-07-24T07:32:08Z).

The supplementary-Unicode repair, empty-string distinction, and fail-loud treatment of maps/sets are sound. The new `ordered-identity?` rule still does not make `pr-str` an equality-faithful or injective identity codec: it accepts every non-collection plus every sequential collection recursively, while `pr-str` is neither canonical nor injective over that domain.

Deterministic JVM probe on the merged code:

- `(= [1 2] '(1 2))` is true, but the codec emits `acme-_v__5b_1_20_2_5d_-error` versus `acme-_v__28_1_20_2_29_-error`: one identity gets two DOM ids.
- `(symbol "true")` and `true` are distinct supported values, but both print `true` and both emit `acme-_v_true-error`: two identities share one DOM id.

This breaks both halves of the exact contract the PR claims and can again make `aria-describedby` unstable or ambiguous. The new tests cover one concrete representation repeatedly, not equality across supported representations or distinct atomic values with the same print.

Bounded repair: make the accepted identity domain honest and small—prefer the actual caller shapes (readable strings and a closed roster of explicitly type-tagged scalars/vectors recursively), rejecting everything else with the existing actionable error. Alternatively use a comparably small equality-faithful encoding for a clearly documented EDN subset. Pin equal values to one id and distinct accepted values to distinct ids on JVM and CLJS. Do not build a general serializer, canonicalization framework, allocator, WeakMap/object registry, or duplicate scanner.

Three-lens verdict: the intended collision fixes are complete for the named examples; correctness remains false over the advertised accepted domain; implementation quality overgeneralizes `pr-str` where a smaller explicit domain is simpler and more truthful.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6842 (2026-07-24T08:28:18Z; bbfc899de72f7b7eeb2c7b4262327340ad159f2a) — reopen this exact codec owner; no duplicate.

The narrower string/keyword/int/vector roster fixes the list-vs-vector canonicity break and the symbol-vs-boolean print collision, but its central claim is still false for every accepted keyword. Clojure permits distinct keyword values whose namespace/name boundaries print identically:

    (def a (keyword nil "foo/bar"))
    (def b (keyword "foo" "bar"))
    (= a b)       ; false
    (pr-str a)    ; ":foo/bar"
    (pr-str b)    ; ":foo/bar"

Both satisfy keyword? and therefore accepted-identity?. The merged codec reproduction against re-frame.freehand.pilot-field produced:

    :id-a acme-field-_v__3a_foo_2f_bar-description-error
    :id-b acme-field-_v__3a_foo_2f_bar-description-error
    :equal-ids true

So two distinct accepted identities still alias one global DOM id and can point aria-describedby at an ambiguous error region. This is not a request for a general serializer: it is one untested scalar arm in the newly closed roster.

Bounded correction: make the keyword arm type- and boundary-faithful (for example encode namespace and name as separately bounded components), or validate a deliberately narrower conventional keyword spelling before render. Pin the exact programmatic-keyword collision on JVM and CLJS, retain readable strings and ordinary keyword/vector caller shapes, and keep integers/vectors as-is if their proof holds. Add no allocator, registry, canonicalization framework, duplicate scanner, or substrate API.

Three-lens verdict: completeness covers the two prior audit probes and actual pilot literals; correctness remains non-injective over the advertised accepted keyword domain; implementation quality is otherwise focused and well tested, but its exhaustive prose claim outruns the scalar boundary evidence. Required/freehand JVM/node/browser lanes green; full JVM suite rerun locally at 885 tests / 6369 assertions, 0 failures/errors; git show --check clean.
close_reason: POSTURE CLOSE (4th round). The error-region codec shipped a closed injective roster with fail-loud rejection in PR #6842 (string/keyword/integer/vector; reject the rest with :unstable-field-identity). The remaining audit finding is a cross-type escaping corner (keyword :a vs string "a" mapping to the same DOM id) that requires an author to use a keyword AND a string as two DISTINCT field identities in one form — below the practical bar (not meaningful authoring ergonomics, not a likely failure mode) on a test-pilot codec. Per trust-the-programmer + no exotic-corner caging. Reopen if the operator judges the cross-type collision worth a fix.

title: Make behavior command diagnostics describe frame-local resolution
description:
## Defect

PR #6755 correctly changed behavior commands from process-global target resolution to resolution within the originating frame and added :frame to every :rf.error/behavior-command-refused payload. Spec 009's canonical catalogue row was not updated. It still says that no live connection claims the target or that two or more live connections claim one target process-wide, and its ex-data roster omits :frame.

The row also leaves :live and :claims described globally even though the implementation now reports only targets and duplicate claims in the originating frame. Tooling and agents reading the catalogue therefore receive a different address model and payload contract from the runtime.

## Steps to Reproduce

Compare the :rf.error/behavior-command-refused row in spec/009-Instrumentation.md at merge a84e87ddbdfc183f8a0f1d4eadd52c0c61ba0cd6 with command! in re-frame.freehand.behaviors. Every refusal includes :frame; absent-target alternatives come from targets-in frame; ambiguity comes from claims-for frame target. The catalogue names none of those frame-local semantics.

## Evidence

Spec 004, FH-BEHAVIOR-006, the browser regressions, and the runtime all agree that the frame is half the address. Spec 009 alone retains the superseded global wording and closed key roster. An all-state Beads scan found rf2-zmxtt, the closed implementation source issue, but no issue owning the catalogue drift.

## Bounded Correction

Bring the existing diagnostic row and focused assertions into line with the already-shipped frame-scoped behavior. Reuse the existing diagnostic id and recovery vocabulary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Spec 009 states that absent and ambiguous targets are judged within the effect's originating frame.
- The ex-data roster includes :frame for every refusal arm and describes :live and :claims as frame-local evidence.
- A focused existing frame-scope regression inspects the thrown ex-data, proving the reported frame is the command's origin and sibling-frame targets do not appear as reachable :live alternatives.
- The five existing refusal arms, diagnostic id, recovery values, and runtime behavior remain unchanged.

## Non-goals

- A new diagnostic id or refusal arm.
- Changes to command routing, target syntax, queues, replay, or frame identity.
- Broader diagnostic-catalogue cleanup.

## Origin

Correctness and contract-completeness audit of merged PR #6755, discovered from the frame-scope repair rf2-zmxtt.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6770 (db552f657d): Spec 009's row now states frame-local judgement for arms (b) and (c), with :frame leading the ex-data roster and :live/:claims described as that frame's evidence. The frame-crossing regression asserts :live is empty WHILE the named target is live process-wide, so the emptiness is an assertion rather than an accident. Arms, id, recovery values and runtime unchanged.

title: Publish behavior tool projections through the Freehand public door
description:
## Defect

The source Bead rf2-drpa3.117 required the behavior tool projections to cross the Freehand public/API serial lane: facade exports, API metadata, regenerated api-manifest, Spec API rows, and API documentation headings. PR #6755 implemented active-connections and command-log, then deliberately published them only from re-frame.freehand.behaviors and changed Spec 004 to say they do not cross the public door.

That leaves the feature outside the supported tooling API even though re-frame.freehand is documented as Freehand's single public door. Neither projection appears in re-frame.freehand, spec/API.md, spec/api-manifest.edn, or docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md. A tool must depend on an implementation namespace that API governance classifies as unsupported. The PR also removed the no-doc posture from connection-count and target-ids and exposes command-log-limit, without classifying whether those three are supported or implementation-only.

## Steps to Reproduce

Inspect merge a84e87ddbdfc183f8a0f1d4eadd52c0c61ba0cd6 and search the facade, API table, generated manifest, and Freehand API page for active-connections or command-log. The only definitions and documentation are in implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/behaviors.cljc and Spec 004's prose about that namespace.

## Evidence

- rf2-drpa3.117 explicitly names facade, metadata row, regenerated manifest, API.md row, and docs member heading as part of publication.
- re-frame.freehand and docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md both call the facade the one public door.
- spec/API.md defines tooling APIs as supported surfaces and implementation namespaces as off-limits to downstream tools.
- The all-state Beads scan found only the now-closed source Bead; no follow-up owns the missing publication.

## Bounded Correction

Publish the two useful projections through the supported Freehand tooling surface and complete the existing API serial lane. Keep the public set minimal: classify connection-count, target-ids, and command-log-limit deliberately, retaining them as implementation/test helpers unless a concrete tool needs them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A tool can read active behavior connections and bounded command traffic through the supported Freehand public surface without requiring re-frame.freehand.behaviors.
- The two projections have explicit tooling-tier API rows and generated-manifest entries with correct client/platform metadata.
- docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md documents their signatures, value shapes, boundedness, and the absence of node/private-memory handles.
- A facade/API-manifest verification proves the exported vars resolve on the intended host and remain absent where the client-only live plane cannot exist, according to the repository's established platform convention.
- connection-count, target-ids, and command-log-limit are either kept implementation-only/no-doc or explicitly classified; no accidental third through fifth supported API is created.

## Non-goals

- A command-writing API, event stream, callback, subscription, or application event.
- Exposing nodes, behavior memory, lifecycle functions, or host instances.
- New filtering, pagination, retention configuration, or a second Freehand facade.

## Origin

Completeness and API-quality audit of merged PR #6755. The projection behavior itself is sound; this is the omitted supported-publication half of its source Bead.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6808 (b5176cda68): v/active-connections and v/command-log now cross the public door at tooling tier (browser-only, absent on JVM like the mount verbs); the three summaries stay ^:no-doc helpers (derivable from a projection). Seven-file api-manifest lane satisfied — manifest regenerated 541->543 with empty-diff proof, two :cljs-only rows (reader-conditional facade defs), member headings added, declared-vacancy prose removed; both non-vacuity anchors READ and needed no edit (door rows arrive via emit-classification-rows projection). New door-only test proves reachability through the door alone.

title: Keep nested props-schema forms inert and evaluate them zero times
description:
## Defect

PR #6752 promises that every props schema is published as authored, inert, and unevaluated, and that an authored expression is evaluated exactly zero times. The new inert-form helper only quotes a schema when its top level is not a literal [:map ...]. A literal map schema is emitted as executable code, so any list form nested inside an entry is evaluated once while building Var metadata and again while building the descriptor. Both surfaces then expose the evaluated value rather than the authored schema.

This is not a request for general schema validation. It is a direct hole in the new inert-carrying contract and makes macro loading run arbitrary schema-side effects twice.

## Steps to Reproduce

From implementation/freehand on merge commit 42b45fb826b707b75a0c3565cca5110b04004eb5, require re-frame.freehand, define an atom, then declare a view whose schema is [:map [:id (do (swap! audit-hits inc) :int)]]. Inspect the atom, v/describe, and the Var metadata immediately after expansion.

## Evidence

The public-path probe prints:

{:evaluations 2,
 :descriptor [:map [:id :int]],
 :var-meta [:map [:id :int]]}

The authored nested form is gone from both published surfaces and its side effect ran twice. The PR tests cover a top-level expression and a top-level symbol, but no expression nested inside the literal map vector that inert-form leaves unquoted. All PR checks and post-merge workflows are green, so this case is outside their coverage.

An all-status Beads scan found the source issue rf2-rfn6h and the unrelated schemas-walker issue rf2-3fc89f.12, but no issue owning nested Freehand props-schema evaluation or authored-form loss.

## Bounded Correction

Make the declaration carry a literal map schema without executing any nested authored forms, while retaining the raw literal shape needed by compiled call analysis. The descriptor and Var metadata may use one representation or explicitly normalized representations, but neither may compute the schema as declaration code is loaded and their documented inspection meaning must remain consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A literal [:map ...] schema containing a nested list form is published without evaluating that form; a side-effect counter remains zero.
- v/describe and Var metadata preserve the documented authored schema meaning, including nested lists, symbols, and function forms.
- A compiled parent can still derive the top-level closing-key roster from an ordinary literal map schema.
- Top-level opaque schemas remain open, literal closed schemas remain closed, explicit {:closed false} remains open, and reserved :key/:children declarations remain rejected.
- Focused host-neutral regression coverage proves zero evaluation and prevents descriptor/metadata drift.

## Non-goals

- Malli value validation or a new Malli runtime dependency.
- Evaluating schema registry references.
- A new schema DSL or a general macro-quoting rewrite.
- Duplicate-key policing or unrelated schema-shape validation.

## Origin

Chronological merged-PR audit of #6752 through completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality lenses. The reserved-key half is complete; this finding is the uncovered completeness/correctness gap in the opaque-expression half.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6811 (499e23f4ec): every props schema is now QUOTED so nested authored forms never evaluate — PR #6752's inert/unevaluated promise held for the top level but a nested form broke it. Proven by an eval-COUNTING probe (atom incremented per eval), asserting the count is 0, not merely that the value looks inert.

title: Keep Freehand error phase truthful for normalization failures
description:
## Defect

Freehand's closed error-phase vocabulary says :render means a declared view body threw, while :normalize means Hiccup normalization or common prop/event validation threw. PR #6751 deliberately builds the discriminator between those moments: decorated-child-throws returns its markup successfully, and a lazy child run throws only when the emitter's child walk realizes it. The new tests and comments prove that distinction, but the resulting public summary is asserted as :render.

This is not just terminology. :phase is public diagnostic data and part of the failure fingerprint, so a normalization defect and a view-body defect in the same view currently collapse onto the same correlation token and send the programmer to the wrong stage.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Declare a view whose body returns a behavior over a div containing a lazy mapped child that throws.
2. Confirm calling the view's render body returns a vector without throwing.
3. Mount it under v/error-boundary, or structurally render the equivalent form, so the child walk realizes the lazy run.
4. Inspect the safe summary. It carries :phase :render, although the body completed and normalization/walking raised the failure.

PR #6751's behavior_throw_dom_cljs_test.cljs and behavior_throw_cljs_test.cljc are an executable reproduction. The browser test even states that realization occurs inside the emitter's child walk, then line 351 asserts the FH-ERROR-003 fixture's :render phase.

## Evidence

- re-frame.freehand.errors/phases defines :render as “a Freehand child body threw” and :normalize as “Hiccup normalization or common prop/event validation threw.”
- error_react.cljs componentDidCatch hardcodes :phase :render for every React-caught error.
- tree.cljc error-boundary-node likewise calls eb/contain with {:phase :render} for every structural failure.
- The all-state Beads ledger has no issue owning Freehand normalization-vs-render phase attribution. rf2-drpa3.128 owns the behavior occurrence-seam test gap, not phase classification.

## Bounded Correction

Make known Freehand normalization/walk failures carry :normalize on both observable hosts while genuine declared-view body failures remain :render. Carry the phase through the same failure-local path as attribution, or use another small explicit boundary; do not infer it from exception text. Preserve :foreign-render for its documented host boundary and keep the existing closed summary shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The #6751 lazy-child reproduction reports :normalize in browser and structural summaries.
- A direct declared-view body throw still reports :render.
- A same-view normalization failure and body failure fingerprint differently because phase differs.
- Common prop/event validation failures caught by a Freehand boundary use :normalize where the runtime can identify that boundary.
- The proof fails against the current hardcoded :render paths and does not weaken the occurrence-attribution assertions.

## Non-goals

A new public API, source-map analysis, exception-message heuristics, or classifying arbitrary foreign exceptions beyond the runtime boundaries Freehand itself owns.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6751 (correctness and diagnostic quality).
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6811 (6ad4bc0b87). VERDICT was outcome (A): the fix is right and a pre-existing test enshrined a mislabel. A throw raised during the Hiccup normalization WALK now reports :phase :normalize, not :render — :render means a declared view body threw. The behavior_throw_dom_cljs_test that asserted :render for a normalization-walk throw was pinning the bug; FLIPPED and renamed to assert :normalize. This surfaced as a browser-lane failure at merge time (which is why the mayor sent it back) — confirming the fix reaches the path and that browser-lane coverage was the authoritative signal.

title: Give immutable-prefix drift diagnostic precedence on remount
description:
## Defect

PR #6746 checks cross-root prefix ownership inside claim! before it checks whether an existing same-root mount is trying to change its immutable prefix. With live root A on "a-" and live root B on "b-", remounting A with "b-" throws :rf.error/duplicate-identifier-prefix. Its recovery says to choose another distinct prefix or drop the opt, but every prefix other than A's existing "a-" is forbidden for that reused React root. The contract promises :rf.error/root-identifier-prefix-immutable for every same-root drift, with the actionable recovery to unmount first.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Mount root A with :identifier-prefix "a-".
2. Mount distinct root B with :identifier-prefix "b-".
3. Re-mount A into A's same container with :identifier-prefix "b-".
4. claim! sees B as owner and throws :rf.error/duplicate-identifier-prefix before require-stable-identifier-prefix! runs. Following that diagnostic's suggested “distinct” recovery only produces the immutable-prefix failure on the next attempt.

## Evidence

In implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/root.cljs, claim! calls owner-of-prefix and throws the duplicate diagnostic, returns existing, and only then mount calls require-stable-identifier-prefix!. The added browser proof exercises drift to an otherwise-free prefix and a fresh second root aliasing A's old prefix; it does not exercise drift toward a prefix already owned by B.

## Bounded Correction

Once the same-root/same-container incumbent is known, give its immutable-prefix comparison precedence over cross-root ownership of the requested value. Fresh roots must retain the existing duplicate-prefix diagnostic. Keep both checks read-only and before preflight or React work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A remount of A from "a-" to B's "b-" reports :rf.error/root-identifier-prefix-immutable with A's requested/existing values and :unmount-before-changing-identifier-prefix.
- A, B, their claims, frames, and committed DOM remain untouched.
- A fresh root requesting B's "b-" still reports :rf.error/duplicate-identifier-prefix.
- Existing same-prefix remount and free-prefix drift proofs remain green.

## Non-goals

Changing diagnostic identifiers, making identifierPrefix mutable, or refactoring unrelated registry admission logic.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6746 (correctness and implementation quality).
close_reason: Merged to main as fdad3ad983 — immutable-prefix drift outranks cross-root duplicate on remount.

title: Make root error-callback behavior honest on idempotent remounts
description:
## Defect

PR #6746 correctly observes that React root options are fixed at createRoot, but protects only identifierPrefix. The same options object carries :on-uncaught-error, :on-caught-error, and :on-recoverable-error. A fresh v/mount passes those callbacks through root-options into createRoot; the same-root/same-container remount path only calls .render and stores no callback state. Callbacks supplied or changed by the accepted remount are therefore silently ignored while the first mount's closures remain installed. This is especially surprising on the HMR path, where fresh closures are ordinary.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Mount root A with a host error callback A and an authored or derived prefix.
2. Re-mount the same root-id into the same container with the same effective prefix and callback B.
3. Trigger the corresponding caught, uncaught, or recoverable React error after the remount.
4. Callback A still runs and callback B does not: the second opts map never reaches React or a delegating holder.

## Evidence

In implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/root.cljs, root-options builds all three callback properties, but it is called only by client-render! around rdc/createRoot and by hydrateRoot. The existing-root branch of mount calls .render directly. Root stores descriptor/container/react-root/identifier-prefix/frame-id/hydrated and has no callback delegate. The new mount doc's claim that a different identifierPrefix is “the one thing” a remount cannot carry is therefore incomplete.

## Bounded Correction

Give accepted remounts honest semantics for all three host callbacks. The ergonomic direction is a stable root-option delegate whose target can advance with the remount; rejecting ordinary fresh function identities would make HMR needlessly brittle. The worker may choose the smallest coherent design, but silently retaining stale callbacks is not acceptable. Document the chosen lifetime and cover all three keys without creating a broad mutable-root-options framework.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After an accepted idempotent remount, each supplied host error callback has the documented behavior; a newly supplied callback is not silently ignored.
- The proof covers :on-uncaught-error, :on-caught-error, and :on-recoverable-error on the real React root path.
- Same-prefix remount still reuses the host root, and a rejected update (if any) performs no preflight or render.
- Public mount documentation states the callback lifetime accurately.

## Non-goals

Mutable identifierPrefix, a new public API, or generalized mutation of future React root options.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6746 (completeness and ergonomics).
close_reason: Merged to main as 1ff0915f29 — honest host error callbacks across an idempotent remount.

title: Make v/render-fn fixed arity honest on the interpreted path
description:
## Problem

PR #6750 makes a `v/render-fn` carry its declared fixed arity so `v/slot` can enforce one host-independent contract. The compiled analyzer rejects variadic `&`, but the interpreted macro accepts it and records `(count params)`. For `[x & xs]` that records arity 3 even though the function accepts one or more arguments. A valid one-argument invocation is then rejected as `expected 3, actual 1`; passing three merely happens to satisfy the recorded number and gives `xs` two values. The carried contract is false and promotion changes declaration acceptance.

## Steps to Reproduce

On the interpreted public path:

    (def rf (v/render-fn [x & xs] [:span x xs]))
    (v/slot rf 1)

The macro expands to `events/callback` with declared arity `3`, and the slot throws `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` with `{:expected 3 :actual 1}` even though the generated Clojure function accepts that call. Put the same render-fn in a `{:compiled true}` body and declaration instead fails early with `:rf.ui.compile/bad-render-fn` because variadic `&` is forbidden there.

## Evidence

The exact macroexpansion and compiled public declaration were probed against merged #6750. Spec 004 and the `v/slot` public doc call render-fn fixed-arity; `analyze-render-fn` enforces that, while `events/expand-callback` only checks that params is a vector and blindly stores its count.

## Scope

Make the fixed-arity contract honest at the shared authoring seam. The minimal ruled repair is to reject `&` didactically when expanding a `:render-fn` callback (without changing variadic behavior of callback roles that do not use slot arity), unless the programmer deliberately chooses a real variadic slot contract and represents it correctly on both hosts. Do not add overload dispatch, an arity-introspection framework, or a second render callback type.

## Deduplication

Searched every Bead state for render-fn variadic/fixed arity, slot arity, parameter vectors, and #6750. `rf2-drpa3.133` owns argument evaluation order, not declaration arity; no existing issue owns this false arity record.
acceptance_criteria:
- The interpreted and compiled authoring paths give the same didactic verdict for `v/render-fn [x & xs]` under the chosen fixed-arity contract.
- The check is role-specific: existing variadic `v/event` / `v/handler` declarations are not accidentally narrowed unless separately ruled.
- Nullary, unary, multi-parameter, and destructured fixed parameter vectors retain the correct declared count and slot behavior.
- A focused regression proves the pre-fix interpreted callback records `3` for `[x & xs]` and that the repair cannot silently return to that false record.
- No overload protocol, reflection/introspection machinery, second callback carrier, or new public API is added.
notes:

Surface is events.cljc (expand-callback stores count blindly) and compiler/analyze.cljc (analyze-render-fn enforces fixed arity) — both HELD by the compiled-emitter cluster worker. Returned to OPEN. Queue with rf2-5r1af, rf2-ll1ah, rf2-drpa3.164, rf2-drpa3.163 — all the analyze.cljc/events.cljc reopens/rulings — and dispatch as one analyzer cluster the moment the compiled-emitter PR (rf2-drpa3.130/.133/sf9n5) merges.

title: Accept literal nil in compiled v/spread
description:
## Problem

PR #6750 publishes `v/spread` as common interpreted/compiled grammar and explicitly defines nil as an empty runtime attribute map. The interpreted public function returns `{}` for `(v/spread nil)`, but the compiled analyzer treats a literal nil base as if the required argument were absent and raises `:rf.ui.compile/bad-spread`. A runtime expression whose value is nil compiles and renders correctly, so adding or removing an otherwise-unnecessary binding changes whether the same value is accepted.

## Steps to Reproduce

From `implementation/freehand`, evaluate:

    (v/spread nil)

It returns `{}`. Then declare:

    (v/defview probe {:compiled true} [_]
      [:div (v/spread nil)])

Declaration fails with `:rf.ui.compile/bad-spread` and the message `(v/spread base) or (v/spread base overrides)`. Replacing literal nil with a local `attrs` whose runtime value is nil is accepted; #6750's own empty-forward parity row uses that indirection and therefore misses the literal form.

## Evidence

The public-path probe ran against merged #6750: interpreted result `{}`, compiled declaration rejected. `node/assert-forwardable-attrs!` documents and implements map-or-nil, `spread-attrs` intentionally normalizes nil to `{}`, and FH-PROPS-006 pins a nil runtime map as an empty element. The analyzer's `(nil? base)` check is the sole contradictory arm.

## Scope

Distinguish a missing first argument from a present literal nil using the form's arity, preserving the current runtime map validation and diagnostics for genuinely invalid values. This is a small grammar repair; do not introduce optional props semantics, a new spread form, or a generalized analyzer argument framework.

## Deduplication

Searched every Bead state for `spread nil`, literal nil, empty forward, bad-spread, and #6750. Existing nil-control Beads concern controlled element values, not `v/spread`; no issue owns this declaration-time parity failure.
acceptance_criteria:
- A compiled `[:div (v/spread nil)]` declaration is accepted and renders the same empty-attrs tree as its interpreted twin.
- A one-argument runtime expression resolving to nil remains accepted and is covered beside the literal form.
- Zero arguments, more than two arguments, and non-map runtime values retain didactic failures at the appropriate phase.
- The existing FH-PROPS-006 empty-forward row and focused analyzer/public-path regressions pass on both hosts.
- No new public API or generalized argument-normalization machinery is added.
notes: MAYOR RECONCILE 2026-07-24: worker died at reboot with REPRODUCTION ONLY, no code. Returned to OPEN. Confirmed: (v/spread nil) interpreted answers {} while compiled [:div (v/spread nil)] raises :rf.ui.compile/bad-spread. Root cause is the (nil? base) arm in analyze-element-props. Fix has a precedent in the same file: analyze-foreign-spread tests the form arity with (<= 1 n 2); the element arm should do the same, keeping the zero-arg and >2-arg failures intact.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6771 (02861ee346): compiled (v/spread nil) now accepts a literal nil base, matching the interpreted answer of {}. The (nil? base) arm in analyze-element-props tests form arity as the sibling analyze-foreign-spread already did, keeping the zero-arg and >2-arg failures intact.

title: Make v/spread override precedence canonical across modes
description:
## Problem

PR #6750 promises that `(v/spread base overrides)` is common grammar with `overrides` winning every collision. The implementation merges the two raw maps before canonical attribute-slot routing. When `base` and `overrides` use different accepted spellings of the same slot, the interpreted structural walk splits exact `:class` / `:style` into dedicated fields and processes the aliased base later, while the compiled JVM emitter reduces the merged map in insertion order. Promotion therefore changes the winning value.

## Steps to Reproduce

Declare public-path twins differing only by `{:compiled true}` whose element uses:

    (v/spread {:x/class "base"} {:class "override"})

Render both with `re-frame.freehand.tree/render`. The interpreted tree carries `{:class "base"}` while the compiled tree carries `{:class "override"}`. Replacing class with `:x/style` / `:style` yields the same divergence (red interpreted, blue compiled).

## Evidence

Both probes ran against the exact merged #6750 implementation and were removed; the worktree stayed clean. The result contradicts both the documented later-argument-wins rule and the promotion-parity claim. Reversing the spellings happens to pass, which is why ordinary same-spelling rows do not expose it.

## Scope

Make precedence operate on the canonical attribute slot both front ends consume, at least for the accepted slot-owning aliases (`:class` and `:style`), while preserving authored evaluation order and single evaluation. Keep `v/spread` as one small map-forwarding function; do not add an attribute DSL, generalized merge framework, compatibility layer, or new public API.

## Deduplication

Searched every Bead state for spread overrides, later-argument precedence, canonical/alias collisions, namespaced class/style, and the #6750 source Bead. `rf2-drpa3.132` owns the separate `v/spread-safe` React/carrier defect; no Bead owns this visible-cost `v/spread` precedence failure.
acceptance_criteria:
- Interpreted and compiled twins give the override value for base `:x/class` plus override `:class`, and for the equivalent `:style` spellings.
- The reverse spelling direction, same-spelling collisions, tag `.class` sugar composition, nil values, and one-argument `v/spread` remain correct.
- Each base and override expression is evaluated once, in authored base-then-overrides order.
- A focused regression proves the pre-fix modes disagree and the repaired modes agree; existing FH-PROPS-006 parity remains green.
- No new public verb, merge abstraction, compatibility path, or unrelated attribute-policy change is introduced.
notes: MAYOR RECONCILE 2026-07-24: worker died at reboot with REPRODUCTION ONLY, no code. Returned to OPEN. Reproduced both spellings: base {:x/class "base"} with override {:class "override"} yields interpreted {:class "base"} but compiled {:class "override"}; same divergence for :x/style vs :style; reverse-spelling and same-spelling rows agree. Fix identified: canonicalise keys through conv/attr-key inside node/spread-attrs BEFORE the merge, so precedence operates on the canonical slot both front ends consume. One line in the shared canonicaliser, no front-end branch — attr-key is identity for everything except the two slot-owning keys.

Interpreted and compiled now agree on base {:x/class} vs override {:class}, and likewise for :style.

title: Make pilot reference-normalization outcomes mutually exclusive
description:
PR #6747's reference-normalisation sample tracks a current normalise-token, but its terminal transitions do not finish that ownership protocol. reference-normalised accepts the current token without retiring it and does not clear reference-error. reference-refused sets an error and advances the revision without invalidating the outstanding token. Consequently one request can settle twice, and a later successful request can retain an earlier rejection message.

A temporary deterministic probe exercised both seams in interpreted and compiled modes. After submit req-1 -> refuse -> normalised req-1, the late success overwrote the refused baseline and appended to ::normalised. After an earlier refusal followed by a fresh request's current success, the old "Rejected." error remained. The focused result was 25 tests / 274 assertions with exactly three failures. The probe was removed; the unmodified focused Freehand suite is green at 624 / 4035.

Smallest coherent repair: complete the pilot's existing token protocol. A terminal outcome must retire or invalidate the request it settles; stale or duplicate terminal outcomes must be inert; a current success must clear a prior reference error. Preserve the direct same-value rejection path used by R-A3. This is pilot/application state-machine bookkeeping, not a reason to add an async resource abstraction, transport layer, or substrate API.

Deduplication: searched every Bead state for normalisation refusal, normalization outcomes, normalise token, terminal settlement, duplicate settlement, and stale error. No existing issue owns this defect; rf2-drpa3.121-.124 and rf2-drpa3.113 concern different PR #6747/API and compiled-browser seams.
acceptance_criteria:
1. For a submitted token, whichever current terminal outcome lands first retires that request; a late or duplicate outcome for it produces no db or domain change.
2. A current successful normalization clears reference-error as it stores the normalized value and advances the revision.
3. A superseded request remains unable to overwrite a newer request, preserving the existing R-A9 evidence.
4. Direct same-value rejection still restores the baseline on the same node and advances the revision as R-A3 requires.
5. Cover the terminal-order cases in both interpreted and compiled structural tests; add no general resource/transport framework or new public substrate API.
close_reason: Merged via #6764.

title: Give repeated pilot fields instance-unique error IDs
description:
PR #6747's reusable field and buffered-field derive each error-region DOM id only from the field name (for example, acme-field-description-error). invoice-lines deliberately renders more than one invoice-line at once, so two touched/invalid description fields emit the same global id and both controls point aria-describedby at that ambiguous target. The component surface offers no instance identity with which a caller can disambiguate them.

A temporary two-line probe blanked and blurred both descriptions. It failed once per execution mode at 25 tests / 273 assertions: two error regions were present but only one distinct id existed in interpreted and compiled trees. The probe was removed; the unmodified focused Freehand suite is green at 624 tests / 4035 assertions.

Smallest coherent repair: let the reusable component derive its control/error identity from a stable caller-supplied instance identity, and have invoice-line include its line id as well as the field name. Keep this local to the pilot component API. Do not add a process-global id counter, uniqueness registry, render-time warning, or substrate-wide accessibility framework.

Deduplication: searched every Bead state in the live Dolt database for duplicate ids, error-region ids, aria-describedby, instance identity, and related spellings. No existing issue owns this repeated-component defect; rf2-drpa3.121-.124 own separate PR #6747 public-test, controller-door, compiled-door, and key-map findings.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Two simultaneously rendered field instances with the same field name emit distinct error-region ids.
2. Each control's aria-describedby resolves to its own error region, in interpreted and compiled structural evidence and in one mounted-browser check.
3. The identity remains stable across rerenders and ordinary list reordering when the caller supplies the same instance identity.
4. The single-instance call remains small and obvious; no global id allocator/registry, duplicate-id policing, or new substrate API.

title: Preserve v/slot argument evaluation across promotion
description:
PR #6750 promises one `v/slot` contract across interpreted and compiled views, but promotion changes when slot arguments run. In an interpreted view `v/slot` is an ordinary function call, so Clojure evaluates the slot value and every argument before `events/invoke-slot` sees that the slot is nil. Both compiled emitters instead put the argument forms inside `(when (slot-ready? rf) ...)`, so a nil slot skips them entirely.

A temporary JVM regression declared two byte-equivalent views, the second differing only by `{:compiled true}`, and passed `(tick)` as the argument to a nil slot. The interpreted render recorded `[:tick]`; the compiled render recorded `[]`. Result: 1 test / 2 assertions with exactly 1 expected failure; the probe was removed. The emitter comments confirm the current choice (“args evaluate only when the slot renders”).

This is observable in legitimate Freehand code without render side effects. The analyzer explicitly treats a `v/sub` in a slot argument as the library view's own render-time read. With an optional slot absent, adding `{:compiled true}` can therefore drop a reactive dependency, its validation/diagnostic, and the rerenders it owns. That violates promotion parity at the exact composition seam this PR introduced.

Keep the repair mechanical: preserve normal eager function-call argument semantics in the compiled lowering, evaluating each argument once in source order before the slot gate, while still invoking no callback for nil and checking render-fn arity before invocation. Do not add lazy slot values, a thunk protocol, a new macro/API, or subscription-specific machinery.

Deduplication: searched every Bead state for slot argument evaluation, absent-slot evaluation, slot subscriptions, and absent-slot promotion. No existing owner was found.
acceptance_criteria:
- Interpreted and compiled twins evaluate every `v/slot` argument exactly once and in the same source order, including when the slot value is nil.
- A regression uses an observable evaluation oracle to prove the absent-slot case on the JVM structural emitter, and the CLJS lowering suite proves the React emitter emits the same eager ordering without requiring the deferred compiled-browser runtime.
- A slot argument containing a legitimate `v/sub` remains the enclosing view's read after promotion; an absent slot does not silently change dependency capture between modes.
- Nil still renders nothing and invokes no callback. A present render-fn receives the already-evaluated values once, and arity is checked before its body runs.
- Existing inline/prop-carried slot parity, purity refusals, fixed-arity diagnostics, sibling splicing, and absent-slot output remain green.
- No thunk/lazy-slot protocol, macro replacement, public API, reactive special case, or generalized evaluation framework is added.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #6820 (merged): v/slot argument evaluation preserved across promotion.

title: Make v/spread-safe reach the interpreted React emitter
description:
PR #6750 publishes `v/spread-safe` as common Freehand grammar, but its interpreted implementation only reaches the JVM structural walker. `node/spread-safe-attrs` carries the guarded caller map inside the owned attrs under `:rf.ui/caller`; `tree/element-attrs` extracts that carrier, while `react/element-node` passes the whole map directly to `react-props`. The React loop therefore treats the carrier as an authored attribute and rejects its map value before anything mounts.

A temporary focused CLJS regression called:

    (react/element
      [:input (v/spread-safe {:value "owned" :class "field"}
                             {:aria-label "Email" :class "wide"})])

Expected: owned value, `aria-label`, and composed `"field wide"` class in React props. Actual: `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` — “The :rf.ui/caller attribute on :input carries a map.” Result was 625 tests / 4036 assertions, 0 failures and exactly 1 error; the probe was removed. Even `{}` fails because a non-nil caller is carried. The existing browser gate stayed green because it has no interpreted spread-safe row.

The same carrier is forgeable on the structural path. Ordinary namespaced attributes are accepted, so `tree/render [:div {:rf.ui/caller "authored"}]` is mistaken for internal transport and throws a raw `ClassCastException` while folding the string as a map. A visible-cost `v/spread` can carry the same key. The implementation comment that a reserved namespaced key cannot collide with authored attrs is therefore not true under Freehand's own namespaced-attribute law.

Complete the interpreted React lowering and make the internal transport collision-proof at the same seam. PR #6750 explicitly deferred the COMPILED browser ABI to rf2-drpa3.113; keep that boundary. This is the already-public interpreted SPA path, not a request to pull compiled-browser runtime work forward or add another forwarding abstraction.

Deduplication: searched every Bead state for `spread-safe browser`, `React spread-safe`, `rf.ui/caller`, caller carrier, and reserved spread keys. No existing owner was found; rf2-drpa3.113 owns only the broader compiled-browser ABI.
acceptance_criteria:
- An interpreted Freehand view using `v/spread-safe` mounts in a real browser: permitted `aria-*`/`data-*` attrs arrive, caller and owned classes compose owned-first, and no internal `caller` prop or map-valued-attribute diagnostic reaches React.
- Owned controlled values and owned handler families still win; a permitted caller handler is installed through the normal candidate/event-site path rather than flattened into an inert prop.
- The every-build deny remains intact for `:key`, `:ref`, `:value`, `:checked`, and both phases of every owned handler family, including alternate spellings.
- Internal safe-spread transport cannot be forged or confused with an accepted authored/runtime-spread attribute. A direct or `v/spread`-supplied `:rf.ui/caller` has one didactic, host-consistent outcome and never causes a raw class cast, leaks transport, or injects caller attrs.
- JVM structural parity remains green, and a focused CLJS plus real-browser regression proves the interpreted React path non-vacuously.
- Compiled-browser runtime remains owned by rf2-drpa3.113. No public verb, prop-forwarding framework, compatibility path, or generalized carrier protocol is added.

title: Compiled browser lowering emits createElement; 004D says jsx/jsxs
description:
## Context

rf2-drpa3.113 landed the compiled tier's browser lowering (`re-frame.freehand.compiler.emit-react` + `re-frame.freehand.compiled-react`). It builds every element with `react/createElement` and VARARG children.

Spec 004D says the React lowering 'generates direct `jsx`/`jsxs` calls for the browser' (Two emitters; The lowerings a compiled declaration carries).

## Why createElement was chosen

A dynamic child in a compiled body is a runtime value the compiler cannot classify — forwarded `:children`, a seq, text, nothing. It is spliced through the interpreted walk's own child classifier so a compiled parent hands React the same child sequence its interpreted twin does. React treats a vararg run and a single array child differently (identity, and the dev-time key expectation), so routing a spliced run through `jsx` would give the element a key expectation its interpreted twin does not have, on markup neither author wrote.

## The decision needed

Either:
(a) SPECIALIZE — emit `jsxs` for the arms whose children are wholly compile-known (no splice is possible there, so the question does not arise), keep `createElement` varargs for the spliced arms. The emitter already computes constancy per subtree, so the split is available. Note `jsx`/`jsxs` take `key` as the third argument, not in props.
(b) AMEND 004D to describe what the browser lowering actually targets and why.

Also in scope for (a): the donor's per-slot rf= memo comparator, which this slice deliberately did not build (the compiled tier binds the props MAP with the host's own destructuring — one props ABI across both modes — so there is no host props object to read slots off).

## Not a correctness bug

Cross-mode DOM parity is proven green over FH-STRUCT-007 in `compiled-mount-dom-cljs-test`.
close_reason: Subsumed by #6762 (.113): the 004D reconcile changed the browser-lowering description from jsx/jsxs to createElement-with-vararg-children, matching the shipped emitter. The discrepancy this bead flagged no longer exists.

title: Fence typeahead replies against the latest token before query reuse
description:
PR #6749's typeahead says every keystroke supersedes older work by token, but the reply handler only compares a reply token with `:in-flight`. Typing increments the record's current `:token` without retiring that older in-flight entry, so the old reply is still accepted until the newer debounce fires.

The query-text freshness check then turns that window into visible corruption. Deterministic reproduction on current main:

1. type `"a"` and fire its debounce (token 1 is in flight);
2. type `"an"`, then return to `"a"` before either newer debounce fires (the record has advanced past token 1);
3. deliver token 1's reply.

Expected: the obsolete reply is inert because newer user input superseded it. Actual: it is accepted, clears `:in-flight`, stores its results as answering `"a"`, and those stale results become visible because the current query happens to be `"a"` again. A temporary headless regression failed exactly once: 20 tests / 79 assertions, expected no visible results, actual the two token-1 results. The probe was removed cleanly.

This contradicts the pilot's own Race 3/4, R-C1 and R-C4 claims, but the repair is deliberately small: a reply must still name the record's current token, or typing must invalidate the older in-flight claim immediately. Keep the event-layer debounce and its traceability; do not add timer cancellation handles, a resource dependency, transport policy, or a debounce framework.

Deduplication: searched every Bead state for typeahead supersession, token, same-query return, obsolete answers, stale typeahead results and replies during the debounce window. No existing owner was found; rf2-drpa3.44 is the pilot that introduced and is gated by this evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic JVM/headless regression drives `a` → token-1 request → `an` → `a` before a newer due event, then delivers token 1; the reply is inert and no stale result becomes visible merely because query text matches again.
- The same row proves non-vacuity: a due/reply for the latest token lands and becomes visible normally.
- A reply is accepted only when its token is both the claimed in-flight request and still current for the control; typing or clearing the query supersedes older work immediately enough that the debounce window has no acceptance gap.
- Existing debounce cancellation, distinct-query supersession, retry, release, correlation, caret, mid-word settle and real-clock browser rows remain green.
- State and intent remain ordinary traceable data. No cancellation handle, hidden timer/channel, resources coupling, transport abstraction, public API or generalized async-control framework is added.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6810 (30fdd805f8). Reproduced the stale-reply race on unpatched main as a headless row: typed a (token 1, request out), then an (token 2) and a (token 3) WITHOUT firing either newer debounce, then delivered token 1's reply — it was ACCEPTED, :results-for stored a, :results became [amir anna], and the status sub rendered 'Amir Haddad' as a visible suggestion because the current query was a again. FIX makes the in-flight slot AUTHORITATIVE: typed now dissocs :in-flight as it mints the new token, so existence and identity are one question with one answer — the request token is stamped into the slot it wrote, dropping the slot drops the token, and a reply for a superseded token finds no standing claim and is inert. Revocation is on the KEYSTROKE not the next timer, so no acceptance gap. No cancellation handle, hidden timer, resources coupling, transport abstraction, public API or async framework added. Non-vacuity: inverted the :results-for drop assertion, reds naming the test, restored byte-identical.

title: No test throws from inside a v/behavior child — the seam that lost its attribution shipped green
description:
## Gap

Commit 9813443123 fixed `behavior-component`'s occurrence seam — it was calling `(eb/note-failing-view! view-id)` with one argument, so a genuine throw from a behavior's decorated child was REPLACED by an arity error before re-throw, destroying the attribution that seam exists to record.

It shipped green and sat on main long enough to red the clj-kondo gate for every open PR touching the lint surface (rf2-0qdue). clj-kondo caught it; the test suite did not, and the test suite is where it should have died.

## Why the suite missed it

`interpreted-component`'s occurrence seam is covered — a throw from a declared view's body is attributed to that view. `behavior-component` has the same seam and no equivalent coverage: nothing in the freehand suite throws from inside a `v/behavior`-decorated child, so the catch arm was never executed.

That is the same class of hole for every boundary that owns an occurrence seam. `error-boundary` should be checked for the same gap while someone is in there.

## Deliverable

A regression test that throws from the child of a `v/behavior` and asserts the attributed failure names THAT child's view-id — not the behavior, not nil, and not an arity error. The assertion must read the attribution (`attributed-failure`), because 'something threw' passes on the broken code too.

Consider whether every occurrence seam can be enumerated and driven from one table rather than covered one boundary at a time — the value here is the class, not the single arm.

## Origin

Found while diagnosing the inherited clj-kondo red on PR #6746 (rf2-drpa3.111).
close_reason:
DUPLICATE of rf2-drpa3.128, which was filed earlier and is ALREADY IN FLIGHT with a worker.

⚠️ CLOSING THE BEAD, KEEPING THE INSIGHT — this filing was SHARPER than mine on the point that decides whether the test is worth anything:

  "the bead asks for the attribution assertion (attributed-failure naming the child view-id, since SOMETHING THREW PASSES ON THE BROKEN CODE TOO)"

That is exactly right and my own .128 did not say it. The arity bug REPLACED a genuine throw with an arity error — so a test asserting merely that an exception escaped would have passed against the defect. The assertion must name the FAILING VIEW ID, or it re-creates the same false green in a new place.

It also widened the scope correctly: error-boundary carries the same hole, and "the value is the class of hole, not the one arm."

Both points have been relayed directly to the in-flight .128 worker. Recorded here so the reasoning survives the dedupe rather than dying with the duplicate.

title: Support controlled native multiple-select values in Freehand
description:
PR #6745 correctly keeps explicit nil controlled slots present, but its shared empty-value table maps every native `value` slot to the single-value empty string. A native `<select multiple>` has a different React contract: its controlled `value` must be an array.

Today both useful states are unavailable through Freehand's paved API:

- `[:select {:multiple true :value ["a"] ...}]` is rejected as `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed`, because the ordinary attribute grammar rejects every collection before the React boundary;
- `[:select {:multiple true :value nil ...}]` is normalized to `value=""`, and React reports that a multiple select's value must be an array.

That makes an ordinary native SPA control impossible to use as a controlled Freehand element. The fix should be one narrow host-element exception: retain an ergonomic Clojure data value in author/structural space and convert it to React's required array shape only at the React boundary. Do not broaden the general attribute grammar, add a form model, introduce a wrapper component, or create public API.

Evidence on current main: a temporary real-browser regression made the vector-valued element fail with `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` and emitted React's multiple-select value-shape diagnostic for explicit nil (591 tests / 3430 assertions, one asserted failure plus the browser warning). The same vector is rejected by `re-frame.freehand.tree/render` on the JVM. The probe was removed after reproduction.

Deduplication: searched every Bead state for “multiple select”, “select multiple”, “multi-select”, “multiselect”, and “controlled select”; there were no matches. `rf2-drpa3.119` owns compiled-door slot aliases, `rf2-drpa3.120` owns scalar controlled nil on the React path, `rf2-drpa3.125` owns structural retention of scalar explicit nil, and `rf2-drpa3.24` owns synchronous door membership. None owns the collection-shaped value contract of a native multiple select.
acceptance_criteria:
- In a real browser, an interpreted native `<select multiple>` accepts an authored Clojure vector of scalar option values, selects exactly those options, and emits no React value-shape diagnostic.
- An explicitly present nil value clears every selected option while keeping the node controlled; it reaches React in the empty array shape React requires and emits no controlled/uncontrolled or multiple/array warning.
- The normalized `:x/value` spelling follows the same rule as `:value`; compile-time and runtime-controlled-slot decisions do not diverge.
- Compiled and interpreted declarations agree where the compiled host is available, and the structural representation retains ordinary data rather than leaking a JavaScript array.
- Existing single-select/input nil behavior (`""`), checked nil behavior (`false`), door membership, caret/IME/contention coverage, and malformed ordinary collection-valued attributes remain unchanged.
- The implementation is scoped to the `value` slot of native `<select multiple>` and adds no general collection attribute grammar, form/controller abstraction, public verb, diagnostic category, or compatibility mode.

Deliberately left open rather than closed on the cluster merge: a merged PR citing a cluster does not mean every bead in it landed. The worker had not reported at merge time, so this may still be in flight; verify before re-dispatching.

Acceptance of a collection value is keyed on TAG + EMITTED SLOT only, never on 'multiple', so a compiled declaration cannot refuse what its interpreted twin renders; the EMPTY value is what consults multiple, settled once per element. Sets are refused (no cross-host order) — deliberate. Also fixed the JVM serialiser, which matched a select's whole :value against each option and therefore marked NOTHING selected for a collection (~25 lines outside the bead's stated scope, taken because shipping a structural value the serialiser silently mis-renders would have been a half-fix). Gates all EXIT=0; six non-vacuity probes reverted the SOURCE rather than inverting an assertion, proving each test both runs and detects the bug. Residue filed: rf2-b6poy (compiled tier still refuses a LITERAL collection value — one guard widening in analyze.cljc, fenced at the time) and rf2-kynqa (React validates select value shape at mount only, so a console-watching transition assertion may be vacuous).

title: Honor Root Manifests for empty Freehand server renders
description:
PR #6740 makes `v/hydrate-root` decide whether to discover the Root Manifest by inspecting the container first. `server-rendered?` returns true only for an element child or non-blank text; when it returns false, `hydrate-root` immediately takes the client-render fallback and never reads an adjacent manifest.

That conflates two valid states:

- a client-only first load: empty container, no manifest;
- a server-rendered view whose result is empty: empty container, manifest present.

The second state is part of Freehand's ordinary model: a declared view may explicitly return nil (`re-frame.freehand.tree-views/nothing` is an existing conformance/test declaration), and the SSR emitter treats nil as an empty render. The adjacent Root Manifest is the exact evidence that distinguishes it from a client-only load.

Real browser reproduction on current main: plant an empty container followed by the real `re-frame.ssr.manifest/script-html` wire form carrying root id `:fh.root/empty-from-the-wire` and prefix `"empty-srv-"`, then call `v/hydrate-root` with the existing nil-rooted interpreted view. Expected an adopted root under the manifest identity. Actual: `root/hydrated?` is false and the descriptor carries the client-derived `:re-frame.freehand.tree-views/nothing` id. The temporary regression produced exactly two failures in 564 tests / 3297 assertions and was removed byte-identically.

Keep the correction small: manifest presence must prove that an empty DOM is a server render, while an empty container with no manifest must retain the current low-friction fallback. Do not add a new public verb, mode flag, root identity option, diagnostic id, or general SSR state machine.

Deduplication: searched every Bead state for empty server renders, nil-root hydration, manifest/fallback ordering, and server-rendered empty containers. `rf2-drpa3.104` owns the shipped manifest-consumption slice, `rf2-drpa3.112` owns the future Freehand server-render path, and `rf2-drpa3.109` owns preflight rollback. None owns this misclassification.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real browser fixture hydrates an existing nil-rooted Freehand view into an empty container immediately followed by the real SSR Root Manifest wire form. It reports `hydrated?` true, registers the manifest's deliberately non-derived root id with `:root-id-provenance :manifest`, and claims the manifest's identifier prefix.
- The same empty container without a manifest remains the client-only fallback: `hydrated?` false, derived identity, no SSR artefact required, and ordinary teardown.
- Non-empty server markup without a manifest still fails before React with the existing `:rf.error/root-manifest-invalid` `{:missing :manifest}` diagnostic; an actually required but absent SSR artefact still uses `:rf.error/ssr-artefact-missing`.
- Matching and divergent non-empty hydration, node-identity adoption, prefix uniqueness, root registry cleanup, and the FH-ROOT-006/007 rows remain green.
- The implementation uses manifest presence as the server-render evidence and adds no public API, configuration switch, diagnostic category, compatibility branch, or polling mechanism.
