THE OMISSIONS ARE LARGER THAN THE ERRORS. 14 of the 32 shipped v/ verbs are never mentioned anywhere in the draft: controller-key, controller-revision, controller-current?, defbehavior, behavior, render-static, hydrate-root, describe, manifest, view?, projections, materialize-event, active-connections, command-log. Plus 3 of the 6 t/ names: find, find-all, with-render. The three controller verbs are the sharpest case — semantic-controllers.md is a nine-block chapter that teaches the :control / :reset-key PROPS correctly, scores 0/9 stale, and never names the three functions rf2-drpa3.122 published so a library author could actually implement one.
READ THE 14% CORRECTLY: the draft is not sloppy, it is HEDGED, and it hedged in exactly the places that turned out wrong — install.md:124 labels the debugging verbs "Design-target tool surface; shapes may refine"; testing.md:149 says "when implemented"; ssr.md:115 says "do not treat a guessed v/hydrate arity as frozen API." 86% of the code is already correct and the running order, voice and chapter shape hold. This is a refinement job, as the description says; the errors cluster in the chapters covering the surfaces that landed LAST (behaviors, presence, the tool plane, the test bracket).

== THE 38-MEMBER SURFACE (the thing being frozen) ==
All three sources agree exactly — spec/api-manifest.edn rows, spec/API.md roster rows, and the member headings in docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md. Checked for disagreement specifically because a disagreement would itself be a finding; there is none.
re-frame.freehand (alias v), 32 verbs:
  Declaration — defview ({:compiled true} selects the compiled tier), view?, describe, manifest
  Reactivity — sub
  Events and callbacks — event, handler, render-fn, raw-fn, projections, materialize-event
  Composition — slot, spread, spread-safe, markup
  Semantic controllers — controller-key, controller-revision, controller-current?
  Lifecycle and phase — presence (mandatory :timeout-ms), presence-phase, client-only (mandatory fallback), error-boundary
  Host boundaries — defbehavior, behavior, ->react (option roster closed at :map-props)
  Roots and SSR — mount, hydrate-root, unmount! (CLJS-only), render-static (JVM/server; the lone macro among the root verbs)
  Framework views and tools — route-link, active-connections (CLJS-only), command-log (CLJS-only)
re-frame.freehand.test (alias t), 6 names: render, find, find-all, attrs, text, with-render.
Six rows are :facade? true — mount, unmount!, hydrate-root, ->react, active-connections, command-log — each a CLJS-only verb re-exported from the namespace that owns it, which is exactly the deliberate single-import re-export the Conventions ruling sanctions.
THE FREEZE IS MECHANICALLY ENFORCEABLE, not merely aspirational: the JVM manifest generator enumerates publics and the CLJS probe treats both Freehand namespaces as fully rowed in BOTH directions, so an added or removed public name without a manifest row is already a failing condition. Codex reported the generator green on the checkout it read (543 repo-wide public vars in sync; the spec/API.md projection green at 244 public rows) — I did NOT re-run the generator, so treat those two figures as Codex-reported rather than re-verified.

== WHAT COULD STILL ADD A VERB ==
NOTHING SCHEDULED DOES. Every open/in-progress bead and every open PR was checked at dossier time (34 open + 1 in progress then; the backlog has since moved to 9 in progress / 0 open, so re-check at ruling time). The single open PR was #6888 — ci(freehand): arm the evidence-elision gate on the Freehand producer surfaces. A CI gate: no facade file, no manifest row. rf2-drpa3.162's acceptance criterion 5 says in terms: "Add no projection form, expression/selector language, dispatcher payload arity, or public API."
TWO GENUINE RISK VECTORS REMAIN, both design questions rather than scheduled work:
 1. rf2-drpa3.167 — does Freehand grow an evidence accumulator? Two workers independently established that the "donor MOVE" framing is FALSE: Xray consumes a live per-occurrence accumulator (explain-render, instance records) that Freehand simply does not have. If Mike rules that it should, the natural shape is one new tooling projection sibling to active-connections and command-log — ONE verb, in the tooling tier, landing in debugging.md, which is the draft's weakest chapter and 3/3 stale already. Its dossier was ai/decisions/rf2-drpa3.167.freehand-evidence-accumulator.md.
 2. F6d cutover via rf2-3bjs8. The examples-migration worker enumerated donor surfaces with NO Freehand equivalent: local, effect, ref, dispatch-fn, frame, frame-root, frame-provider, create-root, render!, custom-element, raw, html, adapter. The disposition for each is "redesign, don't rename" — but if the F6d sweep concludes one is genuinely needed, that is a verb. Freehand deliberately exports NO adapter and NO frame-provider today; those two are the most likely to be re-litigated.
Neither is scheduled and neither needs ruling before the guide is authored — the guide teaches what exists.
DO NOT MISREAD FUTURE api-manifest.edn CHURN AS A BROKEN FREEZE: the EP-0037 routing leaves (rf2-kqxe6.*) will touch that file — .9 says so directly, "this is the api-manifest serial lane if any facade row moves." That is the ROUTING surface (re-frame.routing / re-frame.core), not re-frame.freehand.

== THE FACADE-EXPORT CLASSIFICATION AUDIT: DECOUPLE IT — now rf2-2hpxo ==
Release condition half 2 names this audit. spec/Conventions.md:1198 defines it precisely, and its FORWARD half is already running: every new facade export classifies and justifies itself at diff time, which is why the Freehand rows carry tier, owner and status. The RETROSPECTIVE half — "the full retrospective sweep of every existing non-front-porch export, and the manifest table it produces" — "stays deferred to API-freeze / external-alpha prep", with its deadline set at "before re-frame2's first meaningful external alpha/beta release — NOT before v1", because the moment real users copy examples a namespace move becomes a breaking change.
It is a REPO-WIDE sweep of re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core — the grandfathered exceptions Conventions records — deciding keep / rename / move / internal-public for each. It is NOT a Freehand audit: Freehand's 38 members are already classified at diff time. Gating a Freehand guide on a re-frame.core sweep that Conventions itself schedules for external-alpha prep reads as a DRAFTING ACCIDENT rather than intent. Both analyses reached this independently. RECOMMENDATION: strike it from this bead's release condition, and leave this paragraph here so no future reader re-derives the coupling.
It had NO BEAD (bd list across every status confirmed). FILED 2026-07-25 as rf2-2hpxo (P3, external-alpha prep, explicitly decoupled from this bead) so the obligation stops being invisible.

== WHERE THE TWO ANALYSES DIVERGE, AND MY READ ==
Both say FREEZE NOW. They split on dispatch.
- MAYOR-SIDE POSITION: hold the guide on three named items — rf2-drpa3.53 (F6a conformance) merges, rf2-drpa3.55 (F6c residual) merges, rf2-drpa3.167 ruled. Its core argument is that HOLDING COSTS ZERO ON THE CRITICAL PATH, because under its own bead graph rf2-fby7o cannot be dispatched today anyway (.55 open, .53 open behind it), and rf2-drpa3.57 independently waits on .56 and .52 as well. Four other P1 gates sit ahead of it.
- CODEX POSITION: dispatch on the freeze declaration alone. Recast rf2-fby7o as a parallel child/completion slice of .55 rather than a successor, because F6c's scope ALREADY INCLUDES guides and .55 should become complete AFTER its guide/examples/skills consumer slices are complete. The current modelling reverses the natural dependency. (The mayor-side analysis independently flagged the same ordering as "arguably backwards".)
- MY READ: the Codex position is stronger, because the mayor-side "holding costs nothing" argument is CIRCULAR. It costs nothing ONLY because of the bead-graph ordering that BOTH analyses flag as backwards. If fby7o is properly a slice OF .55 rather than a successor to it, the zero-cost claim dissolves and the hold must justify itself on its own merits — which leaves only the .167 ruling: an item that changes ONE chapter, and a chapter that has to be rewritten from scratch regardless because it is 3/3 stale and teaches four verbs that were never built. Holding 22 chapters on a ruling that touches the one chapter you were rewriting anyway is disproportionate. The empirical case points the same way: 14% staleness after roughly ten days of the fastest surface movement this programme will ever see, concentrated in 5 chapters of 20, with 86% of code already correct.
- THE HONEST COUNTER, which Mike should weigh: an executed-samples harness catches a sample that no longer COMPILES; it does not catch a sample that compiles fine while teaching a superseded idiom. presence.md's phase overrides would have gone red, but a chapter teaching the wrong mental model for controllers can be green and wrong (semantic-controllers.md scores 0/9 stale while omitting the three functions its own subject requires). The harness converts MOST of the rework risk into a test signal, not all of it.

== IF MIKE DECLARES THE FREEZE ==
Record it the way spec/API.md:336 records the previous one — that section blessed the re-frame.core section 2 table as the v1 API freeze on 2026-07-12 00:39 AUSEST, with a ROW-LEVEL DELTA PROTOCOL for anything the correctness pass turned up afterwards. Same shape here: a dated blessing line in the Freehand section of spec/API.md naming the 38 members as the frozen roster, plus the delta protocol. That precedent worked for re-frame.core and there is no reason it would not work here.
WHAT THE FREEZE SHOULD COVER (Codex's formulation, at the right altitude): the 38-member author-facing roster and its documented paved CALL SHAPES, not every implementation detail. No public name added, removed or renamed without an operator-approved API delta; no material call-shape change lands silently; a delta updates facade + manifest metadata + spec/API.md + owning spec + API reference + the affected executable guide fixture in the SAME change. Correctness fixes, better diagnostics, performance work, internal ownership moves and richer non-authoritative evidence stay free to land.
BENEFIT BEYOND THE GUIDE: declaring it converts the two live risk vectors (.167, the F6d equivalences) from ordinary slice work into EXPLICIT UNFREEZE REQUESTS — exactly the scrutiny they warrant.
Then amend this bead's release condition to whatever Mike rules, and state that the facade-export audit (rf2-2hpxo) is decoupled.

== DISPATCH BRIEF MATERIAL (whenever the guide is dispatched) ==
Do not make the eventual worker re-derive any of this.
 1. THE SAMPLE-EXECUTION MECHANISM IS THE DELIVERABLE, and acceptance criterion 1 already owns it. Build it BEFORE the prose is touched — it is what makes every later surface change cheap, turning a broken sample into a red test with a file and a line number rather than silent rot.
 2. DO NOT BUILD A GENERAL MARKDOWN INTERPRETER. That is the gold-plated version and it is rejected. Right shape: put the copyable examples in ordinary checked-in fixture namespaces grouped by chapter, link each runnable guide block to its fixture, and add ONE cheap coverage check that rejects an unowned runnable block. Use the real JVM / CLJS / browser / SSR lane only where that example's claim requires it.
 3. FIVE CHAPTERS TO REWRITE RATHER THAN REFINE: debugging.md (the tool plane is TWO projections — active-connections and command-log — not four verbs), host-boundaries.md and js-libraries.md (the behavior form changed shape entirely: vector-head boundary, not attribute), presence.md (phase overrides became a phase READ via v/presence-phase), testing.md (t/with-render is mandatory and absent). The other 13 chapters hold.
 4. THE 14 SHIPPED VERBS THE DRAFT NEVER MENTIONS (listed above) — the three controller verbs in particular, without which semantic-controllers.md teaches the props but not the mechanism.
 5. Teach v/event and ordinary event vectors as the canonical path. Do NOT teach the disputed D007 key-condition-map event spelling while its deletion decision is pending; either ruling then costs a small explicit delta rather than a guide-wide rewrite.
 6. Author in separable cuts so a late ruling lands on one cut: (a) install, mental model, declaring views, state, subscriptions, events, composition, forms; (b) controllers, presence, compilation, host boundaries, SSR, testing; (c) debugging, adoption, interop, limits, final mkdocs nav.
 7. debugging.md should ship documenting active-connections and command-log, state plainly that no occurrence accumulator is public, and accept a later API delta only if a demonstrated tooling need justifies one. An accumulator should not acquire a main-door verb merely because the donor had one. Acceptance criterion 4 already requires deliberate omissions to be stated.
 8. Donor capabilities with no Freehand twin are NOT automatically an API backlog. Teach the intentional replacements — ordinary re-frame state, registered behaviors, explicit wrappers, the independent host adapters — do not import donor parity into the new design.
 9. The guide replaces docs/core/re-frame.ui/ in the mkdocs nav (11 pages, mkdocs.yml lines 202-213). rf2-drpa3.57's acceptance criterion 1 requires all six EP-0036 gate rows verified green with a named artifact, F6c being one, and F6c's own outcome sentence names docs/core guides explicitly — so donor deletion genuinely cannot open while docs/core/re-frame.ui/ is still the canonical view-layer guide. The dependency is real, not incidental.
 10. rf2-drpa3.92 (compiled manifest coordinates total-or-absent) is a localized manifest-truthfulness change — it may cost a sentence; it does not invalidate guide architecture or call sites.

== REJECTED AS MAKE-WORK ==
- Holding the guide on the retrospective facade-export audit (rf2-2hpxo). Repo-wide re-frame.core sweep, scheduled by Conventions for external-alpha prep; Freehand is already classified at diff time.
- Holding all 22 chapters on the rf2-drpa3.167 ruling, which changes one chapter that must be rewritten regardless.
- A general Markdown extraction/execution toolchain in place of checked-in fixture namespaces plus one coverage check.
- Waiting for an arbitrary quiet period as such. Codex's phrasing is right: it converts "stable" into a calendar superstition. A pre-alpha API becomes stable enough for guide work when its owner deliberately names the baseline and requires proposed changes to pass through an explicit delta.

== WHAT COULD NOT BE VERIFIED ==
- Whether the 2026-07-25 quiet is INTENTIONAL or incidental. The log cannot distinguish "between waves" from "done growing the door". That distinction is exactly what only Mike can supply, and it is why this is a decision rather than a report.
- The staleness rate is a symbol-existence measure, not a semantic one. The samples were not compiled.
- rf2-drpa3.53 / .55 remaining effort. Both open with no worker and no PR at dossier time; acceptance read, but no basis for an estimate.
- The 543-publics / 244-API.md-rows generator figures are Codex-reported, not independently re-run.
AUDIT UPDATE 2026-07-25 — PR #6900 resolved D007 with outcome DELETE, so this guide-owner bead's earlier instruction not to teach the pending key-condition form now has a concrete answer. Two live draft sites still contradict it: `docs/design/freehand/draft-guide/events-and-handlers.md:62-77` teaches the deleted exact-key map with a full copyable example, and `docs/design/freehand/draft-guide/compilation.md:41` still promises finite manifests for “key maps” (the same PR removed a second occurrence later in that file). When promoting/truthing the guide, replace the former with the paved event-vector + `::v/key` handler branch and `(v/event [e] …)` for synchronous browser mechanics, and remove the stale manifest member. This is already rf2-fby7o scope; no duplicate bead was created.
MIKE RULING 2026-07-25: DO NOT FREEZE THE API YET. We are still learning, so the surface stays open. But the DOCS ARE GREENLIT NOW, written against the EXISTING shipped API. This decouples the two halves the 2026-07-24 fold-in identified as accidentally coupled: guide authoring proceeds immediately; api-freeze does not happen and is not a precondition of anything here.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FREEZING (record these, they change how the guide is written):
1. The guide is authored against a MOVING surface. Acceptance criterion 1 (every code sample EXECUTED, not eyeballed) therefore becomes MORE important, not less: an executable-sample mechanism is what keeps the guide honest as the API shifts, and it is the only thing that will catch drift automatically. Do not weaken it.
2. Writing the guide IS an API design review. Mike is still learning the surface, and doc-writing is the highest-signal instrument for finding ergonomic flaws: every place a chapter is awkward to write, needs a caveat, or has to explain an inconsistency is a signal about the API, not about the prose. Guide authors MUST file API-ergonomics beads when they hit that, rather than writing around the problem. Those findings are a primary deliverable of this work, not a side effect.
3. Do not chase the surface. If a verb changes mid-authoring, fix the sample and move on; do not re-plan the guide.

SEQUENCING HOLD HAS LIFTED ON ITS OWN TERMS. This bead said do not dispatch until the F5 composition/integration slices are largely landed. That condition is now MET: the four F5 pilots rf2-drpa3.43/.44/.45/.46 have all closed, and component/library fitness is the one unambiguously GREEN row of the six EP-0036 gate rows (PRs 6747/6749/6776/6767). So Mike ruling go and the bead own precondition now agree.

DRAFT STATE at ruling time (measured 2026-07-24, basis symbol-existence not compilation): 22 files, 118 code blocks, about 14 percent of blocks carry a symbol that does not exist. t/with-render is absent from all 22 draft files despite being mandatory. 14 shipped verbs are never mentioned. Roster is 38 members in spec/api-manifest.edn (32 re-frame.freehand + 6 re-frame.freehand.test). Re-verify all of this at dispatch rather than trusting these figures.

API-FREEZE DISPOSITION: not happening now. rf2-2hpxo (retrospective facade-export classification sweep) stands on its own merits and is NOT gated on a freeze. Any bead that names api-freeze as a precondition should be re-read in light of this ruling.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6914 (2026-07-25): REOPENED for a bounded live guide-truth residue.

The promoted guide correctly rules in mental-model.md that there is no frame provider and in debugging.md that no occurrence accumulator/hot-view surface is public, but three shipped passages still teach the retired design:
- reactivity-and-ownership.md says a frame provider can retarget a subtree A -> B and lists frame retarget as a render cause;
- ssr.md says one root may scope several frames via provider-style retarget inside Freehand;
- adoption.md tells readers to use inspect / hot-views habits, even though those draft tools were never built.

These contradictions remain on current main and are programmer-facing correctness defects: a reader is directed toward a namespace/lowering path that does not exist and a tool surface the guide itself explicitly omits. Reconcile those passages onto the shipped model (two worlds are two roots; v/describe/v/manifest, the two behavior projections, ordinary traces/Xray) without inventing new API.

title: Promote the Freehand draft guide into the tracked design record
description:
Operator request (Mike, 2026-07-23): move `ai/findings/freehand/guide/` to `docs/design/freehand/draft-guide/`.

## Why

The draft is 22 markdown files (~252K) covering install, mental model, building a view, events and handlers, reactivity and ownership, state, semantic controllers, composition, presence, forms, host boundaries, js-libraries, compilation, SSR, testing, debugging, accessibility, limits and escapes, adoption, and a vs-reagent comparison. It currently sits in `ai/`, which is gitignored and local-only — so it exists on exactly one machine, is invisible to every worker and to a clean clone, and would be lost with that checkout.

Promoting it into the design record makes it durable, reviewable, and usable as the base for the guide-authoring work (see the sibling bead).

## Scope

Move the tree. Do not rewrite the content — this is a promotion, not an edit pass. Correct only what the move itself breaks (relative links that no longer resolve from the new location).

`docs/design/freehand/` is the durable, frozen supporting record per EP-0036, and `mkdocs.yml` already excludes `design/freehand/` from the published site because its links are source-tree-oriented. So the draft lands as a design artefact, NOT as published documentation.

## Acceptance

1. All 22 files are at `docs/design/freehand/draft-guide/` and tracked by git — `git ls-files docs/design/freehand/draft-guide | wc -l` reports 22.
2. `ai/findings/freehand/guide/` no longer exists.
3. `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` exits 0. VERIFY whether that checker scans `docs/design/` — if it does, every intra-draft link and anchor must resolve, and any that do not are the move's to fix. Report which it was rather than assuming.
4. `python -m mkdocs build --strict` exits 0 and the draft does NOT appear in the built site (it is excluded).
5. `docs/design/freehand/README.md` gains a one-line pointer to the draft, stating plainly that it is a DRAFT and not the shipped guide.

## Non-goals

Editing the guide's prose; publishing it to the site; reconciling it against the current implementation (that is the authoring bead's job); adding it to mkdocs nav.
close_reason: SHIPPED in PR #6710 (merged). All 22 markdown files promoted from the gitignored ai/findings/freehand/guide/ to the tracked docs/design/freehand/draft-guide/ — the operator draft existed on one machine only and is now durable on origin. Byte-identical apart from one forced link repair (../../../../docs/core/AUTHORING.md -> ../../../core/AUTHORING.md, the only out-of-tree link) and a CRLF->LF normalization to match the repo (21 of 22 sources were CRLF; the docs tree is LF; text character-for-character identical). README.md gained a one-line pointer marking it plainly a DRAFT, not the shipped guide. VERIFIED: check_doc_slugs.py DOES scan docs/design/ (proven by injecting a broken anchor -> exit 1 naming the file); all intra-draft links resolve; mkdocs --strict green with the draft correctly ABSENT from the built site (exclude_docs: design/freehand/ covers the new subdir). The draft is now the base for the authoring bead rf2-fby7o.

title: Make the Freehand public API docs tell the truth about {:compiled true}
description:

title: B-spine falsifiability test is itself timing-dependent and flakes under load
description:
Observed by the F3c worker while running gates under concurrent load, and reported unprompted as "one flake observed, not mine".

`re-frame.freehand.bench.falsifiability-cljs-test/the-moved-timing-really-moved` failed once with a timing ratio of 8.79 against a required minimum of 10, and passed on every other run.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than tolerating

The B-spine harness exists to enforce D021's split: deterministic properties are hard gates, timing is evidence with NO automatic numeric pass/fail. This particular test is a control proving that criterion 3 is meaningful — it asserts the timing measurement REALLY MOVED, because proving that an unchanged timing does not red the build proves nothing.

But the control is implemented as a numeric timing threshold, which is precisely the shape D021 forbids everywhere else. So the harness that mechanises "no timing thresholds" currently contains one, and it flakes for exactly the reason D021 gives for banning them: wall-clock is load-dependent. Under six concurrent workers on this box, a 50x workload produced an 8.79x ratio.

A flaky gate is worse than a missing one — it trains readers to re-run rather than read, which is how a real regression gets waved through.

## Options, for the implementing worker to weigh

1. Make the control deterministic rather than temporal — assert the harness ROUTED the measurement as evidence and that a gate-registered property is untouched, without depending on how much wall-clock moved.
2. Keep a timing assertion but make it robust — compare against a same-run baseline rather than an absolute ratio, or require only a directional move.
3. Widen the margin — cheapest, but leaves a load-dependent gate in place and only moves the flake threshold.

Prefer 1 if it can still prove what the control exists to prove: that the fixture genuinely did more work, so a green criterion-3 result is not vacuous.

## Acceptance

The control still fails if the timing measurement is wired as a gate rather than evidence (its real purpose), and does NOT fail under heavy concurrent load. Demonstrate the second by running it while the machine is loaded, not on an idle box.

## Non-goals

Removing the control; relaxing D021; adding retry logic to hide the flake.
close_reason: SHIPPED #6719 (merged): the B-spine falsifiability control no longer asserts a wall-clock ratio — the exact shape D021 forbids, previously sitting inside the harness that mechanises the ban. Replaced with :falsifiability/render-nodes (exact nodes rendered across the burst), which the repeats knob moves by EXACTLY its factor while leaving the first tree node count untouched; :move is now 50 deterministically. The wall-clock ratio survives as :timing-ratio, reported but deciding nothing. BOTH criteria demonstrated: still reds when mis-wired as a gate (deliberately re-declared render-ms as a gated :value with a threshold — 16 failures, 1 error, named directly); and does NOT fail under load (24 cores oversubscribed 2:1 with 48 burners alongside live workers, 50 runs — :move was 50 in ALL 50 while :timing-ratio ranged 22.40-99.34). ROOT CAUSE of the original 8.79: the ratio DENOMINATOR is the baseline arms p50, ~3.5ms over 5 samples; the moved arm (~91ms) averages its noise away but the baseline cannot, so one scheduling stall on the median baseline sample collapses the ratio. The fragile end was the small arm, not the big one — which is why widening the margin would not have been honest.

title: api-manifest CLJS probe inlines spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn with no build dependency: a sidecar-only edit can leave the probe asserting stale rows
description:
SAME DEFECT SHAPE as rf2-drpa3.65 (Freehand conformance fixtures), found while fixing it.

implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/src/re_frame/api_manifest/cljs_publics.clj slurps spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn at MACRO-EXPANSION time (find-sidecar + slurp in emit-cljs-only-rows / emit-classification-rows / emit-ui-test-signature-contract). shadow-cljs has no dependency edge from re-frame.api-manifest.cljs-manifest-probe-cljs-test to the sidecar, so a SIDECAR-ONLY edit does not invalidate the probe namespace's compile cache and the compiled probe keeps reconciling against the PREVIOUS rows.

Impact is narrower than the Freehand case: the sidecar usually changes in the same commit as the source whose publics moved, and a source change does invalidate. But a sidecar-only reconciliation (the common 'fix the drift report' edit) can report a stale green on a warm cache.

FIX, mirroring rf2-drpa3.65: read the sidecar through shadow.resource/slurp-resource under a CLJS expansion ((:ns &env) is the host test) so the file's last-modified participates in the cache key; that needs spec/ (or a narrower root holding the sidecar) resolvable via io/resource on the shadow classpath. NOTE the Freehand fix put spec/conformance on :source-paths for exactly this reason — the sidecar sits at spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn, one level up, so the root choice needs its own thought rather than a copy-paste.

ACCEPTANCE (same negative control): edit only spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn to something that must fail, run npm run test:cljs WITHOUT clearing .shadow-cljs, and get red.
close_reason: SHIPPED in PR #6709 (merged, LAST of the four-PR baked lane): route-link caller-veto (v/handler unwrap / bare fn / nil accepted; event vectors, maps, v/event, v/render-fn, v/raw-fn, keywords rejected via :rf.error/view-bad-event; FH-ROUTELINK-007 Chromium); api-manifest CLJS sidecar build-dependency edge (warm-cache red/green proven); B1 direct-lowering evidence (deterministic node-count parity gate (+ 5 (* 7 rows)); timing evidence-only via B-spine).

title: Make v/route-link's caller veto obey an explicit Freehand callback contract
description:
PR #6696 adds v/route-link as an ordinary Freehand view, but its :on-click control prop bypasses Freehand's event-position grammar. route_link_seam/anchor captures the caller value in a wrapper, and re-frame.routing.link/activate-link! executes it as `(on-click e)` whenever it is truthy.

That creates a high-probability grammar collision on a corpus-dominant surface:

- Freehand teaches `:on-click [:app/event ...]` as ordinary intent data. On v/route-link, the vector is instead invoked as an IFn collection lookup with the MouseEvent as its key; no application event is dispatched (or the call fails), then routing proceeds.
- `v/handler` is the declared form for imperative foreign work, exactly the role of a pre-navigation veto/confirm callback, but its Callback value is deliberately non-IFn and therefore fails when routing calls it.
- The v/route-link docstring says every other key including :on-click passes through as an HTML attribute, although :on-click is actually a framework-owned control key removed from the anchor and replaced by a routing wrapper.

The underlying Spec 012 donor contract expects an optional user fn. The bug is not that routing still has that compatibility contract; it is that the new Freehand surface neither translates nor fences the value at the boundary where its grammar differs. A programmer following Freehand's primary event idiom can therefore lose an event silently on one of the most common view forms.

NARROW REPAIR: define v/route-link's :on-click explicitly as the imperative pre-navigation/veto seam, not a second semantic intent site. Accept a bare function and the appropriate Freehand imperative callback form (`v/handler`) and invoke it exactly once before routing's decision, with committed freshness through the ordinary outer event site. Reject event vectors, event options and `v/event` at render with a typed, didactic diagnostic: the route click already produces the one routing intent; application reactions belong behind that routing event/transition, while imperative preventDefault/confirm work uses v/handler. Do not add a general callback-composition DSL or change the substrate-neutral routing hook.

Also correct the public prose so :on-click is listed among route-link control props, not among untouched HTML passthrough attributes.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. In a real mounted Freehand/React route-link, a bare fn and v/handler each run exactly once before the navigation decision and can veto with preventDefault.
2. A vector, options map and v/event at this prop fail at render with the named recovery; none is invoked as an IFn or silently ignored.
3. Plain navigation, modifier/middle/download/target deferral, frame capture and SSR remain unchanged.
4. The Spec 012 paragraph, v/route-link docstring and conformance fixture state the same accepted grammar.
5. Compiled and interpreted route-link exercise the same cases when compiled parity lands.

DEDUP: all-state Beads search for route-link / activate-link / caller-on-click / routing event found no issue owning this Freehand grammar boundary. rf2-drpa3.54 owns the broad final browser matrix, not the accepted-value contract.
notes: MERGE-QUEUE NOTE (mayor, 2026-07-23): PR #6709 (this trio) is GREEN-then-DIRTY — it passed all gates, then main moved under it when the race fix (#6705) merged. It is HELD, not broken: no rebase worker is dispatched because four freehand PRs (#6701 shell, #6707 crossings, #6708 checker, #6709) all overlap on freehand.cljc + shadow-cljs.edn + conformance.cljc, and rebasing all four in parallel makes them re-conflict each other on every merge (the baked-lane thrash). SEQUENCE: let the three in-flight rebases + the live shell worker drain, merge strictly one at a time pulling between, and rebase #6709 onto whatever main becomes once the lane clears. This PR also edits spec/012-Routing.md (hot-zone) — sequence it ahead of any other Spec-012 toucher, per the worker note. Its ze3ai fix changes shadow-cljs.edn source-paths (spec/conformance -> spec/), which is the specific conflict point with the race fix that also lives near there.

title: Close remaining standard Markdown block boundaries in wrapped-link extraction
description:
PR #6692 correctly replaces blank-line grouping with shared inline-block scan units and fixes the two executable failures from rf2-8wcbe. The new `_inline_blocks` boundary recognizer still joins link-shaped text across three ordinary Markdown boundaries that the repository's Python-Markdown renderer keeps separate: 1. A quote-only blank line: > A stray [opening > > ](missing.md) The renderer emits two blockquote paragraphs; `_iter_inline_links` yields `(3, "missing.md")`. `_inline_blocks` tests `content.strip()` before removing the quote prefix, so `>` is not seen as blank. 2. Indented code followed by a paragraph: [literal ](missing.md) The renderer emits a code block and a paragraph; extraction yields `(2, "missing.md")`. 3. A block-HTML interruption: A stray [opening
separate
](missing.md) The renderer emits a paragraph, the div, and another paragraph; extraction yields `(3, "missing.md")`. The positive control remains important: `> A real [wrapped` followed by unquoted `link](target.md)` is a valid lazy-continuation link and must keep extracting. The current corpus and both gates remain green, so this is a bounded future false-positive risk rather than a claim that a document is currently broken. SMALLEST REPAIR: keep the one shared extractor and its line-number behavior. Make scan-unit formation respect these standard boundaries—at minimum, detect a blank after stripping the blockquote prefix and keep indented-code and block-HTML blocks out of adjacent inline units. Use renderer-oracle mechanism tests to pin the negative cases and the lazy-continuation positive case. Do not build a general Markdown parser, duplicate the extractor, or reflow documents around the gate.
acceptance_criteria:
- The three executable samples—quote-only blank separator, indented code, and block HTML—yield no extracted link in the shared mechanism and both consuming gates.
- A genuine blockquote lazy-continuation wrapped link still extracts with the destination line number; existing one-, two-, and three-line positive cases remain green.
- Tests compare the boundary cases with the repository's Markdown rendering semantics or equivalently pin both negative and positive controls.
- The current documentation corpus and both checker self-test suites remain green.
- The repair stays in the shared extractor and does not introduce a second parser service or a document-reflow workaround.
close_reason:
CLOSED AT TRIAGE on the posture filter, not on the merits of the analysis — which is correct as far as it goes. This is the THIRD CommonMark-conformance refinement in one chain: blank-line grouping was blind to wrapped links (real, 100 invisible, 6 already broken) -> the fix invented phantom links across headings and multiline code spans (real, would red the gate on a non-link and block unrelated PRs) -> now blockquote-only blank lines and indented code blocks. The first two earned their place; this one does not clear the bar.

REASONING: (1) NEITHER SHAPE EXISTS IN THE CORPUS. PR #6692 established the full file:line -> destination inventory is BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after its change across 588 files and 16838 links, so these are hypothetical constructions, not latent breakage. (2) THE FAILURE MODE IS LOUD, NOT SILENT. A phantom link fails the gate with a named file and line — immediately diagnosable and fixable in minutes. That is categorically different from the original defect, which was a SILENT false green over 100 unchecked links, and different from a false green in a conformance gate. (3) COST/BENEFIT INVERTS HERE. Each further boundary rule (blockquote prefix stripping, indented-code detection, and whatever the next audit finds — reference-style links, HTML blocks, nested emphasis) moves us toward maintaining a general-purpose Markdown parser to check our own documentation. rf2-8wcbe explicitly said "do not grow a general-purpose Markdown parser"; that instruction binds the follow-ups too, not just the PR that carried it.

This is the pre-alpha posture applied deliberately: elegance and power without gold-plating, and no drowning in minutiae. The gate now catches the class of defect it exists for.

REOPEN TRIGGER, and it is cheap and self-announcing: if either shape actually appears in the corpus, the gate will FAIL LOUDLY naming the file and line. At that point the exposure is real, the fix is narrow and justified, and this bead should be reopened rather than re-derived. Until then it is exhaustiveness for its own sake.

title: Keep both rename endpoints visible to the Beads PR guard
description:
## Problem

PR #6691 made `scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh` a required PR gate and correctly changed its range to the branch delta. The path selection still uses:

`git diff --name-only "$BRANCH_POINT" HEAD`

Git's default rename detection collapses a detected rename to the destination path in `--name-only` output. Therefore an exact rename out of the protected tree, such as `.beads/issues.jsonl` to `tracker-snapshot.jsonl`, is presented to `check_beads_boundary` only as `tracker-snapshot.jsonl`. That destination is outside `.beads/**`, so the allow-list classifier exits 0 even though merging the PR deletes the tracker database from its canonical location.

The behavior is already known and fixed elsewhere in this repository: rf2-vxgfnd.137 added `--no-renames` to changed-surface discovery because a rename out of a protected source tree hid the deleted endpoint. A read-only forced-rename comparison during this audit likewise emitted only the destination, and feeding exactly that output to `check_beads_boundary ci` returned 0. Layer 5 of `test-pre-commit.sh` covers add/modify contamination and diverged history, but no rename endpoint.

## Consequence

The required guard can certify a PR whose effective branch delta removes `.beads/issues.jsonl` (or moves another database-derived `.beads/**` path to an allowed destination). The ordinary stale-snapshot case is covered; this is a bounded but material hole in the same tracker-integrity boundary.

## Recommendation

Disable rename detection for the guard's path enumeration: `git diff --no-renames --name-only "$BRANCH_POINT" HEAD`. This yields deletion plus addition, allowing the existing shared classifier to reject the protected old endpoint without any new path rules. Add one real-history rename-out case to the existing layer-5 fixture and keep the merge-base/event behavior unchanged.

Provenance: correctness audit of merged PR #6691. This is a new consumer of the already-understood rf2-vxgfnd.137 Git behavior, not a reopening of that closed changed-surface bead.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An exact-content rename from `.beads/issues.jsonl` to a path outside `.beads/**` fails the PR guard and names `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
2. A rename from any database-derived `.beads/**` path to an allow-listed Beads config path also fails on the protected old endpoint.
3. The guard enumerates both rename endpoints, preferably via `git diff --no-renames --name-only` rather than a second classifier or name-status parser.
4. A regression test creates a real Git history with a detected R100 rename; restoring the current `git diff --name-only` makes the test false-green.
5. Existing diverged-history, ordinary contamination, allow-list, missing-base, and mayor-push cases remain green; do not redesign the guard.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6703 open. check-beads-pr-boundary.sh path enumeration is now 'git diff --no-renames --name-only $BRANCH_POINT HEAD'; merge-base/event/allow-list behaviour unchanged, no new path rules, no second parser. AC1: exact-content rename .beads/issues.jsonl -> tracker-snapshot.jsonl now EXIT=1 naming .beads/issues.jsonl (proved in a throwaway temp-dir repo with a real R100; the OLD enumeration handed the classifier only 'tracker-snapshot.jsonl'). AC2: same move onto the allow-listed .beads/config.yaml also refused, on the protected old endpoint. AC3: both endpoints come from --no-renames, not a name-status parser. AC4: layer 5 gains worker/renamed-out + worker/renamed-to-config on real git history, plus a premise row asserting git really scores it R100; restoring plain --name-only reds exactly 5f and 5g (Summary: 31 passed, 2 failed) and nothing else. AC5: 5a diverged-history, 5b contamination, 5c missing merge base, 5d missing base ref, 5e mayor push all still green — 33 passed, 0 failed (was 31). Control: an ordinary rename of a non-.beads file still EXIT=0. Gates: npm run test:script-policy && npm run test:script-helpers exit 0.

title: Keep wrapped-link extraction inside real Markdown inline blocks
description:
PR #6690 correctly makes wrapped link text visible, but `_blank_line_blocks` equates “no blank line” with “one Markdown inline block”. Blank lines are block boundaries, but they are not the only block boundaries, and CommonMark code spans may cross a line ending. The resulting join can invent links that the renderer does not produce.

Two executable counterexamples against main:

1. A valid multiline code span:

    `[literal
    link](missing.md)`

   (with one backtick opening before `[` and one closing after `)`). Python-Markdown renders one `<code>` span. Because `_strip_inline_code` masks each line separately, neither unmatched backtick is masked; `_iter_inline_links` joins the lines and yields `(2, "missing.md")`.

2. Real block boundaries without a blank line:

    A stray [opening
    # Separate heading
    ](missing.md)

   Python-Markdown renders a paragraph, an H1, and a second paragraph. The new blank-line block joins all three and again yields `missing.md` as a link.

If either sample appears in the scanned corpus, the doc-slug and shared README gate can fail on a non-link. Before #6690, line-oriented extraction did not create these false positives. The current corpus remains green; this is a parser-contract regression exposed by direct mechanism tests, not a claim that a current document is broken.

SMALLEST REPAIR: keep the shared extractor and wrapped-link behavior, but form scan units that cannot cross actual Markdown block boundaries and mask code spans over the same joined inline unit (line endings inside a code span are legal). Reuse the already-installed Markdown machinery if it preserves destination line reporting cleanly, or add only the bounded block/code-span recognition needed by the corpus. Do not grow a new general-purpose Markdown parser or reflow documents to hide the problem.
acceptance_criteria:
- A multiline backtick code span containing wrapped link-shaped text is not extracted by either doc-slug or README checking.
- Extraction does not bridge an ATX heading or another explicitly supported non-blank block boundary; the counterexample above yields no link.
- Genuine one-, two-, and three-line links, including blockquoted forms, still extract with the destination's line number and broken ones still fail the gate.
- Add direct positive/negative mechanism cases and at least one end-to-end fixture; mutation back to blank-line-only grouping makes them fail.
- The current 588-file corpus and both existing self-test suites remain green; no new parser service, duplicate extractor, or corpus reflow is introduced.

title: Reject silently malformed v/defview declarations
description:
PR #6689 documents `(v/defview name docstring? opts? [props] body+)` and assigns malformed declarations the typed `:rf.error/defview-bad-args` diagnostic, but the macro currently accepts two malformed shapes silently.

Reproduced against main:

1. `(macroexpand-1 '(v/defview bodyless [p]))` succeeds. `parse-defview-args` returns a nil body and the expansion creates `(fn [p])`, so an accidentally omitted body becomes a view that quietly returns nil.
2. `(v/defview misspelled {:chilren-policy :none} [p] nil)` succeeds and reports `:children-policy :optional`. Unknown option keys are discarded. The same happens today for reserved-but-not-yet-implemented `{:compiled true}` and props-schema options: the declaration remains interpreted and the option is absent from inspection.

The second case is especially hostile to programmer and AI productivity: a one-character option typo produces valid code with different semantics, and a design-documented future option currently pretends to work. This is a declaration-boundary validation gap, not a request for a general schema system.

SMALLEST REPAIR: make the macro validate the finite option keys whose semantics have landed and require at least one body form. Unknown keys, including reserved options before their owning slice implements them, should fail at macro expansion with `:rf.error/defview-bad-args`, naming the offending keys and recovery. F3b/F3f can extend the accepted-key set when they implement `:compiled` and props schemas. An intentional no-output view remains expressible with an explicit nil body.
acceptance_criteria:
- A declaration with no body fails at macro expansion with `:rf.error/defview-bad-args`; an explicit `nil` body remains valid.
- An unknown/misspelled option key fails at macro expansion and the diagnostic names the offending key plus the supported recovery.
- A reserved future option is never silently ignored: it is either implemented by its owning slice or rejected until then. In particular, `{:compiled true}` must not describe itself as interpreted without an error.
- The four documented declaration spellings with a body, valid children policies, destructuring, docs, source coordinates, and both host test lanes remain green.
- Focused mutation tests prove removal of the body/option validation makes the suite fail; no runtime option registry or compatibility layer is added.
notes: MAYOR SEQUENCING (2026-07-22): CLUSTERED with rf2-llxsw (the ruled Option B IFn amendment) and HELD until the in-flight Freehand wave merges. All three beads modify the same two things — the descriptor type and the defview macro in implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc. Four workers (drpa3.17 tree, .22 events, .25 compiler transplant, .41 route-link) are appending exports to that exact file right now, and rf2-drpa3.63 additionally wants to MOVE the descriptor constructor and runtime helpers behind an implementation boundary — a namespace restructure that would break all four mid-flight. Dispatching now guarantees a four-way conflict on the substrate core file. Dispatch as ONE cluster once that wave is merged; llxsw carries the ruled amendment, .63 closes the public boundary and enrolls the namespace in the manifest machinery, .64 makes malformed declarations fail at macro expansion. They share a surface and a test file, so one PR is both cheaper and safer than three.

description:

title: check_doc_slugs.py is blind to markdown links that wrap across a newline
description:
## Summary

The repo's primary link gate cannot see a markdown link split across a line break, so any wrapped link is silently unguarded.

## Evidence (negative control, not inference)

Found while finishing the 004D ownership labels. `_extract_links` iterates `text.splitlines()` (scripts/check_doc_slugs.py:617-628), so a link whose `](target#anchor)` falls on the next line never matches.

Proved both directions on the real corpus:
- the inbound link at spec/API.md:272-273 IS such a wrapped link. Breaking its anchor back to a retired slug leaves the gate at EXIT 0 — undetected.
- breaking the single-line equivalent at spec/API.md:31 correctly reds with BROKEN ANCHOR.
Both were restored before commit; numstat confirmed no residue.

## Why it matters

check_doc_slugs.py is the REAL anchor gate in this repo — `mkdocs build --strict` does not catch broken anchors, it logs them as INFO and exits 0. So a wrapped link has NO gate at all. Every heading rename since this checker was written could have orphaned a wrapped inbound link with CI green. This is the third distinct instance of line-wrap blindness found in this repo's scanners, which suggests the fix should be a shared normalisation helper rather than a one-off patch here.

## Expected behavior

A link is validated regardless of whether it wraps. Scanning should operate on a joined/normalised view for link extraction, or explicitly document that it is line-oriented and add a separate wrapped-link detector.

## Acceptance

1. The negative control above reds: break the anchor of the wrapped link at spec/API.md:272-273 and the gate must exit non-zero NAMING it. Restore and confirm exit 0.
2. A corpus sweep reports how many currently-wrapped links exist and whether any is ALREADY broken. Report the count; a nonzero already-broken count is a finding in its own right.
3. No regression: the existing single-line detection still reds (keep a positive control).

## Non-goals

Rewriting the checker; reflowing the corpus to avoid wrapped links (that treats the symptom and will silently regress); widening into a general docs audit.

title: Template browser proofs never run in CI: no job provisions a Chromium binary
description:
Found while implementing rf2-igwf7 (2026-07-22). The RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS tier now carries TWO Chromium proofs — the pre-existing SSR DOM-adoption proof and the new emitted dev-page boot proof (mount + 0->1 + zero pageerror). Neither can run in CI today.

EVIDENCE: all three workflows that set RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS=1 (test.yml:jvm-tools-template, expensive-tests.yml:template smoke, template-release.yml) run `npm ci` in implementation/ and nothing else. That installs the playwright NPM PACKAGE but never a browser binary (`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`). Both drivers exit 2 = documented skip when chromium.launch() throws, so the tier stays GREEN with zero browser coverage. rf2-igwf7 made the skip LOUD (a '!!! NOT PROVEN -- SKIPPED' banner in the run output, proven by forcing PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH at a bogus dir) but deliberately did NOT hard-fail, because hard-failing would red every PR on infrastructure.

THE WORK: add a 'npx playwright install --with-deps chromium' step (after the npm ci step) to the three template jobs, then flip both drivers' exit-2 skip into a hard failure — or, if the skip is kept, keep it only for the local fast loop. Until this lands, mask 2 from rf2-igwf7 is closed LOCALLY only: the dev-page boot proof runs on a developer machine and in nothing else.

SURFACE: .github/workflows/{test,expensive-tests,template-release}.yml (hot-zone — sequence it) + optionally tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/emitted_test_run_test.clj (the exit-2 branches).
notes: MAYOR SEQUENCING (2026-07-22): HELD, not forgotten. This bead needs .github/workflows/**, which is a hot-zone currently owned by the in-flight CI cluster (rf2-drpa3.58 + rf2-3mh2f + rf2-drpa3.61 + rf2-5z20y, one PR). Dispatching now would put two workers on the same workflow files. Dispatch the moment that PR merges. NOTE ON SCOPE when it goes out: this is not only about the new dev-page boot cell — the PRE-EXISTING SSR hydration proof has been skipping in CI for the same reason, so the fix retroactively arms two proofs, and the PR should report what the SSR proof reveals once it actually runs for the first time. Expect it to find something; a proof that has never executed has never passed.
close_reason: PR #6695. Provisioned `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` in all three jobs that set RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS (test.yml:jvm-tools-template, expensive-tests.yml:template-emitted-app, template-release.yml:test-template). Exit 2 (no launchable Chromium) is now a HARD FAILURE under CI and a loud NOT PROVEN skip locally, keyed on the CI env var; both call sites share one check-browser-proof! verdict helper that also ECHOES the driver's verdict line on green. release_gate_test.clj pins the release job's provisioning at PR time. CI acceptance on the PR's own run: 5 browser-proof PASS lines (4 dev-page boot variants + the SSR DOM-adoption proof), 0 NOT PROVEN banners, vs 5 banners on the last main run of the same job. FINDING: the SSR hydration proof PASSED on its first-ever execution -- no latent defect, but 5 browser assertions moved from asserted-by-nobody to executed. Cost: --with-deps step 23s; job 8m02s -> 10m47s (35m timeout).

title: Finish canonical 004D ownership labels after the Freehand contract cut
description:
## Summary

Finish the atomic Spec 004 to 004D ownership cut in the small set of canonical current-contract labels that still attribute compiled-tier material to Spec 004.

## Evidence

Merged PR #6682 moved the donor compiled grammar to spec/004D-Freehand-Compiled-Grammar.md and correctly retargeted the substantive links, but three current labels remain inconsistent with their targets:

1. spec/API.md heads the live re-frame.ui compiled API table with “Spec 004”, although its owning link and stage profile are 004D. A same-page link also embeds that old heading slug.
2. spec/Ownership.md says the compiled head-channel absence is “owned by 004, not here”, while the row correctly links to the 004D owner.
3. spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md calls :ui/render-fn the “Spec 004 §Compiled render slots” member, although that compiled section moved to 004D.

These are canonical API/ownership statements, not historical programme prose.

## Expected behavior

Current contract indexes name 004 for the common Freehand contract and 004D for donor/compiled-tier grammar. Readers and tools should not have to infer ownership from a link that contradicts its visible label.

## Scope

Correct those labels and any inbound anchor created by the API heading change. Perform a narrow scan of the same canonical files for equivalent direct owner-label contradictions.

## Non-goals

Do not rewrite historical EPs, donor design provenance, every phrase saying “Spec 004 rewrite”, or the F6 consumer-migration corpus. Do not change semantics or add a compatibility anchor unless a real current inbound link needs it.

Provenance: completeness and correctness audit of merged PR #6682.
design: Keep this a small ownership-truth repair. Visible labels and link targets must agree; link integrity is proved by the existing slug and MkDocs gates. Avoid a broad textual rename because common Freehand semantics genuinely remain owned by Spec 004 and historical donor prose is intentionally retained.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The live compiled-view API heading names Spec 004D, and every current inbound link to that heading resolves after its slug changes.
2. The Ownership head/meta row says the compiled structural absence is owned by 004D.
3. The 004B render-fn sentence names the compiled render-slot owner as 004D.
4. A narrow scan of spec/API.md, spec/Ownership.md, and spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md finds no equivalent visible-label/target contradiction for moved compiled-tier sections; historical provenance wording is explicitly out of scope.
5. python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py and python -m mkdocs build --strict pass.
close_reason: SHIPPED in PR #6687 (merged). Fixed the three named label/target contradictions plus two more of the same class found by the narrow scan, all one token each: spec/API.md heading + its three same-page inbound anchors, the blessed-export-set conformance reference, spec/Ownership.md compiled head-channel row, and two spec/004B references (render-fn member, portability law). Deliberately left alone per the bead Non-goals: the design-provenance heading, the ~20 historical design-freeze matrix cells, the donor-era-moved-intact provenance line, and API.md Specs 004/006/008 (004 genuinely governs re-frame.ui now as the common contract). FINDING, filed as rf2-vpc4c: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py cannot see a markdown link that WRAPS ACROSS A NEWLINE — _extract_links iterates splitlines(), and the inbound link at API.md:272-273 is exactly such a link. Proved by negative control: breaking that wrapped anchor leaves the gate at exit 0, while breaking the single-line one at API.md:31 correctly reds. So one half of this bead was silently unverifiable by CI and was proved directly against the checker SLUGIFY instead.

title: Fold jvm-freehand into test.yml's matrix + all-required-passed aggregator
description:
F1a (rf2-drpa3.15) added the Freehand artefact's JVM lane as a standalone workflow (.github/workflows/freehand-artefact.yml) because .github/workflows/* was hot-zone with several EP-0036 slices adding gates concurrently. GitHub 'needs:' cannot span workflow files, so jvm-freehand is NOT reachable from test.yml's all-required-passed aggregator - the branch ruleset's single required context. It is therefore a visible but ADVISORY check today.

Do this once the workflow hot-zone clears (no other open PR touching test.yml).

ACCEPTANCE: a red freehand JVM suite fails all-required-passed - proof: the job appears in test.yml's needs: list and the standalone workflow no longer duplicates it.

NON-GOALS: changing what the suite runs.

Proof: yaml.safe_load of test.yml reports 57 jobs / 56 aggregator needs / 0 unmatched needs / 0 jobs outside the aggregator, with jvm-freehand present; a deliberately-failing freehand deftest exits 1 (Ran 2, 1 failure) and the aggregator fails on contains(needs.*.result,'failure'). NOT proved end-to-end: no GitHub run of a red jvm-freehand against the aggregator yet (needs the change on main).
