title: Configure the beads Dolt remote (operator action)
description:
FOLLOW-UP from the .beads guard work. This is layer 4 of that bead and is OPERATOR ACTION — it cannot be done or verified from a worker worktree, which is why it was carved out rather than attempted.

THE WORK: configure the Dolt remote for the beads database so tracker state has a durable home independent of the git-tracked JSONL export, and confirm bd dolt push / bd dolt pull round-trip.

WHY IT MATTERS: the JSONL export is a mirror, not the source of truth. Today a git-side accident is recoverable only because Dolt still holds the real state locally; without a configured remote there is no off-box copy.

ACCEPTANCE: bd dolt push succeeds; bd dolt pull round-trips on a second checkout; the configuration is recorded somewhere durable rather than living only in one machine's local config.

ASSIGNEE: Mike (operator). Do not dispatch a background worker at this.
notes:
STATUS RECONCILIATION 2026-07-25: LIVE - but PARTIALLY SATISFIED, and the remaining gap is exactly the one the bead's WHY-IT-MATTERS names. Measured, not assumed: 'bd dolt remote list' returns one remote - origin  file://C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/.beads/backup/origin - and that path is real and populated (1.7G of Dolt chunk/.darc files), so 'bd dolt push' in the session-close protocol does have a target and does round-trip. WHAT IS STILL NOT TRUE: it is not an OFF-BOX copy. The remote lives INSIDE the repo working tree (.beads/backup/, gitignored at .beads/.gitignore:57), on the same machine and the same disk as the database it backs up - a disk loss or a stray recursive delete takes the database and its backup together, which is the precise failure this bead was filed to prevent. Acceptance 2 ('bd dolt pull round-trips on a SECOND CHECKOUT') and acceptance 3 ('recorded somewhere durable rather than living only in one machine's local config') are both still unmet. Remains OPERATOR ACTION, assigned to Mike - not dispatchable to a worker. No status change.
RULING 2026-07-25 05:56 AUSEST (dossier ai/decisions/rf2-4l67v.beads-dolt-remote.md folded in here and deleted; everything below is what survives it).

DECISION: one zero-cost trial, then close either way. No new hosted service. There is no open design question left - both steps are operator commands, which is the only reason this bead is still Mikes.

STEP 1 - the only thing worth trying. Five minutes, no account, no new credentials, no new service, using infrastructure the project already operates:
    bd dolt remote add github-trial git+https://github.com/day8/re-frame2.git
    bd dolt push --remote github-trial
    git ls-remote origin refs/dolt/data
Continue only if the push succeeds AND ls-remote returns refs/dolt/data. Then promote (bd dolt remote has no rename, so remove-before-add):
    bd dolt remote remove origin
    bd dolt remote add origin git+https://github.com/day8/re-frame2.git
    bd dolt remote remove github-trial
    bd dolt remote list      (expect the git+https URL, not the file:// path)
    bd dolt push
Then prove recovery in a disposable clone on a different path, outside the worktree parent so no guard or hook fires: git clone https://github.com/day8/re-frame2 C:\Users\miket\tmp\rf2-dolt-restore-check ; bd bootstrap --dry-run (THE PLAN MUST NAME THE DOLT REMOTE, NOT THE JSONL IMPORT - that is the whole test) ; bd bootstrap --yes ; bd stats (expect 2326 issues) ; bd memories (expect 215) ; bd dolt pull. Delete the clone afterwards - it is a verification artefact, not a working tree. Close DONE recording the URL, refs/dolt/data, and the fresh-clone result.

NAMED TRIGGER FOR THE FALLBACK: GitHub enforces 2 GB max per push and 100 MB max per git object. The local store is about 1.78 GB and the filesystem-remote layout contains individual archive files of roughly 1.08 GB and 638 MB. Whether the Dolt git-remote encoder re-chunks below 100 MB is UNVERIFIED - that is precisely why this is a trial and not a plan. If the push fails on either limit: DO NOT use --force, DO NOT open a DoltHub account, remove github-trial, go to step 2.

STEP 2 - fallback, and a fully respectable close, not a corner cut. Accept the git-committed JSONL as the durable copy and close WONT-DO with the loss list below in the close-reason. Do NOT remove the file:// origin: that breaks the bare bd dolt push in the session-close protocol and throws away a working local copy for nothing. Kill the FALSE SIGNAL instead, which is the actual defect - add a short Backup destination section to the tracked, human-authored .beads/README.md stating that origin is machine-local (.beads/backup/origin, gitignored, same disk as the database it backs up), that the off-box copy is .beads/issues.jsonl on github.com/day8/re-frame2 refreshed every 15 minutes, and that recovery is bd bootstrap falling back to importing the git-tracked JSONL. That satisfies acceptance clause 3 (recorded somewhere durable) honestly, by recording what the durable copy actually is.

REJECTED - DoltHub or any second hosted service (dossier option a). Gold-plating. A new account, new credentials in the environment and a 1.7 GB seed, bought to protect a changelog measured at near-zero information density (see EVIDENCE, item 1 of the loss list). Privacy is not the blocker - the tracker is already public - the cost/benefit is. If step 1 fails, the answer is step 2, not a second provider.
REJECTED - dossier option d, leave the bead open. Now that the misleading-remote finding is recorded, carrying this as an open P2 that everyone reads as durability-is-handled is the worst available state.
REJECTED - filing a bead to protect .beads/interactions.jsonl (16,494 agent-audit records, 6.6 MB, gitignored). It lives OUTSIDE the Dolt database entirely, so no remote under any option would ever have saved it, and an agent interaction log does not warrant its own backup arrangement. Recording the rejection here makes it an explicit decision rather than an accident, which was the dossiers actual ask.
SPUN OUT - rf2-cchlf: pin issue-prefix rf2 into tracked .beads/config.yaml. That is the one item on the loss list that is both real and cheap, and unlike this bead it IS dispatchable.
DEFERRED, conditional only - Dolt GC to reclaim the 1.50 GB single oldgen .darc dated 2026-07-12 (the bulk of the 1.7 GB). Only matters if step 1 succeeds and the seed cost bites; bd 1.0.3 does not appear to expose GC and it was not tested. Do not file unless step 1 lands.
EVIDENCE 2026-07-25, measured read-only with bd 1.0.3 at commit 1b2dd2cb56b31a7fb947845731c67292c34dd29b. Folded from the dossier and spot-re-verified. Keep this; it is the whole basis of the ruling above and nobody should have to re-derive it.

THE CENTRAL FINDING, worse than the beads own premise: a remote IS configured, reads as healthy to anyone who checks, and provides ZERO durability. bd dolt remote list returns
    origin   file://C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/.beads/backup/origin
which is a directory inside this very checkout, on the same disk as the database it backs up, and gitignored (.beads/.gitignore:57 for backup/, :3 for embeddeddolt/). Any event that takes the drive takes the database and its remote together. A MISSING remote announces itself; this one does the opposite. The pushes themselves are real and cheaply incremental - 234 files, 1.7 GB, manifest freshly written, chunk files mostly 100-700 KB after the initial seed. The mechanism works; it is only pointed somewhere useless. Caveat not resolvable read-only: bd dolt show annotates the remote [CLI only] (registered with the Dolt CLI, not a SQL server; bd dolt status reports embedded, in-process, no server). Whether that degrades anything is unclear, but chunk freshness says pushes land.

THE SECOND FACILITY IS ALSO NOT EXTERNAL, and its two surfaces disagree in a way that misleads. bd backup status shows enabled=true, interval 15m, auto-enabled because a git remote exists - that is what keeps .beads/issues.jsonl refreshed. But bd backup status --json reports "dolt": {"configured": false}: no Dolt backup destination has EVER been configured. The local .beads/backup/ tree (3.5 GB including origin/) is a chunk store, not a destination.

WHAT SURVIVES A DRIVE LOSS TODAY, in full, via .beads/issues.jsonl on the PUBLIC repo github.com/day8/re-frame2: all 2,326 issues (34 open, 6 in progress, 16 blocked, 2,274 closed) plus all 215 bd remember memories. Verified COMPLETE rather than a filtered subset - bd export --all (which adds infrastructure beads, templates and gates) yields 2,326 issues + 215 memories = 2,541 lines, the same line count as both the working .beads/issues.jsonl and the copy at HEAD, so nothing is hiding outside the export. The prose layer, which is the part that would actually hurt to lose: close_reason on 2,260 closed beads, 462,374 chars, median 112, 737 of them over 200 chars, longest 2,517 - the irreplaceable why-we-decided-that layer; notes on 1,141 beads, 2,743,023 chars, by volume the largest single body of institutional knowledge in the tracker; acceptance_criteria on 1,364; dependencies on 1,320, so the whole dependency graph reconstructs; description on 2,311; design on 249; external_ref on 503; comments on 46. Recovery is a documented path, not a rescue operation: bd bootstrap explicitly falls back to importing the git-tracked JSONL. And compaction is DISABLED (compaction_enabled=false, auto_compact_enabled=false), so no beads content lives only in Dolt history awaiting a bd restore. HEAD matched origin/main at audit time and 6,869 commits in this repo have touched that file - the mayor heartbeat is doing its job.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE, and honestly what each is worth:
  1. Per-bead Dolt version history. bd history rf2-4l67v returns 1,518 entries for a bead created three days earlier, and every sampled entry shows IDENTICAL state. It is heartbeat noise - one version row per issue per bd dolt commit. Across 2,326 beads this is the bulk of the 1.7 GB at near-zero information density. Losing it costs the ability to answer who-changed-this-priority-on-2026-06-03, a question nobody on this project has ever asked. THIS IS THE ENTIRE ASSET THAT ANY DOLT REMOTE BUYS - which is why a paid or second-provider answer is gold-plating.
  2. .beads/interactions.jsonl - 16,494 bd audit records, 6.6 MB, gitignored. NOTE CAREFULLY: it is a plain file on disk and is NOT inside the Dolt database, so no Dolt remote however configured would ever have backed it up. Written off explicitly in the ruling.
  3. Database-stored configuration - issue_prefix = rf2 and the compaction knobs live in Dolt; .beads/config.yaml line 9 has issue-prefix commented out, so a rebuild would auto-detect from the directory name and come up re-frame2. Spun out as rf2-cchlf.
  4. Dolt branches beyond the default, if any exist. Not enumerated.
The honest summary: the trackers MEANING is safe and refreshed every few minutes; what is exposed is its CHANGELOG - high in bytes, low in value - plus one log file no Dolt remote would have saved anyway.

FEASIBILITY OF THE GITHUB ROUTE, verified against the exact installed bd commit. This CORRECTS the dossiers first half, which concluded that git-backed Dolt storage was not reachable with this version - the absence of refs/dolt/data only shows the ref was never seeded, not that support is missing:
  - docs/SYNC_SETUP.md at 1b2dd2cb tells operators to add the existing git repository as a Dolt remote, push to refs/dolt/data, and recover a new checkout with bd bootstrap.
  - cmd/bd/dolt.go at that commit supports GitHub git URLs, implements bd dolt push --remote, and writes the origin URL into TRACKED .beads/config.yaml as sync.remote for fresh-clone recovery. That is what makes acceptance clause 3 satisfiable by the git route.
  - Dolt official remote docs confirm GitHub/GitLab and other git servers are supported, default to refs/dolt/data, and require either an explicit git+... URL or one ending in .git.
  - bd backup export-git is NOT a real subcommand in 1.0.3 (it falls through to parent help) and is irrelevant to this route; bd dolt remote add plus bd dolt push is the documented path.
  - The Dolt data sits under a nonstandard git ref, so ordinary source clones do not fetch the 1.7 GB database.
OPERATIONAL CARE if step 1 proceeds: the promotion command writes sync.remote into TRACKED .beads/config.yaml and bd 1.0.3 AUTO-COMMITS that change - run it only from a clean mayor checkout, never amid unrelated staged work, and confirm no credential was written. Keep automatic push disabled: concurrent pushes to git-protocol Dolt remotes can race, so the explicit session-close push stays the only writer.
CORRELATED-FAILURE LIMIT, acknowledged not ignored: routing Dolt to the same GitHub repo means losing or losing access to that repo takes both the JSONL and refs/dolt/data. Provider diversity is a different (and lower-value) goal than surviving this laptops disk, which is what the bead was filed about.
PRIVACY IS NOT A CONSTRAINT: day8/re-frame2 is public and .beads/issues.jsonl is committed to it, so every close-reason, note and memory is already published. DoltHub lists public databases as free on its pricing page - the dossiers first half could not verify that, its second half did. It does not change the ruling; cost was never the deciding factor, value-of-the-asset was.
MERGED-PR AUDIT FINDING from PR #6894 (2026-07-25). Fresh-clone recovery was reproduced from only the git-tracked config.yaml, metadata.json, and issues.jsonl. `bd bootstrap --dry-run --json` correctly selected `jsonl-import` and database `rf2`, proving rf2-cchlf and the issue-prefix pin itself work. But `bd bootstrap --yes` exited 1 with `validation failed for issue rf2-kfpf: invalid status: in_review`. The canonical export currently contains 8 `in_review` issues, while this bd importer rejects that status. Therefore this Bead Step 2 fallback and its statement that the tracked JSONL is an executable recovery floor are not currently true, even though the data remains durable and manually repairable. Settle importer compatibility or normalize the legacy statuses in the canonical tracker/export, then prove a disposable fresh-clone bootstrap completes and its issue/memory counts match the export. No duplicate filed: this open recovery owner is the exact home.
RULING AMENDMENT 2026-07-25 10:58 AUSEST (delegated ruling; dossier v2 at ai/decisions/rf2-4l67v.beads-dolt-remote.md — including an independent Codex read-only audit — weighed, folded in here, and deleted). The 05:56 ruling stands in substance: one zero-cost GitHub trial, then close either way, no new hosted service. Four things change, all verified before recording:

(1) NEW GATE — THE TRIAL IS BLOCKED ON THE BOOTSTRAP-FLOOR FIX. PR #6894's audit reproduced `bd bootstrap --yes` exiting 1 on a fresh clone: `validation failed for issue rf2-kfpf: invalid status: in_review`. That is NOT an importer bug. `bd config get status.custom` returns `in_review` — a bd CUSTOM STATUS registered only in the Dolt database, used by 8 beads. A fresh clone has an empty database with no status.custom, imports a JSONL containing in_review, and the validator correctly rejects it. Second instance of the rf2-cchlf trap (load-bearing config living only in Dolt, silently breaking the documented recovery path). CONSEQUENCE: both the step-2 fallback (JSONL as executable recovery floor) and the step-1 trial verification clone (which runs bd bootstrap) currently fail for this unrelated reason. DO NOT START STEP 1 until the fix has merged and a disposable fresh-clone `bd bootstrap --yes` completes clean. The fix is small and dispatchable, unlike this bead; the owner bead is being filed by the in_review-cluster disposition — check bd list for it rather than folding that work in here. The status audit's finding is that all 8 in_review records should close, so the preferred end-state is RETIRING the status, not pinning it.

(2) EVIDENCE CORRECTION — a config.yaml pin for custom statuses DOES exist in bd 1.0.3. The dossier's first half concluded there was no YAML key (only yaml:"custom" beside yaml:"types" in a binary grep); the Codex audit contradicted it; adjudicated against released source at 1b2dd2cb: internal/config/config.go registers viper key `status.custom` (SetDefault ""), and GetCustomStatusesFromYAML is documented as the "fallback when the database doesn't have status.custom set yet". The binary grep missed it because viper keys are not struct tags. So `status:\n  custom: "in_review"` in tracked config.yaml is a legitimate EMERGENCY BRIDGE if disk loss precedes the 8-bead disposition: recover with the pin, close the 8, re-export clean, remove the pin. It is a bridge, not the end-state. (Whether bootstrap consults the YAML fallback before import-validation is for the fix owner to prove in a disposable clone.)

(3) AMENDED ORDERING for step 1 — prove recovery BEFORE demoting the working origin (the 05:56 sequence promoted first; Codex's ordering is strictly safer and costs nothing). Exact operator commands, Git Bash, clean mayor checkout:
    bd dolt remote add github-trial git+https://github.com/day8/re-frame2.git
    bd dolt push --remote github-trial
    git ls-remote origin refs/dolt/data        # must now show the ref
Then, BEFORE touching origin, a disposable clone OUTSIDE the worktree parent:
    git clone https://github.com/day8/re-frame2 /c/Users/miket/tmp/rf2-dolt-restore-check
    cd /c/Users/miket/tmp/rf2-dolt-restore-check
    bd bootstrap --dry-run --json   # plan MUST name the Dolt remote, not jsonl-import — that is the whole test
    bd bootstrap --yes
    bd stats                        # recount against the live export AT EXECUTION TIME (2,365 issues / 219 memories at the 2026-07-25 snapshot; tracker churns, do not hold to stale counts)
    bd dolt pull
Only after both directions prove, promote from the mayor checkout (bd dolt remote has no rename, so remove-before-add):
    bd dolt remote remove origin
    bd dolt remote add origin git+https://github.com/day8/re-frame2.git
    bd dolt remote remove github-trial
    bd dolt remote list             # expect the git+https URL, not the file:// path
    bd dolt push
Delete the clone (verification artefact, not a working tree). The promotion writes sync.remote into TRACKED .beads/config.yaml and bd auto-commits it: run only from a clean checkout, inspect the commit, confirm no credential in the URL. Never a token in the URL — rely on Git Credential Manager; if credential discovery fails, ABORT rather than persist a secret. Keep the explicit session-close push the only writer. Close DONE recording the URL, refs/dolt/data, and the fresh-clone counts.

(4) ABORT TRIGGER REFINED. Primary risk is GitHub's 2 GB per-push ceiling, not the 100 MiB per-object limit as first framed: Dolt's git blob store deliberately chunks large tablefiles below a maxPartSize into a tree of smaller blobs precisely because git hosts impose per-object caps (DoltHub blog 2026-02-19, "Supporting Git remotes as Dolt remotes"). Unverified against THIS store (1.8 GB live, archives of 1.50 GB oldgen + 1.08 GB + 638 MB) — which is exactly why it stays a trial, not a plan. On any failure (auth, push ceiling, repo policy, round-trip): no --force, no DoltHub account, `bd dolt remote remove github-trial`; if a partial refs/dolt/data landed, deliberately delete that exact ref (deletion does not guarantee GitHub GCs the objects immediately); go to step 2.

STEP 2 CADENCE CORRECTION: the fallback README section should say the off-box copy is refreshed at ~3.7 min MEAN / 10.8 min worst over the last 30 touching commits (mayor heartbeat + 60 s auto-export throttle) — NOT "every 15 minutes"; the 15 m interval belongs to the separate LOCAL Dolt chunk-store backup under .beads/backup/, which is a different facility and also same-disk. Everything else in step 2 stands: close WONT-DO with the loss list, KEEP the file:// origin (the bare `bd dolt push` in session close depends on it), and kill the false signal in tracked .beads/README.md — origin is machine-local/gitignored/same-disk; the durable copy is .beads/issues.jsonl on the public repo; recovery is bd bootstrap jsonl-import plus whatever status.custom step the fix leaves behind.

RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-25 10:5x AUSEST, all read-only: `bd dolt remote list` still shows only origin -> file://C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/.beads/backup/origin; local backup live (last backup 2 min prior); `bd backup status --json` still reports "dolt": {"configured": false} while the text surface says enabled=true — the two-surface disagreement stands; `git ls-remote origin refs/dolt/*` still empty; `bd config get status.custom` = in_review. Updated snapshot counts: 2,365 issues (2,315 closed / 38 open / 8 in_review / 3 in_progress / 1 blocked) + 219 memories = 2,584 JSONL records, 10.67 MB; prose layer now ~3.87 M chars descriptions, ~3.02 M notes, 526 K close reasons, 963 K acceptance, 2,115 dependency edges. Codex additionally enumerated Dolt branches: only `main` exists (closes evidence item 4). Per-bead history noise re-measured: 1,805-1,808 entries on this 3-day-old bead with only SIX distinct updated_at values — confirming the changelog any remote protects is heartbeat noise.

REAFFIRMED REJECTIONS: DoltHub (free for public DBs — verified — but gold-plating: a new account, credentials, provider and a ~2 GB seed to protect that changelog; only reconsider if the requirement changes from "survive this machine" to "survive loss of GitHub"); any bead for interactions.jsonl (outside Dolt; no remote option would ever have saved it); leaving this bead open past the trial's outcome. DEFERRED-conditional unchanged: Dolt GC of the 1.50 GB oldgen archive, only if step 1 lands and the seed cost bites.

HONEST CAVEAT, carried forward deliberately: the hazard that has actually destroyed tracker state on this project is the .beads export/import time-travel race (PR #6677 and kin) — a git-side failure no Dolt remote would mitigate under ANY of the options weighed. This bead buys survival of one laptop's disk against the loss of a near-zero-value changelog; it must not borrow the race's urgency. Bead stays OPEN, P2, assigned to Mike, as the operator vehicle — gated on the bootstrap fix per (1).

title: Wire the .beads PR-boundary guard into CI so enforcement is not local-hook-only
description:
FOLLOW-UP from the .beads guard work (see the guard bead's PR for the shipped scripts). The classifier, pre-commit block and CI-arm script all shipped, but .github/workflows/** was fenced at the time because several workers were running concurrently, so the CI arm is UNWIRED.

WHY IT MATTERS: enforcement today is local-hook-only. The hook is bypassable with --no-verify and only fires where it has been installed, so a worker that never installed hooks is entirely unguarded. The failure this guards against has already happened once in this repo (a worker-worktree commit of a stale .beads/issues.jsonl time-travelled the tracker, reopening closed issues and deleting new ones), which is why local-only is not sufficient.

THE WORK: add a pull_request step invoking scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh with the base ref. The script is finished and pre-flightable today; this is wiring, not design. Sequence it as a sole-toucher of the workflow file it lands in.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) a PR touching .beads/issues.jsonl from a worker branch FAILS the new check and the message names the file and the remedy; (2) an ordinary PR passes; (3) the mayor's own checkpoint flow is unaffected. Prove (1) and (2) with real runs, not reasoning.

NON-GOALS: changing the classifier or the hook; making the mayor's checkpoint path harder.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6691 open. beads-pr-boundary is now a job of .github/workflows/test.yml listed in all-required-passed's needs: — UNCONDITIONAL (no needs:, no if:, no path filter), and it self-tests the guard (sh scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh, which ran nowhere in CI before) before enforcing. Proofs run the VERBATIM step body (diffed IDENTICAL against test.yml) on a fixture where main carries two mayor checkpoints landed after the worker branches forked: (1) a worker PR carrying .beads/issues.jsonl FAILS exit 1, naming the file and the rebase/checkout remedy; (2) an ordinary PR PASSES exit 0, including an allow-listed .beads/config.yaml; (3) the MAYOR checkpoint flow is unaffected three ways — test.yml's pre-existing paths-ignore .beads/** means a beads-only heartbeat push runs no job at all (now pinned by a policy test), a mixed push that does reach the job exits 0 via the script's event branch, and the pre-commit hook still no-ops in the primary worktree. Depends on rf2-5z20y in the same PR: with the shipped two-endpoint diff this gate would have reddened most open branches for a file they never edited; that is fixed and held by a diverged-history sequence test. Six policy tests pin the wiring; mutations prove they fire. Gates: script-policy exit 0 (changed-surfaces 195 passed), script-helpers exit 0, test-pre-commit 30/0, hardcoded-paths exit 0, test:cljs 10279/51052 green.

title: B4 evidence: controlled editing under contention, and honest per-keystroke scale
description:
D021 measurement B4. The most product-relevant measurement in the set, and the one with the strongest deterministic half.

OUTCOME: typing, selection and IME while a HEAVY SIBLING IS DIRTY AT 20 Hz. Plus a four-field form and a 100-cell editing grid, in BOTH modes. Published: event-to-commit and settlement/presentation p50/p95/p99. GATED: zero dropped input, stable caret/composition, and per-keystroke event / write / subscription-recompute / render-commit COUNTS.

NON-GOALS: a latency threshold. Note that the COUNTS are deterministic gates even though the TIMES are not.

DECISIONS: D021, D009, D016.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. DETERMINISTIC GATE: zero dropped input under 20 Hz sibling contention - the typed string equals the final value exactly.
2. DETERMINISTIC GATE: caret and composition remain stable under contention.
3. DETERMINISTIC GATE: exact per-keystroke event, write, subscription-recompute and render-commit counts for the four-field form and the 100-cell grid, in both modes. A count regression is a real regression.
4. EVIDENCE: event-to-commit and settlement/presentation p50/p95/p99 published with provenance.

GATES: deterministic - zero dropped input, caret/composition stability, exact per-keystroke counts. Evidence-only: latency distributions.

DEPENDS: B0, F2e, F4b.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #6782 (2026-07-24): keep this exact owner in progress; no duplicate Bead is needed. Three acceptance gaps remain in the merged B4 evidence. (1) `compose-under-contention!` captures `before` from `el` and then compares it only with that unchanged local `el`; it never re-queries the container/current node or checks connectivity, so DOM-node replacement can pass the claimed composition-stability gate. (2) `start-ticker!` is not paired with any assertion that a tick occurred or the heavy sibling rendered during the measured edit; a starved or broken interval leaves every "under 20 Hz contention" assertion green. (3) the browser build supplies no revision, `publish!` detects the defect and then directly console-logs a `NOT CITABLE` record instead of using the B-spine's validated provenance door, and the pinned `freehand-bench` workflow neither runs nor retains B4 browser output. Wire a revision-bearing retained browser evidence lane through the validated door. The PR had 38 successful checks and 33 skipped checks, with no comments/review threads; those greens do not cover these non-vacuity/provenance gaps.

title: B-spine: the measurement harness, its provenance record, and the gate-versus-evidence split
description:
EP-0036 / D021. The scaffolding B1-B5 hang off. Lands EARLY so the first fixture has a home; it does NOT wait for F6.

OUTCOME: one small repeatable harness that runs a named workload and emits a result record naming REVISION, FIXTURE PARAMETERS, BUILD/INSTRUMENTATION MODE, BROWSER/RUNTIME, HARDWARE CLASS, WARM-UP/SAMPLE POLICY, DISTRIBUTION, and BASELINE. The harness enforces the D021 split MECHANICALLY: deterministic properties are hard CI gates; wall-clock and byte distributions are PUBLISHED EVIDENCE with no automatic numeric pass/fail. The four named baselines are supported: interpreted vs compiled Freehand; the absorbed tier vs a named donor cut; before vs after an implementation change; and substrate self time vs end-to-end host time.

NON-GOALS: any performance THRESHOLD (D021 forbids automatic numeric pass/fail); a compilation quota; folklore numbers; requiring compiled mode to win every workload.

DECISIONS: D021 (performance budgets and release evidence).

SPEC OWNERS TOUCHED: none required. FH IDS: none.

HOSTS/MODES: browser and JVM; both build modes.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A result record cannot be emitted with a missing provenance field - proof: a test asserting rejection when each field is omitted in turn.
2. A deterministic property registered as a GATE reds CI when violated - proof: a deliberately violating fixture must fail the gate NAMING the property.
3. A timing measurement registered as EVIDENCE does NOT red CI however it moves - proof: a fixture with a wildly changed timing that still exits 0. This asymmetry is the whole point of D021 and must be proven both ways.
4. The harness runs on a pinned scheduled/release worker, with only a stable subset in PR smoke - proof: workflow wiring.

DONOR DISPOSITION: donor benchmark fixtures, if reusable -> MOVE per the F0c ledger.

GATES: deterministic - the harness's own two-way falsifiability proof (3 above). Evidence-only: everything it measures.

DEPENDS: F1c (something must be renderable to measure).
notes:
Implemented in PR #6702 (branch worker/freehand-bspine-drpa3-47).

SHAPE: four namespaces under implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/ + a :bench alias in the artefact deps.edn.
  bench/measure.cljc      enforcement is a total function of the observable (:count/:flag/:value -> :gate; :duration-ms/:bytes -> :evidence). Wrong restatement rejected at construction; a pass/fail key on evidence rejected; a gate without :expect rejected.

notes:

title: Guard .beads against stale worker-worktree commits + configure dolt remote
description: Incident: PR #6677 committed a stale .beads/issues.jsonl from a worker worktree (135+/136- unrelated: reopened rf2-oe9xi, removed rf2-ncm8j, replaced memories) — the stale-worker-snapshot failure mode; blocker recorded in rf2-x4wua. Root cause: bd auto-stages the full-DB JSONL export in EVERY checkout, so a worktree carries a stale snapshot that time-travels the tracker if committed. Fix in three layers, MAYOR-DISPATCHED (touches hot-zone .github/workflows + mayor-owned .beads policy): (1) pre-commit guard rejecting commits touching .beads/ from any non-primary worktree — POSIX sh + .ps1 pair, reusing scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh's mayor/worker derivation; (2) CI gate failing any worker/* PR whose diff touches .beads/; (3) worktree-creation step runs 'git update-index --skip-worktree .beads/issues.jsonl' in new worker checkouts; (4) durable fix: configure the bd dolt remote so beads sync out-of-band via 'bd dolt push' and the JSONL becomes a mayor-only checkpoint artifact (dolt remote currently unconfigured on this box). Acceptance: a worker worktree commit staging .beads fails locally AND in CI with a didactic message; mayor checkpoint flow unaffected; dolt push round-trips; merge-side rule documented (never --theirs/--ours on .beads; resolve-then-regenerate). Cross-platform per repo rule (Windows/Mac/Linux).
close_reason: SHIPPED in PR #6683 (merged). Delivered: the shared classifier scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-beads-boundary.sh, the pre-commit hook block, the CI-arm script scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh, a block-registry refactor of both installers, 25 hook assertions (up from 6), and CLAUDE.md Beads-durability prose. Guard proven in BOTH directions with a real git commit in a throwaway mayor+worktree pair, and the harness itself mutation-tested (neutering the classifier turns 25/0 into 17 passed/8 failed, so the suite can go red). SUBSTANTIVE FINDING recorded rather than shipped: layer 3 (git update-index --skip-worktree on .beads/issues.jsonl in worker checkouts) is WRONG and was measured, not assumed — with skip-worktree set and the file locally modified (the worker steady state, since bd rewrites it), git status shows a clean tree while git pull --rebase aborts, freezing HEAD at a stale base with nothing on screen to explain why. That converts a loud correct refusal into a silent one. Not implemented; a regression test now asserts the guard message never recommends skip-worktree again. TWO PIECES CARVED OUT rather than dropped: CI wiring is rf2-3mh2f (the .github/workflows hot-zone was occupied), and the Dolt remote is rf2-4l67v (operator action, assigned to Mike).

title: UIx frame-root real-DOM mount logs React child errors (fn-as-child + MapEntry-as-child)
description:
Found by the rf2-b16va G1-G4 external boot proof (2026-07-22 14:05 AUSEST). MOUNT-TIME defect, no interaction needed; the app stays functional (DOM renders, counter seeds and increments) but every real-DOM boot of a UIx frame-root logs one console.error and one uncaught pageerror.

REPRO (exact):
1. Scaffold the UIx template app (tools/template, :substrate :uix), :local/root-rewrite deps, npm install, npx shadow-cljs watch app.
2. Open http://localhost:8280 in Chromium; wait for mount. No clicks.
3. Observe:
   - console.error: 'Functions are not valid as a React child ... re_frame$views$provider$frame_provider ... <Fragment>{re_frame$views$provider$frame_provider}</Fragment>'
   - pageerror (uncaught): 'Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {key, val, __hash, cljs$lang$protocol_mask$partition0$, cljs$lang$protocol_mask$partition1$})' — a cljs MapEntry reached React children.

SCOPE EVIDENCE: the Reagent scaffold uses the SAME frame-root two-pass pattern (rf/frame-root via reagent adapter) and boots with ZERO errors — so this is UIx-adapter-specific, likely in the defui prop/children folding into the shared two-pass core (re-frame.adapter.uix/frame-root -> boundary/frame-root-react-element -> re-frame.views.provider/frame-provider element build). The template's usage matches frame-root's own docstring exactly, so this is NOT a template defect.

WHY EXISTING GATES MISS IT: the UIx adapter smoke (implementation/adapters/uix/testbed) mounts via frame-provider after manual make-frame + dispatch-sync — frame-root's real-DOM path has no browser coverage; node-side tests don't surface React child console errors.

SURFACE: implementation/adapters/uix (+ shared provider spine in core if the fold is shared). Production src — out of rf2-b16va's validation scope, hence this bead.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (proven by isolated repro): NOT the UIx frame-root/defui fold — that path boots clean (verified: scratch UIx app, frame-root mount, real-DOM Chromium, zero errors without the Xray preload). The errors come from the XRAY PRELOAD on a UIx host: day8.re-frame2-xray.mount/mount-shell-into! (+ popout!) hands the HICCUP tree [rf/frame-provider {:frame :rf/xray} [shell/shell-view ...]] to substrate-adapter/render; the React-hook spine's make-render (shared by UIx/Helix/ui) passes the tree to React untouched inside its Fragment wrap. React iterates the CLJS vector as children: the frame-provider FN becomes a Fragment child (console.error #1, names re_frame$views$provider$frame_provider) and the props map iterates to MapEntry objects, which are not iterable -> uncaught 'Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {key, val, __hash, ...})'. Reagent template boots clean because its render slot is hiccup-native. Repro red/green captured with a scratch shadow build (template shape + xray preload): before fix = exactly the 2 recorded errors; after fix = 0 errors/pageerrors + one intentional console.warn. FIX: substrate render-shape gate in xray mount (denylist :rf.adapter/ui|uix|helix -> :unsupported-substrate diagnostic + console.warn, no mount); uix adapter smoke now mounts via frame-root and asserts a clean boot.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6673 (worker/uix-frameroot-qgfo4). Root cause was NOT the UIx frame-root/defui fold (proven clean by isolated real-DOM repro): the Xray preload handed its hiccup shell to the UIx host's element-shaped :render, so React iterated the hiccup vector as children (frame-provider fn-as-child console.error + uncaught MapEntry pageerror). Fix: xray mount verbs refuse React-element substrate kinds (:rf.adapter/ui|uix|helix) with an :unsupported-substrate diagnostic + one console.warn; uix adapter smoke now mounts via frame-root and asserts a clean boot (zero console errors / pageerrors). Red/green captured on the actual failing path. Follow-up (real Xray-on-UIx support or template preload removal): rf2-p6f6u.

title: Routing popstate-mid-push-stress flakes intermittently under nightly CI load (invariant-3 slice non-convergence)
description:
Split off from rf2-wh5to (nightly expensive-tests repair). The JVM stress test re-frame.routing-concurrency-stress-test/popstate-mid-push-stress (implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_concurrency_stress_test.clj:330) fails INTERMITTENTLY in the nightly 'JVM slow/stress tests (routing)' job — NOT every night. When it fails it fails HARD: e.g. run 29760811080 (2026-07-20) reported 28 assertion failures, invariant 3 'per-frame slice converged' — 'Frame :ksbur.pop/f7: slice should reflect the LAST URL pushed by this thread; expected "4999" got "694"'. The slug reflects a mid-run iteration, not the last one, while the per-thread on-match counters (invariants 1+2) are correct — i.e. the [:rf.runtime/routing :current] slice systematically lags for some frames under contention, even though every on-match event fired.

REPRODUCTION STATUS: could NOT reproduce locally on Windows (opus worker, rf2-wh5to). Ran popstate-mid-push-stress in isolation 12x + once standalone — 27 assertions, 0 failures every time. It is load/scheduling dependent (CI runners = 2-4 vCPU; heavier lock interleaving). This is why a validated root-cause fix was out of scope for the wh5to turn.

REGRESSION WINDOW: the test (rf2-ksbur) was added 2026-05-15 and was GREEN on the last-green nightly 2026-07-07 (run 28880733495). It began flaking intermittently within the 07-08..20 streak. Prime suspect: 02ec7dbc4c (2026-07-08 'refactor(api): consolidate frame-state I/O to replace-frame-state!', rf2-t3lftq) — landed on the first-red day and changed the per-frame commit path (commit-frame-record-transition! read-then-replace in implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1319). That path is 'effectively atomic' ONLY under the single-writer-per-frame assumption; this test has one thread per frame so that holds, which makes the slice-lag surprising and worth a careful look. Secondary leads: the routing module-level defonce caches keyed by frame-id (nav_counters.cljc nav-counters-cache, nav_fx.cljc url-claim-order [not used here — frames are :url-bound? false], routing/registry.cljc route-table-cache) and whether any part of url-change-fx's :current-slice publish is deferred past dispatch-sync's drain.

ACCEPTANCE: reproduce reliably (e.g. run under CPU-pinned/oversubscribed contention, or bump n-threads/stress-iters, or add controlled interleaving), root-cause the slice non-convergence, fix it deterministically (NOT a skip/retry/loosened invariant unless the invariant is proven wrong), and show the fix green under the repro. Do NOT touch the compiler-cache/digest surface (C0/u53yy.1). Hot-zone: expensive-tests.yml is NOT expected to change.
notes:
REFRAME (worker, definitive): NOT a concurrent-RMW slice race. Root cause = CPU-STARVATION WALL-CLOCK TIMEOUT. Fetched the actual failing CI log (run 29760811080, routing job 88414672832): popstate-mid-push-stress per-thread counters were [648 660 660 696 664 639 695 689] (expected 5000 each) and Global AtomicLong got 5371/40000 -> the 8 threads completed only ~13% of their 5000 iters within the 120s per-future deref bound. So invariants 1 AND 2 ALSO failed (bead's 'counters correct' premise is FALSE); invariant-3 'slug=694' is a downstream symptom = the slug reflects the ~694th iter where the starved thread stopped, not a lost write. Prime suspect 02ec7dbc4c / commit RMW is a RED HERRING (the RMW predates it; introduced 38c9671d97). Evidence it is NOT a race: (1) instrumented multi-writer detector (add-watch each stress frame's container, flag any frame written by >1 thread) ran ~580 S1+S2 runs pinned 2-core -> ZERO concurrent writers; (2) faithful 'clojure -M:slow-test' normal-heap verified-2vCPU-pins -> 24+ runs green; (3) reproduced the EXACT CI failure signature locally only via extreme starvation (8 JVMs x 8 threads on 2 cores, 128m). Under single-drainer-per-frame (dispatch-sync sets router :scheduled?=true before draining so child :dispatch never arms the async executor) + linearizable clojure-atom containers, a 'counters-correct + slug-lags' race is architecturally impossible. FIX is test/infra tuning, NOT a framework RMW change: the 8x5000-iter test assumes ~60s but the loaded nightly runner starves it ~8x. Needs a decision (Mike/mayor): reduce CI iters (RF2_KSBUR_STRESS_ITERS override / lower default), raise the 120s deref bound, or de-contend the nightly runner so the routing job isn't starved. Does NOT loosen the correctness invariants (they stay; the test just needs to COMPLETE before they're checked). No code changed; worktree clean; blind-patching the RMW was correctly avoided (banned + wrong).
RE-SCOPE (worker STOP-report, evidence-backed 2026-07-21): NOT a slice race — it's a CPU-STARVATION WALL-CLOCK TIMEOUT. CI log (run 29760811080) shows 8 threads completed only ~650/5000 iters before the 120s deref bound; invariants 1/2/3 all fail because the run never FINISHES, not because of a race. Multi-writer detector: ~580 runs, ZERO concurrent writers. The RMW 'prime suspect' predates the named commit + is a red herring. Faithful clojure -M:slow-test: 24+ runs green. The bead's prescribed atomic-RMW fix would fix nothing (blind-patch correctly avoided). NEEDS RULING (hot-zone expensive-tests.yml): re-scope to 'routing stress test times out under nightly CPU starvation'; options (none loosen invariants): (a) lower CI stress-iters (RF2_KSBUR_STRESS_ITERS~500), (b) raise the 120s deref bound (may be insufficient — ~925s needed at worst-case), (c) de-contend the nightly runner. Mayor: surface to Mike for the tuning call.
RULING (Mike, 2026-07-22 00:55 AUSEST): OPTION 1 — LOWER the CI iteration count. Set RF2_KSBUR_STRESS_ITERS ~500 for the nightly expensive-tests.yml routing stress run, so the popstate-mid-push-stress test COMPLETES within the 120s deref bound under the loaded runner (worker proved: it's a CPU-starvation wall-clock timeout at ~5000 iters, NOT a concurrency race; invariants 1/2/3 are correct — they just need the run to finish). Does NOT loosen any correctness invariant. Re-scope the bead to this tuning fix.
DELIVERED (worker, 2026-07-22): Option 1 per Mike's ruling. Set RF2_KSBUR_STRESS_ITERS=500 on the jvm-slow-tests 'Run JVM slow/stress tests' step in .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml, scoped to the routing matrix artefact (${{ matrix.artefact == 'routing' && '500' || '' }}). Before->after: nightly routing stress iters 5000 (default) -> 500 (CI override only). Test DEFAULT unchanged (stays 5000; scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh still full-strength; sibling machines/core/flows stress tests untouched). NO change to the correctness invariants (1/2/3), assertions, 120s deref bound, or frame-state I/O — ONLY the CI iteration count. Gates: RF2_KSBUR_STRESS_ITERS=500 clojure -M:slow-test (routing) EXIT 0 ~88s, 3 tests/73 assertions/0 failures (popstate-mid-push-stress green, completes far under 120s); clojure -M:test (routing) EXIT 0, 458 tests/2382 assertions/0 failures; YAML parse OK. Rebased onto current origin/main (post rf2-vxgfnd.99.2). Sole expensive-tests.yml toucher; disjoint from u53yy.1 S6 + vxgfnd.99.2. PR #6656 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6656 (NOT merged).

description:

This bead is fully self-contained — do NOT look for any ai/ dossier (local-only, absent from worker worktrees). The parent epic carries the end-state seven-name surface and the NOT-BUILD fence; obey both.

BLOCKED on the four sibling implementation children of this epic (dep edges wired on this bead): dispatch! deletion, find/find-all + 004D retirement, with-root-container + query deletion, render narrowing + JVM-arity deletion. Runs LAST — the docs must describe the shipped surface, not anticipate it. No runtime/API change in this bead: prose, skills, and generated-sheet regeneration only. This bead ABSORBS rf2-u53yy.10's ratified frameless-first testing-guide scope (that bead is closed superseded by the mayor; its note points here).

## The surface being taught (the seven names, final)

```clojure
;; JVM structural host
(ui.test/render [view props] {:sub-overrides {query-v value}}) ; opts optional; ONE grammar, ONE option
(ui.test/attrs node)
(ui.test/text node)

;; CLJS mounted host
(ui.test/with-root [container [app-root ...]] body ...) ; binds the connected DOM container
(ui.test/flush!)  (ui.test/flush! thunk)
(ui.test/flush-presence!)  (ui.test/flush-presence! ms)
```

## The work

1. REWRITE docs/core/re-frame.ui/testing.md around the final surface, LEADING with the frameless zero-fixture example:

```clojure
(deftest add-button-carries-intent
  (let [tree (ui.test/render [app/add-button {:product-id 42}]
                             {:sub-overrides {[:cart/locked?] false}})]
    (is (= [:cart/add 42]
           (-> (some #(when (= :button (:tag %)) %)
                     (tree-seq map? :children tree))
               ui.test/attrs
               :on-click)))))
```

(The rf2-u53yy.10 original of this example used `ui.test/find` — rewritten here to the tree-seq idiom because `find` is deleted; the `attrs` read is what closes the `:events` trap.) For a view with no sub reads, show the options map omitted entirely. The frameless example is within one concept of a pure-function data assertion while keeping real view identity — the shortest correct example is the one humans AND assistants copy.

2. THEN the runtime-bracket step-up: `rf/with-new-frame [f (rf/make-frame ...)]` (+ `:initial-events`); drive with `(rf/dispatch-sync [...] {:frame f})` (`{:frame ...}` accepts value or id); assert on a FRESH `(ui.test/render ...)`. title: Delete ui.test/dispatch! — teach rf/dispatch-sync
description:
Ratified from the 2026-07-21 ui.test dedup reviews, Mike-approved; all decisions final; no operator input needed. This bead is fully self-contained — do NOT look for any ai/ dossier (local-only, absent from worker worktrees). The parent epic carries the end-state seven-name surface and the NOT-BUILD fence; obey both.

## The work

DELETE `ui.test/dispatch!` from implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/test.cljc and migrate every call site to the facade spellings. Independent — no dependency on any sibling bead.

Its entire body is `(router/dispatch-sync! event {:frame frame-target})` then `nil` (test.cljc:749-756). It fuses nothing: no tree refresh (Tier-1 re-renders are explicit `render` calls), no extra drain (`dispatch-sync` already drains synchronously-enqueued events to fixed point), no mounted mode (on CLJS the settle work lives entirely in `flush!`'s thunk wrapper).

## Why (the three arguments, settled)

1. No-re-export violation: Spec 008:23 — "re-frame.test-support does not re-export from re-frame.core ... The split is deliberate." `dispatch!` is exactly such a re-export, re-spelled into ui.test.
2. Call-site-capture loss: the facade macro stamps `:rf.trace/call-site` for error-trace attribution ("Captures call-site coords (rf2-ts1a)", core.cljc:1133-1140); the wrapper calls `router/dispatch-sync!` raw and bypasses the stamp — today every `ui.test/dispatch!` test gets WORSE trace attribution than production code.
3. Reversed-argument hazard: `(dispatch! frame event)` vs `(dispatch-sync event {:frame f})` — same operation, two names, two argument conventions; an assistant will inevitably use one with the other's order.

Drift history (the argument made flesh): the one-line wrapper's documentation needed reconciling twice — rf2-vxgfnd.208 (contradictory S1/S2 stage ownership; the cleanup "chose the wrong side") and rf2-vxgfnd.293 (two authorities still wrong after the first fix). The standing attribution-guard block that policed the word `dispatch!` (formerly guide_truth_jvm_test.clj:758-811) is ALREADY GONE — rf2-j97yg / PR #6613 (merged 2026-07-21) deleted guide_truth_jvm_test.clj entirely; verified absent in the mayor checkout. No action is owed on that file; the history stands as evidence only.

## Replacement spellings (both verified working today)

- Headless: `(rf/dispatch-sync [:cart/add 42] {:frame f})` then a fresh `(ui.test/render ...)`.
- Mounted: `(ui.test/flush! #(rf/dispatch-sync [:cart/add 42] {:frame f}))` — tests already use exactly this shape (frame_ops_dom_cljs_test.cljs:78 runs a dispatch inside a `flush!` thunk).

`{:frame ...}` accepts a frame value or id — `frame-target->id` normalizes; "the value is accepted EVERYWHERE a keyword id is (API-shrink #1, rf2-csbbwu)" (frame.cljc:186-198).

title: ui.test minimal surface (dedup-review ratified)
description:
Design ratified by Mike 2026-07-21; all decisions below are final; no further operator input is required to implement. Provenance: ratified from the 2026-07-21 ui.test dedup reviews (two converged adversarial reviews), Mike-approved. Every child bead is fully self-contained — implementing workers must NOT look for any ai/ dossier (the ai/ tree is local-only and absent from worker worktrees).

## End-state surface (SEVEN names, one namespace)

```clojure
;; JVM structural host
(ui.test/render [view props] {:sub-overrides {query-v value}}) ; opts optional; ONE input grammar (the literal plan-free view form); ONE option (:sub-overrides)
(ui.test/attrs node)
(ui.test/text node)

;; CLJS mounted host
(ui.test/with-root [container [app-root ...]] body ...) ; binds the connected DOM CONTAINER, not an opaque MountedRoot
(ui.test/flush!)  (ui.test/flush! thunk)
(ui.test/flush-presence!)  (ui.test/flush-presence! ms)
```

DELETED: `dispatch!`; `find`; `find-all`; `query`; render's `:frame` and `:props` options (and, with `:props`, the bare view-reference input form it serviced); the plan-bearing render route; the public JVM `flush!` arity; the JVM `flush-presence!` no-op; spec/004D-UI-Test-Selectors.md entirely (179 lines). The `^:no-doc` macro/runtime seams stay implementation-only (excluded from docs/manifest); seams only the deleted routes consume are deleted with them.

TAUGHT IN THEIR PLACE: `rf/dispatch-sync` + `{:frame ...}` (and the thunk form inside CLJS `flush!` for mounted); `rf/with-frame` / `rf/with-new-frame` for frame scope; ONE canonical `tree-seq` + visible-predicate idiom for traversal; native `.querySelector` / `.querySelectorAll` on the bound container.

THE ONE-SENTENCE STORY: rf/ drives and reads state, test-support isolates and waits, ui.test renders, projects, and settles.

## Organizing principle

Keep only what crosses a real host boundary, plus the two tree-ABI projections `attrs`/`text`. The projections close the schema traps: `(:on-click node)` silently misses because events live under `:events` — `attrs` is the one attribute read that merges element `:attrs` + `:events`, returns view-boundary `:props`, `{}` on fragment/html (test.cljc:198-226); `text` is document-order text concatenation with the trusted-HTML rule (trusted HTML contributes nothing, test.cljc:228-259). The schema-trap protection always lived in these projections, never in the selector verbs.

## Deletion roster (one-line evidence each)

- `dispatch!` — its entire body is `(router/dispatch-sync! event {:frame frame-target})` (test.cljc:749-756); loses the facade macro's `:rf.trace/call-site` capture (core.cljc:1133-1140); violates Spec 008:23's no-re-export rule; its attribution drifted twice (closed beads rf2-vxgfnd.208 / rf2-vxgfnd.293).
- `find` / `find-all` — a four-predicate selector grammar (tag kw, view-id kw/Var, attr-map by rf=, pred-fn — test.cljc:287-356) over deliberately plain data; `tree-seq` + a visible predicate is ordinary Clojure; its spec (004D, 179 lines) carries a rulings trail (prefix-find rejected, OPEN-2 dropped, find! parked) — the maintenance signature of a bespoke grammar.
- `query` — a guarded `(.querySelector (.-container root) css)` (test.cljc:705-738; its own docstring: "CSS is the whole contract"); with the container bound by `with-root`, the host API covers it — including the `querySelectorAll` the wrapper never offered.
- render `:frame` — the frameless arm inherits an outer binding (test.cljc:928-935, `:else (slice)`), so `rf/with-frame` / `rf/with-new-frame` (bind AND destroy on exit, core.cljc:1484-1504) already cover frame scope; a second spelling for one concept.
- render `:props` — a second input grammar; the literal view form carries props: `(ui.test/render [product-card {:product p}])`.
- the plan-bearing render route — ~200 lines of parallel frame-lifecycle policy (claimed-plan-ids CAS, must-create install, incarnation-pinned teardown — test.cljc:937-1110) for 19 call sites in three framework test files.
- the public JVM `flush!` arity — Tier-1's checkpoint is a fresh render after synchronous `rf/dispatch-sync`; the only verified JVM consumer (reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc:288-304) is the conformance test of the drain itself.
- the JVM `flush-presence!` no-op — false portability: JVM presence has no lifecycle (the JVM emitter renders `:present`, spec/004:648-661); dual-host runner code uses reader conditionals.
- spec/004D-UI-Test-Selectors.md — retired whole with the grammar it specifies.

## NOT-BUILD fence (permanent record; binds every child and all future work)

- NO replacement selector language of any kind. 004D's parked/rejected extensions — `find!`, path/vector selectors, prefix/testid sugar, `query-all` — die with 004D and are recorded HERE as not-build.
- NO gesture/event DSL (Spec 008: "There is no gesture DSL" — native events at Tier 3, intent-equality at Tier 1).
- NO test-only frame constructor or reset (test-support owns fixtures; `rf/make-frame` is the one grammar).
- NO re-export of rf verbs into ui.test (the Spec 008:23 no-re-export rule — the lesson of `dispatch!`).
- NO second flush idiom or setTimeout-settle helper (`flush!` is "the only test flush", spec/004:1207).
- NO test driver/scheduler object.
- NO compatibility aliases for any deleted verb.
- NO traversal helper fn shipped in ui.test — the tree-seq idiom is taught in docs, not packaged.
- Do NOT expose the adapter's `flush-render!` as a settle substitute — it is a synchronous production/tooling commit hook (adapter.cljc:620) without the awaited act/effect boundary that makes `flush!` correct.

## :sub-overrides — documentary consolidation (no code change anywhere)

One conceptual owner: the dynamic var `re-frame.ui.reactive/*sub-overrides*` (reactive.cljc:242-341). `ui.test/render` is the JVM carriage (binds the var around the render thunk, test.cljc:918-920); Story's React context Provider is the mounted carriage (implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/sub_override_context.cljs publishes the map; implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/sub_overrides.cljs:1-36 reads it; implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/viewcell.cljs:113-137 binds the SAME var around each compiled body). Both converge on `reactive/resolve-override` and the single `validate-sub-override!` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/override_schema.cljc). Retain the fidelity warning: overrides affect render reads only — they do not mutate app-db or make `compute-sub` assertions pass. No public `with-sub-overrides`, resolver object, provider API, or second validation layer — the semantic core is already shared at the var.

## Sequencing (mayor executes)

- Child .1 (dispatch!) is dispatchable immediately.
- Children .2/.3/.4 ALL edit implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/test.cljc — SERIALIZE them (one at a time, any order; no wired dep edges among them). Child .1 also touches that file, so in practice keep exactly ONE of the four implementation children in flight at a time.
- Child .5 (docs/skills) runs LAST — dep edges wired (it depends on .1/.2/.3/.4).
- spec/004-Views.md + spec/008-Testing.md + spec/API.md are hot-zone — sole toucher per PR; never two open PRs touching them.
- EVERY child regenerates the api-manifest (from implementation/scripts/api-manifest/: `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen`, then `--check` green — ui.test is under drift enforcement; the curated sidecar spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn rows for deleted vars are removed by hand, the manifest itself is generated, never hand-edited) and, where its surface changes, the generated ui-context sheet (`clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.ui-context` — regenerate, never hand-edit).

## Migration size (repo-internal; no external users)

~58 `dispatch!` sites (~18 files); ~112 `find`/`find-all` sites (15+2 files); ~143 `query` + ~103 `with-root` sites in one mechanical pass; 19 plan-bearing render calls in 3 framework test files; plus the spec/doc/skills sweep. Counts include comments/contract strings — migration-size signals. All mechanical.

title: Make data-rf-render-key an owned, truthful DOM stamp
description: PR #6601 stamps data-rf-render-key imperatively after a connected commit, but the stamp has no explicit ownership boundary. In development it overwrites a programmer-authored attribute that production preserves. If a direct host root changes from no ref to an authored ref while React reuses the DOM node, the old framework callback detaches without removing its stamp, leaving a stale render key on a now-opted-out node. This makes the DOM evidence lie and creates avoidable dev/production drift. Keep the repair narrow: treat own authored data-rf-render-key presence as an opt-out; track and remove only framework-owned stamps when the callback detaches or ownership changes; preserve authored callback/object ref semantics. Specify the exact dev-only attribute and ownership/collision rule in Spec 004. Do not add a history system or a new tooling API. The broader tool-projection work remains with in-progress rf2-vxgfnd.98.1.2.
acceptance_criteria: A programmer-authored data-rf-render-key survives development commits unchanged; framework-owned stamps update on each connected commit; a no-ref to authored-ref transition on a reused host node removes the prior framework-owned stamp without disturbing the authored ref; focused browser tests prove both transitions; Spec 004 names data-rf-render-key, commit-time ownership, development-only erasure, and the collision/cleanup rule; production elision remains green.
notes:
PR #6621 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6621), branch worker/render-key-stamp-98-1-3. Made data-rf-render-key an OWNED + TRUTHFUL stamp mirroring the rf2-x1nbv authored-wins law: authored value wins (opt-out at stamp time against the committed node), framework claims only unclaimed roots + re-stamps only its own node per commit, and removes ONLY its own stamp when host-cb detaches / ownership moves to an authored ref on a reused node (owned-ref tracks the owned node). All DEBUG-gated (host-ref/owned-ref/setAttribute/removeAttribute DCE under :advanced). Spec 004 §Source-DOM navigation now names the attr + commit-time ownership + dev-only erasure + collision/cleanup rule. Red->green proven in browser: pre-fix clobbered 'author-owned' with '339'/'340' and left stale '341'; fixed both green. Gates green: ui JVM 993/0, test:cljs 10366/0, test:browser 512/0 (ran to completion), test:elision 60/60 absent, test:browser-prod-elision 118/0. Disjoint from vz6a1. Not merged.
PR #6621 THREE-LENS AUDIT FOLLOW-UP (2026-07-21): REOPENED. The shipped ownership logic handles an authored data-rf-render-key from first mount and a no-ref -> authored-ref transition, but misses the ordinary same-node absent -> authored-attribute transition. Render 1 claims node and stores owned-ref. On render 2 React commits data-rf-render-key="author-owned", but stampable-host-root? ignores that final prop and the layout effect tests owned-ref identity before hasAttribute, so it overwrites the programmer value with the next numeric render key. This directly violates the authored-wins rule and recreates dev/production drift. BOUNDED FIX: recognize own data-rf-render-key presence on the current final React element props (including spread-produced props) before the owned-node update, relinquish framework ownership without touching the authored value, and prove one same-ViewCell/same-node absent -> authored browser transition. Keep cleanup and DOM collision fallback as needed. No general DOM-ownership framework or history/tool API.

title: Finish foreign ui/spread merge semantics and contract projection
description: PR #6597 added foreign-component ui/spread, but foreign-spread-props does not fully implement the open-props/literal-wins contract and no test executes it. It skips nil literal values, so a forwarded value survives although a normal foreign literal prop supplies an own null and literal ownership is specified to win every collision. It also assigns a forwarded __proto__ key onto {}, invoking JavaScript prototype-setter semantics instead of preserving an own verbatim prop, unlike the existing literal JSX invariant. The contract sweep also left final EP-0031 describing every ui/spread as a 004B rule-table conversion, and the Reagent migration skill says both spread choices are DOM-only immediately before documenting foreign spread. Complete the shipped feature without a generic validator, sanitizer, or merge framework.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve forwarded names and values as own props without changing the output object prototype, including __proto__; layer compiled literal keys by presence so they win collisions even for nil/null, while retaining false and 0; add a focused CLJS runtime or React-capture test that executes the helper and pins verbatim names, ordinary and nil collision precedence, and __proto__ ownership; add a dated EP-0031 correction distinguishing DOM/custom-element conversion from unconverted foreign spread; remove the migration skill contradiction; run focused UI, CLJS, skill, and docs gates; add no public API or generalized defensive machinery.
notes:
PR #6635 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6635) — foreign-spread-props now (1) layers every own literal key by presence (literal wins even for nil/null; false/0 retained) and (2) routes __proto__ through defineProperty (verbatim own prop, no prototype mutation) via a small private set-own!. Focused CLJS test executes the helper directly, red→green (5 failures pre-fix -> 0). EP-0031 dated erratum + reagent-migration catalog-judgment.md 'both DOM only' claim removed. spec/004-Views already correct (literal wins any collision; DOM vs foreign distinguished) so no spec change - disjoint from u53yy.9. Gates: test:cljs 10366/0-0, ui JVM 955/0-0, migration skill drift gates 0. Awaiting merge.
PR #6635 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT RIDER (2026-07-21) — reopen this exact source owner; no duplicate Bead and no generalized merge/object machinery.

Two bounded residuals remain after the otherwise sound #6635 repair:

1. FORWARDED KEY STILL BEATS LITERAL KEY AT REACT. The foreign merge helper correctly layers ordinary props, but the compiler extracts a literal :key from the literal object and calls runtime/jsx-spread3 with it as React's third argument while leaving a forwarded own "key" in the config object. React 19.2.0 applies the third argument first and then config.key, so the forwarded key wins and dev emits the key-spread warning. Reproduced against the checked-in runtime: jsx(F,{key:"forwarded"},"literal").key == "forwarded". This violates Spec 004/API's literal-wins-any-collision contract and the PR's own acceptance. Smallest fix: at the explicit-key jsx-spread3 seam, remove the runtime-built config object's own "key" before calling jsx/jsxs, so the separately compiled literal key is authoritative; add one real React-element regression proving a literal key beats a forwarded key and no config-key path remains. Do not add a validator or generalized props framework.

2. PUBLIC RECOVERY TRUTH STILL SAYS DOM-ONLY. re-frame.ui/spread's public docstring and direct-call error, the compiler's :rf.ui.compile/bad-spread recovery, the re-frame2-ui-context diagnostic row, and Spec 009's :rf.error/ui-spread-outside-template catalogue row still say the form is legal only at DOM/custom props and always uses the conversion rule table. Correct those existing surfaces to name both contextual forms: DOM/custom uses rule-table conversion with later-arg precedence; FOREIGN uses an opaque runtime map layered under compiled literal props. Strengthen the existing error-roster assertion and sync the generated spec mirror. This is a small truth sweep, not an API/runtime redesign or new test framework.

Everything else reviewed clean: own enumerable map-key semantics, null/false/0 layering, forwarded/literal __proto__ ownership, ref/children behavior, evaluation order/once-only, advanced stability, docs/EP + migration projection, and broad green CI. Raw JS objects, Symbols, inherited properties, and a generalized object model are not part of the runtime-map contract and are explicitly out of scope.

title: Correct form-action routing guidance across client and server
description: skills/re-frame2/patterns/form-action.md teaches two incorrect/needlessly indirect routing patterns. Its success fx emits both a server redirect and universal :dispatch of :rf.route/navigate while labelling the latter client-only; on the server that event still changes route state and can run route work even though browser history is absent. The same paragraph tells programmers to register an app-owned effect for a bare URL, although the shipped request grammar directly supports [:rf.route/navigate {:url "/cart"}]. title: Make the S6 commit-record root identity and tool exposure truthful
description:
PR #6582 declares the S6 per-commit record shipped under `re-frame.ui.tool/schema-version` 3, with a serializable authored keyword `:root-id` and Xray/Story/Pair moving in lockstep. The implementation instead stores `(:root st0)` in `:root-id`; that value is the opaque per-mount root-incarnation object, and the initial mount record can be nil-rooted because ViewCell reconciliation commits before `attach-root!`. A rooted JVM repro returns the exact opaque object, not a keyword. The existing tool evidence layer already resolves incarnation -> authored root ID for S3 records, but none of `tool/evidence/instance-records`, `tool/mounted-views`, or `tool/explain-render` reads `reactive/commit-record`. Consequently the public version-3 tool envelopes expose only the old cumulative S3 shape, while Spec 009 says the new record is read through those projections.

title: Make the re-frame.ui tool schema-version boundary real
description:
PR #6582 advertised `re-frame.ui.tool/schema-version` 3 as a lockstep producer/consumer compatibility boundary, but the consumers do not independently own the version they understand. Xray compares an envelope to the producer's own `tool/schema-version`; Story defines `consumed-schema-version` as that same producer var and continues shaping manifest/mounted/render data after setting `:version-mismatch?`; Pair, which can connect to an arbitrarily old or new running app, forwards every stamped envelope as `:ok? true` and has no supported-version check. The changed tests and descriptor golden mostly replace version examples, so they stay green without proving mismatch degradation.

This makes the version contract nominal: an incompatible producer shape can be accepted as if understood. Keep the repair small. Give Xray, Story, and Pair a consumer-owned literal expected version; on mismatch, suppress shape-dependent parsing and return the consumer's existing explicit empty/status form or a typed `:ok? false` mismatch. Add one focused test per consumer that injects a producer stamp different from the consumer pin. Do not build negotiation, migrations, or a compatibility framework.
acceptance_criteria: Xray, Story, and Pair compare producer envelopes with a consumer-owned expected version rather than deriving support from `re-frame.ui.tool/schema-version`; Story does not return parsed shape-dependent fields on mismatch; Pair reports an explicit typed mismatch rather than forwarding it as success; focused mismatch tests fail if only the producer version changes; ordinary version-3 reads remain unchanged.
notes: PR #6618 opened (worker/tool-schema-version-98-1-1). Made the version boundary REAL: each consumer (Xray/Story/Pair) now owns a LITERAL expected schema-version instead of deriving it from the producer's tool/schema-version. Xray rows->[] + version-status mismatch; Story suppresses all shape-dependent fields on mismatch; Pair emits typed :view-tier-version-mismatch (isError) instead of :ok? true. One focused RED->GREEN mismatch test per consumer + a new conformance fixture. title: Make ui/->react's frame prop exact and self-attributing
description:
The public ui/->react bridge reserves a foreign React prop named frame. title: Honor explicit fragment overrides on unmatched raw-URL navigation
description:
PR #6581 promises that :url + :fragment is legal and the explicit request fragment overrides any fragment embedded in the raw URL. That holds when the URL matches a route because route-url rebuilds the address, but the unmatched shortcut pushes unmatched-url verbatim.

Current-main reproduction: [:rf.route/navigate {:url "/missing#old" :fragment "new"}] commits the not-found slice with :fragment "new" but pushes "/missing#old". The address bar, route slice, and guard/pending target therefore disagree. An explicit nil similarly cannot clear an embedded fragment. The focused tests cover embedded-fragment preservation and unmatched URL preservation separately, but not their documented combination.

Use one effective requested URL for unmatched navigation: preserve the raw path/query, replace or clear its fragment from the explicit request key, and feed that same URL to guards, pending-navigation, not-found params, history push, and the committed slice. Add one focused regression including override and clear; do not redesign raw-URL parsing or not-found policy.

While touching the fragment contract, truth the remaining normative residue in spec/012-Routing.md that still mentions route-url's deleted 4-arity and navigate's deleted opt/target-map split. Comments-only fixture/test wording is not an audit deliverable.

title: Make flat navigate and route-url map boundaries exact and total
description:
PR #6581 replaced positional navigation with one flat request map and described the boundary as always-on, closed, and total. Several malformed or half-migrated shapes still escape that contract:

- An in-place request may include :params whenever it also carries :query, :query-merge, or :fragment. Reproduction: after navigating to /items/old, dispatching [:rf.route/navigate {:params {:id "new"} :fragment "x"}] emits no navigate-bad-request and pushes /items/old#x; the supplied params are silently ignored. The ratified table says :params is never accepted in-place because changing params requires :to.
- A non-map request reaches dissoc and throws a raw host exception. A third event element is silently ignored, so a plausible half-migrated [:rf.route/navigate {:to :route/x} {:replace? true}] navigates while dropping the trailing opts.
- Mixed-kind unknown keys reach plain sort and can throw instead of producing :unknown-keys.
- The public single-map route-url boundary has the same rough edge: non-maps/raw missing-:to shapes produce raw or misleading host errors, and mixed-kind bad keys can fail while sorting instead of raising :rf.error/route-url-validation.

This is one authoring-boundary repair, not a validation project. Before request processing, require exactly the two-element navigate event and a map payload; reject :params without a destination; make bad-key reporting total over arbitrary EDN keys. At route-url, require an address map with :to and route all address-shape failures through the existing route-url-validation error. Keep the current closed roster and existing rich behavior.

BOUNDARIES: small explicit checks plus focused JVM/CLJS parity tests. No compatibility shim, Malli/request-schema framework, builder DSL, strict-mode option, or generic validator.
acceptance_criteria: - :rf.route/navigate rejects non-map payloads, extra event elements, and :params without :to/:url through :rf.error/navigate-bad-request before guards; slice and URL stay unchanged. - Unknown-key reporting is total for heterogeneous EDN keys on JVM and CLJS. - route-url rejects non-map, missing-:to, and heterogeneous-bad-key addresses through :rf.error/route-url-validation rather than raw/misleading host exceptions. - Focused JVM/CLJS controls cover the boundary cases. - No compatibility syntax, schema framework, builder, or new public API is added.

title: Attribute :local-state only after a real React commit
description:
PR #6577 claims `:local-state` is attributed only to an "actually committed" state change, but `local-state` calls `reactive/note-local-state!` as a side effect inside the React functional state updater. `Object.is(cur,nv)` proves that one queued step changes its input; it does not prove the batch produces a commit. React also requires updater functions to be pure and may replay/discard their render work.

A real React 19.2 Chromium probe demonstrates the residual contamination without speculative concurrency: one batched `0→1` update followed by `1→0` runs both updater callbacks and renders a candidate, but commits nothing because the final state equals the prior committed state. Probe result: `renders=1`, `commits=0`, `notes=2`, DOM value still `0`; a later unrelated prop commit then occurs with those external notes still present. In re-frame.ui that stale `:local-state` stash is drained into the next unrelated ViewCell commit — the same class of false attribution this PR intended to remove.

The new test does not mount React or invoke the actual local setter; it calls the private gate directly and manually commits a cell, so it cannot reject net-zero batches, replay, or abandoned renders.

Keep the fix commit-aligned and small. A promising shape is a DEBUG layout effect in the local hook that compares the current rendered state with a ref of the last committed state and records the cause before the wrapper's later ViewCell commit layout effect. Equivalent commit-aligned designs are fine. Do not add a scheduler, transaction protocol, or public API.
acceptance_criteria:
- React state updater functions remain pure: they do not mutate the ViewCell/evidence stash.
- A real mounted test through the actual re-frame.ui local-state setter proves a committed value change contributes exactly one `:local-state` cause to that connected commit.
- Same-value setters and same-batch net-zero sequences (for example `0→1→0`) leave no pending marker; a later unrelated subscription/prop commit does not report `:local-state`.
- StrictMode updater replay remains idempotent and does not create false attribution.
- Tests exercise React/host commit behavior rather than only calling a private comparison helper.
- Production erasure remains intact; no scheduler, general transaction machinery, or public API is added.
- EP/docstrings no longer equate Object.is inequality inside an updater with an actually committed change.
notes: RESOLVED in PR #6604 (commit aa4d5179f3). react-set updater is now PURE; :local-state attribution rides a DEBUG committed-value useLayoutEffect (commit-phase only, skips mount, StrictMode-idempotent); note-local-state! sets the commit-time flag. Deleted the note-committed-local-change! updater gate. Proof: MOUNTED browser test drives the real local setter — real change => exactly :local-state; net-zero 0->1->0 commits nothing and leaves no stale marker on a later subscription commit. test:browser + test:elision green.

title: Preserve each detailed view cause instead of fabricating a cross-target span
description:
PR #6577 changed `:rf.view/causes` from keyword tokens to detailed records, but stores pending detail as `{cause-kind -> one detail}`. `merge-commit-cause` therefore merges every subscription movement under the single `:subscription` key: the latest target/query/frame/to/epoch wins while `:from` is retained from the earliest movement regardless of identity.

This fabricates evidence when two dependencies move before one commit. A direct current-main reproduction folded node A (`[:a]`, version 2→3) and then node B (`[:b]`, version 20→21); the pending record became node B/query B with `:from 2` and `:to 21` — a transition that never happened — and node A disappeared. The same one-per-kind assumption drops sibling Story overrides because `mint-commit-record!` uses `some` over `to-acquire`.

EP-0033 deliberately makes causes a vector because one commit can have several causes and its UI may summarize multiple changed dependencies. Preserve one record per distinct causal identity; coalesce repeated subscription moves only for the same observed target, keeping that target's earliest `:from` and latest `:to`. Keep ordering deterministic and bounded by the view's actual sites. This is an identity-aware collection fix, not a general evidence/provenance framework.

Current `commit-record` prose also still says "nine ruled kinds" and mentions only `:epoch-restore` absence, while the shipped surface is six kinds plus fallback with both `:epoch-restore` and `:hmr-remount` deferred. Truth that docstring while touching this surface.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two different subscription targets moving before one connected commit yield two truthful `:subscription` cause records; no record combines identity/version axes from different targets and neither dependency disappears.
- Repeated movement of the same subscription target may coalesce to one record with that identity's earliest `:from`, latest `:to`, and truthful latest epoch.
- Multiple moved Story overrides in one commit retain one detailed record per override identity instead of `some` dropping siblings.
- Canonical kind ordering remains deterministic; same-kind ordering is stable and explicitly pinned.
- `commit-record` documentation names the current six shipped kinds plus fallback and both deferrals.
- Record schema/API stays the existing vector-of-records; no general evidence framework or new public option.
- Current UI JVM/CLJS cause tests and production-erasure gates pass.
notes:
RESOLVED in PR #6604 (commit 31dc5e4693). Coalescing is now per distinct causal identity (subscription keyed on :target), so two distinct targets stay two truthful records (no cross-target :from/:to span, neither disappears); mint collects ALL override siblings with keep (was some). commit-record docstring truthed to six shipped kinds + fallback, both :hmr-remount/:epoch-restore deferred. Proof: two-subscription-targets-yield-two-truthful-records + sibling-story-overrides-each-retain-a-record (red->green).
PR #6604 three-lens audit follow-up (rf2-z2ken, 2026-07-21): acceptance is not complete for repeated lexical sites on one override identity. mint-commit-record! collects override-details per to-acquire SITE, so two sites reading the same overridden query emit two identical {:cause :story-override :override-id … :version …} rows for one changed causal identity.
