title: re-frame.ui boundary + friction programme (UIx-review ratified)
description:
Design ratified by Mike 2026-07-20; all decisions below are final; no further operator input is required to implement. Ratified from the 2026-07-20 UIx adversarial reviews, Mike-approved.

CONTEXT: two independent adversarial reviews of re-frame.ui vs UIx converged, after mutual cross-examination, on this exact programme. The substrate's non-negotiables are unchanged: closed grammar, JVM parity, DCE/elision, manifests. This programme removes boundary/product friction WITHOUT relaxing those.

THE 8 WORK ITEMS (each a child bead of this epic — ids in the CHILDREN list; each child is fully self-contained):
1. Remove the Shadow install/cache tax (pre-publication gate; blocks rf2-vxgfnd.99.2).
2. Ship ui/->react — the outward bridge (spec/API.md row flips planned->live).
3. Complete declared :ref forwarding (delete the stale ref-prop-declared-s1 pin).
4. Admit the if-let binder family (if-let / when-let / if-some / when-some) to both grammar tiers.
5. Allow ui/spread at FOREIGN component call sites (internal views keep the literal props requirement).
6. One effect-dependency equality doctrine: rf= across native and interop tiers.
7. Dev-time :rf.ui.compile/missing-effect-dep diagnostic (warning tier).
8. Generate the AI context sheet from compiler/API data (generated skills/ artifact + drift gate).

DEMAND-GATED ROSTER (recorded dispositions, NOT beads — each fires only on its named trigger; do not file or implement before the trigger):
(a) defview-part — a compiler-owned def-level unit analyzed and INLINED at the call site so local/effect/react sites become the caller's lexical sites (manifests stay sound, position law checked post-inline, elision preserved). TRIGGER: several views across the repo/examples repeat the same local/effect site pattern (the debounce/media-query/interval shelf). The runtime custom-hook mechanism is rejected permanently.
(b) react/use-memo with rf= deps — computation caching for expensive pure render-scoped computations over props. TRIGGER: a named consumer with a demonstrably expensive computation rerunning on unrelated local/sub churn. Never for callback identity (compiler-owned handler identity already solves that).
(c) internal-view code splitting — extend react/lazy to accept a loader yielding an exported defview, composing ui/->react. TRIGGER: a real route needs it. No general Suspense data semantics.
(d) ui/view registry heads — stays wave-2 behind its existing ruled triggers (spec/API.md:309 — the parts-ceiling ruling or a native-table need; re-com is the demand-bar consumer of record).

REJECT FENCE (binding on all children):
- No runtime interpretation fallback for unprovable forms (one fallback arm reintroduces the walker into browser bundles, unsounds the manifest, and collapses the elision proof).
- No concurrent-rendering authoring surfaces over app-db (use-transition / use-deferred-value / Suspense-as-loading). React's own documented contract — react.dev/reference/react/useSyncExternalStore#caveats: an external-store mutation during a non-blocking Transition restarts the update as blocking — makes an imitation API over-promise by construction; the guide states the cession honestly.
- No opt-out memoization.
- No configurable lint platform/framework.
- No generic internal-view prop spreading.
- No second state model (contexts / Suspense-as-data / use-atom).
- No use-state-style overloaded setter (local's set!/update! split stands).
- No UIx feature parity goal.
- No compatibility aliases.

SEQUENCING/CONTENTION (mandatory reading for the mayor loop at dispatch):
- spec/004-Views.md is HOT-ZONE — the ref/grammar/spread/equality children (+ the diagnostic child's spec note) EACH touch it: SEQUENTIAL among themselves and behind whatever currently holds 004 (rf2-rvs56 slice d queues for 004; the rf2-5e8zv lease-excision stages also touch 004). NO ordering edges are wired among those children; the mayor sequences the hot-zone at dispatch time.
- implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/analyze.cljc and implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/hooks.cljc are not hot-zone but CONTEND with rf2-5e8zv.1 (lease S1 deletes lease sites in the same files) — do not run concurrently with it; sequence after 5e8zv.1 merges or before it dispatches, mayor's call at dispatch time.
- spec/API.md is HOT-ZONE for the ->react child (blessed table row flips planned->live).
- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn is HOT-ZONE for the install-tax child.
- No Spec 009 rows are owed by ANY child: :rf.ui.compile/* ids are catalogue-exempt per the Conventions reservation.

DOCS/EXAMPLES/EP COVERAGE (binding on all children; restated per child): every child owns its docs, examples, and EP updates in the SAME PR as the change, never trailing. EP DISCIPLINE: settled EP meaning is preserved through a DATED ADDENDUM/ERRATUM recording the old clause and the new disposition (the EP-0009 convention) — never silently rewrite accepted EP text.
notes:
SKILLS COVERAGE (Mike-directed, 2026-07-20, binding on every child): each child's PR (or an immediately-sequenced follow-up in the same child) must reconcile the EXISTING skills that teach its changed contract — the sweep is GREP-DRIVEN over skills/** for the child's surface vocabulary, not roster-driven. Census at filing time: skills/reagent-migration/{SKILL.md, README.md, references/catalog-judgment.md (12 hits), catalog-mechanical.md, catalog-reject.md, gotchas.md, procedure.md, evals/evals.json (5 hits), spec/authoring-prompt.md} + skills/re-frame2/{patterns/stateful-components.md, patterns/managed-http.md, references/fundamentals/views.md} carry if-let/spread/use-ref/use-effect/->react vocabulary. Evals that assert the OLD contract (e.g. a rejection that child 4/5 legalizes) must be updated in the same PR or they red the eval gates. Gates: check_skill_re_frame2_drift, migration-contract-drift, eval-docs/eval-packaging as applicable. The future re-frame2-ui authoring skill (rf2-cv8a2y, trigger-gated W6) self-corrects: it is authored from then-current contracts at dispatch. Child 8's generated context sheet is additive and unaffected.
REPLICANT-REVIEW ADDENDUM (Mike-approved, 2026-07-21). The 2026-07-21 Replicant adversarial reviews (fable + codex, converged after cross-examination) ratified two additions to this programme, filed as children .9 (react/use-ref -> ui/ref promotion + DOM-node recipe rewrite) and .10 (frameless-first Tier-1 testing docs). Everything else Replicant surfaced was already owned here (.1 install tax — now corroborated by a second competitor; .5 foreign spread; .8 AI sheet) or is recorded below so the analysis survives the local-only review documents.

DEMAND-GATED ADDITIONS (recorded dispositions, NOT beads; fire only on the named trigger):
(e) Compiled nested placeholder splicing — recognize the three existing placeholders (:rf.ui/value/:checked/:key) at any LITERAL position of a literal handler form, compiled as static path writes (no runtime walk). TRIGGER: the first real consumer hitting :rf.ui.compile/placeholder-not-top-level with a map-shaped payload (e.g. [:form/set {:field :email :value :rf.ui/value}]). No vocabulary growth ever.
(f) ui/node-effect — DEMOTED from an earlier draft recommendation; the refutation is preserved so the gate stays honest: object refs attach at commit BEFORE effects fire (no nil-first-pass cost); most widget/chart nodes are STABLE while their data changes, so a node-scoped callback cannot serve the common case without duplicating effect's deps (and tearing the widget down per data change is worse); React 19's ref-callback contract requires stable callback identity (fresh closures detach/reattach every render) — real compiler identity machinery, not a thin lowering; StrictMode deliberately replays ref setup/cleanup in dev; ui/raw-fn already exposes callback-ref cleanup for the expert case. TRIGGERS to revisit: several real cases where the TARGET NODE's identity changes while the view stays mounted, or per-keyed-row node work (focus-the-new-row) proves materially inadequate under ui/ref + effect or the explicit callback-ref path.
(g) Presence attribute-overlay SUGAR — at most a compile-time overlay spelling that LOWERS ONTO the existing presence state machine and literal :timeout-ms law (never a second retention mode). TRIGGER: repeated real-world presence demand beyond toasts/modals. Both reviews agree even the sugar lacks evidence today.

REJECT-FENCE ADDITIONS (binding on all children, from the Replicant axes):
- No transitionend-derived retention or CSS-duration inspection for presence. (Honesty note, verified at source: Replicant is not naive here — replicant/dom.cljc removes stuck unmounting nodes via a fail-safe timer at the longest computed transition duration + 200ms. The contrast is heuristic-CSS-derived bound vs re-frame.ui's explicit, testable, CSS-independent :timeout-ms — reduced-motion, animation-vs-transition, and interrupted commits never change ownership.)
- No lifecycle-as-dispatchable-data (Replicant's :replicant.trigger/life-cycle through global dispatch). A speculative React renderer cannot promise 'mount happened once' — the recorded :on-mount/:on-unmount rejection (spec/004-Views.md:1492-1494) stands; the guide states the cession.
- No optional list keys (the compiler cannot guess which repeated child owns state/subs/presence; the build failure stays).
- No runtime hiccup/alias interpreter arm (the team that wants Replicant's model has the Reagent adapter today; re-frame.ui.data when earned).
- No runtime placeholder interpolation (the postwalk pattern) and no open placeholder vocabulary; ui/event is the door beyond the three scalars.
- No action-vector batching in handler values (a second effects language); no :alias-data-style render-option config channel (that is app-db + subs, frame-scoped).

CROSS-CHECK RECORDED: Replicant's aliases are attractive evidence for the IDEA of concise composition but fire NONE of the existing trigger-gated checkpoints (ui/tpl rf2-1hm7a3, registered ui/view rf2-a62fje, defview-alias rf2-ho1iba) — gates unchanged. The .9/.10 briefs are self-contained; the review documents at ai/findings/replicant/ are local-only provenance, not required reading for any worker.

No unmet audit obligations found on the epic (#6640 rider obligations discharged in S6; #6646 rider repair shipped in #6659).

title: Xray panels/resources tests contaminate the CLJS conformance corpus (order-sensitive test isolation)
description: Pre-existing latent test-isolation fragility exposed by rf2-5e8zv.1's compile-graph reshuffle. When the Xray `day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.resources*` tests run before `re-frame.conformance-corpus-cljs-test` in the shared node-test bundle, 5 `:resources/*` conformance fixtures fail (`[:rf/resource …]` subs return nil; expected traces not seen). PROVEN PRE-EXISTING: (1) the corpus passes in ISOLATION; (2) origin/main WITHOUT rf2-5e8zv.1 reproduces the identical corpus failure with the same `day8|conformance-corpus-cljs-test` --config-merge subset; (3) the same day8 isolation subset fails the unrelated `palette/fuzzy` `camelcase-boundary-bonus` test on origin/main too. main's full-suite compile-graph order happens to avoid the exposure; deleting the lease test namespaces reshuffled it. Root cause not fully localized: resource-registrar + source-store resource-kind clears in `reset-resources!` had NO effect, so the polluted shared state is elsewhere (candidates: the `:rf/resource` sub/image-assembly resolution, egress/observability config, or the corpus's lazily-captured pretest baseline inheriting prior-suite state — the JVM leaf avoids this by requiring [re-frame.resources] + a :reload-style reset; the CLJS leaf does not). FIX DIRECTION: make the CLJS conformance corpus capture a clean baseline / reset resource+egress state robustly, OR make the Xray resources panel tests fully isolate. Surfaced by rf2-5e8zv.1 (PR #6572).
notes: FIXED in PR #6572 (commit 8bfb468ded). Root cause: the CLJS conformance corpus (conformance_corpus_cljs_test.cljs) captured its per-fixture reset baseline LAZILY at deftest start, inheriting sibling-suite (Xray panels/resources) registrations from the shared node bundle. Fix: capture a FRAMEWORK-ONLY baseline at NS-LOAD (before sibling test nses register) and restore to it per-fixture — the CLJS equivalent of the JVM leaf's clear-all!+reload; the lazy snapshot is retained only for the end-of-suite try/finally restore so sibling nses keep their registrations. Corpus now order-independent; full test:cljs green (10312/0). No corpus assertions weakened.

title: S3: tooling instruction examples — re-frame2-pair MCP + eval fixtures
description:
Parent epic rf2-vwwvp: its description is the full normative design and IS AUTHORITATIVE OVER THIS BRIEF — run `bd show rf2-vwwvp` first and read it in full. Do NOT look for any ai/ dossier (local-only, absent from worker worktrees); this bead plus the epic are complete.

## The grammar tooling examples must emit (settled)

    [:rf.route/navigate {request-map}]

One map. Address keys :to :url :params :query :fragment; policy keys :replace? :scroll :bypass-guards?; edit key :query-merge. Positional arities are gone; there is no compatibility form.

Validity rules any emitted example must satisfy:
- :to xor :url; :url excludes :params/:query/:query-merge (:url + :fragment legal, request fragment wins).
- :query xor :query-merge; :query-merge is in-place only (no :to/:url) — cross-route query carry no longer exists; :query-retain is the route-side replacement policy.
- Omitting both :to and :url = navigate-in-place: a PATCH of the current location by key PRESENCE (:query {} clears; :fragment nil clears; omitted keys carried; route+params carried, never accepted in-place). The reserved :rf.route/self target no longer exists.
- Empty maps and pure-policy maps reject; in-place before any current route exists rejects; unknown keys (namespaced included) reject. Structural rejects surface as :rf.error/navigate-bad-request.
- route-url is a single 1-arity taking {:to :params :query :fragment}, strictly address-only.
- Facts spell :route-id; requests spell :to.

Canonical example shapes:
- [:rf.route/navigate {:to :app/home}]
- [:rf.route/navigate {:to :app/article :params {:id "intro"}}]
- [:rf.route/navigate {:to :app/search :query {:q "clojure"} :replace? true}]
- [:rf.route/navigate {:query-merge {:page 2}}]
- [:rf.route/navigate {:url "/some/path"}]

## Scope — tooling instructions

- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp: instruction text and dispatch examples that show or synthesize :rf.route/navigate (the pair-MCP instructions surface, i.e. what get-re-frame2-pair-instructions serves, and any dispatch/dispatch-dry-run examples).

Acceptance: a grep across tools/ shows zero positional navigate examples, zero :rf.route/self, zero navigate-arity-misuse (outside .beads and historical EPs). Relevant tool test suites and the mcp-conformance gate green.

## Fence (binding — emit/describe none of these)

No bare-keyword sugar; no navigate! facade; no positional/deprecated forms; no :in-place? marker key; no :route-id alias in requests; no builder/constructor helpers; no history-stack surface.

title: routing: replace positional :rf.route/navigate with the flat request-map grammar
description:
Design ratified by Mike 2026-07-20; all decisions below are final; no further operator input is required to implement.

Provenance: design ratified from the 2026-07-20 routing-review dossiers, Mike-approved. THIS BEAD DESCRIPTION IS THE NORMATIVE DESIGN. It is fully self-contained: child beads cite it as the in-beads authority. Workers must NOT look for any ai/ dossier (the ai/ tree is local-only and absent from worker worktrees) — everything needed is below.

## The change

Replace the positional navigation grammar `[:rf.route/navigate target params opts]` (and route-url's positional arities) with ONE flat request map:

    [:rf.route/navigate {request-map}]

- Address keys: :to :url :params :query :fragment
- Policy keys: :replace? :scroll :bypass-guards?
- Edit key: :query-merge

Positional arities are DELETED. No compatibility layer, no deprecation shim (pre-alpha posture).

## Validity rules (all loud rejections)

1. :to and :url are mutually exclusive.
2. :url is also mutually exclusive with :params, :query, and :query-merge — a raw URL IS the address; letting address keys ride beside it and be silently ignored is the exact failure class this redesign exists to kill. :url + :fragment IS legal, with the request's :fragment overriding a URL-embedded one (today's precedence, navigate.cljc:352-355).
3. :query and :query-merge are mutually exclusive (one replaces wholesale, one edits).
4. :query-merge requires an IN-PLACE request (no :to / :url). This deliberately DELETES today's cross-route query carry (`[navigate :route/other {} {:query-merge ...}]`, spec/012:483) — the declarative :query-retain route metadata is the replacement policy. Carrying state into another route's query is that route's :query-retain policy, not the caller's imperative choice.
5. A request must carry a destination (:to / :url) OR an in-place change — discriminated by key PRESENCE, not truthiness: `:query {}` (clear the query) and `:fragment nil` (clear the fragment) are valid lone in-place requests. Empty maps (`{}`) and pure-policy maps (`{:replace? true}`) reject loud.
6. An in-place request dispatched before any current route exists rejects loud (there is nothing to patch).
7. Unknown keys reject, NAMESPACED INCLUDED — full closure: `:my-app/replace?` fails as loudly as `:replcae?`. ONE documented internal exemption: the runtime's own resume rider :rf.route/enter-attempts (threaded into a re-issued event's request by :rf.route/continue, can_leave.cljc:446-456) is stripped BEFORE the gate runs; it is continuation bookkeeping, absent from the published grammar, and not a reason to open the schema. No open namespaced-key extension until a real consumer appears.

## In-place resolution table

A DESTINATION request (:to / :url present) builds a FRESH address: omitted :query / :fragment are empty, exactly as today. An IN-PLACE request (no :to / :url) is a PATCH of the current location, discriminated by key presence:

| Key | Present | Omitted |
|---|---|---|
| route + :params | — (never accepted in-place; changing params is a destination) | carried from the current :rf/route slice |
| :query | replaces wholesale ({} clears) | carried unchanged |
| :query-merge | folds into current (nil value removes a key) | — |
| :fragment | set (nil clears) | carried unchanged |

Before a current route exists there is nothing to patch — reject.

Implementation note (trust-the-programmer): requests assembled with conditional key-dropping (cond->-style optional destination) should assert their own :to; the framework adds no marker key or mode flag for this.

This deliberately FIXES today's self-nav surprise: `[:rf.route/navigate :rf.route/self {} {:fragment "x"}]` silently CLEARS the current query, misses the fragment-only short-circuit, and re-fires :on-match. Under the new form, `{:fragment "x"}` carries the query, satisfies the same-route/params/query condition, and MUST land in the existing fragment-only anchor path (fragment-only-nav-fx, navigate.cljc:510-526) — an anchor change, not a reactivation.

## Deletions

- The reserved :rf.route/self target and its resolver branch (in-place = omitted destination now).
- opts-only-keys / misplaced-opts-keys misuse machinery (navigate.cljc:36-62).
- :rf.error/navigate-arity-misuse and its Spec 009 catalogue row.
- The `{:url ...}` TARGET form (becomes the ordinary :url key).
- route-url's 2/3/4 positional arities.

## Enforcement (honest)

Event :schema validation is dev-only AND schemas-optional (router.cljc:752-794: gated on debug-enabled?, late-bound on the schemas artefact) — a Malli schema alone would protect FEWER builds than today's handler-body guard. The design therefore requires a small ALWAYS-ON structural gate in the handler: closed key-roster membership, the exclusions above, and the destination-or-change rule — plain set logic, total over the roster where today's guard covers four of six opts keys. The Malli reg-event :schema rides alongside as the dev-time rich explainer. The gate rejects BEFORE any guard evaluation (as today's misuse guard does, navigate.cljc:527-557), so a malformed request never consumes a :can-leave run.

## Error surfaces, in order (one didactic story)

1. Structural gate (shape) → NEW id :rf.error/navigate-bad-request ({:reason :keys} tags), a ONE-FOR-ONE Spec 009 row swap with the retired :rf.error/navigate-arity-misuse row — no net catalogue growth. Deliberately NOT :rf.error/schema-validation-failure: that category is the dev-only, schemas-artefact-gated validation channel, while this gate is always-on and production-surviving. The channel-classification distinction is deliberate and Mike-visible.
2. Target resolution — an unregistered :to stays the loud handler-level :no-such-route reject (the gate cannot see the registry, and shouldn't).
3. Route-level :params / :query validation — the existing route-url throw path surfacing as schema-validation-failure with :where :event (navigate.cljc:459-498), unchanged.
4. Guards, unchanged.

## Preserved protocols (do NOT touch)

- The pending-navigation ENVELOPE is unchanged: {:id :requested-by-event :requested-url :reason :direction :rejecting-route :rejecting-guard :enter-attempts :url-restored?} (can_leave.cljc:347-355; Spec-Schemas PendingNavigation ~:3624-3646). ONLY the :requested-by-event interior becomes [:rf.route/navigate {request-map}] for the programmatic door; continue's guard-bypass injection becomes a map assoc instead of positional vector surgery.
- :rf.route/continue / :rf.route/cancel by pending :id — unchanged.
- Guards keep receiving the resolved FACT target {:route-id :params :query :fragment :url} (can_leave.cljc:12-18,77-97), derived uniformly across all navigation doors. Facts spell :route-id; requests spell :to — deliberate intent/fact vocabulary, not drift. match-url and the :rf/route slice are NOT renamed.

## route-url

Single 1-arity taking the address map {:to :params :query :fragment}. Strictly address-only: policy keys, :url, :query-merge, and unknown keys reject loud rather than being silently ignored. No in-place form (a pure helper cannot read the current route). Callers project: the navigate handler select-keys'es its request; link-model projects its target map.

## Fence — NOT to build (binding on all children)

- No bare-keyword sugar ([:rf.route/navigate :app/home]).
- No navigate! function facade.
- No positional-arity retention or deprecation shim.
- No :in-place? marker key.
- No prod strict-validation mode flag.
- No :route-id alias accepted in requests.
- No policy keys on route-link.
- No Location record/protocol or spec'd wrapper type.
- No builder DSL or request-constructor helpers.
- No history-stack surface (:rf.route/back, forward, go-n).
- No :history :replace enum rename (:replace? stays boolean).
- No pure [:rf/location] projection sub.
- No route→view auto-render metadata.
- No pluggable routing-engine protocol.
- No nested query DSL / deep :query-merge.

## Docs vocabulary (adopt consistently)

Four terms: route definition / location / navigation request / navigation state. No public renames ride on the vocabulary; it is how the docs talk.

## Staging

Three children: S1 (the CI-atomic vertical cut — runtime + specs + fixtures + tests + examples + Xray; blocks the rest), S2 (prose corpus sweep), S3 (tooling instruction examples). S2 and S3 are blocked on S1.
notes: EPIC CLOSE CONDITION (mayor, 2026-07-20): after .1/.2/.3 all merge, a REPO-WIDE grep (outside .beads/** and historical docs/EP archives) proves zero positional navigate call sites, zero :rf.route/self, zero navigate-arity-misuse. Each child's acceptance grep is scoped to its own surfaces (see .1/.2 notes); this repo-wide check is the epic's final verification, run by the mayor at close.

Positional :rf.route/navigate fully replaced by the flat request-map grammar; grep-clean across product surfaces.

title: Write Codex routing API review and recommendation
description:
## Problem

The current routing navigation grammar uses adjacent positional maps: `[:rf.route/navigate target params opts]`. A query-only navigation therefore needs an empty params placeholder, and the runtime carries special misuse detection for callers who put opts in the params slot. Mike asked for an independent design note that defines this problem carefully, evaluates alternatives, and recommends a more elegant pre-alpha API in light of Replicant's data-driven routing model.

## Deliverable

Create `ai/findings/routing-review/codex.md`. Ground it in current Spec 012, routing docs/implementation, and https://replicant.fun/tutorials/routing/. Explain the whole surface affected (navigate, route-link, route-url, match-url, current route reads, self/query changes, raw URLs, policies), present credible options and consequences, and make an opinionated recommendation consistent with the project's minimal/ergonomic/trust-the-programmer posture. This is analysis only; do not change runtime/spec APIs.

## Acceptance

The document is self-contained, distinguishes route definition/location/navigation request/state, includes representative syntax for ordinary and edge cases, evaluates at least three options, recommends one coherent grammar, states what not to build, and is committed/pushed from a guarded worker checkout.

title: S4: enforce zero lease residue and run the integration proof
description:
## Problem

A removal this broad is vulnerable to forgotten filenames, camel-case classes, generated artefacts, dormant tests, historical research, and future reintroduction. A one-time grep is insufficient, while a non-zero baseline would merely bless existing residue.

## Required work

- After all preceding stages reach zero, add one narrow CI ratchet that scans git ls-files content and paths, excluding only .beads/**. Git history is outside the worktree scan.
- Detect natural-language forms and identifier/path forms, including singular/plural/past/gerund, kebab/snake names, keywords, and camel-case names, while not flagging ordinary words such as release or please. The guard itself must not contain an allowlisted live occurrence; encode/construct its forbidden token if necessary.
- Use no baseline, ceiling, or allowlist for product files: the permitted count is exactly zero.
- Prove the guard discriminates by temporarily seeding and restoring, byte-identically, at least prose, kebab/snake, camel-case, and filename cases. Verify a second introduction after returning to zero still fails.
- Run independent manual residue scans in addition to the new guard, including tracked filenames and generated docs output.
- Run proportional slice gates: UI JVM/CLJS/browser and production elision; adapters; core observation; Resources and cross-subsystem conformance; Xray/Pair/Story; specs/docs/examples; skills/evals. CI supplies the full matrix. Confirm runners select plausible non-zero tests and that deleted/renamed test namespaces did not silently fall out of discovery.
- Audit all children and any files added concurrently since their inventories; zero must be established against the final merged tree, not an earlier snapshot.

## Acceptance

- The final tree outside .beads has zero forbidden content and path matches under both the CI guard and an independent scan.
- Every mutation arm demonstrably fails, restoration is exact, and an unmodified tree passes.
- All proportional gates pass with credible counts; no public export, schema field, example, test, generated page, skill, tool, or AI file retains the rejected construct.
acceptance_criteria: A zero-baseline tracked-content/path ratchet blocks every lexical form outside .beads, mutation proofs discriminate, independent scans are clean, and all affected slice gates pass with credible non-zero selection.

S3B (#6592) RESIDUE INVENTORY for S4's establish-zero audit (mayor 2026-07-21, verified via git grep): (1) implementation/ NOT clean — analyze.cljc has 21 'lease' refs (STALE DOCSTRINGS/didactic messages e.g. reject-reactive-binding! docstring:606 lists '(lease …)' as a reactive call; the grammar LOGIC is clean, only prose/messages stale) + 6 tests (reactive_hmr_matrix, reactive_reconcile, reactive_two_frame [9utbt's 'owned lease' labels], resources_example, observation_port, derivation_algebra) + observation.cljc. (2) GENERATED coupling: skills/re-frame2-ui-context/SKILL.md:348 is generated FROM analyze.cljc:645 — purge analyze.cljc THEN regen the sheet (clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.ui-context), don't hand-edit. (3) checker scripts/check_synthesis_plan_authority.py coupled to an unpurged ai/findings doc. (4) ⚠️ DECISION FOR MIKE: 62 TRACKED ai/findings/new-substrate-* files contain 'lease' (the research that DESIGNED the concept). S4's ratchet scans 'git ls-files content' — either EXEMPT ai/ as non-product (ratchet targets product files only per the bead) OR untrack the design research (per CLAUDE.md's 'nothing under /ai/ tracked' end-state). This deliberately inverts the historical correction recorded by closed rf2-vxgfnd.295 and rf2-vxgfnd.300, whose premise #6572 removed.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-21 07:25 AUSEST)

THE RULING: (b) UNTRACK now — git rm --cached ALL 85 tracked ai/ files (whole trees: new-substrate-synthesis 61 + new-substrate-codex 24; 62 of the 85 carry the lease pattern \b[Ll]eas(e|es|ed|ing)\b|Lease = 43 synthesis + 19 codex; census re-verified at ruling time), disk copies retained. AI file retains the rejected construct"), CLAUDE.md's end state ("nothing under /ai/ is tracked"), and rf2-vxgfnd.99.1's ruled disposition (untrack + consume-gated genuine disk deletion) all read true with ZERO text amendments. title: [BUG] Native editor migration strands the article owner on ordinary route leave
description:
The native re-frame.ui RealWorld editor removed the Reagent Form-3 unmount dispatch, but its app-minted article owner was not fully re-homed. `:editor/load-article` ensures `:realworld/article` with owner `[:lease :editor/article slug]`. Explicit releases cover edit→new, edit A→B, delete, and the old Reagent component's unmount. The compiled `ui_editor.cljc` is a pure `defview`, so an ordinary successful navigation from edit to home/profile/settings fires no release and leaves the owner active, pinning the resource until frame teardown.

This contradicts `ui_editor.cljc`'s claim that `:editor/*` events release the app-minted owner and weakens MIG-17's concrete proof. The browser ergonomic fixture is vacuous at teardown: it says the unmount leaks nothing but asserts only `(is true)` and never inspects `:active-owners`.

This is not `rf2-kkqy6q`: that bead fixed edit→new/delete and explicitly relied on the Reagent unmount for edit→other-route. PR #6549 removed that safety in the native rendition.

Keep the fix proportional. Give the owner a real causal/framework lifecycle that covers every route exit—prefer route-owned `:resources` if it can preserve the seed-on-load continuation cleanly, otherwise a view lease when lifetime truly follows the compiled view, or another explicit causal end path. Do not add a generic `:on-leave` framework feature merely for this example. Tighten MIG-17 guidance so a D-tier view is held until every old teardown responsibility has a proven new owner; naming hypothetical future end events is not completion.
acceptance_criteria:
- Leaving `:realworld.editor/edit` for an unrelated route releases the editor article owner; edit→new, edit A→B, save, and delete remain correct.
- A non-vacuous test observes the resource owner's active/inactive state across a real leave path and would fail on the current native-view leak.
- `ui_editor.cljc`, `article_editor.cljs`, and MIG-17 prose state the ownership model that actually runs.
- No new routing/lifecycle abstraction is introduced unless independently justified by broader demand.
notes:
PR #6553 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT ADDENDUM (three lenses, 2026-07-20). This open P2 remains the exact owner; no duplicate filed. #6553's lease-capability calibration is correct, but the specific changed canonical proof is not: `ui_editor.cljc` still says the route-minted `[:lease :editor/article slug]` is released by `:editor/*` events and the suite proves it, while ordinary edit -> home/profile/settings (and the ordinary successful-leave shape) has no native release. The old Reagent Form-3 still supplies component-will-unmount; the pure native defview does not; the browser teardown assertion remains vacuous `(is true)` and never inspects active owners. Later #6559 preserves this claim.

The same defect reaches the skill's eval id 19. Its prompt establishes only a Form-3 `component-will-unmount` dispatch; it supplies no acquisition site, owner token, route, or causal end events. Expectations 4-5 nevertheless require the answer to assert a route/app-minted owner and a pure no-lease defview. That rewards invented application architecture. In the bounded fix already described here, make the eval require the honest D-tier move: inspect/ask who minted the lifetime and what ends it, hold the whole view until every teardown responsibility has a proven owner, then choose causal re-homing versus `ui/lease`. A route-minted example may be conditional context, not an unstated fact. Keep the existing proportional remedy: real owner lifecycle + one edit-to-unrelated-route active-owner assertion + aligned example/MIG-17/eval; no generic `:on-leave` feature.
PR #6569 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT (three lenses, 2026-07-20) — REOPENED exact source; no new framework or duplicate Bead.

The route-owned resource lifecycle and settled-read exit proofs are sound, but the ownerless seed continuation is not correlated to the route instance/slug. `:editor/load-article` uses `:reply-to [:editor/article-loaded]`; that handler accepts any successful article and replaces the editor slice. Leaving A removes its owner and requests cancellation, but cancellation is best-effort and the resource live-reply gate checks current-work/generation, not the editor's current route/slug. A late accepted A settle (or queued ownerless cache-hit) can therefore reseed A after navigation to edit B, new, home, or another route; different slug keys do not supersede each other's generation.

Bounded repair: include the intended slug in the reply target (for example `[:editor/article-loaded slug]`) and apply only while the current route/editor still targets that slug. Add one deterministic A->B or leave-before-A-settle proof with ineffective cancellation; the late A reply must not overwrite current state. Do not add routing/resource lifecycle machinery. Existing rf2-7a3uc and rf2-8yedm own only the skill/doc/fenced DOM follow-ups.
PR #6628 (worker/native-editor-owner-y4mgw): closes the #6569 REOPEN — the seed-on-load continuation is now slug-correlated. :editor/load-article carries the intended slug in :reply-to [:editor/article-loaded slug]; :editor/article-loaded seeds only while the current route is still :realworld.editor/edit targeting that slug (read from the same :rf.db/runtime coeffect load-article reads — no new lifecycle machinery). This drops a late cross-slug reply (best-effort-uncancelled A settle accepted for A's own entry per release-owner-handler) that previously clobbered the current draft after edit A -> edit B/new/home. Regression: editor-late-cross-slug-reply-does-not-clobber-the-current-draft in the reagent-adapter realworld-resources contract suite drives the REAL reply path — RED before the guard (2 failures: re-slug to article-a + draft clobber), GREEN after. The route-leave OWNER release itself was already merged on main (route :resources model, 3 existing tests). Docstrings in article_editor.cljs + ui_editor.cljc refreshed to the slug-correlated model. Gates green: test:cljs 10371 tests/0 fail; example release build 0 warnings; JVM s3 ergonomic proof 7/0; hardcoded-path check OK. Not touched: routing.cljs (hot-zone; model already on main), MIG-17/skills (rf2-7a3uc/#6570, rf2-8yedm closed).
AUDIT OF MERGED PR #6628 (2026-07-21): REOPENED exact source owner; no duplicate and no framework expansion.

The shipped slug-correlated reply target and current-route/slug guard correctly close the cross-slug A->B/new/home race. Applied and authored substantive patches have identical stable patch-id 8a9b1e124af3df966efe5e66bc4c7ef945232c7b; the focused current-main Resources suite is green (25 tests / 163 assertions).

MATERIAL P2 RUNTIME OMISSION — SAME-SLUG INITIAL LOAD CAN STILL CLOBBER TYPING. The edit route is non-blocking. :editor/load-article resets to a blank draft while the read is pending, and both editor views disable fields only for the save mutation, so a user may type before the article arrives. :editor/edit-field records those fields in the existing :touched set. The accepted same-slug :editor/article-loaded reply passes the new route/slug guard and replaces the entire editor slice via editor-slice, silently discarding those keystrokes. The cross-slug regression cannot catch this because it settles B before editing B. Proportional repair: use the existing :touched set; make the server draft the baseline, seed untouched fields from it, preserve current values for touched fields, and retain the relevant validation bookkeeping. Add one real-handler regression: enter edit A, edit one field before A settles, settle A, and prove the typed field survives while untouched fields and baseline come from the server. No resource/routing abstraction.

MATERIAL TEACHING DRIFT — the canonical example still carries four obsolete/copyable claims: routing.cljs route doc uses uncorrelated [:editor/article-loaded]; article_editor.cljs editor-page doc repeats it; README.md says resource reads have no reply-side hook and seed-on-load remains a Form-3 reaction, then repeats that in the file table. Truth those passages up to the route-owned, ownerless, slug-correlated read :reply-to model. No synchronizer or new test framework.

title: Carry the public context frame through frame-only and event-only SSR wrappers
description:
PR #6550 correctly made `use-frame-context!` return the renderer-agnostic public `React.useContext` value and fixed every sub/lease ViewCell wrapper, but two production wrapper paths still discard that correct frame and re-enter the server-broken private-slot reader:

1. `re-frame.ui.viewcell/render-frame` calls `(use-frame-context!)`, discards its return, then invokes `thunk`. A compiled `(frame)` in that thunk lowers to `frames/frame-ops` -> `resolve-frame` -> `adapter-context/function-component-current-frame`, which reads `_currentValue`. React 19.2 `react-dom/server` populates `_currentValue2`, so a frame-only compiled view under a live `frame-provider` still raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`.
2. Compiler selection prioritizes `render-events` for a production view containing event sites plus `(frame)`. `render-events` retains the hook frame for event capture but invokes the body thunk without binding `frame/*current-frame*`, so the `(frame)` site takes the same broken `_currentValue` path on the server.

Root reproduced the first path with a temporary direct-wrapper Node regression: a live `:app/a` Provider around `render-frame` returned `{:error :rf.error/no-frame-context}`. The temporary diagnostic was removed. Normal DEBUG `defview` coverage is insufficient because DEBUG selects `render-dev`, which already binds the frame and masks the production-wrapper defect.

Keep the repair tiny: reuse the existing `with-current-frame` helper around synchronous body evaluation in the two wrappers. No `_currentValue2` probe, renderer detection, new context abstraction, API, configuration, or broad wrapper rewrite.
acceptance_criteria:
- `render-frame` retains the value from `use-frame-context!` and evaluates its thunk under the existing dynamic-frame binding so a server-rendered frame-only compiled view resolves the closest live provider.
- `render-events` likewise evaluates its body under that binding while continuing to pass the same frame to event capture; this covers production views combining event sites with `(frame)`.
- Focused Node `react-dom/server` regressions directly exercise the production wrappers (not only a DEBUG `defview` path): provider-scoped frame-only and frame+event bodies resolve the provider; an unscoped frame read still fails loud.
- Existing client provider-retarget, event ownership, wrapper-shape/economics, and UI gates remain green.
- No `_currentValue2` access, renderer branch, public API, spec expansion, or new wrapper taxonomy.
notes:
rf2-wobnf resolved in viewcell.cljs (both wrappers), post-lease-keystone (#6572). Re-verified against current origin/main:
- Item 1 (render-frame): STILL BROKEN post-keystone — discarded use-frame-context! return, invoked thunk unbound. FIXED: (let [frame-id (use-frame-context!)] ((with-current-frame frame-id thunk))).
- Item 2 (render-events): STILL BROKEN — kept frame only as event destination, invoked body thunk unbound. FIXED: wrap the body thunk in (with-current-frame frame-id ...) before events/with-capture (same frame still threaded to event capture).
NOTE on the brief's 'compiler render-events selection in emit_cljs.cljc' framing: the bead's acceptance criteria put the item-2 fix in the render-events WRAPPER, not the emitter. The selection cond (subs+events->render-subs-and-events / events->render-events / subs->render-subs / frame-ops->render-frame) is CORRECT as-is: render-events IS the right wrapper for an event+(frame) view (no ViewCell needed); routing it to a combined wrapper would install a needless ViewCell and violate 'no new wrapper taxonomy'. emit_cljs.cljc UNCHANGED.
Red->green proof: direct-wrapper Node react-dom/server regressions in viewcell_server_frame_context_cljs_test.cljs (call the PROD wrappers directly under a live provider-element, since DEBUG masks via render-dev). Pre-fix both threw :rf.error/no-frame-context; post-fix resolve :app/a. Vacuity guard (no provider) fails loud both ways. Behavior-preserving on the client (_currentValue populated there).
Gates: JVM ui 999t/19794a 0F; node cljs 10315t/50966a 0F; elision PASS; browser-prod-elision 112t/483a 0F (55zsd fixtures + selection green). No 55zsd regression; disjoint surface.

title: Server-rendered compiled ViewCell frame context: use-frame-context! reads _currentValue, which react-dom/server (React 19.2) does not populate
description:

THE GAP: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/viewcell (use-frame-context!) discards the public useContext return and re-reads React's private _currentValue to obtain the frame it binds into frame/*current-frame* (the rf2-4rwtd fix, shipped #6540). React 19.2's SERVER renderer (react-dom/server) populates _currentValue2, not _currentValue — so a server-rendered compiled sub/lease ViewCell can still raise :rf.error/no-frame-context. Add one JVM/react-dom-server test: server-render a compiled view whose body subscribes, under a provided frame, and assert no :rf.error/no-frame-context. Three independent lenses agree the client/Reagent fix is complete, correct, and proportionate; the correctness lens found one material CLJS server-renderer residual, independently reproduced by root. IDENTITY: authored empty claim 02fd96718d74fbee2b632b66f7b1c8c1c4ddcb34; authored substantive 5ef6c14da7c69ed796ecd80af5b07e1a15728b4e; applied 4580267a150ae11ec72bb7e54a78d2dc1652fc60; identical stable patch-id bc46f2be316406519619dc1189b6ab69b29045cf; exact range-diff except the empty claim; diff-check clean. No later edit through origin/main f095dd3ab14a2a7fc939fe98e1afba8fae72ad6a touches `viewcell.cljs`, its new test, the compiler wrapper selector, or either ratom reader.

CLEAN CLIENT VERDICT: every compiler-selected sub/lease combination (`render-subs`, `render-leases`, both, the three event combinations, and `render-dev`) binds the retained frame for synchronous body evaluation. `render-events` carries the frame explicitly; `render-frame` reads context directly; the compatibility alias inherits `render-subs`. Reagent and reagent-slim share a dynamic-first reader, so the stand-in is faithful to the failing tier. Provider retargets get a fresh binding; exceptions/Suspense unwind it; lazy descendants render later and establish their own frame. One mounted representative plus existing wrapper-selection gates is enough—seven duplicate browser fixtures would be overengineering.

MATERIAL SERVER FINDING: `use-frame-context!` calls `React.useContext` but discards its return, then rereads private `_currentValue`. Thus a CLJS server-rendered compiled sub/lease ViewCell with no outer binding still loses its Provider and can raise `:rf.error/no-frame-context`; the new Node arms do not mount a Provider. Reopened exact source owner rf2-4rwtd at P2. Small repair: retain the public hook value, preserve `frame/*current-frame*` precedence and existing sentinel/coercion/corruption validation, and add one server-rendered compiled-sub regression. Do not probe `_currentValue2`; no renderer abstraction/config/API.

Three independent lenses: completeness found the public API escape typo; correctness found the raw-text child-shape parity/security defect; implementation quality independently confirmed the ordinary no-content Hiccup regression after exact nil/boolean repros. IDENTITY: authored substantive 55d0e0c9280f08261a75aa1d2fee8e583a03b8e0; empty claim b2038da8ec3b3e1f11e9b5e80ce955f50e70d909; applied 2e096af88957899f4615f7d17898510c2ff5897d; matching stable patch-id 9f170467255b54ed28ca8e43548d0a02ec5e5601; exact range-diff except empty claim and an interleaved Beads checkpoint; diff-check clean. MATERIAL FINDING: legacy sync/streaming raw-text classification requires every original child to be a string. A normal conditional child therefore corrupts an otherwise valid body: `[:script "if (a < b) x()" nil]` emits `if (a < b)`, while `[:style "a > b {}" false]` emits `a > b {}`. Multiple strings are silently joined although React 19.2 emits an empty body with a warning and the static compiler rejects the authored shape. Mixed string/structural bodies can walk a literal nested `</script>` outside the shared closing-sequence guard and terminate the outer element early. `emit-ui-tree` also accepts multiple strings despite its malformed-body contract. Reopened exact source owner rf2-xbvzh at P2. Small repair: remove nil/booleans before legacy classification, accept the one meaningful string path, fail loud on multi/mixed bodies containing strings, preserve pure structural legacy handling, make `emit-ui-tree` reject multiple strings, and add focused parity cases. No policy framework, sanitizer, compatibility mode, or new API.

DOC FACET: the API page says JSON-LD uses the no-op `` `<`→`<` ``; correct it to `` `<`→`\u003c` `` in the same owner. The known hot-zone residual rf2-0yb3w shipped as #6542 while this audit was open and remains closed; its spec work was not duplicated. title: Keep stale capture-frame failures out of same-id successor error sinks

The capture's synchronous supersession precheck reaches `router/emit-frame-destroyed!`, and its durable late expected-incarnation fences in router/subs reach `emit-error-both!`, all with the default frame route enabled. A predecessor failure must remain corpus-observable but must not become successor-owned telemetry.

Reuse #6528's existing internal `route-frame?` seam at the known exact-incarnation capture rejection sites. Preserve corpus records, dev traces, recover-but-emit/nil behavior, realm attribution, query identity/redaction, and ordinary address-directed or missing-frame routing. Do not add a public option, policy snapshot, token API, or generalized routing framework.

- Both the immediate supersession precheck and the existing late expected-incarnation mismatch seams suppress only frame-owned routing; normal address-directed errors still route.
- A focused JVM/CLJS reincarnation proof is non-vacuous (B's sink is demonstrably armed) and existing capture race tests remain green.
- The repair reuses the internal route-frame? seam with no public API or routing abstraction.

title: Keep production-callable epoch projection fail-closed for HTTP bodies
description:
## Problem

`re-frame.epoch/projected-record` is intentionally callable as a pure off-box projection transform even when `re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?` is false, for already-held or synthetic records. Its public contract promises fail-closed handling of stamped unschematized HTTP response bodies.

The HTTP body-slot table in `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc` is currently created wholly inside `(when interop/debug-enabled? ...)`. In a real production-start JVM (`RE_FRAME_DEBUG=false`) or an advanced CLJS build, that table is nil. `omit-off-box-http-bodies` then passes every stamped HTTP body through. A fresh-process reproduction with a valid frame and a synthetic `:rf.http/replied` trace carrying `{:rf.http/off-box-body :omit :value "TOP-SECRET"}` returned the literal body from public `projected-record` while `debug-enabled?` was false. This violates the mandatory off-box-safe boundary and can expose response data from imported/held records.

Existing disabled-gate tests miss the seam: they load the namespace while the gate is true and project records with empty `:trace-events`.

## Smallest repair

Keep the five production-real HTTP operation rows available to the pure projector regardless of the debug gate. Conditionally add only the dev-only `:rf.http/retry-attempt` row so its keyword can still disappear from advanced production bundles. Add one focused production-start/advanced assertion for a stamped production-real HTTP body. Do not add a new projector, privacy framework, runtime switch, or compatibility mode.
acceptance_criteria:
- With the debug gate false from namespace/process start, public `projected-record` replaces a stamped unschematized body for each production-real HTTP operation (`:rf.http/replied`, `:rf.http/accept-failure`, `:rf.http/http-4xx`, `:rf.http/http-5xx`, `:rf.http/decode-failure`) with `:rf/redacted` by default.
- `:include-sensitive? true` remains the explicit trusted-local opt-in; normal dev behavior and idempotency remain unchanged.
- The dev-only `:rf.http/retry-attempt` row still redacts in debug builds, while its sentinel remains absent from the advanced production bundle.
- A focused JVM production-start or equivalent source-load fixture and the existing CLJS production-elision probe pin both privacy and DCE behavior.
- The fix stays within the existing slot table/projector and tests; no public API, generalized privacy sweep, new gate, or framework.

title: Make the documented UIx hydration path use the adoption reporter
description:
## Problem

PR #6523 correctly documented that native UIx/Helix React-element roots were outside both hydration-mismatch channels. PR #6526 then added the existing React-native adoption reporter to `re-frame.substrate.spine/make-render` and changed Spec 011 to say native UIx/Helix roots now verify through that channel. That is true only when a programmer mounts through the low-level adapter-contract `re-frame.substrate.adapter/render` path.

The first-class UIx guide teaches the ordinary native idiom instead: `uix-dom/create-root` plus `uix-dom/render-root` (`docs/core/how-to/use-uix-helix-or-slim.md`), and the adapter namespace exposes no render/hydrate helper. `spine.cljs` and the shared adapter tests explicitly note that substrate-native mounting bypasses `make-render`. #6526's mounted mismatch proof calls `substrate-adapter/render {:hydrate? true}`; it does not exercise the documented UIx root path. A UIx programmer hydrating through UIx/react-dom therefore still gets React's own recovery but no framework `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`, despite current Spec 011's unqualified promise.

## Bounded solution

Give UIx one canonical, ergonomic hydration boot path that passes through the existing adoption reporter, and teach it in the UIx/SSR guidance. Prefer a tiny adapter-owned hydrate entry/helper over asking application code to reach into `re-frame.substrate.adapter`; alternatively, if host-owned roots deliberately remain outside framework instrumentation, narrow Spec 011 and the guide explicitly. Keep ordinary client-only native mounting unchanged. Helix may inherit only if genuinely free through shared code; do not build Helix-specific API for an adapter scheduled for removal.

Do not intercept or monkey-patch arbitrary React roots, add a DOM diff/hash/introspection layer, duplicate the reporter, or build a hydration framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- The canonical documented native UIx SSR/hydration boot goes through the existing `make-render` adoption reporter (or the contract is explicitly narrowed so host-owned roots are not promised framework diagnostics).
- A mounted UIx fixture uses that same public/documented entry: divergent adoption emits exactly one `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`, clean adoption is silent, and an authored recoverable-error callback remains composed.
- The entry has a practical ownership result for teardown/HMR and does not require programmers to unpack the installed adapter map or call an internal-looking namespace.
- Spec 011 and the UIx how-to describe exactly which root owns reporting; no blanket claim covers direct `uix-dom` / `react-dom-client` roots the framework cannot observe.
- Client-only native mounting remains unchanged; no React monkey-patch, DOM diff, structural hash, new reporter, generalized hydration abstraction, or Helix-only work.

title: Keep stale UI bundle failures out of same-id successor error sinks
description:
A compiled re-frame.ui `(frame)` bundle is exact-incarnation authority, but its stale-operation error currently routes through successor state. After frame A is destroyed and same-id B is created with a frame-owned `:observability :errors` sink, invoking A's stale `:subscribe` (or dispatch) bundle emits `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` with A's captured bare frame id. `error_emit/dispatch-on-error!` publishes the required corpus record, then `observability/route-error!` resolves that bare id to current B and delivers A's failure into B's sink.

Deterministic current-main reproduction observed B's sink count become 1 with A's stale query and `:rf.error/frame-destroyed`. The #6516 reincarnation tests create B without observability policy, so they do not see this composition. This violates the existing exact-incarnation rule already enforced for predecessor teardown failures by rf2-vxgfnd.118: successor B must not own predecessor A's error routing.

Use a narrow internal seam to suppress only the frame-owned route for this known-dead-incarnation UI emission. Preserve exactly one corpus-wide always-on record, one dev trace in debug builds, and the typed throw. Preserve ordinary live/address-directed frame error routing. Do not add a policy snapshot, public option, general routing framework, or compatibility path.
acceptance_criteria:
- A JVM/CLJS reincarnation regression creates A, captures its UI frame bundle, destroys A, creates same-id B with an `:errors` sink, and proves invoking A's stale operation sends zero records to B's sink.
- The stale operation still emits exactly one corpus-wide `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` record, one dev trace where enabled, and then throws the typed bounded exception.
- Subscribe retains raw query identity; dispatch/dispatch-sync retain source redaction; capture remains payload-free.
- Ordinary live/address-directed errors still reach their frame-owned sinks.
- The fix is an internal, call-site-exact route suppression with no public API or general framework.

title: Put native UIx hydration in an honest verification tier
description:
## Problem

PR #6507 defines two hydration-mismatch tiers, but its new Spec 011 text incorrectly places native UIx and Helix views in the hashable Hiccup tier. Native UIx/Helix roots are React-element programs, not pure portable data trees, and their shared hydration path did not receive the new adoption reporter. They therefore satisfy neither framework verification path the specification claims.

## Evidence

- `spec/011-SSR.md` says “Reagent / UIx / Helix views are pure functions returning a hashable render-tree.” The same spec already says UIx/Helix are not Hiccup.
- `re-frame.views/apply-adapter-wrap-view` explicitly documents that UIx/Helix registered-view output is a React element. The UIx/Helix adapter testbeds use native `$` with `defui` / `defnc`; a registered UIx production test directly proves `(rf/view ...)` returns a React element.
- `re-frame.substrate.spine/make-render` calls React `hydrateRoot` without root options. It has neither a structural `:render-tree-fn` comparison nor PR #6507's `onRecoverableError` adoption wrapper.
- Reagent/Reagent-slim can provide a Hiccup data projection; native UIx/Helix views, especially hook-using views, cannot be safely called headlessly and hashed as if they were Hiccup.

## Consequence

A UIx programmer following the new specification can hash an opaque React element and receive false confidence, while actual React hydration divergence produces no `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` framework diagnostic. This is a material hole for UIx, which remains a first-class adapter. Helix is planned for removal, so it does not justify adapter-specific machinery.

## Bounded Solution

1. Correct Spec 011 immediately: name the tier by representation, not adapter brand. The structural-hash tier covers Reagent/Reagent-slim and any host that explicitly supplies the same pure data render tree on server and client. Native UIx/Helix roots are React-element roots and are not currently covered by that channel.
2. Give the shared React-hook hydration path the same small adoption-recovery reporting primitive as compiled UI: pass `hydrateRoot` options, emit only for React-recoverable errors during the initial adoption window, and preserve React's default (plus an authored callback if the existing open render opts expose one). A one-shot passive adoption sentinel is sufficient; do not hash or introspect React elements.
3. UIx is the required proof. Helix should inherit only if the implementation stays genuinely shared and free; do not build a Helix-specific branch for an adapter scheduled for removal.

No structural realization, React-element walker, DOM diff, console scraping, or generalized hydration framework is warranted.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 011 scopes structural hashing to hosts that actually provide an equivalent pure data render tree; it no longer says native UIx/Helix views are hashable Hiccup.
- A native UIx hydration fixture proves: clean adoption emits no mismatch; a recoverable initial mismatch emits one `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`; post-adoption recoverable errors are not misclassified; React default reporting and any callback exposed through existing render opts are preserved.
- The implementation reuses one small shared React-root adoption reporter/passive sentinel. Helix inherits only through that shared path; no Helix-only work is added.
- No React-element hashing/introspection, DOM diff, console interception, structural realization, or new hydration framework is introduced.
notes: DOC portion done — PR #6523. Corrected spec/011 §Hydration-mismatch detection: native UIx/Helix removed from the hashable Hiccup tier (they are React-element roots per apply-adapter-wrap-view; spine/make-render calls hydrateRoot without adoption opts). AC#1 satisfied. REMAINING (code, out of doc-PR scope): AC#2/#3/#4 — extend the compiled tier's shared React-root adoption reporter to the React-hook hydrate path (spine/make-render) + native UIx hydration fixture. Keep OPEN or file a code follow-up bead; do not close on #6523 merge.

title: Reject static special-element child shapes that diverge across React and JVM SSR
description:
## Problem
The shared compiler currently accepts source shapes for statically-known special elements that the two hosts do not interpret alike. `[:textarea (ui/html s)]` lowers to React `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, which React 19.2 rejects, while the JVM tree and `emit-ui-tree` emit trusted markup (and currently even apply leading-LF compensation). For `<script>`/`<style>`, multiple authored children reach React as an array that warns and loses the body, while the JVM tree coalesces adjacent text and emits it; statically structural children are likewise dropped/stringified by React but rejected later by the JVM serializer.

This is a developer-feedback and hydration-parity bug, not a request for a general HTML content-model checker. The analyzer already knows the literal host tag and source child forms, so the useful fix is a few local, static rules.

## Solution shape
At `analyze-element`, reject `ui/html` beneath static `<textarea>` with a didactic direction to use `:value` or ordinary text. For static `<script>`/`<style>`, accept no body, one non-structural text-producing expression, or sole `ui/html`; reject multiple source child forms and visibly structural sole children, directing the programmer to construct one string (for example with `str`) or use the explicit trusted-markup bypass. Keep runtime-dynamic values programmer-trusted. At the public structural-tree seam, reject a manual `{:html ...}` child beneath `<textarea>` through the existing malformed-tree path and limit trusted-HTML LF compensation to `<pre>`/`<listing>`.

Do not add a generic validator, sanitizer, policy option, compatibility layer, or runtime framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- The compiler rejects `(ui/html ...)` beneath static `<textarea>` with a concise actionable diagnostic; ordinary text and `:value` remain supported.
- Static `<script>`/`<style>` source forms cannot compile into known host-divergent multi-child or structural-child shapes; no body, one text-producing expression, and sole `ui/html` retain their intended paths.
- `emit-ui-tree` rejects an equivalent hand-written trusted-HTML-under-textarea tree through `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed`; trusted-HTML leading-LF compensation applies only to `<pre>`/`<listing>`.
- Focused CLJ/CLJS tests demonstrate the previously divergent React 19.2 and JVM cases and the accepted cases.
- The relevant 004/004B grammar prose is accurate; coordinate the leading-LF wording with `rf2-13mou`.
- No generalized HTML content-model checker or new public configuration.

title: DECISION: reconcile ordinary script/style raw-text semantics across spec/004B, spec/011, spec/Security, and the legacy hiccup render-to-string emitter
description: ⚠️ NEEDS A MIKE RULING (STOP-reported by rf2-0spji #6500, criterion 5 — a recommendation needing acceptance, NOT a determinable fix). #6477 made the compiled emit-ui-tree serialize <script>/<style> as HTML RAW TEXT (React-aligned, with closing-sequence rewrite). QUESTION: should the LEGACY hiccup render-to-string emitter (the reference ssr-ring path, lifecycle.clj) ALSO adopt React-aligned raw-text for script/style, so BOTH SSR paths agree? And the normative reconciliation across spec/004B + spec/011 + spec/Security of what 'raw text for script/style' means (trust boundary, XSS posture, the :html bypass). THE FORK: (a) align both emitters to React-raw-text (consistency, but touches the legacy emitter); (b) keep them divergent (compiled=raw-text, legacy=escaped) and document the difference; (c) something else. This is a 'what should the two SSR paths agree on' design call across 3 hot-zone specs + a runtime — Mike's ruling. Cross-ref rf2-0spji (#6500), rf2-2dh3b (#6477), rf2-993fz (#6484).
notes: DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-20 08:34 AUSEST) RULING: Option (a) — ONE raw-text semantics for ordinary ` payload can no longer terminate the element and pivot into HTML parsing); residual JS/CSS-language-context safety of interpolated data is author-owned, exactly as in React. Raw-text emission is NOT sanitization — say so. - Data payloads (JSON-LD head channel, __rf_payload/EDN wire): UNCHANGED, keep their stricter data-aware escapes — `<` inside string literals -> `\u003c`, and the EDN breakout reject :rf.error/ssr-edn-script-breakout. This is the house "raw + context-appropriate guard" style (html_helpers.cljc :78-190). - Net effect: refusal is removed, not weakened — refusal was pushing real content into the genuinely unguarded trusted shell opts (:head/:body-end), which is strictly less safe than a guarded render-tree element. TESTS: convert the sync + streaming throw-tests into emission tests; both legacy emitters and emit-ui-tree must BYTE-AGREE on a representative inline script/style corpus: literal JS/CSS operators (`if (a < b)`, `a > .b { }`), `&` unmolested, case-insensitive `` that round-trips through JSON.parse. Do NOT duplicate the compiled path's exhaustive React byte-parity corpus (ui_tree tests own it); focused corpus only. WHICH RECOMMENDATION AND WHY: both recommendations independently converged on (a); I followed their union — the dossier's ruling text extended by Codex's three verified deltas (streaming.cljc as a second legacy surface, the nonexistent-`:head-extra` correction, docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md in the retirement roster) — because one semantics across client render, compiled SSR, and hiccup SSR is the elegance/clarity/correctness call with zero security cost: every path carries the exact guard React itself applies, and the stricter data-payload escapes are untouched. ⚠️ MAYOR HOLD — keystone collision (2026-07-20). RULED Option (a) is dispatchable, BUT it edits BOTH SSR emitters incl. compiled emit-ui-tree (implementation/ssr/.../ui_tree.cljc) — the SAME file the render-static keystone (rf2-oo5lb / #6511 branch) touches for the pure-:server static emit path. Two workers on ui_tree.cljc = collision risk on the S6-opening keystone. DISPATCH xbvzh AFTER #6511 merges (render-static shipped, S6 opens) + rebase on it. xbvzh is INDEPENDENT (not S6-gated) so the short wait costs nothing; protecting the keystone is worth it. Brief from the RULED semantics in this bead's DECISION note (author content trust-the-programmer visible escape; data payloads unchanged; convert sync+streaming throw-tests to emission tests; both legacy emitters + emit-ui-tree BYTE-match). Cross-ref rf2-oo5lb #6511. PR #6539 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT RESIDUAL (2026-07-20; three independent lenses, current origin/main rechecked after #6542). MATERIAL RUNTIME BUG: the new legacy raw-text fast path is gated by `(every? string? children)`. Ordinary no-content Hiccup children (`nil`, `true`, `false`) therefore disqualify an otherwise valid script/style string and fall through to entity escaping: for example `[:script "if (a < b) x()" nil]` emits ``, and `[:style "a > b {}" false]` emits `a > b {}` in both sync and streaming paths. Multi-string and mixed string/structural bodies are also silently joined or walked: two strings are accepted although React 19.2 renders an empty body with a warning and the static compiler rejects the authored shape; a nested `[:script "x" [:script "alert(1)"]]` can place a literal `` outside `escape-raw-text`, allowing the HTML parser to terminate the outer element early. `emit-ui-tree` likewise says multi-child is malformed but `(every? string? children)` accepts multiple strings. BOUNDED REPAIR: in both legacy emitters, discard only ordinary no-content children (`nil` and booleans) before classifying a raw-text body. Accept zero/one meaningful string as appropriate; if a body contains a string and is multi/mixed, fail loud instead of silently corrupting or diverging. Preserve the existing no-string structural legacy handling. In `emit-ui-tree`, accept empty or exactly one string (or the existing sole `:html` bypass) and reject multiple strings. Add focused sync, streaming, compiled, and React-parity cases for nil/true/false, multiple strings, and mixed string/structural children. Keep this local; no child-policy framework, compatibility mode, sanitizer, or new public API. PUBLIC API TYPO: `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md` currently describes the JSON-LD escape as the no-op `` `<`→`<` ``. Correct it to `` `<`→`\u003c` `` so it matches the shipped `escape-script-body-string` path. The obsolete :rf.error/ssr-raw-text-in-body catalogue/refusal was retired correctly, but the prior note's claim that #6542 fixed all hot-zone spec surfaces was too broad. The already-ruled prose reconciliation remains owned HERE; do not create a parallel Bead. In an HTML raw-text script body entities are not decoded: JSON containing `<` round-trips to the literal six characters rather than `<`, so the current prose corrupts data if followed. spec/011-SSR.md:308 also describes composition only through the JSON-LD branch. spec/Security.md omits the ruled split: programmer-authored ordinary script/style is raw text with React's closing-sequence breakout rewrite, while structured JSON-LD uses `\u003c`; residual JS/CSS language-context safety is programmer-owned and the rewrite is not sanitisation. implementation/SECURITY.md:158 repeats the same `<` falsehood. title: Correct migration guidance for projection-side epoch redaction
description: PR #6481 changed `migration/from-re-frame-v1/observability-logging-sweep.md` to recommend the epoch `:redact-fn` as a stronger alternative to per-forwarder projection, claiming it erases each record as committed and that the ring buffer and listener fan-out therefore see redacted data. The shipped contract is deliberately the opposite: `:redact-fn` runs only inside `projected-record`, after the built-in frame/profile projection, once per egress projection call. Raw history and in-process listeners stay raw so replay remains exact. A programmer following the migration text could send a raw listener record off-box believing it was already scrubbed, leaking sensitive data. Keep the fix to this guidance: every off-box epoch forwarder must call `projected-record`; the configure hook is an advanced post-projection override, not storage-time mutation or a replacement for the egress boundary.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The migration observability guide no longer claims `:redact-fn` runs at commit/storage or changes raw ring/listener records. 2. It says every off-box epoch forwarder must pass the raw record through `projected-record`, where built-in projection runs before the configured override, and that the override runs once per projection call. 3. The wording aligns with Tool-Pair's projection-side contract and the epoch implementation/tests. 4. Prose only: no runtime change, new test, compatibility path, or checker; normal docs gates pass.

title: Document epoch creation and listener publication as distinct cadences
description:
PR #6479 correctly changed ordinary epoch RECORD CREATION from once-per-drain to one record per dequeued event, but three edited listener descriptions then equated that with CALLBACK CARDINALITY (docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1234, spec/API.md:842, tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:645). The runtime contract is broader: listeners receive the initial publication of an ordinary event record; record-render!, record-sub-run!, and record-unmount! can re-publish that same epoch after post-settle backfill; replace-frame-state! publishes a synthetic :rf.epoch/db-replaced record without a dequeued event; and the depth-halt path publishes a record for the queued event that never ran. Treating callbacks as a once-per-event clock can make Xray/pair-shaped tools miss corrected snapshots or miscount events.

At the same time, live public and AI/tooling prose still retains the retired once-per-drain model: docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1184; implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2245,2308,2521; implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_epoch.cljc:61; spec/Privacy.md:248; docs/xray/api/runtime-seam.md:92; tools/xray/testbeds/runner/core.cljs:158; implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:1134; and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1137.

Make one bounded documentation/docstring sweep that separates the two concepts: ordinary processing COMMITS one epoch record per dequeued event (parent and child events are separate records), while the listener is a record-publication/change notification and can receive a later version of an existing record plus synthetic tool-write/halt records. Keep the public wording concise; detailed examples can live at one canonical spec site and be linked/reused. Do not change runtime behavior, add compatibility machinery, or build a general prose scanner.

EXISTING OWNERSHIP: rf2-yiwag already owns only skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:1186. Leave that file to rf2-yiwag or close it as a duplicate only if this fix deliberately absorbs it; do not make two fixes for the same line.
acceptance_criteria:
- Public epoch-history text consistently says ordinary event processing commits one record per dequeued event, not per drain.
- Public listener text no longer promises exactly one callback per event; it explains initial record publication, possible same-epoch backfill re-publication, and synthetic replace/halt records at an appropriate canonical level.
- The named core/API/Xray/Privacy/late-bind/manifest stale claims are corrected with a targeted grep showing no remaining misleading per-drain cardinality in those surfaces.
- No runtime/API-shape change, new checker, or compatibility layer; existing docs gates pass.
- rf2-yiwag's preload line is not duplicated.

title: Keep accepted tag names from poisoning reagent-slim's cache lookup
description:
## Problem

`reagent2.impl.template/tag-name-cache` is a plain JavaScript object, and `cached-parse` asks it for hits by calling `(.hasOwnProperty tag-name-cache n)`. String Hiccup heads are accepted. Rendering the valid string head `"hasOwnProperty"` therefore caches a `HiccupTag` under the same property name as the lookup method itself. Every later cache lookup attempts to call that record as a function and throws a raw host `TypeError`.

PR #6478 correctly moved the reserved-`:rf/*` rejection ahead of this lookup, but its audit exposed this adjacent accepted-input failure in the same cache chokepoint.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Render `(template/as-element ["hasOwnProperty" "first"])`; it successfully returns a React element and seeds the tag cache.
2. Render `(template/as-element ["div" "second"])` in the same runtime.
3. Observe `TypeError: tag-name-cache.hasOwnProperty is not a function` rather than a `div` element.

## Expected Behavior

Any accepted tag head, including `"hasOwnProperty"`, can be cached without changing how later entries are looked up; the subsequent ordinary tag renders normally.

## Actual Behavior

The accepted head overwrites the cache object's lookup method. All later tag parsing crashes until the runtime is reloaded.

## Consequence

One data-driven or library-supplied string tag can take down every later render in the application with an opaque host exception. This is a small implementation defect with broad SPA impact, not a request for a new cache abstraction.

## Bounded Solution

Use an unspoofable own-property check such as `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(tag-name-cache, n)` at this cache lookup (and only widen further if the same exact pattern is present on an equally reachable cache). Add one focused ordering regression: seed `"hasOwnProperty"`, then render an ordinary tag and assert both React types are correct. Preserve the existing reserved-key exclusions and the PR #6478 reserved-head behavior. Do not introduce a cache subsystem or generalized map wrapper.
acceptance_criteria: A focused red-before CLJS test renders the accepted string head hasOwnProperty and then an ordinary tag without a raw exception; both returned React types are correct; cache hit behavior, reserved-key exclusions, exact reserved-head diagnostics, and PR #6478's string-seeded reserved-keyword rejection remain green; the fix uses an unspoofable own-property check at the existing cache seam and adds no cache framework or public API.
close_reason: shipped #6501
