title: Make compiled-ui hydration verify the real server-phase snapshot
description:
## Problem

Spec 011 requires a hydrating root's mismatch snapshot to be the fallback-bearing `:server`-phase tree, before the passive `:server` -> `:client` flip. The canonical public boot is two calls: `ssr/hydrate!` installs state and verifies first, then `ui/hydrate-root` adopts the DOM.

The compiled-ui implementation cannot currently make that verification honest:

- `ssr/hydrate!` invokes `:render-tree-fn` synchronously in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc`, before DOM adoption.
- The phase context in `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/runtime.cljs` defaults to `:client`.
- The only `:server` provider is installed later by `runtime/with-phase-flip` inside `ui/hydrate-root*`.
- The CLJS compiler emits direct React elements, not the JVM structural UI tree. If a pre-mount verifier actually materialises the compiled UI, it is outside the provider and sees `:client`; if it merely returns a component vector or opaque React element, the generic structural hash walks an opaque value rather than the rendered fallback tree.

PR #6476's phase-flip browser vertical deliberately skips `ssr/hydrate!`, so it proves clean React adoption and the post-commit swap but not the framework mismatch snapshot that its implementation comments claim remains honest.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Define a `.cljc` compiled root containing `(ui/client-only {:fallback [:p "loading"]} [:button "live"])`.
2. Server-render the root's JVM structural tree and place its real fallback-bearing render hash in the hydration payload.
3. On CLJS, run the canonical boot: `ssr/hydrate!` with a `:render-tree-fn` for that same compiled root, followed by `ui/hydrate-root`.
4. Inspect the value hashed before mount and the resulting mismatch decision.

There is no current path for step 3 to obtain the compiled root's rendered `:server`-phase structural tree. Materialising it before the provider selects client semantics; returning its opaque React/component representation is not an honest rendered-tree snapshot.

## Expected Behavior

The client verifier hashes the same fallback-bearing semantic tree the server hashed, reports no framework mismatch for an identical root, React adopts that fallback DOM, and the one root-scoped passive update then swaps all client-only sites to their client subtrees.

## Actual Behavior

The pre-mount compiled-ui verifier lacks access to the hydration root's `:server` phase and lacks an equivalent structural snapshot. Depending on the host-supplied value, verification can compare the wrong representation/phase or provide false confidence by hashing an opaque wrapper rather than the rendered UI.

## Consequence

A valid compiled-ui hydration can produce a spurious `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` (and abort in hard-error mode), or the framework detector can silently fail to verify the content React is about to adopt. This breaks a central SSR correctness/tooling promise for ordinary programmers using `ui/client-only`.

## Bounded Solution

Give the canonical compiled-ui hydration path one honest server-phase verification seam: either expose a pure fallback-phase snapshot for the pre-mount verifier, or perform compiled-ui verification from the hydrating root's first `:server` render before the existing passive flip. Reuse the existing root phase; do not add parallel phase state, a general React introspector, or a new framework when a compiler/root-local seam suffices. Keep ordinary non-hydrating mounts defaulting directly to `:client`.

Add one end-to-end red-before fixture that carries a real server hash through `ssr/hydrate!` and `ui/hydrate-root`, asserts no framework mismatch for the same compiled root, observes fallback adoption, and then observes the client-only flip. The same vertical may cheaply pin two sibling sites and the single root trace; those proof details do not warrant separate issues.
acceptance_criteria:
- Compiled-tier documentation and catalogue describe the signal precisely as React-recoverable errors reported during initial adoption, not exhaustive server/client divergence detection; they explicitly note that attribute-only mismatches may be warned in development, left unpatched, and produce no framework trace.
- One focused DOM fixture pins that limitation alongside the existing recoverable/text mismatch fixture; host callback composition and the root-local adoption window remain unchanged.
- The public `re-frame.ui/hydrate-root` source docstring, generated API page, and SSR tutorial contain one compact compiled-ui boot example: `ssr/hydrate!` without `:render-tree-fn`, followed by `ui/hydrate-root`, including the optional `:on-recoverable-error` hook.
- Path A remains small: no structural realization/hash, render fingerprint, console scraping, React introspector, parallel phase state, or generalized hydration framework.
- The identical compiled-root DOM vertical uses a root id unique to that test and scopes its sole positive :rf.ssr/phase-flip witness by [:tags :root-id]; a wrong-id substitute probe reds it.
notes:

title: Make the static streaming SSR stand-in preserve failed-boundary hydration
description:
PR #6485 ships examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/index.html as a runnable offline stand-in. It pre-bakes the final swapped DOM and final payload, but removes every suspense mount/template/chunk marker. That shape is not equivalent to fully buffered streaming output: streaming.client/install! sees no failed outcome, finalize! records an empty failed-boundary set, and hydration renders the flaky boundary body (throwing-card) instead of the baked declared fallback.

The previous non-issue ruling correctly verified supported fully buffered server output, where all resolved/failed chunks remain present for the initial sweep. It did not verify this checked-in hybrid artifact, which the repository itself asks developers to run.

The same page also says its final boundary-resolved DOM is emitted by rf/render-to-string. That is false: standard rendering deliberately rejects :rf/suspense-boundary; the streaming shell/continuation/finalization path produces this DOM.

Keep the fix bounded to the example. Make the checked-in stand-in and bootstrap carry a coherent failed-boundary outcome using the existing streaming contract, and correct the explanation. Do not redesign the runtime or add general example-test infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria: Correct the remaining teaching claims in the static streaming example. In core.cljc's flaky-slot comment, explain that the recorded failed-boundary outcome makes ssr/boundary choose its declared skeleton fallback; do not say a missing delta makes card-view render a skeleton (the body is throwing-card and card-view has no such branch). Across README.md, core.cljc, and index.html, replace "captured verbatim" / "same bytes" wording with the precise bounded truth: the checked-in page assembles the emitter's exact shell and continuation chunks, while deliberately substituting the documented placeholder render hash in the final payload. Keep this a prose-only example correction; no runtime redesign, generator, generalized harness, or additional browser infrastructure is required.
notes:
REOPENED BY THE CHRONOLOGICAL PR AUDIT OF #6485 (2026-07-19).

Three independent lenses reproduced a narrower case the original investigation accidentally excluded. The 502-test browser evidence remains valid for real streamed output and for fully buffered output containing all chunks. It does not cover the hand-written index.html, which has final swapped DOM + __rf_payload but deliberately omits every resolved/failed template and mount. With seen={}, finalize! publishes failed #{}, then the CLJS boundary selects throwing-card rather than the baked fallback.

Reuse the existing protocol and keep this an example-coherence fix. The inaccurate render-to-string wording is part of the same cause and same-file repair, not a separate Bead.
REOPENED BY THE CHRONOLOGICAL PR AUDIT OF #6506 (2026-07-20).

PR #6506 fixes the runnable page: a fresh compile plus an exact checked-in-page Chromium smoke reached three resolved cards and the flaky skeleton with zero runtime/hydration errors, and the protocol mounts/templates/delta scripts were gone after finalization. The remaining defect is explanatory, not functional.

examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/core.cljc:168-174 says the failed chunk's missing delta is "the whole story" and makes card-view render a skeleton. Shipped behavior is different: the body is throwing-card, card-view has no nil/skeleton branch, and install!/hydrate preserve the server's failed-boundary outcome so ssr/boundary selects its declared fallback.

The three example files also call the hand-written page "captured verbatim" / the "same bytes" as handle-request while explicitly replacing the emitter's real render hash with "00000000". The shell and continuation chunks do occur byte-for-byte and the payload is otherwise semantically equal; describe that assembly honestly. This is one small prose repair on the existing owner, not a new Bead. Independent correctness review found no runtime defect. A proposed general generator/browser gate was rejected as unnecessary for this bounded example under the project's no-overengineering posture.

title: Bind the ViewCell frame into frame/*current-frame* so ambient subs resolve under ratom-family hosts (W7b prerequisite)
description:
FILED from the 2026-07-19 Xray-on-re-frame.ui investigation, AMENDED same day after the Codex counter-analysis (both in ai/findings/2026.07.19.xray-ui.md — local-only; this description is the durable substance).

THE FIX (unchanged by the amendment; both analyses agree): ambient (sub ...) sites resolve their frame through the routed :adapter/current-frame hook, and the ratom-family readers (Reagent/reagent-slim — provider/current-frame ratom, class-component (.-context cmp) read) return nil inside ui function components, so a compiled view's sub reads raise :rf.error/no-frame-context under a Reagent/slim host. ui's own event/(frame) paths are immune (direct context reader) — a sub-read-only asymmetry, same class ui patched for plain-atom (rf2-vxgfnd.24). FIX at the compiled boundary: re-frame.ui.viewcell's use-frame-context! already reads the frame from React context and discards it — retain it and bind it into re-frame.frame/*current-frame* while evaluating the compiled body thunk, so ambient sub/lease resolution hits the precedence-first dynamic tier regardless of which adapter's reader the hook routes to. Keep the binding scoped to the body evaluation (descendant ViewCells bind their own context; no ambient leak across React's lazy child rendering). REJECTED alternatives (for the record): broadening the Reagent reader (weakens its fail-loud boundary); route-publishing ui's reader for Reagent kinds (one artefact overriding another's installed-adapter behavior); per-site Xray special-casing.

FRAMING (the amendment): this is NOT an Xray-specific patch and NOT part of a guest-root contract. It establishes the general outward-interop invariant — once a ViewCell consumes its frame from React context, every re-frame op its body evaluates observes that frame, whichever compatible renderer owns the surrounding tree. The original filing's guest-root rationale (independent ui/mount roots surviving host-adapter disposal as a feature) is WITHDRAWN: renderer independence is not data-lifecycle independence — a guest root's views consume reactions/sub-caches the installed adapter owns, and dispose-adapter! takes those down (spec/006 adapter symmetry), so a surviving guest root is a zombie, not resilience. The ruled W7b architecture is instead: Xray becomes a ui-COMPILED SUBTREE hosted by the installed adapter — ui/->react (the blessed S6 outward bridge, spec/API.md:249) exports the compiled shell/panels as ordinary React components; Xray keeps its existing substrate-adapter/render mount + returned-unmount lifecycle for every surface (inline shell, overlay, popout, standalone panels). One adapter, one root owner, no guest-root machinery, no new public mechanism.

TEST: one hardening browser test — a ViewCell over ratom-family sub nodes under a Reagent-installed host reads a sub, dispatches, repaints (mechanism-sound via Xray's auto-open watcher precedent, currently untested). The W7b acceptance bar later adds: destroy the host adapter and prove the Xray root IS unmounted (host-owned lifecycle) — the opposite of the withdrawn guest-root expectation.

SEQUENCING: this fix is parallel-safe (viewcell.cljs, not hot-zone) and can land now — it is the general invariant, wanted regardless of W7b. W7b itself sequences behind ui/->react landing (S6). Cross-ref: rf2-vxgfnd.98 (S6 epic, W7b workstream), rf2-vxgfnd.24 (plain-atom precedent), spec/API.md ->react rows.
notes:
PR #6540 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6540) — bind ViewCell frame into frame/*current-frame* around the compiled body (with-current-frame) in all 7 sub/lease wrappers; render-events/render-frame unchanged. Hardening test uses a dynamic-tier-only ratom-family stand-in reader: no-binding fails loud, with-binding resolves, mounted ViewCell resolves provider frame + repaints, isolation pin (per-ViewCell, no leak). spec/API.md untouched (internal correctness fix). Gates green: ui-jvm 1016 / core-jvm exit0 / test:cljs 10350 / test:browser 514 / test:ui 904. Do NOT merge (worker).
PR #6540 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT RESIDUAL (2026-07-20; correctness lens, independently reproduced on current React 19.2).

The browser/Reagent repair is correct, but `use-frame-context!` still loses the Provider frame under CLJS `react-dom/server`. It calls `React.useContext(frame-context)` and discards that correct value, then calls `adapter-context/function-component-current-frame`, which rereads the private `frame-context._currentValue` slot. React 19.2's server renderer uses the secondary slot `_currentValue2`: a direct repository-local probe under a Provider showed, during BOTH `renderToStaticMarkup` and `renderToString`, `useContext(C) = "provider"`, `C._currentValue = "default"`, and `C._currentValue2 = "provider"`. Consequently a server-rendered compiled sub/lease ViewCell with no outer dynamic binding binds nil/default instead of its Provider frame and can still raise `:rf.error/no-frame-context`.

The new test does not cover this host: its Node arms manually test the dynamic tier, while its mounted Provider bodies are skipped unless a browser DOM exists. No later edit to `viewcell.cljs` or `adapter/context.cljs` fixes the seam, and an all-state Bead search found no duplicate owner.

BOUNDED FIX: have `use-frame-context!` retain the PUBLIC `React.useContext` return and resolve it with explicit precedence: an existing `frame/*current-frame*` still wins, otherwise use the hook value through the existing sentinel/coercion/corruption-validation rules. Do not inspect `_currentValue2` or add renderer detection/configuration. Add one CLJS `react-dom/server` regression rendering a Provider plus compiled `sub` ViewCell (a lease twin only if essentially free). No new adapter API, server abstraction, compatibility mode, or framework. The public `ui/render-static` path remains JVM-only; this closes the source Bead's broader compatible-renderer/outward-interop invariant for ordinary React server hosts.

title: Reject reserved reagent-slim heads before type-aliased cache hits
description: PR #6460 makes the invalid-hiccup-head rejection carry the exact offending :element, but the rejection still occurs only inside parse-tag. cached-parse consults tag-name-cache first. The cache key for a string head "rf/x" and the reserved keyword :rf/x is the same string, "rf/x". Seeding the cache with the valid string form therefore lets the later reserved keyword take the cache-hit path, bypass reject-reserved-rf-head!, and produce a React element whose type is "rf/x" instead of throwing. A direct probe against the compiled current runtime observed {"seeded":true,"outcome":{"threw":false,"reactType":"rf/audit-cache-twin"}}. title: Treat omitted hydration prefix as React's effective empty prefix
description:
PR #6458 makes `ui/hydrate-root` obtain identity from a validated Root Manifest, but the optional `:identifier-prefix` case bypasses the existing live-root uniqueness fence.

Root Manifest v1 explicitly makes every extension key optional, and `re-frame.ssr.manifest/valid?` accepts an unmodified S1 descriptor. For such a bare manifest, `hydrate-root*` reads a nil prefix, omits React's `identifierPrefix` option, stores nil in the live-root registry, and `check-root-claim!` deliberately skips the prefix arm when nil. React 19.2 does not have a distinct “no effective prefix” state: `hydrateRoot` canonicalizes the omitted option to the empty string `""`.

The result is that two different valid bare manifests on one document are both admitted even though both React roots own the same effective prefix. That defeats Spec 004C Layer 3's promise that two live roots cannot share an effective `identifierPrefix` and can make their `useId` output alias.

A temporary public-API browser test planted two containers with exact matching server DOM and two adjacent valid manifests containing only schema-version and distinct root-ids. The first `ui/hydrate-root` succeeded; the second was admitted. The focused full browser run reported 493 tests / 2756 assertions with exactly two failures, both in the probe: the expected `:rf.error/duplicate-identifier-prefix` and expected effective prefix `""` were absent. There were no test errors or hydration-mismatch page errors. The probe was removed byte-identical afterward.

Correct this at the hydration identity boundary: canonicalize a missing manifest prefix to React's actual effective empty prefix for claim bookkeeping (and report it as `""` on collision). Do not derive a root-id prefix client-side—the server used no prefix, so that would break hydration. Preserve manifest optionality, the existing error id, and the existing two-call boot contract. Reconcile the narrow Spec 004C claim that collisions are “only possible” through authored prefixes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two live `ui/hydrate-root` calls using distinct valid manifests with omitted `:identifier-prefix` reject the second before React work with `:rf.error/duplicate-identifier-prefix`, reporting effective prefix `""` and the owning root.
- A single bare manifest still validates and hydrates successfully; manifest extension keys remain optional and no root-id-derived prefix is synthesized on the client.
- Explicit server-authored prefixes retain their current behavior, including collision detection and exact pass-through to React.
- The live-root registry records the actual effective prefix for hydrating roots, so unmount/release frees the claim normally.
- Spec 004C describes the omitted-prefix route accurately; no new error id, public option, negotiation, cache, fallback, or version machinery is added.
- Focused SSR/UI browser tests and existing root-registry tests pass with non-zero plausible counts.

title: Serialize script and style text with raw-text-aware React semantics
description: PR #6448's emit-ui-tree sends every text node through five-character HTML entity escaping. That is incorrect inside HTML raw-text elements: the parser does not decode entities in script/style, so a valid style node containing a & b < c becomes DOM text a & b < c rather than the authored CSS, and script/style content changes. Closing-tag text is also mishandled: React 19.2 emits context-safe spellings (for example a JavaScript Unicode escape in the script closing name and a CSS escape in the style closing name) so the raw-text parser does not terminate early, while emit-ui-tree emits entity spellings whose entities remain literal. This violates the one-conversion-table/client-SSR coherence contract and can cause hydration/behavior divergence. Fix narrowly with context-aware text serialization for script and style, pinned byte/parsed behavior against React 19.2 for ordinary ampersand/less-than text and embedded closing-tag sequences; update Spec 004B's blanket escaping row to name the raw-text exception. Do not add a general sanitizer or parser framework; ui/html remains the explicit trusted-markup bypass.

title: Linearize custom-element conflict admission across ledger and live registry
description:
## Confirmed cross-atom race

PR #6440 intends a rejected dev/JVM write-through registration to change neither the live `custom-elements` aggregate nor ledger `::sources`. The implementation first swaps `ledger-state`, using a snapshot of `@custom-elements` as a precheck, and only afterward calls the atomic live `write-element!` barrier. Those two atoms are not one transaction.

A forced current-main interleaving with two threads is deterministic:

1. Both conflicting registrations update separate ledger source rows while the live aggregate is still empty, so both prechecks admit.
2. Both reach `write-element!`.
3. One live write wins; the other correctly throws `:rf.error/custom-element-conflict`.
4. Both ledger rows remain. `projected-aggregate` is now nil/conflicting even though the live aggregate contains the winner.

Observed outcome: one `:admitted`, one anchored conflict, live `#{:a}`, invalid projection. This breaks the PR's atomic rejection and “rejected registration never enters the ledger” guarantees. A later reload operates on a ledger that already contains the rejected contradiction.

## Deliverable

Linearize write-through conflict admission across the dev ledger and live aggregate so a registration rejected by the winning live verdict cannot remain in `::sources`, while an admitted concurrent registration cannot be lost by a reload commit. Preserve the production direct path's one-atom/DCE shape and the existing reentrant-watch/commit generation behavior.

Choose the smallest protocol repair. Do not introduce a generalized transaction framework, public API, configuration, or per-render work.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic two-thread fixture places both conflicting registrations after their ledger precheck and before their live writes; exactly one is admitted, the rejected row is absent from `::sources`, and `projected-aggregate` equals the live registry.
- The same proof covers both arrival orders and distinct build ids.
- Concurrent write-through versus commit still produces a legal serial result with no admitted row lost or applied twice.
- Reentrant registration from a publication watch retains the existing generation semantics and does not deadlock.
- Production keeps a single atomic live-registry barrier with the ledger DCE'd.
- No generalized transaction layer, second public registry, API, or new CI job.
notes: Fixed in PR #6475 (commit: linearize write-through admission via write-through-verdict inside the single ledger-state swap; publish live aggregate as a projection). Red-before: 200/200 JVM rounds fail projected-aggregate==live on pre-fix code; green after. Gates: ui JVM 1001t, cljs node 10289t, browser-prod-elision PASS, elision PASS, core 2093t.
close_reason: shipped #6475

title: Preserve every equal custom-element declarer before admitting a replacement
description:
## Confirmed defect

PR #6440 stores one canonical `::owner` on an aggregate entry when several sources contribute `rf=`-equal declarations. That makes the next same-source replacement unable to see the other equal declarers.

Concrete current-main reproduction:

1. `a.ns` declares `:x-el` with `#{:p}`.
2. `z.ns` declares the same `#{:p}`; the aggregate keeps canonical owner `a.ns`.
3. `a.ns` re-declares `#{:q}` on the write-through/REPL path.
4. The write is admitted by `(= owner source)`, even though live `z.ns` still contributes `#{:p}`.

The live manifest becomes `#{:q}` and the ledger projection is conflicting/nil. The next unrelated reload raises `:rf.error/custom-element-conflict` only after the invalid value is already live. This violates the headline pairwise-`rf=` law, last-known-good retention, reject-without-writing guarantee, and ledger/aggregate coherence. The existing tests separately cover equal duplicates and sole-source replacement, but not their composition.

## Deliverable

Retain enough provenance in the same atomic aggregate entry to represent every equal live declarer (or an equivalent single-atom design). Replacing one source must remove/replace only that source's contribution, compare the arriving declaration with every remaining live declarer, and reject atomically when any differs. Keep `custom-element-properties` readers unchanged. The dev ledger must also decline the rejected row, and the production direct path must retain the same law under `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false`.

This is a bounded repair: no second atom, public API, config knob, generalized registry framework, or per-render lookup.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two equal declarers followed by an unequal re-declaration from the canonical owner is rejected before either aggregate or ledger changes.
- The same sequence from the non-canonical owner remains rejected with deterministic two-source evidence.
- A sole source can still replace itself; after another equal declarer is genuinely removed, the remaining source can replace itself.
- Equal duplicates remain order-independent, and a clean aggregate still equals the ledger projection.
- The focused advanced-production fixture composes equal-duplicate admission with canonical-owner replacement and proves the barrier survives DCE.
- Existing staged-reload, permutation, unrelated-reload, and linearizability gates remain green; no new framework or public surface.
notes: Fixed in PR #6475 (commit: ::owner->::owners set on aggregate entry; admit joins/replaces-if-sole/conflicts-naming-all; canonical-owner retired). Red-before: 8 assertions fail on single-owner code (only 2 declarers named, self-replace admitted). Advanced-prod composition pin (equal-dup then canonical-owner replacement rejected under DCE) green. Same gate run as u25hr.
close_reason: shipped #6475

title: Wire the missing G-16 keyed-reorder-under-slots proof
description:
## Confirmed gap

PR #6442 graduated G-16 to the wired roster, but the original slot feature bead `rf2-ri0k6n` required two distinct proofs: normalized client/JVM slotted-output parity, and keyed reorder under slots preserving identity/occurrence paths. The shipped `:slot-vtable` corpus case renders one fixed row order through SSR/static structural normalization. It never mounts, rerenders A/B as B/A, or observes identity/occurrence ownership across commits. `slot_render_fn_arity_cljs_test` covers only the separate dynamic arity contract. A repository-wide current test census finds no slot-specific reorder fixture.

This is a real behavioral boundary, not prose polish: a slot body executes deferred inside the reusable library seam, while the enclosing keyed row must still determine React identity and the runtime occurrence path. One-state SSR parity cannot catch a reorder that remounts or cross-retargets row-scoped evidence.

Add the smallest focused mounted-browser G-16 arm using the existing v-table-shaped slot seam: render two keyed rows through a caller-supplied `ui/render-fn`, rerender the same keys in reverse order, and prove each row keeps its own identity and occurrence ownership. Reconcile the G-16 wired claim only as needed to name that executable proof. Reuse existing root/flush/evidence helpers; do not add a new harness, CI job, generated matrix, or broader keyed-list sweep.

- The same fixture observes the slot-owned/enclosing occurrence identity (or an equivalent row-scoped committed behavior/evidence) and proves it remains attached to the correct key after reorder.
- A focused mutation of the slot/enclosing-row key propagation makes this fixture fail, then the restored tree passes.

- No new test framework, CI job, combinatorial matrix, runtime API, or generalized identity machinery.

notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 17:58 AUSEST)

RULED: spec/011 gains §Phase flip — the S5 ui/client-only completion contract. This block is self-contained for the spec worker (the dossier is retired). The ruled contract:

1. PHASE MODEL. A root renders in exactly one of two phases, :server or :client — deliberately the same vocabulary as the Root Manifest :phase key (011:455, ":server — the only v1 value; the field exists so a future phase is additive"): this contract cashes that reservation in rather than minting a third word. A ui/client-only site renders its fallback in :server phase and its client subtree in :client phase; the compiled site is phase-conditional, reading a root-scoped phase value that defaults :client when no hydrating root provides one. Non-hydrating roots (mount / render! / ui.test/render) are born :client and never flip — S3 behaviour is byte-identical for them, existing tests undisturbed. render-static is pure :server output with no manifest and no flip (004C:573 already states this).

2. SINGLE UPDATE. The phase is ONE root-scoped value written exactly once; all client-only sites in the root swap fallback->client in the single update that write produces. Per-site flip state is non-conforming (per-site flips = visible tearing, N updates, exactly what every promise site forbids).

3. TIMING. A hydrating root boots in :server phase: the first compiled (hydration) render renders fallbacks — this is what makes React adoption clean and keeps the §Hydration-mismatch hash honest (server hashed the fallback-bearing tree). The mismatch snapshot is taken over the :server-phase tree and the flip MUST NOT run before that snapshot. After the root's hydration commit, the runtime schedules the flip as the root's next ordinary update (React's own documented two-pass pattern for server/client-divergent content). A painted fallback frame before the swap is permitted and by design — the fallback is mandatory, presentable UI the user has been looking at since first paint. No synchronous pre-paint flush (flushSync in the hydration commit path buys nothing visible and is hostile to streaming/readiness-driven hydration).

4. FAILED ROOT. The flip is a stage of a SUCCESSFUL root boot. A root that failed to boot (011 §Failed-root isolation, the rf2-1b0po contract) never flips: its server-rendered fallback markup stays, inert, as part of what the failed root leaves behind. No additional error is emitted — :rf.error/root-boot-failed already fired naming root/frame/:phase; isolation is not recovery, and the capability-free fallback is precisely the part of the page designed to stand without a runtime. A root that booted but took the mismatch warn-and-replace path DID boot, so it flips normally; the replacement render is an ordinary post-commit client render, no special casing.

5. MULTI-ROOT. The flip is per-root and independent — each root flips when ITS hydration commits. No page-wide barrier; one slow or failed root never delays a sibling's flip (a barrier would couple what §Failed-root isolation decoupled and deadlock on any dead root).

6. OBSERVABILITY. One diagnostic trace: :operation :rf.ssr/phase-flip, :op-type :info, :tags {:root-id ...}, fired once per hydrating root at flip commit; diagnostic channel, DCE'd under :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false like every non-error :rf.ssr/* row. It is NOT an event and mints NO epoch (the 009 epoch unit is a dequeued event; the flip is render-layer root bookkeeping — routing it through dispatch would pollute app event streams). The Spec 009 catalogue row (and Spec-Schemas if touched) lands in the SAME PR as the spec section's first emit description, per the one-catalogue rule.

ACCEPTED CONSEQUENCE (state it plainly in the section): today's client emit (emit_cljs.cljc:670) drops the fallback template entirely; under this contract the compiled site becomes phase-conditional, so the fallback template rides the client bundle. Unavoidable (React must materialise the fallback vdom during the hydration render) and cheap by construction — capability-free static markup in the same emit-standalone shape react/lazy fallbacks already use. Sites cannot be compile-time-gated per root (a root cannot see through defview boundaries). RULED proportionately: NO new elision/size gate — the existing perf-bundle budget gate already covers any real regression; the spec section states the cost in prose, nothing more.

SEVEN PROMISE SITES to reconcile (most need no wording change — their promises become true once §Phase flip exists; add cross-ref pointers only where natural):
  - spec/API.md:251 and :368 (011 named authority; S5 phase-flip hydration fixture)

  - spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md:573 — render-static never flips (already correct)

title: Publish Story with every declared in-repo dependency in its generated POM
description:
## Problem

PR #6435 made `day8/re-frame2-xray {:local/root "../xray"}` a required Story dependency and documents that a future `day8/re-frame2-story` coordinate will bring Xray transitively at the same version. The source graph is now honest, but the package boundary is not implemented.

A clean `clojure -M:clein pom` from `tools/story` reports that it is skipping all five `:local/root` coordinates (core, reagent adapter, machines, HTTP, and Xray). The generated POM contains only Clojure, Reagent, and Malli. This is expected clein behavior and is why release workflows must rewrite local roots before packaging. No workflow currently deploys `day8/re-frame2-story` or performs those rewrites. The lockstep verifier inventories Story but also omits Story's HTTP and new Xray edges from `TOOLS_LOCAL_ROOTS`, so its current green result cannot catch either omission.

The README correctly says Story is not on Clojars yet, so this is a pre-alpha release gate rather than a claim that today's users can fetch it. It is still necessary before the first alpha: publishing the current generated POM would recreate the exact consumer compile failure rf2-r8trk fixed in source.

## Small correction

Give Story one concrete pre-alpha publish path, using the existing local-root rewrite helper and generated-POM verification. Rewrite every main-deps in-repo coordinate to the lockstep Maven version, ensure Xray and the framework leaves are available before Story deploys, and verify the generated POM contains them. Extend the existing lockstep inventory to cover Story's actual edges.

Do not design a general release platform or combine every tool cadence. A small Story-specific workflow or a bounded extension of an existing release path is enough.
acceptance_criteria:
- There is an executable, documented path that publishes `day8/re-frame2-story` for the first alpha.
- Before packaging, every main `:local/root` dependency in `tools/story/deps.edn` is rewritten to the repo `VERSION`; at minimum the generated POM contains core, reagent adapter, machines, HTTP, and Xray at that exact version.
- The release cannot deploy Story before those coordinates, especially Xray, are available.
- A pre-deploy check inspects the generated POM and fails if an expected dependency is absent or any in-tree dependency was silently skipped.
- `verify-version-lockstep.sh` accounts for Story's HTTP and Xray edges. No general release-orchestration framework.

title: Make Story's :xray :filters preset drive Xray's real filter surface
description:
## Problem

Story publicly accepts `:xray {:filters {:in [...keywords...] :out [...keywords...]}}`, but the runtime cannot apply it. `apply-filters!` probes `day8.re-frame2-xray.filters.config/configure!`; that namespace does not exist, so `filters-available?` is permanently false and every non-empty preset only warns. The warning cites `rf2-ak4ms`, which is not a Bead.

The needed Xray surface already exists: `day8.re-frame2-xray.config/configure!` accepts `:rf.xray/filters`, and Xray registers `:rf.xray/hydrate-filters` for the live `:rf/xray` frame. There is also a wire-shape mismatch: Story's schema/examples use bare keywords, while Xray's pill shape is `{:pattern <keyword-or-string>}` (or a typed pill). Executable probe: `(canonicalise-pill :my/noise)` returns `{:kind :never :params {}}`, while `(canonicalise-pill {:pattern :my/noise})` returns `{:kind :event-id-pattern ...}`. Simply redirecting the existing call would therefore still create inert filters.

This is a shipped ergonomic surface, not optional polish: a programmer can declare a schema-valid preset, receive no validation error, and get no filtering.

## Small correction

Keep Story's compact keyword-vector API and lower it at the Story→Xray boundary to Xray's real pill representation. Make the preset work both before the first embedded panel mount and when switching variants after the Xray frame already exists: seed the established config surface for first-mount hydration and update the live frame through the established filter event/helper when present. Reconcile the nearby stale “Xray absent/feature detect” docstrings while touching the seam.

Do not add `filters.config`, a plugin system, a general filter abstraction, or a second Xray registry. Reuse the existing config/frame surfaces and add focused behavioral tests around actual `:active-filters` and event survival.
acceptance_criteria:
- A schema-valid Story preset such as `{:filters {:out [:app/noise]}}` becomes Xray's canonical pill shape and actually hides matching events.
- The result lands for both an initially selected variant (before first embedded-panel mount) and a later variant switch with `:rf/xray` already installed.
- Missing/empty `:filters` remains a cheap no-op; switching to an explicit empty filter set has a deliberate, tested meaning.
- Tests assert the real `:rf/xray` active-filter state and at least one matcher outcome; they do not pass through a shimmed nonexistent namespace.
- Remove the nonexistent-namespace probe/warning and correct the adjacent absent-Xray wording. No new plugin/framework layer.

title: Reject cross-host numeric key and set collisions before manifest emission
description:
## Defect

PR #6437 makes `wire-number?` decide whether each numeric value crosses the JVM→CLJS Root Manifest wire, but the headline invariant is about the **whole accepted manifest**. Per-value acceptance is insufficient for maps and sets because Clojure and ClojureScript do not share numeric key/element identity.

On the JVM, `1` and `1.0` are unequal and can coexist as two map keys. Both individually pass `wire-number?`, so `edn-carryable?`, `manifest`, and `script-html` accept and emit this value:

```clojure
{:props {:lookup {1 :integer, 1.0 :double}}}
```

The CLJS reader represents both as the same JS number. The shipped `read-manifest` therefore rejects the emitted body with `:rf.error/root-manifest-invalid`, reason `Map literal contains duplicate key: 1`. An accepted server manifest does not round-trip at all, contradicting both rf2-v4foc's acceptance criterion and the new Spec 011 exact-wire rule. The same identity-collapse class applies to set elements and to pairs such as `0` / `-0.0`.

## Executable reproduction

JVM, through the shipped assembly/emission paths:

- `{1 :integer, 1.0 :double}` has count 2.
- `manifest/edn-carryable?` returns true.
- `manifest/manifest` preserves both keys.
- `manifest/script-html` emits successfully.
- JVM `read-manifest` round-trips equal, showing why the same-host suite cannot see it.

A temporary CLJS audit test then passed that exact JVM-emitted body to the shipped `manifest/read-manifest`. Focused real runner result: **26 tests / 280 assertions, exactly 1 failure, 0 errors**. The failure reported the existing structured error with `:invalid :unreadable` and reason `Map literal contains duplicate key: 1`. The probe was removed and the test file restored byte-identical (blob `1a77745dd549bb35ad0b6021c48bd04ffef5ddb3`).

## Bounded correction

Keep the current scalar numeric subset and existing error id. Before a JVM manifest is admitted/emitted, reject any map whose distinct keys or set whose distinct elements collapse to one CLJS identity after the supported numeric projection, including nested collections. Name the offending path/pair so the programmer can change one key deliberately. Preserve ordinary single numeric keys/elements and all existing scalar/vector/list behavior.

Pin the crossing with the shipped readers using exact bytes for at least `{1 …, 1.0 …}` and `#{1 1.0}`, plus a signed-zero arm if CLJS treats `0` and `-0.0` identically. Each fixture needs a matching red-before tooth. Do not add a codec, tagged-reader registry, general schema framework, or blanket ban on numeric keys.

## Same-contract wording rider

The new Spec 011 prose says only **finite doubles** ride, while `wire-number?`, the PR/source-bead rationale, and an executable JVM probe admit `##Inf` and `##-Inf` (only NaN is rejected). Resolve this in the same narrow change. Minimal recommendation: retain infinities because EDN round-trips them exactly, change the spec phrase to “doubles other than NaN,” and pin ±Infinity in the admitted corpus. If infinities are intentionally forbidden, make the predicate and both-host tests say so instead.

## Dedupe

Fresh authoritative census: 55 live OPEN/IN_PROGRESS Beads including this audit tracker. Full-field searches for numeric/mixed map keys, duplicate-key reader errors, numeric/set collisions, and cross-host map keys found no owner. Closed rf2-v4foc is the source fix this counterexample escapes; this is a bounded follow-up, not a duplicate.
acceptance_criteria:
- A manifest that the JVM accepts for emission cannot fail or change cardinality on CLJS because distinct numeric map keys or set elements collapse under CLJS identity.
- Nested map/set collisions are rejected before emission under the existing `:rf.error/root-manifest-invalid`, with useful path/pair attribution; non-colliding numeric keys/elements remain accepted.
- Exact JVM-emitted bytes are read by the shipped CLJS reader in map, set, and signed-zero fixtures; matching mutations prove each fixture can red.
- Spec 011 and `wire-number?` agree on ±Infinity, with executable accepted/rejected pins on both hosts.
- No numeric codec, tagged-reader registry, schema framework, blanket numeric-key ban, or new error id is introduced.
- Focused SSR JVM and CLJS gates pass with non-zero plausible counts.
notes:
PR #6489 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6489). Whole-manifest collision walk at the emission gate (script-html); reuses existing :rf.error/root-manifest-invalid id (no new id, no codec/schema framework). Rejects distinct numeric map keys / set elements that collapse to one browser double, any nesting depth, naming path+collapses+browser-number. Map/set/signed-zero arms; signed-zero confirmed real ((= 0 -0.0) true on CLJS). Spec 011 rider resolved: 'finite doubles' -> 'every double except NaN', +/-Inf admitted+pinned both hosts. Gates: SSR JVM 502t/2393a 0/0; CLJS 10314t/50867a 0/0 (warm; cold-run 5 fails were test-quiet subprocess-spawn flake, disjoint from diff); check_doc_slugs 44 self-tests + no broken links; mkdocs --strict ok. Core/Spec009 gate skipped (no catalogue touch). Do NOT merge.
AUDIT RESIDUAL FROM PR #6489 (2026-07-19 AUSEST): reopened. The shipped numeric-collision function groups only directly numeric sibling keys/elements. It recurses into each composite independently, so it misses two JVM-distinct composite identities that become equal after their numeric leaves project to CLJS doubles. Exact witness: {[1] :integer-vector [1.0] :double-vector} has JVM count 2, is edn-carryable?, and script-html emits it. Real CLJS reports (= [1] [1.0]) true and the shipped reader primitive rejects the emitted inner map: Map literal contains duplicate key: [1]. Same class applies to set elements and map/list composite identities. This violates this Bead's first acceptance criterion and Spec 011's promise about any map key/set element collapsing under browser numeric identity. Bounded correction: recursively project each complete key/element into browser equality semantics before sibling comparison; add exact vector-key and vector-set-element byte fixtures plus resolving mutations. Do not add a general codec/schema framework or blanket composite-key ban. Found by audit tracker rf2-uqd7o.
PR #6510 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6510). Extends #6489's emission-gate collision walk to COMPOSITE siblings at arbitrary depth. Residual: #6489's collapse grouped only directly-numeric siblings (filter number? + group-by browser-number), so {[1] .. [1.0] ..} (JVM count 2, edn-carryable?, emitted) escaped though the browser reads both keys as [1.0] and the CLJS reader rejects the dup. Fix: new browser-project folds a WHOLE key/element to browser numeric-equality at any depth; collapse groups siblings by browser-project. numeric-collision cond (recursion + path) unchanged -> #6489 direct cases preserved. Reused :rf.error/root-manifest-invalid + :path/:collapses/:browser-number; NO codec/registry/schema/id. Spec 011 untouched (already carries +/-Inf 'every double except NaN' wording + 'any nesting depth' clause). Red-before confirmed executably (pre-fix grouping returns nil/accepts; new returns colliding members/rejects). Tests: composite vector-key + vector-set byte fixtures (JVM pins tokens + count-2; CLJS reader rejects exact bytes as dup); rejection arms with edn-carryable? levers + full path evidence incl deep map->vector->map->set path [:props :xs 0 :k]; resolving composite mutations. Gates: SSR JVM 506t/2437a 0/0; CLJS 10326t/50920a 0/0; mkdocs --strict OK. Do NOT merge.
close_reason: shipped #6510

title: Real Shadow warm-watch fixture + removed/renamed saved-source :build-sources delta (rf2-4vm19 Arm 2)

title: Reload-producer tag fallback can replace a same-tagged foreign owner
description:
## Defect

PR #6434 says reload-source producer ownership is "object identity, never the tag" and promises that a co-loaded bundle's same-tagged entry is never retired. The implementation still falls back to tag ownership whenever its remembered object is absent:

```clojure
(let [prev @owned-producer
      mine (if prev (.indexOf arr prev) -1)
      i    (if (neg? mine) (tagged-producer-index arr build-id) mine)]
  ... (aset arr i f))
```

If this copy's exact predecessor is no longer on the shared `SHADOW_NS_RESET` array, the first callback carrying the same build tag is treated as ours and replaced. That callback may belong to another co-loaded bundle—the precise case the new comments and test say only identity can distinguish. A newly loaded namespace copy with a fresh ownership cell has the same ambiguity during tag adoption.

## Deterministic proof

A temporary CLJS audit test removed this copy's exact standing producer, inserted a foreign callback tagged with `(current-build-id)`, and called `install-reload-source-producer!`. The focused real `:node-test-ui` gate failed exactly the ownership assertion: the foreign object was gone after reinstall (`Ran 872 tests containing 4660 assertions; 1 failure, 0 errors`). Compilation was clean (358 files, 219 compiled, 0 warnings). Cleanup restored the global array and installer; the diagnostic was removed byte-identical (`rules_cljs_test.cljc` blob `2eac63ac8071da484a551c01d1dc4327e8d9d80e`).

## Consequence

The self-upgrade path can silently evict a co-loaded producer and route its source-reset evidence through this copy instead. It violates #6434/rf2-mp6fz's load-bearing acceptance rule that foreign callbacks are preserved byte-for-byte/in order and undercuts the stated reason for introducing `owned-producer`.

## Bounded resolution

Resolve this with rf2-4vm19's already-open topology ruling, not a general callback registry. If same-tag co-loaded copies are supported, an absent identity must never authorize tag-based replacement; use an unambiguous per-copy proof or fail/append without mutating the foreign object, while retaining the one-time predecessor migration that can actually be proven. If one-build-per-shared-runtime is the chosen boundary, enforce/document it and retire the same-tag-foreign preservation claim/test rather than claiming identity isolation the code cannot provide.

## Dedupe

Fresh census: 53 live open/in-progress Beads. Exact all-field searches for owned-producer, self-upgrading producer, tagged-producer-index, same-tagged/same tag, foreign callback/entry, producer install, and tag fallback found no owner. `rf2-4vm19` is in progress and locked; it owns the broader co-loaded-build topology ruling, not this closed rf2-mp6fz tag-fallback regression, so this is a bounded follow-up rather than an edit to that Bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- When the exact object recorded in `owned-producer` is absent, reinstall never replaces, removes, reorders, or invokes a same-tagged object owned by another bundle.
- The first-upgrade path from the immediately preceding tagged producer is either proven unambiguous or explicitly governed by the chosen one-build-per-shared-runtime boundary; no tag is described as identity proof when it is not.
- The #6434 stale-placeholder-to-current-build migration remains correct and repeated reloads leave exactly the supported producer cardinality with current behavior.
- A sequence fixture covers: owned predecessor present -> replace own; owned predecessor absent + foreign same-tag present -> preserve foreign; recover/reinstall -> invariant still holds. Each arm has a matching mutation tooth.
- The resolution is consistent with rf2-4vm19's co-loaded topology disposition and does not add a general callback registry, public API, legacy munged-name sniffer, or production machinery.
- Focused UI CLJS/JVM gates and advanced/browser production-elision gates remain green with non-zero counts.
notes:
⚠️ BLOCKED on #6440 — SAME FILE. Dispatch only after #6440 (rf2-vxgfnd.143 runtime arm) MERGES. Verify: git log --oneline --grep=rf2-vxgfnd.143 origin/main.
This bead's fix is in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/rules.cljc — the exact file #6440 is modifying (its custom-element conflict law + owner provenance). Two workers on one file = merge conflict. Sequence.
THE DEFECT (verified present in the #6434-shipped code): the reload-source producer ownership fix promised 'object identity, never the tag', but still falls back to tagged-producer-index when its remembered object (@owned-producer) is absent from the shared SHADOW_NS_RESET array. In that fallback the first callback carrying the same build tag is treated as ours and replaced — which may belong to another co-loaded bundle, the precise case #6434's own comments and test say only identity can distinguish. A newly loaded ns copy with a fresh ownership cell has the same ambiguity during tag adoption. So #6434 closed the general case but left the identity-absent fallback still tag-based. ⚠️ This is a follow-up to work merged tonight (#6434, rf2-mp6fz) — the fix is real but incomplete, not wrong.
SHIPPED in PR #6450 (branch worker/rules-cluster-ymfix), commit 4ccc93cd79. FIX: install-reload-source-producer! ownership is now OBJECT IDENTITY ONLY — the tagged-producer-index fallback is removed (and the now-uncalled helper deleted). When @owned-producer is absent from the shared SHADOW_NS_RESET array the install APPENDS its own producer instead of adopting the first same-tagged entry; an absent predecessor is no longer authority to replace anything. The producer tag stays, re-documented as PROVENANCE, not the ownership lever. RED-BEFORE (own lever, observable outcome not exception): new fixture producer-install-appends-rather-than-adopting-a-same-tagged-foreign removes this copy's standing producer from the array, pushes a foreign callback tagged (current-build-id), re-installs — unfixed code EVICTED the foreign object (888 tests, 1 failure); fixed code preserves it (888 tests, 0 failures). The red run is the mutation tooth, so the assertion is not vacuous. #6434's stale-placeholder migration is unaffected (it goes by identity, predecessor IS on the array). DEV-ONLY + UNREACHABLE in production (not merely unguarded): the whole install already sits inside (when ^boolean js/goog.DEBUG ...), owned-producer gated identically; this is a code REMOVAL inside that existing gate — no new gate, no always-on behaviour. Confirmed causally by test:browser-prod-elision (custom_element_reload_elision_prod_test.cljs runs INSIDE the :advanced bundle asserting this exact fn is inert). No new error-id, no Spec 009 row. Gates: ui JVM 977/0F, test:cljs 10239/50574/0F, test:elision PASS 60/60 absent, test:browser-prod-elision PASS 108/0F.

title: CLJS trace listeners violate the post-drain settled-state contract
description:
## Defect

PR #6365 makes Spec 009's listener timing a cross-platform contract: internal drain-owned trace emits are delivered at the post-drain boundary, listeners never observe partially settled state, and listener side effects cannot influence the drain that produced the event. The shipped CLJS path does the opposite. `re-frame.trace.tooling/call-with-deferred-fanout` is explicitly `:cljs (f)`, and `deliver-to-tooling!` therefore invokes the raw trace listener inline while the frame's drain is active.

## Deterministic proof

A temporary assertion was added to the already-live `re-frame.trace-listener-nested-emission-order-cljs-test` namespace. A `:rf.event/run-start` listener read the frame app-db while an event was about to set a `::settled?` marker. Under the promised post-drain contract the listener must see `true`; CLJS observed `nil`, while a control immediately after `dispatch-sync` saw `true`. The consolidated Node gate ran 10,220 tests / 50,497 assertions and failed on exactly that settled-state assertion: 1 failure, 0 errors. The probe was removed byte-identical (`a0d4b08aacaae0852656db52fc9e7d8e32531ca9`).

## Consequence

Browser tools and programmer-authored listeners see a different temporal API from JVM users: they can observe partially settled state and can still alter the in-flight drain. This contradicts the new Spec 009 contract and the PR's JVM-only three-arm test claim that observable outcomes are identical across platforms. Calling inline delivery an implementation detail does not repair a public guarantee that the listener observes only settled state.

## Bounded repair

Give CLJS the same post-drain delivery boundary with a small same-thread pending queue at the existing private trace/drain seam. CLJS needs no monitor or ThreadLocal, but it does need to append drain-owned events and flush them after the lock is released. Preserve bundle isolation and production elision; do not introduce a general scheduler, async delivery loop, public synchronization API, or compatibility layer. If uniform semantics are deliberately rejected, Spec 009 and the JVM-only test must instead stop promising post-drain settled-state behavior on every platform—but that is the less ergonomic outcome.
acceptance_criteria:
- The same observable test runs on JVM and CLJS: a drain-owned `:rf.event/run-start` listener sees the event's settled app-db, and listener mutation is equivalent to the same mutation immediately after `dispatch-sync`.
- CLJS listener callbacks are not invoked until the enclosing drain has released its `:drain-lock`; every event still arrives exactly once, in emission order, before dispatch/drain returns.
- Existing nested outer-before-inner ordering, synchronous nested emit completion, append-time listener snapshots, continuation suppression, registration replacement, and listener exception isolation stay green on both hosts.
- Production/elision and bundle-isolation gates prove no dev-only tooling registry or deferral machinery leaks into advanced bundles.
- The repair stays within the existing private trace/drain seam; no monitor analogue, general scheduler, background loop, or new public API is added.

title: Always-on axis has no production-build evidence: conformance is synthetic + 26/43 categories unpinned
description:
## Cause (one, two faces)

Nothing binds a Spec 009 `always-on` catalogue row to evidence that its REAL emit site survives `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false`. This is the structural reason rf2-2hkfy (#6376) shipped and the reason the class can recur silently.

**Face 1 — the conformance gate is synthetic.**
`implementation/core/test/re_frame/always_on_axis_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` `drive-category!` (~line 294) calls `error-emit/dispatch-on-error!` / `dispatch-error-record!` / `dispatch-frame-teardown-report!` DIRECTLY with a fabricated payload. It proves the LISTENER REGISTRY fans out. It never touches the emit site. Its JVM companion (`error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj`) then pins the parsed catalogue always-on set EQUAL to that literal. So a category can be catalogued always-on, be in the literal, pass both gates — and still have a `goog.DEBUG`-gated (or entirely diagnostic) real emit site. That is exactly the state `:rf.error/unsupported-scroll-strategy` was in before #6376.

**Face 2 — coverage.** Only 17 of the 43 always-on categories are named in ANY `*_prod_test.cljs` (the `:browser-test-prod-elision` build, `{goog.DEBUG false}`). 26 have no production-build assertion at all. The three that do exist (`routing_scroll_always_on_`, `teardown_always_on_`, `frame_ops_always_on_`) were each added REACTIVELY by a fix for a defect of this class.

## Audit result that motivates this (rf2-hk3eb)

All 43 always-on rows were walked to their emit sites. **Zero are currently gated** — no direction-A defect exists on main today. The finding is that nothing WOULD CATCH the next one.

## Important correction to the audit framing

Auditing the catalogue `Channel` column alone could NOT have caught rf2-2hkfy. At `aa27a76f1a~1` the catalogue row for `:rf.error/unsupported-scroll-strategy` correctly read `diagnostic`; the false "ALWAYS-ON" claim lived in the `scroll-fx-handler` docstring and Spec 012 prose. Any recurrence-prevention must key off the EMIT SITE + prose claims, not the Channel column.

## Uncovered categories (no prod-elision assertion)

coeffect-exception, interceptor-exception, machine-action-exception, read-after-release, observation-port-version-mismatch, observation-retry-exhausted, sub-input-fn-exception, sub-input-fn-bad-return, drain-depth-exceeded, no-frame-context, bad-frame-provider-arg, hydration-frame-id-mismatch, malformed-hydration-payload, reg-event-db-removed, reg-event-fx-removed, reg-event-ctx-removed, missing-required-cofx, inject-cofx-removed, machine-spawn-unregistered-type, frame-preflight-evidence-mismatch, root-boot-failed (CLJS-reachable) + sanitised-on-projection, ssr-head-resolution-failed, ssr-render-failed, ssr-streaming-writer-failed, ssr-ring-error-view-failed (JVM/SSR — goog.DEBUG DCE does not apply; the JVM `re-frame.debug` runtime gate does).

## NEEDS A RULING, not a determination

Scope is a judgment call and 26 new prod-elision tests is plausibly gold-plating (the parent bead explicitly rejects new machinery). Options:
  (a) Make `drive-category!` non-synthetic where cheap — drive through the real emit site — so the EXISTING gate gains teeth without new suites.
  (b) Add prod assertions only for the CLJS-reachable uncovered set (~21).
  (c) Accept the gap; treat per-surface assertions as the fix-time obligation of the next defect (status quo).
Mike to rule.

## Provenance
Filed by the rf2-hk3eb audit. Spec 009 was IN FLIGHT on PR #6365 when read; findings are anchored to row content + emit sites, not line numbers. No tracked file changed by the audit.
notes:
Discovered-from rf2-hk3eb (the goog.DEBUG always-on audit). Verified emit-site walk covered 43/43 always-on rows (not sampled). Cross-ref rf2-2hkfy #6376, rf2-5pr75 #6352, rf2-vxgfnd.299 #6416.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 15:04 AUSEST)

RULING: option (c), refined with a change-time evidence ratchet. Accept the gap; no retroactive production-test quota for the 26 uncovered categories; no conformance-driver rework; no source analyser, evidence registry, or new :advanced build infrastructure. The rf2-hk3eb clean 43/43 emit-site walk at origin/main 3947ac610a is the point-in-time baseline.

THE STANDING RULE (four change-time obligations, to be written into TESTING.md):
1. Existing 43 always-on categories: no backfill. The exhaustive clean audit is the baseline.
2. New or promoted always-on category: the SAME change must (i) drive the real emit site in a dev-build test asserting the `:errors` listener (channels are separate registries, so this catches the wrong-channel shape), and (ii) prove the production posture — a real `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false` assertion for a CLJS-reachable site, or a debug-disabled JVM integration assertion for a JVM-only site. Reuse an existing prod-elision fixture when it already exercises the branch; watch the shared prod-elision bundle's composition premises (see routing_scroll_always_on_elision_prod_test.cljs docstring) when adding artefact requires.
3. Refactor of an existing always-on emit site: new production proof only when the change moves or wraps the call chain across a compile-time/debug gate or changes which always-on seam is reached; payload-only/wording/unrelated refactors incur none. The PR must state the always-on call is not transitively inside a goog.DEBUG-derived gate; reviewer checks the gate chain per the rf2-hk3eb method.
4. Production-silence bug fix: always carries the focused per-surface `*_elision_prod_test.cljs` regression pin (the rf2-2hkfy scroll / teardown / frame-ops precedent).

WHERE IT GETS WRITTEN: TESTING.md, under "Test authoring policy" (repo root; NOT hot-zone, parallel-safe). An optional one-line cross-reference from spec/009-Instrumentation.md IS hot-zone — if the implementer adds it, sequence that PR per CLAUDE.md hot-zone rules; it is not required.

SYNTHETIC DRIVER / CONFORMANCE SUITE: `drive-category!` in always_on_axis_conformance_cljs_test.cljc stays synthetic — it pins the listener fan-out, which is its job. Its self-description ("intentionally NOT a re-derivation of each real emit SITE") is accurate and stays; a cross-ref comment pointing at the TESTING.md rule is welcome but optional.

DEFERRED WORK: revisit blanket production-build proof at API-freeze / external-alpha prep, alongside the facade-export audit — when real production consumers exist to protect. Revisit earlier only if a defect of this class gets past the ratchet.

CONSISTENCY vs rf2-ckyfh (RETAIN-AND-PROVE): there, proof was nearly free via the existing corpus/build and caught the real failure shape; here, blanket proof costs ~2-4k speculative test lines plus shared-bundle premise risk and cannot catch the next arrival (which comes with new code) — so accept-and-document, placing proof at the change-time moments where it becomes cheap and mechanical.

RECOMMENDATIONS WEIGHED: both dossier recommendations converged on (c); I adopted the Codex refinement (graduation-time production-posture proof) over the original's reviewer-statement-only form because graduation is precisely when the fixture is cheapest and it is the only mechanical witness for the goog.DEBUG-fold shape; the original's reviewer gate-chain check is retained in rule 3. Load-bearing claims spot-checked before ruling: trace/emit-error! (trace.cljc:790) has no path into the error-emit listener registry; the driver at line 294 is synthetic as described; prod-elision census (33 *_elision_prod_test.cljs incl. the three reactive always-on suites) consistent with 17/43 named.

IMPLEMENTATION SCOPE: one PR editing TESTING.md only (plus the optional sequenced spec/009 cross-ref). No test or src changes required. Close rf2-clgot when the TESTING.md standing rule lands. This bead is authoritative over any earlier briefing.
PR #6443 (worker/clgot-ratchet): TESTING.md standing rule landed as four change-time obligations under Test authoring policy. TESTING.md only; no test/src/driver changes; drive-category! stays synthetic; optional spec/009 cross-ref skipped (hot-zone, contended by #6440 + emit-ui-tree-97). Doc gates green (mkdocs --strict exit 0, check_doc_slugs exit 0). Close on merge per DECISION.

title: Resolve the ownerless G-7 equivalence contract and retire the stale G-16-open row
description:

EP-0034 still says the broad S1-S3 G-7 dev↔prod equivalence matrix over generated shapes has no test. The S4 conformance profile says this debt keeps its "existing named-open owner", but a fresh census of all 61 live Beads plus exact G-7/dev-prod/equivalence searches finds no such owner. Meanwhile rf2-vxgfnd.95.10's close reason says G-7 was certified and S3/S4 are declared conforming, so a programmer or agent cannot tell whether the broad matrix is required, deliberately deferred, or no longer part of conformance.

Reconcile the contract with a bounded, causal choice: either (a) retain G-7's broad S1-S3 equivalence requirement and give it one concrete owner/proof using representative debug-sensitive shapes, pairwise/high-risk capability combinations, and a real mutation tooth, or (b) explicitly narrow G-7 by operator ruling to the proven production-absence + S4-shape arms. Do not build a full powerset, a new test framework, or timing machinery.

The same exact roster also still calls G-16's "manifest slot sites present" arm open, but that arm ships and is directly pinned: analyzer site indexing (`analyze_accept_cljs_test.cljc`), the public `:render-slots` projection (`tool_cljs_test.cljc`), and rf2-ri0k6n's closed acceptance all cover it. Remove that stale open claim while touching the roster. Leave G-14 and future-stage gates outside this bead.

If the broad matrix is retained, a bounded real dev-vs-advanced comparison covers representative S1-S3 debug-sensitive shapes and has a mutation-discriminating control; if narrowed, an explicit ruling records why the proven arms are sufficient. G-16 manifest-slot evidence is no longer listed as open and existing focused proof remains green. No full powerset, new harness/framework, G-14 work, or unrelated gate sweep.
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 14:58 AUSEST)

RULING: G-7 is RETAINED as a bounded dev<->prod correctness gate — arm (a), in the Codex two-layer refinement, staged proportionately. Narrowing (arm b) is REJECTED: the proof vehicle already exists end-to-end, and the unwatched class is real (rf2-vxgfnd.253 records a production-only wrapper-selection bug that dev masked). The original row's "per generated shape + pairwise capabilities + high-risk triples" wording is also rejected — it is unowned combinatorics; the contract below is derived from the code that actually exists.

- Mechanism: the `parity-embed` macro (implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/parity_embed.clj) expands at compile time regardless of optimization level, embedding the JVM emitter's normalized truth for all 43 corpus cases (parity_fixtures.cljc, 28 views incl. the S4 presence/custom-element rows). - Mutation tooth: (1) assert the debug regime is off in-bundle (goog.DEBUG / interop debug-enabled? is false) so the test cannot silently run in the wrong regime; (2) one non-vacuity control in the binding_plan "advanced-build-really-renames" pattern; (3) demonstrated once during development: a deliberate prod-arm mutation (e.g. break defaults application in the direct-memo arm) goes red HERE while the dev corpus stays green.

Layer 2 — production wrapper specialization (ONE dedicated S6 leaf, filed under epic rf2-vxgfnd.98; mayor files it; do not start before stage entry):

Known gaps today: advanced presence retention/removal and custom-element property application (the only advanced custom-element test proves registration bookkeeping, not DOM property application).

title: BUG: debug call-site stamping inserts a pre-call await in CLJS async contexts
description:
## Finding

PR #6432's router ruling premise is disproved. `dispatch-sync!` itself does not yield. The apparent mounted-path yield is introduced by the CLJS compiler around the public macro's DEBUG call-site stamp when the call appears inside an async context (the exact fixture uses `cljs.test/async`).

In the generated `:browser-test` bundle, each `rf/dispatch-sync` in the async test compiles in this order:

1. enter the `re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?` branch;
2. `await` an async IIFE that constructs the `source-coords/coords-form` (`cond->`) map;
3. only then invoke `re-frame.core.dispatch-sync-impl`.

The first call therefore arms the UI flush. The compiler-generated `await` before the second call yields to the microtask queue, which flushes the first mark; then the second dispatch runs. That exactly produces the measured revision sequence `0 -> 1 -> 2` and makes a plain control microtask run between begin/end markers. The captured flush stack correctly terminates at the microtask closure because it runs at the compiler-inserted await, not inside the router.

Two controls distinguish the cause:

- the same call-site `cond->` emitted by the non-async `mount-probe!` helper compiles as an ordinary synchronous IIFE with no `await`;
- the DEBUG-false branch calls `dispatch-sync-impl` directly with no stamp or await.

So the real axis is DEBUG call-site macro expansion inside a CLJS async context, not mounted React versus headless execution. This is a behavior defect: a public API documented and named as synchronous must not acquire a hidden pre-call yield merely because source coordinates are enabled. The same `call-site-form` feeds `dispatch`, `dispatch-sync`, and `subscribe`; at minimum, every synchronously-observable member of that family must retain its ordinary evaluation order.

## Required correction

Make the call-site coordinate emission literal/no-yield in async CLJS contexts while preserving dev coordinates and advanced-production elision. Correct the #6432 scheduler/test prose that attributes the yield to `dispatch-sync!`; then reconcile Spec 006 and the core glossary with the now-proven same-stack behavior rather than asking for a router design ruling.

Keep this bounded to the call-site stamping seam and the directly false contract prose. No router scheduler or new async abstraction is required.
acceptance_criteria:
- An executable CLJS async-context fixture proves two back-to-back `rf/dispatch-sync` macro calls remain synchronous: a microtask queued before the second call cannot run until both calls return, and the two same-stack drains share the pending render batch.
- Generated dev JS proves call-site coordinate construction introduces no `await` before `dispatch-sync-impl`; call-site coordinates are still captured and usable.
- The adjacent `dispatch`/`subscribe` call-site family is checked for the same hidden-yield mechanism and fixed through the shared seam where applicable.
- Existing `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false` call-site/elision sentinels remain green.
- `reactive.cljc`, the DOM fixture prose, Spec 006, and the core glossary state the verified contract without the false mounted-path/router-yield attribution.
- A causal pre-fix or mutation run reds the async ordering assertion, and the final focused browser/core gates pass with non-zero counts.
notes:
Codex PR-audit correction, 2026-07-19: inspected all 58 live Beads before updating; this existing open ruling Bead is the exact owner, so no duplicate was created. Independent temporary browser probe reproduced #6432's `[0 0 1]` post-call revisions, then generated-JS inspection located the two explicit `await (async function(){...coords...})()` expressions immediately before the two `dispatch_sync_impl` invocations. The non-async `mount_probe_BANG_` control contains the same coord-building IIFE without async/await. Temporary source probe was removed byte-identical (working-tree blob equals HEAD).
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 16:14 AUSEST)

RULING — Option A, ratified in full. The #6432 (rf2-kahkr) contract retraction is REVERSED; its premise is disproved. `dispatch-sync!` never yielded: the measured mid-call flush (revision 0 -> 1 -> 2, control microtask running "mid-call") was the DEBUG call-site stamp — `coords-form`'s runtime `cond->` lowering to an `await (async function(){...})()` when the call sits inside a CLJS async context. The yield was instrumentation, not the router.

RESTORED CONTRACT: `dispatch-sync!` and the synchronously-observable call-site family (`dispatch`, `dispatch-sync`, `subscribe`) are same-stack synchronous in EVERY build, dev included. Two back-to-back `dispatch-sync!` calls in one JavaScript stack render once, not twice — this remains a theorem of the four render-batch guarantees ("in one JavaScript stack" does the conditioning), not a promotion of guarantee 3's MAY-share permission into a general rule.

PINNED PRINCIPLE (standing, binds all future macro emission): framework instrumentation must be evaluation-order-transparent. A call-site macro expansion may splice ONLY yield-free expression forms (compile-time literals and plain calls) into the caller's context; any dynamic-scope establishment happens inside the callee's own function body, where it can never compile as an awaited async IIFE.

FIX SHAPE (for the implementation agent):
1. `coords-form` / `prod-coords-form` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc, ~609/644) emit compile-time LITERAL coord maps — the `cond->` runs in Clojure at expansion time, absent keys simply omitted from the literal — harmonising with the machines path's existing literal emission (`form-coords` / walk pattern, same file ~1118). Dev coordinates, rf2-wvsxg `:file` absolutisation, and `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false` elision are all preserved unchanged; the literal stays inside the outermost debug gate.
2. `subscribe`'s `trace/with-call-site` scope push (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_call_site_macros.cljc, `build-subscribe-form` ~110) moves from the caller-side expansion into the impl seam (callee body), per the bead's existing ACs — its `binding` in an async caller is an independent awaited-IIFE yield source of the same class.
3. `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc` ~85-106: restore the unconditional back-to-back example under guarantee 3, delete the retraction, the false "dispatch-sync! ... yields" attribution, and the "deliberately left open" router marker. Correct the same false attribution in `implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/render_batch_host_checkpoint_dom_cljs_test.cljs` fixture prose.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE (verified 2026-07-19): spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md ~1774-1775 and docs/core/glossary.md ~205 were never retracted — both still state the unconditional back-to-back example — so NO hot-zone spec/glossary edit is needed; the worker verifies residue only. The router ruling #6432 parked here is DISSOLVED: no router, scheduler, drain-finalization, or new async abstraction. Registration-macro emission in async contexts stays out of scope (no synchronicity contract; file separately only if it bites). The bead's acceptance criteria stand as written (async fixture red-before/green-after, generated-JS no-await proof, family sweep through the shared seam, elision sentinels green).

BASIS: followed the dossier's Option A recommendation because the Codex audit's mechanics were re-verified against source (runtime `cond->` at the stamp site, caller-side `with-call-site`, untouched spec/glossary, in-repo literal precedent) and ratifying is the minimum-churn path to a coherent record — the spec already says the right thing; only one macro seam and one implementation docstring are wrong.
Implemented + PR #6454 (worker/callsite-sync-i3dvj), 2026-07-19. Option A delivered in full.

FIXES: (1) coords-form/prod-coords-form emit compile-time LITERAL coord maps (cond-> runs in Clojure at expansion time), harmonised with form-coords' machines-path precedent; dev coords, rf2-wvsxg :file absolutisation and :advanced+goog.DEBUG=false elision all preserved, literal stays inside the outermost debug gate. (2) subscribe's trace/with-call-site scope push moved caller-side -> callee body via the SHARED build-stamped-2 opts seam (the same :rf.trace/call-site key dispatch uses); re-frame.subs/subscribe establishes the scope in its own body, mirroring router/dispatch!. (3) reactive.cljc guarantee-3 example restored unconditionally + retraction/false-attribution/router-marker deleted; DOM fixture prose corrected.

EXTRA (required by 2): re-frame.core/stamp-opts — a yield-free TOLERANT merge. A plain (assoc opts ...) broke subscribe's pinned malformed-opts contract (non-map opts must fall to ambient and raise :rf.error/no-frame-context, not a raw ClassCastException); an inline (if (map? opts) ...) needs a let, which is precisely what lowers to an async IIFE. Generic by design so no reserved keyword literal enters a production-reachable body (elision probe stayed 60/60).

EVIDENCE: generated dev JS shows straight-line stamp_opts(...) + dispatch_sync_impl(...) with ZERO await keyword and zero async IIFE between the two calls (the only (async function(){ are the three cljs.test/async test bodies). Causal red-before: reverting ONLY coords-form to the runtime cond-> reds the new fixture at 4 assertions and reproduces #6432's exact symptom — log [:call-1 :control-microtask :call-2], revision 1->2 instead of 1, root-commits 2->3 instead of 1.

RESIDUE CHECK: spec/006 ~1774-1775 and docs/core/glossary.md ~205 both still state the unconditional example — NEITHER EDITED, confirmed. No router/scheduler/drain-finalization/async abstraction added.

INCIDENTAL: the timing shift exposed a latent under-specification in machine_view_unmount_teardown_mounted_dom_cljs_test — its PROCESS-GLOBAL trace listener counted every view's :rf.view/unmounted, catching an unrelated suite's deferred disposals (:rf.22ds-7/probe from frame_provider_context_dom_cljs_test, whose non-async teardown is never awaited). Scoped the count to the view under test.

OUT OF SCOPE (per ruling, NOT actioned): registration-macro emission — with-coords-form still splices a *pending-coords* binding into the caller's context, same lowering class, but registration macros carry no synchronicity contract. Not observed to bite; file separately if it does.

GATES (all foreground, unpiped, to completion): core JVM 2086/10184 PASS; test:cljs 10245/50593 PASS; test:browser 482/2707 PASS; test:elision production 60/60 absent + control 60/60 present PASS; test:browser-prod-elision 108/429 PASS; ui JVM 982/18738 PASS.
close_reason: shipped #6454 — Option A reversal: dispatch-sync! never yielded; the measured flush was the debug call-site stamp lowering to an awaited async IIFE. Generated-JS proof (flat literal, no await before dispatch_sync_impl), causal red-before reproducing #6432's exact symptom, guarantee 3 restored unconditionally as a theorem of guarantees 1/3/4 not a promoted permission. spec/006 + glossary verified never-retracted and untouched. Pinned principle: framework instrumentation must be evaluation-order-transparent. Also exposed and fixed a latent false-green — a process-global trace listener counting other namespaces' events (class filed as rf2-veyfp).

This leaf carries the residue — every item below verified ZERO occurrences in shipped 011 at the evidence baseline.

## Residue inventory (all of it, nothing else)

1. `emit-ui-tree` — the structural-tree -> HTML seam, with the `:rf.error/ssr-ui-tree-version-unsupported` version gate (amendment Pairs 1+2). This is the epic's open obligation (4).
