title: Make both Xray unchanged-sub disclosure controls operator-effective
description: PR #6069's data path is sound, but neither operator-facing disclosure contract is effective. The panel-local button installs a deferred React on-click that calls bare rf/dispatch. The facade reg-view delegates to reactive-panel without threading its lexically injected dispatcher, so after render scope unwinds the click emits rf.error/no-frame-context and leaves Xray state unchanged. The Settings view explicitly removed the promised Always show unchanged subs control while retaining its state slot; spec/021 and the source acceptance still promise a configured pin. Registry tests dispatch inside a manually bound :rf/xray frame, masking the click failure and proving only plumbing. No mounted test exercises the unchanged-section selectors, and the source-text singleton guard only matches dispatch immediately adjacent to an on-* attribute, missing this multiline callback.
acceptance_criteria: The panel-local button dispatches through the surrounding Xray instance's injected or captured frame-bound dispatcher; a real click emits no no-frame-context error, expands the memo-hit rows, and changes only that instance when two frame-scoped Xray panels are mounted. Settings visibly exposes the existing show-unchanged-subs setting and its pin expands the same disclosure according to spec/021; default remains collapsed and the local and configured axes compose intentionally. Mounted regression coverage uses real memo-hit rows and proves default collapsed, local click expanded, Settings pin expanded, and frame isolation. The narrow frame-singleton regression guard or equivalent causal test catches a deferred multiline bare dispatch without introducing a parser or new state machinery.
close_reason: shipped #6181 (merged)

title: Preserve concrete query identity in Xray skipped-sub disclosure
description: PR #6069 carries canonical rf.sub/skip evidence into the Reactive panel, but skipped-subs deduplicates and cross-excludes by the registered sub-id while the subscription cache and trace identify concrete instances by full query-v. In one epoch, if [:item/derived 1] recomputes and [:item/derived 2] memo-hits, project-record builds ran-ids containing :item/derived and suppresses the second instance's skip entirely. Multiple skipped parameterizations are likewise collapsed to the first. The view preserves neither distinction: it keys, test-ids, and labels rows only by sub-id even though each projected row already carries query-v. Xray can therefore claim that no concrete instance was skipped when one was. The canonical query vector is already present; no substrate or compatibility machinery is needed.
acceptance_criteria: Skipped-sub deduplication uses concrete query-v identity, so repeated evidence for the same concrete query is collapsed but distinct parameterizations remain distinct. A recomputed query excludes only a skip for that exact query, not every instance sharing its registration id. Rows display and key by the full query vector (with a small documented fallback only if canonical evidence genuinely lacks it), while source-coordinate lookup may continue using the registered id. A focused counterexample with one same-id recompute and a different same-id memo hit preserves and visibly disambiguates the skipped row; two same-id skipped queries both survive. Ordinary unparameterized behavior and recompute-vs-skip separation remain unchanged.

title: Make the same-root supersession browser proof ordinary and causally complete
description: PR #6067 was opened to satisfy the explicit no-act/no-flush browser arm of rf2-5ep117: two ordinary back-to-back ui/render! calls through the live pending-attempt supersession path. Its fixture instead wraps both renders in one React act batch and describes that manufactured batch as ordinary. More importantly, the assertions do not make A-side settlement observable: removing the call that aborts the old receipt still leaves B able to replace the pending slot, commit its shared frame, clear its own slot, render B, and satisfy every current assertion. The test therefore proves B wins under act but does not causally pin the superseded receipt's terminal settlement. It also never asserts the committed live-root entry has no pending-attempt. This is a bounded browser-proof gap, not evidence of a current runtime defect.
acceptance_criteria: A real-browser fixture performs two ordinary back-to-back same-root ui/render! calls without React act or an explicit render flush between them, and proves the natural uncommitted A-to-B window occurred. A owns an independently observable write (for example a disjoint frame omitted by B) whose exact receipt is terminally aborted by supersession, while the shared frame commits B with zero frame-preflight-evidence-mismatch diagnostics. The committed live-root entry has no pending-attempt and teardown clears root/plan residue. Mutating either the pre-#6060 superseding-receipt handoff or the old-receipt abort makes the fixture fail. Public runtime APIs remain unchanged.

title: Make the exceptional Form-3 subscription recipe instance-safe
description:
PR #6065's copy-pasteable exceptional Form-3 recipe is not safe for multiple instances. Every `live-gauge` mount adds and removes a watch on the cached reaction with the constant key `::feed`. Equal `(frame, query-v)` subscriptions share that reaction and increment its ref-count, so a second mount overwrites the first callback; unmounting either removes the remaining callback and leaves the surviving widget stale.

A current-runtime probe with two captured subscribes to the same query confirmed the shared reaction and produced `{:after-one {:same true, :a [], :b [1]}, :after-removing-one {:a [], :b [1]}}`. The existing Form-3 browser matrix proves ref-count balance but does not exercise two imperative watches. Related owner prose also still states lifecycle subscription reads are categorically unsupported, without naming this rare captured/add-watch/balanced-unsubscribe exception.

Repair the example, test, and directly authoritative owner prose together. This needs a per-mount watch key and precise exception wording, not a new runtime API.
acceptance_criteria:
- The recipe allocates and retains a unique watch key per component mount and uses that exact key in teardown.
- A real Form-3 browser test mounts two same-frame/same-query widgets, proves both receive updates, unmounts one and proves the survivor remains live, then restores the final cache/ref-count baseline.
- Teardown remains balanced under React StrictMode and cannot skip unsubscribe/widget cleanup if watch removal fails.
- Reagent-slim, Stateful Components, migration, and skill owners distinguish ordinary unowned lifecycle reads from the rare explicitly captured and balanced imperative exception without weakening the default guidance.

title: Dispose page-owned playground registrations on instant navigation
description:
PR #6064's page disposal fixes roots and frames but not registrations. `docs/tools/playground/sci/src/rf2_playground/sci.cljs` exposes process-global `reg-*` APIs directly, while `disposePage` only unmounts cached roots and destroys frames. Its comment relies on incoming cells overwriting colliding IDs, which does not protect a later page that dispatches or subscribes to an ID it did not itself register.

Reproduced on current production code: page 1 registered `:page1/stale`; after the real instant-navigation loader disposed the page, page 2 created a fresh frame and dispatched `[:page1/stale]` without re-registering it. The fresh frame received `{:leaked-registration true}` and reported no page error. This violates source Bead rf2-io9mdr's acceptance that navigation cannot reuse another cell's registrations. Current smoke registers incoming handlers before frame creation and therefore remains green.

Keep the repair bounded: give playground cells explicit page registration ownership and clear or restore page `(kind,id)` registrations during disposal, while preserving bundle/framework baseline registrations. Avoid a general registration subsystem redesign.
acceptance_criteria:
- Leaving a Core page removes or restores every registration authored by that page before the incoming page can run.
- Framework/bundle-init registrations that intentionally span pages remain intact.
- A production-bundle instant-navigation test proves a fresh page cannot dispatch/subscribe through an outgoing page-only ID, including when it never re-registers that ID.
- Existing root/frame isolation, cell-less navigation, repeated navigation, and framework-registration controls remain green.
close_reason: shipped #6170 (merged)

title: Make the capture-once retarget guard reject semantic reversals
description:
PR #6061 added a positive cross-owner drift check for the Form-3 capture-once provider-retarget invariant, but the current helper searches each entire document for independent vocabulary tokens. It does not require those tokens to state the locked-handle relationship or reject the opposite polarity.

Reproduced deterministically on current main by importing `_form3_capture_once_problems` and supplying an adopter owner that says "Capture-once automatically follows any provider change; it never goes stale" plus unrelated provider-A-to-B, remount, and recipe-pointer fragments, and a canonical owner that says capture automatically retargets/re-resolves plus an unrelated A-to-B example. The result was `[]`. A second independent mutation saying there is no need to remount also passed. Existing self-tests only delete expected tokens, so they prove vocabulary presence rather than semantic teeth.

The shipped FORM-3 and canonical migration prose are currently correct. Closed `rf2-aalo4n` introduced this guard; closed `rf2-6m5qb` repairs a different Form-3 lifecycle classifier. No live Bead owns this false green.

Keep the repair bounded: validate the capture-once retarget statement within its owning section/paragraph, including polarity and relation, without building a general Markdown or Clojure parser.
acceptance_criteria:
- In each owner, the capture-once/locked-handle statement is causally tied to a surviving provider A-to-B retarget: the handle stays on stale A and does not follow B.
- FORM-3's owning section also carries a supported remedy and the canonical-recipe pointer; unrelated tokens elsewhere cannot satisfy the invariant.
- Explicit semantic reversals such as "automatically retargets/re-resolves", "never goes stale", or "no need to remount" fail even when every positive vocabulary token remains elsewhere in the document.
- Adversarial self-tests mutate each live owner to the wrong polarity while preserving A/B/remount/pointer vocabulary and fail before the repair.
- Current correct prose, legal unrelated mentions, the migration guard self-test, and the live CI scan remain green.
- No general-purpose Markdown parser or new documentation abstraction is introduced.

title: Authenticate the superseding receipt controller before silent settlement
description: PR #6060 suppresses an old preflight receipt's revision mismatch when a later same-root receipt owns the exact current write. The suppression authenticates only the superseding receipt's inner write fields: `superseding-index` discards the receipt's outer `:root-id`, and `benign-supersession?` compares the write root/revision with the old write and current record. A deterministic current-main probe executed attempts A and B for `:root/owner`, changed only B's outer `:root-id` to `:root/foreign`, and aborted A with that tampered superseder. Result: zero `:rf.error/frame-preflight-evidence-mismatch` records while B remained owner-authoritative. Closed source Bead `rf2-5ep117` explicitly required foreign-root and stale-controller mismatches to remain dev-loud; its fixture changes both the outer controller and inner write, so it misses this split-envelope case. No live Bead owns the residual authority gap.
acceptance_criteria:
- Benign supersession authenticates the superseding receipt envelope: its controller/root identity must agree with the writes it presents and with the same current owner required by the suppression path.
- Changing only a legitimate superseding receipt's outer `:root-id` to a foreign controller emits exactly one typed `:rf.error/frame-preflight-evidence-mismatch` and never mutates the current record.
- Ordinary same-root A-to-B supersession remains silent, B remains authoritative, and disjoint old writes still abort normally.
- Foreign inner writes, missing/pruned records, reincarnation, uncovered revisions, and stale/non-supersession settlement remain dev-loud with no authority mutation.
- Keep the public API and single receipt/record ledger unchanged; add the smallest exact cross-host fixture rather than another authority subsystem.
- Focused UI JVM, node, and existing browser supersession gates remain green.

title: Make the Machines tutorial and executable companion one copy-pasteable program
description:
PR #6055 corrected the Machines tutorial to a three-total-attempt lockout policy and advertised it as copy-pasteable, but the complete teaching program still splits into incompatible and non-compiling copies.

First, `docs/machines/tutorial.md` Step 5 dereferences `draft-creds` in the Sign-in callback without defining it anywhere. Isolated compilation reports `Unable to resolve symbol: draft-creds in this context`, so the promised view cannot be copied into a real app.

Second, the linked executable companion says its `login-flow` is the same value lifted from the chapter, yet `examples/capabilities/machines/state_machine_walkthrough/core.cljc` still guards with `< attempts 3`, locks on the fourth submit, and its terminal branch runs only `:lock-account` rather than recording the final error. Its README/browser prose and `implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj` explicitly pin that fourth-attempt behavior. `docs/machines/inspecting-machines.md` likewise calls its `< 3` table the tutorial value. The #6055 docs test block is not version-executed, so the green executable test protects the contradictory program instead of the corrected tutorial.

This is the residual of closed `rf2-099755`, whose acceptance required the third failure and timeout to be executable-gated with the final count/error retained. Keep one small canonical teaching program and one focused existing example test; do not build a general docs code-block runner.
acceptance_criteria:
- The tutorial defines or explicitly accepts every value its view uses, including credential draft state; the complete namespace/view compiles and can be copied without an unresolved symbol.
- Tutorial, inspecting guide, executable walkthrough, README/browser prose, and CI test all use the same three-total-attempt policy.
- The third failure records count 3 and the terminal error before entering `:locked-out`; the third timeout follows the same counted policy and records its message.
- The runnable `.cljc` companion is the actual table exercised by the focused JVM/CLJS tests; no separate hand-copied policy remains falsely green.
- Happy-path submit/effect/session behavior and the low-friction tutorial progression remain intact.
- Focused Machines/example/docs gates pass.

title: Finish the cross-handbook compatibility-anchor contract
description:
PR #6055 closed `rf2-t0ituo` after restoring and gating only the Machines subset, although that source Bead's final acceptance explicitly required one shared compatibility-anchor mechanism across Machines, Async, API, and Routing. Current main still lacks all 14 non-Machines targets:

- Async: `docs/async/examples.md#async-http-examples`; `docs/async/http.md#managed-http-reference`, `#setup`; `docs/async/index.md#in-this-section`.
- API: `docs/api/re-frame.core.md#with-frame--with-new-frame`.
- Routing: `docs/routing/concepts.md#carrying-global-state-through-the-url`, `#converting-routes--urls-by-hand`, `#navigate-in-place-change-the-query-stay-on-the-route`, `#navigating-to-a-raw-url-string`, `#routing-the-url-is-a-sub`, `#what-happens-in-order`, `#when-a-loader-fails`; `docs/routing/examples.md#routing-examples`; `docs/routing/index.md#in-this-section`.

A current-main slug-index probe reports all 14 absent while `check_doc_slugs.py` stays green because its manifest and source-comment scan are hard-coded to Machines. The new `_check_machines_compat_anchors` also skips a missing inventoried page, so deleting/renaming a listed page plus updating ordinary links makes every external bookmark disappear without failing the gate.

Complete the already-chosen small inventory mechanism; do not introduce a new documentation framework or duplicate visible headings. No open/in-progress Bead owns the unfinished closed-source acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
- Restore every listed Async, API, and Routing fragment as an invisible stable compatibility anchor on its intended page, alongside the existing 20 Machines anchors.
- Replace the Machines-only manifest/check naming and path restriction with one bounded cross-handbook inventory covering all source-Bead targets.
- A listed page that is missing or renamed fails the compatibility check; fixture self-tests remain isolated through explicit fixture inputs rather than silently ignoring absent production pages.
- Relevant source-comment links across the covered handbooks are validated by the same mechanism without duplicating visible headings.
- Teeth tests prove deleting an individual anchor and deleting an inventoried page both fail.
- `check_doc_slugs.py`, its self-tests, and MkDocs strict build pass aside from independently owned unrelated baseline failures.

title: Make registration sequestering provenance-safe and truly no-op when absent
description:
PR #6056 corrected the API example to call `sequester-app-registration!` with registrar kind `:route`, but auditing the documented no-op contract exposed a runtime provenance bug in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc`.

`sequester-app-registration!` first looks up `[kind id provenance-ns]` in the source store, then unconditionally removes `(kind,id)` from the live registrar even when that provenance row is absent. On current main, registering `:audit/same` for `"app.b"` and sequestering the same kind/id for `"missing.app"` produces:
`{:returned nil, :registrar-after nil, :source-after <app.b descriptor>}`.

The call therefore returns nil yet clobbers another namespace's live registration while leaving its source-store row behind. This contradicts the API promise that a mismatched/absent row leaves registration unchanged and can make co-loaded test suites observe missing handlers or registrar/source-store divergence.

Closed `rf2-kcd05e` corrected only the documented kind/lease claims and explicitly requested a focused capture/removal test; no live Bead owns this behavior. Keep the repair at the existing helper rather than adding new isolation machinery.
acceptance_criteria:
- An absent `(kind,id,provenance-ns)` row returns nil and changes neither the live registrar nor the source store.
- A requested namespace cannot remove a live `(kind,id)` owned by a sibling provenance namespace; registrar and source-store authority remain coherent.
- A present matching row is captured, removed from both stores, returned, and reinstated by `reinstate-app-registration!` exactly once.
- Focused rows cover correct `:route` capture/removal/reinstatement, mismatched kind, absent provenance, and same-id sibling provenance.
- Existing namespace-tree sequester/reinstate and CLJ/CLJS test-support suites remain green.
close_reason: shipped #6160 (merged)

title: Finish SSR hydration, head-hash, and streaming truth reconciliation
description:
PR #6052 corrected three canonical SSR guides but left the same superseded contracts in sibling/canonical truth surfaces, and introduced two new copyability contradictions.

Current origin/main 0f2fc095321831ba1d30d8e7cbe0706784a8c2ae:
- docs/ssr/coming-from-nextjs.md:20 maps React hydrateRoot directly to state-only ssr/hydrate!; line 52 says hydrate! adopts DOM; line 64 promises automatic SPA head updates and the body's mismatch detector; line 70 promises inert-template fallbacks in the first painted byte.
- docs/ssr/streaming.md:68-70 says a non-JS client waits for the final payload and then hydrate! renders everything. Without JS, templates/chunks/payload remain inert and hydration never runs. A JS client that omits progressive installation is the case that may hydrate after the final payload.
- docs/ssr/head.md:57-59 tells a host to compare the active-head model map directly with the :rf/head-hash string. The host must compare (rf/render-tree-hash (rf/active-head frame-id)) with that hash.
- spec/011-SSR.md:673, 698, and 700 still say the client compares the head and replaces it, contradicting the same section's shipped-status text that the bundled runtime only carries/stashes the head hash and host attribution/reconciliation is external.
- spec/conformance/README.md:498 and spec/conformance/fixtures/ssr-head-emits.edn:53-57 still describe the reverted unified body+head render hash and reserve the already-shipped separate head hash for post-v1.

These are one bounded documentation-truth cluster completing closed rf2-fzza7u, rf2-ttiv2i, and rf2-bgbght acceptance. No live Bead owns it. Correct prose and one narrow drift assertion are sufficient; do not build a head manager, no-JS streaming runtime, or new compatibility layer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hydration prose consistently distinguishes ssr/hydrate! state installation/hash verification from substrate hydrateRoot DOM adoption; the Next.js mapping names both halves.
- Head prose consistently says body/head hashes are separate, the bundled runtime does no automatic head comparison/reconciliation, and a copyable host comparison hashes active-head before comparing with :rf/head-hash.
- Streaming prose distinguishes a JS client that skips streaming-install! from a non-JS client; it never claims non-JS can hydrate or paint inert boundary templates.
- Spec 011 default flow and mismatch section no longer claim bundled client head comparison/replacement while preserving the shipped optional head-hash channel and host-owned seam.
- The conformance index and fixture comments describe the current body-only :rf/render-hash plus separate optional :rf/head-hash, matching the fixture/runtime.
- Add the smallest focused truth/drift check needed to keep these canonical surfaces aligned; doc slugs and mkdocs --strict pass.
close_reason: shipped #6158 (merged): SSR contract reconcile

title: Correct Resources landing lease cleanup and mutation invalidation guidance
description:
PR #6050 corrected the Resources landing/concepts pages but introduced two copyable contract errors that remain on current main.

1. `docs/resources/index.md` now demonstrates `:rf.resource/ensure` with `:owner [:lease :article "hello"]` but never dispatches the matching `:rf.resource/release-owner`. Event-minted owners are durable liveness leases: the entry retains that owner in `:active-owners` and the reverse owner index, so normal stale/GC collection cannot reclaim it. The tutorial itself correctly warns that forgetting release is an orphaned-owner leak. The first landing example should not teach a permanently pinned cache entry.

2. `docs/resources/concepts.md` says final invalidation covers tags “the patch/populate did not already freshen.” Runtime `mutation_events.cljc` passes only `populated-ks` as the same-mutation exemption set, matching Spec 016's populate-only `:refetch-populated?` rule. A patched key is not exempt: the same mutation's invalidation may immediately mark it stale/refetch it. The page therefore overstates patch semantics precisely where it is teaching fixed arm order.

No later edit repairs either page, and no open/in-progress Bead owns these residuals. Closed `rf2-5gj77s`/PR #6050 is the incomplete source.
acceptance_criteria: The landing example either uses an ownerless one-shot ensure or shows the matching `:rf.resource/release-owner` at the consumer lifecycle boundary, with concise prose explaining event-minted lease ownership. The concepts page states the exact success order and accurately explains that only same-mutation populated keys are exempt from invalidation by default; patched keys can still be invalidated/refetched. Keep the example low-friction and copyable, preserve the passive-read/explicit-cause lesson, and pass documentation link/slug/build checks.
close_reason: shipped #6154 (merged, --admin: only-fail was inherited NAMING.md docs gate, 0 spec/003 touch, fixed on main by q75nc #6155)

title: Keep Xray bulk registration retryable after a partial install failure
description:
PR #6046 publishes `registered?` true at registry.cljs:186 before the roughly 900-line bulk registration/leaf-install block, while `installed-schema` is stamped only after the last installer at line 1079. If any registrar or leaf installer throws, the call exits with `{registered? true, installed-schema nil}`. On the next reload/call, the umbrella permanently skips the unfinished bulk install; the nil stamp is interpreted as schema 0, so migrate-schema! installs only the ViewCell bridge and then stamps schema 1. Every handler after the original failure point remains absent while the registry now claims to be current.

The initial error is correctly loud, but a transient install/programming failure followed by an HMR fix falsely succeeds into a silent partial Xray registry until a page reload. This is separate from schema deltas for changed handlers: it is failure atomicity of the fresh-install transition. Migration failures already leave the schema unstamped because the reset follows migrate-schema!.

Make the fresh-install sentinel retryable: use an explicit installing/installed state or catch bulk-install failure, roll the boolean back to false, and rethrow; publish registered/current only after every installer succeeds. Partial registrar writes can safely be replaced on retry. Add a throw-once mid-list leaf fixture proving the schema is not advanced after failure and a second call completes later handlers/topology instead of running bridge-only migration.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh bulk-install exception leaves registration retryable and schema unstamped; a second call replays/completes all leaf installers and reaches one coherent current schema; a throw-once regression proves no silent partial registry.
close_reason: shipped #6161 (merged)

title: Retire the captured failed-root reporter across re-entrant reclaim
description:
In PR #6048's same-drain recovery branch, client/drain-live-roots! proves the snapshot root exact, calls reclaim-consumed-container!, then retires reporter authority by re-reading the mutable live-roots registry with `(root-incarnation-of root-id)`. The sibling pre-existing-quarantine branch correctly uses the captured `(:root-incarnation current)` instead.

Container reclaim executes synchronous host code (`replaceChildren`), so a custom-element callback or the documented low-level/test seams can replace failed root A with same-id successor B during reclaim. The subsequent bare-id lookup returns B: retire-root-reporter! removes B from live-reporters, while release-root! root-id A correctly identity-fences and preserves B's live claim. B is then live without reporter authority, so its teardown may settle synchronously before React's cleanup; A's reporter token also remains strongly retained. This contradicts drain-live-roots!'s stated stale-snapshot rule that a bypass-installed replacement is not owned.

Use the exact incarnation captured in `current`, as the first recovery branch already does, and preferably share the reclaim → captured-token retirement → identity-fenced release sequence. Add a deterministic fixture whose replaceChildren callback installs and commits B, proving A is retired, B stays reporter-live, and B's claim survives.
acceptance_criteria: A same-id successor installed synchronously during container reclaim keeps its reporter authority and live-root claim; the failed predecessor's reporter is retired; recovery uses only the exact captured incarnation and is regression-tested.
close_reason: shipped #6151: reclaim captured-token reporter retirement

title: Migrate changed Xray handlers, not only newly added registrations
description:
PR #6046 introduces a registration schema seam, but its contract and migrate-schema! cover only newly added handlers. The same registered? umbrella also prevents changed handler implementations/topologies inside panel install! functions from being re-registered, so replacements require migration just as additions do.

Current main already demonstrates the gap. Commit f012c70e6f changed :rf.xray/reactive-data from two static inputs to four (adding :rf.xray/reactive-show-unchanged? and the Settings pin) inside reactive-panel-subs/install!, after #6046 shipped. registry/schema-version is still 1, and migrate-schema! only runs the `from < 1` ViewCell bridge clause. An already-running schema-1 process re-running register-xray-handlers! therefore no-ops both the umbrella and migration gates and retains the old two-input reaction body/topology. The newly shipped unchanged-sub disclosure does not respond to its panel or Settings axes until a full page reload.

Treat any gated registration addition OR replacement as a schema delta. Add the smallest version-2 migration that re-registers the changed Reactive-data surface (through its owning facade/seam), update the contract wording, and add a fixture that poses a schema-1 process with the predecessor two-input handler then proves current registration replaces it and invalidates the held cache. A lightweight governance test/check should make future gated registration edits name a schema bump or an explicit no-migration rationale.
acceptance_criteria: A live schema-1 process upgrades :rf.xray/reactive-data to the current four-input topology without a page reload; held cached subscriptions are invalidated; the registry schema contract covers handler additions and replacements with regression/governance proof.
close_reason: shipped #6161 (merged)

title: Reconcile flow single-store documentation and destroy conformance
description: PR #6045 correctly made `{frame-id {flow-id flow-map}}` the sole flow store and made replacement suppression per `(frame-id, flow-id)`, but active documentation and an executable conformance fixture still assert the retired frame-blind registrar model. `spec/002-Frames.md`, `spec/011-SSR.md`, `spec/Managed-Effects.md`, `spec/Runtime-Architecture.md`, `late_bind/directory.cljc`, and `frame.cljc` describe flow registrar ownership/re-pointing or registrar queries. `spec/conformance/fixtures/flow-frame-destroy-teardown.edn` normatively expects `:registrar-flow-slots-after #{:area}`, although the `:flow` registrar slot is reserved-empty. Spec 009 also states the process-global `(kind,id)` dedup rule without the flow exception. This contradicts authoritative Spec 013 and can make implementations/tests conform to two incompatible architectures.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sweep active specs, runtime architecture prose, late-bind descriptions, and source comments to state the sole per-frame flow store and `flows-snapshot`/`flow-meta-at` introspection contract.
- The destroy conformance fixture asserts the `:flow` registrar remains empty before/after teardown while per-frame flow and dirty-input rows are released correctly.
- Spec 009 explicitly scopes generic process-global dedup to registrar-backed kinds and documents flow replacement evidence as the per-frame exception.
- Search/conformance gates fail if retired flow registrar ownership/re-pointing language or nonempty flow registrar expectations return.
- No runtime behavior change or new parallel store is introduced.
close_reason: shipped #6208 (merged)

title: Keep nil owned spread-safe props absent and host-parity preserving
description: CLJS always materializes owned dynamic props in an object, including values normalized to nil, then `Object.assign`s that object over caller props. JVM `tree/element` drops nil owned `:norm`/`:dyn` values before layering caller props. Thus `(ui/spread-safe {:class owned-class} caller)` with `owned-class=nil` erases caller `className` on CLJS but preserves caller `:class` on JVM. The same divergence affects ordinary dynamic owned attrs such as `:title`. Reproduced from the emitted forms plus runtime merge: JVM tree produced `{:attrs {:class "caller"}}`; the CLJS merge produced `{className: null}`. This violates nil-means-absent normalization and host parity; class also fails its special composition contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- Nil-normalized owned dynamic props are absent before layering, on both hosts.
- A caller value survives when the corresponding owned dynamic value is nil; a nonnil owned value wins, and nonnil class values compose owned-first.
- Fix is shared/general for dynamic owned props rather than a class-only patch.
- Paired JVM-tree and CLJS-render tests cover dynamic `:class` and an ordinary attr (for example `:title`) at nil and nonnil controls.
- Existing static, event, style, custom-element, and controlled-input safe-spread behavior remains green.
close_reason: shipped #6209 (merged)

title: Preserve one authored evaluation order for spread-safe on CLJS and JVM
description: The authored form `(ui/spread-safe owned caller)` has divergent evaluation order. CLJS emits `spread-safe-props` with the caller object as its first argument, so it evaluates/guards caller before evaluating owned prop expressions. The JVM emitter evaluates the owned `:norm`/`:dyn`/event slots before its later `:spread-safe :caller` slot. A probe with `(mark! :owned)` and `(mark! :caller)` therefore observes caller-before-owned on CLJS and owned-before-caller on JVM; throwing or denied caller paths also evaluate different prefixes. Each expression runs once, but host behavior is not portable and the CLJS order contradicts the authored argument order.

- Both emitters force that order with single-evaluation temporaries; every owned and caller expression is evaluated exactly once.

title: Make destroyed-reason conformance fail closed on unresolved source and schema shapes
description:
The destroyed-reason conformance gate advertises exact, fails-closed channel/reason authority, but three unsupported shapes remain false-green.

1. Source census: `reason-key-values` extracts `:reason` only from literal maps. `enumerate-emit-sites` records an empty `:reasons` vector for `(assoc ... :reason :bogus)` or a local payload, and the validators merely `doseq` that vector. 2. Host coverage: `read-source-forms` calls the conditional reader once with its default JVM feature view. A different reason under a `#?(:cljs ...)` emitter branch is never inspected. The same source can therefore be valid on CLJ and publish an undocumented reason on CLJS while the JVM-only structural gate stays green.

Appending ``or `:bogus``` to the current ```:reason` is always `:parent-frame-destroyed` ``` sentence leaves the required prefix true, the tags substring true, and the known-other intersection empty. The normative row can therefore admit an unknown extra reason while its claimed exact check remains green.

- The structural census evaluates both CLJ and CLJS reader-conditional views; a reason that differs only in a `#?(:cljs ...)` branch fails.
- The lifecycle Spec-Schemas row is parsed with anchored captures for its exact tags reason slot and exact sole-reason statement; any additional unknown alternative fails.

Keep the surface ergonomic and preserve `rf/image`'s value-oriented semantics; do not add per-kind runtime normalizers or defensive ceremony.

title: Make the frame-lifecycle preflight guard genuinely per-path
description:
## Current defect

#6033 describes the frame-lifecycle guard as causal per host path, but `_client_call_order` is a whole-file substring scan and `_preflight_causal_problems` pools textual preflight credit across function boundaries. Current-main probes leave the checker green when the `render!*` preflight is reader-discarded (`#_`) or wrapped in `(when false ...)`; moving that token into `create-root*` and removing the real `render!*` call can also preserve the expected global token sequence while `render!*` reaches `.render` without preflight. The self-tests remove/reorder tokens but do not exercise dead calls or cross-function migration.

## Required correction

Prove each owned path rather than treating the file as one token stream: the two `mount*` branches, allocation-only `create-root*`, and preflight-before-render `render!*`. A small behavioral seam is preferred if it stays bounded; otherwise scope the lexical checks to the actual function bodies and state their limits honestly.
acceptance_criteria:
- Existing-root refresh and fresh one-shot mount independently prove preflight before their render; fresh mount additionally proves preflight before createRoot.
- `create-root*` remains allocation-only by design, and cannot donate a preflight token to `render!*`; `render!*` independently proves preflight before every render.
- Reader-discarded, dead-conditional, and cross-function-moved preflight counterexamples all make the focused guard/self-test fail.
- The live guard and self-test pass on current source, while documentation no longer overclaims beyond the mechanism actually proved.
close_reason: shipped #6135 (merged): preflight guard per-path

title: Make ui/slot arity exact and host-identical
description:
## Current defect

#6032 declares `ui/render-fn` a fixed-arity callback, but `analyze-slot` never compares slot argument count with an inline render-fn parameter vector and neither runtime carrier records/validates arity. `(ui/slot (ui/render-fn [x] [:span x]) 1 2)` therefore diverges by host: JavaScript invokes the one-argument function and silently ignores the surplus argument, while the JVM emitter invokes the Clojure fn and throws `ArityException`. Too-few calls are likewise left to host behavior instead of the compiler-owned seam.

## Required correction

Make the compiler-owned slot boundary enforce one host-independent arity contract. Reject statically knowable inline mismatches during analysis; carry expected arity for prop-carried render-fns and fail didactically before invocation on both CLJS and JVM.
acceptance_criteria:
- Inline render-fn calls with too few or too many slot args fail at compile time with one didactic slot/render-fn arity diagnostic.
- Prop-carried render-fns carry expected arity and validate it before invoking on both CLJS and JVM; neither host relies on native function-call quirks.
- Correct-arity zero- and multi-argument slots retain current output, nil behavior, manifest evidence, and client/JVM parity.
- Too-few and too-many parity fixtures prove identical category/message data on both hosts, with a mutation control that makes the gate red.

title: Make SSR emitter replay routed, failure-atomic, and precedence-safe
description:
PR #6028 added install-time replay of the retained SSR hiccup emitter. The happy path works, but the lifecycle transaction is neither failure-atomic nor cleanly routed, and its precedence/load-order contract is incomplete.

Current `install-adapter!` seats the new generation, then invokes `rearm-hiccup-emitter!`. The replay calls the global `:reagent/set-hiccup-emitter!` broadcast chain, whose documented semantics propagate a step exception and stop later steps. A throwing setter for any loaded adapter can therefore make `rf/init!` throw after the target generation is already installed. Reproduced on current main: the first `rf/init!` threw `replay failed`, `rf/current-adapter` still returned `:rf.adapter/plain-atom`, and a second `rf/init!` returned success because it skipped the already-seated install. The process has reported failed boot but behaves as installed/partially armed.

The broadcast also re-arms every loaded adapter cell rather than only the adapter being installed. This lets an inactive setter break the active adapter's boot and muddies lifecycle ownership.

Precedence is surprising for the public direct seam. Adapter docs say `set-hiccup-emitter!` is last-call-wins and `nil` resets, but when `re-frame.ssr` is loaded, a pre-init explicit custom emitter/reset is silently overwritten by install replay of the retained default. Existing test-react prose explicitly acknowledges this classpath-dependent winner. Define and pin a low-friction rule: explicit direct override/reset remains authoritative; replay supplies the retained default only when the freshly installed generation is otherwise unarmed.

Finally, closed source bead `rf2-vxgfnd.204` required both clean namespace load orders. The current lifecycle namespace statically loads both namespaces in one compiled process and therefore proves only one selected order. Existing chain tests prove fan-out, not public `re-frame.ui` destroy/re-init in both isolated orders.
acceptance_criteria:
- Installing an adapter plus replaying its retained default is one failure-atomic transaction: any replay failure leaves no generation installed, preserves the replay exception as primary, performs bounded exact-generation cleanup, and permits an immediate clean retry.
- Replay targets only the adapter/generation being installed; a loaded inactive adapter's throwing setter cannot break the active adapter's boot.
- Public direct `set-hiccup-emitter!` precedence is explicit and consistent across re-frame.ui/Reagent/UIx/Helix/test-react: a custom override or explicit nil reset is not silently undone by default replay; default replay arms only an otherwise-unarmed fresh generation.
- Fault-injection tests cover active and inactive throwing setters, exact cleanup, current-adapter state after failure, and successful retry.
- Contract tests under an SSR-loaded classpath prove custom override/reset precedence.
- Two isolated CLJS entrypoints or fresh Node processes run the same public init/render/destroy/reinit assertion in opposite orders: SSR-before-ui and ui-before-SSR.
- Repeated generations still do not accumulate callbacks or let stale cleanup clear a replacement.
close_reason: shipped #6137 (merged): SSR emitter install-replay failure-atomic (exact-gen rollback) + routed via late-bind arm-hook + precedence-safe; frozen 10-fn adapter contract preserved

title: Complete ui/event warning evidence and controlled-input recovery guidance
description:
PR #6027 widened the controlled-input synchronous door to compiler-owned `ui/event`, but three adjacent current contracts remain incomplete.

1. Invocation-time warning arms are uncatalogued and unproved. `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/events.cljs` classifies a vector returned by `ui/event` and calls both `warn-dynamic-placeholder!` and `warn-unregistered!` when the committed callback fires. Spec 009 still describes `:rf.warning/unregistered-event-id` as render-time literal/data/dynamic-handler evidence and `:rf.warning/placeholder-in-dynamic-vector` as render-time `dynamic-handler` evidence only. The focused warning fixture exercises only the runtime-classified render path, not a committed `event-handler` result.

2. The unregistered lookup is generation-blind. `warn-unregistered!` calls bare `registrar/lookup`, which reads the process registrar when no frame generation is bound. Actual dispatch resolves through the committed frame's sealed image generation. After registration/image evolution this can warn falsely for an event present in the committed frame or suppress a valid warning when only the process-current table contains it.

3. The controlled-input fallback warning still says the handler is not a literal data event and prescribes only a literal vector, even though the accepted door is now `#{:vector :ui-event}`. For reusable controls needing the native payload, a literal vector may not express the intended fix; the diagnostic should name both valid forms.

This is one bounded ergonomics/evidence correction around the #6027 widening, not new handler machinery. Open G-8/G-15 production/browser work remains owned by `rf2-vxgfnd.95.10` and is out of scope.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 009 rows for `:rf.warning/unregistered-event-id` and `:rf.warning/placeholder-in-dynamic-vector` describe both render-time dynamic/data paths and invocation-time `ui/event` result paths, with exact timing/evidence.
- A committed-owner/event-handler fixture returns an unregistered vector containing a placeholder, invokes the stable callback, asserts both exact warning envelopes, and proves the unchanged vector dispatches as ordinary data.
- Registration existence is resolved through the committed/captured frame's exact image generation. A two-frame/generation fixture proves both mismatch directions: present only in the frame image does not warn; present only process-current but absent from the frame image does warn.
- The controlled-input async fallback message recommends a literal event vector or `ui/event` as appropriate, and a focused message assertion prevents regression.
- Dev-only/advanced-elision behavior and existing open G-8/G-15 ownership remain unchanged.

title: Make shipped React derived-value construction internally failure-atomic
description:
## Confirmed current defect

PR #6025/closed rf2-vxgfnd.198 states that every shipped adapter satisfies Spec 006 internal failure-atomicity. The React-hook spine used by re-frame.ui/UIx/Helix does not. `make-derived-value-fn` records and installs one watch per source in an unguarded loop (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:563-566`). If a later source's `add-watch` throws, earlier watches remain installed and no derived value is returned, so core has nothing it can dispose. The ordinary `-dispose` cleanup at lines 591-606 only exists after construction returns.

The adjacent `make-state-container` wording is also weaker than its heading: “throw before it returns” does not require a constructor that allocated/pinned a host resource before throwing to unwind it. The current JVM fixture throws before allocation, so its zero-residue state-constructor arm cannot detect that contract violation.

## Bounded repair

Make the existing construction paths honestly failure-atomic without changing the ten-function adapter API. In the React spine, catch installation failure, attempt removal of every successfully installed watch in reverse acquisition order, and rethrow the primary construction error after cleanup. Strengthen the state-container throw branch symmetrically: any host/registry resource acquired before an unreturned throw is released first. Keep resource-free/GC-owned returned state containers and the existing derived-value disposal seam.
acceptance_criteria:
- A CLJS fault fixture makes the second or later source `add-watch` throw after an earlier install and proves zero residual watches/registry entries.
- Partial React-spine installation unwinds successfully installed watches in reverse order, attempts all cleanup, and preserves the primary construction exception even if cleanup also throws.
- Successful construction, notification batching, idempotent disposal, and UIx/re-frame.ui paths remain unchanged.
- Spec 006 and the adapter contract explicitly require `make-state-container` to release any resource acquired before an unreturned throw; the state-constructor fixture allocates/tracks such a resource before its fault and proves cleanup.
- No eleventh adapter function, global reset, timing sleep, or new public surface is added; focused JVM/CLJS construction and adapter gates pass.

title: Keep custom-element reload success honest when publication observers throw
description:
## Confirmed current failure

`commit-reload!` atomically reconciles/closes `ledger-state` and then calls `publish!`. `publish!` performs a bare `swap!` on the public `custom-elements` atom, which synchronously invokes its watches with no containment.

A throwing watch therefore escapes **after** the new ledger and aggregate are already authoritative:

```clojure
(add-watch custom-elements ::boom
  (fn [& _] (throw (ex-info "watch exploded" {}))))
(commit-reload! :app)
```

The independent correctness repro observed the exception propagate while the new aggregate was live and `:cycles` was empty. Shadow can interpret the after-load hook as failed even though the framework committed it; built-in watch fan-out can also skip later observers. This falsifies the reload outcome and risks partially notified DEV/tool consumers.

The repository already fixed the analogous descriptor-HMR problem in closed `rf2-vxgfnd.215`: authority commit and observer delivery need distinct failure semantics. That Bead does not cover this custom-element aggregate.

## Deliverable

Make the post-commit publication boundary honest. If arbitrary watches are intentionally supported, snapshot and isolate delivery. If they are only a test artefact, make the atom private and route the narrowly required framework observers through an explicit contained DEV path. In either design, a listener failure is diagnosable but cannot retroactively turn committed authority into a failed reload.

Do not attempt rollback after commit, add a general event bus, or carry listener machinery into production.

## Provenance and dedupe

Found during the chronological correctness audit of PR #6018. All-status search found closed `.215` as an analogous owner but no live custom-element publication issue.
acceptance_criteria:
- A publication observer failure after ledger reconciliation cannot make `commit-reload!`/Shadow report the successful authority transition as failed or roll it back.
- The live aggregate, projected ledger, and cycle state remain coherent and quiescent after such a failure.
- Every framework-owned observer in the publication snapshot is attempted exactly once regardless of sibling failure; arbitrary atom watches are either explicitly unsupported behind a private state var or receive equivalent isolated semantics.
- The first/aggregate observer failure is surfaced through one bounded DEV diagnostic carrying build/cycle/publication context after delivery, without truthiness bugs for falsey thrown values where representable.
- Reentrant registration/publication still preserves the newer winner and does not duplicate delivery.
- A fail-before fixture installs a throwing observer before good observers and proves current code propagates/skips; restoring bare uncontained publication makes the repaired fixture fail.
- No public event system, production listener machinery, rollback-after-commit, or per-render work is introduced.
notes:
PR #6409. Delivered in full, with one deliberate deviation reported rather than faked.

Observers THROW here (not the silent no-op rf2-1b0po found): publish! swap!s the public custom-elements atom, whose watch fan-out is synchronous and uncontained, so the throw escaped commit-reload! into shadow's ^:dev/after-load and reported a committed reload as failed. publish! now contains the fan-out and reports one bounded DEV diagnostic, mirroring reactive.cljc's report-hmr-listener-escape! (rf2-vxgfnd.215). Containment is sound because both hosts set the atom's value BEFORE notifying watches, so the aggregate/ledger/cycle state survive a contained failure unchanged. Failure identity rides an explicit :failed? bit, so (throw nil)/(throw false) are not silently dropped.

DEVIATION from AC3: isolated SIBLING delivery is not implemented. Watch fan-out belongs to the host IAtom, which abandons remaining watches on a throw; replacing it means a listener framework with no consumer — there are ZERO framework-owned observers of custom-elements (classification reads custom-element-properties; the only add-watch in the corpus is a test fixture). Arbitrary watches are documented as explicitly unsupported observers: contained and diagnosed, delivery completeness left to the host. The atom was NOT made private: the rf2-vxgfnd.144 reentrancy proof legitimately needs to observe publication, and CLJS privacy would not stop a throw anyway — it would be a nominal guarantee, not a real one.

SCOPE: dev-only. Grep-verified in a pseudo-named :advanced bundle — publish_BANG_ and report_publication_escape absent from the re_frame$ui$rules$* surface. Dev-tooling correctness, not a production guarantee.

title: Give custom-element reload commits explicit cycle ownership
description:
## Confirmed contract hole

PR #6018 correctly moved source state and open-cycle staging into one atom for the concrete register-vs-commit race, but it did not give a reload cycle its own identity:

```clojure
:cycles {build-id {:staged ... :touched ...}}
```

`notify-reload!` blindly replaces `[:cycles build-id]`, while `commit-reload!` identifies the thing to close by `build-id` alone. With overlapping same-build activations:

1. cycle N opens/stages;
2. cycle N+1 opens and replaces that row/stages;
3. N's delayed after-load calls `commit-reload! build-id`;
4. it reconciles and closes N+1; N+1's own completion later has nothing to commit.

There is no generation/token that could distinguish the callers, despite the implementation describing a “generation rule.” This is exactly the overlapping-cycle interleaving that closed source Bead `rf2-vxgfnd.144` required.

## Proof gap

The new JVM tests cover register-vs-commit, register-vs-notify, and distinct-build write-throughs. They never race notify against commit or model two same-build cycles. The register-vs-notify test also declines to assert the raced element after settlement, although both legal serial orders retain it; the independent audit ran that stronger assertion for 500 rounds with no current implementation loss, showing it is a cheap useful contract assertion.

## Deliverable

First pin the actual Shadow loader scheduling contract with a real integration fixture. If same-build activations can overlap, carry explicit cycle ownership through the lifecycle. If Shadow is strictly synchronous/single-flight, enforce that boundary fail-closed and retire the broader overlap claim instead of adding unused machinery. In either case, a stale completion must never act on a newer cycle.

Do not solve this with timing sleeps, a process-global lock around user callbacks, or an unowned retry loop.

## Provenance and dedupe

Found during the chronological completeness/quality audit of PR #6018. All-status search found only closed `rf2-vxgfnd.144`; no live issue owns cycle identity/overlap proof.
acceptance_criteria:
- A commit can reconcile/close only the reload cycle that opened it; a delayed completion from cycle N cannot consume or close cycle N+1.
- Registrations and touched-source evidence are assigned to one documented live generation and are never lost, doubled, or left in an orphan row under overlapping scheduling.
- Either actual cycle identity is threaded through begin/stage/commit, or the real Shadow integration enforces and proves a strict single-flight rule that rejects/serializes a second open without replacing live staging.
- Deterministic tests cover notify-vs-commit and two overlapping same-build cycles, plus both legal register-vs-notify serializations; the raced registration is present exactly once after settlement.
- A mutation removing cycle ownership/enforcement makes the overlap proof fail.
- Failed cycles preserve last-known-good state and successful cycles publish only coherent aggregates.
- No sleeps, broad callback lock, unbounded retry, second ledger, public API, or per-render cost is introduced.
notes:
PR #6409. PARTIAL DELIVERY — needs an operator ruling on the remainder.

DELIVERED: notify-reload! no longer supersedes a live cycle silently (bounded DEV diagnostic naming the discarded staged/touched evidence, gated on what was LOST rather than on cycle-key presence); the overlap/ownership overclaim retired in prose; the bead's stated proof gap closed with a notify-vs-commit barrier race (400 rounds), a deterministic two-cycle overlap fixture, the strengthened register-vs-notify settlement assertion, and positive+negative diagnosis fixtures.

NOT DELIVERED — architecturally blocked, same class as escalated sibling rf2-vxgfnd.143. AC1 ('a delayed completion from cycle N cannot consume or close cycle N+1') and the arm-1 reading of AC3 ('actual cycle identity threaded through begin/stage/commit') cannot be implemented at shadow's real seam. Evidence read off the pinned shadow-cljs client (shadow.cljs.devtools.client.{browser,shared,env}):
  1. NO CONVEYANCE — lifecycle hooks are resolved by name off $CLJS and invoked with NO arguments, so a ^:dev/after-load invocation is anonymous and cannot present a claim minted by its own before-load. Any token would be minted AND checked inside the ledger, where commit-reload! could only compare it against the live slot it already reads — a tautology wearing an identity check's clothes.
  2. NO PAIRING — do-js-reload* abandons the remaining task chain on a throw, so a failed load never runs ^:dev/after-load. That also kills every depth/refcount scheme: one aborted reload pins the count above zero and hot reload silently stops committing forever.
Shadow has no single-flight guard of its own; what serializes cycles is JS itself, and only while every lifecycle hook is synchronous. An ^:dev/*-async hook anywhere in the build reintroduces overlap that this ledger cannot repair.

SCOPE NOTE: all of this machinery is dev-only. Grep-verified in a pseudo-named :advanced bundle — no commit_reload/notify_reload/publish_BANG_/ledger_state in the re_frame$ui$rules$* surface. Dev-tooling correctness, not a production guarantee.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 09:54 AUSEST)

Seam finding ACCEPTED. RETIRED: AC1, both arms of AC3 as written, and the overlapping-scheduling clauses of AC2 ("never lost ... under overlapping scheduling") and AC5 (the overlap-proof reading). Why, verified against the pinned shadow-cljs 3.4.10 client jar (byte-identical in 3.4.11; env.cljs unchanged in the jar since 2025-03): shadow resolves lifecycle hooks by name off $CLJS and invokes them anonymously — a sync hook gets ZERO arguments, an async hook only a continuation — so an ^:dev/after-load cannot present any identity for the cycle its before-load opened, and any token minted and checked inside our own ledger only compares against the slot it already reads (a tautology, the fake-guard class this repo rejects); and do-js-reload* abandons the task chain when a load throws, so a failed load never runs after-load — before/after are NOT a paired bracket, which kills every refcount scheme and makes reject-on-second-open wedge the ledger permanently (supersession IS the aborted-reload recovery, so AC3 arm 2's fail-closed single-flight is also unbuildable as written).

RATIFIED CONTRACT (delivered by PR #6409, merge bc0f7decd8): exactly one live cycle per build-id; a second before-load supersedes the live cycle with a loud, bounded, loss-gated diagnostic naming the discarded staged/touched evidence (silent on ordinary consecutive reloads, negative fixture pinned); overlapping same-build cycles (reachable only via ^:dev/*-async hooks, none in this repo) are UNSUPPORTED, with bounded self-healing degradation — possible stale classification rows until the next full page reload — documented in rules.cljc. AC4, AC6, AC7 and the diagnostic reading of AC5 are delivered and stand. Entire surface is dev-only: ledger is compile-time gated and grep-verified absent from :advanced bundles.

"Hold for upstream" was evaluated and REJECTED on evidence: it would require two coordinated shadow changes (hook-argument conveyance + a paired abort signal), neither of which exists or is hinted at, and the seam has not moved in over a year. Do not reopen against shadow-cljs upgrades unless the hook seam itself changes (hooks receive identity AND aborts emit a paired signal). No upstream feature-request chore unless a consumer actually reports the async-hook degradation (the diagnostic will name it). No joint disposition with rf2-vxgfnd.143 — same decision class, independent facts, ruled separately.

CLOSURE RECOMMENDATION for the mayor: close rf2-84173 as delivered by PR #6409; nothing further is buildable or owed on this bead. Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-84173.reload-cycle-ownership-remainder.md retired per Mike's authorization.
close_reason: PR #6409 delivered the explicitly ratified bounded reload-cycle contract; unsupported anonymous async overlap remains deliberately out of scope

title: Make the reload-source producer self-upgrading across the trampoline boundary
description:
## Confirmed current failure

PR #6018's `.145` change puts the new tagged trampoline installer behind the same pre-existing `defonce` it is trying to repair:

```clojure
(defonce ^:private _reload-source-producer
  (install-reload-source-producer!))
```

A live process loaded before `.145` already has that var initialized and an **untagged raw function object** in `SHADOW_NS_RESET`. When the namespace hot-reloads to current code, ClojureScript preserves the defonce value, so `install-reload-source-producer!` never runs. The old object remains installed—the exact stale-callback state `.145` was filed to fix.

The PR's commit order exposes a second concrete live-upgrade failure. `.145` lands first and creates a trampoline capturing `::default`; `.142` then introduces `current-build-id`, but the realized defonce again prevents replacement, so that page keeps routing reset evidence to the placeholder owner.

## Why the tests miss it

`installed-producer-runs-the-current-implementation-after-a-reload` starts from a fresh bundle containing the **final** code, whose defonce has already installed a good trampoline. It then rebinds `reload-source-reset!`. That proves future redefinitions work after a clean final-code load; it does not drive legacy installed object -> new installer migration.

## Deliverable

Give producer installation an idempotent reload-time migration path with explicit ownership. It must replace/retire the exact predecessor shape and refresh the build-owned tag while leaving every foreign callback untouched. Seed the actual legacy array/sentinel shape before loading/evaluating the repaired installer so the regression is causal.

Keep this narrow: no clearing `SHADOW_NS_RESET`, no positional ownership assumptions about foreign callbacks, and no general callback registry.

## Provenance and dedupe

Found during the chronological implementation-quality audit of PR #6018. All-status search found only the closed source Bead `rf2-vxgfnd.145`; no live issue owns the failed upgrade boundary.
acceptance_criteria:
- Starting from the exact pre-.145 state (realized install sentinel plus an untagged raw `reload-source-reset!` entry), evaluating the repaired namespace makes Shadow's existing array entry execute the current implementation without a page refresh.
- The same migration refreshes an entry created by .145 before .142 so it routes through the current real build identity rather than captured `::default`.
- After migration/repeated reloads there is exactly one current re-frame.ui producer per intended build; no stale owned callback executes or accumulates.
- Shadow/foreign callbacks in the shared array are preserved byte-for-byte and in order.
- Subsequent implementation/coercion/routing changes are picked up by the installed trampoline.
- The fail-before fixture seeds the legacy installed state before loading current code; a fresh-final-code install alone is not accepted as migration proof.
- Advanced-production elision and ordinary reload behavior remain unchanged; no global callback-array reset or public API is introduced.
notes:
DELIVERED (PR #6434, 2026-07-19), with ONE deliberate AC deviation flagged for review.

PREMISE CONFIRMED: the defonce at rules.cljc ~1394 pins install-reload-source-producer!, so the installer never re-runs on a hot reload of rules.cljc — no change to the installer, the trampoline's construction, or the owner tag can reach a live page. Also confirmed the existing tests miss it exactly as the bead says: 'installed-producer-runs-...-after-a-reload' starts from final code and rebinds the var; 'producer-install-is-idempotent-...' calls the installer DIRECTLY three times, bypassing the defonce entirely — so the installer's idempotence was proven while the fact that it never RUNS was not.

FIX: install runs on EVERY load; retire-what-this-copy-owns via a defonce'd ownership cell. The defonce moved from the install (where it froze the machinery) to the ownership record (where surviving the reload is the point). It only ever existed to stop the pre-.145 .push appending duplicates — a job the owner TAG took over in .145, which is what made it both redundant and the blocker. Ownership is OBJECT IDENTITY, never tag: tag says which build an entry claims, identity says this copy installed it; they diverge in exactly the migration cases (our own entry whose tag went stale; a co-loaded bundle's entry carrying the tag we are leaving). Cell gated like ledger-state -> no prod allocation.

RED-BEFORE (CLJS, real path): drives shadow's OWN build-id carrier (the object graph current-build-id reads via shadow-build-id), not a stand-in seam. Unfixed source => 2 producers, survivor still tagged ':re-frame.ui.rules/default', array grew by 2 not 1.

DEVIATION FROM AC1 — NOT IMPLEMENTED, needs a call: migrating a PRE-.145 untagged raw reload-source-reset! entry. It is untagged, hence indistinguishable from a foreign callback by any SOUND test; the only handle is sniffing the munged CLJS fn name (.name === 're_frame$ui$rules$reload_source_reset_BANG_'), which is compiler-internal and permanent dead weight. It can only matter to a tab loaded from the ONE-COMMIT window between db31f0288d (.77) and 8c1653ad37 (.145) that then hot-reloads rather than refreshing — in-memory dev-only back-compat, which the pre-alpha stance declines. The GENERAL defect (defonce freeze) and every FUTURE upgrade across that boundary ARE fixed. If Mike wants the legacy sniffer, it is a small follow-up bead.

Elision confirmed unchanged (bead AC): test:elision 60/60, test:ui-advanced-elision 4/4, and test:browser-prod-elision runs custom_element_reload_elision_prod_test.cljs INSIDE the :advanced bundle — mounted prod elision PASS, 105 tests/414 assertions.

title: Finish real Shadow ownership and removed-source reconciliation
acceptance_criteria:
- Every emitted registration, lifecycle hook, reset callback, staged row, removal, and commit for a real dev build uses one stable build identity; no real path silently falls back to `::default`.
- A successful saved namespace delete/rename supplies the removed old owner to that exact build and evicts its runtime declarations without a page refresh; a same-namespace file move preserves ownership.
- Two genuinely co-loaded builds with equal namespace symbols are either proven isolated through real build-scoped identity, or a one-build-per-shared-runtime boundary is explicitly enforced and all synthetic multi-build claims/tests are removed.
- `note-reloaded-sources!` cannot inject a foreign `[build ns]` owner into another build's open cycle: ready-made pairs are rejected or normalized to the addressed build, and an adversarial cross-build fixture proves neither row can evict the other.
- Failed compile/evaluation keeps the last-known-good runtime ledger; a successful retry converges with a clean reload.
- One real Shadow warm-watch/file-edit fixture drives actual before-load -> source reset/evaluation -> after-load ordering without direct lifecycle/seam calls and covers zero-declaration, delete/rename, move, failure/retry, and the chosen build-topology contract.
- Removing a lifecycle annotation or the real build/source producer makes that fixture fail.
- The existing ledger is reused; no second manifest protocol, digest owner token, public API, or per-render work is introduced.
notes:
Independent correctness repro for the same build-ownership contract:

```clojure
(register-custom-element! :a-el {:properties #{:a}} 'shared.ns :a)
(register-custom-element! :b-el {:properties #{:b}} 'shared.ns :b)
(notify-reload! :a)
(note-reloaded-sources! [[:b 'shared.ns]] :a)
(commit-reload! :a)
```

Current `note-reloaded-sources!` accepts the ready-made foreign pair verbatim, so build A's cycle evicts build B's row. Normalize every source to `[build-id ns]` or reject a mismatched pair before it reaches `:touched`; preserve the ergonomic ns-only form.
PARTIAL (PR #6434, 2026-07-19). SHIPPED: the note-reloaded-sources! arm (bead NOTES repro + AC 'cannot inject a foreign [build ns] owner into another build's open cycle'). Sources are normalized to [addressed-build ns], so a cycle's reconciliation is total over its own rows. Chose NORMALIZE over REJECT (the AC allows either) deliberately: reject needs a new runtime error id -> Spec 009 catalogue row, and normalize adds no caller-facing failure mode. Verified NO caller in the corpus ever passed a ready-made pair, so the verbatim branch was unexercised ergonomics that was also the hole. Red-before on JVM: :b-el => #{} (build :b's row evicted by build :a's cycle), :a-el => #{:a} (:a's own row never reconciled) — exactly the bead repro. Green after: ui JVM 958 tests/18660 assertions, CLJS 10221/50503.

BEAD STAYS OPEN — remaining arms untouched, NOT attempted: (1) a real Shadow warm-watch/file-edit fixture driving actual before-load -> source-reset -> after-load ordering; (2) the removed/renamed saved-source graph delta projected from :build-sources into the ledger; (3) the co-loaded-build TOPOLOGY question. (3) needs a RULING, not a fix: the bead asks to either prove real isolation OR enforce one-build-per-shared-runtime and delete the synthetic multi-build tests/claims. rules.cljc lines ~805-808 already determine the FACT (two builds sharing ONE copy of the ns cannot be told apart by any mechanism shadow exposes — the hooks are a single shared singleton); what is undecided is the consequence, which has real blast radius over the explicit-build-arity tests. Worth splitting (1)+(2) into their own bead from (3).
⚠️ PARTIAL — one arm shipped in #6434, TWO REMAIN. Bead stays OPEN.

SHIPPED: the bounded determinable arm. Red-before reproduced the bead's exact repro — :b-el -> #{} (build :b's row evicted by build :a's cycle) and :a-el -> #{:a} (:a's own row never reconciled). The worker also verified a premise the bead did not state: NO CALLER IN THE CORPUS EVER PASSES A READY-MADE PAIR, so the verbatim branch was unexercised ergonomics that was also the hole. Real surface was implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/rules.cljc — NOT tools/builds, which my dispatch brief wrongly named (that is a LABEL on this bead, not a path).
⚠️ NOT the goog.DEBUG trap, and the reason is worth keeping: this fix DOES sit inside reload-ledger?, but the bug is UNREACHABLE in production rather than merely unguarded there — notify-reload! is a ^:dev/before-load hook shadow never installs in a release build, so no production reload cycle exists to inject into. That distinction (unreachable vs unguarded) is what separates a legitimate dev-only placement from the rf2-2hkfy / rf2-5pr75 defect shape.

REMAINING ARM 1 — ⚠️ NEEDS A RULING, NOT A FIX. The co-loaded-build TOPOLOGY question. rules.cljc already DETERMINES THE FACT: two builds sharing one copy of the namespace cannot be distinguished by anything shadow exposes. The bead asks to either (a) prove real isolation, or (b) enforce the boundary and DELETE the synthetic multi-build tests. (b) has real blast radius — it retires existing coverage — so it is an operator call.
REMAINING ARM 2 — determinable, dispatchable: the warm-watch fixture and the removed-source graph delta, both untouched.
⚠️ WORKER RECOMMENDATION, endorsed: SPLIT ARM 2 OUT into its own bead so it can ship without waiting on the topology ruling. Do that before re-dispatching.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 14:56 AUSEST)

ARM 1 RULING — option (b), scalpel version: enforce the boundary and retire the synthetic multi-build coverage. Do NOT attempt to prove real isolation (option a): Shadow's runtime seam conveys no build identity into lifecycle hooks or SHADOW_NS_RESET callbacks (verified in rules.cljc "Bounded by shadow's reload surface", ~lines 796-808), and the topology those tests simulate — two dev builds fused onto one $CLJS — is a broken realm below the custom-element layer (shared cljs.core, shared registrar, defonce collisions) that Shadow itself does not support.

THE BOUNDARY (normative wording, per the Codex refinement): "One Shadow dev build per CLJS global namespace root containing re-frame.ui.rules." NOT "one build per page" or "one bundle per page" — separate output files are not automatically separate runtime copies (standard Shadow dev output shares the global root; single-module release output is wrapped by default). Supported and isolated by construction: one app plus :preloads tools (one build), iframes/workers (separate realms), independently compiled release bundles (output-wrapped, own copy, no ledger), separate pages. Unsupported and unobservable: two dev builds fused onto one shared root.

WHERE IT LANDS: the topology commentary in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/rules.cljc only. Promote the existing "Bounded by shadow's reload surface" section (~796-808) to the normative contract statement; rewrite the ownership rationale at ~722-724 and ~758-771 that presents multi-build reconciliation as shipped behaviour. NO runtime detection, warning, or error — the fused condition is unobservable from inside the shared copy, so any check would be heuristic or tautological; consequently no new error-id and no Spec 009 catalogue row. NO spec/* or docs/* edits (dossier corpus grep verified no page claims runtime multi-build isolation) — so NOT hot-zone; the surface is implementation/ui/ src + test only, parallel-safe.

TESTS TO DELETE (implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/rules_cljs_test.cljc; all six verified present at these lines on origin/main 3947ac610a): build-ids-are-isolated (281), reentrant-registration-into-an-open-foreign-cycle-still-stages (408), co-loaded-builds-retain-independent-declarations (904), one-builds-cycle-never-consumes-another-builds-reload-evidence (932), installed-producer-notes-into-its-own-build-only (983), reload-producer-is-build-isolated (1074). Their sole subject is cross-build independence inside one shared namespace copy — a state no real call path can produce.

TESTS TO KEEP (reframe multi-build wording where present; do not weaken): ready-made-pair-cannot-inject-a-foreign-owner-into-an-open-cycle (946) and ns-only-and-ready-made-pair-are-the-same-evidence (966) — the shipped rf2-4vm19 normalization invariant; build-identity-is-one-rule-shared-by-every-arity (860) and build-identity-is-stable-across-calls (886) — single-build identity coherence; the producer-install trio (~742, ~786, ~823) — the shared SHADOW_NS_RESET array genuinely hosts other libraries' callbacks; the full JVM linearizability suite (rules_reload_linearizability_jvm_test.clj) — its explicit build-ids are re-documented as test-state partition tokens, not a topology claim.

MECHANISM STAYS: keep the [build-id ns] ledger key, current-build-id, the producer tag, and the explicit build-scoped arities — re-documented as the internal producer seam plus test-isolation tokens. The shipped normalization fix (PR #6434) sits on this key; collapsing to ns-only is a second refactor with zero user-visible gain and real regression risk. Do NOT add a two-build browser fixture, per-build registry, owner-token protocol, public configuration switch, or wrapper manager.

ARM 2 SPLIT (rider for the mayor, executed): the real warm-watch/file-edit fixture plus the removed/renamed saved-source :build-sources delta is independent dispatchable engineering — split into its own bead (see cross-ref on this bead) before re-dispatching. Under this ruling, that fixture's "chosen build-topology contract" AC item resolves to proving ONE real dev build's identity at the runtime seam (non-::default build-id, hook discovery/order, annotation load-bearingness) — real and currently untested — NOT two-build isolation. rf2-4vm19 itself remains open until the Arm-1 implementation (test deletions + rules.cljc rewrite) ships.

BASIS: both the original dossier recommendation and the independent Codex recommendation argued option (b) with identical test dispositions; I followed their shared substance and adopted Codex's boundary phrasing because it is the more precise statement of the actual isolation unit (the CLJS root, not the output file) and I verified its load-bearing claims against the source. Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-4vm19.coloaded-build-topology.md retired (deleted) per Mike's authorization.

ARM 1 SHIPPED in PR #6450 (branch worker/rules-cluster-ymfix), commit cd57ac0f6b — implements the DECISION block (Fable, 2026-07-19) verbatim. BOUNDARY now normative in rules.cljc §THE ISOLATION UNIT: one Shadow dev build per CLJS global namespace root containing re-frame.ui.rules; unit is the CLJS ROOT not the page/output file; supported+isolated (one app + :preloads tools, iframes/workers, independently compiled release bundles, separate pages) vs unsupported+unobservable (two dev builds fused on one shared root). Commentary rewritten BY CONTENT (#6440 moved every line the ruling cited): 'Bounded by shadow's reload surface' promoted to the normative contract; the ownership rationale re-documents [build-id ns-sym] as the internal producer seam + test-state partition token, not a multi-build reconciliation claim; the .48 'three holes' list drops the multi-build hole; the .142 test-section header reframed as single-build identity coherence. DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-20 15:03 AUSEST)

RECONCILIATION — the 2026-07-20 note above ("rf2-4vm19 now tracks ONLY REMAINING ARM 1: the co-loaded-build TOPOLOGY question, which NEEDS A MIKE RULING") is ERRONEOUS. The topology ruling was already made on this bead (DECISION block, Fable delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 14:56 AUSEST: option (b), scalpel version) and shipped verbatim in PR #6450, MERGED 2026-07-19T06:43:35Z (commit cd57ac0f6b, merge 459bcbc8eb). ARM-2 CHAIN, verified: sequential splits, both now CLOSED. rf2-tm1xi (first split, 2026-07-19) shipped merged #6503 (compiler-side warm-watch proof), was audit-reopened, then closed stale-open; rf2-lkv72 (second split, 2026-07-20) was the terminal Arm-2 carrier and shipped merged #6552 (runtime ledger-sources delta + warm-rebuild fixture). No live Arm-2 carrier exists.

RECOMMENDATION for the mayor: CLOSE rf2-4vm19 — both arms shipped and merged; no verified remainder found on this bead.
AUDIT CORRECTION after merged PR #6552 (2026-07-20T04:45:48Z): KEEP OPEN. The later recommendation to close this bead because both arms shipped is overturned by the exact applied-code audit. PR #6552 is a useful, bounded partial: its authored and applied patch are identical (stable patch-id 39baa3723b8bf56afb15c74c2372588a403da1de), and its dual-host fixture proves source reconciliation and the installed SHADOW_NS_RESET producer once removed-source evidence is supplied.
