It therefore injects exactly the evidence a saved delete/rename lacks in the real runtime.

The current source itself remains explicit: a deleted source with no reloading dependent never reruns, Shadow never reports it, and its runtime rows persist until a full page load; note-reloaded-sources! is only the seam an authoritative removed-source manifest would feed if one is wired. ledger-sources reports committed contributing-source rows; it is not the compile-side :build-sources membership authority and cannot discover a removal. Same-namespace moves are covered; delete and rename-away are not end-to-end covered.

No new bead was filed: this OPEN P2 is the existing material owner, and closed rf2-tm1xi contains the detailed implementation packet. Finish with the smallest real proof: extend the existing Shadow warm-watch runner to load one emitted runtime (no DOM), project the successful compile-side removed-namespace delta into the existing cycle, prove real evaluation failure/LKG/retry and exact accepted manifest+digest stability, wire the existing gate into CI, and use createHarnessCleanup for exit/signal cleanup. Removing lifecycle annotations or the producer must make the fixture fail. Do not add a public API, second ledger/protocol, browser/framework harness, or multi-build machinery.

Independent completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality reviews agreed the bounded fixture is maintainable and the reconciliation algorithm is correct once evidence exists, but the real saved delete/rename contract and lifecycle-annotation proof remain materially incomplete.
STOP-REPORT (worker/shadow-ownership-4vm19, 2026-07-21 20:11 AUSEST). Dispatch brief hypothesized 'Shadow' = real-DOM Shadow root (a runtime concern confined to rules.cljc, disjoint from S1). description:

title: Close lexical, polarity, and Markdown-boundary gaps in the Form-3 migration guard
description:
## Current defect

PR #6013 strengthened `scripts/check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py`, but the current Form-3 lifecycle guard remains bypassable and noisy at three narrow syntax boundaries:

1. **Clojure lexical context.** `_read_form` treats `;` comment text as arguments, so an actually bare multiline call with a comment is counted arity 6 and passes. `_form3_call_sites` also finds call heads inside strings, so `(log/debug "(rf/subscribe-once query-v)")` is falsely rejected.
2. **Example polarity.** `_polarity_at(..., carried)` carries an inline `BEFORE` exemption across every later block until a recognized `AFTER`; an ordinary later affirmative recipe passes. Polarity regexes also read arbitrary code/string contents: `(log/debug "BEFORE")` exempts a following unsafe call. Conversely ordinary negative prose such as `Not recommended: (rf/subscribe-once query-v)` is falsely rejected. These behaviors contradict closed rf2-vxgfnd.94.20’s criterion that historical examples cannot hide affirmative recipes.
3. **Markdown structural boundaries.** Setext headings are not recognized. A valid `Form-3 lifecycle` Setext section containing a bare call passes, while a later Setext H1 meant to start an ambient-render section fails to end prior lifecycle context. A CommonMark spaced thematic break (`* * *`) likewise fails to reset the bounded context.

Current self-tests and live-corpus scans remain green under these exact mutations. All-status searches for the mechanisms and syntax names found no live owner; closed rf2-vxgfnd.94.15/.19/.20 are the related prior work.

## Bounded repair

Add one small lexical masking/token pass shared by call-head discovery and balanced-form reading; scope historical polarity to explicit prose/comment labels and the concrete example they own; and recognize the missing Setext/thematic structural boundaries. Keep this a purpose-built guard, not a general Clojure or Markdown parser. Merely adding more positive-marker phrases is insufficient because unlabelled affirmative prose must be guarded.
acceptance_criteria:
- Call-head discovery and arity scanning ignore strings, character literals, and `;`-to-EOL comments consistently. Bare calls with comments before/after the sole argument remain arity 1 and dirty; call-shaped text inside a log/string remains clean.
- Inline/block `BEFORE`, negative-example, or “not recommended” prose exempts only the concrete historical example it owns and is not inferred from arbitrary code/string contents.
- A historical example does not bless a later unlabelled or explicit AFTER/positive recipe in the same section.
- Setext H1/H2 headings and CommonMark spaced thematic breaks bound lifecycle context like their ATX/plain-break equivalents: unsafe lifecycle sections remain dirty and a later legal ambient section stays clean.
- Self-tests and live-corpus mutation teeth contain every exact pre-fix repro plus historical, affirmative, multiline/vector/string/character, and frame-qualified legal controls.
- The current corpus passes deterministically without broadening into a general parser or weakening the fail-loud guide scan.

Current Spec 006, synthesis 03, and the core observation docstring still call the table/handle scope the "current synchronous execution slice" and state that nothing survives into a later render slice. Those claims conflict with the executable proof because the interposed microtask render is later and not part of the original synchronous call. The #6009 lifetime census false-greens: it checks for the checkpoint and generic shared-law markers but not their compatible meaning. `rf2-2g7pxq` claimed reconciliation, yet its implementation commit changed UI reactive comments/tests only.
acceptance_criteria: State the lifetime per host without contradictory universal wording: JVM sharing ends with its synchronous render thunk; CLJS sharing may span later callbacks within the bounded host-microtask window and ends after the holder-clear checkpoint. Preserve the exact incarnation/epoch tag safety law and distinguish bounded reuse from stale-value authority. Reconcile Spec 006, synthesis 03, the core observation contract, and other live authorities, then strengthen the census with a mutation that restores the obsolete synchronous-slice/later-render claim while retaining the checkpoint markers. Keep runtime behavior unchanged unless the clarified law exposes a real mismatch.

title: Correct UIx/Helix stateful-component guidance to use hooks adapter APIs
description:
## Defect

Canonical stateful-component guidance still conflates Reagent with hooks-based adapters after PR #5981 and the later adapter-disposition repairs. At current main ca92f4a0e6613a750370bae6069a91e7d25222fa:

- spec/Pattern-StatefulComponents.md tells UIx/Helix users to register via the Reagent reg-view macro and prescribes bare capture-frame uniformly.
- skills/re-frame2/patterns/stateful-components.md repeats that registration/capture guidance.
- skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/frames.md claims reg-view* gives UIx/Helix a Reagent :contextType.
- The pattern introduction says compiled re-frame.ui belongs in the Reagent compatibility appendix, reversing authority: compiled guidance belongs in the main Spec 004/pattern; Reagent mechanics belong in 004A.

The authoritative adapter contract is adapter-specific: UIx/Helix use ordinary defui/defnc, use-subscribe plus use-frame, and optional reg-view* only when registry addressing is needed. Reagent uses the reg-view/reg-view* and render-time capture-frame spelling. UIx is now explicitly first-class, so the present advice directs supported users to the wrong macro and frame-carry idiom.
acceptance_criteria:
- The Reagent worked example remains explicitly Reagent-specific and uses reg-view/reg-view* plus render-time capture-frame where appropriate.
- UIx and Helix guidance shows their exact ordinary defui/defnc, use-subscribe, and use-frame spelling; reg-view* is described only as optional registry addressing, never as a source of Reagent :contextType.
- The main spec, mirrored/compressed pattern, and frame-fundamentals skill leaf agree, and compiled re-frame.ui guidance is assigned to the main pattern/Spec 004 while Reagent mechanics point to 004A.

title: Add the missing browser proof for Xray parallel :always-round rendering
description:
## Acceptance gap

PR #5978 satisfied its runtime and focused JVM/Node behavior, but did not deliver AC5's promised browser gate using real structured records and failing if :rf.machine.microstep/transition is filtered. The real-runtime machine_epochs_harness_cljs_test namespace is Node-only; browser selection runs -dom-cljs-test namespaces. Nightly browser runMachineEpochs asserts per-frame snapshots and explicitly delegates deep microstep render fidelity to the CLJS unit, while PR smoke does not stage machine-epochs.

Consequently, removing the projection operation/view clause for parallel :always rounds can leave every browser check green. No current DOM test asserts data-cascade-round-index, the [ALWAYS] round presentation, actionless round visibility, or the four regional topology edges. This is a missing promised proof, separate from rf2-v528f's handled-self-event correctness bug.
acceptance_criteria:
- A focused DOM/browser fixture is driven by real parallel machine trace evidence, not only hand-built view-model maps.
- It asserts two regional round rows in deterministic order, round-index presentation, actionless-round visibility, and the expected direct-event plus :always topology edges for both regions.
- Filtering or removing :rf.machine.microstep/transition from projection/view handling makes the browser fixture fail.

title: Preserve Xray event edges for handled self/internal transitions followed by :always rounds
description:
## Defect

PR #5978 added first-class parallel :always-round evidence, but current Xray fired-edge extraction drops a real event edge when a parallel region handles an external event without changing state and then takes an :always round. The defect is current at main ca92f4a0e6613a750370bae6069a91e7d25222fa.

A real runtime machine with region :a in :idle handles :go via a targetless/internal transition whose :arm action sets {:armed? true}; a guarded :always transition then moves :idle to :done. Runtime evidence contains the action cascade entry and the :rf.machine.microstep/transition. Both canonical edges exist, but parallel-transition-fired-ids returns only the :always edge and omits region__a__idle__idle__go__a_arm.

The suppressing condition is the handled-but-unchanged branch in tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machines/trace_state.cljs (around line 659), which requires (empty? rounds). handled-regions-from-cascade (around line 364) currently also counts :kind :microstep, so merely deleting that condition would create a phantom event edge for a region that declined the event but participated in stabilization.

## Smallest sound repair

Derive event-handled regions from non-:microstep top-level cascade entries. Recognize a handled unchanged event whenever before equals the event target, regardless of later rounds. Keep declined-event-plus-round negative coverage. Do not broaden this into correlation work for multiple same-actor macrosteps in one epoch: that synthetic case is unreachable under the one-dequeued-event/one-transition-per-actor epoch contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real-runtime parallel fixture where a targetless/internal :go action enables a guarded :always transition marks both the canonical event edge and the canonical :always edge as fired.
- A region that declines the event but participates in a later :always round does not gain a phantom event edge.
- Event-handled-region derivation excludes :kind :microstep evidence while retaining action/exit/entry evidence for handled self/internal transitions.
- Existing direct regional-event, actionless, declined-region, multi-round ordering, projection, and machine-epoch tests remain green.
- A mutation restoring the current rounds-empty suppression or counting microsteps as event handling fails the focused regression.
close_reason: shipped #6115 (merged): xray :always event-edges + browser proof

title: Make bundle-isolation enrollment cover future UI and adapter artefacts
description:
## Problem

PR #5975 / rf2-sh0sp4 added a filesystem-derived completeness check intended to make every new browser-optional publishable runtime fail until it has a bundle-isolation entry. The check permanently excludes implementation/ui in NON_BROWSER_OPTIONAL, with a comment claiming UI is always present because every adapter loads it. That premise is false: day8/re-frame2-ui is a separate JVM+CLJS/browser-capable artefact, the current product posture offers it as an experimental substrate alongside retained Reagent/UIx/reagent-slim adapters, and the adapter artefacts do not depend on it. UI is merely pre-publication today; implementation/ui/deps.edn deliberately has no :clein/build.

The scanner applies NON_BROWSER_OPTIONAL before reading deps.edn. An in-memory mutation adding a valid :clein/build marker to UI therefore yields uiPermanentlyExcluded=true, uiIsolationEntryPresent=false, wouldBeRequired=false, and wouldBeReportedMissing=false. The planned publication owner rf2-vxgfnd.99.2 can make UI publishable while this isolation completeness gate stays green, directly missing rf2-sh0sp4 AC6. The release-inventory validator may catch missing packaging rows, but it does not provide production-bundle isolation.

The current full npm run test:bundle-isolation is green (22 artefacts, 38 sentinels, 8 canonical runtimes) because pre-publication UI is outside the derived set; Resources itself is correctly covered. Later emitted-positive-control hardening did not repair the UI classification.

## Dedupe

Open rf2-vxgfnd.99.2 owns UI package/release publication and is the integration point, but does not own a UI bundle-isolation entry or this false-green. Closed rf2-vxgfnd.173 owns release-workflow inventory coupling, not client bundle isolation. Closed rf2-sh0sp4 is the incomplete source change.
design: Derive publishable browser-runtime paths with the same bounded flat-plus-adapters traversal used by version lockstep. Require each discovered runtime to map either to the generic ARTEFACTS gate or to one explicit existing dedicated isolation gate. Remove ui from the permanent always-present exclusion: because UI has no :clein/build today, pre-publication remains green naturally. Add small executable mutations proving (1) hypothetical publishable UI and (2) a hypothetical new publishable adapter both fail while unmapped. When rf2-vxgfnd.99.2 publishes UI, add its real isolation row/control in that coherent publication slice. Reuse existing gate commands and publishability authority; do not build a general manifest framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- The current pre-publication tree remains green without classifying UI as permanently always-present.
- Adding :clein/build to implementation/ui/deps.edn while no UI isolation row/gate exists makes ordinary bundle-isolation completeness fail and name ui.
- Adding a new publishable browser adapter under implementation/adapters without a generic or dedicated isolation gate makes completeness fail and name the adapter.
- Existing adapters are explicitly accounted for by their real generic/dedicated gates; nested adapter paths are not silently skipped.
- Both mutations are executable and permanent, not only comments or manual proofs.
- The eventual UI gate uses live browser-runtime sentinels, a real matching-options emitted positive control, and a legitimate UI-free negative bundle.
- Existing Resources coverage, current adapter gates, all other canonical optional runtimes, and release-inventory enforcement remain green with one source of publishability truth.
- rf2-vxgfnd.99.2 cannot complete UI publication while the UI bundle-isolation obligation is absent.
notes: COMPLETENESS EXPANSION (same root defect, not a second issue): implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs scans only top-level implementation/* directories and explicitly ignores implementation/adapters/*. The release lockstep authority scans both flat artefacts and nested adapters. Existing adapters happen to have dedicated isolation gates, but a newly publishable adapter is never auto-enrolled and can gain :clein/build without either an ARTEFACTS row or a dedicated gate. This is a second direct counterexample to rf2-sh0sp4 AC6. The correction should use the same bounded flat-plus-adapters discovery and require every discovered browser runtime to map to a real generic or dedicated isolation gate.
close_reason: shipped #6109 (merged): bundle-iso enrollment discover-by-convention + fail-closed; UI-exclusion removed

title: Make re-frame.ui.test API drift enforcement catch host-specific arity changes
description:
## Problem

PR #5972 / `rf2-vxgfnd.200` enrolled the nine blessed `re-frame.ui.test` vars in the generated API manifest and the CLJS public-surface probe, but it did not deliver the source Bead's explicit arity-drift acceptance criterion.

The JVM generator reduces every public var to `[symbol kind]`; its manifest rows contain namespace/name/classification/kind but no arglists or arity facts. The CLJS analyzer emits `[name kind]`, and `cljs-probe/reconcile` reduces those pairs to names. Therefore a function or macro can retain its public name and `:kind` while losing, adding, or reshaping a supported arity, and every ordinary manifest/projection gate remains green.

This matters immediately because the public contract is host-specific: `re-frame.ui.test/flush!` is zero-arity on the JVM but zero/one-arity on CLJS; `with-root` and `render` are macros with blessed call grammars. The drift boundary claims to reconcile the reader-conditional hosts, yet currently verifies only existence.

## Reproduction

In a disposable JVM process on current main, replace `re-frame.ui.test/flush!` with a one-arity root and change its `:arglists` metadata from `([])` to `([changed-arity])`; `gen/build-manifest` before and after is exactly equal and the row is unchanged. An independent reproduction changed `query` from `[root css-selector]` to `[root selector extra]` with the same result. Source inspection proves the CLJS lane is equally name-only. The current manifest `--check`, 59-test projection suite, and selected CLJS probe all pass because none observes signatures.

No all-status Bead owns this exact false-green. Closed `rf2-vxgfnd.200` is the incomplete source owner; closed `rf2-e5692s` owns later API page/member coverage, not call signatures.
design: Extend the existing drift boundary with the smallest coherent host-aware signature check. Keep one optional machine-readable signature authority for the nine `re-frame.ui.test` rows, derive live JVM arities from Var metadata and live CLJS arities from analyzer information, normalize macro/compiler details, and compare each host against its declared contract. Do not populate or redesign all 498 manifest rows unless the reusable mechanism makes that genuinely simpler; do not add a second hand-maintained namespace inventory or parse prose as the authority.
acceptance_criteria:
- The blessed `re-frame.ui.test` surface has an explicit host-aware signature contract covering all nine public vars, including the JVM/CLJS difference for `flush!` and the macro grammars for `render` and `with-root`.
- Removing, adding, or reshaping a supported JVM arity makes the ordinary API drift gate red while name and kind remain unchanged.
- The corresponding CLJS-only arity mutations make the CLJS manifest probe red; reader-conditional differences are represented intentionally rather than forced equal.
- Macro arities are normalized to programmer-visible call shapes; compiler-internal parameters do not leak into the contract.
- Existing add/remove/rename/visibility checks and generated API projections remain single-source and green.
- Mutation tests prove both host lanes fail before the fix and pass after it; no production dependency or bundle residue is introduced.
close_reason: shipped #6108 (merged): ui.test host-arity drift via :ui-test-signatures sidecar

title: Enforce UI compiler-carrier identity at every read, write, and finish boundary
description:
PR #5970 / rf2-vxgfnd.192 introduced ambient-build-id to make the re-frame.ui private carrier authoritative and fail before mutation when its build id is missing or disagrees with Shadow. The validation is not on the actual registry paths. ambient-shadow-slice and ambient-accepted-slice read the compiler state directly; update-current-slice! checks only ui-owned-compiler-state? before mutating scratch/overlay; shadow-finish-candidate trusts its explicit build-id argument. Thus contribute!, aggregate and the property/descriptor/digest helpers can bypass the check that current-build-id performs.

Deterministic current-main reproduction: prepare a private carrier for :A, attach a still-present Shadow bridge id :B, and bind it as cljs.env/*compiler*. contribute! accepts :a/view and aggregate exposes it. current-build-id correctly throws ::private-build-id-shadow-disagreement, yet shadow-finish-candidate succeeds with explicit id :B and returns a snapshot stamped :build-id :B containing A's registry row. A private carrier missing its id likewise lets contribute! create an overlay and exposes the row even though current-build-id throws. A recognized Shadow bridge with no id can also downgrade to the session fallback when no fallback pass is marked open, despite the contract reserving fallback for genuinely plain environments with neither marker nor carrier.

This violates the source bead's fail-before-any-mutation guarantee and can cross-publish registries/digests under contradictory build authority. Focused compiler tests pass because they assert malformed identity only through current-build-id. All-status searches found no exact owner: closed .192 is incomplete; open .195 owns broader real-Shadow integration proof, not this code correction.
acceptance_criteria:
- One validated compiler-state resolver owns private-carrier presence, build-id extraction, and private-versus-Shadow agreement; ambient accepted/scratch/overlay reads and writes all traverse it.
- Missing private identity, a recognized Shadow bridge with no identity, or private/Shadow disagreement makes contribute!, aggregate/committed reads, element/property/descriptor lookups, pass/digest reads, and other ambient helpers fail before observing or mutating the malformed carrier.
- shadow-finish-candidate validates its supplied build id against the accepted private carrier and any still-present Shadow identity before deriving a candidate; contradictory A/B state cannot produce or carry a B-stamped snapshot containing A rows.
- Negative fixtures cover missing private id, missing bridge id, private/Shadow disagreement, ambient contribution/read bypass, and explicit finish bypass, asserting the compiler-env remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Valid private state with the outer marker absent still works; an agreeing canonical marker works; session fallback remains only for a genuinely plain CLJS/REPL environment with neither recognized marker nor private carrier.
- No speculative future-Shadow aliases, second successful-build authority, public API, or compatibility layer is added.
close_reason: shipped #6244

title: Close G-12 false greens for reagent2 and a missing Clojure CLI
description:
The G-12 isolation gate from PR #5964 / rf2-vxgfnd.202 has two reproducible false-green paths.

First, Arm 1 forbids reagent.*, uix.*, helix.*, and the four adapter namespaces, but Reagent Slim's real module namespace root is reagent2.*. The exported checker reports reagent.core.js as forbidden while reagent2.core.js is accepted. Because the consolidated Shadow source paths include adapters/reagent-slim/src, a direct reagent2.core import from first-party UI can enter the selected module closure without adding day8/reagent-slim to ui/deps.edn; Arm 1 misses it and Arm 2 sees no forbidden coordinate. The self-test covers Slim only in coordinate form, so it does not exercise this central mutation class.

Second, the default/full command exits 0 and labels the result PASS when Clojure CLI is absent, even though resolved-graph Arm 2 did not run. Current CI provisions Clojure (closed rf2-3kewru), so this is a local/general gate-integrity defect rather than an active CI escape. A reduced modules-only diagnostic can be useful, but it must be explicit and must not claim full G-12 success.

Reproductions on current main: forbiddenModules([reagent.core.js]) => [reagent.core.js], forbiddenModules([reagent2.core.js]) => []; running the default script with an empty PATH exits 0 with resolved-graph Arm 2 skipped. The real two-arm gate passes 302 selected imports / 15 coordinates and self-test passes, demonstrating the missing controls. All-status searches found no live owner; rf2-3kewru only owns CI toolchain provisioning.
acceptance_criteria:
- Arm 1 rejects the actual reagent2 namespace root used by day8/reagent-slim, using exact namespace-boundary matching without rejecting lookalikes.
- A mutation/self-test proves a direct reagent2.core import in the focused first-party UI closure goes red even when no forbidden coordinate is declared; positive and lookalike controls remain green.
- The default full G-12 command fails closed when Clojure CLI is unavailable or Arm 2 cannot execute. If a modules-only mode is retained, it is explicitly requested and is not reported as a full G-12 PASS.
- Subprocess fixtures cover absent CLI, present-but-untrusted CLI, and spawn failure without shell execution.
- Gate/CI commentary describes wrapper-free experimental substrate isolation: Reagent, UIx, and reagent-slim remain supported siblings; only Helix is retired. No denylist weakening or compatibility machinery is added.
- Self-test and the live two-arm gate pass with the normal toolchain.
close_reason: shipped via PR #6103 (merged): G-12 false greens closed (reagent2 forbidden root + missing-CLI fails closed; mutation-proven; wrapper-free siblings framing)

title: Enforce root verb kinds and literal options in the API drift gate
description:

The API Markdown checker uses the M/Fn cell only as a row classifier, then retains name, qualifier, tier, and line; reconcile compares identity and tier only. It does not compare the documented kind with manifest metadata and does not inspect or otherwise pin create-root's literal-option grammar.

Consequently the focused checker can stay green if the create-root API row changes from M to Fn, drops required :root-id, or admits :disambiguator. Current prose/runtime are aligned, and the later closed rf2-rutuxr repaired retained working-document drift; this bead is the remaining regression-proofing gap, not a compatibility or runtime change. Evidence: implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/api_md_check.clj:88-91, 181-190, 197-250 and the closed source bead's acceptance criteria. All-status searches found no live owner.
acceptance_criteria:
- A focused docs/API consistency gate fails if create-root, render!, or hydrate-root is documented with the wrong public Var kind, or unmount! is documented as anything other than a function.
- The gate fails if create-root's public contract loses required authored :root-id or admits :disambiguator.
- Mutation/unit fixtures prove each wrong-kind, missing-root-id, and admitted-disambiguator case goes red; the committed API/spec/source state stays green.

title: Classify rf.ui tree keys semantically in Conventions
description:
The canonical spec/Conventions.md row for :rf.ui/* and its docs/spec mirror still call :rf.ui/tree-version and :rf.ui/property-props reserved diagnostic keys, tell consumers that unknown :rf.ui/* keys may be ignored, and say normalization strips them all. That contradicts Spec 004B and the shipped normalizer: tree-version is a required schema gate, while property-props is semantic conversion input that MUST be consumed before the marker is removed. A consumer following Conventions can strip property-props early and leak property-only custom-element values into semantic attrs and fingerprints—the exact corruption PR #5967 / rf2-vxgfnd.190 repaired elsewhere.

Evidence: spec/Conventions.md:100; docs/spec/Conventions.md:100; spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:137-160; implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/semantic.cljc:159-164. Focused semantic normalization gate passes 9 tests / 93 assertions, so this is a current contract contradiction rather than a runtime defect. All-status searches found no live owner beyond the closed source bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- The canonical :rf.ui/* Conventions row distinguishes :rf.ui/tree-version as a required gate, :rf.ui/property-props as semantic input consumed before removal, and :rf.ui/presence / :rf.ui/boundary as optional diagnostics.
- Unknown additive :rf.ui/* keys remain ignorable without implying that known required or semantic keys may be ignored.
- spec/Conventions.md and docs/spec/Conventions.md agree, and the normal doc synchronization/slug gates pass.
- The wording points to the owning Spec 004B classification instead of creating a second, divergent authority.

title: Finish falsy failure preservation across UI teardown boundaries
description: PR #5965 fixed presence tracking only in re-frame.ui.test/with-root while closing source bead rf2-vxgfnd.201, whose other four production teardown boundaries remain truthiness-based on current main. reactive/teardown-root! uses a nil-initialized host-error and truthy branches, so throw false/nil can take the success/deferred victim path, miss the exact-root fail-closed sweep, settle/release ownership, and never rethrow. client/reclaim-consumed-container! can overwrite or swallow a falsy first cleanup failure; drain-live-roots! uses when-let on the first error and suppresses a non-empty vector whose primary is false/nil; substrate/dispose-adapter! uses nil slots and a truthy cond, losing failures and primary ordering. Later quarantine/reporter work still relies on these decisions.
design: Apply the same small presence convention already landed in ui.test: a private absent sentinel or tagged slot in each relevant namespace, and seq/count for the error vector. Attempt every cleanup, preserve the exact first thrown value, and retain later failures through the existing diagnostic route with a primitive-safe fallback. Do not coerce programmer-thrown values or introduce a general error framework.
acceptance_criteria: Host unmount false/nil triggers the exact-root fail-closed ViewCell sweep, retains quarantine/ownership invariants, and rethrows the identical value after cleanup. Container reclaim, live-root draining, and composed adapter disposal cannot suppress or reorder a non-empty failure set because its first payload is falsy. All sibling/root/spine cleanup is attempted; later errors stay observable for primitive primaries. Focused tests cover nil, false, Error, mixed primary/secondary order, and mutations restoring truthiness. A source audit finds no remaining caught-error slot in these four boundaries that conflates payload with presence.

title: Surface native derived subscriber failures after contained fan-out
description: PR #5961 fixed rf= movement and sibling containment in native derived fan-out, but the captured primary failure is rethrown directly into drain-scheduler!, whose per-thunk catch discards every escape. Programmer errors therefore remain silent and the source bead's explicit observability acceptance criterion is unmet. The shipped tests prove sibling delivery and falsey capture but assert the initiating replace returns normally; they never observe the original thrown value. The same delivery boundary also lacks the required watcher add/remove snapshot and re-entrant-write proofs, and ordinary one-subscriber movement now allocates a volatile capture cell despite the requested common-path preservation/measurement.
design: Keep this bounded to the existing scheduler/fan-out seam. Attempt every sibling from a snapshot, retain the first escape by presence, drain the queued scheduler work and restore scheduler state, then surface the primary value through the established caller/error channel. Preserve a direct zero/one-subscriber fast path where possible; measure if the simplest correct shape cannot. Do not add a general event bus.
acceptance_criteria: A throwing derived subscriber cannot suppress siblings, and the primary thrown value is observable after delivery with identity preserved, including false/nil-equivalent CLJS throws where representable. Scheduler state is restored and queued/re-entrant writes remain a later pass. Tests cover both subscriber orders, watcher add/remove snapshot semantics, re-entrant writes, and fail against #5961. The zero/one-subscriber common path is allocation-free or its cost is explicitly measured and justified.

title: Make frame-destroyed attribution operation-realm aware and complete
description:
PR #5954 added exact :op to the compiled frame-bundle :rf.error/frame-destroyed records, but source-coordinate resolution ignores it. error_emit/error-source-coord handles every frame-destroyed category by trying [:sub id] before [:event id]. Event and subscription ids live in separate registries and may legitimately share a keyword, as PR #5957 itself demonstrates.

Therefore a stale bundle :dispatch or :dispatch-sync of [:x ...] is attributed to an unrelated subscription :x whenever both exist. A stale :subscribe has the inverse requirement. Off-box tooling points the programmer or AI at the wrong definition. Current comments incorrectly claim a sub id cannot collide with an event id.

The same helper also drops the attempted payload from the typed exception: thrown ex-data contains only :frame and :op even though rf2-vxgfnd.230 required the typed throw to carry attempted-payload attribution. Tests retain only err-id and cannot detect either gap.

Make source lookup operation/realm aware through a private input: dispatch and dispatch-sync resolve :event, subscribe resolves :sub, capture has no component source. Do not expose a new public record field merely to steer an internal lookup. Make the typed exception carry the safe attempted-payload evidence agreed by the stale-payload privacy correction, plus its head. Keep the shared category and exact-one fan-out.
acceptance_criteria: Same-keyword event and subscription registrations are discriminated correctly for frame-destroyed errors: dispatch/dispatch-sync records carry the event coordinate, subscribe carries the subscription coordinate, and capture fabricates neither. Tests cover both collision directions and programmatic registrations with no coordinate. The private steering input does not become a public schema slot. Typed stale-operation exceptions carry frame, op, attempted payload evidence, and event/query head without weakening the fail-closed payload policy in rf2-01ihi. Every arm still emits exactly one always-on record plus one dev trace and then throws the same category. Existing core router/subs frame-destroyed emitters remain correct.
close_reason: shipped #6131 (merged): frame-destroyed source-coord realm-aware via :op

title: Fence older-first overlapping UI digest activations
description:
PR #5953 added a global monotone generation/high-water pair to digest_carrier, which correctly handles newest-first overlap completion. It cannot identify which reload an after-load callback belongs to because after-load carries no cycle token.

Deterministic older-first interleaving on current main:
1. accepted generation 1 is published.
2. reload A runs before-load and stages dA as generation 2.
3. reload B runs before-load and stages dB as generation 3, but its application sources have not completed.
4. older A after-load runs first.
5. A reads the global generation 3 > activated 1, publishes dB and clears updating before B finishes.
6. If B then throws and skips after-load, current continues advertising dB forever instead of remaining fail-closed.

The shipped fixture explicitly releases newest-first and therefore cannot catch this. The closed source bead's close reason acknowledges the older-first residual, but no open bead owns it. Establish exact activation-cycle ownership or explicitly serialize/reject overlapping script reloads. Keep it dev-only and local; no general scheduler.
acceptance_criteria: RULED 2026-07-18 (delegated per Mike, see notes): keep shipped high-water semantics; doc/test PR only. (1) Carrier semantics unchanged: the generation/activated high-water rule stays; no FIFO/serialization, no overlap-reject fence, no loader-mode detection, no change to stage!/before-load/after-load behavior. (2) Docstring truth: the false ":script reload sources load asynchronously" premise in digest_carrier.cljs (lines 33-35 area) is replaced with the verified host fact (Shadow 3.4.10 reload chain is one synchronous macrotask absent explicit :dev/*-load-async hooks; :loader-mode affects initial-load flush only), and reload atomicity is named as a load-bearing host assumption to re-verify on any Shadow upgrade. (3) check-ui-digest-carrier.cjs: the c3 preamble's copy of the same false premise is corrected, and an older-first characterization stanza is added (before A / stage dA / before B / stage dB / after -> publishes dB early in the modeled world) whose comment carries the reachability rationale and cites the ruling. (4) Existing newest-first, stale-after-newer-fence, initial-load, and failed-reload recovery fixture cases remain green. (5) Advanced production remains free of the carrier machinery; no general concurrency abstraction.
notes:
BLOCKED on premise contradiction (czh5k analysis 2026-07-17, ~70min read-only, 0 edits). The digest-carrier after-load fix (digest_carrier.cljs:145-164, the ^:dev/after-load high-water rule from #5953) must satisfy two PROVABLY INCOMPATIBLE ACs: (a) 'failed-reload recovery stays green' → after-load MUST publish; (b) 'AC1 older-first fence' → overlapping older after-load must NOT publish. At the deciding after-load BOTH present identical carrier state (2 before-loads, 2 stages, 0 prior after-loads, generation 2-ahead-of-activated); Shadow's zero-arg :dev/after-load carries no cycle token, so a THROWN reload is locally indistinguishable from an IN-FLIGHT overlapping reload — opposite handling required, distinguishing fact is future/unobservable. Also the bead's own two new clauses (older-first-B-succeeds-publishes-dB vs B-throws-forward-recovery-publishes-dC) are mutually exclusive for the same reason. Context: :script loader-mode (only mode with older-first overlap) is NOT used for HMR in-repo (only a fixture) — purely defensive for downstream :script consumers. OPTIONS (Mike decides): (A) mode-gated serialize — under :script FIFO cycle-ownership (promote oldest unpromoted), :eval unchanged; achieves fence + older-first-B-succeeds, all tests green, residual: B-throws-recovery needs 1 extra clean :script reload; depends on :loader-mode runtime-readable (unconfirmed). (B) reject-overlap — overlapping reloads don't publish, next clean reload recovers; older-first-B publishes on NEXT reload not at B's after-load. (C) relax the acceptance — drop EITHER older-first-B-publishes-at-completion OR B-throws-recovery-publishes-once (they're exclusive). czh5k REC: (C) relax to preferred behavior, then implement (A) [closest to exact-cycle-ownership, zero test risk].
DECISION (2026-07-18, delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18): ADOPT OPTION C — keep the shipped generation/activated high-water semantics in digest_carrier.cljs unchanged. REJECT the dossier's Option B (reject/fence overlap) and the earlier notes' "relax then implement A" plan. One small doc/test PR closes this bead; no semantic change.

RATIONALE (keystones independently re-verified before ruling): (1) digest_carrier.cljs:160-164 is exactly the modeled state machine — after-load promotes whenever generation > activated, publishing whatever :staged holds. (2) Pinned Shadow 3.4.10 sources (client/browser.cljs:23-40 + 71-96, client/env.cljs:191-252, verified from the .m2 jar): hot reload is one synchronous macrotask — websocket load-sources -> do-js-reload -> do-js-load, a synchronous doseq of goog.globalEval; before-load hooks FILO, after-load FIFO; async only via explicit :dev/*-load-async hooks (zero in this repo, grep empty); hook throws still call next, only a load throw aborts. :loader-mode branches only the INITIAL-LOAD flush format — the carrier docstring's ":script loads reload sources asynchronously" premise (digest_carrier.cljs:33-35) is FALSE for reload on 3.4.10. So the feared older-first interleaving is unreachable on the pinned host: "staged but in flight" never spans a task boundary, and every reachable history (serialized chains, throw-then-recover, stale stragglers) is already handled correctly by the shipped rule. (3) Option B is unsound as stated: its trigger — a second before-load arriving while fenced — is exactly the signature of the TESTED throw-then-recover path (check-ui-digest-carrier.cjs:696-734), so B demotes every failed-reload recovery to a full page refresh; its ":eval recovery unchanged" claim is wrong. (4) Option A rests on the false :script-async premise and adds scheduler machinery for an unreachable corner — posture forbids. HOST-FACT COUPLING: correctness is now EXPLICITLY pinned to Shadow 3.4.10's reload atomicity. REVISIT TRIGGER: a Shadow upgrade that makes reload loading async (e.g. a CSP-safe script-injection reload path) RE-OPENS the hazard — re-verify atomicity on every Shadow bump alongside 004C section 2.1.1's pins; upstream shipping a reload cycle token or a load-failure hook converts this into Option D as a small exact fix with no contract change.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (one doc/test PR, no semantic change): (i) digest_carrier.cljs docstring — replace the false async premise (lines 33-35, revising the 33-51 overlap paragraph) with the verified host fact (Shadow 3.4.10 reload chain = one synchronous macrotask absent explicit :dev/*-load-async hooks; :loader-mode affects initial-load flush only) and name reload atomicity as a load-bearing host assumption to re-verify on any Shadow upgrade. (ii) implementation/scripts/check-ui-digest-carrier.cjs — correct the same false premise repeated in the c3 preamble (lines 736-741), and append an OLDER-FIRST CHARACTERIZATION stanza after the existing c3 block (~line 808): before(A)/stage(dA)/before(B)/stage(dB)/after -> pin that the stale A release publishes the newest staged digest dB early in the modeled world; the stanza comment MUST carry the reachability rationale and cite this ruling (documented modeled behavior, NOT an endorsed race). (iii) Close this bead on that PR. OUT OF SCOPE: FIFO/serialization or overlap-reject machinery, loader-mode runtime detection, Shadow patches, any change to stage!/before-load/after-load semantics, spec edits (004C section 2.1/2.1.1 already promises only "consumers activate only successful build output"; EP-0032 does not govern this surface). HONEST RESIDUAL LEFT OPEN: a downstream consumer registering an async after-load hook in a namespace linearized before the carrier, plus an overlapping reload whose load throws, could see a false advertised digest in dev until the next successful reload or page refresh — dev-only, self-healing, not constructible in-repo; the fail-closed ideal is genuinely unmet in that corner.

AC AMENDMENT (old -> new): DROPPED the two provably incompatible clauses — "an older A completion after newer B has staged cannot publish B or clear B's fence" and "an older-first fixture keeps current nil until B's own successful completion; a B-throws variant stays fail-closed and later forward recovery publishes the newest accepted generation once" — and DROPPED "each completion is tied to its cycle or overlap is explicitly serialized/rejected" (no host cycle token exists). KEPT: existing newest-first, stale-after-newer-fence, initial-load, and failed-reload recovery cases remain green; advanced production remains free of the carrier machinery; no general concurrency abstraction. ADDED: docstring host-fact correction + load-bearing-assumption note; older-first characterization stanza with reachability rationale.

FOR THE MAYOR: the decision gating the six-bead reload lane is now made; the lane's structural deps on rf2-czh5k can be released as each brief allows (this bead closes on the doc/test PR above). Deps not modified here per the delegation's rules.

title: Reject malformed letfn* bindings through the typed UI compiler surface
description:
PR #5950 split host letfn* from source letfn and correctly handles legal flat bindings, mutual scope, deferred function bodies, and typed odd/non-symbol failures. Its new rw-letfn* validator still checks only vector parity plus symbol?, then blindly rewrites each initializer.

Current-main counterexamples:
- (letfn* [f 42] f) is accepted by the UI analyzer and fails later in the host compiler.
- (letfn* [f (fn* 42)] f) throws a raw IllegalArgumentException during analysis: Do not know how to create ISeq from java.lang.Long.
- a qualified binding name such as foo/bar is accepted even though the host rejects qualified local names.

This violates rf2-vxgfnd.221's typed-diagnostic contract for malformed flat grammar and leaves AI/programmer feedback dependent on a later raw compiler failure. Held rf2-vxgfnd.224 remains sound: this explicit binder branch needs bounded grammar validation; it does not justify a general special-form roster.

Validate simple unqualified names and legal fn/fn* initializer shape before recursive rewriting, failing through existing :rf.ui.compile/bad-let with useful guidance. Keep the fix local; add no new error id or grammar framework.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed letfn* initializers, qualified names, malformed fn/fn* arities/argv shapes, odd bindings, and non-symbol names all fail deterministically through :rf.ui.compile/bad-let on both hosts, never a raw host exception or later compiler crash. Legal flat letfn* forms retain exact shape, mutual recursion, local shadowing, outer-site lowering, and deferred-body rejection. Focused analyze accept/reject suites include falsifiers for [f 42], malformed fn*, and a qualified name. No special-form roster or new error category is introduced.

title: Teach caller-owned frame cleanup consistently across testing and AI surfaces
description:
PR #5945 added two AI-facing testing recipes that create caller-owned frames with bare rf/make-frame and never release them. The same misleading pattern remains in the installed testing skill and the re-frame.ui.test API docstring/generated page. ui.test/render does not own a frame supplied through {:frame ...}; copied tests leave a live frame in rf/frame-ids and contaminate later tests. A current-main repro changed frame-ids from #{:rf/default} to #{:rf/default :rf.frame/<id>}; the equivalent rf/with-new-frame control leaves no residue. Closed rf2-vxgfnd.279 fixed the public guide only; open W2/W6 promotion beads do not own this current lifecycle-teaching defect.

Keep the correction small and coherent across:
- ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/skill/SKILL.md
- ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/prep/w2-migration-skill-extension.md
- skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing.md
- implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/test.cljc and regenerated docs/api/re-frame.ui.test.md

Teach rf/with-new-frame for synchronous examples and explicit finally/settlement cleanup where ownership crosses async work. State plainly that externally supplied frames remain caller-owned. Remove the false claim that a bare make-frame value is discarded with the test. Do not add a helper framework or hidden ownership magic.
acceptance_criteria: Every copied synchronous recipe releases its frame through rf/with-new-frame; asynchronous recipes release in a primary-failure-preserving finally/settlement path. ui.test/render documentation explicitly says supplied frames are caller-owned. The installed skill no longer says a bare frame is discarded with the test. Generated API docs are refreshed. A deterministic frame-ids regression proves normal and throwing examples leave no residue. Existing render tests remain green; no new public API or cleanup abstraction.

title: DECISION: late-bind DI hook keys (~300) use bare non-rf-root prefixes (:epoch/* :schemas/* :router/* …) — accept internal carve-out or unify under :rf.*?
description:
PROBLEM: The late-bind hook registry (re-frame.late-bind — cross-namespace/cross-artefact forward-reference DI seam so core does not hard-require optional artefacts) keys every hook with a BARE non-rf-root artefact prefix. This is the single largest body of framework keywords outside the :rf.* scheme (~300 keys). Distinct prefixes found via grep over implementation/core: :late-bind/* [111], :epoch/* [24], :schemas/* [19], :error-emit/* [13], :adapter/* [9], :router/* [8], :flows/* [8], :ui/* [5], :observability/* [5], :ssr/* [3], :routing/* [3], :live-frame/* [3], :trace/* [2], :reagent/* [2], :machines/* [2], :http/* [2], :views/* [1], :subs/* [1], :resources/* [1], :event-emit/*. Examples: :epoch/settle!, :schemas/validate-event!, :router/dispatch!, :flows/run-flows-on-db (see late_bind.cljc, core_epoch.cljc:31, core.cljc:2591).

CONTEXT: These are PURELY INTERNAL — a load-time function registry (set-fn!/get-fn), never on any public surface (not app-db, not trace, not error ex-data, not a return value). Already disciplined: an authoritative inventory (re-frame.late-bind.directory) + a drift test enforce the key set. Per the two-regime rule they read as 'closed-local grammar' (regime 1) — EXCEPT regime 1 sanctions BARE (unqualified) local keys, whereas these are namespaced under a NON-rf root, which the scheme does not otherwise permit for framework ids.

OPTIONS:
(A) ACCEPT as an internal-DI carve-out — document in Conventions that the late-bind hook registry is exempt from the :rf.* scheme (internal wiring, never public, own directory+drift-test). Cheapest; preserves the artefact-named grouping that makes the registry readable.
(B) UNIFY under :rf.* — e.g. :rf.hook/epoch-settle! or :rf.late-bind.epoch/settle! (keep artefact grouping as a dotted sub-area). Consistent with the framework's one-language identity. Cost: ~300 key renames across producer set-fn! sites + consumer get-fn sites + the directory + the drift-test; purely mechanical, no functional change (pre-alpha, no back-compat).

CONSEQUENCE: (A) = one Conventions.md note (hot-zone). (B) = large mechanical sweep across implementation/core, own coordinated PR.

RECOMMENDATION: LEAN (A) — the :rf.* scheme is explicitly for the PUBLIC framework surface (Conventions L8 enumerates events/fx/cofx/app-db/trace/errors/warnings), and these keys are invisible internal plumbing with their own guardrails; unifying is ~300 renames for zero public-surface benefit. BUT flag the tension: the rf2-lgeron require-alias ruling chose consistency 'INCLUDING keywords, the deciding lens' even on a non-public authoring surface — by that same lens Mike may prefer (B). Genuine call.

(from rf2-099q90 keyword audit; see ai/findings/2026-07-17-keyword-surface-audit.md §Non-reserved framework surfaces)
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-18, delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18): Option A — keep all 216 artefact-prefixed late-bind hook keys as-is. NO renames, NO aliases, NO migration layer.

RATIONALE: The carve-out already exists as normative spec text — spec/Conventions.md:1697-1716 (section "Late-bind hook key grammar", landed rf2-l8fi6 / commit b88578c8bb) specifies exactly these names, with the directory + drift test as authority. The real defect is that Conventions line 8 ("one root keyword namespace") and line 24 ("there is no third shape") were written without cross-referencing that section, so the file argues with itself. This ruling is therefore a RECONCILIATION, not a new rule. Option B was rejected: verified blast radius is ~2,840 occurrences across ~440 files including 7 sequential hot-zone spec files (not the "~300 renames" the bead estimated), it rewrites a normative grammar a prior ruling landed, and it dilutes the :rf.* signal (may-be-contract-bearing) across private wiring — gold-plating under the pre-alpha pragmatic posture. Option C (two dialects) strictly dominated. Verified during ruling: grammar section confirmed by direct read; :rf2/runtime-version confirmed host-facing (spec/011-SSR.md:64 — "when the host registers the hook at boot") with NO directory.cljc row — so the exception must be stated as the DATA boundary, not "never an extension point".

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (one small PR; spec/Conventions.md is hot-zone — sequence it):
1. In the Reserved-namespaces / two-regime area (spec/Conventions.md:8 and :24), add a cross-link sentence: late-bind registry ADDRESSES are a sanctioned key shape governed by the "Late-bind hook key grammar" section (line 1697) — internal wiring addresses, not framework data identifiers. Soften "no third shape" (line 24) and the line-8 "one root" claim to acknowledge that section (which already sanctions the :rf2/ root at line 1705).
2. State the exception as the DATA boundary: hook keys MUST NOT appear as identifiers on any runtime data surface (trace tags/values, error ex-data, app-db keys, serialized/wire payloads); a key that must cross such a boundary takes the applicable reserved :rf.* vocabulary. Do NOT write "never escapes through extension contracts" — falsified by :rf2/runtime-version.
OUT OF SCOPE: renaming any of the 216 directory keys; any implementation/ src or test change; the conformance fixture capability vocabulary (:fixture/capabilities — :routing/match-url deliberately names both a hook and a capability, different registries); rewriting the grammar-section rules beyond an optional one-line preamble touch-up.
TRAPS FOR THE WORKER: (a) the bead census is polluted — ":late-bind/* [111]" counted the FUNCTION alias late-bind/set-fn!, not keywords; true inventory = 216 directory entries across ~30 prefixes; (b) tools/story publishes :subs/resolve-sub-override outside the directory BY DESIGN (see late_bind_drift_test.clj:41-56 docstring) — not a violation, no action; (c) hook keys DO appear in spec/docs prose (~259 mentions) — prose mentions are fine, the boundary is runtime data.
FOLLOW-UP: see discovered-from child bead for the :rf2/runtime-version governance gap (host-facing, spec-documented, no directory row, outside the drift gate).

title: DECISION: tool-surface :rf.* keyword hygiene — reserve 2 cross-tool namespaces + fix 4 tool-internal shadow/generic segments
description:
PROBLEM: Six :rf.* namespaces live on the TOOL surface but are absent from the Conventions single-root reserved-set table. Two are legitimate cross-tool namespaces MISSING a reservation; four are tool-internal segments that either shadow a reserved full-word or use a generic (non-tool-scoped) name. The framework public core is clean — these are the only shape-conformance items outside the late-bind registry (rf2-099q90 audit).

GROUP C1 — MISSING RESERVATIONS (legit cross-tool namespaces, fix = ADD a reserved-set row like :rf.privacy/*, NOT a rename):
- :rf.editor/* (member :rf.editor/open [82]) — a cross-tool reg-fx BOTH Story and Xray register idempotently (tools/story/.../open_in_editor.cljs:384: 'gate is editor-related, not Story-specific'). Exactly the :rf.privacy/* rationale (Conventions L86) but not in the table.
- :rf.tool/* (member :rf.tool/no-frame-selected [4]) — a cross-tool refusal stamp normatively specified in spec/002-Frames.md:217 and spec/Tool-Pair.md:497. Not in the table. (Sibling stamp :ambiguous-frame is bare — mild asymmetry.) Alt for this one: fold onto :rf.error/* since it is a refusal discriminator.

GROUP C2 — SHADOW/GENERIC SEGMENTS (fix = rename to tool-owned :rf.<tool>/* or the reserved full-word):
- :rf.prov/* (:rf.prov/ns|standard|inline|unknown, Xray image-provenance projection :kind values) — MISNOMER: shadows reserved :rf.provenance/* (L52). Rec: :rf.xray/prov-* or reuse full :rf.provenance/*.
- :rf.warn/* (:rf.warn/schema, Story warn-tape kind) — MISNOMER: shadows reserved :rf.warning/* (L73). Rec: :rf.story/warn-schema or :rf.assert/*.
- :rf.config/* (:rf.config/severity|input|issue|effect|keys, pair-mcp rejected-config record) — DRIFT: generic segment. Rec: scope under the pair tool ns.
- :rf.source/* (:rf.source/uri, pair-mcp handler-meta editor-jump link) — DRIFT: generic segment, adjacent to reserved :rf.handler/source (L62). Rec: fold onto :rf.handler/uri or tool-scope.

CONSEQUENCE: C1 = Conventions.md hot-zone additions (2 table rows) + no code rename. C2 = tool-local keyword renames (bundle-isolated tool dirs; pre-alpha, no back-compat) + any spec/tool-spec touches. C1 and C2 can be separate PRs.

RECOMMENDATION: Do C1 (reserve :rf.editor/* and :rf.tool/*) — clear gap, additive, low-risk. For C2, STRONG rec to kill the two shadow-abbreviations (:rf.prov/, :rf.warn/) since they visually collide with reserved namespaces; :rf.config/ + :rf.source/ are lower urgency (tool-internal, no collision).

(from rf2-099q90 keyword audit; see ai/findings/2026-07-17-keyword-surface-audit.md §Non-reserved framework surfaces + §Candidate 3)
acceptance_criteria: 1. Conventions reserved-set table gains an :rf.editor/* row; NO :rf.tool/* row is added. 2. spec/002-Frames.md + spec/Tool-Pair.md spell the unselected-frame stamp bare :no-frame-selected. 3. Xray provenance :kind values are bare (:ns :inline :standard :unknown); no :rf.prov/* remains in tracked sources. 4. No :rf.warn/* remains in tracked sources (prose corrected to :rf.warning/* / the :schema-violations projection; test mock respelled); no :rf.story.warning/* keyword is introduced. 5. pair-mcp launch-diagnostic maps use bare keys; no :rf.config/* remains. 6. :rf.source/uri is fully replaced by :rf.mcp/source-uri with Conventions row + wire-vocab README pinned entry + vocab.cljc constant + descriptors/spec/skill updated in one PR; uncontracted-marker scan and skill-drift gate green.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-18, delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18) — six dispositions, adopting the Fable C-prime modification of Option C; refuted premises independently re-verified by grep before adoption:
1. :rf.editor/* — RESERVE. Add one additive Conventions reserved-set row (cross-tool editor integration, :rf.privacy/* model). No code change.

notes:
DECISION (2026-07-18, delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18): Option A — KEEP the :rf.nav/* / :rf.route/* two-prefix split. NO rename (options B and C rejected; D rejected outright). Bead reshaped from rename-decision into the doc-drift-fix task below.

RATIONALE (decisive): The split is SPEC-NORMATIVE, not drift. spec/Conventions.md:417 (fx sub-namespace rule, "Audit Finding 2") carries a written membership criterion — an fx-id lives under :rf.nav/* when it is a navigation PRIMITIVE: a thin wrapper over a browser/host navigation API (pushState/replaceState/scroll) that is NOT route-aware (no nav-token threading, no :on-match dispatch, no schema validation) — and states verbatim: "The split from :rf.route/* is deliberate: :rf.nav/* fx-ids could be invoked by a non-routing app that wants the primitive without the routing slice; :rf.route/* fx-ids require the routing artefact's slice and tokens to be meaningful." Override tiers track the criterion (all four :rf.nav/* fx OVERRIDABLE, Conventions.md:390-393; the one route-aware fx :rf.route/with-nav-token is REJECT, row 394). The bead's core premise — routing as the ONLY two-prefix subsystem — is FALSE: Spec 011 owns :rf.ssr/* AND :rf.server/* (Conventions.md rows 78/81), the identical domain-vs-host-mechanism layering mirrored server-side, and Spec 016 owns three prefixes (:rf.resource/*, :rf.mutation/*, :rf.optimistic/*). No one-prefix-per-subsystem rule exists anywhere in Conventions.md. Option C would additionally break routing's own audience signal (012-Routing.md:32 — dotted sub-areas = internal plumbing users must not touch) by demoting the most user-visible OVERRIDABLE fx into the plumbing position. A written spec-normative membership rule is the definition of deliberate; a ~102-file rename (incl. 11 behaviour-pinning conformance fixtures + 5 hot-zone specs) against it is over-engineering. title: audit: keyword-surface consistency sweep — :rf.<area>/* families vs the Conventions scheme (drift, misnomers, entity-vs-namespace leaf)
description:
PURPOSE (pre-alpha elegance/consistency drive, Mike 2026-07-17): the :rf.<area>/* keyword surface is already highly disciplined, but a first-pass reconnaissance found real drift candidates. Audit the WHOLE keyword vocabulary against spec/Conventions.md and produce a concrete "these keywords need adjusting" list — one Mike-ruled decision per genuine rename question (the czn2m0 pattern), NOT unilateral renames.

CANON: spec/Conventions.md §The single-root reserved set + the three naming axes it defines — (1) qualified-vs-unqualified (bare vs :rf.<area>/*); (2) read-model DEPTH (whole-entity read is bare :rf/entity, per-field is :rf.entity/field); (3) the value-side corollary (a bare key may carry a namespaced value). Census across the whole tree (spec/ implementation/ tools/ docs/ examples/); the spec is authority.

SCOPE — enumerate all distinct :rf.<area>/* families (~73 in spec/ alone) and classify each: CONFORMANT | DRIFT | MISNOMER | LEAF-QUESTION. Specifically resolve the three candidates the reconnaissance already surfaced:

1. CROSS-FAMILY DRIFT — :rf.nav/* vs :rf.route/*. Routing carries TWO top-level prefixes: :rf.route/* (757, the domain — navigate/params/id/lifecycle) and :rf.nav/* (214, but only 6 members: push-url/replace-url/scroll/capture-scroll/replace/external — all host history+scroll effects). Is :rf.nav/ a deliberate host-effect sub-area, or drift that should fold into :rf.route/ (e.g. :rf.route/push-url)? Note the tell: :rf.route/navigate (event) coexists with :rf.nav/push-url (fx) — "navigation" spelled two ways by layer. Recommend a resolution.

2. ENTITY-vs-NAMESPACE LEAF (gates rf2-lgeron) — keyword prefixes are entity-SINGULAR (:rf.route/ :rf.machine/ :rf.resource/ :rf.flow/) while the owning NAMESPACES are collection-PLURAL (re-frame.routing / .machines / .resources / .flows). Decide the house rule: (a) ACCEPT the distinction (keyword names the entity, namespace names the subsystem — both rf-rooted, legitimately different axes); (b) rename namespaces to singular (re-frame.route / .machine) so leaves match keywords; (c) other. This DIRECTLY sets the concrete alias leaf in rf2-lgeron (rf.routing vs rf.route) — that bead's convention (dotted rf.<leaf>) is stable, but its leaf spelling waits on this ruling.

3. MISNOMER CLASS — names that mislead about semantics, per the just-ruled :rf.machine/join-auth -> :rf.machine/join-attempt (rf2-cpbjfp; "auth" implied authentication it never provided). Sweep for siblings (any :rf.*/ id whose name over-claims a guarantee, implies a lifecycle it lacks, or names the wrong layer).

Also flag: any bare framework keyword that regime-1/2 says should be namespaced (or over-namespaced value that should be bare per the corollary); any :re-frame/* legacy straggler (Conventions §136 says these don't resolve in v2); singular/plural inconsistency WITHIN a family.

EXCLUDE (already handled): :rf.machine/join-auth rename (rf2-cpbjfp) — use it as the misnomer TEMPLATE, don't re-file it. The require-ALIAS sweep (rf2-lgeron) — distinct surface (namespaces, not keywords), though the leaf question (2) informs it.

OUTPUT: a findings doc under ai/findings/ (per-family table + evidence + per-finding recommendation), plus ONE decision-bead per genuine rename question for Mike to rule (czn2m0 pattern — explain problem, options, consequence, recommendation). Misnomers with an unambiguous honest fix may carry a strong rec. NO unilateral keyword renames — every public-id rename is Mike's call and a hot-zone spec touch.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every distinct :rf.<area>/* family enumerated and classified (conformant | drift | misnomer | leaf-question) in an ai/findings/ doc with per-family evidence.
- The three named candidates explicitly resolved with a recommendation: (1) :rf.nav/ vs :rf.route/; (2) the entity-singular-keyword vs plural-namespace leaf rule (with its effect on rf2-lgeron's leaf spelled out); (3) a misnomer sweep using join-auth->join-attempt as the template.
- One decision-bead per genuine rename question filed for Mike (not unilateral renames); misnomers may carry a strong rec.
- rf2-lgeron updated/annotated with the leaf ruling (rf.routing vs rf.route) once (2) is decided.
- join-auth rename (rf2-cpbjfp) and the alias sweep (rf2-lgeron) NOT re-filed.

title: Clean exact-owner epoch stores when destroy snapshot evidence is nil
description:
PR #5939 made a nil terminal-evidence bundle publish nothing when the pre-dissociation :epoch/snapshot-frame-destroyed hook throws. On current main, re-frame.epoch.listeners/on-frame-destroyed! also nests the exact-owner state/cleanup-frame-owner! transaction inside (when terminal-evidence ...). A snapshot failure therefore suppresses not only fabrication, but cleanup of the destroyed incarnation's id-keyed history, buffer, observation, last-settled epoch, and mount attribution.

Deterministic current-main reproduction: create frame A, settle one epoch, replace :epoch/snapshot-frame-destroyed with a throwing hook, destroy A, then create same-id B without dispatching an epoch. A is gone and B has a distinct token, yet rf/epoch-history for the destroyed id still equals A's history and B exposes A's [:audit/seed] record before its first epoch. This contradicts the documented empty history for destroyed/unknown frames and exact-incarnation isolation.

Causal boundary: frame.cljc converts the throwing snapshot hook to nil; listeners.cljc correctly treats publication as conditional on evidence, but cleanup authority comes separately from the frame-id and owner-token and must still settle. Existing #5939 nil-bundle and later #5956 integrated fixtures assert no fabricated terminal record/reporting/successor frame mutation but never read destroyed or pre-first-epoch successor history.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exact-owner epoch-store cleanup runs after frame destroy even when terminal-evidence is nil because the snapshot hook threw; terminal record/trailer/silencing publication remains conditional and fabricates nothing.
- A deterministic fail-before fixture seeds A history, makes :epoch/snapshot-frame-destroyed throw, destroys A, and proves public epoch-history is [] after destroy.
- Creating same-id B before its first epoch exposes no A history, buffer, observation, last-settled epoch, or mount attribution; B's distinct token/state remains untouched.
- A paused predecessor cleanup that loses exact-owner comparison to a claimed B still cannot erase B.
- The snapshot failure still yields the existing one bounded teardown report and diagnostic, post-dissoc publication hook invocation, complete frame teardown, and no residual trace ring.
- JVM and synchronous CLJS coverage pins the nil-bundle cleanup path; reverting cleanup beneath the evidence guard fails deterministically.

title: Latent AB-BA deadlock: silenced-on-frame-destroy emit fanned out under ledger locks inverts silence-lock/registry-lock vs a frame :drain-lock
description:
PR #6051 (rf2-9bhne6) moved the :rf.epoch.cb/silenced-on-frame-destroy emit INSIDE the ledger locks (claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! runs publish! under with-claim-locks = registry-lock + silence-lock, state.cljc:1204-1216; publish! is trace/emit! fanning to arbitrary trace listeners, listeners.cljc:470-478). This introduces a real AB-BA lock-order inversion with the per-frame :drain-lock.

Order A (new): hold silence-lock+registry-lock -> a trace listener that dispatch-syncs (a framework-blessed listener behaviour per the rf2-1zxlsm half of this same PR; Xray already dispatch-syncs from its collector) enters drain-block!/call-serialized-with-drain! which spin-CAS-acquires the target frame's :drain-lock (router.cljc:3486, frame.cljc:1678). So: silence-lock -> :drain-lock.

Order B (normal every-settle path): a thread draining frame F holds F's :drain-lock for the whole pass; settle -> notify-listeners! -> record-observation! genuine re-arm acquires silence-lock (epoch.cljc:239, state.cljc:1366). The mid-drain-destroy variant takes silence-lock+registry-lock directly under the held drain-lock. So: :drain-lock -> silence-lock (and -> registry-lock).

Cycle: T1 (cold destroy) holds silence-lock, spins on F.drain-lock; T2 (draining F) holds F.drain-lock, blocks on silence-lock -> hard hang. drain-block!'s bounded-wait assumption is violated because the drainer T2 is itself blocked. The PR's deadlock-freedom docstrings (state.cljc:1196-1201) only analyse frame-owner-lock and never consider :drain-lock/router, so the argument is unsound as stated.

Qualifiers: JVM-only (locks are CLJS no-ops); dev/test-only (silence path gated on interop/debug-enabled?), so a CI/dev hang not a prod hang; needs a dispatch-syncing trace/epoch listener concurrent with a draining thread. Escalate to P1 if a first-party JVM trace listener that dispatch-syncs exists (audit tools/story/**).

Fix options (any one; pre-alpha minimal): (a) PREFERRED - reserve mark under lock but emit OUTSIDE the locks and make the signal self-filtering by carrying observed-gen so a late observer discards it when current gen != observed-gen (removes the reason the emit was under the lock; small Spec 009/Tool-Pair wire touch); (b) gate only put-listener!(cb-id) on a narrow per-(frame,cb) publish-in-flight barrier instead of the two global ledger locks; (c) stopgap - forbid dispatch-sync from trace/epoch listeners (async dispatch is safe, does not take drain-lock) and document the emit-under-lock hazard. Add a JVM stress scenario driving claim-and-publish into a dispatch-syncing listener concurrent with a draining thread (epoch_concurrency_stress_test.clj currently routes around it). Correct the deadlock-freedom docstrings to enumerate :drain-lock/router. Also refresh the stale reserve-only docstring at listeners.cljc:378-387.

(found by #6051 audit; see ai/findings/2026-07-17-review-epoch-trace.md)
