title: SECURITY: :rf.cofx dispatch opt is an unclosed public forge route for join authority (nsbwft incomplete)
description:
Shape-3 audit of #6077 (rf2-nsbwft). #6077 removed public event-VECTOR :rf/join-auth metadata as a join-completion authority carrier. But an EQUIVALENT, still-public route remains: the :rf.cofx dispatch OPTION carrying :rf.machine/join-auth. An ordinary public re-frame.core/dispatch(-sync) can mint exact-current join authority and fold a spawn-all child that never completed (resolving an :all join early, cancelling siblings).

REPRO (all via public API): the app owns the parent machine so it knows parent-id/invoke-id/child-id; the runtime-owned :rf/attempt + spawned-id are readable through the PUBLIC re-frame.core/frame-state-value (core.cljc:1890, returns :rf.db/runtime verbatim). Then:
  (rf/dispatch [:my-parent [:child/done :a]] {:rf.cofx {:rf.machine/join-auth {:parent-id :my-parent :invoke-id [:racing] :child-id :a :spawned-id <read> :attempt <read>}}})
folds :a into :done with no completion.

REACHABILITY CHAIN (HEAD): (1) public dispatch is [event opts], :rf.cofx a documented opt (router.cljc:206); (2) validate-cofx! gates only map-shape+EDN+int :rf/time-ms and explicitly lets subsystem-qualified facts pass (router/diagnostics.cljc:198,221); (3) ensure-cofx preserves caller-supplied map verbatim (cofx.cljc:144); (4) assemble-initial-ctx stages :rf.cofx (:rf.cofx envelope) verbatim, framework-coeffect-keys only filters TRACE projection (router.cljc:861, fx.cljc:1558); (5) prepare-machine-ctx assocs it onto :rf/cofx (registration.cljc:438); (6) carrier-auth reads exactly [:rf/cofx :rf.machine/join-auth] with no provenance gate (join.cljc:355). join-auth-current? checks only equality with observable runtime state.

PROOF ALREADY GREEN: the #6077 test join_exact_auth_cljs_test.cljc public-metadata-tuple-is-never-authority step (2) does exactly this via public dispatch-sync and asserts (= #{:a} (:done ...)). The authors treat it as the 'legitimate protected channel'; it is the exploit through the public surface.

VIOLATES nsbwft's OWN acceptance criteria: 'ordinary public events cannot mint/forge authority, including when every tuple field matches current runtime state' and 'no public auth API or secrecy assumption is introduced'. The docstrings call [:rf/cofx :rf.machine/join-auth] the 'SINGLE PROTECTED carrier' but nothing enforces it; 'protected' is aspirational, not a boundary.

TENSION (not a one-liner): cofx was chosen for REPLAY DURABILITY — strict replay re-presents recorded cofx verbatim through a plain dispatch (see #6074 epoch test). So cofx-carried authority is re-injectable via a replay-shaped public dispatch BY DESIGN. Worse, the internal transport child-dispatch! re-enters via the SAME public :router/dispatch! boundary (fx.cljc:705), so validate-cofx! cannot distinguish framework-transport from app-forge by key alone. Durability(replay) vs unforgeability(provenance) genuinely conflict; #6077 conflates 'recordable' with 'protected'.

SEVERITY: single-trust-domain (all app code trusted; not cross-tenant escalation; 'attacker' == app author). Accidental-forge likelihood is LOWER than the metadata route (cofx must be explicitly authored vs metadata riding invisibly on a copy-pasted value). P1 because it falsifies the audit's chartered invariant + nsbwft acceptance criteria as stated; reasonable to downgrade to P2 on the trust-model framing — Mike's call.

FIX OPTIONS: (A) LIGHT/recommended for pre-alpha: scope the claim honestly — accept :rf.machine/join-auth on cofx is as app-forgeable as any recordable coeffect (replay parity), rewrite nsbwft criteria + join.cljc:20-26,95-101,330-356 + machines.cljc:300 + spec/005 to state the REAL guarantee (authority binds to exact runtime-owned attempt/actor identity so stale/duplicate/cross-attempt carriers fail closed — defeats accidental forging, not deliberate authoring; single-trust-domain), drop the 'can never / including when every field matches' absolute. (B) HEAVY: add a framework-minted provenance marker the app cannot set (per-drain nonce, or require :source :machine-action on the carrying envelope) that carrier-auth also requires, and grant strict replay the same privilege via restore-epoch!/replay-mint path; marker must be set before the dispatch! boundary since child-dispatch! shares it.

Findings: ai/findings/2026-07-17-review-join-authority.md
notes:
HELD for Mike's ruling 2026-07-17 (THREAT-MODEL DECISION, do not auto-fix). Audit found #6077 closed the metadata forge route but an equivalent public route remains: dispatch with {:rf.cofx {:rf.machine/join-auth <exact-tuple>}} still mints join authority; tuple constructible from public frame-state-value. TENSION: cofx MUST be replay-re-injectable (strict replay re-presents recorded cofx via plain dispatch — #6074), so un-forgeable-cofx vs replay-durable-cofx conflict. re-frame2 is SINGLE-TRUST-DOMAIN (attacker=app author). Options: (A) LIGHT/recommended — scope the claim honestly (binds exact runtime identity; defeats ACCIDENTAL not DELIBERATE forge; drop absolute 'can never'); (B) HEAVY — framework-minted provenance marker carrier-auth also requires + replay-authorized re-injection path (likely gold-plating for single-trust-domain). Mayor rec: (A). Awaiting Mike's threat-model call before dispatch.
RULING (2026-07-17, recorded per Mike's in-session direction "record the necessary rulings"; both the Fable dossier and the appended Codex analysis independently concur):

DECISION = OPTION A — the honest EXACT-ATTEMPT FENCE. Do NOT add a provenance mechanism (Option B is rejected). Downgrade P1 -> P2.

WHY (decisive under the stated posture — trust the programmer / low friction / not gold-plating / remove over-engineering we find):
- "We trust the programmer" IS the framework's security stance (spec/Security.md:272-285 "trust the explicit invoker; gate accidents not theoretical attacks"). B is distrust-the-app-author machinery bolted onto a trust-the-programmer framework, defending the author against their own single process — the over-engineering the posture explicitly rejects.
- Codex proved B-as-described does not even work: :source and :rf.machine/internal? are themselves public dispatch opts (app can stamp them); an EDN nonce either forges (observable) or breaks replay/SSR/restore (unrecorded host object); a MAC needs a secret lifecycle outside frame state. Real provenance = a NEW authority subsystem (privileged dispatch seam + privileged replay-remint API + serialization-survival design). That is not a bugfix; it is gold-plating for a single-trust-domain.
- The mechanism is not authentication; it is a replayable correlation record. Keep it — it closes real CORRECTNESS hazards (stale / cross-attempt / wrong-child / wrong-actor / duplicate / cancelled / post-resolution completions all fail closed) — and describe it accurately.

ADOPTED SHARPENINGS (from Codex, all pre-alpha-cheap, friction-reducing, over-engineering-removing):
1. VOCABULARY RENAME (kills the misreading at the root): :rf.machine/join-auth -> :rf.machine/join-attempt; carrier-auth -> carrier-attempt; join-auth-current? -> join-attempt-current?. The word "auth" invited the false "can never forge" overclaim. Pre-alpha, no back-compat cost.
2. THIRD FORGE ROUTE (bead + dossier both missed it): :rf.machine/join-dispatch is a normally-registered fx an ordinary app event can emit directly (join_authority_effect_path_test.cljc:293-315 only tests attempt -999; the exact-current tuple would pass the same equality predicate). The reserved-fx tier blocks OVERRIDE/redirect, not direct invocation. So Spec 005's "internal, non-authorable" is false here too, independent of the cofx route. Ruling: keep join-dispatch reserved/non-overridable/non-redirectable (protects the framework path from capture/suppression); direct app emission is UNSUPPORTED but NOT security-prohibited — same honest stance as the cofx route.
3. CONTRACT = the 7-rule exact-attempt fence: (a) runtime stamps an exact completion coordinate {parent-id, invoke-id, logical child-id, spawned actor-id, attempt-id}; (b) recordable/serializable/inspectable/replayable/caller-suppliable — NOT a secret/capability/signature; (c) folds only when every coordinate equals current runtime-owned join state AND the child has not already completed/failed/been cancelled; (d) missing/malformed/stale/redirected/cross-attempt/wrong-actor/duplicate coordinates fail closed, zero join mutation; (e) an exact-current coordinate is accepted regardless of source (normal transport, faithful replay, tooling, or deliberate app authoring); (f) join-dispatch reserved per (2); (g) "opaque" = callers must not depend on the attempt token representation, NOT secret/unobservable.
4. SPEC + DOCSTRING SWEEP before S3 conformance freezes the wording: remove "protected carrier", "only the internal transport populates it", "non-authorable", "can never forge", "freshness is provenance". Prefer "coordinate", "attempt fence", "framework-produced normal path", "exact-current equality". Also correct Spec 005 §Join and the #6077 acceptance criteria to the true guarantee.
5. REGRESSION COVERAGE that makes the boundary impossible to misstate again (accept exact-current from every source incl. deliberate authoring; fail-closed on each of the stale/cross/duplicate classes; join-dispatch capture/redirect still blocked).

DOWNGRADE RATIONALE (P1->P2): single-trust-domain, accident-gating not breach-prevention; it falsified the audit's chartered invariant AS WRITTEN, which the honest-scoping fixes. Not a real-world security breach.

IMPLEMENTATION: filed as rf2-<new> (see BLOCKS/related). This bead is now the durable DECISION RECORD; the new bead is the dispatchable work.
IMPLEMENTATION BEAD: rf2-cpbjfp (machines(join) honest exact-attempt fence). This bead (blwwbw) is the durable DECISION RECORD; cpbjfp is the dispatchable work.

title: Reconcile router nextTick scheduling with the event-loop contract
description:
The router still schedules drains with `goog.async.nextTick` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs`), which Closure documents and implements as task-style scheduling rather than a microtask. `spec/002-Frames.md` and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/impl/live_frame.cljc` nevertheless call it a microtask and promise that background tabs do not throttle event processing. Spec 006 now correctly distinguishes UI `queueMicrotask` from the router `interop/next-tick` macrotask. The active sources therefore specify incompatible host behavior, and the closed contract-sweep bead explicitly required that no active text retain this claim.

Choose one observable contract and make implementation, prose, and tests agree. The smallest likely correction is to describe next-turn/task scheduling and remove the unsupported background guarantee; change the primitive only if a deliberate microtask drain is still required by the architecture.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 002, `live_frame.cljc`, `interop.cljs`, and Spec 006 use one accurate term for router drain scheduling.
- No active normative text calls `goog.async.nextTick` a microtask or promises background-tab cadence the primitive cannot guarantee.
- A focused host-ordering test distinguishes the chosen router boundary from both synchronous work and a true `queueMicrotask` boundary.
- If the runtime primitive changes, fixed-point draining, external-event ordering, machine front-of-queue behavior, and render-batch separation remain green; otherwise this stays a documentation/test correction.
close_reason: shipped via PR #6081 (merged): router next-tick=goog.async.nextTick=MACROTASK; prose (spec/002+009+docstrings) wrongly said microtask incl. a false 'not throttled in backgrounded tab' guarantee. Fixed CONTRACT to match the deliberate macrotask render-interleave (primitive unchanged); adversarial ordering proof; #6079 incarnation fences intact. Filed P4 follow-up for non-normative Design-TransducerRouter.md

title: Make the CLJS slice-memo lifetime contract survive inverse microtask FIFO
description:
The current CLJS slice memo is a module-global holder/table cleared by `queueMicrotask` only after the first probe. Spec 006 and synthesis doc 03 promise that no holder/table survives into a later render slice. FIFO gives a deterministic counterexample: queue microtask A, then synchronously perform the first probe (which queues clears B/C). At the checkpoint A runs first and can perform a genuinely later render while the old holder/table is still installed. A caught exception followed by synchronous retry has the same ambiguity. The existing test queues its later probe after the first probe, so the clear is already ahead and the inverse FIFO is untested.

Exact object/version tags appear to prevent stale-value corruption, making this principally a lifetime/economy and contract-honesty issue. Reconcile the smallest honest boundary rather than inventing a scheduler. Also sweep the still-live Spec-006 amendment draft and S3 ownership spike, which retain unconditional queueMicrotask/normative wording that contradicts the canonical JVM/CLJS split.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic inverse-FIFO test queues a later-render callback before the first synchronous probe and establishes the intended reuse/non-reuse result; include the caught-render/retry case if it is semantically distinct.
- Runtime and canonical Spec 006/synthesis 03 agree on what “render slice” means and the maximum CLJS holder/table lifetime.
- If cross-render reuse within the bounded host-microtask window is safe and intended, document that bounded economy honestly; otherwise implement a genuine render-scoped boundary without losing sibling fan-out reuse.
- JVM thread-local behavior remains correct and CLJS exact tags continue to prevent stale-value reuse.
- The live amendment draft and S3 ownership spike are corrected, tombstoned, or clearly repointed so they cannot be mistaken for current normative law.

It never consumes `rf/epoch-history`, round-trips the actual `:trigger-event` plus post-generation `:rf.cofx`, or calls `rf/restore-epoch!`. A regression in epoch assembly, durable replay material, or restoration can therefore pass while the isolated join logic stays green.

Add one composition proof at the natural epoch/machines boundary. Reuse the existing public raw epoch record and restore APIs and the existing fixtures; do not create a replay framework or broaden production APIs.

- A live join completion that mints the generator-backed fact produces an actual epoch record containing the real trigger event and post-generation `:rf.cofx`.
- The recorded event/cofx survive an EDN round-trip; `restore-epoch!` restores the pre-completion frame state; strict replay reproduces the same fold, authority decision, and terminal evidence without calling the generator.

title: Retire exact root-reporter authority after manual quarantine recovery
description:
PR #5911 introduced `live-reporters`, a strong set of committed root-incarnation tokens. Normal React reporter cleanup calls `report-root-teardown!` and removes the token. On a throwing host `.unmount`, however, the exact reporter cleanup may never run; adapter-wide recovery intentionally clears the consumed container and calls `release-root!`, which only dissociates `live-roots` and does not retire `live-reporters`.

Current main already has a deterministic real-DOM seam in `adapter_public_root_disposal_dom_cljs_test.cljs`: mount/commit a real root (reporter setup runs), replace only that React root's `.unmount` with an immediate throw (reporter cleanup cannot run), dispose the adapter, observe the root registry/container/cells reclaimed, then reuse the same id/container. The old incarnation nevertheless remains strongly retained in `live-reporters`; repeating the terminal recovery accretes one token per cycle. It also leaves stale teardown authority: calling `teardown-root!` for the captured old incarnation after recovery is still classified as reporter-deferred rather than synchronously terminal.

Late real-React cleanup is safe after explicit exact retirement: `report-root-teardown!` disjoins idempotently and its identity check cannot settle a newer incarnation. Dedupe across all bead states found only the closed implementation/cleanup beads (`rf2-vxgfnd.275`, `.291`, `.94.4`), none owning this residual lifecycle symmetry. Keep public isolated-unmount quarantine fail-closed; retirement belongs only at successful exact adapter/manual recovery.
acceptance_criteria:
- After successful adapter recovery of an exact cleanup-failure quarantine, both the public root claim and that same root-incarnation's reporter authority are retired; `live-reporters` cannot retain an incarnation whose terminal container reclaim completed.
- Extend the existing real-DOM throwing-root fixture to capture the committed incarnation, perform adapter recovery, and prove a subsequent no-signal `teardown-root!` for that old token settles synchronously (no stale reporter-deferred classification).
- Repeating committed mount → throwing cleanup → successful adapter reclaim for many fresh incarnations returns the reporter ledger to its baseline rather than growing one strong token per cycle.
- A late `report-root-teardown!` for the retired predecessor is idempotent and cannot clear, settle, or otherwise affect a same-id successor incarnation.
- Failed container reclaim retains both quarantine and reporter authority; public `unmount!` alone still fails closed and does not advertise an unproven container as free.
- Ordinary synchronous teardown, deferred teardown, failed-first pre-commit rollback, adapter-wide sibling draining, and exact stale-handle fencing remain green.
- Mutation teeth that make recovery registry-only again or retire reporter authority before reclaim succeeds make focused tests fail.
- Reuse the existing incarnation identity/settlement machinery; no second registry or broad lifecycle framework.
close_reason: shipped via PR #6048 (merged): retire exact root-reporter authority after quarantine recovery (retire-root-reporter! between reclaim+release; fail-closed on failed reclaim); 4 proofs

title: Migrate the Xray ViewCell reactivity bridge in an already-registered process
description:
PR #5915 adds the ViewCell ownership event/sub/listener and changes `:rf.xray/viewcell-evidence` from an epoch-history-only subscription to a two-input subscription. Every new registration is inside `reactive-panel-subs/install!`, reached only from `registry/register-xray-handlers!`. That umbrella remains guarded by the pre-existing `(defonce registered? (atom false))` plus a single false→true CAS; the PR neither changes nor versions the sentinel.

In the exact live-upgrade sequence the PR is meant to support, a pre-PR Xray process already has `registered? = true` and the old one-input handler cached in the registrar. Shadow reloads the changed preload/dependency code; `register-xray-handlers!` no-ops, then the preload calls the new `viewcell-evidence/acquire!`. The new ownership listener/event/sub and amended evidence subscription are never installed. A held Views subscription can therefore retain its pre-release row until an unrelated epoch pump or a full page reload, despite the PR's immediate-reactivity claim. The existing HMR test calls `acquire!` directly in a fresh current-code registry and does not exercise this old-process→new-code migration.

The construction is deterministic from the exact patch: `registry.cljs` was not changed; the entire leaf install remains behind the defonce boolean; the old handler has only `:<- [:rf.xray/epoch-history]`; the new bridge exists only in that skipped leaf install. Dedupe across all bead states found no owner. Keep the correction bounded to registration-schema migration/reload authority; do not turn it into a general plugin/migration framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- An already-running pre-#5915 Xray process with the registry sentinel set and the old epoch-only evidence subscription upgrades to the current ownership event/sub/listener and two-input evidence subscription without a page reload or test-only reset.
- A deterministic CLJS upgrade fixture first installs the old registration shape, preserves its sentinel/held subscription/evidence span, then runs the current preload or public init path; acquire and release immediately invalidate the held subscription and expose no stale row.
- The migration is idempotent: a fresh current boot and repeated current-version after-load runs emit no repeated handler-replaced warning flood and install exactly one ownership listener.
- Migration preserves the exact current ownership receipt and accumulated evidence for a same-span re-arm, and never clobbers a foreign evidence owner.
- Registration topology proves `:rf.xray/viewcell-evidence` depends on `:rf.xray/viewcell-evidence-ownership` after the live upgrade; the ownership event and sub are callable in `:rf/xray`.
- Mutation teeth that restore the unversioned boolean-only gate or leave the new bridge solely behind a gate already set by the old process make the upgrade fixture fail.
- Use a small versioned/migration-aware installation seam or equivalent; no general migration framework and no unconditional whole-registry re-registration on every reload.
close_reason: shipped via PR #6046 (merged): xray ViewCell reactivity bridge given versioned live-upgrade migration seam (schema-version + migrate-schema!); re-migration proof (5 failures pre-fix); spec/014 updated

title: Scope flow hot-reload evidence to the authoritative frame slot
description: PR #5912 routes flow replacement evidence through the generic process-global hot-reload dedup key `[:flow flow-id]`, and the emitted `:rf.registry/handler-replaced` tags omit `:frame`. Flow definitions are authoritative at `(frame-id, flow-id)`. On current main, two live frames independently replacing the same flow id from the same prior derive function to the same new derive function perform two real replacements but emit only one unattributable event. Same-id frame recreation can likewise inherit a predecessor's dedup shape. This contradicts Spec 013's independent frame ownership and frame-attributed hot-reload evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decide flow replacement suppression from the authoritative frame slot and exact frame incarnation, preferably from prior/new stored values rather than another frame-blind state table.
- Include `:frame` on flow replacement evidence.
- Identical real replacements of the same flow id in two live frames each emit once and are attributable to their frame.
- A subsequent identical hot reload suppresses independently within each frame.
- Destroy/recreate of a frame id does not inherit the predecessor incarnation's emitted shape.
- Cover direct `reg-flow` and reserved-effect registration on CLJ and CLJS, including live controls and same-id frame reincarnation.
- Leave generic registrar dedup semantics unchanged for genuinely process-scoped registrar kinds; do not add a parallel flow registry.
close_reason: shipped via PR #6045 (merged): flow hot-reload evidence scoped to authoritative (frame-id,flow-id) slot + :frame tag; cross-frame proof (11 assertions red pre-fix)

title: Make JVM observation provenance truly reload-safe
description: PR #5910 preserves a versioned JVM provenance holder, but the advertised reload-safety law still fails in two current-main cases. First, a real `(require 're-frame.substrate.observation :reload)` redefines `EmissionProvenance`; retained values in the preserved map are instances of the predecessor class, so `source-covered-always-on?` changes from true to false while the holder identity remains unchanged. Second, `attest-provenance!` and lookup fetch the map and `ReferenceQueue` through separate Var reads; if reload reconciliation replaces the holder between those reads, a key can be installed in one holder's map with the other holder's queue and is immediately undiscoverable from the live holder. Both violate exact-once callback-failure coverage and the explicit same-version/predecessor reload contract. The authored reload test only calls the reconciliation helper and never performs a namespace reload.
acceptance_criteria:
- Store provenance values in a reload-stable representation, or migrate retained values, so an authentic throwable attested before a real same-version namespace reload remains covered and drains exactly once afterward.
- Take one coherent holder snapshot per attest, lookup, and expunge operation; its map and ReferenceQueue must always come from that same holder even if reconciliation runs concurrently or reentrantly.
- Add a real `require :reload` regression: attest before reload, prove holder/entry behavior and exact-once coverage after reload.
- Add a deterministic holder-replacement interleaving test proving no orphaned entry or mismatched queue; expunge stale weak entries from the holder that owns them.
- Retain predecessor-version replacement, same-version idempotence, weak-identity lifecycle, and genuine-Throwable identity coverage.
- Keep CLJS behavior unchanged and do not introduce a second provenance registry or public authority.
close_reason: shipped via PR #6047 (merged): JVM observation provenance reload-safe (reload-stable channel set instead of deftype instance; single coherent holder snapshot); real-reload proofs

title: Make frame lifecycle drift guard causal across every host path
description:
PR #5905 added Rule 7 to protect the compiled-versus-legacy frame-root lifecycle, but the current positive-presence proof accepts the exact partial regressions it claims to catch. On origin/main 47e04e82, scripts/check_skill_implementor_partition_drift.py::_preflight_before_render compares only the first run-preflight! call with the first .render call. client.cljs has three distinct production paths (same-root refresh around 934/954, fresh mount around 978/1027, explicit render!* around 1097/1127). A synthetic correct first pair followed by a render-only or render-before-preflight path still returns true. The guide also overstates the contract as preflight before createRoot for the compiled substrate universally: one-shot mount* does preflight before createRoot, but the intentional split API's create-root* allocates/registers the React root before plans exist and render!* later preflights before .render. Documentation and guard should state and prove these two honest host paths rather than universalizing mount* ordering.

The Conventions check likewise scans the entire document for bare frame-root/frame-provider tokens, so deleting them from the actual artifact inventory rows still passes due to unrelated mentions. The Spec-002 check only preserves literal published fragment strings while describing them as resolvable. Keep the correction bounded and lexical; no general Markdown or Clojure parser.
acceptance_criteria:
- The guide distinguishes one-shot mount* (preflight before createRoot and first .render) from the split create-root*/render!* API (root allocation/registration first by design, then preflight before every .render), without weakening the shared no-render-time-ENSURE law.
- The existing-root mount, fresh mount, and render!* production paths are checked independently for preflight before their corresponding host render; the fresh mount path is also pinned before root creation, while the split path is not falsely claimed to preflight before create-root*.
- Conventions assertions are scoped to the owning artifact inventory row(s) and require both frame boundaries there.
- The two canonical Spec-002 fragments are validated against local headings, or the guard wording is accurately narrowed to presence-only.
- Self-tests independently remove or reorder each production preflight, violate the one-shot allocation ordering, and remove each inventory boundary while leaving unrelated mentions; every mutation fails. Live scan and self-test pass.
close_reason: shipped via PR #6033 (merged): frame-root lifecycle drift guard (Rule 7 in check_skill_implementor_partition_drift.py) made causal across all 3 client.cljs render paths (same-root/fresh-mount/render!*); L4 spec-002 heading-slug validation + L6 inventory-row-scoped boundary check; teeth proven failing-before/passing-after on real sources

title: Bound first-party UI flush convergence and protect its adapter-only branches
description: Current re-frame.ui.substrate/ui-flush-render! describes a bounded fixed point but loops solely while the global pending-cell-count is positive, with no pass or work budget and no local non-quiescence diagnostic. The claimed router drain-depth and React update-depth safeguards do not cover every re-enrolment across separate flushSync passes; a listener or commit path can keep a cell pending and make the synchronous tooling/adapter call spin indefinitely. The only adapter browser fixture performs one ordinary invalidation. Removing either the adapter-specific open-drain guard or the commit-triggered re-dirty loop leaves it green; existing open-drain fixtures exercise only ui.test/flush!. This is a current runtime and regression-net gap in PR #5903. Open rf2-vxgfnd.166 owns host-checkpoint batching and real-router multi-drain truth, not these adapter-only branches.
acceptance_criteria: Give first-party flush convergence an explicit finite pass or work budget and fail loud with one typed diagnostic carrying useful pass and pending counts when it cannot quiesce. Preserve ordinary multi-pass convergence and no-op safety. Add an adapter fixture with deliberate non-quiescent re-enrolment that deterministically trips the bound; a mounted one-shot commit-triggered follow-up that returns with final DOM and zero pending cells; an adapter flush called inside a live event handler that throws :rf.error/flush-in-open-epoch before publication; and a throwing thunk control that propagates unchanged without publishing pending work. title: Treat same-root preflight supersession as expected settlement, not an authority mismatch
description: Current render supersession produces a false :rf.error/frame-preflight-evidence-mismatch. render!* executes the new preflight first, refreshing a same-root frame from rev1/config A to rev2/config B, then seat-pending-attempt! aborts the old rev1 receipt. The later authority diagnostic treats that expected revision overtaking as :record-revision-mismatch. A current-main JVM reproduction using the real frames executor and error listener captured exactly one mismatch with phase :abort while B correctly remained authoritative. Ordinary supported same-root supersession must not be reported as foreign or stale authority failure. The pending-owner mechanism came from PR #5903; mandatory mismatch emission arrived in PR #5994.
acceptance_criteria: A same-root config-changing A-to-B render supersession emits no frame-preflight-evidence-mismatch and B commits as the authoritative attempt. Settlement has explicit knowledge of the superseding receipt and suppresses only writes legitimately overtaken by that same-root attempt. Disjoint old writes are still terminally aborted. Genuine foreign-root, reincarnation, stale-controller, missing-record, and unauthorized revision mismatches remain dev-loud and never mutate current authority. Add a direct JVM receipt-settlement fixture and a no-act/no-flush browser integration fixture that drives two ordinary renders then proves B committed with zero mismatch diagnostics. Keep the public API unchanged and unblock the evidence-reconciliation work only after these semantics are pinned.

WAVE 0 — PRODUCT REGISTER RESOLVED (ruled 2026-07-16, R-1 coordinate confirmed 2026-07-17; the ten rulings R-1..R-10 are durable in docs/EP/EP-0035-component-library-readiness.md §Resolved Decisions and restated in this epic's NOTES, which are authoritative over any summary). Wave-0 scope: freeze native ABI; classify all 72 public Vars (native view / pure helper / compat-only / replacement API / foreign-boundary); package names + cross-host date representation; modernize scripts/kwargs-to-map into dry-run/report; Story + visual baselines BEFORE porting; generic library-authoring internals + guide chapter (public middle artifact only on a second consumer). WAVES 1-5 per the syntheses (structural -> interactive -> overlays -> data-heavy -> adoption/removal); interactive waves depend on the S3 readiness children (rf2-8k14ia sync door, rf2-ri0k6n slots, rf2-isdqjv safe spread, .95.2 atomic local). Release gates: zero Reagent imports in native artifact; no runtime hiccup detection; controlled-input matrix through library APIs; JVM Tier-1 majority + kernel transition traces; StrictMode/reconnect/HMR coverage; visual baselines with CSS frozen; advanced-build one-view isolation; compat deletion criteria written before removal starts.
notes:
ADDITION (2026-07-16, completeness audit — codex §11 release gates 9+10, restored to the durable copy): the native-library release gates also include (9) Story states + accessibility/keyboard/focus checks for EVERY public component (automated coverage plus targeted manual review), and (10) deterministic keys/ids + explicit async cancellation/ownership asserted as GATES (not only ABI shape items).
RULED REGISTER (2026-07-16, delegated decisions per Mike's in-session direction; dossier weighed and retired):
1. PACKAGING — Option B. Same repo initially; native artifact re-com/re-com-ui with namespace family re-com.ui.*; frozen Reagent legacy stays at re-com/re-com and re-com.*. Rationale: side-by-side coexistence is mandatory for leaf-by-leaf migration, legacy apps need zero rename, ns family verified collision-free (MUI @material-ui -> @mui precedent). Final coordinate may be adjusted before first publication only; use distinct aliases (rc vs ui) in all examples.
2. PARTS CEILING — Option A. v1 :parts accepts data/style values plus pure compiled slots only; no registered stateful replacement views (the ui/view trigger rf2-a62fje does NOT fire for re-com v1); arbitrary fns/hiccup/component heads rejected permanently. SHARPENING (adopted as part of the ruling): the slot contract states slots receive the component's declared STATE (open/highlighted/disabled etc), not only item + occurrence — render-prop state access is the power users actually miss and keeps pressure for stateful replacement near zero. Escalation to registered views requires a concrete customization inexpressible via composition/data/pure slot.
3. UNCONTROLLED TIER — Option B, narrow. Controlled components are canonical and the only form recommended for durable application state; selected components may declare a separate uncontrolled tier via :default-value. :value and :default-value are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE; supplying both is a validation failure at the component boundary. Per-component admission only on demonstrated Story/ephemera pain. Type-based ownership inference (value-or-ratom) rejected permanently.
4. THEME TRANSPORT — Option A. Explicit props + frame subscriptions only in v1; no nested context mechanism. FORWARD-COMPAT CLAUSE (adopted): theme values are plain data only (no fns/closures inside theme values) so a later context graduation is non-breaking. Context reconsidered only when a real nested-theme consumer states the required cross-host (SSR/JVM/memo/reconnect) semantics.
5. TABLES/GRIDS — Option A. Foreign-virtualization-first behind a re-com-owned data/event/slot boundary. The ONLY accepted reasons to open a native-virtualization project are the four criteria verbatim: (a) re-com-specific behavior unrepresentable at the boundary; (b) material bundle/perf evidence favoring ownership; (c) JVM structural rendering value sufficient to justify the implementation; (d) a required a11y/interaction guarantee unobtainable from the foreign engine. Foreign-engine selection (TanStack-class vs react-window-class; bundle/license/upgrade surface) is a NAMED Wave-4-entry decision, not an implementation detail inside the prototype bead.
6. HELPER ARTIFACT — Option A. Generic internals (part/slot resolution, safe attribute splitting, event-prefix helpers, theme-data merging, focus/roving-tabindex, dismissal, deterministic-id recipes) written under generic discipline with independent tests, plus the normative component-library authoring guide, from Wave 0. Public middle artifact only after a second consuming library requests substantially the same contracts; organizational override allowed only if stated explicitly.
7. INPUT OWNERSHIP — Option B. Ownership law approved NOW: checkbox/radio, slider/splits, tabs, selected values, dates/ranges, tree selection, sort and filter models are fully controlled; text/time editing and other explicit commit experiences may use a separate commit/draft API; open/hover/focus/highlight/drag/uncommitted-search are local interaction state unless deliberately exposed; a rejected or externally refreshed draft is identified ONLY by an explicit caller-owned revision (:reset-key), never by model-value comparison. Concrete per-component roster frozen at Wave 2 entry as a named bead, then used as the evidence input to rf2-nzst23. Legacy hybrid ownership rejected.
8. CROSS-HOST DATE/TIME REPRESENTATION (new, was missing from the register) — Public date/time models are host-neutral plain data with ISO-8601 strings as the canonical ABI form: dates "YYYY-MM-DD", times "HH:mm[:ss]", datetimes full ISO-8601. No goog.date/cljs-time/js Date/java.time objects cross the public ABI; components parse/format internally at the boundary per host. Rationale: values-only ABI, EDN/app-db inspectability, JVM SSR, and consistency with the project's XState-v6 ISO-8601 duration ruling. Legacy datepicker's cljs-time/goog.date model is compat-tier-only.
9. ACCESSIBILITY TARGET (new, was missing from the register) — Native baseline is WAI-ARIA APG semantics per component class: roles/states/properties, keyboard interaction, and focus management per the matching APG pattern, shipped WITH each component in its wave (a component is not done without them). Release gate 9 is priced against APG, not legacy parity — legacy contains exactly ONE aria- attribute, so "parity" would ship an inaccessible library. Radix/React Aria set the expectation floor for a modern native library; retrofitting is costlier than building in during a rewrite that already touches every interaction.
10. CSS/BOOTSTRAP POSTURE (new, named deferred ruling now ruled) — The bootstrap-derived theme layer is RETAINED through the parity waves (CSS frozen for visual baselines, per the settled CSS-preserved-first posture), but MUST be isolated as a distinct removable theme-data layer in the native theme model so removal is a data change, not an API break. Long-term removal/replacement is a NAMED post-parity decision bead filed at Wave-5/adoption entry, not drift.

title: S3 literal safe policy for ui/spread: owned-key deny in every build (readiness P1-4)
description:
## Problem
Component libraries forward caller attr maps (:attr-style passthrough — 36 re-com files) onto internal elements. Through general ui/spread such a map can override :value/:checked/owned handlers/:ref — and the mere presence of a dynamic map at a controlled site disqualifies the sync-door proof. Libraries need attr passthrough that provably cannot clobber owned props and does not forfeit the controlled guarantee.

## Scope (DIRECTED by Mike 2026-07-16 — readiness P1-4; API-table delta #5; owning doc drafts/component-library-readiness.md, restated here)
A literal safe-policy form joins ui/spread (exact spelling — second arity vs sibling name — decided at spec landing): compiler-visible allow/deny where denied structural/controlled/identity keys (:key :ref :value :checked owned :on-*) FAIL IN EVERY BUILD (not dev-only); allowed :on-* values classify through the existing handler decision table; aria-*/data-*/title/class/style pass through per the conversion table. A controlled site under the policy form RETAINS the sync door; general spread at the same site still forfeits it. General ui/spread remains the visible-cost escape.

## Constraints
Spec homes: 004B conversion table + 004 spread — hot-zone sequenced. Blocks final S3 conformance (.95.10). Never commit .beads/issues.jsonl.

title: Make weak-evidence GC fixtures deterministic and enforce the canonical GC control
description:
## Test correctness gap
#5998 GC fixtures assume weak entries survive until the explicit GC request, which can flake because collection may happen earlier. ## Required correction

Keep a positive control proving the GC handshake executed in canonical CI.

title: Validate usable WeakRef semantics before root mutation
description:
## Confirmed counterexample
PR #5997's platform gate accepts `WeakRef` when `typeof` reports function, but that does not prove the captured value is constructable or implements a working `deref`. An unusable `FinalizationRegistry` constructor likewise should be treated as the optional feature being absent, not crash after mutation.

## Required correction

Convert every missing/unusable mandatory capability to `:rf.error/ui-platform-incompatible` with the existing diagnostic shape. Probe FinalizationRegistry safely; because it is optional, unusable means absent. Do not retain probe objects or add a compatibility fallback.

- Probe allocations are temporary and leave no root/member/evidence residue.

title: S3 explicit callback boundaries, error recovery, and client-only
description:
## Problem
Foreign React APIs and non-data event mechanics need explicit callback forms with phase, identity, and visibility semantics. Without one closed boundary law, stale closures and render-phase side effects become invisible correctness bugs.

## Scope
Implement the frozen callback decision table in `spec/004-Views.md`: `ui/event`, `ui/handler`, `ui/render-fn`, `ui/raw-fn`; the DOM-only bare-function shorthand; explicit callback refs; foreign-component rejection of bare functions; `error-boundary`; and the S3 `client-only` boundary with required deterministic fallback. Committed callback forms are per-site stable and read committed slots. `ui/event` receives the live host event and returns a vector to dispatch or nil. `ui/handler` performs explicit imperative callback work after commit. `ui/render-fn` runs purely during the foreign component render and cannot dispatch/read sub/acquire lease/use hooks. `ui/raw-fn` passes identity through and is the only callback-ref form. Error-boundary payload/phase and client-only SSR behavior must match checked-in Spec 004, not invent a second recovery protocol.

## Constraints
Native bare functions are legal only in known native event properties, never refs or arbitrary function-valued props. Foreign boundaries require an explicit form. No portals (wave 2), resumability, compatibility shims, or runtime guessing of foreign invocation phase. Do not edit the hot zone until transferred; do not commit bead exports.
acceptance_criteria:
- The complete form-by-boundary decision table has compiler and mounted fixtures, including legal DOM shorthand, illegal foreign bare functions, refs, nil, and identity-sensitive raw callbacks.
- Committed forms keep stable identity and observe only the winning commit; render-fn observes current render values and cannot perform forbidden framework operations.

title: S3 local, effect, dispatch-fn, and view-lease confirmation
description:
## Problem
S3 needs view-local ephemera, host effects, and an escape-free way for committed callbacks to dispatch without capturing stale frame authority. These forms must share the existing compiled slot/lifecycle machinery rather than create a second component runtime.

## Scope
Implement compiler-indexed `local`, `effect`, and `ui/dispatch-fn` against `spec/004-Views.md` lifecycle/local/effects law and synthesis 02 §5 / 03 §6. `local` is narrow view ephemera; its setter is host-only, render-phase mutation fails loudly, and committed same-view handlers may read the committed local slot. JVM structural render exposes the initial value but setter invocation raises `:rf.error/jvm-host-op`. `effect` compares literal dependencies with `rf=`, supports `:connect`, honors cleanup on dependency change/disconnect/unmount, and is StrictMode replay-safe by contract. `dispatch-fn` has stable identity, reads the committed frame at call time, and raises `:rf.error/dispatch-disconnected` when no connected incarnation owns it. Confirm the already-landed `lease` implementation still obeys the S3 view-level lease fixture; fix only concrete drift.

## Constraints
Depend on the committed event spine and reuse its slot publication. No generalized hook engine, global local-state store, mount-once spelling, render-time ownership, or implicit effect-to-event bridge. Do not edit hot-zone files until transferred; never commit `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Red-before-fix fixtures prove local initialization, committed handler reads, batched setter behavior, render-phase rejection, JVM initial-value-only behavior, and typed host-op failure.
- Effect fixtures prove `rf=` dependency retention, dependency cleanup-before-restart, `:connect` reconnect behavior, disconnect/unmount cleanup, and StrictMode replay without leaked ownership.
- `dispatch-fn` is referentially stable across renders, retargets only on commit, dispatches through the winning frame, and fails after disconnect/destroy.
- A mixed local-set plus controlled dispatch produces one host render pass while the event drain commits first.
- S3 lease confirmation exercises connect/disconnect/retarget/HMR without adding a second lease mechanism.
- Focused compiler/JVM/browser tests are green; required spec/catalogue edits wait for exclusive hot-zone ownership.
notes: AMENDED 2026-07-16 — component-library readiness P0-1 (DIRECTED by Mike; owning doc drafts/component-library-readiness.md; this note is authoritative over the original Scope where they differ): local returns a THREE-TUPLE [value set! update!]. set! stores its argument EXACTLY — a stored function is a value, never an updater (no useState fn-overload). update! applies (f current & args) to the LATEST HOST STATE (not the committed render's value) so several same-turn host writers (key+pointer, timer+listener, observer+handler) compose instead of last-write-wins — the multi-writer contract a component library cannot build soundly itself (re-com evidence: 348 reset!/swap! lines/27 files; v-table wheel+resize+mouse writers; multi-select click+keyboard). update! is legal in committed handlers and effect callbacks; render-phase use = existing dev error; participates in :local-state cause evidence; rides the HMR hook signature; JVM raises the same typed host-op error as set!. ADDITIONAL ACCEPTANCE: batched two-writer matrix (both writes land, all three arms); fn-value set! stores exactly; mixed update!+dispatch in one turn; StrictMode replay; JVM typed failure; cause-evidence rows (gate G-15 in 07 §5). EXPLICITLY OUT: reset-key/derived local (trigger-gated spike bead on the program epic — key must be an explicit caller revision, never the model value); any fn-overloaded setter. The migrator's swap! rewrite retargets to update!; its MANUAL flag on multi-writer idioms retires with this contract.

description:

title: Make guide test examples install adapters and release caller-owned frames
description:
PR #5886 (exact head 544d6cf2d043365e6a097a464540e832f54d7762) made the public guide examples copyable by replacing ui.test/frame with rf/make-frame, but it left two prerequisites implicit and therefore made several canonical examples false as copied.

A clean JVM namespace cannot call make-frame until a substrate adapter is installed: the runtime raises :rf.error/no-adapter-installed. The repository's Guide-09 fixture silently supplies plain-atom/adapter, but the guide neither teaches nor links that setup. Once an adapter exists, make-frame creates a live anonymous frame whose lifecycle belongs to the caller. ui.test/with-root owns only its React root and DOM container; it does not destroy a frame supplied by the test. The examples in Guide 01, Guide 04, Guide 09, and Guide 10 therefore retain live frame/subscription state on success, and especially on assertion failure, thrown bodies, or rejected Promises.

Correct the examples as one small lifecycle recipe, not as a new test framework: teach the per-suite adapter/reset fixture once; link earlier snippets to that prerequisite; use rf/with-new-frame for synchronous examples; and put caller-owned frame destruction in an honest Promise settlement/finally path for mounted examples. Preserve the primary test failure if cleanup also fails. State explicitly that root ownership and frame ownership are separate.

This is a follow-up to closed guide-authority work rf2-vxgfnd.114 and the mechanical ui.test/frame removal; do not reopen or amend either closed bead.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A reader can copy the first Tier-1 JVM example into a clean test namespace, install exactly the documented fixture, and run it without :rf.error/no-adapter-installed.
2. Canonical synchronous examples use an ownership form that releases their frame on success, assertion failure, and thrown body.
3. Canonical Promise-backed mounted examples release both the root/container and the caller-owned frame after fulfillment and rejection, while retaining the original failure as primary.
4. Focused executable guide fixtures compare live-frame and subscription/cache state with a starting baseline; removing either frame cleanup or adapter setup makes a fixture fail.
5. The prose explicitly distinguishes ui.test/with-root ownership from externally created frame ownership and introduces no redundant public helper.
notes:

Scope corrected after the #5894 renumbering: rf/make-frame test fences with no adapter install are in chapters 01 (L110), 04 (L131), 06 (L168), 07 (L99), 08 (L17, L98, L111). The description's Guide 09/Guide 10 refs are pre-renumbering and no longer hold (current ch 09/10 contain no make-frame); re-verify chapter scope with a grep at execution.
RATIONALE: Verified 2026-07-15: no guide test fence installs an adapter (production paths ch 01 L63 / ch 06 L138 correctly use rf/init! ui/adapter; test fences do not) and no destroy-frame!/with-new-frame/finally cleanup exists anywhere under guide/. IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE: Per the description: teach one per-suite adapter/reset fixture (ch 08 testing is the natural home; earlier chapters' first test fence links to it); use rf/with-new-frame for synchronous Tier-1 examples (real v1 front-porch API, spec/API.md L213 — eval-bind-run-destroy); mounted ch-08 examples release the caller-owned frame via destroy-frame! in an honest Promise settlement/finally path with the primary failure preserved. title: Specify root teardown lifecycle, settlement, and tearing-down diagnostics
description:
## Problem

PR #5885 introduces a live-root lifecycle with deferred host settlement, but the normative contracts still describe unmount as simple root unregistration. Spec 004C does not define `:live → :tearing-down → :released`, the host settlement boundary, double-unmount behavior, quarantine, or when root ID/container/prefix reuse becomes legal. Spec 009's `duplicate-root-id`, `root-container-in-use`, and `root-not-live` rows likewise describe only live/stale cases and omit tearing-down meanings plus the emitted `:existing {:tearing-down? true}` evidence.

Without normative state semantics, implementation, guide, diagnostics and future fixes can disagree about whether framework death, host settlement and claim release are the same event. This is especially unsafe for the cell-less/throwing remainder (`rf2-vxgfnd.275`) and adapter-wide completion (`.276`). PR #5885 explicitly deferred the contract slice; no live bead owns it.

## Smallest elegant correction

After the runtime/adapter settlement law is final, make one sequenced documentation pass: define the exact lifecycle and settlement authority in Spec 004C, align the three existing Spec 009 rows and recovery/data shapes, then update active guide/implementation prose. Reuse existing error IDs and evidence; do not invent another public state machine or diagnostic category.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 004C defines every live-root lifecycle state used by the implementation, legal transitions, the distinction between framework-unusable and host-container-settled, exact-incarnation quarantine, and the precise boundary after which ID/container/prefix reuse is allowed.
- It specifies synchronous, deferred, cell-less/hidden, failed-first-mount, throwing host cleanup, double-unmount, same-id successor and different-id/same-container behavior consistently with `.275`.
- Adapter disposal completion/reinitialization semantics match the ruling and implementation from `.276`, including any asynchronous Promise boundary if selected.
- Spec 009's existing `duplicate-root-id`, `root-container-in-use`, and `root-not-live` rows enumerate tearing-down causes, stable recovery guidance, and exact emitted data including `:tearing-down?`; no new error ID is added.
- Active guide, public/internal docstrings and Specs 004C/006/009 use the same state names and do not say unmount merely unregisters before host settlement.
- A focused contract-drift check enumerates implementation lifecycle states and diagnostic tags; deleting `:tearing-down` or its evidence from either contract fails without adding a general prose parser.
- Historical text may remain historical. Root/browser, diagnostic catalogue and docs gates remain green.
notes: Spec 006 root-teardown-lifecycle SLICE merged (PR #5936: 3-state :live/:tearing-down/:released lifecycle, settlement independence per .275, tearing-down reuse diagnostics, dispose-adapter! sync-nil honesty; source-verified vs reactive.cljc/client.cljs). REMAINING slices (bead stays open): Spec 004C lifecycle-state home; Spec 009 catalogue-row edits; the AC6 contract-drift gate.

title: Close the remaining false-greens in the observation schema gate
description:
## Problem

Merged PR #5884 binds observation callback-failure records to the canonical schema, but three false-green paths remain in the executable proof.

1. The schema intentionally types `:exception` as `:any`, and the generic validator accepts every value. The HMR/disposed fixtures assert exact throwable identity only on the separate always-on record, not the dev-trace tags. Changing trace `:exception` to nil still passes even though Specs 006/009 require the original throwable there.
2. The Spec 009 catalogue comparison uses substring matching. Removing the exact `:exception` tag while retaining `:exception-message` still satisfies the check.
3. The schema-shape pin omits the canonical optional `[:frame {:optional true} :keyword]` row. Because the map is open, deleting that row or weakening it to `:any` leaves real records and every shape assertion green, even though runtime emits the frame tag.

Current runtime/spec values are correct; the problem is causal gate fidelity. Closed source `rf2-qyvyes` cannot be amended. Open `rf2-gsxe1z` owns source-realm attribution for another emission arm, not this schema/test binding.

## Smallest elegant correction

Keep portable `:exception :any`, but assert exact Throwable identity in the real trace fixtures. Compare the Spec 009 tag catalogue using exact backtick-delimited keyword tokens, not substrings. Pin the optional frame row and real frame value, or deliberately remove frame from schema/emission together if that contract is rejected. Use focused extraction helpers; do not build a general Markdown/schema framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Real HMR and disposed fixtures assert `(identical? boom (:exception (:tags trace-event)))`, independently of the always-on record. Mutating only trace tags to nil/a different throwable fails.
- Removing exact backticked `:exception` from the Spec 009 DEV-TRACE row while retaining `:exception-message` fails the catalogue gate. Exact-token extraction does not accept prefixes or prose occurrences.
- The extracted canonical schema is pinned to `[:frame {:optional true} :keyword]`; deleting the row or weakening it to `:any` fails. Real trace tags carry the exact expected frame keyword, while legitimately absent optional frame cases remain valid.
- Required/optional key, enum, vector, category and other type mutations already covered by the gate continue to fail.
- CLJ and CLJS real records validate against the one canonical schema; no handwritten duplicate schema or general parser is introduced.
- Existing provenance identity, HMR/disposed sibling drain, production-elision, Spec 009 catalogue and schema tests remain green.
close_reason: Merged PR #5910 (closed 3 observation schema-gate false-greens: trace :exception identity asserted independently of always-on record; 009 catalogue substring-scan->exact backtick keyword-token extraction; shape pin adds [:frame {:optional true} :keyword]; compile-time canonical schema validates both hosts)

title: Make JVM observation provenance storage reload-safe and weak-lifecycle proven
description:
## Problem

Merged PR #5884 at exact authored head 1a4f03116ed925de66a2c6db85238815cbedcf94 correctly replaces direct Throwable keys with a private weak-identity structure on a fresh JVM, but keeps the same `defonce provenance-by-throwable` Var name while changing its representation. The predecessor value is a synchronized `WeakHashMap<Throwable,Provenance>`; the new implementation expects a plain `HashMap<WeakReference-key,channels>` plus a reference queue. A normal Clojure namespace reload retains the old `defonce` root.

After an upgrade/reload, existing raw-Throwable entries cannot be found through the new WeakReference lookup key. Newly added wrapper keys are themselves weak keys in the retained WeakHashMap and have no other strong owner, so the wrapper may be collected while the underlying Throwable remains strongly live. Authentic provenance then disappears and the same source error can be wrapped/reported again. Fresh-process tests cover equality collisions and hostile methods but never predecessor-state reload or the promised weak-retention lifecycle.

This is an HMR/REPL upgrade-shape problem, not a defect in the fresh-process identity algorithm, which both audits otherwise found sound. Closed source `rf2-fs99nq` cannot be amended.

## Smallest elegant correction

Version or recognize the private storage representation and replace/migrate an incompatible predecessor root during namespace reload. Keep the fix local to this private state; do not create a generic weak-map abstraction, public migration API, or strong global registry. Add focused reload and GC lifecycle proofs.
acceptance_criteria:
- A JVM fixture preloads/seeds the predecessor synchronized `WeakHashMap` representation under the existing Var, reloads the current observation namespace without `remove-ns`, and proves the current versioned representation is installed or correctly migrated.
- After current attestation, retain the Throwable strongly, force bounded GC and subsequent association access, and prove authentic provenance remains covered with no duplicate callback-failure wrapper.
- Release the Throwable, retain only a WeakReference, force bounded GC plus a later map access, and prove the referent clears and private storage returns to baseline; values/keys do not retain it.
- Repeated reloads are idempotent and thread-safe. A reload during ordinary observation use either preserves valid entries or fails closed without silence/corruption according to an explicit private rule.
- Mutation back to an unversioned `defonce` retaining the predecessor map fails the reload fixture. A strong-map mutation fails the reclamation fixture.
- Existing collision, hostile equality/hash, forged/transplanted token, exact-authentic rethrow, CLJS WeakMap, HMR/disposed, and production-elision gates remain green.
close_reason: Merged PR #5910 (reload-safe JVM observation provenance: bundle map+queue into one versioned holder reconciled by idempotent alter-var-root compare-and-replace — defonce Var kept name across #5884's representation change, orphaning predecessor entries on reload; version-mismatch replace drops predecessor provenance->reads uncovered->drain fails LOUD; 3 deterministic weak-lifecycle GC proof fixtures no sleeps)

title: Preserve self-head precedence and prove real CLJS authoring-head routing
description:
## Problem

Merged PR #5883 at exact authored head 990d5c830dbce58a29f98589fa5bb6574b113853 reserves resolved `sub`/`lease`/`frame` component heads before generic component classification, but that new branch also runs before the compiler's pinned self-recursion rule. An unshadowed vector head equal to the current `defview`'s `:self` must classify as an internal view before Var resolution because the view Var may not exist yet.

In a namespace using the documented referred spellings, each of these valid recursive definitions now fails with `:rf.ui.compile/unsupported-form`: `(defview sub [] [sub {}])`, and the equivalent views named `lease` or `frame`. The environment correctly marks `:self 'sub`, but the resolver still sees the pre-existing referred `re-frame.ui/sub`; reserved-authoring-head rejection wins before `env/classify-head` can select self. No grammar rule reserves these words as view-definition names. Local binding precedence must still outrank self.

The PR's acceptance/rejection tests use an injected resolver in a CLJ-host environment. Its real-host proof covers JVM macroexpansion and fully qualified spellings only. It does not exercise production `cljs.analyzer.api/resolve`, referred/aliased spellings, or the separate CLJS root-entry compiler used by mount/render/hydrate. A resolver or root routing regression can therefore reclassify a public authoring verb as foreign while all new tests remain green.

Closed source `.266` cannot be amended. Open `.233` already owns kind-correct frame/lease diagnostic recovery and `.224` owns normative special-form grammar; this bead does not duplicate either.

## Smallest elegant correction

Centralize vector-head precedence: local/dynamic bindings first, then exact unshadowed `:self`, then reserved frame-boundary/reactive-authoring heads, then ordinary internal/foreign classification. Add a lean real CLJS analyzer/compiler fixture covering both defview and one root-entry route. Do not introduce reserved-name rules, a component registry, or a general analyzer harness.
acceptance_criteria:
- Real CLJ and CLJS namespaces that refer public `sub`, `lease`, or `frame` can define a recursive `defview` with the same local view name; its `[self ...]` head classifies as an internal view and compiles.
- A local binding with the same spelling remains a dynamic head and outranks self. Qualified `[ui/sub ...]`, `[ui/lease ...]`, and `[ui/frame ...]` in unrelated views remain typed rejects rather than foreign components.
- One in-memory real CLJS analyzer/compiler fixture uses referred, aliased, and fully qualified spellings for all three verbs through an actual `defview` route and at least one real mount/render!/hydrate-root root-entry route.
- Illegal component-head forms reject before emission; legal leading lease declarations and normal direct reactive calls remain legal and produce the expected manifest/wrapper.
- Mutating precedence back to reserved-before-self fails the recursive controls. Bypassing canonical-FQN reservation in either defview or root compilation makes at least one real-CLJS fixture compile foreign and fail.
- The emitted/advanced output proof shows no illegal public authoring function survives executable output.
- Diagnostic wording work remains with open `.233`; grammar ripple remains coordinated with `.224`. JVM/CLJS compiler goldens and production-elision gates remain green.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5909 (commit 511a834b37, branch worker/self-head-274). Fix: self-head? tier-2 precedence in analyze dispatch — exact unshadowed :self classifies as internal view BEFORE the Var-resolved frame-boundary/reactive-authoring reservations. Root compiler reuses analyze/analyze so ordering holds for mount/render!/hydrate-root. Real-CLJS routing proved via genuine cljs.analyzer namespace state (referred/aliased/fq, defview + root-entry routes, no injected resolver). Mutation controls A (reserved-before-self) + B (bypass reservation) verified red. Gates: ui clojure -M:test 523/6527 green; npm run test:cljs 9400/44601 green. Diagnostics stay with .233; Spec 004 grammar ripple coordinated with .224. LEFT OPEN per brief (do not merge).
close_reason: Merged PR #5909 (preserve self-head precedence + prove real CLJS authoring-head routing: single self-head? predicate gives exact unshadowed :self tier-2 precedence ahead of Var-resolved frame-boundary/reactive-authoring reservations; extends .266/.268; mutation controls red (reserved-before-self + bypass-FQN-reservation); CI green)

title: Make join strict-mint and replay proofs causally distinguish live generation
description:
## Problem

Merged PR #5881 claims strict mint-policy inheritance and strict replay for join completions, but its fixtures do not exercise strict behavior. The target used by the `:strict` transport test declares no generator-backed coeffect requirements, so `:strict` and `:live` are observationally identical; the test merely sees the policy keyword in router options. The alleged replay case supplies `:rf.cofx` but omits `:rf.cofx/mint-policy :strict`, so runtime default `:live` applies. Removing join authority tests the private authority gate, not strict rejection of missing recorded facts.

The suite therefore proves EDN authority survival and parallel controls, but not the load-bearing promise that a completion inherits strict minting, does not consult the host, and replays from recorded causal facts. Green exact-head CI cannot distinguish a transport that silently falls back to live generation.

Closed source `rf2-lud4af` cannot be amended. `rf2-ixjd48` concerns post-resolution authority validation, not mint-policy causality.

## Smallest elegant correction

Add one real generator-backed required coeffect to the join completion target and compare strict with live using the existing record/replay machinery. This is a causal proof task; do not add a join-specific replay format, coeffect, or test framework. If the proof exposes a runtime propagation defect, fix only the existing envelope/policy handoff.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real join completion target requires a generator-backed recordable coeffect. Under inherited `:strict`, omit that fact and prove the generator is never called, the parent does not fold, and the canonical missing-fact outcome is produced.
- A `:live` foil for the same target invokes the generator and completes normally, proving the fixture can observe the distinction.
- Record a genuine completion carrying the required fact, restore pre-event state, and replay with explicit `:rf.cofx/mint-policy :strict`; runtime-db, parent fold/resolution, authority and terminal evidence match without host generation.
- Remove the recorded required fact and prove strict replay fails through the canonical outcome. Stripping or changing the inherited policy to `:live` makes the test fail.
- CLJ and CLJS coverage exercise the shared envelope path; no test succeeds merely by asserting a policy keyword.
- Existing EDN authority, tamper rejection, parallel join, replay, and recordable-coeffect controls remain green; no new public format is added.
close_reason: Merged PR #5929 (.22 triage: join strict-mint proofs were inert; added 4 real causal proofs, red-before-fix; test-only; CI green)

title: Complete frame-boundary lifecycle guidance and artifact inventories
description:
## Problem

Merged PR #5878 at exact authored head 442fa1b4eb6a885914defd070e699057e309e915 updates the implementor skill to name separate `frame-root` and `frame-provider` components, but does not carry the load-bearing lifecycle contract that makes the split safe. The changed `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-2-impl-order.md` tells a port to realize both components while omitting that ENSURE is commit-owned and two-pass: an abandoned render must create/seed nothing; a committed boundary first ENSUREs, then renders ready descendants; initial events run once per live incarnation; StrictMode/remount is idempotent; mounted id/options reconfiguration fails loud. A port can call `make-frame` during render, create ghost frames, and still satisfy every conformance item the skill names.

The paragraph also links to a nonexistent `spec/004-Views.md` `§Frame propagation` heading instead of the authoritative Spec 002 boundary sections. Active `spec/Conventions.md` remains pre-split in four inventory summaries: the core lifecycle/scope overview and core/UIx/Helix artifact rows name `frame-provider` without `frame-root`. That contradicts #5878's claim that the remaining residue was confined to the synthesis/skill and leaves implementors and artifact consumers with an incomplete export inventory.

This does not reopen R-7 and does not justify further investment in retiring UIx/Helix. Their rows need only remain truthful until S7 deletes them. Open `.177` owns compiled 004C-preflight versus Spec-002 ownership, `.179` owns canonical/frozen/retiring classification, and `rf2-vxgfnd.263` owns resolver guidance; none owns this implementor lifecycle matrix and artifact inventory.

## Smallest elegant correction

Add one compact commit-owned/discard-safe lifecycle paragraph and minimum boundary conformance matrix to the existing implementor section, linking directly to Spec 002's actual `frame-root` and `frame-provider` headings. Reuse existing split/lifecycle fixtures and add only a missing causal abandoned-render check if necessary. Add `frame-root` beside `frame-provider` in the affected Conventions inventories; keep UIx/Helix wording minimal and delete it with those adapters at S7. No runtime/API redesign or compatibility mechanism.
acceptance_criteria:
- The implementor guide states: `frame-root` ENSURE is performed only from a committed layout boundary; an abandoned render creates/seeds/emits nothing; the first committed pass may withhold descendants until ready; reuse does not reseed; initial events run once per live incarnation; StrictMode/remount is idempotent; mounted id/options reconfiguration fails with the catalogued error.
- The guide separately states `frame-provider` is SCOPE-only over an already-live frame, creates/seeds/destroys nothing, and fails loud when absent. Both did-you-mean key directions are named.
- Links resolve to the exact existing Spec 002 `frame-root` and `frame-provider` sections; no link claims a nonexistent Spec 004 `Frame propagation` heading.
- The minimum React-host conformance matrix proves abandoned root render causes zero frame/initial-event writes, committed mount exposes descendants only after ENSURE, reuse/StrictMode/remount seed once per live incarnation, reconfiguration fails, provider existing/absent behavior, and both swapped-key diagnostics. Reuse existing tests; add only missing causal rows. Removing commit ownership makes the abandoned-render proof fail.
- Active Conventions core lifecycle/scope and artifact summaries list both boundaries. Frozen Reagent remains fully described; UIx/Helix rows are corrected minimally and remain marked for S7 deletion rather than gaining new features.
- A focused active-doc inventory/link check fails on provider-only summaries or missing headings without adding a general documentation framework.
- No public API or ratified decision changes, and no duplicate work is taken from `.177`, `.179`, or `.263`.

title: State compiled frame ENSURE preflight as already landed
description:
## Problem

Merged PR #5878 at exact authored head 442fa1b4eb6a885914defd070e699057e309e915 correctly says the `frame-root`/`frame-provider` split has landed, but replaces the old history with a new false final-state claim. `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/README.md` and `03-reactivity-and-ownership.md` now say that moving compiled-substrate ENSURE timing to host preflight remains future R-7 work. That behavior is already implemented and shipped in the current `re-frame.ui` substrate.

At the exact head, client mount/render preflight routes extracted frame plans through `frames/execute-frame-plans!` before React root creation/render. The frame implementation identifies itself as the live preflight consumer, and the same 03 document elsewhere already says ENSURE runs at host preflight. Closed `rf2-vxgfnd.9` confirms PR #5711 delivered the behavior. The new future-tense status is therefore both source-inaccurate and internally contradictory.

This matters because the synthesis suite presents itself as authoritative final state. A worker reading the changed paragraphs can schedule an already-complete runtime migration, misread R-7's remaining spec/promotion work as implementation work, or attempt to preserve legacy commit-owned timing in the compiled substrate. Docs-only CI was green because runtime gates were classifier-skipped. No live bead owns this stale status.

## Smallest elegant correction

State the final split by host: both the component split and compiled-substrate host-preflight ENSURE timing have landed; the frozen/retiring legacy adapters retain commit-owned two-pass ENSURE. In the touched Spec-004 rewrite ripple row, describe remaining R-7 work as promotion/reconciliation of the already-live contract, not moving runtime timing. This is a documentation correction only—do not reopen the ruling or change runtime/API behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- The synthesis README and 03 final-state text say that `re-frame.ui` extracts frame plans and executes ENSURE during host preflight before React, while legacy Reagent/UIx/Helix adapters retain commit-owned two-pass ENSURE for their lifetime.
- The Spec-004 rewrite draft and every active R-7 status reference distinguish already-landed runtime behavior from remaining spec/promotion/reconciliation work; no active non-historical passage says compiled host-preflight timing is still to be implemented.
- A classified source-backed check or existing synthesis validator ties the status to the live call chain: mount/render preflight invokes `execute-frame-plans!` before root creation/render. Do not create a new general documentation framework.
- Existing exactly-once, no-reseed, failure-before-host-render, plan extraction, and preflight fixtures remain the behavioral evidence; documentation does not overclaim beyond them.
- Historical records may retain past tense, but the authoritative final-state suite is self-consistent and contains no contradictory future-tense R-7 implementation claim.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5887 (rf2-vxgfnd.269/.270 cluster; commit 5773639ef2). Left open for the mayor to merge.
close_reason: Merged PR #5887 (state compiled frame ENSURE preflight as already landed in synthesis README — split #5691 shipped; frame-root {:id} owns ENSURE, frame-provider {:frame} SCOPEs)

title: Bind observation callback-failure tests to the executable canonical schema
description:
## Problem

PR #5870 (head 26b89b0ac51c04f5fa04c23fe31560288d86921c) advertises a catalogue-to-schema/record validation gate for `:rf.error/observation-on-change-failed`, but the test does not execute or structurally bind the canonical schema.

The runtime validator is a hand-copied predicate. The Spec-Schemas leg only substring-scans the Markdown block for the category and field names. Consequently the canonical schema can change `:where` from symbol to keyword, weaken the `:cause` enum, make required query keys optional, or replace vector types with any; all tests stay green while real HMR/disposed records no longer conform. Spec 009's declared tags can drift independently too.

Separately, #5870 now normatively calls emission provenance opaque/non-forgeable while in-progress rf2-9m4oy7 is changing that runtime contract. This follow-up must validate the final post-9m4oy7 shape rather than freezing today's false claim. Do not amend the active provenance bead.

## Smallest correction

Extract and structurally read this one canonical schema form, normalize it minimally, and validate real records plus the Spec 009 row against it. Avoid building a general Markdown schema framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Real :hmr and :disposed callback-failure records validate against the actual extracted ObservationOnChangeFailedTags form on CLJ and CLJS.
- Required-to-optional, enum-to-keyword, vector-to-any, field type, category/channel and Spec-009/schema tag-key drift each fail deterministically.
- Removing a required runtime field fails the same causal gate.
- The hand-copied predicate is removed or proven generated/equivalent from the canonical form; substring presence is not credited as schema validation.
- After rf2-9m4oy7 lands, Spec 006/009/Spec-Schemas opacity and provenance language matches the final runtime authentication shape.
- No general schema engine, new error category, public API, or duplicate provenance implementation.
close_reason: Merged PR #5884 (bind callback-failure tests to executable canonical schema: compile-time macro extracts ObservationOnChangeFailedTags from Spec-Schemas.md + structural interpreter validates real records; hand-copied predicate + substring scan removed; schema-shape pin + 009-tag-binding tests; drift now reddens; CI green)

title: Finish and correct the two-point ViewCell HMR authority contract
description:
## Problem

PR #5866 (head aecdbda25b741457e4ac46fb4565885330ff96ca) adds the second ViewCell authority fence to Specs 004/006, but active contracts remain inconsistent.

It also says the whole two-point fence and both points constant-fold away in production. - Tracked active HMR contracts describe entry and final-publication fences, both authority axes, and staged-only rollback consistently.
- Spec 006 is self-contained: no unresolved step-1/step-6 coordinates.
- Production wording says registry lookup/revision arm/final re-read erase, while the entry cell-generation comparison remains.
