title: Exercise preflight generation fencing through real ENSURE initial events and receipt cleanup
description:
## Problem

PR #5864's exact-generation preflight code is tested only through client/set-preflight-hook! returning nil and direct minimal substrate lifecycle resets. It does not execute real frame ENSURE, synchronous :initial-events, frames/execute-frame-plans!, or an actual preflight-attempt receipt. Consequently it cannot prove abort cleanup, terminally honest attempt evidence, observation ownership, or protection of a same-id successor. A mutation breaking receipt abort/cleanup while leaving the generation check intact stays green.

Open rf2-vxgfnd.191 owns plan authority/overlap and rf2-vxgfnd.248 owns settlement after React commit; neither owns real initial-event admission and cleanup before createRoot.

## Smallest correction

Use the first-party UI/adapter browser harness with a real frame-root and actual initial event. Coordinate existing owners; do not redesign preflight authority or add a public hook.
acceptance_criteria:
- Real frame-root initial event destroys A before createRoot; mount fails with the expected typed pre-createRoot error.
- Second case destroys A and installs same-id B; no root/DOM/ViewCell/observation owner is created for A, A's attempt receipt is cleaned/terminally honest, and B token/spec/root remain untouched.
- A later legitimate B mount succeeds.
- The fixture observes real frame evidence/ownership ledgers rather than inferring cleanup solely from no live React root.
- Removing receipt abort cleanup or the generation recheck makes the fixture fail.
- Browser/UI ownership gates pass; no public API or authority redesign.
notes: PR #5940 (open, do not merge yet). Test-only: production correct (rf2-vxgfnd.199 fence + .139 receipt cleanup already correct; was under-proven). Added node fixture re-frame.ui.preflight-generation-fence-cljs-test driving client/mount* over the LIVE ENSURE executor with real :initial-events. title: Complete executable proof of both ViewCell commit-authority axes and rollback
description:
## Problem

PR #5862 (head 7dc47ab071f646c63a87b4f68035188821801076) adds the correct final ViewCell authority fence, but its tests cover only registered-view revision movement and observation-only commit. Several independent obligations remain mutation-surviving: cell-local generation can be removed; the 'during acquisition' case actually changes authority after all acquisitions return; stale retarget/drop never has non-empty to-release; zero-owner assertions cannot prove reverse order or exactly-once; and commit-resources! preservation is unexercised.

The runtime algorithm survived correctness review. This bead is a bounded proof completion, not a redesign.

## Smallest correction

Extend the existing HMR authority test namespace with test-only acquisition/release instrumentation. No production seam or API.
acceptance_criteria:
- A direct/unregistered cell advances its local generation during commit; publication is rejected.
- A stale retarget/drop has non-empty to-release and preserves prior query, value, lease identity, lifecycle and revision byte-for-byte.
- Instrumented staged acquisitions release exactly once in reverse order (for staged :b then :c, log [:c :b]); retained prior :a is not released.
- Re-registration occurs inside an obs/acquire! wrapper/cache construction, not only at post-stage-acquire.
- commit-resources! rejection preserves desired/reserved/held state.
- Removing the cell-generation arm, reversing rollback order, or releasing to-release before the final fence makes a fixture fail.

title: Exercise exact-incarnation app-db vacation and epoch fencing for flows
description:
## Problem

The helper, its exact commit-epoch bump, and its immediate post-vacation stop therefore have no executable proof.

A regression to the bare-id helper or an unfenced epoch bump can mutate same-id B while all merged fixtures stay green.

## Smallest correction

- A's already-linearized write stands only in A's detached container.
- B's app-db sentinel, flow row, dirty cache, commit epoch and trace evidence remain byte-identical.

title: Prove mixed-incarnation lease acquisition cannot publish a ViewCell capture
description:
## Problem

PR #5854 (head c85ffb71574c664c569fde99ce45701e71609b06) concludes that candidate-current? rejects a superseded lease before publication, but the committed regression fixture does not exercise the required mixed-incarnation acquisition. Both leases are acquired from A; replacement happens only at post-stage-acquire. The source bead required a deterministic interleave: acquire lease 1 from A, recreate same-id B, then acquire lease 2 from B.

Without that barrier, a regression that combines candidates across incarnations, releases the wrong owner, or mutates B during stale rejection can survive. The algorithm appears sound; this is a narrow executable-proof gap, not a request for a new runtime abstraction.

## Smallest correction

Add a test-only acquisition wrapper/barrier around the existing port. Do not expose a production API or add scheduler machinery.
acceptance_criteria:
- Lease 1 is acquired from A, a barrier destroys A and publishes same-id B, and lease 2 is acquired from B in one staged attempt.
- The mixed candidate set never publishes or connects.
- Newly staged leases release exactly once in reverse order; B's owners/state remain unchanged.
- A live single-incarnation control still publishes normally.
- Mutating candidate-current? or omitting one exact-incarnation check makes the fixture fail on CLJ/CLJS as applicable.

title: CI throughput: trim/prioritize the perennial back-of-queue stragglers (tools/template, example-coverage) — throughput lever 4
description: Evidenced recurring throughput cost (2026-07-14): on nearly every PR — including trivial adapter/docs PRs (e.g. #5863 kopcit, stuck 2+ mayor ticks) and every core-matrix PR — the last two checks to clear are consistently 'JVM tools/template (clojure -M:test)' and 'CLJS (compile every standalone example build, coverage gate)', both sitting queued at elapsed=0 behind the rest of the matrix. They gate 'fully green', so each PR's merge waits on these two back-of-queue jobs regardless of how fast everything else ran. TWO possible fixes (operator/CI-config decision, needs Mike's eye — do NOT auto-implement): (1) narrow the changed-surface classifier so tools/template + example-coverage are NOT selected for change surfaces they cannot be affected by (e.g. a docstring-only adapter change or a core/observation change that can't alter template/example compilation) — mirrors the #5840 rename-classifier work; (2) raise these two jobs' runner-queue priority so they don't perpetually land last. Combine with the throughput levers already adopted (bigger same-surface clusters, ≤2 concurrent core-matrix lanes, settle-between-merges) and the merged .beads paths-ignore (#5837/#5840). NOT on the S2 critical path; a standing CI-efficiency improvement.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option 1 — narrow the changed-surface classifier so the two straggler jobs stop running on surfaces they cannot be affected by; Option 2 (runner-queue priority) is REJECTED as a standalone lever. Sequence strictly AFTER rf2-n8kkum merges.

RATIONALE: Both recorded opinions (original + CComposer research) converge on Option 1, and verification confirms the facts: cljs-examples-compile gates on cljs_browser (test.yml:1779) and jvm-tools-template on template_expensive (test.yml:2744), both blanket-armed by implementation/core/* and implementation/adapters/* in .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh (lines 154-233). Option 2 has no mechanism — every job is runs-on: ubuntu-latest with no priority knob; the tail is org-runner concurrency, and reordering would not remove the wasted work. Option 1 is the CORRECTNESS fix (removes runs that cannot regress) and the ELEGANT one (a job gets its own surface output instead of piggybacking cljs_browser). rf2-n8kkum is a hard prerequisite: PR #5840's eight real-Git discovery cases in implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs fail at process launch on the Windows dev host, so classifier edits cannot be validated locally until it lands.

ONE CORRECTION to the CComposer plan (verified 2026-07-15): the claim 'nightly/post-merge full matrix remains the safety net' for examples-compile is FALSE today. npm run test:examples-compile exists ONLY in test.yml's cljs-examples-compile job and scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh; expensive-tests.yml does NOT run it, and push-to-main runs the same classifier (HEAD^ diff), so un-arming core would leave core-induced example-build breakage with NO CI net. Phase 1 must add the compensating nightly step.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (phased; each phase its own PR; classifier + test.yml are .github hot-zone — sequential dispatch):
- Phase 0 = rf2-n8kkum (already filed): make classifyViaGitDiscovery portable (bash -s stdin or scratch-repo-relative path); all 138 cases must pass on Windows via node implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs.
- Phase 1 (the big win): add a dedicated examples_compile output to .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh; gate cljs-examples-compile on it instead of cljs_browser (test.yml:1776-1836); arm it for examples/**, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/package.json + package-lock.json, implementation/adapters/*, implementation/ui/*, and the per-feature artefact surfaces already in the broad bucket; STOP arming it on blanket implementation/core/*. In the SAME PR: add npm run test:examples-compile to expensive-tests.yml (cheap compile-only, no Playwright) so nightly catches core-induced example-build breakage; update mark_all(), the emit list, _changed-surfaces.test.cjs regression cases, TESTING.md matrix row, and the required-check aggregator expectations (test.yml:3652 needs list — skipped gated jobs must stay green-compatible).
- Phase 2 (smaller, higher care, only if template remains the habitual tail after Phase 1 metrics): surgical template_expensive narrowing ONLY — exclude test-only adapter paths (implementation/adapters/*/test/**); do NOT remove template_expensive from blanket implementation/core/* or implementation/adapters/* (rf2-jdj17.1 regression locks exist after real false-greens; the emitted :app compiles against core + adapters). A core narrowing would first require a maintained manifest of namespaces the emitted app compiles (mirror the is_story_xray_runtime_path predicate pattern).
- Acceptance: a core-only PR (e.g. touching implementation/core/src/re_frame/observation*) shows cljs-examples-compile SKIPPED with the aggregator green; an examples/** or shadow-cljs.edn PR still runs it; nightly expensive-tests.yml runs test:examples-compile unconditionally; all classifier tests pass on Windows and Ubuntu.
- Close rf2-gzavkm when live PRs no longer routinely tail on skipped-work stragglers; revisit dedicated runner capacity only if necessary runs still tail (the Option 3 threshold).

title: G-13: production-erased candidate-scan witness at the observation-port fan-out choke point
description:
## Problem

rf2-vxgfnd.210 hardened G-13 with a named V-independent candidate-work axis
(`port-fan-out` = C*Q, summed over all V live cells) and narrowed the gate's
claim honestly to V-independent DELIVERED push work. It could NOT close the
original criterion 1: a real source mutant that ENUMERATES all V mounted
cells/owners at the start of invalidation but ENROLLS only C (a pure membership
SCAN, O(V) per movement) leaves every delivered count identical and stays
green. A pure scan has no observable downstream effect, so no count and no
(threshold-free) timing can catch it.

The only causal seam is a production-erased counter at the observation port's
candidate-iteration / owner-selection choke point (`core/substrate/
observation.cljc` — the `fan-out!` / owner-selection path). That surface was
out of scope for the .210 worktree (a concurrent worker owned
core/observation.cljc). Scope decision recorded on .210: narrow honestly now,
file this to add the production-side witness.

## Expected behavior

Add the smallest production-erased witness (behind the debug/instrumentation
gate, DCE'd under goog.DEBUG=false, proven absent from the `:advanced` bundle
by the existing G-13 elision scan) that counts real candidate inspections /
bounded owner-selection work per movement. G-13 then compares it across V=100
and V=500 (expected = f(C), independent of V) and a source mutant that scans
all V while enrolling only C makes G-13 deterministically red — the original
rf2-vxgfnd.210 acceptance criterion 1.

## Constraints

- No production API, runtime-global counter in ordinary builds, wall-clock
  threshold, UIx/Helix dependency, or broad benchmark framework.
- Sequence AFTER PR #5860 (the .210 gate landing) and coordinate with the
  core/observation.cljc owner — this touches the production observation port.
notes: 2026-07-14 PR #5860 audit expansion: the emitted :candidate-work-projection and narrowed :proof-scope fields are not asserted by run-ui-g13.cjs, so deleting them or restoring an overclaim remains green. While adding the production-erased candidate witness, validate these metadata fields exactly and add a mutation that makes the gate red when the scope/projection drifts. This belongs here, not in a separate bead.

title: Reconcile and prove the split epoch snapshot/publish destroy contract
description:
PR #5850 introduced a new pre-dissociation late-bind phase, `:epoch/snapshot-frame-destroyed`, and split terminal snapshot from post-dissociation publication/compare-cleanup. The implementation directory is updated, but the normative and executable failure contracts still describe the old one-hook order.

Confirmed drift:
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc`'s ordered `destroy-frame!` docstring still says step 10 is direct dissociation and step 11 receives raw frame snapshots; it omits the pre-dissoc snapshot entirely.
- `spec/002-Frames.md` declares its 11-step order normative/port-required but likewise omits the new snapshot phase and does not state the snapshot/publish/drop ownership split.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`'s exhaustive `:rf.warning/teardown-hook-exception` row omits `:epoch/snapshot-frame-destroyed` and attributes all warnings to `safe-call-hook!`, while this path catches directly and records `:where :safe-call-hook!`.
- Tests pin invocation and arity but never make the new hook throw, so the promised diagnostic plus bounded always-on teardown report, continuation, and final dissociation are non-causal claims.

First land rf2-vxgfnd.244 and rf2-vxgfnd.245 so these documents describe the final terminal-delivery behavior. This bead is contract reconciliation and causal proof, not a redesign of frame destruction.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 002's normative destroy order and `destroy-frame!`'s ordered docstring name the pre-dissoc terminal snapshot, dissociation, and post-dissoc publication/compare-owned drop in their exact runtime order.
- The text distinguishes immutable predecessor terminal evidence from shared id-keyed stores and states which actions are allowed after a same-id successor claims them.
- Spec 009 lists `:epoch/snapshot-frame-destroyed` in the teardown diagnostic/report catalogue and truthfully names the direct catch/record boundary and `:where` evidence.
- A fail-before fixture makes the snapshot hook throw and proves teardown continues, the frame is dissociated, the post-dissoc hook still runs, exactly one diagnostic plus one bounded always-on teardown report identify the snapshot hook, and no fabricated terminal record appears.
- Failure proof also asserts no residual A ring or mutation of a same-id B, consistent with rf2-vxgfnd.244/.245.
- Late-bind directory, Spec 002, Spec 009, implementation docstrings, and tests agree on both hook signatures and ownership.

title: Fence overlapping async HMR activations by transaction generation
description:
PR #5848 stores published/staged digest state and the updating fence in one unversioned activation cell. Shadow build hooks may overlap asynchronously. If reload A pauses after staging d3, reload B stages/promotes d4, and A resumes later, A can regress the active program to d3 and/or clear B's newer fence.

Give activation transactions an ordering/ownership rule that makes stale completions inert. Prefer the smallest correct mechanism (for example a monotonically increasing generation/token checked at promotion and fence release, or explicit serialization). Do not introduce a general scheduler.

This work touches the same carrier and fixtures as the forward-recovery bead, so sequence it after rf2-vxgfnd.242 to avoid conflicts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every activation attempt owns a distinct generation/token or is serialized under an equivalent explicit invariant.
- Only the latest/current transaction may promote staged digest/bytes or clear the update fence; a stale success, rejection, or finally path is inert with respect to newer state.
- A browser/Shadow-shaped fixture pauses two reloads and releases newest-first, proving the active digest never regresses and a stale completion cannot clear the newer fence.
- Failure and retry paths preserve the last accepted program and eventually publish the newest accepted candidate exactly once.
- The implementation is local to activation ordering and does not add an unnecessary general concurrency abstraction.

Honest residual: :script older-first prior-identity window needs per-cycle tokens Shadow doesn't thread = beyond smallest-mechanism, documented.

title: Prove forward HMR recovery and fail descriptors closed with the digest fence
description:
PR #5848 made compiler digest, bytes, and HMR activation one transaction, but its recovery oracle does not prove forward recovery and descriptor publication remains partially open during the fence.

The current recovery test makes a v2 candidate throw, then restores the entire original v1 source. It accepts any recovered digest, so CI may pass by returning to the old digest without proving that the accepted compiler candidate and runtime converge. It also does not observe descriptors.

During an active update the digest carrier deliberately returns nil, yet `client.cljs` can still publish truthy complete component descriptors/index entries stamped with `:build-digest nil`. Spec 004C's complete-descriptor contract requires these surfaces to fail closed together.

Strengthen the oracle by keeping the v2 candidate and changing only the runtime-failure condition, then require the exact accepted v2 digest/bytes to become active. Observe a mounted root and descriptor/index visibility throughout the fence.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fail-before recovery fixture compiles a distinct v2 candidate, induces runtime activation failure, removes only the failure condition, and proves recovery to the exact compiler-accepted v2 digest/bytes rather than the old v1 identity.
- A mounted root remains on the last accepted program while the failed candidate is rejected, then advances exactly once to v2 on successful recovery.
- During the update fence, complete descriptor lookup is nil and descriptor indexes expose no partially complete entry; after recovery all descriptors carry the exact active non-nil digest.
- The test checks the relevant public descriptor fields/properties, not merely map equality, and deletion of the production fail-closed branch makes it fail.
- Stable output URL/rejected-byte retention remains owned by rf2-vxgfnd.237 and is not duplicated here.
notes: PR #5943 (open, do not merge). FIXED (test-only; production correct, was under-proven). digest_carrier.cljs + reactive.cljc UNCHANGED. Strengthened check-ui-digest-carrier.cjs counterexample 2: (1) forward recovery keeps the DISTINCT v2 body + removes only the failure condition -> runtime must converge on the EXACT compiler-accepted v2 digest/bytes (matched vs JVM accepted snapshot), never the prior v1 identity (old oracle restored whole v1 + accepted any bd1); (2) base.cljs mounts a REAL root (base-view->loaded-view) whose rendered program stays on accepted v1 through the fence then advances exactly once to v2; (3) mounted root COMPLETE Root Descriptor :build-digest fails closed (nil, never staged candidate/stale prior) TOGETHER with the carrier, restamps exact digest after recovery (Spec 004C). Red-before-fix via the real oracle: deleting digest_carrier/current fence guard -> fence null-read + descriptor read red (Timeout); reverting to restore-v1 recovery -> exact-v2 convergence assertion red (Timeout). Gates: ui-digest-carrier PASS; ui JVM 535t/6615a 0F/0E; test:cljs 9443t/46359a 0F/0E. SCOPE flag: stricter reading (client/descriptor returning nil / omitting entries during fence vs truthy map with :build-digest nil) is a client.cljs change, out of scope (.261 surface) -> separate ruling.

Stricter descriptor fail-closed (client/descriptor returning nil vs truthy-map-with-:build-digest-nil) = client.cljs change, follow-up.

title: Finish the observation port's closed grammar at every real boundary
description:
PR #5847 added typed rejects at observation-port target/lease boundaries, but the closed grammar is not yet enforced safely at the boundaries that construct and inspect those values.

Confirmed gaps:
1. `resolve-target` can inspect `(first query-v)` before validating the query and can return an empty/non-keyword target rejected by the downstream validator. Scalar/malformed input can therefore produce raw host errors or defer failure to an unrelated call site.
2. `owned?` is not covered by the lease validator used by read/release and still raw-errors on non-lease input. Give it an explicit total contract; the simplest fit with `current?` is false/no-throw for a non-lease.
3. Exact target validation builds `(set (keys target))` on every hot probe/acquire. This allocates/hashes all keys, permits hostile custom key hashing to throw an untyped error, and scales with attacker-controlled extras.
4. Malformed-target diagnostics promise bounded, value-free evidence but serialize raw `:kind` and the full key vector. Large maps produce unbounded messages and structured/secret keys can leak.
5. Spec 009 and focused fixtures do not enumerate the resulting branch/error evidence completely.

Preserve strict production validation, but implement it as a fixed-vocabulary check (`count` plus `contains?`/known fields), and keep diagnostic evidence bounded and normalized. Do not redesign the port or add speculative schemas.
acceptance_criteria:
- `resolve-target` validates query shape before sequence access and either returns a valid closed-grammar target or a typed documented rejection; scalar, empty, non-keyword, and mutated inputs have CLJ/CLJS fixtures.
- `owned?` has a documented total result for non-leases (recommended false/no-throw) and never leaks a raw host exception.
- Exact-key validation does not enumerate/hash arbitrary extra keys or allocate a set on the hot success path; hostile-hash extra keys cannot escape as raw errors.
- Rejection evidence contains only bounded normalized facts (kind class, total/extra count or boolean, known-key presence) and never raw key/value material; secret keys and 10k-key maps have fail-before tests.
- Spec 009 names every new rejection ID/evidence field and correctly states which operations throw versus return false.
- Existing valid-target/probe/acquire/read/release behavior and production validation remain unchanged.
notes:
PR opened (leave OPEN for mayor): https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5895 — commit e67b8aabc3. Closes audit gaps 1-4 (resolve-target query validation, owned? total contract, valid-target? fixed-vocabulary count+contains?, malformed-target bounded/normalized evidence). Gap 5 (Spec 009 doc) filed as rf2-vxgfnd.273. Gates green: JVM core 1978 tests 0/0; CLJS node 9388 tests 0/0 (both hosts). No new error id, no spec re-edit, no parallel validation path.
Rebased onto current main (picked up rf2-vxgfnd.238) + force-pushed: HEAD is now 058bd023bc (was e67b8aabc3; SAME diff, no content change). CI machines-job red on the first run was a FLAKY test (spawn-install-write-live-owner-installs-once / spawn-order fence), NOT a real break: origin/main full machines suite 4/4 green, my branch 8/8 green locally, passes in isolation; and my diff provably cannot touch that surface (machines never calls obs/resolve-target|owned?|valid-target?|probe|acquire!; the observation registrar-hook/drain/global-state is byte-identical to main). JVM core (my actual surface) + CLJS node-test + JVM ui all green on CI. Fresh CI run triggered by the force-push.

title: Prove the reactive legacy-root migration through the real reload hook
description:
PR #5844 added a load-time call to `migrate-legacy-root-cells!` in `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc`, intended to repair legacy root cells during namespace reload/HMR. Every migration test calls the helper directly. Deleting only the production top-level call would leave the suite green, so the behavior actually relied on by reloads is unproved.

Add a causal reload fixture that begins with a legacy root-cell shape, executes the real namespace-load/reload path, and observes the migration without invoking the helper from test code. The fixture should distinguish load-time wiring from the already-tested helper implementation and should match the Shadow/HMR lifecycle the hook is meant to support.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fail-before fixture executes the genuine load/reload entry path and proves a legacy root cell is migrated without a direct test call to `migrate-legacy-root-cells!`.
- Removing or moving the production top-level hook makes the fixture fail.
- The fixture covers idempotent repeat reload and preserves live root identity/state required by the HMR contract.
- Existing direct unit tests remain focused on helper semantics; the new test is explicitly a wiring/lifecycle test.

Production was correct but under-proven: the sibling helper suite calls migrate-legacy-root-cells! directly, so deleting the top-level (migrate-legacy-root-cells!) hook (reactive.cljc:2405) would leave it green. Added JVM-only wiring fixture reactive_root_reload_hook_wiring_jvm_test.clj that drives the REAL reload path (require ...:reload) and observes migration WITHOUT a direct helper call: load-time hook converges the legacy persistent-set entry to the host weak set, idempotent repeat reload (identical object), identity-preserving, converged entry supports .remove (the op that throws UnsupportedOperationException on the un-migrated persistent set). Red-before-green: disabling the hook -> 3 failures + APersistentSet .remove UnsupportedOperationException; fresh-registry no-op case stays green. reactive.cljc byte-identical to origin/main. title: Make Xray ViewCell evidence honor ownership on every init/read path
description:
PR #5844 hardened the Xray ViewCell evidence projection, but two public integration paths still violate the projection's ownership boundary.

1. `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/viewcell_evidence.cljs` records whether Xray actually acquired the projection (`installed?`), yet `rows` reads the shared projection regardless. If another owner installed the slot first and Xray's claim is rejected, Xray can still expose that foreign owner's evidence through rows/subscriptions/UI. Ownership rejection must mean no observation through Xray.
2. The preload path installs the projection, but the supported manual `day8.re-frame2-xray.core/init!` path does not. A clean process that requires core and invokes `init!` therefore enables Xray without ViewCell evidence.

Keep this change local to Xray integration. Do not broaden evidence retention policy; that is already tracked by rf2-vxgfnd.148 and rf2-un54gv.
acceptance_criteria:
- `rows` and every derived Xray query return no ViewCell evidence unless Xray owns the installed projection; a foreign-owner rejection is covered by a fail-before regression fixture.
- `core/init!` installs/claims the projection before exposing ViewCell evidence, with idempotent init/dispose behavior.
- Tests cover preload initialization, direct `core/init!`, foreign-owner rejection, uninstall/re-init, and prove Xray never releases or reads another owner's projection.
- Existing projection ownership/error contracts and release behavior remain unchanged.

(foreign owner's evidence never surfaces via rows/:rf.xray/viewcell-evidence sub/panel); (2) core/init! now claims the projection like the preload (idempotent, never clobbers foreign). Red-before-fix verified. Spec 021 §3.4.1 updated. No implementation/ change; no Spec 009 gap. Gates: focused suite 8t/64a green; full xray cljs 3248t/13674a green (0/0). Browser matrix left to CI.

title: Pin the corrected plain-Reagent no-frame boundary in a real React fixture
description:
## Problem

PR #5843 correctly repairs `spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md`'s plain-Reagent no-frame recipe, but closes P1 bead rf2-vxgfnd.175 without completing its executable acceptance. The existing browser fixture at `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/cross_spec_dom_cljs_test.cljs` around lines 458-575 proves only the base unregistered failure and a registered `reg-view` success.

It does not prove the two tempting repairs now explicitly rejected by the contract: a lexical `with-frame` wrapped around a React subtree, or no-arg `(rf/capture-frame)` inside the unregistered component. It also does not prove a deliberately unregistered component succeeds through explicit carried targeting. Worse, the existing test docstring around lines 471-472 still tells readers that the plain fn may capture no-arg `(rf/capture-frame)` “at render time,” the exact advice #5843 establishes cannot work when the component lacks context wiring and no lexical scope survives React invocation.

Green CLJS/browser CI therefore proves the old negative path but not the corrected decision boundary; the test prose and normative prose disagree. Closed rf2-vxgfnd.175 cannot be amended. Open rf2-vxgfnd.179 owns the broader Vision/Principles/compatibility documentation partition, so this follow-up is intentionally limited to the stock-Reagent executable fixture and its local claims. UIx/Helix/slim are retiring and receive no new compatibility machinery.

## Bounded correction

Extend the existing real-React browser fixture rather than inventing another framework. Pin the two rejected shapes and at least one explicit-target success alongside the existing `reg-view` success. Rewrite its docstring/comments to say ambient capture works only inside a genuinely frame-aware registered ancestor; an unregistered child must receive explicit authority. Keep the fixture in the frozen stock-Reagent tier.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real React fixture proves an unregistered plain Reagent component under `frame-provider` raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` for a bare ambient operation.
- Wrapping the returned subtree/render scheduling in lexical `with-frame` does not leak scope into React's later invocation and still raises the same typed error.
- Calling no-arg `(rf/capture-frame)` inside that unregistered component fails through the same absent-target boundary.
- `reg-view` registration succeeds and targets the provider frame.
- At least one deliberately unregistered explicit path—`(rf/capture-frame frame-id)`, an explicit `{:frame ...}` operation, or a frame-locked bundle threaded from a registered ancestor—succeeds and targets exactly that frame.
- The fixture docstring/comments no longer recommend ambient capture from the unregistered component.
- Mutating context wiring, lexical-unwind handling, or explicit targeting makes a focused browser assertion fail; node-only skip does not masquerade as proof.
- No UIx/Helix/slim surface or compatibility shim is added; broader active-doc cleanup remains with rf2-vxgfnd.179.
notes: 2026-07-14 PR #5852 audit refinement (added while this bead is OPEN): the negative no-arg-capture arm is specifically the provider-only/absent-dynamic-scope case. It must not become a general law that unregistered functions cannot use lexical scope. Add a positive control in which the plain function itself enters `(rf/with-frame frame-id ...)` around the actual ambient operation/no-arg `(rf/capture-frame)`; that succeeds because the dynamic binding is still live. Contrast it with wrapping returned Hiccup or render scheduling, which fails because the binding unwinds before React invokes the descendant. The fixture comments must state both cases. Documentation cleanup remains in follow-up `rf2-vxgfnd.247`.
close_reason: Merged PR #5941 (.22 triage — pin plain-Reagent no-frame boundary in real React fixtures: both rejected repairs + explicit-target success + positive control; rewrote stale #5843-rejected docstring; Playwright 31 tests; test-only; CI green)

title: Reconcile the recorded S0 coverage pass in the authoritative UI plan
description:
## Problem

PR #5843 (authored head d8695108df59ee8fca5db261668243aac9fc02aa) was a current-state reconciliation of the authoritative re-frame.ui plan, but it leaves the S0 coverage gate in two contradictory states.

`ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/12-implementation-plan.md` §4 around lines 188-192 keeps “Post-fold coverage pass over drafts + 11/12 … Q1–Q61” unchecked and says that check “is what remains.” The live program epic `rf2-vxgfnd`, however, records that the S0 coverage pass ran on 2026-07-12, produced a SHIP verdict, and left named S2 obligations in its notes. The same §4 later describes the coverage pass as executed on 2026-07-12.

A fresh worker following the declared authoritative plan will block or file another S0 coverage task; a worker following the program epic will proceed from the recorded pass. Both cannot be authoritative. Closed rf2-vxgfnd.187 cannot be amended, and no all-status follow-up owns this exact checklist contradiction.

## Bounded correction

Reconcile the plan and epic to one durable fact. If the epic's recorded pass is accurate, mark the §4 item complete and link/name the durable result plus the Q1–Q61 disposition/remaining filed items. If it is not accurate, correct the epic and run the pass before checking it. Prefer recording the already-completed pass rather than repeating review work. Do not reopen API/stage decisions or build a general documentation framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- `12-implementation-plan.md` §4 and `rf2-vxgfnd` state one identical status for the Q1–Q61 post-fold coverage pass.
- If complete, the checklist cites the durable result and every unresolved implementer question maps to a named live contract, existing bead, or explicitly ruled future item.
- No completed S0 obligation remains unchecked or described as “what remains.”
- A fresh worker can determine readiness without consulting unstated history or filing a duplicate S0 pass.
- The frozen §2 API table and stage assignments do not change.
- Focused docs/link checks are green; deleting or unchecking the reconciled status makes a simple authority-consistency check fail.

title: Finish the spawn-all exact-authority schema and trace catalogue
description:
## Problem

PR #5842 (authored head 76b8cb1934dbf69b64532f81c5ee1efa2ecca687) was intended to catalogue PR #5839's exact-authority runtime, but three normative seams remain internally inconsistent.

### 1. Schema admits a join that can never authenticate

`spec/005-StateMachines.md` around lines 3650-3659 says every live spawn-all seed mints `:rf/attempt`; runtime `spawn.cljc` around lines 690-700 always adds it, and `join.cljc` around lines 159-173 requires a non-nil exact match. `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2561` nevertheless declares `[:rf/attempt {:optional true} :int]`. A child-bearing join record without the token is therefore schema-valid but permanently unable to accept a completion. Pre-alpha has no persisted compatibility population that justifies this optional arm.

### 2. Reserved-key prose still describes the pre-auth runtime

`spec/005-StateMachines.md` around line 89 says no runtime reads `:rf/spawn-all-id` or `:rf/spawn-all-child-id` and calls them functionally inert. PR #5839 now reads them in `spawn.cljc` around lines 173-186 and 219-252 to identify rejected joins and construct each child's `:rf/join-child` authority record. The old sentence was correct when closed rf2-x76af2.9 landed, but #5839 changed the implementation; this must be a new follow-up rather than reopening that closed bead.

### 3. The authoritative operation catalogue is incomplete/inexact

Spec 009 says its quick reference indexes every operation, but `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:189` omits emitted `:rf.machine.spawn-all/late-completion` and says `stale-completion` is classified by `:reason`; runtime and the detailed row use `:rf.reply/stale-reason`. The detailed `child-completed` row around line 229 enumerates reply evidence but omits the emitted `:rf.reply/correlation` (`join.cljc` around lines 403-442). Tool authors following the catalogue therefore miss a lifecycle operation and a key attribution fact.

## Bounded correction

Finish the catalogue in the existing vocabulary: require the token in `InvokeAllJoinState`; describe the two spawn-all keys as transient FX-routing inputs consumed to build/reject exact authority (not snapshot fields); add `late-completion` to the quick index, use `:rf.reply/stale-reason`, and catalogue `child-completed` correlation. Do not add a compatibility arm, new error family, or new trace operation.
acceptance_criteria:
- `InvokeAllJoinState` requires `:rf/attempt`; a runtime-produced join validates and dissociating the token fails the schema.
- Rejected/sentinel shapes remain explicitly separate rather than making the live authority token optional.
- Spec 005 accurately names every runtime reader and lifecycle role of `:rf/spawn-all-id` / `:rf/spawn-all-child-id`, while retaining the correct statement that they are transient FX args rather than snapshot-internal data.
- Spec 009's quick operation index includes `late-completion` and names `:rf.reply/stale-reason` exactly.
- The `child-completed` detailed row documents emitted `:rf.reply/correlation` and its parent/invoke/child/spawned identity.
- A focused catalogue/schema proof fails if the token becomes optional, a spawn-all completion op disappears, or the classifier key drifts.
- Documentation slug/link gates and the focused machine/schema suites are green; no new public vocabulary is introduced.
notes: PR #5896 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5896) — head 3627d20ce1cddc2689ae8c1b954df9124f5f3ea8. Finished spawn-all exact-authority schema + trace catalogue. Spec-Schemas: :rf/attempt required on InvokeAllJoinState. Spec 009: quick index adds late-completion + :rf.reply/stale-reason classifier; child-completed row documents :rf.reply/correlation. Spec 005: reserved-key prose (spawn-all-id/child-id as transient FX-routing inputs) + exact-authority transport reconciled (:rf.machine/join-dispatch fx + :rf.machine/join-auth recordable cofx, metadata->cofx transition per #5856). New focused proof: spawn_all_authority_catalogue_test.clj. No machines-src change; no new public vocabulary. Gates green (machines 1063/3643, core 1971/9043). Minimal sole-owner spec edits (+7/-5). Left OPEN for mayor to merge.

title: Teach Xray both spawn-all stale-completion operations
description:
## Problem

PR #5839 introduced `:rf.machine.spawn-all/stale-completion` as the canonical pre-resolution exact-authority suppression, while `:rf.machine.spawn-all/late-completion` remains the canonical post-resolution straggler. PR #5842 catalogues both as reply-envelope evidence. Xray does not lower either operation into its uniform reply lifecycle.

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reply_envelope.cljc` around lines 378-500 maps explicit operations and then applies suffix heuristics. Neither join operation is listed. `stale-completion` matches neither `stale-suppress`/`suppressed` nor `completed`; `late-completion` likewise matches no suffix. An executable `phase-of` probe returns nil for both, while the new `child-completed` happens to classify as `:completed` through the heuristic.

Consequently `project-work-events`, `stale-suppressions`, stale tallies and race grouping silently discard the exact evidence developers most need when diagnosing superseded, unverified, duplicate, or post-resolution join completions. Runtime correctness is preserved, but the promised excellent debugging/Xray integration is not.

## Bounded correction

Add explicit, contract-owned lowering for `:rf.machine.spawn-all/stale-completion` to `:stale-suppressed` and `:rf.machine.spawn-all/late-completion` to `:stale-suppressed`. Project their canonical `:rf.reply/*` work identity, status, work-status, stale-reason, correlation and completion time using the existing uniform row shape. Do not broaden the heuristic to classify arbitrary `*completion` operations without reply-envelope proof.
acceptance_criteria:
- `phase-of` classifies both spawn-all stale operations as `:stale-suppressed` and continues to classify `child-completed` as `:completed`.
- Tests feed actual runtime-shaped tag maps for attempt-unverified, attempt-superseded, duplicate-completion and join-resolved late completion through `work-event-row`.
- Projected rows retain machine work-kind, canonical work-id, `:status :stale`, `:work-status :suppressed`, precise `:rf.reply/stale-reason`, correlation, frame and completion time when emitted.
- `stale-suppressions`, `stale-tally-by-kind` and `races-by-work-id` include these rows and do not merge distinct fixed-id attempts once rf2-y4srmh lands.
- Removing either explicit op mapping makes the focused Xray test fail.
- No unrelated non-envelope trace is admitted by a looser suffix heuristic.

title: Make changed-surface discovery tests portable across Windows Bash hosts
description:
## Problem

PR #5840 (authored head 7a7a2ef8fcf84dfcce1dd5d5f59d4d4ce98ab3ee) added eight real-Git discovery cases to implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs. The helper builds SCRIPT_PATH with Node path.join (around lines 1250-1255) and invokes execFileSync("bash", [SCRIPT_PATH]) around lines 1303-1307.

On Windows, SCRIPT_PATH is a host-native C:\... path while bash may be WSL Bash or Git Bash. WSL/Bash consumes or fails to map that operand and reports /bin/bash: C:Users...report-changed-surfaces.sh: No such file or directory. Running node implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs from PowerShell reaches the 130 pre-existing cases, then all eight new DISCOVERY cases fail at process launch; none executes its classifier assertion. Exact-head Ubuntu CI is green, so CI masks the regression on the project's active Windows development host.

This repeats the platform class previously fixed by closed rf2-rcepku, but that bead cannot be amended. Closed rf2-vxgfnd.137 owns the rename-classification change, not this follow-up.

## Bounded correction

Make classifyViaGitDiscovery invoke the exact authored shell script without passing a Windows absolute path through Bash. Two small portable shapes are viable: feed the already-read script to bash -s over stdin, or copy it into the scratch Git repository and invoke a cwd-relative ./report-changed-surfaces.sh. title: Validate join completion authority before post-resolution attribution
description:
## Problem

PR #5839 validates child ownership and exact attempt authority only for unresolved joins. The post-resolution branch runs first and attributes any matching event shape to the current join.

At implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/join.cljc around lines 684-728, :resolved? causes an immediate :rf.machine.spawn-all/late-completion record built from the current join's [:children child-id]. Only later, around lines 730-786, do unresolved paths check child ownership and classify missing, superseded, or duplicate authority.

Counterexample:

1. Completion from old attempt A is queued.
2. The parent re-enters, installs attempt B, and B resolves.
3. A then drains.
4. The resolved-first branch ignores A's authority and emits ordinary join-resolved late-completion evidence carrying B's current spawned/work identity.

An unstamped or unknown-child carrier against a resolved join is likewise attributed before validation. Durable join state is not mutated, but Xray/work-ledger evidence assigns a stale or forged fact to the wrong current attempt, breaking exact-attempt observability.

Closed rf2-nvxehu cannot be amended. No all-status bead covers this validation-order defect.
acceptance_criteria:
- With current attempt B resolved, an old A carrier emits exactly attempt-superseded evidence and no late-completion record bearing B's work-id.
- An unstamped carrier emits attempt-unverified.
- An unknown child emits the canonical bad-child evidence.
- An exact-current authenticated carrier after resolution retains the existing join-resolved late-completion behavior.
- All four paths leave runtime-db, resolution, children, and terminal publication unchanged.
- Xray/work-ledger never attributes a stale/forged carrier to a current attempt.
- Reordering resolved? ahead of ownership/auth validation makes focused CLJ/CLJS tests fail.
- No new public event form, error family, or compatibility path is added.

description:

title: Implement the cross-frame carried-subscribe honesty warning
description:
## Problem

The frozen carried-operation honesty contract requires a development warning when a frame bundle captured under frame A performs :subscribe while invoked beneath a foreign ambient frame B. PR #5838 ships the operation bundle but omits that warning entirely.

Contract anchors:

- ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/03-reactivity-and-ownership.md around lines 307-312 and 390;
- spec/004-Views.md around line 551;
- ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/drafts/spec-009-ui-catalogue-rows.md around line 112 names :rf.warning/cross-frame-carried-op.

Runtime anchor:

- implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/frames.cljc around lines 638-669 checks only captured-incarnation liveness. It never compares a present ambient frame with the captured origin, and the implementation contains no occurrence of :rf.warning/cross-frame-carried-op.

Consequently a bundle captured in A can read A while called under B without the promised honesty diagnostic. The captured-frame semantics are correct and should continue; the missing warning makes an isolation mistake difficult to debug.

No all-status bead matched the warning ID or cross-frame carried subscribe behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Invoking A's :subscribe beneath ambient B emits exactly the specified warning and still reads A.
- The warning carries exact origin, ambient, and query evidence with canonical recovery text.
- A-under-A and no-ambient/async invocation emit no warning.
- Repeated invocation follows the established warning dedup policy.

title: Fan frame-operation bundle failures to production observability before throwing
description:
## Problem

The new frame operation bundle in PR #5838 throws canonical :rf.error/frame-destroyed exceptions for stale-bundle invocation and absent/closing capture, but these new throw sites bypass the required error fan-out.

Exact anchors at authored head 87b42778bed9d79bd7537668f92bd54a9b230f7e:

An exact-head reproduction registered an always-on listener, destroyed the captured frame, and invoked :dispatch-sync. The typed exception was thrown, but the listener saw zero records. If application/framework callback boundaries swallow the thrown exception, the production failure disappears from telemetry. The attempted event/query/operation attribution is also lost even though the catalogue requires it.

title: Route drain-owned typed observation errors through the subscription source realm
description:
## Problem

PR #5836 at authored head 554cfc52c89276181821352db766c1fb7c220189 corrects source-coordinate lookup for the fixed :rf.error/observation-on-change-failed wrapper, but the same drain forwards unfanned typed categories dynamically and still supplies the former owner's subscription ID through the field named :event-id.

Exact path:

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc around lines 675-704 emits an unfanned typed error with the notifying subscription ID in :event-id.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc around lines 108-149 selects the source registry realm from the error category.
- :rf.error/reentrant-graph-op, the motivating typed arm, is not in sub-error-categories, so lookup consults [:event sub-id] rather than [:sub sub-id].

With distinct macro registrations for [:sub :obs/collide] and [:event :obs/collide], an actual typed HMR/disposed drain record is attributed to the unrelated event definition. Without the colliding event, the available subscription coordinate is omitted. The typed fixture asserts counts/event-id but not source-coord; the authored collision fixture exercises only the fixed wrapper category.

This sends Xray/off-box tooling to the wrong source and violates subscription ownership attribution. Closed rf2-q3fmqm covers only the wrapper and cannot be amended. No all-status follow-up matched this dynamic typed seam.
design:
Make the emitting seam carry its internal source realm explicitly, rather than inferring ownership solely from a dynamic category:

- Let this drain request subscription-owned coordinate lookup for the former owner's ID.
- Consume the internal realm during lookup; do not expose a new public record field.
- Preserve category-owned default lookup for ordinary fixed emit sites.
- Keep programmatic subscriptions honest by omitting source-coord when no registration coordinate exists.

A small internal realm parameter is preferable to expanding a global category list with categories whose ownership varies by emit context.
acceptance_criteria:
- Actual HMR and disposed unfanned-typed fixtures use a macro-registered subscription plus a colliding same-ID event and resolve exactly the subscription coordinate.
- The unrelated event coordinate is never selected.
- A programmatic subscription omits source-coord rather than fabricating or stealing one.
- Wrapper-category attribution remains correct.
- Removing/ignoring the explicit source realm makes the collision fixtures fail on CLJ and CLJS.
- No public schema field, category, or API is added.
close_reason: Merged PR #5957 (ALREADY-COVERED: the drain-owned typed observation error mis-routing was superseded by rf2-w55bh0's always-wrap refactor — drain now always wraps uncovered escapes in :rf.error/observation-on-change-failed which error_emit classifies subscription-owned, so [:sub id] is the sole lookup realm; the bead's internal realm parameter would be dead code, deliberately not added; locked with the exact combined-counterexample regression fixture, red-if-regressed proven; test-only; core+machines+node green; CI green)

title: Make the ui-tree-malformed lease arm exact across evidence, recovery, and production reachability
description:
## Problem

Merged PR #5835 at authored head 26fabf35085fdd841ff653f14d60beeec8edcaf2 enlarged the Spec 009 :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed catalogue row to cover lease-descriptor validation and lexical lease-site guards. The resulting catalogue/proof is not exact in two ways.

### 1. Guard evidence and recovery are generalized beyond the runtime

spec/009-Instrumentation.md around line 2290 says the site guards add :site-id plus :resource-id. The actual branches in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc differ:

- duplicate lexical site (around lines 748-756) carries :site-id, :descriptor-keys, and :resource-id;
- outside capture, missing capture, or nil site ID (around lines 772-778) carries :site-id and :descriptor-summary, but no :resource-id.

The descriptor grammar branches use :fix-lease-descriptor recovery, while lexical compiler/capture guards use their guard recovery. The row should enumerate these arms rather than imply one evidence/recovery shape.

The new COMPLETE-payload test at implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/lease_descriptor_jvm_test.clj around lines 48-79 invokes only lease-descriptor/validate-descriptor!. It never exercises reactive/lease-site. The existing duplicate-site CLJS test asserts only the error ID and zero mint. Adding or deleting a guard evidence key therefore leaves every new completeness assertion green.

### 2. The row falsely classifies the whole category as dev/Tier-1-only

The same Spec 009 row calls :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed a Tier-1/dev-only surface. But reactive/lease-site unconditionally invokes lease-descriptor/validate-descriptor!, whose failure unconditionally calls error/throw-error!; neither is guarded by goog.DEBUG or the diagnostic-channel switch. A compiled dynamic descriptor such as {:resource rid} with runtime rid = :unqualified reaches this error in an advanced production build. Diagnostic emission may be elided, but the fail-loud grammar error is production-reachable.

This makes the catalogue unreliable for strict tooling and for production error-budget/DCE reasoning. The source bead rf2-vxgfnd.113 is closed by #5835 and must not be amended. Targeted all-status searches found no existing follow-up for lease-site evidence or this reachability classification.
design:
Make the existing category exact without adding a new error ID or compatibility machinery:

- Split the Spec 009 row by emitting arm, naming the exact evidence keys and recovery for descriptor grammar failures, missing lexical/capture context, nil site ID, and duplicate site ID.
- Qualify environment reachability per arm: structural compiler/Tier-1-only arms versus the production-reachable dynamic descriptor validation throw. Keep diagnostic trace elision distinct from thrown-error reachability.
- Add real lease-site guard tests that pin the complete ex-data key set and values, rather than testing only the helper validator.
- Add the smallest advanced-mode dynamic-descriptor proof that demonstrates the intended production failure contract.

Prefer documentation/test reconciliation with the fail-loud runtime. Change runtime only if a governing frozen contract proves the current runtime wrong.
acceptance_criteria:
- CLJS fixtures directly trigger outside-capture/missing-context, nil-site-ID, and duplicate-site lease-site guards.
- Each fixture asserts exact :error-id, :where, :recovery, and the complete evidence key/value set; adding or removing any catalogued key makes a test fail.
- Spec 009 enumerates branch-specific evidence and no longer claims :resource-id for a branch that cannot supply one.
- An advanced/production fixture proves a malformed dynamic lease descriptor still throws :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed while diagnostic emission remains elided as specified.
- The catalogue distinguishes production error reachability from dev-only diagnostic visibility.
- No new error category, public API, compatibility branch, or runtime allocation is introduced.

title: Reconcile static-override split equality and landed fixture across active S2 authorities
description:
## Problem

Merged PR #5835 at authored head 26fabf35085fdd841ff653f14d60beeec8edcaf2 correctly landed the static Story-override movement-token law in live Spec 006, but the active synthesis authorities still describe an older and underdetermined state.

Exact current anchors:

- The same document around lines 118-128 neither states the frozen split equality law nor recognizes its landed mounted proof; it calls the behavior unprototyped and a future Stage-2 obligation.
- ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/drafts/spec-006-observation-port-amendment.md around lines 243-250 now states the split equality law but still calls the mounted fixture pending.
- Live spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md around lines 1108-1118 and implementation/core/src/re_frame/observation.cljc current? are definitive: :override-id compares with ordinary =; :version compares with the frozen rf=/node-value= law, including NaN; the mounted Story proof has landed.

This is not harmless history: 03 declares itself an implementation authority. A fresh implementer can follow it and either use ordinary = for both token parts or file already-complete Stage-2 work. A concrete semantic divergence is replacement of NaN by a fresh NaN: ordinary equality reports movement, while the frozen value law retains the exact lease.

The source bead rf2-vxgfnd.126 is closed by #5835 and must not be amended. No all-status bead matched this remaining drift.
design:
Reconcile only active/final authorities with the already-landed contract:

- State that subscription evidence carries no value/version payload, while :story-override carries its specified movement token.
- State :override-id by = and :version by frozen rf=/node-value= equality, explicitly including NaN.
- Replace pending/unprototyped fixture language with present-state evidence and a precise link to the landed mounted fixture.
- Preserve genuinely historical spike/review records as historical; do not rewrite evidence history or change runtime/API behavior.

Use one classified repository search to distinguish active normative text from historical records. This is a documentation reconciliation, not a new abstraction.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every active synthesis/spec/draft authority states the same target shape and split equality law.
- No active passage calls the mounted static-override fixture pending or unprototyped.
- The active text explicitly preserves NaN retention under the version value law.
- A classified search documents any remaining old wording as historical only.

title: Spec 004 prose true-up: two special-form tiers in the closed expression grammar (ruled A — no analyzer roster)
description: Ruled 2026-07-15 (delegated): the compiler's :else fallback is the DESIGNED evaluated-only special-form arm and is production-sound (see notes for the full ruling + evidence); the original ask (closed roster, slot table, unsupported-form gate for host-only specials, parity fixtures) is rejected as gold-plating. Empirical finding: analyze.cljc's :else special-form fallback is PRODUCTION-SOUND — every host special form probed (if/new/./set!/def/throw/monitor-enter/do index exactly 1 site; (var sub) safely rejects); no reachable soundness hole. Spec 004 already consistent (bullet 3 lines 194-203 covers the special-form-name arm incl. if). The one real bug (computed callees) already closed by .217. What the bead ASKS — close the fallback, bless a form roster, reject unblessed host-only forms, add a slot table — is a NEW DESIGN POSTURE needing Mike's ruling: which forms to bless (if clearly; interop ./new/set! appear in real view exprs like (.toUpperCase name); host-only monitor-enter/case*/deftype* never do), each form's slot rule, and whether defending against forms nobody writes in a view is warranted under the no-over-engineering posture. DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option A — keep the open :else fallback in analyze.cljc unchanged; the sole deliverable is a Spec 004 prose true-up. Options B (explicit if/interop analyzer branches) and C (full closed roster + per-form slot table + parity fixtures + unsupported-form rejection of host-only specials) are REJECTED as gold-plating.
RATIONALE: Both recorded opinions (worker probe evidence, PR #5950; CComposer structural analysis) converge on A and verify against current code. Spec 004 category 3 (lines 194-203) already designates the special-form-name arm — simple head preserved verbatim, arguments analyzed — and analyze.cljc's :else arm (lines 844-868) implements exactly that, including the .217 computed-callee rule. Soundness is structural, not merely empirical: evaluated-operand specials (if/do/throw/interop) get the correct slot rule by construction; binder forms are intercepted by explicit branches (rw-let/rw-fn/rw-letfn*/quote); any hypothetical fall-through with a non-evaluated slot over-indexes (walks extra positions) but can never under-index, so a visible reactive site can never be lost from the manifest — the only ownership soundness failure. The rewriting is host-agnostic, so CLJ/CLJS divergence has no mechanism. The bead's premise (a reachable soundness gap) does not hold on current code; a roster would defend forms (monitor-enter, case*, deftype*) no view author writes — directly against the no-over-engineering posture.
IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE: Edit spec/004-Views.md, the closed expression grammar (~lines 178-207), prose only. (1) Make explicit that the CLOSED claim is the four categories, not an exhaustive host-special inventory in bullet 1; bullet 1 is the binder-aware structural tier (quote, fn/fn*, let/let*, loop/loop*, letfn/letfn*, try). (2) In bullet 3, name the evaluated-only host specials that ride the plain-head arm — if, do, throw, and interop (., new, set!) as in (.toUpperCase name) — so the prose stops implying if is unaccounted for.
