title: Replace the remaining synthetic digest-carrier obligations with real Shadow host gates
description:
## Problem

PR #5806's digest-carrier gate is valuable but several explicit proof obligations remain synthetic or vacuous, so CI can stay green while host integration drifts:

- Warm-cache version-zero reconstruction is exercised with a handcrafted compiler map, not by stopping one Shadow daemon and starting a second against the first daemon's disk cache.
- No-pass REPL isolation manually binds compiler state rather than driving an actual Shadow CLJS REPL compile/evaluate action.
- The two-build test constructs build A fully and then build B fully; it does not overlap two build lifecycles inside one daemon and cannot expose ambient compiler-env cross-routing.
- Production elision is grepped only in the node-script `:ui-bench` bundle and does not force an advanced browser consumer of the digest/descriptor path, so browser-specific retention can remain unobserved.

CLOSED rf2-vxgfnd.108 later added zero-carrier and hookless-build cases; do not duplicate them. This bead owns only the still-missing real-host dimensions above.

## Required Correction

Replace each synthetic/vacuous arm with the smallest deterministic integration falsifier through the real Shadow 3.4.10 entry point. Reuse one fixture project and process harness where practical. The tests must make their control mutation fail, so green proves the intended host boundary rather than merely reimplementing the production helper in test code.
acceptance_criteria:
- A two-daemon test performs a successful first build, stops the daemon, starts a fresh daemon on the same disk cache, and proves complete byte-identical compiler/client digest reconstruction without a clean.
- A real Shadow CLJS REPL action exercises macroexpand/never-evaluated/runtime-failed/successful no-pass edits and proves none mutate the finalized build digest; the next saved build reconciles source truth.
- Two configured builds overlap within one Shadow daemon with distinct build ids and source sets; accepted/scratch/carrier state remains isolated under deterministic interleaving.
- An advanced browser build contains an explicit dev digest/descriptor consumer in source yet emits no carrier, sentinel, `bd1-` literal, registry traversal, reload producer, or debug-manifest residue.
- Each arm has a documented mutation/revert that makes it fail while narrower unit tests remain green.
- Existing real-browser initial/warm/lazy/failure/recovery, JVM compiler, artifact-isolation, and production-performance gates remain green without adding a second authority.
notes:
PARTIAL via PR #6030 (merged): shipped the NOTES-prioritized final-schedule real-host arm (Shadow hook deep-merge/order, build-local :compile-prepare, seq+parallel scheduling, output-marker retention, fail-loud on missing schedule evidence; red-when-disabled proven). 4 broader DESCRIPTION obligations REMAIN: two-daemon warm-cache reconstruction, real REPL isolation, overlapping build lifecycles in one daemon, advanced-browser elision consumer. Bead stays open for those.
RESEARCH REPORT from the worker whose worktree I destroyed (2026-07-19). It had made ZERO edits, so nothing was lost; all findings verified against source before deletion.

⚠️ #6030 CLOSED NONE OF THE FOUR DESCRIPTION ARMS. It shipped a FIFTH arm (final-schedule) never in the DESCRIPTION list. Each original obligation confirmed still synthetic:
  1. TWO-DAEMON WARM CACHE — compiler_digest_carrier_jvm_test.clj:155 accepted-warm-prepare-preserves-output-present-ui-consumer hand-builds a shadow-state map and hand-sets :cached true. NO daemon restart exists anywhere in the tree.
  2. REAL REPL ISOLATION — compiler_build_hook_jvm_test.clj and build_repl_hmr_convergence_jvm_test.clj both manually `binding` compiler state. No real REPL is driven.
  3. OVERLAPPING BUILDS — compiler_digest_carrier_jvm_test.clj:885 interleaved-build-values-carry-isolated-digests builds A fully THEN B fully. Sequential — exactly the defect the bead describes. Cannot expose ambient compiler-env cross-routing.
  4. ADVANCED-BROWSER ELISION — partially covered, NOT closed. The residue scan is real but lives inline in implementation/scripts/run-ui-bench.cjs:209-224 over out/ui-bench.js. Two gaps: ui-bench is :node-script (shadow-cljs.edn:797), NOT a browser target; and its forbidden list is only [__RF2_UI_DIGEST_XX__, bd1-, digest_carrier], omitting the sentinel/registry-traversal/reload-producer/debug-manifest residue the bead names. No source actually CONSUMES the digest path, so elision has nothing to elide.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE WHOLE PATTERN: compiler_digest_carrier_jvm_test.clj (924 lines, 21 deftests) drives build-hook/hook against a handcrafted map built by the private shadow-state/two-source-state helpers (lines 34-82).

HARNESS GUIDANCE FOR RE-DISPATCH — STAY NODE-SIDE. The established real-host pattern spawns the real CLI: spawnHarnessProcess from implementation/scripts/lib/local-browser-harness.cjs, resolving require.resolve(shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js). Two existing consumers: check-ui-digest-carrier.cjs (839 lines, Playwright, port 8059) and check-ui-final-schedule.cjs (#6030 arm, documented TEETH list in its header). Fixture-project precedent: implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/digest_probe/{hookless,final_schedule}/, each with its own shadow-cljs.edn.
DO NOT GO IN-PROCESS: verified NO deps.edn alias anywhere puts thheller/shadow-cljs on a test JVM classpath, and nothing calls shadow.cljs.devtools.api/.server in-process. Attractive for arms 1 and 3 but a brand-new harness shape with zero precedent — a bigger bet than this bead authorises.

⚠️ ARM 2 IS THE RISK: a real CLJS REPL needs a connected JS runtime; driving it non-interactively on Windows is research-grade. Sequence it LAST or split it out.

SCOPE RECOMMENDATION (worker, and I agree): SPLIT THIS BEAD. Four arms are four distinct real-host mechanisms, not variations on one — #6030 spent a whole PR on a single arm, the strongest available evidence for the right unit of work. Suggested: arms 1+3 together (shared daemon-lifecycle harness), arm 4 alone (cheap, independent), arm 2 solo and last.

BASELINE MEASURED IN-WORKTREE BEFORE DELETION: _changed-surfaces.test.cjs = 168 passed; npm install exit 0. Hot-zone (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, deps.edn) was FREE at 02:25 AUSEST.
✅ ARM 4 DELIVERED in PR #6413 (advanced-browser elision consumer). THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN for arms 1, 2 and 3, which the worker read, confirmed against the research report, and deliberately did not touch.

REMAINING: (1) two-daemon warm-cache reconstruction, (2) real REPL isolation — research-grade on Windows, sequence LAST, (3) overlapping build lifecycles in one daemon. Arms 1+3 share the daemon-lifecycle harness; do them together. Do NOT go in-process: verified that no deps.edn alias puts thheller/shadow-cljs on a test JVM classpath and nothing calls shadow.cljs.devtools.api/.server in-process.

⚠️ ARM 4 FOUND A REAL PRODUCTION BUG, filed as rf2-vxgfnd.299: re-frame.ui.client/descriptor and /descriptor-index carry NO goog.DEBUG gate, so the registry traversal and the :build-digest keyword SURVIVE AN ADVANCED BROWSER RELEASE — exactly the browser-specific retention this bead predicted and the old :node-script scan could never observe. implementation/ui/src/** was fenced from #6413, so the leak is PINNED PRESENT with a self-announcing failure message rather than silently tolerated; that pin also serves as the production non-vacuity floor. Fixing .299 requires updating the pin in the same PR.

⚠️ THE ORACLE FOR ANY FUTURE ARM — both simple greps are WRONG, measured:
  - goog.DEBUG-count: appeared 225 times in a release where the surface was fully eliminated (all docstrings from var reification).
  - Function-name grep: Closure INLINES small fns, so stage_BANG_ and cell stay absent even with their gates REMOVED; before_load/after_load never appear in a DEBUG=true control at all. #6413 built this oracle, measured it, and REMOVED it rather than ship passengers that can never go red.
  USE INSTEAD: a CONTROL BUILD — same entry, same :advanced level, goog.DEBUG the ONLY variable — asserting each sentinel PRESENT in the control and ABSENT in production, string literals only (Closure never rewrites them, so they survive inlining). PLUS a token asserted PRESENT in the production bundle to catch a production-side mis-target the control cannot distinguish from real elision.
  Root consumers BY CALL, not by var — exporting by var keeps an empty fn alive and reports a leak no real consumer has. Keep the fixture HOOKLESS or the sentinel gets patched into a bd1- digest and the grep passes for the wrong reason. Rename teeth must use PREFIX changes: a suffix extension still contains the original.

ARM 4 SHIPPED NO HOT-ZONE CHANGE: no build-id or :dev-http port added (fixture carries its own config, per the digest_probe/{hookless,final_schedule} precedent), no workflow change, 172-assertion pin unmoved.
MAYOR ASSESSMENT (2026-07-20): arms 1-4 SHIPPED (d1e3c256cf real-Shadow-host-gates + e005987bd6 arm-4 advanced-browser-consumer; #6030 shipped a 5th final-schedule arm). REMAINING = (1) two-daemon warm-cache reconstruction, (2) real REPL isolation — the bead itself flags these 'research-grade on Windows.' ⚠️ HELD FROM BLIND DISPATCH — needs scoping first: rf2-tm1xi (#6503, MERGED-pending) just shipped a REAL 8-pass Shadow warm-watch fixture that DELIBERATELY does SINGLE-build identity (per the 4vm19 Arm-1 ruling, explicitly NOT two-build isolation). QUESTION before dispatching .195's remainder: does tm1xi's single-build warm-watch fixture already discharge the INTENT of the two-daemon reconstruction (proving warm-cache topology survives real rebuilds), making the literal two-daemon arm redundant/over-engineered? Or is two-daemon genuinely needed for something single-build can't prove? This is a scope call — if two-daemon is research-grade-Windows-hard AND tm1xi covers the intent, the remainder may be closeable-as-covered (trust-the-programmer/no-gold-plating posture favors NOT building research-grade infra for a property already proven). Recommend: assess against merged #6503 before any dispatch; likely a Mike scope-confirmation or a close-as-covered. Do NOT dispatch a worker onto two-daemon Windows reconstruction without that determination.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-20 08:34 AUSEST)

RULING: Close as covered — all three remaining arms (two-daemon warm-cache reconstruction, real REPL isolation, overlapping builds in one daemon). Scope correction first: the 2026-07-20 mayor note said "arms 1-4 SHIPPED"; in fact #6413/e005987bd6 shipped arm 4 and #6030/d1e3c256cf shipped a fifth (final-schedule) arm — arms 1, 2, 3 were the true remainder, and each closes for cause below. No new fixtures, no new beads.

ARM 1 (two-daemon): the AC as written ("byte-identical digest reconstruction from disk cache without a clean") targets a path the shipped architecture deliberately refuses. Verified at build_hook.clj:481-525: validate-ui-cache-blocker! throws unless dev UI builds declare :cache-blockers #{re-frame.ui} ("refusing a plausible but incomplete warm-cache digest"), and reset-cold-ui-consumer-output evicts retained UI-consumer output on every fresh daemon (accepted version 0), forcing real macroexpansion recompile. A restarted daemon never trusts the cache for the digest; it reconverges through the same real compile machinery #6030 and #6503 already prove against a live Shadow 3.4.10 daemon. Cache-shape drift (only possible via a deliberate pin bump) fails loud through three classified tripwires: the cache-blocker throw, output-marker classification, and missing-pass-provenance — the last proven red on the real host in #6030.

HONEST RECORD of what is NOT literally exercised: no gate restores a populated disk cache into a fresh JVM. #6503's fixture wipes .shadow-cljs/out before starting (check-ui-warm-watch.cjs:444-447), so all its warm passes are in-memory within one daemon lifetime — the answer to the mayor's literal question ("does tm1xi's fixture exercise the two-daemon path?") is no. The intent is discharged by architecture (refuse-and-recompile + loud tripwires), not by that fixture. Related: install-re-frame-ui.md:118 says "npm run test:ui-digest-carrier is the in-repo proof" adjacent to the step-3 warm-restart smoke — that sentence overstates warm-restart coverage; mayor may fold a one-line softening into a doc pass or leave it, since step 3 itself correctly instructs the manual restart smoke.

ARM 2 (real REPL): structurally enforced — no-pass REPL contributions go to a separate repl-overlay seeded from the accepted snapshot, never feed accepted registries or the digest, cleared on next prepare — and unit-pinned (compiler_build_hook_jvm_test.clj pins non-publication + clearing). A non-interactive connected-runtime Windows REPL harness is research-grade infrastructure for a dev-only, structurally-enforced property: declined as gold-plating.

ARM 3 (overlapping builds): the carrier keeps no ambient JVM state to cross-route (per-build compiler-env, no process-global authority; the two process atoms are test-harness fallbacks never consulted under a real compile). A real overlapping fixture would test pinned Shadow's internal per-build isolation, not a re-frame2 seam — the compiler-side analog of the topology rf2-4vm19 ruled not worth testing, and exactly the architecturally-refused-topology test the posture names as the trap.

RIDER (must survive this bead's closure): any future Shadow pin bump (currently pinned 3.4.10) MUST include one manual warm-restart smoke of a UI dev build before merge — stop a watch with output retained, restart it, app renders and digest finalizes; a process note on the bump PR, not new infrastructure. Mayor: on closure, record this via `bd remember` so it outlives the bead. The consumer-facing procedure already exists at docs/core/how-to/install-re-frame-ui.md steps 1-4 ("Prove it works", step 3).

OPINIONS WEIGHED: followed the dossier's primary Recommendation (Option A) over Codex's Option B (bounded restart pass) because B's only purchase is pin-bump CI insurance on a pinned dependency, bought with a permanent fixture plus an extra cold JVM boot in the gate forever — priced as gold-plating under the pre-alpha posture, with the rider covering the same residual.

FOR THE MAYOR: recommend closing rf2-vxgfnd.195 as covered, citing this block; record the rider via bd remember at closure. Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-vxgfnd.195.two-daemon-scope.md retired (deleted) per Mike's authorization.
close_reason: RULED close-as-covered (Mike-delegated 2026-07-20): all 3 remaining arms (two-daemon warm-cache reconstruction, real REPL isolation, overlay) covered by shipped arms 1-4 (d1e3c256cf real-Shadow-host-gates + e005987bd6 arm-4 advanced-browser + tm1xi #6503); research-grade, not blocking

title: Route compiler authority through the UI-private build carrier when Shadow outer markers drift
description:
## Problem

PR #5805 (authored head f81266084fdeffa2bc1aab57294fc056dca3b4fe, merged as e790f737f37981ec4ad8fbd03dee09dd9df0c51f) hardened re-frame.ui compiler build authority, and PR #5806 added compiler-private accepted/scratch state carrying an explicit build id. The ambient compiler routing path still recognizes a Shadow compiler environment only when the private outer key `:shadow.build.cljs-bridge/state` exists.

If Shadow renames or removes that outer bridge key while re-frame.ui's own private accepted/scratch state remains present, `shadow-compiler-state` returns nil. `current-build-id`, accepted-registry reads, contribution writes, element/property lookups, descriptor reads, and finish bookkeeping then silently fall back to the process/session build instead of using the explicit private build id. Two interleaved builds can therefore cross-route manifests and collision authority into the same global slice. This breaks the compiler's central per-build isolation invariant and defeats the private carrier specifically introduced to make build identity authoritative.

This is the unresolved compatibility arm of CLOSED rf2-1rxznn. That bead must not be reopened or amended; this follow-up tracks the current defect.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open two compiler passes A and B with distinct build ids and re-frame.ui private accepted/scratch state.
2. Remove or rename only the outer `:shadow.build.cljs-bridge/state` marker in each compiler environment, leaving the private re-frame.ui state intact.
3. Interleave a contribution and accepted-registry/property read from A with equivalent operations from B while the session/global fallback names a third or last-started build.
4. Observe that both operations resolve to the fallback slice, private accepted state is invisible, both private scratch maps remain untouched, and rows from A and B accumulate together.
5. Restore the current Shadow outer marker as a control; each operation routes to its own compiler-private slice.

The exact #5805 probe routed two renamed environments to `:session/global`. The same probe on current main shows the defect despite the new private carriers: A/B writes accumulate globally, while a canonical-marker control stays isolated.

## Required Correction

Define one closed compiler-ownership recognizer used by identity resolution, accepted-state reads, scratch/overlay reads, contribution writes, collision/property/descriptor queries, and finish. Recognize re-frame.ui's private accepted/scratch carrier independently of Shadow's outer implementation-detail marker. Resolve the build id from the private accepted snapshot; when private compiler state exists but the id is missing or disagrees with a still-present Shadow id, throw a stable typed compiler error rather than downgrading.

Retain the session/global fallback only for genuinely plain CLJS/REPL environments carrying neither re-frame.ui private compiler state nor a recognized Shadow bridge state. Do not add compatibility aliases for guessed future Shadow keys: re-frame.ui should rely on its own carrier once the build hook has established authority.

## Scope

Primary surface: `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/build.cljc` and its JVM/real-Shadow compiler tests. Audit every ambient read/write helper, not only `current-build-id`; a partial fix would still route accepted registries or scratch writes incorrectly. No frozen public API change is required.
acceptance_criteria:
- With the Shadow outer marker absent or renamed but valid re-frame.ui private A/B state present, all contribution, collision, property, element, descriptor, accepted-registry, scratch, overlay, and finish operations remain isolated to their explicit build ids.
- Interleaving A and B leaves the process/session fallback unchanged and never exposes one build's rows to the other.
- Private compiler state with a missing build id, or with an id that disagrees with a still-present Shadow id, fails loudly with a stable typed diagnostic before any mutation.
- The current canonical Shadow-marker path remains green and resolves to the same private build id.
- A genuinely plain CLJS/REPL compiler environment with no private UI carrier retains the intentional session fallback.
- At least one real-Shadow smoke distinguishes compiler-private resolution from a same-valued session fallback; it cannot pass accidentally because both ids happen to match.
- Regression fixtures fail against current main and pass after the correction; compiler build/HMR convergence, duplicate-id, clean/incremental/watch/REPL, and artifact-isolation gates remain green.
notes: FIXED via PR #5970 (branch worker/compiler-carrier-192, SHA 34e90c6f17). Routed compiler authority through a single closed recognizer ui-owned-compiler-state? (private carrier ::accepted-snapshot/::scratch/::repl-overlay OR Shadow bridge marker); ambient-build-id resolves from the private accepted snapshot and throws ::private-build-id-unresolved / ::private-build-id-shadow-disagreement on missing/disagreeing id. Red-before-fix: 6 new drift tests in compiler_build_jvm_test.clj (10 failures on main -> 0 after). Gates green: ui clojure -M:test (554/0), npm test:cljs (9476/0), test:ui-digest-carrier PASS. Not design-bearing. Left open for mayor merge.
close_reason: Merged PR #5970 (route compiler authority through UI-private build carrier on Shadow outer-marker drift: build.cljc recognized Shadow env only via outer :shadow.build.cljs-bridge/state → drift while private carrier intact downgraded identity/reads/writes/finish to global fallback, cross-routing interleaved builds into one slice; fix = closed ui-owned-compiler-state? recognizer (private carrier key OR bridge marker) routing all ambient read/write helpers + ambient-build-id resolving private-snapshot-first (typed errors, no downgrade); no speculative future-Shadow-key aliases; red-before-fix 10→0; ui+node+digest-carrier green; CI green)

title: ui preflight: bind plan decisions to exact frame authority and fail closed on overlap/lifecycle loss
description:
## Problem

PR #5804 correctly prevents one stale post-destroy plan-record resurrection, but `execute-frame-plans!` still separates decision, frame mutation, and publication without carrying the authority that justified the decision. Three independently reproduced cases violate the root-preflight contract:

1. Stale refresh mutates a replacement incarnation.
   - Phase 1 chooses `:refresh` from incarnation A's install record (`implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/frames.cljc:374-414`).
   - Phase 2 later calls `make-frame` against whichever incarnation currently occupies the ID (`456`).
   - Publication captures the token only after mutation (`216-226`), so it validates unrelated replacement B rather than A.
   - Observed result: B kept its app-db but its config became root A's config and its plan record named root A.

2. Lifecycle loss silently reports successful ENSURE.
   - If setup destroys its own planned frame, publication returns nil on lost liveness (`216-235`).
   - The executor treats nil as "skip bookkeeping," finalizes successfully (`440-466`), and client mount proceeds to `createRoot`/render (`client.cljs:486-508`) with no ensured frame.
   - Observed direct result: preflight returned, frame absent, no plan entry, descendant read nil.

3. Same-thread nested preflight overwrites another root's successful plan.
   - Outer root A seats F and drains synchronous `:initial-events` before publishing.
   - A handler invokes inner root B's config-less plan for F.
   - B observes live F without a record, adopts and publishes successfully.
   - A resumes and overwrites B's adoption with A's install record. Both calls returned success.
   - A reentrant JVM monitor such as open PR #5834 does not fix this and CLJS has no cross-thread lock to help.

These are distinct from `rf2-vxgfnd.35`'s concurrent JVM executor race. That in-progress bead/open PR #5834 serializes separate threads but deliberately permits same-thread re-entry and does not bind phase-1 decisions to an expected incarnation.

## Steps to Reproduce

Stale refresh:

1. Seat A under root A with an install record.
2. Start a multi-plan refresh and pause it after phase-1 decision but before target mutation.
3. Destroy A and create same-ID boot-authoritative B with different token, config, and app-db.
4. Resume.
5. Observe B's token/app-db remain B while its config and plan ownership are overwritten by stale root A authority.

Lifecycle loss:

1. Plan a new frame whose synchronous setup event destroys that same frame.
2. Execute preflight.
3. Observe it returns success with no live frame/plan record.
4. A real mount can then create/register/render a host root scoped to an absent frame.

Nested run:

1. Outer install of F triggers an initial-event handler.
2. Handler synchronously executes an inner root's config-less plan for F.
3. Inner run adopts/publishes successfully.
4. Outer run resumes and overwrites the inner record; both returned success.

All three reproduce on exact #5804 and current main. The first and second also reproduce on open #5834; the completeness audit confirmed the third there.

## Deliverable

Make plan execution authority explicit and fail closed:

- Carry the decision-time incarnation token plus relevant install-record identity into phase 2.
- Revalidate before any `:refresh`/adopt/found-live mutation and publish against the expected token; never recapture unrelated current authority after mutation.
- Treat liveness loss/publication rejection as a typed preflight failure, so client host creation cannot continue without ENSURE.
- Define a cross-host overlapping-run policy for same-thread nesting. The simplest fully correct shape is to reject a nested plan-bearing run that overlaps an in-flight plan for the same frame before it writes; disjoint or plan-free nesting may proceed only under a clear deterministic rule.
- Ensure provisional/in-flight claims, if used, are identity-owned and removed on throw, self-destroy, replacement, and retry.

Build on `rf2-vxgfnd.35` after it lands. Do not replace its concurrency proof or introduce a non-reentrant lock that deadlocks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Controlled A-to-B replacement during a stale refresh fails or safely re-decides before touching B; B retains its config, app-db, boot authority, and no root-A record.
- Equivalent stale `:found-live` and absent-to-install/new-boot-frame arms are pinned.
- Self-destroying setup throws a canonical typed preflight lifecycle-loss error; no `createRoot`, live-root registration, DOM mutation, or plan record occurs.
- A later ordinary destroy/recreate retry succeeds.
- A real initial-event nested same-frame plan cannot have two successful runs or last-writer overwrite; outcome is deterministic on JVM and CLJS and cannot deadlock.
- Plan-free and disjoint-frame nested runs follow an explicit tested policy.
- No stale provisional claim survives failure/replacement.
- #5804 destroy/publication fixture and `rf2-vxgfnd.35` concurrent barrier suite remain green.
- Fix remains bounded to preflight authority/coordination; no frozen public API change or compatibility layer.

## Evidence and provenance

Independent completeness and correctness audits of PR #5804 exact head `82baddff7cdeddd67d58cbb015494eaffc96da97` constructed separate deterministic counterexamples. All findings persist on current `origin/main` `f5a4381ff5ada6928281f05b8d1611a11e7880b4`; open PR #5834 fixes only the duplicate cross-thread arm. Full all-status inventory found no exact bead. Closed `rf2-vxgfnd.52` fixed live-root registry clobber, open `.139` owns evidence identity, and closed `rf2-m1dsuw` owns the narrower stale-record resurrection; none covers these phase-authority failures.
notes:
SPLIT after full re-verify (worker STOPPED design-bearing, no guess). All 3 defect mechanisms + 2 review-gaps confirmed LIVE on origin/main. BOUNDED CORE A+B → child rf2-5svfa1 (fail-closed lifecycle-loss typed error + decision-time-token revalidation; dispatched). DESIGN-BEARING CORE C = THIS BEAD, HELD FOR MIKE — 4 decisions: (1) REMOVE vs FENCE the landed .35 process-wide lock (reversing a deliberate design from a different landed bead; must be proven deadlock-free via a forked-JVM counterfixture coordinated with .225); (2) the per-id in-flight RESERVATION SCHEME shape (replaces process-wide lock); (3) the disjoint/plan-free NESTING rule (deliverable bullet 4 leaves it explicitly undefined); (4) the :found-live FOREIGN-AUTHORITY SETTLEMENT shape — fail-closed-on-incomplete / explicit-ownership-transfer / separate-per-root-evidence, coordinated with .248 (React commit ack) + .249 (evidence reconciliation, which THIS bead blocks). Cannot implement the bead's own 'fail closed on overlap' without picking the coordination shape. Recommendation: land 5svfa1 now; rule C at Mike's convenience (not S3-blocking — the bounded A+B closes the silent-success + stale-refresh holes).

DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option A — all four rulings made now, as one reservation-architecture ruling shared with rf2-vxgfnd.197; the rule-#2-only / defer deferral is rejected. (1) REMOVE the .35 process-wide preflight monitor, do not fence it. (2) Replace it with ONE shared, simple, FAIL-FAST per-frame-id reservation primitive in core (frame-id → opaque owner-token map; NO generation counter — generations already live on :rev and incarnation tokens), consumed by both core construction (.197) and UI preflight; the primitive NEVER blocks — a same-id second claimant gets an immediate typed rejection. (3) Nesting rule: disjoint ids proceed independently (independent reservations, no cross-id ordering); ANY plan naming a currently-reserved id — install, refresh, adopt, AND would-be found-live alike — rejects fail-fast with the typed overlap error; runs touching no reserved id proceed. (4) Settlement scoped to the receipt's root-attempt, fail-closed on foreign authority: finalize/abort require BOTH rev match AND root-authority match (:installed-by / :adopted-by = receipt :root-id); cross-root equal-fingerprint found-live remains a valid scoping no-op (many-to-many, 03 §8 I-8 — the mount proceeds) but confers NO settlement rights and never enters the receipt's settleable writes.

Fail-fast/never-block IS the deadlock-freedom argument — no thread ever waits on a reservation, so no circular wait can form; this sits inside .197's acceptance envelope ("deterministic wait/retry OR typed-loss" — a cross-thread caller wanting settle-then-evaluate retries AFTER release against committed state, at the caller, never inside the primitive), and .225 already requires the race proof to hold without preserving a process-wide monitor. Slice (i): core per-id reservation primitive in implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc + the .197 construction transaction + remove preflight-run-lock in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/frames.cljc. PROOF GATE: do not merge the lock removal before the .225 counterfixture is retooled mechanism-agnostic (forked-JVM; proves the BEHAVIOR — no decide/record last-writer-wins — not the monitor). Slice (ii): UI overlap rejection + settlement guards + Spec 009 rows. rf2-5svfa1's A/B fixtures must stay green. Primitive shape: defonce atom, frame-id → owner-token (e.g. {:kind :construction :token <incarnation>} / {:kind :preflight :root-id <kw> :attempt <monotone>}); acquire at first touch of the id in a run, release in finally on success/throw/destroy/replacement; stale-owner release via identical? on the token (same pattern as publish-plan-for-live-incarnation!). Typed rejections: :rf.error/frame-construction-in-progress (core) and :rf.error/frame-preflight-overlap (UI) — BOTH need new Spec 009 catalogue rows (the drift gate fails locally without them), plus :rf.error/frame-preflight-evidence-mismatch for #4. UI executor: reserve each plan's id at phase-1 decide, hold through publish, release in finally at end of run; the reservation window is the executor run ONLY — never held across the host render/commit; post-run settlement integrity is #4's root+rev guard, not the reservation. #4 mechanics: receipt :writes entries gain :root-id (alongside :rev + :provenance); finalize-writes!/abort-writes! guard on both; found-live enters :writes only when the arriving root owns the record (or is the legitimate first adopt); a guard mismatch on a carried entry at settlement never touches the record and surfaces the typed evidence-mismatch diagnostic (dev-loud) — it does not retroactively tear down an already-committed host root (cannot un-render; the overtaker's authority stands). This is the settlement spine .249 consumes — unblock .249 spec reconciliation once slice (ii) lands. Re-evaluate the rf2-5svfa1 still-present closing-race silent-skip once the reservation lands: a publication rejection under an active same-id reservation becomes the typed overlap error, not a skip. NOTE on the description's "Build on .35 / do not replace its concurrency proof": superseded in exactly this sense — the monitor is removed, but the property .35 proved is preserved by the reservation and re-proven by the .225 fixture; the reservation is not a blocking lock, so the no-non-reentrant-deadlock constraint holds. title: spec(ui tree): classify property-props as semantic conversion data, not optional diagnostics
description:
## Problem

The promoted JVM tree contract incorrectly classifies `:rf.ui/property-props` as optional diagnostic metadata that may be absent/broken/stripped without changing semantics.

`spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:122-133,193-200` (from `drafts/jvm-tree-and-conversion-contract.md:123,134,191`) says every `:rf.ui/*` key is optional diagnostics, ignored by fingerprints, and removed during normalization. But current implementation uses `:rf.ui/property-props` as semantic conversion data:

- `implementation/ui/src/.../tree.cljc:240` records which authored custom-element keys are property-only.
- `semantic.cljc:120-179` reads that set when producing final attrs so those keys do not leak into HTML/SSR markup.

If a consumer follows the normative "safe to omit/strip" rule, property-only values can be emitted as attributes, changing normalized output, SSR markup, hydration behavior, privacy, and custom-element semantics. The marker itself should not reach final output, but it must be honored before removal.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a JVM tree node equivalent to `{:attrs {:model value} :rf.ui/property-props #{:model}}` for a custom element.
2. Convert/normalize it with current semantic conversion; `:model` is treated as a property and omitted from serialized attrs.
3. Follow Spec 004B's optional-diagnostic rule and strip `:rf.ui/property-props` before semantic conversion.
4. Convert again; `:model` can now be treated as an ordinary attr and reach markup.
5. Observe that removing supposedly ignorable metadata changes the semantic output/fingerprint boundary.

## Deliverable

Split reserved tree fields into:
- semantic fields consumers MUST honor (including `:rf.ui/property-props`), consumed at the defined conversion phase and omitted only from final output; and
- genuinely optional diagnostic fields that may be missing/broken/stripped without semantic effect.

Reconcile normalization order, fingerprint language, JVM/CLJS conversion expectations, custom-element docs, and fixtures. Keep the representation minimal; a precise classification table is sufficient.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Spec 004B no longer says all `:rf.ui/*` keys are optional diagnostics.
- `:rf.ui/property-props` is explicitly semantic, required when property-only classification exists, and consumed before marker removal.
- A fixture proves the marker prevents `:model` from reaching markup, while removing it changes semantics and is not advertised as safe.
- Diagnostic-only fields remain demonstrably ignorable and excluded from semantic fingerprints.
- JVM conversion, SSR/hydration, and client behavior agree for custom-element property-only props.
- No marker key itself appears in final attrs/HTML.
- The change does not add a second classification channel or per-render scan.

## Evidence and provenance

Independent correctness review of PR #5800 exact head `ef4225e3b01a411eb6ceaa763a9a81dfb1e2b630` confirmed this internal contradiction against the implementation. It persists on current `origin/main` `f5a4381ff5ada6928281f05b8d1611a11e7880b4`. Full all-status inventory found no matching bead; closed `rf2-vxgfnd.2` implemented the tree, while closed `rf2-vxgfnd.60` catalogued diagnostics without resolving this ABI classification.
close_reason: Merged PR #5967 (classify property-props as SEMANTIC conversion data not optional diagnostics: code was already correct (semantic.cljc N-step-5 consumes :rf.ui/property-props to omit property-only custom-element props) but spec/004B 'Reserved diagnostic keys' falsely claimed every :rf.ui/* key is optional-strippable; reconciled 004B to a three-role classification (semantic MUST-honor / required-gate / diagnostic) + N-step-1 docstring; regression-lock proves stripping the marker changes N output (falsifies pre-fix prose); ui+node green; CI green)

title: spec(ui): align create-root's macro kind, required root-id, and option grammar
description:
## Problem

The promoted root contract and API table contradict the already-shipped `ui/create-root` compile-time surface.

Current implementation:
- `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui.cljc:122` exposes `create-root` as a macro and requires an authored `:root-id`.
- `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/root.cljc:683` rejects missing `:root-id` and rejects `:disambiguator`.
- The generated public manifest correctly classifies it as a macro, with compile-error fixtures for these cases.

Conflicting contracts:
- The retained root draft applies all identity options, including `:disambiguator`, to `create-root` and shows `(ui/create-root dom-node opts)` without a required root ID (`drafts/root-identity-and-mount.md:145,152`).
- It says only `render!`/`hydrate-root` require macro realization (`line 175`).
- `12-implementation-plan.md:44,88` repeats function classification.
- The stale wording was promoted into `spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md:232-264`, and `spec/API.md` also labels `create-root` a function.

A user following normative docs can write a form the compiler intentionally rejects; an implementer can "fix" the correct compiler toward the wrong contract.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Follow Spec 004C and call `(ui/create-root dom-node {:disambiguator :x})` without `:root-id`.
2. Compile.
3. Observe the macro rejects both the missing required `:root-id` and the invalid `:disambiguator`.
4. Compare source metadata/generated manifest to `spec/API.md` and the plan; observe macro-versus-function disagreement.
5. Existing compile-error fixtures confirm current implementation behavior is deliberate, not accidental.

## Deliverable

Reconcile the contracts to the shipped, pre-alpha surface:
- classify `create-root`, `render!`, and `hydrate-root` as macros;
- classify `unmount!` as a function;
- require an authored `:root-id` for `create-root`;
- state that `:disambiguator` is invalid for `create-root`;
- align the retained draft, plan, promoted Spec 004C, `spec/API.md`, manifest commentary, and guide examples.

Do not weaken fail-loud compile-time identity validation or add a runtime compatibility arity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every normative/public table agrees with source metadata and generated manifest on root verb kinds.
- Every `create-root` example supplies authored `:root-id`.
- `:disambiguator` is documented/accepted only where the final grammar permits it and is explicitly invalid for `create-root`.
- Existing missing-root-id and invalid-option compile fixtures remain green and are cited by the contract.
- A docs/API consistency check compares public Var kinds and required literal options.
- No frozen API addition or compatibility overload is introduced.

## Evidence and provenance

Independent correctness review of PR #5800 exact head `ef4225e3b01a411eb6ceaa763a9a81dfb1e2b630` confirmed the contradiction. It persists on current `origin/main` `f5a4381ff5ada6928281f05b8d1611a11e7880b4`. Full all-status inventory found no live contract-reconciliation bead; closed `rf2-vxgfnd.3` implemented the current macro behavior, open `rf2-vxgfnd.182` concerns teardown fencing, not grammar/kind.

title: migration(ui): collapse the competing 36-rule and 34-rule W1 authorities into one rulebook
description:
## Problem

The tracked migration work has two incompatible documents claiming normative authority over the same W1 rewrite program:

- `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/drafts/migrator-rewrite-rules.md:3,1019` says W1 implements 36 `R-*` rules.
- `prep/w1-migrator-rule-table.md:4` tells the W1 worker to start from that table.
- `prep/w2-migration-skill-extension.md:13` declares its 34 `MIG-*` rules normative.
- The open implementation bead `rf2-gria2b` points only to the 34-rule prep table.

There is no complete 36-to-34 mapping, no explicit retirement record for unmatched rules, and no precedence law. A worker can implement either apparently authoritative rulebook and satisfy one document while silently omitting or duplicating another rule. PR #5833 edits the 36-rule document but, while inspected, did not establish one authority or a complete mapping.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Begin W1 from `drafts/migrator-rewrite-rules.md`; enumerate 36 `R-*` obligations.
2. Begin from the open W1 implementation bead/prep table; enumerate 34 `MIG-*` obligations.
3. Attempt to map them by number or heading.
4. Observe there is no normative crosswalk and unmatched/split/merged rules have no explicit disposition.
5. Follow W2's statement that its MIG table is normative; this conflicts with the draft's claim that W1 implements the R table.

## Deliverable

Choose one normative migration rulebook for W1/W2/S6 and make every active plan, README, skill-extension brief, and implementation bead point to it. Add a complete, reviewable mapping from each superseded rule to exactly one current rule, an intentional split/merge, or an explicit retirement with reason. Mark the non-authoritative document historical/supporting and remove language that grants it equal force.

Prefer the smallest representation: one canonical table plus a temporary crosswalk. Do not maintain two synchronized normative rule systems.

## Acceptance Criteria

- W1, W2, S6, README, skill preparation, and open implementation beads name one canonical rulebook.
- Every one of the 36 R rules and 34 MIG rules appears in a checked crosswalk with current canonical ID or explicit retirement.
- No rule is silently omitted, duplicated, or assigned two incompatible automation classes.
- A worker can implement or test a rule without resolving document precedence.
- The crosswalk has a bounded completeness check (unique source IDs, unique/current targets where required, explicit split/merge cardinality).
- The historical rulebook cannot be mistaken for live implementation authority.

## Evidence and provenance

Independent completeness review of PR #5800 exact head `ef4225e3b01a411eb6ceaa763a9a81dfb1e2b630` found this conflict. It persists on current `origin/main` `f5a4381ff5ada6928281f05b8d1611a11e7880b4`; no merged later correction was found. Full all-status inventory found no matching live or closed decision/implementation bead.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option A — `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/prep/w1-migrator-rule-table.md` (MIG-01…34) is the single canonical W1/W2/S6 rulebook; `drafts/migrator-rewrite-rules.md` (36 R-*) becomes historical/supporting, with a complete R->MIG crosswalk so nothing is silently dropped.

RATIONALE: Both recorded opinions (original recommendation + CComposer independent read) converge on A, and independent verification confirms the pillars: the R-* doc self-labels "DRAFT — not merged" and is pedagogical in shape (before/after/trap per rule), while the MIG table is machine-actionable (detector/transform/tier/ordering — the shape a rewrite-clj worker implements), independently derived from ratified specs (doc-10, 11 W1 row, Spec 004/004B/004C) plus the shipped `ui.cljc` surface, and is what the live chain (rf2-gria2b, w2-migration-skill-extension.md "normative on rewrite mechanics") already names. Option B re-points live artefacts at a self-labelled draft in the wrong document shape; Option C re-authors what is already near-canonical (gold-plating). The mandatory crosswalk protects CORRECTNESS in either direction; A wins on CLARITY (one live authority), ELEGANCE (smallest representation: one table + temporary crosswalk), and GOOD PRACTICE (least churn).

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
1. Crosswalk: add `prep/r-to-mig-crosswalk.md` (or a section appended to the canonical table) mapping every R-01..R-X* id to exactly one of: a MIG-id, an intentional split/merge (cardinality stated), or retired-with-reason. Include the reverse direction: every MIG-only rule (no R source) noted as such. Bounded completeness check per the bead's acceptance criteria: all 36 R ids and all 34 MIG ids appear exactly once as sources; targets unique/current where required.
2. Starting map (CComposer preliminary — VERIFY, do not trust): merges R-C1+R-C2+R-C6->MIG-01; R-T3 + loop facets of R-H7/R-Q1->MIG-08; R-C3+R-C4+R-S1->MIG-16; R-H3+R-H4->MIG-18; R-X2+R-X3(+R-S4)->MIG-20. MIG-only: 03, 24, 25, 26, 30, 31, 32, 33. Likely retirements needing explicit disposition: R-T5, R-T10, R-Q2, R-M2 (-> reagent-compat-boundary.md concern), R-S3, R-X7.
3. Banner `drafts/migrator-rewrite-rules.md` as historical/supporting ("pedagogical catalogue; normative automation spec = w1-migrator-rule-table.md") and strip its lines claiming W1 implements the 36 R rules (header + ~line 1019).
4. Sweep W1/W2/S6 surfaces so only the MIG table is named normative: w2-migration-skill-extension.md (already correct), 11-adoption-workstreams.md W1 row, README/skill prep in new-substrate-synthesis, epic rf2-vxgfnd.98 text if it cites the R draft. Do NOT amend rf2-gria2b's description (already points only at the MIG table); note its "MAYOR CHECKOUT ONLY" caveat is stale — all three docs are git-tracked on main.
5. Escalation trigger: if the crosswalk finds an R rule whose mechanical obligation is missing from every MIG row and cannot be retired with reason, add it to the MIG table as a new numbered row (per-rule addition), not an authority flip; surface the addition in the PR description.
6. Acceptance = the bead's existing criteria: one named authority everywhere, checked crosswalk, no silent omission/duplication, historical doc unmistakable as non-live.
AUDIT CONTRACT INPUT 2026-07-17 (PR #6024; coordinate with rf2-vxgfnd.95.14): the canonical MIG rulebook must absorb two shipped S3 rulings while the R->MIG authority is consolidated.

1. Atomic local: any `swap!`/multi-writer migration must target the third tuple member `update!`, which applies to latest host state. Never emit `(set-a! (f a ...))` over a committed render value; `set!` stores its argument exactly, including function values.
2. C-13a: ordinary function props on INTERNAL defview call sites are legal opaque identity-compared values with no implicit invocation phase. MIG-27 must not call every such prop a compile error or gate/rewrite it automatically. It may recommend data intent for serializability or `ui/handler`/`ui/render-fn` where a phase/stable identity is required, while preserving foreign bare-fn rejection and the narrow native-event shorthand.

The checked crosswalk/one-rulebook work must make these semantics explicit and add truth fixtures; rf2-vxgfnd.95.14 owns current Spec/skill prose, not the migrator implementation.

title: observation: suppress watchable NaN-to-NaN fan-out under the rf= movement law
description:
## Problem

PR #5803 correctly changed observation node versioning to the UI `rf=`/NaN-stable equality, but the watchable-host notification gate still uses raw `not=` in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc:1090`. For NaN-to-NaN recomputation, `advance-node-record!` therefore leaves the node version unchanged while `make-watch-handler` still emits `{:cause :value}`.

This violates the observation contract: a value-movement notification is emitted without value movement. In the re-frame.ui consumer, that false fan-out can dirty a ViewCell and advance a cell revision/render during a drain even though the lease value and node version are stable. The new NaN fixture uses a non-watchable plain-atom host, so it proves read/version stability but cannot exercise this path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a watchable host/reaction whose derived subscription depends on `:tick` but returns `js/NaN` before and after the update.
2. Warm the reaction, acquire/read an observation lease, and record node version, notification count, ViewCell revision, and render count.
3. Change only `:tick` and flush the watchable host.
4. Observe raw `(not= prev nu)` evaluates true for NaN, so one `:cause :value` notification is emitted.
5. Observe `advance-node-record!` uses `node-value=`, so the advertised node version does not advance.
6. Through a ViewCell, flush the UI drain and observe avoidable dirty/revision/render work despite an `rf=`-stable result.

A deterministic exact-head JVM probe reported one notification with baseline and notified version both zero. The existing watchable-host fixture covers ordinary equality only.

## Deliverable

Use the same movement decision for version advancement and fan-out. Prefer a single result from `advance-node-record!` (or an equally direct `node-value=` gate) so the two cannot drift again. Add the NaN case to the actual watchable Reagent host and assert the downstream ViewCell consequence, not only the core record.

Keep the fix O(1) and on the existing watch callback; do not add normalization passes or a second equality abstraction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- NaN-to-NaN recomputation on a watchable reaction emits no `:cause :value` notification.
- Lease value and node version remain unchanged.
- A mounted ViewCell remains clean: zero revision increments and zero renders attributable to the stable recomputation.
- A real value movement emits exactly one notification, advances version exactly once, and drives the normal one-render drain.
- The actual Reagent/watchable-host fixture covers the path; the non-watchable fixture remains as complementary coverage.
- Spec 006/004 equality terminology is reconciled by the existing `rf2-vxgfnd.126` owner without introducing a competing equality name.
- Production overhead is no greater than the current comparison.

## Evidence and provenance

Both independent reviews of PR #5803 exact head `1ba4e8e2b49ad13b33c8dd53ffe0ae3841354b71` reached the same finding. It persists on current `origin/main` `f5a4381ff5ada6928281f05b8d1611a11e7880b4`. Full all-status inventory found no semantic duplicate; closed `rf2-s9mcy6` fixed version advancement, and closed `rf2-vxgfnd.29` covered general watch-channel presence rather than NaN movement semantics.
close_reason: Merged PR #5966 (suppress watchable NaN→NaN fan-out under rf= movement law: make-watch-handler gated :cause :value fan-out on raw (not= prev nu) while advance-node-record! versions on node-value= (NaN-inclusive) → NaN→NaN recompute fanned a value-movement notification against an unmoved version; fix = gate fan-out on (not (node-value= prev nu)) — one line + docstring, no second equality abstraction; red-before-fix (leaked :node-version 0 note); core+machines+node green; CI green)

title: docs(machines): teach parent-owned parallel always rounds and same-macrostep convergence
description:
## Problem

The public parallel-state guide still teaches the pre-PR-#5801 region-local `:always` model, contradicting both the corrected runtime and Spec 005. In `docs/machines/parallel-states.md`, line 81 says birth always loops settle independently; lines 235-242 say sibling views remain frozen for the whole macrostep and sibling-reading guards converge only on a later event; lines 246-250 say always loops run per region and siblings are not re-evaluated.

The ratified law is different: after the selected event transitions apply, the parent repeatedly freezes the current whole configuration/data for one selection round, selects enabled regional `:always` transitions, applies that set deterministically, and repeats to a fixed point before the same macrostep commits. At birth, the same parent-round process applies. The guide now teaches users the opposite observable result.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Follow the guide's sibling-reading example: an external event moves `:form` to `:valid`; `:checkout` has a guarded `:always` transition enabled by the resulting shared data/state.
2. According to the guide, checkout remains unchanged until another event because sibling views are frozen for the whole macrostep.
3. Run the current engine from PR #5801.
4. After all event transitions apply, the first post-event frozen round observes the updated whole state/data and moves checkout to `:submitting` before the original macrostep commits.
5. Repeat with a birth-time cross-region guard; current runtime converges during birth, not independently per region.

## Deliverable

Rewrite the birth, frozen-view lifetime, convergence timing, and scoping sections around parent-owned per-round selection. Use one compact example that distinguishes:
- frozen selection within a round,
- re-freezing between rounds,
- all event actions applying before `:always`,
- same-macrostep fixed-point convergence,
- deterministic application and bounded failure semantics.

Keep region-local transition targeting distinct from stabilization ownership. Do not preserve obsolete behavior as compatibility advice; this is pre-alpha and the old law was explicitly reversed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The guide contains no claim that parallel `:always` loops settle independently/per-region or wait for the next external event.
- Examples accurately show same-macrostep convergence through one or more parent-owned frozen rounds.
- Birth, external-event, raised-event, and eventless-before-raise ordering agree with Spec 005 and executable fixtures.
- The guide explains that state/data is frozen per selection round, not for the entire macrostep.
- Links resolve and `mkdocs --strict` passes.
- A focused docs/fixture check protects the load-bearing terminology from reverting.

## Evidence and provenance

Discovered by independent completeness review of PR #5801 exact head `3877eceff056381988849c80bf6f30fc738bafbd`; the independent correctness audit found the runtime implementation sound. The passages are unchanged on current `origin/main` `f5a4381ff5ada6928281f05b8d1611a11e7880b4`. Full all-status bead inventory found no active duplicate; related `rf2-42mml` and source `rf2-slfhkx` are closed and cannot be amended.

title: conformance(machines): replace vacuous region-local parallel-always fixture with parent-round proof
description:
## Problem

The normative conformance fixture `spec/conformance/fixtures/parallel-always-cascade-per-region.edn` still describes and tests the superseded region-local drain model after PR #5801 ratified and implemented parent-owned frozen `:always` rounds. Its prose says stabilization runs "PER REGION" and siblings are not re-evaluated (lines 3-9 and 18), while Spec 005 now requires selection across all regions against one frozen snapshot per round (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:1661-1663,1724-1731,1803-1810`) and continues to advertise this fixture.

The fixture has only one region with an enabled `:always` transition. Therefore both the old, incorrect local-drain engine and the new parent-owned engine satisfy it. A normative conformance row currently blesses the rejected behavior and supplies a vacuous portability gate for the load-bearing distinction.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the existing `parallel-always-cascade-per-region.edn` fixture against the corrected engine; it passes.
2. Restore/mutate the old region-local always drain; the same fixture still passes because only one region participates.
3. Construct two variants with regions declared A/B and B/A. Each region's `:go` action writes a distinct shared flag; each region's guarded `:always` transition requires both flags.
4. Under the old local drain, the first region stabilizes before the sibling event action has applied and at least one ordering strands a region.
5. Under the ratified engine, all selected event actions apply before the first frozen always round; both variants reach both resolved states with equal data.

## Deliverable

Rewrite the existing fixture's narrative to distinguish region-scoped targets from parent-owned stabilization. Add portable A/B and B/A cases that prove frozen selection, no prefix settling, declaration-order invariance, shared round identity where the runner exposes it, and convergence within the same macrostep. Wire them through every conformance runner that claims machine parallel-always support.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No normative fixture says parallel `:always` loops settle independently or per-region.
- Both declaration orders resolve both regions and produce equal state/data.
- A mutation that restores region-local draining deterministically fails at least one portable fixture on every claimed runner.
- Fixtures prove all selected event actions apply before the first `:always` selection round.
- Spec 005 links to fixture prose that matches its parent-owned round law.
- Existing depth, rollback, action/fx ordering, and one-publication invariants remain covered.

## Evidence and provenance

Discovered by independent completeness review of PR #5801 exact head `3877eceff056381988849c80bf6f30fc738bafbd`; independent correctness review found the runtime fix sound. The stale fixture persists on current `origin/main` `f5a4381ff5ada6928281f05b8d1611a11e7880b4`. Full all-status inventory found no active duplicate; `rf2-rkkag`, `rf2-7wy0ke`, and `rf2-slfhkx` are closed.

title: xray(machines): consume parent-owned parallel always rounds as first-class trace evidence
description:
## Problem

PR #5801 (exact authored head `3877eceff056381988849c80bf6f30fc738bafbd`) correctly changed parallel `:always` stabilization to parent-owned frozen selection rounds, but Xray still interprets only the enclosing `:rf.machine/transition` record and reconstructs fired edges from the external event plus whole-machine before/after states. The runtime now emits one `:rf.machine.microstep/transition` per selected regional transition with a shared round index (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/parallel.cljc:978-986`), yet Xray's machines trace consumer filters those records out (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machines/trace_state.cljs:87-102,632-668`) and the epoch projection's closed operation set omits them (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc:758-788`).

Consequently, a parallel macrostep can execute correct regional event and `:always` edges while the inspector highlights no matching edge, invents an impossible aggregate edge, and provides no visible parent-owned round. This is a debugging-contract defect: the first-party inspector cannot explain the newly ratified runtime behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use the dual-region fixture shape from `parallel_always_round_cljs_test.cljc`: event `:go` moves both regions from `:idle` to `:staged`, then one frozen parent round co-selects both `:staged -> :done` `:always` transitions.
2. Capture the emitted `:rf.machine/transition` and `:rf.machine.microstep/transition` records.
3. Feed them through Xray's machines trace-state and epoch projection.
4. Observe that Xray searches for aggregate `:idle -> :done` edges labelled `:go`, rather than the two direct event edges and two regional `:always` edges.
5. Observe that the shared round `(actor-id, microstep-index 0)` has no first-class epoch row. An actionless regional `:always` transition is therefore invisible.

The existing Xray regression test covers only a single active always edge; consolidated CI was green because it contains no parallel-round assertion, and the Xray browser/JVM jobs were skipped on the originating PR.

## Deliverable

Consume regional microstep records as first-class evidence. Keep top-level event-handled regions distinct from subsequent `:always` transitions, highlight each actual direct edge, and project/group regional microstep rows by actor and round index while retaining deterministic region order. Do not infer an event edge for a region that declined the external event but later participated in stabilization.

This should remain bounded to Xray's machines/epoch consumers and their focused fixtures; do not change machine semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The shipped two-region fixture highlights exactly four real edges: two event edges and two regional `:always` edges.
- Xray renders one parent-owned round containing regions `[:a :b]`, both at microstep index `0`, in deterministic order.
- An actionless regional `:always` transition remains visible.
- A region that declines the external event but later takes `:always` gains no phantom event-labelled edge.
- Xray focused JVM/CLJS/browser gates exercise the real structured trace records and fail if `:rf.machine.microstep/transition` is filtered out.
- Production instrumentation/elision behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence and provenance

Discovered by independent completeness review of PR #5801; independent correctness review found the runtime implementation itself sound. The defect persists on current `origin/main` `f5a4381ff5ada6928281f05b8d1611a11e7880b4`. Full all-status bead scan found no live semantic duplicate; related `rf2-52u5n`, `rf2-8i1tg3`, and source `rf2-slfhkx` are closed and cannot be amended.
close_reason: Merged PR #5978 (consume parent-owned parallel-always rounds as first-class xray trace evidence: runtime already emits :rf.machine.microstep/transition per regional round (parallel.cljc, ratified #5801) — gap was xray's CONSUME side (trace_state + epoch/projection filtered them out); made rounds first-class — region-tagged fired-edge highlights ([ALWAYS] for <region> · round <n>) + first-class :microstep projection rows; red-before-fix both consumers; real-runtime harness test (AC5); xray-spec 021+003 updated; parallel.cljc untouched (emission complete); machines+xray+node green; CI green)

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:626`: says the childless sentinel is treated as unseeded.
- `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_spawn_unregistered_type_test.clj:35-36,276`: repeats “treats it as unseeded.”
- Tracked published mirrors `docs/spec/005-StateMachines.md:3042,3789` and `docs/spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2062` still carry the entire old no-slot/registered-sibling-later-completes narrative, even though canonical `spec/005-StateMachines.md` was updated.

The shipped runtime physically seeds `{:rf/spawn-all-rejected? true}` at the join slot before per-child effects. It is not a live child-bearing join, registered siblings suppress before installation, stray completion sees a childless-slot no-op, and parent exit clears the sentinel. “No live join” is accurate; “no slot/unseeded” is not, except in the separate pure-transition/no-runtime-db case. This matters especially in Spec 009 because it is the authoritative production error catalogue.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read canonical `spec/005-StateMachines.md:3788`: it describes the childless sentinel and sibling suppression.
2. Follow its error-catalogue link to Spec 009 or read the user actor guide: both say no join-state was seeded.
3. Open the published `docs/spec/005-StateMachines.md` mirror: it still says registered siblings run later and find no slot—the exact orphaning behavior #5763 removed.
4. Compare with the runtime slot in the existing mixed registered/unregistered fixture: the sentinel map is physically present.
5. A fresh reader now encounters mutually exclusive ownership models depending on entry point.

## Required correction

Perform a semantic sweep of every active/published atomic-reject surface and state one precise model: a childless reject sentinel is physically present but is not a live join; the invoke-level preflight owns rejection; later child effects suppress; stray completion is a no-op; parent exit clears the sentinel. Coordinate exact error cardinality with `rf2-smya7a` rather than preserving the current duplicate-producer ambiguity.

Do not mechanically rewrite legitimate “no join-state” prose for pure `machine-transition` calls, where runtime join storage genuinely is absent (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:122`). Distinguish physical absence from childless sentinel by semantics.

Reconcile the tracked `docs/spec` copies with canonical `spec`. If they are generated publishing inputs, regenerate them and make the existing docs staging/parity check fail on canonical/published divergence; if they should not be tracked mirrors, remove the duplicate authority through the repository's ruled docs mechanism rather than leaving stale copies. Avoid a bespoke one-phrase framework.

## Dedupe and scope

Closed `rf2-oalcqo` explicitly requested the nearby audit but was incompletely implemented and cannot be amended. No live bead covers these surviving surfaces. This follow-up is documentation/contract reconciliation only; runtime schema atomicity and duplicate telemetry are separately tracked by `rf2-7u8gen` and `rf2-smya7a`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 009, the machines actor guide, implementation comments, fixtures, canonical Spec 005, and published `docs/spec` surfaces describe the same childless-sentinel/sibling-suppression contract.
- No active rejection passage says the sentinel slot is physically absent, that registered siblings later complete, or that they find no slot.
- Legitimate pure-call/no-runtime-db descriptions remain intact and explicitly distinguish physical absence from a reject sentinel.
- The error-catalogue wording matches the final exact producer/cardinality behavior delivered with `rf2-smya7a`.
- Canonical and published Spec 005/009 content cannot silently diverge under ordinary PR docs checks; a deliberate stale-mirror mutation makes the relevant existing/parity gate fail.
- MkDocs strict/link checks and machines JVM/CLJS contract fixtures remain green; no runtime behavior is changed by this bead alone.
