title: Atomically reject spawn-all when any child fails spawn-time schema validation
description:
## Problem

PR #5794 (authored head `0d460cbfe57eff897b3a079ce44a39ef43afa440`; merge `4a1095dd1f385571d07f949bd3f56a298e9dd5c4`) documents atomic `:spawn-all` rejection for unregistered child types, but the equivalent spawn-time schema-rejection path is still non-atomic. A mixed valid/schema-invalid invoke publishes a live join containing every child, installs valid siblings, and leaves an impossible child in the join forever. The defect persists on current main.

At the authored head:

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:2475-2486` prepares a live join state containing every allocated child; `:2535-2536` emits `:rf.machine/spawn-all-init` before per-child spawn effects.
- `lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:607-637` preflights only unregistered types and otherwise installs that live join.
- Spawn-time schema validation occurs later inside each per-child spawn (`spawn.cljc:433-447`); `:459` suppresses only the rejected child.
- `lifecycle_fx/join.cljc:119-125` requires every declared child for `:join :all`.

A schema-rejected child has no snapshot and can never emit completion, while its valid siblings are real live actors. This violates Spec 005's promise that a parent never observes a half-installed child (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:529`) and recreates the dead-join/orphan class that the unregistered-type sentinel was meant to remove.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register child type `:bad` with an initial-data schema such as `[:map [:n pos-int?]]`, but prepare invalid initial data for it.
2. Register a valid child type `:ok`.
3. Enter a parent state with `:spawn-all {:children [{:id :bad ...} {:id :ok ...}] :join :all ...}`.
4. Observe the live join slot contains both preallocated ids, the bad snapshot is absent, and the valid sibling snapshot is installed/live.
5. Deliver the valid child's documented completion. The join reaches `:done #{:ok}` but can never obtain `:bad`; the parent remains in the join state forever and the valid actor remains owned by an impossible join.

The exact-head audit reproduced this state deterministically with the invalid child first; child ordering does not repair the architecture.

## Required correction

Make the first invoke-level `spawn-all-init` decision authoritative for every fail-closed child admission condition, not only unregistered type resolution. Pass/reuse the already prepared per-child spawn arguments and preflight spawn-time schema validity before publishing a live join or executing any child effect. Do not re-evaluate user `:data` functions or mint a second snapshot/value during validation.

If any child rejects, emit the correct bounded error(s), seed one childless reject sentinel, and suppress every per-child effect—valid and invalid—before snapshot/system-id/spawn-order/trace/start installation. All-valid invokes retain the existing fast path. Keep registration-time shape rejection where it already belongs.

## Dedupe and scope

Closed `rf2-qb1j5z` repairs the same dead-join/orphan class only for unregistered types; closed `rf2-f3kp7` repairs single-spawn schema rejection. Neither composes those guarantees for `:spawn-all`, and closed beads cannot be amended. No live bead covers mixed schema-valid/schema-invalid children, so this is a new runtime follow-up.
acceptance_criteria:
- Invalid-schema children in first, middle, and last positions are preflighted before any live join or child side effect is published.
- A mixed valid/invalid invoke installs no child snapshots, system-id bindings, spawn-order entries, spawned traces, or start dispatches; the join slot is one childless reject sentinel.
- Exactly one schema error is emitted for each invalid child; prepared child data/snapshots and user functions are evaluated at most once.
- `:join :all`, `:any`, and threshold modes cannot observe a half-installed child set after invoke-level rejection.
- Parent exit clears the reject sentinel and no valid sibling remains live/orphaned.
- All-valid `:spawn-all`, single `:spawn`, registration-shape rejection, and unregistered-type rejection remain green on CLJ and CLJS.
- A mutation that moves schema validation back into only the later per-child effect makes the mixed-child regression fail.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6010 (worker/machines-transition-cluster). Premise re-verified at file:line against current main before fixing; each fix pinned by a mutation reproducing the original defect. Machines JVM gate 1123 tests/3917 assertions green (+19 tests/+65 assertions).

title: Add the Resources runtime to the canonical bundle-isolation inventory
description:
## Problem

PR #5798 (authored head `f336273ccf3871bf7852c4ae69532e16b44541a4`; merge `02facfbb37c0559ffc3ba9200f451e02fa3a4b0f`) adds a self-declared completeness check to the bundle-isolation table, but the table omits the published `implementation/resources` runtime entirely. The omission persists on current main.

`implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs` contains a `resources-tooling` entry around exact-head `:345-368`/`:762`, but no primary `resources` artefact. `assertPositiveControlComplete` (`:928-935`) merely cross-checks the script's own two hand-written tables, so an artefact absent from both is defined away rather than detected.

Resources is a real separately published, browser-reachable optional artefact: `.github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh:94,107` includes it in release inventory, while `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc:33-42` explicitly requires that core not depend on it. Its tooling sibling is JVM-only (`resources.cljc:74-82`), so a CLJS runtime leak does not necessarily carry any `resources-tooling` sentinel.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Search the bundle-isolation `ARTEFACTS` table for a primary `resources` entry: none exists; startup completeness remains green.
2. Confirm Resources is in the publishable release inventory and exposes optional CLJS runtime code.
3. Add an accidental production-reachable `:require [re-frame.resources]` from core/Counter.
4. Build the Counter `:advanced` bundle. The Resources runtime is now present, but the gate has no Resources runtime sentinels to search. The JVM-only `resources-tooling` entry need not appear.
5. The gate reports all 22 declared entries complete and the leak passes undetected.

## Required correction

Add a primary Resources isolation entry with stable live-runtime sentinels and a real same-options positive bundle. The existing `:examples/realworld-resources` release is the natural positive target; wire the smallest necessary release into this gate rather than inventing a synthetic application if it already proves real reachability.

Make inventory completeness compare against one canonical list of browser-optional/publishable implementation artefacts rather than only against itself. Reuse an existing release/version artefact inventory or a tiny shared manifest if that removes duplication; do not build a general manifest framework. The check must fail when a separately published optional runtime is missing even if all internal tables omit it together.

Coordinate with `rf2-qmb01i`, which makes emitted positive controls non-vacuous across the same script, but keep this missing-artefact invariant independently testable.

## Dedupe and scope

Closed `rf2-e6qmxk` is the source positive-control defect closed by #5798 and cannot be amended. `rf2-vxgfnd.173` covers release-workflow inventory coupling, not production bundle isolation. No live bead covers the absent Resources runtime entry, so this is a distinct follow-up.
acceptance_criteria:
- The bundle-isolation inventory contains a primary `resources` runtime entry with stable sentinels owned by executable CLJS runtime code.
- Deleting that entry while Resources remains in the canonical optional/publishable artefact inventory fails startup completeness.
- Adding a production-reachable `re-frame.resources` dependency to Counter makes the negative isolation gate fail.
- A real `:examples/realworld-resources` (or equivalently representative) `:advanced` release proves every Resources sentinel present under matching compilation options.
- Resources-tooling remains a separate JVM/tooling concern and cannot satisfy the runtime entry accidentally.
- Adding another optional browser artefact to the canonical inventory without an isolation entry fails automatically; the check does not compare only two copies of its own local table.
- Current legitimate Resources examples/releases and unrelated isolation entries remain green without weakening sentinel budgets.
close_reason: Merged PR #5975 (add Resources runtime to canonical bundle-isolation inventory — meta-hardening: gate had resources-tooling JVM sibling but no primary resources runtime entry (browser-reachable optional) so a re-frame.resources leak into prod wouldn't red; added primary entry (2 live sentinels) + realworld-resources positive control + assertCanonicalInventoryCovered() deriving the REQUIRED set from the deps.edn :clein/build authority — any future published runtime missing from the inventory now reds the gate; mutation-proofs A(resources leak)/B1(new artefact no entry)/B2(removed from both tables); no resources.cljc change; CI green)

title: Require emitted advanced positive controls for every bundle-isolation sentinel
description:
## Problem

PR #5798 (authored head `f336273ccf3871bf7852c4ae69532e16b44541a4`; merge `02facfbb37c0559ffc3ba9200f451e02fa3a4b0f`) claims to make bundle-isolation sentinel drift fail loud, but only 3 of 22 artefacts receive a real emitted-bundle positive control. Fourteen artefacts prove only that the configured literal occurs somewhere in raw source, and five third-party artefacts explicitly perform no positive check. The original vacuous-negative false-green therefore survives for 19 artefacts and persists unchanged on current main.

In `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs` at the exact head:

- `POSITIVE_CONTROL` (`:744-777`) gives `onBundle` only to schemas, machines, and HTTP: 7 of 41 sentinels.
- Fourteen artefacts use `srcRoots`: 26 sentinels. `:831-859` concatenates raw `.clj/.cljc/.cljs` text, including comments, docstrings, JVM-only reader branches, and dead code; `:915-925` accepts any substring hit as proof.
- xyflow, elkjs, cljs-devtools, zprint, and editscript use `gap`: 8 sentinels. `:884-893` returns `{ok: true, checked: 0}`, and `:928-935` calls that table declaration complete.

A source occurrence is not evidence that the sentinel survives the Clojure reader, CLJS compilation, or Closure `:advanced` DCE under the same options as the negative bundle. A documented no-op is not a positive control.

## Steps to Reproduce

Source false-green:

1. Rename every executable Routing occurrence of `rf.error/no-such-route` and `rf.error/missing-route-param` while leaving stale comments in `navigate.cljc` unchanged.
2. Run the implemented `srcRoots` algorithm. It still finds two old-string comment hits for each sentinel and reports the positive control green.
3. Later leak the renamed Routing code into Counter. The reader removes the comments, so neither old sentinel appears in the production bundle. The negative scan also reports green: drift plus leak is undetected.
4. Moving a configured literal into `#?(:clj ...)`, a dead form, or a docstring produces the same false proof.

Gap false-green:

1. Upgrade/remove one selected third-party literal so it no longer occurs in the actual dependency output.
2. Accidentally import that dev dependency from a production-reachable namespace.
3. The stale literal is absent from Counter and the `gap` branch checks zero positive sentinels, so both halves report success.

The authored mutations only changed the configured string to a nonexistent value; they did not rename executable source while preserving stale prose, so they could not distinguish these cases.

## Required correction

Every negative isolation sentinel must have a positive control in real same-options `:advanced` output that deliberately reaches its owner. Reuse focused feature examples where they already exist; add the smallest dedicated Xray/Story/dependency probe bundle for tooling and third-party libraries. One probe may cover multiple artefacts when ownership remains unambiguous.

Delete successful `gap` as a completeness mode. If a sentinel cannot be made present in a compiled positive target, it is not a sound isolation sentinel and must be replaced. Validate sentinel ownership/uniqueness so a common bundle occurrence from another artefact cannot satisfy the wrong entry. Raw source scans may remain as cheap diagnostics, never as proof of emitted reachability.

Keep this a small manifest-plus-build correction, not a general build framework.

## Dedupe and scope

Closed `rf2-e6qmxk` is the exact parent defect and was closed by #5798; these counterexamples prove incomplete closure, so it cannot be amended. Closed `rf2-qyfy1m` is an analogous comment-counting defect on another gate, and closed `rf2-vxgfnd.119` is useful precedent for same-options compiled controls. No live bead covers this bundle-isolation remainder.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every artefact and every configured sentinel has a real inspected `:advanced` positive bundle in which that sentinel is present; a successful summary can never report `checked: 0` or a positive-control gap.
- Renaming all executable Routing sentinels while retaining old strings only in comments/docstrings makes the gate fail.
- Moving a sentinel to a JVM-only reader branch or otherwise unreachable/DCE'd CLJS form makes the positive control fail.
- Each xyflow, elkjs, cljs-devtools, zprint, and editscript sentinel is proven in an actual compiled tooling/dependency bundle; upgrading/removing it makes the gate fail.
- A deliberate production import/leak of every covered artefact makes the negative Counter check fail.
- Sentinel ownership/uniqueness prevents an occurrence emitted by one artefact from satisfying another artefact's positive control.
- Positive and negative builds use equivalent Closure mode/options for the claimed reachability property; ordinary bundle-isolation CI remains deterministic and bounded.
close_reason: verified-delivered by commit 4e43784ec7 (ancestor of origin/main); commit carried no bead-id so never auto-closed. Worker re-ran both gates green (22 artefacts/38 sentinels) + proved non-vacuity (mutated sentinel absent → positive control fails red). No PR: fabricating a diff would be churn against a delivered bead.

title: Enforce the closed target and lease grammar at every observation-port boundary
description:
## Problem

PR #5797 (authored head `abdcae347fd6fd3de7a091e736ec1bf9ffd97ddd`; merge `d25d7c258a76bb780a7edd54393b4bab6bc2ffcb`) added a typed default only for an unknown target `:kind`. The observation port still accepts malformed values that use a known discriminator, and half of the lease-taking surface still throws raw host exceptions. The defects persist on current main and violate Spec 006's typed port-error contract.

At the authored head, `probe` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc:850-887`) and `acquire!` (`:1283-1342`) dispatch solely on `(:kind target)`. A `:subscription` target with a non-vector/empty/non-keyword-headed `:query`, missing frame identity, or wrong field domains enters the accepted arm and reaches operations such as `(first query)`, leaking an untyped host/protocol error. An incomplete `:story-override` target is silently accepted and produces a nil-shaped observation/static lease even though it could not have come from `resolve-target`'s declared shape. The new fixture covers only `{:kind :bogus}`.

Separately, shared `lease-state` field-accesses its argument without validation (authored `observation.cljc:484-486`; current main around `:498`). `read` and `release!` dereference that result (`:1405-1407`, `:1472-1475`). `(read nil)` and `(release! nil)` therefore throw raw `NullPointerException` on the JVM with no `:rf.error/id`; CLJS analogously exposes an untyped host error. A corrupted generated consumer escapes the ViewCell boundary as an unclassifiable exception.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. With a live frame and registered subscription, call `probe` and `acquire!` with `{:kind :subscription :frame-id <live> :query 42}` (and with an empty or non-keyword-headed query). Observe a bare host/protocol error rather than `:rf.error/observation-malformed-target`.
2. Call those operations with an incomplete `{:kind :story-override}`. Observe silent static nil-shaped evidence/ownership rather than a typed reject.
3. Call `(read nil)` and `(release! nil)`. On the JVM both throw `NullPointerException` with `(:rf.error/id (ex-data e)) == nil`; the same commands for `probe`/`acquire!` with `{:kind :bogus}` now correctly throw typed, demonstrating the half-hardened boundary.

## Required correction

Define and enforce the port's closed data grammar at shared boundaries:

- A target validator must accept exactly the complete shapes emitted by `resolve-target`: a valid subscription frame/query identity, or a Story override with all required query/value/opaque-token keys (legitimate nil values remain values when their keys are present). Reject non-maps, missing/extra keys, wrong domains, empty/non-keyword-headed queries, and supported-kind-but-incomplete targets through `:rf.error/observation-malformed-target` before any host operation.
- A lease validator at the shared lease-state boundary must accept only real ObservationLease values and reject nil/maps/arbitrary host objects through a distinct diagnostic `:rf.error/observation-malformed-lease`.
- Preserve `current?` as a pure/no-throw predicate by returning false for a non-lease if that is its ruled contract; reconcile Spec 006 so it does not simultaneously promise typed throws for every op and never-throw predicate behavior.

Catalogue the diagnostic categories in Spec 009. Keep these programmer-defect diagnostics off the always-on fan and preserve production DCE; do not add permissive coercion or turn malformed values into nil observations.

## Dedupe and scope

Closed `rf2-vxgfnd.36` covered only unknown `:kind` and cannot be amended. No all-status bead covers a malformed known-kind target or malformed lease. This follow-up deliberately unifies both because they are one incomplete closed-grammar/typed-error boundary and should share validators/tests rather than grow per-operation patches.
acceptance_criteria:
- CLJ and CLJS fixtures exercise `probe` and `acquire!` with a non-map target, unknown kind, malformed subscription query, missing/invalid subscription frame identity, and incomplete Story override; every case throws `:rf.error/observation-malformed-target` before host operations or ownership.
- Presence checks distinguish a legitimate nil override value/token from a missing required key according to the ruled target schema.
- `read` and `release!` reject nil, maps, and arbitrary host objects with `:rf.error/observation-malformed-lease` on both hosts; no raw NPE/TypeError escapes.
- Valid subscription/override targets, valid static/node leases, idempotent release, and `:rf.error/read-after-release` remain unchanged.
- `current?` has one explicit coherent malformed-value contract (recommended: false/no throw), and Spec 006's error wording matches it.
- Spec 009 catalogues both diagnostic categories with bounded structural evidence; neither fans the always-on channel.
- Advanced-production proof confirms no diagnostic target/lease formatting or extra validation machinery survives beyond the minimal typed boundary behavior.
notes: PR opened (leave open for mayor; do NOT merge): https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5847 — branch worker/obs-grammar-183 @ 90de1f10707c732de7a8b074e17a2980dcb0b970. Closes all 3 repro gaps: (1) malformed known-kind :subscription target [malformed :query non-vec/empty/non-kw-head, absent/nil/non-kw :frame-id, bad key-set] -> typed :rf.error/observation-malformed-target via shared validate-target! before any host op; (2) incomplete {:kind :story-override} -> same typed id; (3) (read nil)/(release! nil)/map/host-object -> NEW typed :rf.error/observation-malformed-lease via shared validate-lease!; current? kept pure no-throw (false for non-lease). Spec 009: added observation-malformed-lease row + broadened malformed-target row (both diagnostic, no always-on fan). Gates all green foreground: core JVM 1932/0, ui JVM 457/0, CLJS 9285/0, markdown validators exit 0, full fast-PR spine PASS. No Spec-Schemas change needed (observation categories carry no per-category Malli tags there). PR-body follow-up noted: Spec 006 prose reconciliation for current? never-throw (spec/006 is another worker's surface).
close_reason: Merged PR #5847 (typed rejects at every observation-port target/lease boundary; new :rf.error/observation-malformed-lease + broadened -malformed-target; 9 red-before-fix fixtures; CI green)

title: Linearize ViewCell invalidation against JVM flush completion
description:
## Problem

PR #5796 (authored head `cc48c6a7cdaea80256d695864be69f804edf646e`; merge `2f668e91895f7e3fb34678c7599e9bae69cd94ba`) made the bounded invalidation summary honest, but its surrounding ViewCell scheduler is not linearizable on the supported JVM host. The defect persists on current main.

In `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc`, an invalidation folds evidence and dirty enrollment in separate transitions, while flush completion separately reads the evidence and then clears `:dirty?`/`:evidence`. A concurrent invalidation can linearize after `complete-flush!` has read the current summary but before it clears the cell. Because the cell is still dirty, that invalidation does not re-enrol it. The flush then erases the new evidence and leaves the cell clean and absent from the dirty registry. A real update has disappeared with no next revision or correction.

Authored-head anchors are `reactive.cljc:778-783`, `:856-871`, and `:873-894`; current main retains the same split transition around `:1087`, `:1170`, and `:1187` at review time.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create one ViewCell, subscribe a listener, and mark it dirty with evidence for epoch/query 1.
2. Start `flush-dirty!` on a JVM future.
3. Place a deterministic barrier immediately before the state clear (`:dirty? false`, `:evidence nil`), after the flush has captured epoch 1.
4. While the flusher is paused, call the cell's invalidation callback with distinct epoch/query 2 evidence.
5. Release the flusher.
6. Observe one delivered summary containing only epoch/query 1, `:dirty? false`, nil pending evidence, revision 1, and no enrolled next window. Epoch/query 2 is absent from both the delivered and pending state.

The audit produced this outcome deterministically by interposing on the exact cell atom's clear transition. It is a legal JVM interleaving, not a timing-only stress inference.

## Required correction

Give each cell one linearizable pending-window transition. An invalidation must atomically fold evidence and perform the dirty false-to-true transition; completion must atomically capture the window, clear dirty/evidence, and advance the revision. Dirty-registry enrollment must correspond exactly to a false-to-true transition, including an invalidation concurrent with completion.

Do not hold a lock through evidence sinks, useSyncExternalStore listeners, or other user/tool callbacks. Preserve the write-side-drain then one read-side render-batch law, the bounded summary semantics, and advanced-production elimination of diagnostic evidence.

## Dedupe and scope

This is not `rf2-vxgfnd.73` (a throwing sink before completion), `rf2-vxgfnd.86` (re-entrant phase-2 ordering), or `rf2-vxgfnd.147` (tool projection owner/generation publication). Those paths are closed or separately scoped; none prevents an ordinary JVM invalidation racing the scheduler's own destructive clear. The finding was discovered while auditing the closed source bead `rf2-vxgfnd.74`, so this must be a new follow-up rather than an amendment.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic JVM barrier fixture forces an invalidation between flush capture and completion; the invalidation either belongs to the captured window or is enrolled as a fresh next window.
- The current outcome—first window delivered, second invalidation absent, dirty false, no pending registration—is impossible.
- Dirty false-to-true and dirty-registry enrollment cannot diverge under concurrent mark/flush operations.
- Completion captures and clears exactly one coherent window while advancing its revision once.
- Bounded target/drop accounting, saturation, and `:dropped-exact?` invariants remain green.
- Re-entrant listener/sink and throwing-consumer fixtures remain green; no lock is held across callbacks.
- Queued write sides still coalesce into one read-side render batch, and advanced production remains free of diagnostic-evidence machinery.
close_reason: Merged PR #5976 (linearize ViewCell invalidation against JVM flush completion — real lost-update race: mark-dirty! landing between completion's capture and clear was lost twice (evidence erased + re-enrolment skipped); fix = enrol-dirty! folds evidence+flips dirty in one swap-vals!, complete-flush! CAS retry loop so racing mark re-reads; *completion-barrier* test seam; red-before-fix deterministic+200-round stress. CI-fix: hoisted debug-enabled? to top-level if so fold-evidence DCEs (prod-elision); JVM-ui fail was pre-existing flaky slice-memo overlap on a disjoint surface; CI green)

title: Separate canonical re-frame.ui guidance from frozen and retiring adapter material
description:
## Problem

PR #5795 re-aims several citations into the compiled Spec-004 contract, but leaves general/current normative documents teaching the retiring adapter model as re-frame2's canonical view architecture.

Current contradictions include:

- `spec/Pattern-StatefulComponents.md:4,28-88,172-188` calls outer/inner `reg-view`, Form-3, render-time `capture-frame`, Reagent-slim, UIx, and Helix the canonical pattern, while its new citations land in Spec 004 sections that explicitly remove Forms and define compiled effects/leases.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:336-394` presents Form-2 wrapping and every React-adapter/cross-language port as unqualified permanent obligations, though the ratified rewrite requires transitional classification.
- `spec/000-Vision.md:533-535` describes ambient capture/plain functions as the current path.
- `spec/AI-Audit.md:382-388` calls Var invocation plus `(view :id)` the v1 surface and grades Form-1 canonical/Form-2 selectively supported.
- `spec/Principles.md:231-237` tells readers to replace Form-2 with Form-1 and says the positional model is formalized in current 004.

The ratified end state is different: compiled `re-frame.ui` is the sole taught layer; stock Reagent survives as an explicitly frozen compatibility tier; UIx/Helix/slim are removed. Resolving a Markdown anchor is not semantic consistency.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start from the spec index/default pattern and follow Stateful Components as canonical guidance.
2. Implement its outer/inner Form-3/capture-frame pattern or choose UIx/Helix/slim as peers.

4. Compare Vision, AI-Audit, Principles, and unqualified 006 adapter obligations with the ratified delivery record: they describe mutually exclusive end states.

## Required Correction

Move Form-1/2/3, `reg-view`, and render-time `capture-frame` into clearly named frozen stock-Reagent compatibility material. Keep the exact plain-function no-frame recovery bug in its own bead; this bead owns the broader canonical-versus-compatibility classification.

title: Align frozen Reagent ViewMeta schema with fields reg-view actually emits
description:
## Problem

PR #5795 reaffirms `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:454-474` as the live carrier for the frozen Reagent `:rf/view-meta` registry-slot shape, but that schema claims `reg-view` stamps `:rf/id`, `:rf/args`, and `:rf/form`. The implementation does not emit those fields.

`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc:88-116` consumes `:rf/id` to choose the registry key and then removes it from slot metadata. It never emits `:rf/args` or `:rf/form`; the only optional form-related field is a separate `:reagent2/form`. An exact-head runtime probe of explicit-id `reg-view` returned only `:handler-fn` when selecting the claimed fields.

A frozen compatibility contract must describe what the frozen runtime actually guarantees. Otherwise tools or migration code may depend on metadata that is always absent.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register Form-1, Form-2, explicit-id, auto-id, and `reg-view*` variants through the frozen Reagent surface.
2. Read `handler-meta :view` / the registered slot metadata.
3. Select `:rf/id`, `:rf/args`, `:rf/form`, `:reagent2/form`, and `:handler-fn`.
4. Observe the macro removes `:rf/id`, never creates `:rf/args`/`:rf/form`, and only the actually implemented metadata appears.
5. Compare with the `ViewMeta` schema; the documented required/available fields do not match runtime values.

## Required Correction

Prefer the simplest pre-alpha correction: remove the three unimplemented fields from the frozen registry-slot schema unless a named live consumer requires them. If a field is genuinely required, implement and test it deliberately, including a precise definition of Form-2 classification that does not conflate `:rf/form` with `:reagent2/form`. Do not preserve fictitious fields for compatibility.
acceptance_criteria:
- `handler-meta :view` exactly conforms to the documented frozen `ViewMeta` shape for auto-id, explicit-id, Form-1, Form-2, and `reg-view*`.
- Every documented field is emitted with defined semantics, or is removed from the schema; no aspirational/fictitious slot remains.
- Registry identity (the key selected by `:rf/id`) is clearly distinguished from metadata stored in the slot.
- Any retained form-classification field has one spelling and executable tests; `:rf/form` and `:reagent2/form` are not ambiguously duplicated.
- Tooling/migration consumers and Spec-Schemas validation stay green without UIx/Helix/slim additions.
close_reason: Merged PR #5977 (RECORD-REALITY: frozen Reagent ViewMeta schema had 3 FICTITIOUS fields — :rf/id (consumed for registry key then dissoc'd, not slot meta), :rf/args (never emitted), :rf/form (wrong key + :form-3 no path produces); reconciled schema to actual expand-reg-view emission — removed the 3, replaced :rf/form with actually-emitted :reagent2/form [enum form-1/form-2, optional, reagent-slim-only]; kept :rf/props (survives dissoc); docs-only, emission correct/unchanged; reg-view JVM contract green; CI green)

title: Assign compiled root preflight to 004C, not Spec 002's two-pass React contract
description:
## Problem

PR #5795 changes `spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md:224-227` to say compiled UI root frame preflight—ENSURE plus initial events before the first `render!`/hydration—is owned by Spec 002. Spec 002 does not contain that host-root contract. Its React compatibility mechanism at 002:1511-1517 intentionally does the opposite sequence: first React render omits descendants, `useLayoutEffect` performs ENSURE after commit, then a second render emits children.

The compiled substrate implementation in `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/client.cljs` performs preflight before `createRoot`/`render`, as 004C states locally. A whole-document Spec-002 ownership citation therefore sends a fresh implementer to an adjacent but incompatible lifecycle and makes it unclear which sequence is authoritative.

Both contracts are deliberate: 004C owns compiled host-root preflight; Spec 002 owns frame construction/idempotence/initial-event semantics and the frozen/transitional component `frame-root` mechanism.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Follow the changed ownership link from 004C's frame-preflight section to Spec 002.
2. Search Spec 002 for `render!`, `hydrate-root`, host-root preflight, or “before React”; no compiled-root rule exists.
3. Read 002:1511-1517; it prescribes empty first render, layout-effect ENSURE, second render.
4. Inspect `client.cljs:386-396,426-491,535-562`; compiled `ui/mount` preflights before React touches the container.
5. Observe that the citation attributes one contract to a document whose only nearby React contract is intentionally opposite.

## Required Correction

Make 004C explicitly own compiled host-root sequencing. Link narrowly to the exact Spec-002 sections only for `make-frame`, idempotence, and synchronous initial-event draining. If Spec 002 needs a compiled-substrate cross-reference, add a clearly separate subsection that points back to 004C without replacing or blurring its compatibility-tier two-pass contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- One tracked 004C section unambiguously owns ENSURE/initial-event completion before compiled React root creation/render/hydration.
- Every Spec-002 link targets the exact frame-construction or initial-event semantics it contributes, not the whole document.
- The frozen/transitional `frame-root` empty-render → layout-effect → populated-render contract remains explicit and distinct.
- Compiled browser tests prove preflight failure occurs before React mutates/touches the container; compatibility tests retain their two-pass behavior.
- Cross-spec and slug/MkDocs checks pass with no circular or ambiguous ownership wording.
close_reason: Merged PR #5979 (assign compiled root preflight to 004C not Spec 002's two-pass React contract — spec-ownership reconciliation: 004C §3 delegated the compiled host-root preflight whole-document to Spec 002, but 002 never claimed it (zero createRoot/host-root refs); fixed by making 004C own the sequencing with 3 precise composition anchors (make-frame construction, idempotent-replacement ENSURE, ordered :initial-events drain) + naming the frozen 002 frame-root two-pass as the OPPOSITE order kept distinct; Spec 002 untouched (nothing to shed); no code change (client.cljs already correct); docs; CI green)

title: Remove draft-only numeric authority from the promoted re-frame.ui specs
description:
## Problem

At the audited head, 52 bare synthesis-style references remain across normative tracked specs:

- `spec/004-Views.md` — 6
- `spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md` — 10
- `spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md` — 20
- `spec/004D-UI-Test-Selectors.md` — 10
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` — 3
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` — 3

Examples include `12 §2b`, `08 §5`, `03 §8`, `07 §2`, and `09 codex2 F1` at 004:203/614/658/665/697, 004B:57/62/126/131/409, 004C:17/93/188/220-223/294/311/437-438/454, 004D:16/20/34/47-48/171-174, 006:872/884/890, and 009:2292/2297/2308. They are not links to tracked specifications and several are load-bearing authority/tie-break statements.

The annexes also retain final-state violations such as “where the synthesis is silent,” “this draft,” rewrite narration, review identities, and unresolved `[S1-CONFIRM]` markers. #5800 later force-tracked the synthesis tree as a temporary handoff measure, but `rf2-vxgfnd.99.1` explicitly removes it after promotion. 2. Follow a reference such as `12 §2b` from the rendered spec; there is no Markdown target or durable owning section.
3. At #5795's exact head, observe the clean worker checkout has no synthesis tree at all.
4. On current main, observe the tree is only temporarily force-tracked and already has an S7 removal bead.
5. A fresh reader can reasonably interpret the number as tracked Spec 012/008/003/007 and lands on the wrong authority.

## Required Correction

Perform a classified final-state sweep. Replace each load-bearing synthesis reference with a precise tracked Markdown anchor, or state the rule locally where the promoted spec now owns it. Remove review identities and draft/rewrite provenance from normative prose; explicitly label genuinely historical material rather than silently rewriting history. Resolve or remove confirmation markers whose stage has already passed.

Add a small lint over normative spec files that rejects bare synthesis-coordinate and review-label patterns while allowing explicit links to numbered tracked specs and intentionally labelled historical annexes.
acceptance_criteria:

- Slug/link, MkDocs strict, and relevant spec consistency gates pass.

title: Make day8/re-frame2-ui publication a blocking pre-tag S7 gate
description:
## Problem

The ratified packaging decision requires `day8/re-frame2-ui` to ship as a separate artefact on the lockstep re-frame2 release train, but the deferred publication work named by PR #5792 has no durable owner or pre-tag gate.

`implementation/ui/deps.edn` is deliberately pre-publication today: no `:clein`, `:clein/build`, version, or package descriptor. That is valid during construction. The gap is that the authoritative stage plan assigns S6 adoption/CI migration and S7 adapter deletion/tag cut, while neither the S7 epic nor the W9 release-pruning work requires adding UI package metadata, pre-deploy proof, deploy topology, or release-body wiring. The current tag workflow can therefore accept a core alpha tag and deploy core without UI once the program reaches tag cut.

Closed `rf2-pc479y` says this work will land in “the ui-publishing stage,” but no such stage/leaf exists. A comment is not ownership.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Inspect `implementation/ui/deps.edn`; confirm the UI artefact is not publishable yet.
2. Inspect the authoritative S6/S7 plan, `rf2-vxgfnd.99`, W9 prep/`rf2-nojiwy`, and `.github/workflows/release.yml`.
3. Observe S7 owns the tag cut and pruning UIx/Helix/slim release rows, but no live obligation adds `day8/re-frame2-ui` to package metadata, lockstep inventory, pre-deploy tests, deploy matrix, or release notes.
4. Set the repository VERSION to an alpha shape and inspect the present tag workflow: its verifier has no readiness condition requiring UI publication, so a core-only alpha is structurally allowed.
5. Search all bead statuses for UI publication/Clojars/release-matrix ownership; only the closed premature bead and general stage epics appear.

## Required Correction

Make UI publication an explicit blocking child/gate of the S7 tag-cut work, sequenced before release-DAG pruning and tag creation. The implementation slice must add the package/build/version metadata and every release surface in one coherent change, then prove the coordinate resolves at the root VERSION. It may be implemented late, but it must be owned now so the deferred work cannot disappear between stages.

Coordinate with the executable inventory validator follow-up from #5792. Do not publish an unfinished UI artefact early merely to satisfy this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- The S7/tag-cut dependency graph has an explicit live owner for `day8/re-frame2-ui` publication, and tag cut is blocked on it.
- UI declares the final `:clein/build`/package/version metadata using the repository root VERSION and the ratified `day8/re-frame2-ui` coordinate.
- Lockstep inventory, JVM pre-deploy test, dependency-correct deploy leaf, release body/docs, and any package descriptor are added coherently before pruning old adapter rows.
- A release dry run/preflight proves core and UI resolve at the same alpha VERSION from the intended repository and that UI depends on the matching core version.
- Attempting a core-only alpha tag fails before deployment.
- No UIx/Helix/slim compatibility work is added; their release rows remain scheduled for S7 deletion, while stock Reagent's frozen tier follows its ratified scope.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option A — rf2-vxgfnd.99.2 is ratified as the explicit blocking pre-tag S7 gate for day8/re-frame2-ui publication. Nothing is implemented now; the bead is the durable owner, and at S7 it must be sequenced BEFORE W9 WP-3 release-DAG pruning and BEFORE tag creation, failing the tag cut closed if UI is not publishable.

RATIONALE: Both recorded opinions (original recommendation + CComposer) converge on Option A, and independent verification confirms the hole: implementation/ui/deps.edn is deliberately pre-publication (no :clein/build, by design), release.yml documents the UI substrate as intentionally absent, and neither the S7 epic (rf2-vxgfnd.99) nor W9 WP-3 obligates adding the UI release surfaces — so a core-only alpha tag is structurally allowed today. Option B (trust epic memory) reproduces exactly the failure mode that killed rf2-pc479y ("lands in the ui-publishing stage" — no such stage existed). Keeping the gate owned-now/implemented-late satisfies CORRECTNESS (fail-closed release integrity) and GOOD PRACTICE (no early publication of an unfinished substrate) at zero present cost.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (for the S7 implementation slice — do not dispatch before S7 opens):
- Sequencing: when S7 leaf children are filed at the S6 boundary, wire this bead as a hard prerequisite of W9 WP-3 adapter-row pruning, tag creation, and external-alpha (rf2-deiym).
- One coherent hot-zone PR mirroring sibling per-feature artefacts (e.g. implementation/schemas/deps.edn):
  (1) implementation/ui/deps.edn: add :clein + :clein/build for day8/re-frame2-ui, :version from repo-root VERSION, dep on ../core via :local/root;
  (2) .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh: add ui to ARTEFACT_PATHS / ARTEFACTS / NON_CORE;
  (3) .github/workflows/release.yml: jvm-ui pre-deploy test (clojure -M:test from implementation/ui), deploy-leaf matrix row after deploy-core (local-root: ../core), github-release body row for day8/re-frame2-ui;
  (4) docs/release-process.md: artefact count + coordinate list.
- Jar/pom preflight (reagent-slim pattern) only if a publication transform risk exists — UI has no ns-rename, so JVM pre-deploy + lockstep likely suffice; do not gold-plate.
- Coordinate with the #5792 executable inventory validator (rf2-vxgfnd.173 / PR #5867): verify that guard is live on the tag-cut branch and fold any gap into this PR.
- Dry-run proof: a temp project must resolve day8/re-frame2-ui {:mvn/version <VERSION>} plus matching core at the same VERSION, with UI depending on the matching core version.
- Acceptance (per bead): tag cut blocked on UI publication; core-only alpha fails before deploy; no uix/helix/slim compat work; stock Reagent frozen-tier scope unchanged.
- Do NOT publish early (S5/S6) and do NOT split the surfaces across PRs (inventory guard + hot-zone release.yml discipline require one coherent change).
publication additionally gated on rf2-u53yy.1 (install-tax removal) per the 2026-07-20 UIx-review ratification — an experimental checkout may carry the cache-blocker tax; a published library may not. Dependency edge wired (rf2-vxgfnd.99.2 blocked-by rf2-u53yy.1).
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-21 17:14:17 AUSEST) - ALPHA PUBLICATION SEQUENCING

THE RULING: Option A - HOLD THE RULED CHAIN. Options B (publish with the documented cache-blocker tax) and C (core-only alpha) are REJECTED. The alpha tag waits on ALL of the following, stated as CONDITIONS not dates: (1) rf2-u53yy.1 closes with its acceptance met (install-tax removal; dedicated solo compiler worker, day-one premise probe first - does Shadow restore arbitrary def :meta into cljs.analyzer/namespaces on a real disk-cache hit); (2) this bead's publication PR lands per the recorded 2026-07-15 implementation guidance, with dry-run resolution proof; (3) the S7-entry proof plus soak condition AS DEFINED BY the rf2-vxgfnd.99 ruling (delegated sibling ruling, same date) - the soak clock has NOT started (nightly expensive-tests.yml red on every scheduled run Jul 9-20, re-verified fresh 2026-07-21), so all dossier tag-date estimates are void; that ruling owns soak semantics and this ruling defers to it by reference. Sequencing within S7 unchanged: this bead before W9 WP-3 release-DAG pruning and before tag creation; a core-only alpha tag fails closed.

NAMED RE-DECIDE CHECKPOINT (adopted, evidence-form): Mike re-decides only on concrete evidence, never on predicted dates or slice counts. (a) If the u53yy.1 day-one feasibility probe FAILS, return to Mike with the failed mechanism plus the smallest honest Option-B contract - that is the reconsideration trigger. (b) If every other tag prerequisite is green (soak passed per the rf2-vxgfnd.99 ruling, Helix removed, W12 done, deiym G1-G4 done) and u53yy.1 is still open, Mike re-decides on that evidence. BASIS: (1) Calendar pressure examined and found empty. The dossier's two-clock analysis showed B/C buy at most 0-2 median days even under its optimistic calendar; the Codex annotation then falsified that calendar's premise - twelve consecutive scheduled nightly failures (Actions runs 29032463675 through 29760811080, Jul 9-20; re-verified: Jul 16-20 all failure) mean zero of the two required greens exist and the one-week no-fallback clock has not started. With the soak gate genuinely unmet, holding the chain costs nothing: u53yy.1 runs while the nightly is repaired and the soak accrues. (2) Permanence: Clojars never yanks; whatever install story ships at 0.0.1.alpha is the substrate's first impression forever. Pre-publication is the free moment to shrink the install contract; post-publication every change is churn or breakage for exactly the earliest adopters the alpha courts. (3) The install tax is the ruled largest product defect (two top-level compiler-internal Shadow entries, no namespace caching ever, exact shadow-cljs 3.4.10 pin in both halves, failure mode surfacing only at app load), corroborated by two independent adversarial reviews (UIx 2026-07-20, Replicant 2026-07-21); publishing it as the front door inverts the alpha's low-friction thesis. (4) Option C additionally violates R-6 (spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1164-1177 - core and UI release together) and is structurally the drift this fail-closed gate exists to prevent (the rf2-pc479y failure mode); the structural hole is confirmed real: implementation/ui/deps.edn deliberately has no :clein, release.yml documents UI as deliberately absent, and the #5867 inventory guard only catches incoherent publication - it cannot require UI to become publishable. (5) The Option-A ruling is Mike-ratified (2026-07-15; the may-not clause 2026-07-20), corroborated since, with no new contrary evidence - only calendar pressure, which per (1) is illusory.

OPINIONS WEIGHED: dossier recommendation (Option A plus checkpoint plus optional strengthener) - adopted except the strengthener. Codex Recommendation (Option A; corrected the soak-clock premise; staged path: bounded S0 probe, sliced solo re-home preserving the warm/cold/watch/module/advanced probe battery, atomic publication PR with an explicit UI-required release assertion, soak as an independent gate not schedule slack; probe-failure as the honest re-decide trigger; decline the strengthener) - adopted, including its checkpoint framing. Option B's honest case (alpha-grade promises are weak; a compiler rewrite can do more harm than a documented caveat) - acknowledged as the fallback contract IF the probe fails, not a reason to pre-empt a day-old Mike-ratified ruling.

title: Preflight WeakRef support before mutating ViewCell root ownership
description:
## Problem

PR #5832 unconditionally constructs `js/WeakRef` for CLJS root membership while only guarding `js/FinalizationRegistry`. A host without `WeakRef` therefore fails with a bare JavaScript `TypeError`. Worse, `attach-root!` records the root on the ViewCell before weak-registry enrollment, so the exception leaves a partially attached cell that names a root but is absent from that root's teardown registry.

This is an under-specified platform boundary, not a request for a broad polyfill. The library must either declare/enforce `WeakRef` as a platform requirement before mutation or provide one explicit, semantically honest fallback.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load the compiled CLJS runtime with `globalThis.WeakRef` and `globalThis.FinalizationRegistry` unavailable (or shadow them in the isolated capability fixture).
2. Create a ViewCell and call `attach-root!`.
3. Construction at `reactive.cljc:2150` attempts `new WeakRef` unconditionally and throws `TypeError: WeakRef is not a constructor`.
4. Inspect the cell: its `:root` was already written by `attach-root!` around 2239, but no registry membership exists.
5. Repeat with `WeakRef` present and `FinalizationRegistry` absent; that supported/degraded combination must continue to work via synchronous compaction.

The current tests cover an absent/delayed finalizer but not absent `WeakRef` or partial attachment.

## Required Correction

Resolve and validate the weak-reference capability before any cell/root mutation. Prefer the simplest explicit contract: if `WeakRef` is a supported-browser minimum, fail at module/root preflight with a typed re-frame.ui incompatibility error and document the requirement; do not fail midway through `attach-root!`. If a fallback is chosen, specify its retention/teardown semantics and ensure it does not silently restore the unbounded strong-registry bug. Keep `FinalizationRegistry` optional, with synchronous compaction authoritative.
acceptance_criteria:
- Capability-matrix fixtures cover WeakRef+FinalizationRegistry present, WeakRef present/finalizer absent, and WeakRef absent.
- An unsupported host receives one deterministic typed framework incompatibility error before any ViewCell/root/registry mutation; no bare constructor TypeError or half-attached cell remains.
- The supported no-finalizer path compacts synchronously and returns registry counts to zero.
- Any chosen fallback is explicitly documented and proves bounded retention; otherwise the browser/platform minimum is documented in the public installation/compatibility contract.
- Root/frame teardown, HMR, and Activity-hidden discovery remain correct on supported hosts.
- Advanced production output does not add polling or per-render capability work.

Probe it once at initialization/root admission before any ViewCell/root/registry mutation; unsupported hosts receive one typed framework incompatibility error with stable recovery guidance and leave ownership registries untouched. FinalizationRegistry remains optional and synchronous compaction remains authoritative when it is absent. Do not add polling, a strong-registry fallback, per-render capability checks, or a second lifetime state machine: there is no named consumer and that would be gold-plating. Implement with the three-arm capability matrix and document the platform minimum.

title: Prune empty root-incarnation entries after weak member collection
description:
## Problem

PR #5832 makes `root-cells` membership weak, but collection-time compaction removes dead member references without removing the now-empty outer root-incarnation entry. `weak-live` in `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc:2168-2185` expunges JVM weak keys / deletes CLJS weak-reference husks but never calls the incarnation-level `drop-root-entry-if-empty!`; `root-cell-count` at about 2260-2267 counts the outer map without first pruning it.

A long-lived app that creates and retires root generations can therefore retain one empty registry entry and weak-set wrapper per incarnation forever. The member cells/values collect, but registry metadata grows monotonically and the claimed bounded/current-membership invariant is false. FinalizationRegistry timing cannot be the correctness mechanism, and JVM has the same outer-entry gap.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create one root incarnation with one attached cell.
2. Drop every strong reference to the cell without explicitly detaching it, force/observe collection, and invoke the available weak scan/count or root teardown path.
3. The cell weak reference clears and the per-incarnation live-member count becomes zero.
4. The global tracked-incarnation count remains one because compaction never removes the outer entry.
5. Repeat across root generations; the empty incarnation count grows.
6. On CLJS, repeat with `FinalizationRegistry` absent or deliberately delayed; opportunistic husk deletion still leaves the entry. On JVM, `WeakHashMap` expunging yields the same result.

The authored fixture keeps a hidden sibling alive and later deterministically detaches it, which exercises last explicit departure but masks the all-members-collected path.

## Required Correction

Make weak compaction incarnation-aware. After every snapshot/expunge operation that can observe an empty weak set—including root teardown, frame teardown, count/inspection, and explicit compaction—remove the outer entry with the existing identity/race guard. Treat FinalizationRegistry as an optimization only. A late finalizer after synchronous removal must be harmless and must not remove a newer incarnation or replacement set.
acceptance_criteria:
- Forced-GC JVM coverage proves an incarnation whose last cell was collected is removed from the outer registry and the global tracked count returns to zero.
- Compiled CLJS coverage with `FinalizationRegistry` unavailable/delayed proves opportunistic compaction removes both dead refs and the empty incarnation entry.
- Explicit teardown of an already member-empty incarnation removes it deterministically.
- A delayed finalizer after synchronous removal is harmless and cannot delete a replacement entry/new incarnation.
- Hidden/connected members remain discoverable, and identity guards preserve concurrent/reentrant additions.
- Repeated root-generation churn has bounded registry metadata; relevant JVM, CLJS, lifecycle, and production-economy gates pass.

title: Finish the tracked per-epoch render-law sweep, including force-tracked ai
description:
## Problem

PR #5790 (`dd83a720849f72ec4510518e70606ca403ca84e0`, squash merge `da15dab4bc7a132143dcdc36ed64a8455b22694c`) closed `rf2-vxgfnd.66` as the tracked-surface sweep that retired the false equation between event/derivation epochs and re-frame.ui notifications/renders. Consequently, active proposal/manual material still teaches the retired per-epoch render law. Current spec, implementation, and Story wording also retain smaller fragments. These hits persist after #5790. ## Steps to Reproduce

3. Read the proposal README and guide README to confirm the material presents itself as an API-design test with normative examples, not merely archival history.

title: Define UI render batches by host checkpoint, not router drain
description:
## Problem

PR #5790 replaces the false “one render per epoch” model with “one render batch at drain quiescence.” The first half is correct—epochs are write/evidence units, not render triggers—but the replacement names a router boundary the implementation does not observe.

The re-frame.ui scheduler has no hook from router drain finalization. Its boundary is a dirty-cell pending window:

- on CLJS, the first mark schedules one host microtask and every mark before that checkpoint folds into the same window;
- on JVM/headless, scheduling is inert and pending cells fold until an explicit test/host flush;
- listener re-entry after a batch has been completed can open another pending window without a new router drain.

Therefore one drain's entire queued write-side cascade always coalesces, but several distinct `dispatch-sync!` drains in the same JavaScript stack—and nested cross-frame drains—also coalesce before the same microtask. Host-yield-separated drains do not. Spec 004/006, Conventions, the glossary, reactive docstrings, and epoch-test banners currently state the stronger false rule that render separation follows each drain.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On PR #5790's exact head `dd83a720849f72ec4510518e70606ca403ca84e0`, run two independent `dispatch-sync!` calls back-to-back without yielding.
2. On CLJS, both drains complete before the scheduled UI microtask; one later notification batch advances the dirty cell once.
3. On JVM, after both drains the cell remains revision 0, notification count 0, dirty with one pending entry; one explicit flush produces revision 1 and one notification.
4. Drive a nested cross-frame synchronous drain and observe the same pending window.
5. In a listener, re-mark after phase-1 completion; a fresh batch is scheduled even though no router drain began.
6. Inspect `reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc`: it calls `mark-dirty!` and `flush-pending!` directly, so it cannot prove a router-drain boundary.

Later `rf2-vxgfnd.12.1` added the open-drain test-flush guard; retain that fix, but it does not couple automatic scheduling to drain finalization.

## Required Correction

Define the production boundary honestly as the pending read/render window ending at the next CLJS host microtask or explicit headless/test flush. State the guaranteed relationship: a synchronous drain cannot be split, while multiple drains before the same host checkpoint may share one read/render batch. This is both simpler and at least as efficient as per-drain flushing.

Reconcile all active contract/docstring/test wording and add real-router fixtures. Coordinate with open `rf2-vxgfnd.12`, which owns the queued-cascade and real-yield mounted gates; do not duplicate its harness. If exact one-batch-per-router-drain separation is instead required, that is a different contract and needs an explicit drain-finalization seam rather than timing inference.
acceptance_criteria:
- Active specs, Conventions, glossary, implementation docstrings, and test banners define one pending read/render window closed by the next CLJS microtask or explicit headless/test flush; none equates every router-drain completion with a batch boundary.
- The contract says one drain's queued writes cannot split, several synchronous/nested drains before one checkpoint may coalesce, and host-yield-separated drains cannot.
- Real-router mounted tests cover a queued child cascade, two sequential no-yield drains, host-yield-separated drains, nested cross-frame drains, listener re-marking after completion, and JVM multiple drains before one explicit flush.
- The sequential and nested cases prove one notification/revision/root commit batch; the host-yield case proves two.
- The existing open-drain `ui.test/flush!` rejection remains green and is not misdescribed as the automatic scheduling boundary.
- The implementation remains one write-side drain-to-quiescence followed by a coalesced read/render opportunity; no per-epoch render trigger, global coordinator, or public API is added.
- Relevant S2 gates, browser tests, JVM UI, node UI, docs, and production-elision checks pass.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option A — the render-batch contract is defined by the host checkpoint: the pending read/render window ends at the next CLJS host microtask or an explicit headless/test flush. Strict one-batch-per-router-drain separation is REJECTED; no drain-finalization seam is to be built.

RATIONALE: Both recorded opinions (decision file + CComposer) recommend A, and the evidence verifies in-repo: the scheduler boundary in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc is the first-dirty-mark microtask CAS (flush-scheduled?); router.cljc's only late-bound flush is the DEBUG-only :live-frame/flush-projection! hook, not a UI-scheduler seam; and no consumer needs per-drain painting (run-to-completion, Spec 002 render boundaries, and Pattern-LongRunningWork all state weaker guarantees that A preserves). A is honest (docs match code), simpler (no new router->scheduler coupling), and strictly more efficient — coalescing N same-stack drains into one batch is a win. B would add coupling to make the framework slower for a guarantee nobody asked for. CORRECTNESS + CLARITY favour truing up the prose; ELEGANCE + GOOD PRACTICE reject machinery for an unrequested contract.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE: Contract wording: "a render batch is the pending read/render window ending at the next CLJS host microtask checkpoint or an explicit headless/test flush." Guarantees to state: (1) a synchronous run-to-completion drain cannot be split across batches; (2) N epochs/events within one drain coalesce to one batch; (3) multiple drains (or listener re-entry) completing before the same host checkpoint may share one batch; (4) drains separated by a host yield render separately. Retire "one batch per router drain" as normative — keep only as the common case when callers yield between drains. Surfaces: spec/004-Views.md, Spec 006 invariant 6, spec/Conventions.md, glossary, reactive.cljc (ns docstring section on drain coalescing, the S2d comment block, and schedule-flush!'s "one microtask per drain" wording — it is armed by the first mark and fires at the checkpoint, folding any number of drains), viewcell.cljs docstring, reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc banners ("separate drain" cases must use a real host yield, not a second same-task flush-pending!). Tests per the acceptance criteria: real-router mounted fixtures — back-to-back dispatch-sync! with no yield -> one notification/revision/commit; host-yield-separated drains -> two; nested cross-frame drains -> one; listener re-mark after completion opens a fresh pending window with no new drain; JVM multiple drains before one explicit flush -> one. Keep the rf2-vxgfnd.12.1 open-drain ui.test/flush! rejection green and do not describe it as the automatic scheduling boundary. Coordinate with open rf2-vxgfnd.12 (owns queued-cascade + real-yield mounted gates) — reuse its harness, do not duplicate G-3/G-13 infrastructure. No new public API, no per-epoch render trigger, no global coordinator. Option B is reserved for a future bead only if a NAMED consumer proves it needs per-drain rendering within one synchronous stack — that would be a new explicit contract with accepted performance cost.

title: Elide provisional-disconnect state and branching from production ViewCells
description:
## Problem

PR #5789 repeatedly claims its provisional-disconnect guard is DEV-only and dead-code-eliminated in advanced production. Only the assignment of `true` and the settle microtask are compile-time guarded.

At exact head `93a903da12a5fe53f08e1d62caeba51df5e22bd6`, and still on current main:

- every ViewCell unconditionally stores `:disconnect-provisional? false` in its production state map;
- every reconnect unconditionally looks up that keyword and branches on it;
- comments claim the field is "false/absent" and the mechanism DCEs, but the field is never absent;
- Closure cannot prove through a mutable atom/map that this keyword read is always false.

The exact-head production-elision jobs were skipped for `implementation/ui/**`, and the advanced G-1 views did not root the reactive ViewCell lifecycle. Green CI therefore did not test the zero-cost claim. This is small per-cell/per-reconnect residue, but it is on the production hot lifecycle of the package whose explicit goal is exceptional production efficiency.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build an advanced `goog.DEBUG=false` entry that actually constructs a ViewCell and exercises connect→disconnect→reconnect.
2. Inspect the rooted reactive lifecycle output/state path.
3. Observe the provisional keyword/state initialization and reconnect lookup/branch remain reachable even though no production path can set the flag true.
4. Compare with the exact-head CI surface classification: production-elision/bundle jobs are skipped, while G-1 does not import this lifecycle.
5. Mutating or renaming debug-only strings does not change this structural residue, so a string-only unrelated elision gate would also false-green it.

## Required Correction

Compile-time gate both halves of the feature. In production, omit the provisional key from new ViewCell state and fold reconnect directly to the ordinary annotation path without a lookup/branch. Keep the entire settle scheduler and evidence-only state behind the same compile-time constant.

Add a discriminating advanced-output fixture that roots the real lifecycle and proves absence of the state member and decision machinery. Wire the relevant production gate for changes to this surface; do not add a runtime feature flag or retain a production stub map entry for convenience.
acceptance_criteria:
- Advanced `goog.DEBUG=false` ViewCells contain no provisional-disconnect state key, lookup, conditional, or settle scheduling machinery.
- Production reconnect follows the ordinary lifecycle path directly and preserves its current Activity behavior.
- Debug builds retain the conservative unsettled reconnect behavior and the StrictMode/Activity evidence fixtures.
- A targeted advanced build requires and executes the real ViewCell connect/disconnect/reconnect path; it is selected by CI for relevant `implementation/ui/**` changes.
- A mutation making either the state field or reconnect lookup unconditional makes the elision gate fail.
- The proof checks compiled reachability/state operations, not only human-readable diagnostic strings.
- G-1/G-13, browser lifecycle, node UI, and JVM UI gates remain green.

title: Stop treating a microtask checkpoint as exact React commit identity
description:
## Problem

PR #5789 tries to distinguish React StrictMode's layout-effect replay from a genuine Activity hide/reveal by marking disconnect provisional until the next host microtask. It then treats any reconnect before that microtask as a same-commit StrictMode replay.

That inference is too strong. A microtask separates JavaScript checkpoints, not React commits. Two real commits can complete synchronously in the same stack:

```javascript
flushSync(() => setMode("hidden"));
flushSync(() => setMode("visible"));
```

React tears down layout effects in the first commit and recreates them in the second before the queued settle microtask runs. On exact head `93a903da12a5fe53f08e1d62caeba51df5e22bd6`, `connect!` sees the still-provisional flag and leaves the real hide interval `:disconnected {:reason :unknown}`. The existing Activity browser fixture inserts a microtask between hide and reveal, so it cannot expose this ambiguity.

The runtime remains ownership-correct; the defect is observability truth. Comments/docstrings currently say only same-commit replay can reconnect before settlement and that a genuine reveal always arrives later. Those claims are false.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Mount a sub-bearing view inside React 19 Activity in visible mode.
2. In one synchronous stack, call `flushSync` once to hide and again to reveal, without awaiting a microtask.
3. Observe two completed commits and layout-effect `cleanup` followed by `setup`.
4. Read the ViewCell intervals after the second commit and after the settle microtask.
5. The interval remains `:unknown`; the runtime has classified the sequence as indistinguishable from replay despite the two real host commits.

A real StrictMode setup→cleanup→setup replay is the control and should also avoid a fabricated Activity proof.

## Required Correction

Treat the provisional flag as what it actually proves: a conservative same-checkpoint/unsettled reconnect heuristic. Remove every claim that it identifies an exact React commit, uniquely identifies StrictMode, or proves that all genuine reveals occur in later tasks. Add the consecutive-`flushSync` Activity case as executable evidence and accept `:unknown` where the host supplies no exact discriminator.

If complete attribution is required later, introduce authoritative host/commit evidence and prove it against both React sequences; do not replace one timing heuristic with another or assume render-capture identity differs on every Activity reveal.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real-browser fixture drives hide and reveal in two consecutive `flushSync` commits without a microtask yield and pins the honest resulting evidence.
- A real React StrictMode replay control remains unannotated; no `:activity-hidden` fact is fabricated.
- Delayed Activity reveal still produces `:activity-hidden {:proof :reconnect}` under the existing settled-evidence contract.
- Source and owning contract prose consistently call pre-microtask reconnect unsettled/same-checkpoint evidence, not exact same-commit or uniquely StrictMode evidence.
- Any future complete-attribution path uses an authoritative host signal and proves consecutive commits, StrictMode replay, delayed reveal, repeated cycles, and root teardown precedence.
- Lease balance, root ownership, and dead/unmounted behavior remain unchanged; browser and lifecycle suites pass.
notes:
AUDIT REOPEN 2026-07-17 (PR #6022): the rf2-vxgfnd.164 honesty contract is still false in advanced production and its StrictMode control is vacuous.

CURRENT PROD CONTRADICTION: reactive.cljc connect! says an unsettled same-checkpoint reconnect (StrictMode replay OR two real consecutive flushSync commits) cannot prove Activity hide and must stay :unknown, but the goog.DEBUG=false branch always annotates :activity-hidden {:proof :reconnect}. tool_evidence_elision_prod_test.cljs explicitly pins that false fact. Production has no StrictMode double-invoke, but it can still have two real commits in one synchronous stack, so closed rf2-vxgfnd.165's direct-production-path premise conflicts with this later honesty ruling. Repair by either retaining enough truthful discrimination in production or eliding/scoping the production interval log; never export a fabricated proof merely to save the provisional branch.

FALSE-GREEN CONTROL: root_incarnation_activity_dom_cljs_test.cljs strictmode-replay-control-stays-unannotated only asserts final connected/no activity-hidden and even says replay "if any". Removing StrictMode leaves it green. Assert positive replay evidence (exact setup/cleanup/setup or an actual unknown disconnect interval) before classification.

Acceptance additions: an advanced-browser consecutive-hide/reveal fixture proves prod and dev make the same honest claim; mutation restoring the direct false annotation fails; the StrictMode control proves a replay actually occurred; preserve ownership and production-economy goals without false evidence.

title: Make destroyed-reason conformance enforce exact channel/reason tuples
description:
## Problem

PR #5831 introduced `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/destroyed_reason_channel_conformance_test.clj` as the drift net for the frozen destroyed-channel/reason matrix. The gate is green but does not enforce the promise it advertises.

At exact head `7bd1ee03df0b951b096f07347bd09bfe80988f98`:

- Lines 192-219 check the Cross-Spec surface primarily by excluding `:parent-unmount-cascade`; they do not assert the documented positive channel/reason tuple.
- Lines 225-273 extract known reason literals but do not prove the channel attached to each actual emit.
- The source scanner silently ignores dynamic/direct emit shapes instead of failing closed.
- Lines 61-80 do not load the conformance fixtures whose reconciliation the test's contract claims to cover; existing destroy/final-state fixtures do not assert the emitted reason.

The result is a false-green gate: a channel move, a changed Cross-Spec pair, or an unparsed new reason can all pass.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the focused test on #5831's exact head, then apply each controlled mutation independently:

1. Change an actual fx emit to use `:rf.machine.lifecycle/destroyed`; the suite remains 9 tests / 143 assertions green.
2. Change Cross-Spec's asserted pair to lifecycle+`:rf.machine/finished` (or change its reason to `:bogus`); the suite remains green.
3. Append a dynamic fx emit such as `{:reason bogus-reason}` to a scanned source form; the relevant source check remains green.
4. Change Spec-Schemas' lifecycle wording to allow `:parent-frame-destroyed` or `:bogus`; the schema-focused checks remain green.

A control mutation replacing the recognized lifecycle reason with literal `:explicit` does fail, showing that only the narrow literal pattern is protected.

## Required Correction

Make the gate compare exact channel/reason tuples across every normative surface and every runtime emit choke point. Structurally enumerate emitter calls and fail on any unparsed or dynamic reason form rather than silently skipping it. Wire executable fixture expectations for explicit, finished, and join-reaped destruction into the reconciliation so fixture drift is real evidence, not prose.
acceptance_criteria:
- The current intended matrix passes as exact tuples, not as independent channel and reason sets.
- Mutating either argument of any lifecycle or fx emit causes the focused gate to fail.
- Mutating the positive Cross-Spec channel/reason pair or adding an extra Spec-Schemas reason causes the gate to fail.
- An unparsed/dynamic reason expression at a destroy emitter is an explicit failure with a useful source location.
- Executable fixtures assert the terminal channel and reason for `:explicit`, `:rf.machine/finished`, and `:rf.machine/join-reaped`; changing any fixture expectation or emit causes the gate to fail.
- The test documents which surfaces are authoritative and avoids regex acceptance that can silently skip new syntax.
- Focused and full machines gates pass on the unmodified matrix.

title: Correct Cross-Spec's implicit view-unmount machine-teardown promise
description:
## Problem

PR #5831 rewrote `spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md:247-249` to say that unmount cleanup dispatches a cancellation event and tears down a view-coupled machine. The runtime does not implement that ownership edge:

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs:372-409` and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1297-1301` emit `:rf.view/unmounted` only; neither dispatches a machine transition nor invokes `:rf.machine/destroy`.
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md:4385-4387` requires named, explicit teardown and lets ports rely on there being no implicit ownership cascade.
- The Cross-Spec scenario still has no executable fixture, so the full machines suite remains green while the normative example promises behavior that is absent.

An application following the example can unmount a route/view and leave the machine snapshot, timers, and owned resources live. This is a contract bug, not a request to add implicit view ownership: the established machine law is explicit teardown.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Mount a view and create a machine that the application considers view-coupled.
2. Unmount the view without dispatching a machine transition or `:rf.machine/destroy`.
3. Observe `:rf.view/unmounted`, but no `:rf.machine/destroyed` or `:rf.machine.lifecycle/destroyed`.
4. Verify that the machine snapshot and its owned timers/resources remain live.
5. Compare this with Cross-Spec-Interactions' statement that the screen cleanup cancels and tears down the machine automatically.

## Required Correction

Rewrite the Cross-Spec example around the existing explicit-ownership contract: view unmount has no machine side effect unless application cleanup names a transition or `:rf.machine/destroy`. When explicit destroy is selected, document the resulting fx-channel terminal as `:rf.machine/destroyed` with `:reason :explicit`; do not describe it as a lifecycle-channel event. Add an executable fixture so the example cannot drift back into an implicit cascade.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cross-Spec-Interactions no longer promises automatic machine teardown from view unmount and agrees with Spec 005's no-implicit-cascade law.
- A mounted integration fixture proves that bare view unmount emits the view lifecycle fact but leaves the machine live.
- A second fixture performs explicit application cleanup and proves exactly one `:rf.machine/destroyed` event with `:reason :explicit`, no lifecycle-channel destroy event, and complete release of the machine's owned timers/resources.
- The fixture is wired into the relevant machines/cross-spec gate and fails if implicit teardown prose or behavior is reintroduced without an explicit contract change.
- Documentation and strict-doc gates pass.
