title: Reconcile machine-destroy consumers with disjoint lifecycle/fx channels
description:
## Problem

PR #5831 established that machine disappearance is split across two disjoint trace families, but the reconciliation stopped before the consumer boundary.

At exact head `7bd1ee03df0b951b096f07347bd09bfe80988f98`:

- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:224,298,316-319` says a lifecycle-only observer—or a consumer of "either" channel—can observe actor disappearance. Normal teardown emits only `:rf.machine/destroyed`; frame-owned teardown emits only `:rf.machine.lifecycle/destroyed`. A complete disappearance observer therefore needs both.
- The same passage tells consumers to disambiguate via `:tags :emitted-from`, but neither emitter supplies that tag.
- `tools/xray/src/.../cancellation_cascade_helpers.cljc:87-129,167-172` validates channel membership and reason membership independently. It accepts impossible cross-products such as lifecycle+`:explicit` and fx+`:parent-frame-destroyed`, and it treats HTTP-only `:actor-destroyed` as a machine-destroy reason.
- `tools/xray/src/.../managed_fx_helpers.cljc:234-245` includes the command `:rf.machine/destroy` but omits the real terminal trace `:rf.machine/destroyed`, so normal machine destruction is ignored.
- Stale symmetric-channel claims remain in `tools/xray/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md:1583,1921` and `019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md:243,260`.

This leaves the normative instrumentation guidance and the shipped Xray projections inconsistent with the channel/reason matrix that #5831 claims to freeze.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On #5831's exact head, call the cancellation-cascade classifier with lifecycle+`:explicit`, fx+`:parent-frame-destroyed`, and fx+`:actor-destroyed`.
2. Observe that all three impossible tuples classify as machine cancellation.
3. Feed the managed-fx projection a real `:rf.machine/destroyed` event carrying `:reason :explicit`.
4. Observe that the projection does not treat it as the normal machine terminal.
5. Read Spec 009's consumer guidance and verify that its "either channel" and `:emitted-from` instructions cannot be implemented from emitted records.

## Required Correction

Define channel-specific allowed tuples rather than independent sets. The lifecycle family admits only `:parent-frame-destroyed`; the fx family admits the actual normal-destroy reasons. Remove the HTTP cancellation reason from the machine vocabulary, consume the real fx terminal, and update Spec 009 plus Xray prose so a complete disappearance consumer subscribes to both channels. Do not invent an `:emitted-from` tag unless the runtime is deliberately changed to emit it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 009 states that complete machine-disappearance observation requires both disjoint channels and makes no claim about a nonexistent `:tags :emitted-from`.
- Xray models allowed channel/reason tuples directly; positive tests cover each emitted family and negative cross-product tests reject lifecycle+`:explicit`, fx+`:parent-frame-destroyed`, and fx+`:actor-destroyed`.
- Xray consumes `:rf.machine/destroyed` as the normal fx terminal and does not confuse the command `:rf.machine/destroy` with the trace event.
- An integration fixture demonstrates Xray observing a real fx-channel `:explicit` destruction and a lifecycle-channel `:parent-frame-destroyed` destruction.
- Xray machine-inspector/cross-cutting prose and source docstrings use the same matrix.
- The relevant Xray and machines gates run (not merely skip) and pass.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6007. All premises re-verified on current main: Xray validated channel+reason independently (accepted lifecycle+:explicit, fx+:parent-frame-destroyed, fx+:actor-destroyed); managed-fx listed the fx-id command :rf.machine/destroy and omitted the real terminal :rf.machine/destroyed; Spec 009 claimed a :tags :emitted-from no emitter supplies and called the registrar axis 'the complete record' contradicting its own matrix; xray M.3 prose named the frame-exit channel for a state-exit cascade. Xray now models the channel/reason matrix directly (emittable-destroy? checks the tuple). Integration fixture drives the REAL machines runtime for both channels. Mutation-verified negatives. Gates: xray 1263/5876, tools 4365/18592, machines 1104/3852, both 009-parsing conformance tests, doc-slug + keyword-drift checks — all green.

title: Keep the Xray heatmap out of the S3 delivery promise
description:
## Problem

PR #5830 (head `6f25c954ac1c8a4b96fc92b5901a35384b06efa3`; merge `b573730a9fc80a9f8578ffa17c73a2276f5817ca`) correctly adds S3 markers to future Guide 07 surfaces, but the marker turns proposals that are explicitly outside S3 into S3 delivery commitments.

`ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/guide/07-performance.md:8,48-49,68-72` now says an Xray heatmap and a causes timeline/timeline cause column land in S3. The owning design disagrees: `04-debugging.md` around §5 says heatmap panels require a later information-architecture review; `guide/06-debugging.md` likewise keeps the overlay behind that review; and `drafts/xray-ui-consumption-ia.md` explicitly caps S3 at enriching existing surfaces, says there is no heatmap and no render-timeline lane, and places cause vectors on existing Views rows/cause chips.

The broad S3 row for `re-frame.ui.tool` and Xray consumption does not authorize every earlier Xray idea. A fully conforming S3 implementation can omit both new panels while Guide 07 now tells users they land in S3. Closed source bead `rf2-vxgfnd.134` cannot be amended; closed `rf2-2fg8h` records the earlier heatmap removal, so this needs a follow-up.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the new Guide 07 stage note and the heatmap/causes passages; record the explicit `lands S3` promise.
2. Read `04-debugging.md`, Guide 06, and `drafts/xray-ui-consumption-ia.md`.
3. Observe the authoritative S3 IA says no heatmap and no render-timeline lane, and maps causes into existing Views rows instead.
4. Run a stage-surface census that rejects `heatmap ... lands S3`; it fails on #5830 despite an otherwise compliant S3 plan.

## Required correction

Keep `effect` and cause labels/chips on the existing Xray Views surfaces marked S3. Mark the heatmap as conditional on a post-S3 information-architecture review. Replace causes-timeline/cause-column wording with the ruled existing Views-row cause-vector surface unless a separate decision later authorizes a new timeline.
acceptance_criteria:
- No Guide 07 sentence says the Xray heatmap lands in S3.
- Heatmap wording matches 04 §5 and Guide 06: conditional on a later information-architecture review.
- S3 cause wording maps exactly to existing Xray Views rows/cause vectors or causation chips and promises no new render-timeline lane.
- The `effect` dependency surface remains explicitly marked S3.

Also sweep the passing "dev heatmap" mention at 02-views.md L100.

title: Prove cold observation probes install zero transient watches
description:
## Problem

PR #5785 claims that 10,000 cold observation probes install zero watches, but `implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_port_cljs_test.cljc:1419-1423` compares only the final watch count with the baseline. That proves zero net retained watches, not the stronger Spec 006 law that a cold probe must not subscribe at all (`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` around § observation-port cold probes; implementation contract near `substrate/observation.cljc:803`).

A regression that performs one `add-watch` followed immediately by `remove-watch` for every probe incurs 10,000 transient subscriptions and can observe concurrent writes, yet leaves the final count at baseline and passes the new assertion. An independent JVM probe demonstrated the current assertion would accept `{watch-installs 10000, watch-count-before 0, watch-count-after 0}`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Instrument or mutate the cold-probe path to add and synchronously remove one host watch per invocation.
2. Run the 10,000-probe fixture.
3. Observe the existing final-cardinality assertion remains green despite 10,000 prohibited registration attempts.
4. On a concurrent host, note that a transient speculative-render watch may also observe a write even though it is not retained.

## Required correction

Keep the final cardinality assertion as a leak check, but also instrument the host `add-watch` / adapter subscription seam and assert zero registration attempts throughout the probe loop. Exercise the law on both JVM and CLJS hosts so the proof covers the concurrent and browser implementations.
acceptance_criteria:
- The 10,000 cold-probe fixtures run on both JVM and CLJS and assert zero watch/subscription registration attempts.
- A mutant that adds and removes one watch per probe fails with exactly 10,000 observed registrations.
- Final watch count still equals the baseline, retaining the independent leak check.
- The fixture does not depend on private collection representation; it instruments the host registration seam.
- Cold `read` results and normal acquired-watch behavior remain unchanged.
- Focused observation-port JVM/CLJS suites and the retained Reagent host path remain green.

title: Prove scheduled disposal-drain latch recovery across callback failure
description:
## Problem

PR #5785 adds a scheduled disposal-drain fixture, but it exercises only nonthrowing callbacks. Existing failure-containment tests call `drain-pending-disposals!` directly (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_port_cljs_test.cljc:904-947`) rather than through the captured next-tick thunk. The two test groups therefore do not compose the scheduler latch with callback failure.

A mutation that moves the `disposal-drain-scheduled?` reset from before the drain to after it can pass both groups independently. Under the real scheduled path, a callback throw before the reset would leave the latch true, suppress every future scheduled drain, and strand later disposal notifications. The production ordering is currently intended to avoid this; the gate does not prove it.

This is distinct from closed `rf2-vxgfnd.28` / `rf2-6ui49w`, which cover direct drain containment and visibility, not scheduled-latch recovery.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Mutate the scheduled thunk so it clears `disposal-drain-scheduled?` only after `drain-pending-disposals!` returns.
2. Run the #5785 scheduled-path test and the existing direct throwing-callback test; both can remain green.
3. Capture and run the real scheduled thunk with a throwing callback followed by a healthy queued owner.
4. Observe the exception path can leave the latch true and prevent later work from scheduling.

## Required correction

Add one composed fixture that captures and executes the actual next-tick thunk with both throwing and healthy work. Assert sibling containment, always-on error visibility, complete queue draining, latch recovery in all exits, and the ability to schedule a fresh later window. The fixture should fail if the latch reset is moved after a potentially throwing drain.
acceptance_criteria:
- A composed scheduled-path fixture includes one throwing callback and at least one healthy sibling.
- The healthy sibling is delivered exactly once and the failure is reported through the always-on error channel exactly once.
- After the thunk returns, the pending queue is empty and `disposal-drain-scheduled?` is false.
- Enqueuing later work captures exactly one new next-tick thunk and drains normally.
- Moving the latch reset after the potentially throwing drain makes the fixture fail.
- Direct-drain containment, coalescing, JVM, and CLJS observation-port suites remain green.

title: Make observation-port scheduled-delivery gates mutation-discriminating
description:
## Problem

PR #5785 (head `4a2e02b4ef139d604ad24c0c197cc364c3aa2d80`; merge `845593f8b757b408f84c2be8c1a957c81b8f149c`) adds observation-port scheduling coverage, but its assertions do not discriminate the scheduling/value laws they claim.

In `implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_port_cljs_test.cljc:618-663`, the next-tick fixture uses one lease, accepts any positive number of captured thunks around line 641, and then executes every thunk. Removing the CAS/coalescing logic at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc:661-665`, or scheduling duplicates unconditionally, still passes. The adjacent `:cause :value` proof uses a cached Reagent reaction, so mutating delivery to dereference again can also pass even though a pull-derived host would turn delivery into extra work and potentially a different value.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Mutate the scheduler to call `next-tick` unconditionally for every independently enqueued disposal/notification.
2. Run the new #5785 fixture; it still passes because it asserts only that the thunk count is positive and drains every captured thunk.
3. Mutate value delivery to re-read the observable instead of using the callback-provided `nu` value.
4. Run the Reagent-backed value fixture; it can remain green because the reaction returns its cached value.

## Required correction

Use multiple independently enqueued leases/nodes in the same scheduling window and assert exactly one captured next-tick thunk. Prove the delivered `:cause :value` path with a pull-derived/instrumented watchable host whose read count and value make any re-read visible. Keep the test at the public observation-port boundary rather than asserting private CAS state.
acceptance_criteria:
- A multi-lease/multi-node fixture asserts exactly one next-tick thunk for one coalescing window.
- Removing the CAS or scheduling one thunk per enqueue makes the fixture fail.
- Executing the single thunk drains all queued work exactly once and permits a later independent window to schedule one new thunk.
- An instrumented pull-derived host proves callback-provided `:cause :value` is delivered without an additional observable read.
- Mutating delivery to re-read the host fails by read count and/or value.
- Existing Reagent watch-path, reentrancy, and JVM/CLJS observation-port suites remain green.

title: Elide the entire ViewCell evidence registry from advanced production
description:
## Problem

PR #5829 claims advanced-production elision of the ViewCell evidence projection, but `re-frame.ui.tool.evidence` allocates `owner*`, `entries*`, and `cell-ordinal*` as unconditional top-level atoms. `force-release!` resets owner/entries outside a compile-time debug branch, and `installed-owner` always dereferences owner state. The advanced production fixture requires the namespace and calls those functions, keeping registry allocation/reset machinery reachable.

The bundle gate checks only two diagnostic strings. Renaming/removing those strings while retaining the atoms and registry operations still passes, so it does not prove the acceptance criterion: no projection/evidence registry or accumulation machinery in production.

## Required correction

Put all projection state allocation and access behind compile-time debug branches. In advanced production, install/uninstall/force-release/installed-owner/projection seams must collapse to constant inert values or be absent so Closure can erase owner/entry/ordinal atoms and registry mutation code. Preserve API shape only where internal/test callers require it; do not keep a live empty registry for convenience.

Strengthen the advanced bundle proof with positive controls that identify actual registry construction/state operations or compiled reachability, not only human-readable strings. The test must fail if any of the three atoms/reset paths are deliberately retained under renamed/minified symbols.

## Proof discipline

Inspect the compiled advanced artefact and use a mutation/positive-control build that forces a registry atom/state operation to remain. Current gate should falsely pass that mutation; the repaired gate must fail. Keep debug functionality fully exercised separately.
acceptance_criteria:
- Advanced production allocates no owner, entries, cell-ordinal, subscriber, or evidence registry state for the projection.
- Production install/uninstall/force-release/installed-owner/projection entry points fold to constant inert behavior or are eliminated without keeping reset/deref machinery reachable.
- The compiled-output gate proves registry construction/state absence with a discriminating positive control, not only two diagnostic string searches.
- Deliberately retaining a renamed/minified registry atom or reset path makes the gate fail.
- Debug builds retain full bounded projection behavior and Xray integration; tool absence and production application bundles remain zero-cost.
- No runtime flag branch, production stub registry, public API expansion, or loss of test cleanup semantics is introduced.
close_reason: Closed

title: Stop the Xray evidence projection retaining ordinarily unmounted ViewCells
description:
## Problem

The evidence projection added by PR #5829 strongly keys its `entries*` registry by ViewCell and prunes only cells whose lifecycle is `:dead`. An ordinary React reconciliation unmount of a conditional/keyed child calls `disconnect!`, leaving the cell `:disconnected` so Activity hide/reveal can reconnect it. If the whole root/frame is not explicitly torn down, the projection row remains forever and its strong key prevents the cell from being garbage-collected.

Under a long-lived root, repeated mount -> invalidate -> conditionally remove cycles monotonically grow evidence entries and retain ViewCells/values even after React has discarded the fiber. #5829 tests only explicit cell teardown or whole-root teardown. This is related to open `rf2-mc62sp`, which covers the separate production `root-cells` strong registry; fixing that registry alone does not remove `tool.evidence/entries*` as a second strong owner.

## Required correction

Make the debug evidence registry non-owning for disconnected cells while preserving Activity reconnect semantics. Recommended shape: weak ViewCell keys/references with deterministic dead pruning plus collected/disappeared compaction; a genuinely hidden Activity fiber remains strongly owned by React and therefore reconnectable, while an ordinarily unmounted fiber becomes collectible. If an explicit unmount-vs-hide signal is introduced instead, it must be exact and shared rather than guessed from `:disconnected` timing.

Coordinate with `rf2-mc62sp` so both registries use one small weak-cell/compaction policy where appropriate, but keep their acceptance evidence distinct. Tool close/uninstall must still clear immediately without waiting for GC.

## Proof discipline

Add a real browser churn fixture under one live root: mount evidence-producing keyed/conditional child, invalidate, remove, force/observe collection/compaction through the supported deterministic seam, repeat many times, and prove row/cell counts return to baseline. Activity hide/reveal must retain and reconnect the same row; root/frame teardown remains immediate. A strong-key mutation must grow monotonically.
acceptance_criteria:
- Ordinary conditional/keyed child unmount under a still-live root does not leave a permanent evidence row or strong ViewCell reference.
- Repeated mount/invalidate/remove churn is bounded and returns projection row/cell counts to baseline through a deterministic weak-reference/compaction proof.
- Activity hide/reveal preserves the reconnectable cell/evidence according to the lifecycle contract and does not confuse hide with final unmount.
- Explicit cell/root/frame teardown and tool uninstall clear matching rows immediately; abandoned render candidates publish nothing.
- The evidence registry remains non-owning after disconnection and composes with `rf2-mc62sp` without duplicating incompatible weak-cell mechanisms.
- A mutation restoring strong ViewCell keys makes the churn fixture fail; browser/Activity/HMR/tool lifecycle suites stay green.
- No polling scan on render, production registry, or UIx/Helix/Reagent compatibility machinery is introduced.
close_reason: Closed

title: Linearize custom-element reload commit with reentrant registration
description:
## Problem

The custom-element reload cycle spans multiple atoms and check-then-swap operations. Registration checks whether a cycle exists and then writes to staging/live state; commit snapshots staged rows, rebuilds/publishes the aggregate, and only afterward removes the cycle. A reentrant or concurrent registration can land after the snapshot but before `dissoc` and be silently dropped.

Deterministic CLJS counterexample: install a watch on the public custom-element aggregate that calls `register-custom-element!` during `rebuild-live!`. The reload cycle is still open, so the registration enters staging after commit captured its snapshot. Commit then removes the entire cycle; the declaration never becomes live. On the JVM, barriers between contains-check and swap can similarly recreate an orphan cycle or write across a newly opened cycle.

This violates the advertised transactional replacement/one aggregate publication law and can lose a valid HMR declaration.

## Required correction

Make cycle extraction/closure, staged-row ownership, ledger transition, and aggregate publication a linearizable state transition. The simplest shape is one authoritative state value containing live ledger, optional cycle/staging, and aggregate/version, updated atomically; alternatively close-and-take the exact cycle before publication with an explicit rule that registrations arriving during/after close belong to a new/live generation and cannot be deleted by the old commit.

Consumer-visible aggregate publication should remain one coherent change per successful cycle. Reentrant callbacks must not execute inside an unsafe half-committed state. Preserve failed-cycle last-known-good semantics and exact build/source ownership.

Do not solve this with sleeps, a process-global lock around user callbacks, or retry loops without an ownership generation.

## Proof discipline

Use a watch-triggered reentrant registration and barrier-controlled register-vs-notify/commit interleavings on applicable hosts. Compare every result to a legal serial execution; mutate away generation/state atomicity to expose loss/orphan cycles.
acceptance_criteria:
- A registration triggered reentrantly by aggregate publication survives exactly once and is assigned to a documented live/new cycle.
- Barrier-controlled register-vs-notify, register-vs-commit, and overlapping-cycle interleavings equal a legal serial execution on JVM/CLJS as applicable.
- No committed registration is lost, applied twice, written into a closed cycle, or left in an orphan staging entry.
- Failed cycles retain the last-known-good ledger/aggregate; successful cycles publish one coherent consumer-visible aggregate transition.
- Exact build/source ownership and later deletion/zero-declaration behavior remain correct.
- Tests fail under the current snapshot-then-dissoc implementation and under mutations that remove generation/atomic ownership.
- No sleep-based test, broad user-callback lock, unbounded retry, public API, or per-render cost is added.

title: Give conflicting custom-element declarations one deterministic law
description:
## Problem

The custom-element registry accepts conflicting declarations for the same tag from multiple sources and currently has two different winner laws. Direct registration publishes the last evaluated call immediately. Reload commit rebuilds the aggregate from ledger rows in sorted owner order. An unrelated reload can therefore flip the effective property manifest without either conflicting declaration changing.

Deterministic current sequence:

```clojure
(register-custom-element! :x-el {:properties #{:z}} 'z.ns)
(register-custom-element! :x-el {:properties #{:a}} 'a.ns)
;; direct effective properties => #{:a}

(notify-reload!)
(note-reloaded-sources! ['unrelated.ns])
(commit-reload!)
;; sorted rebuild effective properties => #{:z}
```

This makes compiler/runtime property classification dependent on evaluation and unrelated reload order. It also obscures which source owns a contradiction.

## Required correction

Define one closed, deterministic cross-source declaration law used by initial evaluation, compiler manifest aggregation, staged reload, and aggregate rebuild. Recommended pre-alpha shape: rf=-equal duplicate declarations may co-exist; conflicting declarations fail atomically with both source/build anchors and leave the last-known-good aggregate unchanged. If a merge/winner law is chosen instead, it must be deterministic and semantically justified for every field—not last-call or incidental sort order.

Conflicts discovered during a reload must not partially publish or evict the previous valid manifest. The compiler must apply the same law before lowering consumers. Do not add silent precedence configuration or per-render conflict resolution.

## Proof discipline

Permute source names, evaluation orders, build identities, clean builds, and unrelated reloads. Every permutation must yield the same valid manifest or the same anchored conflict. The current unrelated-reload flip must fail before the fix.
acceptance_criteria:
- Equal duplicate declarations are handled by one documented deterministic rule.
- Conflicting declarations either fail atomically with both source/build anchors (recommended) or follow one explicitly ratified deterministic merge law across all fields.
- Direct initial registration, compiler manifest aggregation, staged reload, and aggregate rebuild use the same rule.
- An unrelated reload cannot change the effective manifest for an untouched tag.
- A conflicting reload preserves the last-known-good manifest and does not partially publish ledger/aggregate state.
- All source/evaluation/build/reload-order permutations produce identical output or identical conflict evidence.
- No silent last-writer/sort-order precedence, per-render lookup, public configuration surface, or compatibility fallback is introduced.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option A — fail-atomically on conflict. For a given [build-id tag], the effective declaration is the unique value contributed by live sources iff every cross-source pair is rf=-equal; any non-rf=-equal same-tag declaration from a different source fails atomically with BOTH [build-id ns-sym] anchors (plus :file/:line on compiler paths), leaving the last-known-good aggregate unchanged. One law across all four paths: initial eval, compiler manifest aggregation, staged reload, aggregate rebuild. Option B (merge/winner) is rejected; no silent precedence, no configuration knob, no per-render resolution.

RATIONALE: Both the bead recommendation and the independent CComposer review converge on A, and code inspection confirms the premises: register-custom-element! (rules.cljc ~813) is last-call-wins write-through, rebuild-live! (~794) is a sorted-owner merge, and the compiler aggregate (build.cljc ~324) merges with no conflict check — three silent precedence paths, not two. A is the only total law that removes order dependence (CORRECTNESS), surfaces the contradiction to its owning sources instead of masking an ownership mistake (CLARITY), reuses existing infrastructure — contribute-checked!, the staged/commit last-known-good boundary, the rf= duplicate posture, the :rf.error/frame-payload-conflict error shape — rather than inventing per-field merge semantics (ELEGANCE), and matches the pre-alpha fail-closed posture (GOOD PRACTICE). No corpus case shows two sources legitimately contributing different property sets to one tag; property-set union would silently change SSR/hydration classification.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
- rf=-equal duplicates coexist (idempotent); same-source re-declaration replaces per [build-id ns-sym] ledger row and is never a conflict (a source never conflicts with itself).

title: Carry real build and removed-source identity through the custom-element reload ledger
description:
## Problem

The shipped custom-element reload producer from PR #5783 is neither build-aware nor deletion-complete, and its claimed end-to-end test manually drives the seams instead of exercising Shadow reload.

All real emitted registrations and reload lifecycle/reset callbacks use `::default`; only a test-only four-argument seam manufactures a second `:lib` owner. Two logical Shadow builds sharing one JS realm and the same namespace symbol therefore collapse into one ledger row. Reloading one build can evict or replace the other's contributions.

`shadow.cljs.devtools.client.env/before-load-src` runs only for sources present in the new reload set. A namespace deleted from the build graph or renamed to a different namespace never calls the reset callback under its old identity. Reloading a dependent reports the dependent namespace, not the removed namespace. The stale row and tag properties survive until page reload.

The current unit test imitates `before-load-src` locally and directly calls `notify-reload!`, reset, and `commit-reload!`; it cannot prove Shadow hook discovery/order, actual build identity, deletion deltas, failed code evaluation, or production elision. Removing either lifecycle annotation would leave it green.

## Required correction

Feed one stable actual build identity through emitted registrations and that build's reload lifecycle/reset callbacks. Do not use the changing content/build digest as the owner token. Extend the successful build/reload producer with removed-namespace identities for the exact build, and commit those removals only after the new code load succeeds. A failed build/evaluation retains last-known-good ledger state.

Use the existing runtime cycle rather than a second ledger. Same-namespace file moves must not look like namespace removal; namespace rename/delete must evict the old identity. If the supported contract is strictly one build per JS realm, make that explicit everywhere and remove the synthetic multi-build claim—but the recommendation is real build isolation because the closed bead requires it.

Add a focused real Shadow watch fixture that edits copied sources, rather than invoking internal seams. Cover one-to-zero declaration edit, namespace deletion/rename, same-namespace file move, two co-loaded builds with equal ns symbols, code-load failure, and successful retry. Add dev-positive/advanced-negative producer sentinels.

## Proof discipline

Before the fix, deleting/renaming the sole declaration leaves `custom-element-properties` stale; two real builds collide at `[::default ns]`; removing a lifecycle annotation leaves unit tests green. The real watch fixture must expose each gap.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every actual emitted registration, reset callback, before/after hook, staged row, and commit uses the same stable real build identity; no real Shadow dev producer relies on `::default`.
- Two co-loaded real builds with equal namespace symbols retain independent declarations when either build reloads or zero-declares.
- Namespace delete/rename supplies the removed old identity to the exact build's reload cycle and evicts it only after successful code load.
- A same-namespace file move preserves the owner; a dependent reload is never mistaken for removed-namespace evidence.
- Failed build/code evaluation preserves last-known-good rows; a successful retry converges exactly with a clean reload.
- A real Shadow watch/file-save fixture proves hook discovery and order: before -> source reset/evaluation -> after, without direct seam calls.
- Removing before/after annotations or the removed-source/build-id producer makes the fixture fail while existing unit coverage remains useful.
- Advanced production contains no reload producer, `SHADOW_NS_RESET`, ledger, or debug manifest residue; production lookup stays direct.
- No second ledger, content-digest owner token, public API, or per-render cost is introduced.

title: Make custom-element declarations deterministic compiler inputs
description:
## Problem

PR #5783 (head f68ba62b7aae69b315253fd1ea58e06ca768f2fd; merge db31f0288d223708d255cfe8b272a48f7c7f9c1d) wires runtime reload evidence for custom-element declarations, but compile-time property lowering still depends on declaration evaluation order.

A view compiled before `(ui/custom-element :x-card {:properties #{:model}})` sees no declaration and emits `:model` as an HTML attribute. The same forms in the opposite order emit a JS property. Cross-namespace declarations are worse: changing only the declaration namespace updates the runtime ledger but need not recompile dependent views, so already-baked literal property lowering remains stale. The current build digest/fingerprint projection includes view triples but not the effective custom-element declaration input that influenced their lowering.

Deterministic clean-build example:

```clojure
(ui/defview card [] [:x-card {:model model}])
(ui/custom-element :x-card {:properties #{:model}})
```

Reversing the two forms changes emitted behavior. Parallel source ordering can do the same. A declaration-only warm HMR edit may leave consumers unlike a clean build.

This violates deterministic compilation and the clean-build equals warm-build HMR law. Silently imposing declaration-before-use would be brittle and inconsistent with cross-namespace builds.

## Required correction

Make the effective custom-element manifest a deterministic compiler input available before view/template analysis, independent of source evaluation order. Track declaration-to-consumer dependencies so a declaration change invalidates/recompiles every affected literal consumer. Include the relevant effective declaration dependency in template/build freshness without turning the runtime reload ledger into a template interpreter.

Choose one authoritative manifest projection shared by literal properties and dynamic `ui/spread`; both must classify a given tag/property identically. Conflicting declarations are handled by their own closed conflict-law follow-up, not by whichever source compiles first.

Do not add runtime fallback classification on every property write, declaration-before-use ceremony, or a public API change.

## Proof discipline

Compile declaration-before-view and declaration-after-view clean builds, multiple source-order permutations, and a declaration-only warm reload. Compare emitted forms/fingerprints/digests and final DOM property behavior with a clean build. Mutating away the manifest dependency must leave the warm result stale and fail.
acceptance_criteria:
- Declaration-before-view and declaration-after-view clean builds emit identical custom-element property classification.
- Parallel/two-source compile-order permutations are deterministic.
- A declaration-only HMR change invalidates and recompiles every affected literal consumer; warm output/fingerprint/final behavior equals a clean build.
- The relevant effective declaration dependency participates in freshness/build identity without making unrelated declarations invalidate every view.
- Literal props and dynamic `ui/spread` use the same authoritative property manifest.
- Conflicts follow the separately defined deterministic conflict law rather than evaluation order.
- No per-render registry lookup, declaration-before-use rule, runtime template interpreter, or frozen/public API change is introduced.
- Compiler golden, clean-vs-warm HMR, and mounted custom-element fixtures fail under an order-dependent mutation and gate S4 conformance.

title: Fan observation callback failures to Xray and resolve subscription source coordinates
description:
## Problem

The new `:rf.error/observation-on-change-failed` emission added by PR #5782 calls `error-emit/dispatch-on-error!` directly. It reaches the always-on production axis but never the development diagnostic trace. Xray installs a trace-tooling listener, not an always-on error listener, so the failure is invisible in the primary debugging surface. During HMR the registrar swallows the later rethrow, leaving no alternate diagnostic.

A real HMR/disposed callback failure currently produces one always-on record and zero trace events. Existing tests observe only the error listener or drive the category synthetically, so they do not cover the actual two-channel requirement.

The same record mis-resolves source coordinates. It stores the entry subscription id in `:event-id`, but `error_emit.cljc` does not classify this category among subscription-owned errors. Source lookup therefore consults `[:event id]`. With an event and sub sharing a keyword it attributes the error to the event registration; without a colliding event, it omits the available macro-registered sub coordinate.

## Required correction

When the observation drain owns the first emission, use the shared two-channel error fan-out with category-specific trace tags so debug/Xray sees the same logical failure and the production always-on record remains. Coordinate this with the exact-once provenance repair so an already-emitted typed error is not fanned again on either channel.

Classify `:rf.error/observation-on-change-failed` as subscription-attributed for source-coordinate resolution, using the former owner's entry-sub id. Macro registrations should resolve their exact sub coordinate; programmatic registrations may continue to omit it. If the field is renamed from `:event-id`, update the closed schema and all consumers together rather than leaving a misleading realm name.

In advanced production, diagnostic trace machinery remains elided while the always-on record survives.

## Proof discipline

Use actual HMR and disposed notification paths with both trace and always-on listeners. Include an event/sub id collision and a macro-registered sub with no event. A pre-fix trace count of zero and missing/wrong coordinate must turn green. Do not satisfy the proof by calling `dispatch-on-error!` directly in a synthetic conformance table.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real untyped HMR/disposed callback failure produces exactly one always-on record and exactly one debug diagnostic-trace event for the same logical category.
- Xray's existing trace collector can observe the failure without registering a new always-on listener.
- Macro-registered subscriptions resolve the exact `[:sub id]` source coordinate; same-id event registrations cannot steal attribution.
- Programmatic sub registrations continue to omit source coordinates normally rather than fabricating one.
- Already-emitted typed failures do not gain a second trace or always-on record; exact-once provenance composes with the two-channel fan-out.
- Advanced production retains one always-on record while diagnostic trace code/data is elided.
- CLJ/CLJS fixtures exercise the actual HMR and disposed emit sites and fail before the fix with trace count zero and wrong/missing coordinate.

title: Prevent double emission and category spoofing in observation on-change failure drains
description:
## Problem

PR #5782 (head fdc184c9a194338877ce889a10a7c2e2f7ea46b5; merge dd2a57fcf3d510db2dc8fbb2e8297e5a595454f7) makes swallowed observation `on-change` failures visible, but `report-disposal-notify-escape!` blindly re-dispatches every throwable carrying a truthy `:rf.error/id`. It cannot distinguish a canonical typed error already emitted at its source from an unfanned typed error such as `:rf.error/reentrant-graph-op`, and it treats arbitrary application ids as catalogued.

A callback can call an observation operation that emits before throwing. Deterministic example: acquire/release one lease, acquire a live lease whose `on-change` calls `obs/read` on the released lease, then trigger HMR or disposed-drain notification. `obs/read` first emits `:rf.error/read-after-release`; the drain catches the same throwable and emits it again. Current result is two always-on records for one runtime error, with the second record able to replace the source's correct frame/query attribution with the notifying owner's context.

An application `(ex-info "x" {:rf.error/id :app/not-catalogued})` is also passed through as though it were a canonical framework category instead of receiving the stable `:rf.error/observation-on-change-failed` wrapper.

This violates #5782/rf2-6ui49w's exact-one-record and typed-not-double-reported criteria and Spec 009's one-runtime-error law.

## Required correction

Establish explicit internal first-emission provenance or an equivalent single-emission choke point. The disposal/HMR drain must:

- preserve and not re-fan a canonical typed error already emitted by its source;
- fan an unfanned canonical typed error exactly once under its original id;
- wrap untyped, malformed, or non-catalogued `:rf.error/id` throwables exactly once as `:rf.error/observation-on-change-failed`;
- continue the complete sibling drain, then surface the original first throwable with identity/cause intact.

Do not infer catalogue membership or emission history from truthiness of `:rf.error/id`. Do not suppress the source record or introduce a global seen-error registry.

## Proof discipline

Exercise actual `:hmr` and `:disposed` callback delivery on CLJ and CLJS. The released-lease read must show two records before the fix. Include already-fanned typed, unfanned canonical typed, untyped, malformed-id, noncatalogued-id, multiple throwing owners, and sibling-success cases. Mutation removing provenance must fail.
acceptance_criteria:
- An already-emitted typed failure such as `:rf.error/read-after-release` or `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` produces exactly one record with its original correct attribution at both HMR and disposed boundaries.
- An unfanned canonical typed failure such as the existing reentrant-graph case remains visible exactly once under its original id.
- Untyped, missing-id, malformed-id, and non-catalogued application-id throwables each produce exactly one `:rf.error/observation-on-change-failed` wrapper.
- All sibling owners/listeners are notified despite throws; the drain rethrows/surfaces the original first escape after completion without losing identity or cause.
- Exact-once behavior holds on CLJ, CLJS, debug, and advanced production always-on paths.
- Pre-fix composed read-after-release fixtures observe two records; removing the provenance/choke-point repair makes them fail.
- No global error-dedup registry, swallowed error, category spoofing, or public API change is introduced.

title: Make tracked spawn exit prune dead slots without double-destroying actors
description:
## Problem

The destroy paths touched by PR #5779 still permit one declaratively owned child actor to be destroyed twice. A direct keyword-form imperative destroy stops the actor but leaves the parent's tracked `:spawn` slot naming that now-dead actor. When the parent later exits the spawn state, the tracked destroy path treats slot presence as sufficient liveness, reruns teardown, and emits a second `:rf.machine/destroyed` trace.

Deterministic sequence:

- After direct destroy: slot still names `:idem/child#1`, actor is no longer live, destroyed reasons are `[:explicit]`.
- After parent declarative exit: slot is cleared, actor remains dead, destroyed reasons become `[:explicit :explicit]`.

This violates Spec 005's silent-idempotent destroy law and risks duplicate child exit cascades, resource releases, timers, and terminal/diagnostic evidence. Existing tests cover keyword followed by keyword and join cancellation followed by spawn-all exit, but not imperative keyword destroy followed by tracked single-spawn exit.

## Required correction

Separate stale ownership-slot cleanup from actor lifecycle teardown. When a tracked slot names an actor that is already dead for that exact incarnation, remove the stale slot and parent mirror only. Do not rerun exit handlers, child cascades, timer/resource cleanup, terminal replies, or destroyed traces. If the slot names a replacement/live actor, retain the normal exact-incarnation destroy path.

Prefer centralizing the exact actor-live/incarnation predicate used by both imperative and tracked forms rather than adding a special case keyed only to this test. Do not keep dead actors artificially live merely to make the later tracked cleanup run.

## Proof discipline

Add CLJ/CLJS fixtures that instrument lifecycle traces and side effects, not only final registry state. Include direct destroy -> parent exit, repeated parent exit, destroy -> same-id replacement -> old parent cleanup, and ordinary live tracked exit. Mutating the tracked branch back to slot-presence liveness must produce two traces/effects.
acceptance_criteria:
- Imperative destroy followed by declarative parent exit produces exactly one actor stopped transition and one `:rf.machine/destroyed` trace.
- Child exit cascades, lease/resource releases, timers, terminal replies, and other teardown effects each occur at most once for the exact actor incarnation.
- The later tracked exit removes the stale spawn slot and parent mirror without invoking lifecycle teardown for an already-dead actor.
- Repeated exit remains silent-idempotent.
- An old stale slot cannot prune or destroy a same-id replacement/new incarnation; exact incarnation identity is respected.
- Ordinary tracked exit of a still-live child retains current teardown behavior.
- CLJ/CLJS fail-before mutation proves slot-presence alone would double-destroy; focused machine lifecycle/idempotence suites pass.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5839 (join/spawn exact-authority lane; fix committed + red-fixture + mutation-proven; gates green locally: machines JVM 1017/3429, test:cljs 9256/43792, fast-pr spine PASS). Left open for the mayor.

title: Publish one terminal reply for every non-decisive spawn-all child
description:
## Problem

PR #5779 correctly reaps completed spawn-all children without contradictory cancellation, but the join machinery emits terminal work-reply facts only through the final resolution trace. In an `:all` join, a child that completes before the decisive child is folded into `:done` while the join remains unresolved; it never receives a canonical `:completed` reply. When the decisive child later resolves the join, only that child's resolution trace carries a terminal reply, and the earlier child is reaped without cancellation. Its work attempt therefore ends with no terminal status at all.

A deterministic two-child `:all` run currently yields first child A statuses `[]` and decisive child B statuses `[:completed]`. Existing tests assert only that A is not cancelled, masking the missing positive terminal. Failed non-decisive folds have the analogous missing `:failed` fact.

This contradicts the closed one-terminal-per-work-attempt contract and strands work-ledger/Xray state even though actor teardown is otherwise correct.

## Required correction

Emit the canonical completion or failure reply exactly once when each first valid child terminal is accepted/folded into join state. The decisive child may continue to derive its reply from the resolution trace only if the implementation proves it is not also emitted at fold time; choose one authority per child. Repeated pre-resolution signals must not duplicate a terminal. Post-resolution arrivals remain stale. Survivors cancelled by `:any`/failure resolution still close exactly once as cancelled.

Keep lifecycle reaping separate from work terminal publication. Do not synthesize cancellation for completed/failed children and do not wait until actor destruction to guess their work outcome.

## Proof discipline

Add CLJ and CLJS fixtures for two-or-more child `:all` success, non-decisive failure, decisive success/failure, duplicate signals, post-resolution stale arrivals, and survivor cancellation. The original two-child case must fail before the fix with A's empty status vector.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every first accepted completed child in an `:all` join receives exactly one canonical `:completed` work terminal, including non-decisive children.
- Every first accepted failed child receives exactly one canonical `:failed` terminal under the applicable join policy.
- The decisive child is not double-published between fold and resolution authorities.
- Duplicate pre-resolution completion/failure signals do not duplicate terminal facts; post-resolution arrivals remain `:stale`.
- Surviving in-progress children closed by join resolution still receive exactly one `:cancelled`; completed/failed reaps never receive cancellation.
- Work ledger/Xray projections close every attempt consistently, and actor teardown/reap reasons remain unchanged.
- CLJ/CLJS counterfixtures fail on the current empty-terminal behavior and all focused machine/reply-envelope suites pass after correction.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5839 (join/spawn exact-authority lane; fix committed + red-fixture + mutation-proven; gates green locally: machines JVM 1017/3429, test:cljs 9256/43792, fast-pr spine PASS). Left open for the mayor.

title: Finish ui.test/render exact-one-view wording in Spec 008 and retained draft
description:
## Problem

PR #5827 (head aedc5230a240a0a3c3e9be773452ac79b0f0eb08; cumulative main commits 00730d505c, 7393ff6efb, 8abeb322a5, and 83f8695c45) correctly adds the exact-one-mounted-view law to Guide 09 and Spec 004C. Two active contract mirrors still state the old, observably false shorthand:

- `spec/008-Testing.md` around lines 626-629 says Tier-1 `ui.test/render` accepts a literal root form “the same grammar mount takes,” without a cardinality exception.
- `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/drafts/root-identity-and-mount.md` §9 around lines 360-367 repeats that unqualified claim even though the retained draft was edited elsewhere by the same PR.

A test-section comment in `implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/test_render_jvm_test.clj` also retains the shorthand and can seed the drift again.

The shipped contract is narrower. `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/test.cljc` rejects a Tier-1 literal root unless it contains exactly one mounted internal view, raising `:rf.ui.compile/bad-test-root`. Mount's root resolver accepts a multi-view top region when the caller supplies an authored `:root-id`. Spec 004C and Guide 09 now state this correctly.

## Deterministic counterexample

Define known views `a` and `b`.

- Macroexpanding `(ui.test/render [:<> [a] [b]] {})` fails with `:rf.ui.compile/bad-test-root` and two view ids.

title: Prove act discipline across a post-mount compiled-sub rerender
description:
## Problem

PR #5780 closed rf2-vxgfnd.89 by wrapping the frame-scope DOM fixture's mount, render, and teardown operations in the canonical React `act` pattern. The closed bead explicitly required `mount/render/dispatch-driven updates/unmount` inside the act boundary, but the landed fixture never dispatches after a live compiled subscription exists.

`frame_scope_resolve_dom_cljs_test.cljs` seeds `n=42` before mounting the provider case, and the frame-root case seeds through `:initial-events` during mount. These prove mount-time ambient frame resolution, not the important post-mount path: framework dispatch -> queued write drain -> observation callback -> microtask reactive flush -> useSyncExternalStore listener -> React rerender. That path has its own act boundary and scheduling behavior.

This remains actionable on current main. `reactive.cljc` schedules invalidation via a microtask. A post-mount dispatch/flush performed outside `act` can emit React's `not wrapped in act(...)` warning while the browser runner still exits green: `implementation/scripts/run-browser-tests.cjs` records console output for summaries/diagnostics but does not fail merely because a warning appeared. Thus the exact obligation can remain false-green even though #5780's browser CI ran.

## Deterministic reproduction

After the provider fixture renders `n=42`, dispatch `n=43` against the mounted frame and settle the pending framework/reactive work without an act boundary. React can warn that the Root update was not wrapped in act; the current fixture has no assertion for the new DOM value and the runner does not make that warning fatal.

## Required correction

Extend the existing focused fixture with one genuine post-mount compiled-`sub` update. Wrap the dispatch plus explicit pending-work settlement in the canonical `act!`, then assert the DOM renders `n=43`. Add a bounded warning capture/assertion for this operation or focused namespace that forwards diagnostics normally and fails specifically on an act warning. Do not globally suppress or globally promote unrelated console warnings.

## Proof discipline

Demonstrate the fixture red by removing the new update's `act!` boundary: it must fail because of the warning, not merely print it. Keep the fixture on native re-frame.ui/plain-atom and preserve total teardown.
acceptance_criteria:
- The frame-provider/root DOM fixture performs a real dispatch after the compiled subscription is mounted and asserts the changed value after observation/microtask/React settlement.
- Initial mount, the post-mount subscription-driven rerender, and teardown all execute within the canonical React act discipline.
- The assertion depends on the compiled ambient `sub` path, not prop injection, direct ViewCell calls, or a pre-mount seed.
- Removing the update's act boundary makes the focused fixture fail deterministically on React's warning.
- Warning handling is bounded to the focused operation/namespace and still forwards diagnostics; there is no global console suppression or broad unrelated-warning policy change.
- Root/ViewCell/frame/observation ownership returns to baseline; no UIx/Helix/Reagent dependency or runtime/API change is introduced.

title: correctness(S2-audit): root-cells strongly retains every ordinarily-unmounted ViewCell for the root's lifetime
description:
## What / where

implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc:809 (root-cells defonce), :1384 (attach-root!), :1402 (detach-root! — the ONLY pruning path, called solely from teardown! at :1568), :1507 (disconnect! — deliberately never detaches); implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/viewcell.cljs:158-163 (lifecycle layout effect: unconditional attach-root! on mount, cleanup = disconnect! only). Production path — not debug-gated.

## Invariant violated

03 §4: ':disconnected … if React does not reconnect the cell, the cell is GARBAGE'; and rf2-vxgfnd.85 AC5 as stated in the root-cells docstring ('membership is bounded to CURRENTLY-retained cells'). A ViewCell leaves root-cells only via teardown!, which fires only on frame destroy or root teardown. An ORDINARY React reconciliation unmount (conditional subtree, route change, keyed-list eviction) runs only the effect cleanup -> disconnect!, which by design does not detach (hide vs unmount indistinguishable). React drops the fiber, nothing else references the cell — but root-cells holds it STRONGLY until the whole root unmounts or its frame is destroyed. Each retained cell pins its :committed records including last sub VALUES (release-committed! keeps query/target/value with :lease nil) and its :intervals log.

## Failure scenario

Production SPA, one session-lived ui/mount root; a sub-bearing row view toggled/re-keyed N times (pagination, route flip-flop). Each unmount leaves one :disconnected ViewCell — with its last-rendered sub values — pinned in root-cells. Memory grows monotonically with UI churn, unbounded; teardown-root!/teardown-frame! hidden scans become O(all views ever unmounted); each leaked cell remains reconnectable in principle.

NOT a duplicate of rf2-vxgfnd.120 (that is attach-root! re-adding an already-:dead cell after commit rejection on the lease branch); this is the never-proven-dead ordinary-unmount population.

## Fix sketch

Make root-cells membership WEAK: CLJS — per-incarnation set of js/WeakRef (compacted on iteration and/or FinalizationRegistry); JVM — java.util.WeakHashMap-backed keyset. Correctness preserved: a genuinely HIDDEN cell is strongly reachable from React's retained fiber (useRef) so the weak entry lives exactly as long as Activity retention; a reconciliation-unmounted cell becomes unreachable, its leases were already released at disconnect!, it can never reconnect, and the teardown scans lose nothing. detach-root! on teardown! stays as the deterministic fast path.

## Done means

Red fixture first: repeated mount/unmount of a keyed sub-bearing subtree under a live root currently grows root-cell-count by 1 per cycle; after the fix it returns to baseline (allowing a forced GC on JVM / FinalizationRegistry tick on CLJS). Activity hide/reveal reap behaviour (rf2-vxgfnd.85 fixtures) stays green; teardown-root! + teardown-frame! hidden-reap fixtures stay green.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5832 (worker/reactive-correctness-cluster; four-bead reactive-core correctness cluster). Re-verified against post-#5818/#5828/#5829 main — finding still reproduced; fixed with red-proofed fixtures. Gates: ui JVM 438/5495, test:ui 445/2249, browser 342/1848, fast-pr spine PASS (test:cljs 9226/43636). Left open for the mayor.

title: Make the Chapter 02 presence example resolve every view head
description:
## Finding

Completeness review of merged documentation PR #5823 at exact head `6c1ac7288a3858afb039aa2bb406864d5bd551d0` / merge `d1343f707446b8e9bd90b4278dd6c00bab1a1a10` found a concrete copy-paste compiler failure in the newly staged presence example.

`ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/guide/02-views.md` around lines 94-102 defines `toast-tray` first and uses `[toast-card ...]` inside it, but defines `toast-card` only afterward. re-frame.ui resolves component heads eagerly during `defview` macro expansion. `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/env.cljc` around lines 131-158 rejects this forward head with `:rf.ui.compile/unresolved-head` unless the symbol has already been defined or declared with exact `^:rf.ui/view` metadata.

The example is explicitly future Stage 4, but staging does not make its eventual grammar valid: once `ui/presence` exists, copying the fence still fails before runtime. The simplest correction is to define `toast-card` before `toast-tray`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use the compiler's current head-resolution law and macroexpand the chapter fence in its displayed order.
2. Expansion of `toast-tray` reaches `[toast-card ...]` before `toast-card` resolves.

When the Stage-4 guide fixture is activated, compile the exact fence rather than a normalized duplicate and include a mutation that restores forward-use-before-definition. title: Deduplicate resource teardown index tokens per frame incarnation
description:
## Problem

The rf2-vxgfnd.106 resource teardown-discovery index originally retained every frame-token occurrence from desired, reservations, and held state. In steady state each active lease site appears in all three projections, so N sites on one frame retained about 3N references to the identical exact token. The index is recomputed at layout acceptance, staged reachability, failure restore, final publication, disconnect, and teardown.

Anchors: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc resource-frame-index, install-resource-state, accept-resource-capture, staged/final resource publication, and teardown discovery.

## Production impact

The index is only used to discover whether a cell references an exact frame incarnation. Duplicate occurrences add no correctness information but create avoidable allocation, iteration, and retained memory on resource-heavy list/table views. Correctness does require retaining distinct A and B tokens transiently for one frame id during retarget/failure cleanup; it does not require repeated copies.

## Required direction

Retain a deduplicated exact-token collection per frame id. A small set is acceptable while tokens preserve identity-compatible hashing; otherwise use identity-deduped vectors. Do not collapse to one token or change lifecycle/ownership semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
- With N active sites on one exact frame incarnation, steady-state teardown index cardinality is exactly one token, not about 3N.
- Transitional state with old A in held/reservation and new B in desired retains exactly A and B, and teardown discovery works for either exact incarnation.
- Distinct frame ids retain their own token collections and cross-frame teardown remains green.
- A mutation back to occurrence vectors fails the cardinality/allocation assertion.
- JVM and CLJS focused gates confirm token hashing/identity behavior.
- No public API, ownership ordering, or coordinator is introduced.

title: Complete digest-carrier fail-closed proof ledger for zero-carrier and hookless builds
description:
## Problem

PR #5806 merged the compiler-authoritative whole-build digest carrier and its principal real-browser/JVM/production proofs. The exact-head closure audit found two explicit proof-ledger cases that are implemented defensively but still lack their own direct red fixture:

1. A client build with zero digest-carrier resources. The runtime correctly rejects any carrier count other than one, and duplicate-carrier behavior is tested, but count zero is not independently exercised.
2. A real configured build with the digest build hook absent. Runtime sentinel and cache-blocker validation exist, but no end-to-end configured Shadow build proves a hookless pipeline fails closed instead of silently publishing or accepting a stale digest.

These are evidence-completeness gaps, not a confirmed implementation defect. They matter before the S2 boundary review because both correspond to fail-closed assumptions in the new Spec 004C carrier contract. Keep the fix narrow: add deterministic fixtures against the merged behavior; do not redesign the carrier or broaden production machinery.

## Deliverable

Add one direct zero-carrier fixture and one real configured hookless-build fixture using the existing digest probe/harness infrastructure. Each fixture must be demonstrated red when its relevant guard/configuration is removed or weakened and green on current behavior. Assert typed/fail-loud diagnostics, no digest publication, no carrier acceptance, and preservation of the last accepted snapshot where applicable. Keep browser/process teardown total and reuse the existing warm-watch harness rather than creating another orchestration framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- A direct fixture supplies zero digest-carrier resources and proves the client/runtime rejects the snapshot rather than treating absence as an empty or valid digest.
- A real configured Shadow build with the digest build hook removed or omitted fails closed before publishing/accepting a new digest; the last accepted snapshot remains authoritative.
- Both fixtures are recorded red under a deliberate removed/weakened guard and green after restoration, with commands and results in the PR.
- Existing digest-carrier JVM, real-browser lazy/HMR/failure/recovery, production-elision, and changed-surface gates remain green.
- No public API, carrier format, production counter, fallback digest computation, or new general-purpose test harness is introduced.

title: S2 spec honesty: reconcile Spec 004C with compiler-patched digest carrier
description:
## Problem
PR #5806 replaces the client-side whole-build digest recomputation over the live registered-view manifest registry with the Mike-approved compiler-patched O(1) carrier. The semantic law remains whole-build/compiler-authoritative, but checked-in Spec 004C §2.1 still normatively says the client computes from registered manifests and refreshes by recomputing the live registry. That mechanism becomes false. The same section's REPL convergence wording must match the ruled successful-evaluation commit boundary and last-known-good behavior on failed/never-evaluated forms.

## Deliverable
After rf2-n7ff9f lands and the current Spec owner is free, make the narrow Spec 004C correction: compiler is sole digest authority; JVM reads compiler state; dev client reads the compiler-patched carrier in O(1); production carries neither carrier nor digest machinery; successful no-pass REPL evaluation commits both authorities and failure preserves LKG. Update only directly dependent cross-references/goldens. Do not change digest semantics, hash inputs, mount mismatch policy, or the frozen API.

## Proof
Spec wording must be mechanically checked against the final #5806 implementation and its regression fixtures. Search must find no current claim that the client recomputes the whole-build digest from the live registry. Docs/links/API gates green.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 004C §2.1 describes compiler-owned carrier projection rather than deleted live-registry recomputation.
- REPL wording names successful evaluation as commit boundary and failed/never-evaluated LKG behavior.

title: S2 mounted proof: compiled conditional sub acquires, drops, and rejects stale delivery
description:
## Problem
S2 has manual reconciler tests for dependency changes, but no compiled mounted view proves a conditional (ui/sub ...) site is acquired when its branch appears, released when it disappears, and insulated from late delivery. Compiler grammar permits finite conditional sites, so manual mark/reconcile calls can remain green while emitted capture wiring leaks or delivers stale values.

## Deliverable
Using the first-party ui/adapter and the Tier-3 mounted harness, compile and mount a view whose conditional branch toggles a subscription site. Prove connected acquisition, correct DOM/value publication, branch-off release/disconnect, no stale notification after removal, branch-on reacquisition, StrictMode-safe ownership balance, and unmount cleanup. Use real observation callbacks; do not call mark-dirty!/flush-pending! as a substitute.

## Sequencing
Current S2 close-first proof. Run after PRs for rf2-vxgfnd.81 and rf2-vxgfnd.12.1 establish ui/adapter and with-root. Bundle with the shared-harness .12 PR-2 / rf2-vxgfnd.43 / .58 wave only if one owner can keep a clean diff; never pre-empt the active harness owner.
acceptance_criteria:
- A compiled mounted conditional sub acquires exactly once per connected ownership lifetime.
- Turning the branch off releases the lease and late movement cannot render or reattach it.
- Turning it on reacquires and publishes the current value.
- React StrictMode replay and final unmount leave zero cells, observation owners, and callbacks.
- A wiring mutation that omits compiler capture or conditional drop fails deterministically.
- Normal browser CI owns the fixture on the retained first-party adapter.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION PREP 2026-07-13: land only after #5808, .105 exact-capture, and .100 lexical-site identity. Add one dedicated conditional_sub_dom_cljs_test.cljs using the public Promise-safe Tier-3 harness and first-party ui/adapter, not the shared harness file. A compiled StrictMode view always reads enabled? and conditionally reads value. Prove off baseline; on acquisition/current DOM; off release; real value movement while absent causes no render/read/owner change; on reacquisition publishes current value; live movement renders; unmount returns root/ViewCell/sub-cache/observation baselines. Triangulate DOM, committed site/target, cache refcount, active owner count, and render/read evidence. Under StrictMode assert unchanged/increased relationships, not exact render increments. Never call mark-dirty!/flush-pending! or internal scheduling helpers.

Primary mutation skips obs/release! for commit to-release leases. The fixture must then retain owner/refcount, accept a late callback/render while absent, and fail final cleanup. This same real StrictMode ownership-balance proof discharges the remaining narrow rf2-vxgfnd.43 obligation; close .43 with this PR rather than dispatching its obsolete broad scope separately. Keep .58 separate.
POST-.100 PREFLIGHT 2026-07-13: implement as dedicated conditional_sub_dom_cljs_test.cljs plus TESTING.md, normally no production change. Use first-party ui/adapter, Promise with-root/flush!, StrictMode, and one compiled view with always-enabled sub plus conditional value sub. Consume .100's SITE-keyed inspection seam (never target-key fallback). Sequence OFF → ON → one real same-drain value-write then disable chain → absent value movement → reacquire → live movement → teardown. In the race, assert all writes visible in app-db while DOM/read side remains old inside flush thunk, then one final OFF commit drops only the value sid, releases old lease/owner/cache, and ignores already-dirty stale delivery; movement while absent must leave body/read/revision/site map exactly still and not recompute the absent node; reacquire uses same lexical sid, fresh lease, latest value. title: fix(core): linearize frame config and auxiliary trace-policy publication
description:
## Correctness finding

PR #5799 closed rf2-umsyo9 by moving frame trace-policy writes after the guarded `frames` CAS. That fixes the exclusive-loser ordering it targeted, but it does not make auxiliary policy publication atomic with a successful upsert.

Reachable successful-winner race on current main:

1. Actor A wins the guarded create/re-register CAS for frame X and is descheduled before `apply-trace-policy!`.
2. Actor B then wins a later re-registration CAS for X, committing config B; B applies trace suppression/retention policy B and returns.
3. A resumes and applies policy A.
4. The authoritative frame record now carries B while the frame-scoped trace stores carry A. Both calls were successful, so the exclusive-loser guard does not help.

The #5799 regression fixture also does not satisfy the mandatory fix-PR protocol it claims. Its barrier is `*upsert-decide-probe*`; in #5776 that probe ran after the offending pre-CAS policy writes. A paused there, B installed/applied its policy, then A lost the CAS without another write, so the new fixture passes the supposedly unfixed baseline. The test and PR claims that it fails #5776 are therefore false.

A second same-surface mismatch remains: re-registering without `:rf.trace/events-retained` removes the key from stored config but `apply-trace-policy!` does not clear the prior per-frame override, so the old ring/cap survives although Spec 002 and the frame docstring say omission inherits the process default.

Finally, #5799 describes abandoned speculative state containers as safe in an implementation comment, but the adapter contract still treats the container as opaque and does not normatively require allocation-only/disposal-free construction. Avoid speculative construction or prove the shipped adapter contract without silently broadening it.

This is a follow-up to CLOSED rf2-umsyo9; never amend or reopen that bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic barrier fixture pauses successful actor A after its registry CAS but before policy publication, lets actor B complete a later successful re-registration with distinct config/no-emit/retention values, then resumes A; frame config and every auxiliary trace-policy store must all reflect the same final logical winner. The fixture fails current PR #5799 behavior.
- The exclusive-loser regression fixture genuinely fails against PR #5776's ordering and passes the corrected implementation; the PR body/docstrings state the exact mutation/revert used.
- Re-registration that omits `:rf.trace/events-retained` clears the per-frame override and restores inherited process-default behavior; explicit overrides still apply.
- Auxiliary policy writes are incarnation/revision guarded or serialized with the authoritative frame mutation; a successful older upsert cannot overwrite a newer winner's policy.
- Resolve speculative candidate lifecycle without inventing an unapproved public contract: preferably avoid constructing an unowned candidate, otherwise stop and surface any required adapter-contract change to Mike.
- Preserve no-adapter zero-global-write behavior, ordinary HMR/re-registration semantics, initial-events exactly-once behavior, and existing create/create + destroy/re-register linearization fixtures on JVM and CLJS.
- Mandatory fix-PR protocol: key fixtures demonstrated red pre-fix and green post-fix; every touched docstring/spec claim diff-checked against code.
close_reason: Fixed by merged PR #5807 (9ec613b464): liveness/token-linearized auxiliary policy publication, omission clearing, destroy-race fencing, and deterministic concurrency proofs.

--- WHAT A TAG WOULD SHIP TODAY ---
VERSION = 0.0.1.alpha, so the tag is v0.0.1.alpha (release.yml hard-fails unless tag equals v + VERSION). The push runs verify-version-lockstep -> test -> deploy-core -> 13 parallel deploy-leaf -> github-release, publishing FOURTEEN Clojars coordinates at 0.0.1.alpha: day8/re-frame2 (core), -reagent, reagent-slim, -uix, -ui, -schemas, -machines, -routing, -flows, -http, -ssr, -ssr-ring, -resources, -epoch. Publication is F6 territory, and the donor artefact was itself ruled NOT to be published."

CLOJARS IRREVERSIBILITY (verified from primary source, not memory): Clojars does not literally forbid deletion. Its official FAQ (github.com/clojars/clojars-web/wiki/About - "how do I delete a jar") says ordinary project/version deletion is DISCOURAGED and administrator deletion is reserved for malicious/security content or accidentally-published private material; a deployed non-SNAPSHOT version is otherwise immutable except by a valid deletion request. Publishing the wrong product topology is not one of those reasons. Practical recovery is bump-and-supersede, with the unwanted coordinate remaining in the public historical record. docs/release-process.md Recovery says the same.

G1-G4 external-alpha template gate (rf2-b16va, PR #6671). Children 3/3, bd reports eligible for close.
MET (2) SOAK GATES DISCHARGED, NOT PENDING. Despite this epic's title, the EP-0030 addendum records Mike WAIVED the pinned two-leg soak condition on 2026-07-21 21:23 AUSEST ("We don't need a soak clock"). S7 entry reduced to the two merged proofs P-1 rf2-nn5s8 #6648 and P-2 rf2-vvdzx #6651. The same addendum states "the tag remains Mike's one reserved manual act" and defers G-2, G-9, G-10 and G-14's guide-fixtures arm as an explicit exception contract - so the alpha carries NO absolute bundle-size claim.
MET (3) VERSION AND TAG MECHANICS. VERSION = 0.0.1.alpha; the tag-matches-VERSION check would pass; the glob matches; prerelease auto-set; the alpha / alpha-N scheme documented in docs/release-process.md Tag format. G1-G4 ran as a TRUE external consumer (fresh temp dir, documented deps-new invocation, the scaffold's own npm install, no repo node_modules junction) and the PRE-fix template failed G2/G3 on EVERY adapter variant. Three defects, all structurally invisible to in-repo gates: the emitted package.json omitted @xyflow/react and elkjs so the first compile of every scaffold failed; the emitted :shadow alias :main-opts collided with the npx wrapper's own -m, killing every npm run watch / npm test / emitted CI command; the dev CSP lacked unsafe-eval, making the documented first run a blank page. EVERY spawned follow-up is closed: rf2-qgfo4 (#6673 - root cause was the Xray preload handing a Hiccup shell to a React-element-shaped render slot, NOT the UIx adapter), rf2-zgwro (#6672), rf2-igwf7 (#6686 - added an emitted-package.json completeness assert and a Chromium dev-page boot cell, and found that the existing compile assert did not fail on the :main-opts collision because shadow exits 0 after building nothing), rf2-qa5ty (#6695 - provisioned Chromium in all three template jobs, moved five browser assertions from asserted-by-nobody to executed), rf2-p6f6u (#6676 - pulled the Xray preload out of the :uix scaffold rather than ship a scaffold promising a panel it cannot mount).

--- THE EP-0030 / EP-0036 SUPERSESSION, STATED PLAINLY ---
EP-0030 Resolved Decisions (Mike, 2026-07-17) made re-frame.ui a new EXPERIMENTAL substrate offered ALONGSIDE Reagent/reagent-slim/UIx, and this epic's PROOF line follows directly: "Helix gone, tag cut, re-frame.ui shipping as an experimental option alongside the retained adapters, alpha train ready." Both analyses recommend closing rf2-vxgfnd.99 on what it actually delivered (W13 + W12 + G1-G4), with a close reason of the shape "implementation complete; release condition superseded by EP-0036", then closing rf2-vxgfnd behind it, and re-homing the tag onto a fresh release bead. I agree the bookkeeping is right - an open epic holding a tag whose meaning migrated to a different programme is its own inaccuracy - but I did NOT close it: the tag and the decision about what the alpha contains are both Mike's. IF the tag is re-homed, my dissent stands: do NOT write F6e / rf2-drpa3.57 into its acceptance criteria as a hard precondition unless Mike positively decides the first public artefact set must include the native view story. Sensible acceptance criteria for a re-homed alpha bead: rf2-a32r7 landed, CHANGELOG rewritten to the real artefact roster, all-package preflight builds green, and a final check that the intended Clojars coordinates are still unclaimed.

--- OPTIONS AS TABLED, FOR THE RECORD ---
(A) Cut v0.0.1.alpha now. CANNOT BE DONE AS WRITTEN - mechanically blocked, not merely inadvisable. Presupposes rf2-a32r7. If Mike judges that shipping something has independent strategic value (early adopters, feedback, forcing-function on the pipeline's first run), A is defensible in this order: rf2-a32r7 first, CHANGELOG rewrite second, then tag and watch all deploy jobs to completion, plus an explicit README/CHANGELOG sentence stating the compiled-view substrate is not in this release and arrives under a different name. That sentence is what keeps the alpha honest rather than merely early.
(B) Wait for Freehand F6e. Resolves the contradiction by outliving it, but leaves the machinery armed meanwhile and the wait is unbounded. Both analyses reject B alone for the first reason; I reject the unbounded wait outright under pre-alpha posture.
(C) Close S7 without a tag, re-home the alpha decision. BOTH ANALYSES RECOMMEND THIS. I agree on the bookkeeping and on filing rf2-a32r7 immediately; I dissent on writing F6e in as a hard gate.
(D) Cut a non-publishing safety/* or milestone/* marker on the W13 merge commit. Provably publishes nothing - any tag not matching v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+* cannot fire the workflow, and precedent exists (safety/audit-gap-976c96e, safety/perf-fae8fb8, both lightweight 2026-07-15 archaeology markers). Dossier called it a cheap companion; Codex called it ceremony without a demonstrated consumer since the Helix boundary is already addressable by its merge commit. I side with Codex: SKIP unless a concrete bisect, migration or automation consumer appears.

--- COULD NOT BE VERIFIED / DELIBERATELY NOT ESTIMATED ---
- Whether un-publishing ui was deliberately deferred or simply overlooked. No bead, note or comment addresses PR #6654's already-landed machinery after the 2026-07-22 ruling. Oversight is the reading; intent is unprovable.
- Freehand's remaining calendar distance - deliberately NOT estimated, and nobody else should either. rf2-rr26cq (P1, open, the highest-priority open bug in the repo) - canonical self-Var emission: a compiled view named sub in a namespace that refers re-frame.freehand/sub mounts the authoring verb instead of recursing, and a non-recursive colliding declaration defines the authoring Var.
