=== RULING — ALPHA TAG READINESS (delegated decision, 2026-07-25 10:57:30 AUSEST) ===
Ruled under authority delegated by Mike for this one decision. Source dossier ai/decisions/rf2-vxgfnd.99.alpha-tag-cut.md (dossier author + Codex second opinion) is now DELETED; this note is its permanent record. All volatile claims re-verified at main c4d7bf172d.

THE RULING: READY TO CUT — option A, sequenced over two steps. Step 1: land the truthing PR (rf2-vxgfnd.99.4, P2, filed as a child of this epic — full anchors there). Step 2: Mike cuts. The physical tag remains Mike's ONE RESERVED MANUAL ACT — nothing in this ruling authorizes anyone else to push it. Do NOT gate on Freehand F6e (rf2-drpa3.57): one of six gate rows is green and the wait is unbounded; gating the first alpha on another programme's terminal gate turns an alpha into a de facto 1.0, which under pre-alpha posture is precisely backwards. EP-0037 routing churn and the mid-rewrite router API are what "alpha" MEANS — not gates. If Mike positively decides the first public artefact set must include the native view story, that is a positioning call he may make explicitly; it is not an engineering precondition and is not the default.

WHAT THE TAG SHIPS (verified against the release.yml deploy matrix + verify-version-lockstep.sh ARTEFACTS roster at HEAD): THIRTEEN Clojars coordinates at 0.0.1.alpha — day8/re-frame2 (core, implementation/core); adapters day8/re-frame2-reagent, day8/reagent-slim, day8/re-frame2-uix; per-feature day8/re-frame2-schemas, -machines, -routing, -flows, -http, -ssr, -ssr-ring (also deps ssr), -resources, -epoch. Plus a GitHub Release auto-marked prerelease whose body ALREADY enumerates all 13 correctly (release.yml:597-610). NOT shipped: re-frame.ui (no :clein/build; release.yml:39-53 marks the absence load-bearing — do not re-add without a ruling reversing 2026-07-22) and Freehand (publication is F6 territory by design). day8/reagent-slim is the one coordinate off the re-frame2-* naming pattern — deliberate publication-time namespace rename, implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/deps.edn:38-43; worth one eyeball before it becomes permanent.

MACHINERY: the hard blocker recorded in the folded dossier above is GONE and stays gone. REQUIRED_PUBLISHABLE has zero hits in .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh; the ARTEFACTS/NON_CORE rosters carry no ui; the conditional inventory guard fails closed via implementation/scripts/lib/publishable-runtimes.cjs (catches any :clein/build reappearing outside the inventory). Gate last ran green: 17 artefacts (13 implementation + 4 tools) pinned to 0.0.1.alpha. A tag can no longer publish the donor.

PIPELINE-DEBUT RISK (priced in, not a reason to defer): zero release.yml runs ever, zero remote tags, zero releases, no workflow_dispatch by design — the first tag IS the pipeline's first end-to-end run against real Clojars credentials. fail-fast:false on deploy-leaf gives two failure shapes: (a) at/before deploy-core — nothing public; delete tag, fix, retag; cheap. (b) AFTER deploy-core succeeds — core is on Clojars permanently with a partial leaf set; the same version cannot be re-run (Clojars 409s the duplicate core upload); recovery is bump VERSION to 0.0.1.alpha-1, retag, ship everything, note the abandoned version in CHANGELOG.md per docs/release-process.md §Recovery step 6. Bounded, documented, survivable — a bad afternoon, not a bad decision. The pipeline never becomes more tested by sitting; better a debut at thirteen coordinates nobody depends on than at 1.0.

CREDENTIALS — NEW HARD PREFLIGHT FINDING (Codex, independently confirmed at HEAD): `gh secret list` returns ZERO repository-level Actions secrets, and the repo is org-owned (day8), so an org-level CLOJARS_USERNAME/CLOJARS_PASSWORD grant may exist but is UNVERIFIED from this identity. Do not discover this by pushing the tag. Mike must positively verify both secrets are visible to this repo and that the token is a reusable Clojars deploy token authorized for ALL thirteen day8 coordinates (not single-use/single-artefact). A stale/absent secret fails at deploy-core — the benign shape — but only if the run is watched.

CORRECTED FACT (supersedes the 2026-07-24 "compiled tier not browser-mountable" claim recorded above): the compiled tier IS browser-mountable when the ClojureScript compiler expands the declaration. lowering-unavailable! (implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/react.cljs:534-546) is a CROSS-HOST guard — its own error text says the descriptor "was built by a JVM expansion and handed to a browser". CLJS-expanded compiled views mount, proven by implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/compiled_mount_dom_cljs_test.cljs. rf2-drpa3.113 genuinely shipped. This weakens one argument for waiting on Freehand; it does not change the ruling's logic (F6e remains 1-of-6 green and unbounded).

DOSSIER CORRECTIONS — state moved under it between writing and ruling: (1) rf2-lzq43 CLOSED (PR #6914) — install-re-frame-ui.md now shows :local/root plus the donor-only-never-published admonition; the page's DELETION is rf2-ote5u (blocked on the shadow-config JVM gate retarget) and is NOT a tag gate. The examples/ui/minimal-counter echoes were NOT cured and are folded into rf2-vxgfnd.99.4. (2) The GitHub Release body is no longer a bare CHANGELOG link — it already enumerates the 13 coordinates; the residual defect is the blob/main/CHANGELOG.md link, which should pin to the tag ref (in .99.4). (3) rf2-rr26cq closed (#6910). (4) rf2-kqxe6.6's permanent-:loading liveness bug is fixed on main (#6902; verified at implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:1026-1027); the bead remains in_progress only on a narrower diagnostics finding (false :contributor attribution when caught ex-data carries a colliding unnamespaced key) — a misleading error message, not a stuck app; not a gate. Nothing open is a bug against core or any of the three shipped adapters.

VERSION / TAG STRING: no new scheme decided here; mechanics constrain it. release.yml hard-fails unless the tag equals "v" + the VERSION file; VERSION is 0.0.1.alpha today, so the tag is v0.0.1.alpha unless Mike changes VERSION in the release commit — the exact string is Mike's to pick at cut time. Recovery increments are v0.0.1.alpha-N (docs/release-process.md §Tag format). One release commit carries VERSION + CHANGELOG together (preflight :112).

CUT-TIME CHECKLIST (Mike, step 2): (1) rf2-vxgfnd.99.4 merged; (2) CLOJARS secrets positively verified — see CREDENTIALS above; (3) all 13 coordinates still 404 on Clojars (a pre-existing 0.0.1.alpha would 409 the core upload); (4) quiescent commit, all required checks green, rerun bash .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh; (5) one release commit (VERSION + CHANGELOG), tag, push, then WATCH every job to completion — do not walk away after deploy-core goes green; that is exactly where the expensive failure lives. If a partial deploy occurs, go directly to 0.0.1.alpha-1; never retry the same immutable version.

AFTER THE CUT — close bookkeeping (endorsing both analyses): close this epic honestly as "W13 Helix removal, W12 meta-docs and the G1-G4 external-alpha gate delivered; the 're-frame.ui shipping as an experimental option' half of the PROOF was superseded by EP-0036 rather than met; tag cut at v0.0.1.alpha" — then close rf2-vxgfnd behind it with the same supersession note (its title no longer describes the ruled outcome and has not since 2026-07-17). Option D (a non-publishing marker tag) remains SKIPPED — redundant under A.

Therefore this is not an independently missing thing. An error id with no emitter is exactly what this repo says must not exist; it cannot land before emit-ui-tree lands. It is a rider on item 2 and should never be scheduled separately.

Question worth ruling before rf2-vxgfnd.97.2 fixes the spelling: does the SSR seam need its OWN error id at all?

Two ids for one condition at two boundaries is a consistency cost, and #{1} is a versioning scheme with exactly one implementation.
Evidence against: spec/004B:376-380 wants the SSR boundary to match "the artifact's construction-time error posture (:rf.error/ssr-missing-payload-policy style)", i.e. ssr-tier ids are ssr-spelled.
Exact wording if the operator rules to retire it:

The S5 serialiser's root version gate reuses the shipped shared id :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed with the same {:got :supported} ex-data, exactly as re-frame.ui.semantic/normalize's root version gate already does. :rf.error/ssr-ui-tree-version-unsupported is withdrawn; no dedicated Spec 009 row is owed; spec/004B §The SSR consumption boundary and the forward reference inside the :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed row are amended to name the shared id. rf2-vxgfnd.97.2 residue item 1 drops the version-gate id and keeps emit-ui-tree."
I am NOT recommending this. It is a real ruling, it is small, and it is cheaper to make BEFORE .97.2 writes the spelling into spec/011 than after.

=== IS THIS EPIC'S OBLIGATIONS LIST ACCURATE? MOSTLY YES ===
Re-verified each of the five S5-OBLIGATIONS against emit sites:

The "STILL OPEN — four items" list above is correct in substance. Item 1 of that list (rf2-vxgfnd.97.1) is now STALE: that bead was RULED (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 09:55 AUSEST) — the prepared amendment is RETIRED as substantially consumed, and its surviving residue was re-filed as rf2-vxgfnd.97.2. It is no longer an open routing question.

=== IS ANYTHING ELSE IN S5 A NAME RATHER THAN AN IMPLEMENTATION? ===
Swept the epic's SCOPE line. One more genuine unbuilt item, consistently and honestly marked:
  - the client-only SSR PHASE FLIP. Named at implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui.cljc:597, compiler/analyze.cljc:2399, compiler/emit_cljs.cljc:669, spec/004-Views.md:666 and :1369, spec/API.md:251 and :368 — all as "completes S5". Genuinely unbuilt; correctly labelled; no leaf owns it.

Nothing else in the S5 scope line is a bare name. spec/011-SSR.md (1686 lines) contains ZERO occurrences of render-static / emit-ui-tree / ui-tree — confirming rf2-vxgfnd.97.2's residue inventory is complete and correctly scoped.

title: fix(core): exclusive frame CAS loser must not overwrite winner trace policy
description:
## Correctness finding

PR #5776 (`817c9de2c1408791275b3c12c31ad724aa566c96`) linearizes frame-record decide/install through the `frames` atom and adds internal `:rf.frame/must-create?`. Its exclusive collision contract says the loser wrote nothing, but `upsert-frame!` mutates two frame-scoped process-global policies before the guarded CAS:

- `trace/set-frame-no-emit!` always writes the id's suppression flag.
- `:trace.tooling/set-frame-events-retained!` writes the id's retention override when supplied.

Those stores are separate from `frames`, so the guarded CAS does not linearize them.

Reachable interleaving:

1. Exclusive actor A reads frame id X absent and builds its speculative record.
2. Ordinary actor B wins installation of X, with (for example) `:rf.trace/frame-no-emit? true` and/or its own retention override.
3. A then applies its trace settings (the unconditional suppression setter defaults omission to false), reaches the frames CAS, observes B's record, and throws `:rf.error/frame-id-taken`.
4. B remains the live owner of X, but its trace policy now reflects losing actor A's config. A's supposedly zero-write collision can make an inspector frame emit self-noise or change the live frame's ring retention.

The new race fixture cannot expose this window: `*upsert-decide-probe*` fires after both policy writes, so the fixture only pauses between those writes and the CAS. The current test proves frame-record ownership, not atomicity of the other frame-owned stores.

There is also avoidable speculative allocation: when A's initial snapshot was absent, `new-frame-record` invokes the adapter's `make-state-container` before the CAS; on a create/create loss the never-installed record is abandoned. Today shipped containers are atom-backed and GC-able, so this is not by itself a resource leak, but the adapter contract should not be forced to tolerate abandoned speculative construction if the algorithm can defer or explicitly clean it.

## Required correction

Make all winner-owned side effects occur only after ownership is established, or give them the same incarnation/rollback guard as the frame record. An exclusive collision must not modify any process-global state for the winning incarnation. Preserve ordinary re-registration semantics, where the successful re-registrant's config intentionally updates trace policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic barrier/latch fixture pauses an exclusive constructor after its absent snapshot but before its policy writes/CAS, lets another actor install the same id with distinct `:rf.trace/frame-no-emit?` and `:rf.trace/events-retained` values, then resumes the loser; after `:rf.error/frame-id-taken`, the winner's suppression and retention settings are unchanged.
- `:rf.frame/must-create?` collisions are zero-write across the `frames` registry and all frame-owned auxiliary stores, not only the frame record.
- First registration and ordinary re-registration still apply the winning config's trace suppression and retention policy exactly once.
- The concurrency test seam can open the actual pre-side-effect race window; the test fails against PR #5776's ordering.
- Resolve the speculative never-installed state-container lifecycle: either construct only for the CAS winner (without moving no-adapter validation after global writes), or document/prove a disposal-free allocation contract and avoid claiming that no unwind is needed without that contract.
- Core JVM and CLJS frame/concurrency suites remain green.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5799: exclusive-CAS trace-policy writes linearized onto the winning branch via apply-trace-policy!; loser is zero-write across frames + trace/retention stores. JVM barrier fixture fails pre-fix. Disposal-free speculative-container contract documented. destroy-frame! signature untouched.

title: S2e Fast-Refresh stable-component-shell: wire the render-path so a live browser preserves state across a same-signature reload
description: Flagged by rf2-vxgfnd.11 (S2e HMR matrix, #5791) as a deliberately-deferred substrate gap — NOT a blocker; the six-cell S2 HMR gate is fully delivered + green. GAP: the §10 'Fast Refresh integration' piece — a STABLE COMPONENT SHELL (React Refresh or var-indirection) so a live browser PRESERVES local state across a same-hook-signature file save. Currently memo-view binds a FRESH React component per re-eval, so the real runtime REMOUNTS on every reload regardless of signature. #5791 built + proved the preserve/remount DECISION (the view-generation registry consuming the S1b hook-sig hash) + the stale-cell REJECTION mechanism (advance-generation! → commit! :stale); what's missing is the RENDER-PATH CONSUMPTION — a stable component shell that survives re-eval so state can actually be preserved. Deliberately NOT wired at S2 because: (a) it'd be inert (every S2 defview emits the empty-plan hook signature, so nothing to preserve yet), and (b) it needs the stable shell (React Refresh var-indirection / a persistent component identity across re-eval) which is runtime glue, not a substrate primitive. Likely S2f/S3 territory (real defviews with hooks). Surface: memo-view / the compiled-view component binding in reactive.cljc or the emit path + a React-Refresh integration + a real-browser state-preservation DOM fixture. Sequence: after a stage ships real hook-bearing defviews (so there's state to preserve). Reference #5791's generation-registry + advance-generation! seam as the decision/mechanism half already in place.
notes:
S2 BOUNDARY RECONCILIATION 2026-07-13: this is a real close-before-conformance obligation. Spec 004 promises the full HMR matrix and stable shell; current memo-view creates fresh component identity on re-evaluation, so same-signature reload remounts and loses local/child state. Sequence after the digest/compiler hot-zone owner. No compatibility mode; prove preserve for same signature and remount for incompatible signature in a real browser.

IMPLEMENTATION PREP 2026-07-13: evolve the existing dev-only view-generations entry into the single per-view HMR slot; do not add a registry or make registrar a second authority. Atomically hold hook signature, body revision, remount generation, current render/comparator/manifest descriptor, one stable outer shell, one stable inner body, and the minimal uSES revision store. Increment body revision on every successful registration; increment remount generation only on hook-signature change. Return the same Outer object on every dev registration. Outer subscribes to body revision and delegates comparison to the current descriptor, then renders stable Inner keyed only by remount generation. Inner calls the current render fn as an ordinary function so hooks remain on the stable Inner fiber. Same signature refreshes body while preserving local/ref/child state; changed signature changes key and remounts safely.

CORRECTNESS REPAIR: current generation language conflates body freshness with remount identity. Split them. Mint/sync a ViewCell at current body revision before capture, and reject commit when the capture revision differs from the current slot revision—not merely the cell-local revision. Registration publishes descriptor and both revisions atomically before notifying, closing render-before-registration/layout-after-registration stale ownership.

PRODUCTION: emitted defview uses an explicit goog.DEBUG branch. Dev registers/returns the stable shell; production stays the current direct React.memo(render, comparator). Advanced output must contain no slot/listeners/dynamic lookup/extra fiber. Browser proof mounts hooks, refs, effect, and stateful child; same-signature v2 updates without root.render while preserving all state and shell identity; incompatible v3 preserves public shell identity but resets inner state and orders cleanup/setup once without hook warnings. Add render-to-commit stale-revision proof plus compiler golden and production DCE gate. Mutation teeth include fresh shell, always/never bump key, missing notify, React-element invocation of current render, frozen comparator, cell-local-only revision check, prod residue, and stale equal-deps effect.
close_reason: Completed and merged in PR #5817 (faaa1b4a8a): stable dev Outer/Inner shell, fixed hook skeleton, exact per-view publication transaction, same-signature state/ref/child preservation, incompatible-signature remount, stale-capture rejection, Shadow/REPL registration path, and zero production HMR residue; exact head independently approved and 54-check green.

title: Key frame/destroying-frames by incarnation token so ui frame-close revalidation can close rf2-vxgfnd.88 Failure-2
description: Follow-up from rf2-vxgfnd.88 (PR #5784). The ui commit-close revalidation now compares the acquire-time incarnation token, fixing Failure-1 (an old-incarnation commit surviving on a same-id replacement). But the RECIPROCAL Failure-2 — an old incarnation A's stale bare-id close marker (present in the JVM window between destroy-frame!'s step-6 dissoc-frame! and its terminal finally that clears destroying-frames) tearing down a LIVE replacement incarnation B's cell — CANNOT be closed from re-frame.ui.reactive alone: frame/destroying-frames is a set of bare frame-ids, so {frame-closing?, frame-incarnation-token} cannot distinguish an A-marker (stale) from B being genuinely in-flight closing (both give frame-closing?=true, current-token=B). Fix: key core's destroying-frames by incarnation token (or add a frame-incarnation-closing? predicate that checks whether the CURRENTLY-live incarnation is the one being destroyed). Then reactive.cljc's frame-close revalidation can scope the frame-closing? clause to the acquired incarnation. Note: on CLJS this window is unreachable (single-threaded destroy runs to completion before any recreate); it is a JVM multi-thread concern. Surface: re-frame.frame (core, off the .88 worker's ui surface). AC per rf2-vxgfnd.88: 'A's close authority cannot tear down a cell that owns B.'
notes: HELD until #5784 (reactive-activation, .88/.92/.93) MERGES — .94 is the RECIPROCAL of .88 (Failure-2): a stale bare-id close marker in core's frame/destroying-frames (a BARE-ID set) can tear down a live same-id REPLACEMENT incarnation's cell in the JVM dissoc-frame!→finally window. reactive.cljc CANNOT distinguish an A-marker from B genuinely in-flight — needs CORE frame.cljc to key the close marker by incarnation TOKEN (the frame-incarnation-token/:drain-lock). Surface: frame.cljc (core) + reactive.cljc's revalidation reading the token-keyed marker. Dispatch after #5784 lands so it builds on .88's incarnation-token revalidation. Filed by the reactive-activation worker; #5784 closes Failure-1 (primary), .94 = Failure-2.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5787 (commit 1). destroying-frames keyed by incarnation token {id->token}; new frame-incarnation-closing? predicate; ViewCell frame-close revalidation scoped to the acquired incarnation. JVM barrier fixture proven fail-pre-fix.

title: G-1 todos-20 direct-render parity gate is marginal/flaky (sits at the 1.10 budget, ~50% fail rate)
description: Found investigating a false-red on #5778/.91 (2026-07-13). The G-1 :advanced bench direct-render parity gate's todos-20 fixture genuinely runs ~1.10-1.12x hand-written jsx for the 20-keyed-row case on CI hardware — right at the p50/p95 1.1 budget. On a FIXED bundle it swings p50 1.03-1.10 / p95 1.04-1.20 across runs (~50% fail rate); raising estimator precision (rounds 7 to 15, warmup 2000 to 4000) made it fail MORE (7/10), converging on a true ~1.10-1.12 ratio. So it red-flags ui_gates-touching PRs BY CHANCE — a merge-gate reliability problem (a real ui PR can be blocked, or a flaky red misread as a touched-surface regression). The byte-equality precheck AND the emitted-JS golden both PASS; only the perf-budget arm flakes. FIX — decide between (a) optimize the compiled keyed for-loop / subview emission to widen the margin below 1.10 (the real win — the compiled todo-list is genuinely ~10-12 percent slower than hand jsx for keyed rows); or (b) make the gate robust — revisit the todos-20 fixture / budget headroom / estimator (more rounds, median-of-medians, or a looser p95). Prefer (a) if emission can tighten without clarity cost; else (b). Standalone; do NOT bury in another PR. Evidence: a worker proved .91 produces byte-identical ui-bench.js output, so the red was pure flake.
notes:
DECISION (Fable delegated, 2026-07-13 08:59 AUSEST): ADOPT Codex's contract-matched baseline. Do NOT demote todos-20 to evidence-not-gate, and do NOT widen its budget. Split G-1's keyed-row measurement into (i) a compiler-overhead gate against a memo-matched hand baseline at the unchanged 1.10 p50/p95, and (ii) a non-gating, labelled "always-memo SSR policy cost" number retained from the current unwrapped baseline.

WEIGHED: Fable (worker draft) recommended (d) demote + (a) chase; Codex disagreed with a contract-matched split. I verified both of Codex's technical corrections against the source and they are TRUE, which is decisive:
- Comparator is created ONCE PER DEFVIEW, not once per row. emit_cljs.cljc emit-defview splices (comparator-form ...) into the single (def vname (runtime/memo-view render comparator display)) form (lines ~404-408). For todos-20 the todo-row comparator + memo wrapper exist once at the todo-row var; the 20 rows are just JSX elements referencing that one memo component. Fable's "20 comparator closures per row" is factually WRONG.
- Key-coercion / duplicate-key work is goog.DEBUG-guarded and ABSENT from the :advanced run. emit-for wraps (check-key! seen kexpr) + the double key-eval in (when ^boolean js/goog.DEBUG ...) (emit_cljs.cljc ~251-254); the key expr passes straight to jsx3/jsxs3. Fable's "defensive key-coercion the compiler does" is WRONG for the production build.
Fable itself labelled its "where the 10% goes" as an unprofiled hypothesis; the code resolves it against Fable. The real, verified confound: bench/views.cljs todo-list renders [todo-row {:key ..}] where todo-row is a defview => React.memo-wrapped once via runtime/memo-view; bench/hand.cljs todo-row* (line 76) is a BARE unwrapped function component. G-1 uses renderToStaticMarkup (initial SSR), where memoization yields ZERO benefit but adds ~20 memo-component hops on the compiled side only. So the gate charges the compiler for the always-memo POLICY, not for lowering OVERHEAD -- apples-to-oranges. This also explains Fable's "more rounds => fails more (7/10)": the true unwrapped ratio genuinely converges on ~1.11 because the policy cost is real and stable; that is a reason to fix the DENOMINATOR, not to demote. Demotion (d) would discard the single most discriminating codegen fixture (Codex: #5703's first run caught a real flag-map lowering regression at 1.51 p50 / 1.37 p95) precisely when the substrate is pre-alpha. The matched-baseline split neither threshold-tunes (budget stays 1.10) nor pretends the ratio is 1.0 -- it satisfies the "bench red escalates, never threshold-tune" posture better than demotion while costing only a modest baseline-authoring effort. Codex's per-defview-comparator correction is VERIFIED TRUE and it moves the attributed 10% from "per-row comparator/key-coercion" (a lowering cost that demotion or emission-tweaks would target) to "the always-memo component hop" (a policy cost that the matched baseline isolates) -- which is why the recommendation flips.

IMPLEMENTATION (the concrete gate change; leave to an implementation worker -- this bead stays OPEN):
1. Add a contract-matched hand baseline for the row in bench/hand.cljs: React.memo-wrap todo-row* with a one-slot comparator over the "todo" prop, semantics-matched to the compiled todo-row rf= comparator (todo-row's header is [{:keys [todo]}] -> single slot "todo", no children). Add a matched todo-list*-memo variant that renders the memo-wrapped row. Memo is SSR-transparent, so this baseline stays byte-identical to the compiled output on renderToStaticMarkup -- byte-equality precheck holds against it.
2. Gate compiled todo-list against THAT matched baseline at the existing budget {:p50 1.10 :p95 1.10} in bench/main.cljs. This measures compiler/lowering overhead only.
3. Keep the existing UNWRAPPED-hand ratio in out/ui-bench.json AND the CI summary as a LABELLED non-gating "always-memo SSR policy cost" number. Never delete/hide it; it must never become green-by-exclusion.
4. Retain byte-equality precheck + emitted-JS golden as HARD gates, unchanged.
5. Print ratios and limits to >= 4 decimal places so a displayed 1.10 cannot fail an inclusive <= 1.10 comparison (Codex's marginal-rounding point).
6. Acceptance: the matched gate must show real headroom (target >= ~0.03 below 1.10 on both p50 and p95 across repeated runs); AND a controlled slow-path/lowering-regression fixture (e.g. the classes-str flag-map lowering shape from #5703, or an equivalent) must STILL fail the matched gate -- proving the new denominator has not blinded the discriminating signal that made todos-20 valuable.

SCOPE (no gold-plating, pre-alpha posture): REJECT the speculative emission optimizations (comparator hoisting / skip key-coercion) as work items -- verified moot: the comparator is already per-defview and key-coercion is DEBUG-only, absent from :advanced; there is no avoidable per-row work to hoist. The broader browser 3-case always-memo client-scenario benchmark (initial mount / rf=-equal parent rerender / single-row update) that Codex floats to adjudicate the always-memo policy is an OPTIONAL FOLLOW-UP (file separately if pursued), NOT part of this fix -- the labelled raw product-cost number already surfaces the SSR side honestly. Do not build a broad benchmark framework. Any future emission-optimization proposal must name a measured hot op and show improvement on both the matched ratio and a relevant client scenario.

SOURCE: ai/decisions/rf2-xwmpm4.g1-parity-gate-marginal.md (deleted after this ruling). Code verified: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/emit_cljs.cljc (emit-defview memo-view wrap + comparator-form + emit-for DEBUG-guarded key check), implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/runtime.cljs (memo-view), implementation/ui/bench/{main,views,hand}.cljs, implementation/scripts/run-ui-bench.cjs.
MIKE DIRECT RULING 2026-07-13 — approved Codex recommendation: G-1 computes p50/p95 from per-sample paired `compiled / matched-hand` ratios, preserving the existing 1.10 limits. Do not divide independently aggregated compiled and hand medians/percentiles; that destroys covariance and can false-red a shared-noise run. Keep the labelled non-gating unwrapped always-memo policy-cost series, byte-equality precheck, emitted-JS golden, >=4-decimal reporting, repeated-run headroom, and mutation/discriminating-slow-path proof from the earlier ruling.
close_reason: Completed in PR #5812 (merged 1820baecb8): memo-matched G-1 baseline and optimized lowering are stable, exact-head CI green

title: (TEST) Pin join-reap reason and already-auto-destroyed final-child composition
description:
The closed source bead rf2-tj3l6a explicitly requires terminal-consistency coverage for "already-auto-destroyed final children." PR #5772 adds three strong non-final-child fixtures (:any success, :any failure, :all), but all use `mk-child`, whose `:done` and `:failed` states are plain maps with no `:final?`. No test drives the composed case where the child reaches a top-level `:final?`, auto-destroys synchronously with `:reason :rf.machine/finished`, and its queued completion event later resolves the parent's join.

That composed path matters to the new reap design. When the parent eventually builds `[:rf.machine/destroy {:rf/actor-id ... :rf/reason :rf.machine/join-reaped}]`, every liveness signal is already gone and the reap must be a silent no-op: no second `:rf.machine/destroyed`, no join-reaped trace for a dead actor, no cancellation terminal, and no mutation of a replacement actor that might reuse an id. The existing silent-idempotent tests cover an explicit keyword destroy after auto-finalization and a non-final spawn-all resolution/exit double sweep, but not the new direct-actor reap carrier after a final child's join completion.

The new tests also never assert the positive destroyed-trace reason for a live non-final completed child. They infer absence of cancellation from work-statuses, but a wrong non-explicit reason would pass. Pin both sides so the new lifecycle vocabulary has an executable signal before the spec-catalogue follow-up lands.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add a `:spawn-all` fixture whose decisive child dispatches its join completion while entering a top-level `:final?` and therefore auto-destroys before the parent handles the completion.
- Parent join resolution remains correct, the child's terminal work status is not `:cancelled`, and the later reap effect is silent-idempotent: exactly one destroyed lifecycle trace (`:rf.machine/finished`), no second `:rf.machine/join-reaped` destroyed trace, no leaked snapshot/timer/resource/spawn-order state.
- Add live non-final completed/failed child assertions that their actual `:rf.machine/destroyed` trace carries exactly `:reason :rf.machine/join-reaped` and no cancellation fields.
- Cover at least success and error finality, or document/prove why one parameterized fixture exercises the shared path.
- Tests fail if completed children are routed back through `:explicit`, if the reap reason is misspelled/substituted, or if a dead final child emits a second destroyed trace.
close_reason: Closed

title: (BUG) Surface untyped observation on-change failures before disposal boundaries swallow them
description:
PR #5766 added per-lease containment to `drain-pending-disposals!`: every former owner is notified, typed re-frame exceptions are fanned to the always-on error axis, and the first escape is rethrown after the drain. The implementation and its own docstring acknowledge that both real drain boundaries discard that rethrow: the `:hmr` drain runs inside registrar's replacement hook, whose per-hook catch drops failures, and the `:disposed` drain runs in an unobserved next-tick Future.

However, `report-disposal-notify-escape!` is called only when `(ex-data t)` carries `:rf.error/id`. An ordinary untyped exception from an `on-change` callback (TypeError, AssertionError, RuntimeException, or a bug before typed wrapping) is accumulated and rethrown, then silently swallowed at either production boundary. Lines 551-553 claim that such a bug "still propagates via the drain's rethrow-after-drain", but it does not propagate to any observer at the actual boundaries. This leaves the second half of closed bead rf2-vxgfnd.28 (the escape must be visible, not only non-starving) incomplete for untyped failures.

This is actionable even though `on-change` is host-internal: a defect in the re-frame.ui callback is precisely the kind of bug that must not disappear during HMR/disposal. Preserve the per-lease drain and typed catalogue identity, but give untyped escapes a production-survivable report path (for example a stable catalogued wrapper id whose cause is the original exception) before the boundary drops the throw. Do not double-fan already typed errors.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fixture with two leases proves an untyped exception from the first `on-change` does not starve the second and produces exactly one observable always-on error record at both `:hmr` and `:disposed` boundaries.
- Typed re-frame errors retain their original catalogue id and are not double-reported.
- The first exception may still be rethrown after draining for direct callers, but correctness does not depend on registrar/Future callers observing that throw.
- Spec 006/009 and the observation docstrings accurately describe typed and untyped containment/visibility.
notes: HELD until #5774 (.14) merges — observation.cljc (surface untyped on-change failures before disposal swallows them). #5774 is pending on observation.cljc. Dispatch after it lands.
close_reason: Closed

title: (BUG) Do not cancel completed spawn-all work during join teardown
description:
## Problem

PR #5763 (head `9dd625e2dd4287193107ee2d4ece7cddaa335040`) correctly closes the runtime leak by destroying every `:spawn-all` child when a join resolves, including a child that reported completion from a non-`:final?` terminal state and therefore remains a live actor. However, it routes those completed children through the ordinary `[:rf.machine/destroy spawned-id]` effect.

The ordinary destroy path uses reason `:explicit`. `lifecycle-fx.traces/emit-destroyed!` defines every explicit destroy as cancellation of an in-progress actor and adds a `cancelled-actor-reply`. For a completed join child, the join interceptor has already emitted `join-child-reply` for the same canonical work-id, with `:status :ok` / `:rf.reply/work-status :completed` (or `:status :error` / `:failed`). The subsequent destroy therefore emits a second terminal outcome for the exact same `[:rf.work/machine spawned-id invoke-id generation]`: `:status :cancelled` / `:work-status :cancelled`.

That violates the “one child attempt, one work-id” and closed terminal-status contract. Xray or a future durable work ledger cannot truthfully decide whether the decisive child completed, failed, or was cancelled. The new lifecycle fixture asserts that both snapshots disappear, but it does not inspect the emitted reply facts, so CI remains green despite the contradictory trace stream.

Surviving siblings are different: they have not reported completion, so their explicit destroy is legitimately a cancellation and must retain the existing `cancelled-on-join-resolution` plus destroyed-cancellation behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Define a `:spawn-all` `:any` join whose child reports `:on-child-done` from a plain non-`:final?` state, as in `spawn_all_lifecycle_leak_test.clj`.
2. Dispatch the decisive child's completion and capture machine traces.
3. Observe the join resolution trace for that spawned child/work-id with `:rf.reply/status :ok` and `:rf.reply/work-status :completed`.
4. Observe the new destroy effect for the same completed child emit `:rf.machine/destroyed` with the same work-id and `:rf.reply/status :cancelled` / `:rf.reply/work-status :cancelled` because its reason defaults to `:explicit`.
5. The same contradiction occurs on the failed-child path (`:error` followed by `:cancelled`). A survivor correctly has only cancellation outcomes.

## Deliverable

Separate “teardown a live actor after its join work has already completed/failed” from “cancel in-progress actor work.” Keep all lifecycle cleanup introduced by #5763—snapshot, handler, timers, resource leases, HTTP work, system-id, classification, spawn-order—but do not emit a cancellation terminal reply for a completed or failed child. Preserve an honest destroyed lifecycle trace if useful, with an explicit non-cancellation reason/shape consistent with Spec 005 and Spec 009. Do not suppress legitimate cancellation for unresolved survivors or direct/cascade destroy of in-progress actors.
acceptance_criteria:
- A success-side completed join child has one canonical terminal result for its work-id (`:ok`/`:completed`) and is never later classified `:cancelled` merely because resolution tears down its still-live actor.
- A failed join child similarly retains `:error`/`:failed` as its sole terminal work result.
- An unresolved survivor destroyed on join resolution still emits the existing cancellation classification and join-resolution attribution.
- Completed/failed non-final children are fully torn down at resolution even when the parent does not exit the `:spawn-all` state; no lifecycle leak is reintroduced.
- Trace fixtures group events by `:rf.reply/work-id` and prove terminal-status consistency for `:all`, success-side `:any`, failure-side `:any`, and already-auto-destroyed final children.
- Spec 005, Spec 009, reply helpers, and destroy/join docstrings agree on which teardown reasons are cancellations and which are post-completion cleanup.
- Xray/work-ledger projection has a deterministic single terminal outcome for every affected work-id.
close_reason: PR #5772 opened. Completed :spawn-all join children reaped via new non-cancellation :rf.machine/join-reaped reason instead of the :explicit destroy — no second (contradictory) :cancelled terminal for an already-terminal child's work-id; surviving siblings keep :explicit cancellation + cancelled-on-join-resolution. #5763's teardown (no leak) preserved identically. Reply-stream tests (group by :rf.reply/work-id) prove exactly-one-terminal for :all / success-:any / failure-:any + survivor still cancels; double-terminal reproduced on reverted code. Gates: machines JVM 965/3075 0-fail, CLJS node-test 9039/42664 0-fail. Spec-catalogue follow-up for the new reason: rf2-280kc2 (dispatch after merge).

title: (BUG) Reject malformed root fallback :on cleanly in machines-viz
description:
## Problem

PR #5762 (head `bd432c914aa96a00d74c807486522e739c7ae3e1`) makes malformed state-node `:on` and `:after` clauses produce clean `definition-defect` values rather than host exceptions. The same validation is not applied to the supported flat-machine root fallback `:on` surface.

`node-defect` now reaches `transition-target-defect`, which checks that a state node's `:on` is a map before iterating it. A flat root definition is validated separately by `root-on-target-defect`; that function still iterates `(:on definition)` without a shape guard. Consequently `{:initial :a :states {:a {}} :on :retry}` throws `IllegalArgumentException: Don't know how to create ISeq from: clojure.lang.Keyword` instead of returning `{:category :rf.error/machine-bad-on-clause ...}`. `valid-definition?` and emitter entry points can therefore throw on precisely the malformed-input path this PR intended to make robust.

This is not an unsupported arbitrary key: root-level `:on` is the documented ancestor-fallback transition surface for a flat machine, analogous to region-root fallbacks in parallel machines. Validation must cover every scope that consumes that grammar.

## Steps to Reproduce

From `tools/machines-viz`, evaluate:

```clojure
(require '[day8.re-frame2-machines-viz.grammar :as g])
(g/definition-defect {:initial :a :states {:a {}} :on :retry})
```

At #5762's merged head this throws `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` while the analogous malformed nested state-node `:on` returns the catalogued defect. The same exception escapes callers such as `valid-definition?` and the Mermaid/SCXML/DOT emission path that first validates the definition.

## Deliverable

Validate root fallback transition-slot shape before iteration and return the same catalogued structural category used for malformed state-node `:on` clauses. Centralize or deliberately share the slot-shape rule so flat root, compound state, region root, and parallel root scopes cannot drift. Preserve the engine's actual fallback precedence and do not accept malformed maps merely to keep emission running.
acceptance_criteria:
- `definition-defect` returns a deterministic `:rf.error/machine-bad-on-clause` defect for a flat root `:on` whose value is not a map; it does not throw a host collection exception.
- `valid-definition?` returns false and each public emitter returns its documented invalid-definition outcome for the malformed root fixture.
- Fixtures cover malformed `:on` at flat root, ordinary state node, region root, and parallel root wherever those scopes support fallback transitions.
- Valid root fallback `:on` definitions still emit correctly, including handler normalization and ancestor-fallback precedence matching the runtime engine.
- The defect exposes only structural coordinates/category and does not leak arbitrary malformed application values.
- The implementation avoids separate unchecked iteration paths that can reintroduce state/root validation drift.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5769 (commit e52d27d): centralized transition-slot-shape-defect applied at flat root / region root / parallel root as well as state nodes; malformed root :on returns clean :rf.error/machine-bad-on-clause defect (was uncaught ISeq exception).

title: (BUG) Reconcile Spec 005 guidance for targeted internal self-transitions
description:
## Problem

PR #5761 (head `003884a2b41feef3b055ff8cbe526e6763e187fb`) correctly changes the runtime docstring for an explicit same-state target: without `:reenter?`, the target node itself is preserved while compound descendants are exited and re-resolved from the target's initial state. The authoritative rules in Spec 005's `Self-transitions` section, its conformance summary, and `Spec-Schemas.md` agree.

However, two later anti-pattern bullets in `spec/005-StateMachines.md` still describe the old, broader equivalence:

- “Using a self-target without reentry expecting a reset” says the transition is observationally identical to a targetless internal transition and leaves the configuration unchanged.
- “Using `:reenter?` when you only wanted an internal data update” advises either omitting the target or targeting the same state, as if those choices have identical descendant behavior.

That is true only for a leaf target. It is false for a compound state. If `:process` currently has descendant `:step3`, then a targetless transition preserves `:step3`, while `{:target :process}` without `:reenter?` preserves `:process` itself but exits `:step3` and enters `:process`'s initial descendant (for example `:step1`). The contradictory anti-pattern guidance can therefore make users choose a transition with different statechart behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read `spec/005-StateMachines.md` §Self-transitions: the table/rules distinguish targetless preservation from targeted internal descendant re-resolution.
2. Read the anti-pattern bullets headed “Using a self-target without reentry expecting a reset” and “Using `:reenter?` when you only wanted an internal data update” later in the same spec.
3. Apply both descriptions to a compound state `:process` whose active leaf is `:step3` and whose initial leaf is `:step1`.
4. The normative rule predicts `:step1` after an explicit internal self-target; the anti-pattern prose predicts unchanged `:step3`.

## Deliverable

Reconcile the anti-pattern guidance with the authoritative targeted-internal semantics. State explicitly that targetless and explicit same-state transitions are equivalent only where there are no active descendants to re-resolve. Give a small compound-state example that makes the distinction tangible. Audit the machine guide/spec summaries for the same obsolete “configuration unchanged” or “identical to targetless” claim, while preserving the ratified XState-v5-compatible runtime behavior introduced before #5761.
acceptance_criteria:
- The two contradictory anti-pattern bullets in `spec/005-StateMachines.md` no longer claim general equivalence between a targetless transition and an explicit internal self-target.
- The documentation states the leaf-state equivalence as a limited case and states that a compound self-target re-resolves descendants from the target's initial configuration.
- A compact `:process/:step3 -> :process/:step1` example (or an equally concrete example) distinguishes the two forms.
- An audit finds and corrects the same obsolete wording in machine guides, schema prose, and examples without changing the ratified runtime semantics.
- Existing conformance tests for targetless preservation, internal compound self-target descendant reset, and `:reenter? true` full exit/re-entry remain green.
notes: HELD until #5765 (lq5yo3) MERGES — d0r6z7 touches spec/005 (targeted internal self-transitions reconciliation), and #5765 just edited spec/005 (hot-zone). Dispatch once #5765 lands.
close_reason: Reconciled the two stale Drain-semantics-gotchas bullets in spec/005-StateMachines.md with the XState-v5 internal-by-default semantics (PR #5771). Spec-Schemas.md audited — already correct, no edit. Doc-slug gate green; no normative rule changed.

title: (BUG) Make re-entrant multi-cell flush semantics order-independent
description:
## Problem

PR #5759 correctly completes each ViewCell before invoking the DEBUG evidence sink, but `flush-scope!` still removes the whole matching batch from `dirty-cells` and then completes/delivers cells one at a time from an identity set. That makes the promised re-entrant behavior depend on arbitrary set iteration order.

With two pending cells A and B, suppose A is processed first and its evidence sink (or another synchronous callback reached by A's revision notification) invalidates B. B has already been removed from `dirty-cells` but still has `:dirty? true`, because its own `flush-one!` has not run. `mark-dirty! B` therefore folds evidence into B's old window and refuses to re-enrol it. B's later `flush-one!` clears that mark as part of the old batch. If B happened to be processed before A, the same re-entrant mark opens a fresh pending window. The number and boundary of correction windows therefore depend on set order.

The new `flush-one!` docstring claims a re-entrant sink that re-marks "this (or any) cell" always enrols a fresh window. The #5759 regression only tests re-marking the same cell, after that cell was already cleared; it does not exercise a different cell that remains in the drained-but-not-completed batch. rf2-vxgfnd.73's acceptance criterion explicitly required same-or-another-cell behavior.

This is primarily a dev/debug correctness issue because the arbitrary evidence sink is DEBUG-only, but the same sequencing also invokes useSyncExternalStore listeners before later cells have completed. The production outcome may still be value-correct because B's one later revision reads the newest value, so do not force an extra render merely for ceremony; the contract must explicitly rule whether re-entrant invalidations join the current correction batch or open the next one, and implement that rule deterministically.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create dirty ViewCells A and B in one `flush-scope!` batch.
2. Install an evidence sink that, when called for A, calls `mark-dirty! B`.
3. Force/observe the order A then B.
4. A is cleared before the sink runs, but B is still `:dirty? true` and absent from `dirty-cells`; the re-mark does not enrol B.
5. B's subsequent old-batch flush clears the re-entrant evidence/mark. Reverse the iteration order and B instead opens a fresh pending window.
6. Compare pending count, revision count, and evidence boundaries across both forced orders.

## Deliverable

Rule and implement deterministic re-entrant semantics for a multi-cell drain. The preferred shape is an explicit batch phase boundary: complete scheduler state for all drained cells before invoking arbitrary debug consumers, then deliver the captured evidence after completion; if useSyncExternalStore listener notification can create the same order dependence, separate state completion from notification or document/prove why listener re-entry safely joins the current batch. Preserve the core rule that all queued write sides drain before one read-side render batch; do not turn N invalidations into N renders.

Keep sink throws contained, deliver each original captured summary once, preserve newly created next-batch evidence, and retain the advanced-production DCE envelope.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic two-cell test forces A-then-B and B-then-A while A's sink re-marks B; both orders yield the same ruled pending/revision/evidence outcome.
- The test covers a re-entrant sink that marks another not-yet-processed cell, not only the already-cleared current cell.
- If the rule is "next batch", the re-entrant mark remains enrolled with its own evidence and flushes once at the next boundary. If the rule is "join current batch", the docs and rf2-vxgfnd.73 acceptance are corrected and the implementation proves no cause/evidence or required correction is lost; behavior remains order-independent.
- A throwing sink still cannot strand or abort any cell, and normal sinks still receive the pre-clear summary exactly once per original batch cell.
- Listener-induced re-entry is either covered by the same phase discipline or has a focused fixture proving it cannot produce an order-dependent lost correction.
- Production keeps one coalesced render batch after queued writes; no per-event/per-cell render regression and no DEBUG evidence machinery survives the advanced production gate.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5773 — two-phase run-flush-batch! (complete whole batch, then deliver) makes re-entrant multi-cell flush order-independent.

title: machines-viz SCXML codec: namespaced keyword whose NAME starts with an escaped char mints '___' (path-sep collision) → decodes to a vector
description: Pre-existing latent injectivity bug in the SCXML id codec, orthogonal to rf2-qgtcvy (found while testing that fix). keyword->id-string joins escaped-ns + '__' (ns-name-sep) + escaped-name. When the NAME segment's FIRST char is non-alphanumeric it escapes to a leading '_' (e.g. any CJK name -> '_u...', or ':a/-b' name '-b' -> '_2db'), so the boundary is <hex>+'__'+'_...' = '___' (triple underscore) — which unescape-id-string treats as the path-segment separator. Result: ':a/-b' (and ':登录/成功', etc.) round-trips through spec->scxml->scxml->spec to a VECTOR [:a ...] instead of the namespaced keyword, silently. Repro (currently commented out of scxml_cljs_test round-trip-non-latin1-ids namespaced sub-test). Fix options: (a) make ns-name-sep distinct from a marker that can prefix an escape (e.g. require the name-segment escaper to never start with a bare '_' at a boundary), or (b) length/framing-based ns/name split rather than substring-search on '__'/'___'. Surface: tools/machines-viz scxml.cljc (unescape-id-string / id-string->keyword / keyword->id-string) + tests. Not a regression from rf2-qgtcvy (old bare-hex escaped names also started with '_').
notes: HELD until #5762 (machines-viz codec) MERGES — same surface (scxml.cljc/grammar.cljc). Pre-existing latent bug (orthogonal to qgtcvy): a namespaced keyword whose NAME segment starts with an escaped char (any CJK name → leading _u, or :a/-b) mints ___ at the ns/name boundary, colliding with the path separator → decodes to a vector not the keyword. Dispatch on the machines-viz codec surface once #5762 lands.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5769 (commit 89bf8d6): SCXML ns/name marker changed __ -> - (a char the escaper never emits), removing the ___ path-sep collision at an escaped-leading-char name boundary. Namespaced-CJK + :a/-b round-trip now exact.

title: observation disposal-cause mislabel: thread cause from cache disposal sites (rf2-x76af2.34 FINDING 1)
description:
rf2-x76af2.34 FINDING 1 (the primary correctness finding) could NOT be fixed under the rf2-vxgfnd.70 worker's surface (observation.cljc only) and is filed here as the follow-up.

## Problem (verified against current code, post-#5753)
The observation port's `enqueue-disposal!` is the SINGLE enqueue path for every node-disposed notification regardless of cause. The cause is assigned solely by WHICH drain boundary fires:
- the registrar HMR replacement hook drains the WHOLE queue with `:hmr`
- the next-tick fallback drains with `:disposed`

So a frame-destroy / cache-clear lease still pending when an unrelated `:sub` re-registration runs is swept into the synchronous `:hmr` drain and delivered `{:cause :hmr}` — a documented `on-change` payload contract violation. A consumer branching `:hmr` (re-acquire same target) vs `:disposed` (target gone) would, on the mislabel, re-acquire against a destroyed frame -> `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` -> view error boundary.

#5753 (.28 per-lease drain containment + .37 weak reaction ref) did NOT thread cause — confirmed against current observation.cljc.

## Why it needs a cross-ns change (out of the .70 worker's surface)
The cause is only known at the four disposal sites in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/cache.cljc`:
- `invalidate-sub-on-replace!`  -> :hot-reload  (=> :hmr)
- `dispose-all-for-frame-destroy!` -> :frame-destroy (=> :disposed)
- `clear-sub-cache!` -> :cache-clear (=> :disposed)
- `dispose-entry-now!` -> :no-more-derefers (=> :disposed)

Each already knows its reason (it emits `:rf.sub/dispose` with it) but calls `interop/dispose!` with only the reaction; the observation `node-disposed-hook` fires with no cause. The port cannot recover the cause at enqueue time from within observation.cljc: HMR and cache-clear are both live-frame; only the disposal SITE distinguishes them. `subs.cache` is required BY `observation`, so it cannot statically require back — plumbing needs a late-bound `*disposal-cause*`/thread-local set by each cache site around its `interop/dispose!`, OR a cause param on the port's enqueue path.

## Fix
Carry the intended cause WITH each queued entry (store `[lease cause]` pairs, or two cause-keyed queues) so `drain-pending-disposals!` delivers each lease its OWN cause, and the registrar HMR hook drains only the `:hmr`-tagged entries, leaving `:disposed`-tagged frame-destroy/clear entries for the next-tick fallback. Have the four `subs/cache.cljc` disposal sites pass their reason into the observation enqueue (e.g. via a late-bound obs cause var bound around each `interop/dispose!`, or a dedicated port callback). `:hot-reload`->:hmr; the other three->:disposed.

Note: `subs/cache.cljc` is a hot-zone-adjacent shared file — sequence, don't parallel, with other subs-cache work.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture enqueues a frame-destroy (or cache-clear) lease, then fires an HMR :sub re-registration drain while that lease is still pending, and asserts the frame-destroy lease STILL receives {:cause :disposed}, never :hmr. Complements (does NOT duplicate) rf2-vxgfnd.29's :disposed-cause drain coverage. Existing HMR/:disposed fixtures stay green; the port stays within its documented cause enum.
notes: HELD until #5758 (.70+x34 observation) MERGES — r8jmdb touches observation.cljc's enqueue side (in-flight in #5758) + subs/cache.cljc's 4 disposal sites. Dispatch once #5758 lands so it rebases on the honest-readiness + weak-ref changes. Surface: subs/cache.cljc (pass cause) + observation.cljc (accept cause per queued entry, late-bound). This is the intrinsic-cause fix x76af2.34 FINDING 1 / .82 pointed at.
close_reason: PR #5766: intrinsic disposal cause threaded from subs/cache.cljc's 4 disposal sites into the observation port via late-bound *disposal-cause*; queue stores [lease cause] pairs; drain partitions by intrinsic cause. Gates green.

title: Machines parallel :data leaks into a later region's guard SELECTION within one macrostep
description: Machines review-wave 2026-07-12 finding #1 — DECISION-FLAGGED (XState parity). parallel.cljc reduce-regions: :all-state + :tags are frozen to the pre-event view (599-600) but :data is threaded region→region (cur-data) and seeded into each region snapshot (676-677) BEFORE that region's transition is selected — so a later region's guard observes an earlier region's SAME-macrostep :data write. Contradicts the code's OWN stated invariant (576-579: 'selection declaration-order-INDEPENDENT, selects against the pre-event context, then applies') and diverges from XState v5/v6 select-then-apply. Scenario: region :a :a1--e-->:a2 action {:data (assoc data :flag true)}; region :b :b1--e[guard (:flag data)]-->:b2. From {:a :a1 :b :b1} data {} dispatch [:e]: XState both guards select vs {} → B stays. re-frame2 region-order [:a :b]: A applies, cur-data {:flag true}, B's guard passes → different config PURELY by declaration order. Same leak at settle-birth (~1577). DECISION for Mike: (a) add frozen-data alongside frozen-all-state/tags, SELECT every region vs it then APPLY threading :data (XState parity — my lean); OR (b) if cross-region :data-flow-into-selection is INTENTIONAL, retract the 'declaration-order-independent/pre-event context' invariant + document the divergence (per XState-v6-parity protocol, a blessed divergence is Mike's call). Surface: parallel.cljc + test. Do NOT dispatch until ruled.
notes:
RULED (a) but HELD until #5761 (cttpk4) MERGES — lq5yo3's SELECT/APPLY split uses the pick-transition seam at transition.cljc:1376, and #5761 is pending on transition.cljc. Also touches spec/005 (HOT-ZONE — sequence). Dispatch on the parallel.cljc+transition.cljc surface once #5761 lands.
RECONCILE (decision-file cleanup 2026-07-13 09:05 AUSEST): ai/decisions/rf2-lq5yo3.parallel-data-selection.md reviewed in full (incl. its Codex section) and deleted as redundant. Codex ratifies the shipped ruling (a) with external-standards citations (W3C SCXML selectTransitions/microstep, Stately parallel-states, current XState macrostep/selectEventlessTransitions source) and confirms #5765's event SELECT/APPLY split is sound. Its ONLY novel content — a 5-step select-then-apply completion contract + paired A->B/B->A birth+event fixtures for the :always/birth stabilization residual — is already owned by rf2-slfhkx (DECISION-FLAGGED); not re-litigated here. No new material contests or improves the shipped :on (event-transition) fix.
close_reason: SELECT/APPLY split shipped in PR #5765 — freezes :data for parallel transition selection; leak proven pre-fix (3 fails) then green; residual (:always sibling-:data reads) documented in spec/005:1731. Gates: machines JVM 962/0, cljs 9030/0, doc-slugs 0.

title: machines-viz id codec: variable-length hex escape breaks injectivity + round-trip >U+00FF
description: Machines review-wave 2026-07-12 finding #3. grammar.cljc:881 encode escape-id-segment emits _<hex> variable-length (format %02x / .toString 16 on the full code point) but scxml.cljc:239 decode matches EXACTLY two hex digits (#"_([0-9a-fA-F]{2})") — neither self-delimiting nor reversible above 0xFF, contradicting the codec's 'distinct inputs → distinct outputs' / 'ANY keyword round-trips EXACTLY' contract. (a) round-trip corruption: CJK :开始 → _5f00_59cb → decodes to :_00Ycb silently wrong; (b) encode collision: \u0111 → _111 AND segment \u0011+'1' → _11+1 → _111 → two paths mint the same node id (xyflow drops a node / mermaid merges / SCXML dup xsd:ID — the rf2-mnp93.6 collision class, in the >0xFF regime). FIX: fixed-width/self-delimiting escape for the full code point (e.g. _uXXXX_) + widen decode regex, OR restrict/normalise ids to Latin-1 at ingestion. Also file-together the machines-viz robustness minors: grammar.cljc:659-668 non-map :on/:after throws uncaught ISeq instead of clean :invalid-definition; mermaid.cljc label-value renders inline-fn guards via pr-str (#object[...]); scxml.cljc:914 parse-attrs matches only double-quoted attrs despite claiming single+double (single-quoted id='idle' keys under nil). Surface: tools/machines-viz grammar.cljc/scxml.cljc/mermaid.cljc + tests.
close_reason: Closed

title: Machines final-state auto-destroy omits spawn-order/forget! (strands liveness bit)
description: Machines review-wave 2026-07-12 finding #2. finalize.cljc:540-552 (:final?-auto-destroy) replicates every teardown step EXCEPT spawn-order/forget! — so a finished actor stays in (spawn-order/frame-order frame), the bit destroy.cljc:83 actor-live? calls 'the most reliable alive-or-gone bit'. Scenario: child :worker#1 reaches :final? leaf → finalize-machine runs but :worker#1 remains in spawn-order → a later stale [:rf.machine/destroy :worker#1] sees it live → teardown-live-actor! RE-RUNS → phantom :rf.machine/destroyed trace + re-fires resource release (violates silent-idempotent destroy); frame teardown also emits phantom :parent-frame-destroyed. FIX: require re-frame.machines.spawn-order in finalize + (spawn-order/forget! frame-id machine-id) alongside the other synchronous teardown side-effects. Surface: finalize.cljc + test.
close_reason: Closed

title: Story result->reports silently drops a run-level :error verdict
description: Causa/Story review-wave finding (2026-07-12). tools/story/src/re_frame/story/result.cljc:1005-1033 (public re-export story.cljc:1544 / is at :1651): the run-level cond in result->reports has branches for :fail/:cannot-run/vacuous-:pass but NO branch for :status :error. A schema-conforming {:status :error :assertions []} → per-assertion [] → worst aggregates :pass → every cond clause keyed to non-:error → run-level []; emit-reports! fires nothing → cljs.test tallies zero → deftest reads GREEN on the most severe verdict. Exactly the silent-pass class the ns exists to prevent. (Not triggered by the in-repo run path today since run-result always backs :error with an :error assertion — latent gap in the PUBLIC projection API.) FIX: add a run-level branch mirroring :fail — (and (= :error status) (not-any? #(= :error (:type %)) per-assertion)) → [{:type :error :message "run :error — the runner errored"}]. Surface: result.cljc + its test.

CLJS-only. f13zth: result->reports gained an :error run-level branch (gated not-any? per-assertion :error) so a bare :status :error no longer projects [] (silent green). title: Finish the native ui/frame-provider manifest and fully row re-frame.ui
description:
PR #5754 correctly adds the missing namespace-specific manifest row for `re-frame.ui/frame-root`, but it closes rf2-vxgfnd.71 after deliberately leaving the other half of that bead incomplete. `re-frame.ui/frame-provider` is already a live public compile-marker, is accepted by the compiler, appears throughout Spec 004 and the guide as the supported SCOPE form, and is included in the JVM `export-surface-is-exactly-the-blessed-set` assertion as an S2c public export. Yet it remains absent from `spec/API.md` §Compiled views and from the API manifest, while `re-frame.ui` remains a curated direction-1 subset that cannot detect future accidental public exports.

The stated reason for deferral is no longer an unresolved product decision. rf2-vxgfnd.24 records Mike's ruling: the native UI runtime will publish its React-context reader through the shared `:adapter/current-frame` hook, with the home in a UI-adapter namespace. That bead implements ambient resolution; it does not remove or internalize the supported `ui/frame-provider` grammar. Therefore the API classification is sequenced behind .24's implementation, but its outcome is known: `frame-provider` remains the native SCOPE form and must receive its own `re-frame.ui` row at the actual S2 stage.

Finish the manifest/API reconciliation after .24 lands. Update the exact-export-set language so it distinguishes the historical S1 set from the current staged public surface, row `frame-provider` at S2 with the correct kind/tier/owner, regenerate the manifest, and make `re-frame.ui` fully rowed. The reverse-direction gate is important: a first-party, closed compiler grammar should not accumulate unclassified public Vars silently.

This is a new follow-up because rf2-vxgfnd.71 is closed and its PR intentionally delivered only `frame-root`; do not reopen or mutate in-progress work.
acceptance_criteria:
1. After rf2-vxgfnd.24 lands, `spec/API.md` §Compiled views lists `re-frame.ui/frame-provider` as the supported S2 SCOPE form with its actual signature, front-porch tier, compile-marker function kind, and Spec 004 ownership.
2. The exact export-set prose and the live `ns-publics` assertion describe the same staged/current surface; the S1 baseline is not presented as the complete current namespace after S2 additions.
3. `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` and regenerated `spec/api-manifest.edn` contain a namespace-specific runtime-verified row for `re-frame.ui/frame-provider`; no core or legacy-adapter row is cited as a substitute.
4. The CLJS manifest probe marks `re-frame.ui` fully rowed. Adding an unclassified public Var fails direction-2 completeness, while removing or renaming a rowed Var fails direction-1 existence.
5. Intentional implementation helpers are private or explicitly `^:no-doc` according to the repository's real policy rather than hidden by leaving the entire namespace curated.
6. Probe/sidecar comments no longer call `frame-provider` decision-coupled or deferred once .24's already-ratified mechanism is implemented.
7. Manifest generation, API projection checks, JVM exact-export test, and CLJS enumeration probe all agree and pass.
8. UIx/Helix removal does not affect this row: it classifies the native `re-frame.ui` grammar only and introduces no compatibility shim.
close_reason: PR #5768 opened: frame-provider rowed in metadata sidecar + generated manifest + spec/API.md §Compiled views; re-frame.ui promoted to :fully-rowed (frame-root + frame-provider were the last two missing native exports, verified against the JVM blessed-set). All gates green: gen --check, api-md-check, story/xray/doc-api projections, check_doc_slugs.py, npm run test:cljs (9039 tests / 42665 assertions, 0 failures).

title: Make observation disposal causes intrinsic instead of drain-timing dependent
description:
The observation disposal queue currently stores only leases in `pending-disposals`; the cause is supplied later by whichever drain boundary wins. `enqueue-disposal!` always schedules an `interop/next-tick` fallback whose drain labels the whole claimed batch `:disposed`. During sub re-registration, the cache invalidation hook disposes the node and enqueues its owners, then a later registrar replacement hook synchronously drains the same global queue as `:hmr`.

Those two drains race on the JVM. `interop/next-tick` submits to a live single-thread executor, so it can run between the cache invalidation hook and the observation registrar hook. Whichever drain first executes `reset-vals!` claims the entries and retroactively supplies their cause. PR #5752, despite changing prose only, exposed the race in CI: `evidence-target-vector-is-bounded-with-a-loss-account` expected ten HMR invalidations but observed `#{:disposed :hmr}`. PR #5753 changes per-owner exception containment but retains this cause-by-drain-timing design.

The same representation can misclassify mixed backlog even without that exact race: an HMR boundary can drain older non-HMR disposals as `:hmr`, or the fallback can drain HMR entries as `:disposed`. The cause must be an intrinsic fact attached when disposal is initiated/enqueued, or derived from an authoritative scoped disposal reason, not inferred from which later consumer happens to empty a process-global queue. Keep notification delivery queued and coalesced, but preserve the correct cause independently for every lease entry.

This is production observability correctness: ViewCell evidence and Xray must distinguish registry replacement from ordinary disposal deterministically. Do not fix it by weakening the assertion or accepting both labels.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An HMR/re-registration disposal is always delivered with `:cause :hmr` on JVM and CLJS, regardless of whether the fallback executor/tick runs before, during, or after registrar replacement hooks.
2. A non-registrar frame destruction or explicit cache disposal is always delivered as `:disposed`; a later unrelated registration cannot relabel an older queued entry as HMR.
3. A deterministic JVM barrier forces the fallback task to contend with the registrar boundary and proves the label remains HMR; the regression fails on the current cause-by-drain-timing implementation.
4. A mixed-batch fixture queues at least one genuine HMR disposal and one genuine ordinary disposal before delivery and verifies each owner receives its own correct cause exactly once.
5. Per-lease exception containment from rf2-vxgfnd.28 remains intact: one bad callback cannot starve siblings, and cause preservation survives a throwing owner.
6. Coalescing remains bounded and exactly-once per disposed lease/node; no notification is duplicated merely because both registrar and fallback drains execute.
7. `reactive_epoch_cljs_test` remains strict (`#{:hmr}`, not an allowed union) and the focused JVM/core plus CLJS UI suites pass repeatedly without timing flakes.
8. Source/spec comments stop describing the drain boundary as the authority for cause if the corrected design makes enqueue/disposal origin authoritative.

Already in flight in the .70+x76af2.34 observation cluster (worker briefed to carry intrinsic cause per queued entry). If that fix needs the DISPOSING cache site in subs.cljc to pass the cause (outside the .70 worker's observation.cljc surface), .82 becomes that subs.cljc-side follow-up; else it closes with x76af2.34's PR. Do NOT double-dispatch.

title: Move the native re-frame.ui tear gate off the retiring UIx adapter
description:
PR #5750 adds the right end-to-end browser invariant for the watch-fired tear window: observation port -> ViewCell -> `useSyncExternalStore` -> React must publish the moved snapshot in a true microtask, before a paint-capable macrotask. However, the native `re-frame.ui` gate imports `re-frame.adapter.uix` and installs the UIx adapter solely because its derived values are `IWatchable`. UIx and Helix are explicitly transitional and will be removed. If the gate remains coupled to UIx, adapter removal either deletes this critical correctness proof or leaves the first-party UI suite depending on an artifact the migration intends to retire.

Move the gate onto the production observation path that `re-frame.ui` will retain. Prefer the first-party/native substrate used by the final runtime. If that watchable path is not implemented yet, make this bead part of that delivery rather than weakening the test to manual `ViewCell` calls or an IDeref-only fake: the important property is that an actual observed value movement fires the port callback and traverses the full uSES/React stack. Stock Reagent may remain as a frozen compatibility tier, but it should not become the architectural owner of the native gate unless the final substrate deliberately uses the same retained observation implementation.

This is migration completeness, not a request to preserve UIx. No new UIx-specific production abstraction should be added. The existing node-level scheduler fixture remains useful but is not a substitute for this real-browser integration gate.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `implementation/ui` browser tear tests no longer require or install `re-frame.adapter.uix`.
2. The replacement fixture uses the production observation/acquire/read/release path retained by first-party `re-frame.ui`, with a genuinely watch-fired value movement rather than direct `mark-dirty!` or manual `flush-pending!` calls.
3. The test still mounts two sibling ViewCells sharing one observable, performs all queued write-side work, and proves one coalesced read-side publication/render at the microtask checkpoint before a paint-capable macrotask.
4. The synchronous checkpoint remains old-but-consistent, the microtask checkpoint is new-and-consistent, and the macrotask checkpoint remains stable.
5. A mutation that schedules the reactive flush as a macrotask makes the browser test fail, preserving the regression discriminator established by PR #5750.
6. The gate runs in the normal browser CI lane after UIx/Helix source and dependencies are removed.
7. UIx removal work explicitly references this gate so deletion cannot silently drop coverage; no compatibility shim or new UIx production surface is introduced merely to keep the test alive.
notes: S2 BOUNDARY RECONCILIATION 2026-07-13: expand this open bead to deliver the already-frozen re-frame.ui/adapter row, not merely migrate one test. Current re-frame.ui exports no adapter; re-frame.ui.adapter only routes context reads through plain-atom, whose CLJS derived values are non-watchable and cannot drive production push updates. Deliver the retained watchable first-party React substrate, export ui/adapter, add init + artifact-isolation proofs, and move tear/Activity/reincarnation/teardown browser fixtures off UIx. This is completion of a frozen S2 API row, not a new contract choice. G-13 must run against this final adapter. No UIx/Helix shim.
