title: Report live-cache retry exhaustion without lying that the frame was destroyed
description:
## Problem

PR #5747 distinguishes a live-cache displacement from actual frame destruction by checking the frame incarnation and retrying, but when its fixed retry budget is exhausted while the incarnation is still live it passes the unchanged `{:recovery :frame-destroyed}` result to `throw-acquire-recovery!`.

The emitted condition is therefore `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` even though the code has just proved the targeted frame incarnation is live. This contradicts the PR/spec claim that the id is now reserved for verified destruction. Under a pathological but legal sequence of repeated HMR registrations/cache clears, an implementer or Xray user is told to recover a destroyed frame that was never destroyed.

The arbitrary budget of 32 also permits up to 33 rebuild attempts synchronously on the commit/acquire path before emitting that false diagnosis. Boundedness is good; reusing a known-false terminal classification is not.

## Deliverable

Give budget exhaustion an honest outcome. Prefer a distinct catalogued acquisition-instability/livelock condition carrying the frame, query, incarnation evidence, attempt count, and recovery, or return/retry through another already truthful ruled state. Never emit `frame-destroyed` while the captured incarnation is demonstrably live.

Keep retry bounded and preserve no-synchronous-fan-out/ref-count cleanup.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic displacer wins every build→canonical-check window through the retry limit while the same frame incarnation remains live; the terminal error is not `:rf.error/frame-destroyed`.
- The terminal diagnostic reports frame/query, attempt budget, and same-incarnation evidence with an actionable recovery; Spec 006 and Spec 009 catalogue the exact outcome.
- Genuine nil/changed-incarnation destruction still emits exactly one `:rf.error/frame-destroyed`.
- Every displaced/retried reaction releases input refs/watches/owners; the exhausted path leaves no cache/ref-count residue.
- Retry work is explicitly bounded and the selected budget is justified or configurable internally without adding public ceremony.
- Normal uncontended acquisition and one/few-displacement convergence retain their current hot-path shape and no-synchronous-`on-change` guarantee.
close_reason: PR #5766: acquire! retry-exhaustion over a live incarnation now throws the truthful :rf.error/observation-retry-exhausted (new always-on 009 row + Spec 006 prose + exercise literal), never a false frame-destroyed. Gates green.

title: Wire the custom-element reload ledger to a real source-manifest producer
description:
## Problem

PR #5744 implements a transactional custom-element reload ledger, but its headline zero-declaration and deleted-source fixes depend on `note-reloaded-sources!` being fed the sources that re-ran or disappeared. No production/compiler/shadow hook calls that function; outside tests it has zero callers.

Consequences in the actual browser reload path:

- If a source retains at least one declaration, emitted registrations populate `:staged`, so commit can replace that source.
- If it deletes its LAST declaration, it stages nothing. With `:touched` empty, `commit-reload!` never includes that source and its old ledger contribution remains live.
- If the source file is deleted, it neither stages nor calls any runtime code; again its old contribution remains.
- The tests pass because they call `note-reloaded-sources!` directly, proving the seam but not the shipped reload integration.

The PR body explicitly says the feed is left for reload machinery / decision-gated `rf2-df9873`. A self-contained uncalled seam does not fix the user-visible cases the PR and closed bead rf2-vxgfnd.67 claim are complete. REPL convergence has the same issue when removing the final form: absence cannot announce itself.

## Deliverable

Wire one authoritative successful-build/reload source manifest into the runtime reconciliation cycle. The producer must report current/reloaded/removed source identity even when a source emits zero declarations, scoped by real build id, and commit only after successful code load. Prefer reusing the compiler/build lifecycle authority rather than adding another watch protocol.

Keep the current transactional last-known-good behavior and direct production lookup. This is native compiler/HMR correctness, not adapter work.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real shadow/file-save integration fixture removes the last `ui/custom-element` form without calling `note-reloaded-sources!` from the test body; the stale runtime classification disappears after successful reload.
- Deleting/renaming a source file is reported by the real build/reload producer and evicts its contribution.
- Failed compilation/evaluation never commits the producer's candidate source set; the prior complete runtime manifest remains live.
- The source feed carries actual build id plus stable source identity, so equal namespace symbols in independent builds cannot evict one another.
- REPL re-evaluation has a ruled way to publish a zero-declaration source or explicitly documents a narrower supported lifecycle; tests match that real entry point rather than manually mutating the ledger.
- Existing staged replacement, multi-build isolation, and atomic one-swap aggregate rebuild stay green.
- Production classification remains a direct lookup; build/reload bookkeeping is dev/reload-only and elided from advanced production output.
notes: HELD until #5778 (.91) MERGES (not just worker-done — beads close on PR-open). .77 wires the custom-element reload ledger to a real source-manifest producer; .91 (#5778) restructured the custom-element compile-path reads (removed the global mirror, per-build element-properties reader) + interacts with phlhfd's build-sources. Dispatch .77 after #5778 lands so it builds on the corrected model + the shadow reload-cycle source-manifest (phlhfd #5777, merged).
close_reason: PR #5783 opened — wired reload-source-reset!/install-reload-source-producer! (SHADOW_NS_RESET producer) feeding note-reloaded-sources! in the shipped browser reload path; zero-declaration eviction now fires end-to-end through the production path (5 CLJS tests drive the shipped producer, not the seam directly). Orphan-file deletion stays bounded per df9873. Gates green: ui JVM 316/0, node-test-ui 295/0, core 9058/0.

title: Wire bounded ViewCell invalidation evidence into the native Xray projection
description:
## Problem

PR #5742 makes bounded ViewCell invalidation evidence readable and adds a global `set-evidence-sink!` callback, but it does not wire any real `re-frame.ui.tool` or Xray consumer. The evidence therefore still stops at an implementation seam. The originating rf2-vxgfnd.46 deliverable/AC required a specified projection consumed by Xray rather than dead cell state; the PR body calls this merely the “intended projection point” and defers the actual consumer.

A bare process-global setter is also not yet a complete tooling lifecycle contract: installing a second observer silently replaces the first, clearing/resetting the scheduler removes the sink, and there is no stable projection tying a ViewCell to root/view/site identity for Xray. Without an owned install/uninstall path, HMR and test/tool coexistence can clobber observation or retain stale consumers.

## Deliverable

Add the smallest first-party tool projection that turns the bounded summary into useful Xray evidence. Define stable identity/context for the flushed cell, install and release the consumer through a lifecycle-safe seam, and render/query the batch evidence without copying full event payloads. Keep the scheduler authoritative and tools observational; sequence after rf2-vxgfnd.73 so a tool failure cannot strand renders.

This is native re-frame.ui/Xray integration. Do not add compatibility plumbing to UIx, Helix, or reagent-slim, which are scheduled for removal.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real Xray or `re-frame.ui.tool` consumer receives each flushed batch's bounded evidence and associates it with stable root/view/cell identity useful to a developer.
- The projection exposes first/latest epoch, total invalidation count, causes, bounded targets, and the finalized honest loss field from rf2-vxgfnd.74 without retaining full event payloads.
- Consumer installation/uninstallation is identity-owned and HMR-safe; one tool cannot silently clear another owner's registration, and teardown releases all callbacks/references.
- A tool absent or closed has zero retained ViewCells/evidence; abandoned/unmounted cells disappear from the projection.
- Evidence-consumer exceptions are isolated per rf2-vxgfnd.73 and cannot alter render scheduling, revisions, or app state.
- Browser/tool integration coverage drives a real observation-port invalidation through ViewCell flush into the Xray projection, rather than calling the sink directly only.
- Advanced production output contains no Xray projection, evidence accumulation, subscriber registry, or diagnostic keywords when debug is disabled.

HELD for .74 merge — .75 (wire bounded ViewCell invalidation evidence into native Xray projection) CONSUMES the bounded-invalidation evidence that .74 (in-flight, reactive.cljc) is making semantically honest. Same evidence surface. Dispatch after .74 merges so Xray projects the corrected evidence. .75 is P2 + Causa/Story/Xray priority — prioritise it once unblocked.

Adds re-frame.ui.tool.evidence — identity-owned install!/uninstall! lifecycle over set-evidence-sink!, bounded per-cell accretion (first/latest epoch, count, batches, causes, capped targets, honest .74 loss field), stable cell-id/view-id/root-id identity, dead-cell pruning, debug-gated + prod-elision-proven. reactive.cljc +14/-1 (cell-view-id read + docstring). tools/xray untouched (spec unchanged). All local gates green (ui JVM 400/5311, test:ui 412/2103, browser 339/1825, prod-elision 80/261 + gate PASS, fast-pr spine PASS). Leave open for mayor to close at merge.

title: Isolate evidence-sink failures from ViewCell flush completion
description:
## Problem

PR #5742 introduces a global debug/tool `evidence-sink` and calls it synchronously inside `flush-one!` before clearing `:dirty?`, clearing evidence, or advancing the ViewCell revision. `flush-scope!` has already atomically removed ALL matching cells from `dirty-cells` before it starts that `doseq`.

If the Xray/tool callback throws:

1. The current cell remains `:dirty? true`, retains its evidence, and never advances/notifies.
2. It has already been removed from `dirty-cells`; a later `mark-dirty!` sees `:dirty? true` and refuses to re-enrol or schedule it.
3. The exception aborts the `doseq`, so every later cell removed in the same scoped/global batch is also left dirty-but-unregistered.
4. The microtask wrapper resets `flush-scheduled?` before entering `flush-pending!`, so no automatic retry exists.

One diagnostic consumer bug can therefore strand an arbitrary batch of mounted views permanently in development. This violates the intended two-plane design: observability is a consumer of the scheduler, not an authority that may prevent the render correction. It is especially dangerous because Xray is the named sink consumer and excellent debugging is a primary substrate goal.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create two dirty ViewCells and install `(set-evidence-sink! (fn [_ _] (throw (ex-info "boom" {}))))`.
2. Call `flush-pending!` or let the scheduled microtask run.
3. Observe the throw from the first cell; both cells were removed from `dirty-cells`, neither reliably completes the flush, and re-marking the first can no-op because its dirty flag is still true.

## Deliverable

Make evidence delivery failure-isolated and finally-safe. Capture the bounded evidence for the consumer, but complete scheduler state transition/revision notification for every drained cell regardless of tool behavior. Report the sink failure through an existing non-recursive diagnostic path (or disable the bad sink after one bounded report); never route that report back through the same evidence sink.

Preserve the production plane and DCE envelope: no new production hot-path allocation or exception wrapper should survive when debug is disabled.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic two-cell fixture installs a sink that throws on the first delivery; both cells leave `:dirty?`, advance exactly once, notify their listeners, and remain re-enrollable on a later invalidation.
- `flush-scope!`/`flush-pending!` cannot leave any cell dirty-but-absent from `dirty-cells`, even when the evidence consumer throws.
- One cell's tool failure does not abort evidence delivery or scheduler completion for later cells in the same batch; ordering is explicitly ruled and tested.
- The failure produces at most one bounded, useful diagnostic per ruled interval or disables/quarantines the bad sink; diagnostic reporting cannot recurse through `evidence-sink`.
- A re-entrant sink that marks the same or another cell preserves the drain-coalescing contract and does not lose the newly scheduled batch/evidence.
- Normal sinks still receive the captured pre-clear bounded summary exactly once per flushed cell.
- Advanced `goog.DEBUG=false` output retains the minimal dirty-bit/set-enrolment/microtask scheduler with the evidence sink and its failure machinery elided.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6879 (2026-07-25) — REOPENED as the exact existing owner of the same two-plane invariant, now regressed on the live Freehand commit seam.

`re-frame.freehand.cell/commit!` publishes the cell bundle, commits events, releases superseded handles, and only then synchronously calls the dev evidence sink. A throwing sink therefore makes `commit!` throw after the commit is irrevocably live. Deterministic JVM probe on the merged code returned `{:result {:thrown "audit-sink-failure"}, :lifecycle :connected, :evidence? true}`. The caller is told the commit failed even though the cell is connected and owns the published bundle.

Bounded repair: keep schema construction/validation fail-loud before publication (so malformed framework records preserve the documented all-or-nothing boundary), but contain/report arbitrary sink-consumer failure after a selected publication so it cannot change `:published` into an exception. Preserve the `interop/debug-enabled?` production-DCE envelope; no new diagnostics framework.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6884 (branch worker/cell-sink-isolation-vxgfnd-73). Split the Freehand commit seam along the publication line: the evidence occurrence-record is built+validated before publish (a malformed framework record fails loud + rolls back handles, preserving all-or-nothing), and the consumer sink is called after publish inside a guard that contains a throwing tool callback (single bounded last-evidence-sink-escape slot + one host console line, never recursing through the sink). Whole plane stays behind interop/debug-enabled? for DCE. Regression proven load-bearing (RES on unfixed seam: commit! threw audit-sink-failure + malformed cell already :connected) then green on both hosts. Gates: Freehand JVM 919/6548 exit 0; Freehand CLJS 996/5638 exit 0.

title: Separate failed preflight-attempt evidence from live-root mount state
description:
## Problem

PR #5738 adds `:mount-incomplete true` to every install/adopt/refresh record written before a later plan in the same `execute-frame-plans!` run throws. The conflict diagnostic then states that the recorded root's mount “did NOT complete” and “no root actually scopes” the frame.

That is truthful for a fresh first mount, but `execute-frame-plans!` is also the preflight for idempotent remount and `render!` on an ALREADY-LIVE Root. The namespace's own Q49 ruling says a failing re-preflight leaves the existing root and its last committed render untouched.

Reachable sequence:

1. Root A is mounted and scopes installed frames F and G; both records are complete.
2. A re-preflight/HMR run changes F's config and contains a later failing plan for G.
3. F's `:refresh` succeeds and rewrites its install record; G then throws.
4. The catch tags F `:mount-incomplete true`, even though A's earlier mount is still live and still scopes F. A later conflict reports that A never completed and no root scopes F—factually false.

The tag models an attempted preflight run as if it were root lifetime state. This matters for debugging/Xray and conflict recovery: the project explicitly added the field to stop diagnostics naming a phantom completed owner, but it now produces the inverse falsehood for re-preflight. The same shape also applies to adoption records, while `throw-boot-authority-conflict!` does not surface `:mount-incomplete` at all, so the new diagnostic state is inconsistent across installed versus adopted authority.

## Deliverable

Represent failed PLAN-RUN provenance separately from whether a live root currently scopes the frame. The smallest honest design may use neutral `:preflight-incomplete` attempt evidence and avoid claims about root liveness, or pass the host operation/liveness context needed to distinguish first mount from re-preflight. Keep irreversible successful sibling work; do not fake multi-plan rollback.

Ensure installed and adopted authority records expose the same truthful attempt status to tooling and conflict diagnostics. This is native substrate observability/correctness, not adapter preservation work.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fixture starts with a genuinely mounted/live root, lets an early refresh succeed, forces a later plan to throw, and proves the root/last DOM remain live while install metadata never says that no root scopes the refreshed frame.
- A fresh first-mount failure after an earlier sibling install still records that the attempted host mount/preflight did not complete, without inventing a completed root owner.
- Conflict diagnostics distinguish installation/adoption authority, last failed preflight attempt, and current known root ownership; every sentence remains true for fresh mount, idempotent remount, and `render!`.
- Adopted records participate consistently: config-bearing boot-authority conflicts surface relevant failed-attempt evidence or the record deliberately uses one neutral shape across both authorities.
- A later successful retry clears only the matching failed-attempt evidence and cannot erase/modify a newer record or incarnation.
- Initial events and other irreversible sibling effects remain committed exactly as Q49 requires; no rollback/destroy/reseed is introduced.
- Tool/test projections and the frames namespace contract document the final record schema, with no per-component-render work and only bounded root-preflight bookkeeping.
notes: HELD (mayor 2026-07-12): touches the :mount-incomplete install/adopt/refresh records + conflict diagnostic = frame-install machinery, likely overlapping .24 (frames). Confirm surface + dispatch once .24 merges.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5781: failed re-preflight of an already-live root now carries neutral :preflight-attempt-failed evidence (live root + last render persist, Q49) instead of a false :mount-incomplete / 'no root scopes' claim; fresh first-mount failures still stamp :mount-incomplete truthfully. Diagnostics branch on the two markers; adopted records read consistently.

title: Make the re-frame.ui manifest cover its actual native public surface
description:
## Problem

PR #5739 enrolls `re-frame.ui` in the CLJS manifest probe and flips 13 rows to `:runtime-verified? true`, but it deliberately treats the namespace as a curated subset and excludes two live public vars: `re-frame.ui/frame-root` and `re-frame.ui/frame-provider`.

That exclusion is not coherent with the checked-in contracts:

- `spec/API.md` §Compiled views says the blessed S1 export set is EXACTLY `#{defview custom-element sub lease raw html raw-fn spread mount create-root render! hydrate-root unmount! frame-root}` and has a compiled-view `frame-root` row. Yet `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` has no `{"re-frame.ui" "frame-root"}` row.
- The sidecar/PR explanation says compiled `frame-root` “rides the re-frame.core façade row.” Manifest identity is namespace + var; `re-frame.core/frame-root` verifies a different Reagent/core façade Var and cannot classify or verify `re-frame.ui/frame-root`.
- `re-frame.ui/frame-provider` is now a live, documented native substrate scope form used throughout Spec 004/004C, but API.md's compiled-view table and exact export-set sentence omit it. The API.md §View ergonomics row cited by the PR describes `rf/frame-provider`/the legacy façade, not `ui/frame-provider`.
- Because #5739 leaves `re-frame.ui` out of `fully-rowed`, both missing rows are invisible to the probe. The 13 existing rows can all resolve and the build stays green while the manifest still does not represent the declared/live first-party surface.

Marking the 13 rows runtime-verified is individually true in direction 1, but the PR's broader claim that it runtime-verifies the shipped `re-frame.ui` surface is incomplete. It also institutionalizes the omission by documenting the wrong cross-namespace substitution.

## Deliverable

Reconcile one exact native compiled-view public surface across `re-frame.ui`, Spec 004/004C, `spec/API.md`, the metadata sidecar, generated manifest, and the CLJS probe. Namespace-specific public API must receive namespace-specific rows. If a live Var is intentionally compiler-only/internal, make that status explicit using the repository's real internal mechanism rather than borrowing another namespace's row; however, `frame-root` and `frame-provider` currently read as supported user grammar and should normally be rowed at their actual stages.

Once the exact surface is rowed, make `re-frame.ui` fully-rowed so future accidental public exports fail the reverse direction too. This is manifest/spec correctness for the first-party substrate, not adapter compatibility work.
acceptance_criteria:
- `spec/API.md`'s exact compiled-view export-set statement and table include every supported live `re-frame.ui` public, including a resolved decision for both `frame-root` and `frame-provider` with correct stage/tier/kind.
- `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` and generated `spec/api-manifest.edn` contain namespace-specific rows for every supported `re-frame.ui/*` export; no row in `re-frame.core` or an adapter is cited as verification for a different namespace.
- The CLJS probe treats `re-frame.ui` as fully-rowed after intentional internals are private or `^:no-doc`; adding an unclassified public Var turns the gate red.
- Mutation fixtures prove both directions: removing/renaming a rowed live Var fails stale-row checking, and adding/removing a manifest row relative to the live namespace fails completeness checking.
- Macro/function kinds match the actual public Var forms (including compile-marker fns), while the existing analyzer limitation remains handled consistently.
- Spec 004, 004C, API.md, the sidecar comments, and probe coverage prose no longer describe `ui/frame-root` or `ui/frame-provider` as being covered by the legacy/core façade row.
- Regeneration produces only the expected reconciled rows/flags and all manifest/API drift gates pass without production runtime cost.
close_reason: PR #5754 opened: added namespace-specific {re-frame.ui frame-root} manifest row (blessed S1 export per API.md §Compiled views); frame-provider deferred to rf2-vxgfnd.24 and recorded explicitly as unrowed pending that ruling. All manifest/API-drift gates + full CLJS probe green.

title: Revalidate live Root ownership after every side-effecting preflight
description:
## Problem

PR #5735 re-checks ownership after preflight only on `mount*`'s fresh-root path. Two already-live paths still capture a Root, run side-effecting preflight (`:initial-events` may execute arbitrary app code), and then use the captured handle without revalidation:

1. `mount*` same-root/same-container fast path: `run-preflight!` then direct `.render` on the old Root.
2. `render!*`: `require-live-root!` runs before preflight, then preflight, then the dev descriptor write and `.render` with no second identity check.

A preflight handler can unmount the captured root and mount a replacement under the same id/container. The outer call then renders through a stale React root. In `render!*`, the descriptor swap checks only that an entry exists, not that it still belongs to the captured Root, so it can also write the old call's descriptor onto the replacement root. This is the same user-code window #5735 correctly closes for fresh mount.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create/mount live root A.
2. Arrange the next plan preflight to synchronously `unmount!` A and mount root B under the same root id (and optionally the same container).
3. Call the idempotent `mount` path or `render!` using A.
4. After preflight returns, current code calls `.render` on stale A; `render!*` may first overwrite B's dev descriptor because it only looks up the id.

## Deliverable

Treat every side-effecting preflight as an ownership invalidation boundary. Revalidate that the exact Root handle, root id, container, and immutable host options still belong together immediately after preflight and before descriptor mutation or React render. On movement, fail through the existing truthful stale-root/claim diagnostic and leave the replacement root completely untouched. Factor one invariant rather than fixing each entry point with drifting checks.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deterministic re-entrant fixtures cover both same-root `mount` reuse and `render!`: preflight unmounts/replaces A, and the outer call fails before stale `.render` or descriptor mutation.
- The replacement root's registry entry, container, descriptor, identifier prefix, and committed DOM remain unchanged.
- `render!*` descriptor updates are identity-guarded to the exact Root, never merely the current entry under the same id.
- Normal idempotent remount/render preflight still runs once and renders successfully when ownership does not move.
- Prefix/container/root-id changes during preflight surface the appropriate existing typed condition without introducing a second claim model.
- Fresh-mount revalidation from #5735 stays green, and all entry points share one post-preflight ownership invariant.
- No production work is added per component render; checks occur only at root host operations.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5746 (commit 2). One post-preflight ownership invariant (require-live-root!) revalidates the captured handle after every side-effecting preflight on both the same-root fast path and render!* before .render/descriptor-write; render!* descriptor swap identity-guarded to the exact Root; deterministic re-entrant fixtures. Gates: JVM ui 260 / node 8986 / browser 293, 0-fail.

title: Keep Root Descriptor build identity complete across compiler and client projections
description:
## Problem

PR #5734 fixes expansion-time digest staleness by removing `:build-digest` from `root-descriptor` and adding a JVM-only `descriptor-index` read projection. That resolves the test index, but it silently creates two descriptor shapes:

- Spec 004C defines Root Descriptor v1 with mandatory `:build-digest` as its build identity.
- The compiler's emitted CLJS descriptor passed to `client/render!*` and stored in the live-root registry now lacks that field permanently.
- Only tests currently call the new CLJ-only `descriptor-index`; no client/Xray runtime consumer can use it.

Thus the compile-time tooling index may be current while the actual dev runtime descriptor—the surface Xray/instance tooling reads—is incomplete. A read-time projection also needs a settled, per-build boundary: reading the current global registry mid-pass or amid interleaved shadow build ids can produce a partial/mixed digest. That lifecycle is owned by rf2-df9873 and is not solved by recomputing on arbitrary reads.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Expand a real `ui/mount`/`ui/render!` under #5734 and inspect the descriptor map emitted to `re-frame.ui.client`.
2. It lacks `:build-digest`, despite Spec 004C's Root Descriptor v1 schema.
3. `root/descriptor-index` returns a digest only on CLJ and has no production/tool consumer outside tests.
4. During an incomplete/interleaved compiler pass, the projection derives from whatever global `build-views` rows happen to be present at that instant rather than a finalized per-build snapshot.

## Deliverable

Define one complete Root Descriptor v1 contract at every consumer while preserving read-time/finalization correctness. Finalize a per-build digest at an authoritative successful build boundary, expose/project it to both the compiler index and the dev client/Xray descriptor path, and update descriptors when a view-only incremental edit changes build identity without requiring mount-site re-expansion. If static descriptor versus live projection are intentionally distinct objects, name and specify both rather than returning two undocumented shapes under one name.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 004C, `root-descriptor`, compiler index, emitted CLJS descriptor, client live-root entry, and Xray/tool projection agree on whether/where `:build-digest` is present.
- Every public/tool-facing value called Root Descriptor v1 is schema-complete and carries the finalized digest for its own build id.
- A view-only incremental edit updates the digest observed by an already-mounted client root without re-expanding its mount site, or the deliberately named live projection supplies that current identity.
- Two interleaved shadow build ids cannot mix view triples or overwrite one another's digest.
- Reads during a failed/incomplete build retain the last known-good finalized digest; no partial mid-pass identity is published.
- Clean, incremental, watch, and REPL paths converge byte-identically through real consumers, not a test-only descriptor-index call.
- Production-elided client output still carries no dev descriptor/digest cost when `goog.DEBUG=false`.
- The implementation composes with rf2-df9873's real build lifecycle rather than inventing a second build-generation authority.
notes: HELD until the reactive-activation cluster (worker/reactive-activation, .92 wires client/unmount!) MERGES — .68 reconciles the Root Descriptor across compiler AND CLIENT projections, and .92 is in-flight editing client.cljs. Collision risk. Also touches spec/004C (hot-zone). Dispatch after reactive-activation lands; confirm whether .68's client side edits client.cljs or is read-only before dispatching.
close_reason: Closed

title: Reconcile zero-declaration and failed-HMR custom-element manifests
description:
## Problem

PR #5734 adds a generation-led per-namespace runtime custom-element ledger, but eviction occurs only inside `register-custom-element!` when that namespace executes its first surviving declaration. If a namespace deletes its LAST `ui/custom-element` form—or the source file is deleted—no registration call executes after reload, `open-element-source!` is never reached, and every old runtime classification remains. The new deletion test retains/renames another declaration in the same namespace, so it does not exercise the zero-current-contribution case that originally motivated rf2-vxgfnd.48.

The replacement is also non-transactional. The first new registration immediately deletes the prior source contribution and mutates the live registry; if a later top-level form throws or HMR aborts, the browser is left with a partial new manifest instead of the last known-good state. Namespace alone is the ownership key, so concurrently loaded build ids are not isolated.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load namespace `app.a` containing only `(ui/custom-element :x-el {:properties #{:help-text}})` and verify runtime classification.
2. Delete that sole declaration and hot-reload `app.a`.
3. `notify-reload!` increments the global generation, but no `register-custom-element!` call for `app.a` occurs; `:x-el` remains classified until full page reload.
4. Separately, reload a namespace with multiple declarations and throw after its first new registration; the old contribution has already been evicted and only a partial new set is live.

## Deliverable

Replace registration-triggered eviction with an explicit current-manifest/reconciliation protocol that represents zero contributions and commits atomically after a successful reload. Ownership must include build identity plus source identity where multiple builds can coexist. Integrate file-save HMR, source deletion, and REPL evaluation through the same path; do not rely on a surviving declaration as the signal that a source was rebuilt.
acceptance_criteria:
- Removing the last custom-element declaration from a live namespace removes all of that source's runtime classifications without a page reload.
- Deleting/renaming the source file also reconciles its former contribution.
- Add/edit/rename/multi-declaration reloads replace the source contribution atomically; consumers never retain a successful-but-stale union after commit.
- A compile failure, top-level evaluation failure, or aborted HMR retains the last known-good complete runtime manifest.
- Multiple build ids and equal namespace symbols have explicit independent ownership; reconciling one cannot delete the other's rows.
- REPL re-evaluation converges to the same manifest as file-save HMR, including a zero-declaration source.
- Fixtures exercise zero-survivor deletion, source deletion, failed reload, multi-build isolation, and full-reload equivalence—not only rename-with-one-survivor.
- Production classification remains a direct lookup with all reconciliation machinery dev-elided or reload-only.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5744: reload-cycle reconciliation protocol (notify-reload!/note-reloaded-sources!/commit-reload!) evicts zero-declaration + deleted + failed-HMR sources; build-isolated ledger; fixtures for all AC cases. Gates green (JVM 265t/4502a, CLJS 8973t/42328a, 0 fail).

title: Finish the drain-batch contract sweep across re-frame.ui docs and gates
description:
## Problem

PR #5733 corrects Spec 006 and `reactive.cljc`, but rf2-vxgfnd.45 was closed while its required contract sweep remains incomplete. The PR itself names only `viewcell.cljs` and Spec 004, yet active synthesis documents also retain the rejected model:

- `01-goals-and-invariants.md` still defines I-6 as one notification per cell per epoch.
- `03-reactivity-and-ownership.md` still says epoch close flushes/notifies.
- `05-production.md` still models React work and cost per epoch.
- `07-testing.md` still contains the explicit false gate `8 epochs ⇒ 8`.
- `spec/004-Views.md` and `implementation/ui/.../viewcell.cljs` still teach per-epoch notification.
- live compatibility/draft/benchmark documents repeat the old equation.

This is not harmless history: several are the active design, testing, production-economics, and implementation guidance for re-frame.ui. They now contradict Spec 006 and can generate incorrect beads/gates. Historical spike/review measurements should not be silently rewritten, but active normative statements and merge-ready drafts must converge or be clearly marked superseded.

## Steps to Reproduce

Search active surfaces for `per cell per epoch`, `one notification per epoch`, `epoch close`, and `8 epochs`. The files above still match after #5733, despite rf2-vxgfnd.45 acceptance requiring no normative/gate text to equate epochs with renders and explicitly naming synthesis docs 03/07/12.

## Deliverable

After rf2-vxgfnd.65 settles the real scheduler boundary, reconcile every active contract, guide, code docstring, compatibility statement, and benchmark/gate definition to the ruled writes-to-quiescence-then-reads model. Classify each hit rather than performing a blind replacement: preserve genuinely historical empirical reports, adding a qualification/cross-reference only where a fresh reader could mistake them for current law; update or retire live drafts that still claim merge readiness.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 004, `viewcell.cljs`, synthesis docs 01/03/05/07/12, and every current guide/compatibility contract agree with final Spec 006 terminology.
- G-5/G-13 no longer contain `8 epochs ⇒ 8 renders`; they require queued writes/epochs within one drain followed by one real read/render batch, plus later external-drain observability.
- Production-cost tables distinguish per-event/epoch write work from per-drain dirty-cell notification and React work.
- Merge-ready drafts are updated or explicitly marked superseded; historical spike/review results remain historically accurate and are not rewritten as if measured under the new gate.
- References to epoch evidence remain where correct, but no active text uses epoch count as a render-count proxy or calls `goog.async.nextTick` a microtask.
- A focused drift check or maintained search roster fails if the retired phrases return to active normative/gate/code-doc surfaces.
- The sweep is sequenced after rf2-vxgfnd.65 so prose describes the scheduler actually shipped, not the premise #5733 assumed.
notes: HELD for #5789 (.44) merge — .66 touches viewcell.cljs docstring, .44 just edited viewcell.cljs. Dispatch after #5789; scope to TRACKED surface only (spec/004-Views drain-batch prose + viewcell docstring; the 01/03/05/07 synthesis docs are ai/ gitignored, not PR-able).

title: Wire explicit root teardown into the ViewCell dead-state lifecycle
description:
## Problem

PR #5731 gives `reactive/teardown!` a production caller for frame destruction, but explicit root/host teardown remains unwired. The finalized lifecycle contract (03 §4) says React cleanup first emits `:disconnected {:reason :unknown}` because Activity hide and real unmount are indistinguishable, then an explicit root/host teardown retroactively proves `:unmounted {:proof :host-teardown}` and makes a retained cell `:dead`.

Today `client/unmount!*` only calls React `.unmount` and releases the live-root claim. React effect cleanup calls `disconnect!`, which removes the cell from `live-cells`; no root-scoped teardown subsequently finds or annotates it. Therefore a real root unmount remains an unknown disconnect forever (unless GC inference exists later), `teardown!` is not invoked for the root path, and the Stage-2 lifecycle matrix's host/root proof is incomplete.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Mount a compiled ViewCell and commit at least one dependency.
2. Call `ui/unmount!` on its Root.
3. React cleanup transitions the cell to `:disconnected` with `:reason :unknown` and releases leases.
4. No explicit root-teardown call annotates the interval as `:unmounted {:proof :host-teardown}` or transitions a retained handle to `:dead`; `client.cljs` has no reactive teardown seam and the disconnected cell has already left the frame-oriented `live-cells` set.

## Deliverable

Complete the explicit host/root teardown path without guessing at effect-cleanup time. Establish root-to-cell ownership sufficient for `unmount!*` (and ruled parent teardown) to provide the later proof, retroactively annotate the prior disconnect when cleanup won first, and prevent retained cells from reconnecting after their root is gone. Keep Activity hide/reveal unchanged: hide remains unknown until a reconnect proves `:activity-hidden`.

Use bounded, non-retaining ownership/indexing; root teardown must not make production reads scan all historical cells.
acceptance_criteria:
- A mounted real-root fixture observes the same immediate `:disconnected {:reason :unknown}` cleanup fact for Activity hide and real unmount.
- Explicit `ui/unmount!` then upgrades the unmount case to `:unmounted {:proof :host-teardown}` and leaves any retained cell `:dead`/non-resumable.
- Activity reveal reacquires and annotates only its prior interval as `:activity-hidden {:proof :reconnect}`; it is never mislabeled unmounted.
- Ordering is robust whether React cleanup happens before or during the host teardown signal, and a throwing host `.unmount` follows the ruled ownership/fact behavior without losing the original error.
- Multiple roots, nested providers, and sibling roots are isolated; unmounting root A cannot annotate or kill root B's cells.
- Root-to-cell tracking is removed on disconnect/teardown and passes a repeated mount/unmount retention test.
- Late callbacks and recommit through a retained cell after root teardown fail through the dead-cell lifecycle, not by accidentally probing a missing frame.
- The 07 lifecycle/root-teardown conformance row is wired into the S2 gates.
close_reason: Closed

title: Catalogue and locate semantic normalization malformation diagnostics
description:
## Problem

PR #5726 correctly made `semantic/normalize` reject unsupported tree versions and ambiguous/discriminator-less nodes, but the new diagnostic shapes are not fully integrated. The existing Spec 009 row for `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` still lists only the older `:value` / `:attr` / `:row` data. The new version arm emits `:got` + `:supported`, and discriminator failures emit `:got` + `:value`; neither shape is catalogued.

Nested failures also report the offending map but not where it occurred. rf2-vxgfnd.20 acceptance explicitly required the malformed node/path, and excellent debugging needs a stable structural path when several equal-looking nodes exist. The current recursive normalizer discards traversal position, so a deeply nested failure can require manually searching the whole emitted tree.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call `semantic/normalize` with `{:rf.ui/tree-version 2 ...}` and inspect ex-data: it contains `:got` and `:supported`, fields absent from the Spec 009 row.
2. Normalize a tree with a malformed map nested several child levels deep.
3. The exception contains `:value` but no root-relative child path; duplicate/equal malformed maps cannot be distinguished by location.

## Deliverable

Make the normalization diagnostic contract explicit and locatable. Thread a deterministic root-relative structural path through the normalization walk, include it on nested node-shape failures, and catalogue every emitted field/arm in Spec 009 (plus the owning tree contract where appropriate). Preserve the version-first rule and do not alter normalized output or production rendering semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
- Version failures retain `:got` and `:supported #{1}`, and Spec 009 documents those fields and their trigger.
- Node discrimination failures carry the offending `:value`, the discriminator set in `:got`, and a stable root-relative child path; a root-node failure has an explicitly ruled root path.
- Paths identify nested nodes through fragments, view boundaries, and elements without depending on map iteration order.
- Tests cover two equal-looking malformed nodes at different positions and prove the diagnostic identifies the correct one.
- Version validation still fires before traversal, valid v1 normalization is byte-identical, and unknown optional `:rf.ui/*` keys remain ignored.
- Spec 004B, Spec 009, implementation messages/ex-data, and tests use one terminology and field schema.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5741. rf2-vxgfnd.20 left the malformation diagnostics under-catalogued (Spec 009 row omitted the version-arm :got/:supported and node-arm fields) and un-located (nested failures carried :value but no position). Threaded a deterministic root-relative get-in :path through the normalization walk (document child order only); enriched the Spec 009 :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed row to document both arms + list re-frame.ui.semantic; added tests proving two equal-looking nodes are disambiguated by :path. No new 009 row (existing id reused). Gates: ui JVM 260/4513, CLJS 8968/42339, conformance 9/21 — all 0-fail.

title: Complete mounted Story override and image-schema conformance
description:
## Problem

PR #5721 established the compiled override lookup and schema-validation foundation, but closed rf2-vxgfnd.21 without completing its mounted conformance obligation. The remaining behavior is where ownership and token semantics become observable: a real React Story provider, image-scoped frame/schema metadata, nested providers, equal-value provider replacement, value changes, and HMR/schema changes. Unit-level resolver tests cannot prove that a mounted ViewCell acquires/releases the right static lease or retargets only when semantic evidence changes.

This is deferred acceptance from the substrate design, not compatibility work for UIx/Helix; those adapters are scheduled for removal.

## Deliverable

Build a Tier-3 mounted Story fixture using the first-party `re-frame.ui` provider/context path and real compiled subscription descriptors. Seed the target frame/image schema through the production metadata route, then exercise closest-provider resolution and ViewCell commit/cleanup. Capture the static override lease's ownership, target identity, validation, and invalidation behavior through provider replacement and HMR.

Keep production erasure intact: when debug/schema checks are disabled, this coverage must not introduce a per-read consult or retain debug metadata.
acceptance_criteria:
- A mounted compiled view under nested Story providers resolves the closest provider and releases its lease on unmount/retarget.
- Replacing a provider with an equal semantic value does not retarget, churn leases, or invalidate the cell; changing the value does.
- Override values are validated against the target frame/image subscription schema through the production metadata path, including useful frame/sub/schema attribution on rejection.
- HMR with an unchanged schema preserves the valid lease/token; an incompatible schema change rejects or invalidates deterministically and reacquires only when valid.

title: Reconcile removed custom-element declarations into the live HMR runtime
description:
## Problem

PR #5719 made compiler-side registries build-scoped, including the custom-element declaration ledger. Runtime custom-element classification is still append-only: emitted code calls the CLJS runtime registration path, but removing or renaming a declaration emits no inverse operation and does not replace/clear the runtime `rules/custom-elements` state. After HMR/REPL rebuild, a deleted declaration can therefore keep forcing stale property-vs-attribute behavior until a full page reload.

Compiler-ledger correctness alone is insufficient because the observable stale state lives in the already-running client.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Compile and load a source declaring a custom element/property classification.
2. Confirm the runtime classifier recognizes it.
3. Delete or rename the declaration and perform the supported watch/HMR rebuild without reloading the page.
4. The compiler ledger no longer contains the source contribution, but the runtime classifier still contains the old declaration.

## Deliverable

Define and implement a build-scoped runtime projection for custom-element declarations so the live client converges to the current compiler manifest after edit, deletion, rename, and REPL evaluation. Prefer an atomic generation/manifest replacement (or another explicitly owned reconciliation protocol) over ad-hoc per-call cleanup. It must coexist safely with multiple shadow build ids and must not erase declarations owned by another concurrently loaded build.

Integrate this into the one REPL=HMR path owned by S2e; do not require a page reload to repair stale classification.
acceptance_criteria:
- Removing a custom-element declaration under watch/HMR removes its runtime classification without a page reload.
- Renaming or changing a declaration replaces the old runtime contribution atomically; no transient or persistent union of old and new remains after commit.
- Re-evaluating the source from the REPL converges to the same runtime state as file-save HMR.
- Multiple build ids have explicit ownership: reconciling one build cannot delete another build's declarations.
- Failed compilation or aborted HMR retains the last known-good runtime manifest.
- Fixtures exercise add, edit, delete, rename, REPL re-eval, build-id isolation, and full-reload equivalence.
close_reason: Duplicate of rf2-vxgfnd.48 (filed ~1h earlier by the monitor worker's #5719 review): same bug — runtime custom-element classification is append-only (rules.cljc:712-723 assocs only; emitted registration at compiler.cljc:270 simply stops executing on delete), stale rows classify until full reload. .48 carries file:line detail + the coordination note with .11 (S2e HMR matrix, natural home). .57's #5719 framing folded into .48 via note.

title: Preserve bounded ViewCell invalidation evidence across a coalesced render batch
description:
## Problem
The observation port deliberately emits a rich constant-work invalidation payload: `:cause`, `:target`, `:node-key`, `:node-version`, `:frame-epoch`, and `:registry-epoch`. re-frame.ui currently throws nearly all of it away. `on-change-fn` passes only `:frame-epoch` to `mark-dirty!`; `mark-dirty!` records that epoch only on the first mark; subsequent invalidations in the same pending drain are ignored; `flush-one!` clears the field without any consumer. The result is an unused first-epoch breadcrumb rather than the causal evidence promised by Spec 006 and synthesis doc 03.

This becomes more important under the correct scheduling model: one render may summarize several queued event epochs. Xray and other tooling need enough bounded evidence to explain that render without forcing a render per epoch. The production hot path must remain exceptionally small.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Follow observation.cljc's value/HMR/disposal fan-out payload into re-frame.ui.reactive/on-change-fn.
2. Observe that on-change-fn projects the full payload to only `(:frame-epoch payload)`.
3. Call mark-dirty! twice before a flush with epochs 1 and 2 (or distinct causes/targets). The second call does not update cell state because `:dirty?` is already true.
4. Flush the cell. `:dirty-epoch` is cleared without being read or exposed, so neither the latest movement nor the coalesced cause span reaches debugging/tooling consumers.

## Deliverable
Define and implement a bounded invalidation-evidence accumulator for a pending ViewCell read batch. It must distinguish notification coalescing from causal evidence: one dirty enrollment/one render, while debug/tool builds retain enough information to attribute the batch to its contributing movement. Specify the exact projection consumed by re-frame.ui.tool/Xray and update the observation/ViewCell contract text accordingly.

Do not retain an unbounded payload vector. Choose the smallest useful summary, such as first/latest frame epoch plus bounded cause/target identity information and loss accounting when a cap is exceeded. Remove `:dirty-epoch` if it has no remaining coherent role.

## Production constraint
In `:advanced` with debug disabled, preserve the minimal dirty-bit/set-enrollment scheduler. Debug evidence accumulation, diagnostic keywords, and collection growth must be gated so the production invalidation path does not allocate per cause or scale with the number of queued events.
design: Keep two planes separate. The production scheduler needs only `dirty?` plus identity-deduped registry membership. The debug plane may accumulate a compact bounded summary behind the existing debug constant. Do not preserve every event payload merely because it is available; prefer first/latest movement plus a small cause/target summary and explicit dropped-count. Xray should correlate richer event detail through epoch/trace identity rather than duplicating full event data in each ViewCell.
acceptance_criteria:
1. re-frame.ui no longer silently discards the observation port's invalidation payload at on-change-fn.
2. Multiple invalidations with different epochs/causes/targets before one flush still produce exactly one ViewCell revision advance and listener notification.
3. The resulting debug/tool evidence correctly represents the coalesced batch (including first/latest epoch or an equally precise span), has an explicit bound, and reports loss/truncation rather than silently dropping overflow.
4. Value, HMR, and disposal causes have fixtures; at least one fixture spans multiple event epochs before one read batch.
5. The evidence is consumable through the intended re-frame.ui.tool/Xray projection rather than remaining dead cell state.
6. A production-elision or compiled-output assertion demonstrates that debug evidence accumulation adds no per-invalidation collection work to the advanced production path.
7. Spec 006 and synthesis doc 03 describe the same evidence and batching semantics as the implementation.
notes: Work COMPLETE in #5742 (bounded debug-gated evidence record + set-evidence-sink!). bd blocked --close on the rf2-vxgfnd.65 dependency, but the substantive dep (real batch boundary before evidence is named) is satisfied by #5742's commit 1 (the microtask primitive). MAYOR: force-close .46 when #5742 merges.
close_reason: Verified complete on current mayor HEAD: PR #5742 merged as b9583a1d294b3ec8110c7fefc2750cffae0d9dc1 with all required checks green; current source retains bounded debug-gated evidence accumulation, sink projection, multi-epoch/loss fixtures, and production-plane separation. Follow-up honesty/sink findings .73/.74 are closed; .75 intentionally remains the S3 Xray consumer.

title: Wire re-frame.ui.compiler.build/begin-build! into the shadow-cljs build lifecycle
description:
rf2-vxgfnd.16 landed the build-scoped compiler state model (re-frame.ui.compiler.build): all five compiler registries route writes through a per-source contribution ledger with cross-registry atomic replace, driven by begin-build! (per compile pass) and reconcile! (whole-build end). The mechanism + conformance fixtures are merged (PR #5719).

REMAINING: begin-build! must actually FIRE once per compile pass in real builds so the per-source replace self-arms under shadow-cljs watch/REPL (today the fixtures drive it explicitly; without a real per-pass hook, a single-file incremental recompile does not bump the generation, so its per-source eviction does not fire in a live daemon). Wire a shadow-cljs :build-hooks / compile-prepare (:compile-prepare or :flush) stage hook that calls (build/begin-build! <build-id>) at pass start, and optionally (build/reconcile!) at flush for whole-build passes (file-deletion reconciliation). Touches implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (HOT ZONE — sequence) and a small hook ns; out of rf2-vxgfnd.16's surface. Prerequisite for rf2-vxgfnd.11's full HMR matrix (clean=incremental=REPL equivalence).
acceptance_criteria:
- A real shadow-cljs lifecycle hook invokes `begin-build!` exactly once at the start of each compile pass, including watch-mode incremental passes and REPL-driven compilation.
- Registry state is keyed/owned per build id: interleaved app, browser-test, node-test, and REPL passes cannot reset or hide one another's contributions.
- Parallel namespace compilation cannot expose evict-then-readd gaps or check-then-assoc races; cross-registry source replacement and duplicate detection are atomic at the required scope.
- A one-file incremental rebuild replaces only that source's prior contribution while retaining untouched sources from the same build.
- Whole-build reconciliation uses authoritative membership and removes contributions from deleted/renamed files without treating a partial incremental pass as the whole build.
- Switching away from a build id and later returning to it cannot leave a registry containing only the most recently recompiled subset.
- Failed/aborted compilation preserves the last known-good generation; a successful retry converges to clean-build state.
- Integration fixtures run through the actual shadow hook for two interleaved build ids, parallel source compilation, edit, delete, rename, failed compile/retry, and REPL; final registries equal a clean rebuild.
notes:
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-07-12: I dispatched this as a simple hot-zone hook (read DESCRIPTION, MISSED the NOTES). A naive per-pass begin-build! hook is UNSOUND — begin-build! is GLOBAL wipe-on-switch, and the daemon compiles re-frame.ui from MULTIPLE builds (:node-test/:node-test-ui/:ui-bench); firing per-pass flip-flops the global build-id so each build WIPES the other's registries → REGRESSES cross-file duplicate detection (:rf.error/duplicate-root-id / frame-payload-conflict). RESET to open, DECISION-GATED. Needs a design ruling: (a) re-key build.cljc state per-build-id (not one global build-id); (b) thread ambient build-id into compiler.cljc/root.cljc write sites; (c) atomicity for check-then-act writes under shadow parallel compile; (d) REPL generation bump without a lifecycle hook. Spans build.cljc + compiler.cljc + root.cljc + shadow-cljs.edn + fixtures — a substantial redesign, NOT a hot-zone hook. Blocks .11 (S2e) + .68.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike 2026-07-12): Option A — re-key ALL build-scoped compiler state per shadow build-id with explicit begin/commit/abort pass boundaries and last-known-good publication; build IDENTITY comes from the per-thread compiler env (cljs.env/*compiler* -> :shadow.build.cljs-bridge/state -> :shadow.build/build-id), NOT from a hook — hooks own only pass boundaries. :cache-blockers #{re-frame.ui} is a non-negotiable part of this fix, and the AC clause "hook invokes begin-build! ... including REPL-driven compilation" is AMENDED: REPL form evals must NOT open a pass; REPL semantics is per-key upsert into committed state.

RATIONALE: Adopted the doc's Option A and both Fable-recommendation corrections; rejected B (global serialization couples independent builds, stalls watch, and still needs commit/abort + a REPL answer) and C (ghost declarations contradict the S2 HMR contract). Verified in code: build.cljc begin-build! is global wipe-on-switch (lines 193-198) so interleaved daemon builds (:node-test/:node-test-ui/:ui-bench) wipe each other; register-root-site!/register-plan-site! (root.cljc:438-501) are check-then-act across separate atoms while shadow par-compile is the default (the "single-threaded macro expansion" premise at build.cljc:76 is false); shadow's resource cache skips macroexpansion for cached namespaces, so without :cache-blockers the registries are incomplete on every warm-cache daemon start under ANY option; and the runtime arm (rules.cljc element ledger, [build-id ns-sym] keys, atomic rebuild-from-ledger commit) already implements the correct model — the compile side converges on that shape rather than inventing a second one. Pre-alpha posture check: this is the simplest fully-correct shape — ONE atom with pure transitions replaces today's 4 ledger atoms + 5 aggregate atoms, no locks, no second watch protocol; speculative machinery is excluded (NO eviction/LRU for inactive build slices — a dev daemon holds a handful of builds; revisit only if observed).

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (two PRs, sequenced):
PR1 (parallel-safe surface — implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/{build,root,compiler}.cljc + consumers + tests):
(1) Collapse build.cljc four atoms (generation/build-id/source-gen/registries) + the five registered aggregate atoms into ONE atom {build-id slice}; slice = {:gen n :committed {reg {k v}} :staged {reg {k v}} :keys {reg {src #{k}}} :source-gen {src gen}}. Every mutation is one swap! with a pure transition; duplicate-root-id / frame-payload-conflict checks run INSIDE the transition (swap-vals!; the contributing thread throws after) — kills both the check-then-act race and the evict-then-readd gap under par-compile.
(2) (current-build-id): dynamic override (tests/REPL) -> (:shadow.build/build-id (get @cljs.env/*compiler* :shadow.build.cljs-bridge/state)) when bound -> ::default (keeps the plain-JVM clojure -M:test path, e.g. compiler_build_jvm_test.clj, working). Read per contribution; DELETE the global wipe-on-switch build-id slot. Pin the internal-ish :shadow.build.cljs-bridge/state access behind one tiny fn so a shadow upgrade breaks loudly.
(3) Key the ledger by ns-sym (matching the runtime arm [build-id ns-sym]); file/line remain in error coords only — dissolves the REPL pseudo-file false-duplicate and the Windows path-normalization risk.
(4) Consumers (descriptor-index, current-build-digest, custom-element-properties, tests) switch from bare @atom derefs to accessor fns resolving the ambient build-id.
(5) REPL policy: pass-open false => contributions upsert into committed per-key (no sibling eviction); deletion via bare REPL re-eval converges at the next watch pass — document as the explicit posture (no design can observe an unsaved deletion).
(6) Tests: extend compiler_build_jvm_test.clj to drive the hook fns with synthetic build-state maps — two interleaved build-ids; futures hammering contribute!/register-root-site! across builds (final state == clean rebuild); edit/delete/rename via membership reconcile; failed pass -> last-known-good; REPL upsert.
PR2 (HOT ZONE implementation/shadow-cljs.edn — dispatch only AFTER PR1 merges):
(7) Hook ns re-frame.ui.compiler.shadow-hook (.clj, zero shadow :requires; hooks receive the build-state map): :compile-prepare -> bump slice gen + mark pass-open; :compile-finish -> commit staged->committed atomically, then reconcile against authoritative membership from :build-sources (safe on EVERY pass, incrementals included — macro silence is never the deletion signal); :flush -> clear pass-open. Failed compiles skip :compile-finish so committed last-known-good survives; the next :compile-prepare discards stale staging.
(8) Wire via top-level :build-defaults {:build-hooks [...]} PLUS :cache-blockers #{re-frame.ui} (non-negotiable for correctness; cost = defview-consuming nses recompile on daemon start, warm-watch incrementals unaffected; file a follow-up bead to move contributions into cacheable analyzer data to recover caching).

SOURCE: decision doc ai/decisions/rf2-df9873.build-lifecycle-authority.md (deleted after this ruling; its analysis is summarized here).
close_reason: PR #5770 opened — per-build-id compiler state authority + pass boundaries + :cache-blockers. Shadow :build-hooks wiring is a small documented follow-up.

title: review(impl/ssr): streaming client drops per-subtree hydration delta when resolved <template> and its delta <script> arrive in separate observer batches
description:
rf2-x76af2 review-wave finding (ssr surface). Framed as a suggestion.

SURFACE: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming/client.cljs

CORE BUG (ordering/race hazard — speculative-hydration delta silently dropped):
The per-subtree hydration delta is consumed ONLY as a side effect of processing the matching resolved <template>:
- sweep! (client.cljs:441-471) iterates ONLY over [data-rf2-suspense-resolved] templates; it never independently scans [data-rf2-suspense-hydrate] delta scripts.
- process-resolved-template! (client.cljs:404-439) swaps the resolved template into the mount, marks the id in `seen`, REMOVES the resolved <template> node (via replace-mount-content! client.cljs:242-260), then calls apply-delta-script! (client.cljs:336-355) which looks up the delta <script> for that id and merges it.

Failure interleaving: the server writer flushes the resolved <template> and its delta <script> as TWO SEPARATE chunks, each with its own .flush — see ssr-ring/streaming.clj run-streaming-writer! write-chunk! at lines 322 (template) and 351 (delta), and write-chunk! itself flushes (streaming.clj:119-121). On the client the HTML parser can therefore surface the resolved <template> in one MutationObserver batch and the delta <script> in a LATER batch (the between-chunk flush makes a parser yield between them likely). In that interleaving:
  batch 1: sweep! -> process-resolved-template! swaps + REMOVES the resolved template + conj's id into `seen`; apply-delta-script! finds NO delta script yet -> no merge.
  batch 2: sweep! -> query [data-rf2-suspense-resolved] no longer returns that id (template removed) -> process-resolved-template! never runs for it again -> apply-delta-script! never re-attempted -> the delta <script> is orphaned and its merge is LOST.
Net: for any continuation that MUTATES app-db during render (the only case that emits a non-empty delta — see streaming.cljc project-delta / subtree-delta), progressive hydration silently fails to apply that delta; a subscription reading the resolved region sees stale (pre-delta) state until the final __rf_payload lands. Not data corruption (the final :rf/hydrate :replace-frame-state is the correctness lock), but it defeats the whole point of the per-subtree delta for the mutating case.

Note the asymmetry that makes this reachable: process-resolved-template! (client.cljs:407-439) was carefully hardened (finding-4 comments) to keep the SWAP retryable across sweeps by gating `seen` on swap success and re-materialising nested fallbacks — but the DELTA application got no equivalent retry: once the swap succeeds the template is gone and the delta can never be re-tried.

FIX SKETCH (suggestion): decouple delta application from resolved-template presence. Options:
  (a) Track a separate `delta-applied` set; in sweep!, after the resolved-template fixpoint, ALSO iterate [data-rf2-suspense-hydrate] scripts and apply/consume any whose id has been swapped (in `seen`) but not yet delta-applied. This makes the delta retryable across sweeps just like the swap.
  (b) When apply-delta-script! finds no matching script for a just-swapped id, record the id as 'delta-pending' and re-attempt on the next sweep.
Either closes the split-flush drop; (a) is the smaller change and mirrors the existing swap-retry loop shape.

WEAK/ABSENT TEST:
The DOM test never exercises the split-arrival case. streaming_client_dom_cljs_test.cljs resolved-chunk-html (test lines 92-98) concatenates the resolved <template> AND its delta <script> into ONE string, and append-chunk! (test lines 126-134) inserts them in a SINGLE DOM mutation — so every test injects the two nodes in the same sweep, exactly the interleaving that works. Suggest a regression test that appends the resolved <template> in one append-chunk! and its delta <script> in a SEPARATE append-chunk! (two observer batches / two sweeps) and asserts the delta still merges into app-db.

SEVERITY: correctness bug on the speculative streaming-hydration path; self-heals at final payload, so no persistent corruption. Worst-case user-visible symptom is a flash of stale state in a resolved region for a delta-emitting boundary.
notes: Dispatched 2026-07-12 (solo P2). Worktree ssr-streaming-x35. Surface ssr/streaming/client.cljs — free (no ssr worker). No-full-spine brief.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5728: sweep-level apply-ready-deltas! decouples delta application from resolved-template presence; handles both split-batch orderings. Gates green (ssr JVM 395/1670, node cljs 8937/42162, browser 285/1004).

title: (BUG) Epoch flush is a MACROTASK — the uSES tear window is NOT closed; docstrings claim microtask alignment falsely (must fix before S2f Tier-3 mounts)
description: ViewCell review finding 1 (MAJOR PLAUSIBLE, 2026-07-12). reactive.cljc:261-272 mark-dirty! schedules flush via interop/next-tick = goog.async.nextTick = MACROTASK; viewcell getSnapshot = revision. Time-sliced pass: cell A renders v1, React yields, drain moves the sub, watch queues macrotask flush, React resumes + renders B seeing v2, commit-time checkIfSnapshotChanged sees A's revision UNMOVED -> paints A=v1/B=v2 torn; correction one task later. Violates 006 invariant 5 ('host corrects before paint') + the 03 §2 two-guard rule's guard-1 leg. S2d (#5713, rf2-vxgfnd.10) lands the epoch-close synchronous flush (invariant 6) which should close this — AFTER #5713 MERGES: verify the sync-flush path covers watch-fired dirt (not only epoch-batched notifications) and add a tearing fixture (concurrent-features testbed or simulated interleaving). If any dirty source still defers to a macrotask, fix to microtask/sync. Surface: reactive.cljc + tests; sequence behind #5713.
notes: STATUS AFTER #5733 (.45's merge, 2026-07-12 09:50): NOT closed — and the falsehood count went UP. #5733 correctly re-ruled the contract (006 invariant 6 = drain-quiescence render batch; epochs are evidence units) and re-keyed coalescing per-drain, but schedule-flush! STILL arms interop/next-tick (reactive.cljc:468-491) and its NEW docstring re-asserts 'a true goog.async.nextTick microtask' — the exact claim the S2d review disproved from Closure's vendored source ('This will NOT schedule the callback as a microtask'; impls: setImmediate/MessageChannel/setTimeout — all tasks). Under time-slicing, React's already-posted continuation task can run BEFORE the armed flush -> the tear paints. THE FIX IS NOW EVEN SIMPLER: coalescing is already per-drain, so swap next-tick for js/queueMicrotask in schedule-flush! title: JVM observation owner record defeats its WeakHashMap key and retains abandoned nodes
description:
## Problem

PR #5710 moved active observation leases into the value of the JVM node-records table, a process-global java.util.WeakHashMap keyed by reaction. Each value now contains :owners, a strong persistent set of ObservationLease objects. Each lease state strongly references its reaction.

That creates this path:

node-records global -> record value -> owners set -> lease -> lease state -> reaction weak key

Java WeakHashMap is not an ephemeron map: a value that directly or indirectly strongly references its key prevents the key from becoming weakly reachable. The source comments and Spec-facing rationale claim the opposite: that records die with reactions with no pruning or retention.

## Steps to Reproduce

Against main 565dda1d85 / merged PR #5710:

1. Create a JVM interop Reaction and an ObservationLease whose state points to that reaction.
2. Invoke the real private register-owner! once, placing the lease in the reaction's weak-table record.
3. Retain only WeakReference objects to the reaction and lease; drop every ordinary reference.
4. Run 20 GC cycles with a matched control Reaction that was not enrolled.

Observed:

{:control-collected? true,
 :registered-reaction-collected? false,
 :registered-lease-collected? false}

The probe then deregistered the owner to avoid polluting the audit process. This directly explains why PR #5710's deterministic active-owner assertions pass while its requested weak-reference/GC proof was not supplied.

## Expected Behavior

The node side table must not be a GC root for either the reaction or its owner leases. If cache/frame teardown is interrupted and the whole node/owner component is otherwise unreachable, the JVM collector must reclaim it just as the CLJS WeakMap/interop design intends.

## Actual Behavior

An active owner stored in the weak-map value closes the weak key back into a strong reachability cycle rooted at the global map. The reaction and lease remain live indefinitely until explicit deregistration/disposal happens.

## Impact

Normal balanced release is fixed by #5710, but an exception or partial teardown that drops a frame/cache and its committed owner without completing dispose/release becomes a process-lifetime leak on JVM SSR/headless hosts. This undercuts the exact failure-resilience reason interop reaction callbacks were moved off a global strong registry. It also makes the source claim that the weak record needs no pruning false.

## Coordination

Distinct from rf2-vxgfnd.15's historical released-owner leak and rf2-vxgfnd.32's hook-installation race. All three share the owner registry surface, so sequence or combine implementation deliberately, but keep separate regression proofs and close criteria. This should block the S2 ownership/leak gate.
design:
Remove every strong value-to-key backedge from the JVM weak side table. Do not paper over the result with periodic pruning.

Plausible restrained designs include a node-scoped owner registry reachable from the reaction's own disposal callback/self-contained object graph, with only a weak reference to that registry in the global evidence record; or a per-node weak-key owner collection whose values do not reference leases/reactions. Split evidence bookkeeping from owner bookkeeping if that produces the clearest invariant. A released owner must still disappear synchronously, and a genuinely live externally-held lease must still be notified exactly once.

Whichever representation is chosen, document the reachability graph explicitly for both java.util.WeakHashMap and js/WeakMap. Avoid relying on Java WeakHashMap as though it had JavaScript ephemeron semantics. Keep the cache entry shape and public adapter API unchanged unless a wider disposal primitive is separately justified.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Add a deterministic JVM WeakReference/ReferenceQueue regression equivalent to the reproduction: the enrolled reaction and lease become collectable after all external/cache references are dropped, and a non-enrolled control demonstrates that the test can observe collection.
2. The regression must fail on PR #5710 and must not depend solely on asserting the logical owner count.
3. While a lease is externally live and its node is canonical, HMR/explicit-disposal notification remains exactly once; two live sibling owners remain independent and balanced.
4. Released-owner churn remains O(current owners) with one node-scoped hook and no retained historical closures; run the originally requested 10,000-cycle fixture on both hosts.
5. Interrupted/exceptional frame or cache teardown cannot leave the global observation tables retaining a reaction/lease component solely through table values.
6. Preserve exact cache-entry shape, constant-time normal acquire/release, no process-wide scans, and production bundle/elision budgets.
7. Update comments/contracts that currently claim records die with reactions so they describe and test the actual reachability invariant.
close_reason: Closed

title: ui: wire frame-provider React-context tier into compiled sub/dispatch resolution (pure-ui substrate)
description: S2c (rf2-vxgfnd.9, #PR) landed frame-provider SCOPE: on CLJS it sets the shared React frame context (re-frame.adapter.context/provider-element) and re-frame.ui.frames/resolve-frame reads that context directly as the tested ambient chain. BUT the compiled view sub-read path (re-frame.ui.reactive/sub-read -> re-frame.substrate.observation/resolve-target -> re-frame.frame/resolve-current-frame) resolves the ambient frame via the :adapter/current-frame late-bind hook, which in a PURE compiled-ui app (no Reagent/UIx/Helix adapter loaded) is UNBOUND. design: Two candidate mechanisms: (a) the ui runtime publishes adapter-context/function-component-current-frame through late-bind/set-fn! :adapter/current-frame at ns-load (same impl UIx/Helix publish) so core's resolve-current-frame sees the context tier — a near one-liner, behaviour-preserving for tests that don't set context, additive for those that do; (b) have sub-read/resolve-target consult the ui context reader directly. Both touch a shared coordination surface. The single-slot :adapter/current-frame hook means a MIXED app (compiled-ui + a classic adapter) would have two publishers (last-writer-wins) — that mixed-substrate coordination is rf2-3yij territory and is the reason S2c deferred this. Decide the home (a ui-adapter ns vs re-frame.ui.frames) and add a DOM fixture: a (sub ...) inside a frame-provider reads the scoped frame's app-db end-to-end on a real React root.
acceptance_criteria: A compiled (sub ...)/dispatch inside a frame-provider subtree resolves the provider's frame on CLJS (real React root), with a DOM fixture proving it; the pure-ui substrate resolves the React-context tier with no adapter loaded; mixed-app single-slot-hook coordination is explicitly ruled or scoped out.
notes: RULED by Mike 2026-07-12: MECHANISM (a) — the ui runtime publishes its React-context frame reader through the SAME :adapter/current-frame late-bind hook UIx/Helix already use (near one-liner, additive, behaviour-preserving). Home: a ui-adapter ns (matches the classic-adapter pattern). Mixed-app (two publishers, last-writer-wins on the single slot): SCOPED OUT to rf2-3yij — pure-ui only for this bead. Consumer frame/require-current-frame! (frame.cljc:320) is unchanged; it already consults the hook. Bundled with rf2-vxgfnd.25 (same frames.cljc surface + same root cause). Unblocks .14/.58/.43/.71-frame-provider-row + S2e(.11)/S2f(.12).
