title: Run an independent adversarial correctness review at each re-frame.ui stage boundary
description:
## Problem

The substrate program is landing unusually large, contract-heavy changes without an independent review submission or recorded adversarial disposition. Stage-1 PRs #5692/#5697/#5699/#5700/#5701/#5703 and the adjacent #5704/#5705/#5706 sequence all merged with zero GitHub reviews; #5704 and #5705 alone touched 617 files, and #5706 added the concurrency-critical observation port.

CI coverage is strong but proves the authored fixtures, not that the contract has no missing state. A fresh independent read of #5706 found two deterministic classes the suite missed: same-id frame reincarnation can evade live evidence comparison, and released leases accumulate disposal closures on a shared live node. Those are now rf2-vxgfnd.14/.15.

The program needs a lightweight stage-boundary adversarial review, not ceremonial approval of every small commit.

## Scope

Start with one S2 review after rf2-vxgfnd.8-.12 and the correctness follow-ups are assembled. Repeat once at each later stage boundary before filing/dispatching the next stage's implementation wave. The reviewer must not be the worker who implemented the reviewed slice and must inspect source/contracts/tests directly rather than treating PR bodies or bead analysis as evidence.

## Review Lenses

- Implementability and cross-document/API coherence.
- Ownership, render/commit concurrency, HMR, lifecycle and rollback failure paths.
- Production efficiency/elision and bundle isolation.
- Test teeth: construct counterexamples outside the authored happy-path fixtures.
- Compatibility-tier boundary and migration/adoption consequences.
- Fresh-build/watch-build equivalence and observability/Xray attribution.

## Non-goals

Do not require a GitHub approval ceremony for tiny/docs-only PRs, duplicate full test runs already green in CI, or reopen Mike's ratified product decisions. The goal is one high-signal independent review per stage, with concrete findings dispositioned.

## RULED OPERATING PROTOCOL (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-12)

The per-boundary review CONTINUES, re-scoped as below. This section is the standing protocol; future boundary-review dispatches are briefed from it. Empirical basis: the S2 cycle produced 67 review findings (58 P1/P2, 87% hit-rate, effectively 100% review-found; only ~4-6 of 67 even gate-catchable in principle), so the review stays — but its cost centre (unbounded review→fix→re-review loops) is bounded by the fix-PR protocol.

LEAN CRITERION (Mike, 2026-07-12): every obligation in this protocol must map to a defect class the empirical record shows; anything that stops earning its hit-rate gets cut at the next boundary, not hedged around. Deliberately NOT built: CI mutation-testing infrastructure, per-PR approval ceremony, full re-reads outside ownership/port/concurrency surfaces.

### 1. Fix-PR verification protocol (mandatory for every correctness-fix PR arising from a boundary review)

- (a) The PR must include a fixture VERIFIED TO FAIL PRE-FIX (the #5750/#5758 mutation method: run the fixture against the unfixed code or a reverted/mutated fix, confirm red, then confirm green with the fix). The PR body must state this was done and how.
- (b) The PR must diff-check every docstring/spec claim it touches against shipped behaviour. (Failure mode this prevents: .45's fix #5733 re-asserted the exact false microtask docstring the .40 review had already disproved from Closure source.)
- Enforcement: in dispatch-brief text — every fix-worker brief carries both obligations verbatim. No CI mechanism yet (fixture-fails-pre-fix is not mechanically checkable without mutation infrastructure); the boundary reviewer SAMPLES compliance instead of full re-reading. Exception: fix PRs touching ownership, observation-port, or concurrency surfaces still get FULL re-read — the .59-.83 wave (25 findings, 9 P1, dominated by second-generation defects in fix PRs) proves fixes on those surfaces are a real defect source.

### 2. Dimensions retiring to S2f gates

Retention/leaks, scaling, fan-in, equality no-op, and push economics move from the review charter to the G-3/4/5/6/13 CI gates (rf2-vxgfnd.12) — but ONLY after the boundary review performs a one-time GATE-TEETH AUDIT: mutate each gated property and confirm the gate goes red. Until that audit passes, these dimensions stay in the review charter (the .39/.43 vacuous-test findings are exactly the false-green failure mode this precondition guards against).

### 3. S2→S3 boundary charter

Run after .11 + .12 merge, before any S3 dispatch (S3 = events + debugging-as-consumer):

- (i) verify the four open P1s (.14, .61, .76, .80) are closed or Mike-ruled non-blocking — all four are ownership/lifecycle, i.e. ineligible for a conditional-advance waiver under this bead's own rules;
- (ii) gate-teeth audit per §2;
- (iii) adversarial HMR/REPL-equivalence pass — .11's NO_SOURCE_FILE ledger-key finding shows this surface is still soft;
- (iv) spec-honesty sweep (006/004 + docstrings vs shipped code — the .49/.50/.66 class), since S3 briefs will cite these contracts as authoritative;
- (v) S3-facing inventory: dispatch path through compiled views, ui.test dispatch!/flush! semantics, and the evidence/Xray projections (.74/.75) that debugging-as-consumer builds on.

Skip re-reviewing compiler/emitter internals (stable since S1) except open .68.

### 4. Reviewer hygiene

Partition surfaces one-reviewer-each and require a pre-file dedup pass against open beads (~6% duplicate rate in S2: .38→.32, .57→.48, .54, .82). Later mechanical stages (S6/S7) get the narrower migration/perf lens already prescribed in DESIGN.
design:
Model this as a stage-close review bead. Give the reviewer the final stage diff plus owning specs, but require an independent surface inventory and targeted runtime probes. Record findings with severity, exact evidence, and recommended fixes; file distinct actionable beads and add them as blockers of the next stage gate. Explicitly disposition clean areas and accepted trade-offs so later reviews do not re-litigate them.

Keep the cadence proportional: one review at S2 close, then one per stage boundary. A stage with only mechanical adoption can use a narrower migration/performance lens; concurrency/SSR stages get the full adversarial set.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Complete an independent S2 review after the implementation/gate set is assembled, covering the observation port, ViewCell, ENSURE/preflight, HMR, ui.test, production elision, and their Spec 004/006 contracts.
2. The reviewer did not implement the reviewed slices and documents a fresh inventory, counterexample probes, findings, clean areas, and final readiness verdict.
3. Every actionable finding becomes a carefully scoped bead with severity, reproduction, design direction, acceptance criteria, and dependency placement; accepted trade-offs are explicitly dispositioned without new work.
4. S3 implementation dispatch does not begin until S2 blocker findings are closed or Mike explicitly rules them non-blocking.
5. Add the same one-review stage-close rule to the substrate program handoff/checklist when that document is next edited; do not retrofit per-PR bureaucracy.
6. Review evidence is preserved in the mayor checkout/bead record and the relevant PR/stage handoff links to it.
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike 2026-07-12): CONTINUE the per-stage-boundary independent adversarial review — do not retire or replace it with gates — RE-SCOPED with (1) a mandatory fix-PR verification protocol, (2) retirement of the retention/scaling/fan-in/equality-no-op/push-economics dimensions to the S2f G-gates once a one-time gate-teeth audit passes, and (3) the five-point S2→S3 boundary charter fixed below. The bead DESCRIPTION has been amended to carry this as the standing protocol (## RULED OPERATING PROTOCOL section); future boundary-review dispatches brief from it.

RATIONALE: The S2 empirical record is decisive: 67 findings this cycle, 58 (87%) P1/P2 correctness defects, effectively 100% review-found, while only ~4-6 of 67 were even gate-catchable in principle — ownership races, false diagnostics, dead/unwired code, test vacuity, and spec/docstring honesty have no gate. The .59-.83 wave (25 findings, 9 P1) was dominated by second-generation defects in the fix PRs themselves (worst case: .45's fix #5733 re-asserted the false microtask docstring the .40 review had already disproved), which is precisely what the fix-PR protocol converts from an unbounded re-review loop into bounded sampled review. Review products also became durable CI (#5750's mutation-verified browser tear gate), so the review compounds rather than merely consuming capacity. Per Mike's lean posture directive (pre-alpha, no gold-plating): every retained obligation maps to a recorded defect class, and ceremony that doesn't is explicitly rejected — no CI mutation infrastructure, no per-PR approval ceremony, sampling instead of full re-reads except where the record shows fixes actually fail (ownership/port/concurrency); any obligation that stops earning its hit-rate gets cut at the next boundary.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:

[A] Fix-PR obligations (every correctness-fix PR from a boundary review): (a) include a fixture VERIFIED TO FAIL PRE-FIX (the #5750/#5758 mutation method — run against unfixed/mutated code, confirm red, then green with the fix; PR body states this was done); (b) diff-check every docstring/spec claim the PR touches against shipped behaviour. ENFORCED IN DISPATCH-BRIEF TEXT (both obligations verbatim in every fix-worker brief), not CI — fixture-fails-pre-fix is not mechanically checkable without mutation infrastructure; the boundary reviewer samples compliance. Exception: fix PRs on ownership/observation-port/concurrency surfaces still get FULL re-read.

[B] Dimensions retiring to S2f gates: retention/leaks, scaling, fan-in, equality no-op, push economics → G-3/4/5/6/13 (rf2-vxgfnd.12). title: Semantic tree normalization ignores schema version and silently accepts malformed discriminator maps
description:
## Problem

The public JVM tree contract is versioned and has a closed five-variant node schema. It requires consumers to fail loudly on a missing/non-integer/unsupported root version and on a map carrying zero or multiple discriminating fields.

`re-frame.ui.semantic/normalize` currently calls `norm-nodes` directly without checking `:rf.ui/tree-version`. Its `norm-node` uses `cond` precedence: `:tag` wins, then `:html`, then `:view-id`/`:children`; a map with no recognized discriminator contributes `[]`. Thus unsupported versions are treated as version 1, ambiguous maps are silently interpreted by branch order, and discriminator-less maps disappear as empty output.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call `semantic/normalize` on a valid root tree whose `:rf.ui/tree-version` is missing, non-integer, or `2`.
2. Observe normal output instead of a typed incompatibility error.
3. Call it on `{:rf.ui/tree-version 1 :tag :div :html "trusted"}`; observe it accepted as an element because `:tag` wins.
4. Call it on `{:rf.ui/tree-version 1}`; observe `[]` rather than `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed`.

## Expected Behavior

Normalization validates the root schema version before traversal and enforces exactly one node discriminator per map. Unsupported input never produces a plausible fingerprint/semantic tree.

## Actual Behavior

Normalization silently projects malformed or future-version trees under today's rules, causing data loss and potentially stable-looking but invalid fingerprints/parity results.

## Impact

`N(tree)` is the semantic equivalence/fingerprint boundary shared by emitter parity and future SSR. Accepting unknown schema versions defeats the version field, while cond-precedence makes corrupted trees non-diagnostic. A future tree-version bump could be consumed incorrectly rather than failing at the boundary.

## Coordination

rf2-vxgfnd.13 is currently promoting the JVM tree contract. Do not edit that in-progress bead. Land this follow-up after its PR so the tracked contract, error catalogue, implementation, and fixtures move together. The S5 SSR-specific error may remain S5; Tier-1 normalization still needs an honest typed failure now.
design:
Add one root validation boundary to `normalize`: require integer supported version 1 before any node work. Then centralize node discrimination so exactly one of `:tag`, `:view-id`, `:html`, or fragment-only `:children` is present; zero or multiple discriminators throw `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed`. Strip/ignore optional reserved diagnostic keys only after structural validity is established.

Use the generic tree-malformed error for malformed version shape if that matches the promoted contract, and reserve `:rf.error/ssr-ui-tree-version-unsupported` for the S5 serializer; alternatively introduce one shared unsupported-tree-version id deliberately and catalogue it. Do not silently coerce or default missing versions.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `normalize` rejects missing, non-integer, and unsupported root versions before traversing children; ex-data includes `:got` and `:supported #{1}`.
2. Version 1 valid trees normalize byte-identically to current golden output.
3. Every pair of map discriminators is rejected, as are maps with none; errors use the canonical builder and identify the malformed node/path.
4. A fragment is recognized only by `:children` in the absence of the other discriminators; empty valid fragments remain legal.
5. Unknown optional `:rf.ui/*` diagnostic keys remain ignored after version/shape validation, per the forward-compatible contract.
6. Add table/property tests covering all five valid variants, all ambiguous pairs, empty maps, nested malformed nodes, and version failures.
7. Ensure parity fingerprints, ui.test projections, and the future SSR boundary share one discriminator/validation implementation rather than drifting copies.
8. Update the promoted tree contract and Spec 009 rows without prematurely implementing unrelated S5 serialization.

title: ui.test/render rejects and cannot preflight contract-valid plan-bearing root forms
description:
## Problem

The root identity contract says `ui.test/render` literal root forms accept the same top-region wrapper grammar as `ui/mount`. A top-region `frame-root` contributes static frame plans; Tier-1 render must run ENSURE against fresh test frames, and must reject `{:frame ...}`/`{:app-db ...}` when the root form owns frames.

Current `render-literal-form` calls the ordinary single-node analyzer and then requires the top AST op to be `:view`. It does not use the root analyzer/scan, collect plans, run preflight, or enforce the plan-bearing option conflict. Consequently a valid wrapper-headed root is rejected as `:rf.ui.compile/bad-test-root`, while the docstring promises support will arrive with the mount slice.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Define a `defview` that reads a subscription from its ambient frame.
2. Call `ui.test/render` with a literal top-region form headed by `ui/frame-root`, containing a static frame config/initial event and the view.
3. Observe macro expansion rejecting the head because the ordinary analyzer returns `:frame-root`, not `:view`.
4. Alternatively combine the plan-bearing form with `{:frame existing}`; current code never reaches the contract's specific 'root form owns its frames' rejection because plans are not scanned.

## Expected Behavior

The literal form follows the same root analysis grammar as `ui/mount`; static plans preflight fresh test frames before JVM structural rendering; the mounted view sees the planned ambient frame; conflicting explicit frame/app-db options fail didactically; all test-owned frames are torn down.

## Actual Behavior

Wrapper-headed valid roots are rejected, plan payloads never execute, and the promised plan-bearing option rule is unimplemented.

## Coordination

rf2-vxgfnd.9 owns the live ENSURE/preflight implementation and is already in progress. Do not edit that bead or duplicate its frame engine. Dispatch this follow-up only after its PR is merged, then reuse its settled preflight primitive from the JVM test host.
design:
Route literal `ui.test/render` through the same compile-time root analyzer/scan used by `ui/mount`, producing the structural AST plus static plans without involving React. Reuse the S2c CLJC ENSURE/preflight transaction to create test-owned frames, bind the resolved ambient frame for the render, and tear test-owned frames down in a `finally` boundary. Keep each render call's document/root registry local.

Reject `:frame` or `:app-db` only when plans are present, with the contract's dedicated didactic message; preserve their plan-free behavior. Do not add a second plan parser, a hidden `:rf/default` fallback, or an interpreted-hiccup path.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A literal root form with top-region `frame-root` compiles, runs its static plan/initial events exactly once, and renders subscription-derived JVM tree output from the planned frame.
2. Top-region fragments/elements/providers surrounding the one mounted view scan identically to `ui/mount`; conditional/list `frame-root` remains a compile error.
3. `{:frame ...}` and `{:app-db ...}` combined with a plan-bearing root fail with the specific 'root form owns its frames' error; the same opts remain valid for plan-free root/view forms.
4. A preflight failure leaves no test frame/root residue and preserves the original typed error; successful renders tear down every test-owned frame in `finally`.
5. Plan config expressions evaluate once at preflight, never during speculative tree traversal.
6. Two `ui.test/render` calls remain separate document scopes; duplicate-root state never leaks between them.
7. Runtime-assembled vectors remain rejected, `:props` remains rejected for literal roots, and `:sub-overrides` composes with both accepted forms.
8. Add JVM fixtures using the real compiler, real frame/sub system, and structural emitter; keep S2c client preflight tests green.
notes: Dispatched 2026-07-12 (solo P2) after #5713/S2c/#5712 landed the mount+root machinery. Worktree uitest-root-vxgfnd19. Surface ui/test.cljc only (calls-not-edits compiler/client).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5720 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5720). ui.test/render literal form now routes through root/analyze-root (same grammar as ui/mount): plan-bearing top-region frame-root forms preflight fresh test frames via frames/execute-frame-plans!, bind the innermost enclosing frame-root as the view's ambient frame, reject {:frame}/{:app-db} didactically, and tear down all test-owned frames. Gates 0-fail: test-render-jvm 29/68, full ui JVM 216/4304, roster+root-analysis+root-mount 42/559, npm test:cljs 8923/42115.

title: Root lifecycle is not exception-safe after host claim or during unmount
description:
## Problem

The active S2c work correctly moves frame preflight before `ReactDOM.createRoot`, so a preflight failure will leave the container untouched. Two adjacent exception paths remain unowned:

1. A new `mount*` registers the live root before evaluating/passing the compiled element to `.render`. If the element thunk or synchronous host render call throws, the root-id/container claim remains installed and the React root is not best-effort unmounted. A retry can then see a phantom live root.
2. `unmount!*` calls React `.unmount` and only afterwards releases the live-root entry. If host teardown throws, registry release is skipped permanently.

These paths violate the root contract's TOTAL teardown/idempotent retry posture.

## Steps to Reproduce

After rf2-vxgfnd.9 lands:

1. Call `client/mount*` for a fresh root with successful preflight and an `element-thunk` that throws a tagged exception.
2. Inspect the live-root registry/container ownership and retry the same root id/container.
3. Separately register a fake Root whose host `.unmount` throws, then call `unmount!*` and inspect the registry.

Current control flow leaves the first root claimed after render construction failure and leaves the second claimed after teardown failure.

## Expected Behavior

A failed initial mount leaves no live-root/container claim or host root residue and preserves the original exception. Total teardown always releases framework ownership in a `finally`-shaped boundary, even if host cleanup reports an error. Retrying a failed mount is safe.

## Actual Behavior

Framework registry cleanup occurs only on the success path after operations that can throw. A single failure can poison root identity/container ownership for the rest of the session.

## Scope and Coordination

rf2-vxgfnd.9 is already in progress in the same file and is implementing preflight-before-createRoot. Do not amend or collide with that worker. Dispatch this follow-up only after its PR is merged (repo close-at-PR convention is not sufficient; verify GitHub state), and retain its Q49 preflight ordering.
design:
Keep the successful path simple. After preflight, evaluate all render input that can be evaluated before claiming the host root. Once `createRoot`/live registration occurs, wrap initial render in a catch/finally-shaped rollback: identity-guarded release of the exact root plus best-effort host unmount, while rethrowing the original mount exception even if cleanup also fails. For `unmount!*`, release the exact live-root claim in `finally`; preserve the host teardown error for the caller and make subsequent calls no-ops.

Do not swallow failures, add retry timers, or weaken stale-handle identity guards. Existing-root re-render failure may keep the prior live root/last committed tree; distinguish it explicitly from failed first mount.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A preflight failure still occurs before `createRoot` and leaves frame, DOM container, and live-root registry untouched (retain rf2-vxgfnd.9 coverage).
2. A throwing initial element thunk leaves no live-root/container claim, best-effort unmounts any created host root, rethrows the original tagged exception, and permits a clean retry.
3. A synchronous `.render` throw after host creation has the same rollback guarantees; cleanup failure cannot mask the original render error.
4. A throwing host `.unmount` still releases the exact framework root/prefix/container claim in `finally`, propagates the teardown error, and makes a second `unmount!*` a no-op.
5. A stale Root handle never releases a newer root's claim.
6. Existing-root re-render failure keeps the existing root registered and its previous committed render intact; document/test this distinct case.
7. Add DOM-level and registry-level fixtures and keep mount/preflight/HMR suites green.
notes: Dispatched 2026-07-12 (mayor 10m loop, solo P2) after S2c/#5711 merged (freed client.cljs). Worktree root-lifecycle-vxgfnd18 at main 469ccd31bc. Surface client.cljs mount*/unmount!* — disjoint from running .10 (reactive/viewcell/ui.test) + #5712 (compiler/spec).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5715 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5715). mount* first-render rollback (release exact claim + best-effort host unmount + rethrow original) and unmount!* finally-release. Adversarial fixtures added (node registry + browser DOM). Gates green: test:cljs 8927/42122 0-fail, test:browser 283/993 0-fail, fast-pr spine PASS.

title: Compiler build registries leak stale views, roots, plans, descriptors, and custom elements across rebuilds
description:
## Problem

The S1 compiler accumulates build facts in process-global `defonce` atoms with no real build/file lifecycle:

- `re-frame.ui.compiler/build-views`
- `re-frame.ui.compiler.root/build-roots`
- `build-plans`
- `build-descriptors`
- `re-frame.ui.rules/custom-elements`

Macro expansion only `assoc`s current declarations. Root registries have a test-only manual reset; view and custom-element registries do not have a build boundary. Deleting or renaming a declaration/file therefore leaves its old contribution in the compiler JVM. Watch builds, sequential builds in one daemon, REPL reloads, and tests can observe stale output that a fresh process does not.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In one long-lived compiler JVM, compile file A containing a `defview`, a root descriptor/static frame plan, and a `ui/custom-element` declaration.
2. Remove or rename those forms (or remove file A) and trigger an incremental rebuild without restarting the JVM.
3. Read `current-build-digest`, root/plan/descriptor indexes, and custom-element property classification.
4. Compare them with a clean-process build of the edited source.

The incremental process retains facts that no longer exist. A later file can also receive a false cross-file duplicate-root or frame-payload-conflict error from the deleted site.

## Expected Behavior

Compiler artefacts are a pure function of the current build inputs. Incremental/watch output after additions, edits, deletions, and renames is equivalent to a clean build, and independent builds sharing one JVM are isolated.

## Actual Behavior

The process lifetime is treated as the build lifetime. Same-key re-expansion overwrites some rows, but deletion, rename, removed files, separate build ids, and custom-element declaration removal have no cleanup path. Build digests/descriptors may contain ghosts and diagnostics may depend on build history.

## Impact

This directly undermines the promised HMR/REPL equivalence, deterministic fingerprints, duplicate detection, and watch-mode ergonomics. It can also classify custom-element props using declarations absent from the current source. Restarting the compiler is not an acceptable correctness mechanism.

## Coordination

This is a prerequisite for rf2-vxgfnd.11's full HMR matrix. Keep it separate from the in-progress S2b/S2c workers; it owns compiler lifecycle/state rather than reactivity or frame preflight.
design:
Introduce one explicit build-scoped compiler state model shared by views, roots, plans, descriptors, and compile-time custom-element declarations. It must know both build identity and source-file/namespace contribution so a recompiled or removed source replaces/removes its entire prior contribution atomically. Derive the aggregate digest and conflict indexes from current contributions, not from append-only process history.

Choose the smallest integration supported reliably by the CLJ/CLJS compiler environments (for example a build-id plus per-file contribution ledger and explicit begin/end/reconcile hooks). Do not scatter ad-hoc resets across macros, because multiple declarations in one file and file deletion make 'clear on first macro' unsound. Keep emitted runtime custom-element registration lifecycle coherent with compile-time removal. No production runtime lookup should pay for compiler bookkeeping.
acceptance_criteria:
1. In one JVM, build source A, then delete/rename a view, root, static frame plan, descriptor, and custom-element declaration; incremental artefacts and `current-build-digest` must equal a clean-process build of the edited source.
2. Two build ids compiled in the same JVM are isolated; neither contributes rows or conflicts to the other.
3. Removing a file clears all of that file's contributions; editing a file with multiple declarations replaces the file contribution atomically without dropping sibling declarations.
4. A deleted root/plan no longer causes false duplicate/conflict errors, while genuine current cross-file duplicates still fail with both source locations.
5. Removing/renaming a custom-element declaration removes stale property classification from compile and runtime/HMR behavior.
6. Build state remains bounded across repeated watch rebuilds and needs no test-only global reset for correctness.
7. Build digest/descriptors remain compile-order independent and deterministic.
8. Add clean-vs-incremental parity fixtures and make them part of rf2-vxgfnd.11's HMR/REPL gate; no production bundle bytes or hot-path branches are added.
notes: Fixed in PR #5719 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5719). New re-frame.ui.compiler.build build-scoped model: all five registries route writes through a per-source contribution ledger with cross-registry atomic replace on begin-build!; reconcile! drops deleted files; reset-build! generalises reset-build-registries!. 11 adversarial fixtures in compiler_build_jvm_test.clj prove clean-vs-incremental parity + no false cross-file duplicate/conflict from deleted sites. Gates: ui JVM 217/0-fail, test:cljs 8914/0-fail, core JVM 0-fail, per-ns isolation 15/15. FOLLOW-UP: wire begin-build! into the shadow-cljs build lifecycle (build/stage hook — hot-zone shadow-cljs.edn, out of this surface).

title: :rf.machine/action-ran's :outcome tag carries no classification pass — a data-classified action return value leaks raw
description:
SUMMARY
Surfaced building the rf2-agb5jk RealWorld password-egress closure test (framework-tree sentinel-sweep, PR #5687). `:rf.machine/action-ran`'s `:outcome` tag — the raw return value of a machine action fn (implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc, `run-action`, ~line 1841: `(assoc base-tags :outcome (if (nil? r) :ok r))`) — carries NO classification pass in `project-machine-tags` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc). The function's cond-> clauses handle `:before` / `:after` / `:snapshot` / bare `:data` / `:input` / `:cascade` / (post-rf2-ghgbqi) `:event`, but not `:outcome`.

REPRO
Register a machine whose SPEC declares `:sensitive [[:data :secret]]` (durable-data-rooted classification, EP-0025 style — e.g. realworld_http's `:settings/form` machine's `:sensitive [[:data :draft :password] [:data :submitted :password]]`). Dispatch a sub-event whose action returns `{:data (assoc data :secret "raw")}`. The emitted `:rf.machine/action-ran` trace's `:outcome` tag shows `{:data {:secret "raw" ...}}` — RAW, unredacted — even though the SAME `:data` shape correctly redacts everywhere ELSE the classification reaches (`:before`/`:after`/`:snapshot`/bare `:data`/`[:input :data]`).

This is PRE-EXISTING and NOT introduced by rf2-agb5jk's app redesign — it affects the settings machine's original `:edit` action identically (present since the machine's `:data`-rooted classification first landed, PR #5636). It was never caught before because no existing test performs a trace-listener sweep of the settings machine's dispatched trace stream; rf2-agb5jk's new closure test (implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_realworld_password_classification_cljs_test.cljs, `settings-machine-routed-password-subevents-echo-slots-redact`) is the first to catch it, and scopes its assertions to the specific `:event` / `[:input :event]` slots rf2-ghgbqi's completion DOES cover, documenting `:outcome` as an accepted residual rather than asserting a false clean bill.

WHY IT MATTERS
Any machine action that returns updated `:data` containing a classified path (the NORMAL, expected shape of a state-mutating action) leaks that data raw via `:outcome` — on EVERY transition, not just ones carrying a routed secret. This is a wider-reaching gap than rf2-agb5jk's `:edit-password` case: it affects the machine's `:data`-rooted classification generally, wherever an action's return value happens to include a classified `:data` subpath (which is most actions that touch classified state).

SUGGESTED FIX SHAPE (not prescriptive)
Add an `:outcome` clause to `project-machine-tags`'s cond->, redacting it with the SAME `:data`-rooted classification path set the bare `:data` / `[:input :data]` clauses already use (an action's `:outcome` map, when it carries a `:data` key, is snapshot-:data-shaped — same redaction fn, `project-data`, should apply). Verify: does `:outcome` ALWAYS carry `{:data ...}` shape, or can an action return other effect keys (`:fx`, etc.) that also need consideration? Check `run-action`'s full contract (Spec 005 §Actions) before assuming shape.

SURFACE
implementation/core (classification.cljc, `project-machine-tags`) and/or implementation/machines (transition.cljc, `run-action` — if the fix instead reshapes what `:outcome` carries rather than adding a projector clause).

title: Nested :dispatch fx + :rf.event/fx aggregate don't propagate a classified TARGET event's :sensitive to the DISPATCHING handler's trace
description:
SUMMARY
Surfaced building the rf2-agb5jk RealWorld password-egress closure test (framework-tree sentinel-sweep, PR #5687). Two related classification-projector gaps in the SAME `:rf.event/fx` / `:rf.fx/handled` trace surface for a handler's OWN returned effect vector — both confirmed to PRE-DATE this PR (present in examples/core/login, the reference model, too — never swept this thoroughly before now).

GAP (a) — nested :dispatch doesn't inherit the TARGET event's classification
A `[:dispatch [target-event ...]]` fx entry NESTED inside another handler's `:fx` vector does not inherit the TARGET event's own `:sensitive` registration at the DISPATCHING handler's own `:rf.fx/handled` (`:rf.fx/id :dispatch`) / `:rf.event/fx` aggregate trace. Per the established mechanism (rf2-6h3c02, documented in examples/core/login's `:auth.login/succeeded` comment and the example_login_success_token_cljs_test.cljs regression), the projector walks each `[fx-id args]` entry in `:rf.event/fx` through THAT FX's own registration — but `:dispatch` itself (a framework built-in) carries no static `:sensitive`, so a classified TARGET event dispatched via `[:dispatch [target-event ...]]` ships its raw args at the PARENT's trace regardless of the target's own classification.

Repro: register event A with `:sensitive [[1 :secret]]`. Register event B whose handler returns `{:fx [[:dispatch [A {:secret "raw"}]]]}`. Dispatch B. B's own `:rf.fx/handled` (`:rf.fx/id :dispatch`) and `:rf.event/fx` aggregate both carry the raw secret; A's OWN dispatched-event trace (`:rf.event/v`) redacts correctly (proving A's own classification is fine — the gap is specifically the PARENT's view of the nested dispatch).

Worked around in rf2-agb5jk's PR by NOT nesting a classified dispatch — the JWT flow inlines a shared `store-session-db` fn called directly (`:db` write) rather than `[:dispatch [:auth/store-session user]]`. NOT workaroundable for a MACHINE-routed sub-event (dispatching INTO a machine has no non-`:dispatch` form) — see rf2-<settings-residual-bead> for that specific instance (realworld_http's `:settings/edit-password` / `:submit-valid`).

GAP (b) — :rf.event/fx doesn't understand :rf.http/managed's dynamic :sensitive? flag
The SAME `:rf.event/fx` aggregate walker only understands STATIC per-fx `:sensitive [[paths]]` registrations (gap a's mechanism) — it has no awareness of `:rf.http/managed`'s DIFFERENT, DYNAMIC privacy model: a per-call `:sensitive? true` flag living INSIDE the request args map (see `re-frame.http.privacy/request-sensitive?`), which the DEDICATED `:rf.http/*` trace ops + the RESOLVED fx's own `:rf.fx/handled` correctly honour (proven, e.g. rf2-agb5jk's `request-body-password-redacts-in-fx-handled-trace` test), but which `:rf.event/fx` does not.

Repro: a handler returns `{:fx [[:dispatch [bare-event]] [:rf.http/managed {:request {:body {:password "raw"} ...} :sensitive? true ...}]]}`. The handler's own `:rf.event/fx` aggregate carries the raw password in the `:rf.http/managed` entry's args, even though the RESOLVED `:rf.http/managed` fx's own `:rf.fx/handled` trace redacts it correctly.

Confirmed present in examples/core/login's `login.model/submit-form` (identical fx-list shape: `[[:dispatch [...]] [:rf.http/managed {... :sensitive? true ...}]]`) — that example's OWN regression test (`example_login_form_slice_cljs_test.cljs`) never caught it because it captures fx via function-value `:fx-overrides` (bypassing the trace/classification pipeline entirely for that assertion), not a trace-listener sweep.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Both gaps mean ANY handler combining a `:sensitive?`-flagged managed-HTTP call or a classified nested dispatch with a sibling fx entry leaks at this ONE trace slot (`:rf.event/fx` on `:rf.fx/do-fx`), even when every other classification surface (the dedicated per-fx `:rf.fx/handled`, the target event's own `:rf.event/v`) is correctly closed. This is genuinely surprising given rf2-6h3c02's stated intent ("the central classification projector now walks each `[fx-id args]` entry through that fx's own registration") — gap (a) shows that intent doesn't extend to `:dispatch`'s target, and gap (b) shows it doesn't extend to `:rf.http/managed`'s dynamic flag either.

SUGGESTED FIX SHAPE (not prescriptive — needs framework-owner judgment)
- (a): when walking `:rf.event/fx` (and the `:dispatch`-specific `:rf.fx/handled`), special-case `:dispatch` / `:dispatch-later` fx entries — recurse the classification lookup using the TARGET event id's own registration classification (rooted at the target's arg-map), not `:dispatch`'s own (empty) registration.
- (b): teach the `:rf.event/fx` walker to also consult `re-frame.http.privacy/request-sensitive?` (or equivalent) for `:rf.http/managed` entries, mirroring what the dedicated `:rf.fx/handled` path already does.

SURFACE
implementation/core (classification.cljc — the `:rf.event/fx` aggregate walker) and/or implementation/http (the privacy-flag lookup gap-b needs to reach into). NOT `implementation/machines` — see rf2-<settings-residual> for the sibling machine-specific gap (`:rf.machine/action-ran`'s `:outcome` tag).

VERIFICATION
Add regression coverage mirroring `example_login_success_token_cljs_test.cljs`'s whole-stream sweep style but for a handler shape combining `:dispatch` + `:rf.http/managed :sensitive? true` in one `:fx` vector (gap b), and a handler nesting `[:dispatch [classified-target ...]]` (gap a). Both should assert the sentinel is absent from `:rf.event/fx` specifically, not just the dedicated per-fx slots.

Found by: rf2-agb5jk (PR #5687), examples/real-apps password-egress closure work, 2026-07-12.

Covers :rf.event/fx aggregate + every [:rf.fx/id :rf.fx/args]-shaped slot. Dual-runtime regressions + login submit trace-stream sweep. Gates green (http 488 / core 1820 / machines 954 JVM tests; 8663 CLJS node).

title: [correctness-review][skill-improver] schemaless leaf fix (b) folds an AMBIENT localStorage cofx into a durable app-db write — violates EP-0017 recordable-coeffect world discipline
description:
SURFACE: skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md
HEAD verified: 54c4c2abea3dd47bd0d32c14d8915e09d5b7c917 (origin/main). Filed from read-only audit rf2-jadgj9.

DEFECT
The schemaless leaf's rehydrate worked-fix teaches a canonical rewrite that breaks replay determinism and contradicts its own sibling leaf.

- schemaless-events.md:106-117 (fix (b), labelled "Better") registers `:session/stored` with metadata `{:doc ...}` only — NO `:recordable? true`, so it is an AMBIENT cofx (cofx.md:32, default false). The `:session/rehydrate` handler folds its live-localStorage value into a DURABLE app-db write: `(assoc db :session stored)`.
- schemaless-events.md:96-104 (fix (a)) reads localStorage INLINE in the handler body and folds into `:db` — itself the primary imperative-effects anti-pattern (ambient host read at a durable write site). Presented as "equivalent" to (b).
- schemaless-events.md:122 exempts the case: "A boot/rehydrate value is the legitimate edge (the persisted durable state itself — no prior epoch to diverge from)."

Per the durable-write rule ("durable state folds facts, never reads"), a durable write MUST consume the value from the token's RECORDABLE coeffects (or the event payload), never from an ambient read. An ambient supplier is not recorded; epoch-restore / SSR-hydration / time-travel re-runs it against LIVE localStorage, so replayed `:session/rehydrate` diverges from the value originally folded.

EVIDENCE (quadruple cross-confirmation)
1. EP-0017 §1 (docs/EP/EP-0017-recordable-coeffects.md:358-374): ambient "Permitted only where no durable write depends on the value"; a durable write "MUST consume world facts from the token's recordable coeffects (or the event payload), never from an ambient read."
2. EP-0017 §Implementation errata (:182-200) — decisive: "Boot/rehydrate localStorage reads registered AMBIENT but folded into durable app-db — RULED, now RECORDABLE." Three examples (todomvc/realworld/realworld-resources) did exactly this on `:*/initialise`; the A.4 "acceptable boot edge" defense was OVERRULED by the operator as a replay hole and shipped as `:recordable? true` (`reg-cofx :todo.storage/todos`). The leaf's line-122 "legitimate boot edge / no prior epoch to diverge from" is the VERBATIM overruled A.4 argument.
3. cofx.md:93-119 — canonical `:todo.storage/todos` recordable-generator example is fix (b)'s scenario one keyword away (`{:recordable? true}` + `:rf.cofx/requires` on `:todo/initialise`).
4. The improver skill's OWN sibling leaf imperative-effects.md:54: "A plain ambient cofx here [durable write] replays to a different value — the defect." And design.md:82: "durable writes fold a recorded fact (declared :rf/time-ms / event payload / recordable cofx)." Fix (b) self-contradicts both.

IMPACT
Under the L3 Edit gate, fix (b) is a CANONICAL-IDIOM-SHAPED rewrite the improver MAY apply verbatim without approval — so the skill would land a rewrite that breaks epoch-restore/SSR/time-travel replay, that the codebase's own examples were corrected away from, and that contradicts imperative-effects.md. Highest-risk failure shape for a critique skill.

FIX SKETCH
1. Mark `:session/stored` `{:recordable? true}` (verbatim the cofx.md `:todo.storage/todos` recordable-generator shape).
2. Correct line-122: the rehydrate read must be a recordable coeffect; remove the boot-edge exemption; cross-link EP-0017 §Implementation errata.
3. Drop or demote fix (a) — an inline host read folded into durable `:db` is not durable-safe; if kept as a schema-only illustration, annotate it still owes the recordable-cofx fix.
4. (Secondary, same root cause) evals.json eval 28 (behav-schemaless-body-read-trap): its fix guidance "a validating cofx/interceptor" folds `js/window.location.search` into `[:search :filters]` (a durable write) — nudge to a RECORDABLE cofx, or params ride the event payload.

ACCEPTANCE
- schemaless-events.md fix (b) `:session/stored` carries `:recordable? true`.
- Line-122 no longer claims a boot-edge exemption from the durable-write rule and cross-links EP-0017's ruling.
- No worked "After" in the leaf folds an ambient/inline host read into durable app-db as a "safe" shape.
- eval 28 cofx guidance is recordable (or payload-threaded).

SCOPE NOTE: distinct from rf2-j538f7.37 (HTTP reply-target contract) — this is the EP-0017 recordable-coeffect world discipline. No open bead owns it.
Confidence: High.

title: [correctness-review][machines-viz] back-edge reroute writes parent-relative coords into the ROOT-absolute :edge-points map
description:
post_elk.cljc reroute-back-edges (write at :783-785) puts back-edge-detour's :in-points/:out-points straight into :edge-points, but those points come from node-center (:626-642) whose OWN docstring says it returns coords 'in WHATEVER frame positions records it -- root-relative for a top-level node, PARENT-RELATIVE for a nested one'. elk-result->positions records each node parent-relative (xyflow parentId), while :edge-points is documented ROOT-ABSOLUTE (elk.json.edgeCoords ROOT) and consumed as absolute by chart/projection + chart/edges poly-path. The ns coordinate-frames docstring (:77-81) even CLAIMS 'the back-edge reroute works in the ABSOLUTE frame the edge-points already use' -- but it does not.

The same-parent? guard (:731-746) only makes the back-edge COMPARISON valid (both endpoints share one frame); it does NOT rebase to absolute before writing. So a same-parent back-edge whose endpoints are NESTED (both siblings inside a compound state or a parallel region, or -- post wrap-in-root-container -- under the synthetic root-container) has its detour drawn offset by the container's absolute origin, floating away from its endpoints.

Trigger: :direction :auto (opt-in) + a same-parent back-edge that sinks (back-edge? true) with nested endpoints. Repro: a compound C {:initial :a :states {:a {:on {:go :b}} :b {:on {:back :a}}}} where the :back event-node ranks past both endpoints -- the return detour is drawn ~(C's absolute x,y) away.

Test gap: reroute-back-edges-rewrites-positions-and-routes (post_elk_cljs_test.cljc:683) uses a FLAT machine + single self-consistent col-positions stub and asserts only contains? on __in/__out keys, never absolute-frame correctness. The only nested test (:716) asserts a cross-hierarchy edge is EXCLUDED; there is no same-parent NESTED back-edge test verifying the written detour is absolute.

Confidence: frame mismatch confirmed by tracing + docstrings' own claims. Exact pixel offset for the FLAT-under-root-container case depends on ELK's placement of root-container (needs a DOM run for magnitude); a compound/region-nested back-edge is definitively offset by the container origin.

Fix sketch: rebase the detour point-lists to absolute before writing -- add the running sum of ancestor container origins for the endpoints' shared parent -- or restrict the reroute to root-absolute (no-:parent-id) back-edges (but post wrap-in-root-container there are effectively none at root, so rebase is the real fix).
acceptance_criteria: A reroute test with a nested same-parent back-edge whose shared parent origin is non-(0,0) asserts the written __in/__out points equal the ABSOLUTE-frame detour (endpoint-centre + parent origin), not the parent-relative values. Ideally a :direction :auto DOM/topology-gate case confirms the rerouted arm lands on its endpoints.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5648 (rebase back-edge reroute detour to root-absolute via container-origin; nested-in-compound regression added)

title: [correctness-review][machines-viz] clipboard copy guard throws ReferenceError on browsers without ClipboardItem
description:
export.cljs copy-svg-to-clipboard! (:448) and copy-png-to-clipboard! (:536) guard availability with (and js/navigator (.-clipboard js/navigator) js/ClipboardItem). In CLJS js/ClipboardItem compiles to a BARE 'ClipboardItem' identifier reference. On a browser that has navigator.clipboard but no ClipboardItem global (older Firefox that shipped navigator.clipboard.writeText before ClipboardItem; some non-secure contexts), evaluating a bare undeclared identifier throws ReferenceError -- so the intended js/Promise.reject :no-clipboard else-branch is unreachable in exactly the case it exists for.

- copy-svg-to-clipboard!: the throw is SYNCHRONOUS (guard at top level, not inside the returned Promise), breaking the 'Returns a Promise... rejecting on failure' docstring contract -- a caller .catch never sees it.
- copy-png-to-clipboard!: guard is inside .then, so it becomes a rejection but a raw ReferenceError, never the typed :no-clipboard ex-info.

The artefact's OWN safe-global idiom is (exists? js/...) -- chart/overlays/overlay_scaffold.cljs:52 uses (exists? js/window), which compiles to a typeof !== 'undefined' check. This guard is inconsistent with it.

Repro: in a headless test, delete globalThis.ClipboardItem (make it undeclared) with navigator.clipboard present; call copy-svg-to-clipboard! on a chart element -> ReferenceError thrown synchronously instead of a rejected :no-clipboard Promise.

Fix sketch: replace js/ClipboardItem with (exists? js/ClipboardItem) in both guards (export.cljs:448 and :536).
acceptance_criteria: A headless test stub that removes ClipboardItem from the global scope (undeclared) with navigator.clipboard present drives copy-svg-to-clipboard! and copy-png-to-clipboard! and asserts a REJECTED Promise carrying :rf.machines-viz.export/no-clipboard -- not a ReferenceError, and not a synchronous throw for copy-svg.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5648 (exists?-guard ClipboardItem; adversarial regression stubbing absent ClipboardItem → :no-clipboard)

title: [correctness-review][core] Cold call-serialized-with-drain! breaks single-drainer release: permanent queue strand + same-thread dispatch-sync self-deadlock (JVM)
description:
JVM correctness defect (CLJS-immune). A COLD `frame/call-serialized-with-drain!` critical section takes the SAME frame `:drain-lock` as the event drainer (frame.cljc:1195-1200) but releases it with only `(reset! drain-lock false)` — no queue re-check, no `:scheduled?` reset (frame.cljc:1204-1209). This breaks the single-drainer release protocol two ways. Real cold callers: flows reg-flow/clear-flow (out-of-drain), destroy-frame!'s mark-frame-destroyed!, Tool-Pair state writes.

(a) PERMANENT STRAND. `drain-try!` (router.cljc:3179-3197, fired from interop/next-tick on a SEPARATE single-thread executor, interop.clj:15-22) CAS-loses to the cold holder and returns, relying on the holder being a DRAINER whose release re-checks the queue (`try-release-on-empty!`, 3119-3139). It is not. Interleave: A enters cold section on F; B `dispatch!`es on F -> `ensure-drain-scheduled!` sets `:scheduled? true` + schedules drain-try!; executor fires drain-try!, CAS-loses, returns; A releases, no re-kick. `:scheduled?` stuck true (cleared ONLY on drain-loop paths: router.cljc:2853/2993/3136/3176) + non-empty queue + no drainer => every later dispatch! no-ops in ensure-drain-scheduled! and the queue strands until a dispatch-sync!/destroy.

VERIFIED (deterministic JVM repro):
  WHILE-HELD    queue=1 scheduled?=true
  AFTER-RELEASE queue=1 scheduled?=true :ran=nil   (cold release didn't re-kick)
  AFTER-2nd-DSP queue=2 scheduled?=true :ran=nil   (fresh dispatch cannot recover)
  AFTER-SYNC    :ran=true                            (only dispatch-sync recovers)

(b) SAME-THREAD SELF-DEADLOCK. `dispatch-sync!`'s nested-sync? (router.cljc:3494-3508) consults :in-sync-drain? and :in-drain? (drainer thread) but NOT the frame :serialized-holder. A dispatch-sync! issued from inside a cold serialized thunk on the same thread T falls to :else -> drain-block! -> spin-CAS on :drain-lock which T already holds -> spins forever. frame.cljc added current-thread-owns-drain-serialization? (1128-1151) for exactly this reentrancy class on the call-serialized side, but the router's nested-sync?/drain-block! were never taught the :serialized-holder axis.
VERIFIED: RESULT: HANG (dispatch-sync from inside cold serialized section self-deadlocked on drain-lock).

Existing flows drain-race tests (flows_lifecycle_drain_race_test.clj) race the lock with dispatch-sync (which BLOCKS on the lock), never the async dispatch!->drain-try!-gives-up path, so neither symptom is covered.

FIX DIRECTION: on cold-section release re-check the frame queue and re-kick (clear :scheduled? + reschedule via the existing :router/* late-bind seam), mirroring try-release-on-empty!; and have nested-sync?/drain-block! consult :serialized-holder (run seed-push + drain directly when the current thread already owns the cold serialization), mirroring current-thread-owns-drain-serialization?.

Repro scripts in the audit findings doc: ai/findings/2026-07-11.core-audit.md (strand_repro.clj, nested_sync_repro.clj).
acceptance_criteria: JVM tests: (a) hold a cold call-serialized-with-drain! section while an async dispatch! schedules a drain-try! that CAS-loses; after release the queue drains, the handler ran, and a fresh dispatch recovers. (b) a dispatch-sync! from inside a cold serialized thunk on the same thread returns instead of hanging.

title: [correctness-review][pair-mcp] dispatch-dry-run rollback failure reads as MCP success while app-db stays mutated
description:
Correctness+safety defect found in rf2-svkcld audit (2026-07-11). Read-only finding.

SUMMARY
A failed rollback in dispatch-dry-run returns an isError:false (green) MCP envelope even though the simulated epoch's db IS now the live app-db. The tool is also annotated readOnlyHint/idempotentHint, so hosts auto-approve and read the result as no-modification. Net: silent live-app mutation + green envelope + read-only annotation, with only a human-readable :rollback-hint string as signal.

FILE:LINE
- skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs
  - docstring "Failure paths:" (~2473-2480) documents `:reason :rollback-failed` (an :ok? false shape, listed beside :no-epoch-recorded / :no-new-epoch).
  - :else branch (~2543-2575): `rolled-back? (boolean (rf/restore-epoch! frame-id before-id))`; `base {:ok? true :rolled-back? rolled-back? ...}`; `(if rolled-back? base (assoc base :rollback-hint <str>))`. The not-rolled-back arm returns :ok? true — the documented :rollback-failed / :ok? false shape is NEVER produced.
- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/dispatch_dry_run.cljs:384-386
  - `(if (false? (:ok? result)) (wire/err-text result) (wire/ok-text result))` — since :ok? stays true, routes to ok-text (green).
- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/tool-descriptors.edn — dispatch-dry-run descriptor carries "readOnlyHint" + "idempotentHint".

REPRO / REACHABILITY
restore-epoch! (implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc, find-epoch-in + refusal) returns false when before-id is not an :ok record in the ring. Reaches the :else branch with an unresolvable before-id via:
(a) before-id nil — dry-run lands the FIRST epoch-recording event in a frame (peek of empty ring = nil); restore to nil finds no matching record -> false. Plausible on a fresh frame; exact reachability (does initial app-db install record an epoch?) needs a live nREPL runtime to confirm.
(b) tiny ring — default depth 50 makes this rare, but `(rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:depth 1}})` means the dry-run's tentative epoch evicts before-id -> restore target gone -> false.
Regardless of frequency, the code/docstring divergence is definite and the MCP isError routing is built entirely on :ok?, so IF rollback ever fails it is guaranteed to read green over a mutated db.

TEST GAP
test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/dispatch_dry_run_test.cljs uses :rolled-back? true throughout (140/155/176/206/314/510/545/588…) and covers :no-new-epoch / :unexpected-shape -> isError, but no case drives :ok? true :rolled-back? false. dry_run_sink_pin_test.clj pins the effect sink, not this envelope.

FIX SKETCH
Align runtime with its docstring: in the :else branch, when (not rolled-back?), return {:ok? false :reason :rollback-failed :rolled-back? false :db-state-after-simulation ... :before-epoch-id before-id :hint <re-restore>} instead of :ok? true + :rollback-hint. The MCP tool's existing (false? (:ok? result)) routing then surfaces isError:true with no MCP change. Belt-and-braces: MCP tool MAY also treat (false? (:rolled-back? result)) as an error at the boundary. Extend spec/003-Tool-Catalogue dispatch-dry-run failure list (today only :no-epoch-recorded / :no-new-epoch) with :rollback-failed.

ACCEPTANCE
- Runtime dispatch-dry-run returns :ok? false :reason :rollback-failed (never :ok? true) when restore-epoch! returns false.
- MCP dispatch-dry-run returns isError:true for that path (new unit + conformance fixture).
- spec/003 documents :rollback-failed.

CONFIDENCE: High (code/docstring divergence + false-green routing, source trace). Medium on live frequency of the false branch (edge; needs live runtime).
Found by rf2-svkcld. Surface: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp + skills/re-frame2-pair runtime primitive.

title: [correctness-review][story] :rf.assert/no-cascade-rerender vacuously passes when the named cause never fired ({:min 0 :max 0} vs :caused fail-closed)
description:
SURFACE: tools/story causal/cascade assertion evaluation.
FILES: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/assertions.cljc:1017-1033 (causal-bounds default {:min 0 :max 0} for id-no-cascade-rerender); tools/story/src/re_frame/story/result.cljc:537-542 (causal-in-bounds?) + :564-571 (causal-record status).

DEFECT (vacuous pass): for :rf.assert/no-cascade-rerender the default count bounds are {:min 0 :max 0}. causal-in-bounds? is (and (>= n min) (<= n max)); when the named cause event NEVER fired, causal-count finds 0 rows for it -> n=0 -> in [0,0] -> status :pass. causal-count cannot distinguish 'cause fired and produced 0 re-renders' (a real pass) from 'cause never fired at all' (premise unmet). So an author who renames the cause event silently turns the over-render guard into a no-op that stays green -- classic regression rot.

ASYMMETRY (the signal this is unintended): :rf.assert/caused defaults to {:min 1} and correctly FAILS CLOSED on a never-fired cause (n=0 < 1 -> :fail). Only no-cascade-rerender passes open. The reactive? guard in match-causal-expectations does not help -- the substrate is exercised by OTHER events, so :reactive-counts is present and the causal matcher evaluates rather than refusing.

REPRO: a run that exercises the reactive substrate, with terminal/in-script [:rf.assert/no-cascade-rerender {:event :typo/renamed :view :my-view}] where :typo/renamed is never dispatched -> n=0 -> [0,0] -> :pass, even though the guarded interaction never happened.

INTENT NOTE (mayor to rule): there is a defensible 'vacuously true' reading (no cause fired => trivially no cascade). But the whole point of the guard is 'when :X dispatches it must NOT cascade-rerender :view'; if :X is gone the guard should FAIL (premise unmet) to catch rot -- same fail-closed reasoning that gives :caused {:min 1}. Related closed bead rf2-e0rpy added tests for the bounds ARITHMETIC (:exactly/:min-on-caused/:sub-over-:view) but did NOT consider the never-fired-premise semantics, so this is not previously ruled.

FIX SKETCH: require evidence the cause DID fire before applying the [0,0] no-cascade check -- e.g. gate no-cascade-rerender on the cause appearing in the reactive :by-cause projection (or dispatched-events), recording :cannot-run / :fail 'cause never fired' when absent; keep 0 re-renders of a cause that DID fire as :pass.

ACCEPTANCE: a no-cascade-rerender whose named cause never fired reports :fail (or :cannot-run 'cause never fired'), not :pass; a cause that fired with 0 re-renders still :pass; an explicit {:max N} override unchanged. Verified against HEAD 79fb2f2da.
notes: RULED 2026-07-11 22:17 (operator-delegated Mike->Fable, after independent Codex review): Option A - reject vacuous truth. Unobserved required cause -> :cannot-run (passed? false, cannot-run? true) with reason wording 'not observed in the retained run tape' (NOT 'never fired' - ring depth 50 means eviction is possible; overclaiming is dishonest). Premise evidence source: the run-sliced :epoch-tape already in project-evidence, matched by canonical :event-id keyword equality. Do NOT use :by-cause (reactive rows only - a cause with zero reactive effects legitimately has no entry) and do NOT use assertions/dispatched-events (frame-global window + privacy filtering could satisfy the premise from a prior run). title: [correctness-review][resources] :page-data-schema dead at runtime; Spec 016 R5 contradicts EP-0025 (per-page egress leak risk for R5-following infinite authors)
description:
SPEC-vs-CODE contradiction requiring a Mike ruling (spec is authoritative + internally inconsistent). Re-verified pre-seeded FINDING 1 of rf2-u10eye against HEAD.

STATE
:page-data-schema is accepted at reg-resource (infinite args schema) and stored on the spec, but has ZERO runtime consumers under implementation/resources/src (git grep hits only a comment classification.cljc:224 + one registration test). It drives neither decode/validation nor egress/classification. Verified :data-schema is likewise not consumed for validation anywhere (only :params-schema is, via params.cljc). Per-page redaction IS implemented, but via projection-relative :sensitive declarations + the index-free fork in project-entry-data (classification.cljc:302-305) — NOT via :page-data-schema.

SPEC CONTRADICTION (both in spec/016-Resources.md)
- R5 lines 1348,1791: ':page-data-schema ... is the per-page egress/classification contract. SSR/tool/trace projection apply it per page so sensitive page fields are classified.'
- EP-0025 line 745: a :data-schema/:params-schema 'VALIDATES only — it does not drive durable egress classification'; the single durable classification surface is projection-relative :sensitive/:large declarations.
The code follows EP-0025. Prior fix bead rf2-byl7bk.3.2 (PR #4577, acceptance 'SSR/tool projection applies :page-data-schema to each page') was satisfied by the projection-relative surface, leaving the key dead and R5's letter unmet. No open bead tracks this.

IMPACT
An author who follows R5 and marks sensitive page fields ONLY via :page-data-schema Malli :sensitive? slots (no duplicate projection-relative :sensitive [[:data ...]]) gets NO redaction => raw per-page fields ship on SSR hydration — a principal/egress leak at the page grain. Registration gives no feedback (key silently stored).

RULING NEEDED
(a) EP-0025-consistent: correct R5 to state per-page classification rides projection-relative :sensitive/:large (index-free fork); :page-data-schema is validate-only like :data-schema; OR
(b) make infinite feeds an EP-0025 exception where :page-data-schema marks classify per page.
CAUTION: the pre-seeded 'extract page-data-schema marks and lower them' fix implements (b) and would VIOLATE EP-0025 as written — do not apply without a ruling.

HARM REDUCTION (regardless of ruling)
Emit a loud registration warning when a resource carries schema :sensitive?/:large? marks but no projection-relative :sensitive/:large declaration, so a misled author learns instead of silently leaking.

ACCEPTANCE
Spec 016 R5 and EP-0025/line 745 no longer contradict; an infinite feed's per-page sensitive fields redact via the documented+implemented surface; :page-data-schema is either wired or explicitly documented+registration-warned as validate-only.
Found in audit rf2-u10eye; ai/findings/2026-07-11.resources-audit.md finding B.

title: [correctness-review][resources] Empty infinite feed strands fresh-forever on hydration (hydrated-data-usable? misses infinite empty-page-vector branch)
description:
