title: [correctness-review][http] Reply-tail exceptions leak into the transport classifier: CLJS retry-storm / JVM silent-swallow
description:
Correctness-review finding (rf2-k0pa70, http audit 2026-07-11). VERIFIED by static reasoning + code inspection.

An exception thrown by the response-side reply tail (a `:after` interceptor, or a malformed reply-target throw) is misrouted into the transport-rejection classifier, causing a retry-storm on CLJS and a silent swallow on JVM.

THROW SOURCES
- middleware.cljc `run-chain*` re-throws a `:after` interceptor throw as `:rf.error/http-interceptor-failed` (~381 `(throw data)`), reached from `run-after-then-dispatch!` → `run-after-chain!` (492-493), which runs the `:after` chain BEFORE the app dispatch.
- encoding.cljc `build-reply-event` throws `:rf.error/http-bad-reply-target` (300-304) for a non-vector non-nil reply target (see companion Finding 5 — this is the easy way to hit the throw).

CLJS DEFECT (transport.cljc ~1552/1565)
`.catch` is chained AFTER `(.then handle-response!)`. On a 2xx, `handle-response!` → `finalise-success!` wins the once-only `:finalised?` CAS and clears the registry (697-701), THEN `dispatch-success!` runs the `:after` chain. A throwing `:after` (or malformed target) rejects the promise; `classify-cljs-error` labels the thrown ex-info `:rf.http/transport` (`:else` at transport_cljs.cljc:455-467 — it is neither AbortError nor cross-origin TypeError). With the common `:retry {:on #{:rf.http/transport ...}}`, `maybe-retry!` re-issues. But the request already COMPLETED (2xx). `maybe-retry!` does NOT consult the completed handle's `:finalised?`; `schedule-backoff-handle!` → timer → `run-attempt!` mints a FRESH handle (fresh `:finalised?`), so the once-only guard does not protect. The success is re-sent up to `:max-attempts` times (each re-running the throwing `:after`), then a bogus `:rf.http/transport` failure reply is delivered for a request whose wire outcome was 2xx. Non-idempotent POSTs are re-sent N times. (The `:rf.http/replied` :ok trace fires once per attempt via `emit-reply-trace!` BEFORE the dispatch tail, but no reply is ever delivered to the app.)

JVM DEFECT (transport.cljc ~1613-1618)
`handle-response!` runs inside the whenComplete BiConsumer `accept`. A throw there escapes into the derived (unobserved) CompletableFuture and vanishes silently — no reply delivered (the app dispatch tail never ran), no retry, caller hangs. The outer `(try ... (catch Throwable ...))` in run-attempt! wraps only the sendAsync call + whenComplete REGISTRATION, not the async callback body.

CONTRACT VIOLATED: spec/014 §Failure mode — a response-side `:after` throw propagates and "the request is not dispatched"; never "the request retries" (CLJS) or silently swallows (JVM). No-silent-swallow principle (JVM side).

FIX SKETCH: fence the reply tail (`handle-response!`'s finalise-dispatch, and the JVM `accept` body) in its own try/catch routed to a NON-retrying, once-only error emit — NOT the transport-rejection classifier. Equivalently: attach the CLJS `.catch` BEFORE the `.then`, and wrap `handle-response!` in a try/catch inside the JVM `accept`.

ACCEPTANCE
- CLJS: a request with `:retry {:on #{:rf.http/transport}}` and a throwing response-side `:after` interceptor over a 2xx endpoint hits the server EXACTLY ONCE (no retry-storm) and surfaces the interceptor failure once (not a bogus `:rf.http/transport` reply).
- JVM: the same scenario surfaces the interceptor failure observably (a reply or an error emit) rather than hanging the caller with nothing.

title: [correctness-review][http] JVM abort-vs-retry race: cancelled request double-replies + re-issues a fresh attempt
description:
Correctness-review finding (rf2-k0pa70, http audit 2026-07-11). JVM-only concurrency race. VERIFIED by static reasoning; deterministic repro needs thread-interleaving injection.

WHERE
- transport.cljc `maybe-retry!` (~952-1061) samples the live-fetch handle's `:aborted?` cell ONCE (`aborted? (some? (aborted-snapshot ctx))`, ~985), decides `can-retry?`, then clears the old handle (~1020) and arms a fresh backoff handle via `schedule-backoff-handle!` (~1021).
- `schedule-backoff-handle!` (~807-950) registers a handle carrying a NEW `fired?` cell and its own abort-fn — NO `:aborted?`/`:finalised?` cell, and NO re-check of request-level abort state after `record-in-flight!`.
- The per-phase abort cells (`:aborted?`/`:finalised?`) are created fresh per live-fetch handle in `run-attempt!` (~1337-1475). They are per-phase-handle, not per-request.

REPRO (JVM: whenComplete runs on a ForkJoinPool thread, abort dispatch on the event thread)
1. whenComplete fires with a retry-eligible failure (5xx/transport/timeout matching `:retry :on`); `maybe-retry!` begins on the completion thread and samples `:aborted?` = nil.
2. Concurrently an abort (`:rf.http/managed-abort` / actor-destroy / supersede / epoch-restore / external signal) fires the OLD live-fetch handle's abort-fn BEFORE `clear-in-flight!` (~1020) removes it. The abort resolves the OLD handle (still in the registry), wins its `:finalised?` CAS, and delivers a `:rf.http/aborted` reply — REPLY #1.
3. `maybe-retry!` continues, arms the backoff timer via `schedule-backoff-handle!`. The timer's `fired?` cell is fresh; the OLD abort-fn knows nothing of it. The timer fires after the delay and `run-attempt!` issues a FRESH network attempt under a brand-new handle whose completion delivers REPLY #2.

Result: double terminal reply AND a fresh network attempt for a request the caller cancelled. For a non-idempotent POST, the cancelled request is re-sent.

NARROWER SIBLING: an abort landing between `clear-in-flight!` (~1020) and `schedule-backoff-handle!`'s `record-in-flight!` (~883) resolves NO handle, silent no-ops, and the timer still fires — the request is un-abortable for that instant.

CONTRACT VIOLATED
- spec/014:486-490 (abort always wins) + :490 ("`maybe-retry!` refuses to schedule a retry once the cell is flipped — a request the caller has cancelled MUST NOT issue a fresh attempt under any retry policy").
- spec/014:492 ("An abort ... during the backoff MUST cancel the scheduled retry — no further attempt fires" + "discoverable ... for the entire backoff window").

CLJS immune (single-threaded — `.then`/`.catch` and the abort dispatch cannot interleave mid-`maybe-retry!`).

NOT COVERED by http_backoff_cancellation_test.clj: that test settles 150ms AFTER the timer is armed, so its abort resolves the (correctly-cancellable) steady-state backoff handle, not this transitional window.

FIX SKETCH: carry ONE request-level `:aborted?` (and `:finalised?`) cell on `ctx`, thread it across all phases, stamp it onto the backoff handle, and re-check it after `schedule-backoff-handle!`'s `record-in-flight!` (the same post-registration re-check idiom already used there for `fired?`/`timer-cell` at ~948). Cancel the freshly-armed phase if the cell is flipped. Finding-3's identity-conditional `clear-in-flight!` is half of this fix.

ACCEPTANCE: a JVM stress/interleaving test that injects an abort between `maybe-retry!`'s abort-snapshot and the backoff `record-in-flight!` observes EXACTLY ONE terminal reply (`:rf.http/aborted`) AND ZERO extra server hits after cancellation. The narrower-sibling window (abort between clear and re-register) also yields one aborted reply and no retry.
notes:
AUDIT PR #6631 — the original finding explicitly named BOTH transition gaps, but #5632 fixed only live-fetch→backoff. Timer-fire→attempt N+1 is still non-continuous on current main: callback wins fired?, clears the backoff handle, checks the old aborted? cell, synchronously emits :rf.http/retry-attempt :retried, then calls run-attempt!, which mints fresh cancellation cells and only later registers the new handle. Deterministic probe at the emitted trace: {:retried-events 1, :abort-result false, :next-attempt-started 1}; a listener-issued abort saw no handle and the next attempt still started. JVM concurrent managed-abort/supersede/actor-frame-epoch cancellation has the same gap and can reissue a cancelled POST. Complete the original continuous-handoff acceptance: register/transfer ownership to the successor before clearing the predecessor or publishing :retried, carry/consult the request cancellation state end-to-end, and pin one deterministic abort-at-handoff/reentrant-listener regression asserting one aborted outcome, zero next attempt, clean registry, and no false :retried. No public API, lock, scheduler, or general state machine.
FIX SHIPPED (PR #6645, worker/http-abort-retry-race-6nczv9). Completed the SECOND transition gap (timer-fire->attempt N+1). The timer callback now hands the predecessor backoff handle + the SHARED :finalised?/:aborted? cells to run-attempt! (continuous handoff, mirrors rf2-wj8vv): run-attempt! reuses the shared cells, registers the successor FIRST, drops the predecessor only after (identity-conditional), and a post-registration re-check delivers the single :rf.http/aborted reply + suppresses the fresh attempt when the shared abort cell is flipped. The honest :retried emit moved with it (fires only after the successor re-confirms not-aborted). Deterministic JVM regression at a new :retry/before-attempt interleave seam: RED without the re-check (server hit twice; cancelled request re-issued), GREEN with it (one aborted reply, one hit, clean registry, no phantom :retried). Gates: http clojure -M:test 493/3787 green; npm run test:cljs 10365/51218 green. Spec 014:486-492 unchanged (runtime now compliant at the 2nd transition). Do NOT close until merged.
CHRONOLOGICAL THREE-LENS AUDIT RIDER — PR #6645 (2026-07-21): REOPENED P2 for one material ownership gap in the timer-fire -> retry-successor handoff.

The shared request-level finalised?/aborted? cells, successor-first ordering, abort re-check, and deterministic managed-abort regression are sound and proportionate. The remaining race is with a REAL same-request-id superseder, which the new test does not exercise.

Exact interleaving:
1. Old issuance N's backoff timer wins fired? and pauses at :retry/before-attempt.
2. Fresh issuance N+1 allocates its work id, supersede! clears/aborts the old backoff, then registers live handle H2 under request id R. The old abort flips the shared aborted? cell but loses the timer's already-won fired? CAS.
3. Old run-attempt! resumes and registry/record-in-flight! unconditionally assocs its stale retry handle under R, overwriting H2.
4. The old retry's post-registration abort re-check identity-clears its own stale handle. R is now absent while H2 remains live.

Consequences are material for ordinary SPA request supersession: managed abort and the next same-id supersede cannot reach H2, and H2 can later deliver an obsolete out-of-order reply.

Smallest repair: add one compact atomic conditional handoff used by retries: install the retry successor only if the request-id slot still holds the exact prev-handle supplied in :rf.http/retry-handoff. If that compare-and-replace loses (including the supersede clear-before-new-register interval), do not add the stale successor to either index and do not emit :retried, prepare the body, or issue transport; the newer issuance owns the id and supersede already owns stale telemetry. Anonymous/no-id first attempts keep the simple path. The existing prev-handle is the ownership token; do not add locks, scheduler changes, a public API, or another state machine.

Add one deterministic :retry/before-attempt latch/interleave test that completes a real same-id N+1 registration before releasing old N, then proves N never retries, H2 remains the lookup-visible/cancellable occupant, later supersession still reaches it, both indexes clean up, and only the current issuance delivers. Existing rf2-ous9e5 is precedent for identity-conditional clear but is not reopened; this is the missing conditional INSTALL/transfer in this bead's exact handoff.
close_reason: verified shipped on main (#6645); audit-loop reopen reverted

title: [correctness-review][examples-real-apps] Login/register/settings password egresses unredacted — only the token is classified (both RealWorld apps)
description:
SUMMARY
Both RealWorld reference apps (examples/real-apps/realworld_http + realworld_resources) meticulously classify the durable JWT ([:auth :token] via :auth/classify-token; wire User :token {:sensitive? true}) but NEVER classify the user PASSWORD. The password is a credential and, per the framework's own data-classification model, it egresses RAW through the dispatched-event trace, the managed-HTTP request record, app-db/machine snapshots, and any registered off-box shipper (Datadog/Sentry) + the on-box Xray panel + the epoch ledger. The managed-HTTP app additionally documents a materially INCORRECT rationale for not classifying it. These are the canonical realistic examples whose stated purpose includes modelling data-classification discipline, so the asymmetry (token protected, password raw) + the wrong teaching comment are the defect.

Part of correctness-review EPIC rf2-x76af2; found by audit rf2-6gciee.

WHY IT IS A DEFECT (framework guidance)
- docs/core/how-to/keep-secrets-out-of-traces.md opens with exactly "[:auth/sign-in {:password \"hunter2\"}]" and classifies it with :sensitive [[:password]], stating the dispatched-event trace AND the HTTP record otherwise ship :password raw. Classification is fail-open + strictly opt-in by path ("a path you never classify ships raw").
- The immutable HTTP carrier denylist covers HEADERS + QUERY-PARAMS ONLY (Authorization/Cookie/X-API-Key/…), NOT request-BODY fields — confirmed spec/conformance/fixtures/data-classification-http-carrier-extends-defaults.edn (:carriers {:headers … :query-params …}). There is NO automatic body-field / field-name ("password") redaction; the doc's login example needing an explicit mark proves it.
- Grep of examples/real-apps/: the ONLY classifications are :sensitive [[:auth :token]] (both apps) and wire User :token {:sensitive? true}. Password classified nowhere.

FILE:LINE EVIDENCE
managed-HTTP app (realworld_http/):
- auth.cljs:172-194 — :begin-login/:begin-register put {:user {… :password password}} in the :rf.http/managed request body (HTTP record ships raw). Password arrives via the dispatched machine event [:auth/flow [:auth/login {… :password …}]] (auth.cljs:322-323, 342-348) — event trace ships raw.
- settings.cljs:258-263 — settings PUT body carries :password; draft lives in the :settings/form machine snapshot [:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots :settings/form :data :draft :password] (settings.cljs:44-49, 92-99) — machine transition/snapshot traces ship raw; SettingsFormData schema (schema.cljs:97-109) does not mark :password :sensitive?.
- ssr.cljc:32-39,53-57 — exportable-runtime-db allowlists :rf.runtime/machines WHOLESALE; asymmetric with exportable-app-db:41-51 which carefully redacts [:auth :token]. (No real server leak today — server never has a typed password — but same missing classification.)
- core.cljs:108-114 — INCORRECT comment: "the login / register password drafts … are throwaway form state that never leaves app-db, so there's nothing there to protect." False: the password is copied into the login/register event arg-maps and the outbound HTTP body, both of which the framework records.
resources app (realworld_resources/):
- auth.cljs:271-289 — :begin-login/:begin-register request bodies carry :password; entered via [:auth/flow [:auth/login {… :password …}]] (auth.cljs:420-435).
- App-db drafts [:auth :login-form :draft :password] / [:auth :register-form :draft :password] (auth.cljs:410-435) — durable app-db state, unclassified.
- settings.cljs:80-87 + mutations.cljs:284-300 — :realworld/update-settings threads draft :password through mutation :params + PUT body; :params-schema (mutations.cljs:286-291) unmarked; draft [:settings-form :draft :password] (settings.cljs:44-66) unclassified.

REPRO (static, per the docs' own Xray section)
Dispatch a login ([:auth/flow [:auth/login {:email … :password "hunter2"}]]) and inspect the event row / HTTP record / (resources) App-DB panel: with no :sensitive mark, "hunter2" renders raw where the token renders :rf/redacted. The token's working redaction is the control proving the mechanism is active and the password is simply undeclared.

FIX SKETCH
Easily declarable now:
- Resources: return :sensitive [[:auth :login-form :draft :password]] / [[:auth :register-form :draft :password]] / [[:settings-form :draft :password]] from the respective */initialise (:settings/load) events (classify-before-write, mirroring :auth/classify-token).
- HTTP app settings: add :sensitive [[:data :draft :password]] (and [[:data :submitted :password]]) to reg-machine :settings/form (projection-relative machine-:data classification).
Needs a framework-pattern decision (login/register HTTP body + machine sub-event trace): creds enter via a machine dispatch [:auth/flow [:auth/login {…}]] whose arg is a POSITIONAL sub-event vector (the doc's "positional secret ships raw" gotcha). Weigh: (a) carry creds in the outer :auth/flow event as a named arg-map slot so :sensitive can reach it; (b) confirm whether :rf.http/managed supports a request-body :sensitive mark (only :carriers headers/query documented today — if unsupported, that is itself a framework gap worth a separate note); (c) classify the request-body :password at the fx-emitting site.
Docs: correct the false core.cljs:108-114 comment (drafts DO reach the event trace + HTTP record) and mirror the corrected reasoning in the resources app.

ACCEPTANCE
- Every surface a password crosses is classified so it renders :rf/redacted, at parity with the token: login, register, settings, in BOTH apps — app-db drafts (resources), settings machine :data (http), and the outbound event/HTTP-body path.
- HTTP app core.cljs classification comment states the TRUE reason (drafts reach the event trace + HTTP record) rather than "nothing to protect."
- No behavioural change to the running app (handlers still read the raw value).

SEVERITY NOTE: P2 chosen (defensible P3). It is fail-open observability hygiene, not an auth bypass, and the demo wires no shipper — but these are the flagship realistic examples that explicitly teach classification, so the token/password asymmetry + the wrong teaching comment justify P2. Downgrade to P3 acceptable if preferred.
notes:
DECLARABLE HALF LANDED in PR #5636 (login/register/settings password now redacts in request-body, app-db drafts, settings-machine :data across BOTH RealWorld apps + false-rationale comment fixed). RESIDUAL (kept open, NEEDS RULING): the RealWorld apps route the credential THROUGH the machine as a POSITIONAL sub-event [:auth/flow [:auth/login {:password}]] (and resources settings via [:rf.mutation/execute {:params {:password}}]) — payloads NO app-level path-:sensitive can address ('positional secret ships raw' in the dispatched-event + :rf.machine/* trace slots). Closing needs EITHER (a) a FRAMEWORK change to classify positional/framework-event payloads, OR (b) an auth-flow REDESIGN keeping the machine credential-free (as examples/core/login does), OR (c) accept the demo-app residual. Changes the apps' deliberate 'auth = one machine' pedagogy → Mike's call. Runtime-measured: declarable slots redact; residual is exactly the positional path. Worker left bead open (correct — P2 security, don't bury). Surfaced in ai/decisions.md.
RULED 2026-07-11 22:17 (operator-delegated Mike->Fable, after independent Codex review): EXPANDED Option B plus two narrow framework projector completions. - Actual: `mount.cljs:786-790` `(toggle!)` calls `(open!)` when hidden; `keybinding.cljs:332-333` does the same before `:rf.xray/palette-toggle`.
- When retained mount is `:overlay`, hidden reopen enters `switch-surface! :inline` (`mount.cljs:689-708`). With no `[data-rf-xray-host]`, inline switch returns `:missing-layout-host` and leaves the overlay hidden (`:visible? false`). With a host, reopen silently re-parents to inline instead of showing the overlay the operator chose.

Impact: The documented no-layout-host workflow (`open-overlay!` fallback) cannot recover via the advertised toggle or palette shortcut after hide; operators must re-invoke `open-overlay!`. Host-present overlay users get an unintended inline surface switch and state churn vs the advertised CSS-only reopen.

→ DO NOT RE-FILE. Tracked as rf2-j538f7.41 (open, P2, wave-2 correctness-review child under rf2-j538f7).

## Finding 1 (P1): acceptance gate 1 underspecifies the three v1-required conformance families

**Problem.** Multiple user-facing implementor surfaces describe **acceptance gate 1** as running only `:core/*` fixtures, while the same skill's D7 / `conformance.md` contract requires **three** always-claimed v1 families: `:core/*`, `:identity/*` (EP-0012 path algebra + CEDN-1), and `:data-classification/*` (Spec 015 egress boundary).

**Evidence (stale `:core/*`-only gate wording):**

- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/cardinal-rules.md:19` — "Acceptance gate 1 — running the `:core/*` conformance fixtures"

- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/output-format.md:96-98` — v1 completion example lists only `:core/*` in the claimed-tag block (omits the two other v1-required families even as examples)

**Evidence (authoritative three-family contract elsewhere in the same slice):**
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md:76-79,114` — `:identity/*` and `:data-classification/*` are v1-required like `:core/*`; fixtures for EP-0012 Mode-B ops and EP-015 projector ops carry those families, not `:core/*`
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-1-decisions.md:395` — D7 always claims `:core/*` + `:identity/*` + `:data-classification/*`
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/decision-record.md:199-202` — same three-family default in the template
- `spec/conformance/fixtures/cedn1-path-algebra-golden.edn` — capability `#{:identity/cedn1}` only (skipped entirely if gate 1 runs `:core/*` filter)
- `spec/conformance/fixtures/sub-cache-dedupes-equal-query-v.edn` — `#{:identity/cedn1}` (identity law via consumer)
- Multiple `data-classification-*.edn` fixtures — require `:data-classification/*` tags (often alongside `:core/*`); e.g. `data-classification-project-egress-fails-closed-no-frame.edn` is `#{:data-classification/classification-effects}` only

**Impact.** An implementor (or agent) following gate 1 literally can green-light "foundation complete" after `:core/*` while never running — or even claiming — the two other v1-required families. That produces ports that miss EP-0012 path-law / CEDN-1 conformance and/or ship EP 015 code without exercising the `:data-classification/*` corpus (privacy/classification regressions survive until gate 2, if ever caught). This contradicts the skill's own done checklist (Spec 015 + shared path foundation) and D7's always-claimed set.

**Suggested fix / acceptance:**
- Rename gate 1 across the slice to the **foundation conformance gate** and state explicitly that it runs the **union of the three v1-required families** claimed in D7: `:core/*` + `:identity/*` + `:data-classification/*` (derive exact sub-tags from fixtures at the pinned commit per `conformance.md` §Capability tagging).
- Update kickoff-prompt "minimum viable port" variation, README, `spec/design.md`, cardinal-rules §3, `output-format.md` v1 example, and per-EP slice-gate examples to reference the same three-family filter (or "D7 foundation claim"), not `:core/*` alone.
- Acceptance: a port author following gate 1 after the fix runs identity + data-classification fixtures before optional EPs; gate 1 prose no longer contradicts `conformance.md` / D7.

**Confidence:** high.

## Finding 2 (P3): SKILL.md contradicts itself on Phase 1 block count

**Problem.** `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md:59` says "Eight decision blocks (D1–D7 plus D5b)" but `SKILL.md:104` describes `phase-1-decisions.md` as "seven decision blocks."

**Impact.** Low — cosmetic routing inconsistency only; `phase-1-decisions.md` itself lists D1–D7 + D5b correctly.

**Suggested fix:** Change line 104 to "eight decision blocks (D1–D7 plus D5b)" or "D1–D7 and D5b."

**Confidence:** high.

Searched open/closed beads and PRs for gate-1 / `:identity/*` / `:data-classification/*` implementor-skill drift. No open bead covers this gate-1 three-family underspecification. `rf2-sp8gg` and `rf2-anj7xc` addressed different implementor drift (already remediated above). title: Make shared redaction scoring preserve repeated-value bindings
description:
## Complete slice inventory

Wave-2 correctness review of the complete 12-file `skills/shared` package at current `origin/main` `c13bd6d65`: the three canonical leaves (`issue-filing.md`, `retro-protocol.md`, `tool-pair-surfaces.md`); structural assurance (`tests/retro_protocol_test.clj`, `tests/tool_pair_surfaces_test.clj`, `tests/README.md`); behavioral fixtures (`tests/fixtures/README.md` and fixtures 01 injection, 02 redaction, 03 Edit-gate); and executable behavioral assurance (`tests/evals/behavioral-evals.json`, `score-behavioral-eval.clj`).

Every direct consumer was reconciled. The retro protocol is loaded by `re-frame2-improver` and `re-frame2-pair-retro`, including their SKILL/README/spec/eval surfaces. The issue-filing recipe is consumed by pair-retro, `re-frame-migration`, and the deliberately local-but-guarded `re-frame2-implementor` recipe; the repo allowed-tools baseline, title-safety drift guard, package-ref guard, approval gate, redaction boundary, and published-skill never-`bd` boundary were checked. The Tool-Pair routing index was reconciled with `spec/Tool-Pair.md`, the pair-MCP catalogue, Pair, pair-retro, improver, and Xray. Pair-retro's Story recorder-session disqualifier correctly routes Story play-sequence refinement to Pair; Story has no direct shared-leaf consumer. No source edits were made.

## Prior-wave remediation verified

Closed `rf2-3fc89f.42`, merged by PR #5526 / commit `fb64ee36c`, repaired several real false-greens and introduced schema-version-2 `redaction_bindings[]` specifically to make Fixture 02's stable-placeholder identity invariant executable. The current structural suites and scorer self-test pass; the other prior repairs remain present. This issue does not re-file those actioned findings.

The residual defect is in the new identity implementation itself. Adjacent open `rf2-j538f7.38` concerns the separate pair-retro session-evidence scorer and does not own this file.

## Defect

Fixture 02 and `retro-protocol.md` require the same sensitive value to receive the same numbered placeholder on repeat mentions across all emitted channels. The manifest says this is scored from harness-captured `redaction_bindings[]`.

But `score-behavioral-eval.clj:124-128` reduces that array to `original -> placeholder` with `assoc`; its comment says “later entries win on duplicate originals.” When the harness captures two occurrences of one raw value with different placeholders, the first is erased. `check-placeholder-identity` sees only the last placeholder and reports no instability. If “per-target” instead means only one row for a repeated raw value, the schema cannot represent a repeat mismatch at all. Either interpretation leaves the stated invariant unproved.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start from the scorer's committed `good-eval2-bindings`.
2. Add another JWT-header binding so the array contains the same `original` twice: first `<REDACTED-TOKEN-9>`, later `<REDACTED-TOKEN-1>`.
3. Keep all other distinct-secret bindings and the two phone renderings compliant.
4. Use safe output containing `<REDACTED-TOKEN-1>` and `<REDACTED-PHONE-1>`, with no raw fixture substring.
5. Run `bb skills/shared/tests/evals/score-behavioral-eval.clj <transcript.json>`.

Observed on current main:

```json
{"eval_id":2,"name":"redaction-universal-no-raw-secrets","pass":true,"failures":[]}
```

Exit status is 0 even though two occurrences of the same JWT value use different numbers.

## Expected versus actual

Expected: exit 1 with an occurrence-stability failure naming the repeated original and both conflicting placeholders.

Actual: later-wins projection destroys the contradictory evidence before any predicate reads it, so the release/checklist artifact certifies PASS.

## Impact

This is a false-green on the shared redaction security gate and a residual hole in the exact prior-wave remediation that claimed same-value stability is machine-checkable. A model can use different masks for one secret between inline findings, a draft issue, and a recap; readers can no longer correlate the masks, yet the artifact says universal redaction passed. Execution remains manual/opt-in, so this is P2 rather than a continuously exposed runtime failure.

## Dedupe and provenance evidence

All-status bead/history searches covered `redaction_bindings`, placeholder identity/stability, duplicate bindings, same-value placeholders, shared behavioral scorer, and false-green scorer. The only matching owner is closed `rf2-3fc89f.42` / merged PR #5526, whose remediation introduced the defective later-wins map; closed owners receive a new follow-up. Current-wave `rf2-j538f7.38` is a different scorer and fixture. Git blame attributes lines 122-176 to `fb64ee36c`. GitHub all-state issue/PR searches found no open issue or PR and only merged PR #5526. The parent had no shared-scorer owner before this filing.
design:
Keep schema version 2 and the manual/opt-in replay posture. Repair only identity evidence preservation; do not build a Claude-in-the-loop harness or semantic grader.

- Treat `redaction_bindings[]` as occurrence evidence. Build `original -> ordered placeholders` (or sets plus occurrence detail), never a lossy last-write-wins map.
- Fail when one exact original has more than one distinct placeholder. Keep normalized same-value groups (the two phone spellings) as a separate comparison.
- Continue checking distinct sensitive originals for collisions and every captured placeholder for shape.
- Clarify the capture rule: repeated emissions across channels must yield enough evidence to prove stability. If capture can only emit one row per target, minimally extend that row with all emitted placeholders/occurrences.
- Add an isolated self-test where one exact original occurs twice with different placeholders and assert the specific predicate fires.
- Preserve injection, redaction-target, transcript-reproduction, Edit-gate, filing, Pair/Story routing, and tracker-boundary behavior unchanged.

This is a small data-shape correction, not a new evaluation framework.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The exact adversarial reproduction—one raw original captured twice with `<REDACTED-TOKEN-9>` then `<REDACTED-TOKEN-1>`, all other Eval 2 inputs compliant—exits non-zero and reports repeated-original instability.
2. Reversing duplicate order also fails; stability is not last-occurrence-dependent.
3. Repeating one original any number of times with the same placeholder passes.
4. Existing normalized same-value behavior remains: the two phone spellings share one placeholder; distinct secrets do not.
5. Manifest and fixtures README define occurrence capture accurately, and scoring fails closed when the supplied shape cannot prove a declared identity invariant.
6. `--self-test` contains isolated good/bad duplicate-occurrence cases and proves the intended check fired by name/detail.
7. Prior Eval 1/Eval 3 behavior and all security, approval, filing, Pair/Story, and never-`bd` boundaries remain unchanged.
8. Scorer self-test, both shared structural suites, skill MCP/eval/package drift gates, README link/inventory gates, and package-reference checks pass.
notes: Audit-only baseline: adversarial transcript exits 0/PASS; scorer self-test PASS; shared retro suite 60 tests / 124 assertions / 0 failures; Tool-Pair suite 6 tests / 9 assertions / 0 failures; skill MCP drift exits 0. Temporary diagnostic transcript was removed and worktree returned clean. No source edit, implementation, PR, closure, or beads JSON commit/push.

description:

Reviewed against Spec 016, 014 managed-HTTP integration, 015 classification (EP-0025 no-propagation), Tool-Pair resource/epoch surfaces. Lenses: lifecycle/teardown, optimistic rollback, cache/principal boundaries, infinite feeds, SSR/hydration/restore, frame isolation, managed-HTTP abort+stale suppression, timer side-tables, false-green tests.

FINDING 1 (P2 — principal/egress boundary): `:page-data-schema` is not a runtime classification or decode contract.
- Spec 016 §Registration :infinite R5 / EP-0021 R5: `:page-data-schema` validates ONE page AND is the per-page SSR/tool/trace egress/classification contract; `:data-schema` must not classify the accumulated page vector.
- Actual: key is accepted at `reg-resource` and stored on the spec (`registry.cljc` assoc path) but has ZERO runtime consumers under `implementation/resources/src` (only a comment at `classification.cljc:224`). Per-page SSR redaction is implemented ONLY via projection-relative `:sensitive`/`:large` declarations lowered into the elision registry; the index-free fork in `project-entry-data` matches `[… :data :field]` across page indices (`classification.cljc:302-305`, `ssr.cljc:367-377`).
- Evidence: `rg page-data-schema` under src hits only `classification.cljc` comment + registration test storage (`resources_infinite_registration_cljs_test.cljc:61`). The closed rf2-byl7bk.3.2 regression (`resources_classification_cljs_test.cljc:387-417`) uses `:sensitive [[:data :author-email]]`, NOT `:page-data-schema` Malli marks.
- Impact: an author who follows spec/docs and declares ONLY `:page-data-schema` with `:sensitive?` / `:large?` Malli slots (no duplicate `:sensitive [[:data …]]`) will ship raw per-page fields on SSR hydration, trace egress, and tool projection for infinite feeds — a principal/egress leak at the page grain.
- Fix: at registration (or first infinite settle), extract `:page-data-schema` schema-prop marks and lower them as `:data`-rooted projection declarations (same path as explicit `:sensitive`), and reject/ignore `:data-schema` on `:infinite true` resources; add regression that `:page-data-schema`-only sensitive page fields redact per page without duplicating `:sensitive`.

FINDING 2 (P3 — Managed-Effects metadata): `:rf.resource/clear-scope` terminal work rows omit causal `:completed-at`.
- `events.cljc:1901-1904` marks in-flight rows `:cancelled {:reason :clear-scope}` without `:completed-at`, while reply-driven cancellations carry the reply token time (`failed-handler` / `aborted-handler`, rf2-rl27r2 tests in `resources_time_ms_cofx_cljs_test.cljc:210-245`).
- Handler does not destructure `:rf/time-ms` (`clear-scope-handler` cofx at `:1955`).
- Impact: epoch/tooling correlation gap for logout/tenant-switch clears; not a stale-suppression or cache-principal bug.
- Fix: thread declared `:rf/time-ms` into clear-scope `:cancelled` outcomes (and trace), symmetric with rf2-rl27r2.

FINDING 3 (P3 — doc drift): `ssr.cljc:128-139` still claims per-slot `:data-schema` `:sensitive?` marks drive SSR `project-egress`, contradicting `classification.cljc:221-236` (EP-0025: schemas validate; durable egress is projection-relative `:sensitive`/`:large` only). Misleading for infinite authors choosing between `:page-data-schema` and `:sensitive` paths.
