title: Make pair-retro session scoring require causal fact bindings
description:
## Complete slice inventory

Wave-2 correctness review of all 19 tracked files in `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro` at current `origin/main` `0ec8580ac`: `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `package.json`, `LICENSE`, `.gitignore`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `agents/openai.yaml`; all four shipped references (`working-style.md`, `known-frictions.md`, `analysis-lenses.md`, `issue-template.md`); all three authoring specs (`inputs.md`, `design.md`, `authoring-prompt.md`); and the complete eval surface (`evals.json`, `session-evidence-evals.json`, `score-session-evidence-eval.clj`, eval README, and `fixtures/session-evidence-scoping.md`).

Direct owners were reconciled where the skill delegates facts: `skills/shared/retro-protocol.md`, `issue-filing.md`, `tool-pair-surfaces.md`, and `tests/retro_protocol_test.clj`; Pair's `SKILL.md`, restore/error/Story guidance, live `discover-app` descriptor and freshness/runtime-instance contract; Story's public `:script` recorder guidance and Story-MCP `record-as-variant` registry contract; and the repo skill-routing / published-skill tracker boundary. Audited activation and post-error consent, one-session evidence selection, causal attribution/supersession, recap provenance, privacy/injection/redaction, GitHub approval and `bd` separation, improvement/issue actionability and dedupe, tool vocabulary, package/install posture, and eval false-red/false-green behavior.

## Prior-wave remediation verified

Closed `rf2-3fc89f.37`, merged by PR #5570 / commit `a5c236a0e`, added the correct runtime contract: one evidence envelope, initiating-call attribution, build/frame/runtime provenance, unrelated-activity exclusion, supersession, unknown-over-inferred, and recap attribution. The contract is present in `SKILL.md`; its structural pins and scorer self-test pass. Current Pair freshness, attach diagnostic ladder, production-elision split, and shared filing/redaction boundaries also match their owners. This issue does not re-file those actioned prose defects.

The residual defect is in the new deterministic scorer introduced by that remediation. Adjacent closed `rf2-3fc89f.42` / PR #5526 repaired the same false-green class in the separate `skills/shared` security scorer, but it does not touch or own `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/evals/score-session-evidence-eval.clj`.

## Defect: the behavioral scorer accepts causal keyword soup with no session facts

Eval 1's four `required_output_patterns` accept the bare tokens `causal ledger`, `supersed*`, `unknown`, and `exclud*`. None requires those claims to bind to the fixture facts: the delayed `cart-dev-a` result and its initiating call; `cart-dev-b` as the successful superseding attach; the never-returned `tools/list` probe as unknown/incomplete; or invoice-export CI, the code-review comment, and the README edit as excluded. The three forbidden regexes catch only narrow wrong phrasings. `score-eval` reports `:pass true` whenever those lexical checks produce no failures.

## Steps to Reproduce

Evaluate the committed Eval 1 regexes against this output:

```text
Causal ledger. This item superseded the prior state. Another fact is unknown. Excluded unrelated noise.
```

The exact predicate result is:

```json
{
  "required_matches": [true, true, true, true],
  "forbidden_matches": [false, false, false],
  "scorer_pass": true
}
```

The output does not identify either build, bind any result to a call, classify the `tools/list` probe, exclude any named out-of-scope activity, or even establish that it reviewed the fixture. It therefore violates every substantive Scenario A expectation while producing the documented machine-readable PASS artifact. The existing self-test stays green because its negative cases delete one keyword at a time; it has no compliant-looking wrong-binding or content-free case.

Eval 2 has the same root shape: `Which session should I review?` satisfies its required pattern and avoids the merge regex without establishing that the two candidates are the cart-coupon and auth-login sessions. The manifest labels naming both candidates human-review-only, but the workflow stores only the scorer's pass/fail artifact and has no separate recorded human verdict. A machine PASS therefore overstates what was verified.

## Expected versus actual

Expected: the automated artifact proves the deterministic fixture facts it claims to score, and explicitly leaves only genuinely non-deterministic semantic nuance to human review. A transcript that merely repeats contract vocabulary, binds the right rule to the wrong entity, or asks a context-free question fails with an on-target reason.

Actual: presence of generic framing words is enough for PASS. The scorer verifies vocabulary, not the session-evidence behavior named by the manifest, eval README, fixture, and prior remediation acceptance criteria.

## Impact

This is a false-green on the skill's central attribution boundary. A model can merge or ignore evidence, emit a content-free retro, and still leave a green artifact that maintainers treat as proof the remediation works. The downstream output can become a confidently wrong root cause, priority, or public GitHub issue. Execution remains manual/opt-in, so this is P2 rather than a universal runtime failure.

## Dedupe and ownership evidence

All-status bead searches covered pair-retro, session evidence, causal ledger, behavioral scorer, lexical false-green, and generic-keyword scoring. The only owners found were closed `rf2-3fc89f.37` (introduced this scorer) and closed `rf2-3fc89f.42` (the separate shared scorer). The full prior-wave child inventory and current wave children contain no owner for this residual. Git history shows the pair-retro scorer arrived only in `a5c236a0e`. GitHub PR/issue searches for `session evidence`, `causal ledger`, `score-session-evidence-eval`, `pair-retro false green`, and `session-evidence-scoping` found PR #5570 plus adjacent PR #5526, and no open issue or PR. Current open wave work does not overlap this eval surface.
design:
Keep the manual/opt-in agent-execution posture and the existing transcript schema. Repair only deterministic scorer fidelity; do not build an NLP grader or add session-capture machinery.

For fixed fixtures, require fixture-bound facts rather than free-floating vocabulary. Prefer small explicit predicate checks (or entity-anchored regexes) that can report which binding is absent:

- Eval 1: require `cart-dev-a` to be associated with the delayed/earlier initiating call; require `cart-dev-b` success to supersede A rather than merely using the word superseded; require `tools/list` to be the item classified unknown/incomplete; and require the named unrelated activity to be excluded rather than accepting generic exclusion prose.
- Eval 2: require the clarification to identify both candidate goals/sessions before asking which one, while continuing to forbid merge/combined handling.
- Keep genuinely semantic judgments in `scored_vs_manual`, but make the scorer report that manual review remains pending instead of representing a lexical-only result as an unconditional full PASS. If a two-state report is retained, narrow the documented claim to exactly what it proves.
- Add isolated adversarial self-tests that retain every generic contract word while omitting or swapping one fixture binding. Assert the intended predicate fails by name so another failure cannot mask it.

This is deliberately a small manifest/scorer correction modeled on PR #5526's explicit-predicate discipline, not a new evaluation framework.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Eval 1 exits non-zero for the exact content-free reproduction `Causal ledger. This item superseded the prior state. Another fact is unknown. Excluded unrelated noise.` and reports missing fixture bindings, not merely a generic regex miss.
2. Eval 1 cannot pass unless output binds the delayed `cart-dev-a` result to its initiating call, describes the healthy `cart-dev-b` attach as superseding that earlier state, marks the never-returned `tools/list` probe unknown/incomplete, and excludes the invoice-export CI, code-review comment, and unrelated README edit from pair-session friction.
3. Add isolated wrong-binding negatives: each keeps all four contract keywords but attaches one rule to the wrong entity (for example, unknown to a different call or supersession in the wrong direction); each must fail through its specific predicate.
4. Eval 2 fails a context-free `Which session should I review?`; passing output identifies both fixture candidates (cart-coupon and auth-login) and asks which to retro without combining them.
5. `--self-test` includes the content-free and wrong-binding cases, proves each intended check fired by name, and retains detailed known-good cases for both evals.
6. `session-evidence-evals.json` and `evals/README.md` accurately separate automatically proven facts from human-review-only judgments. A machine-readable artifact must not present unresolved manual clauses as an unconditional full-contract PASS.
7. Preserve the one-session prose contract, trigger fixtures, opt-in/manual replay decision, no-source-edit retro posture, redaction/injection boundaries, and package exclusions.
8. `bb skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/evals/score-session-evidence-eval.clj --self-test`, `bb skills/shared/tests/retro_protocol_test.clj`, skill MCP/eval/package drift gates, README link/inventory gates, and `npm pack --dry-run --json` pass.
notes: Audit only: no source edits, implementation, PR, or issue closure. Baseline gates are green despite the reproduction: pair-retro scorer self-test PASS; shared retro protocol 60 tests / 124 assertions / 0 failures; skill MCP drift, eval-doc, eval-packaging, package-ref, README-link, and README-inventory gates all exit 0; npm dry-run contains the documented 10 shipped files. Worktree remained clean. Priority P2 follows the central-output/public-filing impact and matches the adjacent scorer-fidelity precedent, tempered by manual/opt-in execution.

title: Make improver HTTP rewrites use explicit reply targets and appended envelopes
description:
## Complete reviewed inventory

Fresh post-remediation audit of all 17 files in `skills/re-frame2-improver`: `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `package.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`; all seven `references/` files (catalogue index plus six leaves); `evals/README.md` and `evals/evals.json` (31 fixtures: 16 trigger, 15 behavioural); and the three `spec/` meta-docs. I checked trigger/routing/progressive disclosure, the shared untrusted-evidence/Edit/redaction protocol, every detection/edge rule and rewrite, package/install behavior, and eval false-positive/false-green risks.

Direct contract owners were traced rather than trusted by cross-link: Spec 014 + Managed-Effects, `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc` and its reply/managed tests, the repaired `examples/core/managed_http_counter` and `examples/real-apps/realworld_http`; Spec 005 + machines implementation/tags/Nine States; Spec 010 + schemas implementation; core fx/cofx and Spec 001/002/011; and Spec 004/view owners. The strongest residual defect is the copied Managed HTTP contract below. The separate canonical `skills/re-frame2` package is owned by `rf2-j538f7.35`; this issue owns only improver files/evals and depends on that upstream correction.

## Post-remediation verification

Prior-wave child `rf2-3fc89f.38` landed in PR #5533 / commit `5ad04a3f9`: `SKILL.md:92` now preserves both Edit-gate polarities, behavioural eval 31 covers the canonical-may-apply branch, and the stale fixture count is gone. `bb skills/shared/tests/retro_protocol_test.clj` passes 60 tests / 124 assertions. Package-reference, eval-doc, and eval-packaging gates are green. No bead IDs leak into the skill prose. That remediation is real and is not duplicated here.

## Defect

`references/manual-retry-loops.md:51-62` presents its canonical “After” handler as a targetless `:rf.http/managed` request and waits for a reply merged under `(:rf/reply msg)`. `references/schemaless-events.md:41-46,61-71` repeats the same retired dialect in both its “Before” and “After” examples. `references/README.md:25` still routes HTTP boundary detection by `:rf/reply`.

Current behavior is deliberately different:

- `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:85-132` requires an explicit app-facing `:reply-to`, `:on-success`, or `:on-failure`; the canonical envelope is appended as the target event's final argument. The implicit reply-to-origin / `:rf/reply` merge was retired pre-alpha.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:124-143` enforces that contract before I/O. With none of the three address keys, `validate-reply-target!` throws `:rf.error/http-no-reply-target`.
- `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_test.clj:94-135` pins both halves: explicit `:reply-to` receives the appended envelope, and a targetless request fails loud.
- Current runnable owners (`examples/core/managed_http_counter/core.cljs:87-180` and `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs:83-128`) use explicit `:reply-to` and consume the appended reply.

Expected: a critique skill's canonical rewrite is copyable current re-frame2 code: the request explicitly addresses its reply, the target consumes the appended envelope, and any unified handler handles the delivered closed statuses `:ok`, `:error`, and `:cancelled` (`:stale` is suppressed). Actual: the suggested rewrite throws before a transport attempt. A partial “fix” that merely adds `:reply-to` is worse: the reply arrives as a third event arg, the two-arg handler ignores it, `(:rf/reply msg)` remains nil, and the reply path re-issues the request.

The schemaless leaf needs an atomic semantic rewrite too. If its unified handler keeps `:rf.schema/at-boundary`, the event schema must describe both initial and appended-reply arities; otherwise the production boundary interceptor rejects the reply event. A small split request/reply pair is the clearer correction: explicit reply target, schema matching the actual target event, and `:decode Article` (or an always-on boundary schema over the reply value).

## Eval false greens / false negatives

The current green gates do not inspect this semantic:

- Eval 17 only requires `:rf.http/managed` plus a declarative `:retry`; an answer can paste the leaf's targetless request and pass every expectation.
- Eval 20 (`evals/evals.json:79-92`) itself pastes the retired `:rf/reply`/targetless form and grades the boundary-validation diagnosis without requiring current reply addressing. It rewards preserving a second, unrelated runtime failure.
- Eval 26 (`evals/evals.json:177-183`) contains another targetless `:rf.http/managed` request while telling the grader not to treat Managed HTTP as an issue. A correct current-contract review can therefore be penalised for identifying `:rf.error/http-no-reply-target`. Use an explicit intentional silence such as `:reply-to nil`, or a real target, so the fixture isolates the diagnostic-time-read polarity.

Thus `python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --verbose --ci`, `check_skill_eval_docs.py`, `check_skill_eval_packaging.py`, and the shared protocol suite all pass while the runtime rejects the taught fix. This is a focused content/eval gap, not a reason for a general documentation framework.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Copy the “After” handler from `manual-retry-loops.md` or `schemaless-events.md` into an app with the HTTP artefact loaded.
2. Dispatch its initial event.
3. The handler returns `[:rf.http/managed {:request ...}]` without any reply-address key.
4. `validate-reply-target!` throws `:rf.error/http-no-reply-target`; no request starts and the advertised reply branch is unreachable.

This violates the skill's locked “implementation is ground truth” pillar at exactly its highest-risk boundary: it can correctly diagnose a manual retry or missing production validator, then apply a canonical-shaped Edit that breaks the feature immediately. The misleading evals can certify that answer.

## Dedupe and history

- `rf2-et4c1s` / merged PR #5449 owns the July 10 runtime/spec decision and repaired implementation, specs, tools, and runnable examples, but did not touch this skill.
- Current-wave `rf2-j538f7.35` owns the separately stale source-of-truth `skills/re-frame2` package; this child is deliberately improver-only and depends on it.
- `rf2-qnwy3q` / PR #5481 and `rf2-f3lg06` / PR #5554 repaired the same retirement in `tools/template` only.
- `rf2-x94pom` / PR #4740 fixed the older schemaless example's app-schema path and interceptor spelling; it predates explicit reply addressing and does not cover this failure.
- `rf2-3fc89f.38` / PR #5533 is the verified Edit-gate remediation described above, not HTTP work.
- Exact `bd search` / JSONL searches for improver + Managed HTTP/reply-to/targetless/co-located terms found no existing improver owner; open-PR searches for `improver reply`, `manual-retry-loops`, `schemaless-events`, and `co-located reply skill` returned none. PR #5449's file list confirms no improver file was swept.
design:
## Restrained design

Repair the reply contract atomically inside this package; do not add compatibility language or change runtime behavior.

1. In `manual-retry-loops.md`, replace the implicit reply recipe with one explicit current form. A unified handler must carry `:reply-to` and destructure the appended reply; a split success/failure pair is also valid. Preserve the leaf's point (transport retry belongs in `:retry`) and handle `:ok`, `:error`, and `:cancelled` wherever one target receives all outcomes.
2. In `schemaless-events.md`, update detection prose, before/after code, and routing signals to the appended-envelope contract. Prefer a small split request/reply example so each event schema matches exactly one event shape and the always-on validation is visibly over the untrusted value. Keep lifecycle status off the `Article` payload path (the prior remediation).
3. Update `evals.json` in place: make eval 17 reject targetless/`:rf/reply` rewrites; make eval 20 exercise a valid current reply-address shape while retaining the missing-production-validation defect; make eval 26 explicitly silence or address its HTTP reply so the diagnostic-read fixture has only the intended finding. Do not weaken existing boundary, false-positive, or Edit-gate assertions.
4. Add reply addressing/appended-envelope ownership to `spec/inputs.md`'s Managed HTTP row/update discipline so the next Spec 014 change routes to both affected leaves and evals. Remove stale `:rf/reply` routing from the catalogue index.
5. Keep the package narrow: no new compatibility shim, generic parser, runtime edit, sibling-skill edit, or catalogue expansion. Verification can use a zero-retired-token scan plus the existing skill gates and focused HTTP owner tests.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No normal-operation improver prose, worked example, routing row, or behavioural fixture teaches/depends on the retired co-located `:rf/reply` default; a package scan has zero unintended `:rf/reply` occurrences.
2. The manual-retry canonical rewrite supplies an explicit valid reply address, consumes the envelope appended to its target event, preserves declarative `:retry`, and handles every delivered terminal status (`:ok`, `:error`, `:cancelled`; `:stale` documented as suppressed if discussed).
3. Both schemaless worked examples use current reply addressing. The “Before” example has exactly the intended missing-production-validation defect, not a targetless-request or event-schema-arity defect. The “After” example validates the untrusted Article value in production, keeps status off `[:article :data]`, and can run through request and reply paths.
4. Eval 17 fails an answer whose Managed HTTP rewrite omits all address keys or reads `:rf/reply`; eval 20's prompt/expected output use the current appended-envelope contract and still require the correct production gate; eval 26's HTTP request is explicitly addressed or intentionally silenced so a correct reviewer is not punished for reporting `http-no-reply-target`.
5. `spec/inputs.md` names explicit Managed HTTP reply addressing/appended-envelope ownership, and the catalogue routing table uses current reply signals.
6. Verification includes JSON parse + unique eval ids/names, `bb skills/shared/tests/retro_protocol_test.clj`, skill package-reference/eval-doc/eval-packaging gates, a zero-retired-token/current-address scan over this package, and focused existing HTTP tests proving targetless throws and explicit `:reply-to` appends the envelope.
7. `rf2-j538f7.35`'s canonical `skills/re-frame2` correction is landed or coordinated first; this change touches only `skills/re-frame2-improver` and does not duplicate sibling ownership.
8. No compatibility shim, runtime change, new anti-pattern leaf, or unrelated prose cleanup is included.

title: [correctness] Bound Story-MCP lifecycle deadlines before synchronous Story work starts
description:
## Reviewed surface

Complete correctness review of `tools/story-mcp`: 38 files (18 production sources, 8 tests/fixtures, 8 specifications, and 4 package/root artifacts). Direct consumers were also traced through `tools/story`, `tools/mcp-base`, `tools/mcp-conformance`, the Story/Pair skills, descriptor generation, and CI routing.

## Defect

Story-MCP advertises `:timeout-ms` as a bounded lifecycle deadline (default 10 s, hard maximum 30 s), but the deadline begins only after `story/run-variant` or `story/preview-variant` has returned. On the JVM, real Story work can execute synchronously before that return, so a lifecycle call can exceed the advertised ceiling and monopolize the single-threaded stdio loop while still reporting `:pass`.

The call path is:

1. `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/lifecycle.cljc` evaluates `(story/run-variant variant-key opts)` before passing the returned value to `async/deref-blocking`.
2. `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/async.cljc` invokes the JVM promise executor synchronously.
3. `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc` drives setup and early phases inside that synchronous executor.
4. `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/runner_events.cljc` implements JVM `[:wait ms]` with inline `Thread/sleep`.
5. Only after the wait and subsequent work finish does Story-MCP receive an already-settled future and begin its timed dereference.

## Reproduction and observed behavior

Using the real handlers and wire pipeline, not a stub:

- initialize the plain-atom adapter and canonical event vocabulary;
- register `:story.timeout/v` with `{:script [[:wait 250]]}`;
- invoke `run-variant` with `{:variant-id "story.timeout/v" :timeout-ms 20 :dedup false :max-tokens 0}`.

Observed on current main: about 323 ms elapsed, `:status :pass`, no lifecycle error. Expected: the existing canonical timeout/error result near the 20 ms deadline, with the obsolete run prevented from continuing.

The same call through the complete in-memory stdio loop took about 314 ms and delayed a following `ping` until the wait completed. A script containing `[:wait 60000]` can therefore overrun the documented 30 s ceiling and block every subsequent MCP request.

## Contract and impact

The behavior contradicts `spec/API.md`, `spec/002-Tool-Registry.md`, `args.cljc`, and generated tool descriptors, all of which present the timeout as protection for the single-threaded server loop. This is both a correctness problem and a local denial-of-service vector for an MCP client that supplies or invokes a long-waiting Story.

## Why tests are falsely green

The current timeout regression in `tools_test.clj` replaces `story/run-variant` with a pre-created never-settling `CompletableFuture`. It proves only that timed dereference works after a future has already been returned; it never exercises synchronous constructor work or a real Story `[:wait]`. The SDK conformance story registers a vacuous no-script variant, so it also misses this path.

## Prior-wave verification and deduplication

Prior remediation `rf2-3fc89f.21` (PR #5535) correctly made unavailable browser-only reads fail rather than return false success. `rf2-3fc89f.22` (PR #5585) intentionally kept Story-MCP same-JVM/headless and assigned live-browser operation to Pair; neither owns this deadline bug.

Older closed issues `rf2-g9fje` (PR #1119) and `rf2-ovmc5e` (PR #3652) introduced the numeric cap and shared lifecycle helper, and explicitly intended that no lifecycle tool block beyond the ceiling. They did not move the deadline around synchronous Story invocation, so this is the unremediated runtime path rather than a duplicate. `rf2-9x5fm` / PR #2964 fixed a distinct CLJS callback-abort issue. Targeted bead, git-history, parent-child, and GitHub PR searches found no active owner or open PR for this defect.
design:
Use one lifecycle deadline owner spanning invocation through settlement.

The smallest coherent direction is to make the JVM Story wait yield asynchronously, matching the CLJS scheduler, using the existing `re-frame.interop/set-timeout!` facility instead of inline `Thread/sleep`. Then `story/run-variant` can return its future before a wait elapses and the existing shared Story-MCP lifecycle timeout can observe the deadline.

A timeout must also invalidate/cancel the corresponding Story run through the existing run-token/clear-state semantics (or one narrow public Story cancellation seam). A scheduled continuation from the timed-out run must be unable to dispatch events, mutate app-db, append assertions/failures, overwrite a newer result, or retain run-state/timer bookkeeping.

Keep timeout normalization in the shared Story-MCP lifecycle layer for both preview and run. Do not add a second timeout dialect, per-tool copies, a compatibility shim, or a new executor when the existing interop scheduler suffices. Preserve the descriptor/schema default and maximum unless they are deliberately revised together with all contracts.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Add a regression using a real registered Story whose script contains a real `[:wait]`; do not `with-redefs` `story/run-variant` to return an already-created future. Invoke both `run-variant` and `preview-variant` with a much shorter `:timeout-ms`. Each returns the existing canonical, schema-valid lifecycle timeout/error well before the wait duration.
2. Exercise the complete stdio run loop with a timed-out lifecycle call followed by `ping`. The ping response is not held until the Story wait completes.
3. After waiting beyond the original timer duration, prove the obsolete run cannot dispatch its post-wait event, mutate app-db, append an assertion/failure, or leave active run-state, step-boundary, pending-exception, or timer bookkeeping.
4. Immediately retry the same variant after timeout. The retry receives a fresh frame/run token and completes independently; the old scheduled continuation cannot overwrite the retry's result or contaminate `read-failures`.
5. Preserve success for fast variants and for waits within a sufficiently large timeout. Preview and run continue to use the same shared deadline policy and the advertised default/max remain descriptor-consistent.
6. Retain a separate never-settling-future test if useful for the post-return dereference arm, but make the real synchronous-wait regression the proof for this bug.
7. Add/adjust JVM and CLJS Story tests to demonstrate scheduler parity and preserve the existing concurrent-rerun and teardown token guarantees.
8. Update Story-MCP API/registry prose to describe the actual end-to-end deadline and cleanup semantics.
9. Pass the focused Story-MCP Clojure suite, descriptor manifest check, stdio roundtrip, Story JVM/CLJS suites, and MCP conformance Story path.
notes: HOLD (mayor, 2026-07-11): premise CONFIRMED (20ms deadline did not bound a 250ms sync wait; 286ms elapsed, :status :pass). Root cause spans TWO surfaces: story-mcp lifecycle.cljc:53 defers timeout AFTER run-variant fully evaluates, BUT the actual blocking site is tools/story runner_events.cljc:1190-1198 (JVM schedule! does inline Thread/sleep; run-loop! recurs sync; async/promise runs body sync) so run-variant returns already-settled and deref-blocking .get(timeout) is a no-op. DESIGN fix (make JVM schedule! yield via re-frame.interop/set-timeout! + a run-token cancellation seam) lives in tools/story — which rf2-j538f7.34 (Story run owner) is concurrently editing. SEQUENCE after .34 merges (tools/story is serialised) OR fold into .34. story-mcp side is then minimal (call a new public Story cancellation seam from lifecycle.cljc). Live DoS vector until fixed: [:wait 60000] overruns the 30s ceiling + blocks the single-thread stdio loop.

title: Correctness review: implementation/ssr-ring (2026-07-11)
description:
SCOPE: full static read of implementation/ssr-ring (ring.clj, pipeline.clj, lifecycle.clj, streaming.clj, payload.clj, shell.clj, headers.clj, cookie.clj, trust.clj, deps.edn) against owning Spec 011-SSR.md, the ssr-side contract surface it consumes (error_listener.cljc, payload_policy.cljc, streaming.cljc, boot.cljc, hydrate.cljc, html_helpers.cljc), and the pinned ssr-ring tests. No builds/tests run. The cookie semicolon-in-attribute issue is already tracked (rf2-j538f7.16) and not duplicated here.

1. P1 — ssr-ring hydration payloads are rejected by the shipped client boot: every SSR page fails hydration in the documented flow.
Files: implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/payload.clj:60-79 + implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc:708 (stamp), implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:157 (gensym frame id), guard at implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc:106-144 and implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc:104-139.
Defect: both handlers build the wire payload with :rf/frame-id unconditionally stamped to the per-request gensym frame (:rf.frame/f####). The client counterpart (ssr/hydrate!) THROWS :rf.error/hydration-frame-id-mismatch on a present-and-different :rf/frame-id, and the :rf/hydrate handler fails closed the same way. A stable client frame (e.g. :app/main) can never equal a per-request gensym.
Failure scenario: a consumer follows the documented pair verbatim — serve with ssr-ring/ssr-handler, boot with (ssr/hydrate! {:frame :app/main :render-tree-fn ...}) reading __rf_payload from the DOM — and hydration throws on EVERY page; frame-state stays unhydrated. Evidence this is real and unreconciled: the only ring-handler round-trip test hand-strips the key (ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj:911-918, comment says dispatching it would trip the guard), and every SSR example dissocs :rf/frame-id before serving (examples/capabilities/ssr/{ssr,ssr_streaming,resources_ssr}/core.cljc) — but those are custom hosts; ssr-handler/stream-handler expose no opt and no strip, so a real ssr-ring consumer cannot apply the workaround.
Fix direction: omit :rf/frame-id from adapter-built payloads (absent is the documented no-conflict shape — the exact pattern the examples use), or add a handler opt naming the client frame to stamp; align Spec 011 payload-scope row for per-request-frame hosts.

2. P2 — contract drift: drain-time projected errors are status-only, but spec + facade docstring promise an error page via :error-view.
Files: spec/011-SSR.md ~791-804 (sanitisation pipeline step 5) and ~831-843 (:error-view table row: "An exception INSIDE the drain or render walk"); implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:139-143 (docstring: ":error-view ... for projected drain/render errors"); actual routing at pipeline.clj — resolve-error-body is reached ONLY from project-render-throw->ring-response (render-time throws).
Defect: a drain-time projected error (handler/fx exception, route-miss 404, schema 400 during :initial-events) stamps the status only; the body is the rendered ROOT-VIEW plus the full hydration payload, and a caller-supplied :error-view is never consulted. Pinned deliberately by ring_draintime_error_test.clj:203-210 and :278-281. Related: a recovered-to-nil reactive sub ships/streams the degraded body under the projected 500 (ring_streaming_test.clj:617-624), vs spec 744/750 wording "yields a 500 error page".
Failure scenario: a caller wires :error-view expecting a branded page for drain-time 500s (as the docstring and spec table state) and silently gets the root-view body rendered against a partially-drained app-db instead.
Fix direction: the pinned status-only behaviour is the better design for the 404/400 routing cases (apps want their own not-found page), so reword spec step 5 + the :error-view table + the ring.clj docstring to scope :error-view to render-time throws — but this needs a ruling on whether 5xx-class drain errors should route through :error-view.

3. P3 — stream-handler docstring misdocuments the recovered-sub arm.
File: implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj ~566-591 (docstring).
Defect: claims "both fail closed to a non-200 projected error page on the request thread, with no pipe or writer thread spawned" and "selected only once the shell is known-renderable (clean render and a success status)". The code has no success-status check: when a recovered-to-nil sub buffers a 500, the full shell still streams through a spawned writer under the 500 head (pinned: ring_streaming_test.clj:617-624). The error-page/no-writer claim is true only for the throw arm.
Failure scenario: doc-reader (or future maintainer adding behaviour to match the docstring) diverges from the pinned contract.
Fix direction: doc-only — align the docstring with the pinned stream-the-degraded-shell-under-500 behaviour.

4. P3 — explicit-nil handler opts violate the spec rule that nil means "use the default" (Spec 011 Trusted shell hook contract: strings "or nil — meaning no override, use the default").
Files: implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:205 (merge handler-defaults raw-opts), implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/shell.clj:73-93 (document-prefix) and :107-113 (document-suffix).
Defect: (a) :html-shell nil overrides the default via merge and is not caught by construction validation — every request then NPEs calling nil in build-full-response* and returns a projected 500; (b) map-destructuring :or does not fire on present-but-nil, so :script-src nil silently omits the bootstrap script tag (page never hydrates) and (c) :app-element-id nil emits <div id=""> (client hydrator cannot find the mount). Realistic trigger: (when prod? asset-url) shapes feeding the opt.
Fix direction: strip nil-valued keys from raw-opts before merging in both handlers, and/or use (or x default) at the shell use sites.

5. P3 — wire EDN serialisation inherits ambient JVM printer bindings.
Files: implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:320 (pr-str rf-payload), implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:350 (pr-str projected delta) and :383 (pr-str final-payload).
Defect: pr-str at the wire boundary respects *print-length* / *print-level* / *print-meta* root bindings. A host that alter-var-roots *print-length* (common for log hygiene) silently truncates every hydration payload and streaming delta into unreadable EDN.
Failure scenario: client read-server-payload fails closed to nil (malformed EDN) — every page silently degrades to client-only render; streaming deltas dropped. No error on the server side.
Fix direction: one shared helper wrapping the three sites in (binding [*print-length* nil *print-level* nil *print-meta* false *print-readably* true] (pr-str ...)).

OTHERWISE CLEAN: writer lifecycle is no-leak on every exit path checked (redirect short-circuits destroy inline, shell-throw tears down before the pipe exists, head-materialise throws short-circuit pre-pipe, writer finally closes pipe + destroys frame); payload embedding is XSS-safe (EDN-aware script-body encoder with fail-loud token breakout, escaped attribute positions, raw hooks named + construction-validated per spec); render-time throws project to non-200 through the same materialiser (headers/cookies accumulated pre-throw survive); post-render re-flush prevents the silent-200 recovered-sub case; CRLF/NUL gates at the cookie wire boundary + token-grammar cookie names; Content-Length stripped on adapter-assembled bodies; case-insensitive header fold with multi-value vectors; request/response side channels cleared on frame teardown; fail-closed non-integer status coercion.
notes: RULED 2026-07-11 22:17 (operator-delegated Mike->Fable, after independent Codex review): Option B, tightened to a projected-error pre-commit contract. Classification is semantic by projected status: projected 4xx (400/401/403/404 arm, generalised 400..499) with renderable app -> app root body + hydration payload, :error-view NOT called; projected 5xx before body commit -> :error-view (or the LOCKED DEFAULT ERROR TEMPLATE when the option is absent - absence must NOT mean keep-root-body, that preserves the unsafe half); unrenderable root/shell throw -> error body regardless of projected status; post-commit streaming failure -> telemetry + truncation only. Manually-set status 500 with NO projection stays on the app arm. Mechanism: add one-frame (ssr/flush-response-result! frame-id) -> {:response .. :public-error ..} consuming the pending trace once; both handlers branch on it after drain (and again after render work); do NOT infer projection from (:status response); redirect precedence first. :error-view API stays one arg (sanitised public-error only; keyword-registered view or fn; fn form invoked under with-frame same as keyword). 5xx materialisation: projected status + safe accumulated headers/cookies, plain String body, NO pipe/writer thread, NO root-view/shell/__rf_payload/app-db/hashes. Containment: error-view throw -> emit :rf.error/ssr-ring-error-view-failed, fall back ONCE to locked template from ORIGINAL public error, no re-projection; only if that fails use :on-error fixed 500. Tighten :rf/public-error validation to status 400..599 + closed four-key set in prod (:details only runtime-appended under dev-error-detail). Open proof: error view with a recovered-to-nil reactive sub (try/catch cannot see it) - either one-shot fallback or constrain error views off reactive subs, with a test. Acceptance list + prose alignment (Spec 011 steps/table/status prose, both docstrings, docs pages, stale test comments) per the Codex section. Full contract: ai/decisions/rf2-oytx7j.ssr-ring-drain-error-view.md (mayor checkout, local-only).

title: Correctness review: implementation/schemas (2026-07-11)
description:
SCOPE: full read of implementation/schemas (schemas.cljc facade, storage/validate/validator/walker/digest/cache/malli namespaces) + owning Spec 010 (and the Spec 009 validation rows) + end-to-end verification of every consumer seam (router step-1 + post-commit, fx.cljc, subs/memo.cljc, spec.cljc boundary interceptor, core_schemas facade wrappers, frame-destroy hook). Static reading only; no builds/tests run.

FINDINGS (most severe first):

1. P2 — implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc:184 (name-bearing :map reduce), :237 (:catn branch), :446 (entry-child-schema). The entry parsers infer props-present via (map? element-1), but Malli 0.20.1 -parse-entry (verified in the vendored jar) accepts an explicit NIL props slot in a 3-element entry [k nil schema] and takes the child schema from element 2 unconditionally. The walker instead treats nil as the schema and never descends into the real child schema, and the opacity fail-closed net has the same hole (entry-child-schema returns nil, then (remove nil?) drops it). Failure scenario: (reg-event :auth/login {:schema [:cat [:= :auth/login] [:map [:password nil [:string {:sensitive? true}]]]]}) is valid Malli and validates normally, but on a failing dispatch BOTH schema-has-sensitive? and schema-has-opaque-child? return false, so the password ships VERBATIM in :value/:received/:explain/:explain-humanized on the event/fx/sub surfaces and through the redact-validation-tags seam used by the boundary/machine/flow/cofx/sub-override emitters. On the app-db surface the leaf decision happens to fail closed (align-in-path descends into nil, falls back, opaque) but whole-sensitive? stays false so :explain/:explain-humanized leak the whole reg-slice and no :sensitive? stamp lands. Same hole for :large?. This defeats the Spec 010 redaction class invariant that rf2-612mri/rf2-6ijdgh/rf2-jqx2at/rf2-ss06u/rf2-4q681i/rf2-hi0tf8 hardened for rarer shapes; no existing test covers nil-props entries. Container-level nil props ([:vector nil :string], also valid Malli per malli.core schema parsing) mis-parse in children-of (nil rides in as a child) but that direction fails CLOSED (spurious opaque = over-redaction + spurious :rf.warning/schema-walker-opaque), no leak. FIX: parse entries by count exactly as Malli does (count>=3: props = element 1 which may be a map OR nil, schema = element 2; count 2: schema = element 1) in walk-flagged-schema (:map and :catn arms), entry-child-schema, align-in-path (~:625), sanitize-sensitive-path (~:828); and make children-of treat a nil element 1 as the props slot.

2. P2 spec-vs-impl divergence, SPEC side wrong — Spec 010 per-step recovery row 4 (spec/010-Schemas.md:181) and the Spec 009 table row (spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2240) say the failing :db effect is NOT installed (no commit) and no :rf.event/db-changed fires; the implementation (implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1357-1475) COMMITS the transition, emits db-changed, validates post-commit, then rolls back and re-emits db-changed with :phase :rollback — the router docstring calls the paired ordering load-bearing, and multiple merged rollback-hardening beads (source-aware elision restore, classification-effect unwind, rollback-slice fix) presuppose commit-then-rollback. Spec 010 is also internally inconsistent (line 152 says roll back the :db effect; the line 407 example says rolled back to pre-handler value with :rollback? true — vs row 4 not installed). :fx IS correctly skipped on failure (the :rolled-back arm, router.cljc:2249). The divergence has real observables the spec should bless explicitly: the invalid state is transiently installed (synchronous frame-state watchers — plain-atom JVM adapter, epoch capture — can observe it between forward commit and rollback) and trace consumers see TWO db-changed events where the spec promises zero. FIX: rewrite 010 row 4 + the 009 row to the actual commit-validate-rollback contract; or, if never-install semantics is preferred, reorder the router to validate new-db/new-runtime-db BEFORE commit-frame-transition! (both values are already computed pre-commit).

3. P3 — implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:499-510 (maybe-emit-schema-violation!): the hot-reload :rf.schema/violation trace redacts :mismatching-value on sensitive/opaque schemas but never consults schema-has-large?, so a :large?-flagged slot ships the whole blob into the trace bus/epoch on every hot-reload violation — the exact flooding the validation-failure size-safety arm (validate.cljc elide-large-slots) exists to prevent. FIX: mirror the validation emit-sites (non-sensitive + schema-has-large? substitutes the :rf.size/large-elided marker). Dev-only surface.

4. P3 spec-hygiene — spec/010-Schemas.md:626 justifies the encapsulated-atoms contract with a frame-reg-locks companion that clear-schemas-by-frame! supposedly clears; no such state exists (storage.cljc:716-722 states the per-frame registry is the only mutable registration state) and Spec 010 line 344 itself says there is no per-frame linearization lock. Spec side stale; replace or drop the illustration.

5. P3 minor — storage.cljc:379: the :rf.warning/schema-walker-opaque payload stamps :schema-kind :compiled-schema-object when (map? schema), but a compiled m/schema value is a reified object, not a map — real compiled schemas report :unknown and plain maps report :compiled-schema-object. Diagnostic label only.

CLEAN OTHERWISE: per-frame isolation holds (validate-app-schema! walks only the named frame; frame targets normalize to keyword ids on both write and read paths so registry keys always line up); frame-destroy cleanup wired (frame.cljc:2619); malformed-schema handling fails closed per-entry with sibling continuation plus the router backstop trace; the boundary interceptor fails closed on validator throw and registration-without-schema is rejected at reg time; elision discipline matches Spec 009 (dev validate bodies behind debug-enabled? as the outermost form, always-on path/batch/metadata shape checks correctly ungated); the digest conforms to the Spec 010 algorithm (CEDN-1 path keys, per-schema sha256, UTF-8 byte-order line sort, sha256: + 16 hex); and every spec-listed surface (event, app-db, fx-args, sub-return, sub-override, flow-output, machine-data, recordable cofx) reaches the shared validator and redaction seams.
notes: RULED 2026-07-11 22:17 (operator-delegated Mike->Fable, after independent Codex review): Option B - validate the complete candidate frame transition BEFORE installing it. This REVERSES the earlier brief recommendation (bless commit-then-rollback); Codex demonstrated the current pair is not observer-atomic (synchronous trace listeners + atom watches CAN read the invalid value; the UIx/Helix spine drains a substrate epoch around EACH replace-container!, so forward writes recompute subs and notify useSyncExternalStore before validation) and that the original decision 0f45e56b53 wanted the deterministic post-condition - the physical restore was later mechanics, not a product requirement. Validators are pure over already-computed candidates, so pre-validation costs nothing on success and deletes two writes + two subscriber walks on failure. The FX-atomicity ruling is untouched (this is the transactional pre-commit side). CONTRACT (Codex normative section is authoritative): build one candidate transition (nil-coerced flow-augmented :db + :rf.db/runtime + commit-plane classification effects) WITHOUT mutating the container; validate all touched partitions conjoined (no first-failure short-circuit); failure/malformed-schema/validator-throw fails CLOSED - emit validation diagnostic with :rollback? true, restore only transient flow bookkeeping, outcome :rolled-back, skip :fx, NEVER call commit-frame-transition!; rejection emits NO db-changed/frame-state-changed/rollback-phase/db-noop events; success = exactly one commit + at most one forward change emit, no post-commit validation pass. :rollback?/:rolled-back stay public vocabulary meaning transaction-rejected (not physical write-pair). Staged implementation per Codex: pin the adversarial contract tests FIRST (listener reads old value during validation error; zero container watch callbacks; zero sub notifications across UIx/Helix/Reagent incl. listener-triggered sync flush); split prepare/validate/install; delete rollback arm + rollback emits + elision-restore overlay if orphaned; validator catch becomes trace-then-REJECT; concurrency: one registry snapshot per candidate under the drain lock + JVM race test; remove :rf.trace/phase :rollback from vocab if producer-free; update Xray/SSR consumers. Spec alignment is WIDE: 010 row4+152+407 example+malformed section, 009 canonical sequence + rolled-back definition + catalogue row + recovery table, 002/006 single-commit contract, 013 flow sequence, 015 successful-only classification install, Spec-Schemas :rollback? meaning, Conventions trace-phase set. Four pre-landing proofs per Codex (cross-adapter notification tests; consumer audit of the old pair; rejected-candidate privacy test; registry-generation race test). Full contract: ai/decisions/rf2-uhk9ko.schemas-commit-rollback-spec.md (mayor checkout, local-only).
close_reason: Option B shipped: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5702 — validate-before-install split (prepare/validate/install), rollback arm + emits + restore-elision-slot deleted, :rf.trace/phase :rollback retired, adversarial cross-adapter tests + registry race test + privacy pin landed first, wide spec sweep (010/009/002/006/013/015/Spec-Schemas/Conventions/005 + Xray specs + fixtures). All gates green (schemas/core/machines/flows/ssr JVM, CLJS node 8809, adapter smokes, mkdocs --strict).

title: Correctness review: implementation/core (2026-07-11)
description:
SCOPE: static read of implementation/core src (~48K lines). Read in full: interceptor.cljc, events.cljc, router.cljc, fx.cljc, cofx.cljc, subs.cljc, subs/cache.cljc, subs/memo.cljc, frame.cljc, registrar.cljc, interceptor_registry.cljc, std_interceptors.cljc, error_emit.cljc, emit_substrate.cljc, router/diagnostics.cljc, substrate/plain_atom.cljc, trace.cljc (partial), elision.cljc (commit-plane + reconcile/restore sections), live_frame.cljc (resolution seam). Specs consulted: Ownership.md, 002-Frames, 006-ReactiveSubstrate (targeted sections). Not deeply read: views.cljs tree, spine.cljs, image/image_assembly, source_coords tree, conformance/test_support, ssr/http facades (thin core_* shims). Test dirs sampled as behaviour evidence (sub_cache_concurrency_test, flows_reg_flow_destroy_linearization_test).

FINDINGS (most severe first):

1. P2 - frame.cljc:1171-1210 (call-serialized-with-drain!) vs router.cljc:3111-3129 (drain-try!) + 3170-3180 (ensure-drain-scheduled!): cold serialized sections break the single-drainer release protocol; a JVM race can PERMANENTLY STRAND a frame queue. drain-try! CAS-loses the :drain-lock and gives up, relying on the invariant that the lock holder is a DRAINER whose release re-checks the queue (try-release-on-empty!). But a COLD call-serialized-with-drain! holder (real callers: flows/registry.cljc:523,648 reg-flow/clear-flow; epoch/tool_pair.cljc:558 Tool-Pair writes) holds the SAME lock and releases it with NO queue re-check and NO :scheduled? reset. Scenario (JVM; next-tick runs on a separate single-thread executor, interop.clj:15-22): thread A enters a cold section on frame F; the executor fires the scheduled drain-try! for a queued dispatch, loses the CAS, returns; :scheduled? stays true; A releases. Every later dispatch! into F sees :scheduled? true and never schedules a drain - the queue is stranded until a dispatch-sync!/destroy ever happens. :scheduled? is cleared ONLY inside drain-loop paths (verified router.cljc:2785,2925,3068,3108). CLJS immune (single thread). SECONDARY same-family gap: dispatch-sync! nested-sync? (router.cljc:3426-3440) consults :in-drain?/:in-sync-drain? but NOT the frame :serialized-holder, so a dispatch-sync! issued from inside a cold serialized thunk on the same thread spin-CASes forever on its own lock (hang on both platforms) - frame.cljc added current-thread-owns-drain-serialization? for exactly this reentrancy class but the router side was not taught it. FIX DIRECTION: on cold release, re-check the frame queue and re-kick (clear :scheduled? + reschedule via the existing :router/* late-bind seam); and have nested-sync?/drain-block! consult :serialized-holder the same way call-serialized-with-drain! does.

2. P3 - subs.cljc:947-968 (compute-and-cache!): concurrent double-build stomps the cache entry (JVM). The cache-HIT path is CAS-after-snapshot hardened (subs.cljc:1252-1262), but the MISS path installs with a plain (swap! cache assoc k {... :ref-count 1}). Two threads that both miss the same query-v build two reactions; the second assoc overwrites the first entry - orphaning reaction1 (its on-dispose never fires, leaking its layer-2 input ref-count bumps) and resetting :ref-count to 1 while TWO callers hold references, so the first unsubscribe drives 1->0 and disposes the reaction the other caller is still using. sub_cache_concurrency_test.clj covers the dispose races but not the double-build. FIX: install-if-absent via swap-vals! and, on collision, dispose the just-built reaction + adopt the winner as a hit (bump), mirroring the hit-path discipline.

3. P3 - subs.cljc:883/1263 + 1632 (compute-sub*): no cycle guard in the sub graph. A :<-/parametric dependency cycle (:a :<- [:b], :b :<- [:a], or a self-edge) recurses subscribe-in-frame -> compute-and-cache! -> subscribe-in-frame with no build-in-progress marker, and compute-sub* memoises only AFTER the body computes - first subscribe/compute dies with a raw host StackOverflowError instead of a structured :rf.error/*. Registration cannot catch it (the other sub may register later; parametric inputs are dynamic), and subs/cache.cljc transitive-dependent-closure explicitly defends against cyclic :<- graphs, so cycles are an acknowledged input. Violates the fail-loud posture (flows already have a typed cycle error precedent). FIX: an under-construction set keyed by query-v (per-frame for the reactive build; the per-call memo atom can double for compute-sub) raising e.g. :rf.error/sub-cycle with the cycle path.

4. P3 - router.cljc:3216-3219 (emit-dispatched-trace!): the enqueue-time :rf.trace/no-emit? gate resolves handler meta via bare registrar/lookup OUTSIDE the image-generation binding (call-with-frame-resolution wraps only process-event!). For an image-loaded frame whose handler exists only in the generation resolver the lookup misses, so an image-registered bookkeeping/tool handler marked :rf.trace/no-emit? true still emits :rf.event/dispatched into the stream it is supposed to stay out of (the exact flood rf2-qsjda closed for registrar-registered handlers). Dev-only surface. FIX: resolve the gate through live-frame/frame-resolution-target + call-with-frame-resolution (one extra record read on the dev path only).

CLEAN (verified, no findings): interceptor chain error capture/ordering incl. after-pass teardown; path-interceptor slice/widen rules 1-5 + the rollback source correctly reading *run-frame-state-before* (not the path-focused coeffect); partitioned commit + source-aware elision restore/reconcile (rf2-5lo1fk/o6rsi2 logic holds as documented); dispatch-later two-phase arm/cancel + frame-destroy release; cofx grades/mint-policy delivery + always-on EDN floors; reserved-fx override reject/strip tiers incl. cascade exclusion; error/event emit substrates (listener isolation, kind-aware coords); subs memo equality-skip + dispose CAS discipline + hot-reload transitive invalidation; registrar warn-once/collision; frame destroy recipe ordering + teardown-report flush; strict :initial-events construction incl. in-band failure capture.
notes:
Filed rf2-x76af2.22 (P2): cold call-serialized-with-drain! strand + nested-sync self-deadlock (VERIFIED repro).
Filed rf2-x76af2.23 (P3): subs cache MISS-install double-build stomp (VERIFIED repro).
Filed rf2-x76af2.24 (P3): no sub :<- cycle guard -> raw StackOverflowError (VERIFIED repro).
Filed rf2-x76af2.25 (P3): emit-dispatched-trace! no-emit? gate image-blind (code shape verified; dev-only).

title: Nine more .cljc test namespaces still miss a lane suffix — the rf2-dn6v7 class recurs
description:
Follow-up from rf2-dn6v7 acceptance criterion 3 ("consider whether a cheap gate can catch the class").

rf2-dn6v7 fixed ONE instance: a .cljc test file whose ns ended in a plain -test, so the shadow-cljs :node-test build (:ns-regexp "cljs-test$") never compiled it while the JVM runner's .*-test$ did — half-covered, and reading as covered. rf2-ezbzvm had already fixed the same class once elsewhere, which is why the bead asked whether the class deserves a gate rather than another one-off rename.

A census of implementation/ after that fix finds NINE more .cljc test namespaces with neither a -cljs-test nor a -jvm-test lane suffix:

  implementation/core/test/re_frame/router_front_of_queue_test.cljc
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/router_transducer_test.cljc
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/source_coord_test.cljc
  implementation/machines/test/re_frame/after_timer_arm_publish_race_test.cljc
  implementation/machines/test/re_frame/join_attempt_effect_path_test.cljc
  implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_cascade_instrumentation_test.cljc
  implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_front_of_queue_test.cljc
  implementation/machines/test/re_frame/region_order_cljc_test.cljc   <- ns ends -cljc-test, not -cljs-test; probably the same typo class
  implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_timer_arm_publish_race_test.cljc

The gate itself is trivial (a Python check over git-ls-files: a .cljc under a test dir whose ns carries no lane suffix), and it belongs with the other scripts/check_*.py static gates. What is NOT trivial, and is the actual work here, is the per-file RULING: each of the nine is either (a) silently half-covered like rf2-dn6v7, and wants the rename plus a CLJS compile that may expose a JVM-only assumption, or (b) legitimately JVM-only in a .cljc file for a stated reason, and wants an explicit -jvm-test suffix (or a documented allowlist entry) so the gate has something to accept.

Deliberately NOT bundled into rf2-dn6v7's PR: that bead was scoped to one rename, and nine rulings plus a new gate is a different size of change. Criterion 3 said to say so and skip rather than grow the bead.

Suggested shape: one worker, census-then-rule, gate added last so it lands green. Sequence after any in-flight machines/ or core/ test work to avoid rename conflicts.

title: beads-checkpoint still commits memory-row churn alongside every real update
description: MERGED-PR AUDIT #6936 (implementation quality). The checkpoint helpers correctly compare row sets to suppress a commit when an export differs from HEAD only by memory-row order, but they then copy the raw unordered export and commit it whenever any genuine row changed. That means the normal case still carries every unrelated memory reorder. Reproduced on the first real audit checkpoint after #6936: the staged ledger showed 211 additions / 208 deletions; exact-line matching found 200 added rows identical to 200 removed rows (pure relocation), while only 11 added and 8 removed lines represented real updates. This defeats the stated no-churn purpose, makes routine ledger review opaque, and increases conflicts in the high-concurrency checkpoint path. Fix narrowly in both scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh and .ps1 by canonicalising the committed memory-row order (or preserving HEAD order for unchanged rows) before copy/add, without changing issue semantics. Extend layer 8 with a database export containing one real row edit plus shuffled untouched memories; the resulting commit must not include the shuffled rows.
acceptance_criteria: With one real tracker-row change and arbitrarily reordered unchanged memory rows, both checkpoint helpers commit the real change without reorder-only diff lines; a reorder-only export still creates no commit; sh/dash and PowerShell sibling behavior remain aligned.

title: resources_route_prefetch_test runs JVM-only — its ns name misses the CLJS lane
description:
Found by the EP-0037 R6 integrated-proof pass (rf2-kqxe6.10) while mapping conformance rows to lanes.

implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_route_prefetch_test.cljc is a .cljc FILE — written to run on both hosts — but its namespace is re-frame.resources-route-prefetch-test, with no -cljs-test suffix. The shadow-cljs :node-test build selects on :ns-regexp "cljs-test$", so the CLJS lane never runs it. The JVM runner's .*-test$ picks it up, so the file looks covered and is half-covered.

What that silently costs: the three warm-mode contract arms (warm-plan-ensures-are-ownerless-cause-only-and-blocking-inert, warm-plan-branch-error-is-a-prefetch-planning-failure, warm-plan-is-a-noop-when-no-branch-contributor-declares-resources) have no CLJS unit arm. EP-0037 row 7 (prefetch isolation) therefore rests on the host-agnostic corpus fixtures plus the DOM tests for the CLJS host, with the planner contract itself JVM-only.

This is the same trap rf2-ezbzvm already fixed once elsewhere (a plain -test suffix silently excluding a CLJS half) — worth noting because it means the class recurs and a rename alone does not prevent the next one.

Fix is a namespace + filename rename to resources_route_prefetch_cljs_test.cljc / re-frame.resources-route-prefetch-cljs-test, then confirm it actually appears in the CLJS run and still passes there — a .cljc that was never CLJS-compiled may have a JVM-only assumption in it.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The ns and filename carry the -cljs-test suffix and the file is discovered by BOTH clojure -M:test in implementation/resources and npm run test:cljs. 2. All three deftests pass on both hosts (fix any JVM-only assumption the CLJS compile exposes, or state why an arm is legitimately host-specific). 3. Consider whether a cheap gate can catch the class — a .cljc under a test dir whose ns lacks -cljs-test is almost always this bug; if a gate is judged over-engineering for the number of cases, say so on the bead and skip it.
notes: Acceptance criterion 3 (a gate for the class) deliberately skipped here, per the criterion's own escape hatch. Census after this fix: NINE more .cljc test namespaces in implementation/ carry neither a -cljs-test nor a -jvm-test suffix, so the class does recur and the gate itself is cheap — but each of the nine needs a per-file ruling (silently half-covered vs. legitimately JVM-only and wanting an explicit suffix), which is a different size of change from one rename. Filed as rf2-lgozq with the roster enumerated. Both-lane proof in PR #6946: JVM 704 tests/6613 assertions exit 0; CLJS 11237 tests/56369 assertions exit 0, with all three deftest vars present in re_frame.resources_route_prefetch_cljs_test.js in the node-test build.

title: EP-0037 row 9's :query-retain migration completeness has no mechanical gate
description:

title: SSR guides never document the route-entry-denial 403 floor
description:
Found by the EP-0037 R6 integrated-proof pass (rf2-kqxe6.10). Filed rather than patched — SSR docs, not routing's surface.

EP-0037 R4 made a server-frame entry denial stamp a default 403 BEFORE the denial event drains, with a defined supersession rule: the application handler may replace it with the canonical :rf.server/redirect (by redirect precedence) or set another status explicitly, and if it establishes neither, the protected route stays uncommitted and no resource or hydration data for the denied target is produced. spec/011-SSR.md:1500-1511 is normative on all of it, and the R6 proof exercises all three arms end to end.

The routing pages advertise it — docs/routing/concepts.md:525, docs/routing/glossary.md:99, and docs/routing/how-to/require-sign-in-on-a-route.md:57 ('Under SSR the same refusal renders the shell under a 403'). The SSR guide tree does not: git grep over docs/ssr/ for 'denial|denied|can-enter' returns ZERO hits, and 403 appears once, incidentally.

That leaves the gap in the worst place. docs/ssr/response.md:14-22, 42-47 and 70-80 enumerate every :rf.server/* effect, the multiple-status policy and redirect truncation — every status the APPLICATION can write, and not the one the FRAMEWORK writes on its behalf. docs/ssr/concepts.md:310 presents 401/403 purely as something 'you register your own projector to add', which now reads as wrong for the routing case.

This is a gap, not a contradiction: nothing in docs/ssr/ states anything false. The fix is a short passage in docs/ssr/response.md (the framework-stamped 403 floor, and the two ways an application supersedes it) plus a correction to the concepts.md framing, cross-referenced to spec/011-SSR.md and docs/routing/how-to/require-sign-in-on-a-route.md rather than restating the routing contract.
acceptance_criteria: 1. docs/ssr/response.md documents the framework-stamped 403 entry-denial floor alongside the application-written statuses, and both supersession paths (:rf.server/redirect via redirect precedence; explicit :rf.server/set-status under last-write-wins). 2. It states the no-hydration-data consequence for the denied target. 3. docs/ssr/concepts.md:310 no longer implies 401/403 are exclusively application-projector concerns. 4. The routing contract is cross-referenced, not restated (no second definition). 5. mkdocs build --strict and the doc-slug gate green.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #6946 (2026-07-25). The denial-floor content is otherwise accurate, but `docs/ssr/response.md` now says “There is exactly one [status] the framework writes on your behalf.” Canonical Spec 011 contradicts that exclusivity: the built-in/custom error projector also stamps the projected public error's status into the same response side-channel (default mappings include 404/400/500; §Response storage says it is written by the seven fx and “the projector's status-stamp”; §Server error projection step 4 sets the public-error status). Reopened this exact SSR-doc owner instead of creating a duplicate. Bounded repair: describe 403 as the framework's non-error route-refusal floor, distinct from projector-driven exception statuses; keep the two supersession paths and denial data-isolation text unchanged.

title: docs/core/images.md has no replaceable-framework-default category, and now over-promises fail-loud
description:
Found by the EP-0037 R6 integrated-proof pass (rf2-kqxe6.10). Filed rather than patched — this is the core/images doc surface, not routing's.

PR #6932 (rf2-0r6q4) introduced a THIRD registration category: the framework's REPLACEABLE DEFAULT, marked with the reserved `:rf/framework-default?` key. `spec/Conventions.md:497` reserves the key. `docs/core/images.md` never mentions it — `git grep -iE "framework-default|replaceable.*default"` over `docs/`, `skills/` and `examples/` returns zero hits — and as a result the guide now over-promises:

1. `docs/core/images.md:39` — "even the default path **fails loud** on a cross-namespace `[kind id]` collision (`:rf.error/image-duplicate-id`) rather than letting load order silently pick a survivor." An application `rf/reg-event :rf.route/entry-denied` beside the framework's own no-provenance copy is exactly a cross-namespace `[kind id]` pair, and since #6932 it assembles cleanly. That IS the fix, and it is the documented auth recipe.

2. `docs/core/images.md:217` — the error table row "Two selected descriptors for one (kind, id) (different source namespaces) inside one image -> :rf.error/image-duplicate-id" needs the same carve-out. Note the surrounding invariants are still exactly true and must stay stated: two APP registrations of one framework-default id remain `:rf.error/image-duplicate-id` (order still decides nothing), and the marker is only honoured together with an ABSENT `:rf.provenance/ns`, so an app descriptor stamping the reserved key on itself is still an ordinary app registration.

3. `docs/core/images.md:303` — "One boundary is absolute: **you cannot override a framework standard**" remains true, but with only two categories on the page a reader cannot tell why `:rf.route/entry-denied` is replaceable and `:rf/set-db` is not. The distinction (STANDARD = protected, `check-standard-collision!` unchanged; REPLACEABLE DEFAULT = the framework ships a safe no-op and expects you to replace it) is the useful thing to teach, and `:rf.route/entry-denied` / `:rf.route/navigation-blocked` are the two live instances.

Keep it to the three edits plus a short third-category paragraph. This is not an invitation to restructure the images page or to introduce a precedence-tier vocabulary — #6932's own commit message is explicit that the marker is neither a winner rule nor a precedence tier.

One adjacent claim on the same page was checked and is CORRECT, so do not "fix" it: `docs/core/images.md:307` says a `reg-*` re-eval resolves fresh sealed generations and swaps them into the affected frames. The R6 proof pins that behaviour for this exact case — a `:rf.route/entry-denied` handler registered AFTER its frame was sealed still receives the denial (`a-denial-handler-registered-after-the-frame-was-sealed-still-fires`, `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/ep0037_r6_integrated_proof_cljs_test.cljc`).
acceptance_criteria: 1. docs/core/images.md names the replaceable-framework-default category, cites :rf/framework-default? (reserved at spec/Conventions.md), and names the two live instances. 2. The line-39 fail-loud claim and the line-217 error-table row carry the carve-out, while still stating that two APP registrations of one framework-default id remain :rf.error/image-duplicate-id and that the marker requires an absent :rf.provenance/ns. 3. The framework-STANDARD boundary stays stated as absolute. 4. No precedence-tier or metadata-inheritance vocabulary is introduced. 5. mkdocs build --strict green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Migration corpus O-8 teaches the retired :on-match-as-loader role
description:
Found 2026-07-25 while sweeping the corpus for EP-0037 (rf2-kqxe6.13, PR #6930). Reported not fixed: migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md is a HOT-ZONE path outside that worker's write surface, so it wants its own sequenced dispatch.

DEFECT. migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md §O-8 ("Adopt the standard routing surface (Spec 012)") step 2 says:

  2. **Move per-route data fetches into `:on-match`.** What was probably a per-route-id
     multimethod or a `route->fetch-effects` helper becomes a vector of event vectors
     on the route metadata. The runtime owns the dispatch.

That is the pre-EP-0037 role. `:on-match` is fire-and-forget ACTIVATION work: it never drives `:rf.route/transition` / `:rf.route/error`, never awaits the async work its events start, and never turns their failures into route state (Spec 012 §Per-route data loading / §Route readiness is a resource projection). A v1 app's per-route data fetches are exactly the managed page reads that belong in `:resources`, which is what drives readiness. A migration performed to this step lands the consumer on a page whose progress bar and error surface never move.

The section intro has the same shape: "re-frame2 ships a first-class routing surface (`reg-route`, `:rf.route/navigate`, declarative `:on-match` data loading)".

SUGGESTED SHAPE. Split step 2 the way the runtime does: managed page reads a v1 router fetched per route become `:resources` entries (with `:blocking?` for anything the page cannot render without, which is also the SSR wait point); genuinely fire-and-forget route-entry work (analytics, host notification, seeding UI state) stays `:on-match`. Worth adding while the section is open: `:parent` composes ancestors' `:resources`, so a shared shell read is declared once (EP-0037 R2); entry gating is `:can-enter` + a `:rf.route/entry-denied` handler rather than a hand-rolled per-event interceptor, because the guard runs in the one planning pipeline and covers every door.

Also check the skill leaves that cite O-8 (skills/re-frame-migration/references/breaking-changes.md row O-8, references/auto-cross-cutting.md) stay consistent with whatever the corpus says — check_skill_migration_cites.py and check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py gate that pair.
