title: Freehand: t/find with a contains? predicate throws on the JVM and returns false in CLJS (text nodes reach the predicate)
description:
t/find and t/find-all are (filterv pred (tree-seq map? :children tree)). tree-seq yields TEXT nodes — host strings — as leaves, so the caller's predicate is applied to strings as well as node maps.

A keyword-lookup predicate nil-puns and is fine. A membership predicate does not:

  (t/find tree #(contains? % :rf.ui/presence))
  ;; JVM   -> java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: contains? not supported on type: java.lang.String
  ;; CLJS  -> false (cljs contains? on a string is total), so it just works

Same class of defect as rf2-erqin: identical author code, two behaviours by host. Hit while writing the rf2-erqin regression test — the pre-existing sibling test presence-survives-as-a-marker-node gets away with the same predicate only because it uses a LAZY (->> (tree-seq ...) (filter ...) first) and the marker node is reached before the first string.

Options to rule between: (a) t/find applies pred only to nodes (map? / string?) — but the docstring says pred reads node fields and text IS a node in the tree; (b) document that pred sees text strings and leave it; (c) make the two hosts agree on a refusal.

Not fixed under rf2-erqin: out of that bead's scope, and it is a t/ surface question rather than a presence one.
design:
RULING (2026-07-25 14:28 AUSEST, delegated ruling authority from Mike): **Option (a)** — t/find and t/find-all apply the caller's predicate to NODE MAPS ONLY. Reject (b) and (c).

Rationale, in order of weight:

1. The defect is a CROSS-HOST DIVERGENCE in a TEST helper, which is the one place a divergence is least tolerable: it makes the tests themselves lie by host. Option (b) documents the trap and keeps the divergence, so it fails on the only axis that matters. Option (c) makes both hosts throw, which fixes agreement by taking a working CLJS call away and buys nothing.
2. (a) is SUBTRACTION of a trap, not addition of surface. No new verb, no new arity, no options map.
3. It matches how callers already read text. The sibling presence-survives-as-a-marker-node test reaches node fields; text content is asserted through the owning node's :children, which is the shape every existing assertion uses. The bead's own evidence is that the sibling only escapes the bug by the ACCIDENT of laziness reaching the marker before the first string — that is a latent failure, not a supported pattern.

Scope:
  - t/find / t/find-all filter the tree-seq to map? nodes before applying pred.
  - CORRECT THE DOCSTRING in the same change. It currently says text IS a node in the tree, which is what made (a) look like a contradiction; after this change pred's domain is node maps and the docstring must say so plainly.
  - Add ONE cross-host regression pinning a membership predicate — (t/find tree #(contains? % :rf.ui/presence)) — answering identically on JVM and CLJS. That is the exact call in the bead report.
  - Sweep for any existing caller that depends on text leaves reaching pred. If one exists, migrate it to read the owning node's :children. Do NOT invent t/find-text; a caller who genuinely wants raw leaves uses tree-seq directly, and that is worth one docstring sentence.

NON-GOALS (fence — stop and report if the change grows past it): no new t/ verb, no predicate-arity dispatch, no node-type coercion of text into a map, no options map on find, no change to tree-seq's branching for any other t/ surface.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #6942, option (a) exactly as ruled in the DESIGN field: find/find-all filter the tree-seq to map? nodes before applying pred. (b) and (c) rejected on the bead, neither implemented.

Docstrings corrected in the same change as the ruling requires — pred's domain is now stated plainly as node maps, with text read via t/text on the owning node or through :children, plus the one sentence pointing a caller who wants raw leaves at tree-seq directly. Same correction in the normative owner (spec/008) and the two mirroring doc pages (prose only, no fenced block, so guide digests unaffected).

Regression: the-predicate-sees-node-maps-only in structural_test_surface_cljs_test.cljc pins the exact call from the report over a tree whose text leaf sits IN FRONT of the marker. Before the fix it was RED on the JVM with 3 errors, all 'contains? not supported on type: java.lang.String'; after, green on both hosts (JVM 1006 tests / 6986 assertions / 0 failures 0 errors, exit 0; CLJS 1073 tests / 6023 assertions / 0 failures 0 errors, exit 0). The CLJS arm was green before AND after — that IS the divergence — so it was rigged (expected timeout-ms 250 -> 999) to prove it executes the path: reds naming the deftest, then reverted green.

Caller sweep: NO caller depended on text leaves reaching pred, so nothing needed migrating to :children. Five callers already DEFENDED against the trap with an explicit (and (map? %) ...) guard (behaviors:171, pilot_react_interop:84, pilot_field:98, pilot_overlay:607, pilot_overlay_parity:93); now redundant but still correct, deliberately left alone rather than swept across five files for zero behaviour change.

Sibling presence-survives-as-a-marker-node tightened per the bead's note — it now filters to maps itself instead of relying on laziness reaching the marker before the first string, with a comment saying why that filter is load-bearing.

Non-goals all held: no new t/ verb, no arity dispatch, no coercion of text into a map, no options map, no tree-seq branching change elsewhere. Public API manifest unchanged.

title: tools/story-mcp + tools/machines-viz declare :clein/build but no workflow publishes them
description:
Found while truthing the alpha release documents (rf2-vxgfnd.99.4, PR #6922). Two Clojars coordinates are declared publishable and are enforced by the lockstep gate, but nothing can ever publish them.

VERIFIED ON main (worktree at origin/main 79d18eaf4f):
- tools/story-mcp/deps.edn:90 declares :clein/build {:lib day8/re-frame2-story-mcp ...}
- tools/machines-viz/deps.edn:85 declares :clein/build {:lib day8/re-frame2-machines-viz ...}
- .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh:300-305,329 has TOOLS=(xray story story-mcp machines-viz) and asserts all four pin repo-root VERSION and carry rewritable :local/root coords. The gate PASSES today (17 artefacts: 13 implementation/ + 4 tools/).
- git grep -n 'clein deploy' -- .github/ finds deploy steps in exactly three workflows: release.yml (implementation/*), release-xray.yml (day8/re-frame2-xray, trigger xray-v*), release-story.yml (day8/re-frame2-story, trigger story-v*). Neither story-mcp nor machines-viz has a deploy job in any workflow, and release-story.yml has no story-mcp step.

So the lockstep gate guards the release-readiness of two artefacts that have no release path. Either they should get one (a deploy job on an existing or new tag glob), or their :clein/build descriptors should come off and they should leave the TOOLS inventory. This mirrors exactly the class of drift rf2-qmhysc closed in the other direction (publishable artefacts missing from the inventory).

NOT AN ALPHA BLOCKER: a v* tag does not touch tools/, so v0.0.1.alpha is unaffected. Filed rather than fixed in rf2-vxgfnd.99.4 because that bead's scope was prose only.

DECIDE FIRST, then implement — this is a product question (is day8/re-frame2-story-mcp a coordinate we intend to publish at all?), not a mechanical fix.
design:
RULING (2026-07-25 14:28 AUSEST, delegated ruling authority from Mike — REVERSIBLE, see the last paragraph): **give both artefacts a release path.** Do NOT strip the :clein/build descriptors and do NOT shrink the TOOLS inventory.

Rationale:

1. spec/Tool-Pair.md makes the MCP pair a CONSUMER surface, not an internal dev convenience. An unpublishable story-mcp means a consumer's agent has no shipping vehicle for driving Story — the contract would be specified with nothing to install. That settles the product question the bead asks: yes, day8/re-frame2-story-mcp is a coordinate we intend to publish.
2. The correction direction matches rf2-qmhysc, which closed this same drift class by ADDING the missing publishable artefacts to the inventory. Removing descriptors would close the drift by making the gate guard less, which is the wrong repair for a gate that is currently telling the truth.
3. It is additive. Deploy jobs mirror two shipped, working patterns (release-xray.yml, release-story.yml); nothing that passes today starts failing.

SHAPE:
  - story-mcp joins the EXISTING release-story.yml on the existing story-v* glob — one tag ships Story and its MCP companion together. They already pin repo-root VERSION in lockstep, so a separate glob would let the pair skew, which is the defect and not the fix. Add the deploy step; do not add a workflow.
  - machines-viz gets its own deploy job on a machines-viz-v* glob, mirroring release-xray.yml. It is an independent tool with no companion, so it follows the established one-tool-one-glob pattern.
  - Verify after: .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh still passes with TOOLS unchanged at four, and 'git grep -n "clein deploy" -- .github/' now accounts for all four tools.

NON-GOALS (fence — stop and report if the change grows past it): no change to verify-version-lockstep.sh, no change to the 17-artefact inventory, no new release orchestration, no version-bump automation, no publishing of anything on the v* glob (a v* tag must still not touch tools/, so v0.0.1.alpha stays unaffected — re-verify that).

REVERSIBILITY NOTE for Mike: this is a product call made under delegated authority because the bead was blocking on it. If you would rather NOT publish either coordinate, the opposite repair is equally small — drop the two :clein/build descriptors and take both out of the TOOLS array — and overturning costs one bead either way.
close_reason:
HALF DELIVERED in PR #6937 — machines-viz shipped, story-mcp BLOCKED and refiled as rf2-2ii52 (P2). Closing rather than leaving open so the machines-viz work is not redispatched; the remainder is carried by rf2-2ii52 with discovered-from:rf2-4u3t1. MIKE MAY WANT TO RE-RULE — see the blocker below.

DELIVERED (machines-viz). The ruling's shape, plus a defect the ruling could not have known about: day8/re-frame2-machines-viz was not merely un-deployed, it was un-BUILDABLE. tools/machines-viz/deps.edn's :clein/build map has no :main, and the day8 clein fork's :noahtheduke.clein.specs/build-opts spec REQUIRES it, so 'clojure -M:clein pom' aborted on a spec failure before doing any work. Fixed by adding :main day8.re-frame2-machines-viz.chart (the artefact's primary public surface per its spec/API.md, same convention as tools/story's :main re-frame.story). Then .github/workflows/release-machines-viz.yml, new, on a machines-viz-v* glob mirroring release-xray.yml: tag-vs-VERSION check, the shared lockstep script, a JVM test gate (632 tests / 2537 assertions green), the :local/root -> :mvn/version rewrite via the shared comment-aware helper (rf2-ldkuk, chosen over release-xray.yml's inline python because its fail-loud abort is what stands in for release-story.yml's generated-pom preflight), a clojure -P ordering gate, then clein deploy. Verified the generated pom locally before and after the :main fix. Also closed an adjacent gap: post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml's EXCLUDE list was missing release-story.yml already and would have been missing the new workflow.

NOT DELIVERED (story-mcp) — three blockers, all verified by RUNNING clein rather than reading deps.edn, all detailed in rf2-2ii52. (1) day8/de-dupe is a main-:deps RUNTIME coordinate of story-mcp declared as a git coord; clein pom SILENTLY SKIPS it exactly as it skips :local/root, and there is no :mvn/version to rewrite it to because de-dupe is not on Clojars. The generated story-mcp pom carries only org.clojure/clojure and cheshire — publishing it would ship a jar missing a runtime dep to a registry with no yank, which is the precise failure class preflight-story-package.sh exists to prevent. (2) story-mcp depends on day8/re-frame2-mcp-base via :local/root; mcp-base declares its own publishable :clein/build, is un-buildable for the SAME missing-:main reason, and is a FIFTH publishable tool jar absent from the four-entry TOOLS array. This bead's fence explicitly barred changing that array, so I stopped rather than publish a Clojars coordinate the lockstep gate does not guard. (3) The lockstep gate is blind to both classes — it reads :version and the :local/root coords, never whether clein accepts the :clein/build map, never whether a non-:local/root runtime coord survives into the pom. It reported 'all 17 artefacts pinned' over an artefact that could not be built.

Blocker (1) is a PRODUCT decision outside this fence: publish day8/de-dupe to Clojars, vendor it, or accept that story-mcp and mcp-base are not Clojars-publishable. That decision gates the story-mcp half entirely.

FENCE HELD: verify-version-lockstep.sh untouched; the 17-artefact inventory and four-entry TOOLS array untouched (gate re-run: PASSED, 'all 17 artefacts (13 implementation/ + 4 tools/)'); no version-bump automation; one workflow mirroring an existing one, no new orchestration. RE-VERIFIED that a v* tag still does not touch tools/: release.yml has zero 'tools/' references and all five tag globs are prefix-disjoint (v, xray-v, story-v, machines-viz-v, template-v), so v0.0.1.alpha is unaffected and this is not an alpha blocker.

REVERSIBILITY (per the ruling's own note): publishing day8/re-frame2-machines-viz was a product call made under delegated authority, not by Mike. Nothing has been published and no tag was created or prepared. The opposite repair is equally small — drop the :clein/build descriptor and take the tool out of TOOLS — and overturning costs one bead. day8/re-frame2-story-mcp's publication is now deferred to rf2-2ii52 and therefore still entirely open.

title: Freehand guide: compilation.md's v/render-fn caller only works from a COMPILED parent
description:
docs/core/freehand/compilation.md, 'Parameterized content (render-fn / slot)', shows a compiled data-table and then a bare caller fragment:

  [data-table {:rows people :row (v/render-fn [person] [:td (:name person)])}]

That caller renders only when it is itself inside a {:compiled true} body. A v/render-fn authored in an INTERPRETED body answers raw hiccup, and a compiled parent's child collector refuses it with :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed ('A compiled view produced a vector where a child was expected'). Reproduced while building rf2-qwsmv's fixtures; the fixture hosts the caller in a compiled declaration with a comment saying why (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/guide/compilation_cljs_test.cljc).

The block sits under a compiled-mode heading so it is not plainly wrong, but the reader most likely to copy it is the one promoting ONE leaf while the parent stays interpreted, which is the guide's own advice everywhere else. Either say so at the block, or make the interpreted->compiled slot crossing work.

Cross-mode composition is otherwise explicitly promised: 'Interpreted parent -> compiled child: fine.'
design:
RULING (2026-07-25 14:28 AUSEST, delegated ruling authority from Mike): **Annotate the guide block.** Do NOT make the interpreted-parent -> compiled-child v/render-fn crossing work under this bead.

Rationale: making the crossing work is a SUBSTRATE slice (the compiled child collector would have to accept raw hiccup from an interpreted v/render-fn, which changes what a compiled body may receive). That is a Freehand grammar/emitter change with conformance consequences, and it does not belong to a guide-truth bead. The guide is wrong TODAY and can be made true today for the price of a sentence; conflating the two leaves the documentation lying while a slice is designed.

Scope: at the 'Parameterized content (render-fn / slot)' caller fragment in docs/core/freehand/compilation.md, state plainly that the caller must itself sit inside a {:compiled true} body, and name what happens otherwise — an interpreted v/render-fn answers raw hiccup and a compiled parent's child collector refuses it with :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed. Say it AT the block, not in a distant note, because the reader who copies it is mid-copy. The page's own 'Interpreted parent -> compiled child: fine' promise stays true and must not be weakened — it holds for ordinary child views; render-fn is the exception, so mark it as one.

If the writer judges that the guide reads better by hosting the caller in an explicitly compiled parent (mirroring the fixture at implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/guide/compilation_cljs_test.cljc, which already carries a comment saying why), that is an acceptable alternative shape for the same ruling — the requirement is that a copying reader cannot end up with the refusal.

NON-GOALS (fence): no substrate change, no grammar change, no new diagnostic, no cross-mode slot crossing, no new guide page. Docs only. If a Freehand fix looks warranted, FILE A BEAD against the owning slice and leave it out of this PR.
close_reason: Closed

title: RULING: should re-frame.freehand.tool be bundle-isolated from production builds?
description:
Left open by rf2-j3evb, which classified `re-frame.freehand.tool` as :tooling on the published API surface (PR #6920) but deliberately did NOT decide this — it is a ruling, not a worker call.

THE QUESTION: `tools/` is bundle-isolated from production builds (nothing in implementation/ may :require from tools/). Should the Freehand TOOL TIER be held to the same rule?

WHAT MAKES IT CHEAP TO ANSWER NOW: the namespace has exactly one var in it. `view-manifest` is a two-line pure read over a value the declaration already carries — `(when (descriptor/view? x) (descriptor/manifest x))` — so it costs essentially nothing to ship, and there is no accumulator/registry/history behind it (those were ruled out permanently, rf2-drpa3.167). The cost argument for isolation is therefore weak TODAY. The argument FOR isolating is precedent: the tier's name says 'tool', and deciding after it grows a second and third var is deciding under pressure.

Note the contrast with the sibling: `re-frame.freehand.test` carries an explicit 'dev/test SCOPE, public SURFACE — nothing in a production bundle may :require it' rule in spec/API.md. `re-frame.freehand.tool` currently carries NO equivalent statement either way, which is the actual gap: whichever way this is ruled, the API.md section should say so, and if isolation is ruled in, a bundle-isolation gate needs to name it.

Filed from rf2-j3evb rather than decided in it.
design:
RULING (2026-07-25, delegated authority from Mike): **YES — bundle-isolate `re-frame.freehand.tool` from production builds**, and state it explicitly in spec/API.md mirroring the wording its sibling already carries. Do NOT move the namespace out of implementation/freehand/.

## The bead's own premise has already expired

This bead argued the decision was cheap because the namespace held 'exactly one var' — a two-line pure read — so the cost argument for isolation was 'weak TODAY', while noting that deciding after it grows a second and third var means deciding under pressure.

That growth happened TODAY, between this bead being filed and being read. PR #6939 (rf2-lvvl2 increment 1) added THREE more vars — read-view-manifest, read-view-dependencies, read-view-event-sites — plus a dev-only re-frame.freehand.registry behind the v/defview expansion. And two further slices are already filed and queued: rf2-xftdv (source 2, a live current-occurrence index and mounted-views) and rf2-cpfbg (source 3, a bounded explain-render folding the Spec 009 ring at read time). Those two are explicitly LIVE-STATE tiers.

So the choice is no longer 'isolate a trivial pure read or not'. It is whether the substrate's production bundle will eventually carry a live occurrence index and a ring-folding explainer. Stated that way it answers itself, and the bead's warning about deciding under pressure is precisely why to decide it now rather than after xftdv lands.

## Reasons, in order of weight

1. **The sibling precedent is decisive and already written down.** spec/API.md gives re-frame.freehand.test an explicit rule: 'dev/test SCOPE, public SURFACE — nothing in a production bundle may :require it'. re-frame.freehand.tool is the same shape — a reader published so TOOL authors can consume it, not part of the authoring surface an application ships. Two namespaces of one kind should not carry opposite contracts, and the bead correctly identifies the real defect as tool carrying no statement either way.
2. **It converts an accident into a contract.** PR #6939 established that re-frame.freehand.tool is NOT door-reachable while cell is, and pinned the mention roster closed at {cell, tool}. The freehand_evidence_elision gate arms four files rather than the tree, and its honesty rests on that reachability claim. Today that holds because of how things happen to be wired; isolation makes it a rule someone must deliberately break rather than one a future require can quietly invalidate.
3. **Trust-the-programmer argues FOR the boundary, not against it.** An application author never needs re-frame.freehand.tool; a tool author does. Naming that line is ergonomic clarity — it tells both audiences which surface is theirs. This is not ceremony imposed on the programmer; it is the substrate being honest about who a namespace is for.
4. **The cost is a sentence and a roster entry, because the machinery exists.** check-bundle-isolation.test.cjs is already the gate and already carries an ARTEFACTS roster (it was edited under rf2-a32r7). Naming tool there is an entry, not a framework.

## Scope

- spec/API.md: add the scope statement to the re-frame.freehand.tool section, mirroring re-frame.freehand.test's existing wording. This is the gap the bead names.
- Name re-frame.freehand.tool (and re-frame.freehand.registry) in the EXISTING bundle-isolation gate's roster so a production :require fails loudly.
- Do NOT relocate the namespace. It must stay under implementation/freehand/ because it reads the manifest the compiler builds; 'bundle-isolated' here means no production bundle may :require it, exactly as for re-frame.freehand.test. Moving it to tools/ would be a real refactor and is not what this ruling asks for.
- Sequence AFTER PR #6939 merges — it is actively editing that namespace and spec/api-manifest.edn.

## NON-GOALS (fence)

No new gate or script. No relocation. No change to the four-file arming of freehand_evidence_elision. Do not weaken the :tooling classification rf2-j3evb already assigned — isolation is about bundle reachability, not about whether the surface is public; it is public AND dev-scoped, which is precisely what the test sibling already demonstrates is a coherent combination.

## Consequence worth recording

This ruling pre-settles placement for rf2-xftdv and rf2-cpfbg: whatever they add lands dev-scoped and production-isolated by default, so neither has to relitigate it. That is the benefit the bead was reaching for when it said not to decide under pressure.

title: Mayor-side .beads revert vector: checkout of HEAD issues.jsonl + checkpoint re-import silently evaporates recent closes
description:
FILED 2026-07-25 10:55 AUSEST from the in_review cluster dossier (delegated ruling). No existing bead owns this vector (searched); rf2-4l67v (Dolt remote) is adjacent and already ruled - reference it, do not merge into it.

THE VECTOR: CLAUDE.md mandates git checkout HEAD -- .beads before every pull (correctly, to avoid the stale-HEAD pull-abort trap). But if a bd close or bd create happened after the last export-commit, that checkout reverts the JSONL to the pre-close state, and the next checkpoint re-imports the reverted file into the database - the close simply evaporates. Neither the pre-commit hook nor the CI beads-pr-boundary gate can see it, because it is neither a commit delta nor a PR: the doctrine that prevents one fault performs the other. This is the LAST live vector of the .beads time-travel fault family (the PR vector is closed by the unconditional CI gate; the local hook arm is rf2-zt65l).

OBSERVED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: rf2-5e8zv was reopened exactly this way and had to be re-verified; commit e80786e007 on main (chore(beads): re-close kqxe6.7/.166/1a9au (merged, reverted by re-import)) records three more closes reverted by re-import and manually re-closed. The eight-bead in_review cluster disposed 2026-07-25 is downstream collateral of the same fault family.

FIX IS PROCEDURAL FIRST, MECHANICAL SECOND - options to rule on:
1. Order the mayor loop so a checkout of .beads never follows tracker mutations within a tick: checkpoint (export-commit) FIRST, then checkout+pull. Amend the CLAUDE.md wording (Beads durability + Workflow sections both carry the bare checkout instruction today).
2. Have checkpoints RE-EXPORT from the Dolt database (bd export) rather than trusting the working-tree JSONL, so a reverted file can never be re-imported over newer database state.
3. Optional guard: warn when the checkout would discard a working JSONL newer than the HEAD copy (mtime or row-count delta).
4. Landing rf2-4l67v (durable Dolt remote) demotes the JSONL to a pure downstream artefact and dissolves the risk class - it is the strategic fix; 1-2 are the cheap immediate ones.

ACCEPTANCE: CLAUDE.md sequence updated so close-then-checkout cannot revert within a tick, AND a bd close performed immediately before the standard pre-pull cleanup demonstrably survives the following checkpoint (verify via bd show).
notes: CLOSED via PR #6936 (2026-07-25 15:2x AUSEST). Options 1-3 done; option 4 (rf2-4l67v Dolt remote) untouched, still an operator action for Mike. (1) CLAUDE.md's BOTH copies of the sequence (Beads durability + Workflow) now read checkpoint -> clear -> pull, so a checkout of .beads can never follow a tracker mutation within a tick. (2) scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh + .ps1: a checkpoint runs 'bd export' and commits THAT, never the working file, so a reverted export is unreachable; refuses an empty export or one that drops >10% of rows (2026-06-10 mid-rewrite incident 7aea52459); commits only .beads/issues.jsonl via explicit pathspec (metadata.json is not in the rf2-ydl2p mayor allow-list); refuses to run in a linked worktree, reusing check-beads-boundary.sh's derivation. (3) --pre-pull / -PrePull warns when the working export is ahead of HEAD and is silent otherwise; it compares row SETS not bytes, because bd export does not fix memory-row order and on Windows 'git checkout' writes CRLF while bd export and 'git show' emit LF - a byte comparison warned every single time (caught by test case 8c, which failed until the EOL/order normalisation went in). ACCEPTANCE: 'bd close rf2-51uz1' then measured the danger window live - HEAD said in_progress, 'bd export' said closed, 2625 vs 2626 rows; bd show confirms CLOSED. The commit half runs end to end in test-pre-commit.sh layer 8 case 8a against a stub bd (close in the DB only -> git checkout HEAD -- .beads -> checkpoint -> the COMMITTED file carries status closed), plus the same shape in a .ps1 sandbox; it is sandboxed rather than run in the mayor checkout because a worker may not commit the tracker and the live mayor loop owns those commits. title: The reachability-control byte figure in test.yml's comment only holds from a cleared build cache
description:
Follow-on from rf2-hce4p (PR #6915), which pinned the build posture for B5's MATCHED PAIR only.

rf2-hce4p's own filing recorded a secondary datum with the same mechanism, outside that PR's write surface:

  .github/workflows/test.yml:2582 records the reachability control pair as '744,100 vs 752,791 chars - 8,691 chars of controller runtime'. From clean that reproduces (748,141 control vs 739,455 production, +8,686). With the evidence-elision gate run first in the same tree it INVERTS: control 739,072 vs production 739,455, i.e. -383.

Confirmed mechanism in #6915: a shadow-cljs build that compiles fresh in a process where a SIBLING build was served from cache gets different Closure identifier/property renaming - measured there as 4,075 raw bytes on the compiled twin, same 4,312 functions. A build compiling fresh with no cache-hit sibling is deterministic regardless of how many siblings preceded it.

NOT a gate defect: check-freehand-reachability.cjs asserts present/absent, not bytes, and passes 2/2 in both postures (re-verified green in #6915). What is wrong is only the BYTE FIGURE in the prose comment, which reads as a stable fact and is not one.

Cheapest honest fix, matching what #6915 did for B5: either route npm run test:freehand-reachability through a cache-clearing clean script the way build:freehand-matched now is (implementation/package.json holds the pattern: clean:freehand-matched), or annotate the comment to say the figure is a from-clean reading at a named revision. The first is preferable and is about three lines; the second is the floor.

Fenced from #6915 because .github/workflows/test.yml was held by another worker that wave.
close_reason:
Delivered in PR #6937. Took the bead's PREFERRED fix, not the floor: added clean:freehand-reachability to implementation/package.json (clears out/ and .shadow-cljs/builds/ for BOTH freehand-release and freehand-release-reachability-control) and routed test:freehand-reachability through it — the same pattern clean:freehand-matched/build:freehand-matched established for B5's matched pair. test.yml's comment now carries the measured figure, labels which side is which, names the revision, states that it is a from-clean reading and why, and tells the reader to read the DELTA rather than the absolutes.

MEASUREMENTS — six runs, every one PASS 2/2 doors. At bb86e780a2: from clean (twice, byte-identical) 733,971 control / 730,039 production; both cached: same; freehand-release cached with the control cache cleared so the control compiles fresh: same; and the bead's exact scenario (clean tree, evidence-elision gate first, then the reachability gate): same. At the rebased base 4cdd518035: from clean 734,264 / 730,332, and evidence-elision-first-then-cleaning-script 734,264 / 730,332.

TWO HONEST CORRECTIONS TO THE BEAD. (1) The specific INVERSION did not reproduce in any posture tried, including the exact scenario the bead describes. (2) The recorded figure was nonetheless wrong by any reading: the real delta is 3,932 chars, not 8,691 — less than half. So the fix stands (the mechanism is real and the posture is now pinned) but nobody should expect to see the sign flip.

USEFUL FALLOUT: the rebase brought implementation/core/src/re_frame/image_assembly.cljc forward, which moved BOTH bundles by 293 chars while the delta stayed at exactly 3,932. That is why the comment now frames the delta as the claim and the absolutes as revision-stamped provenance — and it is why the second commit on the branch is a re-measurement rather than a re-commit of the pre-rebase number.

check-freehand-reachability.cjs UNTOUCHED and unweakened — it asserts present/absent, never bytes, and passed 2/2 throughout. CI will re-run the gate on the PR independently: implementation/package.json arms freehand_reachability in report-changed-surfaces.sh.

title: Spec 012 readiness table: the first failure is picked in canonical byte-key order, not effective plan order
description:
PROSE-ONLY, hot-zone, must be sequenced behind EP-0037 R4 (rf2-kqxe6.8), which holds spec/012-Routing.md.

spec/012-Routing.md:897 (Route readiness table, row 3) says the route's :error is the deterministic first failure 'in effective plan order'. The projector (re-frame.resources.route/reconcile-readiness) actually sorts by state/key-id — the canonical CEDN-1 byte key — because the outstanding blocking slot is a SET and effective plan order is not recoverable at reconcile time. The code is right; the prose is wrong.

Fix: reword row 3 to say canonical byte-key order (state/key-id). Line 973 repeats the phrase WITHOUT the ordering qualifier and needs no change.

REJECTED alternative: persisting effective plan order into the blocking slot so the prose could stand as written. That is machinery — a set becomes an ordered structure, threaded through commit/settle/hydration/restore — to make an arbitrary-but-deterministic tie-break match a sentence. The determinism the spec actually promises is already delivered.

Provenance: found by the 2026-07-25 prep audit for rf2-kqxe6.17 and confirmed while landing PR #6913 (rf2-kqxe6.17 + rf2-kqxe6.6). Fenced out of #6913 because spec/012-Routing.md was held by the live R4 worker; #6913's four code changes do not depend on it.

The readiness-table row now reads: 'the deterministic first failure — the outstanding blocking set is ordered by canonical CEDN-1 resource-key identity, not by hash or plan order, so the pick is stable across settles that prune siblings (:rf.error/resource-route-blocking)'. That is this bead's ask in full: it names canonical CEDN-1 key identity, explicitly rejects both hash order and plan order, and adds the reason the projector sorts that way (stability across settles that prune siblings), which the original 'in effective plan order' wording contradicted.

WHY IT SAYS ORDER RATHER THAN PERSISTING PLAN ORDER: the blocking slot is a SET, so effective plan order is not recoverable at reconcile time. Persisting it would be machinery, and that was rejected when rf2-kqxe6.17 was ruled — the prose was always the right fix, not the code.

title: Published install-re-frame-ui how-to still promises a Clojars coordinate the release contract now says will never exist
description:
POST-MERGE REVIEW of main 9cdc3652e6..d5794fded8.

PR #6899 (rf2-a32r7, commit 8b1dadce8f) made day8/re-frame2-ui non-publishable: it dropped :clein/build from implementation/ui/deps.edn, removed the ui deploy leaf and release-body row from .github/workflows/release.yml, and dropped ui from verify-version-lockstep.sh. docs/release-process.md:15 now states the ruling plainly — 're-frame.ui is **not** in that set and never will be'.

The published how-to was not reconciled and now contradicts it:

- docs/core/how-to/install-re-frame-ui.md:14-21 tells a consumer to declare `day8/re-frame2-ui {:mvn/version "..."}` in deps.edn as the way to install the substrate.
- docs/core/how-to/install-re-frame-ui.md:25 — 'Pre-publication coordinates: day8/re-frame2 and day8/re-frame2-ui are not on Clojars yet. **Until they are**, projects inside a monorepo checkout resolve them with :local/root'.

That sentence is now false and directional: it tells the reader the coordinate is coming, when the ruling is that it never will. The page is in the published nav (mkdocs.yml:191), so this is what a consumer reads. The same 'not on Clojars yet' framing is repeated at examples/ui/minimal-counter/README.md:54 and examples/ui/minimal-counter/deps.edn:3.

What breaks: a reader who follows the page waits for a coordinate that will never be published, or files an issue asking when. Nothing at build time — this is a docs-coherence defect, which per the project's own posture (spec/docs are the artefact) is a real one.

Fix sketch: the :mvn/version snippet becomes the :local/root shape the example actually uses, and the admonition states the ruling instead of a schedule — day8/re-frame2-ui is donor-only and is NOT published; a monorepo checkout resolves it with :local/root, and view work that is not maintenance of existing donor views belongs on Freehand (spec/004). Point at docs/release-process.md for the ruling. The two examples/ui/minimal-counter notes take the same edit.

Care needed: implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/shadow_config_contract_jvm_test.clj reads this page behind the `rf2:shadow-ui-contract` anchor (page-rel, line 53) and the `rf2:shadow-ui-version` anchor. Leave both anchors and their fenced blocks in place, or that gate throws.

Overlaps but is not covered by: rf2-drpa3.55 (F6c migration completeness — Freehand NAMES, not publication claims) and rf2-drpa3.57 (F6e donor deletion — eventually deletes the page, but that gate is not close and the wrong claim is live now).
notes:
MAYOR DISPOSITION CHANGE 2026-07-25, on Mike's direction ('we are removing re-frame.ui and using freehand'): DELETE the how-to, do not repair its coordinate.

The bead was filed as 'the published install-re-frame-ui how-to still promises a Clojars coordinate the release contract now says will never exist'. The obvious repair — point it at a coordinate that does exist — is now WRONG. re-frame.ui is not getting a different coordinate; it is being removed. rf2-drpa3.57 (F6e) deletes the standalone day8/re-frame2-ui artifact and the re-frame.ui public surface outright, and Freehand is the substrate consumers install.

SO: the document should GO, not be corrected. Under the pre-alpha stance there is no deprecation page, no redirect stub and no tombstone — a how-to for installing a thing that will not exist is not content to migrate. Check whether anything links to it (the strict-docs link validator will fail the build on a dangling reference, so removing it means fixing inbound links in the same cut) and whether mkdocs nav names it.

SEQUENCING: this is safe to do BEFORE F6e lands — the coordinate it promises is already guaranteed non-existent by the merged release contract (rf2-a32r7 / PR #6899), so the document is already wrong on main today, independent of when the artefact is deleted. It does not need to wait.

WHY IT IS NOW MORE URGENT THAN ITS P3 SUGGESTS: Mike is preparing an 0.0.0.alpha tag. A published install guide promising a Clojars coordinate that will never be published is a consumer-facing broken promise, and tagging alpha is exactly the moment people start following install guides. Recommend actioning before the tag rather than after.

SCOPE FENCE: delete the how-to and repair inbound links and nav. Do NOT write a Freehand replacement guide in the same cut — rf2-fby7o owns authoring the Freehand guide from the ratified draft, and duplicating it here would collide.
close_reason: PARTIAL, deliberately: the false claim is cured, the DELETION is blocked and is now rf2-ote5u. PR #6914 replaced the :mvn/version snippet with :local/root and swapped the 'not on Clojars YET ... until they are' admonition for the actual ruling (donor-only, never published, pointing at release-process.md and at the Freehand guide for new work). Both rf2:shadow-ui-contract and rf2:shadow-ui-version anchors and their fenced blocks left intact. WHY NOT DELETED: implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/shadow_config_contract_jvm_test.clj locates the repo root BY this file, so removing it errors every test in that suite - and a docs-only diff fires NO jvm gate (verified via report-changed-surfaces.sh), so the deletion would merge green and red main on the next implementation/ui PR. implementation/** was fenced to other workers this wave. rf2-ote5u carries the deletion plus the gate retarget as one change.

title: Classify re-frame.freehand.tool on the published API surface (api-manifest roster + spec/API.md row)
description:
Follow-on from rf2-hytu5, which created `re-frame.freehand.tool` — the
Freehand tool-tier reader door — publishing one var, `view-manifest`.

The generated public-API manifest introspects an EXPLICIT namespace roster
(`implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj`), and
`re-frame.freehand.tool` is not in it, so nothing went stale and no gate is red.
But a supported reader door that tools are told to use should be classified like
its siblings rather than sitting off-roster by accident.

SCOPE (one PR, all three or none — they are one surface):
  - add `re-frame.freehand.tool` to the generator's namespace roster with the
    rationale comment its neighbours carry;
  - add its curated tier/owner/status to `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn`
    (`:tooling` tier looks right — it is the same tier `v/describe` and
    `v/manifest` sit in) and regenerate `spec/api-manifest.edn`;
  - add the `spec/API.md` row `api_md_check` will then require, and mirror the
    namespace in the CLJS probe
    (`implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/`) so the surface is
    reconciled in both directions on both hosts like `re-frame.freehand` and
    `re-frame.freehand.test` are.

Worth deciding at the same time: whether the tool tier should be
bundle-isolated from production builds the way `tools/` is. `view-manifest` is
a two-line pure read over a value the declaration already carries, so it costs
essentially nothing to ship — but the tier question is a ruling, not an
accident, and it is cheaper to answer while the namespace has exactly one var
in it.

NOTE for whoever picks this up: `spec/API.md` and `spec/api-manifest.edn` are
hot-zone files. Sequence, do not parallelise.
close_reason:
DONE in PR #6920 (commit a4d8b2abc3). All three scope items in one PR, as the bead required.

CLASSIFICATION: :tooling, owner 004, status EP-0036 — the tier the bead suspected, confirmed and justified rather than assumed. It is the tier v/describe and v/manifest already sit in, for the same reason: it answers with inspection DATA and is never a dispatch surface. Tooling is back-room and opt-in (the Guide and skills load front-porch only), so this classifies the door without advertising it to application authors — the honest reading of a read an INSPECTOR performs and an application does not.

Deliberately NOT a promotion, and the justification is on the metadata row: the whole difference from v/manifest is TOTALITY (a tool is handed whatever it swept out of a namespace, so every value answers and nil means 'nothing statically known'), which is a tooling property, not an escalation in support level. NOT internal-public either — the taxonomy reserves that for surfaces exported so a host or tool can embed against framework PLUMBING, and this is a first-class published read with a normative owner. Explicitly not the donor re-frame.ui.tool surface (disposition REPLACE, owned elsewhere).

LANDED: generator jvm-namespaces roster + rationale comment; curated tier/owner/status in spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn; spec/api-manifest.edn REGENERATED not hand-edited (543 -> 544 vars); spec/API.md section + row; CLJS probe mirrors the namespace AND enrols it in fully-rowed, so a SECOND public var on either host fails direction-2 completeness — which is what keeps 'reader, not tool framework' true by construction rather than by comment.

GATES: gen --check, api-md-check, doc-api-check, doc-guide-check, skills-check all exit 0; api-manifest projection unit tests 151/369 exit 0; npm run test:cljs (the probe's own host) exit 0 with 11173 tests / 56179 assertions / 0 failures.

NOT DECIDED HERE, deliberately: the bead's open question about bundle-isolating the tool tier is a RULING, not a worker call. Filed as rf2-etqma with the cost/precedent argument laid out, plus the observation that the real gap is that API.md says nothing either way (unlike re-frame.freehand.test, which carries an explicit production-bundle rule).

title: Freehand: retire the unreachable v/raw recognition + the :foreign crossing-prop marker; fix the three diagnostics + the false-green crossing coverage (RULED: retire)
description:
Split out of rf2-tb5yq — the smallest of the five remaining unpublished heads,
kept separate because its entanglement is different from the others'.

STATE, pinned by re-frame.freehand.unpublished-head-absence-jvm-test:
`re-frame.freehand/raw` is interned on neither host and has no
spec/api-manifest.edn row, so `raw-form?` never answers true through the
production door. The `:raw` op is outside `grammar/admitted-ops`, `emit-jvm`
refuses it loudly through its own diagnostic (rf2-drpa3.174) and `emit-react`
has no arm — so it is inert at every stage.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE DELETE: `raw-form?` has a SECOND call site
(analyze.cljc ~2557) where a `(v/raw x)` in a boundary PROP position mints the
`:foreign` marker, and `:foreign` is a member of
`grammar/crossing-prop-markers` — a closed roster the emitter-coverage suites
prove one row per member of, and one the conformance surface reads. Removing the
recognition therefore removes a marker from a pinned roster, which is a
conformance change and not merely a compiler edit.

Note also that `root.cljc`'s `:rf.ui.compile/runtime-root-form` diagnostic tells
authors "v/raw covers a runtime React element" — the same
recommends-a-form-that-does-not-exist defect rf2-rrosy names for `v/html`, so
whichever way this is ruled, that message needs to agree with the outcome.

RULING NEEDED: retire the recognition with its marker and fix the diagnostic
text, or ship `v/raw` with a real lowering. Low priority — unlike `frame` and
`html` this one populates no manifest roster and gates no elision verdict, so
nothing downstream is being decided by a dead input.
design:
RULING (2026-07-25 10:54 AUSEST, delegated ruling authority from Mike): **Option B — RETIRE** the `v/raw` analyzer recognition and the `:foreign` crossing-prop marker it alone can mint. Do NOT publish `re-frame.freehand/raw`. Dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-4gnrs.rule-on-v-raw.md, primary analysis + concurring Codex review) weighed and adopted; load-bearing anchors independently re-verified against main before ruling.

## Rationale (in order of weight)

1. **The capability is not lost.** A runtime React ELEMENT already crosses into a Freehand tree unwrapped, in both interpreted and compiled child positions — `react.cljs:889-894`, and that arm sits OUTSIDE the `walk?` gate so it serves the compiled child seam too. This is the fact that separates `v/raw` from `v/html` (rf2-rrosy), where the escape genuinely has no spelling.
2. **Nothing downstream decides on the marker.** `:marker :foreign` is minted at exactly ONE site (analyze.cljc:2575, behind `raw-form?`); the React emitter treats it identically to a nil marker (falls to default); no manifest roster, no elision input, and no conformance fixture reads `grammar/crossing-prop-markers` — every repo hit is inside implementation/freehand.
3. **Publishing it correctly is a real slice, and half a slice is the worst outcome.** `emit-jvm`'s `:foreign` arm names `re-frame.freehand.tree/opaque-foreign` — a var that exists ONLY in the donor (`ui/tree.cljc:364`); a JVM runtime refusal (`tree/jvm-host-op!`) does not exist either, and `compiler.cljc` emits the structural body on BOTH hosts so a compile-time refusal cannot stand in. Same phantom-lowering class rf2-1a9au removed. Sequencing law shared with rf2-rrosy: never publish the authoring var ahead of its emitter arms.
4. **The coverage gate is false-green on main today.** `react_lowering_jvm_test.clj:173-174`'s `:foreign` row analyses to marker `nil` (no injected resolver — verified by JVM probe), passes its `:reaches` assertion vacuously (nil-marker props emit verbatim), and the roster check at `:243` compares declared LABELS, never the analysed AST — unlike its siblings at `:105` (ops) and `:200-201` (carriers). Retiring the member makes the vacuity visible and fixable; it does not create it.
5. **Precedent on file:** analyze.cljc:56-67 records rf2-1a9au's ruling for the nine host-hook heads — recognition and lowering land together, or not at all.

Divergence from rf2-rrosy (`v/html` = SHIP) is coherent, not inconsistent: html has no alternative spelling and a live `:html-sites` manifest roster; raw names a capability authors already have unnamed. The rf2-rrosy ruling stands untouched.

## Implementation map (ONE PR, emitter-lane serial: analyze.cljc + grammar.cljc + both emitters; line numbers verified on main 2026-07-25)

All paths under `implementation/freehand/` unless noted.

A. **`src/re_frame/freehand/compiler/analyze.cljc`**
   - remove `ui-raw-fqns` (:40) and `raw-form?` (:343)
   - prop branch: remove the `raw?` binding (:2563) and the `raw?` clause of the `:marker` cond (:2575) — becomes `(cond raw-fn? :v/raw-fn :else nil)`
   - child branch: remove the `raw-form?` arm (:3600) and its `:rf.ui.compile/bad-raw` arity diagnostic (:3603); retire the Freehand-only `:rf.ui.compile/bad-raw` test surface with it
   - remove `:raw` from `node-ops` (:34)
   - remove the synthetic-resolver test rows that manufacture the var: `test/.../analyze_accept_cljs_test.cljc` (~:14-27, :1048, :1114-1117, :1137), `test/.../analyze_reject_cljs_test.cljc` (~:1016-1017)

B. **`grammar.cljc`** — remove `:foreign` from `crossing-prop-markers` (:80); remove the `:raw` op-rejection row (~:89-90). **DO NOT touch the `:foreign` AST OP** (foreign component HEAD — analyze.cljc ~:2636, env.cljc:251-253); only the crossing-prop MARKER of the same name goes.

C. **`emit_jvm.cljc`** — remove the phantom `:foreign` prop arm (:215, names the nonexistent `re-frame.freehand.tree/opaque-foreign`) and the dead `:raw` refusal arm (:381-386); update its pin `test/.../emit_jvm_dead_arms_jvm_test.clj:60-67`.

D. **`emit_react.cljc`** — remove the `:foreign` sentence from the crossing-marker docstring (:533-534). No behaviour change: `:foreign` already fell to the default arm.

E. **`compiler.cljc`** — remove the `:raw` capability scan (~:65): a capability bit that can never be set.

F. **Diagnostics — THREE sites recommend the nonexistent verb; all must stop:** `root.cljc:174`, `env.cljc:227`, `analyze.cljc:3768`. Replacement shape: keep the honest neighbours ("runtime-chosen components are v/view / v/element [WAVE-2]") and, in place of the `v/raw` clause, name the recovery that EXISTS — a runtime-assembled subtree keeps the subtree interpreted (`grammar/recoveries` `:keep-interpreted`, grammar.cljc:154-156). Invariant (shared with rf2-rrosy): a diagnostic never recommends an unshipped form untagged.

G. **Coverage strengthening — the regression proof.** In `react_lowering_jvm_test.clj`: remove the `:foreign` row (:173-174) AND add the crossing table's missing axis check — a `markers-of` walk mirroring `carriers-of` (:178-190) asserting each row's ANALYSED AST really carries the marker it names, alongside the emission assertions (:230-235). This is what makes the removal provable rather than asserted, and prevents another label-only green.

H. **Spec alignment (one line each):** remove `:foreign` from 004B's opaque crossing-marker set (`spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:270-276` — that paragraph already says members "arrive with the slice that lands the form"); remove `:raw` from 004D's `:capabilities` list (:338). Donor `ui/raw` passages in 004D (:1243, :1407-1424) are F6c migration text — leave historical, do not rewrite.

I. **`test/.../unpublished_head_absence_jvm_test.clj`** (landed via PR #6910) — update the raw rows from "still recognised" to absence pins consistent with the removal.

## Scope fences (non-goals)

Untouched: `v/raw-fn` (identity-as-protocol callback marker), `v/->react` (outward bridge), `v/html` (rf2-rrosy: SHIP, atomic with both emitter arms), the `:foreign` component OP, the existing React-ELEMENT pass-through (`react.cljs:889-894`), custom-element attribute/property machinery. No compatibility alias, no portal primitive, no generic opaque carrier, no new wrapper framework.

Precision note (Codex): the interpreted pass-through gate is `React.isValidElement` — it accepts React ELEMENTS, not all React NODES (portals/arrays are nodes, not elements). Any doc/diagnostic text describing the surviving capability must say "React element pass-through", never claim a general raw-node capability.

Reconsideration trigger: revisit an inward React-node escape only when at least two real integrations cannot be expressed cleanly as a qualified leaf, registered behavior, or wrapper — and then design it FRESH as a child-only React-node boundary with explicit interpreted/compiled/JVM/diagnostic semantics. Never revive the old child+prop `raw` coupling.

rf2-rrosy (v/html — divergent ruling is deliberate and coherent); rf2-1a9au (phantom-lowering precedent, recorded at analyze.cljc:56-67); rf2-tb5yq (parent split); rf2-wjgle (follow-up filed by this ruling: 004D's enumerability claim for host-React escapes is already untrue in Freehand via the unwrapped `:expr` route — decide whether the property is wanted at all).

title: Pin re-frame.freehand as the sole requirer of freehand.control, so the B5 reachability gate's narrow arm is honest
description:
The B5 reachability gate (`npm run test:freehand-reachability`, wired into CI as the required `cljs-freehand-reachability` job by rf2-zl8ao / PR #6905) is armed on a NARROW set of producer surfaces: re-frame.freehand.control (the two refusal doors the probe greps), re-frame.freehand (the facade, which today is the SOLE requirer of `control` and owns the single production call edge — `controller-key` is `def`'d to `control/record-key`), the two build entries, the build-config trio and the checker. Deliberately not implementation/freehand/**: two `:advanced` builds per PR is the cost rf2-xwa4n declined for the sibling gate.

The sibling gate can be that narrow HONESTLY because a JVM law makes a fourth producer impossible to add silently: `the-evidence-schema-reaches-the-render-path-only-through-the-dev-gated-seam` in evidence_boundary_jvm_test.clj asserts `cell` is the SOLE Freehand namespace mentioning the evidence schema, and _changed-surfaces.test.cjs pins that premise with the routing.

There is no counterpart for `re-frame.freehand.control`. A new `:require` of it from anywhere else in freehand/src — a paved path that starts resolving a controller record — would root the module in production, break the reachability claim, and NOT arm the PR gate. It would be caught by the unconditional nightly run in expensive-tests.yml (red on main, after the fact) rather than on the PR.

PROPOSED (bounded, one law + one pin, no new framework):
1. In the always-armed jvm-freehand lane, assert `re-frame.freehand` is the SOLE Freehand namespace requiring `re-frame.freehand.control` — the same walk shape as evidence_boundary_jvm_test, over the same source tree.
2. Pin that premise from implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, mirroring the existing 'the SOLE-requirer law that keeps the narrow arm honest still exists (rf2-xwa4n)' test, so relaxing the law reds the routing and forces the classifier arm to widen.

If the law turns out to be false today (i.e. some other namespace already requires `control`), the correct outcome is to widen the classifier arm to whatever the real requirer set is — not to write a law around the exception.

Surfaces: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/** (a new or extended JVM boundary test) + implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs. Sequence AFTER PR #6905 merges.
close_reason: Done in PR #6918 (worker/fh-docstring-9y9uv), one law + one pin exactly as proposed, no framework and no widening of the gate's arm. PREMISE VERIFIED TRUE TODAY: re-frame.freehand is the only Freehand namespace whose ns form mentions re-frame.freehand.control, so no arm-widening was needed. (1) re-frame-freehand-is-the-sole-requirer-of-the-controller in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/control_boundary_jvm_test.clj — always-armed jvm-freehand lane, same over-approximate ns-form walk shape as evidence_boundary_jvm_test over the same source tree. The walk is deliberately NOT shared with the sibling: the two laws guard different gates and must fail independently. (2) The routing pin in implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, mirroring 'the SOLE-requirer law that keeps the narrow arm honest still exists (rf2-xwa4n)'. RED-PROOF BOTH DIRECTIONS: adding a second :require of control to re-frame.freehand.tool reds the law (Found: #{re-frame.freehand re-frame.freehand.tool}); relaxing the law's assertion to (is (seq requirers) ...) reds the routing pin (changed-surfaces tests: 1 failed). Both probes reverted, neither in the diff. Non-vacuity is also built in: the law proves its graph is populated, proves the facade really does reach the controller, and guards the re-frame.freehand.controlled near-miss explicitly (its name extends the controller's character for character, so exact matching is load-bearing). GATES green: freehand JVM 948/6819, changed-surfaces 227, test:freehand-reachability PASS (control 2/2 doors present, production 2/2 absent), test-fast-pr.sh PASS.

title: Retrospective facade-export classification sweep (re-frame.core, Story, Xray) for external-alpha prep
description:
The RETROSPECTIVE half of the facade-export classification audit has no bead. Surfaced 2026-07-25 while processing the rf2-fby7o api-freeze dossier; bd list across every status returned no owner for it.

## What it is

spec/Conventions.md:1198 defines the audit in two halves.

The FORWARD half is already running: every new facade export classifies and justifies itself at diff time (tier, owner, status, justification), which is why the Freehand rows in spec/api-manifest.edn all carry their four fields. That half needs nothing.

The RETROSPECTIVE half is unowned. Conventions calls it "the full retrospective sweep of every existing non-front-porch export - and the manifest table it produces" and says it "stays deferred to API-freeze / external-alpha prep".

## Scope

A repo-wide sweep of every non-front-porch export on re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core - the grandfathered exceptions Conventions explicitly records - deciding keep / rename / move / internal-public for each, and producing the manifest table.

NOT a Freehand audit. Freehand's 38 members are already classified at diff time; six are :facade? true (mount, unmount!, hydrate-root, ->react, active-connections, command-log) and every one is a CLJS-only verb re-exported from the namespace that owns it, which is exactly the deliberate single-import re-export the Conventions ruling sanctions.

## Deadline

Conventions sets it itself: before re-frame2's first meaningful external alpha/beta release - explicitly NOT "before v1". The reasoning is that the moment real users copy examples, a namespace move becomes a breaking change.

## Relationship to rf2-fby7o

DECOUPLED. rf2-fby7o's release condition names this audit as half of its api-freeze gate. Two independent analyses concluded that coupling is a drafting accident rather than intent: gating a Freehand guide on a re-frame.core sweep that Conventions itself schedules for external-alpha prep does not make the guide more correct. See rf2-fby7o notes (2026-07-25 dossier fold) for the full reasoning. Mike rules on whether the coupling is struck.

## Acceptance

1. Every non-front-porch export on re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core carries a keep / rename / move / internal-public disposition.
2. The manifest table Conventions describes exists.
3. Anything ruled rename or move is either executed or has a bead.
notes:
DEFERRED 2026-07-25 (mayor), with an explicit release condition so it stops being re-triaged every dispatch tick.

WHY NOT NOW: the bead's own charter defers it. spec/Conventions.md:1198 says the retrospective half 'stays deferred to API-freeze / external-alpha prep', and the FORWARD half is already running (every new facade export classifies itself at diff time, which is why the Freehand rows in spec/api-manifest.edn carry all four fields). So nothing is rotting while this waits.

THE DECISIVE REASON: it is a repo-wide sweep of every non-front-porch export on re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core, producing a manifest table. The alpha is gated on rf2-vxgfnd.99 (EPIC S7 — Helix-removal wave + alpha tag), which by its own title REMOVES a substrate and will move exactly the surface this sweep would classify. Running the sweep before S7 means classifying exports that S7 then deletes or renames, and redoing the table afterwards. Sequencing it after S7 costs nothing and saves the whole second pass.

RELEASE CONDITION — reopen when EITHER holds:
  1. rf2-vxgfnd.99 (S7 + alpha tag) closes, or
  2. Mike calls api-freeze / external-alpha prep explicitly.

Not a rejection: the work is real and Conventions mandates it. This is a sequencing decision only.

title: Advertise :rf.handler/source on the pair-MCP handler-meta surface + AI-Audit rows
description:
The pair MCP already returns :rf.handler/source but never advertises it, so an AI agent debugging a live runtime reaches for the filesystem by reflex instead of reading the handler body it has already been handed. Pure discoverability gap — no runtime work.

Verified 2026-07-25: zero occurrences of :rf.handler/source anywhere under tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/, and zero mention of source-as-data in spec/AI-Audit.md.

HOW IT GETS THERE TODAY (nothing to change here)

- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs:244-335 — returns the remaining map with no source-key whitelist.
The descriptor and catalogue only promise source coordinates and generic "custom slots".

WORK

title: Spec 009: should an event that settles no state be cheap to OBSERVE, not just cheap to run?
description:
SURVIVING FINDING from the D007 key-condition-map gate (ruled DELETE, rf2-drpa3.178). rf2-drpa3.124 found the one genuine argument against deleting the form, and it is not an event-grammar argument at all - it is an observability one. Filed here so it is not lost with the form.

THE OBSERVATION. The paved keyboard spelling puts a site on the element that fires on EVERY key:

    :on-key-down [:acme.ui.buffered/key-pressed k g on-commit ::v/key]

Typing one character into a buffered field therefore dispatches TWO events - a key-pressed that settles a no-op, then the edit. Asserted at implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_field_cljs_test.cljc:1183-1200.

THE COMPUTE IS NEAR-FREE, and that is not the problem. An unmatched key's handler returns {} - no :db effect at all - so nothing commits. There is no :rf.event/db-changed and not even a :rf.event/db-noop, which fires only when a :db effect WAS present and the value did not move (implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1333-1346). What remains is a queue turn, an interceptor chain over an unchanged frame, and a settle.

THE OBSERVATIONAL COST IS THE REAL ONE. One dequeued event is one epoch record (spec/009-Instrumentation.md:323,1064; spec/002-Frames.md, Drain versus event). The per-frame trace ring retains 50 slots by default, one per event (spec/002-Frames.md:528), and epoch-history keeps the last 50 epochs per frame (spec/Tool-Pair.md:100). So typing twenty-five characters into one buffered field consumes an entire post-mortem window with no-op key epochs, and halves the effective reach of Xray's epoch panel, Story's outcome chips and restore-epoch!. Any keyboard-heavy application hits this.

THE QUESTION for Spec 009: should an event that settles NO state be cheap to OBSERVE, as it is already cheap to run? Candidate shapes to weigh, not a design: a retention policy that does not spend a ring slot on a settled-nothing epoch; a fold/collapse of consecutive no-op epochs at the trace surface; a tool-side filter in Xray/Story rather than a substrate change.

EXPLICITLY NOT A REQUEST TO BUILD ANYTHING YET. There is no measured application pain - this was derived from a pilot, not from a real app under real use. The house posture is trust the programmer and do not pre-emptively engineer. Reconsider when a real application shows that no-op keyboard epochs make traces materially worse, and design from those measured cases. The one thing this bead rules out is fixing it back at the listener with a second event grammar: that was tried (FH-EVENT-005) and deleted, because suppression via an exact-key map forces a control that cares about eight keys to write eight branches identical but for the key string.
notes:
RULING (2026-07-25 10:54:16 AUSEST, delegated ruling authority from Mike; dossier ai/decisions/rf2-egt43.no-op-event-observability.md folded here and deleted).

DECISION: PARK CONFIRMED, BEAD CLOSED. Build nothing now, and never in the bead's leading candidate shape. Every citation in the bead was re-verified and holds; the analysis below corrects the framing and is the mandatory starting point for any future pickup.

CORRECTION 1 - "settles no state" is the WRONG DISCRIMINATOR. The controlled field's own site is a pure forwarder: (rf/reg-event :acme.ui.field/changed (fn [_ [_ on-input text]] {:fx [[:dispatch (conj (vec on-input) text)]]})) at implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_field.cljc:163-165. It settles no state - no :db effect, exactly like the unmatched key - yet it is the single most causally important row in the chain: it is why the next epoch (the caller's :acme.invoice/field-edited) exists at all (pair pinned at pilot_field_cljs_test.cljc:1174-1175). A retention policy keyed on "settled nothing" would drop pure forwarders, delegation sites and re-dispatch shims - precisely the rows that explain why the surviving rows happened. "Settled no state" and "not worth observing" are different predicates that coincide on the unmatched-key case and diverge badly everywhere else.

CORRECTION 2 - the retention pressure GENERALISES but the remedy DOES NOT. Paved :on-scroll [:table/scrolled table-key ::v/scroll-top] and :on-pointer-down spellings exist (spec/004-Views.md:473-483) and apply the same ring pressure, but those epochs DO settle state (ordinary db-changed), so a settled-nothing policy reclaims zero slots from them. General pressure, case-specific remedy - which is the argument for the general knob over the substrate.

WORKED EXAMPLE (why the remedy underperforms the shipped knob). Filling one invoice line is about 24 epochs, 10 settling nothing: typing REF-1024 into the buffered reference field = 16 epochs (8 settling nothing; two events per key, pilot_field_cljs_test.cljc:1183-1193); Enter-commit about 2; typing 12 into the controlled quantity field = 4 (2 settling nothing, via the forwarder above); save 1-2. The ring holds 50, so one line is half the post-mortem window. Suppressing settled-nothing rows: 24 -> 14, about 1.7x, and it deletes the forwarder rows per Correction 1. Raising the retention knob to 500: 10x, one config line or two Xray clicks, and it covers scroll/pointer too. The noise is caused by per-keystroke dispatch - the paved, correct design - not by the no-ops; they are 40 percent of the noise, not the noise.

SHIPPED MITIGATIONS (all verified live):
1. Ring depth is author-configurable twice over: (rf/configure! {:trace-buffer {:events-retained N}}), default 50, plus per-frame :rf.trace/events-retained (docs/core/observability.md:156-166; spec/002-Frames.md:528); epoch history (rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:depth N}}), default 50 (spec/Tool-Pair.md:100). Xray exposes the ring knob live in Settings -> Buffer, writing through rf/configure! (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/settings/effects.cljs:472-490, settings/view.cljs:1034-1058). An author can fix their own session in two clicks without a rebuild.
2. Read-side filtering ships: Xray persisted IN/OUT filter pills with :kind :event-id-pattern (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/filters/matcher.cljc:170-181, filters/persistence.cljs:104-127); suppressing high-frequency noise is the docstring's own canonical example :out [{:pattern ":mouse-move"}] (filters/persistence.cljs:36-38). Honest limit: a pill filters display, not retention - it cleans the view without extending reach.
3. The MCP filters server-side: watch-epochs pred supports :event-id, :event-id-prefix, :effects, :touches-path, :sub-ran, :render, :origin, :frame, :timing-ms, applied before anything crosses the wire.
4. An explicit per-handler escape exists: registration metadata {:rf.trace/no-emit? true} silences a knowingly-uninteresting handler while it still executes normally. It stays explicit - never inferred from state equality.
5. Counter-signal against any default-on collapse: the Xray Trace panel's stated principle is "Show every op" completeness-first (tools/xray/spec/023-Trace-Panel.md:41), and it already treats a no-op event's absence of rows as information rather than scaffolding (023-Trace-Panel.md:172, :235). A default collapse would reverse a considered panel decision, not fill a gap.

SUBSTRATE RETENTION (a policy that skips a ring/epoch slot for settled-nothing epochs) is REJECTED ON THE MERITS, not merely deferred: the discriminator deletes causal links (Correction 1); it buys under 2x where the existing knob buys 10x (worked example); and it breaks the one-dequeued-event = one dispatch-id = one ring slot = one epoch invariant that keeps Xray, Pair and replay histories agreeing (spec/009-Instrumentation.md:323,1064; spec/002-Frames.md:528; spec/Tool-Pair.md:92,100). FH-EVENT-005 (fixing it back at the listener with a second event grammar) stays ruled out per the bead. If a measured case ever arrives, the shape to reach for FIRST is a tool-side, default-off, one-click filter or fold in Xray (reversible; the records survive underneath) - never substrate retention.

RESIDUAL QUESTION (narrowed): is 50 the right DEFAULT ring/epoch depth for input-heavy applications? That is a default-tuning question answerable from one measured report - a one-line change, not a retention policy. Not worth holding an open bead; raise it fresh with the measurement in hand.

REOPEN TRIGGER (concrete): a real application - not a pilot - reports a debugging session that lost the epoch it needed, AND (1) raising :events-retained / :epoch-history depth did not resolve it, AND (2) the crowding events are genuinely uninteresting rather than causal forwarders. If (2) fails, the answer is a tool-side filter. If (1) fails repeatedly across apps, the answer is a larger default (one line). Separately: a benchmark attributing material dev-time overhead to observing high-frequency events reopens as "optimize trace capture / epoch assembly / ring append" - never as "erase causal units to disguise an implementation cost".

DISPOSITION: closed rather than parked open, per the rf2-5wuikc precedent - closed beads stay fully readable via bd show, everything actionable here already ships, the bead's leading candidate shape is now known-wrong, and an open park bead is a re-litigation magnet. The dossier leaned park-open with close "defensible"; the independent Codex review recommended close; the drive-to-zero posture tips it to close.
close_reason: Ruled 2026-07-25 (delegated): park confirmed and closed. Substrate settled-nothing retention REJECTED on the merits (wrong discriminator - deletes causal forwarder rows; buys <2x vs 10x from the shipped retention knob). Mitigations already ship: events-retained knob + Xray Settings->Buffer, OUT filter pills, MCP watch-epochs pred, :rf.trace/no-emit?. Residual question narrowed to default ring depth for input-heavy apps - raise fresh with a measurement. Full ruling, corrections with file:line, worked example and reopen trigger in notes.

title: Spec 012 follow-up: record :prefetch + the intent-position grammar in the Freehand route-link descriptor section
description:
Discovered-from rf2-y29wg (route-link descriptor prefetch wiring). spec/012-Routing.md is hot-zone and was fenced for that wave, so two sentences in it are now stale:

(1) Section 'The Freehand route-link descriptor' still enumerates the view's control keys as ':to / :params / :query / :fragment and :on-click'. :prefetch is now one too — it is stripped before DOM emission by both v/route-link and ui/route-link. (The GENERAL law in 'Linking from views' already states that :prefetch is a routing control key on every link surface and is stripped before DOM emission, so the behaviour is specified; only the per-descriptor enumeration is stale.)

(2) The same section should record the Freehand-specific consequence: on a link carrying :prefetch :intent, :on-mouse-enter / :on-focus / :on-touch-start become framework-owned positions and therefore carry the SAME closed callback roster :on-click carries (a plain fn, a v/handler, or nothing), rejected at render on both hosts with :rf.error/view-bad-event + :use-a-plain-fn-or-v-handler. The narrowing is CONDITIONAL on the opt-in — every other link leaves those positions as ordinary open Freehand event positions — and it is forced by the composition law the spec already states (the installed handlers compose with a caller-supplied handler, which means the framework must be able to CALL it). ui/route-link needs no equivalent sentence: a React prop is already a plain fn.

Implemented + proven in the Freehand conformance row FH-ROUTELINK-008 (spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-routelink-008.edn), which cites the '#route-plan-prefetch--warm-mode-intent-preload' anchor; once (2) lands in the descriptor section that citation may be worth re-pointing at it. HOT-ZONE: sequence, do not parallel with another spec/012 bead.
close_reason: Closed

title: Pin issue-prefix rf2 into tracked .beads/config.yaml
description:
Recovery trap found while folding the rf2-4l67v dossier (2026-07-25). The tracker prefix lives ONLY in the Dolt database, not in tracked config:

  bd config list  ->  issue_prefix = rf2
  .beads/config.yaml line 9  ->  # issue-prefix: ""   (commented out)

If the Dolt database is ever lost and the tracker is rebuilt from the git-tracked .beads/issues.jsonl (which is the documented bd bootstrap fallback and the accepted recovery floor - see rf2-4l67v), bd init auto-detects the prefix from the DIRECTORY NAME and comes up "re-frame2", not "rf2". Every existing bead id in 2,326 issues, in 6,869 commit messages, in every PR title and every spec cross-reference is rf2-*. A mismatched prefix on rebuild would be a nasty, silent, entirely avoidable mess.

THE FIX: uncomment line 9 of .beads/config.yaml and set it to rf2. One line.

  issue-prefix: "rf2"

This is safe to dispatch. .beads/config.yaml is named in CLAUDE.md as human-authored config that is fair game to commit from any worktree - it is NOT a database-derived path, so the .beads PR-boundary guard does not apply. Do not touch .beads/issues.jsonl or .beads/metadata.json in the same PR.

/ gzip-6 220,966 / brotli 183,238 / parse+top-level-compile p50 ~17 ms.

This bead is the BUILD-LANE remainder of D021's B5 row, which is out of
the bench/evidence surface because it touches implementation/shadow-cljs.edn
(HOT-ZONE, sequential):

    (interpreted / compiled / mixed) and the per-promotion delta. Only the
    mixed :freehand-release build exists on main today, so only it could be
    measured.
  - the initial-mount time D021's B5 row names needs the mixed bundle
    mounted in a browser; the release build has no :dev-http.

re-frame.freehand.bench.b5/workload already accepts any measured artefact,
so once the matched builds exist this reuses the same probe — no new bench
framework. Sequence after / alongside rf2-drpa3.166 (the deterministic
control-build reachability gate), which also lands shadow-cljs.edn build
entries.
acceptance_criteria: 1. AMENDED (rf2-rhg4q, 2026-07-25) on D021's own wording — the B5 row asks for 'representative interpreted, compiled, and mixed production bundles', REPRESENTATIVE not matched. So: TWO matched :browser release builds in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn differing ONLY in lowering (:freehand-release-interpreted / :freehand-release-compiled, one source in two states, same optimizations, same goog.DEBUG false), PLUS :freehand-release as the representative mixed shipped-cost artefact, deliberately NOT byte-matched to the pair. A delta needs two arms held still against each other; it never needed three. 'interpreted < mixed < compiled' is not a lowering series. 2. re-frame.freehand.bench.b5 measures all three shapes (raw/gzip/brotli + parse/compile) and publishes the per-promotion BYTE delta between the MATCHED PAIR as evidence, with the attribution stated PER ENCODING (raw exact, gzip within a handful of bytes, brotli identity-sensitive) rather than 'only lowering' across the board. 3. Initial-mount time for the mixed shape measured in a real browser. 4. Evidence only - no byte threshold, no timing gate (D021 NON-GOALS). 5. Cross-checked against rf2-drpa3.166's deterministic control-build reachability gate; the two are complementary, not the same.
