The testbed READMEs also claim `npm run test:adapter-smokes` stages these SSR builds, but that orchestrator does not reference them, and ssr-basic names the wrong output directory.

This is a testbed/tooling integrity repair, not an SSR runtime or public API redesign.

## Required work

- Require `re-frame.subs` in each testbed and register its hydration query with `reg-runtime-sub`, reading `[:rf.runtime/ssr :hydration]`. Preserve frame-explicit reads in the multi-frame surface.
- Correct the adjacent source comments and all three READMEs to name runtime-db and the canonical path.
- Correct `re-frame.ssr/verify-hydration!`'s one stale "slot in app-db" phrase.
- Make each README's build/output/serve instructions match an actually supported workflow; do not claim the adapter-smoke orchestrator covers these builds unless it truly does.
- Compile all three existing shadow builds and verify in a real browser that ssr-basic flips to hydrated, mismatch exposes hydrated plus its mismatch evidence, and multi-frame shows three distinct hashes. Reuse an existing browser harness if a tiny pin fits naturally; do not invent a new framework or restore the retired broad Playwright suite.

## Boundaries

No hydration storage migration, compatibility shim, app-db fallback, recovery-vocabulary work, new public API, or general sibling-testbed sweep. Keep the repair to these three concrete SSR surfaces, their truthful guidance, and the one public docstring.

title: presence: elide the undefined-key diagnostic traversal from production
description:
PR #6575 added a useful development warning for a presence child whose key evaluates to JavaScript undefined and is consequently dropped. The corrected React 19 premise and browser fixture are valid: JavaScript undefined produces a nil React key, whereas CLJS nil / JavaScript null is coerced to the string "null" and renders.

AUDIT FINDING: the diagnostic scan is not actually development-only. incoming-identities always evaluates count-keyless before calling the goog.DEBUG-gated warning. A freshly regenerated :advanced, goog.DEBUG=false browser bundle retains the recursive counter and executes its result-discarded call on every production presence render. This adds a second full child-tree walk solely for the narrow advisory and contradicts the intended zero-production-cost posture.

WORK: place the count-keyless traversal itself behind the compile-time goog.DEBUG branch, retain the current warning and browser behavior, and verify in the existing advanced mounted build that the residual counter/call is absent.

BOUNDARIES: one small runtime gating change plus proportional verification. No new diagnostic framework, warning lifecycle state, API, test matrix, or behavior change.

Verified against React 19.2 jsx-runtime (direct probe + headless-Chromium reproduction): a CLJS-nil key VALUE — e.g. the doc example {:key (:id t)} with a toast missing :id — is coerced by jsx to the STRING "null", a valid non-nil .-key, so the child RENDERS (it does NOT silently vanish). Proof: jsx(type,props,null).key === "null"; jsx(type,props,undefined).key === null. collect-elements drops a child only when .-key is genuinely nil, which through the compiled surface requires an UNDEFINED key value (a JS-interop read of an absent property, e.g. (.-id #js {})), NOT a CLJS nil. So the 'silent vanish on nil id' scenario the bead describes cannot occur for idiomatic CLJS keys.

title: presence.md doc completion: worked CSS block + four missing contract truths (enter-timing, literal timeout, re-entry phase, inline-markup fence)
description:
From the adversarial presence review (Mike-directed, 2026-07-20). docs/core/re-frame.ui/presence.md teaches 'the animating is your CSS's job' but shows zero CSS, and omits four contract truths a copy-paste reader will hit. Every claim below was verified against source on main.

SURFACE: docs/core/re-frame.ui/presence.md ONLY. No overlap with rf2-b1wv9's files (mental-model/reactivity/ssr/testing/state/api pages) or Mike's live pairing worktree (events.md, introduction.md). Not hot-zone.

WORK:

1. ADD one worked CSS block immediately after the existing toast example, teaching the robust split:
   - ENTER via CSS animation on insertion (e.g. .toast { animation: toast-in 200ms ease-out; } @keyframes toast-in { from { opacity: 0; translate: 0 8px; } }) — fires on DOM insertion, immune to effect timing.
   - EXIT via the phase class (e.g. .toast.unmounting { opacity: 0; translate: 0 8px; transition: opacity 250ms, translate 250ms; }) with the example's :timeout-ms 300 >= the 250ms transition, tying back to the page's existing 'match or exceed' sentence.
   - A prefers-reduced-motion block disabling the motion.
   - One sentence on WHY enter-by-class-transition (.mounting -> .present) is the fragile spelling: the phase flip rides a passive useEffect (presence_runtime.cljc PresenceComponent, step '3. flip every :mounting entry to :present'); it usually lands after first paint so a transition usually fires, but React does not guarantee passive-effect-after-paint (sync flushes, hidden documents) — when the flip lands before first paint the browser never computes the .mounting style and the enter transition silently does not fire. animation-on-insertion sidesteps this entirely; @starting-style is the modern alternative for transition authors. Do NOT add runtime hardening (double-rAF etc.) — deliberately rejected as gold-plating (review 2026-07-20); the doc teaches the immune pattern instead.

2. ADD one sentence: :timeout-ms must be a positive number LITERAL in the opts map — a var/design-token fails compile with :rf.ui.compile/bad-presence (analyze-presence, implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/analyze.cljc ~2600-2635 checks (number? (:timeout-ms opts)) on the literal map).

3. TIGHTEN the re-entry bullet: removal-then-reinsertion interrupts the exit and resumes at :present — the enter animation does NOT replay (:unmounting flips straight back to :present, presence_runtime.cljc reconcile; a mid-exit CSS transition reverses from its current position, which is the good behavior worth stating).

4. ADD the inline-markup fence: the phase Provider wraps each child ELEMENT, so inline literal markup under the boundary evaluates its props in the PARENT's render and provably cannot read its own (ui/presence-phase) — the phase-reading child must be a separate keyed defview (the page's toast-card shape). Note the compiler backstop: focusable inline literals fail with :rf.ui.compile/a11y-presence-exit-interactive (compiler/a11y.cljc check 4, rf2-0ufty).

BOUNDARIES: prose + one fenced CSS block + one fenced clojure delta only; no runtime/spec changes; keep the page's tight human voice and its 'deliberately not an animation system' framing. The SSR client-half sentence is NOT owned here — rf2-uqe1b's DOC RIDER owns it (avoid double ownership). title: Give managed-HTTP retry timeline honest recovery dispositions
description:
## Problem

PR #6555 correctly makes the shared Recovery schema an open keyword vocabulary. Its independent audit exposed a pre-existing producer/contract mismatch in managed HTTP:

- Spec 009's `:rf.http/retry-attempt` catalogue row promises `:recovery :retried` and says a new attempt is scheduled.
- Spec 014 describes the per-attempt timeline and also deliberately retains a terminal-exhaustion marker with `:next-backoff-ms nil`.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc` emits `:rf.http/retry-attempt` in both places, but neither tag map supplies `:recovery`.
- `trace/build-event` hoists `:recovery` for `:info` events only when the producer supplies it, so Xray and other consumers receive nil rather than the documented disposition.

The two emit arms are not semantically identical: the intermediate arm schedules another attempt and is honestly `:retried`; the terminal marker schedules nothing, so blindly stamping `:retried` on both would make the metadata look complete while remaining false.

## Smallest coherent repair

Keep the existing category and timeline. Stamp `:recovery :retried` on the intermediate scheduling emit. Give the retained terminal-exhaustion marker an honest existing disposition (recommended `:no-recovery`, since no further retry occurs), and update the single Spec 009 row / narrow Spec 014 wording to document the two cases. Extend the existing managed-HTTP exhaustion test to assert the intermediate and terminal recovery values, including the `:next-backoff-ms nil` discriminator.

Do not add a recovery registry, runtime validator, new public API, new trace category, policy hook, Xray special case, or generalized conformance framework. The open keyword schema is correct; this is one producer's missing/ambiguous metadata.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every emitted `:rf.http/retry-attempt` carries a keyword `:recovery` matching what that particular attempt did.
- An intermediate retry that schedules another attempt carries `:retried`.
- The retained terminal-exhaustion marker carries an honest non-retry disposition (recommended `:no-recovery`) and remains distinguishable by `:next-backoff-ms nil`.
- Spec 009's catalogue row and Spec 014's retry timeline describe both arms without claiming the terminal marker scheduled a retry.
- Existing HTTP retry tests assert both recovery values; focused HTTP tests pass.
- No registry, runtime-wide validator, new category/API/policy, or tooling-specific handling is added.
notes:
PR #6565 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT ADDENDUM (2026-07-20) — reopen the exact source owner for one bounded correctness repair; no new recovery vocabulary/API/machinery.

The normal retry/exhaustion tags are correct, but the intermediate `:recovery :retried` emit is ordered before the existing cancellation-safe backoff handoff. `maybe-retry!` emits at transport.cljc:1177-1205, then the deterministic `:maybe-retry/before-schedule` interleave can abort the request, and the backoff guard correctly prevents any fresh network attempt. The existing `abort-injected-in-maybe-retry-window-no-double-reply-no-reissue` fixture proves exactly one server hit / zero retry, yet a trace listener observes `:rf.http/retry-attempt` with non-nil backoff and `:recovery :retried`.

That contradicts Spec 009's recovery law (the field tells tools what the runtime did; `:retried` means the runtime retried and surfaces the result) and this bead's own honesty AC. A tool can currently report a retry that never happened.

SMALLEST REPAIR: emit the intermediate `:retried` disposition only at the cancellation-safe point where the timer callback has won its transition, confirmed the request was not aborted, and is about to call `run-attempt!`. Preserve the existing event/category/tags and terminal `:no-recovery`; do not add a registry, validator, category, policy hook, or new recovery spelling. Extend the existing deterministic abort-race fixture to record traces and assert that an in-window cancellation with zero reissue does not claim `:retried`; retain the ordinary exhaustion proof for the two real retries plus terminal marker. If implementation details require a nearby equivalent commit point, the invariant is simple: no `:retried` row unless attempt N+1 is actually permitted to start.

Separate normative spec synchronization remains exactly owned by open `rf2-s5wby`; do not duplicate it here. The source comments/test prose are verbose, but cleanup is not standalone work—tighten only where the fix already touches them.
AUDIT PR #6590: the new normative wording calls every nil-:next-backoff-ms/:no-recovery row a terminal-exhaustion marker where attempts are exhausted. The actual guard emits after can-retry? fails whenever attempt > 1 OR the current kind is retry-eligible. Thus attempt 1 can retry a 5xx, attempt 2 can terminate on a non-retryable decode failure under max-attempts 3, and still emit the nil-backoff marker before the budget is exhausted. While repairing this same retry-timeline truth seam, use the honest term terminal retry-sequence/stop marker and state its two cases: budget exhausted, or a later failure became ineligible. Align Spec 009, Spec 014, and the abbreviated API rows; pin one mixed-category sequence. This is wording + one focused fixture, not a new category or mechanism. It is folded here because this open Bead already owns honest :rf.http/retry-attempt timing and the same source/spec/test seam.
AUDIT PR #6631 — one promised proof remains. The audit addendum required a mixed-category sequence, but current tests cover only retryable-5xx exhaustion. Add ONE focused attempt-1 retryable 5xx → attempt-2 non-retryable decode failure under max-attempts 3 fixture: exactly one actual :retried row, then one nil-backoff :no-recovery terminal STOP before max attempts; true nearby test prose that still calls every nil row exhaustion/scheduling. spec/API.md:635 residue is ALREADY owned by open rf2-4xobm — do not duplicate it here. No new category, policy, validator, or framework.
PR #6641 THREE-LENS AUDIT CONFIRMATION (2026-07-21) — reopen the exact runtime/spec owner because its final audit addendum remains unresolved through #6646.

The tree still lacks the one promised focused proof for the non-exhaustion terminal-stop arm: attempt 1 retryable 5xx -> attempt 2 non-retryable decode failure under max-attempts 3, yielding exactly one actual :retried trace, one nil-backoff/:no-recovery terminal STOP before the budget is spent, and one final failure reply. title: Complete reagent-migration's Form-3 lifecycle decision table
description:
The reagent-migration skill calls MIG-17 the Form-3 lifecycle decision but currently classifies only mount/unmount work. It never names three supported, deployed Reagent-slim shapes: `:component-did-update`, `:get-snapshot-before-update`, and `:component-did-catch` (`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/FORM-3.md`). This matters for the upcoming re-com rewrite: re-com has ten Form-3 sites using `:component-did-update`; re-frame-10x uses snapshot+did-update for scroll restoration; audited apps use did-catch boundaries.

These methods cannot safely fall through the generic host/DOM→effect advice. Did-update needs explicit dependency/update semantics and often a library-update recipe; snapshot+did-update is a paired pre-commit/post-commit protocol with no passive-effect translation; did-catch should route to the shipped `ui/error-boundary` when its recovery/logging semantics fit, otherwise the view stays on Reagent or is redesigned.

Update that one row; do not add executor machinery.

A setup increment plus cleanup decrement, or push plus matching pop, is replay-safe and correct. The 011-OWNED residue that .97.2 correctly left out of its S5 emit-seam scope: (1) ui-tree-fingerprint algorithm (FNV-1a/hex) — re-frame.ui.fingerprint + 004B both defer it to Spec 011; (2) server-tier duplicate-root-id CODE (009 row notes 'lands S5' but code pending); (3) the Layer-2 server page-assembly registry CODE (004C §7 has the spec, code absent per #6511 audit); (4) :rf.error/ssr-static-root-requires-runtime (spec-ahead, no emitter). ⚠️ GATED: this is Spec-011-owned work — NOT dispatchable until the 011/SSR-fingerprint stage is reached. Tracking bead so the owed leaf isn't lost. Cross-ref rf2-vxgfnd.97.2, rf2-is3rs, spec/011, spec/004B, spec/004C.
notes:
PR #6546 THREE-LENS AUDIT RESIDUAL (2026-07-20): reconcile authority BEFORE implementing any fingerprint machinery. At #6546's base, Spec 011's compiled-tier hydration contract already says compiled roots have no hashable client render-tree, deliberately carry no structural fingerprint channel, and that reviving one is a deferred future leaf rather than a current defect. PR #6546 nevertheless leaves Spec 004B presenting re-frame.ssr/ui-tree-fingerprint as the second S5 function whose implementation is owed. That conflict is now actionable because this bead treats the function/algorithm as roadmap work. Smallest disposition: keep the shipped emit-ui-tree contract final; make the fingerprint text a non-binding candidate gated on Spec 011 explicitly reviving the channel and a concrete consumer need, rather than an outstanding S5 obligation. Correct the shared 'recommended names' heading so the shipped emit API is final while the fingerprint remains deferred. Also remove or defer 004C's claim that :rf.error/root-hydration-mismatch already has a Spec 009 row: no such row exists, and no id should be minted before the fingerprint channel is deliberately revived. Do not build a client structural-realization/hash framework merely to satisfy stale stage prose. The response-local page-registry/duplicate-root-id work in this bead is independent and remains concrete.
PR #6546 COMPLETENESS ADDENDUM: two source-residue dispositions were omitted when rf2-is3rs transferred work into this bead. (1) The proposed server wire-accounting surface (per-root manifest/payload byte sizes, plus its teardown rider) is still absent. Apply the demand bar here: either identify a concrete production-budget consumer and specify the smallest per-response accounting seam, or explicitly retire it; do not create a metrics/ledger framework by default. (2) The #6546 close note incorrectly equates server-side per-root render-throw containment with :rf.error/root-boot-failed. That error isolates CLIENT boot failures during preflight/install/hydrate/mount; current Spec 011 instead projects an unrenderable server root/shell to the request error page. Before reviving a failed-root wire comment/fallback, rule whether per-root server continuation is actually wanted or whether the current whole-response fail-closed policy wins. Recommendation under the current posture: retire the old failed-root wire artifact unless page-assembly work demonstrates a concrete multi-root need. These are dispositions on this existing residue bead, not reasons for new Beads or generalized machinery.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-20 20:42 AUSEST)

RULING 1 — ui-tree-fingerprint: DEMOTED to a non-binding candidate, gated on Spec 011 explicitly reviving the structural render-hash / manifest render-fingerprint channel AND a named concrete consumer. It is NOT an owed S5 obligation. Basis (verified 2026-07-20): spec/011-SSR.md:812 states the compiled and native tiers deliberately carry no such hash and that reviving the render-fingerprint channel is "a deliberately-deferred future leaf, not a defect"; spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:449-463 ("Stage — the emit seam ships; the fingerprint leads code") contradicts this by presenting re-frame.ssr/ui-tree-fingerprint as the owed second S5 function, under the shared 004B:419 "Signature (recommended names...)" heading with the shipped emit-ui-tree. Decisive: the channel is write-only today — no ui-tree-fingerprint function exists anywhere in implementation/ (only a deferred-to-S5 comment in re_frame/ui/semantic.cljc), 011:453's :render-fingerprint manifest key has zero writers and zero readers, and a compiled root's client views are React elements, so no client-side structural tree exists to re-hash and compare (011 verifies compiled/native tiers by React adoption instead, catalogued at 009 row 1974 as :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch). Building it would satisfy stale prose, not a consumer. 011 is the authority on the channel; 004B's Stage prose is the stale side and gets edited at stage time. RIDER: spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md:465 cites :rf.error/root-hydration-mismatch as "an existing Spec 009 catalogue row" — verified FALSE, no such row exists in spec/009 (grep exit 1). Disposition: REMOVE or defer-with-the-channel that roster row; mint NO 009 row (an error id with no emitter and no revived channel violates rows-land-with-stages). OWNERSHIP: rf2-vxgfnd.249 owns this edit — its note (line 55) already carries the fold-in for the dangling reference within its 004C↔009 reconciliation (currently blocked on .248/.191). This bead does NOT double-own it; the direction ruled here (remove/defer, do not mint) binds .249's fold-in. Consequence for this bead: no fingerprint function, no hash algorithm work, no 009 mismatch row in the stage dispatch.

RULING 2 — server wire accounting: RETIRED (quarry-later). Basis: the per-root manifest/payload byte-size ledger plus teardown-table rider survives only in the retired S7-tombstoned amendment and bead notes — zero presence in spec/ or implementation/, zero consumers (production budgets are client bundle gates via test:perf-bundle; a host wanting response-size numbers measures the Ring body with zero framework help), and a naming collision besides ("ledger" in shipped 011 means the client payload-install ledger). If a real consumer ever appears (per-root cache layer, SSR cost dashboard), the retired amendment's tables can be quarried and the seam designed against that consumer's actual shape. Consequence for this bead: no accounting seam is specced or built; nothing in the stage dispatch.

RULING 3 — failed server root: whole-response FAIL-CLOSED stays (current spec); the failed-root wire artifact (fallback markup / HTML comment in the failed root's slot) is RETIRED. Basis: spec/011-SSR.md:1405 — "An unrenderable root/shell throw always uses the error page — regardless of the projected status — because a throw cannot supply a body" — and 011:1398, a pre-commit projected 5xx discards the root body and hydration payload and renders the :error-view. That is specced, shipped, and honest: the server never asserts a page it could not fully build. CORRECTION recorded: the #6546 close note's equation of server per-root render-throw containment with :rf.error/root-boot-failed (009 row 2382) is WRONG — row 2382 is CLIENT boot containment (hydrate-page! per-root boundary isolating preflight/install/hydrate/mount failures); server-side per-root continuation was never shipped, so nobody should later "restore" it as regressed behaviour. Per-root continuation is not foreclosed: 004B:533-535 reserves containment as a page-assembly decision "taken above the seam", so the door stays open in exactly the right place — revisit only if Layer-2 page-assembly work surfaces a concrete multi-root need, at which point the essentiality policy (a failed nav is not a failed news widget) gets answered against a real page. Consequence for this bead: no per-root server render boundary, no wire artifact shape, no degraded-page status policy, no new server-tier error id.

WHAT STAYS CONCRETE in this bead after the three rulings: the Layer-2 per-response page-assembly registry code (spec/004C §7 Layer 2, lines ~395-406, complete normative text; re-frame.ssr.manifest and re-frame.ssr.install docstrings both mark the registry explicitly absent/"a later S5 leaf") together with its server-tier :rf.error/duplicate-root-id emitter (009 row 2375: "The Layer-2 server page registry lands S5") — these are ONE piece of work, the error is what the registry raises, and it needs a response-scoped owner (a real multi-root page assembler) to attach to. Verified correction to the bead's item (4): :rf.error/ssr-static-root-requires-runtime has ALREADY SHIPPED under the spelling :rf.ui.compile/static-root-requires-runtime (raised from re-frame.ui.compiler.root/render-static-form, implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/root.cljc:903, with green tests in render_static_jvm_test.clj and error_roster_cljs_test.cljc); the :rf.error/ssr-* spelling appears nowhere in spec/. The stage worker must NOT rebuild it — at most reconcile any stale prose naming the old spelling.

OPINIONS WEIGHED: (a) the two audit notes already on this bead (#6546 three-lens residual + completeness addendum) — followed; their recommendations (demote fingerprint, demand-bar the accounting surface, retire the failed-root artifact) survived independent re-verification of every cited line. (b) The mayor's dossier — followed on all three recommendations (1b / 2b / 3a); its verification chain checked out exactly. (c) The dossier's appended Codex Recommendation — concurs on all three dispositions; its material corrections were spot-checked and two were adopted here (static-root id already shipped under the compiler spelling; registry+duplicate-root-id are one piece needing a response-scoped owner). Codex's further reaches (delete :render-fingerprint from the manifest v1 roster/constructor/tests now; prune the bead to one sentence; the S5-conformance-profile staleness) are NOT ruled here — they exceed the three questions put to decision; the manifest key is an optional extension key that costs nothing to leave reserved, and the conformance-profile honesty repair is a separate finding for the mayor to bead if verified. No Mike annotations were present on the dossier; ruled on the merits under the standing pre-alpha demand-gated posture (no over-engineering; retire/defer wins absent a named consumer).

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE for the eventual 011-stage worker: (1) spec/004B edits — soften the Stage section (449-463): "lands at S5" framing becomes "a deferred, non-binding candidate; Spec 011 owns whether the render-fingerprint channel ever revives, and it revives only with a named consumer"; split the shared "Signature (recommended names; final naming rides the diff-time facade rule)" block at 419-428 so the shipped emit-ui-tree reads as final/shipped contract while ui-tree-fingerprint reads as deferred candidate; keep the algorithm prose (canonical-EDN over N(tree), §Markup and fingerprint) as design-of-record for IF it revives. (2) spec/004C:465 — the dangling :rf.error/root-hydration-mismatch roster row is OWNED BY rf2-vxgfnd.249 (fold-in note already on it); direction ruled: remove or defer-with-the-channel, mint no 009 row. Do not edit it from this bead unless .249 has already landed its reconciliation, in which case verify it is gone. (3) NO wire-accounting seam — do not spec or build any per-root byte accounting. (4) NO failed-root wire artifact — do not add per-root server continuation, fallback markup, or an rf2-root-failed comment shape; fail-closed per 011:1398/1405 stands. (5) FENCE: no client structural-realization or DOM-hash framework, no per-root continuation machinery, no new error ids for any of the retired surfaces. (6) The dispatchable substance is the Layer-2 registry + server-tier duplicate-root-id as one unit, attached to a real multi-root page assembler when one exists, plus :rf.error/ssr-static-root-requires-runtime prose reconciliation only (code shipped as :rf.ui.compile/static-root-requires-runtime). HOT-ZONE: spec/004B, spec/004C, spec/011, spec/009 are all hot-zone files — sequence those edits, never parallel, per the dispatch rules; coordinate ordering with rf2-vxgfnd.249's reconciliation PR if both are in flight.

Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-v2gv9.spec-011-residue-dispositions.md retired (deleted) per Mike's authorization.
PR #6571 THREE-LENS AUDIT RESIDUAL (2026-07-20). Reopened exact source; no duplicate and no implementation framework. (1) Correct implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/semantic.cljc's live namespace doc, which still says N is consumed by re-frame.ssr/ui-tree-fingerprint at S5, to the ruled truth: parity consumes N now; a fingerprint consumes it only if Spec 011 revives that channel for a named consumer. Preserve the deliberately reserved/optional :render-fingerprint manifest field unless Mike separately rules removal, but make every active description unambiguously reserved/deferred rather than an owed producer/reader. (2) Reconcile the Layer-2 registry disposition across spec/004C §7 + stage table, spec/009's duplicate-root-id/root-manifest rows, and the implementation docstrings. They currently place the response registry and server duplicate-id/prefix arms at S5 while manifest.cljc/install.cljc confirm no registry exists. State the actual trigger consistently: a real response-scoped multi-root page assembler plus concrete need. Do NOT implement a registry ahead of that consumer; keep this Bead open as the named gate. Wire-accounting retirement and whole-response server fail-closed are complete. The separate 004C root-hydration-mismatch residue remains owned by open rf2-vxgfnd.249.

title: reagent-migration skill: post-#6549 residue pass — lease-scoping calibration, MIG-16 carve-out, stale fixture count, runs-once nit
description:
Follow-up from the rf2-14dj2 delegated review decision (PR #6549 merged as-is; these are the non-blocking residues). One small sequential worker pass over skills/reagent-migration/ (+ optionally one example docstring line). Cross-ref rf2-14dj2.

'does not fit an app-minted, conditionally-held, or dynamically-keyed owner'. The 'conditionally-held / dynamically-keyed' part over-restricts: the compiler explicitly accepts nil + dynamic descriptors (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/analyze.cljc:336-374, 'a symbol/call may evaluate to nil or a descriptor at render time'), the mounted suite exercises (ui/lease (when (ui/sub [::activate?]) {:resource ::feed :params {:n N}})) (resource_lease_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs:238-245), and Spec 004's canonical example is dynamic ({:params {:slug slug}}, spec/004-Views.md:593). Reword to the OWNERSHIP-based rule: (a) if resource lifetime genuinely follows this lexical view site's presence, ui/lease is valid even when activation is conditional or params are dynamic (framework owns ensure/retarget/release); (b) if an event/route/machine minted the owner, keep causal ownership in the dataflow and release via the causal end events — switching it to a view lease is an ownership-model decision, not a mechanical migration; (c) either way, never dispatch-at-unmount. Keep the steering preference — spec/004-Views.md:613: 'routes/events/machines remain the preferred causal owners (I-11)'. 'App-minted' stays a correct exclusion; only the capability claim over-states. OPTIONAL same-pass: soften the same 'unconditional model' phrasing in the canon reference docstring the skill quotes it from (examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/ui_editor.cljc:41-43) — its conclusion stands (that owner IS app-minted), only the capability wording overstates.

2. MIG-16 CARVE-OUT (catalog-judgment.md:30, untouched by #6549): 'with-let's finally clause maps to effect cleanup' — add the MIG-17 domain-work carve-out: only HOST teardown maps there; a finally that dispatches follows MIG-17 (no dispatch-at-unmount; re-home). One cross-reference sentence.

RUNS-ONCE NIT (gotchas.md, StrictMode section added by #6549): 'Reagent's :component-will-unmount runs once, at the real unmount' — false under React 18 StrictMode dev, which also remounts class components (componentDidMount -> componentWillUnmount -> componentDidMount). Drop the false contrast; the rule is simply that ALL teardown must tolerate dev replay. One clause.

5. COSMETIC (optional, same pass): (a) gotchas.md StrictMode quote renders the ui.cljc docstring parenthetical '(that is what cleanup is for)' as an em-dash clause inside quotation marks — restore verbatim; (b) two retro-history lead-ins in catalog-judgment.md ('The deepest correction, and the one a skill-only migration gets wrong', 'The hand-migrated reference states it directly') carry roadtest flavour into consumer-facing guidance — neutralise the voice, keep the doctrine.

ROADTEST FINDINGS (rf2-8er3t complete 2026-07-20; worker retro + MAYOR reference-diff of roadtest_editor.cljc vs hand-migrated ui_editor.cljc). Triaged, most→least important:

[P1 ARCHITECTURAL — found by the MAYOR reference-diff, NOT self-reported] MIG-17 leads to a FORBIDDEN unmount pattern. The skill guides ':component-will-unmount -> effect cleanup that dispatches the lease-release'. But re-frame.ui's LEAKED-LISTENER LAW forbids dispatch from a disconnected view (a committed dispatcher rejects firing at disconnect). The hand-migrated reference REJECTS the whole approach: native re-frame.ui has NO dispatch-at-unmount, so the view owns no lease and the resource lifecycle RE-HOMES OUT of the view (to the resource owner / mutation tier). The skill must teach: there is no dispatch-at-unmount in native re-frame.ui; unmount domain-work moves OUT of the view, it is NOT preserved via an effect cleanup. The worker (skill-only) got this wrong AND thought it was right — the deepest gap.

[P1 SIGNATURE] effect's signature is undocumented. Worker guessed the React useEffect shape (setup returns cleanup) -> double-nested cleanup that COMPILES but SILENTLY never fires (a leak, no error). Real contract ((effect :connect body…), body's return is the cleanup) lives only in ui.cljc. Add effect's signature + worked example; surface the 'read ui.cljc' aside as a REQUIRED step for effect, not a not-shipped footnote.

[P2] MIG-17's mount/unmount taxonomy has no bucket for domain-work-on-unmount (subsumed by the P1 architectural fix — the answer is 're-home it, don't dispatch at unmount').
[P2] StrictMode idempotency (component-will-unmount once vs effect cleanup per-disconnect) — promote from footnote to named gotcha.

[P3] 'provably-literal :value' wording ambiguous — means 'the key appears literally (not via spread)', not 'value must be literal'; reword (controlled-input door).
[P3] Note: a single-file migration with out-of-file callers is PROVISIONAL until the caller mounts it through a compiled route component.

WHAT WORKED (keep): M-tier airtight for form views (MIG-01/02/04/05/06/14 textbook); the bare-symbol trap fired correctly on a real site; whole-view + closed-subtree + outward-bridge reasoning is strong. The skill carries the 80% cleanly; the gaps are all at the ONE non-hiccup construct (lifecycle/effect). Evidence: worker/skill-roadtest (reap after actioning).

title: Make epoch listener guidance frame-qualified, publication-shaped, and terminal-record accurate
description:
## Problem

The epoch listener is a publication stream, but current public/spec/tooling prose conflates event handling, ring storage, and callback publication. The precise lifecycle is:

1. A successfully-started handled event assembles and publishes one initial `:rf/epoch-record` at run-to-completion. It is retained in `epoch-history` only when the frame's configured history depth permits storage.
2. A dequeued event rejected before `:rf.event/run-start` (for example, no handler) produces no epoch record or callback. “One record per dequeued event” is therefore only a shorthand for ordinary handled events, not a universal law.
3. `:rf.epoch/db-replaced` and `:halted-depth` are nonordinary publications with no completed event run. They are ring-retained when depth permits; `:halted-depth` names the queued event that never ran.
4. `:halted-destroy` is different: it exists only when an already-dequeued event started and was interrupted by frame destruction. It is delivered to listeners and deliberately absent from history after destroy cleanup.
5. Render/sub-run/unmount backfill can publish a corrected record carrying the same identity. A callback is not an event clock.
6. The listener is process-global, while the public contract guarantees `:epoch-id` uniqueness only within one frame. Consumer identity is `[(:frame record) (:epoch-id record)]`; `:outcome` is record state, not identity.

Current consequences:

- `docs/api/re-frame.core.md` and `docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md` overpromise ring storage, misclassify destroy halt, and recommend bare-ID reconciliation.
- `docs/xray/api/runtime-seam.md` describes every history record as one per dequeued event, omitting db-replace/depth-halt entries and depth-zero storage behavior.
- `spec/API.md`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/Tool-Pair.md`, `docs/core/observability.md`, and the #6499-edited `spec/Privacy.md` still contain universal once-per-event assembly/callback claims. The Tool-Pair worked consumer performs accumulative work and can double-count a backfill publication.
- `tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md` uses bare identity and treats terminal destroy as synthetic/eventless; `tools/xray/testbeds/runner/core.cljs` promises once-per-event delivery.
- Public docstrings in `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_epoch.cljc`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc`, and `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs` retain event-only or universal cadence wording.
- `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md` and `migration/from-re-frame-v1/observability-logging-sweep.md` retain the callback-counting mental model for programmers and AI.

This is one documentation/consumer-contract defect. The Xray collector implementation is already safe: it carries `(:frame record)` and re-reads/replaces that frame's ring snapshot.

## Scope and proportional fix

Make one bounded prose/example pass over the named live surfaces. State ordinary handled-event assembly separately from conditional ring retention and listener publication; make consumer examples replace the latest publication under `[frame epoch-id]`; and describe no-record rejection, db-replace/depth-halt, destroy-halt, depth zero, and backfill only where the surface needs that distinction. Keep concise surfaces concise and put the lifecycle matrix in one canonical spec section.

Do not change runtime behavior, add listener dedupe, introduce validation/compatibility machinery, or build a prose checker. Do not rewrite narrowly-scoped test names that make no false universal claim.

## Ownership / deduplication

Closed `rf2-69fyr` / PR #6499 fixed the old per-drain language but left the lifecycle distinctions above incomplete and introduced some overbroad per-dequeued-event wording. Open `rf2-yiwag` separately owns only the Pair preload listener/streaming comments; leave those files to that bead. Closed `rf2-3fc89f.39` fixed Pair runtime attribution and independently proves why frame-qualified identity is required; this bead changes guidance only.
design: Use a small lifecycle matrix as the canonical formulation: handled event -> one initial publication, stored only when depth permits; rejected/no-run-start -> none; db-replaced and halted-depth -> nonordinary publications, stored when depth permits; halted-destroy -> already-started event, listener-only; backfill -> replacement publication with the same `[frame epoch-id]`. Consumer examples cache by `[(:frame record) (:epoch-id record)]`, replace the value, and inspect `:outcome` as state.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every named public/spec/tooling/AI surface distinguishes ordinary handled-event assembly, conditional ring retention, and listener publication; none claims universally that every dequeued event creates a stored record or exactly one callback.
2. Cross-frame consumer guidance uses `[frame epoch-id]`; `:outcome` is described as record state, not identity.
3. The Tool-Pair worked consumer is replacement/reconciliation-shaped, so same-ID backfill cannot double-count an epoch.
4. Rejected/no-run-start events, depth-zero publication, `:rf.epoch/db-replaced`, `:halted-depth`, and `:halted-destroy` are described with their real event/storage lifecycles at the canonical explanation; concise surfaces link or avoid overbroad claims.
5. The explicit inventory includes `docs/xray/api/runtime-seam.md`, `spec/Privacy.md`, the epoch/core/late-bind public docstrings, and Xray `install.cljs` as well as the original public/spec/tooling/AI sites.
6. No runtime/API/checker/compatibility work is added. `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `python -m mkdocs build --strict` pass.
7. `rf2-yiwag`'s Pair preload files remain outside this bead.
notes:
PR #6499 AUDIT INVENTORY ADDENDUM (rf2-jugsp): keep this as the same bounded prose/example correction, but explicitly include three authoritative surfaces the original inventory did not name:
- `docs/xray/api/runtime-seam.md` — its `get-epoch-history` description says each ring record is one per dequeued event, omitting stored `:rf.epoch/db-replaced` and `:halted-depth` records that have no completed event run.
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc` (`register-epoch-listener!` docstring) — “each assembled event epoch record” is still event-only callback guidance despite backfill republications and terminal/depth-zero listener-only delivery.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs` (`register-epoch-collector!` docstring) — describes the collector as firing on each event settle, omitting same-record backfill republication and nonordinary records.

These are the identical record-commit-versus-publication defect already owned here. Correct the wording alongside the named corpus; do not add runtime dedupe, new API, a checker, or another Bead.
PR #6499 correctness lens also falsified the shorthand “one stored record per dequeued event”: a no-handler/no-run-start dequeue produces no record, depth-zero records publish without storage, and halted-depth names a never-run queued event. title: Finish raw query identity on every frame-destroyed subscribe surface
description:
PR #6497 made the ordinary core subscribe and internal observation-port `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` records obey the ruled identity contract: a subscription query vector is public identity and egresses raw whenever `:op :subscribe` identifies the realm. The compiled re-frame.ui `(frame)` bundle still violates that same invariant on its stale `:subscribe` arm.

Current `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/frames.cljc` funnels dispatch, dispatch-sync, subscribe, and capture through `emit-and-throw-frame-destroyed!`, which replaces every non-nil payload with `:rf/redacted` before `error-emit` sees it. That remains correct for dispatched event payloads, but a subscribe query vector is identity under closed rf2-zwgqe and rf2-alk8a. The current UI regression test explicitly expects all three operation bodies to be redacted, proving this is live behavior rather than stale prose. It contradicts Spec 015's rule that query vectors ship verbatim on every query-vector-bearing slot and Spec 009's statement that `:subscribe`-realm frame-destroyed `:event` is raw; the same Spec 009 row and `FrameDestroyedTags` commentary still describe the UI arm as source-redacted.

Minimal correction: in the existing UI helper, pass the payload through unchanged only for `op = :subscribe`; keep source redaction for `:dispatch` / `:dispatch-sync` and nil for `:capture`. Split the existing UI regression expectations accordingly. Do not add a policy snapshot, new classifier, or new API.

Two small completeness pins belong in the same invariant pass. The separately modified observation-port branch is currently covered only for category/throw, so strengthen its existing destroyed-frame test to assert raw `:event`, `:op :subscribe`, and realm-exact (including anti-stealing/omit) source attribution. Correct the central `error_emit.cljc` architecture comments that still say core subs emitters omit `:op`; after #6497 only the ordinary router/dispatch path is op-absent. This is test/comment reconciliation around the same shipped rule, not a new framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- A stale re-frame.ui `(frame)` bundle `:subscribe` emits its query vector verbatim on the always-on `:event` slot with `:op :subscribe`; the thrown exception remains bounded to structural attribution.
- Stale bundle `:dispatch` and `:dispatch-sync` bodies remain source-redacted, and `:capture` remains payload-free.
- The existing UI reincarnation/elision test distinguishes subscribe identity from dispatch payload and pins both branches on JVM and CLJS where the suite already runs.
- An existing observation-port destroyed-frame test pins raw query identity, `:op :subscribe`, and realm-exact/anti-stealing source-coordinate behavior.
- Spec 009 and Spec-Schemas no longer claim the UI subscribe arm is source-redacted; central `error_emit.cljc` comments say only op-absent ordinary dispatch uses the legacy fallback.
- No new config, policy snapshot, classifier, API, or general-purpose checker is introduced; focused core/UI tests and relevant doc gates pass.
- The post-projection dev trace preserves a stale subscribe query vector verbatim even when an event registration shares the sub id and declares matching classification paths; dispatch counterpaths remain projected.

Minimal repair: skip bare-event registration projection only for `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` + `:op :subscribe`, and add one JVM/CLJS same-id event/sub collision regression with a dispatch counterpath. title: Align custom-element contract prose with the implemented law
description:
## Problem
PR #6475 changed the custom-element law from one canonical owner to a set of equal declarers and changed the dev/JVM authority path, but the normative and programmer-facing prose still teaches the old design. Spec 009 says a source always replaces its own row and calls evidence a sorted pair. `rules.cljc` still says every registration traverses `write-element!`, conflicts carry both anchors, and recovery should align both sources. In reality a source may replace only while it is the sole declarer; evidence is a sorted vector; dev/JVM decides in `ledger-state` and publishes its projection, while advanced production uses the direct `write-element!` barrier.

## Steps to Reproduce
Read `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` at the `:rf.error/custom-element-conflict` row and the architecture comment/docstrings around `write-element!` and `register-custom-element!`, then compare them with `admit` and the dev branch added by PR #6475. Register two equal declarations and change either source: the implementation rejects because another declarer remains, despite the spec's unconditional self-replacement statement. The dev branch calls `write-through-verdict` plus `publish!`, not `write-element!`.

## Consequence
This is programmer and AI-facing contract drift, not cosmetic prose. It gives the wrong HMR/REPL expectation and points future maintenance at the wrong atomicity/DCE seam. It also over-specifies evidence cardinality: staged reconciliation currently stops after a deterministic contradictory witness pair, whereas direct admission can name all equal incumbents. Exhaustive evidence has no known consumer and is not needed to fix the declaration.

## Bounded solution
Update authoritative `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, its `docs/spec/009-Instrumentation.md` mirror, and the relevant `rules.cljc` comments/docstrings/error text. State equal co-declaration and sole-declarer-only replacement; describe `:declarations` as a deterministic sorted vector containing actionable contradictory declarations without promising a fixed pair or exhaustive N; distinguish dev/JVM ledger authority from the production-direct barrier. Coordinate the same hot-zone edits with open decision `rf2-k1ouh`, which concerns error-channel classification. Add no runtime machinery, state, API, listener, schema, framework, or CI job.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 009 and its docs mirror state the actual equal-declarer and sole-replacement behavior.
- Evidence is documented as a deterministic actionable vector without a false pair or exhaustive-cardinality promise.
- `rules.cljc` identifies `ledger-state` as dev/JVM admission authority and `write-element!` as the advanced-production direct barrier.
- Programmer-facing recovery text works for any number of declaring sources.
- The edit is coordinated with `rf2-k1ouh` and introduces no new machinery.
- Runtime-law prose in Spec 009, the rules.cljc architecture comment, and the runtime conflict-test namespace states that one shared JS realm is keyed by tag; [build-id ns-sym] is declarer provenance, not a partition key.
- The runtime realm-wide rule is explicitly distinguished from the compile-time arm's per-build registry; existing cross-build tests remain the proof, with no new machinery.
notes:
PR #6513 (worker/conflict-evidence-xdpje). Reconciled spec/009 :rf.error/custom-element-conflict row + rules.cljc comments/docstrings/error-text to the #6475 set-of-declarers law: SET of equal declarers (not one canonical owner), sole-declarer-only replacement, :declarations as a deterministic sorted vector (no false pair / no exhaustive-N), ledger-state = dev/JVM admission authority vs write-element! = advanced-production barrier, N-declarer recovery text. Prose-only: no runtime/classification/schema change. docs/spec/009 is a gitignored CI-generated cp mirror (edited source only). Gates green: core 2097t/0f, test:cljs 10326t/0f, ui-JVM conflict 1001t/0f, mkdocs --strict, check_doc_slugs, check_keyword_catalogue_drift. Not merged; awaiting mayor merge/close.
PR #6513 AUDIT RESIDUAL (completeness/correctness/implementation quality, source verified): the central phrase 'For a given [build-id tag]' still teaches false runtime build isolation in rules.cljc:1010, Spec 009's :rf.error/custom-element-conflict row, and the runtime conflict-test namespace docstring. Runtime admit indexes the shared aggregate by tag alone; build id is only part of declarer provenance [build-id ns-sym]. The existing cross-build runtime test proves :app and :lib conflict on a differing manifest in one JS realm, while the compile-time test correctly permits different manifests in different builds. Minimal fix is prose-only in those three teaching surfaces, explicitly separating realm-wide runtime scope from per-build compile scope. No code, API, schema, new test, registry abstraction, or isolation machinery. Reopened this exact owner rather than creating a duplicate.
PR #6527 (folded with rf2-k1ouh, same 009 row + rules.cljc surface). RESIDUAL FIXED (three-outcome: (a) genuinely stale). The #6513 set-of-declarers reconciliation was correct, but the phrase 'For a given [build-id tag]' taught false per-build runtime isolation in three teaching surfaces. VERIFIED against code: runtime admit (rules.cljc ~1123) indexes agg by TAG; aggregate (~1190) folds ALL [build-id ns-sym] sources into one tag-keyed map; the two-builds-contradicting-one-tag-conflict-with-both-build-anchors test proves :app and :lib build-ids contradict on one tag in one realm. So [build-id ns-sym] is DECLARER PROVENANCE, not a partition key. Fixed prose-only in rules.cljc law comment (~1010), spec/009 :rf.error/custom-element-conflict row, and runtime conflict-test ns docstring -- each now separates realm-wide runtime scope from the compile arm's per-build registry. Changed NO law logic, NO test logic. Gates green (see rf2-k1ouh). NOT merged.
AUDIT OF #6527 (rf2-hpmeq, 2026-07-20): REOPENED for a material scope correction. #6527 replaced the false `[build-id tag]` runtime partition with the opposite overclaim: “one shared registry across the JS realm.” Current `rules.cljc` explicitly defines the isolation unit as ONE loaded `re-frame.ui.rules` copy / CLJS root. Independently compiled bundle copies can coexist in the same realm and remain isolated by construction; only sources/build ids sharing the same loaded runtime copy share its namespace-local `defonce custom-elements` atom.

The cross-build runtime test passes `:app` and `:lib` provenance through one loaded copy, so it proves build-id is not a partition key WITHIN that copy; it does not prove cross-bundle realm sharing. Correct the three #6527 teaching sites (`rules.cljc` law comment, runtime conflict-test namespace/comment, Spec 009 row) to: within one loaded rules runtime / CLJS root, the aggregate is keyed by tag and `[build-id ns-sym]` is provenance; separate runtime copies are isolated; the compile arm remains separately per-build. No registry bridge, realm singleton, runtime detection, new API, or new fixture framework.

The set-of-equal-declarers law, sole-declarer replacement, atomic rejection, evidence vector, and dev/JVM-vs-production authority split remain correct. Focused UI conflict tests 33/161 green; required PR checks green.

title: Derive the mounted proof-pack roster from the real library
description:
PR #6459 adds a mounted browser suite for all six current proof-pack views and names its final test `every-library-view-is-rendered-somewhere-in-this-namespace`. The test comment explicitly says that adding a seventh library view arms the test, but its only roster assertion is `(= 6 (count [lib/controlled-input ... lib/inline-popover]))`: both the expected count and the referenced vars are hand-maintained in the test. A new `defview` in `library.cljs` does not affect either side.

The fresh browser build completed 943 files / 259 compiled / 0 warnings, and the whole suite remained green: 495 tests / 2765 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors. Thus the suite can regress to the exact condition #6459 was intended to prevent—a shipped proof-pack view rendered nowhere—while its roster-completeness assertion stays green.

Keep the correction small and source-derived. `check-ui-facade-isolation.cjs` already derives the complete defview/sentinel roster from `library.cljs`; extend that existing authority (or an equally direct existing checker seam) to compare the derived roster with the mounted suite's explicitly covered selectors/views. A seventh library view must fail until it is mounted and exercised. Do not add a public/runtime view registry, generated CLJS namespace, new Shadow build, new CI job, or generalized source-analysis framework.

title: op-nil ordinary-subscribe frame-destroyed egress — RULED Option A: stamp :op :subscribe, :event raw (see DECISION note)
description:
SPLIT OFF rf2-px0i9 (#6467). rf2-px0i9 fixed the coincidental-path-match identity mutation on a LIVE frame for sub query vectors on both error egress routes. RESIDUAL, out of that bead's scope by its own STOP-and-report fence:

An ORDINARY address-directed subscribe to a MISSING/DESTROYED frame emits :rf.error/frame-destroyed with the raw query vector and :op nil (subs/emit-frame-destroyed-recovery! 2-arity + the nil-expected-incarnation arm at subs.cljc ~1607; observation/throw-frame-destroyed!). Because the frame is UNRESOLVABLE, elide-wire-value fails closed to :rf/redacted (rf2-t55hxg.18, a DIFFERENT mechanism than the coincidental-path match). Per rf2-zwgqe the query vector is IDENTITY and should egress verbatim even here; per rf2-t55hxg.18 an unresolved-frame :event fails closed to avoid an empty-policy leak.

This is a genuine DECISION TENSION (rf2-t55hxg.18 vs rf2-zwgqe), NOT a clear fix:
 - Making it raw requires the emitter to carry the :subscribe realm on the op-nil ordinary path, which REVERSES rf2-a2x2w's deliberate op-omission in subs.cljc (outside the error_emit surface) and changes the pinned assertions frame-destroyed-subscribe-listener-survives-prod / listener-fires-on-frame-destroyed-subscribe (currently assert :rf/redacted).
 - Or rule that query-vector IDENTITY is exempt from the unresolved-frame fail-closed on the error :event slot (a rf2-t55hxg.18 amendment).

NEEDS A RULING before any code. Enumerated sites: subs.cljc emit-frame-destroyed-recovery! (2-arity + 1607 nil arm); observation.cljc throw-frame-destroyed! (814, always unresolvable).
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 22:20 AUSEST)

RULING: Option A — RAW. Query-vector identity (rf2-zwgqe, Spec 015 "A subscription's query vector is identity, and it egresses raw") governs the always-on error :event slot even under an unresolvable frame. The rf2-t55hxg.18 fail-closed protects policy-walked VALUE slots and does not apply to identity slots, which never consult frame policy. Stamp the ratified public :op :subscribe at both op-nil subscribe-realm frame-destroyed emit sites so the existing #6467 discriminator routes :event verbatim on both egress routes. Options B (spec carve-out enshrining an access-path-dependent asymmetry) and C (private realm channel, violates a2x2w's no-hidden-steering-slots criterion) are REJECTED.

EMITTER EDITS (2 source files; error_emit.cljc UNTOUCHED — raw-identity-query-vector-event? already routes frame-destroyed raw when :op is :subscribe):
1. implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc — emit-frame-destroyed-recovery! (defn ~934): emit :op :subscribe UNCONDITIONALLY; collapse the 2-arity nil arm (the fn is subscribe-realm by construction — its only two runtime call sites are ~1040, which already passes :subscribe, and ~1607-1608). At ~1607-1608 delete the conditional (when (some? expected-incarnation) :subscribe) — always :subscribe. Rewrite the docstring paragraph (~953-958) that documents the nil legacy-fallback arm.

title: Reclassify custom-element-conflict instead of fabricating always-on fan-out
description:
## Confirmed contract mismatch

PR #6440 classifies `:rf.error/custom-element-conflict` as `always-on`, but the real `re-frame.ui.rules` site calls only `error/throw-error!`. That helper builds and throws `ex-info`; it does not fan a record through the error-emit substrate. A registered `:errors` listener receives zero records when the conflict fires. The core conformance suite hides this by adding the id to its literal and calling `dispatch-on-error!` synthetically, even though its own test says every always-on category must be exercised through its real listener axis.

This contradicts Spec 009's explicit meanings:

- `always-on` means real production-surviving `:errors` listener fan-out.
- A thrown registration rejection is diagnostic-channel for catalogue purposes and is not delivered to that listener.
- Promotion requires all three legs. This category is production-reachable, but the caller immediately observes the throw and fixes the declaration at its call site; no suppressed state or silent compounding failure remains because the atomic barrier retains last-known-good.

The runtime law surviving `:advanced` is necessary and already proven by the UI production-elision fixture. That is independent of observability-channel classification.

## Recommended bounded correction

Reclassify the Spec 009 row as `diagnostic`, remove the id and synthetic special-case prose from the core always-on exercise literal, and correct `rules.cljc` comments that call a bare throw an always-on seam. Keep the unconditional production write barrier, canonical thrown id/evidence, and the real advanced-production elision proof unchanged.

Do not add an emitter, listener route, frame/sink plumbing, schema, hook, or new test job merely to justify the mistaken label.
acceptance_criteria:
- The `dispatch-on-error!` docstring no longer claims every production-reachable runtime error must fan through that helper or otherwise be silent; it accurately scopes the helper to categories promoted onto the always-on listener axis.
- Spec 009's channel/promotion and production-observability summary statements distinguish production reachability from listener promotion: caller-observed pure throws can be production-reachable while remaining diagnostic-channel.
- The `:rf.error/custom-element-conflict` row, always-on set, unconditional throw, atomic retention, and advanced-production proof remain unchanged.
- Prose-only: no emitter/listener/schema/hook/API/test-job/framework change.
notes:
⚠️ SEQUENCED behind the u25hr+7uyl9 rules.cljc cluster (dispatched now). k1ouh RECLASSIFIES :rf.error/custom-element-conflict from always-on — which touches spec/009 (HOT-ZONE) AND the core exercise literal in always_on_axis_conformance_cljs_test.cljc (the THIRD co-edit arm that red-lit #6440). It also touches rules.cljc, which the u25hr/7uyl9 cluster holds. Two reasons to sequence: (1) same rules.cljc surface as the live cluster; (2) removing an id from always-on must reconcile the catalogue row + Spec-Schemas + the core exercise literal together, and the core conformance suite parses that catalogue — a bungled reclassification reds core (exactly #6440's failure). Dispatch after the u25hr/7uyl9 PR merges, as a careful solo change. ⚠️ Verify the CLAIM first: does the real re-frame.ui.rules emit path make this diagnostic-not-always-on? If the runtime genuinely only throws it at a dev/compile boundary, reclassify; if it IS a production-survivable throw (which #6440's whole point was — the direct write path survives :advanced), then the catalogue is RIGHT and k1ouh's premise is wrong — STOP and report. This is a verify-which-is-wrong bead, not a mechanical reclassify.
VERDICT (2026-07-19 21:51 AUSEST, ce-prodbehav-7hyzr worker): k1ouh's PREMISE IS CORRECT — the always-on classification IS inconsistent with Spec 009's own definitions. BUT this reverses a deliberate .143 design decision and is a design fork (reclassify vs make-it-fan-out), touching HOT-ZONE spec/009 — so REPORT for Mike's ruling; did NOT unilaterally execute the co-edit. No code change.

The mayor-brief decision rule ("production-survivable throw => always-on correct => STOP") CONFLATES TWO INDEPENDENT AXES: (1) does the throw survive :advanced? YES. (2) does the error FAN A RECORD to the error-emit listener (surface #4)? NO. Spec 009 defines always-on on BOTH conjunctively.

Factual premise CONFIRMED:
- rules.cljc throw-element-conflict! calls error/throw-error! (error.cljc:127) = a PURE (throw (ex-info ...)). It does NOT call dispatch-on-error! / emit-error-both! / any error-emit fan-out. A registered :errors listener receives ZERO records when the conflict fires.
- Spec 009 always-on definition (line ~1910): "the production-survivable always-on error-emit axis (surface #4)... fanning a tight record to registered error shippers."
- Spec 009 diagnostic definition (same block): "A `thrown ex-info` registration rejection (the 'Surfaced as a thrown ex-info' rows) is diagnostic-channel for catalogue purposes — it is not delivered to the error-emit listener." + "every always-on category is exercised through the error-emit listener in at least one test (so promotion is real, not documentary)."

- custom-element-conflict is that exact shape (production-reachable pure throw, no fan-out) — yet classified always-on. It is the ONLY thrown-ex-info row marked always-on, and the ONLY always-on category driven SYNTHETICALLY in the exercise test.
- always_on_axis_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:229-250 ADMITS this: "It is a THROWN ex-info ... NOT an error-emit fan-out — always-on means production-survivable ... this leg drives the category through the per-event :else axis (dispatch-on-error!) SYNTHETICALLY." (matching the sibling throwing surfaces) — arguably better serves .143's intent that the conflict reach production off-box error shippers; k1ouh forbids E but a designer may prefer it. DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 23:41 AUSEST)

title: check_adapter_disposition.py runs with zero classifier coverage — editing the files it pins does not fire it
description:
FOUND by the rf2-rf7gu worker (#6455) while fixing the sibling gap in report-changed-surfaces.sh. SAME BUG CLASS, DIFFERENT GUARD — and closing it needs a scope decision, so it was deliberately NOT actioned.

THE GAP: scripts/check_adapter_disposition.py runs in the synthesis-docs CI job but has ZERO classifier coverage in .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh. Its ACTIVE_AUTHORITIES roster reaches OUTSIDE the synthesis tree:
  docs/EP/EP-0030-the-compiled-view-substrate-program.md
  spec/004-Views.md
  implementation/README.md
  skills/re-frame2-implementor/...
⚠️ So a PR editing any of those does NOT fire the guard that pins them. The guard exists precisely to stop adapter-disposition drift (Reagent/UIx/reagent-slim first-class; only Helix leaves at S7) — and the highest-traffic files it protects are outside its trigger.

WHY IT WAS NOT ACTIONED: closing it means classifying docs/EP/** and spec/** as synthesis_docs in report-changed-surfaces.sh — well beyond what rf2-rf7gu authorised, and a materially broader CI trigger surface (those are two of the busiest trees in the repo; every spec/EP PR would newly fire the synthesis-docs job). ⚠️ THAT IS A SCOPE/COST DECISION FOR MIKE, not a determinable fix.

OPTIONS (for the ruling):
  (a) Classify docs/EP/** + spec/** as synthesis_docs — closes the gap, but widens the trigger to two high-traffic trees and lengthens most PRs CI.
  (b) Give check_adapter_disposition.py its OWN narrow classifier keyed to its ACTIVE_AUTHORITIES roster, so only those specific files fire it — narrower, but the roster is a hardcoded list that will drift from the classifier (the exact rf2-rf7gu defect, reintroduced one level down).
  (c) Derive the classifier FROM the roster at CI time so they cannot drift — most robust, most machinery; weigh against the pre-alpha no-gold-plating stance.
  (d) Accept and document, per the rf2-clgot change-time-ratchet precedent: no trigger change; the obligation moves to review time for PRs touching ACTIVE_AUTHORITIES files.

⚠️ NOTE the precedent: rf2-clgot ruled option (c)-equivalent for the always-on axis — accept the gap, write a change-time ratchet into TESTING.md rather than build blanket machinery. That may be the cheapest answer here too.
⚠️ WHEN ACTIONED: whatever the choice, add red-before arms to implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs (currently 173 after #6455) proving the newly-covered paths fire and unrelated paths do NOT — write the arms FIRST and run them against unfixed source, as #6455 did. A trigger-path fix whose test passes before the fix proves nothing.
Cross-ref rf2-rf7gu (#6455, the sibling gap, fixed), rf2-d9v3n (#6127, which expanded SYNTHESIS_ROOTS and created the original drift), rf2-clgot (the accept-and-ratchet precedent), rf2-cwhsh (#6404, the adapter-disposition corrections this guard protects).
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 18:34 AUSEST)

RULED: fix now, option (e) — a refinement beyond the enumerated (a)-(d): make the guard UNCONDITIONAL by moving it out of the surface-gated synthesis-docs job into the always-on verify-readme-links job. Do NOT touch the classifier at all. This is the dossier's "Codex Recommendation", chosen over the dossier's primary (c') because running a sub-second, stdlib-only, fixed-inventory guard on every PR dissolves the roster<->classifier synchronization problem entirely, whereas (c') adds a second copy of the roster plus a cross-language regex ratchet whose only job is policing that duplication — machinery the posture (no over-engineering) says not to build when zero-list is available. Conditional execution keyed to a diff classifier is a category mismatch for guards that scan a fixed inventory rather than the diff; that mismatch is what produced this bug class three times in one week (rf2-d9v3n, rf2-rf7gu, this bead). Coverage under (e) is total and permanent: every roster file, every FUTURE roster addition (the guard docstring already flags release.yml pending via rf2-nojiwy), and every edit to the guard itself are covered automatically, at ~1s per PR inside a job that already checks out the repo and provisions Python. Cheaper than (c') (~8 vs ~27 runner-min/week) and stronger than (a)/(b)/(c) combined; (d) accept-and-document is rejected on the same grounds as the rf2-rf7gu fix-now ruling for this job's sibling guard (no compensating witness; peak churn window; five live drift sites found in-roster within a day of the guard shipping).

EXACT FIX SCOPE (self-contained; the dossier is deleted):

title: Honor raw query-vector identity on production sub-error egress
description:
PR #6441 deliberately rules subscription query vectors to be raw identity on every query-vector-bearing surface, with only the existing schema-validation-failure whole-slot scrub retained as a narrower exception. The production always-on sub-error path does not currently honor that contract.

CONCRETE REPRODUCTION

1. Create a live frame.
2. Install a valid durable app-db sensitivity declaration at concrete path `[1]` through `elision/apply-classification-effects`.
3. Emit `:rf.error/sub-exception` with query vector `[:patient/record "SECRET"]` through `error-emit/dispatch-on-error!`.
4. The registered production error listener receives:

    {:error :rf.error/sub-exception
     :event [:patient/record :rf/redacted]
     :event-id :patient/record
     :frame :probe}

Directly, `elision/elide-wire-value` produces the same `[:patient/record :rf/redacted]` result. This is expected from the generic walker: concrete integer paths are valid and intentionally match vector coordinates (`elision_test.clj` pins this for position-precise app-db elision).

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT

`error-emit/dispatch-on-error!` currently runs every `event` argument through the frame's durable app-db elision registry. For event errors that is payload hygiene. For sub errors the argument is not app-db or an event; it is the subscription query vector. A coincidentally matching app-db path therefore mutates identity at egress, contradicting #6441 / rf2-zwgqe's explicit ruling that the always-on error `:query-v` / `:event` slots carry query identity verbatim. The closed decision note also incorrectly reasoned that an app-db path could not match a query vector; concrete integer paths prove otherwise.

SCOPE / POSTURE

Keep this narrow. Do NOT add a query-argument classification axis, blanket scrubbing, taint tracking, or new privacy policy. The required behavior is the already-ruled ergonomic contract: subscription identity remains raw; ordinary dispatched events keep their existing elision. Enumerate the production query-vector-as-`:event` callers, including realm-attributed `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` subscription cases, so the fix does not depend only on a category-name prefix. Preserve the separate schema-validation-failure scrub exactly as-is.

Also inspect the frame-owned observability sink route, which receives the raw argument after corpus-wide listener fan-out and may project `:event` independently; the identity contract must be consistent on every production error egress promised by #6441.
notes: PR #6467 (worker/subvec-identity-px0i9). Fix in error_emit.cljc (corpus route) + observability.cljc/projection.cljc (frame-owned sink route): structural raw-identity-query-vector-event? discriminator (query-vector-event-categories superset + frame-destroyed :op :subscribe), skips app-db elision for a sub query-vector :event on BOTH routes. FOUND-vs-NAMED: reading every emit site surfaced 2 query-vector categories NOT in sub-error-categories — :rf.error/read-after-release + :rf.error/observation-retry-exhausted (the latter fires on a LIVE frame). Residual op-nil ordinary-subscribe fail-closed case (rf2-t55hxg.18 vs rf2-zwgqe tension) split to rf2-alk8a — needs a ruling. Gates all green (JVM core 2093, CLJS 10264, elision, browser-prod-elision 113, catalogue-drift). No spec/009 touch, no new error id.

title: Keep data-rf-root out of the emit seam root-identity boundary
description:
## Problem

PR #6436 added a normative `emit-ui-tree` boundary in `spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md`. Its "No container, no identity" bullet groups "the root marker attribute" with root-id, identifier-prefix, and element locator as root identity that is settled before the seam and stamped around its output.

That is false for the concrete marker this contract refers to. `spec/011-SSR.md` §Root Manifest v1 pins `data-rf-root` as a **bare discriminator on the immediately-adjacent manifest `<script>`**, explicitly carrying "no value, no identity". `re-frame.ssr.manifest/script-html` implements that rule, and the manifest tests assert the marker is bare. The tree-to-HTML seam should indeed stay free of identity/page assembly, but calling the marker identity obscures which layer emits it and invites an implementer to stamp it on the root container or emitted tree.

## Required correction

In the single 004B boundary bullet, keep root-id, identifier-prefix, and element locator outside `emit-ui-tree` as page/root assembly facts. Describe `data-rf-root` separately as the bare manifest-script discriminator emitted by the page assembler next to the container, and link the owning Spec 011 wire-form section. Do not change the marker spelling, add identity to it, alter the seam signature, or expand into the remaining S5 page-assembly work.

## Evidence

- `spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:455-459` — newly added conflicting classification.
- `spec/011-SSR.md:471-487` and resolved decision at `:1670-1677` — marker is bare, on the manifest script, and carries no identity.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/manifest.cljc` — `script-html` owns the wire element.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/root_manifest_cljs_test.cljc:253-267,699-701` — exact bare-marker and spelling pins.

This is the sole new correctness finding from the PR #6436 audit. The fingerprint algorithm/encoding and other page-assembly residue are already owned by the live S5 authority graph (`rf2-vxgfnd.97`, `rf2-vxgfnd.97.1`, and the delivered/residual notes on `rf2-vxgfnd.97.2`); no duplicate is filed for them.
acceptance_criteria: 004B no longer classifies `data-rf-root` as identity or suggests the emit seam stamps it; it names the marker's adjacent manifest-script placement and Spec 011 ownership; the edit remains confined to this boundary correction; doc slug and strict MkDocs gates pass.

Doc-only correction; premise verified: code was already correct (script-html emits bare marker; #6448's ui_tree.cljc carries no root identity). Sites 1 found / 1 named. title: Align the EP process and template with the PEP structure established by #6433
description:
## Current contradiction

PR #6433 deliberately puts EP-0030..EP-0035 into one PEP-style structure: Abstract → Motivation → Specification (with scope and guide impact) → Rationale → Backwards Compatibility → Resolved Decisions → Open Issues → References. The PR explicitly names EP-0009/template alignment as follow-up.

Current authoring authorities still prescribe a different shape. `docs/EP/EP-0009-the-ep-process.md` §Document conventions names Goals/Non-Goals, Relationships, Bead Plan / Reference Implementation, and Recommendation as standard top-level sections; `docs/EP/EP-template.md` emits exactly those headings and has no References or standard Resolved Decisions position. A programmer or agent following the template therefore cannot produce the corpus shape #6433 now presents as the improved standard.

## Bounded resolution

Make the two authoring authorities state one forward-looking structure. Recommended: adopt #6433's compact PEP shape for new and materially revised EPs, folding goals/non-goals into Specification scope, dependencies/provenance into References, implementation tracking into Beads, and landed rulings into Resolved Decisions. Preserve EP-0009 lifecycle/durability semantics, including rf2-r7ahi's freeze-meaning-not-bytes rule. If the six UI EPs are intentionally exceptional instead, say that explicitly in both authorities rather than leaving contradictory instructions.

Do not rewrite older EPs, manufacture missing sections, add a section-order checker, or build a documentation framework. This is two small authoring-document edits aimed at low-friction human/AI ergonomics.

## Dedupe

Fresh all-live-Bead census before filing: 52 open/in-progress. Exact searches for EP-0009, EP-template, template alignment, document conventions, PEP standard/PEP-standard, and section names found no owner. rf2-r7ahi owns how settled meaning is corrected; rf2-hgwpq owns residual EP-0009 ledger/status cleanup. Neither owns the section-structure contradiction.
acceptance_criteria:
- `docs/EP/EP-0009-the-ep-process.md` and `docs/EP/EP-template.md` prescribe the same forward-looking top-level structure and explain where scope, relationships/provenance, implementation tracking, resolved rulings, and recommendation material live.
- The choice is explicit: either the #6433 PEP shape becomes the authoring default or the six-EP exception is documented in both authorities.

title: Align reagent-slim invalid-hiccup-head payload with the widened catalogue contract
description:
## Problem
PR #6431 widened Spec 009's `:rf.error/invalid-hiccup-head` catalogue row so the unrecognised-reserved-head arm is also thrown client-side by reagent-slim, while retaining the promised payload fields `:head`, `:element` "(both arms)". The existing JVM/server arm supplies both fields, but `reagent2.impl.template/reject-reserved-rf-head!` receives only `head` and emits ex-data with `:head` but no `:element`. The source Bead rf2-01zvu explicitly warned that the catalogue conformance test does not validate the tags column, and #6431's new tests assert `:head` but not `:element`, so all gates remain green while the newly widened contract is false.

Consequence: a diagnostic consumer following Spec 009 can show the complete offending hiccup vector for server failures but receives nil for the same category/recovery on reagent-slim. That is avoidable cross-host friction in a structured error API.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Render `[:rf/suspense-boundry {:id 1}]` through `reagent2.impl.template/as-element` and catch the `ExceptionInfo`.
2. Inspect `(ex-data ex)`: it contains `:rf.error/id`, `:head`, `:where`, `:reason`, and `:recovery`, but no `:element`.
3. Compare Spec 009's `:rf.error/invalid-hiccup-head` row, which promises `:head`, `:element` for both arms, and the server arm in `re-frame.ssr.emit/reject-reserved-rf-hiccup-head!`, which supplies both.

## Bounded Resolution
Prefer passing the original hiccup vector to the cache-miss reject and adding `:element` to the ex-data, with one direct assertion. If the client payload is intentionally narrower, change the catalogue row to state the per-emitter difference instead. Do not introduce a new error id, builder dependency, or diagnostic framework.
acceptance_criteria: For reagent-slim's `:rf.error/invalid-hiccup-head` reserved-head arm, runtime ex-data and Spec 009 agree about every promised payload field. A direct client test asserts the chosen shape (including `:element` if the cross-host shape remains canonical), the existing cache-collision and production-survival rows remain green, and bundle isolation remains intact.

title: Simplify G-13 containment proof; retire the private-source lexer
description: PR #6388 correctly added the missing post-commit witness, and its runtime checks now prove every measured cycle advances app-db by exactly queued-writes. title: a11y drop-frame-state! is never called in production
description:

CONSEQUENCE: a11y state for a destroyed variant frame is never reclaimed. `violations-by-frame` and `run-state` accumulate an entry per frame ever scanned, for the life of the page. The violations bag holds raw axe-core JS violation objects, each retaining DOM node references via :nodes/:target — so this also retains detached DOM for every scanned-then-destroyed variant.

NOTE the interaction with rf2-2amkm: the supersession fence now makes teardown SAFE (a settlement after drop-frame-state! refuses rather than resurrecting the frame — measured, 10/10). But safe-when-called is not called. Wiring the teardown is what makes the frame-destroyed path actually reclaim.

SCOPE: find the canvas/shell teardown seam that destroys a variant frame and call drop-frame-state! from it (the docstring names the intended caller). Check whether ui/chrome-a11y needs anything — it does not: singleton state, no per-frame accumulation.

Surface: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/ (+ wherever variant-frame teardown lives). Test: assert the per-frame slots are gone after a variant frame is destroyed.
