title: Story a11y run-state mutations are unfenced in .then callbacks
description:
FOUND by the rf2-6pfpt worker (#6405), named not fixed — outside its scope fence.

THE SITES: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/a11y.cljs (run-axe!) and chrome_a11y.cljs both mutate `run-state` and `violations-by-frame` inside `.then` callbacks with NO frame-existence check and NO supersession check.

⚠️ WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC — the exact failure #6405 measured on the sibling path: under teardown the unfenced callback DOES NOT THROW on CLJS, because (inc nil) is 1. It RESURRECTS a phantom run-state entry. That entry carries no :run-token, and the loop guard only fires when a token is PRESENT, so the resurrected run was never aborted and ran on to :status :pass FOR A FRAME THAT WAS GONE. A fabricated green, not a hang, not a crash. Assume the same shape here until measured otherwise.

METHOD THAT WORKED ON #6405, REUSE IT:
  - Thread the existing run token (run! already mints one per run, stamps it as :run-token, and passes it to run-loop!). The token was already conveyed correctly on the sibling path — what was missing was the COMPARISON on the settled-Promise path: record-result! ran first, the check after, so the mutation sat on the far side of the fence.
  - Use a VALUE fence compared against the live slot, NOT a ^:dynamic Var or ThreadLocal. This is the rf2-vxgfnd.171 situation INVERTED: the hazard is a run OUTLIVING its claim, not a claim failing to reach a child, so a conveyed mechanism would agree with the callback by construction. Keep check + mutation in ONE synchronous turn so nothing can take the slot between them.
  - Do NOT pin execution order — re-enter the loop unconditionally and let its own stale branch settle via the existing abort path. One abort decision, not a second copy.
  - ⚠️ Beware a BOUNDS check masquerading as an identity check: #6405 found the stepper guard was a size test that declines while :results is short and then PERMITS the clobber once a new cursor grows back past the index. It now fences on object identity (identical?, not =). Identity was chosen over a generation counter because stepper-step-back! pops only the last step, so a session-level generation would be actively WRONG for an amendment still owed at an earlier index.

⚠️ MEASURE, DO NOT REASON. #6405 ran 10 trials reverted (10/10 RED, 11 failures each, identical failure set) and 10 applied (10/10 GREEN), after converting the intermittent race into a deterministic test — a real js/Promise settles on a microtask the test cannot interleave against, which is what makes this class flaky in the wild.
⚠️ PROVE THE SEQUENCE, not just the cases: ADMIT -> REFUSE -> ADMIT again -> REFUSE again, in one process. A guard carrying state can pass every single-transition test and still be broken (the ai/ ratchet was).
⚠️ VACUITY-PROBE THE GATE: the CLJS runner prints no per-namespace headers, so a green total does NOT prove your namespace ran. Flip an assertion, confirm the full gate reds naming your probe, then restore.

GATES: cd tools/story && clojure -M:test (~1836 tests) + npm run test:cljs (~10140). Never pipe a gate through tail/head. Use TEST COUNTS not assertion totals; what matters absolutely is non-zero — a bare clojure -M:test -n <ns> from implementation/ silently runs 0 tests and READS AS GREEN.

ALSO NAMED, DELIBERATELY LEFT by #6405: runner-events/run-step! settle callback emits an unfenced emit-trace! for an abandoned stepper session. It judged this acceptable — a public late-bound one-shot executor with no session identity, whose RECORDED VERDICT is fenced caller-side. Re-verify that judgement rather than inheriting it.
notes:
DELIVERED — PR #6410 (worker/story-a11y-fence-2amkm).

MEASURED FAILURE MODE (both sites): SILENT RESURRECTION, not a throw. Fence removed, 10/10 trials RED with 19 failures and **0 errors** — nothing throws. `(swap! run-state assoc frame-id :done)` over a dissoc'd map resurrects the entry; `status-for` then reads :done for a frame that is gone, and the resurrected violations-by-frame entry is what browser/register-a11y-reader! serves to :rf.assert/a11y. Fabricated green, exactly the shape the bead predicted from #6405.

MECHANISM: per-run token minted by run-axe!, stamped INTO the run-state slot, compared with identical? against the live slot at every post-await mutation (check + mutation in one synchronous turn). Value fence, not conveyed — the hazard is a run outliving its claim, so a conveyed binding would agree with the callback by construction. Token lives IN the slot so existence and identity are ONE question: every present/future clearing path revokes the claim by construction, no side atom to keep in step.

EXISTING GUARD AUDIT: there was NO guard at either site — every post-await mutation was unconditional, including the .catch's :error write (also fenced now). So no bounds-check-in-disguise to unmask, unlike #6405's stepper.

TRIALS: 10/10 RED reverted (identical failure set, single md5), 10/10 GREEN applied. Deterministic — settlement placed by the test via the fake axe's synchronously-invoked run; assertions chain off run-axe!'s tail promise and off a signal fired by the second run's scan. No microtask counting.

SEQUENCE PROOF per fence: ADMIT -> REFUSE -> ADMIT -> REFUSE, four transitions on one slot in one process (the-fence-does-not-latch, the-chrome-fence-does-not-latch). Both red with the fence removed.

VACUITY PROBE: flipped assertion -> full npm run test:cljs exit 1 with VACUITY-PROBE-rf2-2amkm as the SOLE failure. Namespace confirmed live in the gate. Restored.

EXECUTION ORDER NOT PINNED: one predicate at each mutation point, chain otherwise untouched, every run still settles its own tail promise. A superseded run additionally declines to SCAN (nothing to learn about a torn-down tree).

run-step! VERDICT: UPHELD, left unfenced — re-verified on independently checked grounds, not inherited. emit-trace! mutates no verdict slot; every trace listener under tools/story/src was checked and none consumes :rf.story.play/step (the only verdict-bearing one captures :rf.error/handler-exception); and the content is TRUTHFUL-but-late (the step really ran and really produced that result), categorically unlike the a11y sites which fabricate a verdict about a surface that no longer exists. Fencing it would mean inventing session identity for a public one-shot executor whose recorded verdict is already fenced caller-side.

GATES: npm run test:cljs 10180 tests / 0 failures / exit 0; tools/story clojure -M:test 1836 tests / 0 failures / exit 0. Both re-run after final commit.

description:

title: Identify what advances a pending ViewCell batch on a second same-stack dispatch-sync
description:
## Observation (measured, PR #6393)

While pinning the rf2-vxgfnd.166 host-checkpoint contract on the mounted React 19 path, a real-browser measurement produced this sequence on the watchable `ui/adapter`:

```
base                : {:rev 0, :body-runs 1, :root-commits 1}
after dispatch-sync : {:rev 0, :dirty true, :pending 1, :body-runs 1}   <- drain 1 COMPLETE
after dispatch-sync : {:rev 1, :dirty true, :pending 1, :body-runs 1}   <- drain 2
```

Drain 1 behaves exactly as the ruled contract describes: the drain runs to completion and the pending window stays open (revision unmoved, cell still dirty). That is the guarantee PR #6393 asserts, and it is green.

The open question is drain 2. Between the two logs the revision advanced 0 → 1 while `body-runs` stayed at 1, so React did not re-render — meaning the advance came from a scheduler flush (phase 1 advances the revision; phase 2 notifies), not from `commit!` step 8. Something inside the second `dispatch-sync` flushed the first drain's pending mark, after which drain 2's own movement re-marked the cell.

A microtask cannot have run between two synchronous statements in one task, so this is a synchronous flush on the second drain's path.

## What was ruled out

- `flush-render!` — an explicit Tool-Pair/MCP surface; nothing in core or the router invokes it automatically.
- `re-frame.ui.events/dispatch-committed!` → `reactive/flush-frame!` — that is the DOM callback sync door, not `rf/dispatch-sync`.
- A late-bound core→UI flush hook — none exists; `:live-frame/flush-projection!` is the router's only late-bound flush and is a live-frame projection, not a UI-scheduler seam.
- The armed microtask from drain 1 firing early — impossible mid-stack.

## Why it matters, and why it is not urgent

The ruled contract says several drains before one checkpoint MAY share a batch. It is a permission, not a guarantee, so this behaviour does not violate it, and the headless fixture demonstrates real sharing where React is out of the loop. PR #6393 therefore asserts only the guarantee on the mounted path and documents the measurement rather than guessing at the cause.

But the mechanism should be named. Either it is deliberate (and belongs in the contract prose as a stated consequence of `dispatch-sync`), or it is incidental coupling worth removing.

## Suggested approach

Instrument `flush-pending!` / `flush-scope!` with a stack capture in a DEBUG build and re-run `re-frame.ui.render-batch-host-checkpoint-dom-cljs-test`, which already drives the exact sequence. Then either document the behaviour in the Spec 006 §Render-batch finalization prose or file the coupling as a defect.

Do NOT weaken the existing fixtures to accommodate whatever is found — the guarantee assertions are the deliverable and are green.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT rf2-l91ds (#6393): the open question is already tracked here, but the contradiction is stronger than the current notes record. Current active authorities still say the MAY-sharing case is a fact: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc lines 81-84 and spec/006 lines 1773-1776 say two back-to-back dispatch-sync! calls in one JavaScript stack render once, not twice; docs/core/glossary line 205 repeats it. The PR's own real-browser measurement says the second same-stack dispatch advanced the first drain's pending mark, so mounted React does NOT universally behave that way. Resolve this Bead by identifying the synchronous flush and then either remove the coupling or narrow all three authority statements to the actual permission; do not leave MAY followed by a false unconditional example. No new Bead filed (all-state dedupe to this open owner).
RESOLVED by measurement (see rf2-i3dvj for the ruling that remains). What advances the pending batch on a second same-stack dispatch-sync: the ORDINARY armed schedule-flush! microtask checkpoint, landing mid-call because dispatch-sync! yields to the host microtask queue. Traced with stack capture on flush-scope! + advance-revision! plus begin/end console markers, 3 browser runs identical: revision 0->1->2; every flush-scope! stack was flush-scope! <- flush-pending! <- the microtask closure, terminating there with NO router frame above it; advance-revision! (commit*/step-8) never fired. CONTROL: a plain js/queueMicrotask enqueued by the fixture just before the 2nd call also ran mid-call, so the checkpoint is genuinely the host's and no re-frame code is in that callback. There is NO hidden synchronous flush and NO incidental scheduler coupling to remove — the scheduler is correct as specified. The filer's four ruled-out suspects were all correctly ruled out; the closest (drain-1 microtask firing early) was right about the microtask and wrong only in assuming a mid-stack fire was impossible. ACTIONED: reactive.cljc guarantee 3 narrowed — the unconditional 'two back-to-back dispatch-sync! calls in one JavaScript stack render once, not twice' is RETRACTED (holds headless, false mounted); the DOM test ns docstring + in-test note carry the full instrumentation record. DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: neither sharing nor non-sharing across two dispatch-sync! calls — the former asserts a permission as a guarantee, the latter freezes possibly-unintended router behaviour into a contract. The remaining question (should dispatch-sync! be microtask-atomic?) is a ROUTER ruling in implementation/core (held by #6365) and is filed as rf2-i3dvj. spec/006 ~1773-1776 + docs/core/glossary ~205 still carry the retracted claim; left for after that ruling (hot-zone, and would need rewriting twice).

title: Build digest ignores custom-element declarations, so two different builds share one identity
description:
FOUND by the rf2-vxgfnd.141 worker, in-fence and small but deliberately left because fixing it alone is a half-.141.

build/digest-for-slice (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/build.cljc:712) folds only the `views` rows. Two builds with IDENTICAL view sources but DIFFERENT custom-element declarations therefore produce the SAME build digest.

WHY IT MATTERS: the digest is build identity. Anything keyed on it — caching, staleness detection, served-output freshness — cannot distinguish two builds whose element classification differs, and classification decides whether a prop is emitted as an attribute or a property. So the digest says "same build" for two builds that emit different DOM.

SCOPE: small and self-contained (one fold), unlike its parent rf2-vxgfnd.141 which needs a source-harvest pass, declaration->consumer dependency edges and a new namespace. Split out so it can land independently.

⚠️ ACCEPTANCE MUST BE CAUSAL, not a green run: construct two builds identical in views and differing only in custom-element declarations, assert the digests DIFFER, and prove the test reds if the declarations are dropped from the fold. title: G-14 quadratic-vs-runaway charter gap — RULED Option C: reword to runaway + refresh stale spec/008 G-14 row; no new arm
description:
SURFACED by the rf2-gv8gr worker (#6388), which refused to ship the stronger claim and rewrote its own docstring, the bar comment and EP-0034 to state the limit explicitly.

THE GAP: the bead charter language implies the watch-loop arm catches an accidentally-quadratic rebuild pass. It does not at the shipped roster size. Arithmetic from the worker: K=11 views, per-view ~1.6ms, so a quadratic pass costs ~K/2 = 5.5x linear (~95ms) — comfortably inside the 550ms bar (K x the ratified 50ms per-view bar). Separation only appears once K > ~64.

WHAT SHIPPED IS STILL REAL: an honest runaway tripwire with 4 mutations / 4 red, plus an anti-vacuity witness (K realisations, K DISTINCT fingerprints, forced inside the span) checked BEFORE any duration. The worker also closed a hole M2 surfaced: a lazy map would have moved every expansion OUT of the timed span and reported "cheap" — realisation is now forced in-span, and the lazy variant costs ~12.8ms rather than ~0. No bound was widened, no threshold tuned down, no retry added.

⚠️ THIS IS A COST/SCOPE DECISION FOR MIKE, NOT AUTO-DISPATCHABLE. Closing the charter arm needs EITHER a namespace-scale roster (K > ~64 views) OR a scaling ratio (compare per-view cost at two roster sizes and assert it stays flat). The worker was explicit that the answer is NOT a tighter number — tightening the bar at K=11 would just make the arm flaky without buying quadratic separation. A K>64 roster multiplies CI time on a gate that runs per-PR, and the worker-gate memory records that worker wall-clock is already dominated by cold shadow-cljs compile.

RECOMMENDATION: the scaling-ratio shape is cheaper and strictly more diagnostic than a big roster — it measures the property (per-view cost is constant in K) rather than a proxy for it. But whether the arm is worth closing at all is a posture call: the runaway tripwire already catches the failure that would actually ship, and the quadratic case is currently hypothetical. If the answer is "not worth it", the honest action is to AMEND THE CHARTER to say runaway rather than quadratic, so no future reader believes the arm proves more than it does.

ALSO NOTED, benign understatement, no action needed unless the /ai untracking (rf2-vxgfnd.99.1) leaves them in place: the G-14 rows in 07-testing.md and 12-implementation-plan.md still read "named open" because the worker correctly did not touch ai/**. WHY C, verified against the repo (not just the dossier):
1. The normative spec never made the quadratic promise about the rebuild arm. spec/008-Testing.md:682 attaches 'e.g. accidentally quadratic' to the single-defview EXPANSION-P95 arm — where the claim is defensible (a within-view quadratic multiplies the ~5ms large fixture by ~15-20x, through the 50ms bar) — and says only that the rebuild delta 'rides later stages'. The overclaim lives in the rf2-gv8gr bead brief and local ai/ synthesis rows, not in tracked normative text. Honesty is restored by wording, not machinery.

Verified in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/build.cljc: contribute-view-checked! aggregates conflict evidence across OTHER sources ((effective slice views source) excludes the current namespace), so growing one namespace's roster does not exercise the path where per-view work actually aggregates across views — and that path is eval-time registration, which the rebuild arm (macroexpansion-only; register-view! emitted, never evaluated) cannot see under ANY G-14 shape. title: check-per-ns-isolation: RULED Charter A — add 2 allowlist entries (story open-in-editor + presence-real-clock) + header limits/rf2-ybqse review-bar section
description:
FOUND by the rf2-i36h6/qw31o worker (#6385), named not fixed: "widening its charter is a decision, not a worker call."

THE FINDING: implementation/scripts/check-per-ns-isolation.cjs exists precisely to catch namespaces that only pass in company. Its curated allowlist is 15 re-frame.* frame-construction namespaces. THREE instances of this family surfaced on 2026-07-18/19 and the gate watched NONE of them:
  1. rf2-oslyz — Story open-in-editor ownership ns alone gave 5 :rf.error/no-adapter-installed errors; it only ever passed because an earlier ns had called init!. Selected in the other order: 5 :rf.error/image-duplicate-id errors.
  2. rf2-ybqse (#6336) — a fixture captured (.now js/Date) in a top-level def while the panel compared at render time; test:cljs loads all namespaces before executing any, so a 60s horizon decayed across the suite prefix.
  3. rf2-i36h6 (#6385) — tools/story presence_real_clock_cljs_test yielded one setTimeout 0 on the premise that a macrotask lands after React act settles. It does not. Alone it was RED on 4 of 10 runs.

⚠️ THE HARD PART, and why this is a decision not a chore: instance 3 is INTERMITTENT alone (4/10), not deterministic. A gate that runs each namespace once in isolation would have called it green six times out of ten. Any widening has to answer: how many runs, or what structural property replaces run-counting? rf2-ybqse established the standard — prove the failure is UNREACHABLE (a margin, an invariant) rather than merely unobserved. For instance 2 the margin was measurable (+30461ms of a 60s horizon already burned); for instance 3 the structural answer is "await the thenable rather than racing a macrotask against it".

ALSO NOT UNIFORM: instance 1 is missing setup (fixable by the ns installing its own adapter, as #6367 did), 2 is a clock captured at namespace-load, 3 is a lost race. A single mechanical check will not catch all three. Decide what the gate is actually for before widening the allowlist.

QUESTIONS FOR THE RULING: (a) widen the allowlist to all test namespaces, or keep it curated and add these three; (b) run-count or structural property; (c) is the cost acceptable — running every namespace in isolation multiplies CI time, and rf2-worker-gate memory records that worker wall-clock is already dominated by cold shadow-cljs compile.

Gate if actioned: the checker own self-test + npm run test:script-policy + whatever suite it gates. A bare clojure -M:test -n <ns> from implementation/ silently runs 0 tests and READS AS GREEN — confirm non-zero counts.
notes:

RULING: the checker keeps its original rf2-32siq3.44 charter (Charter A). implementation/scripts/check-per-ns-isolation.cjs IS a curated, one-pass, deterministic tripwire for test namespaces that are RED when run ALONE against the consolidated node-test bundle — fixtures leaning on sibling-leaked runtime state. It is NOT a certifier of test-order independence: it is structurally blind to green-alone/red-in-company defects (load-time capture, the rf2-ybqse class) and only probabilistically sensitive to intermittent races.

(a) ALLOWLIST — stays curated. Add exactly TWO entries to ISOLATION_NAMESPACES:
  1. re-frame.story.open-in-editor-ownership-cljs-test (rf2-oslyz, #6367) — the gate's exact design class; deleting its adapter self-install is visible ONLY alone; ~11s/run.
  2. re-frame.story.play.presence-real-clock-cljs-test (rf2-i36h6, #6385) — deterministically green solo post-fix (10/10 measured), so zero noise while healthy; its regression is company-masked by the warmed act path, making this gate the only automatic detector; on regression it becomes a ~40%-per-run tripwire that fires within a few PRs. (Codex's dissent on this entry was weighed and overruled: the "flaky gate" scenario only exists AFTER a real regression merges, at which point a red is a true positive of a bug nothing else in CI can see.)
Do NOT add day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.resources-cljs-test (rf2-ybqse, #6336): running alone SHORTENS the load-to-render gap and makes load-time-capture bugs GREENER — listing it spends ~11s/run forever while implying coverage the mechanism cannot provide.
Roster comment: note the list now carries a second stratum — shipped order-dependence regressions whose failure signature is red-alone — alongside the EP-0023 frame-construction lineage.

(b) DETECTION — one deterministic pass per namespace. NO run-counting; NO structural-property machinery in the gate. The rf2-ybqse structural-unreachability standard is a REVIEW-TIME bar for fixes in this family, not gate code: a fix must prove the failure UNREACHABLE (a measured margin, an invariant, an awaited thenable), not merely unobserved, and carry a positive control that fails in the consolidated run. Add to the script header (after "THE CHECK"; wording may be lightly fitted to house style):

  WHAT THIS GATE IS NOT
  ---------------------
  This gate detects ONE direction only: deterministic "red alone, green
  in company" fixture defects. It does NOT certify test-order
  independence. It is structurally blind to the inverse direction —
  green alone, red in company (e.g. a wall-clock captured in a top-level
  def decaying across the suite prefix, rf2-ybqse): running such a
  namespace alone makes the bug LESS likely, not more. And it is only
  probabilistically sensitive to intermittent races (rf2-i36h6 was red

  permutation, or timing analysis here. The bar a FIX in the
  order-dependence family must clear is the rf2-ybqse
  structural-unreachability standard, enforced at REVIEW time: prove
  the failure unreachable (a measured margin, an invariant, an awaited
  thenable) rather than merely unobserved, with a positive control that
  fails in the consolidated run.

(c) COST — the current ~2m39s curated pass (~3 min with the two additions) is ACCEPTED on CI and the fast-PR spine. REJECTED at any cadence, including nightly (whys recorded so these are not re-proposed):

title: Make the synthesis standing census ignore local untracked AI drafts
description:
PR #6372 says its standing-marker census covers authority-shaped, git-tracked synthesis documents, but `directory-roster` uses Java `.listFiles` and therefore includes every local untracked `.md` under `drafts/`, `spikes/`, or `reviews/`.

That conflicts with the project policy shipped in #6368: `/ai` is local by default, current tracked exceptions are transitional, and programmers/agents are expected to create local AI material without force-adding it. A local scratch review or draft with no standing banner now makes the full `implementation/ui` suite red even though the file is ignored by Git, cannot reach CI, and changes no shipped authority. Conversely the stated roster is specifically the tracked authority surface.

Keep the marker-presence logic and directory discovery, but derive admission from Git's tracked set (or an equivalent exact tracked-file source). Do not replace it with a hand-maintained filename list or broaden into content validation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adding an ignored, untracked local `.md` under each censused directory does not change the census result or break the UI suite.
- A newly force-added/tracked `.md` in any censused directory is admitted automatically in that same commit and fails until it has an accepted preamble marker.
- Every currently tracked `.md` in drafts/, spikes/, and reviews/ remains covered; a censused directory with no tracked documents still fails non-vacuously until its S7 row is deliberately retired.
- The existing per-directory vocabularies, preamble/deep-link rule, real-disposition controls, and mutation teeth remain; no maintained filename roster, Markdown parser, or general content-consistency framework is introduced.
- Focused/full UI tests run with non-zero counts.
notes:
DELIVERED in PR #6423 (worker/ep0008-census-0b9b0), not merged.

MECHANISM: directory-roster kept .listFiles for DISCOVERY; ADMISSION is now a new tracked-markdown-names helper shelling 'git ls-files -z -- <dir>' (clojure.java.shell) from repo root, filtered to direct children ending .md. The roster is the intersection. -z avoids Git's quoted-path form. A non-zero git exit THROWS rather than yielding an empty set, so an unreadable tracked set cannot read as a clean census.

Because ls-files reads the INDEX (not HEAD), a force-added doc is admitted by the very commit that tracks it — acceptance criterion 2. Verified in a THROWAWAY repo in scratchpad (staged-but-never-committed file returned; untracked sibling not). Done outside this repo deliberately: nothing was git add -f'ed under ai/, and git diff --diff-filter=A origin/main...HEAD -- ai/ is empty, so the AI-tracking ratchet is safe.

Intersection rather than ls-files alone: a tracked file absent from the worktree stays out of the roster instead of throwing in slurp; the new coverage assertion reds on that instead.

PER-ENTRY, NOT UNION (the rf2-nyjml lesson): new deftest the-standing-census-roster-is-gits-tracked-set loops censused-directories and per directory asserts (a) tracked set non-empty, (b) roster == tracked set (coverage), (c) a real untracked file spat into that directory does not enter the roster. A roster that dropped one directory entirely would still look populated in aggregate.

PROOF BOTH DIRECTIONS (bug reproduced first, not assumed):
- BEFORE: 3 ignored untracked .md (one per directory) => 3 failures, message wrongly claiming each was 'authority-shaped and tracked'.
- AFTER: same 3 files present => green, 0 log mentions.
- STILL HAS TEETH ON A GENUINE TRACKED DEFECT: mutated the real tracked reviews/09-review-disposition.md to strip its '**Status:**' marker => census RED naming that file, while the untracked probes stayed silent. Mutation reverted; marker verified restored.

Counts: census namespace 13 tests / 120 assertions (was 12/111; +1 test, +9 = 3 dirs x 3 assertions). Full implementation/ui suite 956 tests / 18656 assertions / 0 failures (brief expected ~955 pre-existing + my 1 new deftest).

Untouched as required: marker vocabularies, preamble/deep-link rule, real-disposition controls, negative-arm mutation teeth. No filename roster, no Markdown parser, no content validation. Anti-vacuity message updated to name the tracked-set reason a directory can census nothing.

FENCE: no overlap with any live worker. The census lives in implementation/ui/test/, NOT implementation/scripts/ — so no collision with spec009-cardinality (G-13 proof) or ruled-trio-b72to (check-per-ns-isolation.cjs, .gitignore).

title: CI ratchet: the tracked-file count under ai/ must never increase
description:
PROPOSED by the rf2-4lv73 worker (#6368) as the mechanical pin for Mike end-state ruling. Filed because it prevents a demonstrated, expensive failure — not as tidiness.

MIKE RULING (2026-07-18, in-session): "Nothing under /ai should be tracked" is the END STATE; files stay tracked as long as necessary. rf2-4lv73 states that policy in CLAUDE.md and .gitignore as PROSE. Prose does not stop a force-add.

THE GUARD: a CI check that fails when `git ls-files ai/ | wc -l` INCREASES against a committed baseline. Properties that make it the right shape:
  - it pins the ruling mechanically rather than by linting wording;
  - a new force-add fails the build at the moment it happens;
  - the number can only FALL as S7 removes trees (rf2-vxgfnd.99.1), so the guard needs no maintenance;
  - it RETIRES ITSELF at zero.
Current baseline: 89 files — findings/new-substrate-synthesis 61, findings/new-substrate-codex 24, decisions 4. Verify before pinning; do not trust this number.

WHY IT CLEARS MIKE POSTURE BAR (rf2-seuvt): on 2026-07-18 a force-added ai/decisions/ dossier carried a literal personal worktree path into CI. scripts/check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh failed on main, and because CI evaluates the PR merge commit, EVERY open PR went red for about an hour. Cost: six worker dispatches — three chasing a phantom on clean branches, one diagnosing, one fixing main, one rebasing three branches. Four separate workers independently identified the tracking as the root cause and said the leak class will recur while it stands. This is a likely, already-realised failure mode with a known cost.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
  - Keep it to a count ratchet. Do NOT enumerate tracked trees — Mike ruled CLAUDE.md states policy only and git state is the roster; an enumerating guard would reintroduce exactly what the ruling forbids.
  - Decrease must PASS (S7 removals must not be blocked). Only increase fails.
  - The failure message must name the offending paths (diff the current listing against the baseline) — a bare count mismatch is not actionable.
  - .github/workflows/* is HOT-ZONE; check no other worker holds it, and note implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs pins workflow shape at 168 assertions.
  - Prove teeth by mutation: force-add a scratch file under ai/ -> gate fails naming it; remove -> passes. Also prove a REMOVAL passes.
  - Gate script itself should be shellcheck-clean if written in sh; portability.yml shellchecks its own gate for exactly this reason.
notes: PR #6380 (worker/ai-ratchet-lsp1i). Baseline VERIFIED at 89 (synthesis 61 / codex 24 / decisions 4) — matches the filing number. Gate: scripts/check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh (POSIX sh, invoked via 'sh' so no exec bit needed on runner; mode 755 to match siblings). Baseline: scripts/ai-tracked-baseline.txt (snapshot of git ls-files ai/, LF-pinned in .gitattributes; used ONLY to name offending paths in the message — pass/fail is the count comparison alone, no tree enumeration). Wired as a 2nd job in .github/workflows/portability.yml (not a new workflow) — ratchet is the upstream lock for the exact leak that workflow catches downstream; keeps post-merge-workflow-sanity EXCLUDE list unchanged. Shellchecks its own script per the portability precedent. TEETH all 3 proven: force-add -> exit 1 naming the path; S7-style 28-file removal (89->61) -> exit 0 PASS; unmutated -> exit 0. Gates: _changed-surfaces 168 passed (no pin moved), test:script-policy exit 0 (331 assertions), check-no-hardcoded-paths exit 0, sh -n + dash -n OK. shellcheck NOT available locally — runs in CI only. FINDING FOR MIKE: .gitignore un-ignores /ai/extended-context/** as 'durable committed project context (mayor contributes on retrospectives)'. Empty of tracked files today so not in the baseline, but blessed to grow and needs no git add -f — the next retrospective contribution WILL trip this gate. Intended under the end-state ruling (bump baseline in-PR, growth becomes visible), but it is a live collision between .gitignore wording and the ruling. Excluding the tree was deliberately NOT done: that would be enumerating trees.

title: presence-real-clock test passes only because another namespace runs first

DEFECT: implementation .../presence_real_clock_cljs_test real-flush-presence-advances-the-framework-clock FAILS (2 assertions) when its namespace is selected ALONE. It passes under npm run test:cljs only because presence-cljs-test runs first and leaves the state it depends on.

Do NOT fix it by pinning execution order; that preserves the coupling and hides the next instance.

⚠️ PROVE IT, do not assume: run the namespace ALONE (red before, green after) AND in the full suite (green both), and state both counts. A green full-suite run is exactly the evidence that failed to catch this in the first place.

Gate: the affected namespace alone + npm run test:cljs to completion (baseline 10071 tests / 49717 assertions after #6367). A bare clojure -M:test -n <ns> from implementation/ silently runs 0 tests and READS AS GREEN — confirm non-zero counts.

title: Authority-shaped synthesis drafts and spikes are enumerated by no census — the reason stale claims keep surviving
description:
FOUND TWICE, by rf2-3b931 (#6353) and rf2-cpalh (#6359). Filing on the second sighting because a mechanism, not an instance, is now identified.

DEFECT: ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/drafts/ and .../spikes/ hold authority-shaped, git-tracked documents that NO census enumerates as a class.
- The #6310 compiler-model-authorities census (implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/guide_truth_jvm_test.clj) names 8 specific paths; neither directory is among them (established by #6353).
- check_doc_slugs.py --synthesis-only covers drafts/ for LINK VALIDITY only and does not cover spikes/ at all — the S3 spike report is not among its 41 files (established by #6359).
- mkdocs does not build the ai/ tree.

CONSEQUENCE: a document can state a retired model indefinitely and no gate objects. That is precisely how both files survived rf2-er64a, and how spec-004-interim-amendment.md sat at "Status: final draft / Merge condition: immediately" carrying wording Spec 004 had retired. Someone can act on these.

WHY IT CLEARS MIKE 2026-07-18 POSTURE BAR (rf2-seuvt): material maintenance/AI friction with a demonstrated failure mode, twice. Not exhaustiveness — these are documents an agent or a human is invited to treat as authority.

PROPOSED SHAPE (from #6359, deliberately bounded — do not build a cross-document consistency checker): a directory-level enumeration asserting every tracked file under drafts/ and spikes/ carries EITHER a current-status marker OR a supersession marker. Not content validation. #6359 already added a marker-presence arm to the existing bounded census slice_memo_lifetime_census_jvm_test.clj (rf2-2mop6r) for its two files — extend that shape to the directory rather than inventing a new framework.

⚠️ THE DISPOSITIONS ARE NOT UNIFORM — the guard must not force one. #6353 superseded a draft whose anchors were GONE from the live spec. #6359 superseded a draft whose anchors were all PRESENT but whose edits had ALREADY LANDED (re-applying would duplicate them), and deliberately did NOT supersede a dated experimental record whose model is still the binding shape source cited by live Spec 006 — retiring it would kill a document the spec depends on, and rewording it would falsify the record. A guard that demands a single marker vocabulary will force one of those into the wrong shape.

Gate: the census suite from implementation/ui (a bare clojure -M:test -n <ns> from implementation/ silently runs 0 tests and READS AS GREEN — confirm non-zero counts) + prove the arm reds on an unmarked file and greens on each of the three real dispositions.
notes:
REFERENCE CLASS EXTENDED (rf2-rzzlw / PR #6370, 2026-07-18): add reviews/ and the tombstone README.md to the uncovered set. check_doc_slugs.py --synthesis-only enumerates exactly 41 files (guide/, drafts/, prep/, 11-adoption-workstreams.md, 12-implementation-plan.md); reviews/, spikes/, README.md and the numbered chapters 01-10 are all outside it. rf2-rzzlw repaired six broken relative references in reviews/09-review-disposition.md - a doubled reviews/reviews/ prefix, a dangling markdown link, and four drafts/* spans wrong by one directory level - and NOT ONE of them would have been caught by any gate. The relocation that introduced them (rf2-mgy7pz #6231) also passed green. Post-S7 this matters more, not less: reviews/ and spikes/ are the permanent survivors, so they become the only synthesis paths left and the only ones still uncensused.
DELIVERED — PR #6372 (worker/synthesis-census-5jbev), 2026-07-19.

SHAPE: one directory-level marker-PRESENCE arm appended to the existing bounded census implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/slice_memo_lifetime_census_jvm_test.clj — the same file #6359 put the two-file marker arm in. No new framework, no new tracked file under ai/, no guide/** touched.

ROSTER = THE DIRECTORY LISTING (.listFiles filtered to *.md), for drafts/, spikes/, reviews/. A file landing tomorrow is censused the day it lands. A vanished/empty directory REDS rather than passing vacuously, so the S7 wave (rf2-vxgfnd.99.1) must drop the drafts/ row deliberately.

PRESENCE ONLY, PER-DIRECTORY VOCABULARY. Three marker classes, each a line-anchored presence regex: :status (**Status:** …), :supersession (leading **SUPERSEDED / HISTORICAL / RETIRED / ⚠ CORRECTION / DELTA BANNER / DRAFT** banner), :record (**Date:** / **Written:** / **When:**). drafts/ accepts {status, supersession} only — an undated draft is actionable, so a bare date does not declare standing there. spikes/ and reviews/ also accept :record, because a dated experimental/adversarial record's date IS its standing; demanding **Status:** of a 2026-07-11 review would be the wrong-shape failure this bead warned about. What a marker SAYS is never read.

ALL THREE REAL DISPOSITIONS PASS, and are pinned BY NAME in a dedicated deftest so a future edit cannot quietly exclude one: (1) drafts/spec-004-interim-amendment.md superseded/anchors-gone; (2) drafts/spec-006-observation-port-amendment.md superseded/edits-already-landed; (3) spikes/s3-ownership-report.md NOT superseded — dated experimental record still cited by live Spec 006, carrying a scoped ⚠ CORRECTION.

DEEP-LINK GUARD GENERALISED: the marker must sit in the preamble, ahead of the first ## heading. A directory census cannot name the section carrying a claim without validating content, but it can guarantee no anchor-linkable section precedes the marker.

MUTATION PROOF: 6 on-disk mutations, 6 RED. (1-3) a brand-new unmarked .md added to each of the three directories — red in all three, proving the roster is the listing, not a file list; (4-6) the live marker stripped from one file per directory (spec-004-interim-amendment, s3-ownership-report, 09-review-disposition) — red each. All reverted; tree clean. In-test the negative arm additionally strips markers from EVERY conformant document in all three directories and requires each to red, with a no-op guard that throws if a strip fails to land.

ONE PROSE FIX (per the rf2-cpalh precedent — fix the prose, not the checker): reviews/09-review-disposition.md was the single document in the three directories carrying no recognised marker. It gains a **Status:** line declaring what it is — a standing, append-only decision log and a permanent S7 survivor. Its dates were per-entry only, so nothing at the top declared the document's own standing.

GATES (all foreground, run to completion): implementation/ui clojure -M:test = 926 tests / 16114 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors (baseline 919/16016 + 7 new deftests); check_synthesis_plan_authority.py exit 0; --self-test exit 0; check_doc_slugs.py --synthesis-only exit 0 (41 files); mkdocs build --strict exit 0.

NOT ACTIONED (out of scope, deliberately): the bead's third-sighting 'smallest pin' proposal — two exact-token assertions in guide_truth_jvm_test.clj on spec/API.md's §2b dispatch! S1-clause row and the spread-safe rows. That is content validation of a graduated spec file, a different guard from this one, and guide_truth_jvm_test.clj was outside this dispatch's fence. Worth a follow-up bead if still wanted.

title: Scope the ui/raw manifest claim to view-level enumerability
description:
PR #6321's `ui/raw` portal caveat is behaviorally correct, but its stated surviving containment guarantee overclaims the shipped manifest. Spec 004 now says "every site declares the `:raw` capability and is recorded in the manifest, so the set of such escapes is finite and listable."

The compiler records only a VIEW-LEVEL capability bit:

- `compiler.cljc`'s `capabilities` AST scan folds any `:raw` node into the manifest set as `:raw`.
- `env.cljc`'s site table has events/subs/leases/htmls/frame-ops/slots/locals/effects/dispatch-fns/react/diagnostics, but no raw-site collection.
- the `ui/raw` analyzer returns `{:op :raw ...}` and never calls `env/add-site!`.
- `re-frame.ui.tool/view-manifest` exposes the capability set and site counts, but no raw site ids, paths, coordinates or count.

Therefore tools can list which compiled VIEWS contain at least one raw escape. They cannot list every escape site, distinguish one from many, or locate the sites. The sentence's "every site ... is recorded" and "set of such escapes ... listable" are false.

Keep the portal/trust-boundary guidance and the programmer-trust posture. The smallest honest correction is prose: call this view-level enumerability (`:raw` tells tools that a view contains one or more raw escapes), not site enumerability. Do not widen the versioned manifest/tool schema solely to preserve one sentence. If a concrete Story/Xray/agent consumer later needs per-site coordinates, that should be an independently justified tooling feature with a schema-version decision.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 004 accurately states that `:raw` is a view-level manifest capability bit, not a per-site record.
- The portal/head ownership, JVM host-op, and structured Spec 011 guidance remain unchanged.
- No claim says every raw escape site, count, or coordinate is listable unless implementation and the versioned tool projection actually provide it.
- Documentation-only by default; no manifest-schema expansion, runtime inspection, portal restriction, or tooling feature without a named consumer.
close_reason: Filtered by product posture: view-level versus per-site ui/raw manifest enumerability is a minor wording precision with no current SPA-authoring or tooling consumer impact; no new schema/prose task warranted.

title: Align Xray concrete-query selectors with CLJS equality at NaN, regex, and sequential values
description:
PR #6318 correctly preserves CLJS record type in Xray's concrete-query `data-testid` encoder, but its new "honestly stated" supported domain still overclaims injectivity and equality-canonicality at three ordinary CLJS value seams.

REPRODUCED on the repository's current ClojureScript runtime:

  (pr-str js/NaN)                  => "##NaN"
  (= js/NaN js/NaN)                => false
  (pr-str (js/RegExp. "x" "g"))   => #"x"
  (pr-str (js/RegExp. "x" "i"))   => #"x"
  (= (js/RegExp. "x" "g")
     (js/RegExp. "x" "g"))        => false
  (= [1 2] '(1 2))                 => true

`canonical-str` sends NaN and RegExp values through the `:else (pr-str x)` branch, so two `=`-distinct NaN- or regex-bearing concrete queries mint one selector. It also renders vectors with `[...]` and seqs with `(...)`, so two `=`-equal query arguments can mint different selectors. This contradicts both directions of the function/spec contract: distinct supported identities are injective, and value-equal identities canonicalize to one selector.

The domain text explicitly includes every `number` and `regex`, so these are not covered by its raw-JS-object exclusion. Query-vector validation constrains only the vector and keyword head; these values are legal arguments. Xray's `skipped-subs` dedupe and the subscription cache describe identity in terms of the concrete query vector's ClojureScript equality, so the selector must align with that same equivalence relation.

Keep the local/no-framework posture. Canonicalize all ClojureScript sequential values that are `=` under one sequence representation instead of distinguishing vector vs list. Treat non-reflexive NaN and identity-equality host values such as RegExp as explicitly outside the injective domain unless a genuinely small, equality-faithful representation exists; do not add a WeakMap/object-id registry or general serializer merely to distinguish host identity. Correct the function/spec wording so it never names regex or all numbers as faithfully covered when they are not. Add adversarial rows for the supported equality law and explicit boundary tests/prose for excluded scalars.
acceptance_criteria:
- Equal vector/list sequential query arguments mint one selector, matching ClojureScript `=`.
- The supported-domain contract no longer claims regex or non-reflexive NaN are injectively represented by `pr-str`; excluded identity-like values are named honestly.
- A string containing an unmatched UTF-16 surrogate cannot throw during selector generation and remains distinguishable from other strings; adversarial coverage pins the URI-safe encoding.
- Adversarial CLJS tests pin the NaN/RegExp boundary and the supported sequential equality law.
- Record type preservation, map/set/record insertion-order canonicality, hash-collision coverage, labels, React keys, projection and `data-query-v` remain unchanged.
- The correction stays local; no general serializer, object-id registry, WeakMap identity system, lossy U+FFFD folding, or query-grammar redesign.
notes: ADDITIONAL SAME-SEAM REPRO (2026-07-18 audit): the supported-domain claim includes strings, but `concrete-query-selector` passes the final canonical string directly to `js/encodeURIComponent`. ClojureScript `pr-str` preserves a lone UTF-16 surrogate inside the quoted string; `encodeURIComponent` throws `URIError: URI malformed`. Exact probe: `(let [s (js/String.fromCharCode 55296) p (pr-str s)] ...)` produced code units `[34 55296 34]`, then `js/encodeURIComponent p` threw. Thus a legal string-bearing query can crash the Xray panel while generating its test id. Fix at the same small codec seam with an injective, URI-safe escaping of unmatched surrogate code units (preserve distinct input strings); do not merely replace them all with U+FFFD, which would introduce collisions, and do not add a general serializer.
close_reason: Filtered by product posture: rare NaN/RegExp/vector-vs-list/lone-surrogate behavior in an internal Xray data-testid codec does not materially affect SPA authoring ergonomics or correctness; fixing it would litigate edge semantics beyond justified value.

title: POLICY: are EP decision records editable in place, or frozen with dated addenda?
description:
OPERATOR RULING NEEDED (surfaced by rf2-d1yhx / PR #6304; this bead carries the policy call, which is reversible either way). [CORRECTED 2026-07-18: PR #6304 was OPEN/unmerged at decision time; an earlier version of this description wrongly said the mayor had merged the truth-fix.] [RESOLVED 2026-07-18: see the DECISION block in NOTES -- ruling (b) precised as "freeze meaning, not bytes", with the concrete PR-branch disposition for #6304.]

THE SITUATION: rf2-d1yhx corrected teardown terminology across active authorities. To do it, it edited EP-0008's 'The ruling' and 'R2' prose â€” clauses that made PRESENT-TENSE FACTUAL CLAIMS about where the runtime emits (they credited safe-call-hook! with stamping/conj'ing that record-teardown-failure! actually does). The worker limited itself strictly to those factual clauses, left the rest of the EP untouched, and FLAGGED the judgement rather than deciding it.

THE FORK:
(a) EDIT IN PLACE (what shipped in #6304): EPs read as current truth; a reader never meets a false present-tense claim. COST: the record of what was decided WHEN gets quietly rewritten â€” the EP stops being archaeological evidence.
(b) FREEZE + DATED ADDENDUM: the decision record stays honest about its own moment; corrections are visible AS corrections. COST: readers must reach the addendum to learn the prose above it is stale.

MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION: (b) freeze + addendum. An EP's value IS being the record of what was ruled and why; if it silently tracks the code it stops being evidence and becomes just more docs. But this is a call about the project's memory and taste, not correctness â€” hence a ruling, not a dispatch.

SCOPE OF THE RULING: it should settle the GENERAL policy (all EPs, all future corrections), not just EP-0008. If (b) is chosen, this bead's implementation is: revert the EP-0008 ruling/R2 prose to its as-written form and append a dated addendum recording the correction. The worker confirmed that is a clean follow-up â€” nothing about #6304 forecloses it. If (a) is chosen, close this bead and consider recording the policy in the EP template/README so future workers don't re-raise it.

RELATED: rf2-3i7tr (head-policy normative home) is the other open operator ruling of this shape.
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-18 18:07 AUSEST)

PR #6304 STATE AT DECISION TIME: OPEN, unmerged; EP-0008 edit commit 23c06c185f is NOT on origin/main. The description's "the mayor merged the truth-fix" is stale — the EP-0008 reshaping below happens ON THE PR BRANCH (worker/docs-truth-cluster) before merge, not as a post-merge revert.

RULING — (b), precised as "freeze meaning, not bytes" (dossier Option C; Codex and Fable recommendations concurred). Applies to the whole EP corpus, all future corrections:

- Once an EP is accepted and implementation is in flight, its settled decisions and rationale are a historical record.
- TIER 1 (edit in place, undated): purely editorial maintenance that cannot change a reasonable reader's understanding of the proposal, alternatives, rationale, ruling, or scope — spelling, meaning-preserving grammar, formatting, broken/renamed-link repair, index/status sync, mechanical errata-ledger updates (row strikes/closures).
- TIER 2 (visible dated correction): any edit that changes the apparent meaning, scope, factual premise, ruled name/shape, or implementation context of a settled passage. Preserve the original text; add a dated erratum/addendum BESIDE the affected passage (EP-0001 Decision-2 / EP-0013 adjacency pattern) when that minimizes reader friction; banner or end addendum for document-wide changes.
- TIER 3 (new EP or explicit operator ruling): corrections that change public contract or design policy. An erratum is not a back door for a new decision.
- Current normative truth stays in the EP's named normative home (spec/ for graduated standards-track EPs; the EP itself for active process EPs). No enforcement machinery — the written rule plus review suffice.

Decisive fact beyond the dossier's options analysis: EP-0008 (~line 310 on main) asserts "The ruling, rationale, and refinements are recorded here verbatim." The in-place edit falsifies that sentence inside the document itself; option (a) would require abandoning the verbatim convention corpus-wide.

The runtime later added guarded direct teardown steps (`safe-teardown-step!` — e.g. the `:frame/notify-machine-destruction!` machine cascade); they join the late-bound hooks at the same shared `record-teardown-failure!` boundary and the same single bounded `:rf.error/frame-teardown-failed` report. title: Rule the normative home of the re-frame.ui head policy
description:

notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-18 18:06 AUSEST)

RULED: Option A — split ownership by responsibility.
- Spec 004 (spec/004-Views.md) is the NORMATIVE OWNER of the compiled-view structural boundary: re-frame.ui templates, their AST and JVM tree, and the root/mount surface expose no ui/head, no head target, and no portable head channel. - Spec 009 owns ONLY the trace/error projection (:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch head-mismatch arm, :rf.error/ssr-head-resolution-failed). Touch 009 only if a trace fact actually changes (none does).
RATIONALE: ownership follows the abstraction boundary, not the shared noun "head". Spec 011 specifies an OPTIONAL artefact (day8/re-frame2-ssr); the no-head-channel fact constrains every compiled template even in client-only apps that never load it, so only the grammar-owning spec can normatively define the grammar's completeness. The exact export-surface guards (implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/defview_grammar_jvm_test.clj export-surface-is-exactly-the-blessed-set + the S3 conformance catalogue guard) already enforce Spec 004/API.md's catalogue, and a future head-capable form (ui/portal Wave-2 trigger) would be a Spec 004 grammar change first. title: Make README anchor checks use GitHub duplicate slugs
description:
PR #6290 correctly fixes literal `{#id}` suffixes because GitHub and the attr-list-disabled docs renderer both slugify that suffix as visible heading text. But review of the affected checker exposes a broader, explicit renderer mismatch: `check_readme_links.py` says these READMEs are read on GitHub and not in MkDocs, then intentionally validates MkDocs `_N` duplicate slugs and tells users the rules are "NOT GitHub's".

The bundled `underscore_disambig_ok` fixture blesses `#errors_1` for the second `## Errors` heading. GitHub's heading slugger uses `errors-1`; the fixture itself documents that fact. Current `_slug_index` returns `{'errors', 'errors_1', ...}`, so the gate can certify a fragment that the actual README renderer does not mint and reject the real one. This is latent in live links today, but tracked READMEs already contain duplicate headings, so the mismatch is not hypothetical structure.

Make this checker renderer-honest with the smallest GitHub-specific seam. At minimum, use GitHub's `-N` duplicate suffix and reverse the fixture controls (`#errors-1` green, `#errors_1` red), and reconcile the module/error prose. Verify the existing base-slug cases before widening; reuse a small local slug helper if the base rules agree. Do not import a Markdown renderer, call the network in CI, or force README content into MkDocs rules merely to share code.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two `## Errors` headings index as `errors` and `errors-1` for README targets; `#errors-1` resolves and `#errors_1` is reported broken.
- The checker/module/error text states that GitHub-rendered README anchors use GitHub rules, not MkDocs `_N` rules.
- Existing `{#id}` full-title behavior, inline/fence masking, HTML anchors, target checks and current live scan remain correct.
- Focused controls cover real duplicate suffixes and the wrong-underscore negative; any further base-slug divergence is measured before inclusion, not assumed.
- No general Markdown parser, GitHub network call in CI, new renderer dependency, or repo-wide README rewrite.

title: Qualify the host-owned head policy for ui/raw portals
description:
PR #6289 correctly establishes that re-frame.ui has no structural head API and that `ui/html` cannot escape its DOM-element parent, but the new Spec 004 prose overstates containment across the deliberately opaque `ui/raw` boundary. It says "every template form ... produces nodes beneath [the body] root" and that no compiled-view form renders into `<head>`.

`emit_cljs.cljc` lowers an analyzed `:raw` node to `(:form node)` unchanged. A valid React node can be a portal. Independently reproduced with the repository's React/Playwright versions: a body-root render containing `ReactDOM.createPortal(<meta name=rf-portal-probe content=yes>, document.head)` produced the meta in `document.head` while the ordinary sibling stayed under the body root. Wrapping that portal value in `ui/raw` crosses the compiler unchanged by design. This does not mean re-frame.ui supplies or should supply a head channel—the programmer has explicitly entered host React—but the absolute structural sentence is false unless the foreign escape hatch is named.

Add a narrow caveat: compiled structural forms and `ui/html` target only beneath the root; `ui/raw` may carry host constructs such as portals that render elsewhere, and those are outside re-frame.ui's head ordering/deduplication/hydration guarantees. An app doing so owns the host behavior; use Spec 011 `reg-head` / `active-head` when the structured SSR head contract is wanted. Trust the programmer and keep the escape hatch; do not ban portals, inspect opaque React values, or add head machinery.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 004's host-owned-head section scopes its containment claim to compiled structural forms and `ui/html`, not opaque `ui/raw` host values.
- It explicitly notes that a `ui/raw` React portal can target `document.head` (or another external container) and is caller-owned host behavior outside re-frame.ui head ordering/dedupe/hydration guarantees.
- The preferred structured SSR head path remains Spec 011 `reg-head` / `active-head`; no new view-level head API is implied.
- Existing trusted-markup and raw foreign-boundary contracts remain unchanged.
- Documentation-only; no portal prohibition, host-value inspection, head runtime, sanitiser, compatibility layer, or conformance promise for portals.
notes: MAYOR SEQUENCING (2026-07-18): genuine gap — S4-D (#6289) established that re-frame.ui has no structural head API and ui/html cannot escape its DOM element, but emit_cljs.cljc lowers an analyzed :raw node to (:form node) UNCHANGED, and a valid React node can be a PORTAL — which can render into <head>, escaping the host-owned head policy S4-D just documented. HELD, not blocked: its surface is spec/004-Views.md §Interop, where rf2-74vlo (S4-C, the last S4 feature leaf) is LIVE adding the compile-tier a11y warnings subsection. Dispatch after 74vlo merges. Also relates to rf2-3i7tr (the head-policy normative-home ruling) — if Mike rules the policy moves to Spec 011, this bead's surface moves with it.

title: Rule 6b(i) :contextType suppression is blunt proximity — tighten it
description: FOUND by rf2-szw6c (#6299) and deliberately NOT fixed (outside that bead's acceptance; tightening changes an existing rule's semantics corpus-wide). scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py Rule 6b(i) suppresses a :contextType residue hit whenever 'Reagent' appears within ~40 chars (regex ':contextType[^.]{0,40}Reagent'). DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-18 18:10 AUSEST)

RULING: Option C — repair Rule 6b(i)'s attribution SCOPE and DELETE the proximity suppression; do not refine the suppression. This block is self-contained; the dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-xlxrl.contexttype-suppression-boundary.md) is retired/deleted.

SURFACE: scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py only — Rule 6b(i) in hooks_sentence_problems, the CONTEXTTYPE_REAGENT_OWNED_RE regex (~lines 463-467), and the --self-test fixtures (~lines 1281-1423). Zero corpus edits are expected; if the implementation somehow ends up touching spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md or any other spec/ file (Rule 6c anchors), THAT is hot-zone and the mayor must sequence it.

THE DECIDED RULE:
1. Clause carving for 6b(i): split the sentence at strong clause separators — `;`, em dash `—`, and the contrast connectives `, while` / `, whereas` / `, but`. Do NOT split at `:` (that regresses the S2 fixture "UIx is not special: reg-view* gives it :contextType.", which must stay red). The connectives are required: carving alone leaves the lawful "Reagent's wrapper gives the component `:contextType`, while UIx uses `use-frame`." red.
2. DELETE all three arms of CONTEXTTYPE_REAGENT_OWNED_RE (Reagent-forward proximity, token-forward proximity, comparison-cue arm). Nothing live or self-tested depends on any arm — see EMPIRICAL FACTS.
3. The only Reagent-ownership allowance that remains: the token-adjacent possessive/compound — `Reagent's :contextType` / `Reagent-only :contextType` — recognised inside a clause that names a hooks adapter (it keeps "UIx components never get Reagent's `:contextType`." green, where the 8-char negation window misses). A clause that names Reagent and no hooks adapter is simply not a hooks clause and is never evaluated by 6b(i).
4. Keep the existing tightly-scoped "no `:contextType`" hooks negation (CONTEXTTYPE_NEGATED window), applied per clause.
5. REQUIRED ambiguity branch (not polish): a clause carrying `:contextType` plus a positive attribution verb but naming neither adapter, inside a sentence that names a hooks adapter, FAILS with a rewrite diagnostic ("name the owner or split the sentence"). This is load-bearing, not just principle: under clause carving, the existing Rule 6c block-mutation self-tests (e.g. the views-row insertion "use-frame, which gives the component a `:contextType`", fixture ~line 1376) land in a `;`-separated cell away from the adapter token — WITHOUT the ambiguity branch those established red mutations silently go green and the self-test loses its teeth.
6. Failure message: name the failing clause; suggest either "say the hooks adapter has no `:contextType`" or "split the Reagent comparison into a separate clause / name the owner explicitly".
7. Stay a bounded regex guard (~30 lines proven sufficient by prototype). No prose parser, no escape-hatch annotation (no corpus evidence either is needed).

SELF-TEST EXPECTATIONS (pin the fifteen validated probe shapes; at minimum):
RED — the reproduced false negative as a regression case, BOTH directions: (a) "On UIx / Helix, `reg-view*` gives the component a `:contextType`; the `reg-view` macro stays Reagent-flavoured." (passes today — the demonstrated hole); (b) "The macro stays Reagent-flavoured; UIx gets a `:contextType` too." (also green today). Also red: S2 stray-far-"not"; the ambiguity shape "UIx is not special; reg-view* gives it `:contextType`." (caught via the ambiguity branch); the Rule 6c block mutations.
GREEN — S3 "UIx/Helix differ from Reagent's `:contextType` mechanism." (note: green because it has NO attribution verb — it never depended on the comparison arm); S4 explicit hooks negation; S5 Reagent-only sentence; V2 Reagent-owned comparison; the token-adjacent possessive "UIx components never get Reagent's `:contextType`."; the `, while` mixed sentence; and the per-adapter semicolon HOUSE STYLE: "On Reagent register it via `reg-view*`, which gives the class a `:contextType`; on UIx / Helix carry the frame with `use-frame`." — this shape is a false positive under the CURRENT rule and under Option B; it must be green under the new rule.
ACCEPTED BOUNDARY: the period-variant pronoun attribution ("UIx is not special. reg-view* gives it `:contextType`.") is uncatchable today and stays uncatchable. Consistent, statable, not worth a parser.

EMPIRICAL FACTS WORTH PRESERVING (measured against the live checker, HEAD 2f4e8d8d2b, corpus unchanged since f5281a3b):
- The FULL --self-test passes with the Reagent-owned suppression disabled. Not one fixture depends on any of its three arms; their only measurable behaviour today is the false negative.

The suppression fails in both directions at once: pardons the unlawful adjacency, fails to protect the lawful idiom.
- Suppression-dependent hits in the live corpus: ZERO. 50 leaves / 7,416 lines + 4 bounded blocks; 11 :contextType occurrences on 7 physical lines; only the two frames.md lines become hooks-recipe sentences with the token and both are green via the tight negation, not the suppression. Re-running with the suppression deleted produces zero new findings.
- Option B (delete suppression, keep shared sentence scope) was measured to turn four natural lawful shapes red including the house style — its zero-new-findings result is fragile (one ordinary rewording away from fighting the corpus voice). Rejected in favour of C. Options A (keep hole) and D (parser) rejected.

CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION:
- The ⚠️ CAUTION ("tightening WILL surface currently-suppressed hits ... enumerate ... triage") is EMPIRICALLY DEFUSED: the suppression-disabled enumeration was done and the inventory is zero. Do not redo it as a triage exercise; just report the zero baseline in the PR so any new hit is visible.

title: Preserve record type in Xray concrete-query selectors
description:
PR #6274's local `canonical-str` promises an injective encoding of the full concrete-query identity, but its first branch is `(map? x)`. ClojureScript records satisfy `map?`, so the encoder discards their record tag/type and emits only canonicalized entries. Distinct concrete queries can still receive one `data-testid`.

Exact ClojureScript probe on current dependencies:
- `(defrecord A [x])`, `(defrecord B [x])`
- `a = (->A 1)`, `b = (->B 1)`, `m = {:x 1}`
- `(map? a)` and `(map? b)` are true.
- `(= a b)` and `(= a m)` are false.
- Applying the PR's map rendering to each produces the same string `{:x 1}`.

The product already calls out records as legal concrete query arguments in its fresh-object cache diagnostic (`map / collection / record built inline`), so this is not an exotic host-object expansion. Two surviving unchanged-sub rows keyed by these unequal query vectors remain unaddressable independently, violating rf2-haoip's every-distinct-valid-query AC and the updated normative Xray claim.

Preserve the small local solution. Add an explicit, stable record-type discriminator before canonicalizing record entries (and keep unordered extension entries canonical), or use an existing type-preserving canonical identity codec if one already exactly fits. title: Presence ruled DOM-agnostic/timeout-only: reconcile SPresence prose + ui/presence docstring to the ruling
description:
RULED 2026-07-18 (delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18 - full rationale in NOTES): presence stays DOM-AGNOSTIC and TIMEOUT-ONLY. No per-child wrapper/clone; :timeout-ms stays MANDATORY as THE exit retention duration and terminal bound; the three automatic refinements (transitionend early-completion, inert/aria-hidden on exit, reduced-motion immediate path) are REJECTED as framework automatics - presence-aware children own them via (presence-phase) = :unmounting. The SPresence prose bullets promising them are drift from the recorded Resolved-decisions ruling ('no reserved nodes'); this bead now carries the reconciliation.

SCOPE (doc/prose-only; spec/004-Views.md is HOT-ZONE - sequence): (1) spec/004-Views.md SPresence ~553-563 - retract the three automatic promises; reword :timeout-ms as the explicit retention duration + terminal bound; add author-facing guidance (child stamps inert/aria-hidden + exit class against :unmounting; the child's stylesheet owns prefers-reduced-motion); keep the hydration sentence and the 'not an animation system' framing. (2) implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui.cljc ui/presence docstring - drop 'exit completes OR ... whichever first'. (3) Sweep docs/ + skills/ for echoes of the retracted promises. Resolved-decisions line ~1213 and S4 conformance row ~1161 stand UNCHANGED. NO runtime/grammar/test changes; JVM parity untouched.

ACs: spec prose, public docstring, and runtime agree on timeout-only; no automatic-DOM promise remains on any tracked surface; the rf2-74vlo coupling honoured (presence-exit-interactive remedy = author-owned stamping, never framework inert-on-exit). Future seam (child-attached exit-scoped completion signal racing the mandatory timeout) is consumer-gated on the first presence-using re-com widget (rf2-6ajm6z) - new bead then, per NOTES.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-18 14:57 AUSEST, delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18):
D1 = STAY MINIMAL / DOM-AGNOSTIC. The presence surface does NOT expand: no per-child DOM wrapper, no clone/ref contract, no automatic transitionend completion, no automatic inert/aria-hidden, no framework-owned reduced-motion path.
D3 = :timeout-ms stays MANDATORY - it is THE exit retention duration and terminal bound, not a safety cap over a completion mechanism that does not exist.
D2 = the follow-through (spec-prose retraction) happens NOW; this bead is re-scoped to carry it.

RATIONALE (spot-verified against main 2026-07-18):
1. The spec-already-promises reframe, verified - and decisive in the OPPOSITE direction from the dossier's Option-C reading. spec/004-Views.md SPresence prose (~553-563) does promise all three refinements while the runtime (presence_runtime.cljc) is timeout-only, so staying minimal is indeed not a no-op: a spec edit is required either way. BUT the prose contradicts the recorded Resolved-decisions ruling itself (line ~1213: 'wrapper form, NO RESERVED NODES; :timeout-ms mandatory') and the section's own boundedness declaration ('not an animation system - anything beyond enter/exit retention is out of scope', ~544-545); the S4 conformance row (~1161) matches the implementation. The prose bullets are DRIFT from the ruling, not ruled promises. Retracting them RESTORES the recorded ruling; expanding would OVERTURN it. The truth defect is fixed by reconciling prose to ruling.
2. Grammar correctness: presence children are fragments, compiled defviews, foreign components, and host elements - no uniform DOM root. A framework-inserted wrapper breaks HTML content models (ul>li), direct-child selectors, and SSR/hydration shape (the JVM emitter renders a fragment); display:contents removes the box, not the node or the content-model problem. cloneElement cannot reach a component's DOM (the defview declared-props ABI does not forward unknown host props to its root). Every automatic mechanism is false for part of the legal child grammar; a small contract true for every legal child wins under the masterpiece posture.
3. transitionend is not a one-event fact: one event per transitioned property, bubbling from descendants, transitioncancel yields no end event, and zero-duration transitions (exactly what reduced-motion CSS produces) never start so they fire NOTHING - a timer must always exist, and automatic first-event completion is wrong without an unambiguous DOM root + transition inventory the grammar cannot supply.
4. Automatic inert/aria-hidden is not a free a11y win: aria-hidden over sequentially-focusable descendants is itself a WCAG violation (ACT rule 6cfa84), and the HTML spec cautions inert is for content that is also visually obscured/non-critical - product facts the boundary cannot infer. The layer with that knowledge is the child / component library: presence-aware children (re-com widgets) stamp their own inert/aria-hidden + exit class against (presence-phase) = :unmounting. Explicit over implicit; trust the programmer; the same posture that rejected Suspense-as-loading for hiding behaviour in the substrate.
5. Determinism preserved: timeout-only keeps flush-presence! the sole and COMPLETE exit driver on both hosts; a browser-event completion route would create behaviour unit tests cannot reach.

FUTURE SEAM (ruled direction, consumer-gated - do NOT implement now; do NOT re-litigate from scratch): if the re-com port (rf2-6ajm6z) proves early completion materially necessary, the sanctioned extension is a narrow, exit-incarnation-scoped, idempotent completion signal delivered through presence context which the CHILD attaches to its own chosen DOM event (e.g. its onTransitionEnd on the root it knows); it funnels into the existing exactly-once fire-timer! registry (presence_runtime.cljc ~107-121, verified race-ready: a completion route is just a second route into the same atomic claim) racing the still-mandatory :timeout-ms. Wrapper elements, cloning, computed-style inference, and automatic attribute stamping remain rejected even then. File that bead (discovered-from this one) only when the first presence-consuming re-com widget lands.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (this bead, re-scoped; doc/prose-only; spec/004-Views.md is HOT-ZONE - sequence per CLAUDE.md):
- SPresence (~553-563): bullet 1 - the exiting child is retained for exactly :timeout-ms (mandatory, unit-suffixed, THE exit retention duration and terminal bound); drop 'until its transition/animation completes ... safety bound'. Bullet 3 - drop 'exiting children are inert/aria-hidden by default; reduced-motion takes the immediate path'; replace with author-facing guidance: presence-aware children own their exit styling and a11y - stamp inert/aria-hidden and the exit class against (presence-phase) = :unmounting; the child's stylesheet owns prefers-reduced-motion. KEEP 'hydration does not fabricate enter transitions' (S5-adjacent, outside this ruling) and keep the 'not an animation system' framing (now fully honest).
- Resolved-decisions line ~1213: stands unchanged (it was already correct); may append '(:timeout-ms is the exit duration - rf2-0ufty)'.
- Conformance row ~1161: unchanged (accurately names the fixtures that exist).
- implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui.cljc ui/presence docstring (~612-614): remove 'until its exit completes OR ... whichever first' -> retained until the mandatory :timeout-ms retention bound fires. presence_runtime.cljc docstring already truthful - no change.
- NO runtime, grammar, or test changes. JVM parity untouched (presence-phase -> :present; structural node; flush-presence! sole driver) - verified all DOM/clock code is cljs-fenced.
- Sweep docs/ + skills/ for prose echoing the three promises at implementation time (git grep transitionend/inert/aria-hidden/reduced-motion near presence on tracked files).

COUPLING TO rf2-74vlo (S4-C - that ruling can rely on this one): the presence-exit-interactive diagnostic is PROMOTED from interim mitigation to the PRIMARY a11y mechanism for exit windows. Its remedy prose must point at author-owned inert/aria-hidden against (presence-phase) = :unmounting - NOT at a framework inert-on-exit, which this ruling rejects; no S4-C check may depend on framework inert-on-exit existing. S4-C's 'Deps: after A' stands satisfied by S4-A as shipped.
CONVERGENCE NOTE (2026-07-18 15:30): an independent Codex analysis of the same decision dossier arrived after the delegated ruling above was recorded. It CONCURS with the ruling in full (for 0ufty: same conclusion incl. the retract-the-prose-promises call, with additional platform-contract citations — per-property transitionend/CSS-Transitions §6, React cloneElement-fragility guidance, W3C ACT rule 6cfa84 making automatic aria-hidden over focusable descendants itself a violation). Two independent analyses converging strengthens this ruling; no reconciliation needed.

Follow-up from rf2-3neiv (which fixed the conformance MATCHER test-side). Two core-src comment sites still DESCRIBE the retired frame-blind :flow registrar model as if reg-flow/destroy prune registrar rows. Per rf2-en00bk the :flow registrar kind is reserved-EMPTY (flows live in the per-frame {frame-id {flow-id flow-map}} store); nothing is ever written to or pruned from the registrar. Sites:
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc ~line 3738-3740: destroy-hook enumeration says ':flows/teardown-on-frame-destroy! — drop flows + last-inputs rows + dead :flow registrar slots.' (no registrar slots exist).
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc ~line 3996-3999: destroy-hook comment says 'prune the :flow registrar slot when the destroyed frame was the last owner.' (nothing to prune).
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc line 290: :flows/teardown-on-frame-destroy! :description says '...and any :flow registrar entries whose last owning frame was destroyed.' (no such entries).
Reconcile all three to the per-frame-store release language (Runtime-Architecture.md, Managed-Effects.md, spec/013 already reconciled by rf2-k8ir2; the runtime behaviour is CORRECT — comment-only edits, no behaviour change).

## Context
Deferred from rf2-3neiv because that PR was scoped test-side (test(flows): matcher fix, no rebuild) per the dispatch title + 'prefer test-side / no rebuild'. These comment edits are core-src and force an SCI-bundle rebuild disproportionate to comment-only changes — hence split out to amortize the rebuild.
acceptance_criteria:
- Both `frame.cljc` comments and the `late_bind/directory.cljc` description describe only release of the destroyed frame's sole per-frame flow-store slot, last-input rows, and pending-vacation state; none claims a `:flow` registrar row is pruned.
- `live_frame.cljc` no longer cites the removed `re-frame.flows.registry/_hot-reload-hook` as a current one-time registrar-hook precedent; retain only real current hook precedents or describe the local `defonce` law directly.
- Comment-only; zero runtime behavior change.
- Because all affected files are under `implementation/core/src` and are in the SCI playground input-digest roster, rebuild `docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js` (or batch with another required rebuild) and pass `sh scripts/check-playground-sci-freshness.sh`.

The flows hook no longer exists; single-store `reg-flow` invalidates directly. Fold this fourth core-src comment into this existing SCI-rebuild-amortized owner rather than create a duplicate. Separate non-core test/proof residue is owned independently from rf2-0p4jj.
2026-07-19: PR #6384. All four sites were COMMENT-wrong, code correct — no behavioural bug. teardown-on-frame-destroy! dissocs exactly flows/frame-last-inputs/frame-abandoned-output-paths; flows/src has zero register! calls, so no registrar row can exist to prune. EXTRA FINDING: the live_frame.cljc site cited TWO dead precedents, not one — re-frame.routing's `_url-bound-exclusivity-hook` also does not exist (check-url-bound-exclusivity! is a plain fn called from routing.cljc, never a defonce registrar hook). Repointed at substrate.observation/_registrar-hooks + subs.cache/_hot-reload-hook.
