title: Dev-mode SSR hydration annotation asymmetry: client stamps data-rf-view, SSR emitter does not
description:
Discovered while proving rf2-byio7 (SSR startup recipe adopts server DOM).

In a DEV build, the reagent CLIENT render stamps BOTH `data-rf2-source-coord` AND `data-rf-view` on a registered-view (`reg-view`) root DOM element (re-frame.views.source-coord-annotation / substrate.spine cloneElement). The SSR HTML emitter `rf/render-to-string` (re-frame.ssr.emit/inject-coord-on-root-hiccup) stamps ONLY `data-rf2-source-coord` — never `data-rf-view`. reagent.dom.server/render-to-string of the same tree likewise did not reproduce the client annotations in a quick probe.

Consequence: for a REGISTERED view, server markup (from either emitter) can never byte-match the same view's dev client hydrate render, so React 18 treats hydration as a mismatch and REGENERATES the subtree — discarding the server DOM (the 'no flash / adopt existing DOM' property is lost in dev). Production elides both annotations (interop/debug-enabled? gate + closure DCE), so prod hydration is clean; the divergence is dev-only.

This is why the rf2-byio7 proof (PR #6250) uses a PLAIN component (no view annotations either side) to get a clean adopt signal, rather than a reg-view.

Scope to decide: (a) confirm/quantify — does the SHIPPED capability example (examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr, reg-view-based) actually regenerate on dev hydration? (b) if so, should the SSR emitter also stamp data-rf-view for parity (making dev adoption clean), or is the dev-only regeneration acceptable (prod is fine)? The existing source_coord_parity_test only pins the data-rf2-source-coord VALUE format across hosts, not that both sides emit data-rf-view.

Files: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc (inject-coord-on-root-hiccup), implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/source_coord_annotation.cljs, implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs (~1354).
notes:
RULING (Mike, 2026-07-18 18:00 AUSEST): Dev-mode view annotation is part of the view-registration contract on every host; SSR emitters carry no annotation logic. This is a dev-tooling decision, not an SSR feature: data-rf2-source-coord and data-rf-view are debug-gated development evidence for the programmer and AI tooling. Production output is annotation-free on both hosts and stays that way. The dev hydration warning is cited as the evidence the server half of the contract was missing, not as the thing being fixed.

IMPLEMENTATION (Option A-prime from the decision analysis; the emitter-side Option A is rejected — it only reaches keyword-ref boundaries, which hydratable pages cannot use):

1. In core reg-view* :clj branch, wrap the registered :handler-fn in a debug-gated annotation walk mirroring Spec 006's client injection rules: merge both :data-rf2-source-coord and :data-rf-view (value = (str id), same as client format-view-id) onto a hiccup DOM-tag root; preserve author-supplied values; recurse through Form-2 fns; skip fragment/fn-head roots per the documented exemption; degrade coordless (programmatic) registrations to the client's <ns>:<sym>:?:? coord form so both hosts match there too.

2. DELETE emitter-side injection: inject-coord-on-root-hiccup and both call sites (re-frame.ssr.emit, re-frame.ssr.streaming). Streaming shell/fallbacks/continuations inherit annotation through the wrapped handler-fn. This also removes the latent dev-mode arity leak where a keyword view-ref root got the coord map spliced in as the inner view's first argument.

3. No config knob, no wrapper element, no hydration-warning suppression, no post-hydration DOM patch, no ownership of Reagent's separate server renderer.

4. Specs: Spec 011 says SSR mirrors Spec 006's full view-tagging contract at the registration boundary (both attributes, value format, root exemption, preservation, production gate); Spec 006 names the registration boundary as the single architectural home on every host. Both are hot-zone files — sequence the spec edits.

5. Tests: standard + streaming parity; debug on/off; author-supplied value preservation; fn-ref composition parity against the client wrapper's output (the shape hydratable pages actually use); keyword-root shape; coordless-slot degrade parity; render-hash verify on the shipped example flow; browser hydration regression with a REGISTERED view (server node identity survives, handler live, NO hydration warning, both attributes present). Correct the plain-component adoption test's causal commentary: on React 18.3/19.2 an attribute-only mismatch warns and is left unpatched but does NOT replace the node — this bead's original "React regenerates the subtree" claim is refuted by browser probe.

KEY EVIDENCE (full dossier ai/decisions/rf2-8vi4q.dev-ssr-view-annotation-parity.md removed after ruling, per Mike): keyword view-refs are resolved only by the two JVM emitters and cannot render client-side (Reagent parse-tag drops keyword namespaces), so isomorphic pages compose via (rf/view :id) fn-refs, where the JVM stores the raw unwrapped handler-fn — emitter-side annotation therefore never fires on any boundary a hydratable page actually contains; the shipped non-streaming example reaches its DOM root with neither attribute server-side while the client stamps both.

Separate follow-up (NOT in this ruling's scope): the streaming example's shared views embed keyword refs ([:dashboard/card :revenue]) that the client renders as literal <card> DOM tags — deeper isomorphism break, filed as its own bead.
⚠️ YOU NOW INHERIT A HALF-DONE STEP 2 — from rf2-j81hs (#6378, 2026-07-19).

The j81hs ruling §5 said to sequence emit.cljc/streaming.cljc with-or-after this bead. That sequencing was INVERTED in practice: j81hs landed first because this bead is open, unclaimed, with no PR and no live worker (so there was no edit collision, but also nothing to sequence behind).

CONSEQUENCE, per the ruling that the coord injection "dies WITH the branch": server-side source-coord annotation is now STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE. j81hs deleted the keyword-head probe from both emitters and removed registrar + interop as dead requires, leaving the JVM emitter a pure hiccup->HTML function with no registry dependency.

WHAT j81hs DELIBERATELY LEFT FOR YOU: format-view-source-coord and inject-coord-on-root-hiccup are still in place. It did NOT delete them, so as not to pre-empt this beads design. It pinned the interim ABSENCE in both affected namespaces, and re-pinned the production-elision guarantee as an UNCONDITIONAL so it cannot lapse in the gap.

SO YOUR SCOPE IS NOW: decide whether the dev-mode SSR hydration annotation asymmetry (client stamps data-rf-view, SSR does not) is resolved by deleting those two functions outright, or by re-establishing the annotation through a route that does not reintroduce a registry dependency in the emitter. Read gh pr diff 6378 first — the emitter purity it achieved is a real simplification and should not be undone casually.

⚠️ Also from j81hs: examples/ README still asserts the emitter resolves keyword heads, which is now FALSE. That correction is owned by rf2-ycz3k (the example rewrite), not by this bead.
IMPLEMENTED (worker, gates green): annotation moved to reg-view* :clj branch via new re-frame.views.jvm-source-coord-annotation (debug-gated hiccup walk mirroring client rules — Form-2 recursion, DOM-tag root merge preserving author values, fragment/callable-head skip, coordless <ns>:<sym>:?:? degrade). Emitter-side format-view-source-coord + inject-coord-on-root-hiccup DELETED (call sites already gone in #6378); ssr.cljc re-export removed. Tests: JVM ssr_source_coord_test rewritten (annotation-present + prod-gate arms), source_coord_parity_test extended to pin data-rf-view + end-to-end callable-head render, CLJS parity companion extended, NEW browser twin-run adoption proof (reg-view adopts annotated server markup / RED-before complains), byio7 causal commentary corrected, ssr_keyword_head_contract + smoke updated for the new dev annotation. No new error id, no spec/009 row. SPEC 006/011 prose edits STOPPED (hot-zone; spec/011 has live phaseflip-spec-jygc8 worker) — filed rf2-0qpqu to land them after phaseflip merges. Gates: core JVM 2088/0, ssr JVM 491/0, cljs 10273/0, browser 495/0, elision PASS (prod 60/60 absent, control 60/60 present), browser-prod-elision 113/0.

title: Reconcile reserved-fx source/target policy across specs and diagnostics
description:
PR #6243 / rf2-1w4af split the old `rejected-reserved-fx-ids` into two independent policies: `non-overridable-source-fx-ids` and the narrower `non-redirectable-target-fx-ids` (join-dispatch alone). Current `spec/Conventions.md` §Reserved fx-ids and Spec 005/009 still describe the old single conflated REJECT set and falsely say every non-overridable source is also a non-redirectable target. Reconcile those normative surfaces to the shipped source-vs-target contract; this is the original docs/spec-only residue and includes the Conventions hot zone.

The capped merged-PR audit rf2-w6th6 also found the same conceptual drift in programmer-facing runtime diagnostics, so include the bounded implementation correction rather than file a duplicate. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc`'s always-on `:rf.error/reserved-fx-override` reason says every rejected source installs/clears durable runtime state or threads a nav-token. That is false for direct `:rf.machine/join-dispatch` overrides: its independent source rationale is protecting the private join-completion transport from capture/suppression. The introductory roster in `fx_test.clj` likewise omits join-dispatch. Make the diagnostic policy-accurate or id-specific and pin its reason. Do not change runtime policy or add error ids.
acceptance_criteria:
- Conventions §Reserved fx-ids and Specs 005/009 distinguish non-overridable sources from non-redirectable targets and no longer claim the whole source set is target-protected.
- The normative roster states that spawn/destroy and other directly registered source-protected effects may still be legitimate redirect targets; join-dispatch alone retains the redirect-specific private-transport/self-recursion fence unless runtime policy deliberately changes in the same work.
- `:rf.error/reserved-fx-override` gives an accurate reason for every source-policy member, including the private join-completion transport; a direct join-dispatch override is not described as a runtime-state or nav-token write.
- Focused tests assert the join-dispatch diagnostic rationale and keep existing source-vs-target behavior unchanged.
- Existing error ids, recoveries, effect resolution, and registry machinery remain unchanged; this is a bounded truth/ergonomics reconciliation.
- Conventions hot-zone sequencing is respected and focused core/machines/docs gates pass.
notes:
Expanded while auditing #6243 under rf2-w6th6. The original normative spec residue remains this Bead's core scope; added the adjacent unowned always-on diagnostic/test-prose correction so the same two-policy reconciliation is completed once, without a duplicate P3.
PR #6386 (worker/reserved-fx-0qsp5). VERDICT: docs wrong, code right — no behavioural bug. Registrar: non-overridable-source-fx-ids = {spawn destroy join-dispatch reg-flow clear-flow with-nav-token} (6); non-redirectable-target-fx-ids = {join-dispatch} (1). The split is correctly implemented and already pinned by fx_test §7d + join_authority_effect_path_test §8. Flagship doc defect: Conventions §Reserved fx-ids asserted '{:dispatch :rf.machine/spawn} is refused' — classify-fx-override returns :applied-redirect for it. 002/009 rosters listed 5 of 6 source members (omitted join-dispatch); 005 derived target-protection FROM reject-tier membership (invalidated inference, true conclusion). Diagnostic :reason was blanket 'installs/clears durable runtime state (or threads a nav-token)' — false for join-dispatch; now derived per id + states source-vs-target. NO Spec 009 shape change owed (:reason already a string in existing :tags — data-inside-existing-tag case); 009 row changed for its own prose defect. New fx_test §7e: red-before 8 failures, green-after. Gates: core 2074t/9930a, machines 1197t/4172a, cljs 10099t/49944a, error-catalogue 9t/21a, drift+slugs+mkdocs --strict+paths all exit 0. rf2-3ec16 NOT absorbed. Spotted not actioned: join-dispatch has no row in the Conventions reserved-fx-ids TABLE (prose only) — separate editorial call.

title: Remove :rf2/runtime-version late-bind hook — SSR-owned pattern-protocol constant read by both wire ends
description:
Ruled 2026-07-18 (delegated per Mike 2026-07-18): REMOVE the hook — full rationale + implementation guidance in NOTES. Supersedes the original governance framing (directory row / host-published marker / public knob all rejected).

TASK: delete the :rf2/runtime-version late-bind hook and make the SSR artefact own the hydration pattern-protocol version as a compiled-in constant (initially 1) read by both wire ends — server payload assembly (payload_policy.cljc resolve-version) and the client-side scalar :rf.ssr/check-version path (hydrate.cljc runtime-version-lookup). Keep the explicit :version payload-builder opt (higher priority) and the {:expected :actual} map form. Wire key :rf/version ([:rf/version :int], Spec-Schemas.md:3592) unchanged. Census baseline: 44 mentions across 14 files (2 src consumers, ~20 test sites, 3 hot-zone specs, docs/api + skills pages). One sequential PR (hot-zone: spec/011-SSR.md, spec/009-Instrumentation.md, spec/Conventions.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- Zero occurrences of :rf2/runtime-version in tracked files (git grep clean; baseline 44 mentions / 14 files).
- Version resolution: explicit :version opt -> SSR-owned constant; invalid explicit values emit :rf.ssr/invalid-version and fall back; every payload carries an integer :rf/version.
- Scalar :rf.ssr/check-version compares the server value against the compiled constant; genuine skew emits :rf.ssr/version-mismatch; hydration stays degraded-but-running; the version-side compatibility-check-skipped branch is removed (schema-digest half keeps the emit alive).
- spec/Conventions.md :rf2/<runtime-stamp> grammar row deleted + line-8 :rf2/* carve-out mention trimmed; spec/011-SSR.md:64 false client-fallback sentence fixed in the same PR; 009:1941-1942 re-scoped.
- Tests updated including the deliberate meaning shift (skipped-mode baselines -> silent 1==1 match), called out in commit/PR text; docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md + skills ssr-authoring.md updated.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-18, delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18): REMOVE the :rf2/runtime-version late-bind hook. Replace it with an SSR-artefact-owned pattern-protocol constant (integer, initially 1) read by BOTH wire ends — server payload assembly and the client-side scalar :rf.ssr/check-version path. Keep the explicit payload-builder :version opt and the {:expected :actual} map form for overrides/tests. NO host-published directory marker, NO facade/configure! knob, NO :ssr/ rename half-measure.

RATIONALE (keystones spot-verified during ruling): (1) DEAD BY DEFAULT — the in-tree reference Ring host (implementation/ssr-ring) never registers the hook (sole mention: payload.clj:35 docstring); the only set-fn! sites are test fixtures, so the promised check runs in skipped mode in every real deployment including our own. (2) OWNERSHIP BACKWARDS — Spec-Schemas.md:3592/3618 defines :rf/version as the hydration pattern-protocol version, a fact compiled into the SSR artefact's wire code; a host cannot know it better than the artefact, and a host publishing a different value lies to the check. title: State only portable next-tick guarantees across CLJS and JVM
description:
PR #6081 correctly changed the router contract from microtask to task scheduling, but its new prose adds two stronger host-ordering promises the implementations do not provide.

On CLJS, `interop.cljs`, Spec 002's heading/body, and `router_next_tick_ordering_cljs_test.cljs` say `goog.async.nextTick` is "not a timer" and avoids the nested-timer clamp. The pinned Closure 20250515 implementation prefers native `setImmediate` or a `MessageChannel`/postMessage emulation, but explicitly falls back to `setTimeout(cb, 0)` when those mechanisms are unavailable. The focused test proves only the portable property — nextTick runs after a same-stack `queueMicrotask` — so the timer fallback passes unchanged.

On the JVM, `interop.clj` says the single-thread executor callback runs "after the caller returns". `Executor.execute` creates no such ordering edge: the worker may start concurrently before `next-tick` returns. Spec 002 already states that this can happen and uses the drain lock to make it safe.

State the exact guarantees only: asynchronous task-style scheduling, not a host microtask; implementation choice and relative start-versus-return timing are host-dependent. This is wording/test naming, not a scheduler redesign.
acceptance_criteria:
- CLJS docs say `goog.async.nextTick` is task/macrotask scheduling and accurately describe preferred immediate/message-channel mechanisms plus the supported setTimeout fallback; they do not promise absence of timer clamping.
- JVM docs say the callback runs asynchronously on the executor and may start concurrently with the submitting caller; they do not promise it starts after the call returns.
- Spec 002, interop docstrings/comments, and focused test namespace/names assert only the portable microtask-vs-task boundary.
- The causal queueMicrotask ordering proof remains and fails if the CLJS primitive becomes a true microtask.
- Runtime scheduling and router locking are unchanged; no portability abstraction or gold-plated scheduler is added.

title: Elide the custom-element reload ledger from advanced production
description:

- `ledger-state` is an unconditional `defonce (atom {:sources {} :cycles {}})`;
- every production `register-custom-element!` still performs `swap-vals!` against that atom before updating `custom-elements`;
- production cannot open a reload cycle, so this state is unused bookkeeping rather than part of classification.

The added production test proves that producer installation is inert, the identity falls back, and the visible classification works. It does not inspect hidden source/cycle state. The bundle scanners also carry no custom-element ledger sentinel. Thus the test comments promise a stronger elision result than the artefact proves or delivers.

## Deliverable

Use a compile-time `goog.DEBUG` split in the CLJS registration/state path: development keeps the existing source/cycle ledger; advanced production performs the one direct aggregate update it actually needs. Keep the JVM path needed by compiler/test fixtures. Add both lexical and causal elision proof so a future refactor cannot leave a renamed rooted atom behind.

This is a small pre-alpha cleanup, not a generalized registry abstraction or micro-optimization campaign.

## Provenance and dedupe

Found during the chronological completeness/quality audit of PR #6018. All-status search found only closed `.142`; no live issue owns the production residue.
acceptance_criteria:
- In advanced CLJS production, emitted custom-element registration updates the live property classification directly; no source/cycle ledger atom is allocated, rooted, read, or mutated.
- The dev build retains the one authoritative ledger and all reload semantics unchanged; JVM/test behavior remains available where required.
- A lexical advanced-bundle sentinel proves the ledger/reload state is unreachable, and a causal runtime oracle proves registration leaves no hidden ledger/root residue.
- A development-positive control proves the sentinel would fail if the ledger branch were accidentally removed from dev as well.
- Production lookup stays a direct map read and emitted registration remains once per declaration, never per render.
- No second production registry, public switch, compatibility branch, or measurable per-render cost is introduced.

title: Make observation current? total across throwing opaque equality
description:
## Current defect

PR #6014 / rf2-tuysqw reconciled the observation-port prose so `current?` is a total, pure, never-throw predicate, matching its docstring and the malformed/non-lease behavior. A supported `:story-override` lease can nevertheless throw through its opaque version comparison:

```clojure
(deftype Boom [] Object
  (equals [_ _] (throw (ex-info "boom-from-equals" {}))))

(let [target {:kind :story-override
              :query [:demo/q]
              :value nil
              :override-id :slot
              :version (Boom.)}
      lease (obs/acquire! target nil)]
  (obs/current? lease (assoc target :version (Boom.))))
```

Current JVM result is `THREW boom-from-equals`. The target passes the port grammar and acquisition; the exception escapes later through `node-value=`. Non-lease `current?` and `owned?` correctly return false. All-status searches for throwing equality, opaque version, and current?/never-throws found no owner; closed rf2-tuysqw and rf2-vxgfnd.241 are related but do not cover opaque token equality.

## Bounded repair

Honor the total predicate contract at the kept-check boundary: an equality comparison that cannot establish sameness should classify the lease as not current, without weakening fail-loud behavior of the port’s non-predicate operations. Keep the catch local to predicate comparison unless evidence shows a shared no-throw equality helper is needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- `current?` returns false, never throws, when a supported target/lease comparison encounters a version or identity token whose host equality implementation throws.
- Equivalent JVM and CLJS adversarial fixtures exercise throwing equality through a real acquired static/story-override lease.
- Ordinary identical/equal tokens remain current; unequal, released, malformed/non-lease, moved-frame, and retargeted controls retain their existing results.
- `probe`, `acquire!`, `read`, and `release!` keep their existing typed fail-loud contracts; the repair does not blanket-swallow equality failures outside the documented total predicate.
- Observation-port docs, Ownership wording, implementation docstrings, and tests continue to state one exact total/no-throw predicate contract.

title: Qualify parallel-always order independence and remove stale birth wording
description:
## Problem

PR #6008 correctly implemented and taught parent-owned parallel `:always` rounds, but two current teaching surfaces still overstate or contradict the law.

At current `origin/main`:

- `docs/machines/parallel-states.md:321` says reordering regions "cannot change the outcome" and declaration order never changes which transitions are chosen. Frozen selection guarantees that only within one round. Because selected actions apply in declaration order, non-commuting shared-`:data` writes can change the data frozen for a later `:always` round and therefore change a later selected transition.
- `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_property_cljs_test.cljc` invariant 9 broadly says reordering cannot change resolved configuration or data, although the actual generator makes writes commute.
- `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/birth_always_cljs_test.cljc:37,248-251,359-361` still says parallel birth `:always` transitions "settle independently". The assertions are valid for uncoupled guards, but that wording is the superseded region-local model that the guide truth guard itself classifies as false.

A concrete counterexample has regions A and B handle one event with ordered writes of `:x` to 1 and 2, then region C chooses a next-round guarded `:always` target from `:x`. Reversing A/B leaves each round's selection atomic but changes the later frozen value and C's target.

## Required correction

Qualify order independence to frozen selection within a round, and state plainly that non-commuting apply-phase writes may affect later rounds. Rename the stale birth fixtures/descriptions using parent-owned freeze/select/apply-round terminology. Extend the terminology protection to the executable teaching surface so the superseded "settles independently" claim cannot return.
acceptance_criteria:
- The guide no longer claims unconditional outcome independence under region reordering.
- It distinguishes order-independent selection within one frozen round from declaration-ordered action/data application and possible effects on later rounds.

title: defview header: qualified-group-symbol name-collides-explicit leaves a dead comparator/manifest slot (collapse invariant violated)
description:
Shape-3 review of #6075 (rf2-qa5wkd). The canonical binding plan is host-faithful for BINDING VALUE on every defview header shape (verified vs clojure.core/destructure). But for the shape {:keys [ns/x] x :other} — a QUALIFIED :keys group symbol whose bare NAME collides an explicit local — parse-header produces TWO :entries both {:pattern x}: [{:key :other :slot other :pattern x} {:key :ns/x :slot ns/x :pattern x}], slots => [:other :ns/x].

Impact (LOW): binding value is correct on both hosts (x <- :ns/x, last-wins matches host bes-order native destructure). The wart is the DEAD slot :other surviving in declared-slots -> the memo comparator over-compares (spurious re-renders when :other changes but :ns/x does not) and the manifest :prop-slots over-declares :other (and under CLOSED :props, :other is silently accepted). It also VIOLATES the invariant the PR advertises in three docstrings (header.cljc:117-119, binding_plan.cljc:21-25, emit_cljs.cljc:575): 'two header entries binding the same local COLLAPSE to a single entry - never two'. The collapse only holds when the group symbol's FULL identity equals the explicit local (e.g. {:keys [x] x :foo}); a qualified group symbol does not collide in the host bes map so it does not collapse.

Pre-existing (OLD parser also emitted two entries); #6075 correctly FIXED the binding order for this shape but did not remove the dead slot.

Fix sketch: in header/parse-header, after building entries, de-dup by :pattern keeping the LAST (host bes-order winner) -> collapse to [{:pattern x :key :ns/x}], slots [:ns/x]. Makes the invariant true and drops the dead slot. CAVEAT to rule: dropping :other from declared slots changes CLOSED-:props acceptance for :other (arguably correct since the :other binding is dead) - semantic call, hence file-and-rule not silent-fix. Alternative: keep behaviour, soften the docstring invariant wording.

Files: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/header.cljc:150-163; emit_cljs.cljc:568-586; compiler.cljc:253-260. Repro: header {:keys [ns/x] x :other}.
close_reason: shipped via PR #6083 (merged): defview {:keys [ns/x] x :other} left dead comparator/manifest slot :other (spurious re-renders + over-declared prop; collapse invariant violated). Added header/collapse-entries folding units by bound local (host bes-order winner); analyzer scope-walk still sees both units. CLOSED-:props behaviour fix (dead-shadowed :other now correctly rejected; OPEN unchanged) — clear-fix, pinned both ways. Proven vs real JVM destructure

title: capture-frame bundle :subscribe is not incarnation-fenced (retargets same-id successor)
description:
Shape-3 audit of #6079 (rf2-9pyles). The rf2-9pyles capture fence wraps ONLY :dispatch/:dispatch-sync of the make-capture-frame bundle (capture-dispatch!, core.cljc:1177-1183,1233-1244). The :subscribe closure (core.cljc:1245-1251) is unchanged — (subscribe-impl query-v {:frame frame}) with no captured-token gate; subscribe-impl=subs/subscribe resolves address-directed at call time.

FAILURE: a capture pinned to incarnation A, after A is destroyed and a same-id successor B reseats, SILENTLY subscribes into B (reads B app-db, caches a reaction in B sub-cache) instead of recover-but-emit :rf.error/frame-destroyed. This is the same silent cross-incarnation retarget rf2-9pyles closed for dispatch. Asymmetry: the SYNCHRONOUS (frame) bundle already fences subscribe (re-frame.ui.frames/fence-subscribe throws, frames.cljc:1199-1213,1239), and Spec 006:475 calls the capture fence 'the async-safe sibling of the throwing fence the (frame) bundle already applies' — implying a parity subscribe does not have.

Read-only, no mutation of B (subscribe is read-only; bead AC was mutation-scoped), and async-callback subscribe from a capture is unusual+leaky — hence LOW/P3. But it is a silent wrong-incarnation read + persisted reaction leak into B, the class of bug this fence family exists to kill.

FIX (either): (a) fence the capture :subscribe with the same capture-target-superseded? gate, recover-but-emit :rf.error/frame-destroyed and return nil (async analogue of fence-subscribe's throw); or (b) if subscribe is deliberately address-directed, say so in the core.cljc fence comment (core.cljc:1140-1171 names only dispatch/dispatch-sync) AND soften Spec 006:475 so 'sibling…already applies' does not imply subscribe parity.

Ref: ai/findings/2026-07-17-review-incarnation.md Finding 1.

title: publish-commit! registry-axis linearization overstated in docstring (residual check-to-use window)
description:
Shape-3 review of #6078 (rf2-77pb08). publish-commit! (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc:3516-3582) fuses final HMR body-authority validation with state publication. The CELL-LOCAL axis is a genuine single-atom CAS linearization (airtight). The REGISTRY axis is a best-effort slot-identity gate: (and (identical? token (get @view-generations view-id)) (compare-and-set! st s published)) reads TWO different atoms, so there is a residual two-expression window (identical? read -> st CAS) in which a concurrent re-registration would publish a stale-revision capture (st untouched by the registry swap, so the CAS still succeeds).

NOT a correctness defect: unreachable on the single-threaded CLJS render host (where HMR/registry authority lives) - no preemption between two non-yielding expressions and no callback runs in the window (accept-capture/published computed before the if). The :pre-publish barrier fires at loop top (before the identical?/CAS block), and the JVM two-thread probe parks fully at that barrier (CountDownLatch handoff), so neither exercises the identical?->CAS window. Reopens ONLY under out-of-contract unsynchronized multi-threaded concurrent commit+re-registration of the same view; JVM production DCEs the whole arm (debug-enabled? false).

Actionable = doc precision only: the docstring (reactive.cljc:3516-3520, 3543-3550) says validation+publication are 'ONE compare-and-set! transition' with the registry token identical? 'at the instant of the CAS'. That overstates the registry axis and could mislead a future maintainer / async-host author. Fix: state cell-local axis = genuine single-atom linearization; registry axis = best-effort slot-identity gate consulted immediately before the CAS (correct on single-threaded host, residual sub-instruction window only under out-of-contract concurrency). Replace 'at the instant of the CAS' with 'immediately before the CAS'. No code change. Hot-zone: reactive.cljc is NOT in the hot-zone list; single-artefact doc edit.

title: Sweep residual 'data loop' / 'dataflow loop' language to 'event pipeline'
description:
## Why
Canonical vocabulary is **event pipeline** / **pipeline run** (glossary + docs/core/AUTHORING.md). Older spellings (event cascade, turn of the loop, the loop, data loop, dataflow loop) are retired for the event-traversal sense. Residual 'data loop' / 'dataflow loop' phrasing still lives in a few surfaces and steers AIs and authors off the ruled term.

## What
Review the repo for residual terminology and rewrite to event-pipeline language. Do not invent a second synonym; prefer **event pipeline** (structure) and **pipeline run** (one traversal) per glossary.

## Known leftovers (starting inventory — re-search; do not treat as complete)
- docs/api/re-frame.ui.md — 'pure dataflow loop'
- spec/Tool-Pair.md — 'data loop'
- skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/initial-spec.md — 'data loop'
- skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs — 'data loop' (comment)
- examples/core/counter/README.md — 'dataflow loop'
- examples/core/notebook/core.cljs — 'dataflow loop'
- ai/findings/re-frame-ui-guide.html — local-only; optional fix, not commit

## Scope notes
- Search case-insensitively for: data loop, dataflow loop, data-flow loop, turn of the loop, event cascade (event-traversal sense only).
- Legitimate 'loop' uses stay: drain loop, dispatch cycle, for/loop index, microstep loop, agent loops, etc. (AUTHORING.md).
- Machines cancellation cascade keeps its name.
- Do not rewrite historical/migration prose that is deliberately quoting retired terms if the surrounding text already teaches the preferred name — but prefer updating teaching surfaces.

## Acceptance
- Repo search for 'data loop' and 'dataflow loop' is clean on committed teaching/spec/skill/example surfaces (or remaining hits are justified comments/history).
- Wording uses event pipeline / pipeline run consistently where the event-traversal structure was meant.
- No drive-by refactors outside terminology.
acceptance_criteria: Search for data loop / dataflow loop is clean on committed teaching surfaces; event pipeline / pipeline run used; legitimate loop uses preserved
notes:
AUDIT REOPEN 2026-07-17 (PR #6023): the touched teaching/spec surfaces still contain retired event-traversal synonyms, and one replacement introduced a false purity claim.

Current residues: examples/core/counter/README.md says buttons "drive the loop"; skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs and spec/Tool-Pair.md say "dispatch loop" (runtime also says "no cascade"). These are event-pipeline traversal uses, not legitimate algorithm/event-loop senses under rf2-glw1bh. docs/api/re-frame.ui.md now links to "the pure event pipeline"; the entire pipeline is not pure because commit/perform executes impure effects and is best-effort after the db write. Say the event pipeline without the false adjective, or precisely identify pure handlers/subscriptions.

Acceptance additions: re-search the complete touched files for loop/cascade senses, correct these four current sites, and add/extend the vocabulary residue gate so variants cannot recur. Historical EP uses may remain when clearly historical.

title: test(docs): guard parallel :always parent-round terminology from reverting
description:
## Problem

rf2-1rdo4j rewrote `docs/machines/parallel-states.md` around the ratified parent-owned `:always` round law (PR for rf2-42xtcd / rf2-1rdo4j). Its acceptance criteria asked for 'a focused docs/fixture check protects the load-bearing terminology from reverting'. That criterion was NOT delivered: the implementing agent's file-ownership fence covered only the guide itself and `machine_property_cljs_test.cljc`, and the guard needs a new file.

The executable protection for the LAW shipped (property INVARIANT 9 + the pinned `parallel-always-round-*` deftests fail if the engine reverts). What is unprotected is the GUIDE reverting to region-local prose while the engine stays correct — the exact drift that produced rf2-1rdo4j.

## Deliverable

A focused check that fails if the guide reacquires the superseded claims. Cheapest credible shape: a grep-style assertion over `docs/machines/parallel-states.md` rejecting the reverted phrasings ('settles independently', 'per region' applied to the always loop, 'converges on the NEXT EVENT', 'frozen ... for the whole macrostep') and requiring the load-bearing terms ('parent-owned', 'round', 're-freeze'). Decide the home: a docs-drift gate alongside the existing skill<->MCP-drift gates, or a small test in the machines artefact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The check fails on a deliberate revert of any of the four superseded claims.
- It does not fire on legitimate uses of the same words elsewhere in the guide (e.g. ':bump-count runs ONCE PER REGION' describes the apply phase and is correct).
- Runs in an existing CI gate; no new workflow.

## Evidence and provenance

Filed from the rf2-42xtcd / rf2-1rdo4j implementation. Guide + property tier are on branch worker/machines-parallel-rounds. Spec 005 §Per-region `:always` / `:after` / `:spawn` scoping is the law reference (do not edit; hot-zone).

title: Descriptor fail-closed during HMR fence — RULED Option A (field-level): document contract in client.cljs docstrings, no logic change
description:
Follow-up of rf2-vxgfnd.242 (PR #5943). The .242 oracle proves descriptor fail-closed at the :build-digest FIELD level (nil during the HMR digest fence, exact after); the worker flagged a stricter possible reading (client/descriptor / descriptor-index returning nil / omitting entries entirely while fenced).

RULED 2026-07-15 (delegated): Option A — field-level fail-closed IS the contract; the whole descriptor stays present with :build-digest nil during the fence. Remaining work is docstring-only: state the fence contract on client/descriptor and descriptor-index (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/client.cljs ~193-216, optionally the block comment ~163-182). No logic change, no oracle change. See NOTES for full rationale and acceptance.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option A — field-level fail-closed is sufficient and is the intended contract. During the HMR digest fence, client/descriptor and descriptor-index return the truthy static core with :build-digest nil (exact digest after promotion); the whole descriptor is NOT absented. No client.cljs logic change; document the contract and close.

RATIONALE: Both recorded opinions (holder recommendation + CComposer analysis in the decision file) converge on A, and the code confirms it: descriptor/descriptor-index are thin read-time projections that assoc :build-digest from digest-carrier/current, which is nil while fenced — the digest is the only field carrying build identity, so the no-leak invariant proven by the .242 oracle is fully closed at the field level. Absenting the whole map (Option B) would overload nil (not-live / pre-render! / production / fenced become indistinguishable — a CLARITY loss), discard legitimately stable static-core fields (Spec 004C: static core is last-known-good per root), and add production code for a stricter guarantee no in-tree consumer needs — gold-plating. Field-level is the smallest correct thing and matches the shipped .205 hookless pattern (:build-digest nil on a truthy descriptor as the honest "identity not yet committed" negative).

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE: Docstring-only change in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/client.cljs — state the fence contract on `descriptor` (~193-201) and `descriptor-index` (~203-216), optionally extend the block comment at ~163-182: during an active HMR digest fence these surfaces return the static core with :build-digest nil; consumers requiring a FINALIZED complete descriptor must treat a nil digest as "not yet known" and must not infer build identity from the static core alone mid-fence. No logic change to descriptor / descriptor-index / digest_carrier.cljs; no oracle change (.242 field-level assertions in check-ui-digest-carrier.cjs remain the shipped proof). Acceptance: docstrings state the contract, behaviour untouched, existing gates green. Close on merge.

title: Make the JVM preflight race proof causal and correct its caller claim
description:
## Problem

PR #5834 at exact authored head e2b518f946270d48b2d31f36b6cd420b9a4a435d adds frame_plan_preflight_race_jvm_test.clj and calls its latch arm deterministic proof that removing JVM serialization exposes the decide/record race. The fixture can false-green on the unmodified implementation.

In concurrent-install-serializes-and-the-loser-sees-the-winners-record:

- Root A is causally paused inside initial-event drain.
- Root B is submitted as a future.
- The test immediately checks (deref b 250 ::pending), but has no latch proving B started or attempted executor admission.
- If the scheduler does not run B during those 250 ms, the pending assertion passes even without the lock. After A is released and publishes, B runs serially by scheduling alone and observes the completed record, so all later assertions also pass.

The 50-repetition CyclicBarrier arm is stress coverage, not a deterministic counterexample. A barrier releases both callers together but a legal scheduler can still run one complete preflight before the other reaches phase 1; the unmodified implementation then produces the expected one-winner/one-conflict result. Stress probability is useful supplemental evidence, not a proof that must fail pre-fix.

The fixture's namespace docstring at lines 10-12 also says ui.test/render drives execute-frame-plans! on the JVM since #5720. At this exact head, implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/test.cljc:991-1046 performs exclusive direct make-frame installs, and its own line 1018 note says production execute-frame-plans! semantics are deliberately unchanged. Repository callers are the CLJS client host plus direct executor tests. Therefore the current JVM fixture proves the internal CLJC executor, not a real ui.test host path.

This is separate from the executor authority/deadlock work in open rf2-vxgfnd.191. It owns the quality and honesty of the regression proof that bead .191 is required to keep green.

## Deliverable

Make the pre-fix race proof causal and correct its reachability claim:

- Coordinate both callers so the test knows B reached the relevant admission/decision window while A's run is still open; a scheduler delay must not satisfy the assertion.
- Prefer test-local instrumentation or controlled with-redefs/barriers over a production-visible hook. If a seam is unavoidable, keep it JVM test-only, private, zero-cost in production, and narrowly named.
- Preserve a separate stress arm if it provides useful scheduler breadth, but label it probabilistic/stress rather than deterministic proof.
- Demonstrate mechanically that removing/bypassing the serialize-or-reservation mechanism makes the deterministic fixture fail on every run.
- Rewrite test/source rationale to name actual current callers. Add a host-level JVM/SSR proof only when such a host starts using this executor; do not imply ui.test/render does today.
- Keep the test compatible with rf2-vxgfnd.191's likely coordination redesign; prove the behavior, not the current global-monitor mechanism.

Do not add sleeps as causal proof, make the suite timing-fragile, or retain the global monitor merely to satisfy a lock-shaped assertion.

## Proof

Run the focused test repeatedly against both fixed and lock/reservation-disabled mutations. Fixed must be stable; each mutation must fail deterministically before any broad suite is considered. Ensure failed assertions cannot strand futures, latches, frame drains, or the JVM process.
acceptance_criteria:
- The focused two-caller fixture proves B entered the intended contention/decision window before A is released; scheduler non-start cannot count as success.
- Removing or bypassing the concurrency control fails the deterministic arm on every repeated run.
- The stress arm, if retained, is explicitly supplemental and does not carry the mutation-killing claim.
- Namespace/source docstrings accurately distinguish current direct JVM executor tests, the CLJS client host, ui.test/render's separate exclusive path, and any future S5 JVM/SSR caller.
- Tests use bounded waits with cleanup that cannot strand a future, drain lock, latch, or process on assertion failure.
- rf2-vxgfnd.191's eventual coordination shape can satisfy the test without preserving a process-wide monitor.
- Focused JVM UI tests and the fast PR spine remain green; no production/runtime API or CLJS cost is added for test instrumentation.
close_reason: Merged PR #5986 at exact reviewed head 26a7bf710218071af34b95a0873f35d3e99864ed; deterministic causal race proof, Throwable-safe cleanup, full CI green.

title: Keep quoted sub-read lookalikes opaque to compiler hoisting
description:
## Problem

PR #5821 introduced a post-emission literal-query hoister and a template-fingerprint projection that recognize compiler-lowered reads solely by the list shape `(re-frame.ui.reactive/sub-read sid query)`. Both walkers recurse indiscriminately through quoted forms.

A quoted data value that merely resembles the internal form is therefore rewritten even though the compiler's expression analyzer correctly treats quote as non-executable. Executed on current main using the real hoister:

```
input  (str '(re-frame.ui.reactive/sub-read :fake [:q]))
output (str '(re-frame.ui.reactive/sub-read :fake quoted-shape$query$0))
defs   [(def quoted-shape$query$0 [:q])]
```

At runtime, the quoted vector `[:q]` has become the symbol `quoted-shape$query$0`; quote prevents that symbol from resolving to the hoisted value. The rendered/user data is observably wrong. `template-fingerprint-projection` likewise rewrites a quoted lookalike into `(re-frame.ui/sub ...)`, so build identity no longer fingerprints the authored literal.

The trigger uses an internal-looking fully-qualified symbol, so severity is low, but compiler transformations must preserve ordinary Clojure quote semantics. There is no all-status bead for quoted sub-read shapes, quote-aware hoisting, or this literal-data corruption.

## Expected behavior

Only executable compiler-owned lowering nodes are candidates for query hoisting or sid stripping. Quoted data is opaque and round-trips exactly, regardless of whether it resembles an internal form.
design:
Make both compiler transformations quote-aware:

- Stop descending into the payload of `(quote ...)` / reader quote in `hoist-literal-sub-queries` and `template-fingerprint-projection`.
- Prefer recognizing compiler-owned lowered nodes using their known manifest sid set or a private compiler marker in addition to raw list shape; do not trust arbitrary user data solely because its first symbol matches an internal var.
- Preserve metadata and spelling of untouched quoted forms.
- Keep literal query hoisting for genuine executable compiler-lowered reads and retain cross-site dedup only where currently intended.
- Use a small dedicated recursive walker rather than a general postwalk if that is the clearest correct shape.
acceptance_criteria:
- A defview containing quoted `(re-frame.ui.reactive/sub-read :fake [:q])` returns/renders that exact data; no query def is synthesized for the quoted lookalike.
- Nested quote payloads inside lists, vectors, maps, and sets are likewise byte/EDN-equivalent after compilation.
- Template/build fingerprint projection retains the complete quoted literal and changes when that literal's sid/query-looking data changes.
- Genuine executable compiler-lowered literal queries still hoist, retain their manifest sid, and preserve existing production allocation/performance results.
- A mutation restoring generic postwalk-through-quote fails a focused compiler golden/runtime fixture.
- No public API, runtime branch, compatibility parser, or production bookkeeping is added.
close_reason: Merged PR #5989 at exact independently reviewed head 6e215566574f18f05c995ccd41a354bbe1c9f0f6; compiler quote preservation/frame guidance green. The one initial JVM failure was an unrelated base-owned concurrency flake and passed on failed-job rerun.

title: Align live W1/W2 migrator beads with the ratified Stage-6 schedule
description:
## Problem

The ratified substrate adoption plan now places W1 (the Reagent→`re-frame.ui` migrator) and its W2 migration-skill extension in Stage 6, but the live execution beads still authorize much earlier work:

- `rf2-gria2b` says W1 is built in S3–S4 and used in S5–S6.
- `rf2-nwgzha` schedules W2 for S5–S6 and depends on that early W1 posture.
- `11-adoption-workstreams.md`, `prep/w1-migrator-rule-table.md`, and `prep/w2-migration-skill-extension.md` now say W1 first builds/runs in S6.

S3 is open, so `bd ready` can surface work whose own brief contradicts the authoritative stage plan. That can consume workers early, bake migration rules before the substrate surface stabilizes, and create avoidable conflicts with implementation-stage hot zones.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the current W1/W2 passages under `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/`; they place the migrator wave in S6.
2. Run `bd show rf2-gria2b`; its title/brief says `build S3-4, used 5-6`.
3. Run `bd show rf2-nwgzha`; it schedules the skill extension for Stage 5-6 around the early W1 tool.
4. Observe that the tracker may dispatch W1 during S3 even though the authoritative plan deliberately defers its build and first use to S6.

## Expected Behavior

Authoritative documents and dispatchable work items name one W1/W2 schedule. No ready bead invites work before its ratified entry stage.

## Actual Behavior

The source plan says S6 while two live work briefs authorize S3–S5 execution.

## Provenance

Found by the independent audits of merged PR #5814 at exact head `797431e8e283b63be52309e52c394697629781c8`. Full all-status search found no dedicated reconciliation bead. This follow-up does not amend the already-open execution beads; it gives the mayor an explicit, reviewable action.
design:
Treat the tracked final-state synthesis plan as authoritative unless Mike explicitly reverses it. Reconcile W1 and W2 together so the tool, rule table, and skill extension cannot drift:

- Make W1 unavailable until the S6 predecessor/gate is satisfied.
- Make W2 depend on the reconciled W1 delivery and use the same S6 boundary.
- Preserve preparatory rule-table research already completed; only executable build/rollout timing changes.

This is tracker/brief hygiene, not a new migration architecture.
acceptance_criteria:
- `rf2-gria2b`, `rf2-nwgzha`, `11-adoption-workstreams.md`, and both W1/W2 prep documents name the same S6 build/first-run schedule.
- Dependency/defer/gate state prevents either execution bead from appearing ready before the S6 predecessor is satisfied.
- W2 cannot dispatch before the reconciled W1 tool and rule table are complete.
- Existing preparation is retained; no implementation or frozen API work is pulled forward.
- `bd ready` and `bd blocked` demonstrate the intended pre-S6 state, and `bd dep cycles` remains clean.
notes:
RULING (2026-07-17, delegated decision per Mike's in-session direction; dossier weighed and retired):

(a) DECISION: The Stage-6 schedule is CONFIRMED as the single truth for W1's build and first run. Reconciliation shape = dossier Option B (beads + doc single boundary) implemented with the Codex Option-3 refinement: encode a preparation/delivery split rather than a blunt all-S6 label. Concretely — W1 (migrator tool) is implemented and first run ONLY in S6, after S5 closes and after the canonical MIG rulebook is reconciled (rf2-vxgfnd.188); W2's S5-shaped preparation is already done (prep doc exists 2026-07-13) and its remaining graft/verify/ship work is S6, gated on W1's actual shipped flag/report contract. Option A (beads-only) REJECTED: it leaves prose as the only gate on the doc side, fails this bead's acceptance criteria as written, and leaves doc 11 advertising a W2 window whose remaining work is impossible. Option C (reverse to early S3-4 build) REJECTED: no new evidence, contradicts doc 11's ratified rationale ("W1-W4 deliberately trail the API surface stabilizing at Stage 3"), and the rule table's TARGET-STAGED markers prove the rewrite targets (local/effect/dispatch-fn/->react/SSR emit) are not shipped yet — an early build guarantees rework against moving APIs.

(b) RATIONALE (which arguments won): (1) The operational bug is graph state, not prose — both rf2-gria2b and rf2-nwgzha have ZERO blocking dependencies, so bd ready surfaces them in S3 despite DO-NOT-DISPATCH sentences (verified 2026-07-17: both in bd ready). Real dependencies are the fix. (2) The S6 ratification is deliberate, recent (2026-07-11, doc 11 Status: final), and corroborated by EP-0030, EP-0031, 12-implementation-plan S6 ordering, and both prep docs — one line of tracked-doc wording is cheap insurance against every future audit re-flagging the drift. (3) Codex's stale-premise catch is correct: "Stage 5-6" for W2 is defensible only if the phase boundary is explicit; replacing it wholesale with "Stage 6" would falsely imply prep should not have happened pre-S6. title: Reconcile ui.test dispatch! S1 core versus S2 mounted-stage attribution
description:
## Problem

The authoritative synthesis suite still gives `re-frame.ui.test/dispatch!` contradictory stage ownership, and the later cleanup chose the wrong side of that contradiction.

The actual implementation history is split by capability:

- PR #5700 (S1d) introduced the Tier-1 `dispatch!` function with real frame-targeted synchronous dispatch-and-drain behavior.
- S2 later added Promise-backed mounted `with-root`, mounted CSS `query`, and React-aware `flush!`/settlement semantics; `with-root` specifically landed in PR #5808, not #5713.

Current plan/draft passages assign `dispatch!` wholly to S2 mounted semantics, while the merge-readiness record still names it as S1 structural core. Current Guide 09 was changed to S2 to remove the textual contradiction, but that erases the actual S1 landing rather than describing the capability split. `dispatch!` itself has no separate mounted mode.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Inspect PR #5700 at S1d: it adds `re-frame.ui.test/dispatch!` and its frame dispatch/drain behavior.
2. Inspect PR #5713: it adds coalescing/flush work but not `with-root`.
3. Inspect PR #5808: it introduces the Promise-backed Tier-3 mounted harness including `with-root`.
4. Compare current `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/12-implementation-plan.md`, the Spec-004 rewrite/readiness drafts, and Guide 09.
5. Observe that some material calls `dispatch!` S1 structural core, other material calls it S2 mounted semantics, and the latest wording resolves the mismatch by assigning the already-shipped S1 function to S2.

## Expected Behavior

Stage documentation attributes each capability at the granularity it actually landed: Tier-1 `dispatch!` in S1; mounted harness/query/React fixed-point semantics in S2. Historical evidence cites the PR that introduced each behavior.

## Actual Behavior

The suite alternates between mutually incompatible stage assignments and currently misattributes the base `dispatch!` function to S2.

## Provenance

Both independent audits of merged PR #5814 at exact head `797431e8e283b63be52309e52c394697629781c8` found the same unresolved split. Closed `rf2-30csx0` and `rf2-vxgfnd.114` cannot be amended; full all-status search found no live follow-up.
design:
Reconcile the small set of stage tables and guide prose against the actual merged PRs. Use a two-row/two-clause attribution rather than forcing the public name into one monolithic stage:

- S1: Tier-1 `dispatch!`, frame-targeted synchronous dispatch, router drain.
- S2: mounted `with-root`/CSS query and React-aware Promise/fixed-point flush settlement that composes with dispatch.

Cite #5700 for the first row and #5808 (plus the precise intermediate flush PR where relevant) for the second. Do not redesign the test API or reopen the frozen surface.
acceptance_criteria:
- `12-implementation-plan.md`, Spec-004 rewrite/readiness material, Guide 09, and any stage matrix agree that the base Tier-1 `dispatch!` landed in S1.
- S2 is credited only with the mounted/Promise/React-settlement extensions that actually landed there.
- `with-root` is attributed to PR #5808; no passage claims #5713 introduced it.
- Each historical citation resolves to a diff containing the named capability.
- A tracked consistency check or focused assertion catches future S1/S2 attribution drift for the frozen `ui.test` rows.
- No public API, implementation behavior, or frozen-table spelling changes.

title: Lock the full deps-new repo override token instead of reconstructing its prefix
description:
## Problem

PR #5810 corrected four concrete local-template override examples to deps-new's working single-percent spelling, but the accompanying regression test does not test those complete documented tokens. tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/repo_split_spec_test.clj extracts only a suffix matching (%+io.github.day8/re-frame2-template) and then prepends the expected day8/re-frame2-template repository itself.

That reconstruction hides both classes the test is intended to prevent:

- A documented token with the wrong repository prefix still passes because the test discards that prefix and substitutes the expected one.
- A documented token with %% or %%% still reaches deps-new's parser; deps-new interprets the extra field as a deps-root and can still produce the expected :template, so the current assertion stays green.

The prose also twice calls the two-component spelling repo%root%template-sym (005-Repo-Split.md §2.1 and §4). Pinned deps-new v0.12.1 calls the actual two-component grammar repo%template-sym; repo%deps-root%template-sym is the separate three-component form. The current concrete shell commands work, so this is a regression-durability and terminology defect rather than a current execution failure.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Evaluate documented-local-overrides against text containing io.github.day8/wrong-repo%io.github.day8/re-frame2-template.
2. Observe the helper reconstructs day8/re-frame2-template%io.github.day8/re-frame2-template and the test passes.
3. Evaluate it against day8/re-frame2-template%%%io.github.day8/re-frame2-template.
4. Observe the regex retains %%% and deps-new treats the middle field as a deps-root; :template can still equal the canonical symbol, so the test passes despite violating the mandated one-separator grammar.

## Deliverable

- Correct both prose labels to repo%template-sym and, if useful, name repo%deps-root%template-sym separately so the fields cannot be confused.
- Extract and validate each complete documented override token. Do not synthesize or replace the repository half in the test.
- Assert the token equals exactly day8/re-frame2-template%io.github.day8/re-frame2-template, contains one separator, preprocesses to the canonical template symbol, and keeps the day8 repository outside deps-new's auto-git-url path.
- Add negative examples/mutations for a wrong repository prefix and extra separators. They must fail the guard even when deps-new can parse them into the same :template.
- Keep the production preprocess-options path and the local-root/no-auto-clone behavior under test.

Relevant files are tools/template/spec/005-Repo-Split.md and tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/repo_split_spec_test.clj. This is a follow-up to closed rf2-2jtujj; do not reopen or amend the completed bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every intended occurrence is the complete exact token day8/re-frame2-template%io.github.day8/re-frame2-template.
- The prose names the two-component grammar repo%template-sym and distinguishes the optional three-component deps-root grammar accurately.
- The test reads complete tokens from the document and never supplies their repository prefix itself.
- Wrong-base, %%, and %%% mutations deterministically fail.
- The exact token preprocesses to io.github.day8/re-frame2-template, bypasses auto-git-url for the base repo, and resolves the canonical resource path.
- Focused tools/template tests and documentation/link gates pass.

title: docs(core/ui): describe frame-destroy hook's disconnected root-owned ViewCell sweep
description:
## Problem

PR #5803 expanded `:ui/on-frame-destroyed!` from connected observers to a union that also includes disconnected root-owned ViewCells whose retained targets name the destroyed frame. The implementation is functionally correct (and its initial strong-retention defect was later fixed by PR #5832), but three active caller/registry descriptions still promise connected-only teardown:

- `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/frames.cljc:608`
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:3095`
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:1121`

That description is now materially incomplete. Activity-hidden/disconnected cells are exactly the non-obvious reason the hook exists and the class most likely to be omitted by a future refactor following the stale contract.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the late-bind directory entry and frame destroy recipe; derive the stated obligation that only currently connected ViewCells are transitioned.
2. Inspect `teardown-frame!` and the root-owned victim union in current UI reactive code.
3. Create a disconnected but React-retained/Activity-hidden ViewCell holding a lease into frame F.
4. Destroy F and observe the hook must discover and reap that cell even though it is not currently connected.
5. A future implementation faithful to the active descriptions could remove that branch while still satisfying the documented hook contract.

## Deliverable

Update the hook registry, core destroy recipe/comment, and UI hook comment to state one exact obligation: tear down connected observers plus disconnected root-owned cells whose retained targets belong to the destroyed frame, deduplicated and incarnation-safe. Name the ownership/liveness predicate rather than implying all historical cells are scanned. Link or cite the focused fixture that protects the hidden-cell case.

No runtime redesign is required; PR #5832 already resolved strong ownership retention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No active description of `:ui/on-frame-destroyed!` says or implies connected-only teardown.
- Core, late-bind registry, and UI comments use the same bounded victim-set terminology.
- The prose distinguishes React-retained disconnected cells from collected historical cells.
- A source-level contract check or focused test description anchors the hidden-cell obligation.
- No production code or hook surface changes are introduced unless required to make an existing name truthful.

## Evidence and provenance

Independent completeness review of PR #5803 exact head `1ba4e8e2b49ad13b33c8dd53ffe0ae3841354b71` found this drift; the independent correctness pass confirmed the runtime hidden-cell sweep. The stale descriptions persist on current `origin/main` `f5a4381ff5ada6928281f05b8d1611a11e7880b4`. The strong `root-cells` retention bug is already closed by `rf2-mc62sp`/PR #5832 and is not duplicated here. Full all-status inventory found no description-reconciliation bead.

title: test(machines): extend randomized oracle to parent-owned parallel always rounds
description:
## Problem

The randomized machine regression oracle deliberately excludes the exact cross-region data dependency fixed by PR #5801. `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_property_cljs_test.cljc:273-294` still calls evolving-data local always draining documented/correct behavior. Its generator then restricts always guards to constants and removes shared-data writes (`309-321`), and the property restates that exclusion (`810-817`).

This makes the strongest randomized tier blind by construction: restoring the old region-local drain can leave the property green even though declaration order again changes the selected `:always` set. The example tests are good, but the property suite advertises a broader invariant while preserving obsolete semantic rationale.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Inspect the generated machines: no region writes a distinct shared flag consumed by a sibling's guarded `:always` transition.
2. Mutate the engine back to settling each region's always loop before visiting the next region.
3. Run the current property suite; its constant-guard/no-shared-write domain cannot distinguish that mutation.
4. Add commutative region-specific writes plus sibling-data guards, and generate both A/B and B/A declaration order.
5. The old engine produces unequal/stranded configurations while the parent-owned frozen-round engine produces equivalent resolved state/data.

## Deliverable

Remove the obsolete local-drain rationale and add a small generated family specifically for the parent-round law. Generate two or more orthogonal regions with commutative region-owned writes, sibling-reading always guards, and declaration-order permutations. Compare final state/data and relevant round/publication invariants. Keep the generator constrained enough to yield minimal, reproducible counterexamples; this is a focused semantic oracle, not a general statechart fuzzer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Seeded CLJ and CLJS property runs cover sibling-data guarded `:always` transitions in parallel regions.
- A/B and B/A declaration orders produce equivalent resolved state/data under the corrected engine.
- A local-drain mutation deterministically fails the property with a minimized counterexample.
- Property comments and names match the parent-owned per-round law in Spec 005.
- Generated actions remain commutative so an order failure identifies selection semantics rather than legitimate effect ordering.
- Runtime of the property tier remains bounded for normal CI.

## Evidence and provenance

Discovered by independent completeness review of PR #5801 exact head `3877eceff056381988849c80bf6f30fc738bafbd`; independent correctness review found the runtime implementation complete. The blind spot persists on current `origin/main` `f5a4381ff5ada6928281f05b8d1611a11e7880b4`. title: Correct active-path transition prose for declaring-compound descendant targets
description:
## Problem

PR #5794 (authored head `0d460cbfe57eff897b3a079ce44a39ef43afa440`; merge `4a1095dd1f385571d07f949bd3f56a298e9dd5c4`) was the follow-up intended to remove stale targetless-equivalence guidance from transition geometry. It leaves one old contradictory block and introduces a new over-generalization that is false for parent-declared descendant targets. Both survive on current main beside the load-bearing cascade calculation.

In `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` at the authored/current lines:

- `:2960-2975` still says an active-path target is effectively internal by default and causes no exit/entry churn, despite executable `internal?` being exactly `targetless?` around `:3140`.
- The newly rewritten `:3030-3044` says an active-path target node is never re-entered and that targeted and targetless behavior coincide when the target is a leaf.
- `:3115-3121` explicitly detects a proper descendant target declared by a compound state, and the higher-priority branch at `:3182-3185` uses `count(target-base)-1`, re-entering that target even when it is already active and is a leaf. The accurate exception is already described at `:3147-3157`.
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md:336` makes the same general statement before later carving out its descendant exception, leaving the normative reader to reconcile incompatible rules.

The determining relationship is not merely “target lies on the active path”; it is target versus declaring state. A maintainer following the nearby prose could remove the descendant-priority branch and regress XState-v5 semantics.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use active state `[:parent :leaf]`.
2. Compare a targetless transition declared on `:parent` with a transition also declared on `:parent` that explicitly targets its already-active proper descendant `[:parent :leaf]`, with no `:reenter?`.
3. Targetless produces only `[:act]` and preserves the leaf.
4. The explicit descendant target produces `[:exit-leaf :act :enter-leaf]`: the target leaf itself is re-entered.
5. This directly contradicts both “no exit/entry churn” and “the two coincide when target is a leaf.”

## Required correction

Rewrite the geometry comments and Spec 005 rule as three explicit cases:

1. Targetless: the only internal/no-cascade case; configuration survives unchanged.
2. Explicit self or proper-ancestor target on the active path: the target node survives, but its active descendants exit and re-resolve through `:initial`.
3. Proper descendant target of the declaring compound: the target itself re-enters, even when already active and even when it is a leaf; this relationship takes priority over the generic active-path case.

Describe separately what `:reenter? true` restarts for self/ancestor versus declaring-compound relationships. Remove every remaining claim that all active-path targets are internal or that leaf-ness alone makes targeting equivalent to targetless.

Add focused behavior fixtures while touching this contract so the prose cannot drift from the branch precedence again; no runtime semantic change is requested unless a fixture exposes another implementation mismatch.

## Dedupe and scope

Closed `rf2-900jnw` is the exact incomplete documentation task and cannot be reopened or amended under the review protocol. Closed `rf2-gt1pu` and `rf2-d0r6z7` establish the correct runtime/spec rule. No live follow-up covers the remaining/introduced contradiction, so this new bead records the omitted work explicitly.
acceptance_criteria:
- `transition.cljc` and Spec 005 state the targetless, self/proper-ancestor, and declaring-compound/proper-descendant cases separately and consistently.
- No source/spec comment calls an explicit active-path target “internal,” promises no cascade, or says leaf targeting necessarily equals targetless.
- Fixtures pin exact exit/action/entry identities for targetless, self-leaf, proper-ancestor target, parent-declared leaf descendant, and parent-declared compound descendant.
- Both `:reenter? false/absent` and `:reenter? true` are covered where meaningful, including branch precedence for an already-active proper descendant.
- The parent-declared active leaf regression produces exit-leaf/action/enter-leaf; the targetless control produces action only.
- Existing XState parity fixtures remain green and no runtime change is made merely to fit stale prose.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6010 (worker/machines-transition-cluster). Premise re-verified at file:line against current main before fixing; each fix pinned by a mutation reproducing the original defect. Machines JVM gate 1123 tests/3917 assertions green (+19 tests/+65 assertions).

title: Emit each spawn-all unregistered-child reject exactly once
description:
## Problem

PR #5794 (authored head `0d460cbfe57eff897b3a079ce44a39ef43afa440`; merge `4a1095dd1f385571d07f949bd3f56a298e9dd5c4`) says `:spawn-all` invoke preflight emits one `:rf.error/machine-spawn-unregistered-type` per offending child, but every offending per-child effect emits the same error again. Actor-state atomicity is correct; production error cardinality is doubled. The defect persists byte-identically on current main.

`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:628-629` emits once per unregistered child from `spawn-all-init-fx`. Later `spawn-fx` checks `unregistered-spawn-type?` before `spawn-all-invoke-rejected?` (`:367-379`), so each offending child bypasses the childless-sentinel suppression and calls `reject-unregistered-spawn!` a second time. Each call emits both an always-on record and a dev trace (`:108-155`). The fixture at `machine_spawn_unregistered_type_test.clj:221-228` asserts only `1 <= count`, deliberately accepting duplicates rather than pinning the documented cardinality.

Duplicate production-surviving error records distort off-box failure rates and make one malformed invoke look like two independent boundary failures per child.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register a parent whose `:spawn-all` has two missing child machine types and one registered sibling.
2. Enter the state and collect the always-on error records/dev traces by machine-id.
3. Observe the childless reject sentinel and no installed child actors, but four error records: two for missing-a and two for missing-b.
4. The documented/structural failure count is two—one offending child of each id—not four.

## Required correction

For a per-child effect that belongs to a `:spawn-all`, consult `spawn-all-invoke-rejected?` before the child-local unregistered-type gate. The init effect remains the sole emitter for the rejected invoke, and every later child effect—registered or unregistered—suppresses silently under the sentinel. A standalone single `:spawn` has no rejected invoke sentinel and must continue to run its own unregistered-type check exactly once.

Pin exact cardinality rather than a lower bound. Do not deduplicate downstream in the trace/error listener; preserve one authoritative producer.

## Dedupe and scope

Closed `rf2-qb1j5z` established actor-state atomicity, and closed `rf2-oalcqo` documented the sentinel; neither covers duplicate telemetry. No all-status bead pins exact invoke-reject error cardinality. This is a new follow-up from the closed documentation source, not an amendment.
acceptance_criteria:
- A rejected invoke with N unregistered children emits exactly N always-on `:rf.error/machine-spawn-unregistered-type` records and exactly N dev traces, one per offending machine-id.
- Counts are invariant under child order and the number/placement of registered siblings.
- Every per-child effect suppresses under the invoke sentinel; no snapshots, system ids, spawn-order entries, spawned traces, or start dispatches occur.
- Parent exit still clears the sentinel and join completion remains impossible/no-op while rejected.
- A standalone unregistered single `:spawn` still emits exactly once and fails closed.
- Fixtures assert exact counts on CLJ and CLJS; restoring the old gate order fails them.

title: Clear detached ViewCell state when resetting the scheduler
description:
## Problem

PR #5796 (authored head `cc48c6a7cdaea80256d695864be69f804edf646e`; merge `2f668e91895f7e3fb34678c7599e9bae69cd94ba`) exposes a test-support scheduler reset that does not actually return ViewCells to a clean scheduler state. The defect persists on current main.

`reset-scheduler!` in `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc` clears the global dirty-cell registry and scheduled flag, but it does not clear `:dirty?` or pending evidence in the cells removed from that registry (authored head `:1078-1091`; current main around `:1446`). A later invalidation sees `:dirty? true`, folds into the pre-reset evidence, and refuses to re-enrol. The cell is permanently dirty-but-unregistered: `flush-pending!` returns zero, revision never advances, and listeners never run. Evidence also leaks across fixture boundaries, contradicting the function's clean-slate purpose.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a ViewCell and subscribe a listener.
2. Mark it dirty for epoch 1; verify the scheduler has one pending cell.
3. Call `reset-scheduler!`.
4. Mark the same cell dirty for epoch 2.
5. Observe `:dirty? true`, pending-cell-count zero, evidence with first epoch 1/latest epoch 2/count 2, and `flush-pending!` returning zero; revision and listener count remain zero.

This is deterministic on the exact PR head and demonstrates both a stranded cell and cross-test evidence contamination.

## Required correction

Reset must snapshot/detach the pending cells and clear each detached cell's dirty/evidence window without advancing revisions or notifying listeners. Define reset-versus-mark concurrency so a mark is coherently classified as pre-reset and cleared or post-reset and enrolled; it must never be dirty while absent from the registry.

Keep the operation test-support-only. Do not add a public lifecycle abstraction or redesign ordinary teardown. Update the stale nearby test comment that still says `dropped-count` so it names the actual bounded `:dropped` set and exactness flag while touching this fixture surface.

## Dedupe and scope

Closed `rf2-vxgfnd.73` and `rf2-vxgfnd.86` repair sink/re-entrant delivery paths that can strand cells; neither addresses administrative scheduler reset or fixture-boundary contamination. No all-status bead covers this path. The finding came from the closed source bead `rf2-vxgfnd.74`, so it is a new follow-up rather than an amendment.
acceptance_criteria:
- After `reset-scheduler!`, every cell detached from the pending registry is clean, has nil evidence, and is not enrolled.
- A subsequent epoch-2 mark creates a fresh window, appears in pending-cell-count, flushes exactly once, advances revision once, and notifies once.
- Reset itself never advances a revision or invokes listeners/evidence consumers.
- A deterministic JVM reset-versus-mark race admits only coherent pre-reset-cleared or post-reset-enrolled outcomes; dirty-but-unregistered is impossible.

title: Preserve falsy CLJS listener escapes in flush containment
description:
## Problem

PR #5832 contains listener exceptions so every listener/cell is delivered, then rethrows the first escape. In CLJS, `notify-listeners!` records that escape with `(or acc e)` and later uses `some?` to decide whether to throw. JavaScript permits throwing falsy values. A thrown `nil`/`null` is therefore silently lost, while a first thrown `false` is replaced by a later truthy exception. This violates the PR's explicit first-escape/original-identity contract.

Fan-out completion remains correct; the defect is exception containment fidelity and observability.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Subscribe a listener that executes JavaScript `throw null`, followed by an ordinary sibling listener.
2. Flush the cell. The sibling fires, but no escape is rethrown because `(or nil nil)` leaves the accumulator nil and `some?` is false.
3. Subscribe a first listener that throws JavaScript `false`, then a listener that throws an Error/ex-info.
4. Flush. The later truthy exception is rethrown, not the first value `false`.
5. Exact compiled-CLJS probes reproduced both: `onlyNull` did not throw; `falseThenError` threw the second error.

Existing fixtures use only truthy `ex-info` values, so they cannot detect truthiness-based loss.

## Required Correction

Represent escape presence independently of escape value, for example `{:escaped? true :error e}` or a private sentinel plus a value slot. Never use JavaScript/Clojure truthiness as the presence test. Preserve the existing two-phase guarantee: deliver all listeners and cells, retain the first escape exactly, report diagnostics as specified, then throw that exact value even when it is nil/null or false.
acceptance_criteria:
- A compiled-CLJS fixture proves `throw null` is rethrown after all same-cell and sibling-cell listeners deliver.
- A first `throw false` followed by another exception rethrows exactly `false`, preserving first-escape order and identity.
- Truthy Error/ex-info behavior, sink diagnostics, listener ordering, and reentrant re-marking remain correct.
- No cell is left dirty/pending solely because a listener threw; a clean follow-up drain succeeds.
- JVM behavior remains unchanged, and advanced production output adds no debug-only bookkeeping beyond the required containment state.
