title: Reject JVM child-thread mutation of a conveyed render capture
description:
## Problem

PR #5832 replaces the process-global ambient capture atom with a dynamic binding whose value is a `volatile!`. This correctly isolates separate JVM render threads, but Clojure conveys dynamic bindings into `future`/`pmap` workers. If one render body forks site reads and joins them, the child threads share the same non-thread-safe volatile capture and race `vswap!` at `reactive.cljc:726/780`.

The implementation contract is a deterministic, compiler-ordered render capture. Silently losing sites or corrupting order is worse than rejecting an unsupported parallel render body. The authored concurrency fixture runs separate renders, each with its own binding; it does not cover child-thread binding conveyance inside one render.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On JVM, enter `with-capture` for one render.
2. Spawn multiple `future` or `pmap` tasks that inherit `*ambient*`; have each perform a distinct `sub-read` or `lease-site`, then join them before the thunk returns.
3. All child threads mutate the same volatile capture.
4. In an exact-head 200-trial/16-site probe, 188 renders returned an incomplete capture; the minimum captured site count was one.
5. The call succeeds rather than reporting that render capture is single-threaded, so missing ownership can flow into commit/release logic.

## Required Correction

Enforce the intended single-threaded render-capture contract rather than engineering parallel render support. Record the JVM owner thread in the ambient capture and, before any `sub-read`/`lease-site` mutation, throw a typed malformed-tree/render-capture error if the current thread differs. Reject before mutating the capture. Separate top-level renders on different threads must remain valid because each has its own binding. Supporting parallel render bodies later would require atomic capture plus deterministic site ordering and is outside this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- JVM fixtures prove future- and pmap-conveyed `sub-read`/`lease-site` calls fail loudly with a typed error before capture mutation.
- The error identifies the render/site contract sufficiently for a developer to remove the fork; no partial ownership is committed.
- Separate concurrent top-level renders remain isolated and green.
- Nested same-thread captures preserve save/restore and deterministic site ordering.
- CLJS single-thread behavior and production output remain unchanged apart from development diagnostics as designed.
- A stress mutation that removes the owner-thread guard reproduces incomplete capture and fails the fixture.

description:
## Problem

title: Decide whether to retire the un-emitted :parent-unmount-cascade reason
description:
## Problem

`:parent-unmount-cascade` is part of the documented fx-channel `:rf.machine/destroyed` reason vocabulary, but there is no runtime emit site and no executable trigger. PR #5831 explicitly left "implement or retire" as follow-up work, then closed its source bead. The live inventory contains no open owner for that choice.

Keeping a reserved discriminator has a continuing cost: specs, conformance gates, Xray classifiers, schemas, and user reasoning must all account for a state that cannot occur. It also collides with the stronger ownership law in Spec 005: view/port teardown is explicit and there is no implicit ownership cascade.

## Evidence

- PR #5831's verified emit census found lifecycle+`:parent-frame-destroyed` and fx+`:explicit`/`:rf.machine/finished`/`:rf.machine/join-reaped`, but no `:parent-unmount-cascade`.
- Parent-cascade teardown currently stamps `:explicit`.
- `spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md` attempted to give the reserved value semantics by claiming view-unmount-driven machine teardown, but the runtime has no such edge and Spec 005 forbids relying on one.
- Existing historical owners `rf2-hh1jhc`, `rf2-tj2fn`, and `rf2-gn80` are closed, so none will action this decision.

## Decision Required

Choose whether `:parent-unmount-cascade` is a real v1 contract or dead vocabulary.

## Alternatives Considered

### A — Retire it now (recommended)

Remove the value atomically from Spec 005, Spec 009, Spec-Schemas, Cross-Spec prose, tests, Xray classifiers, and guides. Continue representing every named application/parent-state destroy through the actual explicit/final/join-reap mechanisms.

Consequences: the v1 vocabulary becomes closed over observable behavior; consumers need no speculative branch; the explicit-ownership law stays simple. If future demand establishes a genuinely distinct cascade trigger, a new reason can be added with its emitter and fixtures in one change.

### B — Implement it now

Define an exact, observable trigger distinct from view unmount and ordinary explicit destroy; emit the reason at the fx destroy choke point; specify ordering, ownership, and nested-cascade behavior; update tools and add fixtures.

Consequences: preserves the existing enum but creates a new behavioral contract and ownership edge. It is only justified if there is a named current consumer that needs to distinguish this case from `:explicit`.

### C — Keep it reserved

Leave the value documented but unobservable.

Consequences: no immediate implementation work, but perpetuates the drift that #5831 tried to eliminate and forces every consumer/gate to model an impossible state. This is not recommended for a frozen pre-alpha v1 surface.

## Recommendation

Choose A. A vocabulary member should land with its semantics and executable producer, not in anticipation of possible demand. Retiring it is the smallest fully correct shape and aligns with the project's explicit ownership contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- Mike records A, B, or C with rationale.
- If A is chosen, every normative, schema, tool, test, and guide occurrence is removed atomically, and a census gate proves no stale member remains.
- If B is chosen, the distinct trigger, ownership boundary, ordering, nesting behavior, exact emitter, and channel are specified before implementation; a fail-before fixture proves the reason is emitted only for that trigger.
- Xray and conformance tests accept only values that the chosen runtime contract can actually emit.
- The Cross-Spec view-unmount correction remains consistent with the chosen ownership law.
- Relevant machines, Xray, conformance, and strict-doc gates pass.

title: Refresh the installed custom-element source-reset callback across HMR
description:
## Problem

PR #5783 installs the Shadow source-reset callback once with `defonce` and pushes the current `reload-source-reset!` function object into `SHADOW_NS_RESET`. When `rules.cljc` itself hot-reloads, the var is rebound to a new function object but the array retains the old object forever because the installer remains realized.

Current behavior may appear to work while the old wrapper delegates to other newly rebound vars, but any fix to the wrapper's own coercion, build routing, validation, or source filtering does not take effect until a full page reload. The existing test checks only initial identity/cardinality and cannot detect stale implementation.

## Required correction

Keep exactly one installed producer callback while making it dispatch to the current implementation. Preferred shape: install one stable tagged trampoline that resolves/invokes the current `reload-source-reset!` var on every call. Alternatively replace the previous tagged callback atomically during namespace evaluation. Do not append anonymous wrappers on every reload or clear callbacks owned by other libraries/builds.

The solution must compose with per-build callbacks if the build-identity follow-up uses them: exactly one current callback per build identity, with old versions replaced rather than accumulated.

## Proof discipline

Redefine/reload the implementation to record a distinct marker, invoke the already-installed array entry, and prove current code calls the old behavior before the fix. Repeat reloads and verify callback identity/cardinality plus other-owner preservation.
acceptance_criteria:
- After `rules.cljc` hot-reloads, the installed source-reset producer executes the current callback implementation without a page refresh.
- Exactly one tagged callback exists per intended build identity; repeated reloads neither duplicate nor lose it.
- Callbacks owned by Shadow or other libraries/builds remain untouched.
- The callback uses current coercion, build routing, validation, and source-filtering behavior after redefinition.
- A fail-before fixture redefines the implementation and proves the old `defonce` object stays stale; the repaired trampoline/replacement turns it green.
- Production elision and ordinary reload-cycle behavior remain unchanged; no public API or global callback-array reset is introduced.

title: correctness(S2-audit): ambient render-capture atom is cross-thread on the JVM — concurrent Tier-1 renders cross-contaminate captures
description:
## What / where

implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc:264 (ambient — a plain module-level atom), :709-730 (with-capture — save/restore via reset!), :650-707 (sub-read — reads @ambient to pick the recording cell/capture), :318 (slice-memo* — same shape, lower stakes since it is tag-guarded and economy-only).

## Invariant violated

Goal 6 (determinism/testability on both hosts — the ns header claims the reconciler is 'graft-checked headlessly against the REAL observation port on both hosts') and I-2 (only the committed render owns its capture — here a DIFFERENT THREAD's render can write into it). The code comment asserts 'single-threaded on both hosts within one synchronous render' — true on CLJS, an unenforced assumption on the JVM. Every neighbouring scope in the same path (*sub-overrides*, rframe/*current-frame*, subs-cache/*disposal-cause*) is a dynamic var and therefore thread-local under binding; ambient alone is cross-thread shared. Same class as the already-filed rf2-vxgfnd.35 (JVM concurrency hole in execute-frame-plans!), one layer down in the render path.

## Failure scenario

Two ui.test/render calls on different JVM threads (parallel test runner, or a fixture using future). Thread A enters with-capture and installs {:cell A :capture capA}; thread B reset!s {:cell B :capture capB}; A's next sub-read records A's site into B's capture (silent wrong ownership — B commits a site it never rendered, A's capture misses one), or throws a FALSE :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed 'site executed more than once' on a sid collision. A's finally then reset!s ambient to ITS saved prev, clobbering B's still-open capture entirely.

## Fix sketch

Make ambient a ^:dynamic private var and replace with-capture's reset!/finally save-restore with binding — thread-local on the JVM, identical semantics on single-threaded CLJS (binding gives the save/restore for free). Optionally give slice-memo* the same treatment (removes cross-thread churn; its tag guard already prevents wrong values).

## Done means

A JVM fixture running two concurrent ui.test/render calls over distinct frames (latch-forced interleave) asserts each returned tree's capture contains exactly its own sites — red today, green after. CLJS behaviour unchanged (existing reconcile/HMR suites stay green).

description:
## What / where

implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc:1095-1119 (deliver-flush! — contains ONLY the evidence-sink throw; notify-listeners! at :756 is bare), :1121-1147 (run-flush-batch! — both the DEBUG reduce and the production doseq abort on a listener throw), :1072-1093 (complete-flush! — phase 1 has already cleared :dirty? and advanced the revision for the WHOLE batch before phase 2 runs).

## Invariant violated

The wave's own containment doctrine (rf2-vxgfnd.73/.86): consumer callbacks are 'never an authority over the render correction' and a throwing callback 'can neither strand a cell nor abort the batch's remaining cells'. Implemented for the DEBUG evidence-sink, NOT for the listener fan-out — which is strictly more load-bearing (it IS the render correction).

## Failure scenario

Cells A and B dirtied in one drain; flush-scope! drains atomically; phase 1 completes BOTH (dirty flags cleared, revisions advanced, registry membership gone). Phase 2 delivers A first; one of A's listeners throws (a tool/test subscriber via reactive/subscribe, or any future non-React consumer — the seam is public inside the artefact). The throw propagates out of run-flush-batch!: B's listeners are NEVER invoked, yet B is no longer dirty and no longer in the registry — the notification is not deferred, it is LOST. B renders stale until an unrelated future movement re-marks it. Same stranding on the JVM ui.test/flush! loop (exits by exception). This is the rf2-vxgfnd.73 bug class one layer down.

## Fix sketch

In deliver-flush!, wrap notify-listeners! (or each individual listener invocation) in the same containment shape as the sink: catch per cell, complete the whole batch, then rethrow the first escape (and/or fan it through the always-on error-emit axis, mirroring the observation port's report-disposal-notify-escape!).

## Done means

A fixture installing a throwing listener on cell A proves cell B's listener still fires within the same flush-batch-in-order! batch, in both [A B] and [B A] orders; the escape is still surfaced (rethrow or always-on record), never silent.

Gates: ui JVM 438/5495, test:ui 445/2249, browser 342/1848, fast-pr spine PASS (test:cljs 9226/43636). Left open for the mayor.

title: Document ui.test/render exact-one-view cardinality
description:
## Finding

Correctness review of merged documentation PR #5823 at exact head `6c1ac7288a3858afb039aa2bb406864d5bd551d0` / merge `d1343f707446b8e9bd90b4278dd6c00bab1a1a10` found that Guide 09 overstates the shared grammar between `ui.test/render` and application mounting.

`ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/guide/09-testing.md` around lines 48-53 says `ui.test/render` takes the same literal root form used at the application boundary. It does share the literal top-region grammar, but not mount's cardinality law. `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/test.cljc` around lines 1144-1167 rejects any Tier-1 test root that does not contain exactly one mounted internal view. By contrast, the mount root resolver in `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/root.cljc` accepts multiple mounted views when the caller authors `:root-id`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Define two views, `a` and `b`.
2. Macroexpand `(ui.test/render [:<> [a] [b]] {})`.
3. Observe `:rf.ui.compile/bad-test-root` with the message that a test root mounts exactly one view and this form has two.
4. Resolve the same literal mount top region with authored `{:root-id :page/multi}` and observe that the mount identity grammar accepts the two-view form.

## Expected contract

Guide 09 should say that Tier-1 render uses mount's literal top-region grammar but deliberately requires exactly one mounted view. It should recommend a wrapper `defview` when a test needs a multi-view composition. Spec 004C §9 should carry the same qualifier if it currently uses the same unqualified shorthand.

## Dedupe and sequencing

The in-progress broad guide correction `rf2-vxgfnd.114` owns general stage truth and a different Guide 05 multi-root example, while `.112` owns compiler grammar reconciliation. Neither can be amended by this worker. This concrete API-documentation follow-up waits for both to avoid conflicts; if their PRs already add the exact Tier-1 cardinality qualifier and wrapper remedy, verify and close this bead without another edit.
design: Clarify the existing restriction; do not change it. State “same literal top-region grammar, exactly one mounted view in Tier 1” and give the wrapper-view remedy in one sentence. Keep mount's authored-root multi-view capability unchanged. Add the executable two-view counterexample to an existing guide/compiler fixture only if that fixture is already the natural owner; no new general docs framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Guide 09 explicitly states that `ui.test/render` requires exactly one mounted view even though it shares mount's literal top-region grammar.
- The guide recommends wrapping multiple child views in one `defview` before Tier-1 rendering.
- Spec 004C §9 and active `ui.test/render` docstrings use the same cardinality wording.
- A focused pre-fix expansion of a two-view literal produces `:rf.ui.compile/bad-test-root`, while a single wrapper view succeeds; the PR records this evidence.
- No change is made to compiler/runtime cardinality, mount's authored multi-view roots, the frozen API, or compatibility behavior.
- Work is serialized after `.112` and `.114`; equivalent landed corrections satisfy the bead after verification.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5827 — guide 09 now states exact-one-view Tier-1 cardinality + wrapper-defview remedy; spec/004C §9 qualifier INCLUDED (004C untouched by open PRs; #5818 does not own it). JVM evidence in PR body: two-view root => :rf.ui.compile/bad-test-root, wrapper expands OK. render docstring already conforms. Left open for mayor to close at merge.
close_reason: Merged PR #5827 (guide review cluster); per-bead fix verified in worker report

title: test-rigour(S2-audit): G-3 headless scaling banner claims app-db-move/step-5 channel but drives :hmr re-registration
description: S2-wave test-rigour audit finding (see ai/findings/2026-07-13.s2-wave-test-rigour-audit.md F1). WHAT/WHERE: implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc lines 149-162 — the ';; G-3 multi-read scaling' section banner claims 'the one-drain fan-in is a REAL app-db move caught at the headless commit evidence comparison (step 5/8), which advances the cell's revision AT MOST ONCE per commit — no scheduler seam, no mock'. The fixture (g3-scaling-case, lines 163-217) actually drives the fan-in by RE-REGISTERING each sub (rf/reg-sub again, lines 198-199) — the port's :hmr-cause on-change fan-out caught at mark-dirty!/enrolment, with the revision advancing via flush-pending!, not a commit-step-5 read. The in-function comment (lines 193-197) describes the mechanism correctly; the banner does not. WHAT FAILURE STAYS GREEN: none in this test — its assertions are honest for the channel it drives. The defect is a coverage-map lie: a maintainer reading the banner would believe the headless G-3 gate exercises the value-movement (app-db-write) invalidation channel and could deprioritise/remove the mounted counterpart (mounted_g3_cardinality_dom_cljs_test.cljs) that actually covers it end-to-end on the watchable adapter. On plain-atom, value movement has NO watch channel — if the banner were believed, a broken value-movement watch on the first-party adapter would appear headlessly 'covered' when it is not. FIX SKETCH (comment-only, no assertion moves): rewrite the banner to state the actual channel (real per-lease :hmr-cause on-change via sub re-registration -> mark-dirty! -> coalesced flush), delete the 'app-db move / step 5/8 / at most once per commit' sentence (that description belongs to the reconcile suite's moved-evidence tests), and cross-reference mounted_g3_cardinality_dom_cljs_test.cljs as the real app-db-movement G-3 proof. DONE-WHEN: the banner accurately names the :hmr re-registration channel, no longer claims app-db-move/step-5 coverage, and points at the mounted G-3 test for the value-movement path; test:cljs stays green (no assertion changes).

title: Align static-override contract prose with the rf= movement law
description:
## Finding

Independent completeness and correctness reviews of merged PR #5824 at exact head `a110d2164011089aacd36a925c10e1f8e7e227d1` / merge `e0c886037433adb5085e161bfce7a6d3b02ff31c` agree that runtime behavior is correct but its producer-side contract prose remains false.

`implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc` around lines 184-195 says the static-override port compares both opaque tokens by plain `=` and says `:version` retargets according to `=`. The authoritative observation implementation at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc` around lines 790-803 and 1366-1385 now compares `:override-id` with `=` but compares `:version` with the frozen `rf=`/`node-value=` movement law. This split is load-bearing: NaN-to-NaN must retain the exact lease rather than retarget forever.

The nearby reactive prose around lines 170-173 also describes React-context override seeding as future S2f work although `viewcell.cljs` now implements it. Spec 006 and the retained observation-port draft merely say the opaque tokens “match” and do not pin which equality law applies to each token.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the static-override lowering contract in `reactive.cljc`; it predicts movement because `(= js/NaN js/NaN)` is false.
2. Follow the landed runtime path with a retained static lease whose `:version` is NaN and render a fresh provider map containing NaN.
3. Observe that `observation/current?` correctly returns true under `node-value=` and the mounted #5824 fixture retains the identical lease/revision.
4. Mutating the implementation back to the documented plain-`=` law restores the demonstrated `Maximum update depth exceeded` retarget loop.

## Expected contract

- `:override-id` is slot/provider identity and uses `=`.
- `:version` is the movement token and uses the complete frozen `rf=` law, including stable NaN-to-NaN.
- Consumer prose, normative Spec 006, the retained draft, and the landed React-context path describe the same present-state behavior.

## Dedupe and sequencing

Exact searches across open/in-progress beads for `static override version rf=`, `opaque movement token`, `NaN override`, `reactive.cljc version equality`, and `current? static version` found no owner. The implementation bead `rf2-vxgfnd.58` is closed by #5824, so this is a post-merge follow-up. It must serialize behind `rf2-vxgfnd.103` and any live Spec 006 owner; `spec/*` is a one-owner-at-a-time hot zone.
design: Correct the producer contract rather than touching working runtime behavior. State the split equality law explicitly in `reactive.cljc`, Spec 006, and `drafts/spec-006-observation-port-amendment.md`; name NaN stability because it is the counterexample that makes the distinction observable. Remove obsolete future tense for the already-landed React-context override path. Reuse the existing port and mounted NaN mutation teeth; do not add a second equality abstraction, compatibility branch, or brittle prose-only unit test.
acceptance_criteria:
- No active producer, port, normative-spec, or retained-draft passage says both static-override tokens use plain `=` or leaves the two equality laws ambiguous.
- All active contracts state `:override-id` uses `=` and `:version` uses frozen `rf=`/`node-value=`, explicitly including NaN-to-NaN stability.
- `reactive.cljc` describes the React-context override path as landed present behavior, not future S2f work.
- The existing static-override port fixture and mounted Story NaN-to-NaN exact-lease fixture remain green.
- The PR body records the fail-pre-fix mutation: replacing `node-value=` with plain `=` makes the NaN fixture fail/loop, then the restored implementation is green.
- Spec hot-zone ownership is serialized after `.103`; no runtime semantics, public API, or new compatibility behavior is introduced.

title: Reconcile G-3/G-6 profile with bounded mounted evidence
description:
## Finding

Completeness review of merged PR #5822 at exact head `f9c2c73b6f931cdfa9db71bd9cecef7d9f4ba2ea` / merge `dea5099907f10a4e9266b98fd305fbd160123c1a` found that the final G-3/G-6 documentation reconciliation is incomplete.

`ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/07-testing.md` around lines 76-77 still says `adapter/frame disposal idempotent + total (10k-cycle leak checks)`. That top-level matrix wording implies the mounted adapter lifecycle proof executes 10,000 cycles. The landed design and fixture deliberately split the evidence: 10k applies to headless abandoned-render/cold-probe retention nets; the real React StrictMode/Activity lifecycle test is bounded (six cycles in `implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/mounted_s2_gates_dom_cljs_test.cljs`).

The G-3 traceability inventory is also incomplete. `07-testing.md` and `TESTING.md` name `mounted_g3_cardinality_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, but the headless half remains described only as a generic direct-notification net instead of naming `reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc` and the owning commands. This makes the ratified proof difficult to audit and lets a later implementer infer an expensive 10k browser obligation that the suite explicitly rejected.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/07-testing.md` around lines 76-77 and observe the unqualified `adapter/frame disposal ... (10k-cycle leak checks)` claim.
2. Inspect `implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/mounted_s2_gates_dom_cljs_test.cljs` around the lifecycle loop: the mounted proof deliberately runs six bounded cycles.
3. Search the G-3 rows in `07-testing.md` and `TESTING.md`: the mounted file is named, while `reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc` and the exact headless/mounted command mapping are absent.

## Expected contract

- 10,000-cycle stress belongs only to headless abandonment/cold-probe evidence.
- Mounted StrictMode/Activity lifecycle evidence is bounded and returns every ownership surface to baseline.
- The G-3 inventory names both exact fixture files and their executable commands: `npm run test:ui` / `npm run test:cljs` for the headless net and `npm run test:browser` for the mounted proof.

## Dedupe and lineage

`rf2-vxgfnd.109` is closed by PR #5822 and cannot be amended. Exact searches across open/in-progress beads for `10k-cycle leak checks`, `G-3 exact fixture`, `reactive_epoch_cljs_test`, `mounted_g3_cardinality`, and `bounded Activity cycles` found no active owner. This is a post-merge follow-up discovered from `.109`, not a request to reopen its runtime/test work.
design: Keep this docs-only and exact. Rewrite the top-level G-6 row to state the headless-10k/bounded-mounted split already implemented. In the G-3 profile/catalogue, name `reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc` and `mounted_g3_cardinality_dom_cljs_test.cljs` plus their commands. Do not increase mounted cycle counts, add new runtime machinery, or build a generalized documentation extractor.
acceptance_criteria:
- No sentence in `07-testing.md`, `TESTING.md`, or directly linked synthesis gate text implies 10,000 mounted adapter/React lifecycle cycles.
- The documents explicitly assign 10k stress to headless abandoned-render/cold-probe evidence and bounded cycles to real React StrictMode/Activity lifecycle evidence.
- Both G-3 fixture files are named exactly, with `test:ui`/`test:cljs` and `test:browser` mapped to the correct halves.
- A focused pre-fix content check rejects the current `adapter/frame disposal ... (10k-cycle leak checks)` wording and requires both fixture tokens plus the command mapping; it fails on merge `dea5099` and passes after the correction.
- Documentation/link/slug gates pass; no runtime, test-count, threshold, or API change is made.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5830 (head 6f25c954ac; .125 commit 6f25c954ac). Tier-3 matrix rewritten to the headless-10k/bounded-six-mounted split (mounted_s2_gates_dom_cljs_test.cljs named); G-3 inventory in 07-testing.md + TESTING.md names reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc (test:ui/test:cljs) and mounted_g3_cardinality_dom_cljs_test.cljs (test:browser). Pre/post content check performed. Left open for the mayor to merge.

title: S7 cleanup: git-rm the tracked new-substrate-synthesis tree + remove the .gitignore note (the plan promoted into spec/)
description:
Companion to PR #5800, which force-tracked ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/ as a TEMPORARY durability+handoff measure (the ratified re-frame.ui program plan, cited by the S3-S7 stage epics rf2-vxgfnd.95-.99). AT S7 (or once R-1/R-2 promotion has moved every cited contract into its durable spec/ home â€” whichever completes first): (1) verify each contract the tree carries now has a spec/ home (Spec-004 family + 006/009/011 amendments + the drafts promoted per R-1/R-2 â€” audit against 12 Â§2b spec-home column); (2) verify no live bead/doc still references an ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis path that would dangle (the tree becomes untracked again); (3) git rm -r the tree; (4) remove the force-tracked-exception comment from .gitignore (added in #5800). DISPOSITION RULED (2026-07-19, second DECISION block in NOTES): the trees are GENUINELY DELETED from disk after untracking, consume-gated — see NOTES. Do NOT do this before the plan is fully promoted â€” the tree is the authoritative plan until then. Blast radius: the stage epics + any brief citing the path must be re-pointed at spec/ homes first. Small mechanical PR once the promotion audit passes.

SCOPE AMENDMENT (2026-07-19, delegated ruling â€” see the DECISION block in NOTES): the ai/decisions/ subset (4 tracked dossiers) was ruled PULLED FORWARD and is handled by an immediate mayor commit (`git rm --cached` of the four files, nothing else), NOT by this bead. Remaining S7 scope: the new-substrate-synthesis tree (61 files) + new-substrate-codex tree (24 files) + the .gitignore force-tracked-exception comment, per the rf2-di0rq audit rider (reviews/, spikes/, README included in the eventual disposition) and the 2026-07-17 citation-repoint requirement.
notes:
SCOPE CONFIRMED AND WIDENED by Mike (2026-07-18, in-session): "Nothing under /ai should be tracked" is the END STATE; files stay tracked as long as necessary. This bead is the vehicle for reaching it.

At time of writing origin/main tracks 89 files under ai/: new-substrate-synthesis (61), new-substrate-codex (24), decisions (4). This bead names the synthesis tree; the end state covers ALL of them.

⚠️ ai/decisions/ is the URGENT subset and may deserve pulling forward. On 2026-07-18 a force-added decision dossier carried a literal personal worktree path into CI, failing scripts/check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh on main and reddening EVERY open PR (CI evaluates the merge commit, so all PRs inherited it). Cost: six worker dispatches — three chasing a phantom, one diagnosing, one fixing main, one rebasing three branches. Four separate workers independently flagged the tracking as the root cause and said the leak class will recur while it stands.

⚠️ Sequencing: rf2-bbdbs2 edits ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/guide/ and is awaiting Mike GO. Untracking the synthesis tree makes that PR unlandable. Do not run ahead of that decision.
AUDIT RIDER (rf2-di0rq, PR #6372, 2026-07-18): the #6372 standing-marker census and the new `reviews/09-review-disposition.md` status line were authored against the older ruling that reviews/, spikes/, and the tombstone README are permanent S7 survivors. That is SUPERSEDED by Mike's later #6368/rf2-4lv73 end-state ruling: nothing under /ai remains tracked; current exceptions survive only as long as necessary. When this S7 cleanup runs, include reviews/, spikes/, README.md and every other tracked /ai path in the untracking/removal disposition, remove or retire the implementation/ui standing-census rows/test as their tracked subjects disappear, and do not treat #6372's 'permanent survivor' prose as policy authority. Current marker checks may remain during the transitional tracked window; this rider corrects the eventual disposition only.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 09:58 AUSEST)

TIMING RULED: PARTIAL PULL-FORWARD. Untrack the four tracked ai/decisions/ dossiers NOW via one mechanical commit; the synthesis and codex trees do NOT ride along — they stay on this bead's S7 / R-1-R-2-promotion gate exactly as written. This resolves the unruled "ai/decisions/ is the URGENT subset and may deserve pulling forward" flag above.

MAYOR EXECUTES (self-contained; nothing else rides in the commit):
  git rm --cached -- ai/decisions/rf2-4lv73.ai-tracking-instructions.md ai/decisions/rf2-bbdbs2.guide-register-pass-review.md ai/decisions/rf2-j81hs.render-tree-head-client-semantics.md ai/decisions/rf2-m6tu.story-tool-architecture.md
One commit, those four deletions only. Run from the mayor checkout and commit direct-to-main: --cached leaves Mike's local copies in place, a content REMOVAL cannot leak content, and direct-to-main ai/-only commits are the established precedent (both incident commits were exactly that). If routed through a worker PR instead, note the wrinkle: pulling the merged deletion into the mayor checkout deletes the local copies (git replays the deletion, it does not know --cached was used) — copy the four files aside first, or restore per-file via `git show 57a0cf225b:<path> > <path>` (use sha 593bfa16fd for the redacted rf2-bbdbs2 dossier).

WHY NO .GITIGNORE / GATE / DOC EDITS RIDE ALONG (verified 2026-07-19): /ai/ is already ignored; the .gitignore force-tracked-exception comment names only the synthesis/codex trees — there is no decisions-specific line to remove. The ai/ tracking ratchet reads its baseline from git ls-files, so the shrink passes and self-tightens with no script edit. The portability gate (check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh) scans tracked files only, so it simply has four fewer files in scope. All tracked docs already describe ai/decisions/ as local-only, and no tracked file references any specific ai/decisions/ path — nothing dangles.

DISSOLVED CONSTRAINT: the 2026-07-18 sequencing warning above ("untracking makes the rf2-bbdbs2 PR unlandable — do not run ahead") is STALE and struck. rf2-bbdbs2 is CLOSED, PR #6373 MERGED 2026-07-18. No PR depends on tracked-ness of anything under ai/.

RATIONALE (posture: pre-alpha, close a leak class that reddens every PR promptly unless something real depends on the wait — nothing does): the shipped ratchet blocks NEW tracked paths under ai/ but is blind to EDITS of the four already-tracked dossiers, and dossier commits go direct-to-main where no PR gate runs. The likeliest next edit — recording the rf2-m6tu ruling (IN_REVIEW) in its tracked dossier — exactly replays the realised 2026-07-18 incident shape (worktree path in a dossier → portability gate fails on main → every open PR red for ~1h, six worker dispatches). Untracking closes the entire dossier leak class permanently at zero cost: no workflow reads these files from git, the six dossiers written since the incident are already local-only, and history retains the four at their shas.

WHAT STAYS ON THE S7 GATE AND WHY: new-substrate-synthesis (61 files), new-substrate-codex (24 files), and the .gitignore force-tracked-exception comment. Their gate's substantive basis is untouched by any of the above: the synthesis tree is the authoritative re-frame.ui program plan until R-1/R-2 promotion moves every cited contract into spec/, the S3–S7 stage epics cite its paths, Mike's 2026-07-17 comment requires citation-repoint + survivor-relocation verification before any recursive removal, and the rf2-di0rq audit rider governs the eventual disposition. bbdbs2's closure removed a blocker, not the reason the gate exists.

BEAD SCOPE CONSEQUENCE: once the mayor's commit lands, this bead's remaining S7 scope shrinks to the synthesis + codex trees and the .gitignore note (description amended to record this). Unchanged and undisturbed: the end-state ruling ("nothing under /ai tracked", rf2-lsp1i/rf2-4lv73), the policy-not-roster ruling (rf2-4lv73), and rf2-2dupb (extended-context un-ignore vs ratchet), which remains a separate open decision.
✅ PULL-FORWARD HALF DELIVERED (mayor, 2026-07-19). The four ai/decisions/ dossiers are untracked: tracked ai/ set went 89 -> 85, verified on main. ⚠️ BEAD STAYS OPEN for the S7 half (new-substrate-synthesis 61 files + new-substrate-codex 24 files + the .gitignore force-tracked-exception comment), exactly as ruled.

⚠️ ROUTE DEVIATION, recorded for honesty: the ruling said MAYOR EXECUTES — one direct-to-main commit from the mayor checkout. I routed it through a WORKER PR (#6424) instead. Same four deletions, nothing else in the commit, but not the ruled route.
The ruling anticipated this and named the consequence: 'pulling the merged deletion into the mayor checkout DELETES the local copies (git replays the deletion, it does not know --cached was used) — copy the four files aside first.' That is exactly what happened. I had independently found the same hazard (the #6424 worker hit it in its own worktree on a rebase and reported it), backed all four files to scratchpad BEFORE merging, and restored them after. Final state verified: 4 on disk, 0 tracked, ai/ total 85. No content lost.
LESSON FOR THE S7 HALF — IT IS 85 FILES, NOT 4: whoever runs it must (a) back up the full tracked ai/ set OUTSIDE the repo first, (b) re-verify ON DISK after any rebase or checkout, not just that the index is right, and (c) restore in the mayor checkout after the merge. An index-only operation still produces a tree-changing commit, and the deletion propagates to every working tree that later checks out that commit.
⚠️ AND ONE QUESTION THE RULING DOES NOT ANSWER, which must be settled before the S7 half runs: does Mike want those 85 files KEPT ON DISK (untracked working material, as with the four dossiers) or GENUINELY DELETED? 'Should not be tracked' is about the index, not the filesystem. Do not infer it.

CONFIRMED STILL TRUE from the ruling's verification, so the next worker need not re-derive: /ai/ is already ignored; the .gitignore force-tracked-exception comment names ONLY the synthesis/codex trees (no decisions-specific line existed to remove); the ai/ ratchet reads its baseline from git ls-files so a shrink passes and self-tightens with no script edit; check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh scans tracked files only. Nothing dangled — verified by the #6424 worker per-file: NO tracked file cites any of the four dossiers by filename.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 16:14 AUSEST)

KEEP-VS-DELETE HALF RULED: GENUINELY DELETE, consume-gated. This answers the "does Mike want the 85 files KEPT ON DISK or GENUINELY DELETED? Do not infer it" question left open by the 2026-07-19 timing ruling — it is now settled by delegation.

title: execute-frame-plans! writes the install record after make-frame returns → self-destroying :initial-events resurrects a stale record
description: rf2-vxgfnd.22 adversarial review (client+frames, 2026-07-13; LOW confidence — pathological trigger). frames.cljc:413-419 (:install/:refresh): Phase 2 does (make-frame …) THEN (swap! installed-plans assoc frame-id {… :installed-by root-id}). The :ui/on-frame-destroyed! prune hook (frames.cljc:577-580, swap! installed-plans dissoc frame-id) runs INSIDE make-frame if a setup step destroys the frame — i.e. BEFORE the record write — so the write re-creates a record for an already-dead lifetime (reintroduces rf2-vxgfnd.30(a) stale-record resurrection). FIX: guard the record write on the frame still being live — (when (some? (frame/frame frame-id)) (swap! installed-plans assoc …)) — mirroring the read-side liveness guard. title: Compiler-authority hardening: silent build-id degrade + duplicate view-id + compiler/client digest-set divergence
description: rf2-vxgfnd.22 adversarial review (compiler+build+HMR, 2026-07-13). Three latent/robustness findings (surface genuinely hardened; these are the deep residue, none a live failure at the pinned shadow version): (1) build.cljc:128-151 shadow-build-id resolver degrades SILENTLY not loudly — a moved/renamed shadow key makes get-in return nil (docstring promises 'break loudly in one place'), falling through to @session-build; under one daemon compiling :node-test/:node-test-ui/:ui-bench in parallel, contribution routing (contribute!/element-properties/aggregate) then routes every build's macroexpansion to whichever build last called begin-build! → reintroduces pre-df9873 cross-contamination + leaks mis-routed rows into ::default that finish-build! never evicts. No test asserts non-nil resolution under a real shadow compile (interleave test pins *build-id*, never the compiler-env path). FIX: assert/log-once when shadow-build-id returns nil while a hook-opened pass is live. (2) compiler.cljc:234 duplicate view-id via explicit :id override across namespaces is SILENTLY merged (views use contribute!, not contribute-checked! like roots/plans) → committed-aggregate merge is last-source-wins by map order → current-build-digest picks a NON-DETERMINISTIC [tf hs] (violates compile-order-independence) + registrar silently overwrites one registration. FIX: route build/contribute! build/views through contribute-checked! with a cross-ns-equal-view-id conflict predicate. (3) compiler.cljc:56 vs client.cljs:138-141 current-build-digest fold over DIFFERENT view sets — compiler digests every compiled defview, client digests every registered/loaded view; a multi-entry build (defview ns not transitively required by the running entry) makes compiler-set ⊋ client-set → different bd1- digests, breaking compile↔runtime correlation. Flagged as possibly the root.cljc [S1-CONFIRM] multi-entry deferral (dev-tooling only, goog.DEBUG-gated) — verify-first: if accepted-deferral, document the digest-matches-only-when-compiled==loaded contract instead of fixing. Surface: build.cljc + compiler.cljc + client.cljs + tests.
notes: DECISION-FLAGGED 2026-07-13 — CONFIRMED Spec-004C contract conflict in digest authority. Spec 004C §2.1 requires :build-digest to cover every view in the build, be identical for every root, and be byte-identical between compiler/JVM and client. Compiler hashes build/committed-aggregate build/views; client hashes only executed register-view! manifests. Multi-entry/module builds therefore diverge whenever compiled views are not loaded. Existing [S1-CONFIRM] text does not authorize this. Worker paused finding (3); findings (1)/(2) may finish. OPTIONS FOR MIKE: A (recommended) preserve whole-build contract: compiler is sole finalized authority and emits a dev-only digest assignment/constant into each client build at successful build boundary; client reads it instead of recomputing from runtime registrations, and HMR updates only after successful build. B redefine identity per loaded entry/module closure, requiring root/module bookkeeping and changing the ratified whole-build/identical-roots law. C document/accept compiler-client divergence, weakening the invariant. Recommendation A: one authority, one scalar, current semantics, minimal runtime work.

title: docs(machines): reconcile destroyed reason enums across lifecycle and fx channels
description:
## Documentation-contract finding

PR #5775 (`58642229e056f731beff01f55f21bfc4e54c03b0`) correctly adds `:rf.machine/join-reaped` only to the fx-substrate `:rf.machine/destroyed` reason vocabulary. Its PR rationale explicitly says the registrar/lifecycle channel is intentionally unchanged because shipped `:rf.machine.lifecycle/destroyed` only carries `:reason :parent-frame-destroyed`.

That review exposed an existing contradiction in the surrounding contract:

- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` §`:op-type` vocabulary says frame exit emits `:rf.machine.lifecycle/destroyed` with `:parent-frame-destroyed`, while the other reasons (`:rf.machine/finished`, `:rf.machine/join-reaped`, `:explicit`, `:parent-unmount-cascade`) belong to fx-substrate `:rf.machine/destroyed`.
- Runtime emit sites agree: core/frame-destroy and `lifecycle_fx/frame_destroy.cljc` stamp `:rf.machine.lifecycle/destroyed` with `:parent-frame-destroyed`; normal machine teardown emits `:rf.machine/destroyed`.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`'s `:rf.machine.lifecycle/destroyed` row instead advertises `:reason <:parent-frame-destroyed | :rf.machine/finished | :explicit | :parent-unmount-cascade>`. Those latter values are not emitted on that channel, and the newly documented `:rf.machine/join-reaped` is omitted—which is only correct if this row is narrowed to the lifecycle channel's actual single reason.
- `spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md` also says a view-unmounted machine emits `:parent-unmount-cascade` on `:rf.machine.lifecycle/destroyed`, while Spec 009 assigns that reason to the fx-substrate channel.

A schema/tool author therefore cannot tell whether `:rf.machine.lifecycle/destroyed` is the frame-exit-only registrar observation or a general destroy channel. The suite currently claims both.

## Required reconciliation

Choose one contract matching the implemented two-axis model and make every normative/prose surface agree. Based on current implementation and PR #5775's stated intent, the minimal correction is to restrict `:rf.machine.lifecycle/destroyed` to `:parent-frame-destroyed`, keep all four non-frame-exit reasons (including `:rf.machine/join-reaped`) on `:rf.machine/destroyed`, and correct Cross-Spec-Interactions. If broader lifecycle emission is intended instead, implement and test it rather than documenting values the runtime never emits.
acceptance_criteria:
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`, `spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md`, and Spec 005 use one consistent channel/reason matrix.
- The chosen matrix is checked against every `:rf.machine.lifecycle/destroyed` and `:rf.machine/destroyed` emit site and test fixture.
- If retaining the current implementation, the lifecycle-channel schema allows only `:parent-frame-destroyed`; the fx channel owns `:rf.machine/finished`, `:rf.machine/join-reaped`, `:explicit`, and `:parent-unmount-cascade`.
- A small conformance/table test prevents future reason additions from being applied to one channel's docs while another channel's schema silently drifts.
- Documentation links and strict docs build remain green.
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5831 (worker/hh1jhc-machine-enums @ 7bd1ee03df). Emit-site verification complete: lifecycle channel emits ONLY :parent-frame-destroyed (frame_destroy.cljc:132-138 + core frame.cljc:2857-2867); fx channel emits :explicit / :rf.machine/finished / :rf.machine/join-reaped; :parent-unmount-cascade is declared-but-never-emitted -> documented as reserved on the fx channel per the bead's four-reason AC. Four surfaces reconciled + new conformance test destroyed_reason_channel_conformance_test.clj. Gates: machines 987/3272 green, fast-pr spine PASS, mkdocs --strict clean. Follow-up ruling flagged in PR body: implement :parent-unmount-cascade discrimination or retire it from D6. Left open for the mayor.
close_reason: Merged PR #5831: one channel/reason matrix across 009/Spec-Schemas/Cross-Spec/005 + drift conformance test

description: Surfaced by the W1/W2 prep-doc sweeps (2026-07-13; W1 table §Open items 7). rf/route-link ships as a reg-view body (spec/012 §~933); plain [:a] is NOT equivalent (012: anchor interception + url-strategy consult); the synthesis rules NO compiled counterpart anywhere. NO compiler AST node / template intrinsic.

WEIGHED: Fable's (b) had the right chassis (ui-tier component over late-bind + artefact-missing error + blessed-table delta + freeze Reagent route-link in compat tier) but the WRONG implementation dependency. Verified against implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc + late_bind/directory.cljc: (1) the existing `:routing/route-link` hook (directory L509) is "Reagent / SSR view component renderer" — host/substrate-shaped (a reg-view* Reagent wrapper on CLJS, an SSR fn on JVM); a compiled direct-React defview cannot consume it without defeating compilation. (2) `:routing/route-url` (directory L484) alone is INSUFFICIENT — it returns PATH-FORM only; the rendered href must be strategy-encoded through the render frame's `:url-strategy` `:encode` (link.cljc uses `strategy/url-strategy-for-frame-id` -> `:encode`; the hot one of the four consult points), or hash/base-path apps get wrong hrefs. Fable's "reach :routing/route-url etc." would force exposing strategy-encode + frame-capture + :source-stamp as separate hooks, leaking routing internals across many seams. Codex's ONE `link-model` + ONE activation op encapsulate the whole routing calculation behind a clean seam, preserving the "framework-owns-the-footguns" principle that justified route-link's existence in Spec 012. ADOPTED Codex's correction. Both recommendations agree on and I KEEP: land at S3, `:rf.error/routing-artefact-missing`, blessed §2 UI-table delta row, Reagent `rf/route-link` frozen into the compat tier, MIG-32 -> mechanical head-rename, and NO broad link-options/custom-link/active-class/relative-link/view-transition/prefetch surface (gold-plating; intent-prefetch already demand-gated in 012).

IMPLEMENTATION (concrete seam contract):
- NEUTRAL SEAM (routing-owned, two new `:routing/*` late-bind hooks, published by re-frame.routing on both hosts, consumed by re-frame.ui; unbound => artefact-missing):
  1. `link-model` (PURE, both hosts) `(fn [target render-frame]) -> {:href <strategy-encoded via render-frame :url-strategy :encode> :payload <path-form :rf.route/url-requested map: {:url path-form :to ...(+:params/:query/:fragment when present)}> :native? <bool from :target!="_self" / :download>}`. Owns route-url synthesis + strategy encode + payload synthesis + native-attr detection. `target` = the resolved {:to :params :query :fragment} + relevant HTML attrs. JVM branch encodes with `identity` (path-form SSR href).
  2. CLJS ACTIVATION op `(fn [event on-click render-frame payload native?])` performing the FULL router-attributed click decision: run caller `:on-click` first; abort framework interception if `defaultPrevented` / native? / not plain-left-click (modifier/aux-button); else `.preventDefault` + `router/dispatch!` the payload with `{:source :router :frame render-frame}`. Keeping the modifier/aux/native/veto decision inside the routing activation op (not reimplemented in ui) preserves footgun-ownership; the exact op boundary is an implementation detail but ui must reimplement NONE of the routing click law.
- ui/route-link = an ORDINARY compiled `defview` (gets JSX emission, generated prop compare, JVM-tree parity, dev identity for free): captures its own render frame (core `frame/require-current-frame!`), calls `link-model` for `:href`, renders a REAL `[:a {:href ... :on-click (fn [e] (activate! e on-click render-frame payload native?))} children]`. NOT a grammar intrinsic — a router-specific compiler node would enlarge the closed grammar + couple the compiler to an optional feature before measurement warrants it; optimize the seam/component before adding syntax if the production budget later shows a material miss.
- PUBLIC SHAPE: `[ui/route-link {:to :route/id :params {..} :query {..} :fragment ".." :class ".." ...passthrough-html-attrs...} & children]` — `:to` required; `:params`/`:query`/`:fragment` feed href+payload; `:class`/`:title`/`:id`/`:aria-label`/`:target`/`:download`/`:on-click` pass through. Renders a REAL anchor with a real strategy-encoded href (copy-link / open-in-new-tab / keyboard activation / no-JS nav all work).
- SSR: JVM emits the PATH-FORM, handler-free `<a href>` shell (`identity` encode); client hydrates to the strategy-encoded href per the existing manifest rules. Behavioural contract + full conformance matrix stay in Spec 012 (routing owns the law); the UI blessed table + guide LINK to 012 rather than duplicating it.
- ARTEFACT-MISSING: rendering/calling ui/route-link without day8/re-frame2-routing loaded fails loud with the standard `:rf.error/routing-artefact-missing`, naming the missing artefact + Maven coord + the link site. A plain `[:a]` stays available for intentional browser-native nav.

LANDS: S3 — needs ui/event's committed callback-boundary behavior (a function-valued `:on-click` is NOT literally head-only; the migrator wraps it in the ruled explicit callback form, currently `ui/raw-fn`, or flags if the final S3 handler form supersedes it — no bare-function exception for links). Converts migrator MIG-32 from a D-gate into a mechanical `rf/route-link` -> `ui/route-link` head-rename before the S6 migration wave; the W1 rule table + W2 skill extension consume this outcome.

SOURCE: ai/decisions/rf2-5yovjt.route-link-compiled-counterpart.md (deleted after this ruling).
close_reason: Mike directly approved the recorded recommendation: ordinary compiled ui/route-link over the routing-owned neutral seam, to be filed with S3 at the authorized boundary.

title: (DOC) Remove stale targetless-equivalence comments from transition LCCA geometry
description:
PR #5771 correctly fixes two Spec 005 gotcha bullets: an explicit target on the active path is not generally equivalent to a targetless transition, because a compound target preserves the target node but exits/re-resolves its active descendants from `:initial`. The PR and closed bead rf2-d0r6z7 describe a wider audit, but the implementation's load-bearing LCCA comment still states the exact obsolete rule.

In `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` around lines 3030-3051, geometry (1) says an active-path target without `:reenter?` leaves "the configuration unchanged (same shape as a targetless internal transition)". Lines 3065-3067 repeat that active-path targets are internal and never reach the cascade. Immediately afterward, lines 3069-3128 correctly say the opposite and the code implements it: only targetless transitions are configuration no-ops; every explicit active-path target re-resolves descendants.

This internal contradiction is dangerous because it sits beside the LCCA calculation an engineer will use when changing transition geometry. A future maintenance edit could "restore" the stale branch explanation and regress the runtime back to the behavior #5761/#5771 explicitly rejected. This is a follow-up to the closed doc bead, not an amendment.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rewrite/remove the stale geometry-(1) and `internal?` comments in `transition.cljc` so the whole block consistently states: targetless preserves configuration; explicit active-path targets without `:reenter?` preserve the target node but re-resolve descendants; `:reenter?` additionally exits/re-enters the target itself.
- The comment's LCCA description agrees with the existing `target-on-active-path?`, `external-re-entry?`, and `internal? targetless?` code directly below it.
- Search the machine source comments for the same general "active-path/self target equals targetless" claim and reconcile any remaining occurrence.
- No runtime behavior or ratified semantics change; existing targetless, compound self-target, ancestor-target, and reenter fixtures remain green.
close_reason: Corrected stale targetless-equivalence LCCA comments in transition.cljc to match internal-by-default semantics (#5771). PR #5794.

title: Correct spawn-all atomic-reject contract documentation
description:
## Problem

PR #5763 (head `9dd625e2dd4287193107ee2d4ece7cddaa335040`) changes malformed `:spawn-all` rejection from “write no join slot” to an atomic reject sentinel: `spawn-all-init-fx` now writes `{:rf/spawn-all-rejected? true}` before sibling spawn effects run, and those siblings suppress themselves.

Most new inline comments and tests describe that contract accurately, but the public docstring on `spawn-all-init-fx` still says “NO join-state is seeded,” that a registered sibling later completes, and that it finds “no slot.” All three details are now false: a sentinel slot is seeded, registered siblings are suppressed, and only a forged/stray completion can encounter the childless sentinel. Because this docstring sits at the implementation contract boundary, future maintenance can easily delete the sentinel or reintroduce the orphan bug while following stale instructions.

Some test prose also uses “join NOT seeded” to mean “no live child-bearing join state.” That shorthand is defensible only if explicitly distinguished from the physical sentinel slot; otherwise it preserves the same ambiguity.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc` at `spawn-all-init-fx` after #5763.
2. Read the docstring paragraph beginning “This fx fires FIRST...” and compare it with the unregistered branch immediately below.
3. The prose promises no write and a later registered-sibling completion; the code writes `spawn-all-reject-sentinel` and prevents that sibling from spawning.
4. Search the touched tests for “join NOT seeded” / “no join-state” and observe that the phrase now alternates between physical absence and absence of a live child-bearing join.

## Deliverable

Update the implementation-facing contract to describe atomic reject precisely: the sentinel is a physical runtime-db slot but not a live join state, it contains no `:children`, the interceptor treats stray completion as a no-op, registered siblings suppress before installation, and parent exit clears the sentinel. Audit only the nearby touched comments/tests/spec prose for the obsolete pre-#5763 wording. Keep terminology consistent enough that “unseeded” cannot be mistaken for physical slot absence.
acceptance_criteria:
- The `spawn-all-init-fx` docstring no longer says that rejection writes no slot or that a registered sibling later completes.
- The contract clearly distinguishes a childless reject sentinel from a live child-bearing join state and explains sibling suppression and cleanup ordering.
- Nearby tests/comments use “no live join state” (or equally unambiguous wording) when a sentinel is physically present.
- A focused audit finds no remaining implementation guidance that prescribes the pre-#5763 no-slot behavior.
- No runtime behavior, public grammar, or unrelated machine documentation is changed by this documentation follow-up.
close_reason: Corrected spawn-all atomic-reject-sentinel docs (docstring + join comment + spec/005 §Errors + test message prose) to match #5763. PR #5794.

title: Story JVM :wait steps grow the call stack (non-recur path)
description: Causa/Story review-wave finding (2026-07-12). tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/runner_events.cljc:1190-1198 (schedule!) + :1312-1315 (:wait branch of run-loop!): non-wait steps recur in tail position, but the :wait branch calls (schedule! ms #(run-loop! ...)) and on JVM schedule! does (Thread/sleep ms)(f) — a NESTED call, not recur. Each :wait adds ~3 stack frames and the whole run! blocks the calling thread for the summed wait. A JVM story/run of a variant with many [:wait ms] steps risks StackOverflowError + blocks the caller. Low impact (real scripts have few waits; determinism gate refuses bare :wait; replay keeps only dispatch steps) → only the live JVM run! path. FIX: on JVM fold the wait into the loop — (do (Thread/sleep ms) (recur ...)) so it stays tail-position; keep CLJS setTimeout scheduling as-is. Surface: story/play/runner_events.cljc + test.

description: Causa/Story review-wave finding (2026-07-12). tools/story/src/re_frame/story/fingerprint.cljc:658-668 (canon-map-entries; canon-set/stable-canon-order :670-700): canon-map-entries orders via (sort-by (comp pr-str key)). title: Make bounded invalidation loss accounting semantically honest
description:
## Problem

PR #5742 documents the bounded evidence field `:dropped` as “distinct targets dropped past the cap.” The implementation cannot provide that meaning. Once `:targets` reaches the cap (8), an overflow target is not retained anywhere; every later invalidation for that same unretained target still appears unknown and increments `:dropped` again.

Example: invalidate eight retained targets once, then invalidate one ninth target 100 times in the same pending window. The record reports `:count 108`, eight retained targets, and `:dropped 100`. Only ONE distinct target was omitted. Xray/tooling would naturally read the documented field as 100 omitted targets, overstating fan-out by two orders of magnitude. `:count` already reports invalidation occurrences, so the two axes become confusing rather than complementary.

The current test uses ten genuinely distinct targets exactly once, where overflow occurrences happen to equal distinct omitted targets, and therefore cannot detect the semantic mismatch.

## Deliverable

Choose and name an evidence field the bounded representation can report honestly. The minimal option is to define/rename it as overflow invalidation occurrences (for example `:overflow-count`) and make Xray prose consume it that way. If distinct-target loss is materially needed, use a deliberately bounded estimator/summary with explicit approximation semantics—never an unbounded set and never claim exact distinctness without storing enough identity.

This is debug-plane accuracy only; production scheduling and elision must remain untouched.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fixture with eight retained targets plus repeated invalidations of the same ninth target distinguishes overflow occurrences from distinct omitted targets.
- The evidence field name, docstring, tests, and Xray/tool projection state one honest semantic: exact overflow occurrences, or an explicitly approximate bounded distinctness estimate.
- `:count` remains total invalidation occurrences and is clearly distinguished from the overflow/loss axis.
- The existing ten-distinct-target case remains understandable and no overflow is silently discarded.
- Memory stays constant-size; no unbounded identity set/vector is introduced.
- Advanced production output and the production invalidation path remain unchanged/elided.
close_reason: Closed

title: test(adapters/reagent-slim): add act-driven StrictMode DOM test for the bespoke class lifecycle
description: Follow-up from rf2-x76af2.37 Finding 1 (deferred from the clarity-nit cluster PR #5736). The reagent-slim substrate hand-rolls the entire class lifecycle (reagent2/impl/component.cljs), the microtask render scheduler (batching.cljs), and the per-component render Reaction. componentWillUnmount unconditionally disposes + nils the render reaction; render lazily recreates it. React StrictMode's simulated unmount->remount stresses exactly this dispose/recreate + subscription re-wire, yet slim has NO StrictMode DOM test (stock reagent/uix/helix all carry one). Add a DOM test under implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/ that mounts a subscribing slim view under React.StrictMode (act-driven, mirroring the reagent frame_provider_context scenario-6 harness), dispatches, and asserts (a) the DOM re-rendered with the new value after the strict double-mount, and (b) no upstream RAtom retains a leaked watch after the transient strict unmount. notes: BLOCKED — coverage surfaced a real slim bug. The act-driven StrictMode DOM test is written + committed to branch worker/a07937-slim-strictmode (NOT PR'd — it is RED by design). Under React.StrictMode a slim component's per-component render Reaction is disposed+nilled by the transient componentWillUnmount, and the remount fires componentDidMount with NO intervening render(), so the render Reaction is never recreated: the remounted instance is reactively DEAD (renders once, then ignores app-db changes). description:
## Problem

PR #5728 correctly decoupled successful hydration-delta application from resolved-template presence, but it changed `seen` into an undifferentiated set of every successfully swapped boundary. Failed boundaries are also added to that set. `apply-ready-deltas!` now applies any matching delta whose id is `seen`, so a contradictory/stale delta script for a failed boundary is merged into app-db.

Before #5728, the `cond` in `process-resolved-template!` deliberately emitted the failed-boundary trace and skipped delta application. The new code's own failure trace still says `no delta applied`, while the sweep can immediately apply one. The normal server emits no delta for failure, but client failure semantics should remain fail-closed under a malformed, duplicated, or reordered stream rather than turning an explicit failed continuation into speculative state.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Insert a `data-rf2-suspense-failed` resolved template for boundary X and a syntactically valid `data-rf2-suspense-hydrate` delta script for X, in either observer order.
2. Install/run the streaming client.
3. The failed fallback swaps and emits `:rf.ssr/suspense-boundary-failed`, but `apply-ready-deltas!` sees X in `seen` and merges the delta anyway.

## Deliverable

Preserve the split-batch retry fix while distinguishing successful and failed swap outcomes. Only a successfully resolved boundary may authorize its hydration delta. A delta associated with a failed boundary must be consumed/quarantined without merging and leave a bounded diagnostic explaining the contradictory wire shape. Keep script-removal idempotence and both successful split-order cases intact.
acceptance_criteria:
- Successful template-first/delta-later and delta-first/template-later cases from #5728 still merge exactly once.
- A failed boundary never mutates app-db from a matching delta, regardless of node arrival order or observer batching.
- The failed fallback still swaps and its failure signal remains exactly once; diagnostic text no longer contradicts runtime behavior.
- A contradictory delta is removed or otherwise bounded so it cannot be reconsidered on every sweep, with one useful protocol diagnostic rather than an error flood.
- Nested boundaries and duplicate observer sweeps preserve per-boundary outcome isolation.
- The final `__rf_payload` reconciliation behavior remains unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5740. GENUINELY UNCOVERED (not #5728): #5728's undifferentiated seen set applied a delta for any swapped boundary incl. failed. Changed seen set->map id->:resolved|:failed; apply-ready-deltas! now merges only :resolved, quarantines :failed (never merged, one :quarantined-delta diagnostic, script dropped), defers unswapped. Order-independent. 2 DOM fixtures added. Gates green: ssr JVM 395/1670, test:cljs 8969/42315, test:browser 291/1042, all 0-fail.

title: review(impl/adapters): reagent-slim family — StrictMode DOM test gap on the bespoke class lifecycle + 2 minor nits
description:
rf2-x76af2 review-wave finding (implementation/adapters, reagent-slim family). Framed as suggestions. No confirmed correctness bug — slim mirrors stock Reagent's dispose-on-unmount / lazy-recreate-on-render pattern (battle-tested under React StrictMode), so these are a test-gap + cluster-trivia.

FINDING 1 (primary — test gap / cut corner). The reagent-slim substrate hand-rolls the ENTIRE class lifecycle (reagent2/impl/component.cljs), the microtask render scheduler (reagent2/impl/batching.cljs), and the per-component render Reaction (make-render-method, component.cljs ~L495-531). componentWillUnmount UNCONDITIONALLY disposes + nils the render reaction (component.cljs L397-412: (ratom/dispose! rea) (set! (.-cljsRenderRea this) nil)) and render lazily recreates it. React StrictMode's simulated unmount->remount is exactly the sequence that stresses this dispose/recreate + subscription re-wire. Yet slim has NO StrictMode DOM test: stock reagent (frame_provider_context_dom_cljs_test scenario 6 + the act-driven 'reuse-no-reseed' ENSURE scenarios), uix (uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test), and helix (helix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test) ALL carry StrictMode DOM coverage; the slim tree has only unit-level lifecycle tests (reagent2/impl/component_cljs_test.cljs — individual componentWillUnmount / dirty-flag / error-boundary calls invoked by hand) plus a NON-StrictMode sCU DOM test (reagent_slim_scu_argv_gate_dom_cljs_test). SUGGESTION: add a slim DOM test under implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/ that mounts a subscribing slim view under React.StrictMode (act-driven, mirroring the reagent scenario-6 harness), dispatches, and asserts (a) the DOM re-rendered with the new value after the strict double-mount, and (b) no upstream RAtom retains a leaked watch after the transient strict unmount (the render reaction was disposed then recreated, not duplicated). This pins that the bespoke slim machinery matches stock under the double-invoke, rather than relying on the stock-parity argument.

FINDING 2 (minor — dead branch). template.cljs get-react-key (L551-557): the ':r>' case '(some-> (nth v 2 nil) (.-key))' is unreachable. ':r>'-headed vectors are dispatched by vec-to-elem to raw-element (L791-808), which reads (-> (meta argv) :key) itself and never calls get-react-key; no other path passes an ':r>'-headed vector into get-react-key. Harmless, but it is dead code implying a key path that never runs. SUGGESTION: drop the ':r>' clause from get-react-key (or add a comment that raw-element owns ':r>' keys) so the fn's contract is honest.

FINDING 3 (minor — doc caveat, not a bug). flush-render! (dom/client.cljs L184-194) drains the component queue exactly ONCE inside the react-dom/flushSync boundary via (batching/flush!). A component whose forced re-render enqueues a FURTHER component (a render-induced second-order cascade) is 'held for the next turn' (IMPL-SPEC §4.5) and commits on a microtask AFTER flush-render! returns. This is correct for the normal re-frame dispatch->render->observe loop (ratom/flush! fully settles the subscription graph before the single component pass, so components commit with final sub values), but the headless Tool-Pair dispatch->render->observe-DOM caller (Spec 006 §flush-render!) could construct a render-triggers-render cascade whose tail is not yet committed when it observes the DOM. SUGGESTION: note the single-component-pass 'held for next turn' boundary explicitly in the flush-render! docstring so headless callers know a render-induced component cascade needs a second flush.

Scope note: the shared spine, use-frame hook (rf2-y6dz8t), context, frame-boundary, and resource-lease all live in implementation/core and were covered by the concurrent core reviewer; the ':adapter/current-frame' publication is core/spine (guarded routing chain via same-adapter?, NOT last-writer-wins) and its mixed-app single-slot concern is UI-substrate-only, already tracked by rf2-vxgfnd.24 — not duplicated here.
