title: review(impl/core): observation disposal-cause mislabel + 2 minor lease-hygiene/hardening notes
description:
rf2-x76af2 review-wave finding for the implementation/core (engine) slice. READ-ONLY review across correctness / completeness / clarity / best-practice / test-rigour lenses over `implementation/core/src/re_frame/**` — the event/fx/router pipeline, subscription/reaction cache, frame lifecycle (frame, registrar), interop, and the `re-frame.substrate.observation` port. Overall the engine is exceptionally solid: the sub-cache ref-count/CAS-after-snapshot disposal (subs/cache.cljc), the two-phase-atomic `:dispatch-later` timer side table (fx.cljc:274-398), the single-drainer `:drain-lock` invariant + reentrant/hold-lock drain entries (router.cljc:3096-3228), and the HMR transitive `:<-` invalidation closure (subs/cache.cljc:190-253) are all correct and well-reasoned. Findings below are minor; all framed as suggestions.

FINDING 1 (correctness-under-race + elegance; primary) — observation disposal-cause is decided by WHICH drain fires, not by why the node died, so a frame-destroy/cache-clear notification can be delivered mislabeled `:hmr`.
- observation.cljc:342-382 (`pending-disposals` / `enqueue-disposal!` / `drain-pending-disposals!`) and :925-935 (registrar HMR-drain hook). `enqueue-disposal!` is the SINGLE enqueue path for every node-disposed notification regardless of cause (it is invoked from `node-disposed-hook`, which fires for HMR invalidation, frame-destroy, cache-clear, and 1->0 ref-count disposal alike). The cause is assigned solely by the draining boundary: the registrar replacement hook drains the WHOLE queue with `:hmr`; the next-tick fallback drains with `:disposed`. `drain-pending-disposals!` (observation.cljc:359-370) applies its single `cause` arg to EVERY pending lease.
- Consequence: if a frame-destroy (or explicit cache-clear) enqueues a lease and its next-tick fallback has not yet fired when an unrelated `:sub` re-registration runs, that frame-destroy lease is swept into the synchronous `:hmr` drain and delivered `{:cause :hmr ...}`. The `:cause` value is a documented part of the port's `on-change` payload contract (ns docstring §HMR-disposal notifications; `acquire!` docstring lists `:cause :value|:hmr|:disposed`). A consumer that branches on `:hmr` (re-acquire same target) vs `:disposed` (target gone) would, on the mislabel, attempt a re-acquire against a destroyed frame and hit fail-loud `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` -> view error boundary. Narrow window (needs a frame-destroy/clear notification still pending when an HMR re-registration lands; on CLJS goog.async.nextTick usually beats the next hot-reload macrotask, so mostly a JVM-reachable ordering) but it is a genuine contract violation.
- Fix sketch: carry the intended cause with each queued entry rather than deriving it from the drain boundary. Have the disposing cache sites pass the cause into the reaction's disposal so `node-disposed-hook`/`enqueue-disposal!` store `[lease cause]` pairs (or keep two queues keyed by cause). `drain-pending-disposals!` then delivers each lease its OWN cause, and the registrar HMR hook drains only the `:hmr`-tagged entries, leaving `:disposed`-tagged frame-destroy/clear entries for the next-tick fallback. This also reads more clearly than "cause == which boundary happened to drain me".

FINDING 2 (leak-hygiene; minor) — a released node lease keeps a strong ref to its now-disposed reaction.
- observation.cljc:863-911 (`release!`). The live->released transition flips `:status` and detaches the watch + owner enrolment + ref-count, but leaves `:reaction` (and `:on-change`) in the lease's `state` atom. A released-but-still-reachable lease therefore pins the disposed reaction object (and its closed-over compute state) until the consumer drops the lease. This is the mirror of the rf2-vxgfnd.15 direction (there: reaction retaining released leases; here: released lease retaining the reaction) and is bounded by consumer lease-retention rather than unbounded, so it is hygiene not a true leak — but nil-ing `:reaction`/`:on-change` on the release transition (they are unused after release; `read`-after-release only needs `:query-v`/`:frame-id` for its error text) would drop the dangling ref promptly and matches the "released lease retains nothing" intent already asserted for the owner-set.

FINDING 3 (JVM hardening; minor) — `acquire!` can register the node-disposed hook on an already-disposed reaction, which then never fires.
- observation.cljc:731-763. Between `subs/acquire-cache-reaction!` returning a reaction and `interop/add-on-dispose! reaction (node-disposed-hook reaction)`, a concurrent HMR/frame-destroy on another thread could dispose that reaction. JVM `interop/dispose!` clears the Reaction's `callbacks` and never re-fires (interop.clj:92-98), so a hook appended afterward is dead and the owner is never notified. Not observably broken today: the ref-count was bumped so ordinary 1->0 cannot hit; and the headless read-point posture means `current?`/`read` at commit still detect the non-canonical node and retarget. Worth a one-line note in the acquire docstring (or an is-disposed re-check) so the reliance on commit-time detection for this window is explicit rather than incidental.

TEST GAP (complements, do NOT duplicate, rf2-vxgfnd.29) — the mixed-cause drain in FINDING 1 is unexercised. observation_port_cljs_test.cljc drives only the pure-`:hmr` path (`hmr-reregistration-notifies-former-owners-once-with-cause-hmr`) and never the `:disposed` next-tick fallback nor the frame-destroy-lease-swept-by-a-coincident-HMR interleaving. rf2-vxgfnd.29 already flags ":disposed-cause drain untested"; a case that enqueues a frame-destroy/clear notification and then fires an HMR drain, asserting the frame-destroy lease still receives `:disposed`, would pin FINDING 1's fix.
close_reason: Addressed in PR #5758 (commit 6c23e27). FINDING 2 (leak-hygiene): JVM reaction strong-pin already resolved by #5753 (.37 weak ref); this nils :reaction + :on-change on the live->released transition so a retained released lease pins neither the on-change closure (both hosts) nor the CLJS reaction (both-host fixture added). FINDING 3 (install-on-disposed-reaction note): subsumed by the rf2-vxgfnd.70 honest-readiness rewrite (canonicality re-check + own-backstop-hook, made explicit in docstrings). FINDING 1 (disposal-cause mislabel, the real one): REAL + unresolved by #5753, but the fix needs the four subs/cache.cljc disposal sites to thread their cause into the port enqueue — outside this worker's observation.cljc-only surface — filed as follow-up rf2-r8jmdb with full plan + acceptance test.

title: review(tools/story): recorder new-variant-id silent fallback + read-failures/with-variant-id doc drift
description:
rf2-x76af2 review-wave finding for the tools/story + tools/story-mcp slice. Read-only review; framed as suggestions. Overall the slice is in excellent shape — the override/isolation model (sub_overrides render-path context carriage), the MCP wire contract (protocol/normalize-frame no-intern ingress, wire-pipeline dedup→cap ordering, mcp-base conformance), and the unified run-result consumption are all correct and heavily tested (DoS frame-cap + UTF-8 byte counting + surrogate recombination, too-wide body caps, unknown-arg diagnostics, and the CLJS→UI→MCP run-result roundtrip all have direct tests). The 20-tool registry matches spec/002 and the shared tool-names.json fixture. Findings below are minor.

FINDING 1 (low-med; behavioral gotcha, snippet-only recorder path) — tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc:291-307
In tool-record-as-variant, the non-write-back branch resolves :new-variant-id via `(or (args/safe-keyword (:new-variant-id arguments) (story/ids :variant)) vk)` — i.e. it only honours an id that ALREADY names a registered variant, else silently falls back to the source `vk`. Net effect: in the read-only (no write-back / no --allow-writes) path, the generated `(reg-variant ...)` snippet's first-line :variant-id literal can NEVER carry a genuinely NEW id — the very case the arg exists for (you record a canvas to author a NEW variant). Passing e.g. :new-variant-id ":story.cart/recorded" on a snippet-only call silently emits a snippet titled with the SOURCE id, no diagnostic. The no-intern rationale is sound, but the SNIPPET is text — a first-line literal needs no interned keyword. Suggest: after grammar-validating the string via `story/valid-variant-id?` (as the write-back arm already does with fresh-keyword-checked), either render the validated string literal directly in the snippet, or surface an `isError`/diagnostic that the suggested id was ignored because it is unregistered and :write-back was not set — rather than silently substituting a different value than the caller asked for. At minimum, tighten the docstring/description to say snippet-only recordings cannot title with a fresh id (use :write-back).

FINDING 2 (low; doc clarity) — tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/args.cljc:421-432 and tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:365-371
The with-variant-id docstring says it is for "tools whose reads tolerate an unregistered variant (read-a11y-violations, read-failures, unregister-variant)" and then immediately states "the no-intern bound means an UNREGISTERED variant id can't resolve through this surface either" — self-contradictory. What these tools actually tolerate is a REGISTERED-but-never-RUN (body-less) variant; they still require registration (safe-keyword against `story/ids :variant`). tool-read-failures example 3 ("Never-run variant: {:variant-id ":story.never/run"}") reads as though any id works, but a genuinely unregistered id returns "Variant not found". Suggest rewording "unregistered" → "never-run (but registered)" in both places so a maintainer/agent doesn't infer these tools accept arbitrary ids.

FINDING 3 (low; spec/doc precision) — tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md:80-93 (§Egress indicator counts)
The spec groups read-failures with preview-variant/run-variant as tools that "replace over-threshold / schema-:large? :app-db leaves with the :rf.size/large-elided marker". But read-failures carries NO :app-db (nor a derived tree) and its egress path (egress/scrub-assertions+count → sensitive/strip-sensitive) only DROPS :sensitive? records — it never runs elide-wire-value, so its :elided-large count via count-elided is structurally always 0 and the slot is always omitted. Behaviour is correct (omit-when-zero), but the spec text overstates read-failures' egress. Suggest clarifying that read-failures contributes only :dropped-sensitive, and relies on the wire-boundary cap (overflow marker) for size bounding rather than per-leaf elision.

Non-blocking observation (no action requested): protocol.cljc read-bounded-line's byte-exact surrogate-pair recombination (322-420) is elaborate for a 4 MB DoS bound, but it is fully tested (read-frame-cap-counts-utf8-bytes-not-chars + the supplementary-plane test) and defensible since the cap advertises BYTES — treated as intentional correctness, not gold-plating.

title: review(impl/routing): bare :keyword-typed route param/query cannot round-trip and is silently accepted at reg-route
description:
rf2-x76af2 review-wave finding (routing slice). Framed as a suggestion.

A bare (unbounded) :keyword-typed :params or :query slot on a route is a silent prism footgun — the exact 'cannot round-trip' class that :double is fail-loud-rejected for, but handled inconsistently (silently accepted).

Mechanism:
- registry.cljc:567-568 normalize-type-form maps bare :keyword -> :rf.route/keyword-unbounded and keeps it in the coerce table.
- registry.cljc:764-769 coerce-by-type-form leaves :rf.route/keyword-unbounded as a STRING on the inbound side (deliberate rf2-3k3o7 keyword-interning-DoS guard).
- route-url emission (registry.cljc ~1615-1618 path, ~1752-1757 query) runs the value through enum-keyword-token, which only inverts a [:rf.route/enum-keyword ...] vector; for the plain :rf.route/keyword-unbounded token it passes the keyword through to url-encode -> host (str v). So (route-url :r {} {:sort :asc}) emits ?sort=%3Aasc.
- match-url then decodes to the STRING ":asc" (kept string per the unbounded rule) and validate-route-shape against [:sort :keyword] FLAGS :validation-failed? true. So the URL route-url just built fails the SAME route's own schema on re-match.
- assert-url-value! (registry.cljc:1314) does NOT catch this: a keyword IS canonical EDN, so it is admitted. There is no way to use a bare :keyword slot that round-trips: a string value fails route-url validation up front; a keyword value emits %3A... and fails inbound validation.

This is the reject-decimal-route-schema! (registry.cljc:259-299, called ~385) situation exactly — 'no canonical-EDN-round-trippable URL form' — but :double fails loud at reg-route while bare :keyword slips through.

Suggested fix (pick one, mirror the :double precedent):
- Preferred: extend the authoring-boundary guard to fail-loud reject a bare/optioned :keyword (non-[:enum]) :params/:query slot at reg-route (a keyword_type_form? twin of decimal-type-form?), with a message steering authors to [:enum ...] (bounded) or :string. Zero in-repo non-test registrations to migrate.
- Or, at minimum, a reg-route ADVISORY (warn, like advise-query-promotion!) naming the unbounded-:keyword slot.
- Or reject a keyword value for a :rf.route/keyword-unbounded slot inside assert-url-value! at emission time.

Test gap: routing_enum_prism_cljs_test.cljc covers [:enum :asc :desc] (bounded) round-trip on path/query/query-retain, but there is NO coverage of bare :keyword — add a fixture asserting the chosen fail-loud/advisory behaviour.

Severity: correctness footgun, silent, edge (bare :keyword slots are uncommon since [:enum] is idiomatic) -> P3.
notes: Dispatched 2026-07-12 (solo, routing bug). Worktree routing-keyword-qot6ii. Surface implementation/routing registry.cljc — free (no ui/core worker touches routing).

Added reject-keyword-route-schema! at reg-route (twin of the :double reject) throwing :rf.error/route-keyword-unbounded-unsupported for bare/optioned non-[:enum] :keyword :params/:query slots; [:enum ...] still round-trips. Tests + behavior-corpus co-change. Gates: routing 423/0, npm test:cljs 8924/0.

auto-wire); violations-by-frame is in the UI ns re-frame.story.ui.a11y, which cljs-resolve deliberately
does NOT require (bundle isolation — deps.edn forbids dragging the Story UI into the MCP helper classpath).
The nil is forced, but the ASYMMETRY is the defect: nothing (no load-time signal, no ns-level contract)
flags that a browser host MUST rebind *a11y-provider*, and the substrate precedent invites a bridge author
to assume a11y "just works".

WHY LOW/LATENT: no build compiles story-mcp to CLJS (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn has no story-mcp
target); the browser bridge is explicitly out of scope ("a later bead owns it — the transport itself is
OUT OF SCOPE here", cljs_resolve ns docstring). Fails closed (reports cannot-answer, never a false-empty
{:violations []}). Distinct follow-up to rf2-3fc89f.21 (which introduced the seams); NOT owned by
rf2-j538f7.31.

FIX SKETCH (design call): make the two seams consistent —
  (a) make *substrate-provider* ALSO nil in CLJS so the browser-bridge bead wires both symmetrically
      (no half-working default); OR
  (b) add an optional CLJS wiring ns (browser-bundle-included, requiring re-frame.story.ui.a11y) that
      binds *a11y-provider*, keeping cljs-resolve UI-free; OR
  (c) at minimum hoist the "browser hosts MUST rebind *a11y-provider*" contract from the var docstring to
      the ns-level future-browser-bridge note so the asymmetry is loud, and align substrate to the same
      posture.
No new :rf.error/* id required (reuses the existing capability-unavailable id) → no Spec 009 co-edit.

ACCEPTANCE: in a CLJS runtime with a live violations-by-frame, read-a11y-violations on a frame with
recorded violations returns them (not capability-unavailable); OR the contract explicitly documents the
required rebind at ns level AND substrate matches the same (both-seams-consistent) posture.

title: [spec-015] whole-vector :sensitive example (95-112) contradicts shipped arg-map-rooted contract (fd34661e0) — needs reconciliation ruling
description: Separate follow-up from the rf2-agb5jk ruling (Mike/Fable 2026-07-11, 'SEPARATE FOLLOW-UP: file, do not fold'): Spec 015:95-112 shows a whole-vector :sensitive example that contradicts the shipped arg-map-rooted classification contract (pinned by fd34661e0). Needs its OWN reconciliation ruling — is the spec example wrong (fix to arg-map-rooted) or is there a second addressing form? Likely the former (align the example to the shipped contract). NEEDS RULING before dispatch — file in ai/decisions if Mike wants to weigh in, else default: correct the spec example to the shipped arg-map-rooted form.
notes:
RULING (decision-agent, 2026-07-12): Option A — correct the spec example(s) to the shipped PAYLOAD-ROOTED form. One addressing contract; no second form; no implementation change.

CHOSEN: Registration :sensitive/:large paths index into the registration's OWNED payload — for events, the SECOND element of the event vector (canonically the arg-map). Correct form: {:sensitive [[:password]]} for [:auth/login {:password ...}]. Spec 015 line ~95 ({:sensitive [[1 :password]]}) and the line ~112 prose ("the event vector — [1 :password] reaches the arg-map's :password") are documentation drift: under the shipped walker, [[1 :password]] looks up key 1 INSIDE the arg-map, silently no-ops, and the password egresses RAW — a copy-paste privacy trap in the security spec.

CAUTION — the brief's framing is INVERTED: the original brief called event-vector-rooted the shipped form. It is not. The Codex addendum in the decision file is the correct account, independently verified against: redact-event-vec (implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc ~287-308, destructures [id payload & rest-args], walks only payload); both egress paths share it (project-event-tags dev trace + redact-event-by-registration always-on error/observe via projection.cljc); conformance fixture data-classification-event-arg-sensitive-path-redacts.edn; observability_routing_cljs_test; examples/core/login; docs how-tos; and Spec 015's OWN later prose (~line 206: "rooted at the arg-map"). fd34661e03 is docs+test only and pins payload-rooting + the positional fail-open. rf2-825mzj (4990c94c61, mutation envelope egress) does not touch these premises. The machine test (machine_routed_event_classification_cljs_test) is NOT a counterexample: a machine's routed payload IS the inner event vector, so [1 :password] there is an integer index into a vector-shaped payload — same payload-rooted rule, do not "fix" it.

REJECTED: (B) bless a second outer-event-rooted form — intrinsically ambiguous ([1 :password] would mean two things), partially reverses fd34661e03's deliberate fail-open scoping, grows the egress surface with no consumer demand. (C) caveat-only — validate-classification! accepts integer path segments, so [[1 :password]] registers cleanly and fails silently at egress; a caveat cannot make a copy-pasted declaration safe; contradicts the pre-alpha no-doc-debt posture.

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. spec/015-Data-Classification.md ~line 95: {:sensitive [[1 :password]]} -> {:sensitive [[:password]]}. ~Line 112: reword to "the event payload (the second element, canonically the arg-map — [:password] reaches its :password)"; state explicitly that paths never index the outer event vector (index 0 / event-id is not addressable; outer positions 2+ pass through raw — the documented positional fail-open, cross-ref Conventions canonical event-vector shape).
2. docs/EP/EP-0025-data-classification.md ~line 202: same one-line fix. Repo scan finds the bad form ONLY in these two files (plus machine-context tests where the integer index is legitimate).
3. NO semantics change to implementation or tests. Optionally tighten docstrings to say "event payload (second element)" consistently.
4. Acceptance: existing gates green (data-classification conformance corpus, core CLJS+JVM, security CLJS incl. positional fail-open regression). If not already covered, add one small dual-runtime unit test around redact-event-by-registration proving: [[:password]] redacts a payload field; [[]] redacts the whole payload while preserving the event id; a trailing positional arg rides raw.
5. Optional hardening (implementer judgment; may be a follow-up bead): narrow docs-CI drift guard rejecting reg-event classification examples taught outer-vector-rooted (reg-event + :sensitive [[<int> ...]]) across spec/, docs/, skills/ — scoped so machine-classification integer paths stay legal. NOTE: .github/workflows/* is hot-zone; if the guard is included, flag for sequencing.
6. Dispatch note: spec/015 and EP-0025 are not hot-zone; parallel-safe except vs other beads touching Spec 015.
close_reason: Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5686 — Option A per the 2026-07-12 ruling: spec/015 + EP-0025 examples corrected to payload-rooted {:sensitive [[:password]]}, addressing prose reworded (outer event vector never indexed; positional fail-open documented, Conventions cross-ref), new dual-runtime unit test pins the three legs. No implementation change; machine integer paths untouched; docs-CI drift guard deferred as optional follow-up.

title: [correctness-review][core] Default-image standard-shadow filter silently drops an app descriptor colliding with a framework standard; explicit path fails loud (fail-loud asymmetry)
description:
VERIFIED (JVM repro). image_assembly.cljc:879-909 select-and-lower-image default-image branch drops standard shadows by BLANKET [kind id] match: (remove #(contains? standard-keys (descriptor-kind+id %)) descriptors). Intended to drop the framework's OWN no-provenance registrar shadow of a dual-registered standard (e.g. :rf/set-db, record-descriptor! nil-provenance slot). But the raw [kind id] match ALSO drops a PROVENANCED app descriptor colliding with a standard -> it never reaches app-resolver, so check-standard-collision! (:606-631) never fires. The app registration is SILENTLY IGNORED and the standard is used. Violates documented guarantee (assemble-default docstring :1216-1220; default-image :304-308): default path FAILS LOUD 'exactly as an explicit image's collision does'.

REPRO (JVM, core classpath): register-standard! :fx :rf.nav/push-url {:handler-fn :std}; pool = [{:rf.provenance/ns "shop.nav" :kind :fx :id :rf.nav/push-url :handler-fn :app} ...].
  DEFAULT : (assemble-default pool) -> {:threw false, :fx-resolves-to :std, :app-nav-present? true}   (app :app silently dropped)
  EXPLICIT: (assemble [(image {:id :x :select-ns {:include ["shop.nav"]}})] pool) -> throws :rf.error/image-standard-replacement-forbidden
Same misconfiguration, two outcomes. No existing test covers a standard-colliding descriptor in the default POOL. Bypassed-gate: the injected defect PASSES check-standard-collision! on the default path.

RELATIONSHIP: same image-vs-registrar-resolution class as owned rf2-x76af2.25 (emit-dispatched-trace! gate) but DISTINCT surface (image-assembly standard protection, not trace).

FIX SKETCH: narrow the filter to drop only the framework's own no-provenance shadow so a provenanced app descriptor survives selection and hits check-standard-collision!:
  (remove #(and (contains? standard-keys (descriptor-kind+id %)) (nil? (:rf.provenance/ns %))) descriptors)
Reuses existing :rf.error/image-standard-replacement-forbidden -> NO new error id, NO Spec 009 catalogue co-edit.

ACCEPTANCE: a default-path (assemble-default / assemble []) projection whose pool carries a provenanced descriptor colliding with a registered standard throws :rf.error/image-standard-replacement-forbidden (same id+timing as explicit); the framework's own no-provenance shadow is still dropped (default-projection-includes-the-whole-pool-plus-standards stays green).

title: [correctness-review][skill-shared] redaction eval keys on non-secret JWT header; raw payload+signature leak scores PASS
description:
Read-only correctness review of skills/shared (rf2-x76af2.4, wave 2026-07-11).

DEFECT (teeth gap on the redaction SECURITY gate's flagship secret)
The behavioral redaction eval (fixture 02) pins ONLY the JWT header as forbidden, but the header is a non-secret constant. The sensitive payload + signature are unmodeled, so a transcript that leaks them raw scores PASS.

The JWT at skills/shared/tests/fixtures/02-redaction.md:33 is:
  eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9 . eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NSIsIm5hbWUiOiJNaWtlIFRob21wc29uIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ . SflKxwRJSMeKKF2QT4fwpMeJf36POk6yJV_adQssw5c
    header (constant)                     payload (sub + name PII)                                                    HMAC signature

- skills/shared/tests/evals/behavioral-evals.json:74 forbids ONLY the header substring `eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9`.
- Same header is distinct_value_originals[0] (behavioral-evals.json:100).
- That header = base64url of {"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"} — present in EVERY HS256 JWT, zero secret.
- payload decodes to {"sub":"12345","name":"Mike Thompson","iat":1516239022} — the exact PII fixture 02 calls out (L54, L137-139).
- payload + signature substrings appear ONLY in the fixture recap; grep confirms neither is pinned in behavioral-evals.json or score-behavioral-eval.clj.

CONSEQUENCE (inverted vs sensitivity):
- mask payload+sig, leak header raw (harmless constant) -> header present -> correctly FAILS.
- mask header, leak payload+sig raw (PII + crypto) -> header absent, nothing else covers them -> PASS.

REPRO:
  bb skills/shared/tests/evals/score-behavioral-eval.clj <transcript: raw payload+sig in output, header masked as <REDACTED-TOKEN-1>, good bindings>
  => { "eval_id": 2, "pass": true, "failures": [] }  (exit 0)
Baseline gates all green (60/124, 6/9, self-test PASS), so the gap is invisible to CI.

NOT a documented exemption: scored_vs_manual.manual_only (behavioral-evals.json:24) excuses only the DECODED name "Mike Thompson" (first-name false-positive risk). The raw base64url payload + signature are high-entropy and unambiguous; their omission is unaddressed.

Also touches the structural test's JWT self-test cases (retro_protocol_test.clj:412-417 "eval2 raw JWT"; good-eval2-bindings JWT original at :273) — all model "the JWT" as its non-secret header.

FIX SKETCH:
- Add payload + signature to eval 2 forbidden_output_substrings, and/or a forbidden_output_pattern `eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`.
- Anchor distinct_value_originals[0] on the payload, not the header.
- Update fixture 02 secrets-table identifier from "(eyJhbG...)" to name payload/signature as the redaction target.
- Repoint the scorer --self-test "raw JWT" negative to the payload.

ACCEPTANCE: a transcript leaking the raw JWT payload OR signature scores FAIL; --self-test's raw-JWT negative keys on the payload not the header.

SEVERITY P3: marquee secret of the redaction security fixture; executable check inverted vs sensitivity. Tempered by: whole-token leak still caught; no CI harness yet (release/checklist gate only).
CONFIDENCE: High (decoded + reproduced).

title: [correctness-review][mcp-base] marker cap-skip: structural proof does not bound marker BODY size (over-budget single-key marker bypasses cap)
description:
## Summary

The marker fast-path cap-skip (`envelope/marker-text?`) confirms a CLOSED single-key `:rf.mcp/*` wrapper but NEVER bounds the marker body SIZE. A single-key `{:rf.mcp/overflow {…huge…}}` / `{:rf.mcp/cache-hit {…huge…}}` result therefore skips `apply-cap` and reaches the agent un-capped. This is the body-size dimension of the same threat class rf2-j538f7.20 fixed (which caught only the SIBLING-key variant).

Focus area named in the audit brief: 'response-marker detection (the marker-cache-bypass structural-proof requirement)'.

## Where

- Gate: `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/envelope.cljc:228-245` (`closed-marker-envelope?` — proves closure + map body, NOT size) and `marker-text?` (247-282).
- Skip sites (consumer): `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools.cljs:315` (`:skip-when? (wire/marker? result)`) and `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/cap.cljs:196` (`(if (wire/marker? result-js) result-js (base-cap/apply-cap …))`).
- Unsound invariant (stated verbatim): `envelope.cljc:161-166` and `spec/envelope.md` §Closed-wrapper confirmation — 'a marker is sub-cap by construction holds only for a complete, closed, single-key marker map'. False for a single-key marker with an over-budget body.

## Repro (verified in-repo, clojure -M -e)

    {:rf.mcp/overflow {:limit :reached :blob <8000 x's>}}  => marker-text? = true  (len 8047)
    {:rf.mcp/cache-hit {:blob <8000 x's>}}                 => marker-text? = true  (len 8031)

Body can be arbitrarily large (100 KB ≈ 25 000 tokens ≫ 5 000-token default cap) and still returns true → cap skipped.

## Vacuous-gate proof (inject-and-check)

The gate PASSES (returns true, cap skipped) on the injected over-budget defect. The existing envelope test `envelope_test.clj:151-161` places the 8 K string in a SIBLING (→ false, correct); line 189 blesses additive body fields with only a TINY body. No test places an over-budget payload in the marker BODY, so the un-bounded-body skip is uncaught.

## Reachability / severity (LOW)

Requires a handler to emit a top-level reserved `:rf.mcp/overflow` / `:rf.mcp/cache-hit` key as its SOLE payload key with a large body — a `:rf.mcp/*`-reserved-namespace violation, the SAME abnormal precondition the fixed sibling case required. No normal tool payload can trigger it. Impact: one over-budget response reaches the agent (context bloat); no corruption, no privacy leak. Filed because the project already chose to harden against reserved-key-shaped handler results (rf2-j538f7.20) — this leaves that mitigation incomplete.

## NOT a duplicate

rf2-j538f7.20 (PR #5589) is CLOSED and covers the extra-top-level-SIBLING case only. This is the disjoint BODY-SIZE case; searched open beads, none exist for it.

## Fix sketch

One of: (a) verify the marker TEXT is itself under the cap before skipping (direct expression of the 'sub-cap by construction' invariant); (b) bound the marker body via the conformance-schema size the real builders always satisfy; or (c) still route marker-shaped results through apply-cap's measurement (a genuine tiny marker passes trivially). All keep legitimate cache/cap markers on the fast path (their text is always small).

## Acceptance

A RED-then-GREEN test (mirroring the sibling-key test) where an over-budget-BODY single-key `{:rf.mcp/overflow {…huge…}}` (and `:rf.mcp/cache-hit`) is NOT skip-eligible (or is still measured/replaced by the cap step), on BOTH the JVM envelope_test and the CLJS branches suite.

title: [correctness-review][skill-pair] undo-to-epoch reports a rejected restore as {:ok? true} (false-green backstop)
description:
SURFACE: skills/re-frame2-pair — shipped preload runtime.cljs (the backstop time-travel sugar).

DEFECT (file:line, HEAD 2409c9e1):
skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs
- undo-to-epoch failure branch: lines 2690-2694 returns {:ok? true :epoch-id ... :restored? false :frame ... :reason :restore-rejected}
- Correct sibling undo-step-back: lines 2677-2678 returns {:ok? false ... :reason :restore-rejected}
- Canonical restore-epoch: line 2627 returns bare false on failure (MCP tool wraps to :ok? false)

When (rf/restore-epoch! frame-id epoch-id) returns false (any of the seven Tool-Pair time-travel failure modes: aged-out epoch id, schema/version mismatch, restore-during-drain, halted-cascade target, unknown frame), undo-to-epoch returns :ok? TRUE while :restored? false. Every other envelope fn in the file (undo-step-back, restore-epoch, dom-source-at :no-element, pair-dispatch-sync!, dispatch-consequence!, dispatch-dry-run rollback-failed) returns :ok? false on genuine failure — undo-to-epoch is the lone outlier. Copy-paste bug: the failure branch :ok? should be false.

WHY IT MISTEACHES LIVE OPERATION: the skill trains the agent to pattern-match :ok? first. undo-to-epoch is the documented time-travel BACKSTOP reached via raw eval-cljs (ops.md:253, STATUS.md:36). eval-cljs returns the raw form value un-wrapped, so the agent reads {:ok? true} directly and concludes the undo succeeded when the runtime REJECTED it and the frame never moved — a silent 'I rewound you to epoch N' over an unchanged frame. Docstring compounds it: claims 'same shape as restore-epoch's success envelope' and documents no failure shape.

SCOPE / SEVERITY P3: canonical dedicated restore-epoch MCP tool is UNAFFECTED (wraps bare false correctly). Reachable only on the backstop eval surface the skill de-prioritises. Requires a restore to actually be rejected.

REPRO (live nREPL against any pair-preloaded app):
  (re-frame2-pair.runtime/undo-to-epoch :epoch/does-not-exist)  ;; aged-out / bogus id
  => {:ok? true :epoch-id :epoch/does-not-exist :restored? false :frame ... :reason :restore-rejected}
  ;; compare: (re-frame2-pair.runtime/undo-step-back) on a single-epoch frame => {:ok? false :reason :no-prior-epoch}

FIX SKETCH:
1. runtime.cljs undo-to-epoch failure branch: change :ok? true -> :ok? false (match undo-step-back; keeps :restored? false :reason :restore-rejected).
2. Fix the docstring to document the {:ok? false :reason :restore-rejected} failure shape.
3. Add a Babashka structural pin under skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/runtime/ (mirror dry_run_rollback_failure_pin_test.clj): assert BOTH undo-step-back and undo-to-epoch failure arms are :ok? false :reason :restore-rejected so the two sugars can't drift.

ACCEPTANCE:
- undo-to-epoch restore-epoch!-false branch returns :ok? false.
- Docstring documents the failure shape.
- New structural pin green; existing skill test suite stays green.

CONTEXT: Fresh read-only correctness audit (rf2-x76af2.3). Prior-wave dry-run findings (rf2-j538f7.39 sink, rf2-glg4uo rollback-failed) verified FIXED + pinned green; this undo-to-epoch false-green has no bead and no test coverage (bd search + tests grep both empty). No existing owner.

title: [correctness-review][skill-xray] SKILL.md frame-picker one-liner overstates scope ('every tab and the spine rebind to it')
description:
SURFACE: skills/re-frame2-xray/SKILL.md:321-322 (§The chrome around the tabs, L1 frame picker bullet).

PROBLEM: SKILL.md:321-322 says the Frame control 'chooses which frame Xray observes — every tab and the spine rebind to it (mode-independent: it scopes both Dynamic and Static).' The 'every tab ... rebind' clause contradicts the maintained mixed-scope model in the SAME package.

CONTRADICTS (internal):
- SKILL.md:219-233 (its own scope matrix): Graph (Declared projection), Frames, and Resources (static registry) are in the 'Process-global / registry-wide' row — they 'read the same in every frame' and do NOT change on a frame switch.
- references/chrome.md:16-28 (§L1 frame picker): the picker 'does not re-scope the process-global definition catalogues ... what it moves are the per-frame live projections.'
- references/panels.md:70-89 (§Scope model): same three-axis model.

VERIFIED against tool: frame_switcher.cljs (available-frames / select-frame) moves the observed-frame axis; the process-global catalogues (derivation_graph.cljs Declared projection over xray-contributors; module_view.cljs over re-frame.live-frame; Static definition catalogues) read the shared registrar (Spec 001) and are frame-invariant. Only the focused-epoch lenses and observed-frame projections move with the picker; 'every tab rebinds' is false for the process-global catalogues.

WHY IT MATTERS: an agent answering 'what does the frame picker do?' from this one-liner over-claims that switching frames re-scopes Frames / Graph-Declared / Static registry catalogues, misrouting operators who expect registry-wide browse surfaces to follow the picker.

REPRO: read SKILL.md:321-322 vs the scope matrix at SKILL.md:219-233 and chrome.md:16-28 — direct inconsistency.

FIX SKETCH: replace 'every tab and the spine rebind to it' with the mixed-scope wording already used in chrome.md, e.g. 'the picker moves the per-frame live projections and the spine's observed frame; the process-global catalogues (Graph Declared, Frames, the Static definition catalogues) read the same in every frame.' Keep the 'mode-independent' note.

ACCEPTANCE: SKILL.md's frame-picker one-liner no longer claims all tabs rebind; it matches the scope matrix (SKILL.md:219-233) and chrome.md:16-28.

NOTE: matches a pre-seeded finding in the rf2-13h2cm bead description; re-verified independently. No existing open bead tracks it (grep .beads/issues.jsonl for frame-picker scope / 'every tab rebind' → only unrelated trace-leak bead rf2-0ax6f). Filed on its own merits.

Read-only audit (rf2-13h2cm). No source edits in this audit.

title: [correctness-review][skill-xray] chrome.md teaches an unshipped visual cue: 'the head row pulses while live'
description:

title: [correctness-review][pair-retro] README/design enumerate 'four state-injection mutators' — retired count; contradicts cited single-source

skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/README.md:42 (SHIPPED — in package.json files array) and skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/spec/design.md:26 (authoring meta-doc; inside a 'cardinal What-to-avoid rule') both enumerate the Tool-Pair surface families and name 'the four state-injection mutators'. Both README.md:42 and design.md:26 explicitly frame their list as pointing at ../shared/tool-pair-surfaces.md, 'the single source' — so they contradict the very source they cite. The three names implied by 'four' (replace-app-db!, reset-app-db!, replace-runtime-db!) are retired API names consolidated away by API-shrink #3. A retro reasoning about upstream state-injection routing from this list would name a mutator family that no longer exists.

## Repro

grep 'one partial-map mutator' skills/shared/tool-pair-surfaces.md  -> current correct count

## Fix sketch
In both leaves replace 'the four state-injection mutators' with 'state injection (replace-frame-state!)' (or 'the one partial-map state-injection mutator'), matching tool-pair-surfaces.md:16. No other content change.

## Acceptance

title: [correctness-review][machines-viz] export docstrings claim embedded/self-contained fonts but no @font-face is emitted
description:
export.cljs docstrings (lines 31, 231, 247, 391) state the exported SVG carries 'Embedded fonts' and is 'self-contained'. The only <style> block is viewport-css (:269-287), which declares font-family:'JetBrains Mono',... BY NAME ONLY. There is no @font-face with base64/WOFF data anywhere in the export path (grep-confirmed: viewport-css is the sole style block; no @font-face in the file). So an exported SVG/PNG rendered on a host without JetBrains Mono installed silently falls back to generic monospace -- the artefact is NOT font-self-contained as documented. Fidelity + contract/doc mismatch (matters in an AI-first spec-is-the-artefact repo).

Fix sketch: either embed the font faces as @font-face { src: url(data:font/woff2;base64,...) } in viewport-css, or correct the docstrings to say the export references fonts by name (not embedded).
acceptance_criteria: Either the serialised SVG contains an @font-face with a data-URI src (true font embedding), or the export.cljs docstrings no longer claim embedded/self-contained fonts.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5648 (docstrings + 2 spec claims corrected to named-fonts/system-monospace-fallback; no @font-face exists, doc-only)

title: [correctness-review][machines-viz] guarded-fork elk.position hint hardcoded to X axis, wrong under adaptive :lr
description:
chart/projection.cljc:915-916 (->elk-children) emits the guarded-fork within-layer priority hint as {"elk.position" (str "(" pos ",0)")} -- the fork index always on the X axis -- justified by a comment ('the chart's DOWN direction -> within-layer axis is X'). But ->elk-children takes NO direction argument (->elk-input has direction but does not pass it down), and post_elk/aspect-direction routes exactly the branchy machines (max-out-degree >= 3, i.e. the guarded forks) to :lr on the :direction :auto path. Under :lr (RIGHT) layers stack horizontally, so the within-layer/cross axis is Y, not X -- the priority index is written to the wrong coordinate for precisely the machines the heuristic sends landscape. The position hint cannot be direction-aware because the direction is never threaded in.

UNVERIFIED: whether ELK crossingMinimization.semiInteractive actually mis-orders (branch weaving) vs simply degrades/ignores an off-axis position needs a browser/ELK run. Trigger: :direction :auto + a guarded multi-branch fork (e.g. a 3-way :gate/check).

Fix sketch: thread the resolved ELK direction into ->elk-children and emit '(0,pos)' for :lr and '(pos,0)' for :tb.
acceptance_criteria: A :direction :auto guarded-fork lays out with monotonic branch order under :lr (priority index 1..N top-to-bottom); confirm the fix threads direction into the elk.position hint and add a projection/layout test pinning the axis per resolved direction.
close_reason: FIXED (not downgraded) in PR #5648. Axis-inconsistency VERIFIED by code inspection: aspect-direction routes max-out-degree>=3 forks to :lr while ->elk-children hardcoded the elk.position hint to X. Threaded resolved direction into ->elk-children; emits (0,pos) for :lr, (pos,0) for :tb. Unit-pinned per direction. End-to-end ELK branch-order magnitude remains browser-gated but the coordinate correctness is a definite fix.

title: [correctness-review][core] reject-tier reserved fx-id mapped to the documented nil/false no-op placeholder fires a spurious :rf.error/reserved-fx-override (per-event flood)
description:
Consistency defect + mild production error-flood. The reject-tier reserved-fx gates test only KEY PRESENCE, never the override VALUE: handle-one-fx's reject-override? (fx.cljc:979-980) and strip-rejected-overrides (fx.cljc:740-741) both use `(contains? overrides id)`. So an override entry `{:rf.fx/reg-flow nil}` -- the documented "no override, fall through" placeholder (the `{:some-fx (when cond? stub)}` idiom collapsing to nil; cf. resolve-fx-with-overrides:836-837) -- is treated as an ATTEMPTED reject-tier override and emits :rf.error/reserved-fx-override onto the always-on error channel (-> MCP / log / off-box shippers). The OVERRIDABLE tier treats nil/false as a silent no-op; the reject tier does not.

Because the router runs strip-rejected-overrides once per event on the merged per-frame join per-call map, a frame carrying such a nil-valued reject-tier key in :fx-overrides emits one spurious production error PER dispatched event.

VERIFIED (JVM runtime): `strip {:rf.fx/reg-flow nil}` returned {} and emitted :rf.error/reserved-fx-override; the dev per-call handle-one-fx path emitted it too.

FIX: gate both on an actual override value -- `(let [v (get overrides id)] (and (contains? overrides id) (some? v) (not (false? v)) (contains? rejected-reserved-fx-ids id)))` -- mirroring the OVERRIDABLE nil/false no-op treatment; strip only emits + drops on a real override (fn/keyword), leaving nil/false to fall through silently.
acceptance_criteria: An :fx-overrides entry mapping a reject-tier reserved id to nil (e.g. {:rf.fx/reg-flow nil}) or false falls through silently with NO :rf.error/reserved-fx-override emitted, matching the OVERRIDABLE tier nil/false no-op treatment; a real fn/keyword override still emits + strips.

title: [correctness-review][core] reg-fx accepts a handler-less registration; fails late at fire-time with a misleading :rf.error/fx-handler-exception (asymmetric vs reg-cofx)
description:
Fail-loud asymmetry. reg-fx (fx.cljc:118-124) accepts a handler-less registration: `(reg-fx :my/fx {:doc "..."})` (a plausible typo) parses to handler-fn nil and registration SUCCEEDS with :handler-fn nil in the registrar. The failure is deferred to fire-time: handle-one-fx invokes `(nil ctx args)`, the NPE is caught by the fx try/catch, and it surfaces as :rf.error/fx-handler-exception reading "Effect handler `:my/fx` threw: Cannot invoke IFn.invoke..." -- blaming the handler for THROWING when it is actually ABSENT.

This is inconsistent with the sibling reg-cofx, which explicitly rejects the analogous mistake at REGISTRATION time (cofx.cljc:264-270, an ambient fact with (nil? supplier) -> :rf.error/cofx-registration-invalid).

VERIFIED (JVM runtime): reg-fx returned the id (registration succeeded); registrar :handler-fn = nil; fire emitted :rf.error/fx-handler-exception with the misleading "threw" reason; the reg-cofx analogue threw :rf.error/cofx-registration-invalid at registration.

FIX: in reg-fx, after resolving [meta handler-fn], guard `(when-not (ifn? handler-fn) (throw :rf.error/fx-registration-invalid ...))` naming the missing handler; consider a shared register-with-classification! precondition since both kinds want it.
acceptance_criteria: (reg-fx :id metadata-only-no-handler) throws :rf.error/fx-registration-invalid at registration time, naming the missing handler -- mirroring reg-cofx's registration-time rejection.

title: [correctness-review][core] emit-dispatched-trace! :rf.trace/no-emit? gate is image-blind -> image-registered no-emit handlers still flood :rf.event/dispatched (dev-only)
description:
Dev-only correctness gap (the whole emit DCEs under :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false). The enqueue-time :rf.trace/no-emit? gate in emit-dispatched-trace! (router.cljc:3250-3288) resolves the target handler's meta via a BARE `(registrar/lookup :event event-id)` (3285-3286). This runs at enqueue time from dispatch! (router.cljc:3448) / dispatch-sync! (3545), OUTSIDE the call-with-frame-resolution binding (that wraps process-event! only, router.cljc:2697).

registrar/lookup is generation-aware (registrar.cljc:760-782 / generation-resolver 219-226): when *generation* is bound it resolves through the frame's image resolver, else the global active-registrar atom. An image-loaded frame's inline :reg-event handler lives ONLY in the frame's generation resolver, and inline reg-event descriptors carry :metadata (image_assembly.cljc:343-403), so such a handler CAN be marked :rf.trace/no-emit?. Because the bare enqueue-time lookup is image-blind it MISSES the handler -> handler-meta nil -> no-emit? false -> the :rf.event/dispatched trace is emitted into the very stream the handler is marked to stay out of. This is the exact flood rf2-qsjda closed for registrar-registered handlers, still open for image-registered ones.

STATUS: code shape VERIFIED (bare lookup is definitively image-blind + runs outside the resolution binding; inline reg-event metadata path confirmed). Reachability requires an image-only no-emit? handler; no end-to-end image-frame repro was built (narrow, dev-only).

FIX: resolve the gate through live-frame/frame-resolution-target + call-with-frame-resolution (one extra record read on the dev path only), matching how process-event! resolves handlers.
acceptance_criteria: An image-loaded frame whose inline :reg-event handler is marked :rf.trace/no-emit? does NOT emit :rf.event/dispatched at enqueue time (the gate resolves the handler meta through the frame's image generation).
notes: BLOCKED (not fixed) — collision boundary. The fix must make emit-dispatched-trace!'s enqueue-time :rf.trace/no-emit? gate image-aware, but that gate is the bare (registrar/lookup :event event-id) at router.cljc:3285-3286 — router.cljc was owned this session by the live sibling core worker rf2-x76af2.22/.23. Per dispatch collision rule I did not edit router.cljc. Sequence after the sibling's router.cljc PR merges (or reassign to that worker). Fix: resolve the no-emit meta through call-with-frame-resolution / the frame's image generation, matching process-event!. (rf2-x76af2.26/.27 shipped in PR #5645.)

title: [correctness-review][core] No cycle guard in the sub graph: a :<- dependency cycle dies with a raw StackOverflowError instead of a structured :rf.error/sub-cycle
description:
Fail-loud violation. A :<- dependency cycle in the sub graph (`:a :<- [:b]`, `:b :<- [:a]`, or a self-edge `:self :<- [:self]`) recurses subscribe-in-frame -> compute-and-cache! (subs.cljc:882-935 input subscription -> 1263 recursion) with NO build-in-progress marker, and the pure compute-sub* per-call memo (subs.cljc:1632) memoises only AFTER the body computes. So the first subscribe/compute dies with a RAW host StackOverflowError instead of a structured :rf.error/*.

Registration cannot catch it (the other sub may register later; parametric inputs are dynamic). subs/cache.cljc transitive-dependent-closure EXPLICITLY defends against cyclic :<- graphs, so cycles are an acknowledged input class; flows already ship a typed cycle error precedent. A raw SOE violates the AI-first fail-loud posture.

VERIFIED (deterministic JVM repro): two-node cycle (:a<->:b) -> RAW StackOverflowError (NOT structured); self cycle (:self<-:self) -> RAW StackOverflowError.

FIX: an under-construction set keyed by query-v (per-frame for the reactive build; the per-call memo atom can double for compute-sub) raising e.g. :rf.error/sub-cycle carrying the cycle path, recovering to nil. Repro: ai/findings/2026-07-11.core-audit.md (subs_repro.clj).
acceptance_criteria: Subscribing a cyclic :<- sub (two-node or self-edge) emits a structured :rf.error/sub-cycle with the cycle path and recovers to nil, rather than throwing a host StackOverflowError.

title: [correctness-review][core] subs cache MISS-install is a plain overwrite: concurrent double-build stomps the entry -> orphaned reaction + input-ref leak + premature dispose (JVM)
description:
JVM correctness defect (CLJS-immune; the sub cache is single-threaded on CLJS). The sub-cache HIT path is CAS-after-snapshot hardened (subs.cljc:1252-1262: swap-vals! bumps ref-count only if the slot still holds the SAME reaction, else rebuilds). The MISS path installs with an unconditional plain swap (subs.cljc:947-950): `(swap! cache assoc k {:reaction reaction :inputs input-signals :ref-count 1})`.

Two threads that both observe a miss for the same query-v both call compute-and-cache!, both build a reaction, and the second assoc OVERWRITES the first. Consequences: (1) reaction1 is orphaned (its on-dispose never fires -> its layer-2 input ref-count bumps leak); (2) :ref-count is reset to 1 while TWO callers hold references. Because unsubscribe decrements by cache-key query-v (subs.cljc:1712-1730), NOT by reaction identity, a phantom holder's unsubscribe drives the CACHED reaction 1->0 and disposes it while the other caller still uses it (premature dispose).

sub_cache_concurrency_test.clj has exactly 3 deftests (invalidate-sub-on-replace / dispose-entry-now / unsubscribe-drop-to-zero); none cover the MISS-install double-build.

VERIFIED (deterministic JVM repro; two compute-and-cache! calls model two racing misses, since the defect is the unconditional overwrite):
  reaction stomped?  true   (cache holds r2, r1 orphaned)
  :sum ref-count     1      (should be 2 for two subscribers)
  :a input ref-count 2 ; :b 2  (bumped once per build => leaked)
  after 1 unsubscribe: :sum present? false ; :a rc 1 ; :b rc 1  (nonzero input rc, no live :sum = leak)

FIX: install-if-absent via swap-vals!; on collision dispose the just-built reaction and adopt the winner as a HIT (bump ref-count), mirroring the hit-path discipline. Repro: ai/findings/2026-07-11.core-audit.md (subs_repro.clj).
acceptance_criteria: A JVM contention test (pattern of sub_cache_concurrency_test.clj) asserting: after N concurrent same-query-v subscribes, exactly one reaction is cached, its ref-count == subscriber count, and there are zero orphaned/leaked input refs after all unsubscribe.

title: [correctness-review][skill-implementor] v1-completion-report tag-set example omits :identity/* + :data-classification/*
description:
## Problem

skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/output-format.md:96-98 — the v1 completion report template's 'Claimed capability tag set' example block shows only:

    :core/*
    <list of optional tags from D7>

It lists only :core/* as always-claimed and buries everything else under 'optional tags from D7'. But :identity/* (EP-0012 path algebra + CEDN-1) and :data-classification/* (Spec 015) are v1-REQUIRED, not optional — they are always-claimed alongside :core/*.

## Why this is a residual defect (distinct from the already-closed gate)

The three-family foundation-gate fix (commit 510a4e5be / PR #5608 / rf2-j538f7.36) updated every GATE DESCRIPTION in the slice to ':core/* + :identity/* + :data-classification/*'. It missed this one TEMPLATE EXAMPLE in the completion report. Evidence it was an oversight, not intentional:
- decision-record.md:199-202 (the D7 template this report copies from) lists all three with '; always — v1-required' comments.
- README.md:20, kickoff-prompt.md:26, spec/design.md:168,172 all enumerate the three.
- The completion report is explicitly 'the public surface of this port exists and conforms' (output-format.md:135) and is copied into the port's public README (SKILL.md:99: 'Port README states claimed capability tags').

DEDUP NOTE: the pre-seeded Finding 1 (rf2-j538f7.36) cited output-format.md:96-98 among its evidence; PR #5608 fixed all other cited locations but this one survived. This is the single residual instance, NOT a re-file of the gate itself. Mayor's call whether to dedup against rf2-j538f7.36.

## Repro

grep -n ':core/\*' skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/output-format.md  # → only line 96, no :identity/* or :data-classification/* in the example block

## Impact

A port author copying this template verbatim publishes ':core/* + optional tags' as their claimed set, silently omitting the two v1-required families they actually claimed and ran — under-stating the public conformance claim and contradicting their own D7 record. Low severity (self-correctable by an author who cross-reads D7).

## Fix sketch

Change the example block (output-format.md:96-98) to:

    :core/*
    :identity/*
    :data-classification/*
    <list of optional tags from D7>

optionally mirroring decision-record.md:200-202's '# always — v1-required' comments.

## Acceptance

The v1-completion tag-set example enumerates the three always-claimed v1-required families before optional tags; copying it yields a claim consistent with D7 and the required-foundation gate. Verified statically at HEAD a8e2ebd11.

title: [correctness-review][skill-setup] Template deps.edn comment wrongly says missing schemas artefact "soft-passes" (it throws)
description:
SURFACE: tools/template (found during the skills/re-frame2-setup correctness review, rf2-nhkvps, EPIC rf2-x76af2). The SKILL itself is correct on this axis; the defect is in the generator template that ships to every generated project.

DEFECT: the emitted deps.edn comment reads:
  ;; The starter app's whole-app-db schema (see schema.cljs) needs
  ;; this artefact for validation to actually fire; without it
  ;; CLJS soft-passes per Spec 010 §Recommended soft-pass.
The "without it CLJS soft-passes" clause is factually wrong. The starter's schema.cljs calls (rf/reg-app-schema [] CounterDb) at boot. rf/reg-app-schema routes through re-frame.core-schemas/reg-app-schema (core.cljc:130,289) whose absent-artefact policy is :on-absent :throw (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_schemas.cljc:143). So WITHOUT day8/re-frame2-schemas the call THROWS :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing at boot (and events.cljs's [re-frame.schemas] require would itself fail to compile). It never reaches a runtime soft-pass. Spec 010 §Recommended soft-pass (spec/010-Schemas.md:585) is about the VALIDATOR LIBRARY (Malli) being absent while the schemas artefact IS present — unreachable on the CLJS default path (re-frame.schemas self-wires Malli). The comment mis-applies that section to the artefact-absent case.

FILES (systematic across all deps variants):
- tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/deps.edn:25
- tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_uix/deps.edn (~25)
- tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_helix/deps.edn:24
- tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/deps_with_ssr.edn:42
- tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/deps_with_story.edn:31

REPRO: remove day8/re-frame2-schemas from a generated deps.edn and boot — the app throws :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing (or fails to compile on the events.cljs require), NOT a silent soft-pass as the comment claims.

CONTRAST: the skill references/deps-versions.md documents the CORRECT behavior ("throw :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing (loud, NOT a silent soft-pass)"), and Spec 010 CLJS-reference note agrees. Only the template deps.edn comments are out of step. The template _shared/schema.cljs + _shared/events.cljs comments are already correct.

FIX SKETCH: replace the "soft-passes" clause with the loud-error contract, e.g. "without it, schema.cljs's reg-app-schema call throws :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing at boot (this artefact is a hard requirement for schema registration, not a soft-pass)."

ACCEPTANCE: no template-emitted deps.edn / deps_with_*.edn claims a missing schemas artefact "soft-passes"; the comment names the :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing throw. version_lockstep_test + template_emission_test stay green.

SEVERITY: low — edge case (user must manually delete a day-one dep) and the actual behavior (loud throw) is safer than the described silent soft-pass; a doc-accuracy defect that ships to every generated project, not a runtime bug.

title: [correctness-review][mcp-conformance] realm-slot-absence guarded only by author fixtures + an OPEN schema (self-referential)
description:
SELF-REFERENTIAL + OPEN-SCHEMA GAP. The docstring's load-bearing claim is 'no realm coordinate anywhere in the wire shape' (the re-frame.realm substrate was removed, rf2-udl74a). But the only assertion guarding it iterates the 4 hand-authored local success-fixtures and asserts they don't (contains?) :realms/:operating-realm/:selected-realm/:frame-realms. It never touches a real emitter -- self-referential to the author's own fixtures. And OperatingFrameSuccess is [:map {:closed false} ...] (OPEN), so an emitter that re-introduced a :realms slot still validates against every schema-conformance test at :194-208. Net: a genuine realm-slot re-introduction on the wire is caught by nothing in this file.

FILE
- tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/test/re_frame/mcp_conformance/operating_frame_address_test.clj:230-239 (no-realm-slots-on-the-envelope); schema OperatingFrameSuccess :90-100.

REPRO (HEAD)
OperatingFrameSuccess is declared {:closed false} at :95. no-realm-slots-on-the-envelope only maps over the local success-fixtures. Adding a :realms key to a real emission would pass the schema tests (open map) AND this fixture-only test (the fixtures don't carry it) -- no gate goes RED.

BACKSTOP
None within this artefact for the realm-reintroduction case. The dissoc/type negatives in the same file DO have teeth for the PRESENT public slots, so this is a targeted gap, not a wholesale vacuity.

FIX SKETCH
Either (a) drive the real operating-frame emitter (JVM-reachable projection) and assert absence on its output, or (b) add a closed negative to the schema -- a [:map {:closed true} ...] variant or an explicit [:fn (complement has-any-realm-key?)] predicate on OperatingFrameSuccess -- so a re-introduced realm slot fails validation. Fixture-only absence checks over author-written maps cannot catch an emitter regression.

ACCEPTANCE
An authored/emitted success envelope carrying a :realms (or any *-realm*) slot must go RED.

title: [correctness-review][mcp-conformance] :include-sensitive vocab-pin row satisfied only by a docstring (vacuous, backstopped)
description:
VACUOUS ROW (backstopped). Gate 5 mcp-base-pins-the-canonical-slot-keywords greps mcp-base/vocab.cljc with raw (str/includes? src literal) for each of #{":rf.size/include-large?" ":rf.size/include-sensitive?" ":include-sensitive"}. The bare ":include-sensitive" (no ?, no namespace) is NOT a code constant in vocab.cljc -- its ONLY occurrence there is the DOCSTRING at line 181 ('the :include-sensitive wire-arg'). It is not a substring of :rf.size/include-sensitive? (a / precedes 'include', not a colon). So that row asserts 'vocab.cljc pins the canonical bare wire-key as a source-of-truth constant' while nothing but prose satisfies it -- it can never fail while the docstring exists and never verified a real constant.

FILE
- tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/test/re_frame/mcp_conformance/slot_name_test.clj:392-402 (mcp-base-pins-the-canonical-slot-keywords); literal set :171-184.

REPRO (HEAD)

title: [correctness-review][story] test vacuity: url_state watcher/popstate idempotency tests assert only no-throw, not the no-doubled-fires/no-stacking they name
description:
SURFACE: tools/story url-state test.
FILE: tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/url_state_cljs_test.cljs:163-172 (state-watcher-install-and-teardown-noerr, assertion :172) and :176-189 (popstate-listener-install-is-idempotent, assertion :189).

DEFECT (test vacuity / over-promising name): both tests name an IDEMPOTENCY invariant -- 're-install replaces under same key (no doubled fires)' / 're-installing the popstate listener replaces rather than stacks' -- but the body double-installs, removes, and asserts only (is true \"... without errors\"). Neither mutates the atom / dispatches a popstate to COUNT how many times the handler fired, nor checks the registered watch/handler count. A regression that STACKED watchers/listeners (double-fire) would pass unchanged; only a thrown exception during install/remove is caught. Confirmed the .cljc sibling (url_state_test.cljc) has no install-state-watcher/idempotency coverage, so these are the only coverage of the claim.

Additionally, popstate-listener-install-is-idempotent wraps its whole body in (when (browser?) ...), so under the default node gate (npm run test:cljs) it executes ZERO assertions and passes vacuously; even under the browser build it only asserts (is true).

FIX SKETCH: state-watcher test -- install twice, swap! the atom once, assert the watcher side-effect fired EXACTLY once (or that the atom carries exactly one watch key). popstate test -- after a double-install (browser), dispatch a popstate and assert the handler ran once (no stacking); keep the browser gate but replace (is true) with the fire-count assertion.

ACCEPTANCE: each test asserts the no-doubled-fires / no-stacking invariant it names via a fire-count (or watch/listener-count), not merely 'no exception'; a stacking regression fails the test. Verified against HEAD 79fb2f2da.

title: [correctness-review][story] test vacuity: dialog-survives-fresh-recording asserts (is true), never exercises the snapshot-independence it names

title: [correctness-review][story] frame teardown re-resolves decorator stack at teardown time -> hot-reload :init/:teardown asymmetry
description:
SURFACE: tools/story per-variant frame lifecycle.
FILES: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc:997-1000 (run-teardown-walks! re-resolves the decorator stack) vs allocate! (:frame-setup :init runs against the stack the runtime resolved at ALLOCATE time, threaded into allocate!). Contrast destroy-inline! (frames.cljc:920-949), which correctly uses the exact decorator-stack captured at allocate-inline! time.

DEFECT (asymmetric setup/teardown under hot-reload): run-teardown-walks! (shared by destroy! and the in-place reset-state!) resolves the decorator stack at TEARDOWN time:
  (let [stack (decorators/resolve-decorators variant-id)]
    (apply-frame-teardown! variant-id (:frame-setup stack)))
allocate! ran each :frame-setup decorator :init against the stack resolved at ALLOCATE time. If the variant/story body's :decorators changed between allocate! and destroy!/reset-state! -- hot-reload, a first-class supported operation per the module docstring -- the :teardown walk runs a DIFFERENT decorator set than :init did: a resource opened by the old set's :init is never torn down, and the new set's :teardown runs against a resource that was never opened. Stateful :frame-setup decorators (open in :init, close in :teardown) leak / mis-teardown across a hot-reload edit.

The inline twin destroy-inline! does NOT have this issue (it uses the allocate-time stack), which highlights the registered-path inconsistency. The docstring (frames.cljc:996) frames the re-resolution as a caller-surface convenience without flagging the hot-reload asymmetry.

REPRO SKETCH: register a variant with a stateful :frame-setup decorator D1 (:init opens R1, :teardown closes R1). allocate!. Hot-reload edit the variant to use D2 instead (D2 :teardown closes R2). reset-state!/destroy! -> teardown resolves {D2} and runs D2's :teardown (R2 never opened) while D1's R1 (opened at :init) is never closed -> leak + spurious teardown.

FIX SKETCH: carry the allocate-time decorator stack to the teardown walk (mirror destroy-inline!) rather than re-resolving at teardown -- e.g. stash the resolved stack on the frame at allocate! and read it in run-teardown-walks!, or thread it through the destroy!/reset-state! callers the same way the inline path threads it.

SEVERITY: low-moderate -- only bites stateful :frame-setup decorators edited mid-hot-reload; most decorators are stateless. But it is a genuine lifecycle correctness asymmetry with a clean, already-demonstrated (destroy-inline!) fix pattern.

ACCEPTANCE: after a hot-reload that changes :decorators, teardown runs the SAME :frame-setup set that :init ran (the allocate-time stack), not the re-resolved current set; a stateful-decorator open/close pairs correctly across the edit. Verified against HEAD 79fb2f2da.

title: [correctness-review][story] recorder DOM type-buffer + debounce timers survive start-recording!/clear! -> cross-recording keystroke bleed
description:
SURFACE: tools/story interaction recorder (Causa/Story priority).
FILES: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder/dom_capture.cljs:117-123 (type-buffer defonce atom), :194-221 (schedule-type-flush!/buffer-type! arm a setTimeout), :165-192 (flush-type-buffer!); tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder.cljc:696-711 (append-dom-buffered -- appends REGARDLESS of :recording?), :873-882 (record-dom-event-buffered!), :791-809 (start-recording!), :820-826 (clear!), :811-818 (stop-recording!), :828-834 (toggle!).

DEFECT (cross-recording state bleed): the DOM-capture type-buffer is a defonce atom holding {selector -> {:value :t :timer}} with a pending js/setTimeout flush (default debounce 250ms). NEITHER start-recording! (swap! state start ...) NOR clear! (reset! state initial-state) resets type-buffer or cancels its pending timers -- they only touch the recorder atom. When the pending timer fires, flush-type-buffer! calls recorder/record-dom-event-buffered! -> append-dom-buffered, which conj's the buffered [:dom/type selector text t] onto the CURRENT recorder state's :entries UNCONDITIONALLY (no :recording? check, no recording-identity check). So a keystroke buffered during recording A can land in recording B's :entries, carrying A-relative :t.

REPRO (stop path that does not flush + restart/clear within debounce-ms):
1. start-recording! :A (started-ms 1000).
2. type into #note -> buffer-type! stashes {:value \"x\" :t 50 :timer T}, T scheduled ~+250ms.
3. stop via a NON-flushing path -- facade re-frame.story/stop-recording! (story.cljc), recorder/toggle!, an MCP stop, or a keyboard shortcut. T still pending.
4. Before T fires: start-recording! :B (fresh :entries []) -- OR clear!.
5. T fires -> record-dom-event-buffered! [:dom/type #note x 50] -> appended into B's (or the idle) :entries. B now contains a [:dom/type] step the user never performed in B, with an A-relative timestamp -> wrong generated :script.

ORIGIN: rf2-eztym.3 (PR #3198) deliberately made flush-type-buffer! bypass the :recording? re-check (via record-dom-event-buffered!) so the FINAL keystroke survives a flush firing after stop -- correct for stop-into-SAME-recording, but it left the buffer + live timers untied to the recorder start/clear boundary and gave buffered entries no recording identity. The rf2-eztym.3 browser test only covers stop-before-flush + remove-after-stop, not stop->restart/clear-within-debounce.

REACHABILITY: the everyday toolbar Stop routes through a handler that flushes (ui/recorder.cljs), so the common UI path is safe; the exposed paths are the PUBLIC facade stop-recording!, toggle!, MCP stop, keyboard-driven stop, and clear! (discard) -- all real surfaces. Narrow timing window (stop->restart within debounce-ms) but a genuine 'state not cleared on reset -> bleeds between runs' defect.

FIX SKETCH: start-recording! and clear! should drain+cancel the DOM-capture buffer (cancel pending timers + reset! type-buffer). recorder.cljc cannot :require dom_capture.cljs (layering: dom_capture requires recorder), so use a late-bind seam (e.g. :recorder/reset-dom-buffer that dom_capture registers, invoked by start-recording!/clear!), OR stamp each buffered entry with the recording's started-ms/variant-id and have append-dom-buffered drop on mismatch.

ACCEPTANCE: a keystroke buffered under recording A, followed by stop (non-flushing path)+start-recording! B within debounce-ms, does NOT appear in B's :entries; clear!-while-typing leaves no phantom entry in a subsequent recording; the rf2-eztym.3 stop-into-same-recording final-keystroke survival still holds. Verified against HEAD 79fb2f2da.

title: [correctness-review][resources] clear-scope AND remove cancelled work rows omit causal :completed-at (no :rf/time-ms cofx)
