title: [correctness-review][resources] Mutation handlers omit with-classification-lowering => elision registry drifts out of step with :entries after mutations
description:
The resource reply/lifecycle handlers are each wrapped in resource-events/with-classification-lowering (resources.cljc:405-527), folding classification/reconcile-registry over the returned runtime-db so the per-frame elision registry stays 'in step with :entries regardless of which handler ran' (events.cljc:93-95). The MUTATION handlers are NOT wrapped: :rf.mutation/execute, :rf.mutation.internal/succeeded, :rf.mutation.internal/failed (resources.cljc:545-560). git grep confirms neither mutation_events.cljc nor mutation_runtime.cljc ever calls reconcile-registry.

WHY IT MATTERS
Each unwrapped handler creates/patches/evicts durable resource :entries: execute-handler (optimistic apply/seed), succeeded-handler (:patches/:populates/:removes), failed-handler (conflict-aware rollback restore/remove/invalidate). A :populates may CREATE a brand-new registered-resource entry (populate-entry builds on empty-entry). If that resource carries fine-grained projection-relative :sensitive [[:data ...]]/:large declarations and the entry was never previously ensured (no wrapped resource event reconciled it), the elision registry holds NO declaration for it, and project-entry-data's registry-classifies-under? gate (classification.cljc:318) rides the value VERBATIM. The stated invariant is violated.

REACHABILITY (latent today)
The fine-grained registry-gated projectors (project-entry-data/project-entry-params) are called ONLY from SSR (server-side; mutations do not run during server render). Client-side tool/trace egress uses the COARSE whole-entry-disposition verbatim for :serialize entries (ssr.cljc:228-229) — registry-independent — so a coarse :sensitive? resource is safe everywhere. The gap bites (i) any future client-side fine-grained DATA egress surface and (ii) the correctness invariant + test coverage now.

TEST VACUITY
Every classification test manually calls reconcile-registry before asserting redaction (resources_classification_cljs_test.cljc:96,199,220,242), so none exercises the un-reconciled mutation path.

FIX SKETCH
Wrap the entry-mutating mutation handlers in with-classification-lowering (idempotent, value-independent — safe to add), or fold reconcile-registry into their :rf.db/runtime commit.

ACCEPTANCE
After a :populates creates a fresh entry of a resource declaring :sensitive [[:data :field]], the elision registry carries the lowered declaration and SSR project-entry-data redacts the field WITHOUT a manual reconcile-registry call in the test.
Found in audit rf2-u10eye; ai/findings/2026-07-11.resources-audit.md finding C.

title: [routing/core] Custom-URL-strategy validation needs a reg-frame pre-registration preflight (follow-up to rf2-j538f7.11/PR #5633)
description: PR #5633 (rf2-j538f7.11) added fail-loud validate-url-strategy! + a failure-atomic listener install, scoped to implementation/routing. But the FULLER acceptance needs a CORE preflight: on a URL owner's FIRST registration with a malformed custom strategy, the frame container + initial-events already RUN before validation throws in the post-create hook. To fail BEFORE the container/initial-events run, reg-frame (implementation/core) must preflight the routing strategy config at registration time. Scoped out of #5633 (touches implementation/core). Also: Spec 012-Routing may need a note on the validation timing. Re-registration + all consult paths are already covered + fail-atomic by #5633; this is only the first-registration-preflight gap. Verify against implementation/core reg-frame + routing strategy validation.
notes:
RULING (decision-agent, 2026-07-12): ADD the registration-time preflight, landing NOW at the existing single frame-config commit chokepoint (the frame/reg-frame ENGINE in implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc) — NOT sequenced behind the frame-chain beads (nyea0r/h1vqa4). This is the Codex-recommended variant of Option A; the brief's original "fold into make-frame/frame-root rebuild" sequencing is REJECTED because its premise is falsified: h1vqa4's investigation + ruling KEEP the engine (renamed to private upsert-frame!; only the public reg-frame spelling dies), so the semantic home — "the one frame-config commit chokepoint" — already exists today, and h1vqa4 is a large multi-PR migration; holding a real fail-loud/atomicity hole behind it buys nothing.

WHY: (1) fail-loud is only honored if the frame fails BEFORE observable side-effects; today a malformed custom :url-strategy on first registration throws only in the post-create hook (directory.cljc:518) after container + :initial-events + :rf.frame/created. (2) Re-registration is ALSO not transactionally safe today: registrar/register! (frame.cljc:1893), the frames swap (:2018-2019), and :rf.frame/re-registered (:2028) all precede the hook's validation (:2030) — PR #5633 made only the LISTENER handoff atomic, leaving a working old listener over poisoned new metadata. (3) The defer-writes precedent already exists in this exact function (rf2-hhlzky / 1f9ab5f007: new-frame-record built before registrar/trace writes), and the late-bind preflight pattern already exists at frame.cljc:1875-1877 (:frame-classification/validate!) — this ruling extends both, no new machinery class.

CHOSEN SHAPE (ownership: routing owns the meaning, core owns the timing):
1. New pure preflight fn in implementation/routing (calls existing re-frame.routing.strategy/validate-url-strategy!): no-op when :url-strategy ABSENT; when PRESENT — including explicit nil, which is malformed (presence semantics, omission alone selects the default) — validate with {:frame frame-id} so :rf.error/invalid-url-strategy names the frame.
2. Publish as ONE late-bind key :routing/preflight-frame-config! on both hosts + a re-frame.late-bind.directory row. No chain-fn!, no generic validation-plugin subsystem.
3. Core engine invokes the hook with the final expanded config (after expand-preset + merge-coords) alongside the existing pure preflights, BEFORE existing/new-frame-record, registrar/register!, trace-policy writes, the frames swap, setup dispatch, or any trace emit. If :url-strategy is present but the hook is unpublished, fail loud (routing-artefact-missing) — storing config nobody can validate/execute is worse than a dependency error. The :url-bound?-only late-load case is unchanged.
4. ATOMICITY COMPLETION (required, not optional): move record-frame-generation-pool! (live_frame.cljc:737, currently BEFORE the frame/reg-frame call at :745) to after the engine returns successfully (or stage it with the candidate), so failed creation AND failed re-construction preserve old provenance.
5. CONSULT-PATH SIMPLIFICATION (in-scope, gated): once every public write path is preflighted, url-strategy-from-config may become a trusted read (drop the per-consult map?/fn? checks that route-link pays per render). GATE: only after tests pin load-order + absence of internal direct-write bypasses; if that audit is not clean, keep a debug-only assertion and file a follow-up instead of blocking this bead.

INVARIANT (acceptance): after preset expansion + source-coordinate merging, the complete candidate config is validated before any candidate-derived write or user code. Failed FIRST registration leaves no frame record, no registrar/source-store row, no generation-provenance row, no trace policy/retention state, no URL claim/listener, no trace event, no :initial-events effect. Failed RE-registration leaves every previously committed value and listener unchanged and emits no :rf.frame/re-registered.

REJECTED: (a) sequencing behind nyea0r->h1vqa4 — falsified premise, see above; (b) Option B-as-framed ("throwaway on doomed reg-frame") — void for the same reason, the engine survives rename; (c) Option C accept-the-gap — contradicts fail-loud posture + the 1f9ab5f007 no-residue precedent, and the hole is wider than briefed (re-registration metadata poisoning); (d) validating IN core — reverses the artefact boundary, core must not require routing (bundle isolation; late-bind exists exactly for this direction); (e) the registrar registration-hook seam — post-write and exception-swallowing (registrar.cljc register! writes then swallows hook throws); (f) executing strategy legs during preflight — shape/callability is the enforceable static contract; probing :push!/:replace!/listener install would itself cause browser effects. Keep #5633's install-new-before-teardown listener handoff.

TESTS (proof gates): CLJS first-registration via BOTH rf/reg-frame and rf/make-frame — malformed custom strategy + an :initial-events handler incrementing an external probe; assert :rf.error/invalid-url-strategy, zero probe calls, no frame/registrar row, no URL claim/listener, no trace-policy residue, no :rf.frame/created. CLJS re-registration — valid URL owner, snapshot registrar metadata/config/generation/provenance/listener identity/claim order/traces, submit malformed replacement, assert all snapshots unchanged + no :rf.frame/re-registered (extend the #5633 listener-survival test in routing_history_cljs_test, which today proves only listener survival). JVM+CLJS units: host-specific required legs, valid shipped/custom, absent-vs-explicit-nil, frame-id ex-data, missing-routing-artefact diagnostic; keep a callable-but-throwing installer test proving the #5633 handoff stays atomic. Run core late_bind_drift_test, core frame lifecycle/initial-events tests, routing JVM + CLJS history tests, and the routing/core production bundle-isolation gate.

SPEC/DOCS: amend Spec 012-Routing strategy contract — final frame config is host-validated at construction/re-construction BEFORE commit; omission alone selects the default; failure preserves the previous frame on re-registration. Cross-reference Spec 002's construction failure-atomicity paragraph. Confirm/add :rf.error/invalid-url-strategy + routing-artefact-missing catalogue rows; document that :url-strategy requires the routing artefact loaded before frame construction. NOTE: spec/002 (and 012 if hot-listed) are HOT ZONE — sequence those edits per dispatch rules. No public API addition.

SEQUENCING: land against today's frame/reg-frame immediately; frame.cljc is not hot-zone. If h1vqa4's engine rename (upsert-frame!) lands first, rebase — the preflight + tests carry unchanged to the renamed engine; whichever lands second rebases. The dependency is on the chokepoint, not any constructor name.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #5688 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5688). Registration-time :url-strategy preflight at the frame/reg-frame commit chokepoint per the 2026-07-12 ruling: routing-owned pure preflight-frame-config! (presence semantics, {:frame} ex-data) published as :routing/preflight-frame-config! on both hosts + directory row; core invokes it with the final expanded config before any candidate-derived write, failing loud :rf.error/routing-artefact-missing when the hook is unpublished; record-frame-generation-pool! moved after the engine commit (atomicity completion). Consult-path simplification NOT taken — audit not clean (direct registrar/register! :frame writes in-tree); follow-up rf2-ecb4sx filed. Full test matrix per the ruling's TESTS paragraph; Spec 012/002(minimal cross-ref)/009 amended. Gates green: routing JVM 415t, core JVM 1807t, CLJS node 8648t, bundle-isolation, mkdocs --strict.

title: [correctness-review][routing] scroll-position cache: capture keys canonical, restore keys raw incoming URL
description:
SURFACE: capture implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/scroll.cljc:178-201 (current-route-url -> registry/route-url of the leaving slice); restore lookup plan.cljc:135-136 (lookup-scroll-position scroll-cache url) with the RAW incoming url threaded from url_change.cljc:177 (:url url).

DEFECT: scroll-position cache keys are asymmetric. On leaving a route, the position is SAVED under the CANONICAL route-url reconstruction of the leaving slice (canonical query key order, no trailing slash, canonical percent-encoding). On :restore (popstate / Back), the lookup key is the RAW popstate URL from the history entry. Any history entry whose spelling differs from canonical never finds its saved position (saved-pos nil), so Back silently skips scroll restoration.

TRIGGERS: a deep link with trailing slash (/cart/), non-canonical query order (?b=2&a=1), or alternate percent-encoding — i.e. any history entry the browser holds that was not produced by route-url. In-app forward/back round-trips are unaffected because both legs use route-url output.

FIX SKETCH: canonicalise the restore lookup key the same way capture does — round-trip the incoming URL through match-url -> route-url before the lookup, with a raw-URL fallback on a match miss (so a not-found popstate still attempts a raw lookup). Keep capture unchanged. Alternatively key BOTH sides off the raw URL, but canonicalising both is the round-trip-stable choice.

ACCEPTANCE: navigate away from /cart (canonical), then popstate Back to a non-canonical spelling of the same route (/cart/ or reordered query) finds the saved scroll position (saved-pos non-nil, :rf.nav/scroll :restore uses it). Part of correctness-review EPIC rf2-x76af2 / audit rf2-u4yter.

title: [correctness-review][routing] nil-valued :query opt leaks into route slice while elided from the URL
description:
SURFACE: implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/navigate.cljc:317-344 (non-:query-merge path) -> events.cljc:143 (merge-route-slice writes :query). Contrast the nil-strip in navigate.cljc:340-343 (:query-merge branch) and route-url elision in registry.cljc:1443-1446,1483.

DEFECT: on the plain :query opt path, query-params (e.g. {:sort nil}) is written verbatim into the slice via commit-navigation :query query-params (navigate.cljc:548 -> events.cljc merge-route-slice). But route-url ELIDES nil-valued query keys for the URL AND validates the ELIDED map — so the URL omits ?sort= and validation passes. The nil-strip runs ONLY in the :query-merge branch. Spec 012:479 mandates the strip for :query-merge explicitly 'to keep the slice consistent with the URL'; the identical rationale is not applied to the plain :query opt, even though nil-valued query keys are a documented supported input (route-url nil-policy, 012:665-672 / registry.cljc:1395-1400: nil means 'omit this key').

REPRO: route-url half CONFIRMED at runtime — (route-url :route/search {} {:sort nil}) => "/search" (no throw, validation passed on the elided map). Then [:rf.route/navigate :route/search {} {:query {:sort nil}}] pushes /search yet writes {:sort nil} into [:rf.runtime/routing :current :query] (code-reading fact: query-params not nil-stripped before commit).

CONSEQUENCE: :rf.route/query sub exposes a junk {:sort nil} entry (SSR-hydrated too). A later URL-driven nav to /search yields :query {} (match-url produces no sort key), so identical-route-target? compares {:sort nil} vs {} -> not equal -> the rule-3 no-op fails and :on-match spuriously re-fetches.

FIX SKETCH: strip nil-valued query keys once in the navigate handler before BOTH the slice write and route-url — e.g. reuse the (remove (comp nil? val)) the :query-merge branch already applies (navigate.cljc:341) so it covers the plain :query opt too. Matches route-url's elision policy and keeps slice==URL.

ACCEPTANCE: [:rf.route/navigate route {} {:query {:sort nil}}] leaves [:rf.runtime/routing :current :query] with NO :sort key (matches the pushed URL); a subsequent URL-driven nav to the same URL is a rule-3 no-op (no :on-match re-fire). Part of correctness-review EPIC rf2-x76af2 / audit rf2-u4yter.

title: [correctness-review][routing] sequential optional groups: later group emits into earlier group's slot (prism break)
description:
SURFACE: implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:1594-1626 (route-url top-level loop) + match.cljc:282-405 (regex build). Grammar allows adjacent optional groups (validate-optional-group! permits them; cf. test routing_registry_test.clj:2204 uses /docs{/a}?{/b}?).

DEFECT (EP-0012 prism-law break, SILENT data corruption): each optional group's presence is checked INDEPENDENTLY on emission — no prefix rule prevents a later group emitting after an earlier sibling elides. For /docs{/:section}?{/:page}? the regex is ^/?docs(?:/([^/]+))?(?:/([^/]+))?$ (capture 1 = section, capture 2 = page). Supplying only the later param builds a URL that match-url reads into the FIRST group's capture.

REPRO (CONFIRMED at runtime, JVM clojure -M -e):
  (reg-route :route/docs {:params [:map [:section {:optional true} :string] [:page {:optional true} :string]]} "/docs{/:section}?{/:page}?")
  (route-url :route/docs {:page "5"})  => "/docs/5"
  (match-url "/docs/5")               => {:route-id :route/docs :params {:section "5"}}
{:page "5"} in; {:section "5"} out. Both keys optional so both legs pass :params validation — the page value lands in the section slot with NO error. match-url(route-url(x)) != x.

FIX SKETCH: fail closed on emission — throw (:rf.error/route-url-validation or a dedicated id) when a later optional group would be emitted after an earlier group elided (prefix rule), OR verify match-url(route-url(x)) recovers x for multi-group patterns and throw on mismatch. Same fail-closed rationale as the existing empty-string-segment reject (registry.cljc:1528-1538).

ACCEPTANCE: route-url on a two-sequential-optional-group route with only the later param supplied throws (or the round-trip is verified); a test pins the prism law for multi-group patterns. Reachability is an unusual pattern (two adjacent named optional groups) but the corruption is silent. Part of correctness-review EPIC rf2-x76af2 / audit rf2-u4yter.

title: [correctness-review][routing] route-shadowed-by-equal-score warns on structural rank, ignoring co-matchability
description:
SURFACE: implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:420-433. Pinned by test routing_registry_test.clj:982-1001 (T1, uses /x/:id + /y/:slug — different literals, never co-match).

DEFECT: the shadow scan warns whenever (= structural (subvec other-rank 0 5)). Rank tuples ignore literal segment text, so every same-SHAPE pair ties regardless of literals: /home vs /about -> both [1 1 1 1 1]; /x/:id vs /y/:slug -> both [1 1 2 1 1]. Spec 012 rule 6 (012:189) scopes the MUST-warn to 'an equal structural score ON THE SAME URL FAMILY' — routes that can actually match a common URL. Routes with different literal segments present no ambiguity (rule-6 tiebreak never fires between them) and should not warn.

IMPACT: every ordinary multi-page app emits N-1 spurious shadow warnings for its N single-segment static routes at registration. Tooling / AI scaffolds consuming the warning to flag genuine rule-6 conflicts (same literals, different param names — e.g. /a/:x vs /a/:y) are flooded; the one real shadow is buried. Degrades a spec-MUST diagnostic to noise for essentially every real app.

TENSION (needs ruling): a committed test (T1) pins the current over-broad behaviour, so this is a spec-text-vs-impl+test divergence, not a one-sided bug.

FIX SKETCH: (a) after the structural tie, additionally require co-matchability — for equal-shape patterns that is exactly 'all corresponding literal segments equal (params/splats wildcard)'; update T1 to use same-literal-different-param-name routes; OR (b) drop the 'same URL family' qualifier from spec 012:189. Recommended (a).

ACCEPTANCE: registering N same-shape static routes with distinct literals emits ZERO shadow warnings; two routes with identical literals but different param names (/a/:x, /a/:y) DO warn. Part of correctness-review EPIC rf2-x76af2 / audit rf2-u4yter.
notes: RULED 2026-07-11 22:17 (operator-delegated Mike->Fable, after independent Codex review): Option A, executed as the full contract reconciliation (not a registry-and-one-test patch). Warn iff equal rules-1-5 rank AND canonical path-pattern languages INTERSECT (some normalised path matches both). Do NOT implement naive corresponding-literals comparison - proven false negatives with optional groups (/a{/x}?/b vs /a/x{/b}? share rank AND intersect at /a/x/b despite differing literal sequences; /x/:id and /:kind/y intersect at /x/y). Implement segment automata (literal / one-segment param / final splat / optional epsilon branches) + product-automaton reachability after the rank prefilter, using match-against canonicalisation/case/trailing-slash rules. Spec surface is wider than 012: Spec 009:2133 canonical warning row currently says rank-equality alone - update it; sync Spec-Schemas:3281-3300 projection, docs/api/re-frame.routing.md, docs/routing/concepts.md, docstrings. Fix payload-direction issues while touching the row: earlier registration wins so the NEW route is the shadowed one (spec 009 says the reverse); :shadowed tag misnames the winner; Spec-Schemas promises a :rank tag that impl+009 omit. Tests: replace T1 disjoint pair with /a/:x + /a/:y true conflict; exact no-warning assertions for distinct static + param-prefix pairs; the overlap table (cross-position, splats, optional groups incl. the shifted witness) on BOTH CLJ and CLJS; property-test predicate vs brute-force URLs; registration benchmark on a large table. Note conformance :trace-emissions is subset-tolerant so a negative fixture needs a dedicated mechanism - acceptable to pin ref-impl-only if that is too big. Full contract: ai/decisions/rf2-6gzobp.route-shadow-warning-scope.md (mayor checkout, local-only).
close_reason: Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5689 — co-matchability (segment automata + product-automaton reachability) after the rank prefilter per the Option A ruling; payload direction reconciled (:route-id = new/shadowed, :shadowed-by = existing winner, :rank added); 009 row + Spec-Schemas + 012 rule 6 + docs + fixture synced; ruling's test table (true-conflict T1, exact no-warning pairs, cross-host overlap table incl. shifted witness, brute-force property test, registration benchmark) landed. Negative conformance fixture pinned ref-impl-only (subset-tolerant :trace-emissions), noted in fixture.

title: [correctness-review][routing] programmatic navigate lacks fragment-only short-circuit
description:
SURFACE: implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/navigate.cljc:424-575 (the commit cond). Contrast url_change.cljc:120-196 (fragment-only? branch) + plan.cljc:82-97.

DEFECT: navigate-handler computes identical-nav? (id+params+query+FRAGMENT all equal) but never fragment-only? (id+params+query equal, fragment differs). A programmatic nav that changes ONLY the fragment therefore takes the FULL commit path: fresh nav-token, re-fires every :on-match loader, pushes URL, and never emits :rf.route/fragment-changed. The two URL-driven doors (:rf.route/transitioned / :rf.route/handle-url-change) correctly short-circuit via plan/fragment-only?. Same-logical-operation asymmetry across the two commit paths.

REPRO: app at /docs/routing#a with :on-match [[:docs/load-page]]; dispatch [:rf.route/navigate :route/docs {:page "routing"} {:fragment "b"}]. Observed: :on-match re-fires (re-fetch of unchanged data) and the token bump stale-suppresses any in-flight loader for the unchanged route — the exact thrash Spec 012 Fragments rule 3/4 forbids (012:1109-1120).

SPEC STATUS (ambiguous — needs decision): spec 012:1109-1120 states the no-re-fire rule but frames the normative sentence as 'whichever URL-change event fires'; 012:1140-1152 (Programmatic navigation with fragments) is silent on on-match re-fire. Conformance fixture spec/conformance/fixtures/route-fragment-change.edn drives ONLY :rf.route/transitioned (lines 32-40) so the programmatic path is unpinned. Common anchor-link case is covered (route-link -> url-requested -> transitioned); only explicit programmatic fragment nav is affected.

FIX SKETCH (needs ruling): (a) add a fragment-only? branch to navigate-handler after the guard gate — write :fragment only, emit :rf.route/fragment-changed, push/replace the fragment URL, no token alloc, no :on-match (recommended, matches url_change + spec intent); OR (b) state in spec that programmatic navigate is deliberately exempt.

ACCEPTANCE: extend route-fragment-change.edn (or a navigate-path fixture) with a [:rf.route/navigate ... {:fragment ...}] step asserting :on-match does NOT re-fire and :rf.route/fragment-changed emits; OR a spec sentence documenting the exemption + a test asserting the current full-commit behaviour. Part of correctness-review EPIC rf2-x76af2 / audit rf2-u4yter.
notes: RULED 2026-07-11 22:17 (operator-delegated Mike->Fable, after independent Codex review): Option A with Codex implementation contract. Add fragment-only? branch to navigate-handler, classified AFTER target resolution/normalisation/validation AND after can-leave/can-enter guards pass. On that branch: (1) assoc ONLY [:rf.runtime/routing :current :fragment] - preserve route-id/params/query/transition/error/nav-token byte-for-byte; (2) emit exactly one :rf.route/fragment-changed {:route-id :prev-fragment :next-fragment :frame}; no token alloc trace, no activated/deactivated pair, no resource route-plan; (3) do NOT call commit-navigation (no :on-match, no settle, no resource ensure/release, no token counter bump - in-flight loaders stay eligible); (4) history: default push, {:replace? true} replace, via registered effects (never window.location.hash); (5) scroll: capture leaving scroll, push/replace URL, then emit resolved :rf.nav/scroll unless :scroll false (do NOT copy url_change fragment-only-fx verbatim - it carries capture only). pushState does NOT scroll natively (verified) so :rf.nav/scroll is required; make NO focus/:target parity claims. Identical target stays the existing complete no-op. Spec 012: amend Fragments rules + Programmatic-nav section to cover all three doors; qualify nav-token each-commit-allocates wording. Tests: new programmatic conformance case (loader unchanged, token unchanged, one fragment-changed, push effect) + :replace? variant + JVM navigate-handler integration + resources no-replan proof. ADJACENT (separate follow-up, do not fold in): URL-driven fragment-only path computes a scroll plan but drops scroll-fx. Full contract: ai/decisions/rf2-k4exp1.fragment-only-navigate.md (mayor checkout, local-only).

title: [correctness-review][machines] spec/Conventions reserved-key tables misdocument :rf/spawn-all-id / :rf/spawn-all-child-id (claim :data-stamped + finalize-cascade consumer; neither exists)
description:
spec/005-StateMachines.md:83-84 and spec/Conventions.md:571-572 document :rf/spawn-all-id and :rf/spawn-all-child-id as (a) living 'inside :data', (b) 'Stamped by the spawn-fx on each child of a :spawn-all', and (c) consumed by 'the finalize-cascade ... to locate the parent's join bookkeeping' / 'mark exactly which child finished'. All three are wrong at HEAD: 
- The keys are placed on the :rf.machine/spawn FX ARGS (the InvokeSpec) by handle-spawn-all-decl's args-builder (transition.cljc:2470-2471), which the conformance fixtures ASSERT on the spawn FX, not in child :data (spawn-all-join-all-completes.edn:100-120, spawn-all-any-cancels-extras.edn:87-112). 
- stamp-framework-data (spawn.cljc:173-184) stamps only :rf/self-id / :rf/parent-id / :rf/invoke-id into a child's :data -- never the spawn-all keys. 
- No runtime code READS either key (repo-wide: only the docstring at transition.cljc:2346 and the write at 2470-2471). The real join is the child-dispatched [:on-child-done <child-id>] protocol intercepted at the parent handler boundary (spec/005:3682 'Child completion protocol'; spawn_all_test.clj:12-15; join.cljc), NOT a finalize-cascade auto-mark. 
Net: the rows describe a :data location + finalize-cascade consumer that do not exist; the keys are contract-visible (asserted on the spawn FX) but functionally inert. 

FIX: spec-side -- rewrite/remove the two rows in BOTH spec/005-StateMachines.md and spec/Conventions.md to match reality (keys ride the spawn FX args; join protocol is [:on-child-done]). Optionally impl-side -- drop the dead FX-args keys (requires updating the 2 conformance fixtures that assert them).
acceptance_criteria: The 005 + Conventions reserved-key tables no longer claim :rf/spawn-all-id/:rf/spawn-all-child-id are :data-stamped or finalize-cascade-consumed; they describe the spawn-FX-args location and the [:on-child-done] join protocol. If keys are dropped impl-side, fixtures updated + conformance green.
notes: From correctness-review rf2-etvobo (machines contract surface). Primarily a spec-doc defect (spec/005 + spec/Conventions), optional impl cleanup. Verified no runtime reader at HEAD.

title: [correctness-review][http] Spec 014 surface drifts: 1-arity call-site helpers listed but not shipped; backoff carried-attempt off-by-one
description:
Correctness-review finding (rf2-k0pa70, http audit 2026-07-11). Two small spec-surface drifts. Doc-side. VERIFIED.

(a) BACKOFF CARRIED-ATTEMPT OFF-BY-ONE
spec/014:492 says a supersede during backoff records the carried work-id of "the retry attempt the request was about to make" (attempt N+1). The impl deliberately carries the JUST-FAILED attempt N on the backoff handle (transport.cljc:893-910; the timer's `(update :attempt inc)` advances only on fire). The impl's choice (last REAL attempt) is defensible and is what http_backoff_cancellation_test.clj deftest 3b asserts (`[:rf.work/http :shared 1 2]` for a sleeping attempt 2). FIX: correct the spec parenthetical at :492 to "the just-failed attempt" (or, if the spec wording is deemed authoritative, bump the carried attempt in schedule-backoff-handle! — but that contradicts the landed test).

(b) 1-ARITY CALL-SITE HELPERS LISTED BUT NOT SHIPPED
spec/014:888-897 (§Call-site helpers §Surface) lists 1-arity helpers `(rf.http/get url)` alongside `(rf.http/get url args)`. `re_frame/http.cljc` ships 2-arity ONLY, deliberately (rf2-3fc89f.9 — a URL-only call always fails `:rf.error/http-no-reply-target`; the docstrings state "There is no one-argument arity"). FIX: drop the 1-arity column from the spec surface table for all seven verbs (get/post/put/delete/patch/head/options).

NOTE: spec/014 is a hot-zone file — sequence these doc edits (can fold into the Finding rf2-uu10wq spec pass).

ACCEPTANCE: spec/014:492 wording matches the impl's carried-attempt semantics; spec/014 §Surface lists only the 2-arity `(rf.http/<verb> url args)` forms. mkdocs build --strict passes.

title: [correctness-review][http] Spec 014 epoch-carry stale-suppression passages (:427, :1535-1543) describe an unimplemented mechanism
description:
Correctness-review finding (rf2-k0pa70, http audit 2026-07-11). Spec/impl divergence — SPEC side is wrong (pre-EP-0011 residue). Doc-side fix; Mike decides. VERIFIED.

WHERE: spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:15, :427, :1535-1543.

DEFECT: the spec promises an "epoch carry" stale-suppression for plain managed HTTP that has NO implementation counterpart.
- :427 "Each retry advances the carried epoch (per Pattern-StaleDetection); a stale request (e.g. one whose target route changed mid-retry) is suppressed without dispatching the reply."
- :1535-1543 "Stale-suppression piggy-backs on the epoch carry ... managed requests inherit the dispatching event's epoch carry; replies that arrive after a newer navigation / actor restart are suppressed at the dispatch site."

`grep -i epoch implementation/http/src` matches only the `:epoch-restored` restore-quiesce, `epoch-now-ms` (completion clock), and `re-frame.epoch.tool-pair` (off-box projector). The ACTUAL stale-suppression triggers for plain `:rf.http/managed` are exactly: (a) same-request-id supersede, (b) actor-destroy obsolescence, (c) epoch-restore quiesce, (d) frame-destroy. There is no "each retry advances the carried epoch," no "route changed mid-retry -> suppress," and no "replies arriving after a newer navigation are suppressed at the dispatch site." Route/navigation staleness is owned by resources/nav-tokens (Spec 012/016), NOT plain HTTP.

FIX SKETCH (doc-side): rewrite :427 and :1535-1543 to name the real suppression triggers (supersede / actor-destroy / epoch-restore / frame-destroy) and to state that route/navigation staleness for plain HTTP is owned by resources/nav-tokens. Alternative (Mike): consciously grow plain HTTP a route-epoch carry — but no sibling surface expects that of it. NOTE: spec/014 is a hot-zone file — sequence this doc edit.

ACCEPTANCE: spec/014 no longer claims plain `:rf.http/managed` suppresses replies on route change / navigation via an "epoch carry"; the stale-suppression section enumerates the four real triggers. mkdocs build --strict passes.

title: [correctness-review][http] Reply-target SHAPE validated at completion time, not dispatch time (spec/014:176 says dispatch-time)
description:
Correctness-review finding (rf2-k0pa70, http audit 2026-07-11). Spec/impl divergence — impl side is wrong. VERIFIED.

WHERE: handlers.cljc `validate-reply-target!` (124-143) vs spec/014:176; the SHAPE check lives in encoding.cljc `build-reply-event` (300-304) and fires at completion time.

DEFECT: spec/014:176 lists `:on-success` / `:on-failure` -> `:rf.error/http-bad-reply-target` among the DISPATCH-TIME guards (alongside `:retry :on` -> `:rf.error/http-bad-retry-on` and `:url` -> `:rf.error/http-bad-request`, both of which ARE dispatch-time in the impl). But `validate-reply-target!` checks only key PRESENCE (it throws `:rf.error/http-no-reply-target` when NO target is supplied). The vector-or-nil SHAPE check lives in `build-reply-event` and fires only when the reply is DELIVERED — after the request already ran. A typo'd `:on-success :items/loaded` (bare keyword) therefore issues the request and throws inside the async completion, feeding the Finding rf2-ln85eg leak (CLJS retry-storm / JVM silent-swallow) instead of failing loud at the dispatch site.

FIX SKETCH: validate vector-or-nil for `:reply-to` / `:on-success` / `:on-failure` inside `validate-reply-target!` (dispatch-time), throwing `:rf.error/http-bad-reply-target`; keep the `build-reply-event` guard as belt-and-braces. Matches the spec's stated dispatch-time guarding and closes the Finding rf2-ln85eg entry point for the malformed-target case.

ACCEPTANCE: dispatching `[:rf.http/managed {:request {:url "/x"} :on-success :items/loaded}]` (bare keyword, non-vector non-nil) throws `:rf.error/http-bad-reply-target` at the fx-call site, BEFORE any transport attempt (no server hit). `{:on-success nil}` (explicit fire-and-forget) and a proper event vector still pass.

title: [correctness-review][http] clear-in-flight! 2-arity dissoc is unconditional by request-id — can evict a successor's live handle
description:
Correctness-review finding (rf2-k0pa70, http audit 2026-07-11). JVM-only concurrency race. VERIFIED by code inspection (asymmetry is on-its-face).

WHERE: registry.cljc `clear-in-flight!` 2-arity (114-119).

DEFECT: the 2-arity does `(swap! in-flight dissoc request-id)` UNCONDITIONALLY by request-id — it does NOT check whether the slot still holds `handle`. Contrast `remove-from-actor-index!` (75-84), which IS identity-based (`(remove #(identical? % handle) v)`). So the request-id index can be cleared out from under a live SUCCESSOR.

REPRO (JVM interleaving): request A in flight under request-id R (handle H_A). A fresh same-id request B arrives; `managed-handler` calls `supersede! R` (registry.cljc:257-263) which clears H_A (1-arg) and fires H_A's abort-fn, then run-attempt! registers B's handle H_B under R. Meanwhile A's natural completion (whenComplete thread) has already won A's `:finalised?` CAS (supersede's abort-fn loses the CAS — no-op on the reply), and A's `finalise-*` then calls `clear-in-flight! R H_A` (2-arg, transport.cljc:698/790) → `dissoc R` → EVICTS H_B. The live successor B becomes invisible to `:rf.http/managed-abort R` and to further supersedes — two effectively-live requests under one id, the out-of-order-reply pattern supersession exists to prevent. Also reachable via the abort-fn clear in Finding 1's interleavings.

FIX SKETCH: make the 2-arg dissoc identity-conditional, mirroring `remove-from-actor-index!`:
  (swap! in-flight (fn [m] (if (identical? (get m request-id) handle) (dissoc m request-id) m)))
Cheap; also constitutes half of Finding rf2-6nczv9's fix.

ACCEPTANCE: a test (JVM interleaving or a direct unit test of `clear-in-flight!`) where H_B is registered under R and then `clear-in-flight! R H_A` is called with H_A != H_B leaves H_B present in `in-flight` under R (the successor survives). Existing single-request cleanup behaviour unchanged.

title: [correctness-review][xray] Stale view-scope frame → controlled <select> value with no matching option
description:
SURFACE: tools/xray (frame view-scope picker).

DEFECT: An explicitly-picked view-scope frame is never reconciled against the currently-available frames, so after that frame leaves the stream the controlled `<select>` carries a value with no matching `<option>` (React warning + blank render) and the label shows a now-unpickable frame.

EVIDENCE (confirmed at the sub; view-layer traced):
- `frame_switcher.cljs:483-488` `:rf.xray/view-scope-frame` = `(or slot target-slot (head-frame event-bundles))`. Once the user picks a frame, `:view-scope-frame-slot` wins forever — no membership check against `:rf.xray/available-frames`.
- `:rf.xray/current-frame` (508-511) returns that stale frame; the picker view sets `[:select {:value (str active)}]` while rendering `<option>`s only for `available-frames`. When the picked frame drops out (e.g. `:palette/clear-trace-buffer` empties event-bundles, or the frame stops emitting / is destroyed), the select value matches no option → React "value not in options" warning + blank; the label span shows the unpickable frame; with `available-frames` empty the control is `:disabled` yet still carries the stale value.

FIX SKETCH: clamp `:rf.xray/current-frame` (or `view-scope-frame`) to membership in `:rf.xray/available-frames`, falling back to `head-frame`/first; or reconcile the `:view-scope-frame` slot when the picked frame leaves the available set.

ACCEPTANCE: after the picked frame disappears from `available-frames`, the picker falls back to a valid available frame (no controlled-select mismatch, no React warning, no unpickable label).

title: [correctness-review][xray] Space hijacked from focused shell buttons/summary (target-editable? too narrow)
description:
SURFACE: tools/xray (global keybinding spine branch vs focused controls / a11y).

DEFECT: `target-editable?` exempts only INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT/contenteditable, so a focused `<button>` / `[role=button]` / `<summary>` INSIDE the Xray shell falls into the spine branch. Space then dispatches `:rf.xray/toggle-live-pause` and `.preventDefault`s, blocking the control's native Space activation.

EVIDENCE (confirmed):
- `keybinding.cljs:215-228` `target-editable?` returns true only for INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT/`isContentEditable`.
- Spine branch (354-363) fires when `(mount/visible?)` AND `target-inside-xray?` AND `(not target-editable?)` AND `(not target-inside-modal?)`. A focused shell `<button>`/`<summary>` satisfies all four.
- `spine-key-id` (259-260) maps Space→`:rf.xray/toggle-live-pause`; line 360 calls `(.preventDefault event)`, suppressing the button's native Space activation.

REPRO (cross-platform via Tab): Tab to any ribbon `<button>` inside the shell, press Space → the LIVE feed pauses instead of the button activating. (Enter is unaffected — not a spine key — so `<a href>` links still work; the concrete victims are `<button>`/`<summary>`.)

FIX SKETCH: in the spine guard, also bail when the target is an activatable control (`<button>` / `[role=button]` / `<summary>`), OR do not `preventDefault` Space when the focused element natively handles it.

ACCEPTANCE: a focused shell `<button>`/`<summary>` activates on Space; the LIVE feed pause binding only fires when focus is not on an activatable control.

title: [correctness-review][xray] No event.repeat guard — held toggle chords flap (Ctrl+Shift+C / Cmd-K / Cmd-Shift-M / Space)
description:
SURFACE: tools/xray (global keybinding handler).

DEFECT: No `event.repeat` guard on the global keydown handler, so HOLDING a toggle-style chord fires it repeatedly at the OS key-repeat rate — the shell / palette / mode / live-pause flap open↔closed.

EVIDENCE (confirmed): `keybinding.cljs` `handle-keydown` (291-363) and every predicate contain no `(.-repeat event)` (nor `isComposing`) check anywhere in the file. Held toggle bindings flap:
- Ctrl+Shift+C shell toggle (294-296) → shell flickers open↔closed.
- Ctrl/Cmd+K palette-toggle (324-342) → palette flaps.
- Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+M mode-toggle (302-306) → Dynamic↔Static flaps.
- Space → `:rf.xray/toggle-live-pause` (spine-key-id:259-260) → pause flaps.
(Held j/k stepping is fine/desirable — this is specifically the toggles.)

REPRO: hold Ctrl+Shift+C — the shell repeatedly toggles.

FIX SKETCH: bail early on `(.-repeat event)` for the toggle bindings (or globally at the top of `handle-keydown`, keeping j/k repeat if desired by exempting the step bindings).

ACCEPTANCE: holding Ctrl+Shift+C / Cmd-K / Cmd-Shift-M / Space triggers the action exactly once per physical press (repeat events are ignored for toggles).

title: [correctness-review][xray] Command palette frame source diverges from I1 filter (ignores internal-frames + show-tool-frames?)
description:
SURFACE: tools/xray (command palette frame source vs frame-isolation invariant I1).

DEFECT: The command-palette "Switch focus to frame …" source filters out ONLY `:rf/xray`, ignoring the canonical `frame-switcher/internal-frames` set (which also holds `:rf/re-frame2-pair`) and ignoring `show-tool-frames?` entirely. This diverges from the ribbon picker and is an I1 (frame-observation isolation) leak on the palette surface.

EVIDENCE (confirmed):
- `palette/sources.cljc:147-163` `frame-items` builds the source from `(remove #(= :rf/xray %) frame-ids)` — bespoke single-id removal.
- Canonical picker: `frame_switcher.cljs:521` `:rf.xray/available-frames` → `distinct-frames` excludes the FULL `internal-frames #{:rf/xray :rf/re-frame2-pair}` (frame_switcher.cljs:110) and is designed to honour `show-tool-frames?`.
- `frame-ids` comes from `(rf/frame-ids)` (ALL registered frames, `palette/subs.cljs:137`), so once the MCP-pair tool frame is registered, Cmd-K's frame list surfaces it even with `show-tool-frames?` OFF (I1 leak on the palette). The divergence (weaker exclusion + no toggle awareness) is present today; runtime leak is gated on the pair frame being registered.

FIX SKETCH: build `frame-items` by filtering through `frame-switcher/internal-frames` (and thread `show-tool-frames?`) rather than the hand-rolled `:rf/xray`-only removal — one exclusion source of truth shared with the ribbon picker.

ACCEPTANCE: with a registered tool frame and `show-tool-frames?` false, the palette frame source excludes every `internal-frames` member; flipping `show-tool-frames?` on re-includes them (matching the ribbon picker).

title: [correctness-review][xray] filters/persistence <-edn throws on corrupt scalar :in/:out (violates never-throws-into-init)
description:
SURFACE: tools/xray (filters/persistence localStorage load path).

DEFECT: `<-edn` can throw on a corrupt/hand-edited payload whose `:in`/`:out` value is a non-seqable scalar, violating the documented "the load path never throws into init" contract.

EVIDENCE (confirmed):
- `filters/persistence.cljs:111-121` `<-edn`: the `try/catch :default` wraps ONLY `reader/read-string` (line 116). After the `(map? parsed)` guard, the coercion `{:in (vec (get parsed :in [])) :out (vec (get parsed :out []))}` (lines 119-120) runs OUTSIDE the try. A map like `{:in 5}` / `{:in :oops}` / `{:in true}` parses fine and is `map?`, so `(vec 5)` throws "5 is not ISeqable", escaping `<-edn` → escaping `load`/`hydrate!`.
- Docstrings of `<-edn` (112-114) and `load` (125-133) both promise the load path never throws into init and degrades unrecognised shapes to `{:in [] :out []}`.
- Existing tests (`persistence_cljs_test.cljs:63-68`) cover only unparseable ("this is not edn") and non-map ("[1 2 3]") shapes — the scalar-`:in`/`:out` bucket is untested and unguarded.

BLAST RADIUS: default boot runs `::reset-transient-filters` → `filters-persistence/clear!` (not `load`), so default boot is NOT exposed. But `load`/`hydrate!` are public + documented as reachable by hosts that opt back in (`filters.cljs:462-471`) and are called by the test harness — the contract violation is real on the opt-in hydration path and any direct `load` caller.

FIX SKETCH: coerce defensively — `:in (let [i (:in parsed)] (if (sequential? i) (vec i) []))` (same for `:out`), or move the coercion inside the existing `try`.

ACCEPTANCE: `(<-edn "{:in 5 :out []}")` returns `{:in [] :out []}` instead of throwing; a test covers scalar `:in`/`:out` payloads.

title: [correctness-review][xray] resizable-table column drag missing pointercancel + defensive teardown (listener pile-up)
description:
SURFACE: tools/xray (views/resizable_table column-drag pointer plumbing).

DEFECT: The resizable-table column drag attaches window-level `pointermove`+`pointerup` but omits a `pointercancel` handler and a defensive pre-attach teardown, so a missed `pointerup` leaks the move listener and piles up listeners across drags. Diverges from the two sibling drag surfaces that do it correctly.

EVIDENCE (confirmed code gap; leak needs a missed pointerup to trigger at runtime):
- `views/resizable_table.cljs:315-364` `on-pointer-down`: attaches `pointermove` + `pointerup` on `js/window` (363-364); `on-up` removes both (359-362). No `pointercancel`; no `removeEventListener` of a prior drag before attaching a new pair.
- Sibling reference pattern (correct): `resize_handle.cljs` attaches `pointercancel` + defensive detach (lines 163/244/503/569); `shell.cljs` col-divider (385-411). `resizable-table` is the lone diverger.

CONSEQUENCE: if `pointerup` is never delivered (touch `pointercancel`, browser gesture preemption, context menu, pointer leaving to another window), `on-move` stays bound to `window` and fires `:rf.xray.column-widths/resize-pair-tick` on every subsequent window pointermove; the next `pointerdown` adds another pair without removing the orphan → listener pile-up, each orphan dispatching per mouse-move.

FIX SKETCH: mirror `resize_handle.cljs` — hold the handler fns, add a `pointercancel` handler running the same cleanup, and run cleanup once at the top of `on-pointer-down` before re-attaching.

ACCEPTANCE: firing `pointercancel` (or a synthetic gesture-preempt) during a column drag removes the move/up listeners; a second drag never leaves an orphaned `pointermove`. A unit test drives `on-pointer-down` then `pointercancel` and asserts listener teardown.

title: [correctness-review][test-react] README drifted behind the two transactional-failure commits (:forced-teardown triggers + failed-update whole-root teardown undocumented)
description:
FILE: implementation/adapters/test-react/README.md:93 (lifecycle-phase table).

The README documents :forced-teardown as firing only when dispose-adapter! drains a still-mounted root. In the source (implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc), force-teardown-record! (:184-202, which logs :forced-teardown) fires from THREE paths:
 1. dispose-adapter! (:386-387) — the documented drain.
 2. Failed-INITIAL-mount rollback — mount-tree! (:283-284) -> roll-back-speculative-children! (:216-219). Landed in 488bf70df (rf2-3fc89f.2).
 3. Failed-UPDATE whole-root teardown — trigger-update! (:499-500) -> force-teardown-subtree! (:235-237). Landed in bd14ef705 (rf2-j538f7.1, PR #5580).

The README also nowhere states that a failed UPDATE now unmounts the WHOLE live root (React 18 uncaught-render semantics) rather than preserving the prior tree. Source docstrings (trigger-update! :459-480, run-render! :123-140) and the tests (test_react_cljs_test.cljc B.5 layer, :699-954) are fully current; only the README — the onboarding surface a test author reads first — lags and would mis-model failed updates.

VERIFIED read-only: git log confirms 488bf70df + bd14ef705; force-teardown-record! call sites enumerated above.

SUGGESTED FIX: extend the :forced-teardown table row (fires on dispose AND both transactional-failure paths) + add one sentence on failed-render/failed-update transactional semantics (whole-root teardown, original exception rethrown, no :did-update).
acceptance_criteria: README.md:93 :forced-teardown row lists all three trigger paths (dispose-adapter! drain, failed-initial-mount rollback, failed-update whole-root teardown). A sentence documents that a failed UPDATE unmounts the whole live root (no :did-update, original exception rethrown), matching the source docstrings + the B.5 tests.

title: [correctness-review][reagent] slim installs no default shouldComponentUpdate; contradicts FORM-3.md 'only re-render when subscribed values change'
description:
reagent-slim component.cljs installs NO default shouldComponentUpdate anywhere (install-lifecycle! :380-450, create-class* :525+, make-render-method :487-523; grep for shouldComponentUpdate/should-component-update = zero hits; cap-keys :125-133 does not include :should-component-update). __rfArgv is a fresh CLJS vector per render, so React has nothing to bail on. React's default sCU returns true -> every reagent-slim class ALWAYS re-renders when its parent re-renders, regardless of whether its argv changed.

Stock Reagent installs an argv-equality sCU (a child whose argv is = does NOT re-render on parent re-render) -- the signature fine-grained-rerender property.

DOC CONTRADICTION (strengthens from perf-only to correctness): FORM-3.md:165-170 states 're-frame2's reactive substrate already gates render at the subscription level (views only re-render when their subscribed values change)'. Without a default argv-equality sCU that claim is FALSE for parent-driven re-renders: a child with unchanged argv DOES re-render when its parent re-renders. The documented guarantee is exactly what the absent sCU would provide. The USER :should-component-update cap key is discussed (IMPL-SPEC:1137, DESIGN-RATIONALE:124-128, FORM-3.md:153-170) but the FRAMEWORK-DEFAULT argv-equality sCU is never mentioned as a removed behaviour.

CONSEQUENCES: every parent re-render cascades a full reagent-component subtree re-render (render Reactions re-capture, Form-2 render bodies re-run); :component-did-update / :get-snapshot-before-update fire on value-identical argvs where stock would skip -- an observable lifecycle-frequency divergence plus loss of the fine-grained-rerender property.

SUGGESTED FIX: install a default sCU comparing prev/next __rfArgv with = (matches stock), OR document the always-rerender choice explicitly as a spec decision AND correct FORM-3.md:165-170's 'only re-render when subscribed values change' claim. Mayor/Mike decision.
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) a default sCU comparing prev/next __rfArgv with = is installed on reagent-slim classes, a test asserts a child with = argv does NOT re-render when its parent re-renders, and FORM-3.md's subscription-gating claim holds; OR (b) the always-rerender behaviour is documented as an explicit decision in IMPL-SPEC/DESIGN-RATIONALE and FORM-3.md:165-170 is corrected to stop asserting 'views only re-render when their subscribed values change'. Decision recorded on the bead.
notes: RULED 2026-07-11 22:17 (operator-delegated Mike->Fable, after independent Codex review): Option A, tightened. Install a framework-owned internal argv-equality sCU on every reagent-slim class (compare __rfArgv with =; render if either argv missing; if comparison throws, fail OPEN and render with dev warning). Keep :should-component-update OUT of the public seven-key cap. forceUpdate bypasses sCU so subscription-driven updates are unaffected. Fix FORM-3.md to the NARROWER accurate contract (subscription invalidation targets its view; equal-argv parent propagation skipped; argv change/local state/context/force-update still render) - do NOT restate the old over-broad claim. Also remove FORM-3.md:160-163 reactify-component escape prose (unshipped fn - impossible advice). Proof: real React-19 DOM regression (parent rerender with = child argv -> child render+update lifecycles do NOT run; changed argv -> they do) plus keep existing subscription/forceUpdate browser coverage green. Full contract: ai/decisions/rf2-5al9d7.slim-default-scu.md (mayor checkout, local-only).

title: [xray] Auto-open-on-error watcher (settings/effects.cljs:593) is a third surface-reverting reopen route (follow-up to rf2-j538f7.41)
description: rf2-j538f7.41 (PR #5606) made the two GLOBAL reopen routes (toggle! Ctrl+Shift+C + palette Cmd/Ctrl+K) preserve the realized mount surface. A THIRD generic-reopen route remains with the same bug class: tools/xray settings/effects.cljs:593 — the auto-open-on-error watcher calls late-bound open_BANG_ directly on the empty→error edge, which would revert a hidden OVERLAY mount back to inline on auto-open. .41 was explicitly scoped to toggle! + palette and forbade a generalized surface framework, so this was left untouched. Decide: should the emergency/error auto-open also preserve the realized mode (route through the mode-aware toggle! instead of hard-coded open!)? If yes, small fix mirroring .41. Surface: tools/xray settings/effects.cljs (+ mount test).

title: Make manual setup compile coverage dependency-honest across all substrates
description:
## Slice inventory
Reviewed all 15 files in skills/re-frame2-setup: .claude-plugin/plugin.json; evals/evals.json; LICENSE; package.json; README.md; SKILL.md; references/{deps-versions,entry-namespace,first-counter,shadow-cljs,shared-dataflow}.md; spec/{authoring-prompt,design,inputs}.md; and tests/setup_drift_test.clj. Cross-checked the emitted shapes against VERSION, implementation/{package.json,deps.edn}, implementation/core, the Reagent/UIx/Helix adapters, implementation/schemas, tools/template resources/hooks/tests, Xray deps/preload/host ownership, examples/core/counter, docs/skills/re-frame2-setup.md, and skills/README.md.

## Post-remediation result
The prior-wave runtime defect is fixed. references/shared-dataflow.md now supplies both events, the sub, and CounterDb/register-schema!; both UIx and Helix core snippets require all three shared namespaces, attach the schema under with-frame, then dispatch-sync the seed. PR #5532 / rf2-3fc89f.40 landed that repair, and the current structural gate passes 29 tests / 87 assertions. The Reagent recipe also matches the current reg-frame -> with-frame/schema/dispatch-sync -> scoped render lifecycle. I found no new live recipe/runtime mismatch.

## Finding: the claimed semantic compile net no longer models the documented scaffold and can green through a transitive dependency
Expected: tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/emitted_test_run_test.clj says setup-skill-scaffold-compiles-test extracts the skill's own copyable snippets, synthesizes the dependency graph the skill documents, and provides a semantic compile net for the manual scaffold. Since UIx and Helix are executable manual routes and the prior remediation added new copyable shared source, the net should compile each shipped route with its documented direct day-one dependencies.

Actual:
- skill-deps-edn at emitted_test_run_test.clj:740-758 still says the skill counter registers no schema and deliberately omits day8/re-frame2-schemas. Current first-counter.md requires re-frame.schemas and invokes reg-app-schema, while deps-versions.md and SKILL.md make schemas an explicit day-one coordinate.
- The fixture still passes in a normally provisioned CI checkout because day8/re-frame2-xray itself depends transitively on day8/re-frame2-schemas. That masks the missing direct dependency instead of testing the dependency boundary the skill teaches.
- The materializer at lines 762-798 extracts only first-counter.md into a Reagent project. It never extracts or compiles shared-dataflow.md or either UIx/Helix core/views block. The current Lock 14 checks those routes with regexes only.
- Fixture documentation and failure text at lines 49-78, 665-676, and 843-855 still describe retired :app/main + :initial-events + bare frame-provider/no-schema wiring. Current manual boot uses :rf/default, reg-frame, with-frame, register-schema!, dispatch-sync, and frame-provider {:frame ...}.

## Concrete reproduction
From a directory with no project deps, requiring re-frame.schemas with only local-root core + Reagent fails with FileNotFoundException (namespace absent). Adding only local-root Xray makes the identical require print :schemas-resolved-via-xray. A current git-coordinate clojure -Stree likewise shows day8/re-frame2-xray -> day8/re-frame2-schemas while the direct day-one schemas coordinate wins via :use-top. Thus a compile of the fixture's synthesized map can succeed even though the map omits the dependency the copied source directly requires.

The skill's cheap gates all pass: setup_drift_test 29/87, check_skill_setup_counter_drift.py (including self-test), check_skill_package_refs.py, check_skill_eval_packaging.py, JSON parsing, and npm pack --dry-run (10 intended package files). Those greens are useful but do not compile the newly shipped alternate-substrate snippets. The opt-in compile fixture was invoked in this fresh worktree too; it correctly attempted one Reagent build, but could not complete because this audit worktree intentionally has no implementation/node_modules link. That host prerequisite is documented by the fixture and is not the finding; the dependency masking above was reproduced independently with Clojure CLI.

## Impact
A maintainer can remove or corrupt the explicit schemas dependency while the compile job remains green through Xray, and can break the packaged UIx/Helix snippets without any emitted-project compile failing. Xray opt-out or a future Xray dependency cleanup would then expose the missing namespace in user projects. This is the same class of false-green that let the prior alternate-substrate runtime defect ship, but it is not a duplicate of that repaired defect: the current recipes are sound; their semantic assurance is incomplete and dependency-inaccurate.

## Dedupe and history
- rf2-ae98go / merged PR #3754 created the original Reagent-only emitted fixture before schemas and the current boot shape were added; it does not cover this drift.
- rf2-3fc89f.40 / merged PR #5532 repaired the missing UIx/Helix dataflow. Its acceptance criterion 4 asked for an emitted-project gate for both alternates, but the remediation added only structural Lock 14; this bead records that remaining verification work rather than reopening or duplicating the repaired runtime bug.
- Reviewed closed setup correctness/test beads rf2-agi57x, rf2-aw8234, rf2-ynjts.36, rf2-ynxghf, rf2-74uffk, and relevant history. Searches of the full beads export for setup-skill-scaffold, emitted UIx/Helix, Xray-transitive schemas, and direct schema dependency found no active owner.
- GitHub searches found no open PR for setup-skill-scaffold-compiles-test or alternate setup emitted coverage. Relevant merged PRs are #3754 and #5532 only.
design:
Keep one small fixture family; do not add a second browser harness.

1. Parameterize the existing setup-skill materializer over :reagent, :uix, and :helix. Reagent continues to extract first-counter.md. UIx/Helix extract the three exact shared-dataflow blocks plus the matching core.cljs and views.cljs blocks from entry-namespace.md.
2. Synthesize the dependency map that the skill actually documents: core + selected adapter + schemas + Xray, plus Reagent or UIx/Helix substrate dependencies and the shared :shadow alias. Assert those direct coordinate keys before any local-root rewrite so a transitive Xray edge cannot satisfy the test accidentally.
3. Reuse the existing rewrite-deps-for-local-run!, node_modules link, and compile-app process for all three variants. Keep Lock 14 as the cheap registration/boot-order guard; the emitted compiles add syntax, namespace, classpath, and adapter-root coverage. Existing adapter browser smokes already own click/render behavior, so duplicating Playwright here would be gold plating.
4. Rewrite the fixture comments and failure diagnostics to the current schema-bearing reg-frame/with-frame/dispatch-sync lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The opt-in setup-skill emitted suite materializes three projects solely from shipped skills/re-frame2-setup references: Reagent, UIx, and Helix.
2. Each synthesized deps.edn has direct day8/re-frame2, selected adapter, day8/re-frame2-schemas, and day8/re-frame2-xray entries before local-root rewriting; removing the direct schemas entry fails an explicit dependency-shape assertion even though Xray also depends on schemas.
3. The Reagent project compiles first-counter.md; the UIx and Helix projects each compile the exact shared events/subs/schema plus their exact entry/view snippets and emit a non-empty app bundle.
4. A malformed/missing alternate namespace require, schema attach, adapter root call, substrate dependency, or fenced block makes the relevant variant fail rather than leaving all gates green. Existing Lock 14 continues to fail on missing event/sub/schema registrations or schema-before-seed ordering.
5. emitted_test_run_test.clj no longer claims the current counter has no schema or uses :app/main, :initial-events, or a bare provider; diagnostics name the actual reg-frame -> with-frame/register-schema!/dispatch-sync -> scoped-render path.
6. bb skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/setup_drift_test.clj, python scripts/check_skill_setup_counter_drift.py --self-test, the normal drift script, skill package/eval checks, and the focused RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS=1 three-variant fixture all pass in a provisioned checkout.

title: (BUG) Ignore inert HTML comments in the examples asset inventory
description:
## Slice and complete inventory

Second-wave correctness review of the complete examples/scripts surface at worker baseline 709159ed3. The slice has 13 files:

- Static trust gates: check-examples-assets.cjs and check-reagent-slim-boundary.cjs.
- Asset/staging ownership: examples-asset-manifest.cjs and examples-staging.cjs.
- Port ownership: port-resolver.cjs, examples-port.cjs, and story-feature-load-port.cjs.
- Browser/dev orchestration: serve-example.cjs, serve-and-run-story-feature-load-tests.cjs, run-story-feature-load-tests.cjs, and serve-and-run-story-play-scripts.cjs.
- Shared primitives: spec-helpers.cjs and walk-tree.cjs.

Direct consumers were traced as part of the review. implementation/package.json exposes dev:example, test:story-feature-load, test:story-play-scripts, test:adapter-smokes, and the always-run test:script-policy suite. implementation/adapters/scripts/serve-and-run-adapter-smokes.cjs consumes examples-port, examples-staging, and spec-helpers. The Story launchers consume the shared port/staging modules and implementation/scripts/lib/local-browser-harness.cjs. .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh routes executable/shared changes to the adapter and Story/Xray browser jobs; .github/workflows/test.yml always runs JS harness self-tests and runs the changed-surface browser gates, while expensive-tests.yml runs the full adapter/Story trio. Focused policy coverage lives in _walk-tree.test.cjs, _examples-port.test.cjs, _story-feature-load-port.test.cjs, _story-script-runners-policy.test.cjs, _examples-staging.test.cjs, check-examples-assets.test.cjs, and check-reagent-slim-boundary.test.cjs.

## Post-remediation verification and green baseline

The prior slice finding rf2-3fc89f.31 was fixed in merged PR #5521 / commit ed9e30f2e. The new walk-tree.cjs records every unexpected readdir failure, and all three former fail-open consumers now call walkDir plus assertWalkComplete: host-page enumeration, stock-Reagent source enumeration, and the staging namespace index. The deterministic unreadable-subtree, missing-root, and unreadable-source tests pass. Current origin/main advanced after dispatch only in beads, schemas, and Story/spec files; git diff HEAD..origin/main showed no examples/scripts change, so the reviewed slice is still current.

Other adjacent remediation was checked rather than re-filed: selected output directories are cleaned under OUT_ROOT before staging; local servers use the shared owned-readiness token and tracked process-tree cleanup; port overrides parse strictly and bind loopback; Story play discovery is non-vacuous and pageerror-fatal; the asset manifest feeds both staging and scanning; CSS block comments are stripped; and the HTML reference logic was consolidated into one inventory pass.

Current gates are healthy:

- npm run test:script-policy: PASS, including 112 changed-surface cases, 7 walk-tree cases, 5 examples-port cases, 4 Story-port cases, 17 Story-runner cases, 26 teardown cases, 24 staging cases, and the complete asset/slim suites.
- node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs: PASS, all 35 host pages and the shared tree.
- node examples/scripts/check-reagent-slim-boundary.cjs: PASS, all 73 stock-Reagent sources.
- node --check over examples/scripts/*.cjs: 13/13 PASS.

No checked-in example currently violates the asset contract. The finding below is a latent but concrete trust-gate bug, reproduced against the current exported scanner.

## Finding: inert HTML comments satisfy live asset contracts

check-examples-assets.cjs:504-607 implements extractHtmlReferenceInventory. Its single walk applies /<([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9:-]*)[^>]*>/g directly to the raw HTML at line 531. Unlike the CSS extractors, it performs no lexical removal of comments before tokenizing tags. scanPage then converts that inventory to a refSet at lines 1356-1360 and treats membership as proof that the page live-references each required shared asset.

Expected: only live HTML markup can satisfy REQUIRED_SHARED_ASSETS or enter the load-time/network and og:image views. A tag inside an HTML comment is inert: the browser neither fetches it nor exposes it as document metadata.

Actual: link/meta/script/img tags inside <!-- ... --> are indistinguishable from live tags to the inventory. Commented-out required refs can make the required-asset check pass; commented remote or missing refs can also false-fail an otherwise clean page.

## Concrete reproduction

Against the current exported module, a synthetic page had only one live asset tag, script src=main.js. Its head contained one HTML comment holding:

- link rel=icon href=_shared/img/favicon.svg
- meta property=og:image content=_shared/img/og.png
- link rel=stylesheet href=_shared/css/style.css

extractHtmlReferenceInventory returned all three commented refs in localRefs, tagged the two commented links and commented og:image as load-time assets, and returned the commented og.png in ogImages. Running scanPage with an injected filesystem that proves the referenced source files exist returned:

{ relIndex: "examples/synthetic/index.html", errors: [], refs: ["_shared/img/favicon.svg", "_shared/css/style.css", "main.js", "_shared/img/og.png"] }

The page has no live stylesheet, favicon, or social-preview metadata, yet the gate reports no violation. The current table-driven inventory suite covers quoting, attribute order, query/hash stripping, srcset/imagesrcset, poster, navigation, OG, data-* boundaries, and deduplication, but has no inert HTML markup case.

## Impact

A maintainer commonly comments out a link/meta tag while debugging, replacing an asset, or retiring markup. The always-run gate can then advertise that the required shared contract is intact while the staged/browser page actually ships without its stylesheet, favicon, or OG metadata. Existing files on disk do not help: resolution also trusts the same commented inventory, so all three missing live references remain green. This is the same class of parser-context error already corrected for CSS comments, but with the more serious false-green polarity on required assets.

The live tree is correct today, so P3 reflects a latent guard failure rather than a broken checked-in page.

## Dedupe and history evidence

All-status bead data was searched across title, description, design, and acceptance criteria for HTML comment, commented asset/link/meta, inert markup/HTML, extractHtmlReferenceInventory, and stripHtmlComments. No matching open, in-progress, or closed issue covers inert HTML comments.

Nearest issues are distinct:

- rf2-lvw3z9 / merged PR #5360 strips CSS block comments before @import/url extraction; it explicitly addresses inert CSS false positives. The HTML inventory still scans raw comments.
- rf2-6a3rgx / merged PR #5557 created the single HTML inventory and its 13-case table; its bead, PR body, diff history, and tests cover supported attribute/reference shapes but not whether markup is live.
- rf2-3dzb6h, rf2-cnu7qy, and rf2-arkvq8 fixed unquoted attributes, order-independent og:image, and srcset/poster visibility. None distinguishes commented from live tags.
- rf2-3fc89f.31 is the now-verified filesystem-walk completeness remediation.
- rf2-j538f7.24 covers PNG raster semantics in examples/_shared, not page reference liveness.

git log -G over the scanner/tests found the inventory refactor and SVG-comment work but no HTML-comment sanitization. GitHub all-state searches for check-examples-assets plus HTML comment, commented asset, extractHtmlReferenceInventory, and inert markup found no relevant PR beyond the CSS-comment and inventory work above. This is therefore a post-remediation axis, not a duplicate of an actioned finding.
design:
Keep the fix at the one inventory choke point. Before extractHtmlReferenceInventory walks tags, remove HTML comment spans from the text once, including an unterminated <!-- through end-of-file so tags in an unfinished comment cannot satisfy the contract. A focused lexical helper is sufficient for this contract; do not add a general HTML parser or duplicate filtering in localRefs/assets/ogImages. This mirrors the existing stripCssComments posture and preserves one parse feeding all three views.

Do not broaden this bead into a new staging abstraction, DOM renderer, or network crawler. The purpose is simply that inert markup contributes zero references while live markup immediately before/after a comment retains current ordering and classification.
acceptance_criteria:
- extractHtmlReferenceInventory returns no localRefs, assets, or ogImages for link/script/meta/img tags that occur only inside a closed HTML comment.
- A synthetic scanPage page whose three required shared refs exist only inside a comment reports all three as missing even when those files exist on disk.
- A commented remote script/link/image does not trip the direct-network policy, and a commented missing local asset does not trip disk resolution; inert markup is absent in both verdict polarities.
- Live references immediately before and after a comment retain their current order, tags following a closed comment are still discovered, and an unterminated <!-- makes the remaining would-be tags inert rather than satisfying the gate.
- Add the inert-markup cases to the single table-driven HTML inventory suite, plus at least one scanPage teeth test proving the required-asset false green is closed.
- All 35 real example host pages and the shared tree remain green; npm run test:script-policy, node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs, and the existing staging/port/Story policy suites pass.
notes: Audit only: no source edits, commits, PR, or closure. Reproduction was an in-memory Node invocation of the current exported scanner and left the worktree source-clean. Worker baseline 709159ed3; later origin/main commits did not touch examples/scripts.

title: Drain open-in-editor child output before waiting for exit
description:
## Slice and complete inventory

Post-remediation correctness review of the complete `tools/testbed-support` surface (all 9 current files):

- `README.md`, `deps.edn`
- `src/re_frame/testbed/config.cljs`
- `src/re_frame/testbed/story_host.cljs`
- `src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj`
- `test/re_frame/testbed/config_cljs_test.cljs`
- `test/re_frame/testbed/story_host_cljs_test.cljs`
- `test/re_frame/testbed/story_host_dom_cljs_test.cljs`
- `test/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server_test.clj`

Traced the slice into `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`, the browser client `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords/open_endpoint.cljs`, core source-coordinate resolution, `spec/Tool-Pair.md`'s POST/loopback/runtime-resolution contract, and all direct Story/Xray/example consumers. The focused JVM suite is green: 28 tests / 141 assertions. The focused CLJS command could not start in this fresh audit worktree because no local `shadow-cljs` binary/node_modules is installed; its complete test source was inspected. No source was edited.

## Post-remediation and dedupe evidence

The wave-1 finding `rf2-3fc89f.24` is correctly remediated by merged PR #5550: `config.cljs` now distinguishes decode failure with `::decode-failed`, skips malformed query pairs, and falls through to the build root; focused malformed-value/key/fallback tests are present. Earlier testbed-support fixes were also checked rather than re-filed: POST/loopback security (`rf2-pnr56s`), literal-plus query parsing (`rf2-62hu6k`), malformed-query 400 (`rf2-bhejni`), missing-file false success (`rf2-i877cj`), JSON controls/column-only coordinates (`rf2-2loouf`), classpath resolution reuse (`rf2-hf0vqa`), and endpoint negative-path coverage (`rf2-bnv3cu`, `rf2-jwdi4r`).

Dedupe searched open and closed bead export/current tracker text for `ProcessBuilder`, `launch-editor timed out`, stdout/stderr, pipe buffer/deadlock, output drain, and open-in-editor process/timeout. No testbed-support match exists. Git history searches for `redirectErrorStream`, timed `waitFor`, error-stream reads, pipe-deadlock, and launch-editor timeout show no remediation on this slice. GitHub PR searches for `launch-editor timed out`, `testbed-support ProcessBuilder`, `open-in-editor stderr`, and `pipe deadlock` found no overlapping testbed-support PR. PR #3584 / `rf2-spzkgo` fixed the same Java subprocess pipe-deadlock class in the separate `implementation/test-quiet` harness; it is useful precedent, not ownership overlap.

## Finding: undrained child pipes manufacture a timeout

Expected: `launch!` classifies a child that exits 0 as success and a child that exits nonzero as a launch failure, independent of how much diagnostic output it writes. The 10-second timeout should mean the child did not exit, not that the parent stopped it from exiting.

Actual: `open_in_editor_server.clj:105-113` starts `ProcessBuilder` with separate pipes, calls timed `.waitFor` before reading either pipe, reads stderr only after exit, and never reads stdout. OS pipes are bounded. Once Node or `launch-editor` fills either pipe, its write blocks, so it cannot reach `process.exit`; the JVM waits for an exit that its own undrained pipe prevents. At lines 114-120 the artificial stall is returned as `launch-editor timed out` after ten seconds.

Executable reproduction from `tools/testbed-support` used an existing `README.md` path and temporarily rebound private `launch-shim`, so it exercised the real `launch!` / `ProcessBuilder` path without opening an editor:

- `process.stderr.write('controlled failure'); process.exit(7)` -> `{:ok false, :message "controlled failure"}` in 65 ms (control).
- `process.stderr.write('x'.repeat(1048576)); process.exit(7)` -> `{:ok false, :message "launch-editor timed out"}` in 10,017 ms.
- `process.stdout.write('x'.repeat(1048576)); process.exit(0)` -> `{:ok false, :message "launch-editor timed out"}` in 10,028 ms.

The latter child is explicitly successful yet is reported as a failure. Existing tests never execute an existing-file `launch!` child: endpoint tests redefine `launch!`, while direct launch coverage stops at missing-file rejection and pure file-spec construction. Thus all 28 JVM tests stay green while the real subprocess boundary deadlocks.

## Impact

A verbose Node warning, dependency diagnostic, editor-discovery failure, or future `launch-editor` version can turn a prompt success/failure into a guaranteed ten-second stall. The dev-http worker is occupied for that duration, the browser receives 422 and unnecessarily falls back to `editor://`, and the response lies about the cause. Repeated clicks can tie up multiple server threads. This is dev tooling rather than production runtime, so P3 is proportionate, but the external-process boundary is live and the failure was reproduced on the current Windows worktree.
design: Keep the process boundary small and explicit. Ensure every piped stream has an owner before waiting: preferably discard/inherit stdout (the endpoint does not consume it) and start one bounded stderr drain immediately, then perform the timed wait. Retain only a modest diagnostic tail so a noisy dependency cannot trade the pipe deadlock for unbounded memory. On timeout, destroy the child, wait briefly for termination, and force termination only if necessary; join/close the drain on every branch. Avoid a general subprocess framework or compatibility layer—the slice needs one correct launch primitive. The already-merged `rf2-spzkgo` concurrent-drain pattern is a local precedent, but this timeout-aware implementation should remain tailored to `launch!`.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Add a real-subprocess regression using a controlled Node shim that writes more than a plausible OS pipe capacity (at least 1 MiB) to stdout and exits 0; `launch!` returns `{:ok true}` promptly, never the timeout result.
2. Add a companion shim that writes at least 1 MiB to stderr and exits nonzero; `launch!` returns a non-timeout failure carrying a bounded useful diagnostic or the real exit code. Keep a small-stderr control assertion.
3. Make the regression bounded so reintroducing wait-before-drain fails as a test timeout rather than hanging the suite; prove the test is red against the current ordering.
4. Exercise the genuine timeout branch with a short test-configurable budget: it returns the timeout message within the bound and proves the child is no longer alive after cleanup (including a force-termination fallback where normal destroy does not complete).
5. Preserve the existing no-shell argv boundary, file/line/column/editor argument composition, missing-file-before-spawn behavior, 200/422 endpoint mapping, and POST/loopback/origin guards.
6. Run `clojure -M:test` in `tools/testbed-support` plus `npm run test:testbed-support` and the relevant browser gate from `implementation`; all remain green.

title: Pair: document the live-browser Story recipe (drive re-frame.story/* via eval-cljs)
description:
Follow-on from the rf2-3fc89f.22 ruling (B, Mike 2026-07-11): the pair (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp) is the live browser Story host; Story-MCP stays the headless same-JVM surface. The pair already owns the hardened nREPL/cljs-eval channel, so re-frame.story/* is reachable in any attached browser heap today — but the recipe is undocumented.

The recipe is verified against a running testbed once, with the transcript (or condensed form) in the doc. 3.
