title: Validate custom URL strategies before routing lifecycle use
description:
Wave-2 post-remediation correctness review of the entire `implementation/routing` surface found one distinct invalid-input defect.

SURFACE INVENTORY
- Reviewed all 59 artefact files at origin/main 1a4889609: 25 source files (`routing.cljc` plus 24 `re-frame.routing.*` namespaces), 32 test files, `deps.edn`, and `LICENSE`.
- Audited route compilation/matching/rank precedence; path/query/fragment encoding and history/hash/base-path strategies; URL ownership, listeners, registration and destruction handoff; guards, effects, replies, loaders/integrations; navigation tokens/counters and frame/epoch lifecycle; SSR/browser conditionals; public facade/tooling; invalid-input and test coverage.
- JVM gate: `clojure -M:test` => 394 tests, 1761 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors. The inventory contains 509 `deftest` forms including CLJS/conditional/stress coverage not all selected by that gate.

POST-REMEDIATION PROOF / NON-OVERLAP
- Prior bead rf2-3fc89f.11 is closed and its PR #5540 / commit 3f8d25c83 is present. `history/reconcile-url-listener!` resolves current owner+strategy, preserves an exact match, tears down/reinstalls on owner or strategy change, and treats the destroyed frame as excluded (`history.cljc:147-204`). Registration and destruction lifecycle hooks call reconciliation (`routing.cljc:388-414`). Browser tests cover incumbent destruction/successor rebind, cross-strategy handoff, owner opt-out, same-owner strategy change, and non-owner destruction (`routing_history_cljs_test.cljs:620-730`). This finding does not duplicate that remediation; it concerns validation and failure atomicity before those callbacks are invoked.
- `bd search` for `url strategy validation`, `invalid url strategy`, `missing install-listener`, and `malformed strategy` returned no issues. GitHub searches found no open PR implementing validation (repository-wide open PR list was empty during review).

DISTINCT EVIDENCE
- Spec 012 documents `:url-strategy` as a map with callable `:encode`, `:decode`, `:push!`, `:replace!`, and `:install-listener!` (`spec/012-Routing.md:79,1501-1554`).
- `url-strategy-from-config` returns every truthy config value verbatim, without checking map shape or callback callability (`strategy.cljc:340-346`). Tests explicitly pin verbatim pass-through for a partial custom map and have no malformed-value assertions (`routing_url_strategy_test.clj:148-158`).
- Browser consumers invoke keys blindly: listener installation captures `:decode` / `:install-listener!`, tears down the current listener, then calls both (`history.cljc:126-143`); route-link invokes `:encode` (`link.cljc:150-157`); navigation effects invoke `:encode` plus the selected `:push!` / `:replace!` (`nav_fx.cljc:246-258`).
- In particular, `install-listener-for-owner!` calls `teardown-current!` before calling the unvalidated replacement strategy's `:install-listener!` (`history.cljc:135-140`). A malformed hot-reload replacement therefore removes the known-good listener and only then fails.

EXPECTED VS ACTUAL
- Expected: malformed frame-level routing configuration fails at a stable authoring/preflight boundary with a canonical structured error naming the missing/non-callable strategy legs. Re-registering a URL owner with invalid config must not destroy the currently working browser listener or leave routing ownership in a silently degraded state.
- Actual: malformed maps/non-map truthy values enter the frame registry unchanged. The first consult produces a host- and call-site-specific raw nil-function/TypeError. On browser owner re-registration, reconciliation first tears down the old listener, then throws while invoking the missing callback, leaving the registered owner without a browser URL listener.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
From `implementation/routing` on current origin/main:
`clojure -M -e '(do (require (quote [re-frame.routing.strategy :as s])) (let [resolved (s/url-strategy-from-config {:url-strategy {:decode (constantly "/")}})] (println :resolved-keys (keys resolved)) (try ((:encode resolved) "/active") (catch Throwable t (println :failure (class t) (.getMessage t))))))'`
Observed: `:resolved-keys (:decode)` followed by `java.lang.NullPointerException Cannot invoke "clojure.lang.IFn.invoke(Object)"`.
Browser lifecycle repro: register a URL-bound owner with `history-url-strategy`, capture the installed popstate listener, re-register the same owner with `{:url-bound? true :url-strategy {:encode identity :decode (constantly "/")}}`; the post-registration reconciliation removes the old listener and then raises when `install-listener!` is nil.

IMPACT
A typo, partial custom adapter, or dev hot-reload intermediate value can break Back/Forward/deep-link synchronization for the sole URL owner. Failure differs by host and consult point, lacks the documented structured error contract, and the browser replacement path destructively loses previously working listener state. This is an authoring/configuration error rather than corrupt external input, so P3 is appropriate.
design:
Add one central host-aware URL-strategy validator and use it before any strategy becomes operational.

- Validate that an explicit `:url-strategy` is a map. On both hosts require callable `:encode` and `:decode`; on CLJS require callable `:push!`, `:replace!`, and `:install-listener!`. Permit extension keys and preserve the shipped JVM strategies, whose browser-only legs are reader-conditionally absent.
- Raise canonical structured `ex-info` (proposed `:rf.error/id :rf.error/invalid-url-strategy`) with frame id, config/operation context, required keys, and the missing/non-callable keys; update Spec 009 error catalogue and Spec 012 strategy contract.
- Run validation at the earliest optional-routing frame-config preflight seam. Because core cannot depend statically on routing, publish a routing late-bind validator and consult it from `frame/reg-frame` before registrar/container mutation, or introduce an equivalent generic optional-artefact preflight hook. Also validate existing registrations during routing late-load reconciliation.
- Independently make listener reconciliation failure-atomic: validate/prepare the candidate strategy before `teardown-current!`; if installation itself throws, retain or restore the previous installed listener record rather than orphaning the owner.
- Keep SSR semantics explicit: SSR does not execute browser legs, while malformed shared custom strategies still receive deterministic host-appropriate validation instead of raw call-site failures.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Explicit non-map, missing-key, and non-callable-key custom strategies fail with canonical `:rf.error/invalid-url-strategy` data identifying frame/context and bad legs; tests cover CLJ and CLJS host requirements.
2. Valid shipped strategies, `with-base-path` strategies, and complete custom strategies continue to work; extension keys remain allowed. JVM validation does not require reader-conditionally absent browser callbacks.
3. First registration with invalid strategy fails before leaving a frame registration/container, URL claim, listener, or initial-event side effect. Routing loaded after a pre-existing invalid declaration reports the same structured error deterministically.
4. Re-registering the active URL owner with an invalid strategy does not tear down or replace its existing working listener and does not dispatch an initial URL sync through the invalid strategy; a browser regression test asserts listener identity/count and teardown count.
5. `route-link`, push/replace effects, listener install/rebind, and `with-base-path` no longer expose raw nil-function/TypeError failures for malformed strategy maps; focused tests pin the structured failure boundary.
6. Spec 009 and Spec 012 document the error id, required host-specific callable legs, recovery/failure semantics, and late-load behavior; JVM routing gate and consolidated CLJS routing/browser gates pass.

title: Decide whether the machine-backed login should keep its write-only slice :status
description:
login/core.cljs's :auth.login/initialise-form seeds the login-form slice with a :status :idle field, while the :auth.login/flow machine ALSO tracks the flow state. The slice :status may be a write-only mirror of the machine state (a canonical/mirrored-login redundancy). Decide whether to keep it, derive it, or drop it.

## Context
Explicitly flagged as out of scope for the frame-init fix rf2-3fc89f.28 (that fix only ensures every Story variant seeds the slice; it did not touch the login event model). This is a broader canonical/mirrored-login design question for login/core.cljs.
notes: DECIDED 2026-07-11 (operator-delegated to Fable; dossier + Grok + Codex unanimous, all source-verified): Option (1) — DROP the slice :status entirely. Evidence: written at 3 sites only (initialise-form :idle, submit-form clean path :submitting, reset-form :idle in examples/core/login/model.cljs), read NOWHERE (no sub projects it; views answer busy/authed/locked via [:rf.machine/has-tag? :auth.login/flow ...] and :auth.login/state / :auth.login/error); the file own comment calls it a mirror; AND (Grok) the mirror is INCOMPLETE - machine reaches :error-shown/:authed/:locked-out but the slice sticks at :submitting forever, so any future reader would see a stuck lie. The flagship machine-backed example must model one-truth (docs/core/app-db.md store-facts-derive-conclusions), not violate it. IMPLEMENTATION (per Grok steps): remove :status from the initialise and reset seed maps + the assoc-in ... :status :submitting in submit-form; trim comments describing flipping/re-seeding slice :status; leave machine reads as-is; do NOT add a derived :status sub (demand bar - tags + :auth.login/state already expose flow vocabulary; the form-only recipe in build-a-form.md legitimately keeps ITS :status - different pattern, untouched); grep-confirm zero readers of [:auth :login-form :status] across examples, Story variants, and both substrate ports; smoke Story login variants + UIx/Helix ports (shared model, no port logic change expected); align any README line still implying form-recipe :status for the machine example.
close_reason: Verified-duplicate: ruling (drop write-only login-form :status slice from the machine-backed example) was ALREADY implemented on origin/main by commit bbfee0cda 'fix(examples/core): drop dead login form-slice :status mirror' (bead rf2-fai6a8, Mike Thompson 2026-07-11). That commit removed :status from both initialisers + the submit-form clean branch, trimmed the mirror comments, added NO replacement sub, aligned model+README prose, and updated the framework form-slice test (example_login_form_slice_cljs_test.cljs asserts no :status on both branches). Grep-verified ZERO readers/writers of the [:auth :login-form :status] slice path across examples/core/login (model+stories+ports UIx/Helix — they :require the shared model), Story variants, and README. Remaining :status hits are unrelated HTTP reply-envelope/401 tags, or the DIFFERENT slice-form recipe pattern (build-a-form tutorial + realworld_http) which the ruling explicitly excludes. No PR needed.

title: instant canonical form: RULED A (unparked) — canonical returns reserved tagged tuple [:rf.identity/instant <utc-ms-text>]; canonical-bytes t:/s: unchanged
description: From #5229 impl-review, verified. canonical normalizes an instant to a bare string, diverging from canonical-bytes which tags t:/s: — encode-map accepts a heterogeneous instant+string-keyed map that canonical-map rejects, falsifying the fns own docstring (implementation/core/.../identity.cljc:317). NEAR-ZERO practical severity. DECISION FOR MIKE (Conventions ruling): the obvious fix is platform-sensitive — CLJS js/Date has NO value equality (the reason the string form exists), so the canonical form of an instant needs a Conventions ruling before touching it. Low priority / trigger-watch; recorded so a future audit does not re-discover it.
design:
RULED 2026-07-08 (Mike — adopted dossier+Codex rec): KEEP PARKED as trigger-watch. Do NOT spend a ruling/dispatch now.

PROBLEM (near-zero severity, LATENT): re-frame.identity has two identity surfaces that should agree but diverge for instants — canonical (identity.cljc:317) collapses an instant to a BARE STRING (instant->utc-millis-string), while canonical-bytes/encode (identity.cljc:233) keeps kind via a t: tag (and a real string gets s:). So (canonical T) = (canonical S) but (identical-identity? T S) = false, and a heterogeneous {T :a, S :b} map is REJECTED by canonical-map (:duplicate-canonical-map-key) yet ACCEPTED by canonical-bytes. This falsifies BOTH functions docstrings (which claim the two surfaces never disagree — written around the Date-vs-Instant case, missing instant-vs-string). NEAR-ZERO severity: no live surface feeds heterogeneous instant+string map keys into identity; production consumers use canonical-bytes/identical-identity? for equality-sensitive work.

DISPOSITION: PARKED / trigger-watch (the bead parks itself). UN-PARK TRIGGER = any of: work touching identity canonicalization; an instant appearing in a real identity position (storage/work-ledger/trace/replay key); or the next audit re-finding it.
WHEN TRIGGERED, rule Option A (kind-preserving tagged canonical form): canonical returns a Conventions-BLESSED tagged EDN value for instants (NOT a bare prefixed string — that recreates the collision one level down; the shape must be collision-resistant vs user data, and canonical-bytes must treat it as the SAME instant fact), so instant-vs-string stays distinct on BOTH surfaces mirroring t:/s:. Rejected B (drop the t: tag on canonical-bytes) = weakens CEDN-1 kind fidelity that the t:/s: design intended + would break the frozen conformance fixture / Conventions "every CEDN-1 value has a type tag" contract. A needs a Conventions ruling on the tagged instant SHAPE (hot-zone spec/Conventions.md) + identity.cljc change + regression tests (heterogeneous map behaves identically on both surfaces; (canonical T) != (canonical S)).
SAFE INTERIM (anytime, no ruling needed) = Option C: docstring-only fix on identity.cljc (~lines 272-273 + 292-294) stating the present asymmetry truthfully (canonical collapses instants to UTC strings; canonical-bytes preserves kind; heterogeneous keys rejected by one surface, accepted by the other). Zero behaviour change, zero risk, stops the docstrings lying. Does NOT foreclose A. Do C if the docstring falsehood bothers you before the trigger fires; otherwise leave fully parked.
notes:
RULING (decision-agent, 2026-07-12): UNPARK NOW + Option A — canonical form of an instant is the reserved tagged tuple [:rf.identity/instant "<RFC-3339 UTC millisecond text>"], e.g. [:rf.identity/instant "2026-06-10T00:00:00.000Z"]. canonical-bytes UNCHANGED (host instant AND the tagged tuple both emit t:<text>; plain strings stay s:). This supersedes the 2026-07-08 KEEP-PARKED disposition by executing its own trigger clause.

WHY: (1) The park's un-park trigger has fired: instants sit in a real identity position — resource params flow through canonical in re-frame.resources.state/scoped-resource-key (state.cljc:594-623) before key-id, so {:at #inst "X"} and {:at "X"} alias to ONE scoped key and identical s:-based key-id, contradicting Spec 016 §Resource identity and Conventions' "type tag is part of the bytes, so ... cannot collide" guarantee. Shipped consumer path, not latent. (2) The park's platform premise is false: CLJS extends js/Date with IEquiv (.valueOf comparison) + date hashing (cljs.core r1.12.145 L1441-1462, L1073-1089), so "js/Date has no value equality" never justified the bare string. (3) The 2026-07-08 ruling pre-committed "WHEN TRIGGERED, rule Option A (kind-preserving tagged canonical form, NOT a bare prefixed string)"; this ruling fixes the remaining SHAPE detail. (4) Text payload over epoch-ms: the byte contract already pays for the UTC text spelling, one scalar spelling per canonical projection, and readability is an explicit identity goal (Conventions §disposition 5: tools retain a human-readable EDN projection). Precedent: [:rf.path/param <name>] reserved tuple.

REJECTED: keep-parked — both factual premises falsified + trigger fired. B (keep bare string, patch docstring/map behavior) — a normalized map cannot retain instant + same-looking string as two keys; leaves canonical-bytes(canonical(x)) != canonical-bytes(x) and the live resource-key alias. Drop the t: tag — violates the Conventions type-tag rule and the frozen conformance fixture. Return #inst / host Date — mutable, JVM Date vs Instant not =, host-shaped storage. [:rf.identity/instant <epoch-ms>] — two scalar spellings for one projection, forces tools to format. Custom reader tag / record — unnecessary machinery vs the reserved-tuple precedent.

NORMATIVE SEMANTICS:
1. Accept java.util.Date, java.time.Instant, js/Date as instant inputs; project immediately to the tagged tuple at epoch-millisecond precision (Instant.toEpochMilli semantics); timezone spelling is never identity. Do NOT promise raw-host-date vs #inst-literal provenance (#inst reads as host dates — recordable.cljc:53-71); state the truthful boundary rule instead.
2. canonical returns [:rf.identity/instant "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'"]; an already-tagged valid tuple is validated and returned unchanged (idempotent), never reinterpreted as a generic vector.
3. Laws, normative + tested on BOTH hosts: (= (canonical (canonical x)) (canonical x)); (= (canonical-bytes (canonical x)) (canonical-bytes x)); (not= (canonical instant) (canonical same-looking-string)); same distinctness for bytes. A heterogeneous {instant :a, string :b} map is LEGAL on both surfaces (two entries). JVM Date + Instant denoting one millisecond as two map keys still fails closed :duplicate-canonical-map-key.
4. Reserve the ENTIRE tuple grammar: add :rf.identity/* to the reserved-namespace table; under the marker, wrong arity / non-string payload / non-UTC or non-millisecond spelling / impossible date fails :rf.error/non-edn-identity with reason :invalid-canonical-instant — never falls through as a generic vector.
5. Convert host leaks (js/Date RangeError on invalid time value; JVM ArithmeticException from toEpochMilli) to :rf.error/non-edn-identity with :invalid-instant / :instant-out-of-portable-range.
6. Portable range RULED here (do not re-litigate): the four-digit-year RFC-3339 window, inclusive [0000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z .. 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z] — fixed-width yyyy, inside JS Date's +/-8.64e15 ms envelope on both hosts; outside -> :instant-out-of-portable-range. Pin in Conventions + fixtures.

IMPLEMENTATION:

title: Framework: native React DevTools inspector panel for re-frame2 (à la Redux DevTools / Apollo / MobX)
description:
## Why

React DevTools has an extension API for libraries to register a
**custom inspector panel** for their components. Apollo Client,
MobX, Redux DevTools all use it — each gets a native presence in
DevTools' Components inspector alongside the standard Props /
State / Hooks panels.

re-frame2 could do the same. The substrate has rich data that no
generic React DevTools view can surface:

- The view's registered id (post-quick-wins bead, this is the
  React displayName — but the inspector panel can show MORE)
- Subs the view currently consumes + their LIVE values from the
  sub cache
- The frame the view is running in
- Last render epoch + duration (from the trace stream)
- Schema violations attached to the view or its parent handler
- Click-to-source jumping straight to the `reg-view` definition

This would make re-frame2 a first-class React DevTools citizen
the way Redux is — operators investigating a re-frame2 app
via DevTools see substrate context inline, not just generic
React props.

Blocks-on / sibling: P2 quick-wins bead (displayName + JSX
source-coord props + Context labelling). The native inspector
builds on top of those.

## What changes — high level

A custom inspector panel registered with the React DevTools
backend API. The panel renders inside DevTools' Components
inspector right pane (alongside Props / State / Hooks), titled
"re-frame2".

For a selected reg-view'd component, the panel shows:

### Source surface
- Registered view-id (keyword)
- Source coord (file:line)
- "Open in editor" link → reuses Story's `open-in-editor` launcher

### Reactive surface
- Subs the view consumed during last render (read from sub
  cache; rf2-mrnur's dispose trace tells us the active
  derefer-set)
- Live values for each sub (via `edn-inspector/mini` for
  one-line rendering, expand-to-full inline)
- Visual indicator if any sub's value changed since last render

### Cascade surface
- Last render epoch-id + wall-clock duration
- "Show in Xray Trace" link → dispatches into the host's
  `:rf/xray` frame to focus that epoch
- Render-count since page load

### Frame surface
- Frame-id this view is in (`:rf/default` / `:rf/xray` / custom)
- Frame's preset / fx-overrides / etc. (from `rf/frame-meta`)

### Schema surface
- Any `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` events attached to
  the view's owning handler in the recent trace buffer
- Recovery posture (rolled-back / fx-skipped / etc.)

## Technical considerations

### React DevTools backend API

React DevTools is open-source; the API for libraries to
register inspector panels is in the `react-devtools-shared`
package (`reactDevtoolsAgent.addInspectorPanel(...)` or
similar — worker confirms exact API surface). Apollo's
implementation is a reference. The API is dev-only — there's
no production cost.

### Bundle isolation

The DevTools inspector code MUST live in a build path that
elides under `interop/debug-enabled? false`. The pattern
matches Xray's bundle-isolation contract (per
`npm run test:bundle-isolation`). Code lives in
`implementation/core/devtools/` or a sibling
`implementation/devtools/` artefact; nothing in production
paths `:requires` it.

### Cross-frame considerations

A view rendered under `:rf/xray` shows different data than the
same view under `:rf/default`. The inspector panel reads the
view's actual current frame (already known to the framework)
and surfaces frame-scoped data. Same view-id under two frames
shows two different sub-value sets.

### Hot-reload + identity

The inspector panel should survive `:after-load` hot-reloads of
the user's app. If the React DevTools backend tracks component
identity by displayName + position, the panel rebinds cleanly.
Worker confirms the API's reload semantics.

### Integration with existing Xray

The inspector panel's "Show in Xray Trace" link assumes the host
app has Xray installed. When Xray isn't present:
- Either degrade gracefully (link greyed out with tooltip "Xray
  not installed in this app")
- Or surface ALL the data inline in the DevTools panel without
  cross-linking

Lean: graceful degradation. The DevTools panel works
standalone; Xray is an optional cross-link surface.

## Possible scope additions (bundled or follow-on)

These naturally fold into the inspector panel work:

- **View args as named React props** (item 3 from pair-debug's
  bullet list): pretty-print CLJS view args instead of opaque
  varargs blobs. Reuses the inspector's edn rendering.
- **React Profiler integration** (item 6): tag `:rf.view/render`
  trace events with React's render-id so the operator can
  cross-reference Xray's per-cascade trace with React's profiler
  timeline.
- **Hot-reload identity preservation** (item 8): verify reg-view'd
  components preserve identity across `:after-load`. If they
  don't, fix or document.

Worker decides whether to fold into this bead or file as P4
follow-ons.

## What does NOT change

- The framework's runtime contracts — additive panel only
- Production builds — entire panel elides
- React DevTools itself — uses its existing extension API
- Xray's own surfaces — they remain the canonical heavy-data
  view; the DevTools inspector is the lighter Components-tab-
  embedded surface

## Acceptance

1. Loading a re-frame2 app with React DevTools installed shows a
   "re-frame2" subpanel in the Components inspector right pane
   when a reg-view'd component is selected.
2. Subpanel renders the source / reactive / cascade / frame /
   schema surfaces enumerated above.
3. Live values update as the underlying state mutates.
4. "Open in editor" + "Show in Xray Trace" links function (the
   latter degrades gracefully when Xray isn't installed).
5. Production builds elide the entire panel; bundle-isolation
   gate passes.
6. Worked example in `examples/<...>` demonstrates the inspector
   panel + documents the React DevTools setup required to see
   it.

## Coordination

- New code under `implementation/core/devtools/` (or a sibling
  artefact). Hot-zone consideration if it lives under core.
- Possibly spec/006 §Source-coord annotation + a new
  spec/DevTools-Integration.md normative doc.
- Pre-alpha posture: lock in to React DevTools backend API as
  the integration shape; no fallback for non-React-DevTools
  inspectors.

Per pair-debug 2026-05-27.

## Blocks-on

P2 quick-wins bead (displayName + JSX source-coord props +
Context labelling). The native inspector layers on top of those
foundations.
notes: DEFERRED (Mike, 2026-05-28): post-alpha. Native React DevTools inspector panel is a feature epic; not pre-alpha-critical and Xray already covers live inspection (app-db, trace stream, epoch scrub). Revisit after alpha.
close_reason: REJECTED (2026-07-25). Two independent findings each settle it. (1) THE PREMISE IS FACTUALLY WRONG: React DevTools ships no public API for a library to register a custom inspector panel. react-devtools-shared is internal and unpublished with no documented extension points; the feature request for exactly this (facebook/react-devtools#1086) sits in a repository ARCHIVED 2020-06-26 and never shipped; Apollo Client DevTools and Redux DevTools are STANDALONE browser extensions with their own top-level tabs, not panels inside React DevTools; the addInspector/setupDevtoolsPlugin custom-inspector API the bead describes is VUE's, which is almost certainly where the premise came from. What React documents for libraries is only displayName, Context displayName and useDebugValue. So the bead is not expensive — as specified it is NOT BUILDABLE; the nearest buildable substitute is shipping and maintaining a re-frame2 browser extension (store listings, MV3 churn, a message-passing bridge), a materially larger commitment yielding a third surface rather than a panel. (2) ALREADY SERVED: all six requested surfaces (view-id, subs consumed with live values, owning frame, last render epoch, schema violations, click-to-source) are already rendered by Xray's Views tab (Dynamic tab 3 of 9, spec tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md sec 3 - note 012-Views.md is superseded) plus the Epoch panel, and served to agents by the Tool-Pair MCP (list-subscriptions --include-values, read-sub, read-view-dependencies, explain-render, handler-meta, read-ui). The one gap is a per-view wall-clock duration column, which is a one-column Xray bead, not a reason for a second front-end. THE CHEAP HALF ALREADY SHIPPED under rf2-fa4ly: displayName, Context labelling (rf2-frame / rf2-sub-overrides) and data-rf2-source-coord are on main and work in React DevTools today. RESIDUAL CRUMB if ever wanted (not filed): useDebugValue on Freehand's shell/ViewCell hooks to put view-id and consumed-sub set into the standard Hooks pane at near-zero cost, plus verify Freehand react.cljs displayName writes elide in production (it carries no goog.DEBUG gate, unlike re-frame.ui/runtime.cljs). IF RE-PROPOSED: must be re-filed as 'ship a re-frame2 browser DevTools extension' with the extension's real cost stated, and sequenced AFTER rf2-drpa3.113 (browser-mountable compiled views) and after the Xray/MCP re-point off re-frame.ui.tool onto Freehand - otherwise it is built against a data plane EP-0036 deletes at F6e (rf2-drpa3.57).

title: Audit local-atom-as-scratch-accumulator usage across the codebase; refactor to functional shape where idiomatic
description:
Mike directive 2026-05-11: prefer functional programming over imperative when given the choice; efficiency matters where it's measurable.

Mike spotted an instance at implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:79 (pattern-shape) — three atoms (i, depth, seen) used as scratch accumulators inside a loop. Imperative-flavour code that would read more idiomatically as loop/recur threading state through.

Likely a class issue, not a one-off. Initial grep found 52 files matching the broad pattern (let [... (atom ...) ...] ...) but most are legitimate uses (registry atoms, test fixtures, async queues, anything where state persists or crosses thread boundaries). The smell is specifically: **local atoms used as scratch accumulators inside a tight loop, never escaping the function, where loop/recur or reduce/transducers would express the same algorithm functionally**.

## Audit scope

For each of the 52 files:
- Identify each (atom ...) call site at top of let binding.
- Classify:
  - LEGITIMATE: state genuinely needs to persist beyond the function (registry, fixture, queue), cross a boundary (async, thread), be observable to watchers, or back a public reactive API.
  - SCRATCH-SMELL: local accumulator inside a tight loop or recursive walk, never escapes, no concurrency.
  - HOT-PATH-EFFICIENCY: scratch-shape but materially faster than the functional alternative on a measurable hot path (worth keeping with a one-line rationale comment).

For each SCRATCH-SMELL site, propose a refactor (typically loop/recur threading the accumulator state, or a reduce/reduce-kv form).

## Principle (Mike's directive 2026-05-11)

Prefer functional over imperative. Trade-offs to weigh:
- **Readability**: functional is usually clearer. Win.
- **Aliasing safety**: functional is safer (immutable bindings can't be aliased). Win.
- **Performance**: imperative atom-mutate is sometimes faster on tight loops, but only when the loop is genuinely hot. For 99% of code paths, the difference is invisible.
- **Pre-release**: no back-compat concerns; refactor freely.

Rule: prefer functional unless there's measurable evidence the imperative form is needed for performance. If kept imperative for efficiency reasons, leave a rationale comment.

## Concrete starter

routing.cljc:79 (pattern-shape) — refactor to loop/recur threading [i depth seen]. ~15-line edit.

## Output

- findings/imperative-atoms-audit.md — per-file classification + refactor proposals.
- A bd bead per SCRATCH-SMELL site (or one bead per file, depending on volume).

## Dispatchability

Direction-set. Background agent can do the audit. The refactor work splits into per-bead PRs after Mike reviews the audit findings. Could batch into a single sweep PR if the volume is manageable.

2026-05-11: Cross-link to pre-existing Codex-filed specific-instance beads. Three sites already surfaced + filed by Codex 2026-05-10:
- rf2-w0am: topo-sort in flows.cljc:65
- rf2-lckc: routing.cljc pattern-shape:79 + compile-pattern:225 + collect-param-names-in-group:404 + route-url:435
- rf2-d6a2: http_managed.cljc json-read*:291

Audit scope: SKIP these three; cover the rest of the 52 files matching the broad pattern. Output findings doc + file follow-up beads ONLY for sites not already covered by rf2-w0am/lckc/d6a2.
2026-05-11: Audit complete. findings/imperative-atoms-audit.md (~2700 words). Filed 3 follow-up beads for SCRATCH-SMELL sites in production source: rf2-8jmn (router.cljc:284 last-event-a — drain hot path), rf2-9hxy (ssr.cljc:584 replace-header seen?), rf2-2fny (epoch.cljc:578 missing-references). Together with the three Codex-filed beads (rf2-w0am, rf2-lckc, rf2-d6a2) the roadmap covers all SCRATCH-SMELL sites in re-frame2: ~6 specific sites across 5 files. No HOT-PATH-EFFICIENCY sites found — every imperative-atom site has a functional alternative at parity. Test files all use atoms as legitimate assertion fixtures; not flagged. Two borderline test-infra sites (conformance_test.clj:188 + :885) noted in the doc but not filed, per Mike's test-bias guidance.

Audit ran 2026-05-11; all six follow-up refactors are on main and verified as ancestors of origin/main: 3f05671a32 (flows topo-sort), 60dfec6eb8 (routing pattern walkers), bca7778ec6 (http json-read), 1915ff95ef (router drain), 79d67cb694 (ssr replace-header), 95b446d694 (epoch missing-references). The last residual site was cleared 2026-07-25 by 4e3183e0e1 (#6898, rf2-b8goi): conformance.cljc collect-cofx-keys now walks the step tree via tree-seq + transducer. The programme has zero residue. It looked un-run for two reasons: findings/imperative-atoms-audit.md lived under gitignored ai/ (never tracked, now gone from disk and unrecoverable) and the six follow-up beads were erased from the tracker by a .beads export time-travel incident. Lesson: findings meant to survive go in a tracked spec tree, never under gitignored ai/.

title: Independent research + refinement of re-frame-2-story SOTA features (compares vs rf2-m6tu)
description:
Follow-up to rf2-m6tu. Different framing: 'what features would make re-frame-2-story state-of-the-art?' rather than 'what should it minimally support?'

Two-phase work for one agent:

## Phase 1 — Independent research (no peeking at rf2-m6tu)

Agent does its own survey of component-development tools focused on the SOTA question:
- What's the highest-bar capability set? Not 'minimum viable.'
- Which tools (Storybook + non-Storybook) ship features that feel best-in-class?
- Cross-tool: what's been borrowed, refined, surpassed?
- Storybook addons (https://storybook.js.org/addons) — which are state-of-the-art? a11y? play / interactions / test? composition? designs? viewport with breakpoints? args + controls type-generation?
- Beyond Storybook: Histoire's vue-specific magic, Ladle's perf claims, React Cosmos's fixture model, Bit's component-as-package, Lookbook's Rails-flavoured ergonomics.
- The answer should reach for SOTA, not the average.

Agent writes its independent answer to a scratch file: findings/re-frame-2-story-sota-draft.md (or holds in agent memory).

## Phase 2 — Comparison + refinement

After own answer is written:
- Read findings/re-frame-2-story-feature-set.md (the rf2-m6tu output).
- Compare:
  - Where do they agree? (Confidence: both reached the same conclusion independently.)
  - Where does rf2-m6tu under-claim vs SOTA? (Add to refined doc.)
  - Where does rf2-m6tu over-claim vs realistic? (Question.)
  - Where does the independent SOTA framing surface features rf2-m6tu missed entirely?
- Refine the rf2-m6tu document in place: findings/re-frame-2-story-feature-set.md gets the synthesis.
- Drop the scratch draft after merging if used.

The refined doc should:
- Carry forward rf2-m6tu's organisation (don't restructure for its own sake).
- Add SOTA features the original missed.
- Surface tensions where SOTA-pursuit conflicts with re-frame2's ethos (e.g. 'Storybook composition is SOTA but conflicts with our spec-first / single-source-of-truth ethos — recommend skip').
- Preserve attribution: 'Refined 2026-MM-DD against independent SOTA research; the following sections were strengthened: ...'

## Why two-phase

Pre-loading the agent with rf2-m6tu's findings biases the research. Mike wants the independent eyes first — different agent, different framing prompt, no shared context — to surface SOTA features the original missed.

Blocked-by rf2-m6tu (can't compare to a doc that doesn't exist yet).

title: Interactive playground / tutorial for re-frame2 (inspired by Svelte's tutorial) — viable with self-hosted ClojureScript?
description:
Mike (2026-05-10): Svelte's tutorial at https://svelte.dev/tutorial is a brilliant interactive learning experience — edit code on the left, see live output on the right, compiled in the browser. Would love to create something like that for re-frame2.

## The question

Is self-hosted ClojureScript complete enough to power this?

## Background — what's needed

A Svelte-tutorial-like experience needs:
- In-browser code editing (Monaco / CodeMirror).
- In-browser compilation of user-edited code.
- Live execution into a sandboxed re-frame2 runtime.
- Tutorial step navigation with progressive concept reveal.

## Options — evaluate

### A. Self-hosted ClojureScript (cljs.js bootstrap)

CLJS can compile itself in-browser via cljs.js. Used by Klipse, Lambda Island, etc.

Open questions to research:
- Does Reagent work under self-hosted CLJS today? (Klipse demos suggest yes.)
- Does re-frame2's macro layer (reg-event-fx, reg-machine, reg-view, source-coord stamping) survive self-hosted bootstrap?
- Bundle size of cljs.js + Reagent + re-frame2 — is it acceptable for a tutorial site? (Likely 1-3MB minified.)
- First-compile latency — typical 'hello world' compile time in self-hosted CLJS is sub-second; complex deps slower.
- Macro packaging — re-frame2's macros need to ship as analyser metadata (cljs.analyzer) for self-hosted to expand them.
- Does the macro-rich code re-frame2 emits (reg-machine source-coord stamping, reg-view source-coord stamping) introspect okay under self-hosted?

### B. Klipse

Pre-built self-hosted CLJS playground. Mature. Used by lambdaisland.com and others. Could be embedded.

Open questions:
- Does Klipse handle re-frame2's adapter init (rf/init! adapter)?
- Per-step state isolation — Klipse cells share global state by default; may need adaptation.

### C. Pre-compiled snippets per step

Each tutorial step is a separately-compiled bundle. User clicks 'Next', the right-pane swaps to the next pre-compiled bundle. No in-browser compilation.

Pros: no self-hosted CLJS dep; bundle-per-step is small.
Cons: user can't edit code, defeating the Svelte-tutorial inspiration.

### D. Hybrid — pre-compiled lessons + Klipse for the user-edits-code part

Lesson narrative + hard-coded examples are pre-compiled; the 'try it' boxes are Klipse-powered. Best of both.

### E. Squint (CLJS-flavour to native JS)

https://github.com/squint-cljs/squint — fast in-browser compile. But: not full ClojureScript (subset). Macros work differently. Re-frame2's macro-heavy registration would likely need adaptation. Worth surveying.

## Likely answer

Self-hosted CLJS is viable but slow + large for a polished tutorial. A hybrid (lessons pre-compiled, Klipse for try-it boxes) is the pragmatic shape. Worth a research pass to confirm Reagent + re-frame2's macros work under self-hosted before investing.

## Disposition

P3 — post-beta. Outreach / DX investment, not pre-1.0 blocker. But the answer to 'self-hosted CLJS works?' affects what tooling we can ship in the guide chapters too (interactive snippets in docs/guide/).

## Recommended next step

A small spike: build one tutorial step ('your first counter') using self-hosted CLJS or Klipse, see if it works end-to-end. ~1 day of investigation. File as a separate bead when ready to spike.

title: CLJS reference: capture handler source-as-data on registration (dev-only)
description:
Mike's observation during the revertibility / atomification iteration: ClojureScript's macro story makes it natural for reg-* macros to capture the handler body as quoted-form data alongside the live fn value. The fn isn't serialisable; the source is.

Distinguish from source coords (already captured: :ns/:line/:file via existing macros). Source-as-data is the full quoted form of the handler body, attached as :rf/source on the registration entry.

Use cases (dev-only):
- AI introspection / explanation: AI reads handler source directly from the frame snapshot, no file-system access required.
- Pair-improver retrospective analysis: tool has handler source as input material for suggestions.
- Cross-process debugging snapshots: bug report includes frame value with handler source attached; dev loads snapshot complete with exact handlers, even after local source drift.
- Time-travel that survives hot-reload: snapshot remembers what each handler was at the moment the event fired.
- Auto-generated documentation: walk the registry, render docstrings + source.
- Conformance fixtures self-contained (overkill given fixtures-by-id, but possible).

Use cases that don't need source-as-data (work via plain serialisation already):
- SSR hydration (already specced).
- Persistence (localStorage / IndexedDB / backend).
- Bug reports (data only).
- Cross-tab sharing.
- Time-travel within a session.
- Test fixtures captured from real runs.

Cost / risks:
- Build size — strict dev-only.
- IP exposure — config flag to strip source before transmitting snapshots remotely.
- Deserialisation: source-as-data is for inspection; the live fn is what runs. Document carefully.

Where it fits in the spec:
- Pattern level: 'registrations are values' is already the spirit of the registry-in-app-db design.
- CLJS reference: dev-build macros attach :rf/source; production-build macros omit it (compile-time elide). Document in 009 §Instrumentation alongside source-coords.
- Conventions.md: reserve :rf/source as a metadata key (dev-only).
- Host-profile matrix: flag as CLJS-specific affordance other hosts may not match cheaply.

Action items (deferred):
1. Spec the macro extension for :rf/source capture.
2. Add :rf/source to the reserved metadata-keys list in Conventions.md.
3. Document compile-time elision in production builds (parallel to existing trace elision).
4. Spec the snapshot-strip mechanism for source before transmission.
5. Update 009 §Instrumentation with the dev-mode capture story.
6. AI-Audit: revisit AI-introspection rows once source-as-data is available.

Status: deferred — explore when dev-mode tooling sections of 009 are firmed up, and when the AI-introspection / pair-improver story is being concretised. Not blocking any v1 lock.
design:
SHIPPED MECHANISM (reg-event, dev-only)
compile-time pr-str of &form -> bound through the source-coords/*pending-form-source* dynamic var -> merged into registry metadata by the registrar. Two elision layers, both gated on interop/debug-enabled?: the macro emits (if interop/debug-enabled? <pr-str> nil), and the registrar gates the merge again. implementation/scripts/check-elision.cjs pins the absence in the release bundle by asserting on the rf.handler/source keyword plus a captured-form sentinel.

Key pieces:
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_macros.cljc:291-336 (defreg-event-macro)
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc (*pending-form-source*, already a GENERIC dynamic var)
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:871-896,976-1040 (private merge-form-source; register-event!)
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_machines.cljc:93-132 (machine guard/action source derived from the enclosing machine spec, not duplicated onto registrar rows)

DESIGN FOR THE DEFERRED WIDENING (do not build until a named consumer exists — see notes for the trigger)
Widening to the other fourteen registrars rides existing machinery; no new machinery is needed.
1. *pending-form-source* in source_coords.cljc is already generic. Nothing to change.
2. The only event-specific piece is the private merge-form-source in events.cljc. Move it to the shared registrar/register! chokepoint, exactly where source-coords/merge-coords already sits at each registrar.
3. With 2 done, the defreg-macro / defreg-event-macro split collapses into ONE macro. The fourteen coordinate-only call sites in implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc then get the slot for free: reg-sub, reg-fx, reg-cofx, reg-interceptor, reg-flow, reg-route, reg-resource, reg-mutation, reg-resource-scope, reg-app-schema, reg-app-schemas, reg-error-projector, reg-head, reg-http-interceptor.
4. Elision story is IDENTICAL — same (if interop/debug-enabled? <pr-str> nil) macro gate plus the same registrar-side gate. check-elision.cjs extends by adding strings to its assertion list.
5. Delete or invert implementation/core/test/re_frame/handler_source_test.clj:127-136, which currently asserts reg-sub does NOT carry the slot.

COSTS OF THAT WIDENING (real but modest)
- More dev-bundle bytes. A reg-sub-heavy app has many more subs than events, so this is the dominant term, not a rounding error.
- Hot-zone tax: spec/009-Instrumentation.md and spec/Conventions.md are both sequential-lane files, so a widening PR cannot run parallel with anything else touching them.
- A wider elision-probe surface to keep honest.
notes:
RULING 2026-07-25 05:57 AUSEST — CLOSED AS DELIVERED (dossier fold-in from ai/decisions/rf2-qys.handler-source-as-data.md, now deleted; investigated read-only at e80786e007).

SHORT VERSION: this bead shipped in May 2026 under a different key name than it proposed, and nobody came back to close it. Grep-driven triage kept looking for :rf/source, finding nothing, and re-deferring. The release condition ("when 009 dev-mode tooling is firm and the AI-introspection / pair-improver story is concretised") expired in May.

== WHAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED ==
- Key is :rf.handler/source, NOT the :rf/source this bead proposed. It landed under the :rf.handler/* sub-namespace rather than colonising the single-root :rf/* set. THIS IS THE REASON THE BEAD LOOKED UNIMPLEMENTED — record it so the next grep-driven triage does not reopen this.
- Value is a STRING, not a quoted form: pr-str of the whole user-written form, stamped at macro-expansion time. Deliberate — a string survives the EDN wire to a tool without the reader needing to be safe against arbitrary data-reader tags, and every documented reg-event shape round-trips without special-casing.
- Coverage is reg-event only (the single defreg-event-macro call site), plus machine guard/action source derived from the enclosing machine spec rather than duplicated onto registrar rows.
- Dev-only, two-layer elision: the macro and the registrar each gate on interop/debug-enabled?. Under :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false the slot is absent and the source bytes are not in the bundle at all. JVM is always-on.

A dev-build registration entry therefore carries: :rf/id, :doc, :ns, :file, :line, :column, :interceptors, :handler-fn, and :rf.handler/source (the pr-str of the whole reg-event form).

== PROVENANCE (verified against git log; the two originating bead ids have since been GC-ed out of the tracker, the commits have not) ==

== FILE:LINE EVIDENCE ==
Implementation:
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_macros.cljc:291-336 — defreg-event-macro takes pr-str of the complete &form and binds it through source-coords/*pending-form-source*
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc — *pending-form-source* dynamic var (already generic, not event-specific)
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:871-896,976-1040 — private merge-form-source; register-event! merges the slot into registry metadata
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_machines.cljc:93-132 — handler-meta derives machine guard/action source from the enclosing machine spec
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc — the fourteen coordinate-only defreg-macro call sites (reg-sub, reg-fx, reg-cofx, reg-interceptor, reg-flow, reg-route, reg-resource, reg-mutation, reg-resource-scope, reg-app-schema, reg-app-schemas, reg-error-projector, reg-head, reg-http-interceptor)
Spec (all normative, all settled):
- spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1877-1902 — the :rf.handler/source section: capture semantics, scope, consumer access, user-override rule, CLJS two-layer elision, JVM always-on, mechanism (compile-time pr-str + dynamic-var thread + registrar merge)
- spec/001-Registration.md:214-229 — source-coordinate capture + registration-metadata elision classification
- spec/Conventions.md:499-503 — the reserved-key row, including the normative rule "Never lands in app-db / runtime-db / a frame-state snapshot — it lives only on registry meta"
Tests:
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/handler_source_test.clj (including :127-136, which explicitly proves reg-sub does NOT acquire the slot)
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/handler_source_cljs_test.cljs
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/machine_handler_meta_test.clj
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/elision_probe.cljs
- implementation/machines/test/re_frame/handler_source_egress_strip_cljs_test.cljc:93-132
- implementation/scripts/check-elision.cjs — the release verifier
Consumers:
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:3887-4024 — the Epoch panel event-handler source block reads (:rf.handler/source (rf/handler-meta :event id)). This is the named consumer that scoped the feature.
- tools/xray Machine Inspector focused-transition lens
- skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:732-761 — registrar-describe drops the live :handler-fn and passes every other key through, so the pair MCP gets the slot BY PASSTHROUGH
- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs:244-335 — returns the remaining map with no source-key whitelist

== MEASURED VERIFICATION (fresh runs during the dossier investigation) ==
- npm run test:elision passed: all 60 dev-only sentinels ABSENT from the production bundle, all 60 PRESENT in the control bundle
- focused JVM capture/machine tests: 18 tests / 76 assertions passing
- frame-state egress boundary tests: 2 tests / 9 assertions passing

== THE SIX ORIGINAL ACTION ITEMS ==
1. Spec the macro extension — DONE (009 section; 001 source-coordinate capture)
2. Reserve the key in Conventions.md — DONE (full row, as :rf.handler/source)
3. Compile-time elision in production builds — DONE (001 elision classification + check-elision.cjs probe pinning the absence)
4. Snapshot-strip mechanism before transmission — DONE BY A STRONGER ROUTE, see below
5. Update 009 with the dev-mode capture story — DONE (same section)
6. AI-Audit: revisit AI-introspection rows — NOT DONE. spec/AI-Audit.md has zero mention of source-as-data (verified by grep, 2026-07-25). Rolled into the follow-up bead.

== THE IP-EXPOSURE CONCERN, RESOLVED STRUCTURALLY (action item 4) ==
The bead asked for a config flag to strip source before transmitting snapshots. The design went further and made the leak structurally impossible instead of strippable. Source-as-data lives ONLY on registry metadata; it never enters a frame durable state, and frame state is what actually travels off-box (SSR hydration, epoch/time-travel, Xray and pair-MCP snapshot, bug-report captures). handler_source_egress_strip_cljs_test.cljc deep-walks (rf/frame-state-value fid) after starting a machine and asserts none of :rf.handler/source, :source-code, :source-coords appears at any depth.

The one surface where a spec genuinely does travel off-box is the machines-viz share URL, and it strips explicitly: tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/share.cljs recursively drops :source-coords and :source-code, with comments calling out that local-filesystem coords reveal usernames and directory structure.

Residual exposure judged ACCEPTABLE: an agent running handler-meta against a colleague dev build sees that handler source — but that same agent can already run eval-cljs (default-ON per rf2-a0z0h) against the same runtime, so the marginal exposure over the existing surface is nil.

== TWO LIMITS OF THE SHIPPED CONTRACT — record accurately, they were MOTIVATING IDEAS ON THIS BEAD THAT DID NOT SHIP ==
The value lives on the CURRENT registry entry, not in an epoch or a frame snapshot. Xray performs a live handler-meta lookup when rendering an old epoch. Therefore:
(a) It does NOT preserve "the exact handler that ran" across a later hot reload.
(b) A standalone frame snapshot does NOT carry source for cross-process debugging.
Both were listed as use cases in this bead description. Neither is a property of the implemented contract. Historical source pinning would need its own privacy, size, retention and egress design and MUST NOT be smuggled into this completed registration feature. No consumer asks for it today; do not file it speculatively.

== WIDENING TO THE OTHER FOURTEEN REGISTRARS — REJECTED FOR NOW, WITH A NAMED TRIGGER ==
Ruled NOT to file a widening bead. A public surface here ships when a named consumer needs it. That is exactly how the May scope was chosen: reg-event shipped because the Xray Epoch panel needed it; the other fourteen registrars did not ship because nothing needed them. As of 2026-07-25 nothing has changed — no tool in tools/, no skill in skills/, and no open bead is blocked on reading a reg-sub body off a running runtime. Widening now would build a surface ahead of its consumer.

THE TRIGGER TO REOPEN THIS (a trigger that names a consumer, since this bead original vague trigger is precisely what aged badly): a specific tool that demonstrably cannot complete a real workflow using source coordinates plus file access, and therefore needs a particular NON-EVENT registration body over the runtime wire. When that tool exists, file the widening then. The design for how to do it is on this bead --design field.

== WHY THE "AN AI HAS FILESYSTEM ACCESS ANYWAY" REJECTION ONLY HALF-LANDS ==
The bead headline claim was "no file-system access required," and in this repo that constraint mostly does not bind: skills/re-frame2-improver is declared with allowed-tools [Read, Edit, Grep, Glob] and works entirely from disk, and the pair MCP deliberately hands agents vscode:// / cursor:// links via tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/source_uri.cljs (:rf.mcp/source-uri) precisely because it assumes an editor is right there. But it DOES bind in the two cases Xray actually exercises: reading what a handler was at the moment an epoch fired after source has drifted under hot reload, and reading a handler in a runtime the reader has no checkout of. Narrow, genuine, and reg-event coverage is the right size for it.

== THE ONE REAL RESIDUAL DEFECT ==
The pair MCP — the surface an AI actually drives — returns :rf.handler/source silently but does not advertise it. Verified 2026-07-25: zero occurrences of the key anywhere under tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/. The handler-meta tool descriptor and tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md only promise source coordinates and generic "custom slots". An agent therefore reaches for the filesystem by reflex instead of reading what it already has. That is a discoverability gap, not a capability gap, and it is the whole of the remaining work. Filed as a documentation follow-up (see the linked bead) together with the missing AI-Audit.md rows.
FOLLOW-UP FILED: rf2-1tyxh (P3) — advertise :rf.handler/source on the pair-MCP handler-meta descriptor + spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md, and add the source-as-data rows to spec/AI-Audit.md (original action item 6). That is the entire residual of this bead. No implementation, widening, or snapshot-strip work remains here.

Widening to the other fourteen registrars and historical source pinning are separate demand-gated work, deliberately not filed — see notes for the named trigger. title: The shipped RealWorld example's :parent branch is never navigated to by any test
description:
Found by the EP-0037 R6 integrated-proof pass (rf2-kqxe6.10) while mapping conformance rows to lanes.

examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/routing.cljs is the one shipped example that exercises the EP-0037 branch-plan surface: :realworld.profile/favorites declares BOTH :parent :realworld.profile/show AND its own :resources, so activating it should compose the parent's shell reads with the leaf's.

Nothing ever navigates there. implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs (~28 deftests) drives the example's production source chain, but greps for 'favorites' hit only mutation payload fields; the only profile navigation in the suite is {:to :realworld.profile/show} (around lines 713 and 1220). So the example's :parent composition and partial-activation path are unexercised.

Why it is worth a small bead rather than nothing: the framework claim itself is now covered directly — rf2-kqxe6.10 added implementation/resources/test/re_frame/ep0037_r6_integrated_proof_cljs_test.cljc, which proves branch composition, partial revalidation and owner handoff against a purpose-built exercise app. What is NOT covered is this EXAMPLE's own route table, and an example is what users copy. A broken :parent link or a mis-declared leaf :resources here would ship silently.

Small and bounded: one navigation to :realworld.profile/favorites in the existing suite, asserting the parent shell read and the leaf read are both ensured and that a sibling move keeps the shell read. Do NOT add a Playwright spec (examples are test-free, rf2-8cevm) and do not grow the example.
acceptance_criteria: 1. re-frame.realworld-resources-cljs-test navigates to :realworld.profile/favorites and asserts both the parent-contributed and leaf-declared resource identities are ensured. 2. A move between the profile's sibling tabs asserts the parent read is kept (generation unchanged). 3. No new spec.cjs anywhere; the example itself is unchanged. 4. npm run test:cljs green.

title: 004D: compiled-tier enumerability claim for host-React escapes is untrue in Freehand
description:
Surfaced by the rf2-4gnrs ruling dossier (2026-07-25, ruled: retire v/raw). spec/004D:1407-1424 argues that raw widens the head-reachability surface but stays ENUMERABLE - "every site declares the :raw capability and is recorded in the manifest, so the set of such escapes is finite and listable". In Freehand that claim is already untrue: a runtime React element reaches React through an ordinary :expr child position with no capability bit recorded (react.cljs:889-894, the pass-through arm sits outside the walk? gate so it serves the compiled child seam too). Publishing v/raw would NOT buy the property back, because the unwrapped route stays open beside it.

DECIDE: is the enumerability property wanted at all for host-React escapes? If yes, it needs its own fresh design (e.g. manifest recording for element pass-through sites) - not a revival of the retired child+prop raw coupling (see rf2-4gnrs reconsideration trigger). If no, the 004D passage gets corrected or retired with the F6c donor-material cut (004D:1243, :1407-1424 are donor ui/raw migration text).

Precision note: the interpreted pass-through gate is React.isValidElement - it accepts React ELEMENTS, not all React NODES (portals/arrays are nodes, not elements). Any text stating the current capability must say "React element pass-through".

title: B5's :mixed release shape is not byte-matched to the matched pair
description:
Surfaced while discharging rf2-x4jda R1 (PR #6909).

Acceptance #1 of rf2-x4jda asks for THREE matched :browser release builds
differing only in lowering. R1 delivered TWO: :freehand-release-interpreted and
:freehand-release-compiled are now one source in two states, censused on every
run, and the published delta is taken over those two alone.

The third, :freehand-release (the MIXED shape), is NOT byte-matched to them. It
is built from re-frame.freehand.release-app, which has its own view names
(counter / counter-compiled against counter-a / counter-b), its own registered
ids, its own root DOM id and a ~1,486-byte namespace docstring that ships three
times. Its bytes therefore sit between the pair's by structure, not by
construction: reading interpreted < mixed < compiled as a lowering series is not
warranted.

R1 made the claim honest rather than making the artefact match -
b5/matched-bundle-paths now names :mixed as the SHIPPED-COST artefact, measured
for context, with no delta taken against it. That is defensible: the mixed
bundle's job is to be a real small app whose absolute cost is the headline
figure, and the delta only ever needed two arms.

MAYOR DECISION: either accept the two-arm reading and amend acceptance #1, or
fold release-app into the matched shape as a third arm. The second is not free:
release-app is named by check-freehand-reachability.cjs and
check-freehand-evidence-elision.cjs (both hard-code the sentinel
re-frame.freehand.release-app/bump), by b5_reachability_control_app.cljs, and by
implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, which pins its path. A worker
was fenced out of the last two at the time of filing.
notes:
Filed by the rf2-x4jda R1 worker (PR #6909), so the gap between acceptance #1 and what R1 shipped is on the record rather than silently redefined.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6909 FOLLOW-THROUGH — this existing Bead remains the exact owner for the third-arm/matched-language decision. Include one bounded stale authority in its eventual resolution: .github/workflows/freehand-bench.yml:224-230 still calls the three shapes matched, says all three vary only lowering, labels the step "Build the three matched release bundles", and says the pair still ships a namespace-docstring confound. Current truth is two source-censused arms plus one separately-shaped :mixed shipped-cost artefact, and #6909 removed namespace docstrings from the pair. Reconcile those comments/step wording with whichever mayor decision this Bead takes; no new workflow or checker.
close_reason: Resolved by taking D021's own wording: the B5 row asks for 'representative interpreted, compiled, and mixed production bundles' plus a per-promoted-view delta — REPRESENTATIVE, not matched. A delta needs two arms held still against each other and never needed three, so acceptance #1 of rf2-x4jda ('three matched ... same entry app') was a bead-local restatement stricter than the document it cites, and is AMENDED to: two matched arms carry the delta, :freehand-release is the representative mixed shipped-cost artefact and is deliberately not byte-matched. the two shapes the rubric most explicitly protects.

SITE CLASSIFICATIONS

1. nrepl.cljs:477  `frames*`  ->  LEGITIMATE (swap!-inner-value extraction)
   The textbook idiom named in the rubric. The atomic `swap!` on `conn-atom`
   concatenates the chunk onto the framing buffer AND decodes it in one CAS —
   the docstring is explicit that splitting the two opens a double-decode
   window — so the decoded frames can only reach the outer scope through a
   side cell. Removing it would require reintroducing exactly the race the
   single-swap design closes.

2. nrepl.cljs:683  `state`  ->  LEGITIMATE (async accumulator)
   Per-op nREPL response accumulator. Mutated from the `on-frame` socket
   callback across an unbounded number of asynchronously-arriving frames
   (`:value`/`:out`/`:err`/`:ex`/`:status`), and read as `@state` to resolve
   the outer Promise only once a `"done"` status lands. Also raced against a
   `js/setTimeout` deadline callback. Nothing local about it.

3. shadow_discovery.cljs:128  `settled?`  ->  LEGITIMATE (once-only latch)

   settle paths: non-200 reject, multi-chunk body `end` resolve, request
   `error`, and the bounded `setTimeout` destroy+reject. It exists to make
   double-settle impossible on a Promise; that is a concurrency guard, not an
   accumulator.

4. subscribe.cljs:546  `terminated?`  ->  LEGITIMATE (idempotence latch)
   `compare-and-set!` first-wins guard on `terminate`. The comment names the
   real double-fire case (abuse-detected firing the same tick the max-events
   cap trips), which would otherwise release the resource-controls stream slot
   twice and double-resolve the outer `tools/call` Promise. Closed over by
   both `terminate` and `poll` for the stream's whole lifetime.

5. subscribe.cljs:554  `drain-errors`  ->  LEGITIMATE (async counter)
   Consecutive-rejected-drain counter (rf2-ajhwbm). `reset!` to 0 inside the
   drain `.then` (line 613) and `swap! inc` inside the drain `.catch` (line
   687) — both async continuations of a long-lived, self-rescheduling poll
   loop. Deliberately kept OUT of the shared `state` map because that atom is
   session-visible bookkeeping surfaced on the final summary; the code already
   documents the separation. It spans poll cycles, so no loop/recur applies.

4. build.cljc:480 `updated` — LEGITIMATE (swap!-inner-value extraction). Irreducible: the key `k` it writes under is computed INSIDE the swap! fn from the compiler-state (`(if (contains? compiler-state scratch-key) scratch-key repl-overlay-key)`), so the caller cannot address the inner slice on swap!'s return without duplicating that branch. 5-7. build.cljc:502, :510, :519 `updated` — LEGITIMATE (swap!-inner-value extraction). See CONSIDERED-AND-DECLINED note below.

8. build.cljc:546 `outcome` — LEGITIMATE, irreducible. Extracts the conflict DECISION, which never enters the container, so swap!'s return cannot carry it. Already carries its call-local rationale comment.

9. build.cljc:658 `outcome` — LEGITIMATE, irreducible. Same shape as :546 in `contribute-element-checked!`.

10. harvest.clj:198 `harvested` — NOT A LOCAL ATOM. `defonce ^:private` top-level per-build harvest cache with docstring + `reset-harvested!` test seam. Grep false positive.

CONSIDERED AND DECLINED (recorded so it is not rediscovered as "a missed refactor"):
For :502/:510/:519 only — three byte-identical blocks over the plain `state` atom — the extraction cell is technically redundant: `(swap! state update build-id f)` returns the whole new state map, so `(get _ build-id)` yields the same slice, and that form also drops a `reset!` from inside a `swap!` fn (the documented no-side-effects-in-swap! caution; correct here only because last-retry-wins).   -        ast       (analyze (assoc e :sites sub-sites :hooks-region? false) form)
  +  (let [sub-sites (atom {:events [] :subs [] :htmls [] :frame-ops [] :slots []})

None is a local scratch accumulator. The bead's 10 are exactly the `let`-bound atoms in the tree.

title: Remove the remaining Freehand :redef suppression by renaming the local Box fixture
description:
Follow-on from PR #6807, which removed the one known :redef in the Freehand artefact.

implementation/shadow-cljs.edn's :node-test-freehand build carries `:compiler-options {:warnings {:redef false}}` — it silences the whole :redef CLASS. The only redefinition anyone had identified in Freehand was fingerprint.cljc's private -write shadowing cljs.core/-write, and that is now renamed to canonical-token, so the release build reports 0 warnings where it previously reported 1.

## The question

If -write was the only :redef in the artefact, that silencing is now dead and should go: a build that suppresses a warning class it no longer needs teaches nothing and will quietly hide the NEXT accidental redefinition. If it is still covering something — the test namespaces are in scope for this build and are NOT in scope for the release build, so a redef could live there — say what, and narrow the suppression to that one rather than the class.

## How to check

Flip `{:redef false}` off in :node-test-freehand and compile. Whatever the build then reports is the honest answer; there may be nothing.

## Sequencing

implementation/shadow-cljs.edn is HOT-ZONE — sole owner, sequential, never parallel. This is a two-line change on a file every other PR depends on, so land it quickly once started rather than holding the lane. The same applies to :freehand-bench-node, which carries the identical silencing.

## Posture

P4, low stakes and possibly a no-op. Do NOT resolve it by leaving the suppression in place 'just in case' — either it is covering a named warning or it goes.
notes:
Audit follow-up from merged PR #6828 (merge 19388266ced08715bb78baa1d7f1ec20902f4076, 2026-07-24T07:17:57Z).

title: In-repo template gates structurally mask external-consumer failures (node_modules junction + no dev-page boot proof)
description:
Found by rf2-b16va (2026-07-22 AUSEST). All three defects fixed in PR #6671 shipped GREEN through every in-repo template gate because of two structural masks:

1. NODE_MODULES JUNCTION: the RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS tier junctions implementation/node_modules into emitted scaffolds — so an emitted package.json missing a compile-required npm package (@xyflow/react/elkjs, defect 1) can never fail in-repo. Every npm package the emitted compile graph requires resolves from the monorepo's tree regardless of what the scaffold declares.

2. NO DEV-PAGE BOOT PROOF: no gate anywhere loads the emitted index.html + dev bundle in a browser. The CSP missing 'unsafe-eval' (defect 3 — blank first page on EVERY variant) and the npx-route :main-opts collision (defect 2 — npm test/watch dead) were both invisible: the tier compiles via the pure-JVM route and the only browser proof (SSR DOM-adoption) drives a synthetic _ssr_proof.html without the CSP meta, and exits as a documented skip when Chromium is absent (CI).

DISPOSITION OPTIONS (mayor judgment — this may be a WONTFIX-now): the 2026-07-19 deiym restatement already places the authoritative consumer-realistic gate in the EXTERNAL repo's protected pre-tag workflow (fresh directory + empty caches), which closes both masks by construction at split time. If interim in-repo teeth are wanted before the split, the cheap options are (a) an emitted-package.json completeness assert (string-requires reachable from the emitted compile graph must be declared) and (b) a Chromium dev-page boot cell (mount + zero pageerror) riding the existing RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS gate next to the SSR proof. title: Rule + document the presence child-order contract: incoming reorder is currently ignored (kept keys render in first-appearance order)
description:
From the adversarial presence review (Mike-directed, 2026-07-20). VERIFIED FACT (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/presence_runtime.cljc, reconcile ~L41-70): the next entry vector maps kept keys over COMMITTED order and appends brand-new keys at the end; the incoming children's ORDER affects only the appended tail. Consequence: reordering the children under a (ui/presence ...) boundary does not reorder the rendered DOM — a sorted/reordering list under presence silently keeps first-appearance order until keys leave and re-enter. render-entries emits in entry order, so React receives the frozen order.

The reconcile docstring claims less than the code does ('Retained (:unmounting) keys hold their slot; new keys append at the end') — it is silent that PRESENT keys also ignore incoming order. Neither spec/004 §Presence nor docs/core/re-frame.ui/presence.md states any order contract. Nothing is wrong for the canonical toast/notification use-case (append + remove, never reorder), but the behavior is a silent surprise and today it is contract-by-accident.

THE RULING (small; delegatable unless Mike pulls it): pick one —
(A) BLESS THE FREEZE (recommended). Presence children render in first-appearance order; incoming reorder is deliberately ignored; slot stability is part of the retention contract (an exiting child never jumps position mid-animation, and order churn cannot retrigger layout during exits). Cost: one normative paragraph + docstring truth-up + one pinning test. Fits the ruled deliberately-bounded posture (rf2-0ufty: timeout-only, not an animation system) and the actual consumer shape (toasts).
(B) RESPECT INCOMING ORDER for non-retained keys: kept :present keys re-sort to incoming order each render; retained :unmounting keys stay anchored (needs a deterministic anchoring rule — e.g. a retained key holds position relative to its committed predecessor; ambiguous when the predecessor itself moved/left). Real design+test surface (interleaving retained keys with a reordering live set), no demonstrated consumer. Only worth it if a real app wants exit animations on a SORTED list — that is the trigger; do not build speculatively.

WORK once ruled (assuming A):
1. spec/004-Views.md §Presence: one normative paragraph stating the order contract (first-appearance order; reorder ignored; slot stability during exits). ⚠️ HOT-ZONE spec/004 — sole toucher, sequence per dispatch rules (rf2-rvs56 slice d also queues for 004).
2. presence_runtime.cljc reconcile docstring: state that ALL kept keys render in committed order, not only retained ones.
3. docs/core/re-frame.ui/presence.md: one sentence ('children render in first-appearance order; presence is for enter/exit, not reordering — sort upstream of the boundary if order matters before removal'). Coordinate with rf2-xqmt7 (same file) — one PR for both doc deltas is fine.
4. One cheap pinning test in implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/presence_reconcile_cljs_test.cljc: committed [a b] + incoming [b a] -> entries stay [a b] (both :present). Red under (B), green under (A) — makes the contract executable instead of accidental.

BOUNDARIES: no runtime behavior change under (A); no order machinery, no second reconcile mode, no per-boundary option (:reorder? etc. is exactly the option-creep the bounded ruling forbids).

ACCEPTANCE: an explicit ruled order contract exists in spec/004 §Presence; docstring + guide state it; one reconcile test pins it; no runtime change (A) or a demonstrated-consumer-justified minimal reorder (B, with the anchoring rule specified and tested).

Cross-ref: rf2-xqmt7 (doc sibling), rf2-0ufty (bounded-presence ruling), presence_dom_cljs_test.cljs (existing behavior suite — untouched).
notes:
HOLD behind S1 (rf2-5e8zv.1, mayor 2026-07-20): touches presence_runtime.cljc/analyze.cljc which S1's lease-deletion modifies-or-deletes (presence is part of the lease vertical slice). RE-EVALUATE after S1 merges: if S1 deletes presence_runtime.cljc, this presence-review follow-up may be SUPERSEDED (close); if it survives with changes, sequence + re-verify the finding against the post-S1 file.
RE-VERIFIED post-keystone (rf2-5e8zv.1 merged), 2026-07-21 00:30 AUSEST, by presence-review-cluster worker (worker/presence-review-cluster). VERDICT: finding still REAL; keystone did NOT obviate it; NOT closed; NOT actioned (gated). Current code confirms the freeze:
- presence_runtime.cljc reconcile L57-69: kept = (mapv … committed) maps kept keys over COMMITTED order; added appends brand-new incoming keys at the tail. Incoming ORDER affects only the appended tail; a committed key that is still incoming keeps its committed slot regardless of its incoming position. So committed [a b] + incoming [b a] -> entries stay [a b] (both :present). The finding holds verbatim against post-keystone source.
- Docstring nuance: reconcile docstring L48 already says 'Rules, in committed order then appended new keys' (covers the substance), but the summarizing L55 'Retained (:unmounting) keys hold their slot; new keys append at the end' still names only retained keys — the finding's truth-up target.
NOT ACTIONED because: (1) requires Mike's A/B RULING (bless-the-freeze vs respect-incoming-order) — unruled, so this worker will not pre-empt it by landing a pinning test or normative paragraph that bakes in (A); (2) the acceptance core (spec/004-Views.md §Presence normative paragraph) is HOT-ZONE and OUTSIDE this cluster's code fence (presence_runtime.cljc + analyze.cljc + tests); (3) the guide sentence is a docs-lane edit (presence.md, coordinates with rf2-xqmt7). ROUTE to a ruled dispatch: once Mike picks A/B, the docstring truth-up (in-fence) + reconcile pinning test + spec/004 paragraph (hot-zone, sequence) + guide sentence land together.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-21 07:25 AUSEST)
THE RULING: (A) BLESS THE FREEZE — presence children render in FIRST-APPEARANCE order; incoming reorder is deliberately ignored; new keys append at the tail regardless of incoming position; slot stability during exits is part of the retention contract; reorder-sensitive lists sort upstream of the boundary (order-at-first-appearance), and a list whose RENDERED order must track a changing sort does not belong under a presence boundary — handle display order at the presentation layer. No runtime change.
BASIS: the contract matches shipped behavior (verified post-keystone: reconcile at presence_runtime.cljc L57-70 maps kept keys over COMMITTED order and appends brand-new incoming keys at the tail) — zero runtime change, zero runtime risk; fits the ruled bounded-presence posture (rf2-0ufty: DOM-agnostic, timeout-only, not an animation system) and the actual consumer shape (toasts append and remove, never reorder); no consumer for reorder-under-presence exists.
THE ANCHORING-AMBIGUITY DEMONSTRATION (preserved from the retired dossier — the analysis that kills (B)): committed [a b c] with b exiting (:unmounting), incoming reorder [c a]. Anchoring b after its committed predecessor a yields [c a b] (b jumps middle -> last); anchoring b before its committed successor c yields [b c a] (b jumps middle -> first). Two plausible rules, OPPOSITE answers, and both move the exiting child mid-animation — the exact artifact retention exists to prevent; when the anchor key itself moved or left, the rule must recurse. (B) therefore requires a genuinely arbitrary rule. RE-TRIGGER: a REAL app wanting exit animations on a SORTED list may reopen (B) as a demand-gated design, with the anchoring rule specified against that consumer's actual shape.
DISSENT PRESERVED (a Codex recommendation was appended to the dossier post-authoring; weighed on the merits, not adopted; no operator preference was stated): Codex recommended (B) with this candidate rule — build live entries in incoming order; reinsert each exiting key at its previous committed index, left-to-right, clamping when out of range (committed [a b c] + incoming [c a] -> [c b a], exiting b keeps index 1; idempotent on the next render since [c b a] becomes committed). Its valid critique is folded into the ruling prose above: "sort upstream" is NOT a remedy for rendered order (the sorted upstream vector IS the incoming order reconcile discards, and a prepended new key renders at the tail: committed [a b] + incoming [x a b] -> [a b x], verified), so the contract must state honestly that ORDER AND INSERTION POSITION freeze at first appearance. Not adopted because committed-index reinsertion resolves the ambiguity by fiat, not in substance: numeric-index stability is not visual stability — in [c b a] the exiting b keeps index 1 but BOTH its neighbours changed (was between a and c, now between c and a), so the exiting child still sits amid reshuffled neighbours mid-exit-animation, and the clamp plus left-to-right reinsertion order are further arbitrary choices; a rule this arbitrary should be designed against a real consumer (the named re-trigger), not speculatively — adopting (B) now is a runtime change plus a real design/test surface (pure reorder, prepend, reorder-during-exit, re-entry, idempotence) for zero demonstrated demand, against the bounded posture, pre-alpha.
IMPLEMENTATION (this ruling RELEASES the held presence-review-cluster worker; the bead's WORK list stands, restated compactly): (1) spec/004-Views.md #Presence gains ONE normative paragraph — first-appearance order; incoming reorder ignored; new keys append at the tail; slot stability during exits; sort upstream if first-appearance order matters, and do not wrap a list whose rendered order must track a changing sort — HOT-ZONE 004, sequence per dispatch rules. (2) presence_runtime.cljc reconcile docstring truth-up: ALL kept keys render in committed order, not only retained ones. (3) docs/core/re-frame.ui/presence.md: one sentence stating the order contract (coordinate with the shipped rf2-xqmt7 page, which currently has NO order sentence — verified). (4) One pinning test in presence_reconcile_cljs_test.cljc: committed [a b] + incoming [b a] -> entries stay [a b] (both :present). BOUNDARIES unchanged: no order machinery, no second reconcile mode, no :reorder? option.
Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-1kb0v.presence-child-order.md retired (deleted) per Mike's authorization; its analysis is preserved in this note.
