title: Investigate compiled-view event-to-commit latency vs hand-written React (~2-5ms Chromium)
description: fnkmi (#6224) G-8 evidence surfaced: the compiled re-frame.ui control's event-to-commit p95 runs several× the hand-written React (useState/onChange) baseline in Chromium (~5.2ms vs ~1.0ms; WebKit ~18 vs ~16 rAF-quantized), noisy across runs. Well within a frame budget + correctness is solid, so NOT gated (vindicates the evidence-only/no-threshold G-8 posture — a hard 10% gate would flake). Investigate whether the ~2-5ms delta is real framework dispatch cost (event → capture-dispatch → epoch → ViewCell commit → React) or measurement overhead. Read out/ui-g8.json for the per-engine artifact. Perf serves the primary lenses (elegance/clarity/correctness) — this is an awareness/understanding bead, not a must-fix.
acceptance_criteria: Key each sample to a fresh input and record its endpoint in that arm's Profiler onRender while retaining the exact-one-attributable-commit assertion; alternate compiled-first and hand-written-first pair order to remove fixed sequence bias; compare the resulting true event-to-commit evidence with the existing settlement measurements before attributing the delta; preserve raw per-engine artifacts and the evidence-only/no-threshold posture; add no benchmark framework, production instrumentation, or timing correctness gate.
notes:
PR #6224 audit rf2-5qz8z proved the current metric boundary before attribution: dev.cljs latency-sample! starts before ui.test/flush! and stops when that Promise resolves; ui.test/flush! resolves only after awaited React act, framework draining, and any further framework/React convergence. The Profiler callbacks count commits but do not timestamp them. The samples are therefore input-to-global-quiescence/act settlement, not literally input-to-the-arm's Profiler commit, and every pair runs compiled first then hand-written. Resolve those two measurement effects before treating the observed delta as framework cost.
rf2-dpwel RESOLVED (PR #6662). Measurement corrected per acceptance: (1) each sample keys a fresh input to its arm's React.Profiler onRender commitTime — the TRUE event-to-commit endpoint — with the exact-one-attributable-commit assertion retained PER SAMPLE (!=1 commits throws as a structural failure); (2) the former input-to-flush-settlement span is recorded alongside as a second 'settlement' channel per engine; (3) pair order alternates compiled-first/hand-written-first. Evidence-only posture preserved (no thresholds/gates; raw distributions verbatim in out/ui-g8.json).

CORRECTED NUMBERS (2 local runs, p95 ms, compiled vs hand-written): chromium commit 1.4-1.7 vs 0.2; chromium settlement 2.0-2.3 vs 0.3-0.4; webkit commit 3-5 vs 1; webkit settlement 16-19 vs 16.

ATTRIBUTION: the previously reported ~2-5ms Chromium delta (and WebKit's 18-vs-16 shape) was SUBSTANTIALLY MEASUREMENT BOUNDARY. WebKit's settlement channel is an rAF-quantized ~16ms plateau for BOTH arms (ratio ~1.0) that fabricated the absolute magnitude and hid the real 3-5x commit-channel difference. Chromium's settlement boundary inflated the compiled arm ~+0.5-0.9ms (post-commit framework draining the bare useState baseline doesn't pay). Alternating order changed nothing — sequence bias was not the driver. The RESIDUAL delta is real framework dispatch cost but small: ~1ms/keystroke Chromium, ~2ms WebKit (un-optimized dev bundle, instrumentation live) — event → capture-dispatch → app-db commit + epoch bookkeeping → ViewCell revision → React commit — vs a bare setState baseline; the 3-8x ratio is that ~1ms fixed cost over a ~0.1-0.2ms baseline at 0.1ms timer granularity. Comfortably within frame budget; no fix warranted; evidence-only posture vindicated. G-8 now reports both boundaries permanently.
close_reason: Delta attributed (PR #6662): the observed ~2-5ms Chromium / 18-vs-16 WebKit gap was substantially measurement boundary — the old metric spanned flush settlement (WebKit: rAF-quantized ~16ms plateau on both arms; Chromium: +0.5-0.9ms post-commit draining only the compiled arm pays), not event-to-commit. With the Profiler-commitTime endpoint + alternating pair order, the true residual framework cost is ~1ms/keystroke Chromium, ~2ms WebKit (dev bundle) — real, fixed, within frame budget; no fix warranted. G-8 now records both commit + settlement channels, evidence-only.

title: capture-frame over a frame VALUE silently loses the incarnation pin
description:
Shape-3 audit of #6072+#6079 (rf2-moftbs+rf2-9pyles). capture-target-incarnation (core.cljc:1173-1176) pins via frame/frame-incarnation-token, an ID-keyed lookup ((some-> (frame id) :drain-lock), frame.cljc:842). When the capture target is a frame VALUE (a map) not a keyword, (frame <map>)=(get @frames <map>)=nil, so capture-target-incarnation returns nil => the capture is UNPINNED/address-directed.

FAILURE: (capture-frame <frame-value>) silently loses the incarnation fence, whereas (capture-frame <frame-id>) pins it — even though the value now CARRIES its own exact incarnation token (:rf.frame/incarnation-token, the whole point of rf2-moftbs). capture-target-superseded? uses the same nil-returning lookup so the two stay internally consistent (uniformly unpinned, no false positive) — the fence is just silently absent. Reachable because API-shrink #1 (rf2-csbbwu) accepts a frame value everywhere a keyword id is, and dispatch-impl normalises it fine, so the bundle 'works' minus the fence.

LOW/P4: capture-frame 1-arity is documented for frame-id (keyword); a value is an undocumented-but-plausible edge; impact is a silently unfenced capture, not a wrong destroy.

FIX (trivial): in capture-target-incarnation prefer the value's carried token — (or (frame/frame-value-incarnation-token frame) (frame/frame-incarnation-token frame)) — so a value pins its exact incarnation and a keyword pins via registry lookup. Makes moftbs+9pyles compose on the value path.

Ref: ai/findings/2026-07-17-review-incarnation.md Finding 2.

title: (TRIGGER-GATED) defview-alias: zero-wrapper facade aliases
description: DO NOT DISPATCH until trigger fires. TRIGGER: a facade prototype proves canonical-defs-in-the-public-namespace materially harmful for a real library (re-com.core carries 72 plain (def button buttons/button) aliases — the fallback WITHOUT this feature is defining the canonical defviews in the public ns and demoting impl namespaces to helpers; try that first). SCOPE if it fires: a zero-runtime alias facility — the compiler follows the alias to the canonical template/props schema; tooling records both public alias and canonical view id; alias cycles and aliases-to-non-views fail at compile time; emitted output contains no wrapper; no bundle-retention regression (G-18 arm). Provenance: readiness §4; codex P7.
notes:
RULING (2026-07-16, delegated decision per Mike's in-session direction; dossier weighed and retired):

DECISION
1. Gate stays TRIGGER-GATED; Option A stands as the facade strategy NOW: canonical `defview` definitions live in the public component namespaces, impl namespaces are demoted to private helpers, consumers use per-namespace production imports. Do NOT build `defview-alias` yet. Option C (wrapper views / dynamic forwarding) is rejected permanently as a facade strategy.
2. If the trigger fires, Option B is authorized AS THE META-COPYING MACRO, not a compiler naming graph. The dossier's §3B cost framing is corrected: head classification is meta-driven, so no new compiler graph, cycle detection, or manifest machinery is needed.
3. Trigger amended (one addition): besides material organizational harm in a real facade prototype (cycles / incoherent ownership / duplication across many views), a consumer incident traceable to silent check-loss through a bare def alias in a published library facade also counts as trigger evidence. "We prefer impl namespaces elsewhere" remains insufficient.
4. Dev-only warning: RULED IN, lands NOW (independent of graduation) — warn in the dev arm when a :foreign-classified head's runtime value is a registered re-frame2 view shell. Rationale: the one dangerous failure mode of a bare alias is that it compiles fine while the Q2/Q4 checks and view identity silently vanish; converting silent to didactic drops the urgency of B to near zero. This is S3-adjacent compiler work; see MAYOR TODO below.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (mechanics re-verified against source 2026-07-16)
- Classification is by VAR METADATA at expansion time: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/env.cljc:150-153 (classify-head — resolved meta carries :rf.ui/view => :view with view-id via view-id-of env.cljc:123-129, else :foreign). The bare-def corner is already documented at env.cljc:23-25: `(def card2 card)` copies value not var meta => classifies :foreign.
- Emitted def shape: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/emit_cljs.cljc:598-602 stamps var-meta {:rf.ui/view true, :rf.ui/view-id, :rf.ui/children?, :rf.ui/closed-prop-keys (when closed), :doc}; :611-622 defs the var to the dev register-view! shell or prod React.memo (memo-view) — the runtime VALUE is the stable shell keyed by view id.
- What a bare def alias SILENTLY LOSES at every consumer call site (all compile-time): Q4 children-not-accepted check (analyze.cljc:1545-1557), Q2 closed-props/undeclared-prop gate (analyze.cljc:1558-1575), the internal view identity on the AST edge — :op :view + :view-id (analyze.cljc:1576-1579, feeds tooling/manifest) — and ref handling flips to the foreign path (emit_cljs.cljc:372).
- What KEEPS WORKING through a bare alias: rendering (emit-component emits the head symbol, emit_cljs.cljc:360-377; same runtime value = same registered shell), zero wrapper, same React identity, HMR, JVM/SSR identity. The failure is purely compile-time and silent — that asymmetry is why the dev warning is ruled in.
- Facade count (dossier grep-verified): re-com/src/re_com/core.cljs carries exactly 72 `(def x ns/x)` alias Vars — 64 components, 8 plain fns (5 box/*-style helpers, show-row-data-on-alt-click, make-tour, start-tour). Only ~64 would ever use an alias facility; the 8 fns need nothing.
- Meta-copying macro sketch (if B fires): `(defview-alias public-name target)` => resolve target at expansion (env/resolve-sym); fail didactically unless its meta carries :rf.ui/view; emit `(def public-name target-fqn)` with :rf.ui/view / :rf.ui/view-id / :rf.ui/children? / :rf.ui/closed-prop-keys (+ :doc) copied onto public-name's var meta. Cycles impossible by construction (target must already resolve to a stamped var). Zero wrapper, HMR-both-names, and JVM/SSR identity fall out of the shared stable shell for free. NOTE: meta is sufficient TODAY — a def that hand-copies the four :rf.ui/* keys already classifies :view with the canonical id; the macro exists only to make that non-drift-prone.
- TRIMMED PROOF LIST if the trigger fires (supersedes dossier §3B's seven): (1) alias-follows-schema — Q2 closed-props + Q4 children checks enforce through the alias with the canonical literal props schema; (2) dual-name tooling identity — manifest/tooling record both the public alias and the canonical view id coherently; (3) G-18 bundle-retention arm — unused aliases and sibling views cause no retention regression. Plus cheap regression tests pinning the free properties (zero wrapper, HMR both names, SSR identity).
- Dev-warning sketch: dev arm of register-view! marks its shells (property or registry set); the emitter's foreign-head path gains a goog.DEBUG-only check (first render is enough) — if the head's runtime value is a marked shell, warn: registered view reached through a bare alias; use the canonical name, a namespace alias, or (if graduated) defview-alias. Elided entirely in production; one didactic message + one test.
- FALLBACK FIRST: any real facade prototype (re-com native rewrite or otherwise) MUST first try canonical defviews in the public ns with per-namespace imports and run the advanced one-view bundle scan. Build nothing until that shows material harm.

title: (TRIGGER-GATED) ui/portal graduation: overlay stacking/focus after inline parity
description: DO NOT DISPATCH until trigger fires. TRIGGER: post-parity overlay evidence — modal/dropdown/popover/tooltip consumers (the re-com port Wave 3 family) demonstrate clipping, stacking, or focus requirements inline structure cannot meet acceptably. NOTE: re-com itself never used portals (verified — zero createPortal in the checkout), so visual PARITY needs none; this is the durable-quality graduation, never a Wave-3 blocker. SCOPE if it fires: promote the wave-2 (ui/portal node child) row — frame context passes through; focus return + inert background; nested overlay stacking; SSR fallback; Activity/StrictMode teardown proof. Provenance: readiness §4; wave-2 trigger recorded in 12 §2.
notes:
RULING (2026-07-16, delegated decision per Mike's in-session direction; dossier weighed and retired):

DECISION: Option A adopted, AMENDED to A+ = inline structure + native top-layer elements as the sanctioned escape. This is the overlay plan of record for port Wave 3. ui/portal stays trigger-gated with a RAISED bar: graduation now requires evidence that the TOP LAYER cannot solve it, not merely that inline flow failed (exact triggers below). Option C (thin ReactDOM portal wrapper without the full contract) is rejected permanently. If the gate ever fires, the dossier's section-3B proof pack (frame context across the boundary; focus entry/containment/return + inert ownership; deterministic nested stacking + dismissal; explicit JVM/SSR fallback; hydration without silent relocation; total teardown under StrictMode/Activity/HMR/target-removal; unambiguous test selection/drain) is the spike's acceptance suite.

RATIONALE: re-com achieves parity with zero portals, so parity cannot require one. But re-com is not "inline in flow" — it EMULATES a portal via position:fixed + getBoundingClientRect, and ships that emulation's failure modes (stale anchor tracking; defeat by any ancestor transform/filter/will-change, which creates a containing block for fixed elements; ad-hoc z-index ladders 4/20/30/1020). Native top-layer elements — dialog.showModal() and the popover attribute, both Baseline across evergreen browsers by 2026, plain elements/attributes to React — keep the child in its structural parent while the browser hoists rendering above every z-index and stacking context, immune to ancestor overflow AND to the transform containing blocks that defeat re-com's fixed hack. Modal dialog adds native backdrop, background inertness, initial focus, Esc cancel, and focus return — most of the portal proof pack's obligations for free — so the port EXCEEDS re-com's zero-a11y modal instead of rebuilding portal machinery to match it. Pre-alpha masterpiece posture: platform primitive over new custom cross-host contract.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (port Wave 3 overlay strategy — what "inline + top-layer" concretely means):
- Modal family: <dialog> element + showModal(), imperative open/close owned by ref/layout-effect (an existing substrate pattern; no new core primitive). Backdrop styling via ::backdrop; inert background, Esc, and focus entry/return come from the element natively.
- Anchored overlays (dropdown, popover, tooltip): popover attribute for top-layer rendering + re-com-style measured geometry (getBoundingClientRect) for placement. CSS anchor positioning may replace the placement JS once Firefox support is confirmed for the support matrix.
- Everything else: position:fixed/absolute + pure geometry, in-tree.
- In all three shapes, frame context, SSR, and teardown stay trivial BECAUSE every node remains in its structural parent: no boundary to propagate frame context across, SSR just emits the element, hydration relocates nothing, teardown is plain unmount.
- Inline-port evidence reports MUST classify each recorded overlay failure as "solved by top layer" vs "portal-only" so this gate reads cleanly later.

VERIFIED RE-COM FACTS (the parity bar; independent read of the re-com checkout, 2026-07-16):
- Zero portals: case-insensitive grep for portal/createPortal across src/re_com returns nothing.
- modal-panel is inline fixed-position CSS: wrapper position:fixed full-viewport z-index 1020, backdrop z-index 1, child z-index 2 (modal_panel/theme.cljs:7-27); backdrop-click dismiss (modal_panel.cljs:82-84). NO focus trap, NO inert, NO Esc handling, NO focus return anywhere in re-com — the behavioral parity bar for modals is that low; dialog clears it with headroom.
- popover is measured geometry with visible warts: anchor position:relative z-index 4 (popover/theme.cljs:67-70); two-pass render parks the body at top/left -10000px until measured (popover.cljs:337); margin-right:-2000px wrap-prevention hack (popover.cljs:345-347); viewport-clip detect-and-reposition (popover.cljs:212-224, 301-309); a .parentNode .parentNode .parentNode anchor walk (popover.cljs:304).
- The clipping escape is position:fixed + getBoundingClientRect and it is the DEFAULT for whole families: no-clip? switches the wrapper to fixed with measured viewport coordinates (popover.cljs:455-460, 494-496); defaults TRUE for tooltip (popover.cljs:685), datepicker-dropdown (datepicker.cljs:679), daterange-dropdown (daterange.cljs:513), tag-dropdown (tag_dropdown/theme.cljs:17). re-com's own arg-doc concedes: "slightly inferior because the popover can't track the anchor if it is repositioned" (datepicker.cljs:664).
- dropdown v2 body is likewise in-tree position:fixed with measured coordinates, z-index 30 (dropdown.cljs:308, dropdown/theme.cljs:24); anchor gets z-index 20 when open.

GRADUATION TRIGGERS for ui/portal (gate fires ONLY on a written repro; triggers 2 and 3 must recur across 2+ overlay families; aesthetic preference or React convention never fires it):
1. A consumer must render into a FOREIGN DOM node re-frame2 does not own (host-page container, embedding shell) — the one genuinely portal-only capability.
2. A recorded requirement the top layer cannot express (e.g. overlay must stack BENEATH a designated sibling; partial-pane containment with backdrop; ::backdrop styling insufficiency).
3. A documented host/webview in the support matrix lacking top-layer support where the fixed-position fallback is ALSO defeated (e.g. ancestor transform) — observed, not hypothetical.

title: (TRIGGER-GATED) registered ui/view invocation: stateful replacement slots
description: DO NOT DISPATCH until trigger fires. TRIGGER: the v1 parts-power-ceiling ruling (ai/decisions/re-com-readiness.product-rulings.md Q2) selects stateful registered replacement, OR a native table/grid decision proves a dynamic stateful-view requirement. SCOPE if it fires: graduate registered-view invocation — (ui/view id-or-var props children...) resolving REGISTERED views only — with explicit identity/props contract, production registry entries + reachability contract, SSR/JVM identity, HMR, conservative capability propagation, unknown-id diagnostics; sites flagged :dynamic in the manifest. HARD CONSTRAINTS: no general ui/element; no arbitrary fn/tag heads — pure render slots (ui/slot, S3) cover the parameterized-markup tier; this is ONLY the residual stateful tier. Provenance: readiness §4; wave-2 row trigger recorded in 12 §2.
notes:
RULING (2026-07-16, delegated decision per Mike's in-session direction; dossier weighed and retired):

DECISION: Do not fire. Gate stays CLOSED for re-com v1 (option A: composition + data/style config + pure render slots is the parts ceiling). Bead remains open and trigger-gated, with the trigger REFINED below — the original "stateful replacement" framing is superseded. Option C (general ui/element / arbitrary runtime heads) rejected outright.

RATIONALE: Statefulness and runtime-chosen identity are orthogonal; only the latter needs a registry. A stateful replacement is already expressible: a pure slot body compiled under the closed template grammar mounts a statically referenced stateful defview — (ui/render-fn [props] [my-stateful-defview {...}]) — identity static, DCE-sound, state living in the child view's own cell; runtime choice among a known finite set compiles as a case over view heads inside the slot body. Verified re-com evidence: part.cljs:139-143 resolves every part from the authored props map — ZERO sites select a part implementation from runtime data by id; 0/9 v-table injected renderers are stateful by contract (v_table.cljs:505-513; invoked as heads at 195,313,420); of ~74 default :impl parts, the stateful ones (close_button.cljs:64; popover.cljs:278-284,451-453,578-579; input_text.cljs:78-79) hold library-owned state that ports to local + the C-6 layout tier inside the library's own defviews. Cost side: production defview emits a direct React.memo with NO registry entry at all (emit_cljs.cljc:611-621; the readiness §4 "529-537" line ref has drifted) — firing this gate would create the substrate's FIRST-EVER production registry and its reachability contract from scratch. Zero demonstrated demand vs maximal structural cost = keep closed.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (refined trigger — fires ONLY on runtime-OPEN identity, not statefulness):
Fire iff (a) the v1 parts-power-ceiling ruling (ai/decisions/re-com-readiness.product-rulings.md Q2) selects stateful registered replacement (Q2 = B); OR (b) a named repo consumer (examples/tools/fixtures; project-authored guide examples excluded per spec 004 Interop demand bar) presents a part/renderer whose identity is irreducibly a runtime value arriving as data (open set: config/app-db/CMS), AND a finite compiled case over known view heads is proven inadequate, AND re-frame.ui.data (the runtime-authored-tree artefact) is proven the wrong home. If fired: option B bounded spike ONLY — registered declared views (id-or-var), production registry + reachability contract, advanced-build DCE proof, JVM/SSR identity, HMR/stable tool identity, conservative capability declarations, duplicate/unknown-id diagnostics, versioned manifest with sites flagged :dynamic; bundle/reachability proof mandatory BEFORE any public API ruling; no second elision mode (readiness §4 row 7); no general ui/element, ever.

DEPENDENCY: the coverage argument assumes rf2-ri0k6n's slot grammar permits internal view heads inside slot bodies (spec 004 grammar row [view-sym {...}]). Watch-item already pinned on rf2-ri0k6n: if that grammar excludes internal view heads, the stateful-replacement coverage claim collapses and this ruling's analysis must be redone before any reliance on it.

title: (TRIGGER-GATED) ui/tpl checkpoint: lexical template-as-value for unparameterized named content
description: DO NOT DISPATCH until trigger fires. TRIGGER: re-com port Wave 1 (box/label) or Wave 3 (popover anchor/content) shows REPEATED unparameterized named-content pain after compound child views + render slots are the baseline — this is a SCHEDULED checkpoint (evaluate at those waves), not an open-ended maybe. SCOPE if it fires: (ui/tpl [:span.bold "Hi"]) — a lexically-visible LITERAL template in expression position compiled by the owning view's pass into an element value legal in prop position; sites index into the owning view's table (closed-grammar soundness holds); JVM emitter yields a tree fragment; static-only tpls hoist; dynamic-content memo cost stated honestly (fresh host value per render). HARD CONSTRAINTS: literal lexical syntax only — NEVER runtime data; takes no arguments (parameterized rendering is ui/slot, already S3). Provenance: readiness §4; fable I-1 + grok/codex gating.
notes:
ADDITION (2026-07-16, completeness audit — grok ruling Q7): whichever way this checkpoint dispositions (ui/tpl ships, or the children/compound-view API break is published instead), the outcome must be ONE multi-slot convention for the WHOLE library — do not leave each component to invent its own; the disposition writes that convention down as part of closing this bead.
RULING (2026-07-16, delegated decision per Mike's in-session direction; dossier ai/decisions/rf2-1hm7a3.lexical-template-value-checkpoint.md weighed and retired):

DECISION: Disposition A — keep ui/tpl demand-gated; do NOT add it for v1. Option C (runtime Hiccup values / a general template function) is REJECTED permanently, in all futures. The gate stays armed with three sharpenings adopted from the independent review: (1) the PRIMARY evidence checkpoint is Wave 3 (popover anchor/content), with Wave 1 (box/label) downgraded to an early-warning sample only; (2) if the trigger ever fires, the authorized spike is pre-committed in shape: ui/tpl as literal-only call-site SUGAR lowering onto the existing zero-arg ui/render-fn + ui/slot machinery — not a new parallel element-value primitive; (3) the library-wide content-category convention is decided NOW, tpl-independently (stated below), so no future sugar decision can force an API break.

RATIONALE: Both the dossier analysis and the Fable review agreed on gating (choose A) and on rejecting C; the review's sharpenings won because they are grounded in verified measurement. Wave 1 is a near-null probe: box :child, h-box :children, and label :label all map to plain child position in any native redesign, so a quiet Wave 1 is NOT gate-closing evidence — ~18 of the 23 direct hiccup-value prop rows in re-com (re-com @ 0e2675a) concentrate in the popover/tooltip/label micro-fragment families, i.e. Wave 3. And ui/tpl is not a genuine third content category: once slots land, an unparameterized named fragment already has a conforming spelling — a zero-arg ui/render-fn prop invoked via ui/slot (Svelte 5 snippets are production proof this collapse works: they REPLACED slots with one lexical compiled construct passable as props). Framing ui/tpl as sugar over that lane removes most of Option B's stated costs (second rendering model, new host representation, tooling growth) and makes the eventual spike materially smaller.

CONVENTION (decided now; ONE convention for the whole library per the earlier grok-Q7 addition on this bead):
1. Primary rich content -> child position / compound child views (e.g. popover-root + popover-anchor + popover-content).
2. Parameterized fragments -> ui/render-fn props invoked via ui/slot (body lexically visible, compiled at the consumer site, pure render phase — no dispatch/sub/lease/hooks; see spec/004-Views.md:296 and bead rf2-ri0k6n).
3. Unparameterized named fragments -> zero-arg ui/render-fn props, SAME slot lane as (2).
4. Plain strings stay plain data props (no wrapper).
ui/tpl, if it ever ships, is call-site sugar for lane 3 only — adopting it later is additive, never a break. Every library component API must state which category each content prop accepts.

TRIGGER (measurable; evaluate at the Wave 3 checkpoint, or earlier if a component hits it). Fire the gate only if ALL of:
(a) >=3 UNRELATED components (not one family — popover variants count once) still want an unparameterized named-fragment prop in their best compound-child/slot redesign;
(b) >=20 recorded call sites in port fixtures/demos authoring the zero-arg (ui/render-fn [] ...) spelling, with a side-by-side table (best compound-child/slot form vs proposed ui/tpl form) showing a material difference — "feels more familiar" is insufficient;
(c) >=1 demonstrated defect BEYOND verbosity — e.g. per-site identity stabilization fails for zero-arg render-fns (measured re-render noise) or a static fragment cannot hoist.
(a)+(b) alone justify only the sugar spike; (c) is what would justify new semantics. Absent all three at Wave 3: close this bead by publishing the convention above as the disposition (the convention must be written down either way — that is this bead's close condition).

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (for the eventual worker, if the trigger fires):
- Spike shape: ui/tpl is literal-lexical-only sugar; (ui/tpl [:span.bold "Hi"]) compiles at the owning defview site to a zero-arg render-fn value consumed via ui/slot. Runtime values, parameters, and dynamic/arbitrary component heads are compile-time REJECTS with didactic messages (parameterized rendering is ui/slot's job, already S3).
- Soundness constraints that must hold (from spec/004-Views.md): expression positions are value-opaque under the closed audited macro grammar (004-Views.md:165-178) — ui/tpl must be an audited grammar member whose site is compile-indexed in the owning view's manifest; the sanctioned markup channels remain child position + ui/raw (004-Views.md:151-157); no general runtime Hiccup interpreter may be introduced (runtime trees belong to re-frame.ui.data).
- Proof obligations: browser and JVM emitters agree on the produced tree; HMR preserves identity + source diagnostics; static-only tpls hoist; dynamic-content memo cost stated honestly (participates in the slot memo law — output treated like child output, not a fresh-value-per-render element story).
- Fallback: only if slot-lowering provably cannot satisfy the hoisting/identity constraints may the element-value representation from this bead's DESCRIPTION be revisited — and that finding returns to Mike before implementation.
- Evidence context for the checkpoint evaluator: re-com @ 0e2675a has 48 hiccup-typed args-desc rows = 23 direct hiccup-value props (child family x4: box.cljs:364,417,492 + modal_panel.cljs:35 + args.cljs:5-10; popover family x6: popover.cljs:426,428,561,562,655,660; tooltip x4: buttons.cljs:158,426 + close_button.cljs:48 + single_dropdown.cljs:73; labels x5: radio_button.cljs:42 + dropdown.cljs:208-217 + multi_select.cljs:308,313; splits.cljs:57-58; buttons.cljs:337) vs 25 fn->hiccup renderer props (slot territory; v-table's nine renderers at v_table.cljs:505-513). Internal literal call sites are sparse: :tooltip [ x0, :label [ x10, :child [ x7 — mostly dynamic-content templates, not static fragments. Newer re-com already migrates named fragments to its parts system (:top-level-arg? x28).

MAYOR TODO: (1) when briefing the re-com port Wave 1 (box/label) work, note this checkpoint is early-warning only — record any named-content pain but do not treat a quiet Wave 1 as gate-closing; (2) the content-category convention above is tpl-independent and may be published to the port/spec docs ahead of the Wave 3 checkpoint (hot-zone sequencing applies if it lands in spec/*); (3) at Wave 3, dispatch the checkpoint evaluation against the measurable trigger above.

title: (TRIGGER-GATED) reset-key local spike: derived/buffered input state
description: DO NOT DISPATCH until trigger fires. TRIGGER: the re-com port splits fully-controlled vs commit/draft input APIs (port Wave 2) — a second consumer of buffered inputs also fires it. SCOPE: spike (local init reset-key) — same-render reinitialization for buffered inputs (React adjust-during-render idiom, bounded; render-phase set! stays banned generally). NON-NEGOTIABLE (codex P3A correction, tri-synthesis consensus): the key is an EXPLICIT CALLER REVISION, never the model value — a parent reasserting the SAME value to reject an edit is invisible to value-equality, so (local model model) silently keeps a rejected draft. PIN in the spike: host render-retry behaviour; multiple resettable slots composing in one view; caret/selection/IME through the buffered path; cause evidence; HMR; JVM. Provenance: component-library readiness §4 (drafts/component-library-readiness.md; directed 2026-07-16).
notes:
RULING (2026-07-16, delegated decision per Mike's in-session direction; dossier weighed and retired):

DECISION — Gate disposition UPGRADED from speculative trigger-gate to SCHEDULED. The bounded `(local initial reset-key)` spike runs at re-com port Wave 2 entry, as/immediately after the controlled-vs-commit/draft input classification. This supersedes the description's "DO NOT DISPATCH until trigger fires" framing: the trigger is near-certain — the need already exists in legacy form (re-com hand-rolled exactly this revision signal in input_text.cljs as a three-layer workaround stack) and 8 distinct re-com components carry internal-model machinery. The classification's real question is not "does the need exist" but "does it survive redesign into an explicit commit/draft API"; if every internal-model case dissolves into fully-controlled state, identity/keying, or a clean event protocol, the spike ABORTS at that classification step (an abort condition inside scheduled work, not a gate on scheduling). Ordinary `local` stays unchanged until the spike proves the contract. PROMOTION to the public v1 surface still requires a second DISTINCT buffered consumer (input-password/input-textarea do NOT count — they share input-text-base, input_text.cljs:213-226) plus all ten pins green. Option C (general render-time state setting) is REJECTED permanently: the user-spelled render-phase set!/update! ban (spec/004-Views.md, :rf.warning/render-phase-set!) stays fully intact; the spike sanctions only a bounded compiler-emitted lowering.

INIT RE-EVALUATION RULING — `initial` IS re-evaluated at reset time; the reset target is the CURRENT value of the init expression, not the mount-time snapshot. Evidence: re-com's real-world reset targets latest-ext-model (input_text.cljs:111-113), i.e. the parent's current assertion — a commit-input rejecting a draft must reinitialize to what the parent asserts NOW. That evaluation must be render-pure and retry-correct (pin Q2).

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (spike worker):
- Evidence base — read re-com src/re_com/input_text.cljs in full first (local checkout: C:/Users/miket/code/re-com):
  * 78-79: form-2 closure over external-model/internal-model twin atoms;
  * 111-113: render-phase double reset! sync when the external model diverges — exactly the move the spec bans for user code;
  * 91-94: documented blindness — a parent reasserting the PRIOR :model value to reject an edit is invisible to the not= check, so the user's typed value stays displayed;
  * 105 (within 102-110): workaround forces (reset! external-model @internal-model) on every commit so the next render's comparison misfires "changed";
  * 96-101: that workaround creates the documented flicker bug under async on-change;
  * 104-110: which spawned the arity-sniffed 2-arity on-change done-fn ((.-length ^js/Function on-change)).
  That stack is a hand-rolled, callback-timed revision signal; explicit reset-key is its honest spelling. Q10 closes the loop: the primitive must fully retire it.
- React mechanics constraint: the ONLY sound mechanism is the bounded compiler-emitted adjust-during-render idiom (react.dev "adjusting state when a prop changes"; hooks successor of getDerivedStateFromProps): prev-key slot + inequality-guarded same-render set. React discards the in-progress output and re-renders synchronously before commit — zero stale paint; loop-impossible by construction because the reset is a pure derivation of (not= key prev-key); abandoned/interrupted renders discard the reset and re-derive it correctly on retry. Effect-based reset (useEffect/useLayoutEffect) is DISQUALIFIED — it commits a stale-value frame first, clobbering caret/IME. Key-remount is DISQUALIFIED as a destination — it destroys focus, selection, mid-flight IME composition, and every unrelated local slot (acceptable only as interim guidance until the spike lands). The compiler-emitted lowering can GUARANTEE the guard discipline React merely asks humans to maintain — that is why a bounded exception is structurally safe while the general ban stays.
- NON-NEGOTIABLE: reset-key is an EXPLICIT CALLER REVISION, never the model value. The (local model model) failure mode, spelled out: saved value "A" -> user drafts "B" -> parent rejects the draft and reasserts "A" -> the model value before and after rejection is identical -> value-equality sees no change -> the rejected draft "B" silently persists. This is precisely re-com's lines-91-94 bug; value-equality is provably blind to same-value rejection.
- App-db-owned drafts are the right answer only when the draft IS product state (live filtering, per the placement rule); they are not the general resettable-draft answer — that inverts the placement law and floods epochs with keystroke noise.
- Relationship to P0-1 (rf2-vxgfnd.95.2): reset-key is explicitly OUT of the three-tuple [value set! update!] local contract; the spike composes on top of that landed machinery.

SPIKE MUST PIN (all ten):
1. The compiler-emitted lowering (prev-key slot + guarded same-render set) yields zero stale paints under React 18/19 concurrent interruption and StrictMode double-render; abandoned-render resets never commit.
2. `initial` re-evaluates at reset (per ruling above) and that evaluation is render-pure.
3. Ordering vs P0-1 update!: does a key-driven reset clobber pending same-turn host updates or compose after them — pin one, with a fixture.
4. Multiple resettable slots in one view: independent keys reset independently and deterministically in one pass.
5. Caret/selection/IME through a reject-and-restore cycle in a real browser (controlled-input caret semantics, not remount).
6. Cause evidence: distinct :local-state row for key-reset vs handler set!/update!.
7. HMR: the reset slot rides the existing hook signature without slot-index drift.
8. JVM: the key cannot change within one structural render — specify "reset never fires; value = init" and test it.
9. Misuse guard: the dev build detects/lints (local model model)-shaped keys (key expression identical to the value expression).
10. The primitive fully retires input_text's done-fn/flicker workaround stack in the ported commit-input.

MAYOR TODO:
- Dispatch the spike at Wave 2 entry of the re-com port (input classification), and only after rf2-vxgfnd.95.2 (three-tuple local) merges — the spike builds on that landed machinery (Q3 needs update! to exist). Brief the worker from this ruling; the bead is authoritative over any brief.
- Keep the bead open until then; re-prioritise from P4 at Wave 2 if desired. Promotion beyond the spike to the public v1 surface (second distinct buffered consumer + all ten pins green) returns to Mike for sign-off.

title: Apply the guide bare-frame convention consistently
description:
## Problem

PR #5823 (head `6c1ac7288a3858afb039aa2bb406864d5bd551d0`, merge `d1343f707446b8e9bd90b4278dd6c00bab1a1a10`) establishes a guide-wide body-form convention in `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/guide/README.md`: view body forms are referred to bare, including `frame`, with “one convention, every chapter.” Guide 05 nevertheless uses `(ui/frame)` at two locations around lines 77 and 83.

This is not a runtime defect, but it makes the newly declared ergonomic convention false on the same merged guide. The bare `(frame)` spelling is the intended body-form teaching surface.

## Evidence

`rg '\(ui/frame\)' ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/guide` currently finds the two Guide 05 occurrences. The README names bare `frame` explicitly.

## Dedupe and sequencing

The broad guide correction `rf2-vxgfnd.114` is already in progress and cannot be amended. This low-priority follow-up waits for it. If its PR removes the two qualified body-form spellings or deliberately revises the convention coherently, verify and close this bead without another edit.
design: Prefer replacing the two occurrences with bare `(frame)`, matching the README and section teaching model. Weaken the README convention only if another concrete body form requires qualification. Do not change namespaces, runtime APIs, or add tooling solely for these two tokens.
acceptance_criteria:
- `rg '\(ui/frame\)' ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/guide` returns no body-form usage.
- Guide README and Guide 05 use one consistent convention for `frame`.
- The resulting snippets remain unambiguous in their documented namespace context.
- Docs/link gates pass; no runtime/API change or new generalized lint mechanism is introduced.
- Work is serialized after `.114`; an equivalent correction there satisfies this bead after verification.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5827 — both (ui/frame) occurrences in guide 05 replaced with bare (frame); rg sweep clean. Left open for mayor to close at merge.

title: review(impl/ssr-ring + impl/http): reviewed clean — no actionable correctness findings (rf2-x76af2 wave)
description:
rf2-x76af2 review-wave summary bead. Two surfaces reviewed READ-ONLY and found clean of correctness bugs; recording as one summary per the wave's clean-surface convention. Framed as suggestions — nothing actionable found.

SCOPE REVIEWED:
- implementation/ssr-ring/src/** : ring.clj, pipeline.clj, lifecycle.clj, streaming.clj, response consumers, cookie/header/shell/trust/payload.
- implementation/http/src/** : transport.cljc (attempt/retry/abort lifecycle), registry.cljc (in-flight + actor + issuance indexes, supersede, frame/actor/epoch aborts), handlers.cljc, managed.cljc, middleware.cljc, reply.cljc, encoding.cljc.

WHAT WAS CHECKED (the wave's focus axes), all HELD:
1. Per-request frame isolation (no cross-request app-db bleed): ssr-ring gensyms a fresh rf.frame/<gensym> per request (pipeline.clj setup-request-frame!), keys all side channels (request/response/pending-error) by frame-address; SSR error listeners (error_listener.cljc candidate-frame-for-error / error-emit-projection-listener) route strictly on the stamped :frame and never guess among live frames, so concurrent requests cannot cross-attribute. Response accumulator + request slot live outside app-db (response.cljc / request.cljc) so they can't ride the hydration payload.
2. http async lifecycle — cancellation / error paths / in-flight dedup / ordering: the once-only :finalised? CAS + abort-always-wins :aborted? precedence cell (transport.cljc finalise-success!/finalise-failure!/dispatch-aborted!), continuous-registration across the backoff transition (schedule-backoff-handle!), identity-conditional 2-arg clear-in-flight! (registry.cljc, prevents evicting a same-id successor), and the monotonic per-request-id issuance counter with conditional-atomic eviction all compose correctly. Supersede, actor-destroy (obsolete-target suppression), epoch-restore, and frame-destroy aborts all route through reply-suppressing-abort-reasons consistently; reply-tail throws are fenced (emit-reply-tail-error!) so a throwing :after cannot retry-storm a completed 2xx (CLJS) or vanish in an unobserved whenComplete (JVM).
3. Streaming lifecycle teardown (ssr-ring/streaming.clj): every leaf owns exactly one destroy-frame-quietly! (redirect / projected-error inline; writer-thread finally for the streamed leaf) with deliberately NO outer finally, avoiding a destroy racing the live daemon writer; head/cookie materialisation is done BEFORE spawning the writer so a serialisation throw can't orphan the pipe.
4. SSR hydration boundary (server tree == client first render): render-document-hash (body-only) is shared by wire marker + payload :rf/render-hash; hash.cljc canonical-EDN walker + canonical-number normalise JVM/CLJS number/fn-head divergence, and emit.cljc reuses hash/canonical-number for numeric leaves (emit.cljc:435) so markup and hash stay byte-consistent; hydrate.cljc + boot.cljc enforce the frame-id-mismatch + malformed-payload fail-closed guards at both the boot helper and the handler boundary.

NO correctness bugs, hydration mismatches, resource leaks, or over-engineering flagged on these two surfaces. The one actionable finding in this wave is on the ssr surface (streaming client delta drop) — filed separately as rf2-x76af2.35.
close_reason: ssr-ring + http reviewed clean (rf2-x76af2 wave): per-request frame isolation, streaming teardown-ownership, redirect/error classification, CRLF/token fail-fast (ssr-ring); once-only finalised CAS + abort-precedence, backoff transition, in-flight dedup/eviction, abort routing, reply-tail fence (http) all verified correct. title: (:rf.mutation/execute {:from-db} scope: docs promise vs literal-canonicalize + nil-policy)
description: Follow-up spun off from rf2-oo8cv7 (invalidate-tags symmetric {:from-db} resolution). docs/resources/concepts.md:429,445 teach {:from-db} on :rf.mutation/execute, but mutation_registry/resolve-scope (mutation_registry.cljc:395-421) canonicalizes a {:from-db …} :scope LITERALLY under a fail-OPEN global default — inconsistent with the use-time-resolution rule ensure/clear-scope/invalidate now share. DECISION NEEDED (its own ruling): either (a) the docs stop promising {:from-db} on :rf.mutation/execute :scope, or (b) execute gains ScopeInput resolution symmetric with the others. If (b), the nil-policy question is open: fail-open exec global default (current) vs throw (scope-requiring, like ensure/invalidate). Do NOT smuggle into rf2-oo8cv7.
notes:
MAYOR NOTE (2026-07-12): premise half-resolved — option (a) ALREADY SHIPPED via rf2-jok6kz PR #5682 (concepts.md no longer promises {:from-db} on execute; docs+runtime now consistent). Remaining question is (b) only: should :rf.mutation/execute GAIN ScopeInput resolution symmetric with ensure/clear-scope/invalidate-tags (elegance/API-uniformity), and if so nil-policy = fail-open global default (current) vs throw (scope-requiring)? Genuine design fork — awaiting ruling (Mike/decision-agent). Do not dispatch until ruled.
RULING (decision-agent under Mike's 2026-07-12 'nothing gates on me, you decide' delegation, 2026-07-12): Option (b) — :rf.mutation/execute GAINS ScopeInput resolution symmetric with ensure/clear-scope/invalidate-tags, and the nil-policy is THROW (:rf.error/resource-scope-unresolved-reference — scope-requiring, like ensure and invalidate-tags; NOT clear-scope's warn/no-op, NOT the current fail-open global).

WHY: (1) This is a correctness fix wearing a uniformity coat: today an explicitly passed {:scope {:from-db :x}} canonicalizes LITERALLY, so tag matching compares against the literal reference map and silently matches nothing — the exact silent zero-match failure mode oo8cv7 just eliminated on invalidate-tags. (2) Fail-open-to-global on nil resolution contradicts Spec 016's own fail-closed law ('a derived scope that can't resolve is fail-closed — never a fall-through to global'; optimistic-tags already drop targets on nil rather than writing globally). A session-derived write executing while logged out must fail loudly, not silently operate on global entries. (3) The absent-:scope default (:rf.scope/global) is UNCHANGED — this ruling governs only an explicitly supplied reference that fails to resolve.

REJECTED: keep-literal (silent zero-match; inconsistent public contract for the same :scope key across sibling ops); fail-open-global on nil (violates 016 fail-closed law; cross-viewer leak risk); warn/no-op (execute is scope-requiring — a write with an unresolvable derived scope is a bug, unlike clear-scope teardown).

IMPLEMENTATION: reuse scope-registry/resolve-scope-input (shipped in PR #5683) — execute becomes its third consumer; no new resolution branch. Resolve at event-execution time against the handler's app-db coeffect; the mutation engine, trace, instance records, and continuation projections only ever see the RESOLVED concrete scope (no {:from-db} map in egress — consistent with rf2-825mzj's projection derivation). Unregistered resolver id throws :rf.error/resource-scope-not-registered before any mutation start (same as invalidate-tags). Docs: concepts.md re-gains {:from-db} on execute TRUTHFULLY in the same PR (rf2-jok6kz removed the promise because the runtime lacked it; this restores both sides consistently — cite both beads in the PR body). Spec surfaces: 016 execute payload section, Spec-Schemas MutationExecuteArgs :scope -> ScopeInput union, 009 gains the throwing surface on the existing error rows. HOT-ZONE: Spec-Schemas + 009 + 016 — sequence against other spec-schema beads, never parallel. Tests: instance-keyed execute with {:from-db} resolving (a) concrete -> invalidates match in resolved scope, (b) nil -> throws before any mutation start (no instance record, no optimistic patch), (c) unregistered id -> throws. Verify descriptor-level per-target scopes still override the mutation-level default after resolution.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #5690 — :rf.mutation/execute :scope is a ScopeInput via scope-registry/resolve-scope-input (third consumer); supplied {:from-db} resolving nil THROWS :rf.error/resource-scope-unresolved-reference per the (b)+THROW ruling; absent-scope global default unchanged; instance/trace/reply see only the resolved concrete scope. Tests mirror #5683 acceptance shape incl. descriptor-override leg; 016/Spec-Schemas/009 additive; concepts.md re-gains {:from-db} on execute truthfully (pairs with rf2-jok6kz #5682). Gates: resources JVM + CLJS node + mkdocs --strict all green.

title: [correctness-review][core] Two anonymous images in one composition produce a degenerate {:image nil :shadowed-by nil} shadow-report entry (violates shadow-report id invariant)
description:
VERIFIED (JVM repro). image_assembly.cljc shadow-report (:672-723) + check-unique-image-ids! (:852-877); reachability gate live_frame.cljc validate-images! (:401-431). check-unique-image-ids! rejects only DUPLICATE non-nil ids (exempts anonymous via (keep :rf.image/id images)); validate-images! requires only a non-empty vector, not ids. So a composition of two ANONYMOUS images is accepted. When both define the same [kind id] (via disjoint :select-ns), shadow-report records a shadow whose loser AND winner are both nil. Violates the code's own shadow-report contract (:668-670): 'Images are named by their composition-unique id ... so the two ids name exactly one image each.'

REPRO (JVM): img-a (image {:select-ns {:include ["app.a"]}}) and img-b (image {:select-ns {:include ["app.b"]}}) both anonymous; pool defines [:event :x] in app.a and app.b.
  (asm/generation-shadows (asm/assemble [img-a img-b] pool)) -> [{:registration [:event :x], :image nil, :shadowed-by nil}]
Resolution itself is correct (image-order layering still wins); only the shadow REPORT (dev/introspection surface via (:rf.gen/shadows (rf/frame-generation f))) is degenerate.

FIX SKETCH: fail loud when a MULTI-image composition (>1 image) carries an anonymous image (an image with no :id cannot participate in composition, per image docstring). Add to check-unique-image-ids! or validate-images!. If a NEW :rf.error/* id is minted (e.g. :rf.error/anonymous-image-in-composition) it MUST land with its Spec 009 §Error catalogue row in the same PR; alternatively reuse :rf.error/image-duplicate-image-id reframed as 'un-nameable image in composition'. (Merely omitting the nil/nil entry hides the misconfig -> not preferred under fail-loud.)

ACCEPTANCE: a 2+ composition containing any anonymous image fails loud at make-frame with a distinct :rf.error/id; shadow report never contains {:image nil :shadowed-by nil}. A SINGLE anonymous image (local-test case) still assembles.

title: [correctness-review][skill-shared] placeholder-identity fail-closed omits distinct_value_originals; unbound distinct secret passes unverified
description:
Read-only correctness review of skills/shared (rf2-x76af2.4, wave 2026-07-11).

DEFECT (asymmetric fail-closed in the stable-placeholder identity check)
check-placeholder-identity (skills/shared/tests/evals/score-behavioral-eval.clj:142-197) fails closed in two cases only:
  (a) eval declares placeholder_identity but transcript has ZERO bindings -> :placeholder-bindings-absent;
  (b) a same_value_groups rendering has no binding -> :placeholder-binding-missing (the `missing` seq, lines 155-161).
There is NO missing-binding fail-closed for distinct_value_originals. So a distinct secret the agent claims to have masked, but for which the harness captured no binding, has its "distinct secrets -> distinct numbers" invariant silently unverified while the eval PASSES.

REPRO: drop the AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE binding (all other bindings present; secret absent from output) ->
  bb skills/shared/tests/evals/score-behavioral-eval.clj <that transcript>
  => { "eval_id": 2, "pass": true, "failures": [] }  (exit 0)

WHY IT IS A DEFECT: the scorer's own rationale for fail-closing same-value groups (:154 "each rendering ... is guaranteed present in the fixture recap, so a missing binding means the stability check can't run") applies EQUALLY to distinct_value_originals — they are all present in the fixture recap too. So the asymmetry is an inconsistency, not a principled exemption. forbidden_output_substrings backstops an actual raw leak, so only the placeholder-uniqueness half of the invariant escapes -> P4.

FIX SKETCH: extend the `missing` seq to also require a captured binding for every distinct_value_originals entry (fail closed if absent), OR document in the placeholder_identity note why distinct originals are exempt while same-value groups are not.

ACCEPTANCE: a transcript missing a binding for any distinct_value_originals entry scores FAIL; add a self-test negative `neg "eval2 missing distinct binding"` alongside the existing "eval2 missing same-value binding" (:461).

SEVERITY P4: bounded — raw-leak substring check still catches an actual leak; only placeholder-uniqueness verification escapes, and only on incomplete harness capture (the manual harness is contracted to capture all bindings, behavioral-evals.json:13).

title: [api-consistency] :rf.resource/invalidate-tags does not resolve {:from-db} scope like :rf.resource/ensure (found in rf2-j538f7.29)
description: rf2-j538f7.29 (PR #5620) found: :rf.resource/invalidate-tags canonicalizes a {:from-db ...} scope LITERALLY (does not resolve it against db), unlike :rf.resource/ensure which resolves it. Apps dispatching invalidate-tags directly with a {:from-db} reference must resolve the concrete scope in-handler via resolve-resource-scope first. Not a bug (the example worked around it correctly, mutations resolve their own descriptors), but a sharp API-consistency edge. DECISION: should invalidate-tags resolve {:from-db} scopes symmetrically with ensure, or is the literal-canonicalize deliberate (invalidate is a raw tag operation)? If symmetric resolution is wanted, small fix in implementation/resources. Low priority.
notes:
RULING (decision-agent, 2026-07-12): OPTION A — SYMMETRIC RESOLUTION.

CHOSEN: the direct :rf.resource/invalidate-tags event resolves a {:from-db <resolver-id>} :scope against its handler's app-db coeffect at event-execution time, exactly like ensure/clear-scope. Define one public ScopeInput (ConcreteScope | {:from-db <kw>}) for public scope-taking resource-operation slots; the matcher and cache only ever see the resolved canonical concrete scope. :rf.scope/same stays descriptor-only (no enclosing mutation on the direct event).

WHY: Spec 016 already declares {:from-db} "the single use-time resolution rule, uniform across every site" (spec/016-Resources.md:223) — the direct invalidate event being the lone raw exception contradicts the spec's own model; its omission from the site list (016:213-221) is a spec hole, not a design stance. The literal-canonicalize failure mode is a SILENT zero-match, observationally indistinguishable from a legitimate no-match — exactly the class of silent no-op this codebase fail-closes everywhere else (rf2-pvdae1, clear-scope unresolved). RealWorld already pays the ergonomic tax with a weaker workaround (manual resolve + silent nil no-op: examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/views.cljs:162-184). History says integration gap, not abstraction boundary: e9616ca48d unified the resolver sites; 90b2181cbe fixed the identical literal-map miss in clear-scope.

REJECTED: (B) keep-literal-and-document — a documented sharp edge every caller must memorise; visually identical :scope slots with different semantics; turns a likely mistake into a legit-looking zero-match trace. (B-prime) resolve-in-producers / raw public engine — unenforceable without a second public event name; it remains a fine INTERNAL lowering invariant (mutation settlement keeps dispatching concrete scopes; no double resolution).

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Payload is a closed union: scoped {:scope ScopeInput :tags ... :cause optional} vs cross-scope {:cross-scope? true :tags ... :cause REQUIRED, :scope ABSENT}. REJECT {:cross-scope? true :scope ...} loudly (fail-closed error; never resolve-then-ignore). NOTE: this tightens current permit-and-ignore behaviour — update the pinned test at implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_invalidation_gc_cljs_test.cljc:190-196 to drop :scope from the cross-scope dispatch.
2. Scoped-branch failure semantics: missing/nil :scope keeps :rf.error/resource-invalidate-scope-required; concrete scope through state/canonicalize-scope exactly ONCE (existing reserved-typo / wrapped-global / host-value failures stay pinned); unregistered resolver id throws :rf.error/resource-scope-not-registered; a resolver returning nil emits the causal :rf.resource/scope-resolved row (:resolved-nil? true) then THROWS :rf.error/resource-scope-unresolved-reference (invalidate is scope-requiring like ensure — NOT clear-scope warn/no-op, which stays the deliberate destructive-teardown exception); a throwing resolver propagates unwrapped — no runtime-db write, no :rf.resource/invalidated summary.
3. Shape: do NOT hand-copy a fourth from-db branch. Add one small helper in re_frame.resources.scope_registry — (resolve-scope-input scope db where resource-id) => canonical concrete scope, nil only when a reference resolved nil; concrete arm canonicalizes, reference arm resolve-from-db-reference (result already canonical — never canonicalize twice); nil policy stays per-operation at call sites. Use it in invalidate-tags-handler (destructure app-db :db — the ordinary event coeffect map already carries it, implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:1623-1676) and refactor clear-scope inline branch (events.cljc:1965-1977) onto it; optionally resolve-descriptor-scope / resolve-exact-target-scope in the same focused change. match-invalidation-keys unchanged; mutation-originated invalidations stay concrete (zero resolver calls).
4. Spec/docs: spec/016-Resources.md — add direct invalidate-tags to the resolver-reference site list (:213-221), state causal-db timing + nil-throws in the Invalidation section, payload example, error roster; spec/Spec-Schemas.md — ScopeInput authoring schema applied to the event payload; spec/009-Instrumentation.md ~:2246 — generalize the :rf.error/resource-scope-unresolved-reference row to "a scope-requiring resource operation", :resource-id optional, resolver id + :where required; update docs/api/re-frame.resources.md, docs/resources/concepts.md, the invalidation how-to, resource skill leaves, docstrings. HOT-ZONE: Spec-Schemas.md + 009-Instrumentation.md are hot-zone files — sequence this PR against other hot-zone work.
5. Dogfood: replace the manual resolve in RealWorld :ui/follow-author-replied (examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/views.cljs:162-184) with {:scope {:from-db :realworld/viewer}} and remove the silent nil guard (loud throw is correct; follow is auth-gated).
6. Acceptance (CLJ/CLJS, handler boundary + dispatch-sync): reference resolves and invalidates only the matching principal (equal tag in another scope untouched); active-owner refetch carries the CONCRETE scope, never the reference map; nil resolution = one scope-resolved nil row + canonical throw + no entry change + no refetch; unregistered id throws before any mutation; throwing resolver propagates with runtime-db unchanged; concrete/global/typo/wrapped-global/host paths stay pinned; cross-scope rejects a supplied :scope, requires :cause, never invokes a resolver; mutation settlement resolves exactly once (counter test: 0 resolver calls on concrete + cross-scope paths, 1 on derived); :rf.resource/invalidated summary carries only the resolved concrete scope. Existing production-mode invalidation suite stays green; no memoization layer, resolver cache, alternate event, or second tag index.
7. FOLLOW-UP (file a separate bead; do NOT smuggle into this fix): docs/resources/concepts.md:429,445 teach {:from-db} on :rf.mutation/execute, but mutation_registry/resolve-scope (mutation_registry.cljc:395-421) canonicalizes literally under a fail-OPEN global default — either the docs stop promising it or execute gains ScopeInput; the nil-policy question (fail-open exec default vs throw) needs its own ruling.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5683 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/5683). invalidate-tags resolves {:from-db} symmetrically with ensure via scope-registry/resolve-scope-input; closed-union rejects :cross-scope?+:scope; nil fail-closed throw; clear-scope refactored onto the helper; RealWorld dogfood; spec/009/016/Spec-Schemas + API doc updated. Gates green (resources JVM 657t, CLJS node 8647t). Follow-up rf2-l11670 filed for :rf.mutation/execute {:from-db}.

title: [correctness-review][xray] App-DB on-box reveal grain (raw?) unwired + config docstring overclaims profile scope (spec-drift)
description:
SURFACE: tools/xray (on-box panel egress reveal grain) — spec/doc drift, NOT a functional leak (fails closed).

DEFECT: The per-(tool,frame) on-box reveal grain that spec 004 describes has no implementation, and the config docstring overclaims the profile's scope. Filed for clarity + xray-specs-current, not as a leak — App-DB fails CLOSED.

CONTEXT (why the prior-review "App-DB ignores :rf.xray/egress-profile" is NOT a bug): spec 015 §373 + spec 013 scope `:rf.xray/egress-profile` to the TRACE-COLLECTOR whole-event `:sensitive?` drop only. On-box panel field-level `:sensitive` redaction is a SEPARATE per-(tool,frame) grain carried by `local-render-value`'s `raw?` arg (spec 004 §Egress §728-736). So App-DB correctly does NOT read the global profile.

THE RESIDUAL DRIFT:
1. `panels/app_db_diff_subs.cljs:305` always calls `local-render-value` at the 2-arity (`raw?` defaults false), and NO operator surface anywhere sets `raw?` true. So the "explicit trusted-local operator act flips the grain to `:rf.egress/local-raw`, carried by `local-render-value`'s `raw?` arg" that spec 004 §730-732 describes has NO implementation — the `raw?` parameter is dead across every `local_render` consumer.
2. `config.cljc:581-589` docstring overclaims: "every value-bearing slot it surfaces on a dev surface ships under this profile ... the trace-collector snapshot feed every panel" — FALSE for App-DB and Resources, which read LIVE frame state (`rf/app-db-value` / epoch records / runtime-db), bypassing the trace-collector profile gate.

FIX SKETCH (either): (i) update spec 004 + the config docstring to state the on-box reveal grain is deferred/unimplemented and the profile governs only the trace collector; OR (ii) wire an operator reveal act for on-box panels (per-frame toggle) that flips `raw?`. Per xray-specs-current rule, spec + code must agree.

ACCEPTANCE: spec 004 + config docstring accurately describe the shipped behaviour (no described-but-absent reveal path; no overclaimed profile scope), OR the reveal grain is wired end-to-end with a test.

title: Correctness review: tools/mcp-base (2026-07-11)
description:
## Scope

Fresh read-only correctness review of `tools/mcp-base` for the 2026-07-11 wave (epic rf2-x76af2). Focus areas mandated by dispatch: **review cap**, **diff encoding**, **envelope markers**, **sensitive scrubbing**, **descriptor manifest**. Also cross-checked consumer wiring in `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` and `tools/story-mcp` where those five primitives are load-bearing. No source edits.

## Inventory

46 tracked paths: 13 CLJC source namespaces, 14 test namespaces, 15 spec contracts, package/config manifests. Reviewed implementation + specs + tests for: `cap`, `diff-encode`, `envelope`, `sensitive`, `descriptor-manifest`, plus supporting `overflow`, `vocab`, `args`, `section-grouping`.

## Verification

- `clojure -M:test` from `tools/mcp-base`: **271 tests / 917 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors**.

## Focus-area verdicts

### 1. Review cap (`cap.cljc`)

**VERIFIED CORRECT.** Prior defect rf2-5rdit (negative `:max-tokens` → negative cap lockout) is fixed: `max-tokens` rejects negatives, sub-1 positives, and non-finite/out-of-range values with `{:rf.mcp/invalid-arg ...}`; consumers gate via `invalid-arg?` before `apply-cap`. Fractional ≥1 floors benignly; only `0` disables (nil). Two-stage `over-cap?` (token sum + char ceiling `cap*8`) closes the per-string quotient-loss hole (many sub-4-char slots). `ResultIO/wire-payload-strings` contract requires every payload-bearing wire slot; pair-mcp `cap.cljs` now appends `JSON.stringify` of `:structuredContent` (rf2-13wbe/ycfu1 class). Regression tests pin negative/fractional/non-finite rejection, char-gate reachability, and structuredContent budgeting.

### 2. Diff encoding (`diff-encode.cljc`)

**VERIFIED CORRECT.** Added-key detection uses `find` (presence), not sentinel values — no spurious patches for unchanged sentinel/nil leaves. Same-length vectors diff element-wise under numeric index paths; length deltas whole-leaf replace (documented grammar limit). Encoder/decoder Malli gates (`validate-patches!` / `validate-sections!`) with value-free EP-0015 diagnostics. Closed marker-body guard `validate-diff-marker-body!` enforces exactly `{:rf.mcp/diff-from :db-before :sections [...]}` before replay (rf2-71kxvb fixed). `assoc-in-safe` / `dissoc-in` surface structured replay failures instead of host exceptions.

### 3. Envelope markers (`envelope.cljc`)

**VERIFIED CORRECT.** Prior cap-bypass hole rf2-j538f7.20 is fixed: `marker-text?` requires BOTH (a) exact leading-key prefix with EDN token terminator (rejects `:rf.mcp/overflowed` lookalikes) AND (b) structural confirmation — parsed closed single-key map with marker key + map body via EOF-exhausted EDN read rejecting tagged literals/trailing forms/extra top-level siblings. Mixed wrappers with a reserved first key plus an unexpected top-level sibling correctly return false. Tests cover both flat and namespaced-map print forms.

### 4. Sensitive scrubbing (`sensitive.cljc`)

**VERIFIED CORRECT.** Fail-closed posture: only boolean `true` drops; malformed truthy stamps drop + bump `malformed-count` + value-free stderr/console warn (never echo stamp payload). `strip-sensitive` single-pass with identity-preserving fast path. `scrub-snapshot` strips `:traces`/`:epochs` only (documented shallow design — app-db redaction remains caller `project-egress` responsibility per EP-0015). Fail-closed single-map slice path routes through caller `strip-fn` so union predicates (e.g. epoch rollup `:rf.epoch/sensitive?`) cannot leak via the non-sequential arm.

### 5. Descriptor manifest (`descriptor-manifest.cljc`)

**VERIFIED CORRECT (intentional governance boundary).** Row projection guards catalogue identity: sorted `:input-keys`, `:gated-input-keys`, `:required` (subset-enforced), `:output?`, `:annotations`, `:typicalTokens`. Drift-check `:changed` rows name per-slot deltas. Deliberately does NOT fingerprint full `outputSchema` nested shape or MCP 2025-11-25 fields (`title`, `icons`, `execution`) — documented in spec as out-of-scope for this gate (wire validity pinned by mcp-conformance SDK harness). Re-filing rf2-d84oqh's outputSchema-fingerprint suggestion would be design debt, not a correctness regression; servers remain pinned to 2025-06-18 protocol docs.

## Dedupe rationale

- **rf2-5rdit** (negative `:max-tokens` lockout): CLOSED/fixed in cap.cljc + consumer invalid-arg surfacing; verified present and tested.
- **rf2-giznxn** (prior clean mcp-base review, 0 findings): same slice, no surviving open defect; this review supersedes for the 2026-07-11 wave with deeper focus-area coverage.
- **rf2-j538f7.20** (marker prefix-only bypass): CLOSED/PR #5589; structural confirmation present in envelope.cljc.
- **rf2-71kxvb** (diff marker body gap): CLOSED/PR #4732; `validate-diff-marker-body!` present.
- **rf2-13wbe** (cursor tags + structuredContent cap): CLOSED; cap contract + tests present.
- **rf2-d84oqh** (descriptor manifest outputSchema fingerprint): CLOSED as CLEAN; intentional catalogue-only gate per spec.
- Targeted open-bead search: no open/in-progress duplicate for cap bypass, diff marker body, sensitive leak, or envelope marker holes on this slice.

## Numbered findings

1. None.

## Acceptance

No implementation work required from this slice review.

title: Make shared PNG assurance validate raster semantics, not just zlib
description:
## Slice and complete inventory

Second-wave correctness review of the complete `examples/_shared` source surface at origin/main `709159ed3`: `README.md` (2,948 bytes), `css/style.css` (9,351), `css/structure.css` (5,232), `img/favicon.svg` (878), `img/og.svg` (2,675), and the served `img/og.png` (283,967; SHA-256 `CF4D79D0E44DA0868637969AC8185C3F030767672F820CEA101DAD1C6EE44804`).

Direct consumers were traced rather than inferred. `check-examples-assets --list` enumerates 35 `index.html` / `*.index.html` hosts: all 35 reference `_shared/img/favicon.svg` and `_shared/img/og.png`; 34 reference `_shared/css/style.css`, with TodoMVC's single stylesheet exemption encoded in `examples/scripts/examples-asset-manifest.cjs`. `style.css` imports `structure.css`. `examples/scripts/examples-staging.cjs` owns the normal `_shared` fan-out used by `serve-example.cjs` and the adapter-smoke orchestrator; `implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-xray-feature-gate.cjs` mirrors the tree for its example-backed surfaces. The static contract owner is `examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs`, with live/negative coverage in `implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs`, staging coverage in `_examples-staging.test.cjs`, and the always-run JS harness CI job.

## Post-remediation evidence

The prior-wave issue `rf2-3fc89f.27` landed in merged PR #5529 / commit `5971e2b25`: it repaired the live XML-illegal comments and replaced a 24-byte PNG header sniff with chunk bounds, CRC, IDAT zlib inflation, IEND, and dimension checks. Related merged work was also checked: PR #3650 (responsive shell and OG re-export), #4320 (CSS `url()` network policy), #5452 (single asset/exception manifest), #5557 (single HTML-reference inventory), and #5389 (earlier `validatePng` branch coverage).

The current artifacts are healthy. Strict `System.Xml.XmlDocument` loads both SVGs with root `svg` in `http://www.w3.org/2000/svg`; Pillow 12 fully loads the shipped PNG as RGB 1200x630. The live asset scan passes all 35 hosts, all scanner tests pass, and all examples-staging tests pass. Shared CSS/README contracts, canonical relative paths, TodoMVC's exception, local-only styling, AA token/focus rules, Cells scoping, and the responsive inline-Xray shell were reviewed with no new live defect found.

## Residual verification risk: zlib inflation is not PNG decoding

`validatePng` still calls a PNG "decodable" after verifying only the chunk envelope and that concatenated IDAT bytes inflate. It never validates the IHDR semantic fields (legal bit-depth/colour-type combinations, compression/filter/interlace methods) or that inflated bytes form the declared raster's complete scanlines with legal filter bytes. The remediation test helper reinforces the gap: `buildPng(1200,630)` labels its output "genuinely valid" but compresses only four bytes for an 8-bit truecolour 1200x630 image, far short of the required pixel/scanline payload.

Two isolated reproductions preserve correct signature, dimensions, chunk bounds, CRCs, zlib stream, and terminal IEND:

1. Change the real PNG's IHDR colour-type byte to `1` (forbidden by the PNG specification) and recompute the IHDR CRC. `validatePng` returns `{ok:true,width:1200,height:630}`; Pillow rejects it as `UnidentifiedImageError` (System.Drawing also rejects it).
2. Keep the real 1200x630 IHDR, replace IDAT with a valid zlib stream that expands to four bytes, write correct CRC/IEND. `validatePng` again returns `ok:true`; Pillow rejects it as `OSError: image file is truncated`.

Expected: the gate's advertised complete/decodable image contract rejects a structurally wrapped but semantically invalid raster. Actual: both non-images pass, so a bad exporter or carefully rewritten corrupt asset can leave the all-35-host gate green while every social preview serves unreadable bytes. The checked-in asset is valid today, so this is an honest P4 assurance gap rather than a fabricated live bug.

## Dedupe evidence

All-status description searches for `validatePng`, `IHDR`, `color type`, `decompressed`, `Pillow`, and image-integrity terms found only closed `rf2-3fc89f.27` and closed branch-coverage task `rf2-bdamni`; neither covers IHDR semantics or scanline geometry. The current children of `rf2-j538f7` contain no image/PNG overlap. Git history and GitHub searches for `IHDR color type`, `PNG decoder examples`, `pixel payload`, `single svg root`, `examples/_shared`, and `shared assets` found no open or merged action beyond the prior work above. This issue is the post-remediation semantic axis that PR #5529's syntactic checks did not implement, not a re-file of its fixed live SVG comments/header-prefix cases.
design: Keep this narrow and explicit. Either (a) define the one canonical PNG encoding the social card is allowed to use (for example 8-bit RGB/RGBA, non-interlaced) and fully validate that format's IHDR fields, exact decompressed scanline length, and per-row filter byte, or (b) use one maintained decoder already appropriate to the Node gate. Do not grow another partial general-purpose PNG parser. Replace the four-byte `buildPng` oracle with a genuinely decodable fixture. Preserve the current shared paths, artwork, staging/manifest ownership, and no-remote-assets posture; no compatibility shim is needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fixture with forbidden IHDR colour type `1` and a recomputed valid IHDR CRC fails `validatePng`/`checkSharedTree` with an actionable IHDR-semantic error.
- Legal bit-depth/colour-type combinations are accepted only when supported; illegal combinations and nonzero/unsupported compression, filter, or interlace methods fail explicitly rather than falling through to `ok:true`.
- A 1200x630 fixture whose IDAT zlib stream expands to only four bytes fails as an incomplete pixel payload; a payload with extra bytes also fails.
- Each decoded scanline has the required byte width and a legal PNG filter byte (0..4); a bad filter fixture fails.
- The positive synthetic fixture is independently valid/decodable and contains the full declared raster payload; tests no longer describe a four-byte payload as a valid 1200x630 PNG.
- The real `examples/_shared/img/og.png` still fully decodes as RGB 1200x630, both SVGs remain strict-XML-valid, and all 35 hosts retain canonical favicon/OG references plus the existing TodoMVC-only CSS exemption.
- `node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs`, `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs`, and `node implementation/scripts/_examples-staging.test.cjs` pass, with negative tests proving each new rejection path.
notes: Audit-only review: no source edits or PR. Verified on worker branch based exactly at origin/main 709159ed3. Current green evidence: asset scan 35/35; check-examples-assets tests all passed; examples-staging tests all passed; strict XML and independent Pillow decode passed for the shipped artifacts. Reproduction used temporary files under the OS temp directory and removed them after decoding.

title: (DEFERRED) public :rf.timer/after managed timer surface — un-defer on named trigger
description: DEFERRED public surface, carved out of rf2-zqefg3.6 (re-scoped 2026-06-11 to a test-only conformance probe; that probe proves the nine-property inheritance and reserves :rf.timer/* in Conventions). DO NOT ACTION until a trigger fires. WHY DEFERRED (the analysis): demand is ZERO today — the debounce/idle/retry-delay class is already served twice: machine :after (the TAUGHT path — guide ch.12 names debounce explicitly; epoch-suppressed; XState-gold-standard-aligned: delayed transitions are machine territory) and HTTP :request-id supersession (changed-input-mid-load, used by realworld :articles/load); :dispatch-later covers fire-and-forget. No example, guide chapter, or skill hand-rolls timer generations. Shipping a third public delay mechanism without a consumer fails the demand bar AND creates an EP-0007 hazard: two public "run this event later" surfaces (:dispatch-later vs :rf.timer/after) and three public debounce mechanisms, each needing a recorded relationship rule. UN-DEFER TRIGGERS (any one): (a) a real consumer needs a cancellable/suppressible STANDALONE delay that is genuinely neither a machine-state timeout nor transport supersession (the test: if modelling it as a machine :after feels like ceremony for a one-off delay with cancellation, the trigger has fired); (b) the EP-0011 graduation review (zqefg3.10) finds the timer row of the work-id table unservable by the probe alone; (c) a skill/guide authoring need where teaching machine-:after-for-debounce is demonstrably the wrong altitude for the simple case. design: KEEP-PARKED (reaffirmed 2026-06-18 via independent source-of-truth verification). No un-park trigger has fired.
