DECISION (operator-delegated 2026-06-18): KEEP PARKED — confirmed. No un-park trigger fired (EP-0011 trigger (b) spent; the 4 in-repo timer uses are periodic loops / machine-scoped).

REAFFIRMED 2026-07-09 (Mike, direct ruling): KEEP PARKED. Do NOT promote a public managed timer surface until a real caller needs a standalone, cancellable/suppressible one-shot delay with a LOGICAL TIMER IDENTITY. Repo evidence still supports the existing trio: :dispatch-later (cheap delayed dispatch — frame-routed, source-stamped, per-frame pending-handle tracked, cleared on frame destroy; NOT raw setTimeout), machine :after (state-scoped timeouts — owns entry/exit lifetime, epoch stale-detection, cancel traces, SSR no-op, reply lowering; XState v5 delayed-transition aligned), and HTTP/resource machinery (request-id supersession / latency / freshness).
REFINED UN-PARK TRIGGERS (any one, all requiring a genuine standalone logical timer): (1) notification auto-dismiss WITH EXPLICIT EARLY CANCEL; (2) a timed undo-window whose commit/cancel is a real timer attempt; (3) standalone debounce where machine :after is demonstrably ceremony AND :dispatch-later + app-level generation-guard is repeated boilerplate.
WATCH SIGNAL (NOT yet a trigger): current docs carry simple toast/notification auto-dismiss examples on :dispatch-later. If they grow into robust notification-stack / manual-dismiss guidance they must EITHER carry an app-level notification id/generation guard OR become the concrete consumer that un-parks this bead.
DOC/EXAMPLE CAVEAT (separate concern, does NOT force the surface): a naive [:dispatch-later {:event [:toast/clear]}] can clear a NEWER toast when notifications overlap — a docs/example correctness matter, fixable with an app-level id/generation guard; it must NOT by itself mint the framework surface.
Conventions reserves :rf.work/timer as a work-id head; the public :rf.timer/* reservation stays DEFERRED (future namespace to add ON promotion, not shipped API). Keep :dispatch-later as the cheap surface unless its semantics fully collapse into the managed surface without adding ceremony to the common case.
PROMOTION SHAPE (settled, if a trigger fires): promote the test-only re-frame.timer-probe to a public :rf.timer/after fx — closed args map, :rf/reply-to, [:rf.work/timer logical-id generation], data-only stale suppression, cancellation-as-data, frame-scoped in-flight registry, frame-destroy/restore cleanup, SSR no-op, trace/error catalogue rows, Spec-Schemas + Conventions updates [HOT-ZONE], facade export/classification, EP-0007 rule-3 three-way-delay vocabulary entry, Property-6 abort/teardown-as-data.
RULING (decision-agent, 2026-07-12): KEEP PARKED. The Codex unpark recommendation is REJECTED; Mike's 2026-07-09 direct ruling stands unmodified, refined triggers unchanged.
WHY: The claimed trigger consumer — the Pattern-WebSocket per-request deadline (examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs :register-request/:clear-request) — is transport-correlation territory: request-id-keyed :in-flight slot + :current-socket? epoch guard, and a fast reply clears the slot so a late timeout is a guarded data no-op. That is exactly the 'transport supersession' class trigger (a) excludes, and it matches none of the three refined 2026-07-09 triggers. It was also already in evidence at BOTH prior rulings (the 2026-06-18 consumer check lists 'websocket timeout' explicitly) — re-litigation, not new demand. The one genuinely novel Codex datum — a fast reply cannot RELEASE its host timer, so N fast-completing requests retain N pending closures until deadline (verified against fx.cljc dispatch-later-timers: no per-timer release; cleanup only on fire/frame-destroy) — is a bounded efficiency cost (default 30s), not a correctness gap; and Pattern-WebSocket.md deliberately pins this correlation as APP-LEVEL, not the framework envelope ('re-frame2 does not ship a managed WebSocket'), so converting the worked example onto a framework-managed timer would blur a pinned boundary. The docs toast point re-litigates what the 2026-07-09 note already ruled a DOC/EXAMPLE CAVEAT that 'must NOT by itself mint the framework surface'. EP-0007 hazard unchanged: second public run-event-later surface + third debounce mechanism with zero qualifying consumer fails the demand bar.
REJECTED: (1) Codex unpark (:rf.timer/after + :rf.timer/cancel now, convert websocket deadline) — no refined trigger fired; consumer is supersession-shaped and was already considered; retention is cost, not correctness. (2) Optional :id/cancel mode on :dispatch-later — violates keep-the-cheap-path-cheap (Codex rejects it too). (3) Machine :after for the request deadline — N concurrent deadlines in one state; per-request machines are the ceremony Pattern-WebSocket bans (all parties agree).
RECORDED FOR PROMOTION TIME (Codex design refinements worth keeping; supplements the existing PROMOTION SHAPE, do NOT act now): (1) do NOT promote re-frame.timer-probe verbatim — runtime must allocate generation (the probe's caller-supplied :generation is a defect to remove) and the 'closed' args map must actually reject surplus keys; (2) ship an explicit idempotent :rf.timer/cancel companion verb (missing id = normal no-op); (3) linearization point = successful token claim — cancellation is an optimization, the token/generation check is the correctness boundary; (4) implementation starting point is the proven token-owned protocols in re-frame.fx/arm-dispatch-later! + re-frame.machines.timer/schedule-after-timer!, dedicated compact [frame-id logical-id] table, not the machine/resources table shapes; (5) 0ms yield stays on :dispatch-later.
WATCH-SIGNAL DATUM (recorded, not a trigger): dispatch-later closures for fast-completing deadlines are retained until expiry (no logical-id release). If a future consumer's timer volume/duration makes this a MEASURED problem, weigh it as supporting evidence when evaluating the refined triggers.

DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): KEEP PARKED — reaffirmed. No un-park trigger has fired; :rf.timer/after stays a test-only probe, not a public surface.

GOOD PRACTICE and ELEGANCE both point the same way: the probe already discharges the nine-property conformance obligation; a public surface adds vocabulary without adding capability.
IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE: No implementation work; the bead stays DEFERRED/parked and open as the un-park marker. value: FAN-OUTS DEFEAT PRE-LOOP GUARDS — a check taken BEFORE a loop does not fence the loops later iterations. Found by rf2-sdeae (P1, #6361, 2026-07-18). rf2-qfrh4 had fenced every epoch-restore SEAM on the exact-ownership token, but three of those seams are fan-outs: the guard ran once, then the loop kept invoking callbacks that could seat a successor mid-flight. Three interleavings were constructed on the same thread, inside the callback, between the read and the write. Sharpest: the quiesce chain first hook (:machines/on-frame-restored!) destroys frame A and seats B; A second hook (:http/abort-in-flight-for-frame!) then aborts B in-flight requests — a dead frames tail mutating a live successor. RULE: when auditing an ownership or liveness guard, ask whether the guarded region contains ITERATION or CALLBACK RE-ENTRY. If it does, the guard must travel INTO the region (widen the token through the loop) rather than gate its entry. FIX SHAPE that worked: an ORDER fix, not a new gate — detach-slots! removes slots in one swap-vals!, THEN aborts the detached values, so no host side effect runs inside the retriable swap. The sibling timers/release-frame! already did this; the work-ledger table was the odd one out, so the fix converged on established local discipline instead of inventing a mechanism. BONUS SIGNAL WORTH COPYING: the adversarial re-entrancy case exposed unbounded amplification — a callback re-entering release-frame! re-read the not-yet-dropped slot and re-aborted it 1101 times in the red run. If a re-entrancy test produces a COUNT rather than a boolean, the count is the evidence. Related: rf2-uhouu (#6339) collapsed two reads into one atomic decision; this is the same discipline in the opposite direction — the decision existed and had to travel.

A DEFECT-WITNESS TEST AND ITS FIX ARE MUTUALLY INVALIDATING — merging both without flipping the witness REDS MAIN, in either order. Cost a P0 red-on-main on 2026-07-24.

THE MECHANISM: a validation pilot reproduces a known hazard and writes it down as a LIVE TEST asserting the CURRENT (broken) behaviour. A separate slice FIXES that hazard. Each PR is green against a main lacking the other. Merge both and the witness test fails, because the defect it documents no longer exists.

THE CONCRETE CASE: the dropdown pilot independently reproduced the ref-composition hazard and shipped `a-behavior-and-a-top-layer-state-on-one-element-lose-a-ref` — a test that PASSES ONLY WHILE THE BUG IS PRESENT. I merged the pilot, then merged the ref-composition fix, and main went red with 2 failures. Every other gate stayed green, so it read like a mystery regression in a slice that had been CLEAN as a PR.

I DESTROYED A LIVE WORKER WORKTREE (2026-07-19) — deterministic branch names collide with HISTORICAL merged PRs.

WHAT HAPPENED: my deferred-cleanup loop removes a worktree when `gh pr list --head worker/<name> --state all` reports MERGED. I derive branch names deterministically from the bead id, so I dispatched rf2-vxgfnd.195 onto `worker/shadow-host-gates-195` — the SAME name a previous session had used for the same bead, whose PR #6030 merged on 2026-07-16. The cleanup matched that historical PR, and removed the live worktree plus the branch (local AND origin) while the worker was mid-run. Work lost, worker orphaned.

WHY THE OBVIOUS GUARDS DID NOT CATCH IT: the worktree was clean (worker had not committed yet) so the dirty-check passed; the PR state was genuinely MERGED so the state-check passed; `--state all` is what made a long-closed PR visible. Every individual condition was satisfied. This is the SECOND time I have removed a running worker worktree (the first was k8l1m), and the deferred-cleanup pattern I adopted after that incident did not prevent this one, because it addressed timing rather than identity.

TWO FIXES, USE BOTH:
1. MAINTAIN AN EXPLICIT LIVE-WORKER SKIP LIST. I dispatch the workers, so I know their worktree names — skip every one still running, unconditionally, before any state check. This is the reliable guard; the PR-state heuristic is the unreliable one.
2. REQUIRE THE MERGED PR TO BE *THIS* WORKTREE WORK, not merely same-named: compare `git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD` against the PR `headRefOid` (`gh pr view <n> --json headRefOid`), or require `mergedAt` to be LATER than the worktree creation. A name match alone proves nothing — bead ids are stable across sessions, so a re-dispatch of any partially-delivered bead reproduces the collision exactly.

GENERAL LESSON: a deterministic naming scheme makes names non-unique ACROSS TIME. Any cleanup keyed on a name will eventually match a historical artefact. Key destructive operations on identity (a SHA, a creation time), never on a name.

ALSO NOTE: a bead can stay legitimately OPEN after a PR citing it merges — #6030 delivered part of rf2-vxgfnd.195 (the final_schedule probe harness) while its four synthetic arms remained. So "a merged PR names this bead" does NOT mean the bead is done, and must never be used to infer cleanup safety either.

ROOT CAUSE (final): BEADS GIT HOOKS AUTO-IMPORT THE JSONL — 'git checkout HEAD -- .beads' DESTROYS CLOSES EVEN WITHOUT AN EXPLICIT 'bd import' (2026-07-25). bd installs tracked hooks at .beads/hooks/post-checkout and .beads/hooks/post-merge that run 'bd hooks run <hook>', which re-imports .beads/issues.jsonl into the Dolt DB. So the mayor's merge routine 'git checkout HEAD -- .beads && git pull --ff-only' does TWO destructive things: the checkout reverts the export (losing any close since the last commit), and then the post-checkout/post-merge hook writes that STALE file back INTO the database, reopening beads that were legitimately closed. Removing my explicit 'bd import' was only half the fix — the hooks do it automatically. CONFIRMED on rf2-a32r7 (closed three times, zero AUDIT-REOPEN notes, resurrected each time) and rf2-kqxe6.17. CORRECT MERGE/CHECKPOINT SEQUENCE — COMMIT BEFORE PULL, never checkout-before-pull: (1) bd export --all -o .beads/issues.jsonl  (2) guard wc -l >= 2000  (3) git add .beads/issues.jsonl && git commit  (4) git pull --rebase  (5) if issues.jsonl conflicts: git checkout --theirs, bd import it, bd export, commit — the documented resolve-then-regenerate, which is the ONE legitimate use of import  (6) git push. Never 'git checkout HEAD -- .beads' while the DB holds uncommitted closes. If a pull must be unblocked, commit the export first. DIAGNOSTIC: a procedure-revert has ZERO AUDIT-REOPEN / MERGED-PR AUDIT notes and reads pre-close; a genuine reviewer reopen names an unmet defect at a code site. Grep before re-closing.

MAYOR DISPATCH DRIFT, caught 2026-07-24 on a reread of the method dispatch-prompt-template. Three things I had been omitting from briefs, in descending order of how much they matter.

1. ⚠️ THE WORKTREE BOUNDARY BLOCK MUST GO IN VERBATIM, AND THE GUARD SCRIPT IS NOT IT. I had been writing "run the worktree guard and report WORKTREE_ROOT" and stopping there. The method says plainly that a start-of-session guard CAN BE FOOLED: some edit-tool path resolution resolves a relative path against the SESSION ROOT rather than the git root, so a write lands in the mayor checkout even after the guard passed — the leak happens mid-session, in one tool call. The real backstop is two things I was not asking for:
   (a) re-verify the git root BEFORE EVERY EDIT — `git -C <worktree> rev-parse --show-toplevel` must print the worktree — and use ABSOLUTE paths under it for every write;
   (b) AFTER WRITING ANY NEW FILE, check BOTH TREES. A new GITIGNORED file leaking into the mayor checkout is INVISIBLE in the worker own git status, so it fails silently. This is the worst case and the one a guard cannot catch.
   On a leak the worker must STOP and report both paths — not repair, commit or push.

2. THE PR BODY NEEDS A SECTION HEADED EXACTLY `## Quality gates`. The verbatim heading is a CONTRACT for automated PR audits, not a style preference. List what ran with counts and exit codes; a skipped gate needs a one-line reason there, because a silent skip fails review. Some workers were doing this spontaneously; it should not depend on their initiative.

3. P1 IS ALWAYS SOLO — one bead, one PR — so it merges on its own green and is never blocked by a cluster-sibling. I bundled TWO P1s (rf2-berc2 + rf2-51d4q) into one dispatch because they were the same defect class in the same files. The surface reasoning was right and one agent SHOULD own that surface; the error was in the SHIPPING shape. The method already covers this case: a tightly-coupled surface is its own SERIAL LANE — one agent, but SEQUENCED PRs, later ones rebasing on the earlier merge. Corrected mid-flight by telling the worker to open a PR per bead.

THE GENERAL LESSON: I re-derived my brief boilerplate from memory each wave and it drifted from the written template. The template exists precisely because these are hard-won and non-obvious. Reread the SIBLING files on the cadence, not just the README — the boundary block and the shape-selection rules live in dispatch-prompt-template.md, which I had not opened this session while writing a dozen briefs.

Worker path-leak mechanism (CONFIRMED 2026-07-17, rf2-r09qj + flagged by rf2-klyw5): a subagent that Reads MAYOR-checkout absolute paths during exploration can have its SUBSEQUENT Edit tool-calls carry that mayor path — so edits land in the mayor checkout, NOT the worktree. Invisible in the worker's OWN git status (the worktree looks clean); visible only from the mayor side. MITIGATION that works: the boundary-block's post-write BOTH-TREES check catches it — the worker self-recovers (git checkout-restore the mayor file, copy completed work into the worktree, verify mayor clean). HARDEN BRIEFS: instruct workers to Read AND Edit only worktree-absolute paths (never the mayor checkout, even for exploration reads), re-verify rev-parse per edit, and run the both-trees check after the first edit + any new file. BEADS CHECKPOINT GUARD — the shell precedence trap that truncated the export (2026-07-25). The mayor's checkpoint guard was written as: if [ $L -gt 500 ] && ! git diff --quiet X || ! git diff --cached --quiet X. Shell parses this as (A && B) || C, so the C clause ALONE was sufficient — the size guard was bypassed entirely and a 0-line issues.jsonl was committed and pushed (2541 deletions, commit 9c79500371). ALWAYS write the guard as a standalone gate first: L=$(wc -l < .beads/issues.jsonl); if [ $L -lt 2000 ]; then echo ABORT; exit; fi — then do the commit unconditionally inside. Never combine the size check with a dirtiness check using && / || on one line. RECOVERY (fast, no data loss — the Dolt DB is unaffected by a JSONL truncation): bd export --all -o <scratchpad>/regen.jsonl, compare 'wc -l' against the last good version (git show <good-sha>:.beads/issues.jsonl | wc -l), cp over .beads/issues.jsonl, commit + push. Restored in commit 3389497f55. ALSO: on this Windows setup 'git cat-file -p ref:path' and 'git show ref:path' piped to Bash wc -l return 0 due to path-separator mangling — verify with PowerShell ((git cat-file -p 'ref:path' | Measure-Object -Line).Lines) or you will misread a healthy file as empty.

GATE EXIT-CODE TRAP, SECOND VARIANT (2026-07-25, found by the rf2-kqxe6.20 worker): a BACKGROUNDED or compound gate invocation can report 'exit code 0' while its log says FAIL. The worker's first scripts/test-fast-pr.sh run was reported exit 0 while the log read 'FAIL CLJS node integration' — the 0 belonged to a TRAILING ECHO in the compound command, not to the runner. This is distinct from the known pipe variant (piping a gate through tail/grep returns the PIPE's status). So the rule needs both halves in briefs: (a) never pipe a gate through tail/grep; (b) never read the exit status of a compound or backgrounded command as the runner's — capture the runner's own status immediately into a variable (rc=$?) on the line after the runner, echo THAT, and cross-check it against the log's own PASS/FAIL lines before believing either. A gate that reports success while its log says FAIL is the single most dangerous failure mode available to a worker, because it produces a confident false green.

Fix is 'npm ci' under implementation/ inside the worktree (NOT a junction into the mayor tree — a junction makes git worktree remove destroy the mayor's real node_modules). AN ORACLE CROSS-CHECK MUST TEST WHAT THE ORACLE ACCEPTS, NOT ONLY WHAT IT REFUSES — otherwise it confirms your intent rather than the truth. Found by the rf2-drpa3.90/.97/.98 worker (PR #6733, 2026-07-23), and it is the sharpest refinement of the verify-the-verifier discipline this project has.

THE SETUP: the Freehand compile checker hand-rolls reader-conditional branch selection, so the established technique is to cross-check that selection against `clojure.tools.reader` at `:features #{:clj}` and `#{:cljs}` — an oracle independent of the code under test.

THE INSIGHT, in the worker own words: "the oracle only caught it because I cross-checked the ACCEPTING cases, not just the refusing ones... that is what separated the reader refuses this from MY RULE refuses this."

THE CONCRETE CASE IT SAVED: `{#?(:clj :a) #?(:clj 1)}` reads as `{}` for `:cljs` under tools.reader — perfectly legal. A naive "refuse any entry with an elided side" rule would have REFUSED it. That is a FALSE-RED, and false-reds are HARDER to notice than false-greens because the tool looks like it is working — it is confidently rejecting something, and nobody investigates a refusal that matches their expectation. The fix was to DROP an entry whose key AND value both elide, matching the real reader. Neither that case nor the companion `{#?(:clj :a) 1 :b #?(:clj 2)}` (which re-pairs to `{1 :b}` for the real reader) appeared anywhere in the bead.

THE RULE FOR ANY ORACLE-BACKED WORK: enumerate BOTH directions before trusting the cross-check —
  (a) cases the oracle REFUSES that your rule must also refuse (guards against false-green), AND
  (b) cases the oracle ACCEPTS that your rule must NOT refuse (guards against false-red / over-refusal).
Only (a) is the instinctive half, and only (a) is what a bead usually enumerates. A cross-check limited to (a) is not an independent oracle at all — it is a restatement of the intent you already had.

RELATED, SAME FAMILY, ALREADY RECORDED HERE: a probe that has never flagged anything has not been tested; run it against a KNOWN-PRESENT and a KNOWN-ABSENT instance. A blanket mutation that reds three fixtures while leaving two green certifies falsifiability it has not established. A guard proven on cases can still fail on SEQUENCES. This adds the missing axis: a guard proven on refusals can still fail on ACCEPTANCES.

BRIEF LANGUAGE THAT WORKS: "cross-check against <independent oracle>, and enumerate what it ACCEPTS as well as what it refuses — a rule that only reproduces your intended refusals has not been checked against anything."

TRUE-CONCLUSION-DEAD-REASONING — a documented defect class, seen twice on 2026-07-19 and subtler than plain drift.

DEFINITION: a document states a correct conclusion resting on an inference that has since been invalidated. Nothing looks wrong — the conclusion checks out — so a reviewer confirms the conclusion and moves on. But the NEXT reader follows the stated reason, finds it false, and "corrects" the conclusion in the wrong direction. The rot is in the justification, not the claim.

INSTANCE 1 (rf2-0qsp5, #6386): spec/005-StateMachines.md derived :rf.machine/join-dispatch target protection FROM its REJECT-tier membership. Worker verdict: "The conclusion is true; the inference is precisely what the split invalidated." Preserving the reasoning would have re-merged the two fx policies the next time anyone extended it.

INSTANCE 2 (rf2-vxgfnd.188, #6391, worse): the canonical W1 rule table declared SEVEN verbs unavailable — ui/adapter, local, effect, ui/event, ui/handler, ui/render-fn, ui/dispatch-fn. ALL SEVEN SHIP, exported from ui.cljc. MIG-16/17/18 "this gates" conclusions stayed TRUE, but the reason inverted: from "the verb has not shipped yet" to "the decision belongs to the human". Retiering alone would have let the next reader check whether S3 shipped, find it had, and UNGATE RULES THAT MUST STAY GATED. The worker rewrote the reasons and left the tiers.

HOW TO CATCH IT: when reconciling a document against code, verify the DERIVATION, not just the conclusion. Ask "if the stated reason were false, would the conclusion change?" If yes and the reason IS false, the conclusion is correct by luck and the next edit will break it.
HOW TO FIX IT: rewrite the reason, keep the conclusion. Do NOT retier/restate/delete the conclusion just because its stated basis collapsed.

PIPING A GATE INTO tail OR grep DISCARDS ITS EXIT CODE — a false-green generator affecting EVERY worker. Found 2026-07-24 by the worker whose PR it burned, and refined by that same worker afterwards.

THE MECHANISM: `npm run test:browser | tail -20` exits with the status of `tail`, not the runner. A worker reads "0 failures, 0 errors", sees a zero exit, reports green. The runner had exited NON-ZERO the whole time.

THE BRIEFED FORM — REQUIRE THIS IN EVERY DISPATCH:
  npm run test:browser > /tmp/gate.log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?"; tail -20 /tmp/gate.log
Capture to a file, ECHO THE EXIT CODE, then read. A worker reporting a gate green must include the EXIT CODE, not just the counts.

⚠️ GREP IS WORSE THAN TAIL, not equivalent. Tail masks the exit code; grep masks the exit code AND hides the explanatory line — because a pattern chosen BEFORE you know what the failure looks like cannot match it. The real message here was "cljs.test summary was green, but the browser emitted 1 uncaught pageerror(s)" and it matched none of the workers `FAIL|failures` patterns. Capture-then-read fixes both: the file keeps everything and you can grep it as many times as the diagnosis needs.

⚠️ SCOPE THE COMPANION RULE CORRECTLY — do NOT over-generalise it. implementation/scripts/run-browser-tests.cjs fails a run on ANY uncaught pageerror even when every assertion passes (rf2-mwx08). That is BROWSER-LANE-SPECIFIC; the JVM and node lanes have no equivalent, and there the summary IS the verdict. State that distinction in briefs, or workers will start distrusting counts everywhere and re-derive exit codes from scratch each time. THE EXIT CODE IS THE UNIVERSAL ANSWER; the pageerror rule is merely why a green summary was never sufficient in that one lane.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY FALSE GREEN: the test summary is GENUINELY green. cljs.test reported 0F 0E inside a job that failed. Every human-readable signal says pass; the failure lives only in the discarded exit code.

A DISCIPLINE THAT PROVABLY WORKED, worth keeping: my brief for the fix DELIBERATELY REFUSED TO NAME A CAUSE (per the standing symptoms-not-causes rule, adopted after three of my asserted causes were wrong). A WORKTREE YOU DID NOT EXPLICITLY DISPATCH MAY BE YOUR OWN WORKER SPAWNING A SECOND WORKTREE — not a concurrent session. Misdiagnosed 2026-07-24. I dispatched a 4-bead cluster to ONE worker; it did 3 beads in worktree A (PR one) then created worktree B for the 4th bead (PR two). My hygiene scan found worktree B, had no record of creating it, and I concluded a concurrent session was also dispatching workers. WRONG — it was my own worker branching per bead. THE COST: the false belief made me over-cautious about that surface being externally contested. THE DISCRIMINATOR before concluding concurrent-session: a branch named worker/<desc>-<beadid> whose bead you assigned to a live worker IS that worker, even as a second worktree. Check worker completion reports and open PRs first — a worker report names every worktree and PR it created. Track by BEAD ownership (who did I give this bead to), never by worktree count: one worker is NOT necessarily one worktree or one PR. The genuinely-separate process here (the pr-audit loop) FILES beads, it does not dispatch code-editing workers, so it never contests a code surface. No harm done — I correctly did not touch the worktree or re-dispatch the bead.

NEVER dispatch two workers to the SAME git worktree/branch concurrently — even for two DIFFERENT fixes both needed on one PR. They share the worktree index + merge state and corrupt each other. Observed 2026-07-07: a bead-id-leak fix-worker AND a docs-reconciliation merge-worker both sent to the lxwpob #5234 worktree (worker/frame-lifecycle-collapse-rf2-lxwpob) -> the merge-worker's git merge origin/main collided with the fix-worker's concurrent commit, left the worktree stuck mid-conflict. Recovered ONLY because the merge happened to capture both commits (parents = both), but it was fragile. RULE: when a PR branch needs a second fix, SEQUENCE it — dispatch the second worker only AFTER the first has pushed and you have verified; or fold both into one worker's brief. One worktree = one live worker, always.

NEW "Ran 0 tests" VARIANT — `clojure -M:test -v ns/a ns/b ns/c` SILENTLY RUNS ONLY THE FIRST VAR. Found by the rf2-vy2hj/z53ph worker (#6419) on 2026-07-19, caught only because it noticed an ASSERTION COUNT OF 6 WHERE 16 WERE EXPECTED. Multi-var selection does not error, does not warn — it just quietly ignores every var after the first, and the run reports green.
RULE: verify each var INDIVIDUALLY, or verify the expected assertion count. Never trust a multi-var `-v` invocation to have run what you listed.

THIS IS THE FOURTH DISTINCT WAY "green" HAS MEANT "nothing ran" in this repo:
  1. A bare `clojure -M:test -n <ns>` from implementation/ silently runs 0 tests and prints "Ran 0 tests".
  2. A CLJS runner selecting nothing after a namespace rename (the :ns-regexp "cljs-test$" trap — renaming *-cljs-test to *-test deletes it from the suite silently).
  3. A clojure.test MAP FIXTURE — a map is IFn, so {:before f} composes to a fn returning nil and the body never runs. (cljs.test DOES support map fixtures; the trap is clojure.test only.)
  4. THIS: multi-var `-v ns/a ns/b ns/c` running only ns/a.
THE ONLY RELIABLE DEFENCE, and it works against all four: demand a NON-ZERO AND PLAUSIBLE count, and know roughly what the count should be. #6419 caught this by expecting 16 and seeing 6. A worker who only checked "non-zero" would have shipped it.

ALSO FROM #6419, the counterpart discipline: it VACUITY-PROBED by flipping an assertion and confirming the FULL gate redded NAMING ITS TEST, then restored and verified the tree byte-identical. That probe is what distinguishes "my namespace ran and passed" from "my namespace was never selected".

CROSS-MODE SNAPSHOT TESTS ON outerHTML ARE A FALSE NEGATIVE — the two emitters write attributes in DIFFERENT ORDER. Found 2026-07-24 by the F5h virtual-table pilot, whose first browser parity row failed on this and nothing else.

THE OBSERVATION: [:span.acme-cell {:role ... :data-col ...}] renders its attributes as `class role data-col` INTERPRETED and `role data-col class` COMPILED — the sugar class is written FIRST by one emitter and LAST by the other. Nothing in a browser observes this; the structural trees are identical because attrs are a map; and no user-visible behaviour differs.

⚠️ BUT IT MAKES outerHTML STRING EQUALITY USELESS FOR CROSS-MODE PARITY. A snapshot test comparing rendered HTML strings across interpreted and compiled will fail for a reason that means nothing, and — worse — the obvious "fix" is to loosen the comparison, which throws away the real coverage.

THE RIGHT ORACLE, which the pilot adopted: compare a DOM SHAPE — tag, SORTED attribute map, text, and children in document order. That is STRICTER than string equality in every way that matters and blind only to write order. Do not normalise by sorting the HTML string; extract the structure and compare it.

GENERALISES: whenever two independent code paths produce the same semantic artefact, the serialised form may differ in ways the semantics do not. Before asserting equality on a SERIALISATION, ask whether the serialiser guarantees a canonical order. If it does not, compare the STRUCTURE, not its rendering. Same family as the earlier finding that a per-line census cannot see a claim that wraps — the representation carries incidental detail the assertion should not depend on.

MERGE-LOOP JSONL CHECKOUT SILENTLY REVERTS WORKER BEAD CLOSES (observed 2026-07-25, re-confirmed). The mayor merge loop does 'git checkout HEAD -- .beads' before 'git pull --ff-only' (needed: an uncommitted issues.jsonl aborts the pull and silently freezes HEAD). But that checkout DISCARDS the bd auto-export of any close a worker performed since the last commit — and a later 'bd import' of the reverted file resurrects the bead as open/in_progress. Observed: rf2-kqxe6.17 and rf2-b617w both closed by their worker on PR #6895, both back to in_progress after the post-merge checkout; misdiagnosable as a reviewer reopen. MITIGATION: after every merge+pull, re-verify the merged PR's beads with 'bd show' and re-close any that reverted, citing the merge commit. Better: commit the .beads export BEFORE merging rather than checking it out — commit-before-pull, never checkout-before-pull, when a worker has just closed something. DISTINGUISH FROM A REAL REVIEWER REOPEN: a genuine reopen carries a MERGED-PR AUDIT / AUDIT-REOPEN note naming an unmet defect at a code site; a checkout-race revert has NO such note and the bead simply reads in_progress with its pre-close state.

Brief SYMPTOMS not CAUSES in CI-fix/bug dispatches (learned 2026-07-17, 3 recurrences). My fix-briefs asserted a specific CAUSE and were wrong each time; the workers correctly verified past me: (1) rf2-1hob1 — I said surface=reactive.cljc, worker STOPPED at the fence: real surface=evidence.cljc (re-dispatched correctly). (2) rf2-v2j8e #6143 — I said 'arity + manifest broke'; worker found the arity gate was already GREEN (both image fns 1-arg, no 4-arg call-site) — only the manifest :fn→:macro kind-drift was real. (3) rf2-vxgfnd.95.5 #6142 G-1 — I said 'emit regression shifted the classes-str lowering'; worker proved the emit was byte-identical with/without the change — real cause was the G-1 control REGEX couldn't cross a nested ')'. FIX: in fix-briefs, state the SYMPTOM (which gate, the log line, the diff surface) + 'diagnose the cause, run the ACTUAL failing gate locally, it may be a stale control/test not the feature' — do NOT assert 'the cause is X'. WSL bash.exe DOUBLE-EXPANDS a -c command string. Found by rf2-sefx0 (#6357, 2026-07-18) with a decisive probe: bash -lc with FOO=hello then printf of the escaped dollar-FOO prints the literal dollar-FOO under Git Bash (single pass) but prints hello under WSL bash (an outer pass already substituted it). CONSEQUENCE: any -c string that READS BACK a variable the SAME string assigns is broken under WSL — the outer pass substitutes the not-yet-assigned name to empty. That is how a PATH= assignment referencing a FIXTURE_DIR assigned immediately to its left silently produced /bin:<real PATH>, so stub executables were never found and 15 of 15 cases failed before reaching the code under test. Pre-existing vars (PWD, PATH) survive both passes, which is why the bug looks selective. FIX SHAPE: build one env-prefixed command whose every dollar-NAME already exists in the parent environment; let the child script read the rest from its own environment rather than from the command string. DISPROVED on the way: the semicolon separator is fine, and double-quoting is fine — do not chase those. TESTING LESSON (the important half): a BEHAVIOURAL test for this cannot protect you, because Git Bash and the Ubuntu CI runner both expand ONCE — a reintroduced self-reference stays green on CI while breaking only for Windows contributors. sefx0 pinned the STRUCTURE instead (assert the command references only pre-existing variables) with a non-vacuity guard. Generalise: when a defect is invisible on the platform your CI runs, a structural pin beats a behavioural one.

CLEANUP MUST PARSE `git worktree list`, NEVER CONSTRUCT NAMES (2026-07-19, second instance of this root cause in one session).

BUG: my hygiene loop derived a worktree branch as "worker/<dirname>" and derived the worktree from a branch by the same rule. WORKTREE DIRECTORY NAMES AND BRANCH NAMES ARE INDEPENDENT. Concrete case in this repo: the directory re-frame2-worktrees/core-handbook-html has branch worker/codex-audit-live checked out. Consequences of the wrong derivation, both live:
  (a) core-handbook-html resolved against a NONEXISTENT branch worker/core-handbook-html -> no PR found -> any decision keyed on that lookup is meaningless, and had a same-named PR existed it would have acted on the WRONG branch.
  (b) worker/codex-audit-live appeared to have NO worktree -> nominated for deletion WHILE CHECKED OUT. A belt-and-braces re-check (git worktree list | grep -c <branch>) aborted it; the primary scan was simply wrong.
Also missed: a detached-HEAD worktree (fix-6365-consumers) has NO branch at all, so any name-derived lookup silently returns nothing rather than erroring.

CORRECT SOURCE: `git worktree list` prints "<path> <sha> [<branch>]" or "(detached HEAD)". PARSE THAT. Path and branch are BOTH given — never construct either from the other, and handle the detached case explicitly.

SAME ROOT CAUSE AS THE WORKTREE I DESTROYED EARLIER TONIGHT (see memory: i-destroyed-a-live-worker-worktree): there I keyed a destructive action on a BRANCH NAME that collided with a historical merged PR. Both bugs are one mistake — DERIVING IDENTITY FROM A NAME INSTEAD OF READING IT. Names are not unique across time (bead ids repeat across sessions) and not unique across dimensions (dirname != branch). Key destructive operations on read identity: the SHA, the parsed branch, the PR headRefOid.

STANDING CHECKLIST for any destructive worktree/branch operation:
  1. Live-worker skip list first, unconditionally.
  2. Parse identity from `git worktree list`; never construct.
  3. Require merged-PR headRefOid == worktree HEAD before removal (name match proves nothing).
  4. Require 0 commits ahead of origin/main OR state==MERGED before branch deletion.
  5. Canary `ls implementation/node_modules | wc -l` (baseline 101) before and after every batch.
  6. Re-verify immediately before the destructive call; if the re-check disagrees with the scan, ABORT and investigate — the scan is the thing that is wrong.

MAYOR CI-merge gotcha: gh's statusCheckRollup includes STALE entries from superseded commits — when a worker force-pushes a fix, the prior commit's in-progress checks become conclusion=CANCELLED and its aggregates (e.g. 'Lint required','All required checks passed') linger as FAILURE in the rollup. A naive 'any conclusion!=SUCCESS' filter reads these as failures. For the merge decision use the DEDUPED latest-per-check view: 'gh pr checks <PR>' (pass/pending/fail/skipping per check). Merge only on 0 fail AND 0 pending there. Confirm ambiguity by checking a specific check has both a CANCELLED and a SUCCESS entry (latest wins).

THE SITUATION: my hygiene pass reaps worktrees that are 0 commits ahead of main, clean, and have no PR — the profile of a worker that never started. That is correct for STALE ones. But a worker that started SECONDS AGO has exactly the same profile: it has created its worktree and not yet committed anything. A worktree named pr-audit-6756, belonging to a DIFFERENT session audit loop, sat at 0-ahead/clean/no-PR while actively running.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS FRESHNESS, NOT SHAPE. A dead-stale worktree is parked on an OLD main commit and its files have not been touched in hours. A live one sits at or near CURRENT origin/main and has filesystem activity within minutes.

ADD TO THE STANDING CHECKLIST, as a rule that fires BEFORE any 0-commit removal:
  (a) Is HEAD at or very near current origin/main? Stale ones are behind by many commits — check `git -C <wt> rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main`. A large number means genuinely abandoned; ~0 means it just branched.
  (b) Any filesystem activity in the last ~30 minutes (excluding node_modules and .git)? `find <wt> -maxdepth 2 -newermt "-30 minutes"`. If yes, IT IS LIVE — skip unconditionally.
  (c) Is the worktree one I dispatched this session? If I cannot account for it, assume ANOTHER SESSION owns it and skip. Concurrent sessions independently create worker/* worktrees and branches in this repo; my dispatch list is not the full roster.

⚠️ THIS IS THE THIRD TIME THE SAME ROOT CAUSE HAS THREATENED LIVE WORK: I destroyed a live worktree by matching a HISTORICAL merged PR on a branch NAME, and separately nominated a checked-out branch for deletion by deriving the worktree from the branch name. All three are the same mistake — INFERRING LIVENESS OR IDENTITY FROM A PROPERTY THAT DOES NOT CARRY IT. A name is not identity; a commit count is not liveness.

STANDING RULE, unchanged and reinforced: reaping is only ever safe on (1) a merged PR whose headRefOid EQUALS the worktree HEAD, or (2) a worktree that is BOTH zero-commit AND demonstrably cold AND accounted for. When in doubt, leave it — an unreaped worktree costs disk; a reaped live one costs a worker its work.

MY WORKTREE-BOUNDARY BLOCK CAUSES A CI FAILURE — add the counter-warning to every dispatch. On 2026-07-18 THREE PRs (#6360 sy7zr, #6361 sdeae, #6362 vxgfnd.290) all failed the same gate, "No hardcoded personal/home paths" (scripts/check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh, run by .github/workflows/portability.yml). The gate passes clean on main, so each PR genuinely introduced the path. ROOT CAUSE IS MINE: the mandatory worktree-boundary block repeats the literal absolute path C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/<name> four or five times in every brief, and workers paste it into test fixtures and helper code. The block is necessary — it prevents edits landing in the mayor checkout — but it hands the worker the exact string the portability gate forbids. FIX, now standard in every editing dispatch: add a line saying the worktree path is for NAVIGATION ONLY and must never appear in committed content; resolve paths at runtime instead (relative fixtures, System/getProperty user.dir, a temp dir, or whatever the surrounding tests already do); and note that scripts/check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh git-greps the tracked tree and will block the PR. Also worth saying explicitly: do NOT fix it by weakening or allow-listing the gate. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE THREE PRs: the gate exists because Mike is on Windows and the ecosystem is on Mac/Linux — a committed personal path is a portability defect for every contributor, not a cosmetic one.

MAYOR OPS: timeout-guard every test-heavy worker dispatch. A worker can ship a NON-TERMINATING fix (rf2-um6d9: a stranded flows fix had (recur (inc i)) lexically inside the inner loop [j ...], rebinding j not i → infinite oscillation) that makes the JVM/CLJS test suite never complete and silently burns the box (~9 cores, 5+ CPU-hours), masquerading as 'slow CI' for an entire session. DETECTION: a hung-but-IN_PROGRESS worker = check the worktree (uncommitted work + 0 commits + no PR across many ticks) AND per-process CPU: CPU-seconds >> wall-minutes (CPU-HOURS in wall-MINUTES, cores pegged) = runaway, not slow. RECOVERY: TaskStop the agent (kills its child JVM), verify children died (an orphaned node-test process may survive → Stop-Process it), then re-dispatch a FRESH worker that (a) distrusts the stranded fix, (b) hard-caps EVERY test run with 'timeout 180 clojure -M:test' / 'timeout 540 npm run test:cljs' so a runaway is caught in <3min not 5 CPU-hours, (c) is authorized to return a root-cause writeup instead of forcing a fix. Make timeout-guards STANDARD in test-heavy dispatch briefs.

Event-handling pipeline atomicity (Mike CONFIRMED 2026-05-24). Architecture: interceptors (incl. the path std-interceptor) mutate the :db/:fx EFFECTS in interceptor context; app-db gets a SINGLE deferred install only after the ENTIRE chain (all :after interceptors + the flow transform) is done. Flows run at the OUTERMOST :after (framework-prepended :rf/flows, fires last) because flows read full-app-db :inputs and path's :after reshapes :db. CONTRACT: ANY throw BEFORE install (cofx, handler, interceptor :after, flow) => the deferred install simply does NOT happen => app-db UNCHANGED, NO :rf.event/db-changed, NO :fx. No partial commit (a flow throw must NOT commit prior flows' writes). The :db install is the atomic commit boundary. The ONLY post-commit stage is :fx: an fx throw surfaces an error but does NOT wind back app-db (fx side-effects http/nav/dispatch may already have fired and are irreversible). Uniform: flow-throw behaves like every other pre-install throw.

git rm --cached DOES NOT PROTECT FILES FROM A LATER CHECKOUT — and this will bite rf2-vxgfnd.99.1 at 85 files. Found by the ai/decisions untracking worker (#6424) on 2026-07-19, in its own worktree.

THE HAZARD: `git rm --cached` leaves the file on disk IN THE BRANCH WHERE IT RUNS — but the COMMIT RECORDS A DELETION. Any later rebase, checkout, or `git reset --hard` ACROSS that commit removes the working-tree copies too, silently and with no warning. The worker rebased onto post-#6422 main and its four dossiers vanished from disk; it caught this only on a final on-disk verification and restored them.
⚠️ THE SAME THING HAPPENS IN EVERY OTHER CHECKOUT WHEN THE COMMIT MERGES. The mayor loop `git reset --hard origin/main` after a merge will delete the operator working copies. On 2026-07-19 I backed the four dossiers up to the scratchpad BEFORE merging #6424 and restored them after, so they end up UNTRACKED BUT PRESENT — which is what "should not be tracked" means. "Untrack" is not "delete".

⚠️ rf2-vxgfnd.99.1 WILL HIT THIS AT 85 FILES (ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis + new-substrate-codex). Its brief MUST carry:
  1. Back up the full tracked ai/ set to a location OUTSIDE the repo before the untracking commit.
  2. A POST-REBASE ON-DISK RE-VERIFICATION step — after any rebase or checkout, confirm the files are still present, not just that the index is right.
  3. The same restore step in the mayor merge sequence, or the operator local working material disappears from every checkout that pulls.
  4. State explicitly whether the operator wants them KEPT on disk or genuinely DELETED — do not infer. Mike instruction was "this path should NOT be tracked", which is about the index, not the filesystem.

GENERAL FORM: an index-only operation still produces a tree-changing commit. Whenever you `git rm --cached` anything a human is still using as working material, the deletion propagates to every working tree that later checks out that commit. Back it up first; verify on disk afterwards; and say plainly to the operator that the files will vanish from their checkout unless restored.

DISPATCH BRIEF FIX (mayor, 2026-07-25): three workers in one session ended their turn with work committed-but-unpushed and NO PR, each waiting for a long local gate (scripts/test-fast-pr.sh spine) to finish first. The instruction 'do not end your turn with uncommitted work' is NOT sufficient — workers read it as satisfied by a local commit. Every editing brief must instead say, in this order and with the reasons: (1) PUSH as you go, not at the end, because pushed commits are the only durable worker state and a worker that dies mid-run takes local commits with it; (2) OPEN THE PR as soon as commits exist, because a PR is how work becomes visible to the merge gate and is NOT a claim of green — state any still-running gate in the '## Quality gates' section as reliance-on-CI, which is acceptable, whereas a silent omission is not; (3) the merge decision is CI's, not the worker's local run, so if a gate later reds it is a fix-worker on the existing branch and needed no waiting. Recovery when it happens: SendMessage-resume the SAME worker (it holds the branch and worktree; never dispatch a second worker onto one branch). Pair this with the two log hygiene rules workers also miss: capture gate output to a WORKTREE-LOCAL path (the machine temp dir is shared, so two concurrent workers writing one log path read each other's green), and echo the exit code explicitly (piping a gate into tail/grep returns the PIPE's status, not the runner's, so a failed run reads as '0 failures').

REAGENT 2.0.1 SWALLOWS :on-recoverable-error — hydration error-capture harnesses built on reagent.dom.client/hydrate-root are VACUOUS. Found by the rf2-53lsj worker (#6407) on 2026-07-19, in its OWN test harness, before shipping. Reagent destructures :on-recoverable-error and NEVER PASSES IT to React hydrateRoot, so the callback fires for nothing: the harness captured NOTHING on either input and passed identically on broken and fixed HTML. Driving React hydrateRoot DIRECTLY, React 19 correctly reports the mismatch ("Hydration failed... + revenue / - :revenue").
RULE: to assert on hydration mismatches, call React hydrateRoot directly. Do not route through Reagent for error capture. And whatever harness you use, PROVE IT CAPTURES: feed it known-bad input and confirm it reports, before trusting a green on good input.
SECOND FINDING FROM THE SAME PR, easy to get backwards: Reagent renders a keyword/symbol child via (name x), which DROPS THE NAMESPACE — :a/b renders as "b", not "a/b". A JVM emitter fix that merely strips the leading colon would emit "a/b" and leave the hosts FURTHER apart while appearing closer. Namespaced symbols diverge identically. Always diff the actual BYTES against the client, never reason about the shape.

MERGE-LOOP HAZARD — I remove a worker worktree the instant its PR merges, but the WORKER MAY STILL BE RUNNING. On 2026-07-19 rf2-k8l1m reported: "The PR was merged by you, not me... EP-0002 carried-frame pattern for DEFERRED dispatch (event handlers / async): a React :on-click (or any callback firing LATER) runs OUTSIDE the render's dynamic extent and any with-frame scope, so a bare (rf/dispatch [...]) resolves no frame -> :rf.error/no-frame-context (runtime never synthesises a frame from absence). FIX: carry the frame into the deferred dispatch — capture it at RENDER time via (:dispatch (rf/frame-handle)) (the reg-view resolves the frame-provider's frame through React context during render; the handle closes over it), OR default {:frame fid} for single-frame apps. Used for the reagent adapter testbed + SCI playground smokes (#3662). UIx/Helix use the same frame-handle pattern.

Fresh worker worktrees revert bead claims: a new worktree checks out a stale-content/new-mtime .beads/issues.jsonl, and the FIRST bd invocation inside it re-imports that stale JSONL into the shared dolt DB, clobbering any claims/closes made between 'git worktree add' and the worker's first bd call. Rule: claim beads AND commit .beads/issues.jsonl BEFORE creating worker worktrees; re-verify claims/closes after a wave of new worktrees comes online.

BACKLOG COUNTING — `bd list --status=open` EXCLUDES EPIC CHILDREN; `bd ready` includes them. On 2026-07-19 I reported "backlog 49" for many hours while `bd ready --limit 0` held 70. The 23-bead gap was entirely dotted epic-child ids (rf2-vxgfnd.141, .143, .164, .166, .167, .176, .188, .195, .196, .249, .271, .292, .295, .296, .97, .97.1, rf2-6ajm6z.1) plus five (TRIGGER-GATED) P4s. THIS IS THE SECOND OCCURRENCE of the same failure — the existing memory recount-ready-backlog-each-tick records under-saturating at 1-3 workers while 108 beads were ready. Same cause both times: a count that silently omits a whole class.

THE COUNT TO USE: `bd ready --limit 0 | awk $1=="○"{print $2} | sort -u | wc -l` — field-based, on the ready list, which is the pool that matters for dispatch. Do NOT count `bd list --status=open`, and do NOT grep -c on a bare glyph.

BD CONFIG UNSET LIES ABOUT CUSTOM STATUSES (found 2026-07-25, rf2-gtynf). 'bd config unset status.custom' reports SUCCESS and a following 'bd config get status.custom' then reads '(not set)' — but the status is NOT retired: 'bd statuses' still lists it, and a bead can still be moved into it (exit 0). The only thing that actually retires a custom status is 'bd config set status.custom ""' (explicit empty string). DETECTION: 'bd statuses' disagreeing with 'bd config get' is the tell — trust 'bd statuses' and an actual move attempt, never the config read. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS BEAD: status.custom lives ONLY in the Dolt DB, never in tracked config, which is the same shape as the issue-prefix trap (rf2-cchlf). A fresh clone has no custom statuses, so 'bd bootstrap' REJECTS any exported row carrying one — proved end-to-end: a DB with the custom status accepted a bead into it, exported, and a fresh 'bd bootstrap --yes' of that export failed exit 1. So a custom status is a fresh-clone bootstrap landmine, not a cosmetic preference. GENERAL RULE: after any bd config mutation, verify with the command that READS THE BEHAVIOUR (bd statuses, an actual state transition) rather than the command that reads the setting — this tool has at least two settings where the config read and the effective behaviour disagree.

CLJS EMITS NO ARITY CHECK FOR A SINGLE-FIXED-ARITY defn — a wrong-arity call does NOT throw, it silently BINDS THE WRONG THING. Measured 2026-07-24 by the rf2-drpa3.128 worker while building the regression test for a shipped arity bug.

THE CASE: `note-failing-view!` is `[thrown view-id]`. A caller passed ONE argument. On the JVM that is an ArityException. IN CLJS IT IS NOT AN ERROR AT ALL — `view-id` landed in the `thrown` position and `thrown` became the only bound arg.

⚠️ WHAT MADE IT INVISIBLE, and this is the generalisable part: the value was then used as a WEAKMAP KEY. A CLJS Keyword IS an object, so the guard `attributable?` ACCEPTED it. The write succeeded against the wrong key. The real exception therefore carried no note, and the error report shipped `unknown-view` with `:loss {:reason :failing-view-unobserved}` — in the worker phrase, "A CONFIDENT nobody-saw-the-thrower FOR A PLAINLY OBSERVED FAILURE."

That is worse than a crash: the system emits a DEFINITE NEGATIVE about something it plainly witnessed, and every downstream consumer believes it.

THREE RULES THAT FALL OUT:
1. In .cljc, do NOT rely on arity errors to catch a wrong-arity call — the JVM raises, CLJS does not. A cross-host fix green on the JVM has NOT been exercised on CLJS (see also identical-on-a-keyword-literal, the same asymmetry in a different guise).
2. A TYPE/SHAPE GUARD THAT ACCEPTS TOO MUCH TURNS A WRONG-ARITY BUG INTO A WRONG-DATA BUG. `attributable?` was doing its job — a Keyword genuinely is a valid WeakMap key. When a guard exists to reject non-objects, it will not notice the object is the WRONG object. Prefer a guard that asserts the value IS WHAT IT SHOULD BE, not merely that it CAN be used.
3. ⚠️ WHEN TESTING SUCH A BUG, "SOMETHING WENT WRONG" IS NOT AN ASSERTION. The defect produces a well-formed report with the wrong content. A test asserting a throw, or an error, or a non-empty report, PASSES AGAINST THE DEFECT. Assert the ATTRIBUTED IDENTITY.

MAYOR NOTE: my brief asserted the runtime consequence was "the seam itself throws while a render throw is unwinding". That was JVM-shaped and WRONG on the host where the bug lived. The worker verified past me and said so. This is the standing symptoms-not-causes lesson again — I described a CAUSE I had not measured, and the correct brief would have said only "this path is untested; determine what the defect actually does on each host."

HTTP 504' — NO test body runs. These show up in gh pr checks as RED checks (JVM ssr/xray/routing/pair-mcp, Lint/manifest, browser-test, wire-vocab, etc.) that look like REAL deterministic failures and even RECUR across reruns/commits because the outage window spans them. dispatch-id uniqueness: the portable trace contract (re_frame/trace/projection.cljc:182 + pair-mcp spec 003:2486) only guarantees a :rf.trace/dispatch-id is unique WITHIN a frame -- cascades group by [frame dispatch-id], not dispatch-id alone. BUT the current runtime over-delivers: router.cljc allocates ids from a process-GLOBAL monotonic counter (defonce dispatch-counter, swap! inc), so cross-frame same-id collisions essentially never happen today. This makes any consumer that keys cascade events / trace-events by dispatch-id ALONE (rf2-1we9fa: the pair preload cascade-bundle-events did exactly this) a LATENT bug -- correct against the global-counter accident, broken against the contract. It flips latent->LIVE the moment id allocation honors the per-frame contract, which EP-0010 (deterministic replay ids) and EP-0013 (N realms in one page, per-realm/per-frame counters) will introduce. Reagent's get-react-key (reagent2.impl.template L407) only reads :key meta from VECTORS. ^{:key k} attached to a function-call list form (e.g. ^{:key g} (group-section g …)) is lost on evaluation — the meta lives on the source list at READ time, not on the returned value. Two fixes: (a) put ^{:key k} on the vector literal returned by the function, or (b) wrap the result in (with-meta result {:key k}). Found in views_view.cljs PR #1471 fixing rf2-gphsi; same anti-pattern exists across several other panels (audit bead rf2-?? filed). Tell future test authors: a test that asserts :key meta on the rendered child reproduces the bug.

CLJ-KONDO LOCAL/CI VERSION SKEW — the local binary reports NINE PHANTOM ERRORS that CI does not. Quantified 2026-07-24 by two workers independently.

LOCAL on this machine: clj-kondo v2025.10.23. CI PINS: 2026.04.15.

The older local version reports 9 errors of the form `Expected: throwable, received: boolean/nil` in `implementation/ui/test/**` — DONOR TEST CODE — which CI version does not report at all. A worker reproducing a lint failure locally will chase nine non-existent failures in code it did not touch.

THE RULE: when a lint or gate verdict must be AUTHORITATIVE, read CI OWN JOB LOG rather than trusting a local run.
  gh pr checks <PR> --json name,state,link      # find the job id
  gh run view --job=<id> --log-failed           # what CI actually said
If you must reproduce locally, pin the CI version first. And run CI exact invocation from .github/workflows/lint.yml — same flags, same lint paths — not a convenient approximation of it.

⚠️ THIS COMPOUNDS WITH THE PIPED-EXIT-CODE TRAP (see piping-a-gate-into-tail-discards-its-exit-code). Together they produce the worst case: a local run that reports failures CI does not have, through a pipe that hides the exit code, so a worker can conclude either "I broke something" or "I am green" with equal confidence and be wrong both times. Capture to a file, echo the exit code, and when it matters read CI log.

MAYOR NOTE — A SEQUENCING ERROR I MADE ON THE SAME INCIDENT, worth not repeating: several PRs were red on clj-kondo. One worker reported that a specific open PR carried the fix, so I instructed another worker to STAND DOWN and wait for that PR to merge. Wrong on two counts: (a) the fix had ALREADY landed on main as a separate direct commit, and (b) the PR I named was a different change. The correct remedy was simply A REBASE ONTO CURRENT MAIN. Had the worker obeyed, its gate would have stayed red and we would have lost a cycle; it had already rebased and told me so.
GENERALISATION: when a gate is red because of something INHERITED, the fix is almost always "rebase onto a main that has the remedy", NOT "wait for a specific PR". Verify WHERE the remedy actually is (git branch -r --contains <sha>) before telling anyone to wait on anything.

NEVER `git checkout HEAD -- .beads` AFTER AN OPERATION THAT CHANGED THE DOLT DATABASE — re-export from Dolt instead. Learned the hard way 2026-07-23 during a bead GC.

THE NORMAL REFLEX IS CORRECT AND THAT IS THE TRAP. The mayor loop runs `git checkout HEAD -- .beads/issues.jsonl` before every pull, because an uncommitted export otherwise aborts the pull and silently freezes HEAD. That reflex is right on an ordinary heartbeat and I run it dozens of times a session.

WHAT HAPPENED: after `bd gc --older-than 14 --force` deleted 462 closed beads (2610 -> 2148 issues, export 2774 -> 2313 lines), my very next checkpoint began with the usual `git checkout HEAD -- .beads` — which RESTORED THE PRE-GC 2774-LINE EXPORT over the freshly shrunk one. Dolt now said 2148 while the git export claimed 2774. The commit reported success. Nothing looked wrong.

WHY IT IS DANGEROUS, not merely untidy: bd RE-IMPORTS the JSONL in various flows (a fresh worktree first-touch, a checkpoint re-import). Re-importing that stale export would have RESURRECTED ALL 462 DELETED BEADS. This is the same mechanism as the older reference_bd_close_reverted_by_jsonl_checkout memory, but at 462x the blast radius.

THE RULE, unconditional and safe in BOTH contexts:
  bd export --output .beads/issues.jsonl     # regenerate FROM the source of truth
  git add .beads/issues.jsonl
  git show :.beads/issues.jsonl | wc -l      # size guard BEFORE committing
  git commit && git push
Never restore the export from git over a database that has moved. Dolt is the source of truth; the JSONL is a projection of it. Regenerate the projection, never resurrect it.

HOW I CAUGHT IT: by VERIFYING the result rather than trusting the "committed + pushed" line — compare `bd stats` Total Issues against `wc -l` on the export. A git success message tells you a commit happened, not that it committed the right thing. Make that comparison part of any checkpoint following a bd operation.

ALSO FROM THE SAME GC (useful defaults): `bd gc --older-than N --dry-run` previews all three phases; the real run needs `--force`; it deletes ONLY closed issues older than N days and preserves every open/in-progress/blocked bead AND all memories (165 survived intact). Verify a handful of live bead ids and the memory count after any GC before committing the shrunk export.

STALE .shadow-cljs CLASSPATH MIMICS THE shadow.resource UNBOUND-VAR RACE — two different causes, one identical error string (2026-07-23).

THE SYMPTOM, identical in both cases: `unbound fn: #(quote shadow.resource/slurp-resource)`, surfacing as a compile failure (seen in scripts/api-manifest/probe/).

CAUSE A — STALE CLASSPATH (benign, one-time): commit 6328dca436 changed the shadow-cljs :source-path classpath root from spec/conformance to spec/. Any worktree with a WARM .shadow-cljs still holds the old classpath.edn and fails this way after pulling that commit. CURE: delete .shadow-cljs in that worktree and recompile (1811 files, 0 warnings observed). Every warm worktree that pulls that commit needs the one-time clear — expect this across a whole wave of workers, not just one.

CAUSE B — THE REAL RACE (rf2-sff2s, recurring as rf2-drpa3.78): requiring-resolve performs its first resolve BEFORE entering the namespace require lock; shadow/resource.clj ships un-AOT-d so it compiles from source on first use, and shadow-cljs macroexpands in parallel — a thread arriving mid-load gets the interned-but-UNBOUND Var. Cured per-consumer by a namespace-local delay, and process-wide by one shared choke point that enters the serialized require path before resolving.

⚠️ WHY THIS PAIRING IS DANGEROUS: a worker fixing the race can read a stale-classpath failure as its bug reproducing, or conclude its fix failed when it actually worked. And a worker hitting the stale classpath can waste a cycle believing it found a concurrency defect.

THE DISCRIMINATOR: a shadow-cljs COMPILE failure is not reliable evidence of the race in either direction. The race must be evidenced by a CONCURRENCY PROBE in a clean Clojure process — one thread cold-loading shadow.resource, an observer resolving the same Var and reporting its state — which observes the Var directly and does not depend on any build. If clearing .shadow-cljs makes the failure vanish, it was Cause A.

MAYOR RULE: when a wave of workers is running warm worktrees and a source-path or classpath-root change lands on main, expect this error across several of them and say so in briefs; do not let it be diagnosed independently five times.

Dependency-chain gating gotcha: workers close their bead on PR CREATION (not merge), so a 'bd dep add A B' where B closes-at-PR-creation makes 'bd ready' surface A as soon as B's PR is OPENED — BEFORE B's code is on main. If A and B touch the same files (surface-conflict sequencing), dispatching A off origin/main then conflicts when B merges. FIX: for surface-conflict gates, do NOT rely on the bd dep / bd ready alone — verify the BLOCKER PR is actually MERGED (gh pr view <#> state==MERGED) before claiming+worktreeing the dependent, and create its worktree off the POST-merge origin/main. A GUARD PROVEN ON CASES CAN STILL FAIL ON SEQUENCES — demand the sequence, not the cases. On 2026-07-19 I commissioned the ai/ tracking ratchet (rf2-lsp1i, #6380), accepted a three-teeth proof, merged it, and reported to Mike that his "nothing under /ai should be tracked" end-state was mechanically enforced. An independent audit (rf2-ow7dz) then showed it is a STATIC CEILING, not a ratchet: 89->61 passes (correct), and then 61->62 ALSO passes with exit 0 because 62 is still under the stored 89. Equal-count replacement admits a new path. After a decrease to zero the stale ceiling permits additions forever — i.e. the guard goes inert exactly when S7 starts removing files, which is the moment it was built for.

THE THREE TEETH WERE ALL REAL AND ALL PASSED: force-add fails and names the path; an S7-style removal passes; the unmutated tree passes. Every one tested a SINGLE transition from the pristine baseline. None tested a SECOND transition. The defect lives only in the composition.

THE RULE: when a guard carries STATE (a baseline, a ceiling, a high-water mark, a cached roster, an allowlist), case-based teeth are insufficient. Specify the SEQUENCE in the brief and demand per-arm exit codes for each step: pristine -> pass; violate -> fail; legitimately change -> pass; THEN violate again -> MUST STILL FAIL; and the degenerate end state (here, count 0) -> still guards. My acceptance bar was case-based all session while I asked every worker for mutation proofs against that same weak bar.

RELATED, SAME SESSION: rf2-wlqfq found one blanket mutation reddening three fixtures while leaving two green — certifying falsifiability it had not established for those two, because they named different levers. Both findings are the same lesson from opposite ends: A PROOF IS A CLAIM LIKE ANY OTHER AND NEEDS THE SAME SCEPTICISM AS THE THING IT PROVES. Ask what the proof does NOT cover before accepting it.

ALSO: a `bd close` can silently fail to take. rf2-r94by stayed OPEN for hours after I closed it and resurfaced as phantom work in the ready pool I was quoting counts from. REBASE conflict resolution: --ours/--theirs INVERT vs merge. In a rebase, --ours = the branch you are replaying ONTO (e.g. origin/main), --theirs = the commit being replayed (the worker's own branch). So to take MAIN's version of a generated file (e.g. docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js) during a rebase, use 'git checkout --ours <file>', NOT --theirs. My earlier dispatch instructions said --theirs for this and were WRONG (caught by the rf2-ywwpx worker on #6284, 2026-07-18, which verified empirically: stage2/--ours == origin/main, stage3/--theirs == its own stale commit). Harmless for a generated file that gets regenerated afterwards, but on a NON-generated conflict the same wording silently takes the wrong side and can revert main's work. ALWAYS instruct workers to verify which stage matches origin/main (git show :2:<file> / :3:<file> and compare digests) rather than trusting the label.

Instead: have the worker run its SLICE gates (the artefacts it touched) + a quick smoke, then OPEN the PR and let the PR's CI run the full matrix. The mayor merges on green CI. Reserve full-local-suite only for the very few beads where CI can't cover it. Applies to future B7/B9 + any big core bead.

FREEHAND API-MANIFEST IS A SERIAL LANE for public-verb beads — the biggest merge-friction in the Freehand build wave (2026-07-23). re-frame.freehand is a FULLY-ROWED manifest surface: adding ANY public verb requires FIVE co-edited files in ONE PR — implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc (facade block), spec/api-manifest.edn (REGENERATE, never hand-edit), spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn (classification row), spec/API.md (roster row + remove the declared-vacancy prose), docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md (member heading + remove vacancy prose). FOUR gates enforce it: the api-manifest gen --check entry point, api-md-check, doc-api-check, and the CLJS manifest probe under npm run test:cljs.

THE TRAP THAT COST THREE REBASES (presence PR 6713, measured — the most important part): git rebase AUTO-MERGES the generated spec/api-manifest.edn with NO conflict markers, merging the var ROWS correctly while leaving a STALE :var-count HEADER (observed 517 against a set of 519). The file looks cleanly merged and is SELF-INCONSISTENT. The drift gate then reds with "var set identical; :meta or formatting differs — regenerate", which READS LIKE a formatting or toolchain problem and sends you hunting the wrong cause. IT IS NOT A TOOLCHAIN TRAP. Cure: run the plain generator (no --check flag) to overwrite byte-exact, then --check must exit 0 AND git diff spec/api-manifest.edn must be EMPTY after that fresh run — the empty diff is the proof the committed file equals the generator output.

RULE: for a GENERATED file, a clean auto-merge is NOT evidence of correctness. Treat every rebase touching api-manifest.edn as resolve-by-REGENERATE whether or not git reported a conflict.

PROVE A COMMITTED TEST WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THE ORIGINAL BUG — build a mutant of the broken version. Established by the rf2-fr5yx worker (#6414) closing out my own failure.

BACKGROUND: I commissioned the ai/ ratchet (rf2-lsp1i #6380), accepted a three-teeth proof, merged it, and told the operator his end-state ruling was enforced. It was a STATIC CEILING: 89->61 passed, then 61->62 ALSO passed. All three teeth were genuine; each tested a SINGLE TRANSITION from a pristine baseline. The defect lived only in the composition, and the proof lived only in a chat report, so nothing re-ran it.

WHAT #6414 DID, and what to copy: it did not merely commit the seven arms. It BUILT A FAITHFUL MUTANT OF THE ORIGINAL BROKEN GATE (stale root-commit ceiling + count comparison) and ran the new suite against it. Result: arms 3+4, 5, 6b and 7 FAILED while arms 1 and 2 still passed — and arm 3+4 failed on exactly the right assertion (decrease passed, then the increase also passed, 0 !== 1). That demonstrates the committed test CATCHES THE SHIPPED BUG, rather than merely passing on the fixed code. It also kept a second, lighter control: the old decision rule reproduced in-test and asserted to pass the arms it should pass.

THE RULE: when committing a regression test for a bug that already shipped, do not stop at "green on the fix". Reconstruct the broken behaviour and show the suite REDS against it, arm by arm. A suite that only ever ran against correct code has never been shown to discriminate. This is the same scepticism as the mutation-proof rule, applied to the proof itself — and it is how you find that a tooth is a passenger (rf2-kxork found a suffix rename still contained its sentinel; rf2-vxgfnd.195 arm 4 built a function-name oracle, measured that it could never go red, and DELETED it).

A SHELL SCRIPT COMMITTED WITHOUT THE EXEC BIT (100644) PASSES LOCALLY ON WINDOWS AND FAILS CI ON LINUX. Found by the #6457 story-package fix-worker, 2026-07-19.

THE MECHANISM: a new .github/scripts/*.sh invoked DIRECTLY (./script.sh on PATH) needs the executable bit on Linux. Committed at git mode 100644 it gives "Permission denied" / exit 126 in CI. But WINDOWS-LOCAL GIT HAS core.filemode OFF, and bash runs the script regardless of the bit, so the author's local run exits 0. This is the exact local-green-≠-CI gap, and it is SPECIFIC to this repo's cross-platform setup (Mike develops on Windows; CI is Linux). The .github/scripts/_preflight-story-package.test.cjs harness gate went red on all 10 cases with "env: './...preflight-story-package.sh': Permission denied  126 !== 0" while test:script-policy had passed on Windows.

THE FIX (satisfies policy, changes zero content): git update-index --chmod=+x <script> — flips 100644 -> 100755, blob hash unchanged. Match the passing sibling's mode.

⚠️ IT IS ALSO A REAL BUG BEYOND THE TEST: the same script was invoked directly by release-story.yml, so the missing bit would have broken the actual release path, not just the harness self-test.

RULES:
1. Any dispatch that ADDS a .sh under .github/scripts/ (or anywhere invoked as ./script) must set the exec bit — check `git ls-files -s <script>` shows 100755, and mirror a passing sibling's mode.
2. A brief that adds a shell script must say: run the FULL CI harness command (npm run test:script-policy && npm run test:script-helpers), not just test:script-policy — CI runs both after &&, and test:script-helpers / the new .test.cjs is where a mode/policy break surfaces.
3. This joins the cross_platform_maintainers memory: file MODE, line endings, and path separators are all invisible-on-Windows / enforced-on-Linux. When a gate is green locally on this Windows box but red in CI, SUSPECT A PLATFORM-VISIBILITY DIFFERENCE (exec bit, CRLF, case-sensitivity) before assuming a flake.

RESOLVED 2026-07-23 by PR #6700 — the fixture-cache warning is NO LONGER needed in Freehand worker briefs. Freehand conformance fixtures are now a shadow-cljs build dependency, so a fixture-only edit invalidates the cache and the compiled test sees the new expectations.

WHAT THE BUG WAS, kept because the shape recurs: re-frame.freehand.conformance/fixture inlined its .edn at MACRO-EXPANSION time, and shadow-cljs had no dependency edge from a test namespace to the fixture it inlined. A fixture-only edit therefore did not invalidate the build cache, and the compiled test kept asserting the PREVIOUS expectations. A green CLJS or browser conformance run after a fixture change was worthless. The JVM side was never affected.

MEASURED TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY, by two workers with no stake in each other's finding — which is why it was believed rather than argued about. The route-link slice mutated a fixture and got 484 tests / 2746 assertions / 0 failures, green on a fixture that MUST fail; its probe passed TWICE before it cleared the cache. The CI-classifier slice separately flipped FH-CALL-001 :predicates :view? true->false and saw a warm cache recompile 1 file and report 0 failures, versus 124 files and 1 failure after clearing.

⚠️ THE GENERAL LESSON, WHICH OUTLIVES THIS FIX AND IS WHY THIS MEMORY SURVIVES: a table-driven gate whose expectations are INLINED AT COMPILE TIME can silently decouple from its data. Whenever test expectations live in a separate file that a macro reads, ASK WHETHER THE BUILD SYSTEM KNOWS ABOUT THAT EDGE — and prove it the only way that counts: mutate the data WITHOUT clearing any cache and require RED. A fix verified only after a cache clear proves nothing, because that is the broken state's own behaviour.

THE RULE: when grepping to establish whether code exists, EXCLUDE the tracker export and other generated/derived files:
  git grep <pattern> -- implementation/ spec/ docs/     # scope it

DUPLICATE deftest — CLJS WARNS, THE JVM IS SILENT. rf2-9e4lf (#6349, 2026-07-18) verified this with a standalone probe rather than assuming: a Clojure namespace defining the same deftest twice, with the FIRST body deliberately failing, reports 'Ran 1 tests... 0 failures' and emits ZERO diagnostic output. Clojure's 'already refers to' warning only fires ACROSS namespaces, so there is no JVM equivalent of shadow-cljs's :redef-in-file. CONSEQUENCE: a duplicate deftest in a .cljs/.cljc file is detectable (shadow-cljs warns on every build — rf2-qo5xk's went unread for months); the same defect in a .clj file is COMPLETELY INVISIBLE. Only the test count reveals it. PROOF TECHNIQUE (use this, not a green suite): to show a resurrected test body actually executes, temporarily INVERT one of its assertions and confirm the suite reds AT THE NEW SYMBOL NAME — that is impossible while the body is being replaced. Then revert and gate on the reverted tree. A green suite plus a +1 count is weaker: the count can rise for unrelated reasons and green proves only that nothing failed. Both instances found so far (qo5xk, 9e4lf) were genuinely DISTINCT tests collapsed onto one symbol by different causes — a rename sweep and a copy-pasted parallel test block — so archaeology first, never assume the cause from a sibling case.

A CONSOLE SHIM IN THE BROWSER LANE PASSES VACUOUSLY — replacing js/console.warn does NOT intercept what the runner sees. Found 2026-07-24 by the rf2-drpa3.114/.115 worker, in its own harness, before shipping.

THE MECHANISM: the worker wrote an `advisories` helper that replaced `js/console.warn` and counted the sentences it captured, to assert that N advisories were published. THE WARNINGS STILL REACHED PLAYWRIGHT CDP CAPTURE AND THE COUNTER STAYED AT 0. So the assertion "exactly N advisories were published" was TRUE-BY-EMPTINESS: it would pass whether the code published N, zero, or a thousand.

WHY: in `npm run test:browser`, console output is captured by Playwright over the Chrome DevTools Protocol AT THE BROWSER LEVEL, not by whatever the page has bound to `js/console.warn` at that moment. Rebinding the JS symbol changes what PAGE code calls; it does not change what the RUNNER observes, and it does not stop the real emission.

THE FIX THE WORKER CHOSE, and it is the right one: DO NOT ASSERT ON CONSOLE OUTPUT IN THE BROWSER LANE. Assert on the TRACE RECORDS instead — which was the bead actual contract anyway. The console sentence is a human-facing rendering of the event; the record is the thing with a schema.

THE DEFENCE IS THE SAME ONE EVERY TIME AND IT IS CHEAP: make the assertion FAIL ON PURPOSE before trusting it. Publish a known number and confirm the counter sees it; if the counter reads 0 when something plainly happened, the harness is broken, not the code. A counter that has never counted anything has not been tested.

GENERAL FORM: when a test asserts on OBSERVED OUTPUT rather than on a RETURNED VALUE, ask WHO IS DOING THE OBSERVING. If the observer sits outside your process or below your language runtime — a CDP capture, a subprocess pipe, a native logger — then rebinding a symbol inside the runtime does not intercept it.
